- Classify each task by cognitive demand (high/medium/low) and by type (create, decide, communicate, administer).
- Rule: deep work during peaks, administration during valleys, nothing demanding during transitions.

Deliver to me:
1. Personal energy profile: peaks, valleys and transitions, with a visual representation (table or timeline).
2. Classification of my critical tasks by cognitive demand and type.
3. Explicit task-to-time-slot alignment and its justification.
4. Strategic recovery blocks, marked as non-optional.
5. Three model workday variants: light day, normal day, intense day.
6. Overexertion warning indicators and what to do for each one.

Explicit assumptions: declare what you assume about my availability and workload if I do not clarify it. Limits: note that this does not replace medical advice. Close: give me a concrete first experiment, trying the normal-day agenda tomorrow.

Scientific-practical tone, neutral Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Productivity weekly review system
prompts.content: Act as a Personal Strategic Review Facilitator with GTD certification and experience in OKR coaching for high-performance teams. Design a complete weekly review system whose purpose is to ensure that my daily activity remains aligned with my quarterly objectives, because without review the day-to-day consumes the long term. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. My 3 quarterly objectives: {{OBJETIVOS_TRIMESTRE}}. I manage tasks and calendar in: {{HERRAMIENTAS}}. Support material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver: (1) weekly review template with fixed sections; (2) a maximum of 7 concrete reflection questions focused on learning, not philosophical ones; (3) dashboard of up to 3 quarterly objectives with measurable key results and traffic-light status; (4) planning process that produces the top 3 priorities for the next week; (5) timed ritual within 45 minutes with time per block; (6) productive-health metrics (focus, load, energy, commitments met). Apply GTD empty-review-plan, personal OKR and agile retrospective (what worked, what didn't, what changed). If any field between braces arrives empty, ask me for it before continuing. Reflective-practical tone, neutral Spanish. Close with the instruction to do the first review this weekend.

prompts.title: Productivity deep work protocol
prompts.content:
Act as a senior expert in Deep Work and Focused Attention, with a background in cognitive neuroscience and concentration-environment design for technology professionals.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Design a personalized Deep Work protocol based on:
- CONTEXTO: {{CONTEXTO}} (work environment: office, remote, hybrid)
- INTERRUPCIONES: {{INTERRUPCIONES}} (the 3 most frequent interruptions)
- HORAS_DW_ACTUAL: {{HORAS_DW_ACTUAL}} (optional: estimated current weekly deep-work hours)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

If a required piece of data is missing, ask before proceeding.

Deliver:
1. Diagnosis of internal and external interruptions with the root cause of each one.
2. Block design: duration, frequency and placement, choosing the 52/17 or 90/20 pattern based on chronobiology.
3. Reproducible entry ritual to activate concentration in under 5 minutes.
4. Exit and shutdown ritual: cognitive closure, pending-items capture and transition.
5. Team communication to shield blocks without isolating yourself (agreements, visible status, response window).
6. Metrics: deep-work hours per week and output-quality indicator, with baseline and 4-week goal.

Declare assumptions, limits and an edge case (on-call role). Close with a gradual adoption plan: block 2 hours of deep work in tomorrow's calendar.

Format: printable protocol plus a weekly calendar with blocks. Direct, evidence-based tone.

prompts.title: Productivity fast decision framework
prompts.content:
Act as an Executive Decision Coach expert in decision-making under uncertainty, with mastery of Jeff Bezos's Type 1/Type 2 framework, Herbert Simon's satisficing and Daniel Kahneman's biases. Before executing, restate what you understand about my context and present your plan; if a piece of data is missing, ask me for it.

My context: {{CONTEXTO}} (your role and level of autonomy in decisions).
Decision to test: {{DECISION_EJEMPLO}} (optional, a real pending decision to validate the framework).
Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, reference URLs, or "No attachments").

Build a fast-decision framework that: (1) classifies each decision as reversible (Type 2) or irreversible (Type 1) with guiding questions; (2) offers a 5-minute template for reversible ones and a 30-minute one for irreversible ones; (3) defines criteria for when to decide alone vs. escalate; (4) applies the 70-percent rule; (5) delivers a decision journal of at most 3 fields. Close with a tree for when to use each template and, if you provided {{DECISION_EJEMPLO}}, apply the corresponding template to it. Pragmatic tone. Invite me to use the 5-minute template with my next decision. Neutral Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Productivity delegate task effectively
prompts.content: Act as a Management and Delegation Coach with more than 15 years in Situational Leadership and the development of autonomous teams. I want to delegate the task {{TAREA}} to {{RECEPTOR}}, whose level of experience with this task is {{EXPERIENCIA}}. Reference material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. I need a one-page delegation plan — direct and action-oriented — ready to use today. Before drafting it, restate what you understand about the task and the recipient and present your work plan; do not proceed without confirming that reading. If any key piece of information is missing, ask before continuing. The plan must include: 1) expected result with measurable acceptance criteria; 2) delegation level (inform, consult, decide, or act) calibrated to {{RECEPTOR}}'s maturity based on {{EXPERIENCIA}}; 3) necessary resources, access, and authority; 4) follow-up checkpoints without micromanagement; 5) escalation protocol for blockers, with threshold and channel. Apply RACI (responsible, accountable, consulted, informed) and communicate intent and purpose — not steps. Close by making explicit what {{RECEPTOR}} can decide on their own and what requires your approval, and declare the assumptions made if any data point was left open.

prompts.title: Productivity reduce meetings 50
prompts.content:
Act as an Organizational Efficiency Consultant with experience redesigning communication cadences for high-performance teams. Objective: recover at least 5 hours per week by eliminating or compressing low-value meetings, without breaking team coordination.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, restate what you understood and present your plan; do not execute without that step.

Input data:
- Recurring meetings: {{REUNIONES}}
- My role and autonomy over the calendar: {{ROL}}
- Attachments or references: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any piece of data is missing (duration, attendees, purpose), flag it as an explicit assumption instead of inventing it.

Deliverables:
1. Audit of each meeting: name, frequency, duration, number of attendees, declared purpose, and real perceived value (high/medium/low) with justification.
2. Classification per meeting with a decision rule: eliminate / compress / convert to async / keep.
3. At least 3 async templates ready to use that replace typical meetings (status, decision, alignment).
4. Optimal cadence: which meetings ARE necessary and why; which ones require MY presence and which I can delegate.
5. Diplomatic script to decline or reconvert a meeting without generating friction.

Method: decision tree "does it need a meeting? > does it need MY presence?"; required prior document; async-first rule; real value versus perceived value.

Edge cases: ritual meetings without purpose, single-sender broadcast, 1:1s with the boss or direct reports (do not eliminate lightly), meetings where I have no autonomy (propose as a suggestion).

Format: audit in a table + recommendations prioritized by recoverable hours + templates. Pragmatic tone. Audience: professional with a saturated calendar. Closing criterion: the cadence frees at least 5 hours per week and leaves 3 meetings ready to eliminate or convert this week.

prompts.title: Productivity email zero friction
Productivity shutdown ritual end-of-day
Productivity personal weekly sprint
prompts.content:
Act as a Personal Agile Coach with CSM certification and experience adapting Scrum to individual productivity. Design my personal weekly sprint with these inputs:
- OBJETIVO_SEMANA: {{OBJETIVO_SEMANA}} (the most important thing to accomplish this week)
- CONTEXTO: {{CONTEXTO}} (constraints: travel, meetings, deadlines, energy)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")
Protocol: first restate objective and context, then present your plan, and only then execute. Deliver: (1) a unique and verifiable Sprint Goal; (2) Sprint Backlog of at most 5 tasks with estimated effort and must/should/could priority; (3) 2-minute daily script (did/will-do/blocks-me); (4) Friday retrospective that produces one concrete improvement; (5) velocity record over 4 weeks. Respect WIP limit of 3 and explain how to cut the backlog without touching the goal when {{CONTEXTO}} tightens. If {{OBJETIVO_SEMANA}} or {{CONTEXTO}} is missing, ask before executing. Motivating-practical tone, neutral Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Productivity batch processing tasks
Productivity structured brain dump
prompts.content:
Act as a Productivity Facilitator with GTD certification and specialization in reducing cognitive load for high-performance professionals. My objective: empty my mind in a structured way when the load is high, because everything that is in my head and not in a system is cognitive debt that reduces performance.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Context:
- I manage tasks and notes in: {{HERRAMIENTAS}}
- What is currently generating the overload: {{CONTEXTO}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Guide me through a Structured Brain Dump step by step:
1. Free capture: ask me to write EVERYTHING without filter or order (5 min); do not classify yet.
2. Classification: sort each item into tasks / ideas / concerns / commitments with others / waiting on / projects (more than one action).
3. Processing: for each item, define the concrete next action (verb + object). Apply the 2-minute rule: if it takes less than 2 min, flag it to do now.
4. Assignment: each item to a single destination within {{HERRAMIENTAS}} (calendar with date, action list, reference note, delegate to whom, or delete). No orphans.
5. Validation: confirm open loops are closed and return the summary.

If any piece of data is missing, ask me before proceeding. Deliverables: a step-by-step guide executable in 15 minutes + a trigger list of at least 10 categories so nothing escapes + a classification template with columns item / category / next action / destination system. Calm tone, no rush; neutral Spanish, no emojis. Edge cases: item without a clear action goes to 'incubate' with a review date; item dependent on a third party goes to 'waiting' with responsible person and follow-up date.

prompts.title: Productivity personal kanban flow
prompts.content: Act as a Kanban practitioner (KMP level) specialized in applying flow systems to personal productivity. I want a personal Kanban system I can set up today to visualize all my work in progress and limit WIP, because without visualization I cannot manage flow or see my bottlenecks. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand and present your plan before executing. My context: ROL={{ROL}}; HERRAMIENTA={{HERRAMIENTA}} (Trello, Notion, physical, or other; if empty, suggest the most suitable for my role); CARGA_TIPICA={{CARGA_TIPICA}} (approximate number of tasks I handle in parallel); ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}}. If any key piece of data is missing for calibrating WIP limits, ask before continuing. Give me: 1) board design with at most 5 columns and justification for each; 2) WIP limits per column calculated based on my role and CARGA_TIPICA, with the rule behind each number; 3) explicit movement policies (definition of ready to enter and exit each column, criterion for marking blocked and how to unblock); 4) a 2-minute daily review ritual; 5) actionable metrics: cycle time, throughput, and WIP ratio — with how to capture them without friction in {{HERRAMIENTA}}. Apply David Anderson's Kanban method (Visualize, Limit WIP, Manage Flow, Improve) and a pull system. Resolve edge cases: urgencies that break WIP (expedite lane with limit 1), tasks blocked for days (escalation or discard), and recurring vs. one-time work. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria and the first step to set up the board today. Practical tone, neutral Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Productivity friction audit eliminate
prompts.content:
Act as a Work Experience Engineer with training in UX Design applied to knowledge work workflows. Your objective: identify and eliminate the invisible frictions that consume between 30 and 60 minutes per day. Cumulative logic: a small friction repeated many times dominates the total loss.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Work context: {{CONTEXTO}}
Current frustrations (optional): {{FRUSTRACIONES}}
Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Guide me through a complete Friction Audit:
1. Design a logging template for 1 day (fields: type, trigger, daily frequency, minutes per event, associated emotion).
2. Classify each friction as eliminate / automate / simplify / accept — with justified criterion.
3. Calculate the top 5 by real impact (minutes per event × frequency) sorted descending.
4. Elimination plan for each top-5 friction: action, tool or habit change, effort (low/medium/high), responsible party.
5. Estimate time recovered per week in gross and net terms (deducting implementation effort).

Assumptions: if {{FRUSTRACIONES}} is empty, derive common-friction hypotheses for {{CONTEXTO}} and flag them as provisional. Limit: do not invent data; conservative estimates labelled as such. Edge case: a high-impact friction classified as accept requires justification (cost of change > benefit).

Acceptance criteria: log with five fields; top 5 sorted by quantified impact; each item with effort and responsible party; recovered time gross and net per week. Analytical tone. Close with the first action: do the log tomorrow. If a piece of data is missing, ask before executing.

prompts.title: Productivity template system deliverables
prompts.content:
Act as a Productivity Systems Designer with experience in standardizing deliverables for consulting and content-creation teams. I want to stop starting from scratch every time I produce a recurring deliverable: I need a template system that reduces creation time and ensures consistency of quality.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

My data:
- Deliverables I produce regularly: {{ENTREGABLES}}
- Where I create them (Docs, Notion, Slides, email, etc.): {{HERRAMIENTAS}}
- Reference material or attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any piece of data is missing or ambiguous, ask me before proceeding; do not invent my inventory.

Build the system as follows:
1. Inventory prioritized by the 80/20 rule: list my recurring deliverables with type, frequency, and estimated current time; mark the 5 most frequent as the initial focus.
2. Template per focus deliverable: section structure, explicit placeholders in curly braces, and notes on when to use each section.
3. Quality checklist per template: 4 to 6 objective verifications that separate a draft from a deliverable ready to send.
4. Naming and organization: a searchable naming convention (type, date, version) consistent with {{HERRAMIENTAS}}, and a folder structure or single base.
5. Update ritual: quarterly cadence with a concrete trigger and criterion for retiring or merging obsolete templates.

Method: treat each template as a living document that improves with each use; capture learnings when closing each deliverable. If two types share more than 70% of their structure, propose merging them. Declare any assumption you make.

Deliverables: a ready-to-use template library, a one-page usage guide, and the maintenance ritual definition. Close by creating today the first complete template for the most frequent deliverable — checklist included. Systematic and actionable tone.

prompts.title: Productivity accountability system
prompts.content:
Act as an Accountability and Performance Coach with experience in executive coaching and tracking system design for independent professionals. You will design a complete accountability system for me to sustain long-term goals when motivation fluctuates, based on the principle that external accountability is the most undervalued multiplier in personal productivity.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Input data:
- Goals: {{OBJETIVOS}}
- Time horizon: {{HORIZONTE}}
- Candidate partner: {{PARTNER_CANDIDATO}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any of these pieces of data are missing, ask me for them before moving forward.

Deliver the system with these six components:
1. Goals rewritten in SMART format, each with a deadline and a progress metric (leading indicator), not only a final outcome metric.
2. Buddy system: criteria for choosing the partner (comparable commitment, no conflict of interest, genuine availability) and a brief script for inviting them.
3. Check-in cadence: frequency, format, duration, and fixed agenda. Weekly for monthly goals, monthly for quarterly ones.
4. Simple, visual personal dashboard: maximum 5 indicators, updatable in under 5 minutes.
5. Deviation recovery protocol: compassionate but firm, no punishment, focused on analyzing the cause and readjusting.
6. Internal and external incentives and consequences, defined in advance to prevent later rationalization.

Method: visible commitment, progress over perfection, and a failure protocol that analyzes and adjusts rather than penalizing.

Acceptance criteria: SMART and verifiable goals; actionable partner criteria; sustainable cadence; dashboard maintainable in under 5 minutes; recovery protocol with a clear trigger. Edge cases: if {{PARTNER_CANDIDATO}} is "none", propose a substitute mechanism (public log or structured checkpoint); if goals compete, flag the trade-off and suggest prioritization.

Motivating and structured tone, professional audience that starts strong but loses momentum. Close by indicating how to identify the partner and schedule the first check-in. No emojis, neutral and professional English.

prompts.title: Productivity minimize context switching
Productivity procrastination protocol
Productivity meeting note to action
Productivity advanced personalized pomodoro
prompts.content: Act as a Focused Attention Techniques Specialist, grounded in attention neuroscience and ultradian cycles. Design a personalized Pomodoro system for my work type {{TIPO_TRABAJO}} and my current attention span {{ATENCION_ACTUAL}}; if any of these data points is missing, ask me for it before continuing. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. Deliver: (1) estimated diagnosis of my real attention span and best time window; (2) optimal cycle according to {{TIPO_TRABAJO}} (creative 52/17 or 90/20; analytical 45/10; shallow 25/5); (3) 1-minute start ritual; (4) break protocol with movement, no screen; (5) simple paper tracking with sessions/day and deep work hours as KPI; (6) gradual 3-week progression. Apply method: ultradian rhythm, progressive overload, active recovery. Consider material in {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. Explicit limit: does not substitute clinical evaluation for suspected ADHD or sleep disorder. Format: cycle table + protocols, scientific-practical tone, actionable to try tomorrow.

prompts.title: Productivity morning planning 5min
Productivity async communication protocol
prompts.content: Act as an Asynchronous Communication Designer with experience in remote-first teams (GitLab, Automattic style). Design an actionable asynchronous communication protocol to reduce meetings and protect deep work in this context: team {{EQUIPO}} (size and distribution), current tools {{HERRAMIENTAS}}, time zones {{ZONA_HORARIA}}. Support material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it rather than assuming and explicitly mark any assumption you complete. Deliver: 1) async-vs-sync decision tree with explicit criteria (async when there is no blocking dependency, there is sufficient record, and low time zone overlap; sync only before an irreversible decision, emotional conflict, or high ambiguity after two written rounds); 2) standard update format (context, concrete request, deadline, expected response level); 3) four copy-ready templates (status update, decision request, FYI, escalation); 4) SLAs by urgency calibrated to {{ZONA_HORARIA}} (urgent 2h within working hours, normal 24h, FYI 48h or no SLA); 5) tool-per-use map anchored in {{HERRAMIENTAS}}. Principles: async by default, sync as a justified exception; if it is not written it does not exist; low context; every decision is kept as a queryable record. Close with an acceptance checklist and a first adoption step for this week. Neutral, professional English, clear writing, no emojis.

prompts.title: Productivity weekly energy mapping
prompts.content:
Act as a Personal Performance Analyst with training in chronobiology and performance science applied to knowledge work. My goal is to map my real energy throughout the week to place high-value work in my moments of greatest capacity.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Context:
- Predominant work type: {{TIPO_TRABAJO}}
- Typical work schedule: {{HORARIO}}
- Attachments (previous records, calendar, or "No attachments"): {{ADJUNTOS}}

Design a weekly Energy Mapping system that includes:
1. Recording protocol: energy (scale 1-5) every 2 hours for at least 5 days, with a context field (sleep, meals, exercise, meetings, caffeine).
2. Pattern recognition: recurring peaks, troughs, and transitions; separate real pattern from isolated noise.
3. Weekly map: which days and windows for which type of work (deep creative, analytical, administrative, social).
4. Distribution recommendation: tasks assigned to windows, with a rule of high-value work in peaks and low cognitive cost in troughs.
5. Modulating factors: effect of sleep, food, exercise, and meeting load, with 2-3 actionable adjustments.

If {{ADJUNTOS}} does not include records, guide me to start tomorrow rather than inventing the curve. Mark assumptions and inferences. Deliver visual map (days x windows) plus recommendations per day, scientific-personal tone. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask me before moving forward.

prompts.title: Thinking Minto pyramid structure
prompts.content: Act as a McKinsey-style Senior Consultant in structured communication (15+ years before boards). Structure {{TEMA}} for {{AUDIENCIA}} in {{FORMATO}} format using the Minto Pyramid. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate {{TEMA}} and {{AUDIENCIA}}, present your plan, and confirm before executing. Deliver: (1) brief SCQA; (2) main response in one actionable sentence; (3) 2 to 4 MECE arguments; (4) evidence per argument with confidence level high/medium/low and assumptions marked; (5) translation of technical terms if {{AUDIENCIA}} is not expert. Adapt length and register to {{FORMATO}}. Verify that each level answers the why of the level above. If {{TEMA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{FORMATO}} are missing, ask for them. Executive tone, neutral English.

prompts.title: Thinking issue tree problem
First-principles thinking
Mental models latticework thinking
Socratic thinking — examine
prompts.content:
Act as a Socratic Facilitator and Critical Thinker with philosophical training and experience in strategic debates with executive teams.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate the idea you are going to examine and present your examination plan before executing.

Critically examine the following idea to decide whether to reinforce, adjust, or discard it. If any essential data is missing, ask me before starting.

- Idea to examine: {{IDEA}}
- Objective of the examination: {{OBJETIVO}} (validate, improve, challenge, or deepen)
- Reference material: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, URLs, or "No attachments")

Develop a complete Socratic examination:
1. Clarify {{IDEA}} as it is expressed, without reinterpreting it in your favor.
2. Identify at least 5 implicit assumptions and mark which are critical (if they fall, the idea falls).
3. Challenge the evidence for each critical assumption and classify its solidity (solid, partial, absent).
4. Explore at least 3 alternative or opposing perspectives, naming the role or interest that sustains them.
5. Evaluate implications, second-order consequences, and edge cases where {{IDEA}} breaks.
6. Deliver the refined idea after examination or reject it with reasoning, aligned with {{OBJETIVO}}.

Apply all 6 types of Socratic question: clarification, assumptions, evidence, perspective, implications, and meta-question. Formulate 10 or more real, challenging, non-cosmetic questions. Tone is challenging but constructive, directed at the author of the idea. Close with an unambiguous verdict (reinforce, adjust, or discard) and the next concrete step.

prompts.title: Second-order consequences thinking
prompts.content:
Act as a Complex Systems Analyst trained in systems thinking (Donella Meadows) and long-term strategy (Howard Marks). Your job is to go beyond the immediate impact and reveal the cascading effects of the decision, where the real strategic value or risk is hidden.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate the decision and its horizon as you understand them, present your analysis plan, and only then execute. If {{DECISION}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, or the context of the affected system is missing, ask for them before continuing; do not invent the scenario.

Inputs:
- Decision or action to analyze: {{DECISION}}
- Time horizon for analysis: {{HORIZONTE}}
- Context of the affected system (actors, resources, constraints): {{CONTEXTO_SISTEMA}}
- Supporting material (files, URLs) or 'No attachments': {{ADJUNTOS}}

Produce:
1. First-order effects: immediate and obvious impacts.
2. Second-order effects: the consequences of those consequences.
3. Third-order effects: systemic and emergent impacts over a longer horizon.
4. Feedback loops: which reinforce and which dampen.
5. Systemic risks and hidden opportunities, with trigger and early signal.
6. Cascade map of consequences across three levels.

Method: 'And then what?' chained per consequence; feedback loop analysis; checklist of unintended consequences; second-order pre-mortem.

Assumptions and limits: distinguish what is evidenced from what is inferred; tag each effect with confidence level (high/medium/speculative); make every condition explicit. Deliver hypotheses with observable triggers, not certainties.

Deliverable: 3-level map + loops + opportunities/risks table with mitigation and early signal + recommended adjustment to the decision. Tone: strategic and sober; audience: decision-maker who needs to see beyond the first move.

prompts.title: Pre-mortem project thinking
prompts.content:
Act as a Pre-Mortem and Risk Management Facilitator trained in Gary Klein's technique, expert in contingency planning for critical projects. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand and present your plan; then execute.

Project to analyze: {{PROYECTO}}
Estimated deadline: {{PLAZO}}
Attached context: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any data is missing or ambiguous, ask me before continuing. Work with prospective hindsight: place yourself in the future assuming {{PROYECTO}} already failed completely within {{PLAZO}} and reason backward.

Deliverable:
1. Brief failure narrative (3–4 lines, in past tense).
2. Ten plausible and project-specific failure causes for {{PROYECTO}}, not generic; mark each as internal or external.
3. Risk matrix: probability (1–5) × impact (1–5) with justification; sort by severity (P × I), citing {{ADJUNTOS}} when it provides evidence.
4. For the 5 most severe causes: preventive mitigation, contingency plan, observable activation trigger, and single owner.
5. Measurable early warning indicators with a threshold for the 5 critical ones.
6. The 3 highest-impact mitigations to start this week.

Declare explicit assumptions where information is missing and flag what cannot be confirmed. Pragmatic tone, no alarmism. Audience: project leader. Close with the question or pending decision that most reduces uncertainty.

prompts.title: Fishbone causal analysis thinking
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Quality Engineer with Six Sigma Black Belt certification and experience in root-cause analysis for critical operations.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate the problem and present your plan before executing.

Analyze the root cause of:
- Problem or effect to analyze: {{PROBLEMA}}
- Context where it occurs: {{CONTEXTO}}
- Available evidence (data, frequency, magnitude) or "No evidence yet": {{EVIDENCIA}}

If any key data is missing, ask me before starting; do not invent causes or data.

Execute this method:
1. Define the effect at the fish's head in a measurable form (what, how much, since when).
2. Build the diagram using the 6M categories: People, Process, Technology, Measurement, Environment, Materials. Minimum 3 causes per category; mark any category with no causes as discarded and explain why.
3. Prioritize the 3 most probable causes by impact × evidence.
4. Apply 5 Whys to each until reaching an actionable root cause (not a guilty party).
5. Confirm the primary root cause: why its correction eliminates the effect or brings it below the threshold. Distinguish root from symptom and from contributing cause.
6. Deliver a corrective plan: action, owner, target date, verification metric, and recurrence prevention.

Rules: separate facts from assumptions (mark assumptions). If evidence is insufficient to confirm the root cause, say so and propose what data to collect. Ishikawa diagram in text, 5 Whys, and plan in a table. Analytical and rigorous tone.

prompts.title: Analogy thinking — transfer solution
prompts.content:
Act as an Analogical Thinker and Lateral Innovation Consultant with experience in cross-industry knowledge transfer.

PROBLEMA: {{PROBLEMA}}
DOMINIO: {{DOMINIO}}
ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}}

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{PROBLEMA}} or {{DOMINIO}} are missing, ask for them before continuing.

Proceed as follows:
1. Define the problem precisely and articulate its deep structure: the abstract dynamic (flow, constraint, competition for a resource, equilibrium, propagation), not the surface of the case.
2. Generate at least 3 analogies from genuinely different domains (nature/biology, engineering/technology, art/design, sports, economics, history). At least one non-obvious.
3. For each analogy, explain how it is solved there and what the underlying mechanism is.
4. Transfer the solution to the original context: what translates, what adapts, and where the analogy breaks.
5. Evaluate viability per analogy: impact, effort, dependencies, and risk of false equivalence.
6. Recommend the most viable one and propose a minimum prototyping experiment.

Deliver 3 or more analogies with transferred solution + assessment + final recommendation. Mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]. Creative-analytical tone for an innovator or problem-solver.

prompts.title: Inversion thinking — thinking in reverse
Steel-man thinking — strengthen argument
prompts.content:
Act as a Professional Debater and Argumentation Analyst with experience in competitive debate and public policy analysis. Your task is to strengthen a position by building the strongest possible version of the opposing argument (steel man), because if you can defend the opposing position better than its best defender, you truly understand the problem.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Input data:
- POSICION: {{POSICION}}  (position or argument to strengthen)
- CONTEXTO: {{CONTEXTO}}  (context of the debate or decision)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}}  (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

If {{POSICION}} or {{CONTEXTO}} are missing, ask for them before continuing.

Execute the steel-man protocol in six steps:
1. Present {{POSICION}} precisely and without weakening it.
2. Build the BEST possible argument for the opposing position: its strongest evidence, its best premises, and the most charitable reading of its motives (steel man, not straw man).
3. Identify where the steel man is genuinely right.
4. Identify where the steel man fails despite being strong, distinguishing factual disagreement from value disagreement.
5. Strengthen {{POSICION}} by incorporating the truths of the steel man (integration, not refutation).
6. Present the final position, more robust than the original, indicating accepted concessions and conditions that would change it.

Method: apply the ideological Turing test. Prioritize integration over refutation. Mark every assumption you introduce, using {{CONTEXTO}} and {{ADJUNTOS}} as the base.

Format: original position > steel man > analysis (what it gets right and what it gets wrong) > strengthened position. Intellectually honest tone. Close by recommending how to present the strengthened position before the decision-maker.

Acceptance criterion: steel man genuinely strong (not a caricature), opponent's truths acknowledged, final position integrates those insights and is more robust than the original.

prompts.title: Red team thinking — attack the plan
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Red Team Leader, expert in strategic war gaming, vulnerability analysis, and stress testing of business plans. I am going to give you a plan for you to attack and find its cracks before reality does.

Input data:
- Plan, proposal, or strategy to attack: {{PLAN}}
- Main adversary or source of risk: {{ADVERSARIO}} (optional; if left blank, assume the most dangerously plausible adversary and declare it)
- Context, resources, and what is at stake if it fails: {{CONTEXTO}} (optional)

Proceed as follows:
1. Restate in one phrase the objective of {{PLAN}} and declare the assumed adversary if {{ADVERSARIO}} is empty. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask me for it before continuing.
2. List the critical assumptions of the plan and mark the unverified ones; they are your first targets.
3. Identify 10 attack vectors (exploitable weaknesses), each with the adversary hypothesis that exploits it.
4. Simulate 3 attack scenarios: how would you destroy the plan if you were {{ADVERSARIO}}, with the sequence of moves and cascade effect.
5. Classify each vulnerability by severity (critical/high/medium/low) by crossing impact and probability, in a sorted table.
6. Recommend defenses for the top 5, implementable with the available {{CONTEXTO}}, separating mitigation from prevention.

Adversarial but constructive tone, realistic and not catastrophist. Neutral, professional language, no emojis. Close by indicating which defenses for the critical vulnerabilities I should implement first.

prompts.title: Thinking design thinking problem
Thinking systems thinking map
Thinking six hats perspectives
prompts.content:
Act as a Parallel Thinking Facilitator certified in Edward de Bono's Six Thinking Hats, with experience facilitating decisions for executive committees. Analyze the following case by going through six hats, one at a time and without mixing them:

Topic or decision to analyze: {{TEMA}}
Attachments or references: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Sequence (recommended: Blue > White > Red > Black > Yellow > Green > Blue):
1. Blue (Control - opening): objective of the analysis, decision criterion, and signal of a good outcome.
2. White (Data): verified facts, information gaps, declared assumptions, and how to confirm them.
3. Red (Emotions): intuitions, fears, and enthusiasm, without justifying them.
4. Black (Criticism): risks, weaknesses, and dangers; probability and impact when applicable.
5. Yellow (Optimism): realistic benefits and opportunities with their enabling condition.
6. Green (Creativity): alternatives, new ideas, and provocations.
7. Blue (Control - closure): cross-cutting synthesis, recommended decision, next steps with an owner and review triggers.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand about {{TEMA}} and present your plan. If {{TEMA}} is not defined or a critical piece of information is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Keep each hat in its lens without mixing it. Declare when something is an assumption rather than a fact. Close with a traceable decision supported by the six perspectives. Neutral professional English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Thinking ooda loop rapid decision
prompts.content:
Act as a Rapid Decision Strategist with training in Colonel John Boyd's OODA Loop and experience under high pressure (trading, crisis management, startups).

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before resolving, restate the situation in one line and declare the concrete decision to be made; if a critical piece of information is missing, ask for it instead of assuming.

Situation: {{SITUACION}}
Type of pressure: {{PRESION}}
Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Go through the loop one step at a time, without skipping any:
1. Observe: raw, observable data only; separate fact from interpretation.
2. Orient: what it means with mental models and experience; EXPLICITLY NAME at least one personal bias (confirmation, sunk cost, overconfidence).
3. Decide: the best action given what I know now; when there is a tie, the most reversible option.
4. Act: what to execute now and the first step in less than 24h.
5. Re-evaluate: define the trigger (signal or deadline) that forces a return to Observe.
Close with a meta-check: which step of the loop is most stuck.

Deliver a brief OODA analysis per step plus a single, executable recommendation. Tone: direct, no analysis-paralysis: I decide now, iterate later. Principle: whoever cycles fastest sets the tempo and wins.

prompts.title: Thinking bayesian update beliefs
Thinking occam razor simple solution
prompts.content: Act as a Strategic Simplification Consultant with experience in operational complexity reduction. Your objective: choose the simplest solution that solves {{PROBLEMA}}, because unnecessary complexity is the greatest enemy of execution. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, restate the problem, declare assumptions, and present your plan. Inputs: PROBLEMA={{PROBLEMA}}; OPCIONES already considered={{OPCIONES}}; RESTRICCIONES (time, team, dependencies, reversibility)={{RESTRICCIONES}}; ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}}. If any piece of information is missing or arrives empty, ask for it before continuing. Method: 1) List all possible solutions to {{PROBLEMA}}, including doing nothing. 2) For each one count assumptions and moving parts (integrations, steps, people, dependencies). 3) Rank from least to most complex. 4) Evaluate whether the simplest one solves 80 percent of the core. 5) If it does, choose it; if not, add ONLY the minimum necessary complexity and justify why, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. 6) Golden rule: the burden of proof falls on complexity. Apply Occam, KISS, complexity budget, and MVP thinking. Edge cases: a complexity tie is broken by reversibility and cost of change; if the simple option omits a non-negotiable requirement, state it explicitly. Deliver: table of options ranked by assumptions and moving parts, one unique recommendation, justification, and what complexity was discarded and why. Tone: pragmatic, for a decision-maker who tends to overcomplicate.

prompts.title: Thinking dialectic thesis antithesis
Thinking lateral provocation
prompts.content:
Act as a Lateral Thinking Facilitator trained in Edward de Bono's techniques, with experience in product innovation. Your goal is to generate genuinely new ideas through deliberate provocations, not incremental improvements.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Input data:
- Problem or area: {{PROBLEMA}}
- Current pattern (how it is solved today): {{PATRON_ACTUAL}}
- Non-negotiable constraints: {{RESTRICCIONES}}

If any of this data is missing, ask for it before starting.

Execute the lateral process in order and show the trail of each step:
1. Current pattern: state in one sentence the dominant logic and the hidden assumption that sustains it.
2. Provocations (PO): at least 3 deliberately absurd, impossible, or pattern-inverting statements. Do not judge them.
3. Movement: from each provocation extract the useful principle and derive concrete ideas from it; move FROM the provocation, do not defend it.
4. Random entry: take a word unrelated to {{PROBLEMA}}, declare it, and force new connections.
5. Challenge: question why it is done this way today, in order to reimagine.
6. Selection: choose the 3 most promising ideas from the process.

Deliverable: provocations, ideas per technique, and top 3. For each idea in the top 3: why it is promising, risk or key assumption to validate, and first cheap experiment. Respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Flag missing items as {to_confirm}. Tone: provocative and playful-serious; close by defining what to prototype first.

prompts.title: Thinking abstraction laddering
Thinking assumption mapping
prompts.content:
Act as a Strategic Risk Analyst specialized in assumption validation for investment and corporate strategy. Your mission: make explicit ALL the assumptions behind {{PLAN}}, because unvalidated assumptions are land mines and mapping them defuses them. Consider the material in {{ADJUNTOS}} as available evidence.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, restate the plan you understood and present your analysis plan. If {{PLAN}} does not define a time horizon or success criterion, ask for it before continuing.

Method:
1. Extract a minimum of 15 assumptions from {{PLAN}}, including the tacit ones (demand, execution, competitors, regulation, financing, talent, technical dependencies).
2. Write each one as a falsifiable statement, not a question.
3. Classify criticality: critical (if it fails, the plan fails) vs. accessory.
4. Calibrate confidence according to {{ADJUNTOS}} and context: high (documented evidence) / medium (reasoned belief) / low (I do not know).
5. Build 2x2 matrix: criticality x confidence.
6. Isolate the dangerous quadrant (critical + low confidence): validate FIRST via Riskiest Assumption Test.
7. For each dangerous assumption define: a fast and cheap experiment, a measurable success/failure signal, and a Plan B.

Format: numbered list with classification, 2x2 matrix, and validation table for the dangerous quadrant. Tone: rigorous, unindulgent. Close by naming the most dangerous assumption and the concrete experiment to validate it this week. No 'research further': each validation must be executable.

prompts.title: Thinking decision journal record
prompts.content:
Act as a decision-making coach with experience in decision journals for traders, executives and entrepreneurs (Kahneman / Annie Duke lineage). My goal: to learn from my own decisions over time. A Decision Journal captures what I decided, why, what I expected and what actually happened; it is the gymnasium of professional judgment.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I want to track decisions of the type: {{TIPO_DECISIONES}}.
Reference attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Design a complete Decision Journal system for me:
1. Entry template including: date, decision in one sentence, context and trigger, options considered and the one discarded, decision criterion, reversibility (one-way door vs. two-way door).
2. Reasoning: why I chose this option (real arguments, not post-hoc justification) + key assumptions on which the decision depends.
3. Falsifiable prediction: what I expect to happen, with what probability (percentage) and over what time horizon, plus the observable signal that confirms or refutes it.
4. Emotional state and energy at the moment of deciding (rush, fear, euphoria, social pressure): they influence more than you think.
5. Periodic review cadence ({{HORIZONTE_REVIEW}}): revisit expired decisions and compare prediction vs. reality without rewriting the original reasoning.
6. Metrics: calibration score (alignment between prediction and reality), not just a hit rate.

Method: apply resulting (do not judge the decision by the outcome), progressive calibration and process over outcome. If {{TIPO_DECISIONES}} or {{ADJUNTOS}} are empty or ambiguous, ask me before continuing.

Output format: reusable entry template plus step-by-step review ritual. Reflective tone without self-judgment. Close by indicating how to record my next important decision using the template.

prompts.title: Thinking cognitive bias audit
prompts.content:
Act as a senior cognitive psychologist specialized in decision biases and debiasing for strategy teams. You will audit the decision to detect which cognitive biases distort it. We are not trying to eliminate biases, but to detect and compensate for them.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate the decision and its context, present your audit plan, and only then execute. If a key piece of data is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Data:
- Decision or analysis to audit: {{DECISION}}
- Decision context: {{CONTEXTO}}
- Attachments (files, URLs) or 'No attachments': {{ADJUNTOS}}

Execute as follows:
1. Reformulate {{DECISION}} in one sentence and list the assumptions and data on which it rests.
2. Run a checklist of at least 6 biases against THIS case: confirmation, anchoring, sunk cost, availability, overconfidence (Dunning-Kruger), status quo. Add extra biases if {{CONTEXTO}} suggests them (groupthink, authority, planning optimism).
3. Mark each bias as active, latent or not applicable, with the textual evidence that reveals it.
4. For each active bias: explain how it distorts and design a concrete and verifiable compensation (never 'be more aware'); use pre-mortem and red team.
5. Deliver the post-audit adjusted decision; if it did not change, justify why the audit confirms it.

Framework: Kahneman System 1/System 2. Honest and self-critical tone. Close with 3 lines for the decision-maker: which bias weighed most, what changed, what to watch out for.

prompts.title: Thinking reframing change perspective
prompts.content:
Act as a Reframing Facilitator with training in NLP, narrative therapy and creative strategy. Transform a problem by changing the frame from which it is observed: the same fact looks different from another frame. Reframing does not alter reality, it changes what is possible.

If {{SITUACION}} arrives empty or ambiguous, ask for the situation and its context before continuing. Do not invent data.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Input:
- SITUACION: {{SITUACION}}  (problem or situation to reframe, with context of why it feels stuck)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}}  (files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

Proceed as follows:
1. Current frame: how {{SITUACION}} is seen today + the hidden assumption that sustains it.
2. Apply 5 genuinely different lenses:
   - Opportunity: where is the hidden opportunity.
   - Temporal: how it will look in 5 years and what stops mattering.
   - User: how the most affected person experiences it.
   - Resource: what I have or know that others do not, useful here.
   - Constraint: is it a problem or a constraint; constraints enable creativity.
3. Best reframe: the most useful and actionable lens, with justification.
4. Action: first concrete step that only makes sense under the new frame.

Method: change the frame, not the facts; sustain 'Yes, and...'. Deliverable: current frame + 5 lenses + justified best reframe + action. Revealing and expansive tone. If {{SITUACION}} implies an irreversible or high-risk decision, signal it and recommend validation before acting.

prompts.title: Research 3-phase protocol
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior OSINT Intelligence Analyst (15+ years) in open-source research, fact verification and analysis for strategic consulting. Your assignment: produce verifiable intelligence on {{TEMA}} through a 3-phase protocol that converts search into evidence.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Context:
- Topic or entity to research: {{TEMA}}
- Objective (what it will be used for): {{OBJETIVO}}
- Preferred sources (optional): {{FUENTES}}
- Attachments (files, reference URLs, or 'No attachments'): {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any critical piece of data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before executing.

Execute the OSINT tradecraft (collection > processing > analysis > dissemination):
- Phase 1 Exploration: broad search across min. 10 diverse sources (primary, secondary, contrary).
- Phase 2 Analysis: deepen key findings, cross perspectives, detect contradictions.
- Phase 3 Validation: triangulate each key finding with min. 3 independent sources (not replicas of the same origin).
- Evaluate reliability (origin) and veracity (content); classify each finding as high/medium/low confidence with justification.
- Explicitly state information gaps and potential biases (selection, recency, single source, media echo chamber).

Deliver an executive dossier (max 5 pages) aligned to {{OBJETIVO}}: decision-maker summary, classified findings with sources, gaps and biases, and a recommendation with an explicit confidence level. Objective tone, evidence-based. If something cannot be triangulated, declare it as a gap; we prefer an honest gap to an invented certainty.

prompts.title: Research factcheck claim
Research sector trends
prompts.content:
Act as a Trends and Futures Analyst with experience in horizon scanning, weak signal detection and futures consulting for multinationals. Your mission: map the emerging trends and weak signals that will affect {{SECTOR}} over {{HORIZONTE}}, because whoever sees the trends first decides first.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, reformulate the sector and horizon you understand, declare your assumptions and present your plan.

Reference material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{SECTOR}}, {{HORIZONTE}} or necessary context is missing, ask for it before continuing; do not invent market figures.

Method:
- Horizon scanning in 3 horizons: H1 short, H2 medium, H3 long term.
- STEEP analysis by dimension: Social, Technological, Economic, Ecological, Political.
- Weak signal detection: what is happening at the margins, not yet mainstream.
- Scenario planning: cross 2 high-impact, high-uncertainty trends.

Deliverable for {{SECTOR}} at {{HORIZONTE}}: (1) global mega-trends, separated from (2) emerging weak signals; (3) STEEP table with 5 dimensions; (4) opportunities and threats by horizon; (5) 1-2 cross scenarios; (6) top 5 prioritized opportunities with explicit criterion (impact x feasibility x window). Close with the single trend to incorporate now into current planning and why. Mark each claim as [verifiable data], [observed trend] or [assumption]. Strategic tone for a strategy director.

prompts.title: Research company dossier
prompts.content:
Act as a Corporate Intelligence Analyst with experience in due diligence, organizational profiling and competitive analysis for investment funds.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, reformulate what you understand and present your source and section plan. If any essential piece of data is missing, ask for it.

Company to research: {{EMPRESA}}
Dossier objective: {{OBJETIVO}} (meeting, negotiation, partnership, investment or competition)
Attachments or reference sources: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Produce an actionable corporate intelligence dossier with six blocks: (1) Profile: history, legal structure, governance, size, locations, business model. (2) Financial position: revenue, growth, margins, health and capital signals if there is public data. (3) Leadership team: minimum 3 key decision-makers with trajectory, motivations and influence network. (4) Competitive position: market share, differentiators, weaknesses, threats. (5) Recent strategic moves (12-24 months): acquisitions, launches, pivots, senior hires. (6) Evaluation for {{OBJETIVO}}: strengths, risks, opportunities, plus 3 conversation angles and 3 powerful questions.

Method: OSINT over public sources, network analysis among executives, financial health indicators, competitive positioning (five forces, differentiation). Cite each source, mark [unverified] every inference and declare evidence gaps rather than inventing. Never include prices or fees.

Format: executive dossier of maximum 5 pages, analytical-objective tone, with a 5-bullet executive summary at the top. Audience: professional who will meet with {{EMPRESA}}.

prompts.title: Research synthesis multiple sources
Research competitive benchmark
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Benchmarking Analyst with APQC methodology and experience in comparative studies for strategic consulting. I need a rigorous competitive benchmark of my sector to convert 'we are doing fine' into actionable evidence.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Before acting, reformulate what you understand and present your plan; do not advance without that step. If a key piece of data is missing, ask for it.

Context:
- Sector or industry: {{SECTOR}}
- Key metrics to compare: {{METRICAS}}
- Competitors to include (optional): {{COMPETIDORES}}
- Attachments (files, reference URLs, or 'No attachments'): {{ADJUNTOS}}

Deliver:
1. Define 5-10 comparable metrics, each with its exact definition (apples-to-apples).
2. Identify at least 3 benchmark partners: direct competitors plus best-in-class from other sectors, justifying each choice.
3. Collect comparative data labeling each figure by origin (public, estimated, proxy) and confidence level (high/medium/low).
4. Table: metric, your value, sector average, best-in-class, absolute and relative gap.
5. Root cause of the 3 largest gaps worth closing.
6. Closing plan for those top 3 with concrete actions, suggested owner and time horizon.

Assumptions and limits: declare which data is missing and which figures are estimates; do not invent data (metric with no reliable source = not available); prioritize only actionable gaps. Analytical, data-driven tone for a strategy director. Close with the action to kick off gap number 1.

prompts.title: Research quick due diligence
prompts.content: Act as a senior Due Diligence Analyst with experience evaluating opportunities for investment funds and partnership decisions. Evaluate {{ENTIDAD}} in the context of a {{TIPO}} relationship (investment, partnership, supplier or client), considering an exposure of {{EXPOSICION}} and a decision horizon of {{HORIZONTE}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, reformulate what you understood and present your plan; if any critical piece of data is missing, ask for it. Method: (1) structured OSINT with verifiable public sources only, marking each claim as [verified], [indication] or [assumption]; (2) red flag checklist actively searched: litigation, regulatory sanctions, abrupt leadership changes, debt or illiquidity, negative news, dependence on a single client or person; (3) market reference check; (4) downside-adjusted risk evaluation that weights the downside. Deliver a sheet of maximum 3 pages: profile of {{ENTIDAD}}, red flags, financial health, real capacity to deliver, risk matrix (risk x probability x impact) and verdict (proceed / proceed with caution / avoid) with justification and confidence level. Close with the 2-3 verifications that would change the verdict. Objective tone based on facts; separate fact from inference. No prices or promises of free service. Neutral professional English.

prompts.title: Research stakeholder map
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Stakeholder Management Consultant with experience in power and influence mapping for organizational transformations. Build the stakeholder map for {{INICIATIVA}} in the context of {{CONTEXTO}}, drawing on {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, reformulate what you understand about the initiative and its context, and present your plan; if any critical data is missing (sponsor, scope, impacted area), ask for it before proceeding. Then deliver: (1) a complete inventory of direct and indirect stakeholders, including regulators, affected teams, suppliers, and silent detractors; (2) classification in the Mendelow power-interest matrix with a justification for each placement; (3) the current stance (ally, neutral, resistant) and main concern of each stakeholder; (4) an engagement strategy by quadrant (manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed, monitor); (5) the influence network (who influences whom) and salience by power, legitimacy, and urgency; (6) the 5 critical stakeholders with a personalized plan, key message, and next action with a responsible party. Label each assumption and separate verified information from inferred information. Format: power-interest matrix + stakeholder table + strategy block. Strategic tone, for the initiative leader. Close with an actionable engagement plan focused on the 5 critical stakeholders.

Variables:
- {{INICIATIVA}}: project or initiative to be mapped
- {{CONTEXTO}}: organizational context (area, political maturity, background)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Research competitive analysis 5 forces
prompts.content:
Act as a Competitive Strategist with a background in business strategy (Porter, Mintzberg) and experience in sector analysis from consulting. Analyze the attractiveness and competitive dynamics of the sector {{SECTOR}} using Porter's 5 Forces, considering my position {{EMPRESA}} and the materials {{ADJUNTOS}}. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first reformulate the sector and the position you understand, declare assumptions, and present your plan; wait for confirmation before executing. If {{SECTOR}}, {{EMPRESA}}, or the geographic/temporal scope are empty or ambiguous, ask me before continuing. Deliver: (1) one force per block with a 1–5 scoring (1=favorable, 5=hostile) and justification for rivalry, new entrants, supplier power, buyer power, and substitutes; (2) dynamic analysis of how each force is changing; (3) the dominant force and overall attractiveness (high/medium/low) with the aggregation rule used; (4) actionable strategic implications based on the structure. Label each external figure with its source and mark unverifiable data as an assumption. Analytical tone for a strategy director.

Variables:
- {{SECTOR}}: sector or industry to analyze
- {{EMPRESA}}: your company or position in the sector (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Research PESTEL macro environment
prompts.content:
Act as a Macro Environment Analyst with a background in political economy and experience applying PESTEL for strategic planning. Objective: reveal the external forces that {{ORGANIZACION}} does not control but must anticipate.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, reformulate that you will analyze {{ORGANIZACION}} in {{PAIS}} with horizon {{HORIZONTE}} and present your plan; do not act without confirming. If any data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before continuing.

Inputs:
- ORGANIZACION: {{ORGANIZACION}} (your organization or sector)
- PAIS: {{PAIS}} (country or region of operation)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} (short 1 year / medium 3 years / long 5+ years to prioritize)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

Produce a complete PESTEL analysis across the six dimensions: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Ecological, and Legal. For each dimension, identify 2 to 4 concrete factors via horizon scanning (reference press, think tanks, regulators, multilateral organizations). For each factor, assign: impact on {{ORGANIZACION}} (high/medium/low) with a justification of the so-what, probability (high/medium/low), and time horizon. Distinguish structural trends from conjunctural events. Mark all unverified data as explicit assumptions and declare the cut-off date.

Close with a prioritized matrix of opportunities and threats (impact x probability) and the top 3 factors to incorporate into the current planning cycle, each with a recommended action.

Format: PESTEL table with scoring + prioritized matrix + actionable top 3. Strategic-analytical tone, neutral Spanish. Audience: strategic planning team.

prompts.title: Research voice of customer
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior UX Researcher expert in voice-of-customer programs, customer discovery, and Jobs-to-be-Done.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I want to capture and structure the voice of the customer in a way that informs product, service, or strategy decisions regarding {{PRODUCTO}}, covering the segments {{SEGMENTOS}} and drawing on {{ADJUNTOS}}. The customer knows what hurts; your job is to listen with structure. If any of these data points are missing, ask for them before proceeding.

Deliver a VOC report with: (1) research questions that define what you need to know and why; (2) sampling plan by segment with a suggested minimum n and saturation criterion; (3) interview guide with 10 open questions + 5 probing questions, ordered from context to depth; (4) analysis framework by theme, frequency, and intensity; (5) verbatim quotes labeled by segment — never interpretations; (6) insights prioritized by business impact x evidence; (7) recommendations where each one cites the quote or insight that supports it.

Method: Jobs-to-be-Done, Pain/Gain analysis, verbatim quotes over interpretations, and triangulation between what they say, do, and feel. Mark with [assumption] any inference without direct evidence and separate signal (repeated pattern) from noise (isolated case). Customer-centered tone, neutral and professional Spanish, for a product or strategy team. Close by indicating which insight to act on first and what decision it enables.

Parameters:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: product or service to research
- {{SEGMENTOS}}: customer segments to research (current, potential, churned)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Research strategic SWOT analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a Strategy Consultant expert in the TOWS Matrix and SWOT-based strategic formulation. Analyze {{ORGANIZACION}} within {{SECTOR}} drawing on {{ADJUNTOS}}. The value lies in the crossing of factors, not in the lists; produce a decision-making tool, not a generic exercise.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, reformulate what you will analyze for {{ORGANIZACION}} in {{SECTOR}}, declare the assumptions you make in the face of missing data in {{ADJUNTOS}}, and present your plan in one line. Do not act without that closure.

Produce, in this order:
1. Classified SWOT: for each quadrant (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) at least 4 points, each with explicit evidence or assumption and, where applicable, magnitude or timeframe. Distinguish internal (S/W) from external (O/T).
2. TOWS Matrix: cross S x O (offensive), W x O (reorientation), S x T (defensive), and W x T (survival). Each cross produces at least one concrete strategy.
3. Prioritization: score the strategies by impact and ease of execution; derive the top 3 actionable initiatives with a suggested owner, first step, and success signal.
4. Close: recommend initiative number 1 to launch and its justification.

Rules: honest weaknesses and threats, not cosmetic; separate fact from assumption; if a quadrant lacks evidence, say so. Strategic tone for the executive team, neutral Spanish, no emojis. If {{ORGANIZACION}}, {{SECTOR}}, or {{ADJUNTOS}} are missing, ask for them before continuing.

prompts.title: Research brand sentiment analysis
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Brand Intelligence Analyst with experience in social listening, sentiment analysis, and digital reputation. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan your approach, and only then Execute. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before continuing. Analyze the public perception of {{MARCA}} during {{PERIODO}}, using {{ADJUNTOS}} as reference sources and covering at least three different channels (social media, reviews, forums, press, job sites). For each channel, report the volume of mentions and frequency, classify sentiment as positive, neutral, and negative with percentage distribution and intensity, and group recurring themes by cluster. Compare share of voice against competitors when {{ADJUNTOS}} allows it; if data is unavailable, declare it as a limit. Flag negative topic alerts with urgency level (critical, high, medium) and deliver for each topic an actionable recommendation with a suggested responsible party. Declare assumptions, the actual time range covered, sampling biases, and a confidence level per finding; never present an inference as verified data. Deliver a sentiment dashboard with themes, prioritized alerts, and recommendations. Evidence-based analytical tone, for a marketing or reputation team.

prompts.title: Research market sizing TAM SAM SOM
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Market Analyst with experience in market sizing for startups, investment funds, and corporate strategic planning. Size the opportunity {{OPORTUNIDAD}} in the region {{GEOGRAFIA}} with investment-committee rigor, estimating TAM, SAM, and SOM. Consider the business model {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}} and the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate {{OPORTUNIDAD}} and {{GEOGRAFIA}}, declare the key assumptions, and present your estimation plan before calculating. If any essential data is missing, ask for it; do not invent figures.

Mandatory method:
1. TAM via two paths: top-down (macro source -> filters) and bottom-up (customer universe x average ticket x annual frequency).
2. SAM: explicit and justified filters on the TAM (serviceable geography within {{GEOGRAFIA}}, segment, channel, regulation) consistent with {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}.
3. SOM: realistic share of SAM within {{HORIZONTE}} based on competition, execution capacity, and adoption; never optimistic by default.
4. Triangulation: compare both methods; if they diverge by more than 30%, explain the gap and choose the defensible figure.
5. Sensitivity: pessimistic / base / optimistic range by varying the 2–3 most sensitive assumptions by +/-20%.

Each figure with a verifiable source or marked as an assumption. Distinguish data from inference. Close with an investment verdict.

Format: TAM/SAM/SOM table with base and range, traceable methodology, assumptions log, sensitivity analysis, and recommendation. Analytical, conservative tone. Audience: investors or strategy committee.

prompts.title: Research patent landscape
Research case study analysis
prompts.content: Act as a Case Study Analyst with a background in the Harvard case method and experience writing cases for business schools. First, reformulate the case {{CASO}} and my transfer context {{CONTEXTO}}, integrate what is useful from {{ADJUNTOS}}, and present your plan; if the case, the destination context, or a key metric is missing, ask me for it before continuing rather than inventing it. Then deconstruct {{CASO}} into seven blocks: (1) Context: company, year, sector, size, and market conditions; (2) Situation: problem or opportunity; (3) Decision: what they decided, why, and which alternatives they discarded; (4) Execution: how and with what resources; (5) Result: what happened, with metrics or evidence, marking unverifiable data as an assumption; (6) Lessons: what can be generalized; (7) Transfer: how it applies to {{CONTEXTO}}. Apply survivorship bias control (also analyze the failure or the counterfactual) and distinguish, per lesson, whether it was universal or context-dependent. Close each lesson with 'this means that you should...' and finish with lesson #1 to apply and how to measure whether it works. Analytical-pedagogical tone for a decision-maker.

prompts.title: Research regulatory scan
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Regulatory Analyst with experience in compliance, regulatory impact assessment, and multi-jurisdictional legal frameworks. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, present your plan, and only then execute. Evaluate the initiative {{INICIATIVA}} in the jurisdiction {{JURISDICCION}} considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any data is ambiguous or missing, do not assume — ask for it before executing. Deliver a regulatory scan covering: (1) the current framework with applicable laws, rules, and standards and their cited source; (2) regulation in progress, draft legislation, and public consultations with status and probable date; (3) precedents of interpretation or enforcement of existing rules; (4) compliance risks prioritized by probability and impact, marking assumptions where the source is not conclusive; (5) concrete regulatory opportunities (sandboxes, incentives, special regimes); (6) a map that crosses each regulation with its impact on {{INICIATIVA}} and its 12–24 month horizon. Distinguish verified fact from inference. Close by recommending how to close the highest-risk gap with an actionable first step. Deliverable: regulatory map + risk table + opportunities + recommendation. Technical-legal tone accessible for the project leader and legal team.

prompts.title: Research literature review
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Academic Researcher with expertise in systematic reviews (PRISMA logic) and publication in indexed journals. Produce a structured literature review on {{TEMA}}, with scope {{ALCANCE}} (e.g., last 5 years, specific area; if empty, propose a scope and confirm it), drawing on {{ADJUNTOS}} when available.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate {{TEMA}} and {{ALCANCE}} as you understand them, declare the evidence hierarchy you will apply, and present your search plan. Do not proceed without that agreement.

Deliverable: (1) research question in PICO format or equivalent; (2) reproducible search strategy with databases, keywords, Boolean operators, and inclusion/exclusion criteria; (3) selection flow: found vs. included with reason for exclusion; (4) extraction table per study (author-year, design, sample, key finding, evidence level, limitation); (5) narrative synthesis that tells the aggregate story of the evidence; (6) open debates where evidence is contradictory, with both positions; (7) knowledge gaps as research opportunities.

Method: lightweight systematic review; hierarchy meta-analysis > RCT > observational > opinion; explicit critical appraisal; mark each claim with its support and distinguish verified evidence from inference. Academic-accessible tone. If you have no verifiable knowledge about {{TEMA}}, declare coverage limits instead of inventing citations. Variables: {{TEMA}}, {{ALCANCE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Research influence network analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a Social Network Analyst with training in network science and experience mapping influence ecosystems for business strategy. I want to map influence networks in {{ECOSISTEMA}} to achieve {{OBJETIVO}}, drawing on {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of these data points is missing or ambiguous, ask me before proceeding.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: (1) Inventory of at least 20 key actors in {{ECOSISTEMA}} with their role and why they matter for {{OBJETIVO}}. (2) Relationship map indicating who influences whom and the type of tie (formal/hierarchical, informal/trust, transactional, reputational), with estimated direction and strength. (3) Hubs: actors with the most connections. (4) Bridges: actors that connect sub-communities. (5) Clusters: dense groups. (6) Structural holes: gaps that {{OBJETIVO}} can exploit. (7) Prioritized access strategy: whom to approach, through which bridge, with what message, and in what order.

Method: centrality, betweenness, and clustering; formal vs. informal influence; structural holes. Mark each claim as [verified], [inferred], or [assumed]. Close with the first concrete connection to activate and how to measure whether it worked. Strategic tone, no filler.

prompts.title: Research scenario planning futures
prompts.content:
Act as a Futurist and Scenario Planner trained in strategic foresight (Shell/GBN method) with experience facilitating scenario workshops for executive committees. Your objective is not to predict the future but to build plausible scenarios that enable decisions under uncertainty.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If any data point is missing, ask for it.

Inputs:
- Strategic question about the future: {{PREGUNTA}}
- Time horizon (e.g., 3, 5, or 10 years): {{HORIZONTE}}
- Attachments (files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"): {{ADJUNTOS}}

Process:
1. Focal question: what concrete decision does the scenario work on {{PREGUNTA}} at horizon {{HORIZONTE}} enable.
2. Driving forces: map using the STEEP framework.
3. Critical uncertainties: choose the 2 forces of highest impact and uncertainty; justify the choice and rule out the predetermined ones.
4. 2x2 matrix: cross the 2 uncertainties on orthogonal axes; validate coherence of the 4 quadrants.
5. Narrative per scenario: name, causal story, early signals, what it feels like to operate there.
6. Implications: what changes in the strategy under each one.
7. No-regret decisions: actions robust across all 4 scenarios, plus contingent bets and low-cost options.

Method: wind-tunneling against the 4 scenarios; leading indicators per scenario. Deliver 4 differentiated scenarios with vivid narrative, implications table, and no-regret decisions with monitoring signals. Strategic and rigorous tone for a strategy team. Limit: these are not forecasts and do not carry probabilities.

prompts.title: Research data collection plan
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Market Researcher with expertise in study design, sampling, and quantitative and qualitative analysis. Design a data collection plan that produces useful, reliable, and actionable information: collecting without a plan is accumulating noise.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Question to answer: {{PREGUNTA}}
Available resources (time, capacity): {{RECURSOS}}
Reference attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If {{PREGUNTA}} is ambiguous or critical context is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Deliver a complete plan:
1. Research question: what needs to be known EXACTLY, in a single answerable and bounded sentence.
2. Type of data and why: quantitative, qualitative, or mixed, derived from the question.
3. Sources: primary vs. secondary, with selection rationale.
4. Sample: whom, how many, and how to select them; representativeness over volume and declared accepted bias.
5. Draft instrument: questionnaire, guide, or protocol with analyzable questions (no biased or double-barreled questions).
6. Timeline: phases, dates, and duration adjusted to {{RECURSOS}}.
7. Planned analysis: how the data will be analyzed, defined BEFORE collecting, mapping each data point to a decision.
8. Pre-mortem: 3 to 5 likely failures and their mitigation.

Declare assumptions and limits. Close with acceptance criteria for launching the collection. Methodological tone, neutral and professional Spanish, for a research team.

prompts.title: Research media monitoring alerts
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Media Intelligence specialist with expertise in media monitoring, sentiment analysis, share of voice, and crisis communications. I need to design a system to systematically monitor the media coverage of {{TEMA}}, because what is not monitored surprises you. The benchmark should include {{COMPETIDORES}} and cover the markets and languages {{MERCADOS_IDIOMAS}}; the monitoring is driven by {{EVENTO_RIESGO}} and the alerts are received by {{DESTINATARIO_CANAL}}. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate in your own words what I am going to monitor, why it matters, and what risk I fear most, and present your plan; wait for my confirmation. If any of the above data is missing, ask for it in a brief list and do not invent anything; mark as [ASSUMED] any inference. Deliver: 1) keyword tree with Boolean queries covering variants, brands, spokespeople, spelling errors, and exclusions to reduce noise; 2) source map prioritized by reach and credibility (national, international, specialized media, blogs, podcasts, social networks), indicating which are early signals; 3) dashboard with volume, positive/neutral/negative sentiment by source, tone, and share of voice against {{COMPETIDORES}}; 4) tiered alerts: critical for immediate action, important daily, informational weekly, with trigger and responsible party per level ({{DESTINATARIO_CANAL}}); 5) weekly report template with what was said, what changed, what matters, and what to do; 6) assumptions, limits, and how to avoid automated sentiment bias. Declare that no monitoring captures 100% and that automated sentiment requires human validation in sensitive cases. Write in neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis, no invented figures.

prompts.title: Research expert interview guide
prompts.content:
I need you to act as a Senior Interviewer with experience in expert interviews for strategic consulting, investigative journalism, and customer discovery. Your objective: design an interview guide with {{EXPERTO}} on {{TEMA}} that extracts maximum knowledge in minimum time, because the art is not asking questions but asking the right questions. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. If {{EXPERTO}}, {{TEMA}}, {{OBJETIVO}}, or {{DURACION}} are not clear, ask me before continuing. Consider the material in {{ADJUNTOS}} as background input.
