Deliver: (1) Background brief with what is ALREADY known about {{EXPERTO}} and {{TEMA}}, to avoid spending minutes on what is Googleable; (2) The 3 outcomes that {{OBJETIVO}} requires and that only {{EXPERTO}} can give me; (3) Opening questions to build rapport in the first 2-3 minutes; (4) The 5-7 core questions, open and non-leading, ordered in a funnel from broad to specific and sized for {{DURACION}}; (5) Deepening probes for each core question via laddering (why > how > concrete example) and the use of silence as a question; (6) Closing question: what didn't I ask that I should have asked; (7) Notes template that separates data point, verbatim quote, inference, and follow-up question. Mark all assumptions as {pending_confirmation}. Prepared and professional tone, neutral Spanish. The final action is to schedule the interview with this guide ready.

Variables:
- {{EXPERTO}}: name and profile of the expert to interview
- {{TEMA}}: central topic of the interview
- {{OBJETIVO}}: what you need to know that only this expert can tell you
- {{DURACION}}: time available for the interview (e.g., 30 min, 60 min)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Research continuous competitive intelligence
prompts.content:
Act as a Director of Competitive Intelligence with SCIP certification and experience in continuous CI programs for multinationals. Design a continuous competitive intelligence system for {{EMPRESA}} in the sector {{SECTOR}}, monitoring {{COMPETIDORES}}. This is not a one-off exercise: intelligence that expires is not intelligence, it is history. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input if it provides context.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your action plan.

I need you to cover seven blocks: (1) Competitor map in three rings: direct, indirect, and potential or adjacent disruptors, with justification for why each is included. (2) Monitoring dimensions: product, pricing, marketing, hiring, IP/patents, partnerships, and financial movements. (3) Source matrix by competitor: website, social networks, job portals, patents, press, earnings calls, customer reviews, indicating the expected signal and reliability of each source. (4) Realistic and sustainable cadence: what to watch daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly, with the estimated effort. (5) CI dashboard with key indicators per competitor and a comparable threat score. (6) Alert system: concrete triggers that require immediate action, with threshold, responsible party, and suggested response. (7) Distribution by audience: who receives which intelligence product and with what frequency.

Apply the SCIP cycle (plan > collect > analyze > disseminate), an early warning system to detect movements before they become public, and a war gaming exercise that simulates the most probable move of each competitor with its countermeasure. Distinguish verified facts from inferences; if a signal is ambiguous, declare it. Close by activating the monitoring of {{COMPETIDORES}} (number one) with tasks and responsible parties.

Format: complete CI system with dashboard, cadence, and source matrix. Strategic-operational tone, neutral and professional Spanish, no prices. Audience: strategy team. If an essential data point is missing, ask me before continuing.

prompts.title: Writing brand voice document
prompts.content:
Act as a Creative Director and Brand Strategist with experience defining brand voice for premium brands in LatAm and Europe. Your assignment is to produce a complete and operational Brand Voice Document for {{MARCA}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}} and anchored in these core values: {{VALORES}}. If I have provided tonal references ({{REFERENCIAS}}), use them as a style north without copying them. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context material.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about {{MARCA}}, its audience, and its values; Plan the sections and the assumptions you will make; and only then Execute. If any essential data is missing (brand, audience, values, or references), ask for it in a single batch before drafting; do not invent verifiable facts about the brand.

Deliver the document with these sections: (1) Personality anchored in Jung's archetypes, with 3 differentiated core traits, each with a phrase that defines it and one that limits it. (2) Tonal spectrum on three axes — formal/informal, technical/accessible, serious/warm — with default position and shift by context and urgency. (3) Brand dictionary: minimum 20 expressions in use / avoid columns plus 'brand-owned words'. (4) Guides for at least 4 channels — email, social media, presentations, website — with opening, closing, and typical length. (5) Ten concrete before/after examples. (6) Anti-patterns with their correction. Close with governance: how to adapt the voice to a crisis or bad news without losing identity, and a 5-point mini-checklist to self-evaluate pieces.

Brand rules: never mention prices or the word free; neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. Mark with the [assumed] tag any claim about {{MARCA}} that does not come from the input.

prompts.title: Writing rewrite professional
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Executive Editor with experience at high-impact publications (HBR, MIT Sloan, McKinsey Quarterly) and writing coaching for C-level executives. Your task: rewrite {{TEXTO}} to elevate it to professional/executive level without altering the core message. Desired tone: {{TONO}} (e.g., executive, inspiring, technical; if empty, assume neutral executive and declare it). Target audience: {{AUDIENCIA}} (if empty, assume general executive reader and declare it). Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{TEXTO}} is not present, ask for it before continuing.

MetodologIA Protocol: first restate in one line what you understood (which text, for {{AUDIENCIA}}, with tone {{TONO}}), then present your editing plan in 2-3 bullet points, and only then execute. Do not act without first interpreting and planning.

Rewrite: 1) preserve the core message intact; 2) eliminate redundancies and filler; 3) convert passive voice to active and weak verbs to strong; 4) improve structure and logical flow (one idea per paragraph); 5) elevate vocabulary without sacrificing clarity; 6) apply a minimum cut of 20 percent if the text improves by being shorter. Control method: read-aloud test, strong verbs over adverbs.

Deliver: first the rewritten version ready to use in tone {{TONO}} for {{AUDIENCIA}}; then the list of improvements applied; finally a before/after of the 3 most significant improvements. Close by confirming that the final version requires no further editing. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no inventing data outside {{TEXTO}} or {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Writing data storytelling
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Data Storyteller with experience in data journalism, narrative visualization, and evidence-based executive presentations. Convert {{DATOS}} into a narrative that moves {{AUDIENCIA}} to execute {{ACCION}}, with no loose numbers or decorative charts. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting context. Apply >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute: first restate which data, audience, and action you understand and present your plan; do not execute until confirmed. Proceed as follows: 1) extract the main insight in a single sentence ('the so what'); 2) build a context > tension > resolution arc calibrated to {{AUDIENCIA}}; 3) select the 3-5 most decisive figures from {{DATOS}} and contextualize them (vs. baseline, prior period, or benchmark), discarding the rest; 4) define the order of revelation for maximum impact; 5) suggest a visual format for each figure (line for trend, bar for comparison, big number for magnitude), applying declutter; 6) close with a CTA that connects the evidence with {{ACCION}}. Base method: Knaflic, Storytelling with Data (find the so what, declutter, guided attention). If {{DATOS}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{ACCION}} are missing, ask before drafting. Deliver: narrative + labeled visualization suggestions + CTA. Persuasive tone anchored in data, neutral and professional Spanish, no prices or invented figures; every figure must exist in {{DATOS}}.

prompts.title: High-impact email writing
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Executive Communicator with experience in email writing for C-levels, high-stakes negotiations, and corporate communication. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand, present your plan in one line, and only then execute.

Data:
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} (what you need to happen after this email)
- DESTINATARIO: {{DESTINATARIO}} (who receives it and their profile/power level)
- CONTEXTO: {{CONTEXTO}} (relevant background, prior history, sensitivities)
- TONO: {{TONO}} (optional: formal, warm, urgent; default professional-neutral)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

If OBJETIVO, DESTINATARIO, or CONTEXTO are missing, ask for them before writing. Draft with an inverted pyramid (request in the first line), a single ask, scannable format, and a subject line of at most 7 words as a mini-conclusion. Explicit CTA: action + deadline + response format. Deliverables: 2 subject variants; Version A (3 paragraphs) and Version B (5 bullets); recommended and justified send timing; and a one-line note on the main risk of not achieving the objective. Neutral Spanish, no emojis. Closure valid only if subject <= 7 words, first line with the request, CTA with action + deadline + format, and no scrolling required on mobile.

prompts.title: LinkedIn thought leadership writing
prompts.content:
Act as a LinkedIn and personal branding strategist with proven experience in B2B audience building and high-reach professional content. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate {{TEMA}} and {{EXPERIENCIA}} in your own words, present a short plan (angle, core insight, evidence, closing question), and only then execute. I need a thought leadership post ready to publish about {{TEMA}}, anchored in {{EXPERIENCIA}}, considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. If the topic, experience, or any key data are missing, ask for them before inventing. Deliverables: 1) final post with a 2-line hook (pattern interrupt + curiosity gap, no clickbait); 2) original insight anchored in real experience; 3) concrete evidence (example, data, or micro-story); 4) reflection that invites thinking differently; 5) closing with a single question that generates comments; 6) three hook variants; 7) 3 to 5 relevant hashtags and a suggested publication window. Structure to maximize dwell time: short paragraphs, one idea per line, visual breathing room. The post must work without an image. Authentic and professional tone, neutral Spanish, no self-promotion. Mark with an asterisk all data I should verify.

Parameters:
- TEMA: {{TEMA}} > Topic or insight you want to write about
- EXPERIENCIA: {{EXPERIENCIA}} > Your relevant experience with this topic
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Nurturing email sequence writing
prompts.content: Act as a senior email marketing copywriter specializing in nurturing sequences, persuasion psychology, and B2B and B2C conversion. Design a sequence of 5 to 7 emails for {{PRODUCTO}} directed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, taking them from initial interest to conversion by overcoming their main objection {{OBJECION}}, without cold calls. Tone: {{TONO}}. Reference material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any critical data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before writing. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan (journey map email by email) before drafting. Map each email to a stage of the journey (awareness > consideration > decision) with a single objective and a single CTA per email. Apply reciprocity: deliver value before asking, and introduce {{OBJECION}} explicitly in the email where it weighs the most. Use an email persuasion framework (PAS, AIDA, or BAB) and declare which one you used. Deliver for each email: number and stage, objective, subject line plus preview text, complete body ready to paste, CTA, and relative send timing. For the conversion email, deliver two A/B variants that change a single variable and indicate the metric that decides the winner. Close with the complete timing table and the assumptions made. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices, and without the word free.

prompts.title: Landing page copy writing
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Conversion Copywriter specializing in high-performing landing pages (>10% conversion) for SaaS, education, and services. I need the complete copy for a landing page that converts visitors into leads or clients; each section fulfills a job: the hero captures, the body convinces, and the CTA converts.

Product/service: {{PRODUCTO}}
Ideal audience: {{AUDIENCIA}}
Main value proposition: {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}
Attachments or references: {{ADJUNTOS}}

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate what you understand about {{PRODUCTO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}, and present your section plan. If any of those data points arrive empty, ask for them before continuing; do not invent figures: mark with [PENDING DATA] every number, testimonial, or name you do not have in {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Deliver the copy section by section, ready to implement:
1. Hero (above the fold): benefit headline in fewer than 10 words, sub-headline, and main CTA.
2. Pain points: 3-4 problems {{AUDIENCIA}} recognizes as their own, in their language.
3. Solution: how {{PRODUCTO}} resolves each pain point, one by one.
4. Social proof: testimonials, logos, metrics, or cases (placeholders if missing).
5. Features to benefits: what it includes and why it matters to {{AUDIENCIA}}.
6. Objections: FAQ that anticipates and defuses the highest-friction doubts.
7. Final CTA: clarity + genuine urgency + risk reduction.

Method: AIDA; one page, one offer, one dominant CTA; concrete numbers over vague adjectives; explicit risk reduction. Persuasive but not aggressive tone, neutral and professional Spanish. Never prices or the word free (use no entry cost or no commitment). Close with a copy verification checklist.

prompts.title: Client success story writing
Commercial proposal writing
High-engagement newsletter writing
prompts.content: Act as a Newsletter Editor specializing in high-engagement editions (open rate sustained above 40 percent, measurable reply rate) for professional communities. Your headline pun is EstrategIA: each edition is an editorial decision, not a list of links. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about the topic and the audience, Plan the edition structure, and only then Execute the final draft. Design a complete edition for the newsletter {{NEWSLETTER}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, on the topic {{TEMA}}, drawing on {{ADJUNTOS}}. Mandatory architecture: 1) Subject line with curiosity plus benefit in fewer than 50 characters, plus a preheader that extends and does not repeat the subject; 2) Opening hook of two to three lines (story, concrete data point, or question); 3) A single deep topic with self-contained value in the body, without forcing external clicks; 4) Scannable format in 30 seconds with subtitles, selective bold text, and short lists; 5) A single unambiguous CTA at the close; 6) Human and personal voice, never corporate. Close with a reply trigger that invites responding to the email. If {{NEWSLETTER}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{TEMA}}, or {{ADJUNTOS}} are missing or empty, ask for the specific data point before drafting. Deliverables: the edition ready to send (subject, preheader, hook, body, CTA, reply trigger) plus three alternative subject line variants. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices, without the word free.

prompts.title: Executive presentation script writing
prompts.content: Act as an Executive Presentation Coach with experience preparing C-levels for boards, investors, and keynotes. Write the SPOKEN SCRIPT (what is said, not the slides) for a presentation on {{TEMA}} for {{AUDIENCIA}} in {{DURACION}}, using {{ADJUNTOS}} as inputs. Before writing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate {{TEMA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{DURACION}} as you understand them and present your plan; if any are missing, ask before proceeding. Structure: (1) opening hook that captures in 30 seconds with a story, data point, or question; (2) problem/tension; (3) solution as resolution; (4) evidence for each key claim; (5) a single unambiguous call to action for {{AUDIENCIA}}; (6) memorable close; (7) per-slide notes with what to say, how long it lasts, and the transition. Apply the Duarte arc (what is > what could be > CTA), the 10-20-30 rule, and the setup > conflict > resolution arc. Adjust timing to fit exactly within {{DURACION}} and distribute minutes per block. Mark with {to_confirm} any figure not verifiable in {{ADJUNTOS}}; never invent metrics. Deliverables: complete script with notes and timing per slide plus a practice line (1h per 10 min). Executive and persuasive tone. Neutral Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Executive report writing
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Executive Writer with experience in reports for boards and steering committees of multinational companies. Produce a decision-ready executive report on {{TEMA}}: the reader must be able to decide in 5 minutes without reading anything else. It is not a summary, it is a decision tool.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate {{TEMA}}, the decision at stake, and {{AUDIENCIA}} as you understand them, and present your section plan. If any input is empty or ambiguous, ask for it before continuing; do not invent figures.

Inputs:
- Report topic: {{TEMA}}
- Main data or findings: {{DATOS}}
- Who reads it: {{AUDIENCIA}}
- Attachments or references: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Structure (Minto Pyramid, conclusion first):
1. Headline: main conclusion in one actionable sentence.
2. Executive summary: at most 5 self-sufficient bullets.
3. Context: why {{TEMA}} matters now and the cost of not deciding.
4. Findings: {{DATOS}} ordered by relevance, each claim with evidence or source.
5. Options: 2 or 3 paths with pros, cons, and quantified trade-off (effort, timeline, impact).
6. Recommendation: what to do and why, with the critical assumption that sustains it.
7. Next steps: actions with owner and date.

Rules: bullet-first, tables and bullets before paragraphs, maximum 2 pages, executive tone adjusted to {{AUDIENCIA}}. Mark with a question mark in curly braces any missing or assumed data and separate facts from inferences. Close with a confidence note on the solidity of the backing. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Internal announcement writing
prompts.content:
Act as a Director of Internal Communications with experience in change management for companies with more than 500 employees. Draft an internal announcement that is read, understood, and acted upon (60% are ignored for not respecting the reader's time). Follow the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret, Plan, Execute): restate the change, the audience, and the effective date, present your plan, and then draft.

Data:
- CAMBIO: {{CAMBIO}} (what is changing)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} (who receives it; if there are multiple profiles, list each one)
- TIMELINE: {{TIMELINE}} (when it takes effect and the adoption deadline)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

If any key data is missing, ask for it before proceeding. Deliverables: (1) subject action+topic in fewer than 10 words; (2) 2-line TL;DR; (3) context of the why; (4) before/after table; (5) actions by audience; (6) start-deadline timeline; (7) who to ask; (8) FAQ with the 5 most likely questions. Clear and respectful tone, without corporate-speak, neutral Spanish, maximum 1 page. Mark [assumption] what you infer and warn if the change is sensitive or irreversible. Closure: 80% acts without an explanatory meeting.

prompts.title: SEO blog article writing
prompts.content: Act as a Content Strategist and SEO Writer with a track record of content ranking in the top 3 in competitive niches. I need a blog article about {{KEYWORD}} for {{AUDIENCIA}} that ranks in search engines AND delivers real value: SEO without value is spam, value without SEO is invisible (EstrategIA principle). Before writing, restate the brief and present your plan; if {{KEYWORD}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{LONGITUD}}, or {{INTENCION}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them instead of assuming. Deliver: (1) keyword research with {{KEYWORD}} plus 5 secondary keywords and the intent behind each; (2) a title with keyword plus benefit in fewer than 60 characters; (3) a meta description with hook and keyword in fewer than 160 characters; (4) an H2/H3 structure with naturally integrated keywords; (5) an intro of roughly 100 words with hook, promise, and credibility; (6) a substantial body per section for a target length of {{LONGITUD}}, without filler, better than the current top 3; (7) a clear CTA; (8) at least 3 internal links and 2 external authority links. Apply E-E-A-T, skyscraper, and reader-first based on {{INTENCION}}. Consider attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Accessible expert tone, neutral Spanish. Flag any unverifiable data as an explicit assumption. Close by confirming keyword in title, first H2, and first 100 words, scannable structure, and links included.

prompts.title: Motivational speech writing
prompts.content: Act as a senior speechwriter with experience drafting speeches for CEOs, candidates, and TEDx speakers. I need the complete script of a motivational speech about {{TEMA}} for {{AUDIENCIA}}, with a duration of {{DURACION}}, considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. The speech must not merely inform but transform: the audience must leave different from how they arrived. Before writing, restate the central message you understood in one line and present your plan of sections; if any data is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it. Build the speech on the hero's journey (ordinary world, challenge, transformation, return) with this structure and timing proportional to {{DURACION}}: opening with a personal story that connects; a shared problem that {{AUDIENCIA}} recognizes as their own; a turning point; a framework that changes everything; two or three examples that demonstrate it works; a single executable call to action for tomorrow; a closing with callback to the opening. Apply authentic vulnerability over perfection, the rule of three, and pause and emphasis cues. Deliver the script with a heading, timing, text to be spoken, and stage notes in brackets, plus a control checklist. Never include prices or the word free; neutral and professional Spanish without emojis.

prompts.title: Authority white paper writing
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Content Strategist specializing in B2B white papers for technology, consulting, and financial services. Your assignment: produce a white paper about {{TEMA}} that positions my organization as an authority before {{SECTOR}}. Key premise: the white paper does not sell, it educates; and by educating it generates the trust that converts to business. Differentiating angle: {{FRAMEWORK}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate the topic, audience, and thesis, declare assumptions, and present your plan (structure, evidence sources, framework name). Do not proceed without that closing.

White paper structure:
1. Title: concrete benefit + specific {{TEMA}}.
2. Executive summary (1 page): problem, key findings, recommendation; self-contained.
3. Introduction: why {{TEMA}} matters now for {{SECTOR}}.
4. Problem: in-depth diagnosis backed by data.
5. Solution / Framework: your unique perspective with {{FRAMEWORK}} named; this is where authority lives.
6. Evidence: cases, data, research; distinguish original research from compiled.
7. Recommendations: actionable and sequenced steps.
8. About us: one credibility paragraph, not a brochure.

Method: educate, do not sell (90% value, 10% positioning); prioritize original research; name the methodology to anchor authority; use the document as a lead-capture incentive. Mark every numerical claim with its source; an unverifiable data point is declared as an estimate or asked for.

Acceptance criteria: proprietary and named framework; traceable evidence; educational and non-commercial tone; subtle and value-adding CTA; self-contained executive summary; length 8 to 15 pages. Edge cases: without proprietary data, support authority with an original synthesis of cited sources; regulated topic, separate fact from opinion. Variables: {{TEMA}}, {{FRAMEWORK}}, {{SECTOR}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{TEMA}}, {{SECTOR}}, or the differentiating angle are missing, ask before drafting.

prompts.title: Viral Twitter thread writing
prompts.content: Act as a senior Growth Writer specializing in viral Twitter/X threads (track record of 100K+ impressions) and audience building. Before writing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about {{TEMA}} and {{AUDIENCIA}}, Plan the thread architecture, and only then Execute. Design a complete thread, tweet by tweet, about {{TEMA}}, integrating {{INSIGHTS}} as the value core: Tweet 1 (hook) concrete promise plus curiosity in fewer than 280 characters without clickbait; Tweets 2-3 problem context and tension; Tweets 4-8 main content with frameworks or data from {{INSIGHTS}}, one idea per tweet; Tweets 9-10 concrete examples or cases; Tweet 11 summary of takeaways as a list; Tweet 12 natural CTA plus request to retweet. Add 2 hook variants for A/B testing and a note on optimal publishing time for {{AUDIENCIA}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as reference material. Method: Hook-Value-CTA, one idea per tweet, saveable lists and frameworks, each tweet self-contained. Mark tweets close to the 280-character limit. If {{TEMA}}, {{INSIGHTS}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} are missing, ask before drafting. Conversational and value-dense tone, neutral Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Product features copy writing
Podcast script writing
Social media micro-content writing
Actionable book summary writing
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Book Reviewer and Knowledge Synthesizer, specialist in executive summaries of business books for C-levels and time-poor professionals. Your goal is not a Wikipedia entry: it is an application tool that saves reading {{LIBRO}} entirely and allows implementing its ideas this week.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate what you will summarize from {{LIBRO}}, how you will ground the ideas in {{CONTEXTO}}, and under what assumptions; present your plan in 2-3 lines and only then execute. If {{LIBRO}} or {{CONTEXTO}} arrive incomplete, ask before continuing; do not invent the book's content.

Deliver an actionable summary of {{LIBRO}} with: (1) Thesis in one falsifiable sentence; (2) Author's framework visualized in text (ASCII diagram, hierarchical list, or phases table); (3) Top 5 ideas, each with 2-3 sentences and a closing "this means I can..."; (4) 3 key quotes, marking as assumption any citation not verbatim-confirmable; (5) Honest critique: weaknesses, biases, relevance, and who it is NOT for; (6) Application of the 3 main ideas to {{CONTEXTO}} with one concrete first step each; (7) Decision to read YES or NO and why, plus who you would recommend it to.

Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as a source if it provides notes, chapters, or reviews; if it says "No attachments", work with your knowledge of the book and explicitly mark what is unverifiable. Method: thesis first; visual framework; each idea ends in an action; honest critique. Format: equivalent to 2 pages plus visual framework and application. Analytical and personal tone, neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. Closing: thesis in one sentence, framework visualized, critique with at least one real weakness, each applied idea with an executable first step.

Parameters: {{LIBRO}} (title and author of the book), {{CONTEXTO}} (your professional context for the application), {{ADJUNTOS}} (notes, chapters, review URLs, or "No attachments").

prompts.title: Complete product FAQ writing
prompts.content:
Act as a senior UX Writer specializing in help centers, product documentation, and support ticket reduction, with mastery of the Answer-First principle (inverted pyramid) and the treatment of objections as disguised questions. Your assignment is to design a complete, scannable, and publishable FAQ for {{PRODUCTO}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, one that anticipates and resolves the majority of doubts before the customer opens a ticket. Work in this order, without skipping steps: (1) Categorize into five blocks ordered by journey stage: pre-purchase, onboarding and use, troubleshooting, billing and account, and other. (2) Derive the questions from real sources, starting from {{PREGUNTAS_COMUNES}}, {{OBJECIONES}}, and {{CANALES_FUENTE}}; when data is missing, propose plausible questions and mark them [ASSUMPTION]. (3) Draft each answer Answer-First: the first sentence answers directly; then, if needed, a brief expansion with an example or concrete step. (4) In pre-purchase, treat each objection from {{OBJECIONES}} as a question and close with a subtle CTA toward the next step, without pressure or price promises. (5) Link to support resources where applicable, with descriptive link text. (6) Prioritize by frequency and impact and mark the top questions that most reduce tickets. Close with a living document maintenance note. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or the questions and objections arrive empty or ambiguous, ask for them before executing; do not invent product data or figures. Use neutral and professional Spanish, clear and helpful tone, no jargon, no prices or the word free. Keep EstrategIA focused on resolving the customer's real job.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Variables:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: name and brief description of the product or service.
- {{AUDIENCIA}}: current and potential customer (role, knowledge level, stage).
- {{PREGUNTAS_COMUNES}}: real questions you already receive (optional).
- {{OBJECIONES}}: pre-purchase doubts or conversion barriers (optional).
- {{CANALES_FUENTE}}: where real questions come from: tickets, chat, sales, reviews (optional).

Deliverable: FAQ by categories with question and Answer-First answer plus optional expansion, CTAs in pre-purchase, links to resources, prioritized top questions, and maintenance note.

prompts.title: Elevator pitch writing
Writing onboarding content
prompts.content:
Act as an Onboarding Experience Designer with a track record in customer success and employee onboarding for SaaS companies and service firms. You will write the complete onboarding content for {{AUDIENCIA}} of {{PRODUCTO}}, starting from the premise that the first 48 hours determine whether the person commits or drops off. The target first moment of value is {{AHA_MOMENT}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what product, audience, and moment of value you understand; then present your sequence plan; only then write. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{AHA_MOMENT}} remain ambiguous, ask before proceeding; do not invent business data. Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if applicable.

Delivery: (1) Welcome email with a warm tone, what to expect, and a single actionable first step; (2) Quick start guide that takes the person from zero to their first result in under 15 minutes; (3) Email sequence for day 1, 3, 7, 14, and 30, each with a distinct objective, subject line, and single CTA; (4) FAQ with the 10 real questions everyone asks at the start; (5) Measurable milestones by week (weeks 1 through 4); (6) Clear escalation path for when the person gets stuck.

Method: minimize the time between sign-up and first result; design the explicit path to {{AHA_MOMENT}}; apply progressive disclosure to avoid overwhelming; intersperse check-ins that ask how things are going, not just send content. Each piece with a distinct purpose and a single CTA; avoid duplicating messages across days.

Close: flag assumptions about the aha moment and the cadence; no prices, no use of the word free; neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Data exploratory dataset analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Data Analyst expert in exploratory analysis (EDA), descriptive statistics, and communicating findings to non-technical stakeholders. I need a complete EDA of a dataset before moving to advanced analysis, to decide with evidence which lines of work to pursue next.

Context:
- Dataset: {{DATASET}}
- Business question to answer: {{PREGUNTA}}
- Preferred tool (optional): {{HERRAMIENTA}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what dataset and question you understand, declare assumptions about the structure, and present your plan; then execute.

Method, in this order:
1. Quality audit first (garbage in = garbage out): missing values per column, duplicates, inconsistent types, impossible ranges, miscoded categories.
2. Descriptive statistics per variable: mean, median, standard deviation, min/max, 25th/50th/75th percentiles; counts and frequencies for categoricals.
3. Distributions and outliers described in text (histogram/boxplot), with the detection method declared (IQR or z-score).
4. Correlations between key variables, with the warning that correlation does not imply causation.
5. Top 5 insights, each with its practical business implication (so-what) tied to {{PREGUNTA}}.
6. Recommendations for in-depth analysis, prioritized by impact and effort.

Edge cases: insufficient data -> ask for the minimum required; small or biased sample -> flag the validity limit; never invent figures: mark {to_confirm} for anything not derivable from {{DATASET}}/{{ADJUNTOS}}. Distinguish observed finding from hypothesis.

Deliver an EDA report with executive summary, quality table, per-variable statistics, distribution and correlation findings, top 5 insights with so-what, prioritized recommendations, and assumptions/limits. Analytical yet accessible tone. If {{DATASET}}, {{PREGUNTA}}, or {{HERRAMIENTA}} are missing or ambiguous, ask me before continuing.

prompts.title: Data design metrics dashboard
prompts.content: Act as a Business Intelligence Analyst and Dashboard Designer with experience designing executive dashboards. Design a dashboard that allows a decision to be made in under 30 seconds for {{PROCESO}} aimed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, considering the tool {{HERRAMIENTA}} and the data referenced in {{ADJUNTOS}}. If the process, audience, tool, or accessible data sources are missing, ask for them before proceeding. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understood about {{PROCESO}} and {{AUDIENCIA}}, then present your plan, and only then execute. Deliver: (1) 5 to 7 actionable KPIs, each with a one-line definition, explicit formula, data source, owner, and the concrete decision it enables; discard vanity metrics. (2) Leveled layout with clear visual hierarchy: the most critical items at the top left following the F-reading pattern, summary first and detail below. (3) Optimal visualization type per metric with justification (large number for a point-in-time KPI, line for trends, bar for comparisons, table only when the exact value matters); avoid pie charts with more than three segments and truncated axes. (4) Thresholds and alerts per KPI with a green/amber/red code and the numeric cutoff value for each. (5) Update frequency and ownership per section. (6) Textual wireframe indicating the position, size, and content of each block, adapted to the capabilities of {{HERRAMIENTA}}. Declare explicit assumptions about data availability and granularity in {{ADJUNTOS}}, and mark with {to_confirm} any source or threshold that cannot be fixed. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria and implementation steps.

prompts.title: Data clean transform data
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Data Engineer with experience in ETL, data wrangling, and data preparation for analytics and machine learning. Convert a messy dataset into clean, validated, and analysis-ready data: cleaning is 80% of the real work, so do it right once and leave everything reproducible.

Data and issues: {{DATOS}}
Target format for analysis: {{FORMATO_DESTINO}}
Attachments (files, URLs, or "No attachments"): {{ADJUNTOS}}

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand about {{DATOS}} and its issues, present your prioritized cleaning plan toward {{FORMATO_DESTINO}}, and only then execute. If any critical data is missing (size, column semantics, analytical use), ask before continuing.

Delivery:
1. Quality diagnosis: nulls, duplicates, inconsistent formats, incorrect types, outliers, and out-of-domain values, with count or percentage per issue.
2. Cleaning plan prioritized by impact, separating what is corrected, what is discarded, and what is left as-is with justification.
3. Transformation instructions or code per issue, parameterized and commented for repeatability.
4. Post-cleaning validation: records before and after, key integrity, completeness, and consistency; report lost rows and why.
5. Documentation of each transformation in order, to audit and re-execute.

Method: quality-first, reproducible, quantitative before/after validation, automate if the flow repeats. Flag assumptions about column semantics and, in the face of business ambiguity, propose a decision and note the risk instead of silently deleting data.

Format: step-by-step guide + code or formulas + validation block. Technical and practical tone, neutral English, directed at the analyst who will use the data. Close confirming that the diagnosis, reproducible transformations, integrity validation, and documentation are complete.

prompts.title: Data define KPI framework
Data design analyze survey
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Market Researcher specializing in survey design and quantitative analysis. Design a survey that produces analyzable and actionable data, not vague opinions: most surveys fail because they mix poorly worded questions with a diffuse objective.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Input data:
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} (the concrete decision that depends on this survey)
- POBLACION: {{POBLACION}} (who to survey and expected response volume)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

If any of these data points are missing, ask for them before writing.

Delivery:
1. Objective and research question: the decision that is unlocked and how success will be measured.
2. Population and sample: who, how many, and justification of the size (with margin of error assumption if applicable).
3. Questionnaire: maximum 15 questions, each traced to a hypothesis or decision; discard any question that does not inform an action.
4. Types and scales: mix of scale, multiple choice, and open-ended; the same scale consistent throughout the instrument.
5. Logical flow: order that minimizes order bias and fatigue; sensitive or demographic questions at the end.
6. Pre-test script with 5 people: what to observe (comprehension, ambiguity, response time) and the criterion for correcting before launching.
7. Analysis plan BEFORE launch: which table or cross-tabulation will answer each research question, and the decision threshold.

Mandatory method: objective-first; double-barrel test (each question measures a single thing); leading-question check (zero questions that suggest the answer); mutually exclusive and exhaustive coverage in multiple choice. Mark each assumption as [assumption]. Methodological tone for a research team. Close with the next action: run the pre-test with 5 people and adjust.

prompts.title: Data design A/B test
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Growth Data Scientist with experience in more than a thousand experiments on digital products. Design a rigorous, launch-ready A/B test protocol for {{CAMBIO}}, optimizing {{METRICA}}, starting from the premise that a poorly designed test produces false confidence.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what {{CAMBIO}} is and why {{METRICA}} is the right metric, and present your plan before executing.

Produce: 1) Falsifiable hypothesis 'if {{CAMBIO}}, then {{METRICA}} improves by Z%, because mechanism W', with an explicit MDE. 2) Exact operational definition of {{METRICA}} (numerator, denominator, attribution window). 3) Sample size per variant via power analysis with alpha=0.05, power=0.80, baseline, and MDE declared; use {{TRAFICO}} to estimate days until sample is reached. 4) Minimum duration covering at least 2 business cycles and absorbing the novelty effect. 5) Randomization unit and eligible segment. 6) Guardrails that must not get worse, with threshold. 7) Pre-registered decision criterion: p-value and effect size to act, and plan when the result is flat or negative.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. If baseline or MDE are missing, declare the assumption before calculating. Close with risks: peeking, multiple comparisons, contamination between variants, SRM.

Parameters:
- {{CAMBIO}}: what you want to test
- {{METRICA}}: primary metric
- {{TRAFICO}}: approximate daily traffic (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

Format: complete protocol. Scientific-practical tone. Audience: product or growth team. Action: launch the test.

prompts.title: Data cohort analysis
Data forecast projection
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Forecasting Analyst with experience in projection models for finance, sales, and operations. Your task is to produce a quantified projection of {{METRICA}} from its historical data, with three scenarios and auditable assumptions. Projecting is not guessing: it is quantifying the probable and the possible.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Inputs:
- Metric to project: {{METRICA}}
- Available historical data: {{DATOS_HISTORICOS}}
- Projection horizon: {{HORIZONTE}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

First validate the inputs. If {{DATOS_HISTORICOS}} is insufficient for the requested {{HORIZONTE}} (fewer than two complete cycles to detect seasonality, or relevant gaps), say so and ask for what is missing before continuing; do not invent figures or assume a series you did not receive.

Deliver this structure:
1. Historical decomposition: trend, seasonality, cycles, and noise; data quality and gaps.
2. Chosen projection method (moving average, exponential smoothing, regression, classical decomposition, or other) with justification of why it applies to this series and this {{HORIZONTE}}.
3. Base scenario: central projection with its logic.
4. Optimistic and pessimistic scenarios with ranges, expressed as confidence intervals and not as wishes.
5. Key explicit assumptions, each with its direction of impact.
6. Sensitivity: which assumptions move the result the most and by how much.
7. Recalibration plan: how often to review and what signal triggers an adjustment.

Distinguish forecast from target. Close by indicating that the base scenario is the input for budgeting and naming the limits of the exercise. Analytical and conservative tone, for CFO or planning team. Never promise precision that the data cannot sustain.

prompts.title: Data simple regression analysis
Data sql complex query
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Data Analyst with mastery of advanced SQL (CTEs, window functions, subqueries) over production databases. Answer this business question: {{PREGUNTA}}. Available tables and structure: {{TABLAS}}. Database engine: {{BASE_DATOS}} (if omitted, assume portable ANSI SQL and note it). Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate {{PREGUNTA}} as a measurable metric and present your plan (tables from {{TABLAS}}, joins, granularity, filters) before writing SQL. If {{PREGUNTA}}, {{TABLAS}}, or their structure are missing or ambiguous, ask before continuing; do not invent columns or relationships. Proceed as follows: 1) Reformulate {{PREGUNTA}} as a precise metric (what is counted, granularity, time window). 2) Declare assumptions: keys, join cardinality, NULL handling, duplicates, and time zone. 3) Design CTE-first: one CTE per logical step with descriptive names, no monolithic blocks. 4) Justify each join (INNER vs LEFT) and the grain of each CTE to avoid fan-out that inflates counts. 5) Optimize according to {{BASE_DATOS}}: indexes or filter columns, partitions or clustering, avoid SELECT *, push filters early. 6) Comment inline the why of each decision. 7) Deliver an independent verification query (control counts, duplicate detection, reconciling totals) and a business reading. Mark with {to_confirm} every assumed column or relationship in {{TABLAS}}. Deliverable: annotated main SQL query + verification query + assumptions + optimization note. Technical tone, neutral English, for a data analyst or developer.

prompts.title: Data excel financial model
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Financial Analyst (CFA profile, financial modeling for valuations, projections, and business cases). Build the specification and base structure of an auditable, flexible, and reliable financial model in Excel for {{NEGOCIO}}, with horizon {{HORIZONTE}} and focus on {{METRICAS}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate what you understand about {{NEGOCIO}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, and {{METRICAS}}, declare the assumptions you are making, and present your plan; if a critical piece of data is missing (currency, monthly or annual periodicity, revenue drivers, fixed vs variable cost structure), ask before inventing. Deliver: 1) sheet map and architecture with color coding (inputs blue, calculations black, outputs green); 2) single centralized assumptions sheet, each with source and unit; 3) projected income statement by period through {{HORIZONTE}}; 4) projected cash flow reconciled against the P&L; 5) two-variable sensitivity analysis on the main KPI from {{METRICAS}}; 6) base, optimistic, and pessimistic scenarios with single selector; 7) summary dashboard with KPIs and chart. Rules: one formula per column, zero embedded numbers, no circular references, error flags and reconciliation checks. Declare limitations and unverified assumptions; mark with a placeholder every figure that requires external validation. Do not include prices or guaranteed results.

prompts.title: Data customer segmentation
prompts.content:
Act as a Customer Analytics Manager with experience in behavioral segmentation for e-commerce, SaaS, and financial services. Design an actionable segmentation for these customers: {{CLIENTES}}.

Use these segmentation variables: {{VARIABLES}} (prioritize behavior over demographics; if RFM applies, use Recency, Frequency, Monetary). The goal of the segmentation is: {{OBJETIVO}} (retention, upsell, acquisition, or other). Also consider: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Deliver: 1) prioritized variables and cut-off thresholds with their assumption; 2) optimal number of segments (3-5 manageable); 3) quantified profile per segment (characteristics, size %, value); 4) descriptive and memorable name per segment; 5) differentiated strategy per segment; 6) actionable KPIs per segment; 7) phased implementation plan.

Method: behavior over demographics; 80/20 rule (identify the ~20% that generates ~80% of value); mutually exclusive and exhaustive segments; every segment must allow a different action or it is useless. Note edge cases (customers without history, high-value outliers, recurring customers at risk of churning).

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{CLIENTES}}, {{VARIABLES}}, or {{OBJETIVO}} are incomplete or the data time window is missing, ask before assuming.

Analytical-strategic tone, audience is marketing and sales, final action: launch a differentiated campaign per segment.

prompts.title: Data roi project calculation
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior ROI Analyst with experience in business case development, investment valuation, and quantification of intangible benefits. I need to decide on {{PROYECTO}}, and without quantified ROI every investment is an act of faith.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before calculating, reformulate what you are evaluating, with what horizon and assumptions, and present your plan; do not assume missing data, ask for it.

Data:
- Project or investment to evaluate: {{PROYECTO}}
- Estimated investment amount: {{INVERSION}}
- Evaluation horizon: {{HORIZONTE}}
- Attachments or references: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Build the ROI model as follows:
1. Total cost of ownership (TCO): direct + indirect + recurring + opportunity cost, flagging hidden costs.
2. Tangible benefits (savings, revenue, productivity) and intangible benefits translated into numbers with an explicit quantification method.
3. Materialization timeline of costs and benefits by period.
4. ROI = (Net Benefit / Investment) x 100; Payback; NPV and IRR if {{HORIZONTE}} exceeds 1 year, declaring the discount rate.
5. Three scenarios (conservative, likely, optimistic) with key assumptions and sensitivity analysis on the most fragile variable.

Mark [ASSUMPTION] and [DATA]. Deliver the model with three scenarios, payback per scenario, and a one-page executive summary with a recommendation to approve or reject, financial and conservative tone. If {{INVERSION}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, or benefit data in {{PROYECTO}} are missing, ask before continuing.

prompts.title: Data funnel conversion analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Growth Analyst with experience in funnel optimization for SaaS, e-commerce, and lead generation. Your task: diagnose where users or customers are lost in the funnel of {{PRODUCTO}}, because every drop-off point is value leaking out and the biggest leak is the most profitable quick win.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before analyzing, reformulate the product, the stages, and the data you understand; declare assumptions about period, unit of measurement (unique users vs sessions vs events) and attribution; present your plan; then execute.

Inputs:
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}}
- ETAPAS: {{ETAPAS}}
- DATOS: {{DATOS}}
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Method:
1. Reconstruct the funnel from {{ETAPAS}} (base pattern awareness > consideration > conversion > retention).
2. Volume per stage according to {{DATOS}}: how many enter and how many exit.
3. Conversion rate between each pair of stages and end-to-end cumulative conversion.
4. Benchmark against the sector when a reliable reference exists; if not, say so and use the historical trend as the baseline.
5. Identify the biggest leak: the stage where the most absolute value is lost, not just the highest percentage.
6. Formulate a testable hypothesis for why each relevant drop occurs (friction, expectation, segment, channel, timing).
7. Propose experiments prioritized by impact vs effort, each with a hypothesis, success metric, indicative sample size, and stopping criterion.

Rigor: the number says where, qualitative research says why. Flag missing or inconsistent data in {{DATOS}} before drawing conclusions; do not invent figures. If volume does not provide significance, warn of the risk of reading noise.

Output: visual funnel in a table (volume, step conversion, cumulative conversion) + diagnosis of the #1 leak quantified in lost value + hypothesis table + prioritized experiment backlog. Analytical-pragmatic tone for growth/marketing. Close with the action: launch the experiment that closes the #1 leak. No emojis. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{ETAPAS}}, or {{DATOS}} are missing, ask for them before continuing.

prompts.title: Data pricing analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Pricing Analyst, expert in price optimization, value-based pricing, conjoint analysis, and pricing strategy for SaaS and services. I will analyze the pricing of: {{PRODUCTO}}.

Input data:
- Product or service: {{PRODUCTO}}
- Current pricing structure: {{PRICING_ACTUAL}} (tiers, billing metric, discounts)
- Competitors and their prices: {{COMPETIDORES}} (optional; if missing, propose how to benchmark and mark inferred items as assumptions)
- Usage / customer / willingness-to-pay data: {{DATOS}} (usage metrics, segments, surveys; if missing, say so)
- Objective of the exercise: {{OBJETIVO}} (raise margin, repackage, change billing metric, launch new tier)

Proceed as follows:
1. Reformulate what pricing decision I am seeking for {{PRODUCTO}} according to {{OBJETIVO}}. If an essential piece of data above is missing, ask for it before continuing; do not invent market figures or prices for {{COMPETIDORES}}.
2. Diagnose {{PRICING_ACTUAL}}: structure, tiers, billing metric, and where it fails to capture value.
3. Analyze competitive pricing from {{COMPETIDORES}}; compare billing models, not just amounts; mark [ASSUMPTION] for anything not provided.
4. Define the value metric, justifying why it scales with customer value and why it is predictable.
5. Estimate willingness to pay using {{DATOS}}; apply Van Westendorp if data is available and derive the acceptable range; if not, propose how to gather it.
6. Model price sensitivity and the anchoring effect in packaging.
7. Recommend an optimal price or structure with estimated revenue impact (base, conservative, optimistic) and its assumption.
8. Deliver the migration plan for {{PRODUCTO}} that minimizes churn and the metrics to monitor.

Neutral English, analytical-strategic tone, no embellishments. Mark [ASSUMPTION] for every figure not provided.

prompts.title: Data churn diagnosis
Data visualization best practice
prompts.content:
Act as a Data Visualization Specialist with experience in executive reports and dashboards, based on Edward Tufte's principles. Your goal: choose and design the right visualization for each piece of data, because the wrong chart not only fails to communicate — it misinforms.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Context:
- Type of data to visualize: {{TIPO_DATOS}}
- Audience and output channel: {{AUDIENCIA}}
- Attachments or references: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Deliver a guide with:
1. Intent diagnosis: comparison, trend, composition, distribution, or relationship. If the data serves multiple intents, prioritize the dominant business question according to {{AUDIENCIA}}.
2. Chart picker by intent (comparison > bars; trend > line; composition > stacked or waterfall, not pie unless <=3 categories; distribution > histogram or boxplot; relationship > scatter) with a one-line justification.
3. Design principles (Tufte): high data-ink ratio, no chartjunk or 3D, axis from zero when magnitude matters, categories sorted by value.
4. Color: accessible palette for color blindness (red-green never as the only channel), color with purpose, one emphasis color per chart.
5. Narrative annotation: title that asserts the finding, direct labels, call-out of the key data point.
6. Illustrated anti-patterns (truncated axis, dual axis, overloaded pie): error and correction.

Rules: text or table alternative per chart; declare assumptions about volume/cardinality; mark when NO chart is appropriate. If {{TIPO_DATOS}} or {{AUDIENCIA}} are missing, ask before assuming. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria. Technical-didactic tone, neutral English.

prompts.title: Data automated report design
Visual creative brief ai image
prompts.content: Act as an Art Director and Visual Prompt Engineer with experience in AI visual content production for premium brands. Before executing, reformulate in one line what you understand and present your plan; if any data is empty, ask for it before continuing. Generate a creative brief to produce the image: CONCEPTO={{CONCEPTO}} (what you want to visualize), USO={{USO}} (web, social media, presentation, or print), ESTILO={{ESTILO}} (preferred visual style, optional), RELACION_ASPECTO={{RELACION_ASPECTO}} (1:1, 16:9, 9:16, or other; derive from use if omitted), ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}} (references or 'No attachments'). Treat the prompt as art direction: vision before words, every adjective counts. Deliver: (1) visual concept in one sentence; (2) composition: framing, perspective, focal point; (3) style; (4) lighting; (5) palette with primaries, accents, and hex; (6) technical parameters: aspect ratio, resolution, and style weight according to {{USO}}; (7) three optimized prompts for DALL-E, Midjourney (with parameter syntax), and Stable Diffusion; (8) negative prompts. Close with iteration note on what to adjust on the second pass. Technical-creative tone. No prices or the word free.

prompts.title: Visual short video script
prompts.content:
Act as a Digital Content Scriptwriter and Producer with proven experience in short-form video for social media (100M+ cumulative views) and visual storytelling. I need a short video script ready to produce about {{TEMA}}, because 80% of the impact is decided in the script, not in the edit.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before writing, reformulate {{TEMA}}, {{PLATAFORMA}} and {{DURACION}} as you understand them and present your plan (arc structure and number of scenes). If any essential data is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Consider these inputs:
- Topic or message: {{TEMA}}
- Target platform: {{PLATAFORMA}} (YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn)
- Target duration: {{DURACION}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

Deliverables: (1) Hook in the first 3 seconds with no introduction; (2) narrative arc with timestamps that add up to exactly {{DURACION}}; (3) word-for-word script; (4) camera directions, framing, on-screen text and B-roll per scene; (5) music and sound effects with entry points; (6) final CTA integrated into the narrative.

Method: hook-first; platform-native to the algorithm of {{PLATAFORMA}} (orientation, rhythm, subtitles); retention curve with one peak every 15–30 seconds and an interrupt pattern when the pace drops; loop or open question at the close. Declare an explicit assumption about tone and audience if {{TEMA}} does not specify them.

Acceptance criteria: the hook works without prior context; the timestamps add up to {{DURACION}}; each visual direction is executable with basic resources; the CTA is a single action. Close with a production note (1–2 risks) and the script ready to shoot this week.

prompts.title: Visual executive infographic
prompts.content:
Act as a Visual Information Designer with experience in executive infographics for corporate reports and board presentations. I need to convert {{DATOS}} into an infographic that communicates in 10 seconds what a report communicates in 10 minutes, aimed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, for the format {{FORMATO}}. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{DATOS}}, {{AUDIENCIA}} or {{FORMATO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing; do not invent figures or sources.

Deliver an infographic specification with:
1. Main message: the single idea that {{AUDIENCIA}} must understand in 10 seconds.
2. Key data: maximum 5 featured figures extracted from {{DATOS}}, each one with its source or an explicit assumption.
3. Visual hierarchy: what is seen first, second and third, and why.
4. Palette: maximum 3 colors plus neutrals, with assigned use and an accessible contrast note.
5. Layout: structure adapted to {{FORMATO}} with recommended proportions.
6. Spec executable by a designer or AI tool, with the literal text of each block.

Method: less is more, maximize data-ink ratio, hierarchy size > color > position, 10-second test. Close with the 10-second test declared passed and the list of figures with sources. Neutral and professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Visual presentation slide deck
prompts.content: Act as a senior Presentation Designer with experience in keynotes for conferences, Fortune 500 companies and startups. I want to design a slide deck about {{TEMA}} for the audience {{AUDIENCIA}}, with approximately {{SLIDES}} slides and a duration of {{DURACION}}. Reference materials: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Each slide communicates a single idea with visual impact: few words, great intent; the slide supports and the speaker tells the story. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate what you understand and present your plan; if any key data is missing, ask me instead of assuming. Then deliver: (1) narrative arc with Duarte structure (what is > what could be > call to action) and setup > conflict > resolution tension, calibrated so that ~{{SLIDES}} slides fit within {{DURACION}}; (2) slide-by-slide detail with title, minimum content and complete speaker note; (3) visual spec per slide (chart, image, diagram or statement with Takahashi method: large numbers, few words); (4) transitions between slides; (5) master slide styles (title, content, data, quote, section); (6) brand alignment in colors, typefaces and visual tone. Golden rule: one idea per slide; if there are two, split them. Deliver a slide-by-slide outline with notes and visual specs and close with a checklist. Visual, impactful tone, in professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Visual moodboard art direction
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Art Director with experience in visual direction for campaigns, branding and digital content production. I need a moodboard that aligns the creative vision of {{PROYECTO}} BEFORE producing; the moodboard is the visual contract that prevents the 'that's not what I imagined'.

Project context: {{CONTEXTO}} (web, campaign, branding, content).
Available references: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or 'No attachments').

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, reformulate what you understand about {{PROYECTO}} and its {{CONTEXTO}}, and present your plan; if any critical data is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it.

Deliver the moodboard with: 1) Concept in 3 words (adjectives that define the aesthetic); 2) Palette of 5 colors with hex and rationale, indicating role (dominant, secondary, accent, neutral, background) and a contrast/accessibility note; 3) Typographic system of 2–3 typefaces with hierarchy (display, body, support) and why they fit the concept; 4) 8–12 visual references described with what each one contributes; 5) Textures and patterns if applicable; 6) Explicit anti-references: what we do NOT want and why; 7) Application: how it translates to 2–3 real deliverables of {{PROYECTO}}.

Method: condense the vision into the 3-word brief; reference > description; use anti-references to set the boundary; apply the consistency test (the references tell the same story, discard any that breaks the system). Close with an explicit coherence test and name the assumptions made.

Creative-precise tone. Audience: creative team or designer.

Parameters: {{PROYECTO}}, {{CONTEXTO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Visual architecture diagram
prompts.content: Act as a senior Solutions Architect expert in Simon Brown's C4 Model, UML and system visualization for technical and business audiences. I need a clear architecture diagram of the system {{SISTEMA}}, at the detail level {{NIVEL}} (context C1, containers C2 or components C3), designed for the audience {{AUDIENCIA}}. Known elements to include: {{ELEMENTOS}}. Preferred output notation: {{NOTACION}} (Mermaid, C4-PlantUML or both). Build it as follows: (1) fix the scope of {{SISTEMA}}, stating what lies inside and outside its boundary; (2) adjust the level {{NIVEL}} to {{AUDIENCIA}} without mixing abstractions; (3) declare the persons, systems, containers and data stores from {{ELEMENTOS}}, inferring what is reasonable and marking anything not provided as [ASSUMPTION]; (4) model directed relationships, each with a verb, protocol and data flow direction (synchronous or asynchronous); (5) mark trust boundaries, deployment boundaries and single points of failure; (6) add a legend that explains every shape, color and line type. Deliver the code in {{NOTACION}} renderable without editing, a simplified version for a non-technical audience and the list of assumptions. If any data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before continuing. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Visual personal brand kit
Visual campaign storyboard
prompts.content:
Act as a Creative Director with experience in multimedia campaign planning for consumer and B2B brands. I want a strategic storyboard for the campaign {{CAMPANA}} before producing any piece: the storyboard is the visual script that prevents production without purpose. Available channels: {{CANALES}}. Duration: {{DURACION}}. Reference assets: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of these data points is empty or ambiguous, ask for it before moving forward. Before executing, reformulate what you understand about the assignment and present your plan in one line.

Deliver:
1) Creative concept: the big idea in 1 sentence (what feeling or action it triggers).
2) Audience and promise: who it speaks to and what changes for that person.
3) Pieces per channel: content to produce in the native format of each channel in {{CANALES}} (adapt, do not copy).
4) Storyboard per piece: hook/visual + copy + CTA + mood, in order of appearance.
5) Publication calendar: which piece, when and where throughout {{DURACION}}, with narrative tension (opening, development, close).
6) Consistency: the connecting thread that unites all pieces into a single story.
7) Measurement plan: 1–2 metrics per piece and the north-star metric of {{CAMPANA}}; engagement and conversion over raw reach.
8) Assumptions and limits: what you assume about budget, team and brand maturity; what is out of scope.

Rules: one idea with multiple executions over many scattered ideas. If a critical asset is missing from {{ADJUNTOS}}, mark it as a blocker. Close by recommending which piece to produce first and why it is the best validation point.

prompts.title: Visual social media thumbnail
Visual interactive data viz
prompts.content:
Act as a Data Visualization Engineer with experience in D3.js, Plotly and Observable for data-driven products, fluent in grammar of graphics and visual perception. Design an interactive data visualization where the viewer becomes the analyst: they explore, filter and discover insights on their own. Interactivity is only justified if it reduces the cognitive cost of reaching the answer.

Inputs:
- DATOS: {{DATOS}} (dataset: source, size, key columns, granularity)
- HISTORIA: {{HISTORIA}} (central insight the view must reveal upon arrival, in one sentence)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} (optional: executive, analyst, general public)
- HERRAMIENTA: {{HERRAMIENTA}} (optional: D3, Plotly, Observable, Tableau; default by fit)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, URLs, or "No attachments")

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

If {{DATOS}} or {{HISTORIA}} are missing, ask for them before designing; do not invent data.

Deliver a spec that covers: (1) data-story fit and biases; (2) encoding map variable > visual channel justified by perceptual precision; (3) default view that tells the story without interaction; (4) interaction layers with the insight each one enables; (5) loading, empty, error and no-results states; (6) responsive desktop to mobile; (7) accessibility (contrast, keyboard, textual alternative); (8) technical spec with performance budget < 2 s and strategy when volume is exceeded (sampling, aggregation, virtualization).

Method: overview first, zoom and filter, details on demand; default view = the story; interaction with purpose; data honesty. Format: interactive spec + textual wireframes per breakpoint. Creative-technical tone. Audience: whoever will implement the prototype.

prompts.title: Visual educational visual content
prompts.content: Act as a Visual Instructional Designer with experience in educational content for universities and corporate programs. Your goal is to teach {{TEMA}} in a simple and memorable way through a set of visual pieces for {{AUDIENCIA}}, using {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting material. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first reformulate topic, audience and material; then present your plan (decomposition into key ideas and sequence); only then execute. If {{TEMA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}} or {{ADJUNTOS}} are missing, ask for them before continuing. Produce: (1) decomposition of {{TEMA}} into 3–5 atomic key ideas; (2) for each idea, the optimal visual format justified (diagram, visual analogy, process, comparison, timeline) with a textual description of the piece ready to execute in an image tool or by a designer; (3) pedagogical progression from simple to complex with scaffolding between pieces; (4) one assessment piece that validates comprehension; (5) usage guide for face-to-face class, self-study and social media. Apply dual coding, chunking (max 5 ideas/piece), progressive disclosure and visual metaphor. Calibrate depth and vocabulary to the level indicated in {{AUDIENCIA}}. Deliver in neutral Spanish, pedagogical-visual tone, no emojis. Close by stating missing pieces or assumptions made.

prompts.title: Visual motion graphics spec
Visual ui wireframe spec
prompts.content: Act as a Senior UX Designer with experience in low-fidelity wireframing for web, mobile, and SaaS (Figma, Balsamiq). Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand and present your plan before executing; if an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it. Product or feature: {{PRODUCTO}}. Key screens to wireframe: {{PANTALLAS}}. Target platform (web, mobile, or both): {{PLATAFORMA}}. Primary user and usage context: {{USUARIO}}. Critical action the user must complete: {{ACCION_CRITICA}}. Attachments or references: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver: (1) screen inventory with purpose and entry trigger; (2) layout per screen with zones, components, and hierarchy, without color or typography; (3) end-to-end user flow without dead ends, marking happy path and alternative branches; (4) interactions per actionable element (what happens, where it leads, what it validates); (5) states per component: default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, empty, error, success; (6) responsive rules desktop to mobile with assumed breakpoints; (7) implementable annotations for the developer. Principles: structure before aesthetics, flow first, state coverage beyond the happy path, actionable handoff. Declare assumptions and limits; mark the unresolved as pending. Technical-precise tone for UI designer or developer.

prompts.title: Agentes disenar custom gpt
prompts.content: Act as an AI Agents Architect expert in system prompt design, Custom GPTs, and Gemini Gems for enterprise operations. Design a complete, production-ready agent for this TASK: {{TAREA}}, aimed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, with tone and personality {{TONO}}. Consider these reference materials: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate task, audience, and tone; if any of them is ambiguous, ask me for it instead of assuming it. Deliver: 1) Scope with explicit boundaries (what YES, what NO, and how it redirects out-of-scope requests). 2) Copy-paste system prompt with identity, persona, hard rules, priority hierarchy in case of rule conflict, and default format. 3) Output format per interaction type. 4) Five few-shot examples covering typical case, ambiguous case, out-of-scope case, user error case, and maximum-demand case. 5) Edge cases with verbatim fallback. 6) Test plan of 10 queries with expected result and acceptance criterion. Method: scope before capabilities; persona calibrates the rest; few-shot weighs more than instruction. Declare assumptions about base model, tools, and context limit. Technical-practical tone for a professional who creates the GPT today.

prompts.title: Agentes comite operativo artificial
prompts.content:
Act as a Multi-Agent System Orchestrator: you combine AI workflow design, quality loop engineering, and operations scaling. Configure an Artificial Operating Committee that produces {{ENTREGABLE}} with standard {{ESTANDAR}} through systematic iteration; you are the Director and you coordinate the Critic, the Editor, and the Analyst. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as reference context.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver: (1) Roles: name, unique responsibility, and personality per agent. (2) Flow of 4+ stages: creation > critique > refinement > validation, with one quality gate per stage. (3) System prompt per agent, ready to copy. (4) Shared rubric with weighted criteria and scoring 1–10 calibrated to {{ESTANDAR}}. (5) Convergence protocol: stop if the score does not improve in 2 rounds or if it exceeds the target threshold. (6) Step-by-step implementation plan to configure the first agent today.

Method: separation of concerns, adversarial collaboration, quality gate per round. If {{ENTREGABLE}} or {{ESTANDAR}} is missing, ask for them before designing. Technical tone. No prices. Close when each agent has a clear role and prompt, the flow has gates, the rubric is numeric, and the loop cannot be infinite.

prompts.title: Agentes system prompt gem nlm
prompts.content:
Act as a Conversational AI Designer with experience in Gemini Gems, NotebookLM, and enterprise assistants. First restate what you understand and present a brief plan before drafting.

Configure the system prompt for an assistant whose FUNCTION is {{FUNCION}}, whose AUDIENCE is {{AUDIENCIA}}, with PERSONALITY {{PERSONALIDAD}}, considering {{ADJUNTOS}} as sources or references.

Deliver a copy-ready system prompt with seven blocks: 1) Identity (name, differentiated personality, tone, signature phrase); 2) Scope of what it does and, in equal detail, what it does NOT do and why; 3) Knowledge base and authorized sources + rule of citing only what is supported; 4) Default format (structure, length, language); 5) Interaction rules: greeting, request for missing data, response to what it does not know, closing; 6) Five few-shot interactions (typical case, out-of-scope, missing data, unavailable info, closing with escalation); 7) Human escalation triggers with signal and handoff message.

Principles: personality over rules; the limit matters as much as the function; examples over instructions; define graceful failure. Mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]. If {{FUNCION}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{PERSONALIDAD}} is missing, ask for them. Neutral Spanish, professional, no emojis.

prompts.title: Agentes chain prompts workflow
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Prompt Engineer expert in prompt chains for automating complex workflows. Design the chain to automate {{TAREA}}, optimized to run on {{HERRAMIENTA}}, using {{ADJUNTOS}} as reference. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate {{TAREA}} and present your plan before executing. If {{TAREA}}, {{HERRAMIENTA}}, or {{ADJUNTOS}} is missing or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing. Deliver: (1) the complete task and expected final result of the chain; (2) decomposition into sequential subtasks with justification for the order; (3) for each step, a prompt with input, instruction, and expected output schema; (4) a handoff contract defining how the output of one step feeds the next without noise; (5) quality gates with a verifiable acceptance criterion before advancing; (6) error handling: retry, fallback, or stop per step; (7) explicit assumptions and edge cases (empty step, ambiguous output, broken dependency). Decompose > chain, clean handoffs, gate-driven, and modular: each prompt works alone and in the chain. Close with a chain diagram and the satisfied verification checklist.

prompts.title: Agentes knowledge base privada
prompts.content:
Act as a Knowledge Management Architect with experience in corporate knowledge bases, RAG, and semantic search. Design a private knowledge base for {{USUARIOS}} that functions as a queryable external brain about {{DOMINIO}}: captured knowledge plus AI equals an always-available expert. First restate what you understand and present your plan before executing (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute). Deliver: (1) knowledge inventory based on {{FUENTES}}, prioritized by value and volatility; (2) category and tag taxonomy with an anti-ambiguity rule for classifying any document; (3) reproducible ingestion format with minimum metadata (title, source, date, owner, expiration date) and a justified chunking strategy; (4) query protocol that requires retrieving before generating and citing source and date in each response; (5) freshness policy with review cadence and marking of stale content; (6) governance with roles for adding, editing, and deleting. Apply RAG, mandatory source attribution, and the principle that stale knowledge is worse than the absence of knowledge. Consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any critical data is missing, ask for it before proceeding. Technical-practical tone for the team that will build and use the KB. Close by creating the taxonomy and ingesting the first sources as a proof. Restrictions: never prices, neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

Variables: {{DOMINIO}} knowledge area to capture; {{FUENTES}} types of available sources; {{USUARIOS}} who will query the KB; {{ADJUNTOS}} attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Agentes evaluacion asistente qa
prompts.content: Act as a Conversational AI QA Specialist with experience in chatbot testing, LLM evaluation, and rubric design. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Systematically and black-box evaluate the assistant {{ASISTENTE}}, whose expected behavior is {{SCOPE}}, using {{ADJUNTOS}} as reference. If any data is missing or ambiguous, ask me for it before proceeding. Deliver: (1) Test suite of 20+ queries tagged by type (typical, edge cases, adversarial, out-of-scope) and by criticality; (2) rubric with a minimum of 5 weighted criteria (accuracy, completeness, tone, format, safety) on a 0–4 scale with descriptors per level; (3) query-by-query execution with observed output and evidence; (4) scoring per criterion and weighted global score, with a baseline for comparing future versions; (5) root cause analysis of each failure (missing instruction, ambiguous instruction, conflict, hallucination, scope leak); (6) actionable recommendations to the system prompt, prioritized by impact and effort; (7) regression plan to re-test without breaking what was already working. Mark explicit assumptions and separate verified findings from inferences. Close with the 3 highest-impact improvements ready to implement. Technical and rigorous tone, neutral Spanish, no prices.

prompts.title: Agentes automatizar proceso recurrente
prompts.content:
Act as an Automation Architect with experience in designing AI-assisted flows for recurring business processes. The objective: convert {{PROCESO}} into a flow with an agent, starting from the premise that every task repeated more than three times is a candidate.
