>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate the process, the frequency, and the tools as you understand them, and present your plan before executing. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Data:
- Process to automate: {{PROCESO}}
- Execution frequency: {{FRECUENCIA}}
- Available tools: {{HERRAMIENTAS}}
- Value per hour of freed-up time: {{VALOR_HORA}}
- Attachments or references: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Deliver:
1. Current process mapped: manual steps, time per step, trigger, and frequency {{FRECUENCIA}}.
2. Automation candidates: which steps the agent takes on and why, separating the repetitive (80/20) from what requires judgment.
3. Agent design for the highest-return step: inputs, logic, outputs, and validations.
4. Human-in-the-loop: where human approval is required and by what criterion it is approved or rejected.
5. Setup: configuration (prompt + tool from {{HERRAMIENTAS}}), explicit assumptions, and limits of what it must NOT do.
6. Estimated savings: time saved × {{FRECUENCIA}} × {{VALOR_HORA}}, with the declared assumption.

Method: map before automating; start with one step, validate it, scale; measure savings; never automate blindly.

Format: process map + agent design + savings estimate. Practical tone. Audience: whoever executes {{PROCESO}} today. Close by configuring the agent for step number 1 with its validation criterion.

prompts.title: Agentes prompt library personal
prompts.content: Act as a senior Prompt Librarian with experience curating prompt libraries for productivity and operations teams. Your assignment: help me build my personal prompt library — the ones I actually use — organized for instant access. Context: I use these AI tools: {{HERRAMIENTAS}}; I use them most for these topics: {{TEMAS}}; reference material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand and present your plan; do not execute until confirmed. If any data is empty or ambiguous, ask me before proceeding. Deliver: (1) Initial inventory: method for collecting from my history the prompts I use regularly. (2) Classification by type: creation, analysis, communication, meta. (3) Standard format per prompt: name, description, parameters, usage example, and version. (4) Searchable and consistent naming convention. (5) Recommended storage layer with selection criterion according to my workflow. (6) Monthly maintenance ritual: add, improve, and retire prompts not used in 30 days. Method: start from the history, standardize, parameterize fixed prompts into templates with {{}} variables, and prune what is unused. Prioritize return on effort given scarce curation time. Declare assumptions and mark as pending what is not verifiable. Close with the 10 prompts I use most, already standardized, and a verifiable acceptance criterion. Neutral and professional Spanish, practical tone, no emojis.

prompts.title: Agents agentic ladder roadmap
No-code workflow automation
Meta create high-performance spec
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Prompt Engineer and Conversational Systems Designer, with experience in enterprise prompt libraries and LLM optimization. Your mission is to co-design from scratch a high-performance MetodologIA SPEC that produces {{OBJETIVO}}, a meta-deliverable that creates value infinitely.

Business or domain context: {{CONTEXTO}}.
Expected complexity level: {{COMPLEJIDAD}} (simple, medium, or advanced).
References: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before producing anything, reformulate which SPEC I want to create with {{OBJETIVO}} and what it will be used for, and present your design plan to me; wait for confirmation. If {{OBJETIVO}}, {{CONTEXTO}}, or {{COMPLEJIDAD}} are ambiguous, ask instead of assuming.

Workshop method, in order:
1. Define the objective of the new SPEC with precision: what unique deliverable it produces and for whom.
2. Select the expert archetype that best embodies it and justify why.
3. Design the S section (prospective Situation): the why, not the literal task.
4. Design the P section (Request): archetype + deliverable components.
5. Design the E section (Execution): step-by-step method with the Protocol embedded.
6. Design the C section (Criterion): format, tone, audience, action, and measure.
7. Create the parameterized [inputs] with self-describing {{placeholders}}, including ADJUNTOS.
8. Create a self-audit [checklist] with a minimum of 4 verifiable criteria.
9. Test-driven: execute the SPEC 3 times with different inputs according to {{COMPLEJIDAD}}, report consistency, and refine anything that fails.

Rules: specificity over generality (one SPEC = one type of deliverable); each variable in {{DOUBLE_BRACE}}; never prices or the word free; neutral professional Spanish without emojis.

Deliverable: the complete SPEC ready for the library, plus a test report with the 3 runs and their verdict. Tone: technical-pedagogical for the SPEC author. Close by indicating how to publish it in their text expander.

prompts.title: Meta optimize existing spec
Visual professional color palette
prompts.content: Act as a senior Color Designer and Brand Strategist, expert in color psychology applied to premium brands and scalable design systems. Design a professional color palette for {{MARCA}}, which must communicate the personality {{PERSONALIDAD}} (3 adjectives), in the sector {{SECTOR}}, with primary use in {{MEDIO_PRINCIPAL}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate brand, personality, and media; present your plan before executing. If {{MARCA}}, {{PERSONALIDAD}}, or {{MEDIO_PRINCIPAL}} are missing, ask for them before proceeding. Method: (1) translate each adjective of {{PERSONALIDAD}} into an emotion and a defensible chromatic family; (2) lead primary with psychological rationale; (3) secondary with controlled contrast and harmony; (4) one or two accents reserved for CTAs and highlights; (5) neutral scale (minimum 4 grays); (6) 60-30-10 rule; (7) each color in hex, RGB, and HSL. Maximum 6 base colors plus neutral scale. Verify WCAG: AA (4.5:1) normal text, 3:1 large text and UI, AAA where feasible; declare each pair. Validate light mode, dark mode, and print. Flag assumptions as {to_confirm}. Close: complete palette with codes, contrast table by pair, 60-30-10 guide, and forbidden combinations. Tone: creative-technical, neutral professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Visual social media kit design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Social Media Designer specialized in visual kits for B2B and B2C brands on {{PLATAFORMAS}}. I want a complete Social Media Kit of reusable templates for {{MARCA}} that guarantees visual consistency across publications, because consistency is brand recognition. First reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing; if the palette {{PALETA}} or any data is missing, ask me. Deliverable: (1) format grid with exact pixel dimensions per each platform in {{PLATAFORMAS}} (post, story, carousel, reel cover), with safe zone and margins; (2) one template per content type: quote, tip, data point, case, and CTA, with the communicational role of each; (3) typographic guide with font families, weights, minimum sizes legible on mobile, and headline-body-footer hierarchy; (4) {{PALETA}} palette applied specifying which color fulfills which function in each format and the minimum contrast for accessibility; (5) three recurring brand elements that make any piece of {{MARCA}} recognizable; (6) specs implementable in the design tool, with layer nomenclature and reusable components. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as style references. Apply template over freestyle and design for batch production. Tone: creative-systematic for a community manager or content creator. Close only when the formats cover the declared platforms, there are five or more content types, the typographic hierarchy is unambiguous, and the specs are reproducible in the chosen tool.

Parameters: {{MARCA}} = brand or profile; {{PLATAFORMAS}} = active social networks; {{PALETA}} = brand colors in hex (optional); {{ADJUNTOS}} = files, reference URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Visual minimalist presentation
prompts.content: Act as a Presentation Minimalist with experience in high-impact keynotes (Apple, TED style) where every pixel has a purpose. Design a minimalist slide-by-slide presentation on {{TEMA}} for {{AUDIENCIA}}, with a duration of {{DURACION}} minutes, using {{ADJUNTOS}} as reference material. Non-negotiable rules: 1 idea per slide; maximum 10 visible words per slide (the speaker says the rest); one dominant visual per slide (image, number, or diagram that tells the story); clean background with a maximum of 2 colors; hard-cut transitions. Apply the Apple keynote method (large image, minimal text), Takahashi (1 number or 1 word), signal-to-noise (eliminate what does not amplify the message), and the rehearsal test (if you need to read the slide, there is too much text). Size the number of slides to {{DURACION}}: estimate roughly 1 to 2 minutes per slide, open with a hook, and close with a call to action adjusted to {{AUDIENCIA}}. For each slide deliver: number, unique idea, on-screen text with word count, visual description, 2-color palette, and complete speaker note. Before executing, reformulate topic, audience, and duration and present your narrative arc plan. If {{ADJUNTOS}} indicates missing material or if any data is empty, ask before continuing. Close with the verified checklist: 10 words max, 1 idea, complete notes, hard cut.

prompts.title: Visual self-contained HTML dashboard
prompts.content: Act as a Full-Stack Data Visualizer with experience in self-contained HTML dashboards for executive reports and offline presentations. Generate a single HTML file, offline, printable, and shareable by email, with zero external dependencies (no CDN, remote fonts, or third-party JS), from these inputs: DATA to visualize = {{DATOS}}; AUDIENCE who will see it = {{AUDIENCIA}}; BRAND optional (colors and fonts) = {{MARCA}}; ATTACHMENTS = {{ADJUNTOS}}. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret {{DATOS}} and {{AUDIENCIA}}, plan the visual hierarchy, and present your plan before executing. Structure in four layers: (1) Main KPIs as large numbers at the top, without scrolling, with label and delta vs. previous period when the data exists; (2) charts in pure CSS or inline SVG (bars, lines, pie) with titles and legends; (3) responsive and scannable tables; (4) three to five insights that explain the why, not just the what. Mandatory technique: everything inline (CSS in style tag, embedded SVG, system fonts or base64 if {{MARCA}} requires it), @media print included, accessible palette (AA contrast), responsive desktop/tablet/mobile with a single stylesheet. Edge cases: missing data = dash plus note, no inventing; single-point series = no trend; extensive table = paginate or summarize. Deliver a single valid .html file plus a note on how to customize colors and data. If {{DATOS}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{MARCA}} are missing and essential, ask for them before generating.

prompts.title: Visual before after transformation
Visual concept mind map
prompts.content: Act as a Knowledge Architect expert in knowledge visualization. Build a mind map of the concept {{CONCEPTO}} oriented toward the purpose {{PROPOSITO}} (study, plan, or communicate), drawing on {{ADJUNTOS}} if reference material is available. Before executing, reformulate what you understand about the concept and present your plan; if {{CONCEPTO}} or {{PROPOSITO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them. Deliver: central node in a maximum of 3 words; 5-7 MECE Level 1 branches; Level 2 sub-topics per branch; maximum 3 levels; explicit cross-links between branches; one color family per branch. Produce valid Mermaid mindmap code and, below it, an indented text version for XMind. Close with 2-3 insights from the cross-links and flag gaps with {to_confirm}. Tone: visual-analytical, neutral professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Visual icon system coherente
prompts.content:
Act as a senior UI/Icon Designer specialized in iconography systems for digital products and corporate documentation. Design a coherent and auditable icon system for {{PROYECTO}}, valid both in interfaces and in presentations or documents, with a style preference of {{ESTILO}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{PROYECTO}} or {{ESTILO}} are not enough to decide, ask me before proceeding; also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as reference.

Deliverables: (1) single style decision (outlined, filled, or duotone) with justification and trade-off against the discarded alternatives; (2) grid: base size (24 or 32 px), live area or keyline, stroke weight, corner radius, and minimum legible size; (3) catalog of at least 20 icons, one per key concept of {{PROYECTO}}, with name, concept, and semantic note; (4) English, kebab-case naming convention with explicit rule for states, variants, and synonyms; (5) recommended library (Lucide, Phosphor, Heroicons, or custom) with the selection criterion and a plan for missing icons; (6) usage guide: when to use each icon, pairs that are easily confused, and icon-label pairing rules.

Method: consistency over creativity; semantic clarity without a label; same grid for all; 5-second recognition test. Edge cases: abstract concepts with no metaphor, confusable icons, densities and light/dark themes, accessibility (contrast, minimum touch size, do not depend on color alone). Explicitly mark as assumption everything you infer and close with verifiable acceptance criteria.

Variables: {{PROYECTO}} = project or product; {{ESTILO}} = optional preferred style (outlined, filled, duotone); {{ADJUNTOS}} = files, reference URLs, or "No attachments".

Format: icon catalog + style guide + source library, in a technical-visual tone, so that design or development can implement it directly.

prompts.title: Agentes gemini gem especializado
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Gemini Gems designer with experience in configuring specialized assistants for enterprise productivity.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate the function and audience you understand, declare assumptions about scope and sources, and present your plan before drafting the Gem.

Context:
- Main function of the Gem: {{FUNCION}}
- Audience that will use the Gem: {{AUDIENCIA}}
- Knowledge sources (documents or URLs, or "No sources"): {{SOURCES}}
- Attachments (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"): {{ADJUNTOS}}

Design the complete configuration of the Gemini Gem:
1. Name and personality (tone, style, persona in one line).
2. System instructions with explicit scope: what it does and what it does NOT do (boundaries and out-of-scope topics).
3. Knowledge sources: what documents or URLs feed the Gem and how they are cited; if {{SOURCES}} is "No sources", declare that it operates on general knowledge and mark the limit.
4. Default response format (structure, length, language).
5. Edge case handling: out-of-scope query, missing or contradictory source, ambiguous request.
6. Five examples of ideal interactions (user input and expected response).
7. Test plan: ten queries covering the happy path, scope limits, and edge cases, each with the expected result as the acceptance criterion.

Method: scope-first, knowledge-grounded, personality calibration, test-before-publish.

Deliver in neutral professional Spanish, technical tone, for the Gem creator. Close with a verification checklist ready to use when creating the Gem in Gemini. If {{FUNCION}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{SOURCES}} are missing, ask before continuing.

prompts.title: Agentes notebooklm cuaderno
prompts.content:
Act as a senior NotebookLM Producer with experience in curating notebooks for research, education, and content production. I need to design a notebook on {{TEMA}} that works as a queryable knowledge base and multimedia content engine.

Context:
- Topic: {{TEMA}}
- Available sources: {{FUENTES}}
- Required outputs: {{OUTPUTS}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, reformulate {{TEMA}} and the objectives you understand, declare assumptions, and present your plan; do not execute without that validation. If {{FUENTES}}, {{OUTPUTS}}, or {{ADJUNTOS}} are incomplete or ambiguous, ask specifically before proceeding.

Deliverables:
1. Notebook objective: 5 to 8 concrete questions it must answer about {{TEMA}}, along with what is out of scope.
2. Curation of {{FUENTES}}: intentional selection, not a dump; practical limit of 50, quality over quantity; for each source, mark why it is included and its confidence level.
3. Organization: source naming convention for traceability.
4. Chat prompts: 3 to 5 structured queries that require citations and separate facts from inferences.
5. Multimedia outputs: pipeline sources > chat > {{OUTPUTS}}, with the angle and audience for each output.
6. Maintenance: criteria for adding, refreshing, or removing sources and a cadence.

Method: input quality = output quality; specific queries yield better results; every statement traceable to a source.

Edge cases: contradictory sources (make the conflict explicit), undated or low-authority sources (downgrade them), {{TEMA}} broader than {{FUENTES}} (narrow the objective).

Format: notebook plan + source table + chat prompts ready to paste. Practical tone, neutral professional Spanish. Close by creating the notebook with the first 10 curated sources and their naming applied.

prompts.title: Agentes text expander biblioteca
prompts.content:
Act as a Productivity Engineer expert in configuring text expanders for high-performance AI workflows. I need to configure {{HERRAMIENTA}} to have instant access to my prompt library, synchronized on {{DISPOSITIVOS}}. References: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first reformulate what you understand about my situation and present your action plan; do not execute without confirming first. If {{HERRAMIENTA}} or {{DISPOSITIVOS}} are empty or ambiguous, ask me before proceeding.

Deliver: (1) confirmation or recommendation of {{HERRAMIENTA}} with justification based on my case, contrasting open-source vs. commercial alternatives without mentioning monetary amounts; (2) trigger naming convention prefix + category + action (e.g., ;prod-ritual) with anti-collision rule; (3) the most frequently used snippets configured, the most used first rather than the entire library; (4) fill-in fields for variable parameters, with tab order; (5) organization into folders or groups by category; (6) synchronization guide for {{DISPOSITIVOS}} according to the mechanism of {{HERRAMIENTA}}; (7) periodic review routine. Mark explicit assumptions when data is missing and point out the limits of each tool. Step-by-step technical tone. Close: have the first snippets installed and verified today.

prompts.title: Agentes priming contexto sesion
Agentes workflow multimodelo
prompts.content:
Act as an AI Workflow Architect expert in multi-model orchestration and LLM selection by task. Design a workflow that assigns each type of task to the model with the greatest strength and connects the steps with clean handoffs.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If a key piece of data is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Context:
- Frequent AI tasks: {{TAREAS}}
- Models and tools with access: {{MODELOS}}
- Usage restriction or budget (optional): {{PRESUPUESTO}}
- Attachments or references: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Produce:
1. Inventory of {{TAREAS}} classified by type: creation, analysis, live search, coding, deep reasoning, visual or document processing.
2. Model-task matrix for {{MODELOS}}: dominant strength of each model, task where it is optimal, and one line of justification per assignment.
3. Handoffs: how the output of one model passes to the next (expected format, what to clean up or reformat, input prompt of the receiving model).
4. Selection criteria by intensity considering {{PRESUPUESTO}}: when a lightweight model is sufficient and when a higher-capacity one is justified. Without citing amounts.
5. Step-by-step diagrammed workflow: which model at which moment and the human verification checkpoint.

Explicit assumptions when information is missing, design limits, and one edge case (unavailable model or low-quality output). Close with verifiable acceptance criteria.

Format: diagrammed workflow + model-task matrix + handoff guide. Technical-strategic tone. Audience: professional who uses multiple AIs. Action: implementable this week.

prompts.title: Agentes quality rubric outputs
Stack auditar herramientas personal
prompts.content:
Act as a Digital Productivity Consultant expert in stack optimization for independent professionals and remote teams. I am going to audit my toolset to eliminate redundancies: the average professional pays for eight tools and uses three; the other five are silent waste.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before auditing, reformulate what you understand about my situation and present your plan; if a critical piece of data is missing, ask me for it instead of assuming.

Data:
- Tools I use: {{HERRAMIENTAS}}
- Current recurring spend (optional): {{PRESUPUESTO}}
- Frequency or context of use (optional): {{FRECUENCIA_USO}}
- Attachments (files, URLs, or "No attachments"): {{ADJUNTOS}}

Conduct this stack audit:
1. Complete inventory: tool, function category, recurring cost, actual frequency of use, unique value provided.
2. Classification: essential, useful, redundant, or abandoned, with an explicit criterion.
3. Overlap map: which tools cover the same function and which one wins.
4. Optimal consolidated stack: minimum viable, one solid tool per function.
5. Migration plan: export data, retrain habits, deactivate without losing information.
6. Estimated savings: recurring spend freed up plus management hours and context-switching recovered.

Method: inventory first; actual frequency, not perceived; total cost (license plus learning plus maintenance). Weigh switching costs and lock-in before recommending migration. Analytical tone. Close with the first redundant tool to deactivate and the data point that triggers the decision.

prompts.title: Stack seleccionar herramienta
Stack integraciones mapa
Semi-automatic productive ritual automation
prompts.content: Act as an Automated Ritual Designer with experience in behavioural design and personal automation. Convert the ritual {{RITUAL}} into a semi-automated flow that reduces friction and ensures consistency, with the human in the decision loop. Before proposing anything, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate the ritual, declare assumptions, and present your plan; do not execute without that step. Proceed as follows: (1) map {{RITUAL}} with steps, estimated time per step, and friction points, prioritizing {{FRICCIONES}}; (2) classify each step as automatable, assistable, or human-required, with justification; (3) design a concrete trigger per automatable step (event, schedule, condition) and name the tool or mechanism; (4) define a fallback per automation so that, if it fails, the ritual continues manually (graceful degradation); (5) define before-vs-after metrics in total time, consistency (% completion), and cognitive load. Apply friction-first to {{FRICCIONES}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. Limits: do not automate steps that require human judgment; mark them as human-required. Deliver ritual map + automation table (trigger + fallback) + metrics table, and recommend the single point to automate first. If {{RITUAL}} or {{FRICCIONES}} are missing, ask for them before continuing. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. Variables: {{RITUAL}}, {{FRICCIONES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Zapier Make automation recipe
prompts.content: Act as an Automation Specialist with experience in Zapier and Make for marketing, sales, and operations processes. Design an automation recipe ready to implement for the process {{PROCESO}} on the platform {{PLATAFORMA}} using the apps {{APPS}}; consider the material in {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, reformulate what you understand and present your plan; if any data is missing, ask for it. Then deliver: 1) Trigger with event and source app. 2) Filters with conditions that continue or stop the flow and their reason. 3) Actions in numbered sequential steps, with the app and operation of each one. 4) Data transformations between steps with the mapping of key fields. 5) Error handling: what happens if a step fails, retries, and notification. 6) Test plan with real data before production. 7) Estimate of operations or tasks per execution to size consumption. Start simple, maximum 3 steps, and indicate how to iterate. Mark explicit assumptions and limits. Deliver a step-by-step recipe, technical tone, for someone configuring their first automation who must have it running today.

prompts.title: Private corporate assistant engine
prompts.content:
Act as a Corporate AI Architect with experience deploying private assistants with RAG (retrieval augmented generation) in organizations of 50 to 5,000 employees. Design the complete blueprint of a private corporate assistant for {{ORGANIZACION}}: the organization's own ChatGPT, fed with its internal knowledge.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, reformulate what you understand about the assignment and present your action plan. If any critical data is missing, ask for it before proceeding.

Context:
- Organization: {{ORGANIZACION}} (type and size)
- Expected scope: {{SCOPE}} (what the assistant should be able to answer)
- Available knowledge sources: {{FUENTES}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Deliver these seven blocks:
1. Scope: what questions it answers and what falls out of scope in the initial version.
2. Knowledge base: documents, wikis, and processes to ingest; prioritization by frequency and value; handling of contradictory or outdated sources; re-indexing cadence.
3. Access: roles and permissions; segmentation of sensitive information by audience; query traceability.
4. Personality: tone, format, interaction rules, and the obligation to cite the retrieved source.
5. Security by design: what it CANNOT reveal, PII handling, leakage prevention, and response to adversarial prompts.
6. Adoption metrics: usage, coverage, satisfaction, and rate of responses with a verifiable source.
7. Iteration plan: improvement loop with real feedback and detection of knowledge gaps.

Method: RAG architecture anchored to sources; security by design; focus on adoption; iterative improvement. Declare explicit assumptions and name edge cases (hallucination without source, out-of-scope query, outdated data, improper access to segmented information).

Output format: spec + knowledge base plan + security design + metrics dashboard + iteration plan. Technical-strategic tone. Audience: IT or innovation team. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria and the first executable step: define the scope and start curating the knowledge base.

prompts.title: Sales qualification chatbot engine
prompts.content: You are a Sales Operations Architect with experience in qualification chatbots for high-volume B2B pipelines. Design a chatbot that qualifies leads for {{PRODUCTO}} targeting the profile {{ICP}}, integrating with {{CRM}}, before passing them to sales. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as additional context. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate what you understand and present your action plan; do not act without first interpreting and planning. Deliver: (1) qualification questions by BANT (Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline) written conversationally; (2) flow as a decision tree with branches by response and handling of evasive or incomplete responses; (3) scoring model with points per response, weight per dimension, and an explicit qualified/nurturing threshold; (4) handoff rules to sales, to nurturing, and to disqualification; (5) registration schema in {{CRM}} (fields, events, sync timing); (6) bot personality: tone, style, and response speed. Apply progressive qualification. Declare explicit assumptions about {{PRODUCTO}}, {{ICP}}, or {{CRM}} when context is missing, and ask only for data that blocks the design. Close with an acceptance checklist. Variables: {{PRODUCTO}}, {{ICP}}, {{CRM}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Investor pitch deck presentation
prompts.content:
Act as a Startup Advisor with a proven track record building pitch decks that close rounds from seed to Series C in LatAm and the USA. Your job is not to summarize the business: it is to build an evidence-backed opportunity narrative that moves an investor to a follow-up meeting.

Before producing anything, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what I am asking, Plan the approach, and only then Execute. If any key data is missing, ask for it in a single batch; do not invent figures or sources.

Data:
- STARTUP: {{STARTUP}} (your startup or project and what it does)
- RONDA: {{RONDA}} (round type: seed, Series A, etc., and target amount if you have it)
- METRICAS: {{METRICAS}} (current traction metrics with period)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

Deliver a pitch deck of maximum 12 slides in Sequoia format, in this order: 1) Problem (quantified), 2) Solution in one sentence, 3) Market TAM/SAM/SOM with sources, 4) Product (demo or screenshots), 5) Traction (real numbers and period), 6) Business model (revenue and unit economics if they exist), 7) Competition and defensible advantage, 8) Team (why THIS team), 9) Ask (amount, use of funds, runway it buys). Each slide with an affirmative title, concise content, and speaker note.

Principles: show don't tell (charts over text), traction rules, and respect the investor's time (12 slides max). Mark assumptions and data without a source as pending validation. Confident, data-driven tone. Close with checklist: quantified problem, market with source, numeric traction, clear ask, and coherent narrative.

prompts.title: Professional escalation communication
Positive feedback communication for reinforcement
prompts.content: Act as a Team Development Coach expert in positive reinforcement and recognition culture in high-performance organizations. I want to recognize {{PERSONA}} for {{COMPORTAMIENTO}} (observable facts, not interpretations), whose positive impact was {{IMPACTO}}. Consider these support materials: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before drafting, reformulate what you understand and present your plan; if any data is missing or vague, ask for it instead of inventing it. Build a positive feedback script in five blocks: Situation (when and where), Behavior ({{COMPORTAMIENTO}} in observable terms), Impact ({{IMPACTO}}, quantified or concrete), Reinforcement (why I want it repeated), and Connection (to the team or organization's values). Keep it specific, genuine, and timely. Recommend private or public channel based on the case and warn if the message is diluted by mixing it with a criticism. Deliver the script in neutral, professional Spanish, without prices or emojis, plus a brief note on how to deliver it.

prompts.title: 5-minute rapid decision framework
prompts.content:
Act as a Decision Coach expert in rapid decision frameworks for executives and entrepreneurs. Your goal: resolve a reversible decision in less than 5 minutes without analysis paralysis, given that 80 percent of professional decisions require no more.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first reformulate the decision and the context, then present your evaluation plan, and only then execute.

Decision to resolve: {{DECISION}}
Relevant context: {{CONTEXTO}}
Attachments or references: {{ADJUNTOS}}

5-minute process:
1. Classify: reversible (Bezos Type 2, two-way door) or irreversible (Type 1)? If irreversible or of high systemic impact, stop and recommend extended analysis.
2. Realistic worst case: is it tolerable? If not, escalate the analysis.
3. Sufficiency: is there at least 70 percent of information? 100 percent never comes.
4. Cost of not deciding today.
5. Regret minimization: which option would I most regret NOT having taken.

If {{DECISION}} or {{CONTEXTO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing; do not invent data.

Deliver: decision in one line + one main reason + immediate next action with responsible party and deadline + brief record of the reasoning. Direct tone, professional Spanish. Indicate if the decision does NOT qualify for rapid mode.

prompts.title: Weighted decision matrix
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Decision Analyst with experience in MCDA (Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis) applied to investments and strategy. Build a weighted decision matrix to choose among {{OPCIONES}} evaluated according to {{CRITERIOS}}, considering {{CONTEXTO_DECISION}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the context (what is being decided, who decides, constraints, horizon), plan the evaluation approach, and only then execute. If {{OPCIONES}}, {{CRITERIOS}}, or {{CONTEXTO_DECISION}} are incomplete, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent alternatives or weights.

Method: (1) List 3 to 5 options from {{OPCIONES}}; if there are more, filter by minimum non-negotiables and document the discard. (2) Refine {{CRITERIOS}} to 5 to 8 mutually independent factors. (3) Assign weights that add up to 100 percent, separating weighting from scoring. (4) Score each option by criterion on a 1 to 5 scale with a brief rubric per level. (5) Calculate weighted score per cell and total per option. (6) Rank the results. (7) Sensitivity analysis: identify the weight whose reasonable variation changes the winner and declare robustness or fragility.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Declare assumptions, source of each score, and limits; mark as estimated any score without a firm data point.

Deliver: decision table with weights/scores/weighted values, ranking, sensitivity analysis, assumptions, and actionable recommendation with its break condition. Analytical and professional tone, no emojis. Audience: decision team.

Variables: {{OPCIONES}} alternatives to compare; {{CRITERIOS}} evaluation factors; {{CONTEXTO_DECISION}} what is being decided, who decides, constraints, and horizon; {{ADJUNTOS}} files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Leadership difficult conversation
Effective leadership one on one
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Leadership Coach specialized in developing managers at hypergrowth technology companies. I need to conduct one-on-ones that develop people, not just review tasks.

Context:
- Team: {{EQUIPO}} (team size and profile)
- Current 1:1 frequency: {{FRECUENCIA}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{EQUIPO}} or {{FRECUENCIA}} arrive empty, ask me for them before proceeding.

Design a 1:1 system with these pillars:
1. Reportee's agenda: 70 percent is defined by the person.
2. Genuine wellbeing check-in, not a protocol one.
3. Progress: what have you achieved, what is blocking you.
4. Development: what are you learning, what do you need, where do you want to grow.
5. Bidirectional feedback: what can I do better as a leader.
6. Close: one concrete action per person, with owner and date.
7. Base cadence: weekly 30 minutes; never downgrade to monthly 2 hours.

Method: the 1:1 is FOR the person; ask more than instruct; career conversations, not just tasks; follow through on commitments. Adapt the cadence and script to the size/profile of {{EQUIPO}} and correct the anti-patterns you detect in {{FRECUENCIA}}. Deliverable: reusable template, question bank by pillar, recommended cadence and the script for the next 1:1. Human and coaching tone.

prompts.title: Feynman learning explain
prompts.content: I want to master {{CONCEPTO}} by applying the Feynman Technique: if I can't explain it simply, I don't understand it. My current level is {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Act as an educator and simplifier with Richard Feynman's philosophy, where complexity reveals a lack of understanding. Before executing, reformulate {{CONCEPTO}} in your own words and present your plan. Then: explain it as if I were 12 years old without jargon; explicitly mark every point where the explanation becomes blurry or where you hide behind a technical term (that's the comprehension gap); close each gap with the exact definition that was missing; create one or two analogies that anchor the abstract in something everyday and declare where each analogy stops applying. Deliver three levels: simple (12 years old), intermediate (field colleague) and deep (expert, with nuances and exceptions), calibrating the starting point according to {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}}. Close with a concept map: prerequisites, sibling concepts and applications. If {{CONCEPTO}} or {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} are not clear, ask for them before starting. Flag what remains uncertain rather than filling it in. Pedagogical and clear tone, in neutral Spanish.

prompts.title: Learning 90-day competence plan
prompts.content: Act as a senior Learning Designer specialized in accelerated upskilling programs for professionals. Design a 90-day plan (12 weeks) to go from {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} to operational in {{COMPETENCIA}}, with {{HORAS_SEMANALES}} weekly hours available. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context or constraint. First reformulate target competence, current level and hours, and present your plan before executing; if any data is missing, ask me. Apply the 70-20-10 model (70 deliberate practice, 20 mentors and peers, 10 theory) and project-based learning: you learn by doing, not by accumulating content. Deliverable: 1) competence {{COMPETENCIA}} with objective level in observable behaviors by day 90; 2) curated and justified resources, not a link dump: up to three books, up to five courses or programs, up to three reference practitioners, each with its rationale according to {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}}; 3) progression for all 12 weeks sized to {{HORAS_SEMANALES}}, with one verifiable milestone per week; 4) at least three real projects with a deliverable and definition of done, never toy exercises; 5) accountability with progress metric and alarm signal; 6) two fortnightly reviews scheduled to recalibrate. Declare explicit assumptions and limits. Flag missing data as pending. Close with the week 1 action to start today. Motivating and structured tone, neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Negotiation prepare conversation
Creativity SCAMPER innovate
prompts.content: Act as an Innovation Facilitator with experience in Design Thinking and ideation workshops for product teams. Apply the 7 SCAMPER techniques to {{OBJETO}} considering {{RESTRICCIONES}} and reviewing {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, reformulate what {{OBJETO}} is and under what constraints we are working, and present your plan; if {{OBJETO}}, {{RESTRICCIONES}} or the usage context are missing or ambiguous, ask me before inventing. Go through the seven techniques in order with at least 3 distinct ideas each: Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify or Magnify, Put to another use, Eliminate and Rearrange or Reverse. Mark at least one non-obvious idea per technique and use cross-pollination between techniques. Close with a top 5 prioritized by viability times impact, each idea with one line of justification, and a first prototype step for idea number 1. Creative-structured tone for innovator or product team.

prompts.title: Wellbeing anti-burnout protocol
prompts.content:
Act as an Executive Wellbeing Coach specialized in burnout prevention and energy management for high-performance professionals. Burnout is a silent accumulation that is detected and prevented before the collapse. Design a personal anti-burnout protocol for someone whose role is {{ROL}}, whose main declared drains are {{DRAINS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver:
1. Early warning indicators: 5 personal and observable signals (behavioral, physical, cognitive, relational), each with its concrete threshold that triggers action.
2. Energy map: start from {{DRAINS}} for the 3 main drains and propose 3 plausible recharges for role {{ROL}}, with frequency and energy cost/benefit.
3. Non-negotiable limits: 3 to 5 specific boundaries aligned to the role, each with its exception rule.
4. Recovery protocol: actions executable in less than 24 hours, in three levels (green-yellow-red).
5. Weekly check-in: 3 self-diagnosis questions (less than 2 minutes) with escalation criteria.

Consider attachments {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context (calendar, history, evaluations). Method: prevention over recovery; personal signals over generic ones; energy over time; protect limits before you need them. If {{ROL}} or {{DRAINS}} are not clear, ask before inventing them.

Format: one-page protocol + weekly check-in table + tiered recovery plan. Serene and compassionate tone. Close inviting the first check-in today. Clarification: self-management protocol, does not replace clinical care; sustained red refers to professional support.

Variables: {{ROL}} = professional role; {{DRAINS}} = the 3 things that drain you the most; {{ADJUNTOS}} = attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Strategy vision 3 horizons
Strategy quarterly personal OKR
Meta reverse engineer conversation
prompts.content:
Act as a Meta-Prompt Engineer expert in extracting reusable patterns from AI conversations. Convert session {{SESION}} into a permanent shortcut: two prompts ready for my text expander. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. If the history, objective or attachments are missing, ask me before continuing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Proceed as follows: (1) analyze {{SESION}} and identify real objective, key inputs, decisions and format of the final deliverable; (2) extract the generalizable pattern (task type, method that worked, sequence of steps) separating it from the specific content; (3) generate PROMPT A for priming, maximum 200 words, with context, role, constraints and completion criterion; (4) generate PROMPT B in full SPEC format with [inputs], [prompt] S-P-E-C, checklist and deliverable; (5) parameterize both with self-descriptive {{UPPERCASE}} variables to reuse in different contexts.

Assumptions: I work with text, not live execution; if the session is very short I flag it as a limit. Edge case: if {{SESION}} mixes several tasks, separate a SPEC per task or ask which one to prioritize. Deliver the two prompts in separate blocks, in neutral Spanish and technical tone, ready to copy. Close by confirming that the SPEC reproduces results comparable to the original case.

prompts.title: Meta audit my prompts
prompts.content: Act as a senior Prompt Quality Auditor, expert in evaluating and improving prompt libraries. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first reformulate what you understand and present your plan; do not execute until my confirmation or, if I don't respond, assume the most reasonable assumption and make it explicit. Inputs: PROMPTS = {{PROMPTS}} (my most-used prompts or, if I don't have them, a description of my repeated AI tasks), CANTIDAD = {{CANTIDAD}} (how many prompts to audit, default 10), CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION = {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} (usage frequency, impact on my work, or both), ADJUNTOS = {{ADJUNTOS}}. Audit as follows: 1) list the prompts and mark those you reconstructed from my description; 2) score 1 to 10 each SPEC dimension (Situation, Request, Execution, Criterion) with one line of evidence citing the text; 3) calculate gap = potential minus actual weighted by {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} and apply 80/20 to choose the 3 with the highest return; 4) rewrite those 3 to full SPEC standard; 5) deliver before/after side by side showing what changed and why it's better. Close with adoption plan (what to replace in text expander) and a suggested A/B test. Limits: do not invent usage that I haven't stated, mark assumptions with the label assumption, do not inflate changes in prompts that are already solid. If an essential input is missing, ask for it before proceeding.

prompts.title: Meta create agent system prompt
prompts.content:
Act as a senior AI Agent Architect, expert in designing autonomous agents with guardrails for enterprise operations. You will produce the system prompt (the constitution) of the agent: {{AGENTE}} (name and function).

Input data:
- Agent: {{AGENTE}} (agent name and function)
- Audience: {{AUDIENCIA}} (who will use the agent)
- Autonomy: {{AUTONOMIA}} (semi, high, or total)
- High-risk / irreversible actions it may touch: {{ACCIONES_RIESGO}} (e.g. move money, send emails to clients, delete data; if not applicable, state "none")
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate in two or three lines the agent you understood from {{AGENTE}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{AUTONOMIA}}, and present your plan before drafting. If any essential data is missing, ask for it; do not invent capabilities or domains.

Principles: constitution first (limits and guardrails before capabilities); the level of {{AUTONOMIA}} governs the severity of guardrails and escalation; few-shot over instruction; adversarial testing before closing.

Deliver the complete system prompt ready to copy, with: 1) Identity (name, role, personality, calibrated tone); 2) Capabilities (positive scope); 3) Boundaries (negative scope, non-negotiable); 4) Knowledge (sources and what to do without data, no hallucination); 5) Interaction protocol; 6) Output format; 7) Guardrails (safety, ethics, PII); 8) Escalation (concrete triggers to human based on {{ACCIONES_RIESGO}} and {{AUTONOMIA}}); 9) five few-shot examples of real use, with at least one case to reject and one to escalate.

Close with an adversarial test table (attack > expected result) and the design assumptions and trade-offs. Neutral Spanish, technical tone for {{AUDIENCIA}}. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every decision made without confirmed data.

prompts.title: Meta taxonomy prompts organize
prompts.content: Act as a senior Information Architect specializing in content taxonomies and classification systems for digital libraries. Your task is to design a taxonomy that organizes {{BIBLIOTECA}} in a navigable and scalable way, considering an approximate volume of {{TAMANO}} prompts. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan your approach, and only then Execute. If any relevant data is missing, ask for it before continuing. Also consider these inputs: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver: 1) Main categories (maximum 10 per domain, MECE). 2) Sub-categories (maximum 5 per category, maximum 2 levels of depth). 3) Cross-cutting tags: difficulty, output type, and recommended model. 4) Consistent naming convention for keys. 5) Per-prompt metadata schema: category, tags, parameter count, and estimated tokens. 6) Navigation guide that leads a new user to the correct prompt in fewer than three decisions. 7) Migration plan to reassign existing prompts and resolve those that do not fit. Method: organize by what the user searches for, not by how it was created; favor flat over deep; validate that it scales from one hundred to one thousand prompts. Declare assumptions, limits, and edge cases (duplicates, multi-domain, no clear category). Systematic tone, neutral and professional Spanish, directed at the library curator.

prompts.title: Research bibliometric analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a senior bibliometrician with experience in scientific production analysis, citation networks, and knowledge frontier mapping. Map the academic landscape of {{CAMPO}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Variables:
- {{CAMPO}}: field or research topic to map.
- {{PERIODO}}: analysis time window (last 5, 10, or 20 years).
- {{PROPOSITO}}: what it will be used for (thesis state-of-the-art, technology watch, R&D investment decision).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: files, URLs, or reference corpus; use "No attachments" if none.

If {{CAMPO}}, {{PERIODO}}, or {{PROPOSITO}} are missing, ask for them before continuing; do not invent data.

Deliver: (1) volume by year and trend; (2) top authors and collaboration networks; (3) top journals and conferences; (4) keyword co-occurrence and emerging topics; (5) most influential papers by citation count; (6) research gaps as concrete opportunities. Apply co-citation analysis, keyword emergence, and white spaces.

Declare the assumed bibliographic base and its coverage and language bias. Separate evidence from inference and mark unconfirmable metrics with [to be confirmed]. Academic-strategic tone.

prompts.title: Writing procedures manual
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Technical Writer with experience documenting processes for ISO 9001 and operations teams. Document the procedure {{PROCEDIMIENTO}} so that {{AUDIENCIA}} can execute it without ambiguity: the best manual is the one that requires no additional explanation. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as evidence reference. First reformulate the procedure as you understand it and present your plan; do not execute without first confirming the interpretation. If {{PROCEDIMIENTO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{ADJUNTOS}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before drafting. Deliver: 1) title, version, and date; 2) purpose (why it exists); 3) scope (when it applies and when it does NOT); 4) prerequisites (access, permissions, tools, prior data); 5) numbered steps with a single action per step, in imperative form, with a visible expected result; 6) explicit decision points (if X then step Y, if not step Z); 7) screenshot or diagram markers where text is not enough; 8) troubleshooting with the 5 most common problems, their symptom, cause, and solution; 9) the person responsible for updating it and the review cadence. Rules: one action per step, show before describing, write at the level of {{AUDIENCIA}} assuming zero prior context, and record each change with date and responsible party. Mark as pending any unconfirmed data instead of inventing it. Close with a manual ready to publish and test with someone new.

prompts.title: Data pivot table analysis
Data anomaly detection manual
prompts.content:
Act as an expert in Applied Statistics with experience in anomaly detection for fraud, data quality, and operational analysis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I want to detect anomalies and outliers in {{DATASET}} without complex tools, understanding that an outlier is either an error to clean or an insight to investigate.

Variables to analyze: {{VARIABLES}}.
Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

If the dataset description, variables, sample size, or reference files are missing, ask me before proceeding; do not invent data.

Execute as follows:
1. Define the baseline of 'normal' per variable: expected range, distribution, and unit. If the sample is smaller than 30 records or the distribution is highly skewed, declare it as a limitation because Z-score and IQR lose reliability.
2. Apply detection methods: Z-score greater than 3 and IQR times 1.5; describe the expected boxplot and use scatter to contextualize.
3. Classify each anomaly: data error, real event, or potential fraud; mark ambiguous cases.
4. Investigate the root cause of each anomaly with the most likely hypothesis.
5. Decide on action per anomaly: clean, keep, or escalate, with justification.
6. Define automatic alert criteria: threshold, variable, and trigger.

Remember that what is statistically anomalous may be normal in the domain: contrast each finding against business knowledge before concluding.

Deliver: list of anomalies with classification, cause, and action; alert threshold table; and a note on sample limitations. Analytical tone for a data analyst. Indicate as a next step to investigate the 'real event' type anomalies.

prompts.title: Data storytelling presentation
prompts.content:
Act as a Data Storytelling Expert with experience in data-driven presentations for C-levels and boards. Convert {{DATOS}} into a presentation where the numbers tell a story that persuades {{AUDIENCIA}} and moves it to take {{DECISION}}: data without narrative is ignored. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any essential data is missing, ask me before proceeding.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver a presentation outline with: (1) main insight in 1 sentence; (2) narrative arc context > discovery > implication > action; (3) 3-5 protagonist figures that support the story; (4) one visualization per insight with the optimal chart type and its key annotation; (5) comparisons that provide context (benchmark, before/after, projection); (6) call to action that names {{DECISION}} and the cost of not deciding.

Variables:
- {{DATOS}}: data or findings to present
- {{AUDIENCIA}}: who views the presentation
- {{DECISION}}: what decision must be made
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

Method: start with the insight, not the data; one chart tells one thing; every chart carries an annotation; each slide answers 'and what does this mean for us'. Mark with [assumption] any inferred figures and indicate the data limit (sample, date, bias). Close when the insight fits in one sentence, each visualization is annotated, the comparisons provide context, and the CTA is actionable.

prompts.title: Data basic sql query
prompts.content: Act as a Data Analyst who teaches SQL to non-technical professionals. Business question: {{PREGUNTA}}. Available schema (tables, columns, types): {{TABLAS}}. Database engine: {{MOTOR}} (if it says 'unknown', use standard ANSI SQL and let me know). Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. First reformulate {{PREGUNTA}} in a precise sentence and declare your assumptions; if a key column is missing from {{TABLAS}}, ask me before writing SQL. Build the query incrementally (SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT). Deliver: final commented query, line-by-line explanation, verification query (count/sample), and two or three related variants. Handle NULL, case sensitivity, dates, and duplicates; warn if there is risk of a full-table scan or too many rows. Do not invent columns outside {{TABLAS}}.

prompts.title: Agents prompt testing framework
Agents migrate gpt to gem
prompts.content: Act as a senior Cross-Platform AI Architect with experience porting agents between ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and other platforms. Migrate the agent {{AGENTE_ORIGINAL}} to {{PLATAFORMA_DESTINO}}, preserving functionality and personality; consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of those data points are missing, ask for them before starting. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Execute in six steps: 1) Extract scope, personality, hard rules, output format, and tools from {{AGENTE_ORIGINAL}}; 2) Map equivalences toward {{PLATAFORMA_DESTINO}} (instructions vs. system prompt, maximum length, tools/actions, retrieval, memory); 3) Adapt syntax, limits, and capabilities, marking what has no direct equivalent; 4) Migrate or recreate the knowledge base from {{ADJUNTOS}} and note what does not port automatically; 5) Run 10 representative queries on both source and target; 6) Compare outputs with a 1-5 scoring for tone fidelity, accuracy, and format. Assumptions: if there is no access to the source agent, work on the provided instructions and declare it. Limits: do not invent capabilities that {{PLATAFORMA_DESTINO}} does not support; gaps are documented. Deliver: migration guide, mapping table, results of the 10 parity tests, and a differences register with mitigation. Technical tone, neutral Spanish.

prompts.title: Agents monitor performance
Agents document assistant
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Technical Writer for AI products, with experience documenting agents for both end users and administrators.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need you to document the agent {{AGENTE}} for the audience {{AUDIENCIA}}, so that anyone can understand, use and maintain it without depending on the creator. Documentation is the agent's continuity insurance: without it, the agent dies when its author leaves. Reference material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Produce six blocks:
1. Technical profile: name, platform, scope (what it does and what it does NOT do), current owner, version and date of last update.
2. User guide calibrated to {{AUDIENCIA}}: what it is for, how to invoke it step by step, 2–3 real examples of input and output, and common errors with their solution.
3. Administrator guide: how to modify it, how to update it safely, how to roll back, troubleshooting of typical failures and how to test before publishing.
4. Documented system prompt: the complete prompt, with an annotation of each section and the reason for each instruction (why it is there, what happens if it is removed).
5. FAQ: 10 real questions that {{AUDIENCIA}} asks, with direct answers.
6. Changelog: change history with date, author and reason, plus current version status.

Method: prioritize the user guide; show with examples before explaining with paragraphs; treat the admin guide as a survival condition; keep the document as a living doc.

If {{AGENTE}}, {{AUDIENCIA}} or {{ADJUNTOS}} are not enough to verify capabilities or the system prompt, ask before inventing; mark everything assumed as {to_confirm}. Close when a new administrator can maintain the agent by reading only the document.

Deliverable: complete documentation ready to publish. Clear and accessible tone, neutral and professional English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Agents curate knowledge sources
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Knowledge Curator with experience selecting sources for RAG and corporate knowledge bases. You are going to curate the sources that will feed the agent {{AGENTE}} in the domain {{DOMINIO}}, starting from the principle garbage in = garbage out: the quality of the agent never exceeds the quality of its sources.

Candidate sources and reference material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what {{AGENTE}} is, the scope of {{DOMINIO}} and what {{ADJUNTOS}} covers; present your curation plan before executing. If {{ADJUNTOS}} is "No attachments" or the pool of sources is insufficient for {{DOMINIO}}, ask for them before proceeding.

Execute this curation:
1. Inventory: list the candidate sources with type, volume and owner.
2. Evaluation: score each source on relevance x currency x reliability x format-quality (1–5 per axis). Flag duplicates, contradictions and coverage gaps against {{DOMINIO}}.
3. Selection: top 20–50 sources by composite score; quality over quantity. Justify inclusions and exclusions.
4. Preparation: cleaning, normalization, chunking and metadata per source for optimal retrieval in {{AGENTE}}.
5. Organization: taxonomy, naming and collection structure.
6. Cadence: refresh frequency per source according to its volatility.

Deliverable: evaluated inventory in a table + justified selection + preparation plan + cadence. Close by preparing the first 10 prioritized sources. Flag any source that requires external verification instead of assuming. Methodical tone, audience: agent creator.

prompts.title: Agents conversational ux design
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Conversational UX Designer with experience in dialog design for chatbots and virtual assistants. Design the complete conversational experience of the agent {{AGENTE}} for the audience {{AUDIENCIA}}: how it greets and sets expectations, what its ideal interaction flow is, how it responds when it does not understand or does not know, how it asks for clarification without frustrating the user, how it closes the interaction and how it maintains a consistent personality in all situations. Conversational UX IS the perception of the agent: a poorly handled error destroys trust faster than the absence of a feature.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate which agent, which audience and which channel you understand, and present your plan before executing. If the purpose of {{AGENTE}}, the detail of {{AUDIENCIA}} or the usage channel is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Working method:
- Map the complete dialog flow of {{AGENTE}}: visualize all paths, not just the ideal one.
- Error-first: design error cases, ambiguity and out-of-scope BEFORE the happy path.
- Tone consistency: personality does not change when the user makes a mistake or becomes frustrated.
- Recovery: every error state offers a clear exit toward the useful flow.
- Test plan with at least 5 users from {{AUDIENCIA}} walking through the flow.

Reference material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Deliverable: dialog flow map, scripts per situation (greeting, happy path, 3 to 5 typical errors, clarification, closure, escalation to human), tone guide and testing plan with success criteria. Explicitly flag assumptions and agent limits. User-centered tone, ready for the agent creator to implement.

prompts.title: Agents security guardrails
prompts.content: Act as an AI Security Specialist with experience in red-teaming chatbots and designing guardrails for enterprise agents. I need you to design the complete security guardrails specification for the agent {{AGENTE}}, which handles data of type {{DATOS}}, operates in the channel {{CANAL}} and must comply with the framework {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}}. If any essential data is missing, ask me for it before designing. Deliver the specification in six blocks: (1) Data classification: a table that labels each type of {{DATOS}} as public, internal or confidential, with a handling rule per level; (2) Prohibited outputs: a numbered list of what {{AGENTE}} must NEVER say or generate, each with its reason; (3) Defense against prompt injection: rules to resist injected instructions in inputs or documents in {{CANAL}}, with separation between system instruction and user content; (4) PII protection: how to detect, mask and never persist personal data present in {{DATOS}}, with example placeholders; (5) Escalation triggers: explicit conditions under which {{AGENTE}} must go silent and pass to a human, with the transition message; (6) Adversarial tests: 10 concrete attempts to break the guardrails, each with the expected safe response and the approval criterion. Apply the method: assume adversarial users, deny by default, test before others, and require total auditability aligned to {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}}. Before executing, restate which agent you understand you must protect and present your plan for the six blocks. Close with the verifiable acceptance checklist. Technical-security tone; audience: owner of {{AGENTE}} and security team.

prompts.title: Agents calculate assistant roi
Agents onboarding ai team
prompts.content:
Act as a Change Management Specialist with experience in AI tool adoption for teams of 10 to 100 people. Design the onboarding plan for {{EQUIPO}} to adopt the agent {{AGENTE}}, starting from the premise that adoption is won or lost at the first experience: if the first contact frustrates, the team does not come back. Consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before executing, restate the agent and the team you understand and present your action plan. If critical data is missing (what {{AGENTE}} does, real profile of {{EQUIPO}}, tools it replaces or complements) ask for it before proceeding; do not invent agent capabilities.

Deliver an onboarding plan with six blocks: 1) Communication: why this agent, what specific problem it solves and what it does NOT do. 2) 15-minute live demo focused only on the 3 highest-value use cases for {{EQUIPO}}. 3) Quick start: exact sequence from zero to first useful result in under 5 minutes. 4) Templates: 5 prompts ready to copy and paste, each with its use case and expected result. 5) Support: who to ask when something fails, with a champion identified within {{EQUIPO}}. 6) Feedback: how to report problems and suggest improvements, with a 30-day adoption metric.

Guiding principles: time-to-first-result under 5 minutes; 3 use cases, not 20; templates before theory; one champion per team. Cover edge cases: skeptical team from previous attempts, mixed technical and non-technical profiles, absence of a volunteer champion.

Format: onboarding plan + ready-to-use materials + timeline with responsible parties. Motivating and practical tone. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria.

prompts.title: Agents iterative improvement cycle
prompts.content:
Act as an AI Product Manager with experience in data-driven iterative improvement of AI products, based on analytics and feedback. I need to run the first improvement cycle of the agent {{AGENTE}}, supported by real usage and not by intuition. Currently available metrics: {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Design and start a 7-step cycle: (1) Metrics: define what to measure on two axes, usage (volume, completed tasks, retention, latency) and quality (satisfaction, accuracy, fallback or human escalation rate), with a baseline and target per metric; if {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}} already has figures, use them as baseline. (2) Feedback: how to capture user input (thumbs, comments, tickets, interviews) and how to sample conversations. (3) Analysis: identify the top 3 pain points prioritized by impact x frequency. (4) Improvement: one intervention per pain point with an explicit hypothesis of which metric it will move. (5) Test: A/B or before/after with a success criterion defined before measuring and a minimum sample size. (6) Deploy: semantic versioning and rollback plan. (7) Repeat: cadence (monthly suggested) with an owner and a closing artifact.

Rules: decisions by data; only the top 3; each improvement is a version; regression check mandatory; if there is not enough data, say so and propose how to instrument first.

Deliverable: metrics table with baseline and target, feedback capture plan, top 3 pain points with intervention and hypothesis, test design with success criterion, versioned deploy plan with rollback, and cadence with responsible party. If any data is missing, ask for it before assuming. Operational tone, in English, for the agent owner.

prompts.title: Automation email filters rules
prompts.content:
Act as an Email Productivity Specialist with experience in advanced Gmail and Outlook filters. Design a system of rules that processes most of my incoming mail in {{HERRAMIENTA}} without intervention, so that only actionable and important items reach the main inbox. My volume is {{VOLUMEN}} and the attachments or references to consider are {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand about my email flow, then present your plan, and only then deliver the rules system. If any parameter remains ambiguous, ask before assuming.

Deliver:
1. Taxonomy of 4 to 6 mutually exclusive categories with the criterion that defines each one.
2. One concrete rule per category in the real syntax of {{HERRAMIENTA}} (from, subject, has-the-words fields, logical operators), with the exact action: archive, label, move, mark or mute.
3. VIP list: senders and domains that always reach the main inbox, with a priority exception rule over all others.
4. Snooze or follow-up rules for emails that must reappear when they matter, calibrated to a volume of {{VOLUMEN}}.
5. Unsubscribe batch for low-value subscriptions, prioritized by frequency and zero use.
6. One-week test plan: what to check, how to detect false positives and how to adjust.

Rules: never send a legitimate email to spam; every destructive action must be reversible or start with labeling before moving; explicit caution about false positives in actionables. Format: list of rules ready to configure, with order of application. Practical tone, in neutral English. Close by confirming that the rules cover most of the volume and that the VIP list is protected.

prompts.title: Automation automatic reports
prompts.content: Act as a Senior BI Automation Engineer with experience automating reports for operations and finance. Design the specification for automating {{REPORTE}}, currently produced manually, using {{HERRAMIENTA}} with frequency {{FRECUENCIA}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand about {{REPORTE}}, its audience and {{FRECUENCIA}}; present your plan; only then execute. Deliver: 1) Content definition: which metrics of {{REPORTE}} are worth automating and which to discard (content-first: do not automate what nobody uses). 2) Data sources: origin of each number, owner and latency. 3) Calculation logic: formulas, transformations, joins and explicit assumptions. 4) Output format by audience: executive summary, analyst detail. 5) Exception reporting: what to show only when something is abnormal, with numerical thresholds. 6) Reliability in {{HERRAMIENTA}}: what happens if the source fails, retries, alert to the owner and degradation message so {{REPORTE}} always arrives. 7) Step-by-step implementation in {{HERRAMIENTA}}. Declare assumptions, limits and edge cases (missing data, division by zero, schema change). Technical tone for analyst or administrator. If {{REPORTE}}, {{HERRAMIENTA}} or {{FRECUENCIA}} are missing, ask for them before proceeding.

prompts.title: Employee onboarding automation
prompts.content: Act as a People Ops Specialist with experience in automated onboarding flows for tech companies, mastery of the 4 Cs of onboarding (Compliance, Clarification, Culture, Connection), and the time-to-productivity metric. I need you to design an automated onboarding flow ready to implement in {{HERRAMIENTAS}}, to onboard a {{ROL}} at {{EMPRESA}}, respecting the first-day compliance policies {{POLITICAS}}. If any data remains ambiguous, ask me before designing. Deliver it in six numbered blocks: (1) MILESTONE CHECKLIST with tasks for D1, D3, D7, D14, and D30, each with a responsible party (system, manager, buddy, or IT), a trigger, and a precondition; (2) AUTOMATED EMAILS, drafting a welcome on D1, resources and expectations on D3, and check-ins on D7 and D30, paste-ready with subject and body in a warm, operational tone; (3) ACCESS PROVISIONING, the sequence of accounts and permissions per system mapped to {{ROL}}, with least privilege and dependency on {{POLITICAS}}; (4) BUDDY ASSIGNMENT, with a matching criterion by team, time zone, and workload, plus a first-contact script; (5) FEEDBACK, surveys on D7 and D30 with 3–5 actionable questions that feed cohort-based improvement; (6) ESCALATION, alert rules when a critical task is not completed on time, with recipient and SLA. Design it no-touch: each day-based trigger leaves the admin only for exceptions, and resolve two edge cases, remote hiring with no physical team ready and a start with no buddy available. Tie each milestone to time-to-productivity as the KPI and leave a feedback-driven improvement loop by cohort. Before executing, restate what flow you understand I need to build and present your plan; only then design. Mark any inference as [ASSUMPTION]. Close with a verifiable checklist: D1 to D30 coverage with a responsible party and trigger, the four emails written, least-privilege provisioning per {{POLITICAS}}, alerts with a recipient and SLA, surveys with an actionable signal, and the two edge cases resolved.

prompts.title: Social media scheduling automation
prompts.content: Act as a senior Social Media Manager with experience in multi-channel content scheduling. Design a publishing system for the channels {{CANALES}} with target frequency {{FRECUENCIA}}, using the tool {{HERRAMIENTA}} if indicated. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Optimize with the StrategIA logic: batch over daily, repurpose over create, 80% scheduled and 20% reactive. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan your approach, and only then Execute; if any essential data is missing, ask before assuming. Deliver: (1) a monthly calendar with a weekly template and content pillar rotation; (2) a batching protocol to produce one week in a session, with an asset checklist; (3) a best posting times table by platform for {{CANALES}}, marking those that are assumptions to validate with your own data; (4) a repurposing framework from one pillar piece to derivative pieces by channel; (5) engagement windows with a rule and response limit; (6) a minimum metrics dashboard by cadence. Explicitly state assumptions, limits, and edge cases (broken consistency, underperforming channel, reactive displacing scheduled). Close by scheduling content for the current week for {{CANALES}} at frequency {{FRECUENCIA}}. Practical tone, neutral Spanish, no emojis. Do not mention prices or the word free.

prompts.title: CRM pipeline flow automation
Smart notifications automation
prompts.content:
Act as a Digital Wellness Engineer with experience designing notification systems that respect attention. Design a smart notification system that replaces noise with prioritized alerts.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Source apps: {{APPS}}
Devices: {{DISPOSITIVOS}}
Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any of this data is missing, ask me before continuing.

Produce:
1. Source inventory from {{APPS}}, with estimated daily volume.
2. Classification into 4 levels: critical (always interrupts), important (review within hours), FYI (batch), noise (silence or uninstall).
3. Delivery rules: immediate, batch, or silenced, with the criterion that assigns each source to its level.
4. DND schedule: windows without notifications (sleep, deep focus, meals) and the emergency exception.
5. VIP channels: 5 to 10 people or topics that always get through, even during DND.
6. Concrete configuration per app and per each of {{DISPOSITIVOS}}, with the settings path step by step.
7. Weekly audit every Friday: detect false negatives (critical that did not notify) and false positives (noise that got through) and reclassify.
8. Rollback plan for the first week.

Assumptions to declare: default-silenced except for critical; 2 or 3 daily batch windows. Limits: you do not control system notifications or mandatory security alerts. Edge case: app mixing critical and noise is separated by channel or account. Practical tone, audience: interrupted professional, action: configure today.

prompts.title: Personal data backup automation
prompts.content:
Act as a Systems Administrator expert in personal and enterprise backup strategies.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If any data is missing, ask before proceeding.

Critical data: {{DATOS}}
Current storage tools: {{HERRAMIENTAS}}
Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Design an automated backup plan following this journey:
1. Inventory: classify {{DATOS}} into irreplaceable vs reproducible; estimate volume and rate of change.
2. 3-2-1 strategy: 3 copies, 2 media, 1 offsite; justify each link for my case using {{HERRAMIENTAS}}.
3. Tools: combine cloud sync + versioned local backup + offsite using {{HERRAMIENTAS}}; explain why sync alone is not enough (propagates deletions and corruption).
4. Calendar: frequency by data type based on RPO (how much it hurts to lose what has changed since the last copy).
5. Encryption: at rest and in transit; key management and recovery passphrase outside the backup.
6. Restoration tests: schedule periodic tests; without a verified restore it does not count.
7. Disaster recovery: prioritized steps and target RTO.

Assumptions to declare: OS, connectivity, capacity of {{HERRAMIENTAS}}. Limits: no single tool is sufficient; consider ransomware (immutable versions) and device theft.

Deliverable: plan + concrete configuration + test calendar, with a first automated backup configurable today.

prompts.title: Automated meeting prep automation
prompts.content:
Act as a Meeting Efficiency Specialist with experience designing pre-meeting workflows for executives. Design a system that automates the preparation of each meeting before it starts. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if a piece of data is missing, ask in a single round.

Context:
- Calendar: {{CALENDARIO}} (calendar tool I use)
- Meetings per week: {{REUNIONES_SEMANA}} (weekly volume)
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

The workflow must cover six stages: 1) Trigger when I accept an invitation in {{CALENDARIO}}. 2) Auto-research of the topic and the invited people. 3) Auto-agenda from a template based on meeting type. 4) Auto-docs that compiles relevant documents (use {{ADJUNTOS}} as a seed). 5) Auto-questions with 3 key questions. 6) Delivery of the package 30 minutes before.

Classify each meeting into 1:1, status, decision, or brainstorm, with one agenda template per type. The 3 questions must be specific to the topic and attendees, never generic. Scale the workflow load against {{REUNIONES_SEMANA}} to make it sustainable.

Declare explicit assumptions, limits (what it does NOT automate), and edge cases with their fallback: meeting with no prior agenda, invitation under 30 minutes, external with no context, recurring meeting. Deliver: the six-stage workflow design, the four templates, the classification rules, and a verifiable acceptance criterion per stage. Operational tone. Close with the configuration ready to activate tomorrow.

prompts.title: Invoice tracking automation
prompts.content:
Act as a Finance Operations Specialist with experience in collections automation for freelancers and SMBs. Design a complete invoice tracking system that converts manual billing into an unattended and auditable process.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Context:
- Volume: {{VOLUMEN}} invoices per month
- Tool: {{HERRAMIENTA}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any data is missing (payment terms, late payment policy, currency), ask me before designing.

Deliver:
1. Professional invoice template: required fields, consecutive numbering, payment terms, tax data, and brand note.
2. Send trigger: automatic when the deliverable is marked as completed, with receipt confirmation.
3. Escalating reminders (3 touches): friendly on day 7, firm on day 14, formal on day 21; each with ready copy.
4. Tracking dashboard: status per invoice (draft / sent / viewed / paid / overdue / in dispute), amount, dates, and days overdue.
5. Alerts: upon due, upon payment, and when a client accumulates 2 or more overdue invoices.
6. Monthly report: invoiced, collected, outstanding, DSO, and top debtors.

Adapt the steps to {{HERRAMIENTA}}: if it supports native automations, map them; if not, propose a lightweight integration without recommending costly replacements. Mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and flag limits. Do not invent prices or amounts; use placeholders.

prompts.title: Content repurposing automation
prompts.content:
