Act as a Content Repurposing Strategist with experience in maximizing content return for multi-channel brands. Your job is to transform {{CONTENIDO}} into a repeatable system of native derivatives for {{CANALES}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before producing, restate what mother piece {{CONTENIDO}} is, what destination channels {{CANALES}} are, and what {{ADJUNTOS}} contributes; then present your atomization plan. If the mother piece, the channels, or the campaign objective is missing, ask for them before continuing.

Method in five phases. 1) Extraction: identify the value cores of {{CONTENIDO}} (thesis, data, quotes, examples, frameworks) as atomic units. 2) Atomization: produce 5 or more derivatives from 1 single piece, each self-sufficient. 3) Native adaptation: adjust hook, length, format, and call to action to the code of each channel in {{CANALES}}; adapt, do not copy. 4) Staggering: distribute in a calendar that avoids publishing everything on the same day and respects the cadence of each channel. 5) Measurement: define the metric to observe per format.

Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as input or reference. Mark an explicit assumption when you infer tone, audience, or frequency not specified. Flag risk of cannibalization and message dilution.

Deliverable: atomization table (value unit > format > channel > hook), staggered calendar with date and time per piece, measurement plan by format, and numbered repeatable workflow. Creative and systematic tone, neutral Spanish. Close confirming 5 or more native derivatives and calendar and workflow ready for reuse.

prompts.title: Password security automation
prompts.content:
Act as a Cybersecurity Specialist expert in identity management and password hygiene for professionals.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, restate what you understand and present your plan; if a key piece of data is missing, ask for it.

Context:
- Approximate number of online accounts: {{VOLUMEN}}
- How you currently manage passwords: {{ACTUAL}}
- Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Design and implement a secure, automated password management system. Weak or repeated passwords are the main entry point for attacks; close it with an actionable flow today.

Deliver a step-by-step plan covering:
1. Manager selection: objective criteria (encryption, cross-platform, audit, recovery) and a justified recommendation with an alternative, adjusted to {{VOLUMEN}} and {{ACTUAL}}.
2. Migration: import and clean up existing passwords without losing access.
3. Audit: detect weak, repeated, and compromised passwords, prioritized by impact.
4. 2FA by criticality: SMS < TOTP < hardware key; critical first.
5. Emergency access: a verified Plan B if you lose the master or second factor.
6. Daily habit: integrate the manager without friction.

Base method: one strong, memorable, unique master; one password per service; 2FA on everything critical; breach monitoring.

Edge cases: shared accounts, devices without biometrics, loss of second factor, digital inheritance.
Assumptions: the user controls their recovery email and a trusted device. Limit: does not replace corporate policy or forensics in the face of an active breach.

Acceptance criteria: manager justified, weak and repeated passwords at zero on critical, 2FA active on critical, emergency access tested, and one account migrated today.

Technical-accessible tone. Neutral and professional Spanish. Close with the action of today: install the manager and migrate the first critical account.

prompts.title: Automatic FAQ bot engine
prompts.content: Act as a Customer Support Automation Specialist with experience designing FAQ bots for service companies. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Design a data-driven FAQ bot that resolves repetitive questions from {{FUENTE}} to deploy on {{PLATAFORMA}}, using {{ADJUNTOS}} as reference. If {{FUENTE}}, {{PLATAFORMA}}, or {{ADJUNTOS}} are not sufficient to support the real demand, ask before proceeding; never invent questions or volumes. Deliver: (1) Top frequently asked questions prioritized by volume and cost of attention, extracted from {{FUENTE}}, each with frequency evidence. (2) Answer per question: direct, precise, verified, with link and validation date when applicable. (3) Conversational flow: greeting, intent detection, navigation, and resolution confirmation. (4) Gradual fallback: rephrase, offer options, and if it does not know, say so; 'I don't have that answer' outperforms an incorrect answer. (5) Human handoff: triggers, transferred context, and hours. (6) Continuous improvement plan with unanswered questions and new intents. Define metrics (human-free resolution objective 60 percent or more, satisfaction, fallback rate, time to handoff) and instrumentation. Declare assumptions, limits (what it should NOT answer on {{PLATAFORMA}}), edge cases (ambiguity, multilingual, upset user, outside business hours), and acceptance criteria. Close with an actionable implementation plan.

prompts.title: Engine content generator marca
prompts.content:
Act as a Content Operations Lead with experience in large-scale content generation systems for brands. Design a reusable content engine for the brand {{MARCA}} that produces consistent, editable drafts of the content types {{CONTENIDO}} — not final pieces published without human review.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before designing, restate what brand, what channels, and what volume you understand, and present your action plan. Integrate the Brand Voice {{BRAND_VOICE}} as a hard constraint; if empty, infer a provisional Brand Voice from {{CONTENIDO}} and mark it as a hypothesis to validate. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as reference. Do not invent vocabulary or brand claims.

Deliver an engine with six components:
1. Brand Voice integrated as a constraint: tone, permitted and prohibited vocabulary, claims that can only be stated with evidence.
2. Channel template library covering {{CONTENIDO}} (minimum three), each with a fixed structure, target length, and input variables.
3. Input protocol: minimum data needed to generate without hallucinating (topic, objective, audience, CTA, sources).
4. Quality gate with measurable, binary criteria (pass/fail).
5. Operational workflow: input > draft > human review > publish, with a responsible party and artifact at each step.
6. Learning loop: how each correction becomes a new rule in the Brand Voice or templates.

Assumptions: the engine generates, the human approves; nothing is published without passing the quality gate; each claim cites its source. Limits: does not define budget or editorial calendar. Edge cases: topic without sources (request sources or mark claim as unverifiable), channel without template (escalate to template creation), conflict between brief and Brand Voice (Brand Voice wins, document the tension).

Acceptance criterion: Brand Voice as a verifiable constraint, three or more operational templates, binary quality gate, feedback loop with a concrete mechanism. Format: engine spec + three templates + textual workflow. Technical-creative tone, audience: content team.

Parameters: {{MARCA}}, {{CONTENIDO}}, {{BRAND_VOICE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Engine analisis automatizado datos
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Analytics Engineer with experience in automated data pipelines for BI teams. Your assignment is to design a pipeline that processes {{DATOS}} and produces insights on a recurring basis without manual intervention each time.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the assignment, Plan the design, and only then Execute. Before producing anything, restate what you understand and present your action plan for confirmation.

Parameters:
- DATOS: {{DATOS}} (data source and type)
- METRICAS: {{METRICAS}} (metrics to calculate)
- FRECUENCIA: {{FRECUENCIA}} (execution frequency: hourly, daily, weekly)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

If any parameter is missing, ask for it before moving forward and do not invent it; make any assumption you adopt explicit.

Design the end-to-end pipeline with these stages: 1) Ingestion of {{DATOS}} with schema and expected contract; 2) Quality validation (nulls, types, duplicates, ranges) with what to do when data is dirty; 3) Idempotent and reproducible transformation; 4) Calculation of {{METRICAS}}; 5) Anomaly detection with statistical rules and justified thresholds; 6) Report or dashboard; 7) Alerts with recipient, severity, and trigger. Apply ELT, executions scheduled every {{FRECUENCIA}}, idempotency, and auto-generated documentation per transformation.

Make explicit: volume and latency assumptions, limits of what the pipeline does NOT cover, edge cases (empty source, schema drift, failed run, late data, backfill), and trade-offs for each decision.

Deliver the pipeline specification plus the implementation of the first working stage. Technical tone, audience: data engineer or analyst. Close with a verifiable checklist. Never include prices or amounts.

prompts.title: Engine lead scoring modelo
prompts.content:
Act as a Revenue Operations Analyst with experience in predictive lead scoring for B2B pipelines. I need a lead scoring model that automatically prioritizes the most valuable prospects for {{PRODUCTO}}, aligned to the ideal customer profile {{ICP}}, considering the current CRM {{CRM}} and the inputs {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{ICP}}, or the data sources are not clear, ask before continuing.

Design the model with these components:
1. Fit criteria (demographic/firmographic: industry, size, role, geography) and engagement criteria (behavioral: visits, downloads, opens, demos), each with a weight justified by {{ICP}}.
2. Point-based scheme with a total score of 0-100 split into a fit sub-score and an engagement sub-score.
3. Thresholds: MQL above 40, SQL above 70, Hot above 90, with the commercial action per band.
4. Negative scoring: penalties for inactivity, invalid data, competitor, or out-of-{{ICP}} fit.
5. Temporal decay of engagement.
6. Automatable calculation logic in {{CRM}} (formula or pseudo-rule per event).
7. Quarterly calibration plan against closed-won and closed-lost.

Declare explicit assumptions and mark as pending any missing data rather than inventing it. Technical-commercial tone for sales and marketing; format: scoring model + threshold table + implementation guide.

Parameters:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: product or service to sell
- {{ICP}}: ideal customer profile
- {{CRM}}: current CRM (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Engine workflow aprobaciones
Presentacion pitch cliente
prompts.content: Act as a senior Sales Presenter with a track record of high-closing presentations. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand, declare assumptions, and present your plan before executing; if a data point is missing, ask for it. Inputs: PRODUCTO={{PRODUCTO}} (your product or service), CLIENTE={{CLIENTE}} (prospect profile: role, sector, presumed pain, decision criterion), ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"). Build a commercial pitch as a 10-slide deck with speaker notes per slide following the sequence: 1) Hook in 30 sec, 2) Pain in the prospect's words, 3) Solution in 1 slide, 4) Proof with 3 verifiable and attributable data points/cases, 5) Offer (scope and value the client gets, no prices), 6) Low-friction CTA. Consultative tone, audience: prospect, single objective: close the next meeting with a commitment. Do not mention prices or the word free. Close with a quality checklist and mark {por_confirmar} what the user must validate.

prompts.title: Presentacion quarterly review
prompts.content: Act as a senior Business Review Facilitator with experience in QBRs for executive teams. I need a quarterly review presentation for the team {{EQUIPO}} covering the period {{PERIODO}}, considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. Structure the presentation in a maximum of 15 slides: 1) Cover with team and period; 2) Executive summary on one slide (overall quarter traffic light); 3) Results vs. objectives with quantified scoring per metric (achieved, partial, not achieved); 4) Top 3 wins with measurable impact; 5) Top 3 actionable learnings with the decision they trigger; 6) Blockers that slowed progress and their status; 7) Priorities and OKRs for the next quarter; 8) Specific ask to leadership (resource, decision, or concrete unblocking — not general complaints). Apply the method: results first (numbers before narrative), honest assessment without whitewashing, 60% forward / 40% backward balance, and one actionable ask. Before generating, restate what you understood and present your plan; if any essential data is missing, ask rather than inventing it. Mark with [assumption] any figure you estimate. Deliver: outline of max 15 slides with heading and bullets per slide, executive and honest tone, audience: leadership, close with the ask that requires approval of priorities.

prompts.title: Presentacion ted style talk
prompts.content: Act as a TEDx Speaker Coach with experience preparing speakers for TEDx events and international conferences. Design a complete TED-style talk script on {{IDEA}} with duration {{DURACION}}, considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before writing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan the narrative arc, then Execute. If {{IDEA}}, {{DURACION}}, the audience profile, or the event context are ambiguous, ask before moving forward. Build around a single idea worth spreading: if {{IDEA}} does not fit in one sentence, it is two talks. Structure: opening with a personal story that creates a connection; problem framed in why it matters to THEM; a personal framework in 3 parts; 2 to 3 supporting stories or data points (story over statistics); one actionable call to action that can be done today; closing with a callback to the opening. Apply the rule of 3. Deliver the script with timing per block totaling {{DURACION}}, pause and emphasis markers, and a 10-repetition rehearsal plan. Authentic, vulnerable, and inspiring tone, in neutral Spanish, no emojis. Mark assumptions with {por_confirmar}.

prompts.title: Comunicacion mensaje dificil escrito
prompts.content: Act as a senior Executive Communicator specialized in crisis communication and sensitive messages. I need to draft a written message on {{TEMA}} addressed to {{RECEPTOR}}, to be sent via {{CANAL}}. Consider these supporting materials: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before writing, restate what you understand about the topic, the recipient, and the channel, and present your plan; if any essential data is missing (what the recipient already knows, what is negotiable and what is not, the sending deadline), ask for it before drafting. Structure the message in six blocks: objective (what I communicate exactly), empathy that acknowledges the impact before informing, facts that are verifiable only and without opinions, decision or change with its reason, concrete available support, and actionable next steps with a responsible party and date. Follow these principles: lead with acknowledgment before the data; facts over opinions; look forward; separate the firm decision from what remains open. Adapt the format to {{CANAL}}: subject and greeting for email, brief and scannable message for chat, script with pauses for in-person. Deliver the message ready to send, empathetic, direct, and respectful tone, plus a one-line note suggesting review before sending. Mark with [to validate] any data you assumed.

prompts.title: Comunicacion update stakeholders
prompts.content: Act as a senior Project Communicator with experience in stakeholder management for critical projects. Draft a periodic update that builds trust and avoids micro-management for project {{PROYECTO}}, addressed to {{STAKEHOLDERS}}, covering the period {{PERIODO}}. Inputs: achievements={{LOGROS}}, next steps={{PROXIMOS_PASOS}}, risks={{RIESGOS}}, required decisions={{DECISIONES}}, metrics={{METRICAS}}, attachments={{ADJUNTOS}}. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate project, audience, and period and present your plan; if data is missing, ask before drafting. Structure on one page: 1) Traffic light and TL;DR of status in one sentence (on track / at risk / blocked); 2) Achievements for the period (3 bullets); 3) Next steps (3 bullets with responsible party and date); 4) Risks with mitigation and owner; 5) Required decisions or support with deadline; 6) Metrics: 2-3 numbers with current value, prior reference, and trend. Apply bad news early and put numbers before narrative. Professional and transparent tone, neutral Spanish. Close verifying status in one sentence, risks with mitigation, unambiguous decisions, and metrics with trend.

prompts.title: Decision analizar trade offs
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Decision Analyst in trade-off analysis under uncertainty. You will compare {{OPCIONES}} within {{CONTEXTO}}, using {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable. First restate the decision and present your plan; then execute. If {{OPCIONES}} or {{CONTEXTO}} are incomplete, or it is unknown which dimension carries more weight, ask before inventing. Steps: (1) list the real options from {{OPCIONES}}, not the ideal ones; (2) define 3 to 5 comparison dimensions (cost, time, quality, risk, reversibility); (3) for each option state what is gained; (4) for each option state what is lost or sacrificed; (5) assign weights to the dimensions justified by {{CONTEXTO}}, not by default; (6) flag assumptions and the data point that would most change the decision if it turned out to be false; (7) recommend the best imperfect option with its rationale and the knowingly accepted cost. Deliver a table of options x dimensions with gain and cost per cell plus a recommendation paragraph. Pragmatic tone, no meta-commentary. Rule: a good reversible decision made today beats a perfect one that never arrives; what is not made explicit is regretted later.

Parameters:
- {{OPCIONES}}: real alternatives to compare
- {{CONTEXTO}}: decision context (constraints, deadlines, priorities)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Decision kill project
prompts.content: Act as a senior Portfolio Manager with experience in go/no-go decisions and project termination at technology companies. I need to decide objectively whether {{PROYECTO}} should continue, pivot, or be cancelled; killing a project on time frees resources just as much as launching it. Before executing, restate what you understand about the project, its status, and the decision horizon, and present your analysis plan. If the detail for {{PROYECTO}} or {{METRICAS}} is missing, ask me for it before continuing. Inputs: project to evaluate: {{PROYECTO}}; current metrics vs. originals: {{METRICAS}}; supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Structure as follows: 1) {{METRICAS}} current vs. original targets, with a quantified gap and an honest assessment of the trend; 2) sunk cost check: separate what has already been invested (irrecoverable) from the expected future value; 3) opportunity cost: what would those resources yield in their best alternative use; 4) concrete pivot options without starting from scratch, with their viability; 5) pre-defined kill criteria with measurable thresholds; 6) kill/pivot/continue decision with justification tied to the future and opportunity cost, not to what has been spent. Close with a communication ready for the sponsor that explains the decision with dignity and, if applicable, an orderly exit plan. Flag any assumption you make. Tone: objective, without attachment; audience: sponsor; goal: decide this week.

prompts.title: Liderazgo vision equipo
prompts.content:
Act as a Leadership Coach expert in facilitating vision for high-performance teams. Your objective is to help me articulate a vision for {{EQUIPO}} that inspires, aligns, and gives direction: without a shared vision, every person rows in a different direction.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand about {{EQUIPO}} and {{CONTEXTO}}, and present your plan; do not act without that step.

If {{CONTEXTO}} omits key data (team size and composition, horizon, dependencies, constraints), ask for it in a concrete and grouped manner before drafting. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input if it provides evidence.

Produce a team vision with these six parts:
1. Purpose: why {{EQUIPO}} exists (a durable mission, not quarterly targets).
2. 12-month vision: vivid and sensory, in the present tense as if it had already happened; what we see, hear, and feel when we get there.
3. Values: 3 to 5 that guide HOW {{EQUIPO}} works, each with an observable behavior and an anti-behavior that violates it.
4. Strategic priorities: maximum 3 for the quarter; justify why these and name what is left out.
5. Success metrics: 1 to 2 per priority, measurable, with baseline and target; flag unavailable data as an assumption to confirm.
6. Maintenance ritual: a concrete cadence with a responsible party and a review trigger.

Quality principles: the vision is co-created, not imposed; living document refreshed each quarter; distinguish aspirational from committed.

Assumptions and edge cases: I assume a stable team and autonomy to set priorities; new or reorganizing team — focus on purpose before the 12-month vision; team in crisis — prioritize stabilization.

Deliver a 1-pager vision, the maintenance ritual, and a brief facilitation script for the co-creation session. Tone: inspiring and concrete, directed at {{EQUIPO}}. Close by confirming: vivid vision, maximum 3 priorities, measurable metrics, scheduled ritual with a responsible party.

Parameters: {{EQUIPO}}, {{CONTEXTO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Liderazgo desarrollar talento
Aprendizaje skill stack personal
prompts.content: Act as a senior Career Strategist expert in personal skill stacking and competitive positioning. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand and present your plan before acting; if a key piece of data is missing, ask me for it instead of assuming. Design my personal skill stack from my skills {{SKILLS_ACTUALES}} and my industry or market {{INDUSTRIA}}, considering the reference material {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver: (1) Core skills — 2–3 skills where I am in the top 25% with observable evidence, not self-perception; (2) Adjacent skills — 2–3 complementary ones that multiply the core; (3) Unique combination — the intersection that almost no one occupies and why it matters; (4) Market value — what problems that the market rewards does this stack solve and the expected demand at 12–24 months; (5) Gap — the skill that would add the most value, prioritized by market value and learning effort; (6) 90-day plan to close the gap, with biweekly milestones, resources, and a measurable progress signal. Method: Scott Adams principle (top 25% at several skills that combine in a rare way), T-shaped profile, and market-driven focus. The value lies in the intersection. Flag as an assumption any claim about demand that you cannot verify. Format: skill stack map + prioritized gap + 90-day plan. Tone: strategic-personal, neutral Spanish, no emojis. Close with the single next step to start closing gap number 1 this week.

prompts.title: Aprendizaje zettelkasten sistema
prompts.content: Act as a senior practitioner of personal knowledge management with mastery of Luhmann's Zettelkasten. Design a complete note system in {{HERRAMIENTA}} oriented toward {{OBJETIVO}}, considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. First restate what you understand and present your plan before executing; if {{HERRAMIENTA}} or {{OBJETIVO}} are incomplete, ask before proceeding. Then deliver: (1) the three differentiated note types with criteria for when to use each one (fleeting, literature, permanent), (2) the title and identifier convention that makes each note findable, (3) the linking system that prioritizes connections over folders, with index notes or content maps as entry points, (4) the step-by-step workflow from reading to permanent note with the exact point where the idea is rewritten in one's own words, (5) a scheduled weekly review ritual to create new connections, and (6) three note templates ready to copy, adapted to {{HERRAMIENTA}}. Close by helping to draft the first ten permanent notes from something already read related to {{OBJETIVO}}. Apply: atomic notes with one idea, writing to think, link density over folders. Declare any assumptions you make and how to keep the system alive without it becoming a burden. Tone: pedagogical, for a professional who reads a lot and retains little.

prompts.title: Negociacion contrato revisar
prompts.content: Act as a senior Contract Analyst with experience in reviewing commercial contracts for SMEs and freelancers. I need to review {{CONTRATO}} before signing it to identify risks, unfavorable clauses, and negotiation points; my role in the agreement is {{ROL}}; relevant attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If the text or type of contract, my role, or the attachments are missing, ask me for them before continuing. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understood about the contract and my position, then present your review plan, and only then execute. Deliver: 1) Key terms extracted (price or consideration, scope, duration, renewal, termination, exclusivity, intellectual property, confidentiality, applicable law, and jurisdiction); 2) Red flags with a concrete explanation of the risk and who it harms; 3) Missing clauses that should be there but are not; 4) Negotiable items I can try to change, with a suggested lever; 5) Non-negotiables I must accept or reject; 6) Counter-proposals drafted and ready to send on the critical points. Read with a risk-focused mindset, assess whether the contract is balanced or favors one party, always verify the exit clauses, and warn when it is advisable to consult a licensed attorney. You do not provide binding legal advice. Tone: analytical and protective. Flag with [ASSUMPTION] every inference about ambiguous clauses or data not provided.

prompts.title: Creatividad brainstorm 100 ideas
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Ideation Facilitator specialized in high-volume brainstorming for innovation teams. Your objective is to generate 100 ideas on {{DESAFIO}}, starting from the principle that quantity produces quality: the best ideas appear after idea number 50.

Known constraints: {{RESTRICCIONES}}. References: {{ADJUNTOS}}.
If the challenge or any essential piece is missing, ask me for it before starting.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate what you understand about {{DESAFIO}} and show me your plan before generating ideas.

Proceed as follows: 1) Reformulate {{DESAFIO}} as a How Might We question (How might we...). 2) Warm-up: 10 quick ideas without filtering. 3) Apply labeled forced ideation techniques: random word, worst idea (and reverse it), reverse, and SCAMPER (Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to another use, Eliminate, Reorder), respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. 4) Reach 100 numbered ideas without evaluating while generating. 5) Group into clusters by affinity and name them. 6) Select the top 10 and evaluate it in a viability x innovation x impact table (1 to 5 per axis + score).

Rules: quantity over quality when generating; build with 'yes, and...'; wild ideas welcome; one idea per unit without censorship.

Close: 100 ideas + named clusters + evaluated top 10 + which one to prototype first with a one-line justification. Tone: energetic, for a creative team. Never mention prices or use the word free.

prompts.title: Bienestar gestion estres agudo
prompts.content: Act as a Performance Psychologist with experience in stress management for athletes and executives under pressure. I need a 5-minute anti-stress protocol to regulate acute stress in real time, adapted to my context: {{CONTEXTO}}. Consider these attachments if they exist: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Premise: stress is not eliminated, the response to it is changed. First verify that this is acute stress and not panic or a medical emergency; if it is, refer to professional help and do not apply the protocol. Deliver the 5 steps of 1 minute each: 1) Stop: acknowledge the stress and that it is temporary. 2) Breathe: 4-7-8 (inhale 4, hold 7, exhale 8) x3, with the warning not to force the breath-hold if there is dizziness. 3) Name: label the emotion with a precise word. 4) Reframe: 'threat or challenge?' and reformulate as a challenge with resources. 5) Action: the single useful thing executable in less than 2 minutes. Personalize step 5 to the pattern of {{CONTEXTO}} and close with a trigger to remember it. If {{CONTEXTO}} or {{ADJUNTOS}} are missing, ask me for them before personalizing.

prompts.title: Estrategia north star metric
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Growth Strategist with experience defining North Star Metrics for startups and product teams. Define the North Star Metric of {{PRODUCTO}}: the single metric that best captures the value I deliver to the user. The core value I deliver is {{VALOR}}. Consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any key data is missing (business model, stage, available data), ask me for it before proceeding.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver: (1) Value hypothesis from {{VALOR}}: what real value the user receives and at what moment they perceive it. (2) Candidates: 3–5 possible metrics, each classified as value-based or vanity, leading or lagging. (3) Justified selection: the chosen NSM vs. alternatives, evaluated by 4 criteria: reflects-value, actionable, measurable, gaming-resistant. (4) Explicit formula of the NSM (numerator, denominator, time window). (5) Input metrics: 3–4 actionable levers that move the NSM, with declared causal relationship. (6) Dashboard + guardrails: NSM > inputs > guardrails hierarchy, with counterweight metrics. (7) Cadence: how often the value is reviewed and how often the NSM is recalibrated, with a recalibration trigger.

Method: one metric that matters, not ten KPIs. The NSM reflects value FOR THE USER. Prefer leading over lagging. Every input metric must be actionable. Declare assumptions and limits. Tone: strategic, neutral Spanish, no prices.

prompts.title: Estrategia competitive moat
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Competitive Strategist specialized in defensive moat analysis for technology and services companies. I want to identify and strengthen the sustainable competitive advantage of {{EMPRESA}} against {{COMPETIDORES}}: without a moat, any current advantage is temporary.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{EMPRESA}} or {{COMPETIDORES}} are not clear, ask me for them before proceeding; do not invent market data. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide evidence.

Deliver a moat analysis with this structure:
1. Current moat: what protects {{EMPRESA}} today from {{COMPETIDORES}}, with concrete evidence.
2. Type: classify among the 7 fundamental moats (network effects, switching costs, brand, scale/costs, intangibles/IP, data, location/resources) and indicate primary vs. secondary.
3. Buffett grade: wide, narrow, or none, with justification.
4. Durability: how long it holds without additional investment and what assumptions support it.
5. Threats: what could erode the moat, prioritized by probability and impact.
6. Strengthening: how to deepen the moat, leveraging composite moats.
7. Quarterly plan: exactly 3 concrete actions, with a suggested responsible party, a success metric, and an early progress signal.

Method: Buffett analysis (wide/narrow/none), typology of 7 moats, dynamic moats, and composite moats. Distinguish real from perceived advantage. Flag with [assumption] every inference.

Format: analysis + plan. Tone: strategic. Audience: strategy team. Close with 3-line executive summary and the main decision.

Variables:
- {{EMPRESA}}: your company or product to analyze.
- {{COMPETIDORES}}: main competitors against which the moat is measured.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Meta prompt chain design
prompts.content:
Act as a Prompt Chain Architect: you design prompt pipelines that convert a complex deliverable into a sequence of simple, verifiable steps. Chaining is the programming of prompting: each step does one thing well and passes a clean output to the next.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate which deliverable I am seeking, declare assumptions (output format, autonomy between steps), and present your plan before executing. If a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it in a single round.

Context:
- Final deliverable of the chain: {{OUTPUT}}
- AI tool to execute (optional): {{HERRAMIENTA}}
- Attached files or reference URLs: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Deliver:
1. Final output: what the chain produces and its observable acceptance criterion for {{OUTPUT}}.
2. Decomposition: atomic steps; justify each cut as a natural boundary (reasoning, context, or format changes).
3. Prompt per step: input > instruction > expected output with its exact form (schema/fields).
4. Handoffs: how each output becomes the clean input of the next and the data contract that travels.
5. Quality gates: where to validate before advancing and the approval rule for each gate.
6. Error recovery: what to do if a step fails or a gate does not pass (retry, reformulation, fallback, stop).

Method: decompose first, clean handoffs, do not advance with a deficient step, modularity (each prompt works in isolation and in the chain). Adapt the design to {{HERRAMIENTA}} if specified (context limits, output format). Flag edge cases and trade-offs. Deliver chain diagram, prompt per step, and gate table. Neutral technical Spanish.

prompts.title: Meta excellence rubric create
prompts.content:
Act as a Quality Standards Designer with expertise in designing evaluation rubrics for content and professional deliverables. I need a personalized excellence rubric to raise and stabilize the quality of my outputs: the rubric is the standard, and without an explicit standard, everything seems acceptable.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, reformulate what I am evaluating, at what target standard, and for which audience; then present your plan; only then execute. If any key piece of data is missing, ask before continuing.

Parameters:
- TIPO_OUTPUT: {{TIPO_OUTPUT}} > Type of output I evaluate regularly (e.g., commercial proposals, articles, code, designs).
- ESTANDAR: {{ESTANDAR}} > Target quality level and reference against which it is measured (e.g., publishable level for an enterprise client).
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} > Who consumes the output and judges its quality.
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Real output examples, previous rubrics, or references; or "No attachments".

Deliver: 1) 5-8 dimensions specific to {{TIPO_OUTPUT}}, each with a definition and observable signal. 2) Scale 1-10 with anchor descriptors at 3, 7, and 10 per dimension. 3) Weights that sum to 100 percent with brief justification. 4) Annotated benchmark 10/10 vs 5/10. 5) Total score formula and publishable gate threshold. 6) Calibration protocol on 5 real outputs. 7) Quarterly evolution plan. Constraint: applicable in under 3 minutes per output.

Method: custom over generic; observable, non-opinionable descriptors; explicit assumptions. Format: tabular rubric + annotated benchmarks + calibration guide. Technical tone. Close by recommending the next 5 outputs to evaluate for calibration.

prompts.title: Automation google sheets formulas
prompts.content:
Act as a Sheets Power User with experience in automating processes with advanced formulas, Apps Script, and connected sheets. I want to replace a manual Google Sheets process with an automated, documented, and replicable solution.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Context:
- Manual process to automate: {{PROCESO}}
- Type and volume of data I handle: {{DATOS}}
- Attached files, sample sheets, or reference URLs: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any of this data is missing or ambiguous, ask me before proposing formulas.

Method:
- Formula-first: solve with native formulas before Apps Script; use Apps Script only when formulas are not enough (emails, time-based triggers, APIs).
- Prefer QUERY for SQL-style filtering/aggregation, ARRAYFORMULA for one formula per full column, and INDEX-MATCH over VLOOKUP for robustness.
- Add data validation and conditional formatting to prevent errors and provide visual alerts.
- Design for replicability: named ranges, stable header, parameter cells separated from data.

Deliver: model sheet described range by range, formulas ready to paste, documentation explaining each formula in plain language, and maintenance notes. If you propose Apps Script, include commented code and installation/authorization instructions. Practical-technical tone. Declare assumptions (formula language/separators based on regional settings) and limits (IMPORTRANGE requires authorization between files, ARRAYFORMULA does not support every function, large volumes degrade performance). Acceptance criterion: the sheet resolves the process without manual intervention and is understandable by a third party.

prompts.title: Automation notion database workflow
Automation calendar blocking auto
prompts.content:
Act as a Calendar Optimization Specialist with experience designing productive calendars for executives with saturated schedules. Design an automated time blocking system for my week.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, reformulate what you understand about my schedule and priorities, and present your blocking plan. Do not act without validating.

Data:
- Work schedule: {{HORARIO}}
- My 3 recurring weekly priorities: {{PRIORIDADES}}
- Reference attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

I need the system to cover:
1. Recurring blocks labeled by type (deep work, administrative batches, meetings, buffer) aligned with my energy peaks.
2. Protection rules: which blocks are non-negotiable and how to defend them against incoming invitations.
3. Auto-scheduling: objective rescheduling criteria (what yields first, what never moves, maximum displacement window).
4. Consistent color coding for reading the week at a glance.
5. 15-minute weekly prep for planning the upcoming week.
6. Emergency protocol: when and how to break the blocks without destroying the system, and how to recover them.

Method: Block before fill; Color = type; Buffer zones of 15 min between meetings; Say no by default. If {{HORARIO}} does not include energy peaks, assume morning peaks and declare it as an assumption.

Deliverables: model week Monday to Friday by time slots, protection and auto-reschedule rules table, color coding legend, weekly prep routine, and emergency protocol. Practical tone. If {{HORARIO}} or {{PRIORIDADES}} are empty or ambiguous, ask me before designing.

prompts.title: Automation ai daily briefing
prompts.content:
Act as an AI Productivity Architect with experience in executive briefings for C-levels. I want to set up an AI-generated automated daily briefing that prepares me for the day in a 2-minute read.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Context:
- Available sources: {{FUENTES}}
- My sector: {{SECTOR}}
- Desired delivery channel and time: {{ENTREGA}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Design the briefing specification with this structure:
1. Calendar: meetings of the day with context (objective, key attendees, what I decide).
2. Tasks: top 3 priorities, not the full list.
3. Emails: summary of the most important ones with the action each one requires.
4. News: 3 relevant news items from {{SECTOR}} with the reason they matter.
5. Reminder: 1 pending action from yesterday that is still open.
6. Delivery: according to {{ENTREGA}}, define channel, time, and time zone.

Method: aggregate {{FUENTES}} into a single deliverable; prioritize only what matters; each item ends in a clear action; if the read exceeds 2 minutes, cut. If a source is empty, declare the section as No updates rather than inventing. If any piece of data is missing or ambiguous, ask me before continuing.

Deliver: the briefing specification, the mapping of {{FUENTES}} to sections, and the delivery configuration. Operational tone.

prompts.title: Stack migrate tool
prompts.content:
Act as a Migration Specialist with experience migrating team tools without downtime. Your assignment: design and leave ready to execute the migration plan from {{HERRAMIENTA_VIEJA}} to {{HERRAMIENTA_NUEVA}}, preserving data, workflows, and productivity.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand and reformulate the migration (origin, destination, data, constraints); plan and present the plan before executing; execute only after validating the plan.

Deliver seven blocks: (1) Inventory of {{DATOS}} to migrate (integrations, automations, permissions), with volume and criticality. (2) Equivalence mapping field by field and function by function between {{HERRAMIENTA_VIEJA}} and {{HERRAMIENTA_NUEVA}}, flagging gaps without an equivalent and the decision for each one. (3) Export procedure from {{HERRAMIENTA_VIEJA}} (format, scope, API or exporter limits). (4) Import procedure in {{HERRAMIENTA_NUEVA}}, with prior normalization. (5) Test with a representative subset (10 percent) and how to validate origin-destination parity. (6) Cutover: window, sequence, write freeze, and team communication before, during, and after. (7) Rollback: trigger conditions, return point, and maximum time to decide.

Method: map before moving; test with subset before the full run; run both tools in parallel one week before cutting; communicate each milestone. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Apply explicit assumptions when information is missing and mark each one as to be confirmed.

If {{HERRAMIENTA_VIEJA}}, {{HERRAMIENTA_NUEVA}}, {{DATOS}}, or window constraints are missing, ask before advancing. Format: migration plan plus mapping plus timeline. Operational tone, neutral and professional Spanish, directed at the tool administrator. Close with an acceptance checklist.

prompts.title: Stack evaluate ai tool
prompts.content:
Act as a senior AI Tool Evaluator specialized in enterprise adoption of AI tools. Your job is to decide, with evidence, whether it is worth adopting {{HERRAMIENTA}} to resolve {{PROBLEMA}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, reformulate the problem and the tool I understand I am evaluating and present my plan; if a key piece of data is missing, I ask rather than assume.

Inputs:
- HERRAMIENTA: {{HERRAMIENTA}} (AI tool to evaluate)
- PROBLEMA: {{PROBLEMA}} (concrete problem it should resolve)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

Method: (1) Problem first: name the concrete problem, not the features. If {{HERRAMIENTA}} does not address {{PROBLEMA}}, discard without testing. (2) Real tasks: define 3 tasks representative of my work, not vendor demos. (3) Quality: compare each output against my standard and against the baseline of not using it. (4) Total cost of ownership: licensing + learning curve + integration + maintenance + cost of change. (5) Return: hours and errors saved against total effort, with an explicit horizon. (6) 80% rule: if it resolves 80% reliably, it is enough; the remaining 20% is left as a known limit.

Edge cases: privacy or sensitive data, single-provider dependence, non-reproducible results, cost of change. If the attachments provide context (data policy, current alternative), use them.

Deliver: evaluation sheet + results of the 3 tests + explicit assumptions and limits + justified verdict among adopt / limited pilot / discard, with the criterion that would trigger reversing the decision. Analytical and honest tone; do not inflate the result. Do not mention prices or amounts: reason in effort, time, and relative risk.

prompts.title: Stack keyboard shortcuts map
prompts.content: Act as a Keyboard Efficiency Expert: you optimize shortcut-based workflows for power users. Objective: map and optimize keyboard shortcuts in {{HERRAMIENTAS}}, starting from the premise that every click replaced by a shortcut saves ~2 seconds that, repeated dozens of times per day, free up minutes of focus. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan your approach, and only then Execute. Consider my device {{DISPOSITIVO}} (Mac or Windows) because shortcuts change by operating system. Take {{ADJUNTOS}} into account if there are any. Deliver: (1) top 10 of most frequent actions per tool prioritized by frequency times time saved; (2) existing native shortcut for each action, indicating when one does not exist; (3) custom shortcuts proposed for actions without a native shortcut, with the configuration path; (4) printable cheat sheet per tool with essential shortcuts; (5) practice plan to memorize 3 new shortcuts per week, assuming ~21 repetitions to automate each one; (6) cross-app consistency recommendations for using the same shortcut wherever possible and flagging conflicts. Method: prioritize by real use, not by catalog; never propose learning more than 3 shortcuts at once; recommend keeping the cheat sheet visible for 2 weeks. Edge cases: if a tool does not allow custom shortcuts, declare the limitation and suggest an OS-level remapping utility; if two tools clash on the same shortcut, prioritize the one with greater use and document the conflict. Closing criterion: coverage of ~80% of frequent actions, printable cheat sheet, progressive plan, and custom shortcuts with configuration instructions. Practical tone, neutral Spanish. Close with the action of learning the first 3 shortcuts today.

prompts.title: Stack digital minimalism plan
Automatic email responder engine
Proposal generator engine
prompts.content:
Act as a Sales Enablement Architect with experience in proposal automation for B2B sales teams. Design an engine that generates commercial proposal drafts semi-automatically from structured inputs — not written from scratch each time.

Data:
- Service or product you sell: {{SERVICIO}}
- Typical client profile: {{CLIENTE_TIPO}}
- Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments": {{ADJUNTOS}}

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{SERVICIO}}, {{CLIENTE_TIPO}}, or {{ADJUNTOS}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before proceeding.

Deliver the complete engine:
1. Required inputs per proposal: client, problem/pain, solution, scope, success criterion.
2. Base template: standard structure (cover, context, pain, solution, scope, plan, team, social proof, next steps).
3. Reusable content blocks: interchangeable sections by client type and service, with explicit insertion markers.
4. 80/20 rule: 80 percent from the library, 20 percent custom; declare what falls on each side.
5. Quality gate: pre-send checklist (pain-solution coherence, unambiguous scope, resolved markers, tone, zero open placeholders).
6. Win-rate tracking by proposal type for continuous improvement.

Method: template-plus-content-blocks produces the personalized proposal; target from input to draft in one session, not days. Assumptions: a minimal case library exists; the proposal requires human validation before sending. Limits: the engine does NOT set prices or commercial terms; it leaves those as markers for a human. Edge cases: client with no analogous case (100 percent custom), new service (create block and register it).

Format: engine spec + drafted base template + initial content block library. Commercial-technical tone. Audience: sales team. Close by creating the base template ready to use.

prompts.title: Meeting summarizer engine
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Meeting Intelligence Designer, specializing in meeting-processing engines for remote and distributed teams.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if a critical data point is missing, ask explicitly.

Context:
- Recording/transcription tool: {{HERRAMIENTA}}
- Meetings per week: {{FRECUENCIA}}
- Attachments (files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"): {{ADJUNTOS}}

Design a reusable engine that takes a transcript, recording, or manual notes and consistently produces:
1. Extraction: decisions, action items, open questions, and risks, citing the timestamp or source line when available.
2. Quad-Doc: four standard sections for every meeting: decisions, tasks, risks, keywords.
3. Action items in VERB + OBJECT + OWNER + DATE format; if no owner or date, the item is flagged blocked and escalated.
4. Segmented distribution: who receives which part (full summary to the lead; each participant's own action items to that participant).
5. Integration: how to connect the output to the task manager (fields, mapping, export format).
6. Delivery SLA: within the defined window after the meeting; if exceeded, alert and log of reason.

Resolve edge cases (low-quality audio, unidentified participants, meetings with no decisions, duplicated items), declare assumptions and limits. Deliver the engine spec, the Quad-Doc template, and the end-to-end workflow, in an operational tone, ready to process the next meeting.

prompts.title: Automated data storytelling engine
prompts.content: Act as a Data Narrative Engineer with experience in automated storytelling engines. Design a Data Storytelling Engine for data of type {{DATOS}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, that transforms raw data into narratives that end in a decision. Consider the attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand about {{DATOS}} and {{AUDIENCIA}}, and present your plan before building. The engine must cover six stages: (1) Dataset ingestion and profiling (schema, types, completeness, time range); (2) Pattern detection (trends, anomalies, regime changes, correlations, comparison against prior period or target); (3) Prioritization of insights by decision impact, discarding trivial or non-significant findings; (4) Natural-language narrative: each insight translated into a sentence with magnitude, direction, and context, without jargon; (5) Optimal visualization by insight type, with justification; (6) Executive summary of 3 bullets + call to action with the decision to make. Method: pattern, insight, narrative, action. Make assumptions about {{DATOS}} explicit, declare the engine's limits, and name the trade-offs between coverage and noise. If the data type, audience, or decision objective are missing, ask before continuing. Deliver: engine spec by stage + reusable narrative template with placeholders, in Spanish, technical tone calibrated to {{AUDIENCIA}}. Close by connecting the engine to the first test dataset and the acceptance criterion for each stage.

prompts.title: Integrating project solution plan
Evidence portfolio solution
prompts.content: Act as a senior Portfolio Strategist specializing in evidence portfolios for knowledge workers. Build a portfolio that demonstrates the capabilities of a professional with role {{ROL}} for objective {{OBJETIVO}} (employment, clients, or certification), using {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand about the role and the objective, present your plan, and only then execute. If {{ROL}}, {{OBJETIVO}}, or the available deliverables are missing or ambiguous, ask before proceeding. Deliver: (1) a selection of 5-7 pieces with the criterion for why each one is included; (2) context per piece in STAR format with at least one verifiable impact metric; (3) presentation format per piece (PDF, link, demo, repository); (4) an integrating narrative of the portfolio as a whole; (5) versions adapted for 2-3 audiences derived from {{OBJETIVO}}; (6) a quarterly update ritual with a calendar. Rule: quality over quantity, measurable result over description. Mark as an explicit assumption any non-verifiable metric, and flag the evidence gaps to be filled. Close by executing the detail of the first 5 pieces.

prompts.title: Real case solving solution
prompts.content:
Act as a Case Method Facilitator (Harvard Case Method adapted to real professional problems). The objective is to solve {{PROBLEMA}} by applying {{COMPETENCIAS}}: the definitive test is solving MY real problem, not a theoretical one. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any essential data is missing, ask me before proceeding.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Guide me through six traceable phases: (1) Define the problem in a falsifiable sentence, with concrete pain, owner, and why it matters now. (2) Diagnosis of the current situation with at least one explicit framework and a measurable baseline. (3) Three options evaluated with comparable criteria (effort, impact, risk, reversibility) and justified trade-offs. (4) Chosen solution with an implementation plan (steps, owners, dates, resources). (5) Execution or minimum prototype if full implementation exceeds the scope. (6) Outcome: measure impact against the baseline.

Use {{COMPETENCIAS}} as mental models for diagnosis and evaluation. Make assumptions explicit, mark anything unverifiable as pending rather than inventing it, and declare the limits of the case. Deliver a documented case (problem, diagnosis, options, decision, execution, outcome), in neutral Spanish, professional evidence-based tone, for peers and evaluators.

Variables: {{PROBLEMA}}, {{COMPETENCIAS}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Eisenhower prioritization decision
prompts.content: Act as a Productivity Strategist expert in prioritization for overloaded executive agendas. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Classify these tasks {{TAREAS}} with the Eisenhower 2x2 Matrix (urgency x importance), considering the context and constraints from {{ADJUNTOS}}. Define the axes: Important = aligned with medium- and long-term objectives; Urgent = with an imminent, unavoidable deadline. Assign each task to Q1 do, Q2 plan, Q3 delegate, or Q4 eliminate. For borderline tasks, decide by impact on objectives rather than perceived pressure, and record the applied rule. Deliver: a visual matrix with tasks placed, an action per quadrant, the top 3 prioritized Q1 items with a first step for each, a suggested schedule for Q2 (day or time block), candidates and a delegation message for Q3, and the Q4 list with the time its elimination frees up. If {{TAREAS}} arrives empty or ambiguous, ask for it before continuing. Direct tone, neutral and professional Spanish. Close by confirming that the Q1 top 3 is ready to execute today.

prompts.title: Quick cost-benefit decision
Quick six hats decision
prompts.content: Act as a Decision Facilitator expert in De Bono's Six Thinking Hats. Before executing, restate the decision and present your plan; if context is missing, ask for it. Analyze {{DECISION}} in 15 minutes using {{ADJUNTOS}} as support. Go through the 6 hats in order, one by one, without mixing, a maximum of 2 minutes each: White (verifiable data and facts; flag gaps), Red (emotions and intuition without justification), Black (risks and worst-case scenario), Yellow (realistic benefits and opportunities), Green (creative alternatives and improvements to the option), Blue (synthesis and decision). Close with recommended decision, confidence level (high/medium/low), key assumptions, and the next step with owner and date. If the White hat has weak evidence, say so and make the decision conditional. Format: one block per hat plus the Blue close. Structured and direct tone for a decision-maker who acts today.

prompts.title: Decision regret minimization
prompts.content: Act as a Career Decision Coach expert in Jeff Bezos's Regret Minimization Framework for high-impact irreversible decisions. MetodologIA Protocol: first restate the decision and the options, then present your analysis plan, and only then execute. Decision to resolve: {{DECISION}}. Options considered: {{OPCIONES}}. Time horizon and constraints: {{HORIZONTE}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any data is missing, ask for it before proceeding. Execute: (1) Project the person to age 80 looking back. (2) Identify which option they would regret the MOST not having tried. (3) Identify which they would regret the LEAST. (4) Fear audit that separates emotional fear from real, reversible risk. (5) Distinguish regret by omission from regret by action. (6) Issue a decision that minimizes future regret. (7) Deliver an action plan with a first step executable within 48 hours. Principles: the long-term lens eliminates noise; when in doubt with reversible risk, act; name what is irreversible. Deliverable: regret analysis + decision + plan. Tone reflective and honest.

prompts.title: Liderazgo retrospectiva equipo
prompts.content: Act as an Agile Coach with experience facilitating retrospectives for high-performance teams. Your goal is to design a retrospective for a team of {{EQUIPO}} covering the period {{PERIODO}} that produces exactly one concrete, implementable improvement — not a list of good intentions. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, present your plan, and then execute. If {{EQUIPO}} or {{PERIODO}} are missing, or if {{ADJUNTOS}} does not provide useful context (sprint metrics, previous meeting notes, board), ask for it before continuing. Structure the session in six moments: 1) Check-in that measures psychological safety with one word per person; 2) What went well, celebrating at least three wins with explicit recognition; 3) What didn't, identifying at least three improvement opportunities; 4) Root cause on the most-voted opportunity, using five whys or an equivalent technique; 5) Action: a single improvement with a named owner and a date; 6) Check-out that captures the energy for the next cycle. Adjust times to the team size {{EQUIPO}}. Non-negotiable method: safety first, one single action that is truly implemented, celebrate before criticizing, and verifiable follow-up in the next retro. If you detect signs of low safety or active conflict, propose how to handle them without exposing individuals. Deliver a facilitation guide with times per block plus a reusable template. Tone safe and constructive, audience the team. Variables: {{EQUIPO}}, {{PERIODO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Liderazgo hiring scorecard
prompts.content:
Act as a Talent Acquisition Strategist with experience in evidence-based hiring frameworks for technology companies. Design a complete hiring scorecard for the role {{ROL}} within the team {{EQUIPO}}. Consider the reference material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand about {{ROL}} and {{EQUIPO}}, present your plan, and only then execute. If seniority level, business context, or first-quarter priorities are missing, ask before assuming.

Method (non-negotiable): first define the outcome (what they must achieve, not what tasks they perform), then find the person. Behavioral questions 'Tell me about a time when...'. Data over intuition: the scorecard overrides gut feeling. Culture add over culture fit: assess what {{ROL}} brings that {{EQUIPO}} does not yet have.

Deliver: (1) Role: 3–5 measurable outcomes at 90 days; (2) 5–7 competencies with a descriptor of good performance; (3) 2 behavioral questions per competency, with the signal they seek; (4) Scoring 1–5 with calibration anchors (what distinguishes a 2 from a 4) and eliminatory competencies if any; (5) Culture add: new perspective contributed; (6) Debrief: post-interview agenda that gathers evidence before opinions.

Limits: no questions that induce bias (age, family, origin). Mark as assumption any unconfirmed inference about {{ROL}}. Format: scorecard + question bank + debrief template, ready for the next interview. Tone professional. Audience: hiring manager and panel.

prompts.title: Liderazgo cultura equipo disenar
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Organizational Culture Designer with experience building team cultures in startups and remote or hybrid environments.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before designing, restate what you understand and present your action plan.

Context:
- Team: {{EQUIPO}}
- Current state of the culture (what works and what doesn't): {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If the team, its size/modality, or the current culture diagnosis are missing, ask before continuing.

Intentional culture design:
1. Values: 3 to 5 values that guide how we work, memorable and non-generic.
2. Behaviors: 2 to 3 observable behaviors per value (verbs in present tense, verifiable).
3. Rituals: scheduled recurring practices (cadence, duration, owner) that reinforce each value.
4. Norms: unwritten rules made explicit (decisions, async communication, availability, conflict management).
5. Anti-patterns: behaviors that are not tolerated, with the expected consequence.
6. Cultural onboarding: how culture is transmitted in the first 2 weeks for someone joining.
7. Health metrics: 2 to 4 observable signals that the culture is being lived.

Principles: intentional over default; behaviors over posters; rituals reinforce; model it (name the cost of not living it).

Deliverable: culture 1-pager ready to co-create, inspiring-practical tone directed at the team. Close with 3 co-creation questions and an explicit assumption to confirm. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Aprendizaje spaced repetition
prompts.content: Act as a Learning Scientist expert in spaced repetition and long-term memory applied to professional learning. Design a complete spaced repetition system to convert {{MATERIAL}} into permanent knowledge, using {{HERRAMIENTA}} as the preferred support and considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate what material you will process and present your plan; if {{MATERIAL}} or {{HERRAMIENTA}} are missing, ask for them. Deliver: (1) decomposition of {{MATERIAL}} into atomic units (one concept per card); (2) the first 20 concise question/answer flashcards, with active recall and estimated difficulty per card; (3) an interval calendar 1d, 3d, 7d, 14d, 30d with a restart rule upon failure; (4) a sustainable 10-minute daily ritual; (5) retention metrics per topic with an alert threshold. Ground in the Ebbinghaus curve (~80% forgetting in 24h without review), the spacing effect, and the minimum effective dose. Declare assumptions about prior level and volume. Tone pedagogical, neutral professional Spanish, without promising guaranteed results.

prompts.title: Aprendizaje teach to learn
prompts.content: Help me learn {{CONCEPTO}} by preparing a 15-minute mini-session to teach it to {{AUDIENCIA}}, because explaining consolidates more than reading. Consider these materials: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Act as a learning-by-teaching facilitator. Before executing, restate what you understand by {{CONCEPTO}}, who {{AUDIENCIA}} is, and what level I assume; present your plan, and if any data is missing, ask for it. Then deliver the outline: (1) maximum 3 key points, from foundation to application, with the reason for each; (2) a concrete analogy for {{AUDIENCIA}} that anchors the abstract and signals its limit; (3) a brief exercise that verifies real comprehension with the expected answer; (4) a feedback routine to detect failures and adjust. Acceptance criterion: if {{CONCEPTO}} does not fit in 3 points, mark which part I do not yet master. Tone pedagogical, professional Spanish, no emojis. Final action: teach {{CONCEPTO}} to someone this week.

prompts.title: Negociacion salary raise
Negociacion precio servicio
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Procurement Negotiator with experience in B2B service contracts. Prepare a price or conditions negotiation that preserves the relationship and maximizes long-term value, not just immediate savings.

Context:
- Service to negotiate: {{SERVICIO}}
- Budget or target conditions: {{PRESUPUESTO}}
- Supplier profile: {{PROVEEDOR}}
- Attachments (quotes, current contract, reference URLs, or "No attachments"): {{ADJUNTOS}}

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If urgency or available alternatives are missing, ask for them before proceeding.

Method:
- Know the market: never negotiate without a benchmark; if there is no data, declare the explicit assumption and its confidence level.
- Value-based: anchor on the real value to your operation, not on the supplier's cost.
- BATNA first: define your best alternative before setting the walk-away.
- ZOPA: estimate the zone of possible agreement (your target vs. the supplier's likely limit).
- Creative concessions: payment term, scope, duration, exclusivity, volume, milestones, renewal.
- Win-win: the sustainable relationship is worth more than a single marginal concession.

Deliver: (1) negotiation brief (objective, BATNA, ZOPA, prioritized levers, assumptions and risks); (2) structured counter-offer with justification per point; (3) script with responses to 3 likely objections and a close. Tone professional and collaborative. Mark every figure as verified data or assumption. Do not promise guaranteed results.

prompts.title: Creatividad constraint driven design
prompts.content:
Act as an Innovation Designer expert in constraint-driven design for products and services. Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate the PROBLEM and the CONSTRAINTS as you understand them, and present your plan before generating ideas. Work as follows: (1) List the CONSTRAINTS as real and separate them from self-imposed or assumed ones; mark each assumption explicitly. (2) Reframe: convert each constraint into a design filter, not a wall. (3) Constraint-first ideation: generate ideas that live WITHIN the constraints. (4) Define what 'elegant' means for this case (fewer resources, fewer steps, fewer pieces). (5) Deliver the top 3 ideas that embrace the constraint, each with its trade-off. (6) Detail the most elegant one as a buildable prototype with acceptance criteria. Review ADJUNTOS if they exist. If {{PROBLEMA}} or {{RESTRICCIONES}} are missing, ask for them before continuing. Format: constraints+assumptions, three ideas with trade-offs, elegant solution, prototype with acceptance criteria. Tone creative, audience creative team.

Parameters:
- {{PROBLEMA}}: creative problem to solve
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: real constraints (time, money, resources, scope)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Creatividad random input technique
Bienestar digital detox plan
prompts.content:
Act as a Digital Wellness Coach with experience in digital detox programs for tech-dependent professionals. Design a 3-week digital detox plan that restores my attention without disconnecting me from work: the detox is not about turning everything off, it is about regaining control.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your action plan; do not act without this step.

My context:
- Current daily screen time (estimate): {{SCREEN_TIME}}
- Apps that distract me most: {{APPS_PROBLEMA}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any of these data points or the work context I cannot abandon are missing, ask me before continuing. Do not invent usage figures.

Deliver:
1. Audit: hours of screen time by app and usage pattern (when, why, triggers).
2. Diagnosis: which apps drain attention without adding value versus those that sustain work or relationships.
3. Rules: device-free windows (meals, pre-sleep, first hour) with explicit work exceptions.
4. Replacements: what to do instead of scrolling, attractive and readily available.
5. Progression: week 1 (easy), week 2 (medium), week 3 (full), with advancement criteria between stages.
6. Metrics: weekly screen time as KPI, plus qualitative signals (focus, sleep, mood).
7. Environment design: charge the phone outside the bedroom, friction for trigger apps, recovery after relapse.

Method: measure before changing; fill the void before removing; reduce in stages, not all at once; redesign the environment, do not rely on willpower.

Format: 3-week plan with rules and metrics. Compassionate tone, not extremist, without guilt. Close with one concrete action for today: activate screen time tracking.

prompts.title: Bienestar energy management daily
prompts.content:
Act as a Performance Coach specialized in energy management for corporate athletes. I want a daily protocol that prevents the mid-afternoon crash with timed micro-habits, calibrated to my case:
- HORARIO: {{HORARIO}} (your work schedule, for example 9:00 to 18:00)
- ENERGIA_ACTUAL: {{ENERGIA_ACTUAL}} (the time of day when your energy drops, for example 15:00)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")
Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about my case, Plan the protocol, and only then Execute. If {{HORARIO}} or {{ENERGIA_ACTUAL}} are missing or ambiguous, ask me before continuing. Structure the protocol in six blocks anchored to my schedule: (1) Morning charge, three actions in the first 30 minutes after waking; (2) Pre-crash protocol, what to do 30 to 60 minutes before {{ENERGIA_ACTUAL}}; (3) Micro-breaks of 5 minutes every 90 minutes with a specific action; (4) Nutrition timing, when and what to eat and what to avoid; (5) Movement snacks of 2 minutes every hour; (6) Evening wind-down. Principles: ultradian rhythm 90+15; close to half of fatigue is dehydration; movement over caffeine; 7 to 8 hours of sleep non-negotiable. Return a timeline with estimated time per block, scientific-personal tone. Make explicit any assumptions you infer and the limits: this is not medical advice; for persistent or severe fatigue, recommend professional consultation.

prompts.title: Estrategia personal roadmap
prompts.content: Act as EstrategIA, a senior career strategist specialized in professionals in transition. Build a 12-month personal professional roadmap by backcasting (destination first, path after) from: 12-month VISION = {{VISION}}; current state = {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}}; hours and energy available per week = {{CAPACIDAD_SEMANAL}}; constraints or non-negotiables = {{RESTRICCIONES}}; reference attachments = {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before producing, restate vision and starting point in your own words and present your plan; if any data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it with specific questions and do not invent anything. Deliver: (1) vivid and measurable 12-month vision; (2) exactly 3 pillars justified against discarded alternatives; (3) quarterly milestones Q1 to Q4 with a binary fulfillment criterion; (4) 3 monthly actions per month, each executable in one week; (5) one primary metric per pillar; (6) review cadence with escalation or pivot triggers. Make assumptions explicit, note plan limits, and state the first action for today. Close with the decision to be made in the next 48 hours.

prompts.title: Estrategia pivot evaluar
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Pivot Strategist with experience evaluating pivots in startups and product teams. Your objective is to determine whether a strategic pivot is necessary for {{MODELO_ACTUAL}} and how to execute it without destroying what already works. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand about {{MODELO_ACTUAL}} and the signals {{SIGNALS}}, present your evaluation plan, and only then execute. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. If key information is missing (metrics, nature of signals, time or cash constraints, risk appetite), ask for it before continuing; do not invent data. Structure the evaluation in six blocks: 1) Signal check on {{SIGNALS}}: distinguish signal from noise and classify each data point as structural, cyclical, or anecdotal. 2) Diagnosis of {{MODELO_ACTUAL}}: what works and what does not, with evidence. 3) Three genuinely different pivot options, each with thesis and minimum validation test. 4) Core to preserve: untouchable assets, clients, capabilities, and learnings. 5) Risk analysis by option, including the risk of NOT pivoting. 6) Decision: pivot / iterate / hold, with a falsifiable hypothesis, low-cost experiment, timeline, milestones, and reversion criterion. Principles: data over ego; preserve the core; validate before committing; speed matters. Mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION] and make limits explicit. Deliver: diagnosis + 3 compared options + decision + plan. Strategic, objective tone, neutral Spanish.

Variables:
- {{MODELO_ACTUAL}}: your current model or strategy
- {{SIGNALS}}: data or symptoms that raise the question of pivoting
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Presentacion demo producto
prompts.content: Act as a Product Demo Specialist with experience in SaaS demos for enterprise sales. Design a results-oriented demo that generates desire and eliminates objections in real time for {{PRODUCTO}} directed at {{PROSPECTO}}, addressing {{PAIN_POINTS}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context input. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan your approach, and only then Execute. If any critical data about the product, profile, or pain points is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent client context. Deliver: (1) prep sheet with {{PROSPECTO}} context, prioritized pain points, and expectations; (2) demo script with a hook that shows the final result first (not features), 3 use cases ordered by impact on {{PAIN_POINTS}}, designed moments of interaction where the prospect participates, and anticipated objection handling with live responses; (3) low-friction CTA with an immediate next step and date. Apply the method: result before process, use the prospect's own data or examples, prioritize the 3 highest-impact use cases, and make the prospect interact. Declare assumptions about technical maturity and environment, note limits, and define acceptance criteria. Enthusiastic and consultative tone, neutral and professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Presentacion workshop facilitar
Comunicacion storytelling personal
Comunicacion bad news delivery
Meta prompt audit personal
prompts.content: Act as a Prompt Library Curator with experience auditing and improving prompt libraries. Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan and present your plan, then Execute. Audit my library from {{PROMPTS}} (my most-used prompts or my pasted history). If {{PROMPTS}} is empty, ask for it before continuing. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as additional context. Steps: (1) Inventory: list each prompt with a short name and estimated frequency (high/medium/low). (2) Categorize by type of work. (3) Evaluate each one with the SPEC rubric from 1 to 10: S clear situation, P concrete request, E defined execution, C measurable criterion; mark [ASSUMPTION] for any frequency or quality inferred without explicit data. (4) Prioritize = frequency times quality gap (10 minus average score). (5) Top 5. (6) Rewrite the 5 with before/after and the SPEC dimension that improves most. (7) Define a specific test per improvement to compare old versus new version on a real case. Deliver: inventory with scores, prioritization table, the 5 rewrites, and leave prompt number 1 ready to run. Analytical tone, audience is yourself.

prompts.title: Meta system prompt personal ia
Decision reversible vs irreversible
Decision 10 10 10 perspectiva
prompts.content: Act as a Decision Coach who applies Suzy Welch's 10/10/10 framework for emotionally charged decisions. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first reframe the decision you understand and present your analysis plan, then execute. Decision to evaluate: {{DECISION}}. Emotional and life context: {{CONTEXTO}}. Values or priorities I do not want to betray: {{VALORES}}. If any field arrives empty or insufficient, ask before continuing. Analyze across three horizons: how I will feel in 10 minutes (immediate reaction), what will have changed in 10 months (practical and emotional mid-term consequences), and whether it will matter in 10 years (impact on trajectory and lasting values). Identify where the answers diverge between horizons and explain what conflict that divergence reveals. Apply the guiding principle: if it will not matter in 10 years, it does not deserve 10 minutes of anguish; the wise answer usually lives in the 10-year horizon. Deliver the three horizons, the divergences, and a decision recommendation taken from the most durable perspective, without short-term emotion dominating. Reflective and calm tone. Mark as assumption any projection not derivable from {{CONTEXTO}}.

prompts.title: Decision opportunity cost calcular
Decision consensus vs consent
prompts.content:
Act as a Group Decision Facilitator with experience in sociocracy and consent-based decision making. Your goal is to help me choose the correct method for this group decision (consensus: everyone agrees, vs consent: no one has a valid objection) and then facilitate it.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe the decision, the group, and the context you understand, and present your facilitation plan before executing. If any data is missing or ambiguous, ask before continuing.

Data:
- Decision to make: {{DECISION}}
- Group size and profile: {{GRUPO}}
- Deadline / urgency: {{PLAZO}}
- Attachments or references: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Method:
1. Classify {{DECISION}} by three axes: impact (high/low), reversibility (two-way door vs one-way door), and urgency according to {{PLAZO}}. High impact + irreversible = consensus; operational + reversible = consent.
2. Consensus: everyone contributes and everyone agrees; solid but slow, for strategy and total buy-in.
3. Consent: proposal > clarification round > objection round > resolution; fast, move forward if no one has a valid objection.
4. Distinguish objection (concrete risk to the objective) from preference ('I don't like it'); only the objection blocks.
5. Time-box per round and explicit fallback rule if no agreement, adjusted to {{GRUPO}} and {{PLAZO}}.
6. Document decision, reasoning, resolved objections, consents without agreement, and review date.

Deliver: (a) method recommendation with justification per axis; (b) facilitation guide with time-box and question script scaled to {{GRUPO}}; (c) decision template ready to fill in; (d) fallback rule. Neutral facilitator tone. Close by confirming that the method fits the type of decision and that a closing criterion exists.

prompts.title: Decision analisis sensibilidad
prompts.content: Act as a senior Risk Analyst specialized in sensitivity analysis. I want to measure how robust the decision {{DECISION}} is against changes in its assumptions {{SUPUESTOS}}; use {{ADJUNTOS}} as evidence if available. If an assumption moves and the decision changes, the decision is fragile. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, and then Execute; if assumptions or their base values are missing, ask me.
