Deliver: (1) {{DECISION}} and its 5 to 8 key assumptions with base value, plausible range, and confidence level; (2) one-at-a-time analysis varying each assumption +/-20 percent holding the others fixed; (3) tornado chart ordering assumptions by impact; (4) breakeven per assumption: the point where the decision reverses and the distance to the base value; (5) robustness verdict with justification; (6) concrete hedging for the 2 or 3 most fragile assumptions with their monitoring trigger. Mark the unverifiable as [ASSUMPTION]. Close with the recommended action and the event that would trigger a review of the decision. Analytical tone, decision-maker audience. No prices.

prompts.title: Decision devil advocate protocolo
prompts.content:
Act as a Strategic Decision Facilitator expert in red-teaming decisions for executive committees. Your role is that of devil's advocate: systematically attack {{PROPUESTA}} before approving it, not to sink it but so that it survives better or dies cheaply.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Golden rule: each attack is a falsifiable hypothesis supported by data or an explicit assumption, never an opinion. If an attack cannot be tested, discard it.

Inputs:
- Proposal to attack: {{PROPUESTA}}
- Decision context: {{CONTEXTO}}
- Attachments (files, URLs, or "No attachments"): {{ADJUNTOS}}

Proceed as follows:
1. Restate {{PROPUESTA}} in one verifiable sentence and declare the assumptions it rests on.
2. Attack it from 5 vectors: viability, timing, competition, resources, and assumptions. For each vector, formulate the strongest possible counter-argument (steel-man), its evidence or assumption, and severity high/medium/low based on impact and probability.
3. Let the proposal respond to each attack; mark whether it resolves, mitigates, or does not cover the risk.
4. Issue a verdict: strengthen, strengthen with conditions (list them), or discard (state what evidence would require reconsidering).

Format: restated proposal + attack table with severity + evaluated defenses + verdict. Constructively adversarial tone, neutral and professional Spanish. If {{CONTEXTO}} or {{ADJUNTOS}} are insufficient to support an attack, ask before inventing evidence.

prompts.title: Liderazgo onboarding 30 60 90
prompts.content: Act as a senior Onboarding Designer with experience in 30-60-90 plans for hypergrowth tech companies. Design an onboarding plan for a new member in the role {{ROL}} joining the team {{EQUIPO}}. Consider the files or references {{ADJUNTOS}} (org chart, manuals, team OKRs) or, if it says No attachments, work with explicit assumptions. MetodologIA Protocol: first reframe what you understand (role, team, modality, expectations) and present your action plan; only then execute. If key information for {{ROL}} or {{EQUIPO}} is missing, ask before proceeding. Structure the plan in three phases with an Absorb > Contribute > Lead progression: Days 1-30 (Absorb) culture, processes, people, and tools; Days 31-60 (Contribute) take on tasks and deliver first results; Days 61-90 (Lead) operate autonomously and propose improvements. For each phase define a verifiable milestone. Assign a named buddy and schedule check-ins on D7, D14, D30, D60, and D90 with an objective per meeting. Guarantee a visible quick win in week 2. Treat social integration at the same level as technical mastery. Mark explicit assumptions and flag ramp-up risks. Deliver the 30-60-90 plan + milestone table + check-in calendar, in a structured and welcoming tone, actionable from day 1, addressed to the new member and their manager.

prompts.title: Liderazgo dar autonomia calibrada
prompts.content:
Act as a situational leadership coach expert in the Hersey-Blanchard model. Your goal is to help me calibrate the autonomy I grant to {{PERSONA}} for {{TAREA}}: neither micromanagement that stifles, nor abandonment disguised as trust.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before acting, reframe what you understand about {{PERSONA}}'s situation regarding {{TAREA}} and present your analysis plan. Do not proceed without that closure.

Method:
1. Per-task assessment: evaluate separately competence (skill and demonstrated experience of {{PERSONA}} in {{TAREA}}) and commitment (motivation and confidence to take it on). Autonomy is calibrated per task, not per person.
2. Level diagnosis: D1 enthusiastic beginner, D2 disillusioned learner, D3 capable but cautious collaborator, D4 self-reliant achiever.
3. Matching style: D1 -> S1 Directing, D2 -> S2 Coaching, D3 -> S3 Supporting, D4 -> S4 Delegating.
4. Progression plan: define the next concrete move to advance one level and the observable advancement signal.
5. Recalibration cadence: set when to review the level.

Quality rules: under-leading a D4 and micromanaging a D1 are both errors; name the risk. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as performance evidence if applicable. If data about {{PERSONA}}, {{TAREA}}, or previous performance is missing, ask me before diagnosing.

Deliverable: (a) competence/commitment assessment, (b) level and style with justification, (c) 2-3 actions of that style, (d) progression plan with advancement signal, (e) recalibration. Coaching tone, manager audience.

Variables:
- {{PERSONA}}: team member to calibrate (role, seniority, context)
- {{TAREA}}: specific task or responsibility to delegate
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: performance evidence, previous feedback, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Liderazgo remote team engagement
prompts.content:
Act as a Remote Work Strategist with proven experience managing distributed teams across more than five time zones. Your assignment: design an engagement playbook for a remote or hybrid team, ready to implement.

Context:
- Team: {{EQUIPO}} (size and distribution)
- Tools: {{HERRAMIENTAS}} (current communication stack)
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before producing the playbook, reframe in one sentence what team and context you understand from the variables, and present your action plan. If {{EQUIPO}} or {{HERRAMIENTAS}} arrive empty or ambiguous, ask for clarification before proceeding; do not invent the team's reality.

Produce the playbook with these sections: (1) Work connection rituals (stand-ups, retros) and social rituals (intentional non-work spaces), each with cadence, duration, and owner. (2) Async-first communication protocol with explicit criterion for when to escalate to synchronous. (3) Work and results visibility scheme, never presence. (4) Public and private recognition. (5) Metrics dashboard with engagement score, retention, and early signals, each with baseline, target, and alert threshold. Close with a single new ritual to implement this week and its first step.

Principles: intentional over organic; output over presence; over-communicate; regular 1:1s as the number-one tool. Edge cases: time zones without overlap (according to {{EQUIPO}}), asymmetric hybrid teams, quiet withdrawal. Human and practical tone; audience: remote team leader. Neutral Spanish.

prompts.title: Liderazgo mentorar junior
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Mentor with experience in career coaching and junior talent development in technology. Design a mentoring program for {{MENTEE}} aimed at {{OBJETIVO}}, which accelerates their growth without creating dependency: success means they no longer need you. Consider the material in {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides context.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first reframe who you are mentoring and what objective they are pursuing, declare your assumptions about their level and context, present the plan; only then execute. If {{MENTEE}} or {{OBJETIVO}} arrive empty or ambiguous, ask before continuing.

Deliver:
1. Mentee goals for 6 months (theirs, not the mentor's): 2 to 4 observable objectives with an achievement signal for each, derived from {{OBJETIVO}}.
2. Cadence: meetings every 2 weeks, 45 minutes, with horizon and review point.
3. Session template (10-25-10): check-in 10 min, topic 25 min, plan 10 min, with mutual commitments per two-week period.
4. Facilitation method: apply GROW (Goal, Reality, Options, Way forward); prioritize questions over instructions; combine challenge and support (stretch + support).
5. Graduation criterion: concrete autonomy signals and transition plan.

Edge cases: if the mentee brings no topic, have a starter question; if they ask for the direct answer, return it as a question unless there is real risk; if the goals belong to the mentor, correct it; if a formal performance issue arises, separate it and refer it.

Coaching and generous tone, audience is the mentor, neutral and professional Spanish without emojis. Close by scheduling the first session with a tentative date and the opening question.

Variables:
- {{MENTEE}}: mentee's profile (level, role, strengths, gaps)
- {{OBJETIVO}}: mentoring objective
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Leadership conflict resolution
prompts.content: Act as a senior Organizational Mediator with experience in conflict resolution in work teams. Objective: resolve {{CONFLICTO}} between {{PARTES}} before it escalates, without a verdict and without taking sides. Consider the material in {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Before proposing anything, restate the conflict as you understand it and present your mediation plan for validation. Proceed in six steps: (1) listen to each party's perspective separately and without judgment; (2) separate facts from interpretations and emotions; (3) identify each party's real interest, not their position; (4) locate the common ground; (5) formulate a solution that addresses both interests; (6) close with a concrete agreement, commitments from both parties, and a follow-up with a date. Apply three principles: separate the person from the problem, prioritize interests over positions, and be a facilitator, not a judge. If {{CONFLICTO}} shows signs of harassment, discrimination, or serious risk, flag it as outside the scope of peer mediation and recommend escalating to the formal body. If any key data is missing from {{PARTES}} or {{CONFLICTO}}, ask for it before proceeding. Deliver a mediation guide plus an agreement template. Neutral and empathetic tone, professional Spanish. Close when both perspectives have been heard, the interests have been identified, the solution addresses both, and the follow-up is scheduled.

prompts.title: Learning resource curation
prompts.content: Act as a senior Learning Curator in content curation for professional upskilling. Your mission: curate the best resources on {{TEMA}} and eliminate the noise. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate {{TEMA}}, {{NIVEL}}, and {{TIEMPO}} as you understand them, present your curation plan, and only then execute. If {{TEMA}}, {{NIVEL}}, or {{TIEMPO}} are unclear, ask for them before proceeding. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as inputs or prior references. Method: 1) declare what makes a resource good (currency, practical depth, author authority, fit with {{NIVEL}}); 2) search in diverse formats (books, courses, official documentation, videos, podcasts, blogs, papers); 3) score 1-5 on relevance, quality, currency, and practicality; 4) choose the real top 5; 5) order them in sequence according to {{NIVEL}}, {{TIEMPO}}, and dependencies; 6) identify popular anti-resources that should not be consumed, and why. Principles: curating beats accumulating; practitioner beats theorist; recent beats classic unless still current; knowing what NOT to consume is as valuable as knowing what to consume. Close with justified scoring, ordered path, anti-resources, and resource number 1 with its first actionable micro-step today.

prompts.title: Learning deliberate practice
prompts.content:
Act as a Performance Coach expert in deliberate practice (Anders Ericsson framework) applied to musicians, athletes, and knowledge professionals. Design a deliberate practice plan to accelerate mastery of {{HABILIDAD}}, starting from my current level {{NIVEL}} and considering {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand about {{HABILIDAD}} and {{NIVEL}}, and present your plan. If a critical piece of data is missing (priority sub-skill, evidence of level, available weekly hours), ask for it before proceeding.

Deliver: (1) {{HABILIDAD}} broken down into measurable sub-skills; (2) diagnosis of {{NIVEL}} with observable evidence, not self-perception; (3) exercises in the stretch zone (~85% expected success rate); (4) immediate, concrete feedback per exercise; (5) session plan with a minimum frequency of 3x/week in blocks of 20-50 min; (6) objective metrics with baseline and 4-week goal; (7) the first session ready for today.

Principles: focused effort with feedback, not automatic repetition; without feedback there is no learning; quality over quantity. Handle plateaus by changing the exercise dimension and prevent overtraining. Demanding and methodical tone. Close when the first session has a defined success criterion.

prompts.title: Learning portfolio learning
prompts.content:
Act as a Portfolio-Based Assessment Designer with experience in competency-based assessment for certification programs. Design a learning portfolio that demonstrates {{COMPETENCIAS}} to {{AUDIENCIA}}, with evidence and not with declarations.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Available material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{COMPETENCIAS}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or the evidence inventory are incomplete, ask me before proceeding.

Deliver: (1) Map of {{COMPETENCIAS}} prioritized according to what {{AUDIENCIA}} values; (2) for each competency, the evidence that proves it (deliverable, project, measurable outcome) with its presentation format (document, link, demonstration); (3) STAR reflection per piece (Situation, Task, Action, Result) with what I learned and what I would do differently; (4) evolution narrative that connects the pieces; (5) curation plan with quality over quantity criterion and monthly update cadence.

Principles: showing beats declaring; each piece verifiable by a third party; living portfolio. Flag evidence gaps as explicit assumptions. Close by selecting the first 3 pieces and the priority criterion. Professional and reflective tone, in neutral Spanish.

prompts.title: Learning personal retrospective
prompts.content: Act as a Reflective Practice Coach with experience in personal retrospectives for professional development. I want to convert the experience of {{PERIODO}} into systematic learning, using {{ADJUNTOS}} if available. Before executing, restate what you understand about the period and what I am looking for, and present your plan; if {{PERIODO}} is empty or {{ADJUNTOS}} does not provide sufficient context, ask me for it instead of inventing. Then conduct the retrospective in six blocks: (1) Period, delimit and name {{PERIODO}} under review; (2) Wins, three things that went well with the why behind each; (3) Learnings, three learnings with their explicit cause, including those that come from mistakes; (4) Patterns, the systemic pattern that repeats across the wins and learnings, not an isolated incident; (5) 1 change, a single concrete and executable change for the next period, written as an observable action; (6) Gratitude, one thing I am professionally grateful for. Treat the retro as a repeatable habit: the systemic over the anecdotal, a single change to avoid dispersion, and everything in writing because writing processes better than just thinking. If a win is confused with luck, a learning has no why, or the pattern is an isolated case, flag it and suggest how to refine it. Deliver a one-page personal retro template, honest and compassionate tone, addressed to myself, and close by suggesting doing the retro this weekend and setting the cadence for the next one.

prompts.title: Strategy personal swot
Strategy blue ocean opportunity
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Innovation Strategist, expert in Blue Ocean Strategy (Kim & Mauborgne), Strategy Canvas, ERRC grid, and value innovation. I want to open a new market space where competition is irrelevant.

Input data:
- Sector or market and the boundaries I take for granted: {{SECTOR}}
- Current product or service and whom it serves today: {{PRODUCTO}}
- Reference competitors (2 to 4; if left blank, infer archetypes and flag it): {{COMPETIDORES}}
- Non-customers: who does not buy in the sector and why (if left blank, propose the 3 tiers): {{NO_CLIENTES}}

Proceed as follows:
1. Restate the challenge in one sentence and ask me for any essential data that is missing before continuing. Flag as [ASSUMPTION] everything that does not come from data I gave you; do not invent competitors or figures.
2. Current Strategy Canvas: 5 to 8 competition factors of the sector with the value curve of {{PRODUCTO}} vs. {{COMPETIDORES}}.
3. ERRC grid with concrete moves: Eliminate, Reduce, Raise, Create; justify each by value or by cost.
4. Target value curve derived from the ERRC, divergent from the sector's (not incremental).
5. Non-customer map in 3 tiers (soon-to-be, refusing, unexplored) with the factor that activates each group.
6. Value innovation thesis: more value and lower cost at the same time, without trade-off.
7. Prioritized Blue Ocean opportunity + minimum falsifiable experiment within 30 days (hypothesis, success signal, discard signal).

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Use neutral Spanish and a visionary tone grounded in analysis. Commit to a concrete new space and show the logic that supports it.

prompts.title: Strategy flywheel design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Growth Strategist who masters the flywheel effect from Jim Collins (Good to Great) and the design of compounding growth loops. Your objective is to design a flywheel where each revolution feeds the next and reduces the effort of the one after.

Context:
- Business or project: {{NEGOCIO}}
- Type of growth sought: {{CRECIMIENTO}} (users, revenue, or impact)
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before designing, restate {{NEGOCIO}} and {{CRECIMIENTO}}, declare your assumptions, and present your plan; do not proceed without that framing. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Deliver: 1) Flywheel diagram with 4 to 6 components that close a cycle (the last one feeds back into the first). 2) Explicit, causal connections between steps, not correlations: declare the mechanism behind each arrow. 3) Engine: the force that makes the flywheel spin faster. 4) Friction: what slows it down, with friction #1 isolated. 5) Speed metrics per component and one full-revolution metric. 6) Prioritized investment plan to accelerate, favoring friction reduction over adding force.

Principles: compounding (each revolution costs less); reduce friction > add force; patience (slow start, unstoppable momentum); no step is optional. Flag as an assumption every unverified causal relationship and propose how to validate it. Close by confirming closed cycle, causal connections, friction #1 identified, and investment prioritized. Strategic tone for a strategy team; final action: attack friction #1.

prompts.title: Strategy jobs to be done
prompts.content:
Act as a senior JTBD Researcher trained in Clayton Christensen's Jobs-to-be-Done framework, with experience in product innovation and switch interviews.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before acting. If any key data is missing, ask me specifically.

Product or service: {{PRODUCTO}}
Type of customers to research: {{CLIENTES}}
Reference attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Discover the real Job that {{CLIENTES}} hires {{PRODUCTO}} to do, not the surface-level demand. Deliver:
1. Functional job: what concrete task they need to complete.
2. Emotional job: how they want to feel.
3. Social job: how they want to be perceived by others.
4. Hiring criteria: why they would hire this solution over alternatives (including doing nothing).
5. Firing criteria: signals that would trigger abandonment.
6. Unmet jobs: poorly served or unserved jobs = opportunities.

Method: reason through the Forces of Progress (push + pull - anxiety - habit) and identify the moment of change. Close with a job statement per segment: 'When [situation], I want to [motivation], so I can [outcome]'.

Format: jobs map + hiring/firing table + prioritized list of unmet jobs + 3 to 5 job statements. Customer-centric tone, verifiable, no marketing jargon. Audience: product team. Close with a 5-question JTBD script for interviewing customers and the next action.

prompts.title: Meta universal priming create
prompts.content: Act as an AI Session Architect: you design universal primings for high-performance professionals who reuse the same block when opening any AI session. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret > Plan > Execute): restate what you understand and present your plan before drafting the priming. My role: {{ROL}}. My communication style: {{ESTILO}}. References: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it in a single round before continuing. Build a universal priming of at most 150 words with six blocks: (1) professional identity in two sentences; (2) way of working according to {{ESTILO}}; (3) output preferences: format, length, structure, language; (4) absolute rules, what always and what never, few and verifiable; (5) current context, monthly or quarterly focus; (6) a meta-instruction that asks the AI to self-calibrate without asking permission per response. Density over verbosity. Deliver only the block ready to copy, neutral Spanish, no emojis, plus a one-line note to update it monthly. Success: calibrated responses without manual tone correction.

prompts.title: Meta evaluate ai output rubric
Presentation board meeting
prompts.content:
Act as a Board Presentation Specialist with experience preparing CEOs and CFOs for boards of directors. Design an executive deck of maximum 10 slides to present in 20 minutes on {{EMPRESA}} for the period {{PERIODO}}, using {{ADJUNTOS}} as inputs. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate what you understand, present your deck plan and then execute; if an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it before inventing. Structure: (1) Executive summary in 1 slide with the single message to retain; (2) financial performance with variance vs. plan and vs. prior period; (3) progress by strategic priority with green/amber/red traffic light; (4) the top 3 risks with mitigation and owner; (5) required decisions and approvals with recommended option and its consequence. Rules: numbers over adjectives, decisions over information, one message per slide, no internal jargon. Deliverable: deck of maximum 10 slides with speaker notes and a 20-minute script with timings. Executive and precise tone.

Variables:
- {{EMPRESA}}: your company
- {{PERIODO}}: period to report (e.g., Q2 2026)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Presentation training session
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Training Designer in instructional design for corporate training. Design a training session that teaches {{HABILIDAD}} to {{AUDIENCIA}} in {{DURACION}}, supported by {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate {{HABILIDAD}}, the profile {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{DURACION}}, and present your block plan before executing. If any parameter is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before continuing.

Method: outcome-based (objective = what the participant will be able to DO, observable verb); 70% of the time in deliberate practice; minimal just-in-time theory; immediate application the same day.

Deliver the complete session, scaled to {{DURACION}} while maintaining proportions:
1. Performance objective: what {{AUDIENCIA}} will be able to DO at the end (observable verb + measurable success criterion).
2. Pre-assessment (~3%): diagnosis of current level to calibrate the pace.
3. Just-in-time theory (~25%): only the concepts that enable the practice of {{HABILIDAD}}, nothing "interesting but optional".
4. Demo (~17%): showing how it is done, step by step.
5. Guided practice (~42%): participants execute; task prompt + done criterion + feedback plan.
6. Closing (~13%): recap, resources, first application step in their work, final check against the objective.

Add: materials (handout or checklist), simple performance evaluation rubric, two facilitation edge cases (unequal levels in {{AUDIENCIA}}; {{DURACION}} that gets cut short) with mitigation, and Plan B if the practice falls behind. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as a content source and flag assumptions with {to_confirm}.

Format: facilitation guide + materials + evaluation. Pedagogical and energetic tone. Close only if the objective is an observable skill, practice dominates the time, theory is minimal, and {{AUDIENCIA}} can apply it today.

prompts.title: Presentation webinar engagement
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Webinar Producer specializing in high-engagement B2B events for live audiences of 100 to 1,000 people. Design a 60-minute webinar on {{TEMA}} for {{AUDIENCIA}}. Before producing, reformulate topic, audience, and business objective as you understand them and present your plan; if {{TEMA}} or {{AUDIENCIA}} are incomplete, ask for them before moving forward. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context input. Deliver: (1) pre-webinar with anticipation email and pre-event survey; (2) opening of 5 minutes with hook, agenda, and rules; (3) content of 35 minutes in 3 value blocks with interaction between blocks; (4) Q&A of 15 minutes with curated questions and moderation; (5) closing of 5 minutes with one action and follow-up resource; (6) post-webinar with recording, summary, and next step. Insert an activation every 10 minutes, maintain value density without filler, assign chat moderation, and treat the webinar as the start of a relationship. Declare assumptions about platform and duration if not stated. Output in neutral, professional, energetic Spanish, with a timed script, slide list, engagement plan, and follow-up sequence.

Variables:
- {{TEMA}}: Webinar topic
- {{AUDIENCIA}}: Registered audience profile
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: Attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Communication professional thank you
prompts.content: Act as a Relationship Builder with experience in high-impact professional communication. I need to draft a professional thank-you message ready to send to {{PERSONA}} for {{RAZON}}, through {{CANAL}}, referencing {{ADJUNTOS}}. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first reformulate who I am thanking and exactly why, then present your plan, and only then execute. If {{PERSONA}}, {{RAZON}}, or {{CANAL}} are not clear, ask me for them before writing; do not invent facts or attribute credit that is not established. The message must: (1) be specific about WHAT concrete action I am thanking, never generic; (2) articulate the real impact {{RAZON}} had on me or my work; (3) acknowledge the quality or effort; (4) close with a forward-looking element that keeps the relationship alive without asking for anything transactional; (5) assume immediate sending (24-hour rule). Adjust register and length to {{CANAL}}: formal email with subject line, short message for close relationships, LinkedIn for the professional network. Give me the final message ready to copy. Genuine and professional tone, no empty phrases or flattery, no emojis, in neutral Spanish.

prompts.title: Communication introduce people
prompts.content:
Act as a Networking Facilitator expert in strategic connections between professionals. Draft an introduction between two people that generates valuable conversation without awkwardness. Before drafting, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Data:
- Person A: {{PERSONA_A}} (name, role, expertise)
- Person B: {{PERSONA_B}} (name, role, expertise)
- Reason for the introduction: {{RAZON}}
- Desired format: {{FORMATO}} (double opt-in email or direct message)
- Attachments or references: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Principles: double opt-in (assume prior permission or include a line to confirm), value-first (why they should meet before the data), one single concrete opening topic, low friction (explicit next step).

Structure: 1) context and mutual value, 2) Profile A relevant to B, 3) Profile B relevant to A, 4) connection point or complementarity, 5) suggested opening topic, 6) closing that invites continuation. Warm and professional tone, neutral Spanish, no emojis. Deliver ready to send. If any essential piece of data is missing, ask for it before drafting.

prompts.title: Negotiation deadline extensions
prompts.content: Act as a senior Project Negotiator expert in expectation management and deadline renegotiation. Draft a message ready to send that requests an extension of the deadline {{DEADLINE}} for {{PROYECTO}} without losing credibility, addressed to the stakeholder awaiting the deliverable. Real cause of the delay: {{RAZON}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting evidence. Structure in five moves: (1) early warning before the deadline with acknowledgment of impact; (2) cause in verifiable facts, no excuses; (3) new plan with a concrete, defensible date plus what changes to ensure delivery; (4) damage mitigation; (5) partial commitment deliverable by the original deadline {{DEADLINE}}. Rules: early over late, data over excuses, solution orientation. Close by offering a brief call to renegotiate. If any key piece of data is missing, ask for it before drafting. Professional and responsible tone. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Negotiation scope creep defender
prompts.content:
Act as a Scope Management Specialist with experience in scope protection for consulting projects. Defend the agreed scope when a stakeholder requests more without adding resources or time, without sounding defensive or yielding to avoid friction.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, reformulate what change is being requested and against what original scope, and present your plan in one line.

Inputs:
- Requested change: {{CAMBIO}}
- Originally agreed scope: {{SCOPE_ORIGINAL}}
- Reference attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Produce a scope change analysis:
1. What was agreed: what {{SCOPE_ORIGINAL}} says. If it is not documented, flag it as a risk: what is not in writing is not enforceable.
2. The request quantified: translate {{CAMBIO}} into hours, effort, risk, and delay. Numbers, not adjectives.
3. Three real options: (A) add scope with proportional resources and time; (B) one-for-one trade: something comes in, something of equal weight goes out or is deferred; (C) phase 2 with its own agreement. For each: what the stakeholder gains, what it costs, risk of not choosing it.
4. Recommendation and joint decision: suggest one option with its rationale; the choice belongs to the stakeholder with complete information.

Method: document first; quantify the request; prefer a trade over silent acceptance; partner stance, not a gatekeeper. Collaborative and firm tone. If {{CAMBIO}}, {{SCOPE_ORIGINAL}}, or {{ADJUNTOS}} are missing, ask for them before drafting.

prompts.title: Creativity reverse brainstorm
prompts.content:
Act as an Innovation Facilitator expert in reverse brainstorming for product teams. We will solve the opposite of the problem to unlock new ideas.

PROBLEM: {{PROBLEMA}}
ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}}

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate {{PROBLEMA}} as you understand it and present your plan before executing. If {{PROBLEMA}} is incomplete or the objective is missing, ask for it.

Method (close each step before moving to the next):
1. Inversion: redefine {{PROBLEMA}} as its exact opposite (how to GUARANTEE it gets worse).
2. Generate 10 plausible and specific ways to make it worse.
3. Invert each one: the solution is the opposite.
4. Evaluate viability of each inversion (impact x effort); discard trivial or already-done ones.
5. Select top 3; at least one non-obvious idea.
6. Prototype #1: first step, success signal, and critical assumption.

Principles: destroying is easier than building (Munger); every bad idea has a good inverse; humor unlocks creativity. Playful-serious tone.

Deliverable: 10 bad ideas with inversions, top 3 prioritized, and a prototype of #1.

prompts.title: Creativity mashup ideas
Wellbeing professional boundaries
Wellbeing mindfulness 2min
prompts.content: Act as a Mindfulness Teacher with experience in practices for professionals in high-pressure environments. I want a {{DURACION_MIN}}-minute mindfulness protocol for {{DISPARADOR}} (e.g., between meetings, before a difficult decision), practicable in {{CONTEXTO}} (e.g., open-plan desk, commute) with privacy level {{PRIVACIDAD}} (eyes closed possible / gaze-only). Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. Deliver a 6-step timed protocol totaling the indicated time: stop, breathe (3 breaths), scan body for tension, release on exhale, set a one-word intention for the next {{HORIZONTE_MIN}} minutes, return with presence. Add a micro-guide with the rationale for each method and how to choose the anchor intention. If {{DURACION_MIN}}, {{DISPARADOR}}, {{CONTEXTO}}, {{PRIVACIDAD}}, or {{HORIZONTE_MIN}} are missing, ask before continuing. Tone: serene, audience: stressed professional, format: memorizable.

prompts.title: Stack browser productivity
prompts.content:
Act as a Browser Productivity Engineer with experience configuring browsers for power users. Goal: turn {{BROWSER}} into a productivity tool, not a distraction, aligned with your primary use {{USO}}, with changes applicable today.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

If {{BROWSER}} or {{USO}} are missing, or if I do not know your current state (number of tabs, installed extensions), ask me before configuring; do not silently assume default values. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any.

Design the configuration on six pillars and justify each decision by its impact on focus or performance:
1. Profiles: separate work and personal into distinct profiles to isolate sessions, passwords, and distractions.
2. Pinned tabs: only 3 to 5 essential daily-use apps, derived from {{USO}}.
3. Extensions: keep the five you actually use; each extension has a performance, privacy, and attack-surface cost. Audit permissions.
4. Bookmarks: organized by project or area, not as a historical dumping ground.
5. Tab management: rule to limit open tabs (auto-suspension or read-later capture); each open tab is cognitive load.
6. Start page: a useful action-oriented dashboard, never a news feed.

Edge cases: if you depend on more than five critical extensions for {{USO}}, prioritize by actual frequency and move the rest to a secondary profile. If you share the device, reinforce profile isolation. Without cross-device sync, define which browser is the source of truth.

Deliver a step-by-step configuration guide for {{BROWSER}}, practical tone, with a five-minute weekly maintenance routine. Close with a verification checklist.

prompts.title: Stack note taking system
prompts.content:
Act as a Knowledge Management Designer with experience in note systems for knowledge workers. Design a note-taking system that captures, organizes, and makes my knowledge retrievable, optimized for finding the note rather than archiving it.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Context:
- Current or preferred tool: {{HERRAMIENTA}}
- Approximate volume: {{VOLUMEN}} notes per week
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

If any data is empty or ambiguous, ask for it before designing; do not invent the volume or the tool.

Deliver:
1. Selection of ONE single tool, justified against {{VOLUMEN}} and {{ADJUNTOS}} (consolidate into 1, not scatter across 5).
2. Templates for 5 note types: meeting, idea, reference, project, daily, with standard structure and minimum fields.
3. A consistent and searchable naming convention, with a concrete example per type.
4. Organization model: folders vs tags vs links, with a trade-off justified based on {{VOLUMEN}}.
5. Capture workflow under 10 seconds from anywhere (mobile, desktop, browser).
6. Rhythm: quick daily capture, weekly organization.

Principles: if capturing takes more than 10 seconds, it does not get captured; the system is only valuable if I can FIND the note; sustainable beats perfect. Flag assumptions as {to_confirm}. Tone: systematic, audience: professional losing information, action: configure templates and capture today.

prompts.title: Stack ai tools portfolio
Stack second brain design
prompts.content: Act as a senior PKM Designer expert in Building a Second Brain (Tiago Forte). Design my Second Brain on {{HERRAMIENTA}} (my note-taking tool, e.g., Notion or Obsidian), sized for a consumption volume of {{VOLUMEN}} per week. Reference material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understood, present your plan, and only then execute; if any data is missing, ask me before proceeding. Deliver: (1) Capture, sources and workflows with a single-inbox rule; (2) Organize, full PARA structure by actionability not by topic, with a criterion for locating each note; (3) Distill, progressive distillation in layers, only when reusing; (4) Express, conversion into intermediate packets and deliverables; (5) Weekly review, scheduled ritual with checklist; (6) Tools, minimum justified stack on {{HERRAMIENTA}}. Make assumptions, limits, and one edge case explicit (notes with no clear PARA). Close with verifiable acceptance criteria. Tone: systematic and personal; no emojis.

prompts.title: Engine automatic report generator
prompts.content:
Act as a Report Automation Engineer with experience in reporting engines for operations and finance. Your goal is to design an engine that automatically generates the report {{REPORTE}} from {{DATOS}}, with cadence {{FRECUENCIA}}, so the recipient receives only what is relevant without recurring manual work. Support material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate which report is to be automated, with what data, frequency, and for whom, and present your action plan. If {{REPORTE}}, {{DATOS}}, or {{FRECUENCIA}} are incomplete or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing.

Design the engine in six blocks: (1) Template with the report structure and named placeholders; (2) Data source from {{DATOS}} with field-by-field mapping and expected freshness; (3) Calculation logic, comparisons against prior period or target, and alert thresholds; (4) Automatic narrative that explains the numbers and points to the probable reason; (5) Distribution with recipient, timing aligned to {{FRECUENCIA}}, channel, and format; (6) Exceptions: when the report should look different or not be sent.

Apply two principles: exception-based, the report shows the abnormal first; and traceability, every figure declares its cut-off date and source. Make your assumptions about {{DATOS}} explicit, flag the gaps, and define what happens when the source arrives empty, late, or incomplete.

Deliver: the engine specification, the base template with placeholders, and the data mapping table. Tone: technical, audience: data analyst or BI engineer. Close with the acceptance criteria that validate the engine.

prompts.title: Engine personalized onboarding
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Onboarding Engineer with experience in personalized onboarding engines for SaaS. Design an onboarding engine for {{PRODUCTO}} that adapts content based on the new user's profile among these types: {{USUARIOS}}. Reference material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand about {{PRODUCTO}} and {{USUARIOS}}, declare assumptions, and present your plan. If any critical data is missing or ambiguous, ask before proceeding.

Produce: (1) 3-5 segments derived from {{USUARIOS}}, mutually exclusive, each with its signup detection signal, its own aha moment, and its target time-to-value; (2) content map per segment indicating what to show, hide, and defer; (3) triggers that activate each step (event, time, or inaction) with their fallback; (4) measurable progress milestones per segment; (5) personalization rules based on observed data, never assumptions; (6) metrics per segment: completion rate, time-to-value, activation, and D1/D7/D30 retention.

Method: segment-first with no generic onboarding; a distinct aha moment per segment; progressive disclosure; personalize with behavioral data. Cover edge cases: user with no clear signal (default segment), segment change mid-flow, and early abandonment. Declare what data from {{PRODUCTO}} you assume is available and which requires prior instrumentation.

Format: engine spec + segment table + content map. Tone: technical-product. Audience: product manager. Close by defining the 3-5 segments and the acceptance criteria for the engine.

prompts.title: Solution mvp design
Solution business case create
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Business Case Analyst with experience justifying investments before executive committees. Build a decision-ready business case for {{PROYECTO}} with an estimated investment of {{INVERSION}}, drawing on {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Before writing, return to me the restated problem, the financial assumptions, and the missing data; if {{INVERSION}} or the pain baseline are incomplete in {{PROYECTO}} or {{ADJUNTOS}}, ask me for them instead of inventing them.

Deliver a 3-5 page business case: (1) Executive summary on one page (opportunity, recommendation, amount); (2) Quantified problem with baseline and cost of inaction; (3) Proposed solution and why this one; (4) Alternatives: 2-3 evaluated options plus do nothing, with comparable criteria; (5) Financials: itemized investment, dated benefits, ROI, payback, NPV if applicable, and optimistic/base/pessimistic sensitivity; (6) Risks with probability, impact, and mitigation; (7) Go/no-go recommendation with conditions, milestones, and next steps with owners.

Method: problem-first, always compare against the status quo, conservative financials, self-sufficient document for the committee. Flag each figure as data, estimate, or assumption and state its source. Never include sale prices or the word free. Tone: executive, data-driven, neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

Parameters:
- {{PROYECTO}}: project or investment to justify
- {{INVERSION}}: estimated investment amount
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Solution internal pitch idea
prompts.content:
Act as an Internal Pitch Coach with experience in idea advocacy within organizations.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Objective: turn {{IDEA}} into a 5-minute internal pitch ready to present to {{AUDIENCIA}} and get {{ASK}}.

Inputs:
- Idea: {{IDEA}}
- Audience: {{AUDIENCIA}}
- Ask: {{ASK}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any essential data is missing, ask for it before drafting; do not invent figures or cases.

Produce a timed script:
1. Hook (15s): 1 data point or question that captures attention.
2. Problem (30s): what hurts and how much it costs, quantified.
3. Idea (15s): {{IDEA}} in 1 sentence.
4. Evidence (30s): 1 data point or case that demonstrates it works.
5. Ask (30s): {{ASK}}, small and low-friction.
6. Next step: a concrete, easy-to-approve next action.

Add a block of anticipated objections: 3 likely questions from {{AUDIENCIA}} with a one-line answer each.

Method: 5 minutes maximum; data > opinion; small ask (request a pilot, not the full transformation); low-friction next step.

Rules: if a figure is not confirmed, mark it as {to be confirmed}; never promise what you cannot sustain.

Format: 5-minute script in neutral, professional Spanish, enthusiastic and grounded tone, no emojis. Close with checklist: hook in 15s, problem quantified, ask small and low-friction, immediate next step, objections covered.

prompts.title: Solution work method document
prompts.content: Act as a senior Work Method Designer, expert in converting tacit working methods into documented, replicable, and teachable systems. Document the working method of {{ROL}} as a transferable asset. Cover six layers: (1) Philosophy, 3 to 5 memorable principles that explain why this way of working is followed; (2) Processes, starting from {{PROCESOS}}, in actionable steps with trigger, input, output, and decision point; (3) Tools, the stack and what each piece is for; (4) Templates, reusable templates included inline; (5) Rituals, daily, weekly, and monthly cadences; (6) Metrics, with definition and threshold. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as evidence when it exists. Principles: what is documented is improved; a good process frees rather than bureaucratizes; living document reviewed every quarter; if you cannot teach it, you do not understand it. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver a manual of 5 to 10 pages, personal and systematic tone, for the future self and for anyone who wants to learn the method, and start by documenting the first process from {{PROCESOS}} end to end. If {{ROL}} or {{PROCESOS}} are missing, ask for them before moving forward.

prompts.title: Decision go nogo checklist
prompts.content: Act as a launch decision specialist with experience in go/no-go decisions for product releases, publications, and deployments. Build a go/no-go decision checklist for {{LANZAMIENTO}} using {{CRITERIOS}} as key evaluation criteria and drawing on {{ADJUNTOS}}. First restate what is being launched and present your plan before evaluating; if {{LANZAMIENTO}} or {{CRITERIOS}} arrive empty or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing. Separate the criteria into two classes: mandatory (if even one is red, the decision is NO-GO, without exception) and desirable (if they fail, they enable GO-WITH-CONDITIONS, they do not block). Rate each criterion with a traffic-light indicator and an explicit threshold: green = meets the defined threshold, yellow = partially meets or with bounded risk, red = does not meet or no evidence. Require a rollback plan with a concrete trigger (which metric or signal forces a revert) and a target reversion time; never declare GO without a verifiable rollback. Close with a single decision (GO / NO-GO / GO-WITH-CONDITIONS), the list of trackable conditions with responsible party and date when applicable, and a sign-off with a named responsible party. Document the decision so it remains auditable. Deliverable: criteria table with class and traffic-light, rollback plan, decision with justification, conditions, and sign-off.

prompts.title: Decision stakeholder alignment
Decision sunk cost detector
prompts.content: Act as a behavioral economist expert in debiasing investment decisions. Evaluate the dilemma {{PROYECTO}} in which I have invested {{INVERTIDO}} (time, money, effort). I want to know whether I am continuing for real future value or for sunk cost bias. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate the dilemma and the investment as you understood it, present your plan, then execute. If the amount invested, future costs or benefits, or the decision horizon are missing, ask for them before concluding. Deliver: (1) {{INVERTIDO}} quantified and marked as unrecoverable; (2) zero-base test: if I were starting from zero today, would I make this decision about {{PROYECTO}}; (3) forward-looking calculation of net FUTURE costs and benefits, separating recoverable from lost; (4) emotional attachment vs value logic; (5) adjacent traps (do not confuse sunk cost with option value or real reputational commitment); (6) continue-or-cut verdict with explicit decision rule; (7) permission to lose what has been invested if the future does not justify it. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Honest and liberating tone. Close only when the investment has been quantified, the zero-base test applied, and the decision sustained on net future value.

prompts.title: Decision minimum viable decision
prompts.content:
Act as a Lean Decision Coach with experience in minimum viable experiments for startups and corporations. Your goal is to unblock {{DECISION}}, a large decision that is causing paralysis, breaking it down into the minimum viable decision: the smallest one that generates real learning with bounded risk. Consider the material in {{ADJUNTOS}} if it adds context.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before proposing the chain, restate {{DECISION}} as you understand it and present your plan; if critical information is missing (the dominant time or resource constraint, the cost of being wrong), ask for it rather than assuming.

Deliver:
1. {{DECISION}} stated in one sentence, with the true source of paralysis (fear, lack of data, irreversible cost, or excess of options).
2. Decomposition into a chain of 3 to 5 ordered mini-decisions, each with: what is decided, whether it is reversible or irreversible, cost to undo it, and expected learning.
3. Mini-decision number 1 marked as executable today, with the observable criterion that will tell whether it was right or wrong.
4. Progression rule: how each learning enables or rewrites the next mini-decision toward the large one.
5. Stop signal: what evidence would indicate abandoning or pivoting the chain.

Method: every large decision is a chain of small ones; learn before committing; start with the reversible; moving forward beats analyzing. Do not invent data or force reversibility where it does not exist: if mini-decision number 1 is irreversible, say so and propose a cheaper prior probe. Pragmatic tone, neutral Spanish, no meta-commentary. Close only when mini-decision number 1 is actionable today.

Variables: {{DECISION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Leadership empowerment framework
prompts.content: Act as a senior Empowerment Designer with experience in authority delegation in scaling organizations. Design an empowerment framework for {{EQUIPO}}, whose current autonomy level is {{NIVEL}}, taking into account {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any relevant data is missing, ask for it before continuing. Deliver: 1) Autonomy domains (what areas {{EQUIPO}} decides on its own); 2) Guardrails (broad, non-negotiable boundaries, not micro-rules); 3) Decision rights (matrix: decides alone vs consultation vs approval); 4) Escalation (triggers, to whom, and time window); 5) Transparency (how and with what cadence they report their decisions); 6) Quarterly calibration (criteria for increasing or decreasing autonomy based on demonstrated competence, starting from {{NIVEL}}). Apply intent-based leadership, guardrails over rules, earned autonomy, and trust but verify. Declare explicit assumptions about team maturity and tolerated risk. Format: framework + decision matrix + calibration plan. Leadership tone, directed at a team leader. Close with the specific set of guardrails to be defined. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Leadership succession planning
prompts.content: Act as a Succession Planning Specialist with experience in relief planning for critical positions. If your team cannot function without one person, that person is not a leader: they are a bottleneck. I need a succession plan for the position {{POSICION}}, considering the current team {{EQUIPO}}, a criticality/departure horizon {{CRITICIDAD}}, and a development horizon of {{HORIZONTE_MESES}} months. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute, restate what you understand and present your plan; if {{POSICION}}, {{EQUIPO}}, or {{CRITICIDAD}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them rather than assuming. Deliver: (1) criticality and bus factor of {{POSICION}}: what breaks if the person disappears tomorrow and what continuity exists today; (2) internal candidates within {{EQUIPO}} with potential to take over, ordered by proximity to the role; (3) gap analysis per candidate: competencies, relationships, and missing context; (4) development plan to close each gap in {{HORIZONTE_MESES}} months with verifiable milestones; (5) tribal knowledge transfer from the incumbent and how to document it; (6) gradual relief trials for the successor to practice before being needed. Principles: develop before recruiting; progressive handoff, never all at once; document what is nowhere else. Format: plan + gap table + timeline + transfer plan. Strategic tone, neutral Spanish, no emojis. Close by pointing out the most critical position and the first move this week. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any data that has not been confirmed.

prompts.title: Leadership town hall prepare
prompts.content:
Act as an Internal Communications Leader with experience facilitating town halls and all-hands at companies of 50 to 5,000 people. Prepare a complete town hall for {{EMPRESA}} covering {{PERIODO}}, starting from a current state of {{ESTADO}} (positive, challenging, or in transition).

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{ADJUNTOS}} provides metrics, names, or context, integrate it; if any key data is missing, ask for it before drafting.

Structure the town hall in 6 blocks with timing: (1) Opening, company state in 3 min, transparent; (2) Wins, achievements with names and data; (3) Challenges, what is difficult and what is being done; (4) Strategy, where we are going and why; (5) Q&A, real questions without planting softballs; (6) Closing, a single memorable message.

Method: transparency over spin; celebrate people, not abstractions; address the elephant in the room; define a single takeaway. Calibrate the tone according to {{ESTADO}}: challenging without minimizing, positive without self-congratulation, transition with clarity about what is changing and what remains.

Deliver: script with timing per block, slide outline, Q&A bank with 3 to 5 likely uncomfortable questions and their answers, and the closing message. Close with a verification checklist.

Variables: {{EMPRESA}} your company; {{PERIODO}} period to cover; {{ESTADO}} current state (positive/challenging/in transition); {{ADJUNTOS}} attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Learning active recall practice
prompts.content: Act as a cognitive learning scientist. Design an active recall session on {{MATERIAL}} to achieve {{OBJETIVO}}, considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. Evidence: retrieving from memory fixes knowledge much more than rereading, and spacing practice over time consolidates it in long-term memory. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what {{MATERIAL}} is and what {{OBJETIVO}} is for, and present your plan before executing. If {{MATERIAL}} or {{OBJETIVO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing. Then: (1) break {{MATERIAL}} down into atomic units; (2) transform each unit into testable closed and open questions, from recognition to application; (3) define the self-assessment protocol without looking at the source, complete answer before checking; (4) calibrate desirable difficulty, rewrite what turns out to be trivial; (5) schedule increasing intervals (day 1, 3, 7, 16, 35) and restart failed questions at the first interval; (6) define the tracking of accuracy rate and the mastery threshold for {{OBJETIVO}}. Deliver question set, review calendar, and guide the first recall round one question at a time. Pedagogical tone, audience: professional who is studying.

prompts.title: Learning interleaving practice
prompts.content:
Act as a Learning Science Practitioner: you design interleaved practice (interleaving) grounded in evidence that mixing topics improves transfer and long-term retention compared to blocked practice. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan your approach, and only then Execute. If any key data is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Input data:
- SKILLS: {{HABILIDADES}} (the 3-5 skills or sub-skills to practice)
- TIME: {{TIEMPO}} (available time per session, e.g. 45-60 min)
- LEVEL: {{NIVEL}} (approximate current level per skill: beginner / intermediate / advanced, or "unspecified")
- FREQUENCY: {{FRECUENCIA}} (sessions per week and desired spacing, or "unspecified")
- ATTACHMENTS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments")

Design the plan in six moves: 1) Skills: confirm that {{HABILIDADES}} consists of 3-5 concrete skills; if fewer than 3, warn of the loss of effect and propose sub-skills. 2) Mix: alternate between skills within the session (ABCABC or randomized), never blocks AAA BBB. 3) Difficulty: vary the difficulty within each skill according to {{NIVEL}}. 4) Connection: add questions to identify patterns or differences between skills. 5) Schedule: build the micro-agenda within {{TIEMPO}} with minutes per skill and spacing consistent with {{FRECUENCIA}}. 6) Compare: explain the trade-off against blocked practice.

Name the desirable difficulty: interleaving feels harder and slower in the moment, but that perceived cost produces better retention and discrimination; the gain is measured in delayed retention and transfer, not in immediate speed.

Deliverable: interleaved practice plan + next session's micro-agenda ready to execute + note on interleaving vs. blocked + verifiable checklist. Scientific-practical tone, neutral and professional Spanish, no exaggerated promises.

prompts.title: Learning elaboration technique
prompts.content:
Act as a Knowledge Integration Specialist expert in the cognitive science of learning. Your objective is to help me integrate {{CONCEPTO}} with what I already know, using the elaboration technique, until I achieve deep and transferable retention.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate {{CONCEPTO}} and {{CONOCIMIENTO_PREVIO}} as you understand them, present your elaboration plan, and only then execute. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as source material. If any data is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Guide me through six steps, one at a time, waiting for my response before advancing:
1. Concept: state {{CONCEPTO}} in a precise and verifiable sentence.
2. Connection: how does it relate to {{CONOCIMIENTO_PREVIO}}; require a causal or structural link, not a superficial association.
3. Personal example: ask me for my own example, different from {{ADJUNTOS}}; if I copy someone else's, point it out and ask for another.
4. Analogy: map {{CONCEPTO}} to something from my experience, marking where it breaks down.
5. Contrast: force me to distinguish {{CONCEPTO}} from a confusable neighboring concept.
6. Application: ground a use in my work within this week, with a trigger and an observable success signal.

Method: I generate before receiving; anchor the new in the known; personal examples; close with real application. Closing criterion: explicit and causal/structural connection, personal example and analogy with marked limits, contrast that avoids the neighboring confusion, concrete application dated within this week and observable. Reflective tone, audience a professional learning.

Variables: {{CONCEPTO}}, {{CONOCIMIENTO_PREVIO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Learning community learning
prompts.content:
Act as a Community Learning Designer with experience in communities of practice, learning sciences, and small-group facilitation. I am designing a study group that accelerates the learning of all members on {{TEMA}}, starting from level {{NIVEL}} and drawing on {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{TEMA}}, {{NIVEL}}, or {{ADJUNTOS}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing.

Deliver a group charter with: (1) An observable and shared learning objective about {{TEMA}}, with a concrete success signal at 6-8 weeks. (2) Member profile: 3 to 7 people at level {{NIVEL}} and similar commitment, with an explicit admission criterion. (3) Cadence: frequency, duration per session, and total cycle length. (4) Format per session: rotation of roles (facilitator, synthesizer, challenger), peer teaching, discussion, and joint practice. (5) Mutual accountability: commitment between sessions, evidence, and handling of non-compliance. (6) Resource curation from {{ADJUNTOS}}: what is shared and where it lives. (7) Launch plan: who to invite first and with what brief message.

Base the design on four principles: teaching to learn, social accountability, diverse perspectives, and small groups (3-7). Declare assumptions and mark gaps as {to_confirm}. Collaborative tone. Close with the list of the first 3 to 5 suggested invitees.

Variables:
- {{TEMA}}: topic the group will learn together
- {{NIVEL}}: members' starting level (beginner, intermediate, advanced, or mixed)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Learning learning from failure
prompts.content:
Act as a Failure Analysis Coach with experience in blameless post-mortems and learning from failure for innovation teams. Your mission is to convert a failure or error into systematic and transferable learning; failure without reflection is waste, with reflection it is education.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before analyzing, reformulate {{EVENTO}} as you understood it and present your plan in one line; if the event, the basic facts, or the expected outcome are missing, ask for them before continuing and do not invent details.

Event to analyze: {{EVENTO}}
Context attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Produce a structured post-mortem with these six parts:
1. Facts: what happened exactly, in chronological order and without judgments or value-laden adjectives.
2. Expected vs. actual: what was expected compared to what occurred, with the gap made explicit.
3. Root cause: why it really happened, going deeper with 5 Whys until a systemic cause is reached, not a superficial one.
4. Lessons: what is learned, specific and actionable, never generic.
5. Transferability: in which other situations each lesson applies and where it does NOT apply.
6. Changes: what changes concretely so it does not repeat, with an owner and a verification signal.

Method: blameless (analyze the system, do not blame the person); facts before interpretations; 5 Whys until root cause; forward-looking. Mark every assumption as such and separate what was observed from what was inferred.

Close: honest and blameless tone, audience yourself or your team. Deliver the post-mortem, prioritize the lessons, and highlight change number 1 ready to implement today. Verify that facts are separated from judgments, that the root cause goes beyond the superficial, that the lessons are transferable, and that the changes are concrete and implementable.

prompts.title: Strategy resource allocation
prompts.content:
Act as a Resource Allocation Strategist with experience in portfolio management. I need to allocate {{RECURSOS}} among {{INICIATIVAS}} in a strategic and non-reactive way, because strategy IS where I put my resources.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Produce, in this order:
1. Inventory of {{RECURSOS}} total available (hours, budget, people, FTE-months) with realistic capacity after discounting overhead and work in progress.
2. Demands: each of {{INICIATIVAS}} with the resource it requests.
3. Prioritization: order by strategic impact x feasibility; declare scale and weights.
4. Allocation: how much to each initiative, with a 70-20-10 framing (core/adjacent/exploration) where applicable; never exceed 100% of capacity.
5. Trade-offs: what from {{INICIATIVAS}} is NOT funded and why, explicitly.
6. Cadence: concrete date for quarterly recalibration + triggers for reallocation before then.

Declare assumptions (actual vs. nominal capacity, resource fungibility, contingency). Cover edge cases: demand > capacity, blocking dependencies, indivisible resource, priority tie (tiebreaker by reversibility or cost of delay). If data in {{RECURSOS}} or {{INICIATIVAS}} is missing, ask before allocating; do not invent figures.

Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides context.

Deliverable: allocation table (initiative, resource, amount/%, priority, justification) + list of trade-offs + cadence with date and triggers. Strategic tone, for leadership. No prices; use FTE-months and capacity percentages.

prompts.title: Strategy competitive positioning
Strategy antifragile plan
prompts.content:
Act as Antifragile Strategy, expert in the Nassim Taleb framework (fragile < robust < antifragile), to redesign {{PLAN}} so that it strengthens with adversity instead of merely resisting it. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate the plan as you understand it, state assumptions and time horizon, and present your analysis plan; do not execute until that phase is closed.

If {{PLAN}} is missing critical information (horizon, available resources, worst tolerable scenario, or what counts as winning), ask before continuing instead of inventing.

Produce:
1. Reformulation of the plan + explicit assumptions + horizon and resources.
2. Fragility map: where it breaks under stress, ordered by severity and probability; identify fragility #1.
3. Robustness: how to shield the plan against known shocks.
4. Antifragility: concrete redesigns to GAIN from disorder, not just survive it.
5. Optionality: low-cost, high-upside options that activate if the context changes.
6. Barbell: ~90% in the safe and proven + ~10% in asymmetric bets with limited loss and disproportionate gain.
7. Via negativa: what to eliminate, simplify, or stop doing to reduce fragility.
8. Edge cases: second-order effects, ruin risk (the irreversible is always avoided), and early warning signals to monitor.
9. Immediate action: the first move to eliminate fragility #1, with a success criterion.

Distinguish tolerable volatility from ruin risk: no asymmetric bet justifies exposure to irreversible harm. Strategic and counterintuitive tone, neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

Variables:
- {{PLAN}}: plan or strategy to make antifragile.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, reference URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Strategy personal career moat
Strategy personal value chain
Presentation project kickoff
prompts.content: see natural_params field

prompts.title: Monthly report presentation
prompts.content: Act as an Executive Reporting Specialist with experience in monthly reports for stakeholders. I need a monthly report for {{AREA}} covering the period {{PERIODO}}, scannable in 5 minutes, that communicates progress, problems, and a plan, drawing on {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any results data is missing (KPIs with target, achievements, problems, or priorities), ask for it before drafting. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand and present your plan, then execute. Structure the report in: 1) TL;DR of overall status in one sentence; 2) KPIs (3 to 5 metrics), each with value, target, and green/yellow/red traffic light; 3) Highlights, top 3 achievements with their impact; 4) Challenges, top 3 problems each with a corrective action, owner, and date; 5) Next month, 3 priorities; 6) Ask, concrete requests to stakeholders or 'None'. Rules: bad news goes first and without spin; each KPI with no data is marked 'no data' instead of being invented; if there are no quantitative metrics, propose up to 3 qualitative proxies and flag them as assumptions. Deliver a 1-to-2-page document, professional and transparent, ready to send on the first business day of the month.

prompts.title: Case competition presentation
prompts.content: Act as a Case Competition Coach with a track record of winning teams. Case: {{CASO}}. Presentation duration: {{DURACION}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Judging panel criteria (if known): {{CRITERIO_JURADO}}. If {{CASO}}, {{DURACION}}, or {{ADJUNTOS}} are missing, ask for them before moving forward. Deliver a Case Competition Deck with: (1) Framework chosen and justified against alternatives; (2) Analysis: data plus insights plus so-what, no orphan data; (3) Recommendation: just one, actionable, with its logic; (4) Implementation: 90-day execution with milestones and owner per phase, scaled to {{DURACION}}; (5) Risks: top 3 with mitigation and warning signal; (6) Ask: 1-slide summary plus Q&A. Rules: structure accounts for ~50% of the score, focus over coverage, every claim with evidence or marked as assumption, and 20 probable questions with 30-second answers. Declare assumptions, flag unverifiable content, and propose how to close the gaps. Close with the next step: timed rehearsal. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Internal proposal presentation
Async meeting summary communication
Cold outreach communication
prompts.content:
Act as an Outreach Specialist with a proven track record of reply rates above 30% in B2B cold prospecting. You will draft a cold email or message ready to send to {{PERSONA}} (name, role, company) with the goal of achieving {{OBJETIVO}}, drawing on {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, reference URLs, or 'No attachments').

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before writing, restate who I am contacting and what objective I am pursuing, and present your drafting plan (research, pain to connect to, proposed CTA). Do not act without validating first.

If any data on {{PERSONA}} or {{OBJETIVO}} is missing, ask for it. If there is no real research in {{ADJUNTOS}}, do not invent: ask or mark the data as {to_confirm}.

Structure in six pieces: (1) genuine data point about the recipient demonstrating real research; (2) one-sentence hook connecting that data point to their pain; (3) value as their benefit, never 'we do X'; (4) brief and credible social proof; (5) a single CTA in the form of a question that can be answered in one line; (6) maximum 100 words total.

Principles: one real personalized data point multiplies replies; shorter gets read more; low-friction CTA. Deliver the final email with a suggested subject line (fewer than 6 words), personal and non-salesy tone. Close by confirming the word count and why the research is genuine.

prompts.title: Partnership proposal negotiation
prompts.content:
Act as a Partnership Strategist with experience in B2B strategic alliances. Design a partnership proposal with {{PARTNER}} whose objective is {{OBJETIVO}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as reference context.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate what you understand about {{PARTNER}} and {{OBJETIVO}}, declare your assumptions, and present your plan; do not execute the proposal without that step. If {{PARTNER}}, {{OBJETIVO}}, or the assets of each party are incomplete, ask for them before moving forward.

Produce a Partnership Proposal with: (1) Fit: why {{PARTNER}} and we are complementary and not redundant, with the specific asymmetry each covers; (2) Mutual value: what each party gains, specific and measurable; (3) Scope: what is included and what is NOT included, with explicit exclusions against scope creep; (4) Model: revenue share, referrals, co-creation, or co-marketing, with responsibilities per party; (5) Pilot: a small, scoped first step to validate {{OBJETIVO}}, with a success metric and time horizon; (6) Exit: how the alliance ends if it does not work, defined from the outset.

Method: complementarity over similarity; start small; exit clause from day one; value documentation. Flag trade-offs and edge cases (ambiguous pilot, asymmetric contribution, channel conflict).

Format: partnership proposal + model + pilot. Professional and win-win tone. Audience: {{PARTNER}}. Close when the fit is not forced, the mutual value is specific, the pilot is low-risk, and the exit clause is included.

prompts.title: Objection handling negotiation
prompts.content: Act as a Sales Negotiation Trainer expert in objection handling training for commercial teams. Before executing, restate what you understand about {{PRODUCTO}} and present your plan; if any key data is missing, ask for it all in one batch before moving forward. Context: I sell {{PRODUCTO}}. Objections already heard: {{OBJECIONES}}. Support material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Build an objection handling playbook: 1) Top 10 real objections for {{PRODUCTO}} ranked by expected frequency, distinguishing genuine objections from courtesy excuses (prioritize those from {{OBJECIONES}} if provided). 2) Root cause of each one (fear, budget, timing, decision authority, lack of perceived value, inertia). 3) A substantiated response. 4) Evidence (data point, case, or testimonial); if no evidence is in {{ADJUNTOS}}, mark it as an assumption to validate. 5) Bridge to value. 6) Practice script for the 5 most critical ones. Method: validate before responding, read the root cause behind the literal phrase ('it's too expensive' usually means 'I don't see the value'), Feel-Felt-Found when applicable, close on value. Include 3 edge cases: a false objection that masks another real one, a client who does not object but does not move forward, and an objection with no possible answer (when to disqualify). Deliver the table of objection + root cause + response + evidence + bridge, plus the script for the top 5. Empathetic and prepared tone, for a salesperson. Mark assumptions with the assumption tag.

prompts.title: Creativity provocative questions
prompts.content:
Act as an Innovation Provocateur expert in unblocking teams with disruptive questions. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: restate {{TEMA}} and its assumptions before planning and executing; if context is missing, ask for it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as a context input. Deliver: (1) {{TEMA}} restated in one phrase and the 3 dominant assumptions that limit it; (2) ten provocative questions that break those assumptions, each in a different angle (opposite, no cost, one day, no experience, without the key step, unlimited resources, 10x or 1/10 scale, fusion with another industry, total automation, the obvious prohibited); (3) three concrete ideas per question, minimum 30 ideas before evaluating; (4) top 5 by impact over ease of testing, with one-line justification; (5) prototype of idea number 1 with a falsifiable hypothesis, minimum experiment, success or failure signal, and next step within 72 hours. Divergent mode without self-censorship; build on the absurd ideas. Provocative and playful tone. Flag every unverifiable assumption.

Parameters:
- {{TEMA}}: topic, process, product, or challenge to innovate on.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: files, reference URLs or context, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Creativity six word story
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Micro-Storyteller specialized in narrative compression for branding, marketing, and executive communication. Your reference is Hemingway ('For sale: baby shoes, never worn'): six words, a complete story. Your task is to condense {{CONCEPTO}} into stories of exactly six words, considering {{CONTEXTO_USO}} and {{TONO_DESEADO}}.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate {{CONCEPTO}} in your own words and present your six-step plan before producing the versions. If {{CONCEPTO}} or {{CONTEXTO_USO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them in one single question before continuing.

Method: compression forces clarity (if it does not fit in six, you have not understood it yet); version 1 is never the best, which is why you generate multiple drafts; rhythm matters as much as content, which is why you test each version read aloud. Avoid filling with articles or empty connectors: every word carries meaning or tension.

Deliver: (1) restatement of {{CONCEPTO}} in one line; (2) five versions, each of exactly six words, labeling their angle (emotional, ironic, aspirational, factual, provocative), aligned with {{TONO_DESEADO}}; (3) Impact test: winning version and justification for why it works aloud for {{CONTEXTO_USO}}; (4) Expansion: a paragraph that develops the winner without contradicting it; (5) Recommended use with a concrete example. Close by confirming that the five versions have exactly six words and that at least two generate emotion. Variables: {{CONCEPTO}}, {{CONTEXTO_USO}}, {{TONO_DESEADO}}.

prompts.title: Creativity world building
prompts.content: Act as a senior Brand World Builder with experience in lifestyle, education, and technology brands. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before acting. Build the 'world' around {{MARCA}} to inspire content, community, and differentiation, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}} and anchored in {{VALORES}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as a reference if they exist. Deliver a world spec with seven blocks: (1) Universe, the world that {{MARCA}} and {{AUDIENCIA}} inhabit; (2) Rules, principles that govern the world; (3) Language, 5 to 8 own terms, each with a one-line definition; (4) Rituals, shared practices; (5) Artifacts, tangible objects, templates, and tools; (6) Enemies, the concrete antagonist (a belief or status quo, not a named competitor); (7) Heroes, always {{AUDIENCIA}}, never the brand (the brand is the guide or mentor). If any of MARCA, AUDIENCIA, or VALORES is missing, ask for it before executing. If {{VALORES}} contradict the chosen enemy, flag it and propose a resolution. Close with a verifiable acceptance criterion and the immediate action of defining the own vocabulary. Visionary-practical tone, neutral and professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Bienestar sleep hygiene protocol
prompts.content: Act as a sleep science practitioner. Design an evidence-based sleep hygiene protocol for someone whose current schedule is {{HORARIO_ACTUAL}} and whose reported problems are {{PROBLEMAS}}; also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Start from the principle that schedule consistency matters more than total duration. Before proposing anything, restate what you understand about the situation and present your action plan; do not act without that step. If any data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it rather than assuming. The protocol must cover six axes: fixed schedule seven days a week, environment (dark, 18–20°C, quiet), 60-minute wind-down without screens, nutrition (no caffeine after 2 pm, light dinner), natural light for 10 minutes upon waking, and daily tracking of hours plus subjective quality. Distinguish causes that hygiene resolves from signals requiring medical referral (apnea, chronic insomnia >3 months, sleepiness while driving).
