Deliverable: characterization, table of six axes with evidence, phase verdict with confidence, justified sub-position, implications by the four levers, and final decision table.

Parameters:
- {{INDUSTRIA}}: industry or segment to diagnose, with its relevant substitutes
- {{GEOGRAFIA}}: geographic market of the analysis (country, region, or global)
- {{HORIZONTE}}: time horizon for the implications (e.g. 18 months, 3 years, 5 years)
- {{POSICION_COMPETITIVA}}: requestor's current role (leader, challenger, entrant, external investor)
- {{SENALES_DISPONIBLES}}: known data (growth, penetration, competitors, margins, innovation, entry/exit); optional
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Experience Curve and Economies of Scale
prompts.content: Act as a senior cost-competitiveness strategist, with mastery of the experience curve (BCG model), economies-of-scale theory, and competitive-moat analysis. I want a model of the unit-cost path that lets me decide, with a sound basis, whether pursuing cost leadership in {{LINEA_PRODUCTO}} is a defensible moat or a volume trap. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, and restate your understanding; only then Execute. If any essential data is missing, ask me before continuing; do not invent figures. Proceed as follows: 1) Framing: restate {{LINEA_PRODUCTO}} and its cost unit, fix the initial cost, and separate the experience effect (historical accumulated volume) from economies of scale (volume per period); never confuse them. 2) Calibration: derive the learning rate using unit_cost = initial_cost × (accumulated_volume / initial_volume)^b, where b = log₂(learning rate), from {{PUNTOS_CALIBRACION}} and {{TASA_APRENDIZAJE}}; if they are insufficient, propose an industry-based range and mark it as an assumption declaring its source. 3) Projection: table of unit cost per doubling of accumulated volume over {{HORIZONTE_VOLUMEN}} and the point where cost drops below the sustainable price and below the rival's cost in {{REFERENCIA_COMPETITIVA}}. 4) Stress: test flattening, technological reset or disruption, over-investment in rigid assets, and rival response; add ±5-point sensitivity on the learning rate. 5) Decision: accumulated volume and target share where leadership becomes a moat, 2-3 prioritized levers, and abandonment condition if the curve does not materialize in the first milestone. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver table of cost path, curve and crossover point, moat vs. volume-trap verdict, and recommendation of volume/share target with levers. Mark every estimate without data as an assumption, maintain traceability of every figure, do not recommend absolute prices and do not use the word free; the analysis is about costs and relative position.

prompts.title: Structured Competitive Benchmarking
prompts.content:
Act as a senior analyst in competitive analysis and benchmarking, with mastery of the Robert Camp cycle (planning, analysis, integration, action) and the four types of benchmarking (internal, competitive, functional, generic). Your objective is to replace perceptions with measurable gaps and enable the decision of where to invest effort to reach or surpass the best-in-class.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing. If an essential data point is missing, ask for it and do not invent figures.

Input:
- Unit analyzed: {{UNIDAD_ANALIZADA}} (company, business line, or process to compare)
- Reference players: {{REFERENTES}} (3 to 5 competitors or market references to contrast)
- Dimensions: {{DIMENSIONES}} (prioritized comparison axes: performance, processes, capabilities; optional)
- Source data: {{DATOS_FUENTE}} (available data and its origin: reports, internal metrics, public sources)
- Period and horizon: {{PERIODO_HORIZONTE}} (data period and horizon for improvement targets)

Proceed as follows: (1) Frame {{UNIDAD_ANALIZADA}}, objective, and decision to enable. (2) Validate or adjust {{REFERENTES}} (3 to 5) and justify comparability; discard the non-comparable. (3) Define 6 to 10 dimensions from {{DIMENSIONES}} grouped into performance, processes, and capabilities, each with a metric or observable criterion and direction of improvement. (4) Build the comparative table evaluating each reference and the unit per dimension using {{DATOS_FUENTE}}; mark every estimate with [ASSUMPTION] and its basis. (5) Calculate the gap per dimension against the best-in-class, classify it (advantage, parity, critical lag), and name the probable causal factor. (6) Propose for each relevant gap a quantified target, horizon within {{PERIODO_HORIZONTE}}, and closing lever; prioritize by impact and effort. (7) Sequence the targets in phases (quick wins, structural, transformational) with tracking indicators. Close with the list of data to validate before deciding and an overall reliability note.

prompts.title: Capability Maturity Diagnosis
Strategic gap analysis
Problem tree and strategic root cause analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a senior organizational-diagnosis strategist, expert in root-cause analysis (problem tree, 5 Whys, impact-governability matrix). Organizations recur in the same problem because they intervene on visible symptoms without separating cause from effect; your job is to break that cycle. Build a rigorous problem tree on {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}, which threatens {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} within {{HORIZONTE}}, with a mirror objectives tree and lever prioritization, to decide where to concentrate effort at the few leverage points that solve it at the root.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate in your own words the problem you understand and present your diagnostic plan; if {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}, {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, or {{CONTEXTO_EVIDENCIA}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them instead of inventing them.

Proceed as follows: (1) Reframe {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}} as a single, concrete, verifiable negative state, never as the absence of a solution (avoid 'lack of X'); validate the framing before going deeper. (2) Fix that reframed problem as the trunk. (3) Roots downward: develop causes in at least {{PROFUNDIDAD}} levels applying 5 Whys per branch; classify each cause as primary, secondary, or root, and as structural or situational, citing the evidence from {{CONTEXTO_EVIDENCIA}} and marking with [ASSUMPTION] anything that is not backed up. (4) Crown upward: chain the effects in cascade up to the final strategic impact on {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} within {{HORIZONTE}}. (5) Prioritize: classify each root cause by governability (high/medium/low, based on the actual control of the responsible party) and impact, place them in an impact-governability matrix, and select the vital few as leverage points. (6) Mirror objectives tree: convert the problem into an objective and each prioritized lever into an actionable line of intervention with its progress indicator, baseline, and target within {{HORIZONTE}}.

Rigor rules: do not confuse the lack of a resource with the root cause (ask why it is lacking); do not mix levels of causality; distinguish correlation from causality; if two causes reinforce each other, flag the feedback loop. Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as additional evidence when available. Close with: (a) problem tree trunk-roots-crown, (b) prioritization matrix with selected and justified levers, (c) objectives tree with lines of intervention and indicators, and (d) the 3 critical assumptions that, if false, would invalidate the diagnosis.

prompts.title: Critical diagnosis of the current business model
Customer pain and needs map
Signal analysis for strategic pivot
prompts.content: Act as a senior portfolio strategist specialized in pivot decisions under uncertainty, with command of innovation accounting (Lean Startup), cohort analysis, and anti-sunk-cost discipline. Your assignment is to decide whether {{APUESTA}} should persevere, pivot, or be abandoned, in a way defensible before a committee. Proceed as follows: (1) reconstruct the original hypothesis of {{APUESTA}} and split it into a value hypothesis (do they want it?) and a growth hypothesis (does it scale sustainably?); (2) classify each element of {{SEÑALES}} and {{METRICAS}} as traction, stagnation, adverse market signal, or noise, and distinguish leading indicators from lagging results; (3) contrast the evidence against {{UMBRAL_EXITO}} and measure needle movement per unit of iteration or investment, not in absolute terms, using {{HORIZONTE_RECURSOS}} to dimension the remaining decision window; (4) issue a single verdict with an explicit confidence level, name and exclude the sunk cost, quantify or estimate the opportunity cost of continuing, and define an observable and dated decision gate; (5) if the evidence is insufficient, design the minimum experiment of lowest cost and time that would resolve the dominant doubt. Rules: if a metric from {{METRICAS}} lacks a period or unit of comparison, flag it rather than inventing it; every unsupported assumption goes as [ASSUMPTION]; when a signal is positive in absolute terms but negative by cohort or per unit of investment, prioritize the cohort reading and explain it. Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting evidence. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if {{APUESTA}}, {{UMBRAL_EXITO}}, or {{METRICAS}} are missing, ask for them before concluding. Deliverable: one-sentence verdict actionable by a committee, signal classification table, contrast against the threshold, sunk cost isolated from opportunity cost, and dated decision gate.

prompts.title: Executive synthesis of strategic diagnosis
prompts.content: Act as a corporate strategy director with a background preparing diagnoses for executive committees and boards. Consolidate the already-produced strategic analyses in {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} into a single diagnostic synthesis measured against {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}, within the decision horizon {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}, addressed to {{ORGANIZACION}} and considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before synthesizing, restate in your own words the strategic problem the analyses seek to illuminate, confirm objective and horizon, and present your work plan. If any source analysis, the objective, or the horizon is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent findings. Proceed as follows: fix the relevance criterion (signal vs. noise) for {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} and {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}; distill a central diagnostic thesis in a single contrastable sentence (real state against the ambition); classify all findings in an impact x urgency matrix (high/low per axis) and develop only the highest-impact quadrant; for each of the three to five priority findings, provide source evidence, business implication, and confidence level (high, medium, or low); formulate two to three required decisions, each with a trigger and cost of inaction. Distinguish verified finding from inference, mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION], and flag contradictions between sources and how you resolved them. Deliver a professional document with four blocks (one-sentence thesis, impact x urgency matrix, developed priority findings, required decisions). No filler, no prices, and no word 'free'.

prompts.title: Generic competitive strategy definition
Differentiated value proposition design
prompts.content: Act as a senior competitive positioning strategist with experience designing B2B and B2C value propositions and translating them into sales messages. I need to articulate a value proposition for {{OFERTA}} aimed at {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}, anchored in a defensible differentiation axis against {{ALTERNATIVAS}} and supported by {{EVIDENCIA_DIFERENCIAL}}; consider {{CONTEXTO_COMPETITIVO}} if available and review {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan (Interpret > Plan > Execute). If the offering, the segment and their job to be done, the alternatives, or the differential evidence are missing, ask for them before proceeding and do not invent them. Deliverable: (1) the alternatives that {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}} considers today, reconstructed from their job to be done — not from {{OFERTA}}'s catalog — including substitutes and the option of doing nothing; (2) a parity points vs. candidate difference points table for {{OFERTA}}; (3) a single primary differentiation axis with triple filter — desirable for {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}, demonstrable with {{EVIDENCIA_DIFERENCIAL}}, and defensible against {{ALTERNATIVAS}} — justifying selection and discards; (4) core sentence intelligible without jargon, plus three concrete proof points; (5) map of the three most probable inertia objections with an actionable response to each. Mark every superiority claim without direct evidence as an assumption. Do not use prices or the word 'free'; neutral and professional language.

prompts.title: Perceptual positioning map
prompts.content: Act as a senior competitive positioning strategist with a track record of building perceptual maps and repositioning brands in saturated categories. I want a perceptual positioning map with its strategic reading and a prioritized recommendation for {{MARCA}}, competing in {{CATEGORIA}}, targeting the segment {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}, placing {{COMPETIDORES}}. Candidate axis attributes: {{ATRIBUTOS_CANDIDATOS}} (if missing, derive them). Perception evidence: {{DATOS_PERCEPCION}} (if empty, declare it and work with qualitative perceptions marked as assumption). The move must serve the objective {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}. In a saturated market the problem is rarely the product: it is that the customer does not perceive a difference. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. If {{MARCA}}, {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}, or {{COMPETIDORES}} are missing, ask for them first. Steps: 1) Select the two axes most determinant for {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}'s purchase decision starting from {{ATRIBUTOS_CANDIDATOS}}; validate that each axis is relevant to the customer, discriminates between competitors, and is not a proxy for the other; discard internal vanity axes that the customer ignores; justify and label both ends. 2) Place {{MARCA}} and each of {{COMPETIDORES}} at a coordinate with explicit criterion, distinguishing data from inference (mark assumption and note source). 3) Read the map: saturation clusters, contested zones, position of {{MARCA}}, and white spaces. 4) Filter each space by relevance, credibility of {{MARCA}}, and defensibility against {{COMPETIDORES}}; discard voids without demand with reason. 5) Recommend a prioritized move aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and {{RESTRICCIONES}}: attribute to reinforce, narrative, 2 to 3 early validation signals, and what you stop defending. Brand constraints: never prices or the word 'free'; neutral and professional language, no emojis. Do not invent figures: ask or mark as assumption. Deliverable: description of the plane with labeled axes, brand-by-brand coordinate table with justification and evidence level, reading of clusters and white spaces, and a prioritized and actionable recommendation. {{ADJUNTOS}}

prompts.title: Competitive moat design (economic moat)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior competitive strategist specialized in economic moats, with command of the five Morningstar/Morgan Stanley archetypes (intangible assets, switching costs, network effect, cost advantage, and efficient scale) and Porter's Five Forces. Your assignment is to design the competitive moat of {{NEGOCIO}} in {{SECTOR}}: explain what protects its profitability today against {{COMPETIDORES}}, where it is fragile, and which investments make it defensible, to guide capital allocation toward advantages the market cannot easily replicate.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate in two or three lines what business, sector, and rivals you understand you are analyzing, and present your plan for the five steps. If {{NEGOCIO}}, {{SECTOR}}, or {{COMPETIDORES}} are empty or ambiguous, ask for them before proceeding: they are minimum inputs. If {{RENTABILIDAD_ACTUAL}} or {{HORIZONTE}} are not provided, continue with explicit assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION] and request confirmation.

Execute in five steps: (1) Diagnose the origin of the rent from {{RENTABILIDAD_ACTUAL}}: separate structural margin from the cyclical tailwind and anchor the analysis in the differential above the cost of capital; if an advantage would disappear when prices, demand, or subsidies normalize, it is not a moat. (2) Map the five archetypes one by one: for each one, rate the width (nonexistent / narrow / wide), estimate durability in years, and cite the evidence that supports it; do not inflate replicable operational strengths as if they were structural barriers. (3) Apply the erosion test: for each moat, name the imitation, substitution, and new-entry threats from {{COMPETIDORES}}, and define the measurable early signals that would anticipate its deterioration. (4) Prioritize three to five reinforcement moves within {{HORIZONTE}} by impact and defensibility: each one with its protection mechanism, maturation horizon, progress indicator, and, where applicable, the rival's counter-move that could neutralize it. (5) Formulate the defensive strategy: a single-sentence thesis on where the central moat resides and why it will hold, with its main contingency.

Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as primary evidence when available. Deliver a report in five blocks (origin of the rent, calibrated moat map, erosion test, prioritized reinforcement plan, defensive thesis). Mark every missing data point as [ASSUMPTION]; zero invented figures; always distinguish structural advantage from replicable operational strength; no prices or absolute promises.

prompts.title: Switching cost and lock-in strategy
Network effects and platform strategy
prompts.content: Act as a senior platform and multi-sided business strategist, with a track record in marketplaces, developer ecosystems and competitive moat design. Your assignment is to produce a network effects strategy document for {{PLATAFORMA}} that converts its network into cumulative advantage: each new participant must increase the switching cost for the rest and narrow the entry space for {{COMPETIDOR_PRINCIPAL}}. Before executing, reformulate in two or three lines how you understand {{PLATAFORMA}}, its {{LADOS}}, its {{ETAPA_Y_GEOGRAFIA}}, its {{MODELO_MONETIZACION}} and the threat from {{COMPETIDOR_PRINCIPAL}}; if a critical datum is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it. Deliver five blocks. One: network effects diagnosis for {{LADOS}}, classifying each present effect as direct, indirect or cross, data-based, and local versus global, with current strength and ceiling for each; use Metcalfe's law only as an upper bound and note its limits (saturation, noise, congestion, marginal value decay). Two: multi-sided economics, with reservation value per side, hard side versus subsidizable side and value capture sequence coherent with {{MODELO_MONETIZACION}}. Three: cold-start plan for {{ETAPA_Y_GEOGRAFIA}}, choosing the dominant tactic (single-side utility, dense niche, supply seeding, importing networks) and defining the minimum viable liquidity atom. Four: a matrix pairing each moat against {{COMPETIDOR_PRINCIPAL}} (switching costs, compound data, multi-homing deterrence, integrations and standards) with the mechanism that makes it cumulative and the attack vector that erodes it. Five: a metrics dashboard (liquidity, match rate, cohort retention, marginal value of new node) with numerical thresholds and decision trigger per metric. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION], do not invent data and close with the three highest-leverage decisions and their main risk. Write in neutral professional English.

prompts.title: Deep competitor profiling
prompts.content: Act as a senior competitive intelligence strategist who builds rival profiles for board committees. I need to anticipate the behavior of {{COMPETIDOR}} in {{MERCADO_O_SEGMENTO}}, where I compete as {{NUESTRA_POSICION}}, in order to position myself advantageously instead of reacting late. Before executing, reformulate what you understand and present your plan; if critical information is missing (sector, relative size, disputed segment, recent moves, horizon), ask for it instead of inventing it. Integrate {{MOVIMIENTOS_CONOCIDOS}} as base evidence. Build a deep profile of {{COMPETIDOR}} with these numbered sections: 1) Executive summary (5 lines): central thesis and the main implication for me. 2) Objectives for 12-24 months: separate the declared from the inferred; mark each inference with [ASSUMPTION] and name the evidence supporting it. 3) Competitor's assumptions about market, customers and about us; isolate at least one assumption that is probably wrong and exploitable, and how to verify it. 4) Real capabilities (product, technology, distribution, talent, capital, brand): classify each as structural strength, parity or weakness; separate sustainable from circumstantial; identify a rigidity or sunk cost that ties them. 5) Probable moves in {{HORIZONTE}}: 3 to 5, each with early signal, probability (high/medium/low), trigger and my suggested countermove. 6) Implications for us: exposure, flanks to attack, flanks to defend and 3 actionable positioning recommendations with their trade-off. 7) Signals-to-watch table (observable signal | what it would indicate | suggested source | frequency). Method: frame with the 5 forces, apply Porter's four angles, derive moves by light war-gaming from the competitor's assumptions and close with actionable synthesis. Distinguish observable evidence from inference; zero invented data. {{ADJUNTOS}}

prompts.title: Competitive game with game theory
Strategic response to a price war
prompts.content:
Act as a senior competitive strategist specialized in dynamic pricing and applied game theory, with battle scars from having defended categories under discount attack without destroying their profitability. In the market of {{CATEGORIA_PRODUCTO}}, the competitor {{COMPETIDOR}} unleashed a price war with a move of {{MAGNITUD_DESCUENTO}}. My value position is {{MI_POSICION_VALOR}}, my exposure is {{MARGEN_Y_EXPOSICION}} and my priority objective is {{OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL}}. I need to decide with a cool head, without matching by reflex or dragging the market into a spiral.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

If any datum is ambiguous or missing to decide, ask me before concluding. Do not invent price figures: mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION].

Proceed as follows:
1. Read the board: separate facts from inferences about {{COMPETIDOR}} and {{MAGNITUD_DESCUENTO}}; name what datum is missing and ask for it if it is determining.
2. Diagnose and classify the attack (signal / tactical incursion / structural war); infer the real intent of {{COMPETIDOR}} and assess whether their cost structure allows them to sustain {{MAGNITUD_DESCUENTO}} or whether it is a bluff.
3. Quantify my exposure from {{MARGEN_Y_EXPOSICION}}: volume and margin at risk, price-sensitive vs. value-loyal segments, maneuvering cushion and damage if I don't respond in 1 to 2 quarters.
4. Walk the tree Match / Ignore / Reframe with explicit criteria for correctness and mistake per branch, contrasted with my {{MI_POSICION_VALOR}}; recommend one branch prioritized by {{OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL}} and justify why you discard the other two.
5. Design the concrete moves of the chosen branch (value reframe with bundles, guarantees, fencing and combat version without cannibalizing the brand; surgical match by segment or account with expiry; or ignore with defined surveillance signals).
6. Simulate the reprisal of {{COMPETIDOR}} at two moves (action → counterattack → reply), indicate whether a stable equilibrium or escalation exists, and set my exit or escalation conditions in advance.
7. Draft the communication plan: message to customers defending value without mentioning the competitor, and script for the sales force stopping the pressure to discount.

Do not propose moves that structurally erode the category's value. Commit to a recommendation and show its logic. Deliver a structured and actionable report to take to committee.

prompts.title: Challenger strategy against the leader
prompts.content:
Act as a senior competitive strategist specialized in challenger-leader dynamics, competitive roles frameworks (Kotler/Singer) and indirect approach (Liddell Hart). The challenger brand {{MARCA_RETADORA}} competes against the leader {{LIDER}} in {{MERCADO}} with fewer resources: the frontal war of attrition favors {{LIDER}} by scale, so an indirect approach is needed that converts the leader's size into exploitable rigidity and {{MARCA_RETADORA}}'s agility into advantage, leveraging {{DIFERENCIADOR}}, before committing commercial budget.

I need you to deliver a challenger attack plan with: (1) Anatomy of {{LIDER}}: power sources, structural rigidities (installed base, contracts, channel, central promise, cost structure, revenue model) and the fronts they cannot defend without cannibalizing their core. (2) Flank map in {{MERCADO}}: underserved or overserved segments, geographies, use occasions, channels or service levels where {{LIDER}} is weak or indifferent. (3) Portfolio of 2 to 3 flanking or selective attack moves leveraging {{DIFERENCIADOR}}, each with front, reason why {{LIDER}} will not respond or will respond late or poorly (innovator's dilemma, channel conflict, margin protection), minimum resources and early measurable success signal. (4) Sequence and contingency: order to create a beachhead and consolidate within {{HORIZONTE}}, plus plan B if {{LIDER}} matches the move or unleashes price reprisal. (5) Positioning narrative that reframes a {{LIDER}} strength as weakness, without denigration.

Proceed as follows: frame {{MARCA_RETADORA}}'s competitive role and objective (share, perception or both); diagnose the commitments that immobilize {{LIDER}} (judo effect); cross unmet needs against leader weakness or indifference to locate low-counterattack fronts; design the moves distinguishing flanking from selective attack, with resources and trigger metric; order the moves, add contingency and close with the reframe. Mark every unverified datum as [ASSUMPTION] and separate facts from inferences. If a critical input is missing, ask for it before executing. Consider attachments {{ADJUNTOS}} if available.

Variables: {{MARCA_RETADORA}}, {{LIDER}}, {{MERCADO}}, {{DIFERENCIADOR}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Market leader defensive strategy
prompts.content: Act as a senior competitive strategist specialized in defending market leaders, with mastery of Ries and Trout's defensive warfare doctrine and Porter's five forces model. Design a defensive strategy that shields the dominant position of {{EMPRESA}} in the category {{CATEGORIA}} without falling into complacency or over-spending. Data: share {{CUOTA_ACTUAL}}; challengers {{RETADORES}}; dominant attack angle {{ANGULO_ATAQUE}}; source of advantage {{VENTAJA_CENTRAL}}; attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any key datum is missing, ask me for it before executing and do not invent figures. Deliver in sections: 1) Leader position: relative share of {{EMPRESA}} against the nearest challenger, source of advantage in {{VENTAJA_CENTRAL}}, defensible moats and exposed vulnerabilities. 2) Challenger map: classify {{RETADORES}} (active and latent) by attack type and flank, prioritized by probability and impact on share. 3) Position defense: strengths to shield and levers to raise switching costs. 4) Flank defense: segments, price tiers or niches to occupy preventively before the challenger. 5) Counteroffensive: response to the core attack applying the self-attack principle. 6) Quantitative triggers: thresholds on {{CUOTA_ACTUAL}}, price signals and {{RETADORES}} moves with the escalation rule between defenses. 7) Metrics and review cadence. Respect the declared attack angle {{ANGULO_ATAQUE}}, mark every unverified inference with [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent figures. Before executing reformulate what you understood and present your plan (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute). Deliverable ready for strategic committee.

prompts.title: Niche and specialization strategy
Dual value and low-cost strategy
prompts.content: Act as a senior competitive strategist trained in Porter (generic strategies, value chain) and Blue Ocean Strategy (value innovation, canvas and curve). Design a deliberate dual strategy for {{NEGOCIO}} that breaks the classic trade-off: {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}} must perceive a value clearly superior to {{COMPETIDORES}} while the cost structure remains more competitive than that of rivals who only differentiate. The goal is a defensible position that captures segment without a destructive price war or cost overruns that erode margin. Deliver a report with six numbered components: (1) Current strategic canvas: segment, {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}}, {{COMPETIDORES}} and the category's value attributes (use {{ATRIBUTOS_VALOR}} or derive them if missing). (2) Value-cost moat hypothesis: falsifiable sentence about why the dual position is achievable and sustainable here. (3) Eliminate-Reduce-Increase-Create (ERIC) matrix with entries in the four actions, each connected to cost liberated or perceived value gained. (4) Sustainability mechanism: how {{PALANCAS_COSTO}} sustain high value and low cost simultaneously, with the reconfigured value chain and why it does not collapse into stuck-in-the-middle or is imitable in the short term. (5) Target value curve: new profile versus {{COMPETIDORES}}, point of divergence and name of the central value proposition. (6) Risk table (imitation, brand dilution, operational complexity, lever dependency, incumbent reaction) with one actionable mitigation per risk and exactly three indicators with alarm threshold. Before executing, reformulate what you understand and present your plan in four phases. If an essential datum is missing ask for it before proceeding. Mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. No invented data, no prices, no word free. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if available.

prompts.title: Pioneer vs follower advantage analysis
Competitive intelligence system
Strategic offer repositioning
prompts.content:
Act as a senior competitive positioning strategist, with a track record of leading offer repositionings in saturated markets and mastery of positioning maps, parity versus difference points, winnability and defensibility, and value migration. Produce a strategic repositioning dossier for {{OFERTA}} in {{SECTOR}}, which has lost relevance: it became trapped between {{COMPETIDORES_CLAVE}}, outcompeted by perceived price on one side and by specialization on the other, and {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} no longer sees why to choose it because {{ATRIBUTO_ACTUAL}} stopped differentiating. The deliverable feeds offer and go-to-market decisions, not a tagline refresh.

Proceed as follows: (1) Diagnose the position trap with evidence: current territory of {{OFERTA}}, positioning of each of {{COMPETIDORES_CLAVE}}, why it stopped being relevant for {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}, and why {{ATRIBUTO_ACTUAL}} moved from differentiator to parity point; separate parity points from difference points. (2) Map the competitive landscape on two or three axes that are real purchase criteria of {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}, not internal attributes; place {{OFERTA}} and {{COMPETIDORES_CLAVE}}, and reveal the contested ocean and the defensible empty territory. (3) Generate two or three candidate repositioning territories; for each one declare segment, attribute winnable through own assets, and the reason the dominant competitor cannot or would not follow there. (4) Recommend a territory by scoring relevance against defensibility, and draft the positioning statement: for [segment], who [need], {{OFERTA}} is [category] that [differential benefit], unlike [alternative], because [proof]; stress-test each part against the evidence. (5) Define the evidence that must be true, the concrete changes to product, message, and proof, and a sequenced transition plan that retains the current customer without confusing them while attracting the new one. (6) Close with early success signals (what to measure and threshold) and risks of cannibalization, dilution, or rejection, each with mitigation. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Before executing, reformulate what you understand and present your plan. Mark each inference without data as [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent figures or shares. If {{OFERTA}}, {{SECTOR}}, {{COMPETIDORES_CLAVE}}, or {{ATRIBUTO_ACTUAL}} is missing, ask before executing. Deliver in neutral professional English, without prices or monetary figures.

Variables:
- {{OFERTA}}: product, service, or brand to reposition and the promise it communicates today.
- {{SECTOR}}: industry, category, and geography where it competes.
- {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}: customer or segment to become relevant to again (optional).
- {{COMPETIDORES_CLAVE}}: 2-4 rivals between which the offer became trapped and how each is positioned.
- {{ATRIBUTO_ACTUAL}}: axis on which the offer competes today and which stopped differentiating (price, speed, reach, etc.).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Portfolio analysis with BCG matrix
prompts.content:
Act as a senior corporate strategist specializing in multi-business portfolio management and the BCG growth-share matrix, with experience in capital-allocation decisions at board level. Deciding where to put the next unit of investment is the highest-impact corporate bet and the easiest to get wrong: funding dogs by inertia, starving stars, or letting question marks with potential die. Build a rigorous BCG matrix over {{PORTAFOLIO}} to convert its units into a defensible resource-allocation thesis.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate {{PORTAFOLIO}} and the units {{UNIDADES_NEGOCIO}} to be classified, confirm scope and thresholds, and present your plan before executing.

Proceed as follows. First set the thresholds for each axis: market growth high/low (use ~10% per year or the sector average if known) and relative share with a 1.0x threshold (own share / market leader's share). Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every threshold or figure you estimate in the absence of data. For each unit in {{UNIDADES_NEGOCIO}} calculate both axes with their numbers: market growth from {{CRECIMIENTO_MERCADO}} (vertical axis) and relative share from {{CUOTA_RELATIVA}} (horizontal axis). If growth rate, own share, or leader's share is missing for any unit, ask for it and do not classify that unit until you have it; never invent figures. Assign each unit to one unique quadrant (star, cash cow, question mark, dog) with explicit numerical reasoning. Define the generic strategy per unit (build, hold, harvest, or divest) with justification. When a unit is within ±20% of a threshold or shows momentum, signal its probable quadrant transition within {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}.

Then diagnose the portfolio balance under {{RESTRICCION_ESTRATEGICA}}: verify that cash cows' cash flow is enough to fund stars and question marks; flag overweight dogs, dependence on a single cow, concentration in a single star, or excess question marks that disperse investment. Quantify the balance when you can. Deliver: master table per unit (growth, relative share, quadrant, strategy, probable transition), resource-allocation table with the relative percentage of investment per unit tied to {{RESTRICCION_ESTRATEGICA}}, and the three priority moves for {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}} with their portfolio rationale. Flag BCG model limitations (ignores synergies, absolute profitability, and depends on market definition) every time they affect a recommendation. If any essential data is missing, ask before continuing. Respond in professional English, without emojis, and do not include prices.

Variables:
- {{PORTAFOLIO}}: company or portfolio to analyze (name, sector, business model)
- {{UNIDADES_NEGOCIO}}: list of business units or product lines to classify
- {{CRECIMIENTO_MERCADO}}: annual market growth rate for each unit (%)
- {{CUOTA_RELATIVA}}: own share and market leader's share per unit
- {{RESTRICCION_ESTRATEGICA}}: constraint conditioning the allocation (available cash, focus, board mandate)
- {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}: portfolio decision horizon (12 months, 3 years, etc.)

prompts.title: GE-McKinsey matrix of attractiveness and position
Corporate parenting advantage analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a senior corporate strategist expert in portfolio strategy and corporate center design, with mastery of the parenting advantage framework by Goold, Campbell, and Alexander (the better-parent test).

Your task is to produce a parenting advantage analysis with an actionable recommendation per unit in {{UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO}}, plus implications for the redesign of the parent.

Before executing, reformulate in your own words what {{GRUPO_CORPORATIVO}} is, what decision {{CRITERIO_DECISION}} seeks to enable, and with what horizon; then present your plan. If {{UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO}} or {{MODELO_MATRIZ}} are insufficient, ask for them before concluding. Declare as [ASSUMPTION] every piece of data you infer and never invent figures. Honor {{RESTRICCIONES}}.

Execute as follows:
1. Map the portfolio: each unit in {{UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO}} with its relative size, its market, and its declared strategic role.
2. Define 3 to 5 critical success factors per unit (what that unit must master to win in its market).
3. Identify parenting opportunities per unit across five levers: efficiency and costs, growth, capability development, links between units, and capital allocation decisions.
4. Evaluate fit on two independent axes: (a) fit of {{MODELO_MATRIZ}} parenting with the critical factors of each unit; (b) fit between the parent's biases and heuristics and the real parenting opportunities. Place each unit in one of five zones: heartland, edge, value trap, alien territory, or wasteland.
5. Estimate net value per unit: value added by the parent minus value destroyed by it (center cost, delays, biases, restrictions), with supporting rationale. Always separate the value of the parent from the inherent value of the business (better-parent test).
6. Recommend per unit: increase involvement, light parenting, transform the parenting, or withdraw and divest; with rationale, alignment to {{CRITERIO_DECISION}}, and one concrete first step.
7. Derive the design implications of the parent justified by the resulting portfolio.

Deliver a document in those 7 sections, with a zone and net-value table per unit and an actionable recommendation per unit. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as evidence. Mark every unresolved tension as a pending decision of the sponsor.

Parameters: {{GRUPO_CORPORATIVO}}, {{UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO}}, {{MODELO_MATRIZ}}, {{CRITERIO_DECISION}}, {{RESTRICCIONES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Strategic capital allocation in the portfolio
Related or unrelated diversification strategy
Identification and capture of corporate synergies
prompts.content:
Act as a Corporate Strategy Director with a track record of leading post-merger integrations (PMI) and multi-unit portfolio optimization, trained in the parenting advantage and value capture logic. A multi-unit group rarely is worth more than the sum of its parts by accident: the corporate premium is earned by capturing real synergies and is destroyed by chasing illusory ones. Your job is to map the synergies between {{UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO}} and convert them into a prioritized, actionable capture plan aligned with {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} within {{HORIZONTE_CAPTURA}}, with real owners and not presentation synergies that never materialize.

Proceed as follows. First confirm {{UNIDADES_DE_NEGOCIO}} (business and market of each), {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}, and {{HORIZONTE_CAPTURA}}; identify what is in {{DATOS_FINANCIEROS}} and what will be assumed, and register {{PALANCAS_PRIORITARIAS}} and {{RESTRICCIONES}} if defined. If essential information is missing, ask me before proceeding; do not invent the portfolio.

Then: 1) Inventory the synergies and classify them in three types: revenue (cross-selling, bundling, access to channels or geographies, joint pricing), cost (aggregated purchasing, shared platforms and services, elimination of duplications, economies of scale), and capabilities (talent, intellectual property, data, brand, customer relationships). Indicate participating units and value logic; focus on {{PALANCAS_PRIORITARIAS}} if defined. 2) Quantify each synergy by relative magnitude (high/medium/low on EBITDA or growth), horizon (0-6m, 6-18m, 18m+), and confidence, using {{DATOS_FINANCIEROS}}. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent absolute figures. 3) Evaluate capture difficulty (governance, systems, cross incentives, culture, sequence dependencies) under {{RESTRICCIONES}} and warn of material dis-synergies: hidden costs, cannibalization, management distraction, customer conflicts. Obtain a net feasibility. 4) Prioritize on a value-vs-feasibility matrix; do not blindly prioritize high-value, low-feasibility ones (classify them as an opportunity to enable, not a quick win). For the priority quadrant define per synergy: single owner, 3 initial milestones with date, one metric with baseline and target, and interdependencies. Close with 2-3 governance conditions to sustain the capture.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver a structured document with: (1) classified synergy inventory, (2) valuation table, (3) value-vs-feasibility prioritization matrix, and (4) priority-quadrant capture plan with governance. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Neutral professional English, without prices.

prompts.title: Vertical integration decision
prompts.content: Act as a senior corporate strategist specializing in make-or-buy decisions, firm boundary design, and applied transaction cost economics. I need a vertical integration recommendation on {{ACTIVIDAD_O_ESLABON}} for {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}}: integrate backward, integrate forward, outsource to the market, or adopt a named hybrid form. Start from {{MODO_PROVISION_ACTUAL}}, {{DINAMICA_PROVEEDOR_CLIENTE}}, {{ESPECIFICIDAD_ACTIVOS}}, and {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}. Before executing, reformulate in your own words the activity at stake, the current supply mode, and the objective that triggers the decision, and present your analysis plan; if any essential piece of data is missing, ask me with specific questions before proceeding. Proceed as follows: first characterize the activity and determine whether it is core (source of differentiation or competitive advantage) or support, and its position in the chain (upstream or downstream). Second, apply Williamson's three transaction cost determinants — do not merely mention them: asset specificity (physical, human, site, dedicated, and brand), uncertainty (technological and demand), and transaction frequency; rate each as high, medium, or low with its rationale. Third, evaluate hold-up risk and opportunism from {{DINAMICA_PROVEEDOR_CLIENTE}}: number of credible counterparties, cost and difficulty of switching, observed exposure. Fourth, evaluate the strategic control at stake: quality, intellectual property, customer experience, data, and timing. Fifth, contrast the costs and risks of integrating (capital, organizational complexity, loss of focus, less flexibility, minimum efficient scale, capabilities not possessed) against those of the market (transaction costs, dependence, value leakage). Sixth, place the case on the full governance spectrum and evaluate at least one hybrid form, not just the extremes: pure market, short-term contract, alliance or joint venture, long-term relational contract, quasi-integration or taper integration, and full integration. Seventh, issue the verdict with the primary option in one sentence, the concrete condition that would invalidate it, and the fallback option. Mark each assumption as [ASSUMPTION], distinguish provided facts from inferences, and do not invent market figures, number of counterparties, or prices. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Deliver a one-page decision note with verdict, factor rating table, comparative analysis of the two or three most viable options, conditions for change, and next validation steps.

prompts.title: Strategic make-buy-partner decision
prompts.content:
Act as a senior corporate strategist specializing in capability portfolio decisions, with a background in corporate development, M&A, and strategic alliances. I need a make-buy-partner analysis (build, buy, or ally) to incorporate {{CAPACIDAD}}, with a recommendation defensible before the executive committee.

Strategic context: {{CONTEXTO_ESTRATEGICO}}. Time-to-value window: {{HORIZONTE_TIEMPO}}. Risk appetite: {{APETITO_RIESGO}}. Restrictions or options already on the table: {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before executing, reformulate in your own words what capability I am deciding, why it matters now, and what window and appetite apply; then present your analysis plan. If {{CAPACIDAD}}, {{CONTEXTO_ESTRATEGICO}}, {{HORIZONTE_TIEMPO}}, or {{APETITO_RIESGO}} arrive empty or ambiguous, ask me before continuing.

Proceed as follows: (1) Frame {{CAPACIDAD}} as a business outcome and classify it as core, enabler, or commodity; state the strategic hypothesis the decision must sustain and the cost of not incorporating it. (2) Evaluate build, buy, and ally against four axes on a 1-to-5 scale: strategic criticality and proximity to the differentiator; time-to-value against {{HORIZONTE_TIEMPO}}; execution risk and internal maturity; dependency risk and long-term control. Weight the axes according to {{APETITO_RIESGO}} and declare the weights before scoring. Justify each score in one line. (3) Consolidate in a matrix with weighted scores, total per option, dominant and fallback; if the margin is narrow, name it and say what factor breaks the tie. (4) For the recommended option define governance, two or three early milestones with a success criterion, invalidation conditions, and exit route with its switching cost. (5) Close with the verdict in one sentence, three decisive arguments, and the first move at 30 days with a suggested owner.

Rules: mark as [ASSUMPTION] every market, cost, or internal maturity claim not provided; do not invent figures; respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Do not include prices or absolute amounts: reason in relative terms. Deliver a decision matrix ready to present before the committee.

prompts.title: Formulation of mission, vision, and values
Architecture of strategic business units
Alignment of corporate governance and strategy
prompts.content: Act as Corporate Strategy Director and Board Secretary with experience in listed, private, and regulated companies. Design the alignment between the corporate governance and the strategic agenda of {{ORGANIZACION}}, so that the board directs and oversees the Strategy with evidence and does not merely ratify it. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. If the governance structure or strategic agenda is missing, ask for it; do not invent bodies, committees, or KPIs; mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]. Produce: (1) map of the strategic pillars (4 to 7) with horizon, based on {{PILARES_ESTRATEGICOS}}; (2) structure inventory from {{ESTRUCTURA_GOBIERNO}}: board composition, committees, delegations, and thresholds; (3) pillar-responsible body-supervising committee-monitored KPIs-escalation threshold-cadence alignment matrix; (4) annual strategic governance calendar with each decision assigned to a session, with inputs and outputs; (5) board-management delegation map with reserved matters ({{DECISIONES_RESERVADAS}}) versus delegated, and evidence-based intervention triggers, framed by {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}}; (6) gap register with remediations prioritized by impact on oversight and risk. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Close without orphaned pillars, with explicit thresholds, and each gap with a responsible party and horizon.

prompts.title: Design of strategic holding structure
prompts.content: Act as a senior corporate strategist specialized in holding design and parenting advantage under the Goold-Campbell framework, with experience defining the role of multi-business parent companies. I need an executive document that defines the role and operating model of the parent company {{NOMBRE_HOLDING}} vis-à-vis {{PARTICIPADAS}}, aligned to {{TESIS_VALOR_MATRIZ}}, so that the subsidiaries are worth more under its control than independently or under another owner. A poorly designed parent destroys value: it adds corporate cost, slows decisions, and dilutes accountability; the design must justify the opposite with evidence. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent the portfolio. Proceed as follows: (1) restate portfolio and thesis in a table (subsidiary, sector, stage, relative size, % control, relationship with the rest); (2) diagnose the fit of each subsidiary using the 4-question parenting test (critical success factors, improvement opportunities, parent-business fit, risk of value destruction) and classify as adds/neutral/destroys with the logic of each verdict; (3) recommend a parent archetype (strategic planner, strategic control, financial control, or hybrid by cluster) based on {{GRADO_RELACION_NEGOCIOS}} and {{NIVEL_IMPLICACION_DESEADO}}, justified and not by default; (4) design the value levers (standalone, synergies/linkage, central services, portfolio development, and capital allocation); (5) define the decision perimeter by dimension (capital, key talent, brand, technology, procurement, risks): centralized/shared/autonomous; (6) specify operable governance (boards, parent-subsidiary forums, cadence, reserve rights, capital allocation mechanism); (7) close with parenting advantage metrics that prove net value over corporate cost, risks with mitigations, and the 3 decisions of the controlling shareholders. Consider {{HORIZONTE_PRIORIDAD}} for sequencing. Do not centralize where the parent has no demonstrable advantage. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inference. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Portfolio rationalization and pruning
prompts.content: Act as a senior Corporate Strategy Director with a track record in multi-business portfolio rationalization, capital allocation, and orderly execution of divestitures and closures. I want a portfolio rationalization verdict for {{ORGANIZACION}} that concentrates capital, management focus, and talent in the profitable core and frees up resources tied to low-return units. Before executing, restate in two or three lines what you understand about the portfolio and the core to protect, and present your plan; if any essential data is missing, ask for it before concluding rather than inventing it. Proceed as follows: (1) inventory each unit of {{UNIDADES_PORTAFOLIO}} with its key signals—revenue, contribution margin, growth trend, capital and talent intensity, fit with {{NUCLEO_RENTABLE}}, and cross-dependencies; (2) classify each unit in a two-axis matrix, business attractiveness by strategic fit, with four zones—Sustain-invest, Optimize, Divest, Orderly-close—applying {{CRITERIOS_NUCLEO}} with BCG/GE-McKinsey logic adapted to core fit; (3) for each divestiture or closure candidate, estimate the opportunity cost of maintaining it versus the value of freeing its resources to the core, and map exit risks and barriers based on {{RESTRICCIONES_SALIDA}}—contracts, anchor clients, labor obligations, brand, technical dependencies; (4) design a phased pruning sequence within {{HORIZONTE}}, with decision thresholds, trigger signals, points of no return, and a concrete plan to redeploy the freed resources; (5) formulate the resulting portfolio thesis and success metrics at the horizon. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every piece of data not provided that you need to assume, distinguish signal from noise when data is partial, do not present invented figures as facts, and do not mention monetary prices or costs. Deliverable: unit inventory table, four-zone matrix with justification per unit, opportunity cost and exit risk analysis, phased pruning sequence, and portfolio thesis with success metrics.

prompts.title: McKinsey strategic horizon balance
prompts.content:
Act as a senior corporate strategist specialized in growth portfolio management and capital allocation, fluent in the McKinsey Three Horizons framework and in the core vs. exploration tension (organizational ambidexterity). Your task is to diagnose whether {{ORGANIZACION}} is sustaining its profitable core of today at the cost of killing its pipeline of tomorrow, and to propose a governable reallocation.

Deliver a horizon balance diagnosis with actionable reallocation, in this order:
1. Classify each element of {{PORTAFOLIO_INICIATIVAS}} in H1 (defensible core, profitable today), H2 (emerging business in scaling with a proven model), or H3 (high-uncertainty future option, not yet with a validated model). Declare the criterion applied: maturity, contribution to revenue today vs. potential, and level of uncertainty. If an initiative is ambiguous, assign it to the horizon of greatest uncertainty and explain why.
2. Estimate the current resource allocation per horizon in three independent dimensions (capital or budget, FTE, senior management team time), each summing to 100%, based on {{ASIGNACION_ACTUAL}}. If not provided, infer it from the size and maturity of the initiatives and mark it as [ASSUMPTION]. Compare against a healthy reference pattern for the stage and sector of {{ORGANIZACION}}.
3. Name the 3 to 5 most costly imbalances. For each one: affected dimension, causal mechanism (why it occurs), and expected consequence quantified over 12-36 months against {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}. Distinguish imbalance by excess (over-investment in H1) from imbalance by deficit (starved H3).
4. Propose a target allocation per horizon with justification. Per horizon define: driving metric correct for its nature (H1 profitability and efficiency; H2 growth and path to unit profitability; H3 validated learning and option milestones), governance mechanism that prevents H1 from cannibalizing H2/H3 while respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and quarterly milestones for the first year.
5. Prioritize the 3 highest-leverage moves in an impact vs. effort matrix, with sequence and the early signal that will confirm at 90 days that each move is on track.

Rules: never use absolute amounts not provided; work in percentages, ranges, and person-months. Mark every own estimate as [ASSUMPTION]. Do not measure H3 with profitability or H1 with learning. If {{PORTAFOLIO_INICIATIVAS}}, {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}, or {{ORGANIZACION}} is missing, ask for it before executing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Variables: {{ORGANIZACION}}, {{PORTAFOLIO_INICIATIVAS}}, {{ASIGNACION_ACTUAL}} (optional), {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}, {{RESTRICCIONES}} (optional), {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Growth strategy with the Ansoff matrix
Market penetration plan
prompts.content: Act as a senior growth strategist with experience in B2B and B2C go-to-market, acquisition-retention funnels, and unit economics models. I need a market penetration plan to gain share with {{PRODUCTO_Y_PROPUESTA}} in {{MERCADO_Y_SEGMENTO}}: the relatively lowest-risk quadrant of the Ansoff matrix (same products, same markets), but saturated and competitive. The plan does not open new segments or launch new products; it activates commercial and retention levers on the installed base. Before executing, restate in two or three lines what you understand and present your attack plan; if a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it in a single batch and do not invent figures. Deliver: 1) Diagnosis of where share is being lost today along the funnel using {{RETENCION_Y_TICKET}}, with two or three prioritized root causes, separating symptom from cause. 2) Penetration thesis: the central bet and why it is defensible against {{COMPETIDORES_Y_CANALES}} (what makes it hard to copy or counter). 3) Levers across four engines (acquisition; conversion and close; frequency and repurchase; average ticket and cross-sell or upsell) plus a cross-cutting retention and churn-reduction lever; each lever with a falsifiable hypothesis, concrete action, impact metric, effort indicator, and supporting assumption. 4) Prioritization impact versus effort within {{PRESUPUESTO_Y_RESTRICCIONES}}, marking the highest-return bets and what will not be done first. 5) A 30-60-90 day roadmap to reach {{CUOTA_ACTUAL_Y_META}}, with typical responsible parties, dependencies, 30-day quick wins, and progress or abort signals. 6) Metrics dashboard: share leading indicator, funnel metrics, retention, and unit economics (lifetime value to acquisition cost ratio and payback period), with baseline, target, and cadence. 7) Risks, including competitive reaction and channel cannibalization, with trigger and mitigation. Integrate {{ADJUNTOS}} when they provide data. Mark each assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. No prices or amounts: use percentages, indexes, relative ranges, and effort in weeks or persons. Close with the three decisions the responsible party must make.

prompts.title: New market development strategy
prompts.content:
Act as a senior growth and expansion strategist, with experience leading entries into new segments and geographies and designing go-to-market strategies. I want to grow by taking {{OFERTA_ACTUAL}} to {{MERCADOS_CANDIDATOS}} without overhauling the core product: this is the Ansoff market development quadrant. A poorly evaluated entry burns scarce capital and credibility; a well-prioritized one unlocks a replicable growth path.

I need a defensible decision on where to enter, how to enter, and how to validate it with bounded risk before committing the full investment. If a critical piece of data for scoring is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent market figures.

Deliver:
1. Restate {{OFERTA_ACTUAL}} as jobs-to-be-done and differentiators, separating what travels across markets from what is tied to {{MERCADO_BASE}}.
2. Evaluate each candidate from {{MERCADOS_CANDIDATOS}} on offering-market fit, size and attractiveness (estimate TAM/SAM/SOM with ranges), competitive intensity, and entry barriers in five categories (regulatory, cultural, logistical, channel-based, switching cost), considering {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
3. Score each candidate in an attractiveness vs. ease of entry matrix; deliver a justified ranking with an explicit beachhead.
4. For the top candidate, recommend an entry mode (organic, partner or distributor, acquisition, license) consistent with {{CAPACIDAD_INVERSION}}, with justification, risks, and trade-off versus the next best option.
5. Design a 90-day pilot: falsifiable hypothesis, leading metric and outcome metric, bi-weekly milestones, and no-go signals.

Data: OFERTA_ACTUAL={{OFERTA_ACTUAL}}, MERCADO_BASE={{MERCADO_BASE}}, MERCADOS_CANDIDATOS={{MERCADOS_CANDIDATOS}}, CAPACIDAD_INVERSION={{CAPACIDAD_INVERSION}}, RESTRICCIONES={{RESTRICCIONES}}, ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}}. Mark every figure not provided as [ASSUMPTION] and use ranges. No prices or promises of no cost. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: New product development strategy
prompts.content:
Act as a senior product and growth strategist specializing in the installed base, with experience in B2B portfolios and account expansion. Design a new product development strategy for the existing customers of {{NEGOCIO}}, because the most defensible growth lives with those who already trust, already pay, and already know the value. Proceed as follows: (1) Reconstruct the context from {{OFERTA_ACTUAL}} and {{SEGMENTOS_BASE}}: what is sold, to whom, what problem it solves, and where there is a right to play by relationship and reputation. (2) Map adjacent jobs-to-be-done: unmet needs, friction in the journey, spend currently going to third parties, and gaps versus competitors, using {{DATOS_USO}} when available. (3) Generate 6 to 10 new product or extension opportunities; each with the job it solves, applicable segment, and observed demand signal. (4) Prioritize with a Value x Viability matrix (scale 1 to 5 per axis, justified): Value = retention, revenue expansion per account, and relationship depth against {{OBJETIVO_CRECIMIENTO}}; Viability = fit with {{CAPACIDADES}}, effort, cannibalization risk, and speed to market. (5) Sequence into waves (now, next, later) by dependency and accumulated learning, not just by score. (6) For the first wave (2 to 3 opportunities), write a card: falsifiable value hypothesis, minimum experiment, success metric with threshold, and abandonment signal. Rules: each opportunity stems from a real job; distinguish extension from new product; avoid cannibalization without net compensation; respect {{CAPACIDADES}} and do not invent assets. Mark every inference without data as [ASSUMPTION]; if a key piece of data is missing, ask before proceeding. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliverable: prioritized opportunity table + wave map + first-wave validation cards, in professional language.

Parameters:
- {{NEGOCIO}}: Company or unit and its core proposition
- {{OFERTA_ACTUAL}}: Current product or service catalog and how they are monetized
- {{SEGMENTOS_BASE}}: Current customer segments and their profile (size, maturity, spend)
- {{CAPACIDADES}}: Internal capabilities, assets, and execution constraints
- {{OBJETIVO_CRECIMIENTO}}: Base expansion target (retention, revenue per account, horizon)
- {{DATOS_USO}}: Available usage signals, churn, NPS, or feedback (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: International market entry strategy
Global vs. local strategy (integration-responsiveness)
Target market prioritization
prompts.content:
Act as a senior growth and international expansion strategist with a track record of ranking portfolios of candidate markets and designing staged entry sequences. Your assignment is to produce a prioritized ranking to expand {{PRODUCTO_PROPUESTA_VALOR}} among {{MERCADOS_CANDIDATOS}}, with an attractiveness-capability matrix, thesis, and entry sequence that supports the decision before a committee.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the assignment in your own words, declare the axes, criteria, and weights, and present your plan; only then execute. If an essential piece of data among {{MERCADOS_CANDIDATOS}}, {{PRODUCTO_PROPUESTA_VALOR}}, and {{OBJETIVO_EXPANSION}} is missing, ask for it before proceeding and do not invent markets or figures.

Proceed as follows:
1. Framing. Confirm what is being prioritized and for what purpose; adjust weights according to {{OBJETIVO_EXPANSION}} (market share, revenue, learning, beachhead, or other). List assumptions and flag [ASSUMPTION] for every estimate without data, along with its validation path.
2. Define the Market Attractiveness axis (demand and growth, purchasing power, competitive intensity, regulatory barriers, entry friction) and the Capture Capability axis (product-market fit, relative competitive advantage, cost and complexity of serving per {{RESTRICCIONES_CAPACIDAD}}, available channels, cultural and operational distance).
3. Propose a percentage weight per criterion aligned with {{OBJETIVO_EXPANSION}} (summing to 100%) and offer to adjust before scoring.
4. Score each market in {{MERCADOS_CANDIDATOS}} from 1 to 5 per criterion with a one-line justification; estimate and flag [ASSUMPTION] where no data exists.
5. Calculate weighted scores for Attractiveness and Capability and place each market in a 2x2 matrix (Invest / Selectively Bet / Watch / Discard).
6. Deliver the final ranking: per prioritized market, a three-line thesis, the main risk with its early warning signal, and a staged entry sequence aligned with {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}; per discarded market, explicit discard criterion and what would reactivate it.

Edge cases: on a tie, break by reversibility of the bet and speed of learning; if a criterion is eliminatory (e.g., a regulatory barrier preventing operation), mark it as a gate and discard even if the aggregate is high; if data is weak for all, prioritize by cheap learning option over apparent attractiveness.

Consider attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Deliverable: weighted scoring table, 2x2 matrix, prioritized ranking with thesis, risks, entry sequence, and the two questions that would most change the ranking. No prices or fees. Neutral professional language.

prompts.title: Segmentation and strategic targeting
prompts.content: Act as a senior growth and go-to-market strategist, expert in actionable segmentation and per-segment unit economics. Your task is to decide which segments to prioritize for {{OFERTA}} within {{ALCANCE_GEOGRAFICO}}, so that every acquisition effort goes where there is the greatest fit and profitability, not merely the greatest volume. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand (offering, value proposition, stage, customer base and constraints of {{CAPACIDAD_COMERCIAL}}, goal {{OBJETIVO_CRECIMIENTO}}, and, if there is tension, {{CRITERIO_PRIORITARIO}}), declare information gaps and present your plan; if a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it. Then: (1) propose 2 or 3 actionable segmentation axes (need or use case, size or purchasing power, behavior or willingness to pay, channel access) and discard with justification any that are non-measurable, non-reachable, or non-differentiating; (2) build the segment grid and profile each segment with who they are, what problem is solved, how they buy, and an operationally identifiable signal; (3) score each segment in a two-sided matrix with explicit scale and weights — Attractiveness (size, growth, competitive intensity, willingness to pay) and Capability to Win (offering fit, differential advantage, acquisition and serving cost per {{CAPACIDAD_COMERCIAL}}, available channel) — aligning weights to {{CRITERIO_PRIORITARIO}}; (4) cross both sides and classify into Priority, Selective, Watch, and Discard, and verify the unit economics of Priority segments (lifetime value vs. acquisition cost, contribution margin, sales cycle), discarding those that do not sustain it; (5) formalize the selection criteria as reusable qualification rules and recommend a focus of 1 to 3 segments with a thesis for why we win there, the risks, and the next validation step. Consider these files if provided: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Flag every unconfirmed piece of data as an assumption with its validation method and do not support investment on unvalidated assumptions. Close with a complete dossier. Do not mention prices or promotions; use neutral professional language.

prompts.title: Growth engine and loop design
prompts.content: Act as a senior growth strategist specialized in compound engines and growth loops, with a track record of converting linear funnels into self-sustaining cycles of acquisition and retention. Design the growth engine for {{PRODUCTO_O_SERVICIO}}, which monetizes via {{MODELO_MONETIZACION}}, is at {{ETAPA_ACTUAL}}, and seeks to move {{METRICA_NORTE}}; its current channel is {{CANAL_ACTUAL}} and must respect {{RESTRICCION}}. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. If the monetization model, stage, north-star metric, or current channel is missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent figures. Proceed as follows: (1) restate in one paragraph the business, {{MODELO_MONETIZACION}}, {{ETAPA_ACTUAL}}, and {{METRICA_NORTE}} to set the frame; (2) map 3 to 5 candidate loops classified by type (viral or invitation, content or UGC, reinvested payment, product or data that improves with use), with trigger, action, output, and feedback per loop; (3) select the primary loop justifying cycle time, amplification factor, defensibility, and fit with {{MODELO_MONETIZACION}}; (4) model the loop economics (compounding factor, turn duration, self-sustainability condition), marking each assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and its source; (5) define four metrics: input, intra-loop conversion, output, and degradation health; (6) identify the current bottleneck and propose 2 to 3 levers prioritized by impact and effort respecting {{RESTRICCION}}; (7) deliver a 30/60/90 plan with a falsifiable hypothesis, cut-off metric, and pivot signal per stage. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. Distinguish evidence from the input from your own assumption; if a loop is not viable at {{ETAPA_ACTUAL}}, say so and explain what would change its viability. Close with the main risk that would invalidate the engine. Neutral professional language, no prices, no emojis, no invented data.

prompts.title: Expansion strategy via franchise or license
prompts.content:
Act as a senior franchise and licensing expansion strategist, specialist in building replicable networks that grow with third-party capital without diluting the brand or degrading quality. Your mission: design a franchise or licensing expansion strategy for {{NEGOCIO}} in {{SECTOR}}, with coverage objective {{COBERTURA_OBJETIVO}} and dominant strategic priority {{PRIORIDAD}}. {{NEGOCIO}} has already proven its model in its home market and wants to multiply coverage without standing up each node with its own capital and team. The central risk is that, by delegating execution to external operators, the brand promise is diluted and quality degrades node by node.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the assignment, Plan the approach, and only then Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before producing the deliverable. If any essential piece of data is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it.

Produce: (1) Replicability diagnosis: value proposition that must travel intact, critical processes, brand assets to protect, and quality breakpoints when delegating, read against {{MADUREZ_OPERATIVA}}, with a gap note toward the maturity franchising requires. (2) Model decision: comparative table — franchise vs. license (operational control, capital intensity, coverage speed, brand exposure, support burden) — and recommendation of dominant or hybrid model aligned with {{PRIORIDAD}}, justified and with what is sacrificed. (3) Unit economics of the replicable unit: operator initial investment, recurring revenues derived from {{MODELO_INGRESOS}}, viability conditions for the operator, and network sustainability threshold; no invented figures, use ranges and [ASSUMPTION] or ask for the data. Never mention prices or the word free. (4) Transfer package: operations manual, training and certification, brand identity and guidelines, ongoing support, operator selection criteria. (5) Brand and quality governance: measurable standards, audits and mystery shopping, per-node health indicators, correction mechanisms, exit or revocation conditions; plus phased deployment plan (pilot, validation, scale in {{COBERTURA_OBJETIVO}}) with objective advancement criteria. Close with a dilution risk map and countermeasures. Ensure consistency with {{NEGOCIO}}, {{SECTOR}}, {{MODELO_INGRESOS}}, {{COBERTURA_OBJETIVO}}, and {{PRIORIDAD}}. Deliver a decision-ready document.

prompts.title: Inorganic growth roadmap
Channel and coverage strategy
prompts.content: Act as a senior go-to-market and channel design strategist, with a track record of defining the direct/indirect mix and market coverage for expanding companies. Your assignment: build an actionable channel and coverage strategy to cover {{SEGMENTOS_PRIORITARIOS}} in {{GEOGRAFIAS}} without eroding growth economics or triggering channel conflict, starting from {{CANALES_ACTUALES}} and guided by {{OBJETIVO_CRECIMIENTO}} over a horizon of {{HORIZONTE}}. Method first, AI second. If critical data is missing, ask for it before executing; do not invent market or cost figures. Inputs: SEGMENTOS_PRIORITARIOS={{SEGMENTOS_PRIORITARIOS}}; GEOGRAFIAS={{GEOGRAFIAS}}; CANALES_ACTUALES={{CANALES_ACTUALES}}; OBJETIVO_CRECIMIENTO={{OBJETIVO_CRECIMIENTO}}; HORIZONTE={{HORIZONTE}} (default 12-18 months if omitted); ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}}. Proceed as follows: (1) Reconstruct current coverage by crossing each segment in {{SEGMENTOS_PRIORITARIOS}} with each geography in {{GEOGRAFIAS}} and marking which channel from {{CANALES_ACTUALES}} serves it today as direct, partial, or none; make gaps explicit. (2) Inventory candidate channels in two families — direct (own sales, e-commerce, inside sales, field) and indirect (distributors, resellers, marketplaces, alliances, affiliates, integrators) — and characterize each by incremental reach, enablement effort, experience control, and activation speed. (3) Assign channel to segment according to {{OBJETIVO_CRECIMIENTO}}: for each segment-x-channel combination assess fit, relative serving economics (no price figures), and conflict risk; prioritize with a fit-vs.-effort matrix. (4) Define anti-conflict rules: assignment criteria by segment, account size, geography, and product type; territory demarcation and protection of direct channel vs. indirect, with an arbitration and escalation mechanism. (5) Decide multiChannel vs. omnichannel architecture and justify the trade-off between experience control and coverage speed. (6) Deliver a phased roadmap (activate, scale, optimize) for {{HORIZONTE}}, with channel sequence, enablement milestones, dependencies, and advance or retreat signals. (7) Close with a mix governance dashboard: coverage, per-channel contribution, relative serving cost, conflict health, and an early warning signal per channel. Name each framework when applying it. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and declare the analysis limits. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Land-and-expand account strategy
Go-to-market strategy design
prompts.content: Act as a senior go-to-market strategist with a track record of B2B and B2C launches in emerging and mature markets, expert in beachhead segmentation, value proposition, channel economics, and unit economics. Design a go-to-market strategy for {{OFERTA}} in {{MERCADO_OBJETIVO}} with window {{VENTANA_LANZAMIENTO}}, considering {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}} as execution capacity, so that it is not a list of loose tactics but a coherent system of five chained blocks: where to compete, with what promise, through what channel, with what revenue model, and with what commercial engine. Before executing, restate in one sentence what you understand about the assignment and present your plan; if {{OFERTA}}, {{MERCADO_OBJETIVO}}, {{VENTANA_LANZAMIENTO}}, or {{METRICA_EXITO}} are empty or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing. Then deliver: (1) a single beachhead segment justified with accessible size, pain urgency, payment capacity, and ease of reach, with a buyer and user profile and their purchase triggers; (2) value proposition with a central promise, three defensible differentiators against real alternatives including doing nothing, and the evidence that sustains it; (3) two or three channels prioritized by fit to the segment and relative cost of reach, each with mechanics and hypothesis to validate, filtered by {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}; (4) revenue model with monetization structure, packaging and tiers, expansion levers, reasoned in unit economics and lifetime-value-vs.-customer-acquisition-cost ratio without inventing figures; (5) commercial engine from demand to close and retention, first experiment with a falsifiable hypothesis and decision criterion, and a 90-day plan by milestones with guide metrics aligned to {{METRICA_EXITO}}. Close with a one-page executive summary, a one-sentence thesis, a map of the five blocks, three risks with mitigation, and the north-star metric. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they exist. Flag every piece of data not provided as [ASSUMPTION] and verify that the five blocks are mutually consistent. Do not mention prices or the word free; use neutral professional language.

prompts.title: Blue ocean strategy with ERVC matrix
Strategy canvas and value curve
prompts.content: Act as a senior strategist in business model innovation, specialist in Blue Ocean Strategy and in the construction of strategy canvases and value curves. I need to see, not just intuit, where {{OFERTA}} converges with the industry {{INDUSTRIA}} and where it truly diverges against {{COMPETIDORES}}: the strategy canvas makes competition a single comparable image and the value curve reveals whether I am condemned to the red space or have room for a differentiating focus for {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}}. Before executing, restate in one or two sentences what you understand and present your plan. If {{OFERTA}}, {{INDUSTRIA}}, {{COMPETIDORES}} or {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}} are missing, ask for them before continuing and do not invent data. Proceed as follows: (1) Define the horizontal axis with 6 to 10 competitive factors from {{INDUSTRIA}} by which {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}} decides, derived from what the customer pays for and values, never from internal product traits; integrate {{FACTORES_CLAVE}} if provided. (2) Score from 0 to 5 the offering level of {{OFERTA}} and each of {{COMPETIDORES}} on each factor, in a factor-by-competitor table; tag [ASSUMPTION] every unconfirmed datum and state the source or reasoning when it is a fact. (3) Describe the common value curve of {{INDUSTRIA}} and contrast it with that of {{OFERTA}}: name convergences (red ocean) and divergences (focus signal). (4) Apply the four actions framework (ERIC): what to Eliminate, Reduce, Elevate and Create, deriving each action from reading the curves; per action state the value assumption for {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}} and the risk if the assumption fails. (5) Propose the new target value curve of {{OFERTA}} coherent with ERIC and validate it against focus, divergence and compelling message. (6) Close with the strategic tagline of the differentiating promise. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Do not mention prices or monetary figures; a cost factor is expressed as a relative level. If a factor does not apply to a competitor, declare it. If {{COMPETIDORES}} are not comparable, group them into strategic groups before scoring. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver: 0-5 factor-by-competitor table, convergences and divergences, ERIC block with assumptions and risks, validated target curve and final tagline.

prompts.title: Value innovation
prompts.content: Act as a senior value innovation strategist trained in the Blue Ocean framework (Kim and Mauborgne), with practice in the strategy canvas, Four Actions framework, strategic sequence and analysis of the three tiers of non-customers. Your mission is to design a value innovation move for {{OFERTA}} in {{SECTOR}} that pursues differentiation and low cost structure at the same time, redefining the boundaries of the sector rather than outperforming rivals within them.
