Available context: I compete against {{COMPETIDORES_ALTERNATIVAS}}; today I serve {{CLIENTE_ACTUAL}}; I pursue {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}; supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If a critical datum is missing to avoid inventing, ask for it before proceeding; if a datum is optional, propose a reasonable assumption and mark it as such. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver a strategic report with: (1) current strategy canvas with 5 to 10 competitive factors from the sector and the level of offering high/medium/low of the typical player against {{COMPETIDORES_ALTERNATIVAS}}, tagging as assumption every factor assumed without evidence; (2) Four Actions matrix (Eliminate, Reduce, Increase, Create) with the justification of the double effect of each action on cost structure and perceived value; (3) proposed strategy canvas, the new value curve described factor by factor against the current one; (4) prioritized non-customer segment among the three tiers (almost-converts, conscious refusers, unexplored) with the latent demand it activates and why it connects with {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}; (5) honest one-line strategic slogan, plus the three main risks with their mitigation. Verify with three tests: that the proposed canvas visibly diverges from the current one and is not the same improved profile, that at least one factor is Eliminated or Reduced and at least one is Created, and that the sequence exceptional utility, accessibility, adoption and sustainable model holds without competing on price. Do not invent data, do not mention prices or monetary figures and tag as assumption every unverified assertion.

prompts.title: Disruption analysis according to Christensen
Jobs-to-be-done based strategy
prompts.content:
Act as a senior innovation strategist specialized in jobs-to-be-done, with mastery of Outcome-Driven Innovation (Tony Ulwick), the theory of progress (Clayton Christensen) and the four forces (Bob Moesta). My goal is to anchor my innovation decisions in the job my customer is trying to get done, not in my current product.

Input data:
- Customer segment: {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}} (role, context, use situation)
- Current product or category: {{PRODUCTO_O_CATEGORIA}} (from where I observe the job today)
- Main job hypothesis: {{JOB_PRINCIPAL_HIPOTESIS}} (verb + object)
- Available evidence: {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} (interviews, usage data, reviews, support; if left blank, assume and mark it)
- Decision horizon: {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}} (timeframe and type of decision: roadmap, pivot, new line)

Proceed as follows:
1. Reframe the challenge in one sentence: "My customer is trying to achieve [progress] in [context], and today resolves it with [current solution]". If the segment, category, job hypothesis or horizon is missing, ask me for those data before continuing. Do not invent customer evidence.
2. Draft the canonical job statement (verb + object + contextual clarifier) and separate functional, emotional and social job. Do not describe the product.
3. Build the job map in 8 steps: define, locate, prepare, confirm, execute, monitor, modify, conclude. Do not skip steps.
4. Per step, list outcomes with structure: direction + metric + object + context. Each outcome measurable.
5. Score importance (1-10) and satisfaction (1-10) per outcome; calculate gap = importance + max(importance − satisfaction, 0). Classify in under-served (>15), served or over-served.
6. Apply the four forces (push, pull, anxiety, attachment) to the hiring or firing of solutions.
7. Prioritize by gap and formulate an innovation hypothesis per opportunity.
8. For the 2-3 main ones, design the validation test: assertion to falsify, signal and confirmation threshold.

Tag each assertion with [EVIDENCE] or [ASSUMPTION]. Do not invent data or market figures; no prices. Neutral Spanish, professional tone, no embellishments.

prompts.title: Innovation portfolio by horizons
prompts.content:
Act as a senior corporate innovation strategist, expert in growth portfolio management and McKinsey's Three Horizons framework. Organizations that only defend today's business are disrupted; those that bet everything on the future without a solid core burn cash before they get there. Your task is to produce an explicitly balanced innovation portfolio for {{ORGANIZACION}}, with a defensible resource allocation, metrics per horizon and clear graduation or sunset rules.

I need you to: (1) classify each initiative from {{INICIATIVAS}} in H1 (defend and extend the core), H2 (emerging engines with traction that scale in 2-3 years) or H3 (disruptive bets at 3-6 years of high uncertainty), justifying each placement by maturity, traction and proximity to the core, not by affinity or by who sponsors it; (2) per horizon, state the value thesis of each initiative in one sentence and assess maturity, traction and uncertainty; (3) contrast {{MEZCLA_ACTUAL}} of investment and headcount against a target mix coherent with {{APETITO_RIESGO}}, quantifying the gap per horizon in percentage points within {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}; (4) define the governing metrics of each horizon (H1: efficiency, margins, retention; H2: revenue growth, adoption, unit economics; H3: validated learning, discovery milestones, open options) and clarify which metrics do NOT yet apply to each horizon; (5) name the portfolio imbalance risks and their strategic consequence; (6) propose governance cadence and quantitative graduation or sunset criteria; (7) close with three prioritized reallocation moves ranked by expected impact and feasibility.

Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Before classifying, confirm {{ORGANIZACION}}, {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} and {{APETITO_RIESGO}}; if {{INICIATIVAS}} or {{MEZCLA_ACTUAL}} are missing, ask for them or declare them as an explicit [ASSUMPTION] before proceeding; never invent traction or investment data that was not given. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as evidence. Resolve borderline cases by reasoning the boundary. Deliver a document with a classification table, a current vs. target mix table with the gap, a metrics panel per horizon, governance rules and the three final moves. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

Parameters:
- {{ORGANIZACION}}: company, business unit or team whose portfolio will be balanced
- {{INICIATIVAS}}: inventory of initiatives, products or bets with a note of their current status
- {{MEZCLA_ACTUAL}}: current distribution of investment and headcount among H1, H2 and H3 (optional)
- {{APETITO_RIESGO}}: risk appetite and growth ambition (conservative, balanced or aggressive) (optional)
- {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}: strategic planning reference window (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Business model reinvention
Platform and ecosystem strategy
Strategic bets on emerging technologies
Open innovation strategy
Strategic exploration with design thinking
Defensive strategy against disruption
Strategic deployment with cascading OKRs
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Strategy and Execution Director, expert in OKR deployment (Doerr/Grove lineage, Intel/Google model) and in vertical and horizontal alignment. Convert the priorities of {{ORGANIZACION}} for {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} into a cascade of OKRs ready to govern.

A strategy that does not descend to measurable objectives by level remains as mere intention. The cascade unlocks focus, line of sight, and a verifiable execution rhythm.

Produce: (1) 1 to 3 top-level Objectives derived from {{PRIORIDADES_ESTRATEGICAS}}, qualitative, ambitious, and memorable, without metrics in the statement; (2) per Objective, 3 to 5 Key Results with metric, baseline (from {{METRICAS_BASE}} or assumption), and period target, measuring outcome and not activity, as independent of each other as possible; (3) the cascade by {{NIVELES_CASCADA}} over {{ESTRUCTURA_AREAS}}, where each lower-level Objective explicitly connects to a superior Key Result by contributing without cloning it; (4) the horizontal dependency map between areas that share or condition the same Key Result, with the required agreement; (5) the dashboard with a single owner per Objective, cadence (weekly check-in, monthly review, quarterly close), scale 0.0 to 1.0 with bands and green/amber/red signal; (6) the list of anti-patterns with their correction.

Distinguish Objective (direction), Key Result (evidence), and initiative (work). Mark each OKR as aspirational or committed and warn about sandbagging. Before drafting, restate what you understood and present your plan; then execute. If {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, {{NIVELES_CASCADA}}, {{ESTRUCTURA_AREAS}}, {{PRIORIDADES_ESTRATEGICAS}}, or {{METRICAS_BASE}} is missing, ask before inventing; all assumed data must be marked as an assumption with a reasonable starting value. Consider attachments in {{ADJUNTOS}}. Close with a document ready for the first check-in of the period.

prompts.title: Balanced Scorecard design
Cause-effect strategy map
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategist expert in the Balanced Scorecard and Kaplan and Norton strategy maps, specialized in translating strategies into executable and auditable cause-effect chains. Build the strategy map for {{ORGANIZACION}} toward {{OBJETIVO_CUMBRE}}, organized by the four perspectives (Financial, Customer, Internal Processes, Learning and Growth) and with explicit cause-effect links, considering the priorities {{PRIORIDADES_ESTRATEGICAS}} and the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}.

Proceed as follows: (1) confirm the destination from {{OBJETIVO_CUMBRE}} and {{HORIZONTE}}, and make {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} explicit (operational excellence, product leadership, or customer intimacy) because it anchors which processes matter; (2) define 8 to 15 strategic objectives distributed across the four perspectives, drafted as verbs of change, never as metrics or initiatives, and coherent with {{PRIORIDADES_ESTRATEGICAS}}; (3) chain from the bottom up (Learning > Processes > Customer > Financial) and for each link write the 'if... then...' hypothesis, marking its strength as strong, plausible, or assumption without evidence; (4) assign to each objective 1 or 2 leading (guide) and lagging (result) indicators and an indicative target when useful; (5) audit the chain: orphans without a cause or effect, skips that jump a perspective, and the weakest hypothesis on which the entire narrative depends; (6) draft the map's narrative as a single causal story from the base to the result.

Deliver: a table of the map across the four perspectives, a numbered list of cause-effect links with hypothesis and strength, a paragraph of strategic narrative, and an audit note with orphans, skips, and the weakest link. Mark every assumption without data support with [ASSUMPTION]. If an essential data point is missing ({{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}, {{OBJETIVO_CUMBRE}}, or {{HORIZONTE}}), ask for it before building.

Variables: {{ORGANIZACION}}, {{OBJETIVO_CUMBRE}}, {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{PRIORIDADES_ESTRATEGICAS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Policy deployment with Hoshin Kanri
Strategic initiative roadmap
prompts.content:
Act as a Chief Strategy Officer (CSO) with experience sequencing initiative portfolios in technology companies. Convert {{LISTA_INICIATIVAS}} into an actionable roadmap by horizons, not a wish-list calendar. The roadmap must serve {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}, fit within {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}, and respect {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}.

If {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}, {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}, or {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}} is missing, ask before starting: without those three data points the roadmap is not falsifiable. If {{LISTA_INICIATIVAS}} arrives incomplete or ambiguous, normalize what there is and flag the gaps.

Proceed as follows. First, normalize each initiative from {{LISTA_INICIATIVAS}} into a comparable card: objective, expected business outcome, relative effort in T-shirt sizes (S/M/L/XL), tentative owner, and idea maturity (explored, validated, or in execution). Second, surface the dependency matrix: per initiative mark what blocks it (technical, data, organizational, market, or regulatory) and what it unblocks; identify and name the critical path. Third, estimate load per period and verify it against {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}; if any period is overloaded, reassign and explain the move. Fourth, prioritize with {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} combining strategic impact, urgency, and reversibility: bets that are hard to reverse are sequenced later or piloted first with a cheap experiment. Fifth, assign each initiative to H1 (now), H2 (enablers), or H3 (later bets), respecting dependencies and capacity. Sixth, define verifiable milestones per horizon and a go/no-go criterion for advancing to the next one.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver: master table of initiatives, roadmap view by horizon, narrated critical path naming the initiatives that compose it, list of assumptions marked as [ASSUMPTION], and the three most serious sequencing risks with their mitigation. Do not include monetary estimates or prices; effort is expressed in T-shirt sizes and capacity-period units. First restate what you understood and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Initiative prioritization (ICE/RICE)
prompts.content: Act as a senior portfolio strategist expert in evidence-based prioritization with the ICE and RICE frameworks, with judgment to distinguish signal from decimal noise. I need to focus finite resources on the highest-return-per-unit-of-effort initiatives for {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} during {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}, and convert {{LISTA_INICIATIVAS}} into a sequence defensible before the strategy committee. Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan. Then: 1) Confirm the model per {{MODELO_SCORING}} (ICE by default; RICE only if there is a measurable reach per period) and set the scales: Impact and Confidence on 1-10, Effort in person-weeks or relative points, and for RICE the Reach in units per period; declare what each extreme of the scale means. 2) Normalize the data for each initiative in {{LISTA_INICIATIVAS}}; where a value is missing, assign it with an explicit rationale and mark it as an assumption. Do not invent impact or reach figures. 3) Calculate the score showing the formula with real numbers (ICE = Impact x Confidence / Effort; RICE = Reach x Impact x Confidence / Effort) with consistent units. 4) Order from highest to lowest and draw the cutoff line per {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}. 5) Flag ties, dependencies, and distortions from high effort or low confidence. 6) Run a sensitivity test on 2 to 3 borderline initiatives, naming the pivot value that triggers each reordering. 7) Deliver recommended list, discarded with reason, and data to verify before committing budget. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. If an essential data point is missing, ask before calculating. Output in neutral and professional language, no emojis: scoring table + ordered ranking with cutoff line + sensitivity note + final recommendation.

prompts.title: Comprehensive annual strategic plan
prompts.content: Act as a senior corporate strategist with fifteen years designing and facilitating annual strategic plans for medium-sized companies and business units, with mastery of OKRs, cross-SWOT, PESTEL, and impact-effort prioritization. Build a comprehensive annual strategic plan that is executable and ready to present to the executive team of {{ORGANIZACION_Y_SECTOR}} for the horizon {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, starting from {{CONTEXTO_ACTUAL}} and {{PRIORIDADES_LIDERAZGO}}, considering {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}} and respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}; also integrate {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, plan the approach, and present that plan to me; if an essential data point is missing, ask me instead of inventing it. Organize the deliverable into five phases. One, diagnosis: cross-SWOT with FO, FA, DO, and DA strategies, plus PESTEL scoped to factors with real impact; close with three to five actionable conclusions. Two, direction: annual aspiration statement and OKRs, maximum five objectives, each with two to four measurable Key Results with baseline and numerical target; reject unmeasurable Key Results. Three, initiatives: the few that move each Key Result, prioritized in an impact vs. effort matrix, distinguishing bets from baseline work, each with a named owner. Four, resources: person-months per initiative vs. available capacity, plus non-human enablers in qualitative terms (budget without figures, tools, alliances), with explicit bottlenecks; never price or express monetary costs and never use the word free. Five, metrics and governance: dashboard with result and progress indicators, green, amber, and red thresholds, monthly progress and quarterly strategy cadence, and a re-planning trigger. Ensure traceability: each Key Result connects to at least one initiative and vice versa. Mark every unconfirmed inference with [ASSUMPTION] and do not cite external metrics without a source. Deliver a document in sections, with tables for OKRs, initiative prioritization, and the metrics dashboard, in neutral and professional language, ready for approval, and list pending questions at the end.

prompts.title: Strategic KPI architecture
prompts.content:
Act as a Strategy and Performance Management Director with fifteen years designing measurement systems (Balanced Scorecard, OKRs, KPI trees) in multi-unit companies. Build the KPI architecture that connects {{NORTE_ESTRATEGICO}} to measurable operational levers, ready to govern in committee, so that the strategy stops being an annual PowerPoint and becomes governable.

Before executing, restate in your own words the north and the objectives you understand, and present your plan. If an essential data point is missing, ask in a single batch before proceeding; do not invent figures.

Proceed as follows: (1) translate each objective from {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}} into 1-2 business results (lagging) traceable to {{NORTE_ESTRATEGICO}}; (2) under each result identify 2-4 operational levers (leading) and make the causal relationship lever > result explicit; (3) for each indicator define name, calculation formula, unit, frequency, data source (from {{FUENTES_DATO}}), baseline, target at {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, and alert threshold; (4) assign a single accountable owner per indicator and its review cadence (use {{CADENCIAS_REVISION}} or propose one); (5) label each KPI as result or lever and mark with [ASSUMPTION] every causal relationship or figure not validated with data; (6) select 3-5 cover indicators for the committee and list 2 measurement risks (gaming, unreliable data, or latency) with their mitigation.

Limits: avoid vanity metrics, prioritize few actionable indicators (ideally 7-12 total), do not propose a target without a baseline (if missing, declare it and propose calibration), and do not assign shared responsibility (a single owner per KPI). Deliver: a hierarchical table objective > result > lever with the record for each KPI, a textual diagram of the causal chain, and the committee cover block, plus a note on assumptions and data gaps.

Parameters:
- {{NORTE_ESTRATEGICO}}: aspiration or strategic north that orders the priorities (vision, growth thesis, or dominant intent)
- {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}}: list of 2 to 5 prioritized strategic objectives to be measured
- {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}: KPI tree horizon (e.g. fiscal year, 3 years, quarterly cycle)
- {{FUENTES_DATO}}: systems or reports where the data will come from (ERP, CRM, BI, spreadsheets, surveys)
- {{CADENCIAS_REVISION}}: forums and frequency where the indicators will be reviewed (optional; if missing, proposed)

prompts.title: Target Operating Model design
prompts.content: Act as an Operating Model Architect with fifteen years translating corporate strategies into executable Target Operating Models (TOM) in banking, manufacturing, and services. Design the target operating model that will execute {{ESTRATEGIA_APROBADA}}, enabling {{OBJETIVOS_CUANTIFICADOS}} within {{ALCANCE_ORGANIZATIVO}} and the {{HORIZONTE}}, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Deliver: the target state documented across the six TOM dimensions (processes; organizational structure; capabilities; governance and decisions; technology; data and information), with declared design principles, capability gap analysis, governance matrix, and a transition roadmap in waves. Proceed as follows: (1) Synthesize the strategic imperatives from {{ESTRATEGIA_APROBADA}} and derive, for each one, what it demands of the operating model, anchoring yourself to {{OBJETIVOS_CUANTIFICADOS}}. (2) Define the target state across the six dimensions within {{ALCANCE_ORGANIZATIVO}}, declaring the design principles that govern it and avoiding overlaps or gaps. (3) Identify the critical differentiating capabilities and map them against the current state with an explicit build / buy / partner / keep decision and its justification. (4) Specify governance: key decisions, roles with a RACI-type matrix, and one operational indicator per dimension. (5) Propose the transition sequence in waves within {{HORIZONTE}}, with dependencies, verifiable milestones, quick wins from the first wave, and progress indicators, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Ensure traceability: imperative > dimension > design decision > capability > metric. Flag every unprovided datum as [ASSUMPTION] and declare it at the outset; flag model execution risks and redesign triggers. If {{ADJUNTOS}} provides context, incorporate it. Rules: neutral professional Spanish; no prices; no monetary costs (use relative effort, FTEs, or waves). If {{ESTRATEGIA_APROBADA}}, {{OBJETIVOS_CUANTIFICADOS}}, {{ALCANCE_ORGANIZATIVO}}, or {{HORIZONTE}} are missing, ask for them before executing. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Strategy Management Office design
prompts.content:
Act as the Director of a Strategy Management Office (SMO) with fifteen years enabling strategic execution in mid-size and large organizations, trained in the Kaplan and Norton framework (Strategy Management Office) and in the Four Disciplines of Execution. Your assignment: install an operational strategy, a lightweight SMO that closes the gap between the strategic plan and daily operations of {{ORGANIZACION}}, where today initiatives launch and never close, KPIs have no owner, and pivots are decided late or by intuition.

Context:
- Organization: {{ORGANIZACION}} (name and approximate size, e.g. services company, 400 employees)
- Sector or industry: {{SECTOR}}
- Horizon of the current strategic plan: {{HORIZONTE_ESTRATEGICO}} (e.g. 3-year plan, annual OKRs)
- Current execution and measurement maturity: {{MADUREZ_EJECUCION}} (e.g. incipient, no formal cadences)
- Priority challenge the office must solve: {{DESAFIO_PRINCIPAL}} (e.g. initiatives that never close, KPIs without an owner)
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Before designing, restate in two or three sentences the problem you understand and present your work plan; then execute. If the sector, size, horizon, or maturity are missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent those four data points. Flag every assumption you adopt with [ASSUMPTION] and leave ambiguities as {to_confirm}.

Deliver an SMO design document ready for the executive committee, with six blocks:
1. Mandate and scope in one sentence, plus five core responsibilities; each with its explicit counterpart of what the office does NOT do.
2. Governance model with a RACI matrix across five key processes (strategy translation, initiative alignment, performance review, hypothesis management, communication) with roles such as executive sponsor, SMO lead, initiative owners, and KPI owners. A single Accountable per process, with no empty Accountable cells.
3. System of three chained cadences (operational weekly or biweekly, monthly strategic, quarterly QBR-style recalibration): objective, participants, inputs, duration, and concrete decision per cadence; explain what each delivers as input to the next.
4. Minimum viable toolbox: KPI dashboard (columns), strategic initiative register (fields), and strategic hypothesis log (statement and test), with one realistic example row per artifact.
5. Learning mechanism that connects dashboard signals to pivot, persist, or close decisions, with a quantified or observable trigger threshold and a decision owner.
6. Ninety-day plan in three waves with verifiable milestones and the first meeting to schedule.

Adjust each block to {{MADUREZ_EJECUCION}}: if incipient, prioritize few initiatives and a single tool before scaling. Close by verifying that each responsibility has its NOT, that the RACI has no gaps or double Accountable, that the cadences are chained, that each tool brings an example, and that the threshold and the 90-day plan are actionable. No prices or promises of free resources; neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Strategic review cadence
prompts.content:
Design the strategic review cadence of {{ORGANIZACION}}: the system of periodic, nested meetings with no overlap in purpose, where the continued validity of the strategy is assessed and decisions are made with data, within the horizon {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}. Act as a Chief of Staff (Director of Strategy and Operations) with experience in governance rhythms in services and technology companies. Before designing, confirm the sector, team size, the framework {{MARCO_OBJETIVOS}}, the tool {{HERRAMIENTA_SEGUIMIENTO}}, and the horizon {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}; if a key datum is missing or ambiguous, ask for it and do not invent context. Deliver four nested levels: WEEKLY operational (remove obstacles and advance on initiatives), MONTHLY business (metric trends and objective health from framework {{MARCO_OBJETIVOS}}), QUARTERLY strategic (validate assumptions, reallocate capital, replan), and ANNUAL (direction, positioning, and bets within {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}). For each level define seven fields: purpose in one sentence; participants and owner; duration and frequency; 3 to 6 concrete guiding questions; input data ready before the meeting; decision format with explicit thresholds to continue, adjust, pivot, or stop; and artifacts produced (minutes, decisions, actions with owner and date). Then define the escalation rule that connects the levels by naming the specific trigger that moves a topic to the next higher rhythm, verify there is no overlap in purpose, list at least four anti-patterns to avoid, and deliver a 30-day adoption plan with an owner and date per milestone. Integrate {{MARCO_OBJETIVOS}} and {{HERRAMIENTA_SEGUIMIENTO}} into the inputs and artifacts. Professional tone, neutral Spanish, no prices or promises of free resources. Deliverable: one card or table per level with the seven fields, followed by the escalation rule, the anti-patterns, and the 30-day plan, ready to present to the management committee.

Variables:
- {{ORGANIZACION}}: name, sector, and size of the team that will adopt the cadence.
- {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}: horizon of the current strategy (e.g. 1 year, 3 years).
- {{MARCO_OBJETIVOS}}: objectives framework in use (OKR, Balanced Scorecard, KPIs, none yet).
- {{HERRAMIENTA_SEGUIMIENTO}}: tool where metrics and initiatives live (e.g. Notion, Jira, spreadsheet).

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Budget-to-strategy alignment
Strategic execution gap closure
prompts.content:
Act as a Chief of Staff (Director of Strategic Execution) with a track record of closing the gap between formulated strategy and actual results in mid-size and large organizations. The strategy {{ESTRATEGIA_OBJETIVO}} of {{ORGANIZACION_AREA}} was formulated but is not translating into results: the symptoms {{SINTOMAS_BRECHA}} are appearing and current monitoring {{COMO_SE_MIDE_HOY}} is not closing the distance between intent and execution. I need to locate where the strategy-to-result chain is breaking and design mechanisms to restore traction within {{HORIZONTE}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate in your own words what you understood about the strategy, its symptoms, and how it is measured today; present your diagnostic plan; and only then execute. If context about the strategy, team structure, previous unblocking attempts, or how progress is measured is missing, ask before continuing; do not invent data. Flag every assumption explicitly as an assumption.

Proceed as follows:
1. Reconstruct the strategy-to-result translation chain of {{ESTRATEGIA_OBJETIVO}} (from formulated intent to expected result, link by link) and identify the exact break point, with the evidence that supports it or an explicit assumption if there is no evidence.
2. Classify the causes of the gap into five families: clarity (the strategy is not understood or translated into decisions), alignment (priorities compete or do not align across areas), capability (people, time, skills, or budget are missing), execution (there is no owner, cadence, or follow-up), and learning (progress is not measured or course-corrected).
3. Prioritize gaps by combining impact on {{ESTRATEGIA_OBJETIVO}} and governability (real control to close them within {{HORIZONTE}}); justify discarding those that are noise or outside of control, and select the 2 to 3 critical ones.
4. For each critical gap, design a closure mechanism with: a single named owner, a predictive (leading) indicator, a results (lagging) indicator, a review cadence, an actionable first step this week, and the early signal that would indicate the mechanism is working or that a pivot is needed.
5. Define the minimum operational rhythm distinguishing what is reviewed weekly, monthly, and quarterly, and the concrete triggers that would force a strategy recalibration (not just execution).

Deliverables: prioritized gap diagnosis, closure mechanism table (owner, leading, lagging, cadence, first step, early signal), and operational rhythm calendar with recalibration triggers. Always distinguish what you know (with evidence) from what you assume (assumption). If symptoms point to the strategy itself being unviable rather than an execution problem, say so directly.

Parameters:
- {{ESTRATEGIA_OBJETIVO}}: strategy or goal whose execution is stalled (what was meant to be achieved and by when).
- {{ORGANIZACION_AREA}}: organization, unit, or team where execution takes place, with size and basic structure.
- {{SINTOMAS_BRECHA}}: observed signals that the strategy is not advancing (missed milestones, stalled initiatives, flat results).
- {{COMO_SE_MIDE_HOY}}: how progress is monitored today (metrics, dashboards, review meetings).
- {{HORIZONTE}}: time window for closing the gap (optional; if missing, assume and flag as assumption).

prompts.title: Strategic narrative for the board
prompts.content: Act as a Chief Strategy Officer with a track record of building and defending strategic narratives before boards of directors and executive committees. Your assignment is to produce a narrative package that first aligns the board and then, in coherent cascade, aligns leaders and the entire organization behind {{VISION}}, ultimately unlocking {{DECISION_DIRECTORIO}}. Business context: {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}}. Audiences and deployment order: {{AUDIENCIAS}}. Available evidence: {{EVIDENCIA}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before drafting, restate in two or three lines the vision you understand, the world-change that motivates it, and the exact decision to be made; lay out your build plan and, if an essential datum is missing, ask for it rather than assuming it. Deliver four pieces. First: a one-page master narrative, ready as a script for the spokesperson (CEO or president), with a complete arc — status quo running out, disruptive force or tension, vision of the future state, strategic bet, gain versus risk, and call to decision that closes on {{DECISION_DIRECTORIO}}. Second: a three-level message map for {{AUDIENCIAS}} (board, leaders, organization) that preserves the same arc and only adapts language, depth, and detail, without changing the message. Third: three to five memorable, repeatable, jargon-free anchor messages. Fourth: an annex of probable board objections (weak thesis, execution risk, opportunity cost, wrong timing, lack of evidence) with a narrative response for each one — not defensive. Apply What-So What-Now What to each block of {{EVIDENCIA}} and anchor every market or performance claim in a concrete data point; whatever is not in {{EVIDENCIA}} is flagged [ASSUMPTION] and asked for, never invented. Write in neutral professional Spanish, no prices and without the word free. Close with a usage note: how to rehearse the spokesperson's script, what control question to ask the board to force the decision, and what needs to be confirmed before presenting.

prompts.title: Structured scenario planning
Uncertainty-impact matrix
prompts.content:
Act as a senior scenario-planning strategist, trained in the Global Business Network method (Schwartz, Wack) and expert in the critical uncertainty matrix and STEEP driving-force analysis. I want an uncertainty-impact matrix that structures the scenarios for the decision {{DECISION_FOCAL}}, over the horizon {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, within the context {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACION}}, starting from the already-identified forces {{FUERZAS_CONOCIDAS}} and considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. First restate what you understand of the decision, the horizon, and the context, and present your plan before executing; if anything essential is missing, ask before proceeding and do not invent context.

Then proceed as follows: inventory between 10 and 15 driving forces covering the five STEEP dimensions (social, technological, economic, environmental, political) plus the sector's own forces from {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACION}}, with one relevance sentence per force, integrating {{FUERZAS_CONOCIDAS}} without limiting yourself to them. Score each force from 1 to 5 on uncertainty (unpredictability of its evolution over {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}) and from 1 to 5 on impact (how much it alters the outcome of {{DECISION_FOCAL}}), with a brief justification and no unexplained jumps. Classify each force into one of four quadrants: critical uncertainties (high-high), noise to monitor (high uncertainty, low impact), predetermined trends (low uncertainty, high impact, valid in all scenarios), and secondary (both low). From the critical quadrant, select the two verifiably orthogonal axes that maximize divergence of futures: check their independence with an explicit test, justify the choice, and argue against the remaining candidates. Define the two contrasting poles of each axis and name the four scenarios from the crossing, with one memorable phrase each. Close by indicating which decision regarding {{DECISION_FOCAL}} would be robust across all four futures and what early signal would confirm which way reality is leaning.

Deliverables: matrix table (force, dimension, uncertainty, impact, justification, quadrant), separate list of predetermined trends, the two critical axes with their orthogonality test and justified inclusion/exclusion, and the four scenarios named. Flag every assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent data: if a score depends on information you do not have, declare it.

prompts.title: Strategic move wargaming
prompts.content: Act as a senior strategist in competitive wargaming and power games, facilitator of red-team strategic exercises for management committees. I want to stress the move {{MOVIMIENTO_ESTRATEGICO}} in {{MERCADO_Y_HORIZONTE}} before committing resources: simulate how {{COMPETIDORES_CLAVE}} and the regulator of {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}} will react to know whether the strategy holds up under adversarial pressure or buckles, and where, considering {{ACTIVOS_Y_RESTRICCIONES}}. If {{MOVIMIENTO_ESTRATEGICO}}, {{MERCADO_Y_HORIZONTE}}, {{COMPETIDORES_CLAVE}}, {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}}, or {{OBJETIVO_A_DESBLOQUEAR}} are missing, ask me before continuing; do not invent intentions, market shares, or regulations as facts. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver a wargame report as follows: (1) restate in 3-5 lines the move, the horizon, and {{OBJETIVO_A_DESBLOQUEAR}}. (2) Map the board: own player, each competitor from {{COMPETIDORES_CLAVE}}, the regulator from {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}}, and indirect actors with retaliatory power, with declared and inferred objectives, resources, and reaction function; flag every inference with [ASSUMPTION]. Use five forces to size the retaliatory power of each player. (3) Simulate three rounds using applied game theory (each actor's best response to the previous move) and the OODA cycle to estimate response speed: R1 own move; R2 probable countermove plus the most credible aggressive play by each rival and the regulator; R3 own counter-response plus a second wave. For each play give probability (high/medium/low), impact on position, and response speed. (4) Detect break points: the round and play where the strategy stops holding up, each with an observable tripwire that anticipates it (a measurable, non-generic signal). (5) Propose three adjustments that shield the strategy without destroying its logic, respecting {{ACTIVOS_Y_RESTRICCIONES}}; for each adjustment, name which enemy play it neutralizes. (6) Close with verdict: robust, conditionally robust, or fragile, with the condition or risk that defines it. If the move depends on a non-verifiable critical assumption, declare it as the first risk to validate. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Deliverable ready to take to committee.

prompts.title: Strategic risk analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a Chief Risk Officer (CRO) with fifteen years scoring and prioritizing risks that jeopardize the execution of corporate strategies. Your job: protect the achievement of the strategy of {{ORGANIZACION_Y_ESTRATEGIA}} within {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, converting diffuse threats into a prioritized and actionable register for the management committee. Strategies rarely fail for lack of ambition; they fail because of risks that nobody scored in time.

Input data:
- Organization and strategy: {{ORGANIZACION_Y_ESTRATEGIA}}
- Strategic objectives to protect (3 to 5): {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}}
- Time horizon: {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}
- Risk appetite and tolerance: {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}
If any datum is missing, do not invent it: ask for it or declare it an explicit [ASSUMPTION].

Produce, in this order:
1. Objective anchoring: fix the {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}}; if not provided, infer 3 to 5 from context and mark them [ASSUMPTION]. Every risk must threaten at least one; what does not touch an objective is operational, not strategic, and is discarded.
2. Risk register in table: ID, risk as cause-event-consequence, threatened objective, source, Probability (1-5), Impact (1-5), Exposure (P x I), speed (slow/medium/fast), and trend (growing/stable/declining). Before the table, define in one line what each level of P and I means so the scoring is auditable.
3. Heat map in text: four quadrants (high/low probability x high/low impact), separating top risks from monitoring ones.
4. Response plan for top risks: treatment (avoid/reduce/transfer/accept), concrete action, named owner, early-warning indicator, escalation trigger, and expected residual exposure after the action.
5. Emerging risks to watch and correlations or cascade effects among risks.
6. Close: assumptions made and questions that would change the prioritization.

Rules: do not invent figures; traverse sources in a structured way (market, competition/disruption, technology, regulation/geopolitics, talent/culture, finance/liquidity, supply chain/third parties, execution/dependencies, reputation/stakeholders); calibrate Impact against {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}, not against an abstract scale. Deliverable ready for the management committee.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Defining risk appetite and tolerance
prompts.content:
Act as a Chief Risk Officer with a background in corporate governance and the ISO 31000 and COSO ERM frameworks, who has presented risk appetite statements to boards of directors. Your task: build a risk appetite and tolerance framework by strategic category for {{ORGANIZACION}}, auditable and ready to bring before {{ORGANO_GOBIERNO}}.

Context:
- Organization: {{ORGANIZACION}} (name, brief description, and size)
- Sector: {{SECTOR}} (industry and applicable level of regulation)
- Strategic objectives for the period: {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}}
- Absorption capacity: {{CAPACIDAD_ABSORCION}} (reserves, EBITDA, runway, equity)
- Governing body that approves and oversees: {{ORGANO_GOBIERNO}}
- Risk categories to cover: {{CATEGORIAS_RIESGO}} (optional; if omitted, propose the standard set)

If any critical input needed to set thresholds is missing, ask me for it before continuing rather than inventing it.

Proceed as follows: (1) Inventory the strategic categories from {{CATEGORIAS_RIESGO}}, or propose the standard set (growth, innovation, finance and liquidity, compliance and legal, reputation, operations and continuity, talent, cybersecurity and data) and confirm which apply. (2) Per category, a one-sentence appetite statement: stance (averse, cautious, open, or aggressive) and its rationale relative to {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}}. (3) Distinguish appetite (risk sought to create value) from tolerance (maximum acceptable deviation before acting); never as synonyms. (4) Define 1 to 3 measurable metrics per category with unit and green/amber/red thresholds with concrete values calibrated to {{CAPACIDAD_ABSORCION}}; mark every figure without real data as [ASSUMPTION] and request validation. (5) Escalation triggers: action when crossing to amber and to red, who decides, timeframe, and escalation up to {{ORGANO_GOBIERNO}}. (6) Consolidate in a matrix (category, stance, metric, thresholds, owner, escalation), declare 3 governance risks of the framework itself, and set the review cadence.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Final deliverable: consolidated matrix with assumptions flagged for validation, no invented figures, and appetite and tolerance differentiated in each row.

prompts.title: Decision tree with expected value
Valuation of strategic real options
prompts.content: Act as a senior investment strategist and real options analyst, trained in the Trigeorgis / Copeland-Antikarov framework and in the logic expanded NPV = static NPV + value of managerial flexibility. I need a real options assessment with an actionable recommendation on {{DECISION_INVERSION}}, whose main source of uncertainty is {{FUENTE_INCERTIDUMBRE}}, over a {{HORIZONTE}} horizon and with {{REVERSIBILIDAD}} reversibility. Risk appetite or decision-maker's criterion: {{APETITO_RIESGO}}. Available economic data: {{DATOS_ECONOMICOS}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate the decision, source of uncertainty, horizon, and reversibility as you understand them, and present your plan. If cash flows, investment, discount rate, probabilities, or volatility are missing, ask for them in a single round before calculating; do not invent figures. Proceed as follows: (1) Frame the investment and name each real option present (defer, expand, contract, abandon, stage, switch technology or input) with its natural trigger; discard the non-applicable ones with justification. (2) Calculate the static NPV of the base case showing discount rate, cash flows by period, investment, and assumptions. (3) Model the uncertainty with a decision tree of discrete scenarios with probabilities, or with explicit volatility if the underlying asset justifies it; declare method and reason. (4) Value each option as incremental value over the static NPV and report the expanded NPV, verifying reconciliation with the sum and warning if there is interaction between options. (5) Define exercise triggers with observable signal, review moment, and quantitative threshold. (6) Recommend committing now, in phases, or waiting, contrasting the value of waiting against the cost of ceding first-mover advantage, and indicate the condition that would reverse the decision. Mark every assumed estimate as [ASSUMPTION]. Never prices, fees, or the word free; reason in value, relative cash flows, and FTE-months. Close by naming the option that most moves the assessment and what data would make it decisive.

prompts.title: Pre-mortem of a strategic bet
Early warning and monitoring system
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategist in strategic monitoring and early warning systems, with practice in scenario planning, risk management, and leading KPI design. I want to install a layer of sensors on this bet: {{APUESTA_ESTRATEGICA}} (course, market, product, model, or expansion to be monitored). It is a StrategIA with sensors: I defend the course while the assumptions hold and change in an orderly way as soon as they stop holding.

Input data:
- Critical assumptions: {{SUPUESTOS_CRITICOS}} (key beliefs on which the bet rests; if I leave them blank, derive them and mark them [ASSUMPTION])
- Available data sources: {{FUENTES_DATOS}} (analytics, sales, market, external signals; or "Undefined")
- Response options upon an alert: {{OPCIONES_RESPUESTA}} (revisit, pivot, double down, exit; or "Undefined")
- Horizon and decision speed: {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}} (quarter, year, multi-year; calibrates cadences and thresholds)

Proceed as follows:
1. Restate {{APUESTA_ESTRATEGICA}} in one sentence. If any essential data above is missing, ask me before continuing; do not invent the bet or its assumptions.
2. Extract 3 to 5 critical assumptions from {{SUPUESTOS_CRITICOS}}: only those that, if they fail, invalidate the course. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] those you infer.
3. For each assumption define 1 or 2 leading indicators (leading) and separate them from lagging ones (lagging); justify why each leading indicator anticipates the break and by how much lead time.
4. Assign to each indicator a baseline, green/amber/red thresholds, a source from {{FUENTES_DATOS}}, and a cadence consistent with {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}. If a source is missing, propose a proxy marked [ASSUMPTION].
5. Define triggers in the form "if X crosses threshold Y for Z consecutive measurements, then W", where W comes from {{OPCIONES_RESPUESTA}}.
6. Separate signal from noise: confirmation filter against false alarms and explicit contrast between the cost of reacting late and the cost of a false positive reaction.
7. Build a dashboard (indicator, baseline, threshold, status, owner, trigger) and a review ritual with cadence, responsible party, and escalation rule.
8. Close with blind spots: what assumption lacks a reliable leading indicator, what signal could arrive too late, and what to do if two triggers conflict.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Use neutral English and a professional tone without ornament. Each indicator must be measurable and each trigger must end in a concrete action.

prompts.title: Identifying no-regret moves
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategist specializing in decision-making under uncertainty and scenario planning, with mastery of the robust strategy framework (no-regret moves, big bets, real options) in the style of Courtney-Kirkland-Viguerie "Strategy Under Uncertainty" and McKinsey Three Horizons. Your assignment is to build a robustness map for the decision {{DECISION_CENTRAL}} over the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}, so that I can separate the moves worth making regardless of what happens from the bets that depend on a specific future, and advance with conviction without waiting for a certainty that will not arrive.

Before executing, restate in your own words {{DECISION_CENTRAL}}, its horizon {{HORIZONTE}}, and the critical uncertainties {{INCERTIDUMBRES_CRITICAS}}; if the decision, the horizon, the uncertainties, or the candidate moves {{MOVIMIENTOS_CANDIDATOS}} are missing, ask me for them in a single round of questions and do not proceed with silent assumptions. First rate the level of uncertainty (sufficiently clear future, discrete alternative futures, range of futures, or genuine ambiguity), because it defines the method.

Then proceed as follows: identify the two most determinative and mutually independent uncertainties within {{INCERTIDUMBRES_CRITICAS}} and cross them in a matrix to derive three to four contrasting, plausible, and mutually distinguishable scenarios; name each and explain its causal logic in two or three sentences, including at least one adverse scenario. Consolidate the candidate moves {{MOVIMIENTOS_CANDIDATOS}} without filtering them yet. Evaluate each move against all scenarios in a visible matrix of moves by scenarios and classify it as no-regret (net positive value in all scenarios), big bet (high return only if a specific scenario materializes), deferrable option (buys the right to decide later at low initial investment), or to avoid (destroys value or irreversibly commits resources in plausible scenarios); justify the robustness logic of each verdict and consider {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}. For each no-regret move define a trigger, a first actionable step within 30 days, an owner, and an early warning signal of scenario materialization. For each option define the cost of keeping it open, the exercise condition, and the decision deadline. Close with a recommendation ordered as execute now, keep open and decide later, plus the two or three monitoring signals that would trigger a rethink. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent data.

prompts.title: Key assumption sensitivity analysis
prompts.content: Act as a senior strategist in decision analysis under uncertainty, with mastery of one-way and two-way sensitivity, tornado diagrams, and switching value (breakeven value). I want to stress-test the decision {{DECISION_ESTRATEGICA}}, judged against {{METRICA_RESULTADO}}, which rests on {{SUPUESTOS_BASE}} with their ranges {{RANGOS_PLAUSIBLES}}, within {{HORIZONTE_RESTRICCIONES}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they contribute data. If something essential is missing or a range is not plausible, ask me and do not invent figures. Deliver a sensitivity dashboard as follows: 1) Framing: confirm {{DECISION_ESTRATEGICA}}, {{METRICA_RESULTADO}}, and its binary threshold, fix the base case, and verify that each assumption in {{SUPUESTOS_BASE}} has a value, a range from {{RANGOS_PLAUSIBLES}}, and an explicit mechanism of influence. 2) One-way: vary one assumption at a time between pessimistic and optimistic with the rest at base; report the resulting metric and the absolute delta against base, watching for interactions and nonlinearities that one-way hides. 3) Tornado: order by delta amplitude and separate the few critical drivers from the rest with low impact. 4) Switching value: for each critical driver, calculate the value where the conclusion crosses the threshold and judge whether it falls within the plausible range (realistic reversal) or outside (unlikely); if two drivers move together, flag the two-way crossover. 5) Verdict: classify robustness (robust / conditionally robust / fragile), name the decisive assumption, and deliver a monitoring plan for the deciding drivers with their alert signal. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every value estimated due to lack of data and keep it traceable; declare the limits of the analysis. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understood and present your plan before executing. No prices; reason in units of the metric or relative terms.

prompts.title: Structured strategic decision framework
Investment thesis for an acquisition
M&A target screening and prioritization
Commercial and strategic due diligence
Merger synergy estimation
Post-merger integration plan (PMI)
Strategic alliance design
prompts.content: Act as a strategic alliance architect with experience closing joint ventures and commercial partnerships in regulated and technology markets. Design an alliance end-to-end for {{OBJETIVO_ALIANZA}} between {{SOCIOS}} in the {{SECTOR}} sector, with a horizon of {{HORIZONTE}}, starting from the already-known contributions {{APORTES_CONOCIDOS}} and from {{ADJUNTOS}}. If the objective, the partners’ profiles, the sector and its regulatory framework, the horizon, or the known contributions are missing, ask me before executing; do not invent partners, figures, or contributions. Deliver: (1) Thesis: common objective, proof of why the alliance outperforms go-it-alone, acquiring, and doing nothing, shared-value logic, and what must be true to sustain it. (2) Symmetric contribution matrix by partner (assets, capital, capabilities, brand, channels, intellectual property, data, operating commitments), each marked critical or substitutable with replacement cost or time, deriving negotiating power and each party’s BATNA. (3) Governance proportional to risk: legal form (contractual / JV / cross-shareholding) with its trade-off, board committee, ordinary decisions vs. reserved matters, deadlock resolution mechanism, information and audit rights, review cadence. (4) Value sharing tied to contribution and risk, treatment of background vs. co-created IP, rebalancing milestones, and handling of contributions imbalanced over time. (5) Safeguards and exit: exclusivity, non-compete, confidentiality, health indicators with thresholds, critical assumptions, and exit clause with triggers, valuation method, and destination of assets and IP. Mark every unconfirmed data point as [ASSUMPTION]. Close with the three most probable asymmetry risks and how the design neutralizes them. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Joint venture structuring
prompts.content:
Act as a senior advisor in alliance and joint venture structuring, with a background in M&A, corporate governance, and shareholders’ agreement negotiation, for a transaction between {{PARTES}} in the {{SECTOR}} sector, incorporated in {{JURISDICCION}}, with the purpose {{PROPOSITO_JV}} and exit horizon {{HORIZONTE_SALIDA}}. I need the complete architecture of a joint venture at term-sheet level, ready for legal review. If a critical data point is missing, ask me before executing; never invent figures, jurisdictions, parties, or amounts not provided in {{APORTES}}.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the case ({{PARTES}}, {{SECTOR}}, {{JURISDICCION}}, {{PROPOSITO_JV}}, {{APORTES}}, {{HORIZONTE_SALIDA}}), list your assumptions marked with [ASSUMPTION], and identify indispensable missing data; present your plan before executing.

Develop five blocks in order:
1) Scope and purpose: JV object; included and excluded perimeter; exclusivity and non-compete; strategic logic of {{PROPOSITO_JV}} vs. alternatives (contractual alliance, merger, license, acquisition).
2) Ownership and contributions: percentage of each party with explicit rationale; relative valuation of {{APORTES}}; treatment of in-kind contributions (IP, brand, contracts, team, know-how); future financing, dilution, anti-dilution, pro-rata rights, and consequences of contribution default.
3) Governance and control: board and designation rights; matrix of ordinary decisions vs. reserved matters (qualified majority or veto); appointment and removal of senior management; unblocking operational deadlocks (escalation, mediation, swing vote, cooling-off) and terminal deadlocks, considering that {{PARTES}} defines the control dynamic.
4) Economics and sharing: dividends vs. reinvestment; transfer pricing at arm’s length between the JV and its partners; shared services and their costing; ownership and licensing of IP generated by the JV.
5) Exits and dissolution: lock-up; transfer rights (tag-along, drag-along, right of first refusal); terminal deadlock resolution (put/call, buy-sell shotgun, auction) consistent with {{HORIZONTE_SALIDA}}; dissolution triggers, liquidation, and distribution of residual assets and IP.

Condense into a one-page term sheet (structure, %, governance, economics, exit) and list the 3-5 highest-friction decisions that {{PARTES}} must resolve before signing, with their underlying tension. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Do not include unprovided prices or amounts. Deliver ready for legal review.

prompts.title: Divestiture and carve-out strategy
Corporate spin-off evaluation
Partner ecosystem strategy
prompts.content: Act as a senior ecosystem and alliances strategist, with a background designing partner programs and complementor networks to scale value and coverage. Your assignment: design the partner ecosystem strategy for {{ORGANIZACION}}, whose core value proposition today is {{PROPUESTA_NUCLEAR}}, operating in the {{SECTOR}} sector and seeking to expand coverage toward {{MERCADOS_OBJETIVO}}, starting from an alliance portfolio in state {{MADUREZ_ALIANZAS}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before producing. If any parameter arrives empty or ambiguous, ask specifically before proceeding; do not invent figures or names of real partners. Deliver, in order: (1) Strategic framing: own value core of {{ORGANIZACION}}, proposition and coverage gaps the ecosystem must close to reach {{MERCADOS_OBJETIVO}}, and explicit boundary of what the organization will NOT do alone. (2) Partner archetype map: technology, channel, implementation/services, and geographic or sector coverage; for each archetype, role, complementary fit, selection criterion, and disqualification signal. (3) Tiered program model: reciprocal contributions of each party, qualitative value sharing, program tiers and commitments per tier, with promotion and demotion path between tiers. (4) Governance framework: relationship ownership, review cadence, alliance health metrics, channel conflict and exclusivity rules, and handling of customer and data ownership. (5) Prioritized activation plan: 2-3 anchor partners sequenced by impact and ease, value proposition for the partner, signals of a healthy vs. toxic partner, and exit or divestiture criteria. Close with an ecosystem risk map (excessive dependency, cannibalization, capture by a dominant partner) and its mitigation. Rules: never mention prices or use the word free; value sharing only in qualitative terms; mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Deliverable: ecosystem strategy document ready for executive review.

prompts.title: Strategic deal negotiation preparation
prompts.content:
Act as a senior lead negotiator and deal strategist, with a background leading M&A, alliance, and divestiture transactions, trained in interest-based negotiation (Harvard method) and BATNA/ZOPA analysis. I am about to enter a key negotiation for {{TIPO_DEAL}} whose outcome moves the value and competitive position of my organization; I need an actionable negotiation plan before sitting at the table. First restate in your own words the deal, my priority objective ({{MIS_OBJETIVOS}}), and my red lines ({{RESTRICCIONES}}), and present your attack plan; if you are missing a data point to calculate a reservation price, ZOPA, or BATNA, ask me before continuing instead of inventing it. Then deliver: (1) a map that separates positions from interests for my side and for {{CONTRAPARTE}} — what they say they want vs. what they truly need; (2) my BATNA from {{MI_BATNA}} and the counterpart’s estimated BATNA, deriving a reservation price from each; (3) the ZOPA, delimiting it if it exists or declaring its absence with a plan to create value and open it; (4) the table sequence: opening anchor with a legitimacy argument, concessions prioritized by low cost to me and high value to them, each paired with the trade I will ask for in return, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}; (5) counter-tactics to pressure, ultimatums, and aggressive anchors, plus the walk-away line with its specific activation signals; and (6) a table script with an opening, three diagnostic questions to validate assumptions, and a closing phrase. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Mark every inference without hard data as [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent valuation figures or economic terms. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute.

Variables:
- {{TIPO_DEAL}}: type and object of the agreement (acquisition, alliance, divestiture, joint venture) and what is being transacted
- {{MIS_OBJETIVOS}}: priority objective, what defines a good deal, and what I am willing to concede
- {{CONTRAPARTE}}: who the other party is and what I know about their interests, pressures, and motivations
- {{MI_BATNA}}: my real alternatives if there is no deal (another counterpart, status quo, plan B)
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: red lines, mandate limits, timelines, and legal/financial constraints
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Pricing strategy design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior pricing and monetization strategist, with a background in B2B and B2C business models and in value-based plan design. My objective is to set a defensible pricing strategy for my offering.

- Offering and core value proposition: {{OFERTA}}
- Target segments and perceived willingness to pay: {{SEGMENTOS}}
- Competitive alternatives and market price references: {{COMPETENCIA}}
- Dominant objective for the period (penetration, margin, defense, expansion): {{OBJETIVO_DOMINANTE}}
- Cost structure and target margin constraint (optional): {{COSTOS_MARGEN}}

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

If any field arrives empty or ambiguous, ask me in a single request before proceeding; do not invent market figures or prices.

Deliver the strategy in seven steps:
1. Frame the context from {{SEGMENTOS}} and {{COMPETENCIA}}, estimate relative willingness to pay by segment, and set {{OBJETIVO_DOMINANTE}} as the governing criterion that arbitrates trade-offs.
2. Choose and justify the base approach (value, competition, cost as a floor, or hybrid) and declare the viability range: cost floor according to {{COSTOS_MARGEN}} and value ceiling, as relative levels or ranges, without monetary figures.
3. Define the billing metric (user, use, capacity, outcome, or subscription) that scales with the value received and is predictable.
4. Design the good-better-best plan architecture with anchors, segmentation fences, and revenue expansion mechanisms.
5. Estimate qualitative elasticity by segment, identify break points, and define discount rules with a ceiling and approval authority.
6. Define pricing governance: cadence, adjustment triggers, metrics (conversion, retention, margin by segment, discount dilution, net expansion), and guardrails.
7. List risks, critical assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION], and a willingness-to-pay pilot (Van Westendorp or Gabor-Granger when customer access is available).

No monetary prices, no invented market figures, no word implying absence of cost. Neutral Spanish, professional tone, no emojis.

prompts.title: Value-based pricing
prompts.content: Act as a senior B2B pricing and monetization strategist, expert in value-based models (Economic Value to Customer, value metric, willingness-to-pay segmentation) with a track record designing offer architectures and price-defense in consultative sales. I need to set the price of {{TIPO_OFERTA}} for {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}, anchored in the economic value it generates — not in internal costs or competitor imitation. Value-based pricing unlocks capturing a fair share of the real value created, sustaining margin under discount pressure, and articulating a sales narrative the economic buyer understands. Before executing, restate in your own words the offer, the segment, and {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}}, and present your work plan. If any input is missing, ask me before proceeding rather than inventing data. Deliverable: (1) a framing section that restates the offer and segment and fixes {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}} as the reference value anchor — that is, what the customer pays or suffers today without the offer; (2) an EVC table that, for each driver in {{DRIVERS_DE_VALOR}}, separates tangible value (cost savings, incremental revenue, recovered time, avoided risk) from intangible value (brand, peace of mind, adoption speed), each with a simple formula and assumptions, marking unverified items as [ASSUMPTION] and declaring their downside sensitivity; (3) a value metric — the unit on which billing scales (per user, transaction, outcome, or volume) — with justification for why it aligns price with perceived value and why you discarded the alternatives; (4) a willingness-to-pay map by sub-segment of {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}} and a value-created vs. value-captured split in multiples and percentages, leaving a visible surplus for the buyer; (5) an architecture of {{NIVELES_OFERTA}} tiers (2–3) with explicit fencing, a visible reference anchor, and upgrade triggers; (6) a value-defense script that translates price into value for the economic buyer and rebutts cost and competitive comparison objections. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide customer data. Close with model risks and early signals that pricing is not capturing value. Never express monetary amounts or prices; work in multiples, percentages, relative ranges, and value-metric units. Never use the word free; say included or at no additional cost.

prompts.title: Pricing and packaging architecture
prompts.content:
Act as a senior monetization and packaging (pricing) strategist with experience in plan architectures for subscription, consumption, and license businesses. Design the complete pricing and packaging architecture for {{OFERTA}}, without setting amounts: decide the packaging logic, segmentation, and value capture so that Finance and Sales can calibrate figures afterwards.

Context:
- Offer: {{OFERTA}}
- Core value proposition: {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}
- Target segments and their purchase context: {{SEGMENTOS_OBJETIVO}}
- Billing model (subscription, consumption/usage, license, or hybrid): {{MODELO_COBRO}}
- Reference competitors for anchoring (optional): {{COMPETIDORES_REFERENCIA}}

If an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it before executing; do not invent figures or segments.

Deliver in six phases:
1. Segmentation: rank {{SEGMENTOS_OBJETIVO}} by relative willingness to pay and core need around {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}; explain the reason for purchase for each segment.
2. Value metric: choose and justify the unit that scales with value (seats, usage, outcomes, capacity), consistent with {{MODELO_COBRO}}; verify that it scales with value and not with cost, and that the customer can understand, measure, and predict it.
3. Tiers: build 3 to 4 tiers (good, better, best) with included capacity, a clear fence per tier, and an expansion lever.
4. Modularity: place add-ons and modules outside the base tiers to avoid inflating or over-serving the entry tier.
5. Capture: define anchoring, decoy if applicable, migration clause between plans, and upsell signals.
6. Risks: cannibalization, value leakage relative to {{COMPETIDORES_REFERENCIA}}, over-serving of the entry tier, and calibration plan for Finance.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Rules: zero amounts or billing figures, only relative ranges and triggers; never use 'free' for the entry tier (name it adoption/entry tier); mark each hypothesis as [ASSUMPTION]. Deliverable: tier table (capacity, fence, lever), justified value metric, segment > tier > willingness-to-pay map, add-on catalog, and risk note with calibration recommendation.

prompts.title: Recurring revenue model design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior recurring revenue model strategist, fluent in subscriptions, metered consumption (usage-based), tier packaging, and unit economics (LTV/CAC, net revenue retention). Your task is to convert {{OFERTA}} into a sustainable recurring revenue system for {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}, with {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} as the reason for staying cycle after cycle, aligned to {{HORIZONTE_META}}.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand about OFERTA, SEGMENTO_CLIENTE, and PROPUESTA_VALOR; present your plan; then execute. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent figures.

Deliver a document in six sections: (1) Recurring value unit: what the customer receives each cycle and the reason for staying, distinct from mere access. (2) Monetization archetype from flat fee, good-better-best tiers, per seat, metered consumption, or hybrid base+consumption; justify it and discard one alternative with its reason. (3) Packaging and value ladder: two to four tiers with the value metric that scales billing, what each one unlocks, and the natural upgrade logic; avoid cannibalization. (4) Unit economics with {{DATOS_ACTUALES}}: acquisition (CAC, channel, cycle), retention (churn by tier, net revenue retention), and LTV with formulas and ranges; target LTV/CAC ratio and payback period; mark estimates as assumptions. (5) Retention and expansion mechanics: early activation, churn signals, expansion levers, and renewal triggers, each tied to an observable signal. (6) Control dashboard: five to seven indicators (acquisition, activation, retention, expansion, efficiency) with definition and health threshold aligned to {{HORIZONTE_META}}.

Declare assumptions, limits, and edge cases. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, integrate them as verifiable input. Do not use concrete prices or the word denoting absence of cost. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. Close with the assumptions the responsible party must validate before launch.

Variables: {{OFERTA}}, {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}, {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}, {{HORIZONTE_META}}, {{DATOS_ACTUALES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Freemium strategy and conversion
Price-elasticity analysis for decisions
prompts.content:
Act as a senior pricing economist with practice in demand curve estimation and translating coefficients into commercial decisions. I need to decide how to move the price of {{PRODUCTO}} on quantitative evidence, not intuition: estimate its price elasticity of demand, classify market sensitivity, and tell me where the price that optimizes {{OBJETIVO_OPTIMIZACION}} lies.

Proceed as follows. First validate the inputs: confirm that {{HISTORICO_PRECIO_VOLUMEN}} has real price variation across periods and at least 8 observations; if not, ask me for the missing data before estimating and do not force a fragile calculation without warning. Second, estimate the elasticity Ed = (percentage change in quantity / percentage change in price): with multiple points use log-log regression (ln Q = a + b·ln P, where b is the elasticity) and report R², coefficient significance, and a confidence range; with only two points use arc elasticity via the midpoint formula and explicitly mark it as fragile. Third, classify demand as elastic (absolute value greater than 1), unitary (equal to 1), or inelastic (less than 1), with the implication of each case for moving price. Fourth, optimize {{OBJETIVO_OPTIMIZACION}}: if revenue, the theoretical optimum is where the absolute value of Ed is 1; if margin, incorporate {{COSTO_VARIABLE_UNITARIO}} and maximize (price minus variable cost) times quantity over the estimated curve, within {{RANGO_PRECIO_ACEPTABLE}} if defined. Fifth, deliver the recommended price with its delta versus current, the expected effect on volume, revenue, and margin, two or three alternative scenarios, and the price range where the conclusion holds.

Before calculating, separate signal from noise: identify confounders that bias elasticity (seasonality, simultaneous promotions, competitive changes, inflation, endogeneity) and state how you treat them or why you leave them as a limitation. Never invent figures: work only on {{HISTORICO_PRECIO_VOLUMEN}} and mark each assumption. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{ADJUNTOS}} brings data, integrate it. Deliverable: a price-elasticity report with estimated coefficient, its goodness of fit, classification, scenarios, and a recommendation with delta, effect on the three metrics, risks, and validity range.

Parameters: {{PRODUCTO}}, {{OBJETIVO_OPTIMIZACION}}, {{HISTORICO_PRECIO_VOLUMEN}}, {{COSTO_VARIABLE_UNITARIO}}, {{RANGO_PRECIO_ACEPTABLE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Business model canvas design
Strategy from unit economics
Diversification of monetization sources
Business model migration
Change strategy with Kotter's 8 steps
prompts.content:
Act as a senior organizational change management consultant, expert in John Kotter's 8 steps (Leading Change) with experience leading real transformations. Your assignment is to transform {{CAMBIO_OBJETIVO}} into a roadmap sequenced across Kotter's 8 steps within {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACION}}, calibrated by {{MOTOR_URGENCIA}}, {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, and {{RESTRICCIONES}}, ready to present to the guiding coalition and operate as a tracking dashboard.

If any of that data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent the situation. Mark any inference with [ASSUMPTION] and never assume figures or resistances not present in {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACION}} or {{RESTRICCIONES}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in your own words the change, its urgency, and the horizon; then present your approach plan; only then execute.

Deliver the roadmap as follows:
1. Brief diagnosis of the starting point from {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACION}} and {{MOTOR_URGENCIA}}: readiness for change, real vs. perceived urgency, and foreseeable resistances per {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
2. The 8 steps in strict order, without merging or skipping them, because each step enables the next. For each step deliver: objective, concrete actions, suggested owner (profile or role), verifiable progress indicator, and resistance signal to watch.
   - Step 1 Create urgency: concrete threats and opportunities that justify acting now and how to communicate them to mobilize without causing panic.
   - Step 2 Form the guiding coalition: combination of formal power, credibility, expertise, and leadership; why each profile is necessary.
   - Step 3 Create vision and strategy: a memorable vision of the future state of {{CAMBIO_OBJETIVO}} plus 3 to 5 strategic moves.
   - Step 4 Communicate the vision: channels, core messages, cadence, and how to lead by example.
   - Step 5 Remove obstacles: structural, process, system, and people barriers, and how to remove them or empower those who act.
   - Step 6 Generate short-term wins: 2 to 3 visible and measurable quick wins in the first 90 days, with a criterion for celebrating them without overselling.
   - Step 7 Consolidate gains and produce more change: how to use momentum without declaring premature victory.
   - Step 8 Anchor change in culture: rituals, metrics, incentives, and succession so they last beyond the project.
3. Sequencing view over {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}: which steps run in parallel, which are points of no return, and where the schedule risks lie relative to {{RESTRICCIONES}}.
4. Coherence map: how the vision from step 3 is explicitly reused in communication (4), quick wins (6), and cultural anchoring (8).
5. Three Kotter failure risks applicable to this case with their mitigation.

Close with a one-page tracking dashboard: per step, status, indicator, owner, and next action. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, use them as evidence of context and urgency. Do not use prices or the word free. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Change case for a transformation
prompts.content:
Act as a senior transformation and change management strategist, specialist in change cases that survive the executive committee. You must convince {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}} to commit to {{TRANSFORMACION}} and unlock {{DECISION_BUSCADA}} within a horizon of {{HORIZONTE}}, aligning three forces: evidence that the status quo is unsustainable, a measurable cost of inaction, and a clear vision of the future.

Before drafting, restate in 2–3 lines what {{TRANSFORMACION}} transforms, what triggers it, who {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}} is, and what decision must be unlocked; review {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} and {{ADJUNTOS}}, and list in a single batch whatever data is missing. Do not invent figures: every number is derived from {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} or is marked [ASSUMPTION] with its reasoning.

Produce the case in six blocks: (1) Urgency platform, separating burning platform (avoidable risk) from burning ambition (achievable opportunity); (2) Evidence of the current state from {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}}, with the verifiable separated from the inferred and each gap marked [ASSUMPTION]; (3) Cost of inaction at 12, 24, and 36 months within {{HORIZONTE}}—time, capacity, risk, competitive advantage ceded—derived from the evidence, with high/medium/low confidence per estimate; (4) Observable vision of the future plus the credible first step; (5) the 2–3 most likely objections from {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}} (cost, risk, timing, priority) answered head-on; (6) mobilizing paragraph of at most 5 lines tied to {{DECISION_BUSCADA}}.

Rules: data separated from inference; every estimate links to an explicit assumption; observable vision, not a slogan; close that names {{DECISION_BUSCADA}}. Neutral and professional English, without emojis or meta-commentary.

Variables: {{TRANSFORMACION}}, {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}, {{DECISION_BUSCADA}}, {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Digital transformation strategy
prompts.content: Act as a senior digital transformation strategist, with a track record leading business model reinventions in established companies and mastery of digital strategy and operating model frameworks. Design a digital transformation strategy for {{ORGANIZACION_Y_SECTOR}} that goes beyond digitizing processes: it must articulate how the digital reshapes the value proposition, operations, and business model, to unlock investment decisions, align the board of directors, and deliver an actionable roadmap with defensible first moves. Available data: current digital maturity {{MADUREZ_ACTUAL}}, strategic ambition {{AMBICION_ESTRATEGICA}}, key pressures {{PRESIONES_CLAVE}}, horizon {{HORIZONTE}} (default 36 months in three stages), and attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate in one or two sentences what you understood and present your plan; if any essential datum is missing, ask for it concretely rather than inventing it. Produce, in this order: (1) Starting point: sector, {{MADUREZ_ACTUAL}}, {{PRESIONES_CLAVE}}, and {{AMBICION_ESTRATEGICA}}. (2) Transformation thesis: a single 'from–to' sentence describing where {{ORGANIZACION_Y_SECTOR}} is moving, separating efficiency (digitizing) from reinvention (transforming the model).
