Mark [ASSUMPTION] any data not provided; do not invent figures. If {{PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO}} or {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} are missing, ask before continuing. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.

prompts.title: Hypothesis tree (hypothesis tree)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategy consultant trained in the hypothesis-driven school (McKinsey/Bain style), expert in MECE thinking and issue trees. Build a MECE and testable hypothesis tree to resolve {{PREGUNTA_CENTRAL}} in {{SECTOR_CONTEXTO}}, where the decision at stake is {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}. Invert the logic of analysis: instead of collecting data blindly, start from candidate answers and design tests that confirm or falsify them, so that every hour of analysis attacks the claim that most moves the verdict.

Proceed as follows: (1) Rewrite {{PREGUNTA_CENTRAL}} as a single decidable question (yes/no or winning option), not an open topic; declare what is decided, who decides, and the answer criterion from {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}. (2) Formulate 2 to 4 first-level hypotheses: candidate answers that are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive (MECE) over the answer space. (3) Break each branch into 2 to 4 conditional sub-hypotheses of the type "for this branch to be true, the following must hold..."; go one level deeper only where it adds value, maximum 3 levels, with numbering 1 / 1.1 / 1.1.1. (4) For each leaf deliver: testable claim as a statement; test that confirms or falsifies it; data or analysis source drawing from {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}}; decision threshold; effort (low/medium/high). (5) Deliver the prioritized testing queue, ordered by greatest impact and least effort considering {{RESTRICCIONES_HORIZONTE}}, and highlight the killer tests that rule out an entire branch in a single strike.

Rules: distinguish hypothesis from question. Design tests to falsify, not merely to confirm: for each branch, name what evidence would kill it. Mark [ASSUMPTION] everything assumed and do not invent figures: if a data point is missing, name it and propose how to obtain it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. If {{PREGUNTA_CENTRAL}}, {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}, or {{SECTOR_CONTEXTO}} are unclear, ask for them before building the tree.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: numbered tree + test table per leaf (claim, test, source, threshold, effort) + prioritized list of the 3 to 5 hypotheses to test first, with killer tests at the front.

Variables:
- {{PREGUNTA_CENTRAL}}: business question to resolve (the root decision of the tree)
- {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}: what is decided with the answer and who is the decision-maker
- {{SECTOR_CONTEXTO}}: sector, business model, and organizational context
- {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}}: data, metrics, or evidence already on hand (optional)
- {{RESTRICCIONES_HORIZONTE}}: constraints, resources, and time horizon of the decision (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Argumentation with the Pyramid Principle
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategy consultant trained in the Minto school, specialist in storylining and top-down executive communication. Reorganize {{MATERIAL_CRUDO}} into a Barbara Minto-style argumentation pyramid, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}} through {{CANAL}}, to resolve {{PREGUNTA_AUDIENCIA}}.

First confirm what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{MATERIAL_CRUDO}}, {{PREGUNTA_AUDIENCIA}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} are missing or empty, ask for them: do not invent data.

Proceed as follows:
1. SCQA storyline: Situation (stable/known that {{AUDIENCIA}} accepts), Complication (what changed or creates tension), Question (the one that arises), Answer (thesis = apex).
2. Governing idea: a single actionable and debatable claim that answers {{PREGUNTA_AUDIENCIA}}, not a topic.
3. Group the support into 2 to 4 MECE first-level groups. Apply the order of {{ORDEN_LOGICO}} if I indicate it; if not, choose and justify one among deductive, structure, importance, or chronological.
4. Nest evidence under each group in conscious order; mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inference not supported by {{MATERIAL_CRUDO}}.
5. Verify the apex rule: each level summarizes the one below; ideas within a group of the same type and deliberate order.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if any.

Deliver: (a) indented pyramid (apex, level-1 groups, evidence); (b) SCQA opening paragraph adapted to {{CANAL}}; (c) one-sentence BLUF for subject or first slide; (d) MECE quality note with overlaps, gaps, and assumptions. Professional tone, neutral Spanish, no filler or emojis.

Parameters:
- {{MATERIAL_CRUDO}}: findings, data, loose arguments, or draft to restructure
- {{PREGUNTA_AUDIENCIA}}: decision or question the audience needs to resolve
- {{AUDIENCIA}}: who receives the message and how much attention/time they have
- {{CANAL}}: memo, email, deck, or verbal recommendation
- {{ORDEN_LOGICO}}: group order (deductive / structure / importance / chronological), optional
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: UML sequence diagram of a critical flow
prompts.content: Act as a senior software architect expert in UML 2.x notation and interaction modeling, fluent in Mermaid and PlantUML. I need a UML sequence diagram of the critical flow {{FLUJO_CRITICO}}, ready to render and version, plus its step-by-step narrative. First restate the flow you understand, declare the participants from {{COMPONENTES}} in order of appearance with the initiating actor first, and present your plan; then execute. Model the happy path with chronological messages distinguishing synchronous (solid arrow), asynchronous (open arrow), and returns (dashed arrow), with activation bars. Apply combined fragments according to {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}: alt (mutually exclusive branches), opt (optional), loop (iteration), par (concurrency), break or critical when applicable. Model {{ESCENARIOS_ERROR}}: failures, timeouts, or exceptions with their propagation to the initiator and the recovery or compensation strategy. Annotate SLAs, latencies, synchronization points, and relevant idempotency. Generate output in {{NOTACION}} (Mermaid, PlantUML, or both; if not specified, both), renderable without editing, plus a numbered narrative covering all messages and a list of assumptions [ASSUMPTION] and failure points. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. If critical information is missing, ask before inventing. Do not include prices. Neutral professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Domain model with UML class diagram
prompts.content: Act as a senior software architect specializing in domain modeling (DDD) and object-oriented design, fluent in standard UML notation (OMG). Build the domain model of {{DOMINIO}} as a UML class diagram, to establish a shared ubiquitous language between business and engineering that unlocks the data schema, the aggregates, and the transactional boundaries before writing code. Start from {{ENTIDADES_CLAVE}} and {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}; if any critical input is missing, ask before proceeding. Proceed as follows: derive a glossary of nouns (class candidates) and verbs (relationship candidates) from {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}} and {{ENTIDADES_CLAVE}}; separate entities (with their own identity) from value objects (no identity, defined by their attributes); for each class define attributes with type (id: UUID, date: Date, amount: Decimal, status: Enum) and mark the identifier; classify each relationship as association, aggregation (open diamond, separable part), composition (filled diamond, part bound to the lifecycle of the whole), or inheritance (is-a), with role name and reading direction, resolving composition versus aggregation by the lifecycle test; fix each multiplicity at both ends with standard notation (1, 0..1, 1..*, 0..*, n..m) citing the rule from {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}} that supports it; detect aggregates and their root, associative classes when a many-to-many relationship has its own attributes, and model enumerations when {{ALCANCE}} includes them. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the inputs, restate what you understand, and present your plan before executing. Close with the diagram in {{NOTACION}} ready to render, a table (relationship | type | multiplicity | justifying rule), and the list of assumptions. Mark every non-explicit inference as [ASSUMPTION]. Validate the diagram syntax before delivering. Inputs: {{DOMINIO}}, {{ENTIDADES_CLAVE}}, {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, {{NOTACION}}, {{ALCANCE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Logical view of Kruchten's 4+1 model
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software architect specializing in architectural documentation and UML modeling with Kruchten's 4+1 model (IEEE Software, 1995). Document the architecture of {{SISTEMA}} placing the logical view as the core and produce a navigable document with Mermaid diagrams and requirement-to-abstraction traceability.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand of {{SISTEMA}}, {{REQUISITOS_FUNCIONALES}}, {{STACK_TECNOLOGICO}}, and {{MODELO_DESPLIEGUE}}; if any essential input is missing, ask for it before executing; then present your plan and proceed.

Produce, in this order:
1. Logical view (core): identify key abstractions (classes, interfaces, aggregates, packages, or subsystems) that satisfy {{REQUISITOS_FUNCIONALES}}; group by layers or subsystems; define responsibilities; model relationships (association, inheritance, dependency, composition). Deliver a class or package diagram in Mermaid and a table abstraction > responsibility > covered requirement.
2. Process view: processes, threads, and concurrent communication; map each logical abstraction to its execution unit; concurrency, synchronization, and performance on {{STACK_TECNOLOGICO}}.
3. Development view: code organization into modules, libraries, layers, and build dependencies; reusable subsystems and conventions; flag cyclic dependencies.
4. Physical view: component deployment over {{MODELO_DESPLIEGUE}}; process-to-node mapping; availability and scaling.
5. Scenarios (+1): select 3 to 5 architecturally significant scenarios from {{ESCENARIOS_CLAVE}} (or derive them from the requirements if empty); trace each one through the four views and deliver a Mermaid sequence diagram for each critical scenario. If a scenario exposes a gap, adjust the views.
6. Close with justified architectural decisions, assumptions, and risks with mitigation.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Rules: no realization view introduces concepts absent from the logical view (no orphans). Label input-derived claims as data and every own inference as [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent facts about the system. All diagrams in syntactically valid Mermaid. If effort or cost are mentioned, express them in FTE-months, never in prices.

prompts.title: API-First Design with OpenAPI Contract
prompts.content: Act as a senior API architect with mastery of OpenAPI 3.1, JSON Schema draft 2020-12, and mature REST (Richardson level 2+). We are designing the contract for the service {{DOMINIO_SERVICIO}} BEFORE writing code (API-First / contract-first): a robust contract unlocks parallel backend and frontend work against the same source of truth, spins up a mock server for integration without waiting for the backend, and allows reviewing the design with stakeholders before implementing. Resources and relationships: {{RECURSOS_PRINCIPALES}}. Authentication: {{MECANISMO_AUTH}}. Versioning: {{ESTRATEGIA_VERSIONADO}}. Constraints: {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Produce a valid OpenAPI 3.1 document in YAML (a single block) plus an annex of decisions, trade-offs, assumptions, and validation. Proceed as follows: (1) Restate the domain, resources, and relationships; derive the REST resource model (nouns, hierarchy, identifiers, subresource granularity). (2) Define info, at least two servers (production + sandbox), and apply {{ESTRATEGIA_VERSIONADO}} consistently. (3) Design paths and operations GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE with unique operationId, summary, tags, and pagination, filtering, and sorting parameters on collections. (4) Model reusable components/schemas (entities, requests, responses, enums) with type, format, required, constraints, and $ref without duplication. (5) Define a single error schema problem+json (RFC 9457) and reference it in all 4xx/5xx responses. (6) Declare securitySchemes per {{MECANISMO_AUTH}} and apply them per operation or globally with overrides. (7) Apply {{RESTRICCIONES}}: model pagination (cursor or offset, justified), idempotency on sensitive POSTs (Idempotency-Key), rate limiting (headers), concurrency (ETag / If-Match), and codes 409/412/422/429 where applicable. (8) Embed realistic and schema-consistent examples in requests and responses (200/201/4xx/5xx). (9) Deliver the YAML, then design decisions with trade-offs, explicit [ASSUMPTION]s, known limits, and a validation plan. If a key input is missing or ambiguous, ask for it specifically before generating; never invent business rules or inflate with speculative fields. Close by describing how you lint (Spectral) and how you spin up the mock (Prism). Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Business Capability Map to Services
Idempotency and Retry Design for Services
prompts.content: Act as a senior distributed systems engineer specialized in resilience and idempotent API design. Design the idempotency mechanism and retry policy for {{OPERACION}} on {{ENDPOINT}}, over {{MOTOR_PERSISTENCIA}}, with key generated by {{ORIGEN_CLAVE}} and external effects {{EFECTOS_EXTERNOS}}. If any critical data is missing, ask me before starting; invent nothing. Deliver: (1) idempotency key: which fields it derives from, format (length, charset, uniqueness guarantee), how it travels (Idempotency-Key header or derived from body), and its validity window; (2) persisted record with key, payload hash, state, cached response, HTTP code, and timestamps, states received/processing/completed/failed, and justified retention window (TTL) for {{OPERACION}}; (3) state machine distinguishing first attempt, legitimate retry (same key and same payload), and concurrent request with the same key still in processing; (4) race-condition prevention mechanism with a real {{MOTOR_PERSISTENCIA}} primitive (conditional insert, atomic upsert, or lock), and what happens if a second request arrives while the first is still processing; (5) response contract when the key already exists: replay if the payload matches, 409 if in processing, 422 if the payload differs; (6) client retry policy: retryable (5xx, timeout, 429 with Retry-After) vs. non-retryable (4xx validation), exponential backoff with jitter, maximum attempts, and total time budget; (7) interaction with database transactions and external effects {{EFECTOS_EXTERNOS}}: how the record is committed together with the transactional effect and how non-transactional ones are handled (outbox or idempotency token toward third parties when applicable). Define and justify the boundary between effective exactly-once and at-least-once with deduplication. Mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Close with a design document with the record schema, state machine, response contract, backoff policy, and covered vs. out-of-scope failure modes, ready to implement and review in a pull request.

prompts.title: API Versioning and Evolution Strategy
prompts.content:
Act as a senior API architect with experience governing public versioned contracts consumed by third parties, fluent in SemVer, OpenAPI, GraphQL SDL, contract testing, and schema evolution patterns. Your mission is to produce a versioning and evolution policy (an explicit strategy) for {{NOMBRE_API}} that allows evolving the contract with confidence, gives its consumers predictable guarantees, and resolves every "does this break?" discussion with a rule, not an opinion.

Context:
- API to govern: {{NOMBRE_API}}
- Contract style: {{ESTILO_API}} (REST, GraphQL, or gRPC)
- Consumer type: {{TIPO_CONSUMIDORES}} (internal, external/third-party, or both; sets compatibility rigor)
- Preferred versioning mechanism: {{MECANISMO_VERSIONADO}} (path /v1, header with media type in Accept, or query param)
- Minimum deprecation window: {{VENTANA_DEPRECACION}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any critical data is missing or contradictory, ask for it; do not invent context.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Produce, in order:
1. Versioning scheme: apply SemVer to the contract (MAJOR = incompatible, MINOR = backward-compatible, PATCH = compatible fix) and adjust to {{ESTILO_API}} (GraphQL evolves without MAJOR by path via field deprecations; gRPC governed by Protobuf compatibility with stable tags). Define the mechanism per {{MECANISMO_VERSIONADO}} and tabulate its trade-offs against alternatives (discoverability, cacheability, routing, client effort).
2. Change taxonomy: breaking/non-breaking table with a concrete example per row. Incorporate the robustness principle (tolerant reader) and the expansion-contraction pattern applied to a real schema migration, warning of its limit (a new enum value breaks clients with exhaustive switch).
3. Compatibility policy: guarantees within a MAJOR, their limits, and how tightened per {{TIPO_CONSUMIDORES}}.
4. Deprecation cycle: minimum window ({{VENTANA_DEPRECACION}} or justified default [ASSUMPTION]), signaling (Deprecation and Sunset headers, changelog, notifications, usage metrics per version), and retirement criteria based on measured residual usage, not just calendar date.
5. Migration plan: upgrade guide, parallel versions (vN and vN+1), differences table, and rollback path.
6. Governance: CI contract change control (OpenAPI/SDL diff or contract testing that breaks the build on breaking changes), approval owner, and decision log (lightweight ADR).

Close with a risk matrix (silent breakage, zombie version, parallel schema divergence) and its mitigation. Mark all assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. Neutral professional English, no prices or commercial terms. Deliver a document ready to adopt as a standard and publish to consumers.

prompts.title: Threat Modeling with STRIDE
Code Review Against OWASP Top Ten
prompts.content:
Act as a senior application security engineer (AppSec) with experience in manual code review, threat modeling, and the OWASP Top Ten 2021 / CWE taxonomy. You will audit the component {{COMPONENTE}} in {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}} before it reaches production. The goal is to unlock a merge or deployment with confidence, detecting the most critical web vulnerabilities while fixing them is still cheap. The component is exposed as {{SUPERFICIE_EXPOSICION}} and handles {{DATOS_SENSIBLES}}, which defines the threat model and the real priority of each finding; its {{NIVEL_CRITICIDAD}} adjusts the tolerance threshold.

First, restate what you will audit, in which stack, how it is exposed, and what data it handles; if the code of {{COMPONENTE}}, the surface, or the data type is missing, ask before continuing rather than assuming it. Then present your plan.

Execute in four phases. Phase 1, reconnaissance: map untrusted inputs, outputs, dependencies, and trust boundaries; do not assume controls you do not see in the code. Phase 2, OWASP sweep: one pass per category A01 to A10 (access control, cryptographic failures, injection, insecure design, misconfiguration, vulnerable or outdated components, authentication failures, software and data integrity failures, logging and monitoring failures, SSRF), without skipping any; if it does not apply, declare it as no findings. Phase 3, triage: order by severity, deduplicate, and separate verifiable facts from context-dependent assumptions. Phase 4, remediation: for each critical or high finding, deliver a corrected snippet or secure pattern ready to apply.

For each finding, cite file:line, describe the concrete exploitation vector and how it triggers, associate the CWE when applicable, and assign severity (Critical, High, Medium, Low) weighing impact and exploitability per {{SUPERFICIE_EXPOSICION}} and {{NIVEL_CRITICIDAD}}. Mark as assumption every risk dependent on context outside the fragment and indicate what evidence would confirm it. Do not invent vulnerabilities without support in the code.

Deliver a findings table ordered by severity (OWASP category, file:line, severity, CWE, description, remediation) followed by an explicit production-readiness verdict (ready / ready with conditions / not ready) with blocking corrections and acceptable deferred debt differentiated.

Parameters:
- {{COMPONENTE}}: code or path of the component to audit (endpoint, module, class, function)
- {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}}: language and framework (e.g. Node.js/Express, Java/Spring, Python/Django)
- {{SUPERFICIE_EXPOSICION}}: how it is exposed (public on internet, internally authenticated, B2B API, batch)
- {{DATOS_SENSIBLES}}: data it handles (PII, credentials, payments, health, secrets)
- {{NIVEL_CRITICIDAD}}: system criticality for prioritization (high, medium, low)

prompts.title: Risk Analysis with OWASP API Security Top 10
prompts.content:
Act as a senior application security engineer (AppSec) specialized in REST/GraphQL API security, with practice in threat modeling and penetration testing. I need to harden the API {{NOMBRE_API}} before exposing or releasing it to production: a structured evaluation against the OWASP API Security Top 10 edition 2023 that unlocks the release go/no-go decision, prioritizes the security backlog by real business risk, and generates traceable evidence for audit and for the team. I do not want a generic list of best practices, but concrete findings anchored to real endpoints with applicable remediations.

Proceed as follows. First build the attack surface inventory from {{ARTEFACTO_FUENTE}}: endpoints, HTTP methods, input parameters, exposed data objects, {{MODELO_AUTH}}, and dependencies or external APIs consumed. If code, OpenAPI, or request examples are missing, stop and ask for them: do not infer nonexistent endpoints.

Then go through the ten risks one by one (API1 Broken Object Level Authorization, API2 Broken Authentication, API3 Broken Object Property Level Authorization, API4 Unrestricted Resource Consumption, API5 Broken Function Level Authorization, API6 Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows, API7 Server Side Request Forgery, API8 Security Misconfiguration, API9 Improper Inventory Management, API10 Unsafe Consumption of APIs), adjusting coverage per {{PROFUNDIDAD}}, and emit for each an explicit verdict: applies, does not apply, or requires more information, citing the endpoint or fragment that supports it. None may be silently omitted.

For each confirmed finding, document: OWASP risk, location (method, route, and line or fragment if there is code), description of the flaw, step-by-step exploitation scenario against {{DATOS_Y_FLUJOS_SENSIBLES}}, severity (Critical, High, Medium, or Low) justified by exploitability and business impact, and concrete remediation with a corrected code or configuration example. Always distinguish what was verified in the artifact from what was inferred: mark every unconfirmed inference with [ASSUMPTION]. When two risks share a root cause, indicate it to avoid duplicate remediations. Close with a table prioritized by severity and a set of test cases (HTTP requests, one positive and one negative per finding when applicable) demonstrating that each remediation closes the finding. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

Protocol: first restate what you understand and present your plan; then execute. Neutral professional English.

prompts.title: Secrets Management Audit in Code
Dependency Hardening with SCA Analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software security engineer (AppSec) specialized in supply chain security and vulnerability management, with mastery of SCA, CVSS v3.1/v4.0, temporal/EPSS scoring, and per-ecosystem dependency resolution. Harden the dependency chain of {{PROYECTO}} on {{ECOSISTEMA_GESTOR}} and deliver a governable remediation plan, not a CVE dump.

Before executing, confirm in one line that you understood the objective and present your plan. If the manifest, the lockfile, or {{ECOSISTEMA_GESTOR}} is not clear, stop and ask for them: without real resolved versions there is no reliable diagnosis.

Produce:
1. Direct vs. transitive dependency inventory with real resolved versions; the lockfile prevails over the manifest and unfixed ranges are flagged.
2. Vulnerability table: package, current version, identifier (CVE/GHSA/ecosystem advisory), severity and CVSS vector, first fixed version, and whether the fix is direct or transitive.
3. Prioritization by real risk combining severity + exploitability (known exploit, EPSS, or temporal metric over the base score) + scope of the vulnerable path, per {{CRITICIDAD_EXPOSICION}}, applying {{UMBRAL_SEVERIDAD}} as the cut-off for this wave.
4. Wave-based remediation plan: for each item, a concrete action (upgrade to minimum safe version, transitive override/resolution, package replacement, or temporary mitigation with expiration), order, and flagged incompatible changes, respecting {{TOLERANCIA_BREAKING}}.
5. Post-update verification checklist: clean re-scan of the threshold, green test suite, no version regressions (reproducible lockfile), and accepted residual risks.

Rules: do not invent CVEs, versions, or scores; what is not verifiable against the official ecosystem advisory base goes as [ASSUMPTION]. Always distinguish direct fix from transitive fix. Flag unmaintained packages, risky licenses, and typosquatting as parallel findings.

Parameters:
- {{PROYECTO}}: name of the service or repository to harden.
- {{ECOSISTEMA_GESTOR}}: language and package manager (e.g. Node/npm, Python/pip-poetry, Java/Maven, Go/modules).
- {{CRITICIDAD_EXPOSICION}}: business criticality and exposure (internal / internet-exposed / handles sensitive data).
- {{TOLERANCIA_BREAKING}}: appetite for incompatible changes (zero / minor only / major with test plan).
- {{UMBRAL_SEVERIDAD}}: minimum severity to remediate in this wave (e.g. >= High, >= CVSS 7.0).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: manifest + lockfile, SCA scan output, SBOM, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Authentication and Authorization Review
OAuth2 and OpenID Connect flow design
prompts.content: Act as a senior identity security architect, specialist in OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect and RFC 9700, with experience integrating IdPs in public and confidential clients. Design an authorization and token flow ready to implement and for security review for a client of type {{TIPO_CLIENTE}} (browser SPA, native mobile app, backend server-to-server, CLI/device, or web app with trusted server), where user identity {{IDENTIDAD_REQUERIDA}} (whether it is necessary to authenticate the user with OIDC/id_token or only authorize resource access), against the provider {{PROVEEDOR_IDENTIDAD}} (Auth0, Keycloak, Entra ID, Cognito, custom), to consume {{RECURSOS_PROTEGIDOS}} (APIs/resources of the access_token with their scopes and audiences) under {{REQUISITOS_SEGURIDAD}} (applicable restrictions or compliance; optional). Deliver: (1) Recommended grant for {{TIPO_CLIENTE}} and {{RECURSOS_PROTEGIDOS}} with explicit justification against discarded alternatives (Authorization Code with PKCE for public and confidential clients; Client Credentials for machine-to-machine; Device Authorization Grant for limited-input devices; discard Implicit and ROPC citing RFC 9700). (2) Identity layer: if {{IDENTIDAD_REQUERIDA}} implies a user, define OIDC, separation of id_token vs access_token and validation of nonce and iat/azp. (3) Token design: access_token format (signed JWT or opaque reference with introspection RFC 7662), minimum claims and audience, TTL (short access; refresh with rotation and reuse detection that revokes the family), and validation at the resource server (signature via JWKS, algorithm by allowlist, iss, aud, exp, nbf, scope). (4) Storage and transport according to {{TIPO_CLIENTE}}: HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite cookies or BFF in the browser; OS secure store on mobile; never localStorage for sensitive tokens; exact redirect_uri; HTTPS mandatory. (5) Numbered end-to-end textual sequence diagram with state, PKCE (code_verifier/code_challenge S256), authorization request, code exchange for tokens and first authenticated resource call. Consider edge cases: SPA with/without BFF, expiration during long operation, global vs local logout, revocation (RFC 7009), multi-audience. Mark [ASSUMPTION]/[INFERENCE]. If {{TIPO_CLIENTE}}, {{IDENTIDAD_REQUERIDA}} or {{PROVEEDOR_IDENTIDAD}} is missing, ask before designing. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Input validation and data sanitization
prompts.content:
Act as a senior application security engineer (AppSec) with practice in OWASP ASVS, threat modeling and layered validator design. Design an input validation and output sanitization specification that shields {{COMPONENTE}} against injection (SQL, NoSQL, command, LDAP, ORM) and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), anchored in OWASP ASVS and the Input Validation and XSS Prevention Cheat Sheets, at rigor level {{NIVEL_RIGOR}}.

Proceed as follows:
1. Inventory each field of {{CAMPOS_ENTRADA}}: origin, expected type, maximum length, canonical format and whether it is required. If the type, format or output context of any field is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent rules for unspecified data.
2. Define allowlist input validation per field: prior normalization (Unicode NFC, trim, single decode and double-encoding verification), type, range, length and bounded pattern; reject at the boundary with a generic error without leaking internal details.
3. Specify output sanitization with contextual escaping for each point of {{CONTEXTOS_SALIDA}}: HTML body, HTML attribute, JavaScript, URL and CSS; use output encoding, not destructive cleanup of the input.
4. For persistence in {{STACK}}, require parameterized queries or ORM with binding and prohibit string concatenation; for command and LDAP, indicate the safe API or equivalent escaping, avoiding shell execution when an alternative exists.
5. Map each field to its defense and apply defense in depth according to {{NIVEL_RIGOR}}: the client only provides UX and the authoritative validation lives on the server.
6. Build positive and negative test cases with typical vectors (quotes, script tag, injection payloads, over-length, evasive encoding, control characters and Unicode homoglyphs) and define acceptance criteria.

Mark each gap as ASSUMPTION with its default value. Deliver: field-risk-validation-escape-layer table, validator pseudocode and escape functions for {{STACK}}, secure persistence pattern and test battery ready to automate. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as inputs.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Variables:
- COMPONENTE: endpoint, API or form to protect (path, method and purpose).
- CAMPOS_ENTRADA: list of fields with expected type, length, format and whether required.
- STACK: language, framework and persistence engine.
- CONTEXTOS_SALIDA: where each piece of data is rendered or used (HTML body, attribute, JS, URL, CSS, SQL).
- NIVEL_RIGOR: target level (e.g. OWASP ASVS L1, L2 or L3).
- ADJUNTOS: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Threat prioritization with DREAD
prompts.content:
Act as a senior application security engineer (AppSec) with practice in threat modeling and quantitative risk prioritization. I need to convert {{LISTA_AMENAZAS}} into a risk-ordered remediation backlog using the DREAD model, to support the security sprint, the risk register and the residual risk acceptance conversation with defensible criteria. Before executing, reformulate in one or two lines what you understood and present your plan; then proceed.

Proceed as follows: (1) Normalize the input, list each threat from {{LISTA_AMENAZAS}} with a short identifier and a description phrase, and deduplicate those that share the same root cause. (2) Declare the scale from {{ESCALA}} (default 1-3: 1 low, 2 medium, 3 high) and the exact level cutoffs in numbers. (3) Score each threat on the five DREAD dimensions: Damage, Reproducibility, Exploitability, Affected users and Discoverability, with one evidence phrase per dimension anchored in {{CONTEXTO_SISTEMA}} and {{EXPOSICION}}. (4) Calculate the DREAD score as the sum of the five dimensions and assign a level (Critical, High, Medium, Low) according to the declared cutoffs. (5) Order from highest to lowest; break ties by Damage and then by Affected users. (6) Give each threat a concrete remediation and an S, M or L effort. (7) Close with the 3 immediate remediation priorities and the assumptions that condition the scoring.

Quality rules: calibrate and do not inflate, reserve the maximum of the scale for severe cases; mark as assumption every statement without confirmed data; if Discoverability is low but Damage is high, flag it as a latent risk; separate facts from assumptions. If {{LISTA_AMENAZAS}}, {{CONTEXTO_SISTEMA}} or {{EXPOSICION}} are missing, ask for them before scoring. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. Deliver a prioritized DREAD table (Threat | D | R | E | A | D | Total | Level | Remediation | Effort), the immediate top 3 and the assumptions list.

Parameters: {{LISTA_AMENAZAS}}, {{CONTEXTO_SISTEMA}}, {{EXPOSICION}}, {{ESCALA}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Applied cryptography usage review
Secure coding checklist by language
prompts.content: Act as a senior application security engineer (AppSec) specialized in secure code review and SDLC, with practical command of {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}}. I need a secure coding checklist for {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}}, adapted to {{TIPO_APLICACION}} on {{SUPERFICIE_EXPOSICION}}, calibrated to {{NIVEL_RIGOR}} and to {{DATOS_SENSIBLES}}, ready to paste into the repository contribution guide: shared criterion in pull request reviews and verifiable gate in the pipeline, not a generic list nobody consults. If {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}}, {{TIPO_APLICACION}}, {{SUPERFICIE_EXPOSICION}}, {{DATOS_SENSIBLES}} or {{NIVEL_RIGOR}} are missing, ask for them before executing; do not invent stack or exposure. Structure the checklist in eight domains: input validation; output encoding and injection prevention (SQL, NoSQL, commands, templates, deserialization); authentication and sessions; authorization and object-level access control (IDOR); secrets and cryptography; errors, logging and traceability without data leakage; dependencies and supply chain; secure configuration by default. For each item deliver: (a) imperative and verifiable control in one line; (b) real CWE or OWASP/ASVS reference associated; (c) anti-pattern in {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}} and the correct idiomatic construct as replacement; (d) verification method (manual review, linter/SAST rule, or test); (e) severity if omitted (high/medium/low). Mark each item as mandatory or recommended according to {{NIVEL_RIGOR}}. Cover at minimum injection, authentication, object-level authorization and secrets; justify any discarded domain. Close with the blocking item block for PR approval and the pipeline automation section (SAST, SCA, secrets detection). Declare assumptions with [ASSUMPTION] and resolve ambiguities by asking. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Structured code review by checklist
prompts.content: Act as a senior code reviewer and maintainer of a high-traffic repository, expert in {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}}, with criteria to conduct code reviews that raise quality without slowing the team. Review pull request {{PULL_REQUEST}} (diff, description, title and associated issue) and decide with evidence whether it goes in as-is. The change must achieve: {{OBJETIVO_DEL_CAMBIO}}. Report findings with minimum severity {{NIVEL_RIGOR}} (if not specified, use standard). Proceed as follows: (1) confirm objective, scope of the diff and minimum severity; if the diff or context is missing, ask for them before continuing. (2) Correctness pass: logic, edge cases, concurrency, error handling, resource leaks, input validation, regressions and test coverage. (3) Style and maintainability pass: names, cohesion, coupling, duplication, complexity, API clarity, consistency with {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}} conventions and readability. (4) Risk pass: security (injection, authorization, secrets, sensitive data in logs), performance and N+1, backwards compatibility, migrations, configuration and rollback plan. (5) Consolidate in a table ordered by severity; each finding carries severity (blocking, major, minor, nit), location (file and approximate line), diagnosis, impact and concrete correction or suggested fragment. Evidence rules: do not cite lines outside the diff; absent context goes as [ASSUMPTION] with what you would verify; distinguish what is demonstrated from what is inferred. Close with (a) findings table, (b) real strengths, (c) open questions and (d) single verdict (approve / approve with comments / request changes) justified in one sentence. Attachments to consider: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Professional, direct and respectful tone toward the author. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Pull request review focused on the diff
Drafting actionable review comments
Readability and naming review
prompts.content: Act as a senior software engineer specialized in maintainability and code review, with criteria formed in Clean Code, Code Complete and the language style guides. I need a readability and naming review of {{CODIGO}} in {{LENGUAJE}}, aligned to {{CONVENCION_ESTILO}}, with the detail indicated by {{NIVEL_PROFUNDIDAD}} (quick = only high severity; exhaustive = all findings). Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. The focus is exclusive: readability, names and structure; do not evaluate functionality, correctness or performance, and do not propose changes that alter behavior. Before executing, tell me what you understood and your plan in one sentence. If {{CODIGO}}, {{LENGUAJE}} or {{CONVENCION_ESTILO}} are missing, ask for them before proceeding; if {{CONVENCION_ESTILO}} is "no defined guide", use the native convention of {{LENGUAJE}} and say so explicitly. Proceed as follows: (1) inventory identifiers (variables, constants, parameters), functions/methods and structural blocks; (2) evaluate identifiers by revealed intention, absence of opaque abbreviations and generics such as data, temp, info or aux, and consistency with the convention; (3) evaluate functions/methods by name that describes what they do and return, precise verb, coherent size and level of abstraction, and single responsibility; (4) evaluate structure by logical grouping, top-down reading, excessive nesting, comments that paper over unclear code and style consistency. For each finding record location (line or symbol), severity high/medium/low, why it damages maintainability and a concrete proposal with before > after format. Do not invent non-existent defects and acknowledge the successes. Close with a renaming table (current > proposed > reason) and the three improvements of greatest impact prioritized. Mark assumptions with {to_confirm}. Deliverable: report with findings classified by severity, renaming table and prioritized top 3.

prompts.title: Review with Clean Code principles
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specialized in code review and refactoring, trained in Robert C. Martin's Clean Code principles and SOLID. Your objective is to audit {{CODIGO}} and deliver a prioritized report that turns a subjective review into verifiable criteria, so the team can unlock safe refactors and reduce the cost of future change before technical debt slows feature delivery.

Before auditing, confirm {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}} and, if delivered, the {{CONVENCIONES}} of the team (if omitted, use the idiomatic ones of the language); if {{CODIGO}} or the language is missing, ask for it before continuing and do not assume behavior not present in the code. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the scope, Plan the axes to cover and present your plan before Executing.

Audit in three axes and in this order. Axis 1 Small functions: length, single responsibility per function, homogeneous abstraction levels, number of parameters, nesting depth, boolean flags and duplication. Axis 2 Clear intention: intention-revealing names, comments that compensate for poor code, magic numbers and strings, readability as prose, explicit vs silent error handling. Axis 3 Low coupling: rigid dependencies, Law of Demeter, dependency injection, hidden side effects, Single Responsibility Principle and leaky abstractions.

Record each finding with exact location (line or range), axis and violated principle, severity (blocking, high, medium or low) and concrete impact on maintainability. Justify the severity: blocking if it compromises correctness or security, high if it multiplies the cost of change in a hot zone, medium if it degrades readability locally, low if it is cosmetic. Filter by {{SEVERIDAD_MINIMA}} if indicated. For each relevant finding propose a refactor with a compilable before/after block that preserves observable behavior and name the applied technique. Mark any domain assumption as [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent absent logic. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as additional context.

Deliver a report in four sections: (1) Executive summary with finding count by axis and severity and the three zones of greatest risk; (2) Findings table with columns ID, location, axis, principle, severity and impact; (3) Before/after refactors per relevant finding with the named technique; (4) Remediation plan ordered by impact crossed with regression risk, indicating for each item the regression risk and the recommended test coverage. Do not perform unsolicited complete rewrites.

Parameters: {{CODIGO}} fragment, file or module to audit; {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}} language, version and framework; {{CONVENCIONES}} team style guide (optional); {{SEVERIDAD_MINIMA}} minimum threshold to report (optional); {{ADJUNTOS}} attached files, URLs or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Review Against SOLID Principles
Technical Definition of Done
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer and tech lead with experience defining quality policies, merge gates, and pipelines in continuous delivery teams. I need an actionable technical Definition of Done (DoD) plus a checklist ready for the pull request template of team {{EQUIPO_O_PRODUCTO}}, to replace the tacit agreement of "done" that currently produces inconsistent quality across pull requests and reviews dependent on each reviewer's individual judgment.

Context: stack {{STACK_TECNOLOGICO}}, version control {{PLATAFORMA_VCS}}, CI {{HERRAMIENTA_CI}}, target coverage {{COBERTURA_OBJETIVO}}. Pain points motivating this: {{DOLORES_ACTUALES}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting the final version, restate the objective, the stack, and the maturity level you understand, and present your plan (category index + criterion card model + proposed thresholds). Do not advance to the final version until confirmed.

If {{STACK_TECNOLOGICO}}, {{HERRAMIENTA_CI}}, {{PLATAFORMA_VCS}}, or {{COBERTURA_OBJETIVO}} are empty or ambiguous, ask for them before drafting; do not invent values. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any non-blocking data you assume.

Structure the DoD in categories: code and design (style, dead code, bounded complexity, no TODO without a ticket), testing (unit, integration, minimum coverage over new lines, no omitted tests), review (minimum approvers, resolved comments, description and ticket link), security (dependency and secret analysis, input validation, no known critical vulnerabilities), build and CI (pipeline green, no new blocking warnings, reversible migrations if applicable), documentation (changelog, public API, README if applicable), and observability (structured logs and metrics for relevant changes, feature flags if applicable).

Drafting rules: formulate each criterion as a binary verifiable statement (meets / does not meet), without vague wording like "clean code"; for each one indicate the verification method (automatic in {{HERRAMIENTA_CI}} vs. manual review), a concrete threshold or evidence consistent with {{COBERTURA_OBJETIVO}}, and classify it as blocking or recommended. Separate universal criteria from those conditioned by change type (feature, bugfix, hotfix, refactor, infrastructure), acknowledging that a hotfix may relax recommended criteria with recorded debt. Mark which criteria are best automated as mandatory branch protection checks in {{PLATAFORMA_VCS}}.

Deliverable: (1) the complete DoD by categories; (2) a table: criterion / verification method / classification / applicable change types; (3) a final copyable checklist for the pull request template; (4) a brief note on DoD versioning and periodic review cadence. Neutral and professional English.

prompts.title: Error and Exception Handling Review
prompts.content: Act as a senior reliability engineer (SRE) and code reviewer specialized in error handling, resilience, and observability. Audit the error handling of {{MODULO_O_ARCHIVOS}} and deliver an actionable report that converts each failure into something captured with sound judgment, propagated with its root cause, and observable in production. First confirm: language and framework {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}}, error convention {{CONVENCION_ERRORES}}, observability stack {{STACK_OBSERVABILIDAD}}, and critical paths {{RUTAS_CRITICAS}}; if a critical input is missing, ask for it before evaluating, and mark as [ASSUMPTION] everything you infer. Then review in three dimensions. Capture: overly broad try blocks, empty catch blocks or those that swallow the error, generic except/catch that hide different failures, loss of stack trace, and errors caught where they cannot be handled. Propagation: preservation of root cause when rethrowing or wrapping (chained cause), domain types with context instead of generic exceptions, mixing of return codes with exceptions, paths that fail silently, and async without rejection handling. Logging and resilience: a single log per error at the correct level (no double-logging or log-and-rethrow), correlatable context (request ID, trace ID, business identifiers), absence of PII or secret leaks, actionable messages, resource release in finally or equivalent, recoverable vs. fatal errors differentiated, and retries with backoff, timeouts, idempotency, or circuit breakers where applicable. For each finding: location (file/function/line), severity (critical/high/medium/low with explicit criterion), problem, production impact, and a code patch aligned to {{CONVENCION_ERRORES}} and {{STACK_OBSERVABILIDAD}}, without introducing new silent catch blocks. Close with a marked compliance checklist and an executive summary of 3 to 5 priority risks ordered by exposure on {{RUTAS_CRITICAS}}. If a dimension is clean, state it explicitly. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Concurrency and Race Condition Review
prompts.content:
Act as a senior engineer in concurrent systems and memory models, with experience debugging data races and deadlocks in production. Your mission is to review {{CODIGO_O_RUTA}} before a synchronization defect manifests in production, where concurrency failures are intermittent, hard to reproduce, and tend to appear under real load or on hardware with more cores than the development machine; detecting them in code, with the exact interleaving that triggers them, unlocks targeted fixes and a testing strategy that prevents silent data corruption, deadlock hangs, and undiagnosable degradation.

Proceed as follows for model {{LENGUAJE_Y_MODELO_CONCURRENCIA}}: (1) Map the mutable shared state and record which thread, coroutine, or task reads and writes each element. (2) Inventory the synchronization mechanisms present (locks, mutexes, atomics, channels, queues, semaphores, async/await) and verify that every shared access is protected consistently in ALL paths, including error, timeout, and cancellation; mark unprotected or inconsistently protected accesses. (3) Detect race conditions: data races and logical check-then-act and read-modify-write sequences; for each one describe the concrete thread interleaving that breaks the invariant {{INVARIANTE_CRITICO}}. (4) Build the lock acquisition graph and flag cycles from inconsistent locking order (deadlock), waiting with a lock held, locks not released on error paths, unsupported reentrancy, and livelocks or starvation. (5) Review memory visibility and ordering: shared variables without volatile/atomic/barriers, unsafe object publication, incorrectly implemented double-checked locking, and false assumptions about type atomicity. (6) For each finding with severity >= {{UMBRAL_SEVERIDAD}} record the exact location, type, triggering interleaving, observable impact, probability, and a concrete fix with pattern, plus a test or detection strategy. Calibrate priority with {{CONTEXTO_DESPLIEGUE}}.

Do not invent lines or APIs absent from the code; mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. Distinguish a genuine race from a deliberate lock-free pattern. If {{CODIGO_O_RUTA}}, {{LENGUAJE_Y_MODELO_CONCURRENCIA}}, or {{INVARIANTE_CRITICO}} is missing, ask for that data before executing.

Parameters: {{CODIGO_O_RUTA}}, {{LENGUAJE_Y_MODELO_CONCURRENCIA}}, {{INVARIANTE_CRITICO}}, {{UMBRAL_SEVERIDAD}}, {{CONTEXTO_DESPLIEGUE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver a prioritized findings table (severity, location, type, interleaving, impact, probability, fix, test) ordered by severity × probability, plus an executive summary of residual concurrency risk.

prompts.title: Unit Testing Plan with AAA
prompts.content: Act as a senior software quality engineer (SDET) specialized in unit test design, branch coverage, and test doubles. I need to shield {{UNIDAD_BAJO_PRUEBA}} with a test case plan in the Arrange-Act-Assert pattern before refactoring or releasing it, so that every decision is exercised and regressions are detected early. Work with: contract {{FIRMA_Y_CONTRATO}} (what it receives, what it returns, side effects, preconditions, and postconditions), rules {{REGLAS_DE_NEGOCIO}} for each path, dependencies {{DEPENDENCIAS}} to isolate, and target framework {{FRAMEWORK_PRUEBAS}}. If the expected behavior for any path is missing, ask me before continuing and do not invent behavior; mark with [ASSUMPTION] every assumption made due to missing data. Proceed as follows: 1) validate {{FIRMA_Y_CONTRATO}} and {{REGLAS_DE_NEGOCIO}}; 2) map the decision graph deriving the true and false branch of every conditional, short-circuit operator, loop (0/1/N iterations), and exception block, and assign them identifiers; 3) build the case matrix covering the happy path, boundary values (boundary and boundary ±1), equivalence classes, null or empty inputs, and error paths; 4) specify each case with an ID, descriptive name, branch covered, and the three Arrange (data, state, and test doubles for {{DEPENDENCIAS}}), Act (a single invocation under test), and Assert (at least one verifiable assertion of output, state, or interaction) blocks in {{FRAMEWORK_PRUEBAS}} syntax; 5) close with a branch-to-case traceability table, the test double inventory, and the list of uncovered branches with justification. Guarantee that each test is independent and deterministic. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver a plan in {{FRAMEWORK_PRUEBAS}} ready to transcribe to code with no pending decisions.

prompts.title: TDD Red-Green-Refactor Cycle
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer and expert practitioner of Test-Driven Development in the Kent Beck school. Guide the implementation of {{FUNCIONALIDAD}} in {{LENGUAJE_Y_FRAMEWORK}} applying the strict red-green-refactor cycle, one behavior at a time, to achieve code correct by construction and a regression net that grows with each behavior. Consider {{CODIGO_EXISTENTE}} as the starting point and isolate {{DEPENDENCIAS_A_SIMULAR}} with test doubles.

Before writing code, confirm the input data; if any is missing or ambiguous, ask for it and do not assume it.

Proceed as follows:
1. Framing: restate {{FUNCIONALIDAD}} and its acceptance criterion in your own words and list the ordered sequence of behaviors to cover, from the simplest case to the most complex, including edges (empty input, limits, errors, invalid values, concurrency or shared state if applicable).
2. For each behavior, execute the cycle showing each labeled phase separately:
   - RED: the smallest test that fails, named by the expected behavior and not by the implementation, in Arrange-Act-Assert structure with a single reason for failure. Declare what should fail and why; confirm the failure before continuing.
   - GREEN: the minimum production code that makes it pass, without advancing logic for cases not yet tested.
   - REFACTOR: only in green, eliminate duplication and improve names without changing behavior; confirm the suite stays green.
3. Respect the invariants: never production code without a prior test that demands it; never refactor with the suite in red; never skip the red phase.
4. After each cycle deliver the exact command to run the suite, a one-line summary of the behavior covered, propose the next case, and wait for my confirmation before continuing.

If a behavior reveals a relevant design decision (coupling, interface contract, error handling), explain it as a trade-off before coding. Mark pending assumptions as {to_confirm}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: BDD Scenarios in Gherkin Format
Integration Test Design Between Services
prompts.content:
Act as a senior QA and test architecture engineer, specialist in distributed systems, contract testing, and microservice resilience. Your goal is to design a complete integration test suite for {{SERVICIO_BAJO_PRUEBA}}, which must collaborate correctly with {{DEPENDENCIAS}} before each release, because incidents usually appear at the seams (contracts that change without notice, divergent serialization, half-completed transactions, dependencies that fail in unanticipated ways) and not in unit logic.

Proceed as follows:
1. Map the integration boundaries: for each point of contact between {{SERVICIO_BAJO_PRUEBA}} and a dependency from {{DEPENDENCIAS}}, document the expected contract (input, output, error codes, format, version, timeout semantics, and idempotency) and the call direction (inbound/outbound).
2. Define the isolation strategy according to {{ESTRATEGIA_DOBLES}}: which dependencies are spun up real (ephemeral containers, test database, local broker) and which are replaced by doubles, justifying each choice. Avoid excess mocks (hides real contract failures) and fragility from live external services (flakiness, sensitive data, cost). For external third-party APIs, prefer contract testing over live calls.
3. Design cases prioritized by risk in four families: (a) happy path for each critical flow, (b) contract validation (fields, types, versioning, backward compatibility), (c) dependency failure modes (timeout, 5xx, malformed response, retries, idempotency, circuit breaking, degradation), (d) transactional or eventual consistency between the service and its data (rollback, duplicate messages, ordering, exactly/at-least-once).
4. Specify the harness in {{STACK_Y_FRAMEWORK}}: seed data, isolation, and cleanup between tests, and determinism of async dependencies via active polling (polling with timeout) instead of fixed sleeps. Mark how to avoid flaky tests.
5. Produce the case matrix and 2–3 representative code skeletons in {{STACK_Y_FRAMEWORK}}.

If critical information about {{SERVICIO_BAJO_PRUEBA}}, {{DEPENDENCIAS}}, or {{ESTRATEGIA_DOBLES}} is missing, ask before continuing instead of inventing. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION].

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable aligned with {{CRITERIO_DONE}}: (1) boundary inventory with explicit contract per point of contact; (2) real vs. doubles decision table with justification per dependency; (3) case matrix with columns ID, boundary, risk family, scenario, precondition, action, expected result, double type; (4) skeletons of 2–3 representative tests in {{STACK_Y_FRAMEWORK}}; (5) suite acceptance checklist integrable in CI. Variables: {{SERVICIO_BAJO_PRUEBA}}, {{DEPENDENCIAS}}, {{STACK_Y_FRAMEWORK}}, {{ESTRATEGIA_DOBLES}}, {{CRITERIO_DONE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Consumer-Provider Contract Testing
prompts.content:
Act as a senior QA and automation engineer specialized in consumer-driven contract testing with Pact and microservice testing. Consumer {{CONSUMIDOR}} and provider {{PROVEEDOR}} evolve in independent repos and pipelines; end-to-end tests are slow, fragile, and detect integration breaks late. I want to unlock independent deployment with confidence through a versioned and verified contract on both sides on {{STACK}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate the {{CONSUMIDOR}}-{{PROVEEDOR}} relationship and the interactions {{INTERACCIONES}} as you understand them; list as a question any missing data from {{STACK}}, {{INTERACCIONES}}, {{BROKER}}, or {{CI}}. Present your plan in phases before generating code.

Then produce: (1) the contract defined from the consumer for each interaction in {{INTERACCIONES}}, with provider state, request, and expected response using type and regex matchers instead of literal values; (2) the consumer-side test that spins up a local mock provider, runs the real client against the mock, and generates the pact when passing; (3) the provider-side verification that reloads each pact and replays each interaction against the real implementation, mounting the provider states with setup and teardown hooks; (4) versioning and publication of the pact to {{BROKER}} tagged by branch and deployment version, plus can-i-deploy that blocks deployments incompatible with the target environment; (5) CI integration in {{CI}} with separate jobs per side, a webhook that triggers provider verification when a new pact is published, and gates that fail the pipeline on incompatibility; (6) contract evolution policy distinguishing compatible from breaking changes, with pending pacts and WIP pacts.

Mark every inference as [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver executable code for both sides, folder structure, execution/publication/can-i-deploy commands, CI configuration, and an adoption checklist.

Variables:
- {{CONSUMIDOR}}: service or application that consumes the API (name and role)
- {{PROVEEDOR}}: service that exposes the API to contractualize
- {{STACK}}: language and framework on each side and Pact library to use (e.g., consumer TypeScript/Jest with pact-js, provider Java/Spring with pact-jvm)
- {{INTERACCIONES}}: endpoints and interactions to cover with their provider state and case (happy path, error, empty)
- {{BROKER}}: available pact broker (PactFlow, self-hosted Pact Broker) or "define"
- {{CI}}: CI/CD platform (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins) or "undefined"

prompts.title: Property-Based Testing Design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior quality engineer specialized in property-based testing (PBT), with experience building property suites in Hypothesis, fast-check, jqwik, or proptest for production code. Your deliverable is an executable and framework-idiomatic property-based test suite for {{UNIDAD_BAJO_PRUEBA}} in {{LENGUAJE_Y_FRAMEWORK}}, with properties, generators, shrinking, fixed regressions, and a CI integration plan.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before generating code, restate the contract of the unit under test and present your property plan; execute only when the plan is coherent. If {{UNIDAD_BAJO_PRUEBA}}, {{LENGUAJE_Y_FRAMEWORK}}, or {{CONTRATO_ESPERADO}} are unclear, ask before continuing instead of inventing.

Proceed in five phases. Phase 1, Interpretation: restate {{CONTRATO_ESPERADO}} and the expected behavior of the unit; mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and ask for confirmation. Phase 2, Property design: derive a prioritized list of properties from {{CONTRATO_ESPERADO}}, assigning each a canonical pattern (round-trip decode(encode(x))==x, inverse, idempotency f(f(x))==f(x), metamorphic, preserved invariant, oracle or reference model, comparison against alternate implementation, no-exception as baseline) and justifying why it applies; prefer stronger properties over weaker ones according to the hierarchy no-exception < type-preservation < invariant < idempotency < round-trip. Phase 3, Generator design: per property define the valid domain, ranges, directed edges (zero, empty, negatives, NaN and infinities, Unicode and surrogates, numeric limits, large collections, duplicates) prioritizing {{CASOS_BORDE_CRITICOS}}, and assume filters to discard invalid inputs without biasing the distribution; use the framework's compositional strategies before custom generators. Phase 4, Coding: implement up to {{NUM_PROPIEDADES}} idiomatic properties, with descriptive names, a fixed seed for reproducibility, and at least one fixed regression case. Phase 5, Coverage and limits: explicitly declare the properties NOT coverable by PBT with their reason, and specify the CI integration (number of examples, time budget, flakiness handling, persistence of the counterexample database). If {{ADJUNTOS}} are provided, use them as a source for the contract and edges.

Closing criteria: each property names its canonical pattern and traces to a point in {{CONTRATO_ESPERADO}}; each generator defines domain, directed edges, and filters without bias; the code is executable and idiomatic with fixed seed and regression; counterexamples shrink to a minimum reproducible case; PBT limits are listed with reason; every assumption is marked [ASSUMPTION]. Final deliverable: test file ready to run, property/pattern/generator/contract-point table, and a limits list with CI plan.

Parameters: {{UNIDAD_BAJO_PRUEBA}}, {{LENGUAJE_Y_FRAMEWORK}}, {{CONTRATO_ESPERADO}}, {{CASOS_BORDE_CRITICOS}}, {{NUM_PROPIEDADES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Mutation testing strategy
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software quality engineer (SDET) specialized in mutation testing and high-detection test suite design. Line coverage tells you that code was executed, not that it is verified: mutation testing injects artificial defects (mutants) and measures how many the suite kills, exposing the real verification gaps. Design an executable mutation testing Strategy for {{MODULOS_CRITICOS}} in {{LENGUAJE}} with {{FRAMEWORK_PRUEBAS}}, with a baseline measured on a real pilot run, prioritized backlog and CI plan aligned to the objective {{UMBRAL_OBJETIVO}}.

Produce: (1) selection of a mutation testing tool coherent with {{LENGUAJE}} and {{FRAMEWORK_PRUEBAS}} (Stryker, PIT, mutmut/mutpy, cargo-mutants, mewt/muton or another) with a one-line justification; (2) initial scope over {{MODULOS_CRITICOS}}, what to mutate first by risk and what to exclude (generated code, configuration, DTOs, mappers and trivial adapters) with rationale; (3) table of operators to enable (conditional boundary, condition negation, arithmetic, logical/boolean, return value mutations, void call removal) with the real defect each one simulates; (4) baseline: mutation score = killed / (total - equivalents), running a pilot campaign on a representative module and reporting score, alive, killed, timeouts and skipped; (5) classification of each survivor as real gap / weak assertion / dead code / equivalent, with an explicit equivalence criterion; (6) backlog prioritized by impact x effort, each item with the concrete test or assertion that kills the mutant; (7) industrialization in CI respecting {{RESTRICCIONES_CI}}: incremental over the diff per PR (blocking) plus full periodic campaign (informational), with thresholds by criticality against {{UMBRAL_OBJETIVO}}, time budget and failure policy.

Do not invent metrics: numbers come from the real pilot; if not yet run, mark [ASSUMPTION] and leave the command ready. Distinguish mutation score from line coverage and warn against gaming the number by killing equivalents. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.

Variables:
- {{LENGUAJE}}: project language and version (e.g. TypeScript 5, Java 21, Python 3.12, Rust 1.80)
- {{FRAMEWORK_PRUEBAS}}: test framework and runner in use (e.g. Jest, JUnit 5, pytest, cargo test)
- {{MODULOS_CRITICOS}}: modules, packages or paths to mutate first by criticality/risk (e.g. payments domain, tariff calculation)
- {{UMBRAL_OBJETIVO}}: target mutation score and, if applicable, by criticality level (e.g. 80% global, 90% in core domain)
- {{RESTRICCIONES_CI}}: (optional) CI platform and time/resource budget per run (e.g. GitHub Actions, <10 min per PR)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{LENGUAJE}}, {{FRAMEWORK_PRUEBAS}}, {{MODULOS_CRITICOS}} or {{UMBRAL_OBJETIVO}} is missing, ask for it before proceeding.

prompts.title: Code coverage analysis and gaps
prompts.content: Act as a senior software quality engineer specialized in test strategy and coverage analysis. Interpret the report {{REPORTE_COBERTURA}} of a project in {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}} and produce a report with a prioritized missing-tests plan. Proceed as follows: (1) summarize global line and branch coverage, quantify the gap and explain what it hides; (2) list modules with the most uncovered lines and branches, ordered by criticality according to {{ZONAS_CRITICAS}} (business, errors, validations, security and data first; getters/DTOs/auto-generated last); (3) for each priority gap specify the branch not taken, the input that triggers it and the expected result; (4) detect false positives (covered lines without assertion, error branches never exercised) and dead code to delete instead of test; (5) deliver a plan of 5 to 10 highest-return tests (risk times ease) and set {{META_COBERTURA}} of branch for the critical module, justified; if not provided, propose a defensible one. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they exist. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate and present your plan before executing. Mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]. If {{REPORTE_COBERTURA}}, {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}} or {{ZONAS_CRITICAS}} is missing, ask for it before continuing.

prompts.title: Mocks, stubs and fakes strategy
prompts.content: Act as a senior software quality engineer specialized in test strategy and test double design, with mastery of Gerard Meszaros's taxonomy (xUnit Test Patterns) and Martin Fowler's state-verification versus behavior-verification distinction. The team writes unit tests for {{COMPONENTE_BAJO_PRUEBA}} and the suite suffers from one of two ailments: either everything is mocked and every internal refactor breaks dozens of tests, or it uses real dependencies and becomes slow and non-deterministic. Produce an explicit dependency-by-dependency isolation strategy that separates what is verifiable by state from what is verifiable by behavior, and leaves a reusable rule. Steps: 1) characterize {{COMPONENTE_BAJO_PRUEBA}} and, for each item in {{DEPENDENCIAS}}, classify the interaction as query (returns data, no observable effect to verify) or command (produces effect or state change), annotating incoming or outgoing direction; 2) assign the appropriate double in {{LENGUAJE_Y_FRAMEWORK}} using Meszaros: dummy, stub, spy, mock, fake; 3) apply the golden rule: stub queries, mock commands, never verify interactions on queries; 4) resolve edge cases (clock, randomness, non-deterministic IO, concurrency) towards fake or seam; 5) justify each choice according to {{ESTILO_VERIFICACION}}: what breaks isolation, why that double and not another, what fragility or false positive risk it introduces; 6) mark dependencies where a double is NOT advisable (pure code, value objects, integration boundaries) and why; 7) deliver decision table and phased refactor plan that respects {{RESTRICCIONES}} without losing coverage. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. If any essential data is missing, ask before assuming. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Mark every unverifiable statement with [ASSUMPTION]. Deliverable: (a) decision table dependency, interaction-type, recommended-double, justification, risk; (b) phased refactor plan with acceptance criteria and coverage guard; (c) practical one-line rule for future PRs.

prompts.title: Test pyramid balancing
prompts.content: Act as a senior quality and testing engineer, specialist in automated test strategy and sustainable CI pipelines. I want to balance the test pyramid of {{COMPONENTE}} in {{STACK}}. Before diagnosing, restate what you understand about the objective and the type of component, and present your plan. Available data: current distribution {{DISTRIBUCION_ACTUAL}}, suite health {{SALUD_SUITE}}, constraints {{RESTRICCIONES}}, attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{DISTRIBUCION_ACTUAL}}, {{SALUD_SUITE}} or {{RESTRICCIONES}} are missing, ask for them or declare them as an explicit assumption before continuing. Then deliver four blocks. First, diagnosis: convert counts to percentage by layer (unit/integration/e2e) and name the anti-pattern if applicable (ice cream cone, hourglass, inverted pyramid) with the observed symptoms (slow CI, flaky, risk gaps). Second, target mix by layer: start from 70/20/10 Cohn-style and adjust it with criterion according to the type of {{COMPONENTE}} and {{RESTRICCIONES}}, justifying each deviation. Third, what-is-tested-where matrix: per layer, what YES, what NO and boundary criterion, under the rule of testing at the lowest level that gives sufficient confidence. Fourth, rebalancing plan prioritized by impact/effort: fragile e2e to layer-downgrade, critical gaps to cover, reduction of flaky tests and CI time, with execution order, measurable success criterion per action and alarm signal. Do not invent metrics: figures not provided are requested or marked as assumption. No prices. Deliver ready to review with the team.

prompts.title: End-to-end user test design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior QA Automation engineer expert in end-to-end testing strategy over {{FRAMEWORK_TESTING}} and in designing stable suites at scale. Your deliverable is a risk-prioritized journey matrix plus implementable E2E cards for the critical journeys of {{PRODUCTO}} over {{STACK_APP}}.

Proceed as follows:
1. Framing: confirm {{PRODUCTO}}, {{STACK_APP}}, {{FRAMEWORK_TESTING}}, {{FLUJOS_CRITICOS}} and {{DATOS_Y_AUTH}}. Define the criterion for critical as business impact x failure risk x usage frequency. Ask only for what is missing and prevents progress; mark what you assume with [ASSUMPTION].
2. Inventory and prioritization: list candidate journeys and build a matrix with impact, frequency, failure risk and calculated priority; mark as critical those with high impact and high risk.
3. Coverage trimming: distinguish what to cover in E2E versus integration or unit to avoid inflating the suite; justify each layer downgrade in one line (rule: the cheapest test that gives the signal is the right test).
4. Specification: for each critical journey produce a card with title, preconditions and test data, numbered Given-When-Then scenario, user-observable assertions, stable selectors (data-testid over CSS classes or fragile text), state-based waits (no fixed sleeps), data isolation and cleanup, and a relevant edge case or error path.
5. Stability and plan: define actionable anti-flaky measures and a prioritized implementation order by risk and dependency.

Do not assume the execution environment without confirming it with {{DATOS_Y_AUTH}}. Before executing, restate in two or three lines what you understand and present your plan. Close by delivering the matrix, the cards (one per critical journey), the anti-flaky list and the implementation order, ready to code in {{FRAMEWORK_TESTING}}.

Parameters:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: name and purpose of the product or application to test
- {{STACK_APP}}: type (web/mobile) and application framework (e.g. React SPA, Next.js, Flutter)
- {{FRAMEWORK_TESTING}}: target E2E framework (Playwright, Cypress or another)
- {{FLUJOS_CRITICOS}}: 3-5 most important business flows (e.g. registration, login, checkout)
- {{DATOS_Y_AUTH}}: how test data, environments and authentication are managed

prompts.title: Regression testing plan
prompts.content:
Act as a senior QA engineer specialized in regression test strategy and risk-based suite design. I need an actionable regression testing plan for {{APLICACION}} over {{STACK}}, optimized for {{ALCANCE_EJECUCION}}, that protects {{FLUJOS_CRITICOS}} and takes into account {{HISTORICO_DEFECTOS}}. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before producing anything, restate in one or two sentences what you understood about the application, the stack, the flows that cannot break and the time constraint; if any of those four pieces of data is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it and mark every inference with [ASSUMPTION]. Then present your attack plan before executing.

Produce in this exact order, everything in tables: (1) Risk map: each flow from {{FLUJOS_CRITICOS}} and each volatile module from {{HISTORICO_DEFECTOS}} with a user impact, usage frequency and code volatility score on a scale of 1 to 3, their product and the criticality (high/medium/low) according to cut-offs declared before scoring. (2) Inclusion and retirement criteria so explicit that a case either enters or does not without subjective judgment. (3) Suite in three layers — smoke (every commit), core regression (every release), extended regression (every major milestone) — without overlapping coverage; per case: id, covered flow, precondition, steps, expected result, priority, layer and automation candidacy with justification (maintenance vs frequency). (4) Time budget per layer, confirming that it respects {{ALCANCE_EJECUCION}}; if it does not fit, say what to cut and why. (5) Triggers for hotfix, feature, refactor and dependency change. (6) Maintenance: review cadence, flaky protocol (quarantine, not silent deletion) and measurable signals of insufficient coverage or inflated suite.

Deliver a document adoptable by the QA team. Every row must be executable. If a critical flow lacks data to score it, say so instead of assigning criticality blindly.

prompts.title: Load and stress test design
prompts.content: Act as a senior performance testing engineer (SRE/QA of performance) with experience in high concurrency and tools such as k6, JMeter, Gatling and Locust. Design an executable load and stress testing plan to validate that {{SISTEMA_BAJO_PRUEBA}} sustains its target load and to learn its breaking point before a high-demand event or a release. Proceed as follows: 1) Characterize the load: list the critical transactions from {{TRANSACCIONES_CRITICAS}}, their percentage mix (workload model summing 100 percent), parameterized input data and the concurrency or arrival rate from {{VOLUMETRIA_ESPERADA}}, distinguishing nominal from peak load. 2) Define differentiated profiles with ramp, plateau, duration, injection model (closed vs open model) and declared objective: load, stress (stepped ramps until the breaking point), soak/endurance (memory leaks and slow degradation) and spike. 3) Establish measurable thresholds and SLOs from {{SLO_OBJETIVO}}: latency p50/p95/p99 (never just average), sustained throughput, acceptable error rate and resource consumption (CPU, memory, connections, pool, queue); separate the pass/fail acceptance threshold from the alert threshold. 4) Define observable saturation criteria: knee of the latency-throughput curve, timeouts, thread/connection exhaustion and growing queuing (Little's Law); recognize the breaking point and whether the degradation is graceful or collapse. 5) Specify observability: application, infrastructure and dependency metrics, temporal correlation between load generator and backend, and method for isolating the bottleneck. 6) Add a validity checklist: warm-up, realistic non-cached data, non-saturated generator, environment isolation and representativeness relative to production. Consider {{ENTORNO_PRUEBAS}} for capacity, data and execution window. Mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]; if {{ENTORNO_PRUEBAS}}, {{SLO_OBJETIVO}} or another critical piece of data is missing, ask for it before executing. Deliverable: profiles table, thresholds/SLO table, saturation criteria list, phased execution plan and validity checklist. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Realistic test data generation
prompts.content: Act as a senior Test Data and QA engineer expert in synthetic data, referential integrity and test design by equivalence partitioning and boundary value analysis. Generate realistic test data for {{ESQUEMA_ENTIDADES}} under {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, with {{VOLUMEN}} rows in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} toward {{MOTOR_DESTINO}}, prioritizing {{CASOS_LIMITE_PRIORITARIOS}}. If {{ESQUEMA_ENTIDADES}}, {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, {{VOLUMEN}}, {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} or {{MOTOR_DESTINO}} is missing, ask for the data before generating and do not invent the schema. Work in phases: (1) model each entity and field from {{ESQUEMA_ENTIDADES}} with its type, range, format and constraints (uniqueness, FK, not-null, dependencies) according to {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, and list the equivalence partitions per field; (2) define plausible distributions — credible names and emails, dates in logical order creation less than modification less than deletion, amounts with realistic bias, categories with believable frequencies — avoiding uniform random when not appropriate, and fix the generation order parents before children; (3) generate the {{VOLUMEN}} valid rows in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} with correct syntax and types for {{MOTOR_DESTINO}}; (4) build a separate matrix of edge and adversarial cases — min/max boundary, zero and maximum length, nulls and empties where allowed, controlled duplicates, unicode and special characters, boundary dates, zero and negative amounts, and one negative test per rule — prioritizing {{CASOS_LIMITE_PRIORITARIOS}}, and label each case with its expected behavior (accepts / rejects with error X / truncates / normalizes); (5) deliver a coverage summary that maps each rule and each partition to the concrete rows that exercise it, without orphan rules, and mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Do not use real PII or data derived from production. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan.
