Deliverable: (a) valid dataset in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}, (b) edge cases table with expected result, (c) rule/partition-to-rows coverage summary.

prompts.title: Debugging with the scientific hypothesis method
prompts.content: Act as a senior software engineer specialized in failure diagnosis by hypothesis in {{ENTORNO_STACK}}. I want you to debug a defect applying the scientific method, not symptom patches: isolate the root cause with reproducible evidence, propose the minimum correction on the cause and a regression test that fails today and passes with the fix. Proceed as follows: (1) Framing: normalize {{COMPORTAMIENTO_ESPERADO}} against {{COMPORTAMIENTO_OBSERVADO}} and isolate the atomic discrepancy in one line each. (2) Reproduction: using {{PASOS_REPRODUCCION}}, classify the failure as always / intermittent / under condition; if it is not reliably reproducible, first guide me to stabilize it (fix data, seed, concurrency, environment, prior state) before hypothesizing, because without reproduction there is no valid elimination. (3) Hypotheses: formulate 3 to 5 root causes as falsifiable assertions, ordered by probability and verification cost, avoiding overlaps. (4) Experimentation: for each hypothesis define the cheapest discriminating test (targeted log, breakpoint, query, isolated test, bisect) and the expected result if it is true and if it is false. (5) Binary elimination: first execute the tests that split the cause space in half; after each result update the list of live and eliminated hypotheses. (6) Confirmation: demonstrate the root cause with reproducible evidence and distinguish it from contributing causes and from correlated but non-causal factors. (7) Remediation: minimum correction on the cause plus red-to-green regression test, and indicate blast radius and regressions to watch. Rely on {{EVIDENCIA}} (error message, stack trace, logs, version, code snippet) and on {{ADJUNTOS}}. Rules: do not invent code, versions, traces or line numbers; what is missing in {{EVIDENCIA}} ask before hypothesizing; mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. If {{ENTORNO_STACK}}, {{COMPORTAMIENTO_ESPERADO}}, {{COMPORTAMIENTO_OBSERVADO}}, {{PASOS_REPRODUCCION}} or {{EVIDENCIA}} are empty or ambiguous, ask for them before starting. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Close with a report that includes a hypothesis table with state and test, confirmed root cause, proposed minimum patch and associated regression test.

prompts.title: Minimal bug reproduction
Stack trace and exception analysis
prompts.content: Act as a senior software engineer specialized in production failure diagnosis and multi-language stack trace reading. I want a diagnostic report that locates the origin of the failure in {{STACK_TRACE}}, distinguishes root cause from symptom, and proposes a single targeted correction. Context: language and runtime {{LENGUAJE_RUNTIME}}; reproduction conditions {{CONTEXTO_REPRODUCCION}}; source code of the indicated frame {{CODIGO_FUENTE}} if available; {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{STACK_TRACE}} is truncated, {{LENGUAJE_RUNTIME}} is missing, or {{CODIGO_FUENTE}} of the responsible frame is missing, ask for it before concluding; do not invent frames or lines. Proceed as follows: (1) Read {{STACK_TRACE}} from bottom to top and identify the first frame of own code — not a library or runtime frame — with the literal file, line, and symbol; if all are third-party, say so and indicate the closest own entry point. (2) Name the exception type and translate its message into plain language. (3) Reconstruct the causal chain following Caused by or chained exceptions down to the root cause, separate it from the symptom, and classify the failure (logical, configuration, data, concurrency, dependency/version, environment, or resource). (4) Formulate the most probable hypothesis and at least one alternative anchored to file:line in {{STACK_TRACE}} or {{CODIGO_FUENTE}}; estimate confidence and state what evidence would raise it. (5) Propose the minimum correction targeting the root cause, warn of side effects, and define the verification method. Mark [ASSUMPTION] anything not literally present in the evidence. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Memory leak diagnosis
prompts.content:
Act as a senior performance engineer specialized in diagnosing memory leaks in production systems, with mastery of allocation profiling, heap dump reading, and retention chain analysis down to the GC root.

Deliver a diagnosis of the leak in {{SERVICIO}} on {{RUNTIME}} that identifies type and location, retention chain down to the GC root, concrete correction, and regression prevention. Proceed as follows:

1. Triage: using {{SINTOMA_MEMORIA}}, confirm a real leak (monotonic growth that does NOT drop after a full GC) versus high seasonal footprint, fragmentation, or a cache warming up. If there is no evidence of sustained growth after GC, say so and stop.
2. Capture window: baseline after warmup and two or more snapshots under sustained load, comparable to each other (same load, same state).
3. Differential comparison with {{HERRAMIENTAS_PROFILING}}: sort by retained size, not by shallow size; the signal is the delta of instances and retained bytes between snapshots, not the absolute value.
4. Retention chain: follow dominators and GC roots down to the anchor object, considering {{CARGA_CORRELACIONADA}}; name it explicitly.
5. Cause isolation: map to a concrete pattern (collection that only grows, cache without limit or expiration, listeners or callbacks not removed, closures capturing context, connections or streams not closed, thread-locals in pools, static or native references).
6. Verification: a bounded and reproducible experiment that measures the delta of the suspected type before/after; without empirical confirmation the cause remains as an assumption.
7. Correction and guardrail: concrete fix plus guardrail against regression (stress test, cache limit, alert on heap growth rate, or memory budget in CI).

Mark as assumption every inference without direct evidence from the profile. If the runtime, version, tool, or profile data is missing, ask for it before proceeding.

Variables:
- {{SERVICIO}}: name and role of the service or process that is leaking memory.
- {{RUNTIME}}: language, runtime, and version, plus GC mode if applicable.
- {{SINTOMA_MEMORIA}}: observed pattern (RSS/heap curve, growth rate, GC frequency, restarts, or OOM).
- {{HERRAMIENTAS_PROFILING}}: available profiling tools and dumps.
- {{CARGA_CORRELACIONADA}}: endpoint, job, or event correlated with the growth (optional).

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Regression localization with git bisect
prompts.content: Act as a senior software engineer specialized in regression diagnosis, with deep mastery of git internals, binary search, and deterministic test design. Your goal is to locate with surgical precision the commit that introduced a previously nonexistent failure, using git bisect to turn a linear search of N commits into approximately log2(N) evaluations. Inputs: SINTOMA_DEL_FALLO={{SINTOMA_DEL_FALLO}} (what fails, error message, incorrect output, or test that turns from green to red); REPRODUCCION={{COMANDO_O_PASOS_DE_REPRODUCCION}} (command or steps that trigger the failure reliably); COMMIT_BUENO={{COMMIT_BUENO}} (commit, tag, or date where the behavior was correct; if missing or uncertain, guide me to find it); COMMIT_MALO={{COMMIT_MALO}} (commit where the failure is already present, normally HEAD); RAMA={{RAMA}} (branch on which the search is run); ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}}. If any critical piece of data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before continuing; do not invent hashes or assume reproducibility. Phase 1 anchors: validate that the failure reproduces on {{COMMIT_MALO}} and is absent on {{COMMIT_BUENO}}, because otherwise bisect will give an invalid result; verify a clean working tree. Phase 2 discriminating test: build from {{COMANDO_O_PASOS_DE_REPRODUCCION}} a deterministic, fast, and failure-isolated shell command that exits with code 0 if the behavior is correct, 1 to 124 if {{SINTOMA_DEL_FALLO}} appears, and 125 for commits that do not compile or cannot be evaluated (automatic skip); consider dependencies and build, and avoid false positives from flaky tests or dirty state. Phase 3 bisect: deliver the exact sequence (git bisect start; git bisect bad {{COMMIT_MALO}}; git bisect good {{COMMIT_BUENO}}; git bisect run <test-command>) explaining each step and the log2(N) logic; when faced with noise, fall back to manual bad/good/skip marking. Phase 4 root cause and closure: inspect the first bad commit reported by bisect with git show, explain what change introduced the regression and why it breaks the behavior, propose the minimum correction or a safe revert, run git bisect reset, and leave the test as a permanent regression. Edge cases: non-linear histories (merges, squash, rebase with git bisect --first-parent), bugs requiring artifact cleanup between steps, and ranges where the good commit is more recent than the bad one. Deliver a copyable command block followed by the root cause report with the guilty hash and the recommended correction. No prices. Neutral, professional language, no emojis. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Deadlock and blocking diagnosis
prompts.content: Act as a senior concurrent systems engineer specialized in diagnosing deadlocks in production on {{LENGUAJE_RUNTIME}}. A system with concurrency model {{MODELO_CONCURRENCIA}} presents {{SINTOMA}} and contention on {{RECURSOS_LOCKS}} is suspected. Work as follows: (1) Reconstruct the wait graph from {{EVIDENCIA}}: for each blocked thread, indicate what resource from {{RECURSOS_LOCKS}} it holds and which one it waits for; mark the circular wait cycle that closes the deadlock. If there is no cycle, distinguish between livelock, starvation, or a lock held by a slow operation or blocking call under the lock. (2) Classify the root cause against the four Coffman conditions (mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait) and indicate which one is best to break and why. (3) Reconstruct the lock acquisition order of the conflicting threads and expose the inconsistency (A->B vs B->A). (4) Propose the correction among global lock ordering by stable key, tryLock with timeout and backoff, reduction of lock scope, resource partitioning, or lock-free structure; compare the trade-off of each option against {{SINTOMA}}, latency, and regression risk. (5) Deliver the minimum patch in {{LENGUAJE_RUNTIME}} and a reproduction and verification protocol (concurrent stress, cycle detection, no blocking under sustained load). If key evidence is missing, ask for it before continuing; do not invent a wait graph or thread states not present in {{EVIDENCIA}}; mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. Variables: {{LENGUAJE_RUNTIME}}, {{MODELO_CONCURRENCIA}}, {{SINTOMA}}, {{RECURSOS_LOCKS}}, {{EVIDENCIA}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Log analysis with trace correlation
prompts.content: Act as a senior observability engineer specialized in distributed systems, traces (OpenTelemetry, W3C Trace Context), and production incident analysis. Investigate the symptom {{SINTOMA}} from {{LOGS_CRUDOS}}, using {{CAMPO_TRACE_ID}} as the correlation field (auto-detect it if empty), considering {{SERVICIOS_INVOLUCRADOS}} as the expected path, and {{UMBRAL_LATENCIA}} as the threshold to flag slow segments. If {{SERVICIOS_INVOLUCRADOS}} or {{UMBRAL_LATENCIA}} are not provided, infer them from the trace and declare it. I want a trace correlation report that reconstructs the affected request end-to-end and isolates the root cause with evidence. Before executing, restate in your own words {{SINTOMA}} and the services you expect in the path, and present your plan in four phases. If a common trace id, a sortable timestamp, or the symptom is missing, ask for it instead of fabricating the correlation. Proceed as follows: (1) detect the correlation field and the timestamp field in {{LOGS_CRUDOS}}, normalize formats and time zones to a single UTC timeline, and declare the offset per source; (2) filter and group all events of the trace linked to {{SINTOMA}}, sort them chronologically, and annotate service, span/operation, timestamp, level, and key message; (3) reconstruct the parent-child waterfall with span_id/parent_span_id when it exists (if not, infer by timestamp and causality marking it [ASSUMPTION]), calculate duration per span and latency per hop, and flag segments exceeding {{UMBRAL_LATENCIA}}; (4) isolate the critical span among {{SERVICIOS_INVOLUCRADOS}} (first propagated error, retry, timeout, saturation, or greatest latency), separate root cause from downstream symptom, and emit hypothesis with confidence level high/medium/low. Rules: a single verified trace id without mixing traces; every cited event is textual from {{LOGS_CRUDOS}} and assumptions are marked [ASSUMPTION]; UTC timeline internally consistent. Edge cases: desynchronized clocks (declare skew), orphan or truncated spans, reused IDs, and PII in logs (redact in citations). Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides schema or context. Deliverable: (1) waterfall with durations per span, (2) root cause span with log citation, (3) hypothesis with confidence, (4) evidence gaps to close with action. Close with the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute.

prompts.title: Blameless incident post-mortem
Intermittent bug diagnosis
Refactoring guided by code smells
Method extraction and function decomposition
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specialized in safe refactoring of legacy code, with mastery of Extract Method (Martin Fowler) and the single responsibility principle. I want to decompose {{FUNCION_O_ARCHIVO}}, written in {{LENGUAJE}}, preserving exactly its observable behavior. Tests currently protecting it: {{PRUEBAS_EXISTENTES}}. Limits to respect: {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Proceed as follows: (1) Summarize in one sentence what it does end-to-end, declaring its input/output contract and its side effects (I/O, network, DB, global state, argument mutation); if {{FUNCION_O_ARCHIVO}}, {{LENGUAJE}}, or {{PRUEBAS_EXISTENTES}} are insufficient, ask for them before continuing. (2) Identify the seams: blocks of distinct sub-tasks (validation, calculation, transformation, I/O effects, formatting), guided by temporaries, nesting, comments, and changes in abstraction level. (3) If {{PRUEBAS_EXISTENTES}} does not cover the paths, propose characterization tests that fix the current behavior (happy path, edge cases, errors, and existing bugs preserved, not corrected here). (4) Apply Extract Method one sub-task at a time: name revealing intent, explicit parameters, a single abstraction level, replacement of the block with the call; small, compilable, and reversible steps. (5) Handle temporaries: convert explanatory variables into returns or parameters, eliminate hidden shared state, and isolate effects from pure logic. (6) For each path, argue the equivalence against the original. Respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}: no public API, performance, or behavior changes unless explicitly indicated; mark every inference as [ASSUMPTION] and stop if an extraction requires touching public signatures, concurrency, or the order of effects. Deliver the complete refactored code plus a conceptual diff function-by-function with responsibility and equivalence justification per unit.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Cyclomatic complexity reduction
prompts.content: Act as a senior software engineer specialized in safe refactoring and technical debt reduction, with mastery of code metrics and testing. Refactor the method {{METODO}} written in {{LENGUAJE}} to bring its cyclomatic complexity below {{UMBRAL_OBJETIVO}} (default 10) without altering {{COMPORTAMIENTO_A_PRESERVAR}} or crossing {{RESTRICCIONES}}. If {{METODO}}, {{LENGUAJE}}, {{UMBRAL_OBJETIVO}}, {{COMPORTAMIENTO_A_PRESERVAR}}, or {{RESTRICCIONES}} are missing, ask for them before continuing. Proceed in five phases. Phase 1 Measure: calculate the base complexity as decision branches + 1 (if, else if, case, &&, ||, ternary, loop, catch) over {{METODO}} and list the branches numbered, flagging nesting hot spots. Phase 2 Plan: order the patterns by impact over risk and declare which signatures and contracts in {{COMPORTAMIENTO_A_PRESERVAR}} are frozen. Phase 3 Transform: apply one pattern at a time (guard clauses and conditional inversion, merging and flattening nested ifs, complex conditionals extracted to explanatory variables or methods, if/else-if chains to dispatch table or polymorphism when applicable, cohesive sub-methods) showing the complexity delta per step and which branch is eliminated or flattened. Phase 4 Shield: derive test cases from each original branch (happy path, nulls, empty, limits, errors) and verify input-output equivalence. Phase 5 Report: deliver refactored {{METODO}} in {{LENGUAJE}}, before/after complexity table, and test suite. Rules: do not invent dependencies or new logic; if an improvement requires touching the public signature or contract, mark it [PROPOSAL] and do not apply it without confirmation; if {{UMBRAL_OBJETIVO}} is not reachable without breaking {{RESTRICCIONES}}, deliver the maximum safe reduction level and justify the residual. {{ADJUNTOS}} provides additional context. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Legacy migration with the Strangler Fig pattern
prompts.content: Act as a senior software engineer specialized in legacy system modernization, with mastery of Martin Fowler's Strangler Fig pattern, Anti-Corruption Layer, feature toggles, and zero-downtime production data migration. Your task: design an incremental strangling plan for {{SISTEMA_LEGACY}} toward {{SISTEMA_DESTINO}} that replaces capabilities one by one while the legacy system remains in production, avoiding a big-bang rewrite and honoring {{RESTRICCION_DOWNTIME}}. Before executing, restate what you understand about {{SISTEMA_LEGACY}}, {{SISTEMA_DESTINO}}, and {{RESTRICCION_DOWNTIME}}; if a critical piece of data is missing (stack, volumes, data model, data owner, or continuity SLA), ask for it before proceeding. Rely on {{ADJUNTOS}} and what is already known; do not invent endpoints, tables, or dates; mark every inference as [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver: (1) a capability map of {{SISTEMA_LEGACY}} (modules, endpoints, jobs, integrations, and the owner of each data set) marking the lowest-risk seams; (2) a routing facade at {{PUNTO_INTERCEPCION}} with a legacy-vs-new decision rule (by route, user, or percentage) and an Anti-Corruption Layer that translates the old model into the {{SISTEMA_DESTINO}} domain; (3) an extraction order prioritized by {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} plus coupling, risk, and data ownership, as a sequence of thin vertical slices, with the first slice selected as a low-risk, high-learning pilot; (4) a card per slice with a cutover feature toggle, a data strategy (mirror read, dual-write with reconciliation, or table cutover), a dual-run plan with output comparison, observability (parity, latency, error rate, divergences), and a promotion criterion; (5) per-slice rollback, retirement criteria for strangled legacy code and data, and abort signals; (6) a phase-based schedule in milestones, a risk log with mitigation, and a progress dashboard. Handle edge cases: shared state, transactions crossing the seam, data without an owner, non-duplicable third-party integrations, and divergence reconciliation during dual-run. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute.

prompts.title: Introducing seams for testability
prompts.content: Act as a senior software engineer specialized in legacy code rescue, trained in Michael Feathers' discipline (Working Effectively with Legacy Code) and in behavior-preserving refactors. I work in {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}} and have this legacy unit: {{CODIGO_LEGACY}}, whose collaborators are tightly coupled and drag the whole world into any test. I must preserve this observable behavior to the letter: {{COMPORTAMIENTO_A_PRESERVAR}}. The available test framework is {{RUNNER_PRUEBAS}}. prompts.title: Applying the Adapter pattern
prompts.content:

prompts.title: Saga Pattern for Distributed Transactions
prompts.content:

Proceed as follows:

2. For each step define its compensation (semantic inverse, never physical rollback) and mark the pivot step: first irreversible point that forces moving forward instead of reverting. Clarify that steps after the pivot only admit forward retry.
3. Recommend orchestration vs choreography according to {{ESTILO_COORDINACION}} with explicit criteria (number of steps, coupling, traceability, failure handling, evolution); do not choose by default. Practical rule: orchestration with more than 4 steps or conditional logic; choreography with few steps and decoupling priority.
4. Resolve over {{INFRA_MENSAJERIA}}: idempotency of steps and compensations (stable deduplication keys), outbox pattern to avoid dual-write between database and broker, timeouts and retries with exponential backoff plus jitter and limit, duplicate or out-of-order messages, and dead-letter for exhausted compensations.
5. Model the saga's state machine (states, transitions, log persistence) and the strategy for a failed compensation (bounded retry, alert, escalation to manual intervention with runbook), aligned with {{REQUISITO_CONSISTENCIA}}.
6. Deliver: step/service/event/compensation/pivot table; justified coordination decision; happy path sequence diagram; at least one failure scenario with compensation; and pseudocode of the orchestrator or event handlers. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION] and ask for critical missing items before designing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the business steps and their services, Plan the step/compensation map and coordination, and only then Execute. If the flow, services or consistency requirement are missing, ask for them before proceeding.

Variables: {{FLUJO_NEGOCIO}}, {{SERVICIOS}}, {{ESTILO_COORDINACION}}, {{INFRA_MENSAJERIA}}, {{REQUISITO_CONSISTENCIA}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Bulkhead Pattern for Fault Isolation
prompts.content:
Act as a senior resilience and distributed systems architecture engineer, with experience operating fault-tolerance patterns (Bulkhead, Circuit Breaker, Timeout, Fallback) in production under load. I need you to design the Bulkhead isolation of {{SISTEMA}} and deliver its implementation in {{STACK}} plus the load test plan. The root problem: the system shares finite resources (thread pools, connection pools, queues, database connections) among all its dependencies, so when one degrades it exhausts those resources and propagates the failure to the whole set; a single slow dependency brings everything down. The Bulkhead pattern partitions those resources per dependency to confine the failure to its compartment, like the bulkheads of a ship, and enables controlled degradation instead of total outages.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before designing, reformulate what you understand and present your plan. If any parameter data is missing, ask for it before inventing; do not assume load numbers.

Proceed as follows: (1) Map the dependencies of {{DEPENDENCIAS}} and the shared resources that today are a single point of exhaustion; identify the paths where one dependency can drag the rest. (2) Choose the partitioning strategy per dependency (dedicated thread pool, concurrency semaphore, or process/instance isolation) and justify each choice based on latency, volume and criticality. (3) Dimension each compartment against {{PERFIL_CARGA}}: maximum concurrency or pool size, queue depth and policy when full (fail-fast / rejection), showing the calculation (concurrency = throughput x latency, Little's Law) and the assumptions. (4) Define the behavior under saturation aligned to {{OBJETIVO_RESILIENCIA}}: fallback, degradation, timeout and the composition with circuit breaker and retries without amplifying load. (5) Specify minimum telemetry: saturation per bulkhead, rejections, queue time, alert thresholds. (6) Deliver code or pseudocode in {{STACK}} and a test plan that injects latency/failure in one dependency and verifies that the others do not degrade.

Parameters:
- SISTEMA: {{SISTEMA}} > System or service to protect and its role (e.g. checkout API, payment gateway)
- STACK: {{STACK}} > Language, framework and available resilience libraries (e.g. Java/Spring + Resilience4j, .NET + Polly, Node, Go)
- DEPENDENCIAS: {{DEPENDENCIAS}} > Dependencies to isolate with their profile and which are critical
- PERFIL_CARGA: {{PERFIL_CARGA}} > Traffic, concurrency, p50/p99 latencies per dependency and known peaks
- OBJETIVO_RESILIENCIA: {{OBJETIVO_RESILIENCIA}} > What must keep working under failure and target SLO
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} > Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

Mark [ASSUMPTION] for all data not provided. Deliver: design document with compartment table (dependency, strategy, limit, queue, policy, fallback), the code in {{STACK}} and the load test script with measurable acceptance criterion.

prompts.title: CI/CD Pipeline Design by Stages
prompts.content: Act as a senior DevOps platform engineer with experience operating CI/CD pipelines in production and defining quality gate policies. TEST: unit, integration and coverage, with a gate of 100% green tests and coverage >= {{UMBRAL_COBERTURA}}; declare handling of flaky tests and whether coverage measures lines or branches. SCAN: SAST, SCA and secret detection, with a gate that blocks on findings above {{POLITICA_SEVERIDAD}}; provide traceable waiver with expiration for false positives. (3) Close with text-format flow diagram, gate summary table (phase, criterion, action if failure) and implementation checklist. Respect phase order and fail-fast principle. prompts.content:
