Design the complete architecture with these steps: 1) Validate or refine {{TEMA_PILAR}} as the pillar page, confirming breadth for 6 to 12 subtopics with coherent intent for audience {{AUDIENCIA}}; if it is too broad or narrow, propose the adjustment with justification. 2) Derive cluster subtopics from the search intents that orbit the theme, grouped by intent (informational, comparative, transactional), one intent per piece, discarding overlaps that would generate cannibalization. 3) For the pillar and each cluster deliver the complete card: working title, URL slug, dominant intent, main keyword, secondary keywords, differentiating editorial angle, and recommended format. 4) Cross-reference with {{INVENTARIO_EXISTENTE}} to decide per piece: reuse, merge, redirect (with type), or create from scratch. 5) Define the internal linking: cluster to pillar and pillar to each cluster with descriptive and consistent anchor text, plus lateral links only between clusters with real thematic relationship. 6) Deliver the publication sequence prioritized by impact and effort, aligned with {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, and define authority consolidation metrics and review cadence.

If there are no keyword volume or difficulty data, prioritize by funnel logic and declare the assumption; do not invent metrics or ranking promises. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Parameters:
- {{NEGOCIO}}: business, product, or service and its core value proposition
- {{AUDIENCIA}}: target audience and their level of knowledge of the topic
- {{TEMA_PILAR}}: central candidate theme for the pillar page
- {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}: desired result (organic traffic, demand generation, brand authority, or conversion)
- {{INVENTARIO_EXISTENTE}}: relevant published content with URL/title, or "No inventory"
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Technical SEO audit with crawl and indexation checklist
prompts.content:
Act as a senior technical SEO consultant with experience auditing high-volume sites and coordinating remediations with development teams. I need a technical SEO audit of {{DOMINIO}} whose objective is {{OBJETIVO_AUDITORIA}}, on a {{TIPO_SITIO}} type site, with scope {{ALCANCE_URLS}} and access {{HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES}}. The report must convert invisible content failures (crawl blocks, contradictory indexation signals, incorrectly pointed canonicals, dirty sitemaps, JavaScript-dependent content) into prioritized and actionable findings that unlock visibility and protect crawl budget. Before executing, restate what you understand about {{DOMINIO}}, {{OBJETIVO_AUDITORIA}}, and {{ALCANCE_URLS}}, and present your plan; if a blocking data point for crawling is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it.

Audit six fronts in order: (1) Crawling: robots.txt (blocks, wildcards, sitemap directive), crawl budget, click depth, redirect chains and loops, 4xx/5xx codes, and orphan URLs. (2) Indexation: crawlable vs. indexed; meta robots and X-Robots-Tag, parameters and facets, pagination, duplicates, or thin content. (3) Canonicals: self-referential or correct; detect chains, pointing to noindex, mixed http/https, or toward redirects. (4) Sitemaps: only 200 indexable URLs, realistic lastmod, within limits, and referenced in robots.txt. (5) Rendering: raw HTML vs. rendered DOM; JavaScript-dependent content or links, blocked resources, incomplete hydration. (6) Crawl performance: Core Web Vitals and page experience only if {{HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES}} provides data.

Document each finding with description, evidence, affected pages or templates, impact, severity (critical/high/medium/low), and remediation with suggested owner. Distinguish crawlable from indexable and flag contradictions between robots.txt, meta robots, and canonical. Mark inferences without direct evidence as [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent data from unavailable tools and declare any non-auditable front as a gap. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides exports or screenshots. Close with prioritized plan in effort vs. impact matrix and the three quick wins with the highest return.

prompts.title: On-page optimization of titles, meta, and headings
prompts.content: Act as a senior SEO on-page specialist with proven experience optimizing SERP snippets and content hierarchies to maximize relevance and organic CTR. Your assignment is to deliver an optimized, ready-to-paste on-page package for a page competing for {{KEYWORD_OBJETIVO}}. Input data: target keyword {{KEYWORD_OBJETIVO}}; URL or central topic {{URL_O_TEMA}}; current content (title/meta/headings or text summary) {{CONTENIDO_ACTUAL}}; target audience {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}; secondary or long-tail keywords {{KEYWORDS_SECUNDARIAS}}; target search engine or market {{MOTOR_MERCADO}}. If any of this data is missing, ask for it before continuing. Proceed as follows: first, classify the dominant search intent of {{KEYWORD_OBJETIVO}} (informational, commercial, transactional, or navigational) and verify whether {{CONTENIDO_ACTUAL}} satisfies it; if not, mark the gap and do not force the snippet to promise something the page does not deliver. Second, rewrite the title tag with the main keyword as early as possible, 50-60 characters (target approximately 580 px), a value modifier or differentiator, and without keyword stuffing. Third, rewrite the meta description in 140-160 characters, natural keyword, concrete value proposition, and call to action aimed at {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, without clickbait. Fourth, rewrite the unique H1, aligned with the title but not identical, with keyword and benefit focus. Fifth, design the H2 and H3 hierarchy covering subtopics, {{KEYWORDS_SECUNDARIAS}}, and related frequently asked questions, with logical nesting and no level jumps. Sixth, deliver 2 alternative title variants and 2 meta description variants for A/B, each with a different angle (benefit vs. urgency vs. specificity), and list the detected content gaps. Rules: show the character count in parentheses next to each title, meta, and H1; mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent search volume metrics, difficulty, or non-provided competitor data; do not include prices. Before executing, restate in one line what you understood and present your plan. Close with a clean ready-to-paste block with title, meta description, H1, H2-H3 scheme, the 4 A/B variants, and the prioritized gap list.

prompts.title: Linkbuilding strategy with segmented outreach
prompts.content:
Act as a senior off-page SEO strategist with experience in editorial linkbuilding and high-conversion cold outreach campaigns. I want to gain domain authority and improve the organic positioning of {{URL_ACTIVO}} in {{SECTOR_TEMA}} for the query {{KEYWORD_OBJETIVO}}, through a linkbuilding strategy with segmented outreach: quality backlinks in a systematic, predictable, and measurable way, not isolated requests with a low response rate. Before executing, reformulate what you understand and present your plan. If {{URL_ACTIVO}}, {{SECTOR_TEMA}}, {{KEYWORD_OBJETIVO}}, or {{RECURSOS_ENLAZABLES}} are missing, ask me for them all at once instead of assuming.

Deliver in this order: 1) Linkability thesis: why an external site would want to link {{URL_ACTIVO}}, anchored in a real value hook derived from {{RECURSOS_ENLAZABLES}}, not an empty request. 2) Prioritized list of 12 to 15 target domains for {{SECTOR_TEMA}}, grouped into 3 segments (niche media, specialized blogs, curated resources and directories), with a transparent priority criterion that weighs thematic relevance, estimated authority, and likelihood of response; declare the weights you use. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on any unverified authority metric and do not invent real media names: use categories or placeholders to be completed. 3) A different pitch angle per segment, chosen from contextual editorial link, citable resource, broken-link replacement, unlinked mention, and guest article, aligned with {{KEYWORD_OBJETIVO}} and with its fit rationale. 4) A 3-touch outreach sequence per contact: initial email, follow-up 1 at +4 business days, and follow-up 2 at +7 business days; each touch with subject line, customizable opening hook, value proposition, and a single call to action; respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}; no spam or exaggerated promises. 5) Measurement plan with response rate, link acceptance rate, and live backlinks at 30 days, each metric with a success threshold and pivot criterion. 6) Risks and guardrails: toxic link signals to avoid, daily sending volume limit, and when to discard a target domain. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if I provided material.

Use neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. Apply EstrategIA once as the signature of the approach. Close with an actionable deliverable: strategy ready to load real domains and launch the campaign.

prompts.title: Core Web Vitals improvement plan for SEO
prompts.content:
Act as a senior technical SEO and web performance consultant, specialized in Core Web Vitals, critical render path optimization, and JavaScript budget. Your deliverable is a Core Web Vitals diagnostic report plus a prioritized remediation plan for {{URL_O_PLANTILLAS}}, ready to assign to frontend, backend, infrastructure, and content teams.

Proceed as follows:

1) Framing. Confirm {{URL_O_PLANTILLAS}}, {{PLATAFORMA}}, {{DATOS_CWV}}, and {{DISPOSITIVO}}. If any field or lab data is missing, ask before proceeding and do not invent figures: any estimate is marked [ASSUMPTION].

2) Diagnosis. Tabulate per metric the field value (p75), the lab value, and the status, with explicit thresholds: LCP <= 2.5 s, INP <= 200 ms, CLS <= 0.1. Separate {{DISPOSITIVO}} mobile from desktop and field from lab. When field and lab diverge, field determines the actual status and lab is used to diagnose the cause; flag the discrepancy. If a URL does not have sufficient field data, mark it as not evaluable in field and rely on lab data with the explicit caveat.

3) Attribution. For each out-of-threshold metric, attribute 2 to 4 concrete, observable technical causes on {{PLATAFORMA}}, not generic ones. LCP: high TTFB, render-blocking CSS/JS, unprioritized LCP resource, missing preload, image without modern format or without responsive sizing. INP: JavaScript long tasks, blocked main thread, heavy handlers, hydration cost. CLS: images or iframes without width/height, font FOIT/FOUT, content injection or banners above painted content.

4) Prioritization. Build an action table; for each action indicate: target metric, cause it addresses, expected impact (high/medium/low), effort, owner (frontend/backend/infra/content), dependencies or regression risk, and field verification signal at 28 days. Order by impact/effort according to {{PRIORIDAD_NEGOCIO}} and mark the actions that move the URL to good status.

5) Verification. Define how to confirm the improvement in field data (CrUX and Search Console) after the 28-day window and what to watch for to detect regressions.

Rules: never promise guaranteed rankings or confuse correlation with causation; CWV is a page experience signal and tiebreaker factor, not a direct ranking driver. Mark every estimate as [ASSUMPTION]. If there is material in {{ADJUNTOS}}, incorporate it.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Parameters:
- {{URL_O_PLANTILLAS}}: URL or set of templates to audit (home, product page, listing, article).
- {{PLATAFORMA}}: CMS or framework and CDN if known.
- {{DATOS_CWV}}: available data (CrUX field p75, Lighthouse/PageSpeed lab, or both).
- {{DISPOSITIVO}}: dominant device of organic traffic (mobile, desktop, or mixed).
- {{PRIORIDAD_NEGOCIO}}: prioritization criterion (quick wins, recover red-status URLs, highest-traffic template).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Content reinforcement according to E-E-A-T signals
prompts.content: Act as a senior content SEO strategist specialized in E-E-A-T and Google's Search Quality Rater Guidelines, with editorial judgment to distinguish real signals from filler. I need an E-E-A-T audit and reinforcement report for {{PIEZA_O_URL}}, which competes for {{QUERY_OBJETIVO}}. The author is {{AUTOR_Y_BIO}} and the page type is {{TIPO_PAGINA}}; available authority signals: {{SENALES_AUTORIDAD}}. If the piece, the target query, the author, or the page type is missing, ask for them and do not proceed. Work as follows: 1) Classify whether {{PIEZA_O_URL}} is YMYL according to {{TIPO_PAGINA}} and explicitly declare the applicable demand threshold. 2) Diagnose the four pillars in a table: pillar, current signal observed quoting the exact text fragment from {{PIEZA_O_URL}}, gap, and level high/medium/low; never infer a signal that the text does not show. 3) Rewrite 3 to 6 weak passages demonstrating the missing signal with real data to win {{QUERY_OBJETIVO}}, and mark with [ASSUMPTION] any data the author must confirm. 4) Draft a verifiable authorship block from {{AUTOR_Y_BIO}} and {{SENALES_AUTORIDAD}}; no unsubstantiated credentials. 5) Draft a citable sources block; what is not on record, mark it as pending and turn it into an action in the plan; never invent sources. 6) Deliver a plan of 5 to 8 actions prioritized by impact over effort, separating on-page from off-page, each action with a suggested owner and a measurable success signal. Distinguish Experience (first-hand experience) from Expertise (technical proficiency). If there is no identifiable author or verifiable credential, say so directly and propose the minimum path to build trust. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Close with the complete report. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices, and without the word free.

prompts.title: Structured data implementation with schema markup
prompts.content:
Act as a senior technical SEO specialist, expert in schema.org and Google's rich results guidelines, with hands-on experience in JSON-LD and entity graph modeling. I need to implement structured data on {{URL_O_PAGINA}} to make it eligible for rich results and improve its SERP presentation, without marking content that is not visible or not representative that could invalidate eligibility or lead to a manual action for structured data spam.

Working data: page type {{TIPO_PAGINA}}; target rich result {{RICH_RESULT_OBJETIVO}} (if missing, it is inferred from the type); entity data {{DATOS_ENTIDAD}}; output format {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} (JSON-LD by default); attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Proceed as follows: 1) Reformulate page type, intent, and rich result viable today according to Google's documentation; discard unsupported rich result types and justify. 2) Map the schema.org type or types and, where appropriate, nest them in a single graph using @graph. 3) Inventory required and recommended properties; verify that each one reflects visible content on {{URL_O_PAGINA}} and mark with [ASSUMPTION] what cannot be verified. 4) Generate the {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} with stable @context, @type, and @id, integrating {{DATOS_ENTIDAD}} and indicating where real variables go versus example values. 5) Model entity relationships (author, publisher, Organization with reusable @id and sameAs) for a coherent, deduplicated site graph. 6) Deliver validation plan (Google's rich results test plus Schema.org validator), expected errors and warnings and their interpretation, script location (server-side preferred over JavaScript injection) and maintenance, including Search Console monitoring and what NOT to mark.

If any input data is missing, ask before generating the markup instead of inventing it. Deliverable: markup block ready for production, property table with its origin, actionable validation checklist, and maintenance guide.

prompts.title: Local SEO and business profile optimization
prompts.content: Act as a senior local SEO specialist with a proven track record of scaling businesses to the map pack (the three-result block with map that Google shows for searches with geographic intent). Work on: business {{NEGOCIO}}, target location {{UBICACION}}, category {{CATEGORIA_PRINCIPAL}}, site and profile {{SITIO_WEB}}, current reviews {{RESENAS_ACTUALES}}, attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver an audit report plus a 90-day plan governed by relevance, distance, and prominence. Proceed as follows: 1) Audit the NAP character by character across profile, site, and directories; list discrepancies, duplicates, and format variations as priority findings. 2) Validate the primary category and propose justified secondary ones; discard inflated ones and map each to real queries. 3) Review profile completeness (hours, service area, attributes, description with natural local keywords, products/services, geotagged photos, UTM link) and flag empty fields. 4) Design an ethical and sustainable review system (no prohibited incentives) with response templates and a cadence and rating target. 5) Recommend local on-page signals: location landing page, LocalBusiness schema, embedded map, geolocalized content, sector citations/backlinks. 6) Consolidate in a findings table prioritized by impact x effort and a phased plan (0-30 foundations and NAP, 31-60 local content and reviews, 61-90 citations and authority) with owners and metrics. Edge cases: if {{UBICACION}} corresponds to a service-area business without a public address, adjust the distance lever; if {{NEGOCIO}} is multi-location, generate NAP and landing per location. If any data is missing, ask before proceeding; never invent verifiable data and mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Content gap analysis against competitors
Keyword cannibalization diagnosis
prompts.content: Act as a senior technical and content SEO specialist with experience diagnosing keyword cannibalization on sites with hundreds of URLs. On {{DOMINIO}} I suspect that several URLs are competing with each other for the same terms, which splits authority, confuses the search engine about which page to rank, and depresses cluster performance. I need a diagnosis with an actionable verdict per conflict, not a list of symptoms. Proceed as follows: first, group {{LISTADO_URLS}} into cannibalization clusters and, per cluster, name the keyword from {{KEYWORDS_OBJETIVO}} in dispute, the involved URLs, and the evidence (overlapping positions, the URL the search engine alternates, split CTR, double appearance in results) using {{DATOS_RENDIMIENTO}}; without data, base the indication on title, H1, and body overlap, and mark it as an assumption. Second, classify the search intent of each URL: informational, commercial, transactional, or navigational. Third, decide per cluster: same keyword plus same intent plus high overlap leads to CONSOLIDATE (designate canonical winning URL by link authority, indexed age, and performance, plus 301 from the rest); different intents lead to DIFFERENTIATE (assign a unique primary keyword per URL). Fourth, define on-page changes per differentiated URL: title, H1, primary keyword, and internal linking that separates the signals. Fifth, prioritize the backlog by impact versus effort, aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, with the risks of each move (temporary ranking loss, internal and external links to update, misapplied canonical or 301, redirect chains, orphan pages). Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide Search Console exports, crawl data, or site maps. If {{LISTADO_URLS}} or {{KEYWORDS_OBJETIVO}} is missing, ask before executing. Give me a cluster table (keyword, URLs, intent, evidence, verdict), the 301 map, the primary keyword reassignment per URL, and the prioritized backlog with risks. Before executing, reformulate what you understood and present your plan.

prompts.title: Visibility strategy in AI engines (AEO/GEO)
Quarterly editorial calendar by topic and channel
prompts.content: Act as a senior B2B content strategist with experience building and operating editorial calendars that sustain demand quarter after quarter. Build a 13-week quarterly editorial calendar (W1-W13), in table format and ready to operate, for {{MARCA_E_INDUSTRIA}}. Follow these steps: 1) Reformulate {{MARCA_E_INDUSTRIA}}, {{OBJETIVOS_TRIMESTRE}}, {{CANALES_ACTIVOS}}, {{CADENCIA_SOSTENIBLE}}, {{RESPONSABLES}}, and {{HITOS_TRIMESTRE}}; if any of these data points is missing, ask before executing. 2) Define 3 to 5 pillar topics; tie each pillar to an objective from {{OBJETIVOS_TRIMESTRE}} and to a funnel stage (awareness, consideration, conversion) and justify why it deserves space this quarter. 3) Assign a realistic cadence per channel within {{CANALES_ACTIVOS}} respecting {{CADENCIA_SOSTENIBLE}}: pieces per week and tentative publication day, with the weekly sum equal to or below the sustainable ceiling. 4) Build the W1-W13 matrix with columns: week, pillar topic, channel, format, tentative title, funnel stage, owner (from {{RESPONSABLES}}), and target date; balance pillars, channels, and stages, and reserve at least one buffer week. 5) Articulate content around {{HITOS_TRIMESTRE}} with pre, during, and post phases when milestones exist. 6) Define success metrics per channel according to funnel stage and the weekly and monthly review cadence, with criteria to reassign underperforming pieces. 7) Close with a recycling plan that derives each pillar into secondary formats per channel. Declare explicit assumptions if you fill gaps, flag production dependencies, and signal saturation risks. Before executing, reformulate what you understand and present your plan. Deliver in neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices or promises of freeness. Variables: {{MARCA_E_INDUSTRIA}} brand name and sector; {{OBJETIVOS_TRIMESTRE}} business or marketing objectives for the quarter; {{CANALES_ACTIVOS}} channels where content is published; {{CADENCIA_SOSTENIBLE}} maximum frequency the team can sustain; {{RESPONSABLES}} people or roles who execute and approve; {{HITOS_TRIMESTRE}} launches, seasonal dates, or events (optional).

prompts.title: Definition of brand content pillars
Content repurposing and atomization system
prompts.content:
Act as a senior content and multichannel distribution strategist, with a track record building repurposing engines for B2B and personal-authority brands. Your task is to convert {{PIEZA_PILAR}} into a system of channel-specific derivative assets for {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, optimized for {{CANALES_PRIORITARIOS}} and aligned with {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}; not mechanical excerpts, but derivatives that respect the native logic of each platform and maintain traceability to the parent message.

If {{PIEZA_PILAR}}, {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, {{CANALES_PRIORITARIOS}}, or {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}} are unclear, ask for them before executing; do not invent the source content or assume channels. If {{HORIZONTE_DISTRIBUCION}} is missing, assume 14 days and declare it.

Proceed as follows:
1. Dissect {{PIEZA_PILAR}} and extract its value cores: central thesis, supporting arguments, memorable data or examples, phrases with standalone power, and objections it resolves. Do not introduce claims absent from the original.
2. Label each core with its dominant angle: educational, counter-intuitive, narrative, tactical, or inspirational.
3. Map each core to the channel in {{CANALES_PRIORITARIOS}} where it performs best according to that channel's native logic; do not force a core into a channel where it cannot breathe, and justify each assignment in one line.
4. Draft each derivative asset ready to publish or as an actionable script, with an opening hook, development, and a close with a call to action coherent with the channel and {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}.
5. Order the assets in a {{HORIZONTE_DISTRIBUCION}} calendar: open with the one with the highest expected traction, stagger the cadence, avoid cannibalization, and maintain a through-line back to the pillar piece.
6. Build a traceability map connecting each derivative asset to its originating value core.

Constraints: estimate traction as a hypothesis, not a guarantee; mark every figure from the original as coming from {{PIEZA_PILAR}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Close with: a core table with angle, derivative assets by channel, a sequenced calendar, and a traceability map. Neutral professional Spanish, without references to costs or promises of free offerings.

prompts.title: Production brief for a content piece
prompts.content:
Act as a senior editorial strategist with a track record in B2B content marketing, SEO, and message architecture. You are going to produce the brief that precedes the writing of a content piece about {{TEMA}}, aimed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, to be published on {{CANAL}}, with the business objective {{OBJETIVO}}. Target keyword (if applicable): {{KEYWORD_PRINCIPAL}}. References and competition: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand of {{TEMA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{CANAL}}, and {{OBJETIVO}} and present your plan; then execute. If any of those four is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before moving forward rather than inventing it.

Deliver a production brief with these sections, in this order:
1. Objective of the piece: business result derived from {{OBJETIVO}} and the single primary metric it moves (with baseline or target if known); why it matters now.
2. Primary audience: segment, role, level of problem awareness, and the concrete pain point the piece resolves, drawing from {{AUDIENCIA}}.
3. Editorial angle: thesis or differential promise compared to what has already been published about {{TEMA}}; what makes it distinct and why it is credible; review {{ADJUNTOS}} to avoid repeating what already exists.
4. Keyword strategy: starting from {{KEYWORD_PRINCIPAL}}, set the primary keyword with its search intent + 3 to 5 related secondary keywords and, if applicable, a target question. If {{KEYWORD_PRINCIPAL}} is empty, derive it from the topic and objective.
5. Format and length: type of piece and word count range or duration according to {{CANAL}} and the intent.
6. Proposed structure: working headline + numbered sections, each with its core message, not just the heading.
7. CTA: a single call to action coherent with {{OBJETIVO}}, with suggested text and placement.
8. Quality checklist: verifiable criteria before publishing.

Declare explicit assumptions when you fill a gap with an inference. A single objective and a single CTA per piece; if {{OBJETIVO}} mixes two goals, recommend splitting into two pieces. Neutral professional Spanish, without emojis, without prices, and without the word free.

prompts.title: Short video script with hook-retention structure
prompts.content: Act as a senior vertical content scriptwriter and retention strategist, with mastery of direct-response copywriting and the attention levers of the 9:16 short format. I want a complete ready-to-record script about {{TEMA}} for {{PLATAFORMA}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, seeking {{OBJETIVO}}, with a duration of {{DURACION_SEGUNDOS}}, and closing with the action {{ACCION_CTA}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate in one line what you understand and present your plan; if any of those data points is missing, ask for them in a single round. Proceed as follows: (1) define the single central idea and the explicit promise the hook must deliver for {{AUDIENCIA}}; (2) write three hook variants of up to 3 seconds (A/B/C), each with a different lever from: tension or contradiction, concrete promise, uncomfortable question, surprising data, and common mistake — without promising what the body does not deliver; (3) develop the body in 2 to 4 beats with escalating curiosity, fast pacing, and one continuity hook between each beat, with no segment exceeding ~7 seconds without an attention shift, respecting {{DURACION_SEGUNDOS}}; (4) close with a single low-friction CTA aligned with {{OBJETIVO}} using {{ACCION_CTA}}; (5) deliver the script in a scene-by-scene table with timestamp, spoken audio, visual indication, and on-screen text, validating that the total duration matches {{DURACION_SEGUNDOS}} (+/- 5 s). Mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. Constraints: neutral professional Spanish, without emojis, without prices, without the word free, maximum one use of EstrategIA. Deliverable: (1) central idea and promise, (2) three hooks A/B/C, (3) scene-by-scene table, (4) final CTA.

prompts.title: Brand storytelling with the hero's journey
Content message with the StoryBrand SB7 framework
prompts.content: Act as a message strategist and senior copywriter, expert in Donald Miller's StoryBrand SB7 framework. I need a content message for {{OFERTA}} directed at {{CLIENTE}}, ready to publish on {{CANAL}}, where the customer is the hero and the brand is the guide, and where {{ACCION_DESEADA}} becomes the obvious step. First restate what you understood and present your plan; then execute. If the profile of {{CLIENTE}}, the {{OFERTA}}, the {{CANAL}}, or the {{ACCION_DESEADA}} is missing, ask for it before drafting; do not invent it. Stage 1, SB7 map in a table with the 7 modules in order: (1) Character: define {{CLIENTE}} and what they want in concrete terms; (2) Problem: separate tangible external villain, internal problem (how it makes them feel), and philosophical problem (why it is wrong for it to exist); (3) Guide: position the brand with empathy and authority supported by {{PRUEBA_AUTORIDAD}}; (4) Plan: exactly three numbered and memorable steps; (5) Call to action: one direct ({{ACCION_DESEADA}}) and one transitional with less commitment; (6) Failure avoided: what is at stake if they do not act, without alarmism; (7) Success: the concrete and aspirational transformation. Stage 2, integrated final message of 80 to 130 words adapted to the tone and format of {{CANAL}}, plus a one-liner 'we help [customer] to [result] so that [transformation]'. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. Rules: never invent figures, testimonials, or authority beyond {{PRUEBA_AUTORIDAD}}; mark inferences as [ASSUMPTION]; without prices or the word free; neutral professional Spanish, without emojis. Close by verifying the 7 modules, the three layers of the problem, the 3 steps of the plan, the two differentiated calls to action, and the absence of invented data. Parameters: {{CLIENTE}}, {{OFERTA}}, {{CANAL}}, {{ACCION_DESEADA}}, {{PRUEBA_AUTORIDAD}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Topical authority building with a content hub
Editorial series design for a newsletter
prompts.content: Act as a senior newsletter editor specialized in serialized formats with high retention. I want the operational manual for the editorial series on {{TEMA_NEWSLETTER}}, for an audience of {{AUDIENCIA}}, with cadence {{CADENCIA}}, and business objective {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Map {{NUM_ENTREGAS}} installments in the arc. Support material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate in your own words those four parameters and present your plan; if any arrives empty or ambiguous, ask me rather than inventing it. Deliver numbered: (1) Concept and promise in one sentence specific to {{TEMA_NEWSLETTER}}: what the reader gains and why they come back. (2) Fixed sections: 4 to 6 recurring blocks, each with its purpose, indicative length, and own tone, without overlaps, all serving the promise. (3) Arc of the series: chain the {{NUM_ENTREGAS}} installments; title each one and describe its angle in one line, showing progression toward a larger idea. (4) Headline system: a recognizable formula for subject lines, plus 3 consistent examples. (5) Continuity mechanism: the concrete element linking the close of one installment with the opening of the next. (6) Success metrics: 2 or 3 observable signals per installment and the adjustment if they drop. (7) Verifiable production checklist before each send. Close with the edge case of an installment without sufficient material. Neutral professional Spanish, without emojis, without prices, without the word free. Deliverable: manual ready to produce the first issue without pending structural decisions.

prompts.title: Content improvement with the skyscraper technique
prompts.content: Act as a senior SEO content strategist with a proven track record applying Brian Dean's (Backlinko) skyscraper technique and link building. I want an editorial blueprint to build a demonstrably superior version of {{CONTENIDO_REFERENTE}}, a resource that already ranks and accumulates links about {{TEMA}}, so that I can outrank it for {{PALABRA_CLAVE_PRIMARIA}} and capture the links sustaining it today, in service of {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} and oriented toward {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. If any of these data points ({{TEMA}}, {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, {{CONTENIDO_REFERENTE}}, {{PALABRA_CLAVE_PRIMARIA}}, {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}) is missing, ask me in a single round before moving forward. Deliver four blocks. First, a profile of {{CONTENIDO_REFERENTE}}: what search intent it satisfies, structure, depth, format, authority signals, and an explicit hypothesis of why it works for {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}. Second, a gap table with columns: weakness / opportunity / 10x element; cover outdatedness, superficiality, missing angles, reading experience, and unsupported data. Third, blueprint of the superior version: headline and differentiating angle, complete H2/H3 outline, 10x elements (recent dated data, examples, tables, visuals, practical depth), {{PALABRA_CLAVE_PRIMARIA}} and secondary keywords assigned to sections with their explicit intent, and a measurement criterion demonstrating superiority. Fourth, a promotion and linking plan aligned with {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}: prospects prioritized by relevance and probability of linking, contact hook per segment, and how to capture the links pointing to {{CONTENIDO_REFERENTE}}. Rules: do not invent metrics, rankings, or volumes; mark each unverified data point with [ASSUMPTION] and indicate how to confirm it (tool and query). Flag risks such as cannibalization of {{PALABRA_CLAVE_PRIMARIA}} or a reference piece too well defended for outreach. Without prices, without the word free, neutral professional Spanish without emojis. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.

prompts.title: Content map by TOFU-MOFU-BOFU funnel stage
Editorial and writing style guide
prompts.content:
Act as an editor-in-chief and senior brand linguist, with a track record defining editorial style manuals for media and brands in neutral Spanish. Your assignment is to build the editorial and writing style guide for {{NOMBRE_MARCA}}, ready to adopt as the official reference document and to feed a writing AI, so that writers, designers, and AI produce consistent texts without piece-by-piece review.

Proceed as follows. First, distill {{ATRIBUTOS_VOZ}} into three to five principles, each with its operational definition (what to do in practice, not an adjective) and a correct-versus-incorrect example pair; if {{EJEMPLOS_TEXTOS}} exists, extract the actual voice patterns from it rather than inventing them. Second, codify grammar and mechanics: person and tense, active voice, sentence and paragraph length, commas in enumerations, capitalization in headings, and format for numbers, dates, times, percentages, and currencies. Third, define format and structure: heading hierarchy, bullets versus prose, bold, link style, and call-to-action format. Fourth, build a preferred terminology table (approved term versus term to avoid), exact capitalization of product names, and handling of acronyms and anglicisms, calibrated for {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} and {{CANALES}}. Fifth, draft ten to fifteen Do and Don't rules in correct/incorrect pairs. Sixth, list the inviolable brand restrictions in a Compliance section. Seventh, close with a publication checklist.

Each rule must be verifiable, not aspirational, and accompanied by an example where applicable. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] every inference; do not invent brand data. If an essential data point is missing among {{NOMBRE_MARCA}}, {{ATRIBUTOS_VOZ}}, {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, {{CANALES}}, or {{EJEMPLOS_TEXTOS}}, ask for it before executing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver in neutral professional Spanish, without emojis, without prices or the word free. Document in second-level headings, with tables and correct/incorrect pairs. EstrategIA permitted at most once.

prompts.title: Paid search campaign structure by intent
Meta Ads campaign structure with CBO
Responsive search ad copy (RSA)
prompts.content: Act as a senior SEM specialist and direct-response copywriter with proven experience in Google Ads RSA. Produce an upload-ready responsive search ad for {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, targeting {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, that maximizes relevance (Quality Score) and CTR without breaking limits or policies. Before writing, restate what you understand about {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, {{KEYWORD_PRINCIPAL}}, {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}, {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, and {{CTA_DESEADO}}, and present your intent and variation group plan; if any of those five is missing, ask before continuing. Deliver: 15 headlines of up to 30 characters with visible count, distributed across four intents (keyword insertion {KeyWord:fallback} using {{KEYWORD_PRINCIPAL}} with fallback text that fits within 30 characters, benefit from {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}, proof or differentiator, and CTA aligned with {{CTA_DESEADO}}); 4 descriptions of up to 90 characters with count and intent; pin recommendation for positions 1 and 2 for must-have headlines leaving the rest in rotation; variation group per element to avoid cannibalization; and 2 display URL paths of up to 15 characters derived from {{URL_DESTINO}} with a keyword-headline-landing relevance note. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. Rules: no prices, no the word meaning without cost, no emojis, neutral professional English; data without source as [DATA TO CONFIRM]. Return table with columns element, text, count, intent, group, and pin, plus paths block and relevance note, ready to paste into Google Ads. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute.

prompts.title: Paid social creative matrix by angle
Cold, warm, and hot audience structure
prompts.content: Act as a senior paid media strategist with more than ten years in Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, and LinkedIn Ads and full-funnel B2C and B2B funnels. Design a cold, warm, and hot audience structure ready to set up for {{PRODUCTO_OFERTA}} targeting {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} on {{PLATAFORMAS}}, with the objective of {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSION}} and relying on {{ACTIVOS_DATOS}}. Most paid social budget is wasted showing the same ad and the same offer to people at opposing decision moments. Your job is to assign to each funnel level the correct message, offer, creative, and metric. Before executing, restate in your own words business, audience, platforms, objective, and assets; ask for what is missing and mark as [ASSUMPTION] what you infer. Deliver: (1) definition of the three temperatures with mutually exclusive membership criteria and concrete audience source per platform from {{PLATAFORMAS}}: cold new audience with no contact (interests, lookalikes, broad segments), warm engagement without conversion (web visitors, video views from 25 percent, engagement, cart or form abandonment), hot high intent or customer according to {{ACTIVOS_DATOS}} (buyers, leads, own list, checkout retargeting); (2) per temperature, message angle derived from awareness level (Eugene Schwartz's five levels), offer type, and creative format; (3) retargeting map connecting the three levels naming trigger event and time window at each jump, with exclusions to avoid overlap; (4) primary and secondary metric per temperature coherent with its function; (5) suggested budget distribution across levels in percentages with its logic; (6) one-page summary table: temperature, source, awareness level, message, offer, creative, metric; (7) three prioritized A/B tests for the first two weeks with hypothesis, isolated variable, and success criterion for {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSION}}. If the volume of {{ACTIVOS_DATOS}} is insufficient for reliable custom audiences or lookalikes, flag it and propose an alternate route. No prices or the word suggesting absence of cost; neutral professional English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Bid strategy by campaign objective
Retargeting sequence by intent level
prompts.content:
Act as a senior paid media strategist specialized in performance retargeting and audience architecture. Your assignment: design a stepped retargeting sequence by intent level for {{OFERTA}}, ready for a team to configure on {{PLATAFORMAS}}. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before producing the deliverable.

Inputs: offer and audience {{OFERTA}}; purchase cycle and ticket weight {{CICLO_COMPRA}}; available platforms {{PLATAFORMAS}}; events tracked today {{EVENTOS_RASTREADOS}}; action that defines the conversion {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSION}}; attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any is missing or ambiguous, ask before proceeding. Do not invent events or figures: if an event is not in {{EVENTOS_RASTREADOS}}, do not use it as an audience and say so.

Execute in five phases. Phase 1 - Framing: restate {{OFERTA}}, {{CICLO_COMPRA}}, and {{EVENTOS_RASTREADOS}}; mark with [ASSUMPTION] every estimated window or frequency. Phase 2 - Intent ladder: order {{EVENTOS_RASTREADOS}} from lowest to highest intent and justify the cutoff for each retention window based on {{CICLO_COMPRA}}. Phase 3 - Design per step: for each level define the seven elements: audience (exact behavioral condition plus window in days), angle and promise based on awareness level, format and piece, CTA, frequency window plus impression cap per person, exclusion logic, and exit criterion toward {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSION}}. Phase 4 - Exclusions: inclusion/exclusion matrix with mutual exclusivity and exclusion of converters from all steps. Phase 5 - Flow and control: complete journey between steps (advancement, expiration, exit by conversion or saturation) and three control metrics per step (at least one of cost, one of relevance, one of advancement).

Deliver a document with the intent ladder, one card per step, the exclusion matrix, the flow map, and the control metrics. Cover edge cases: audience too small to serve (step merger or window extension, marked [ASSUMPTION]) and overlap between {{PLATAFORMAS}}. Use neutral professional English, no prices, no the word free, and without promising guaranteed results.

prompts.title: Creative testing plan with iterative method
prompts.content:
Act as a senior creative testing strategist in paid media on {{PLATAFORMA}}, with experience managing acquisition budgets and designing experiments with statistical rigor. Design an iterative creative testing plan for the campaign "{{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}", optimized toward {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}}, that turns advertising into a learning machine: each round isolates a variable, tests a falsifiable hypothesis, and promotes only winners with statistical backing, so that the cost of acquisition drops sustainably instead of depending on a lucky break.

First restate what you understand about {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}, {{PLATAFORMA}}, {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}}, and {{VOLUMEN_CONVERSIONES}}; present your plan before executing. If any of those data points or the budget in investment units is missing, ask for it before continuing: without them the sample cannot be sized.

Deliver: (1) prioritized variable table (hook, format, message angle, offer, CTA) by expected impact vs. effort, with one variable per round; if {{VARIABLE_FOCO}} was indicated, place it in the first round; (2) falsifiable hypothesis per variant: if I change X then I expect Y in {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} because W; (3) winner criterion set BEFORE launching: primary metric, minimum relevant improvement (MDE), confidence level, power target, and sample size derived from {{VOLUMEN_CONVERSIONES}}; (4) at least one guardrail metric per test to discard false winners (e.g., CTR rises but CPA spikes, or initial conversion rises but retention or LTV drops); (5) cadence by rounds with an explicit rule for promoting the winner to control and archiving the loser with its learning; (6) accumulated learnings log template; (7) early stopping protocol to halt clearly losing variants without waiting for the full sample.

Size the minimum sample and learning window from {{VOLUMEN_CONVERSIONES}}. If volume does not reach significance, warn about the risk of inconclusive tests and propose alternatives (sequential reading with correction, early signals, consolidate budget into fewer variants, or raise the MDE so the test is decidable). Respect the learning phase of the {{PLATAFORMA}} algorithm and avoid reading results during it. Do not invent benchmarks or historical figures: mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Neutral professional English, no prices.

Variables: {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}, {{PLATAFORMA}}, {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}}, {{VOLUMEN_CONVERSIONES}}, {{VARIABLE_FOCO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Target ROAS and break-even calculation
Performance Max campaign configuration by asset groups
prompts.content:
I need you to configure the complete structure of a Google Ads Performance Max campaign, organized by asset groups, ready to upload to the platform. Act as a senior Google Ads specialist certified in search and display, focused on Performance Max and asset strategy for acquisition.

Data:
- OFERTA: {{OFERTA}} (product or service and its main proposition)
- OBJETIVO_CONVERSION: {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSION}} (action that counts as a conversion: lead, purchase, registration, call; and its value if any)
- PUBLICO_OBJETIVO: {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} (segments to capture: new prospects, returning customers, niches)
- MERCADO: {{MERCADO}} (country or region, language, and seasonality if applicable)
- DIFERENCIADORES: {{DIFERENCIADORES}} (competitive advantages and proof that sustains the message; optional)

Context: PMax consolidates Search, Display, YouTube, Discover, Gmail, and Maps in a single campaign governed by the conversion signal; its performance depends on how asset groups are structured, because each group feeds the algorithm with coherent creatives, search themes, and audience signals. A poorly defined group mixes incompatible audiences and dilutes learning.

Before writing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about {{OFERTA}}, {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSION}}, {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, and {{MERCADO}}; Plan the groups you will create and why; then Execute. If {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSION}}, {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, or {{MERCADO}} is missing, ask for it before producing.

Deliver: 1) 2 to 4 asset groups, each a coherent audience or line from {{OFERTA}} for {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}; name each group and declare who it represents and its funnel stage. 2) Per group, 5 to 10 search themes expressing intent in {{MERCADO}}. 3) Per group, audience signals (own + custom by interest/intent + demographic) with learning justification per signal. 4) Per group, asset inventory with exact counts and limits: 3 to 5 short headlines (<=30), 5 long headlines (<=90), 5 descriptions (<=90, one <=60), business name, up to 5 logos, up to 20 images (landscape/square/portrait), up to 5 videos, and final URL; real copy, not templates. 5) Per group, message angle and value proposition based on {{DIFERENCIADORES}}. 6) Funnel coverage map (prospecting vs. recurring) and 3 early signals at 14 days without touching budget.

Restrictions: zero prices, discounts, or the word indicating the service is given away; neutral professional English, no emojis; unique groups without catch-all buckets; message, theme, and signal aligned to the same intent; verify counts and limits before closing. If {{DIFERENCIADORES}} is empty, derive them from {{OFERTA}} and mark them as assumption. If there is no video, indicate how to substitute with images. Deliverable: document structured by asset groups ready to upload to Google Ads.

prompts.title: Paid media plan and budget allocation by channel
Creative fatigue diagnosis and rotation plan
prompts.content:
Act as a senior paid media strategist specializing in performance and creative management at scale, with the judgment to separate real fatigue from measurement noise. I need a creative fatigue diagnosis and a rotation plan with a calendar for my campaign on {{PLATAFORMA}} with objective {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}, analyzing the window {{VENTANA_DATOS}} and using {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} as the key metric. Estimated target audience size: {{TAMANO_AUDIENCIA}}. Frequency threshold for suspecting fatigue: {{UMBRAL_FRECUENCIA}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before diagnosing, reframe what you understand and present your plan. If a critical piece of data is missing (per-ad data on impressions, frequency, reach, CTR, CPM, {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} and spend), ask me for it before continuing.

Proceed as follows. First, consolidate the data per ad for the period {{VENTANA_DATOS}}: impressions, frequency, reach, CTR, CPM, {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} and spend; validate coverage and quality and list missing fields. Second, trace the performance curve of each creative over time and locate the inflection point where frequency rises while CTR falls and {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} deteriorates. Third, classify each piece as healthy, on alert or fatigued with explicit thresholds: {{UMBRAL_FRECUENCIA}}, relative CTR drop compared to its best week and deviation of {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} from the period average; declare each threshold used. Fourth, discriminate real fatigue (sustained degradation from overexposure) from noise (seasonality, bid or budget changes, exhausted audience based on {{TAMANO_AUDIENCIA}}, supply or tracking problem, insufficient volume). Fifth, issue a verdict per creative: keep, watch, refresh variant or retire, with its numerical evidence. Sixth, define refresh cadence, number of variants per cycle, angles to test and replacement sequence that preserves algorithm learning. Seventh, deliver a 4-to-6-week rotation calendar with monitoring routine and early rotation triggers.

Rules: every verdict is backed by numbers; mark estimates as [ASSUMPTION] and dependencies on missing data as [VERIFY]; if the volume does not permit distinguishing signal from noise, say so; no promises of guaranteed results; no prices.

prompts.title: Welcome and onboarding email sequence
Abandoned cart recovery flow
prompts.content:
Act as a senior email marketing and ecommerce lifecycle automation specialist, with experience measuring recovery rates and deliverability on platforms such as Klaviyo, Shopify Email and HubSpot. I need an abandoned cart recovery flow ready to configure in {{PLATAFORMA}}.

Context: I sell {{TIPO_PRODUCTO}}, with ticket {{TICKET_PROMEDIO}}, in the tone {{TONO_MARCA}}. A high fraction of purchase intent is lost in the cart: the visitor showed explicit desire but did not complete, and that revenue evaporates if we don't recover it through relevance and timing instead of price. I want a strategy that converts without eroding margin or training the customer to wait for discounts, and without burning sender reputation. The non-monetary value courtesy we will reserve for the last email is {{INCENTIVO_NO_MONETARIO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

If any of that data is missing, ask me for it before drafting.

Deliver in four steps. First, reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing. Second, design the cadence: define the entry trigger and the initial wait window before the first email, then a sequence of 3 to 4 emails with send times relative to the abandonment (for example 1h, 24h, 48-72h), each with a different objective and angle that escalates from useful reminder to objection handling to trust reinforcement, without cannibalization between emails. Third, draft for each email a subject line, preheader, brief body and a single CTA that returns to the cart; reserve {{INCENTIVO_NO_MONETARIO}} only for the last email, named by its benefit and never as a discount. Fourth, specify the exit conditions from the flow: completed purchase, opt-out or unsubscribe, and sequence exhausted.

Brand and delivery rules: no prices, no the word free, no false urgency; a single CTA per email; brevity; consistent tone with {{TONO_MARCA}} throughout the sequence; respect suppressions and consent. Close with the cadence table, the copy block per email and the list of exit conditions.

prompts.title: Email list segmentation with RFM model
Nurturing campaign with educational drip sequence
prompts.content:
Act as a senior email marketing and lifecycle strategist, specializing in B2B nurturing, with over a decade building drip sequences that move leads from subscription to conversion. I want an educational nurturing sequence of {{NUM_CORREOS}} progressive emails for {{PERFIL_LEAD}}, anchored in {{ACTIVO_EDUCATIVO}}, aimed at resolving {{PROBLEMA_OFERTA}} and qualifying according to {{CRITERIO_LEAD_MADURO}}. The lead submitted their email but is not yet ready to speak with sales, and pushing them toward conversion now burns them: the purpose is to build trust with real utility before asking for anything.

If {{PERFIL_LEAD}}, {{PROBLEMA_OFERTA}}, {{ACTIVO_EDUCATIVO}}, {{NUM_CORREOS}} or {{CRITERIO_LEAD_MADURO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before drafting; do not invent any of these data points.

Proceed as follows. First, map the five stages of buyer awareness (unaware of the problem, problem-aware, solution-aware, product-aware, most aware) and align them with the decision phases (discovery, consideration, evaluation, decision). Assign each email exactly one stage, so the sequence escalates without jumps or backtracking and each email builds on the idea of the previous one. For each email draft eight fields: number and purpose in one line; awareness stage; send day relative to entry (D+0, D+2, ...) with cadence that opens up as the sequence advances; two contrasting subject line options (one curiosity-driven, one concrete-benefit); opening hook; central educational idea, a single useful concept that adds value on its own and is not a disguised sales pitch, anchored in {{ACTIVO_EDUCATIVO}}; call to action proportional to the stage, escalating from reading to responding to scheduling; behavioral signal that enables progression. Then define the branching logic for three minimum routes: opens without clicking, clicks without responding, and the milestone that declares the lead mature according to {{CRITERIO_LEAD_MADURO}} and hands them off to sales. Include an exit path for the lead who does not interact after two or three emails (frequency reduction or pause, no abrupt unsubscribe) and a handover note to sales with the minimum context the representative needs (stage reached, last asset consumed, triggering signal).

Firm rules: never mention prices or the word free; neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis; do not invent performance metrics and mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Before drafting, reframe what you understand and present the stage-phase map with the email-stage assignment and cadence for confirmation; only then draft the {{NUM_CORREOS}} complete emails and the branching tree, ready to load into the automation tool.

prompts.title: Subject line generation and A/B testing
Win-back reactivation campaign for inactive contacts
Email marketing map by customer lifecycle
Deliverability and sender reputation plan
Sales email copy with PAS framework
prompts.content: Act as a senior direct-response copywriter specializing in sales emails, with mastery of the Problem-Agitation-Solution (PAS) framework. Write a complete, ready-to-send offer email that moves {{AUDIENCIA}} from indifference to {{ACCION_DESEADA}}, anchoring the message in {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}} so the reader feels understood before receiving the proposal for {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}. If {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}, or {{ACCION_DESEADA}} is missing, ask before writing. Produce in this order: (1) three subject lines oriented toward {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}, each up to 50 characters, without mentioning the product; (2) a preheader that extends the subject without repeating it, between 35 and 90 characters; (3) a body of 120 to 200 words with a brief greeting, a Problem block that names the pain in {{AUDIENCIA}}'s literal language without exaggerating, an Agitation block that shows the concrete and verifiable cost of not resolving it (time, money, opportunities, stress) without catastrophizing, and a Solution block that presents {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} as a bridge to the result, translates features into benefits, and applies {{TONO_E_INCENTIVO}} as access, quota, bonus, or priority only if it was provided; (4) a single, unambiguous CTA text toward {{ACCION_DESEADA}}; (5) a brief postscript with legitimate urgency or social proof. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Hard rules: neutral Spanish, short sentences, no emojis; never prices or cost figures; never the word free or equivalents; a single call to action. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any metric, testimonial, or supporting data not delivered; do not invent an incentive if {{TONO_E_INCENTIVO}} is empty. Deliver the final block with subject lines, preheader, PAS body, CTA, and postscript, ready to paste into the sending platform, and close with a line listing the [ASSUMPTION] items used.

prompts.title: Post-purchase cross-sell and upsell flow
prompts.content: Act as a senior email lifecycle strategist specializing in account retention and expansion for brands with a catalog of related products. Design a post-purchase flow of 4 to 6 emails combining cross-sell and upsell, ready to load into an automation platform, based on: purchased product {{PRODUCTO_COMPRADO}}, available complements {{PRODUCTOS_COMPLEMENTARIOS}}, higher-level versions or plans {{NIVELES_SUPERIORES}}, typical purchase cycle {{CICLO_COMPRA_TIPICO}}, sending platform {{PLATAFORMA_ENVIO}}, and {{ADJUNTOS}}. The recently closed purchase is the window of maximum trust; the flow must convert it into incremental value without saturating the inbox. Before writing, restate your understanding of {{PRODUCTO_COMPRADO}}, {{PRODUCTOS_COMPLEMENTARIOS}}, {{NIVELES_SUPERIORES}}, and {{CICLO_COMPRA_TIPICO}}, and present your sequence plan for approval; if any data is missing, ask for it. When executing: 1) Map the post-purchase lifecycle of {{PRODUCTO_COMPRADO}} according to {{CICLO_COMPRA_TIPICO}} (confirmation and reinforcement, onboarding or first use, perceived value moment, cross-sell, upsell, reactivation) and position each email where expected behavior justifies it. 2) For each email define a row: single objective, send day relative to purchase, behavioral trigger, subject line, preheader, body angle, single main CTA, and exclusion condition for those who already converted or returned. 3) Anchor the cross-sell in {{PRODUCTOS_COMPLEMENTARIOS}} with a products-bought-together logic; anchor the upsell of {{NIVELES_SUPERIORES}} in the value gap the customer is already experiencing, not in a generic version. 4) Define per-email metrics (open rate, click rate, incremental conversion, incremental value per customer), attribution window, anti-fatigue frequency rule, and exit plan for the flow. 5) Adapt number of steps and timing to {{PLATAFORMA_ENVIO}} if specified. Limits: 4 to 6 emails; neutral professional Spanish, no emojis; never prices, numerical discounts, or the word free; value through benefit, not through figures. Mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver a table with one row per email plus the metrics and frequency-rules block.

prompts.title: Differentiated organic strategy by social network
Social calendar with balanced content mix
prompts.content: Act as a senior social content strategist who masters content pillars and balanced-mix theory, and who has built editorial calendars for brands with an active audience. I need a complete editorial calendar for {{META_PERIODO}}, directed at {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, publishing on {{CANALES}} with a cadence of {{FRECUENCIA}}, ideally with a distribution of {{PROPORCION_MIX}}. Before executing, restate in your own words the objective, audience, and channels you understand, and present your plan in steps. If {{META_PERIODO}}, {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, {{CANALES}}, or {{FRECUENCIA}} are ambiguous, ask me before continuing; if {{PROPORCION_MIX}} is not provided, propose it yourself and justify each percentage. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as brand inputs or context when they exist. Then deliver: first, the target mix proportion (educational, inspirational, promotional, conversational) in percentages justified against {{META_PERIODO}} and the maturity of {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, without the promotional exceeding a reasonable ceiling such as one-third of the total. Second, the translation of those percentages into the real number of posts by type according to {{FRECUENCIA}} and {{CANALES}}, showing the count and flagging the rounding when they do not yield whole numbers. Third, a table with one row per post: day, channel, mix type, thematic pillar, format (carousel, short video, text, poll, story), specific title or hook, call to action, and primary metric. Fourth, distribute types so that no week repeats the same type on two consecutive days and each week has at least one conversational piece, balancing formats. Close with three recommendations on rhythm, recycling, and cross-channel reuse, plus a note on assumptions and limits. Use neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no mention of prices or the word free.

prompts.title: Campaign brief with creators and influencers
User-generated content (UGC) program
prompts.content: Act as a senior social media and community programs strategist, specializing in UGC for consumer brands, with experience in usage rights, attribution, and moderation. For {{MARCA}}, in the category {{CATEGORIA_PRODUCTO}}, on {{PLATAFORMA_PRINCIPAL}}, I need to activate {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} as creators of authentic content that operates as social proof and multiplies reach, with the priority goal of {{META_PROGRAMA}} and in the tone {{TONO_MARCA}}. The mechanic must be sustained by intrinsic motivation and recognition, never by financial compensation. If any data is missing, ask before proceeding. Deliver an operational UGC program with: 1) objective in one sentence plus measurable success criteria derived from {{META_PROGRAMA}}; 2) tiered incentive mechanic (public recognition, curated repost, early access, creators' circle) coherent with {{TONO_MARCA}}, with the advancement trigger for each level and the anti-promise limit of offering no monetary compensation or gifts; 3) hashtag architecture with one mother hashtag derived from {{MARCA}} (memorable, low collision) plus two or three campaign hashtags, in a table with function, when to use it, and moderation rule, marking as [ASSUMPTION] any availability not verified on {{PLATAFORMA_PRINCIPAL}}; 4) step-by-step curation flow (discovery, quality and brand-fit filter, explicit rights request, permission registration, creator attribution, and publication) with a brief, copyable permission script in the {{TONO_MARCA}} tone; 5) weekly operational cadence and minimum dashboard with UGC volume, approval rate, granted permissions rate, and reuse by channel, each metric with its alarm signal. Add handling for three edge cases: excellent content with no response to the permission request, a creator asking to remove a piece already published, and UGC that mentions a competitor or includes third parties without consent. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if it exists. Before executing, restate your understanding and present your plan. Write in neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices, no the word free.

prompts.title: LinkedIn personal brand strategy by pillars
prompts.content:
Act as a senior LinkedIn personal brand strategist with a proven track record building B2B professional authority and mastery of the platform's editorial formats. I want a pillar-based personal brand strategy, ready to execute, aligned with my objective {{OBJETIVO_PROFESIONAL}}. My role and experience: {{ROL_Y_EXPERIENCIA}}. My target audience and the decision I expect from them: {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}}. Topics where I have a grounded opinion and demonstrable experience: {{TEMAS_DE_AUTORIDAD}}. Sustainable weekly frequency: {{FRECUENCIA_SEMANAL}} (if empty, assume 3 and state it explicitly). Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before producing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan the steps, and only then Execute; restate and present your plan before proceeding. If any essential data point above is missing, ask for it in a single batch.

Deliver: (1) a one-sentence positioning statement with explicit audience + problem + differential angle, derived from {{ROL_Y_EXPERIENCIA}} and {{TEMAS_DE_AUTORIDAD}}; (2) 3 to 4 pillars, each with a name, named strategic purpose (authority, closeness, social proof, or acquisition), topics, and proportion of the calendar summing to 100 percent; (3) per pillar, 2-3 formats with a concrete example angle for the topic; (4) weekly cadence coherent with {{FRECUENCIA_SEMANAL}} without saturating a purpose; (5) three authority metrics (not vanity) with an initial reading and review threshold. Mark [ASSUMPTION] for any inference. Close with the main execution risk and its mitigation. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no empty promises or unsupported superlatives.

prompts.title: Community management plan and interaction rules
Social listening and brand monitoring strategy
prompts.content: Act as a senior social listening and brand intelligence strategist, with a track record in corporate reputation, crisis management, and conversation analytics. Design an operational social listening and brand monitoring strategy ready to implement and tool-agnostic for {{MARCA}}, comparing against {{COMPETIDORES}} on channels {{CANALES}} and in {{IDIOMA_REGION}}, with a primary focus on {{OBJETIVO_MONITOREO}} and using {{UMBRAL_ALERTA}} as the reference critical trigger. Before executing, restate in two lines what you understood and present your phase plan; mark as [ASSUMPTION] any data not provided and, if anything critical is missing, ask for it in a single batch instead of inventing it. Deliver: (1) explicit monitoring objective and who it serves (business, marketing, customer service, leadership), with the business question it answers; (2) taxonomy in four topic trees (brand and products, competitors, category and trends, risk and crisis), and for each topic keywords, synonyms, typos, hashtags, and a Boolean query with AND, OR, NOT, and noise exclusions; (3) scope of {{CANALES}} and {{IDIOMA_REGION}}, with what is explicitly out of scope; (4) four-category sentiment rubric (positive, neutral, negative, irony/ambiguous) with criteria and at least one boundary example per category; (5) alert system with base metrics (volume, estimated reach, net sentiment, share of voice), three severity levels (informational, attention, critical) with numerical thresholds anchored in {{UMBRAL_ALERTA}}, window, recipient, and channel; (6) KPI dashboard with daily, weekly, and monthly cadence; (7) response and escalation protocol by mention type and severity, with roles and target times. Close with assumptions, limits, and how sentiment is calibrated in the first few weeks. Attachments to consider: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis; never cite tool prices or use the word free.

prompts.title: Social content series with a hook bank
prompts.content:
Act as a senior social content strategist and direct-response copywriter, specializing in retention in the first 3 seconds and in editorial series architecture by format. I want a reusable hook bank for my content series.

Input data:
- Topic or niche: {{TEMA_NICHO}}
- Audience (who they are, level of problem awareness, main pain or desire): {{AUDIENCIA}}
- Brand voice (tone, and words I do and do not use): {{VOZ_MARCA}}
- Platforms where I publish: {{PLATAFORMAS}}
- Formats to cover: {{FORMATOS}} (by default carousel, reel/short video, text post, story)
- Minimum hooks per format: {{HOOKS_POR_FORMATO}} (by default 8)
- Subtopics or content pillars: {{TEMAS_O_PILARES}} (if I leave them blank, derive 3-5 for me and mark them as proposed)

Proceed as follows:
1. Framing: summarize in 3-4 lines niche, audience, awareness level, voice, and pillars; mark [ASSUMPTION] for what you infer. If an essential data point above is missing, ask before continuing; do not invent my niche or audience.
2. Create a section for each format in {{FORMATOS}}.
3. In each format generate at least {{HOOKS_POR_FORMATO}} hooks covering without repeating a formula 8 angles: tension/conflict, curiosity/gap, counterintuitive, proof/result, common mistake debunked, enumeration/utility promise, qualifying question, and identity declaration.
4. Write each hook ready to publish, specific to {{TEMA_NICHO}} and {{AUDIENCIA}}, anchored to a pillar from {{TEMAS_O_PILARES}}, without empty brackets. Modulate the opening according to the awareness level of {{AUDIENCIA}}.
5. Per hook: (a) exact opening, (b) angle, (c) pillar, (d) one-line rationale, (e) continuation note that fulfills the promise.
6. Trimming guide for each platform in {{PLATAFORMAS}} up to its visible cutoff; unverified limits go marked [ASSUMPTION].
7. Three mistakes that kill a hook, each with its correction.

Neutral Spanish, professional tone, no emojis. Respect {{VOZ_MARCA}} in every line and deliver hooks pasteable as-is into real pieces.

prompts.title: Multi-platform short-form video strategy
prompts.content:
Act as a senior short-form video strategist who has operated brand accounts on Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok, with a focus on retention in the first seconds and batch production. Design a reproducible pipeline that converts {{PILAR_CONTENIDO}} into multiple vertical 9:16 pieces aimed at {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, adapted to {{PLATAFORMAS}} without re-recording, sustainable over a quarter and oriented toward {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}.

Deliver the pipeline in five layers: (1) Hook strategy: 3 angles for {{PILAR_CONTENIDO}} aimed at {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, each with its named pattern (open question, contradiction, result promise, counter-intuitive data point), the exact text of the first second, and the retention rationale. (2) Script and structure: a reusable hook-tension-payoff-close template with target duration per platform (Reels 15–30s, Shorts up to 60s, TikTok 21–34s) and call-to-action placement according to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. (3) Shooting batch: how to group the recording of {{CADENCIA_SEMANAL}} pieces in a single session, with a shot list, b-roll, and vertical capture requirements that do not crop subtitles. (4) Per-platform adaptation: what changes between {{PLATAFORMAS}} without re-recording (UI safe zones, burned-in subtitles, native vs. licensed audio, on-screen text, Shorts thumbnail, hashtags, and description). (5) Calendar and measurement: weekly cadence with posting times per platform and a KPI dashboard by funnel stage (3-second retention, completion, shares, saves, followers gained), with the numeric threshold that signals reinvesting or retiring an angle.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, present your plan, and then execute. Flag unverifiable estimates as [ASSUMPTION] and missing data as a question before proceeding. Reply in neutral, professional Spanish, without emojis. Close with a five-layer pipeline document ready for one person to execute week after week without re-interpreting.

Parameters:
- {{PILAR_CONTENIDO}}: topic or weekly editorial pillar from which all pieces are derived
- {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}: who the content addresses (profile, pain point, awareness level)
- {{PLATAFORMAS}}: priority platforms (Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, TikTok)
- {{CADENCIA_SEMANAL}}: number of pieces to publish per week per platform
- {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}: quarterly business outcome (reach, leads, community, sales)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Social launch kit for a product or event
Customer journey mapping by stage and emotion
prompts.content: Act as a senior customer experience (CX) and funnel marketing strategist, with practice in journey mapping and emotion-centered design. I need to see my customer's journey as a single piece in order to locate the exact friction point where the customer is lost, prioritize experience investment where it hurts the most, and align marketing, sales, and product around a shared view. The product is {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, the target customer is {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}, the priority objective to optimize is {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, and the dominant channel is {{CANAL_PRINCIPAL}}; deepen or exclude {{ETAPAS_FOCO}} if indicated, and consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate product, segment, objective, and channel; declare with [ASSUMPTION] any missing data and ask me for the critical ones before proceeding. Present your plan: list of stages and column schema. Then: 1) Define the stages starting from the base funnel Awareness, Consideration, Decision, Purchase, Onboarding, Use, Loyalty, Recommendation; merge or adapt according to {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, respect {{ETAPAS_FOCO}}, and justify each adjustment; aim for 6–8 stages. 2) Build a table with one row per stage and columns: customer objective, actions, touchpoints and channels, dominant emotion with intensity 1–5, verbatim customer thought, friction or pain, actionable opportunity, KPI or measurement signal. 3) Identify 2–3 emotional valleys with the greatest drop and propose a concrete lever for each one linked to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, with the expected effect on the metric. 4) Narrate the emotional curve stage by stage, marking peaks, valleys, and intensity deltas. Stay true to {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}: emotions and phrases must sound like that real person; do not invent data as facts. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Full TOFU-MOFU-BOFU funnel design
prompts.content: Act as a senior demand generation strategist who has built full-funnel content funnels and is accountable for cost per lead and stage-by-stage conversion. Design a complete, actionable, and measurable TOFU-MOFU-BOFU funnel for {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, aimed at {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}}, with the goal of achieving {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, distributed via {{CANALES_DISPONIBLES}}, and anchored in MOFU by {{OFERTA_ANCLA}}. If any of the four essential data points (product, audience, objective, channels) is missing, ask before proceeding. Deliver: (1) an ideal customer profile with the central problem, conscious vs. latent pain, an awareness map from latent to decided, and 3 purchase criteria derived from {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}} and {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}; (2) three tables, one per level, with stage objective, anchor piece, prospect intent, 3 to 5 content formats, channels drawn from {{CANALES_DISPONIBLES}}, exact CTA, capture or advancement mechanism, and 1 to 2 KPIs with definition and formula; (3) a transition map that connects the three levels with the behavioral signal that moves the prospect and the bridge piece that triggers the jump; (4) a minimum measurement plan with the funnel's north metric and review cadence. Respect the boundaries: TOFU educates on the problem without mentioning the product; MOFU nurtures and captures the lead with {{OFERTA_ANCLA}}; BOFU resolves objections with at least one proof piece and pushes toward the commercial action. Do not invent figures: flag every benchmark or assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Neutral, professional Spanish, without absolute promises. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Landing page conversion optimization
Lead magnet and capture offer design
Value ladder design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior direct-response marketing strategist specialized in offer architecture and value ladders. Design for {{NEGOCIO}} a value ladder of 4 to 5 rungs in strictly ascending order of commitment, aimed at {{CLIENTE_IDEAL}}, leading from a low-friction entry access to {{OFERTA_CUMBRE}}, the offer that materializes {{TRANSFORMACION_FINAL}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand about {{NEGOCIO}}, {{CLIENTE_IDEAL}}, {{TRANSFORMACION_FINAL}}, and {{OFERTA_CUMBRE}}, and present your plan before executing. If any of those four data points is unclear, ask before proceeding; do not invent it.

Design backwards from the destination: fix {{TRANSFORMACION_FINAL}} and {{OFERTA_CUMBRE}} first, then place the intermediate rungs so that none demands a confidence jump that the previous one has not prepared, starting from the first contact described in {{NIVEL_COMPROMISO_ENTRADA}}. For each rung define: offer name, concrete promise, value it unlocks, commitment level (friction, time, and exposure, never price), role in the journey (entry access, bridge offer, main offer, summit offer, or continuity), and the outcome that enables the next step. For each transition define: evidence of value received, ascension trigger, and objection to resolve. Close with an overview showing the complete ascending flow and pointing to the rung where to concentrate effort.

Rules: the entry rung is named by its function, never as a gift or with the word free. No price figures on any rung. If {{NEGOCIO}} only supports 3 real rungs, say so and justify rather than inflating. Neutral, professional Spanish, without emojis. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliverable: rung table, transition table, and overview, ready to implement.

prompts.title: Tripwire entry offer design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior conversion funnel and offer architecture strategist, specialized in entry offers and value ladders. For {{NEGOCIO_Y_PROPUESTA}} I need to convert cold prospects into first-time buyers: the obstacle is not the product but the psychological barrier of the first yes. Design a tripwire entry offer (relatively low price, very high perceived value) that breaks that barrier and, through the commitment consistency principle, predisposes the buyer to advance through the value ladder toward {{OFERTA_CORE}}. The purpose of the tripwire is not margin — it is to transform the relationship from prospect to customer.

Deliverable: a complete tripwire offer in one page, ready for a landing page.
