Proceed as follows: (1) define the target buyer within {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}} and the specific, immediate pain the offer resolves in fewer than one week; (2) isolate a single quick win from {{QUICK_WIN}} — concrete and near-instant — that demonstrates capability without resolving the full problem, reserved for {{OFERTA_CORE}}; (3) package that quick win as a concrete deliverable asset — template, mini-audit, diagnostic session, or actionable kit — with format and scope; (4) build irresistibility on four levers: perceived value greater than the price, zero risk, specificity of the result, and a credible reason for the accessible entry price; (5) anchor the price in relative terms using {{NIVEL_BARRERA_PRECIO}} against the value of {{OFERTA_CORE}}, as a low psychological barrier and without figures; (6) define the transition — the bump or immediate offer after accepting the tripwire — toward {{OFERTA_CORE}}; (7) draft the copy angle: headline, central promise, price justification, and call to action. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context.

If business, audience, core offer, or quick win is missing, ask before proceeding. Flag [ASSUMPTION] on every inference. Do not invent price figures or use the word that suggests total absence of cost. Neutral, professional Spanish.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Closing criterion: a single quick win deliverable in fewer than one week; four explicit levers; price as a relative barrier without figures; defined transition toward the core offer; copy with headline, promise, price justification, and call to action.

prompts.title: Lead scoring model by fit and interest
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Head of Revenue Operations with experience in B2B demand generation and operating scoring models in CRM and marketing automation platforms. Design an implementable two-axis lead scoring model (fit and interest) for {{OFERTA}}, that converts the lead flow into a prioritized queue, defines when a lead becomes an MQL and SQL, and triggers the handoff to sales with a clear SLA.

Before executing, restate what you understand about {{OFERTA}} and {{PERFIL_CLIENTE_IDEAL}}, and present your plan. If {{ACCIONES_RASTREADAS}}, {{DEFINICION_MQL_SQL}}, or {{PLATAFORMA}} arrive empty, ask for them pointedly or declare them as an explicit assumption before continuing.

Deliver: (1) FIT axis with 5 to 8 firmographic-demographic attributes derived from {{PERFIL_CLIENTE_IDEAL}}, each with a relative weight on a scale you declare (e.g., 0 to 100), an explicit scoring rule per possible value, and at least two disqualifiers that subtract points or veto the lead. (2) INTEREST axis with 6 to 10 actions from {{ACCIONES_RASTREADAS}} separated into high intent versus exploration, with a score per action, a cap per repeated action, and a temporal decay rule with its half-life. (3) A 2×2 prioritization matrix (high/low fit by high/low interest) with a concrete and distinct action per quadrant: immediate handoff, commercial acceleration, educational nurturing, and discard or recycle. (4) Numeric MQL and SQL thresholds per axis aligned to {{DEFINICION_MQL_SQL}}, with a first-contact SLA per quadrant. (5) A calibration plan: historical data to review, validation against real conversion per quadrant, a falsifiable success or failure criterion, and a recalibration cadence in {{PLATAFORMA}}.

Cover these edge cases: high fit with zero interest, high interest without firmographic data (enrich before scoring), insufficient volume to validate per quadrant, and leads that reactivate after decaying. Justify each weight with business logic, mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION], do not invent conversion figures, and avoid vanity scoring. Without prices. Close with an implementable document of tables in {{PLATAFORMA}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Checkout friction reduction
Evergreen webinar funnel design
prompts.content: Act as a senior evergreen webinar funnel strategist, with proven experience in marketing automation, conversion copywriting and sequence architecture. Design an end-to-end evergreen webinar funnel (automated, measurable by stage and replicable) for the topic {{TEMA_WEBINAR}} and the offer {{OFERTA}}, directed at {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}}, implemented in {{PLATAFORMA_AUTOMATIZACION}}, with a webinar of {{DURACION_WEBINAR}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if applicable. Before drafting pieces, derive the angle and the central promise from {{TEMA_WEBINAR}}, {{OFERTA}} and the awareness level of {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}}; declare which awareness level you assume. Deliver six blocks: (1) Funnel map with stages (ad, registration, confirmation, reminders, attendance, pitch, follow-up, reactivation), main metric per stage (CTR, registration rate, show-up rate, retention to pitch, offer rate, conversion, non-attendee recovery) and a reference target value per stage marked as assumption. (2) Registration page: headline and subheadline oriented toward the transformation of {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}}, 3 to 5 value-promise bullets, social proof, minimum form and CTA, with the angle derived from {{TEMA_WEBINAR}}. (3) Confirmation and reminder sequence: immediate confirmation, 24h reminder, 1h reminder and live reminder, each with objective, suggested subject line and key message to raise the show-up rate. (4) Webinar structure and pitch for {{DURACION_WEBINAR}}: hook, promise, real-value teaching, transition to pitch, presentation of {{OFERTA}}, handling of the 3 to 5 most probable objections of {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}}, call to action and close with legitimate urgency (seats, cohorts or expiring bonuses, never fictitious scarcity). (5) Post-webinar follow-up segmented into at least 3 audiences (did not buy, non-attendees with replay, hot prospects) with cadence, objective and trigger per send. (6) Automation triggers and conditions in {{PLATAFORMA_AUTOMATIZACION}}: which event moves the prospect between stages (registration, attendance, pitch minute reached, CTA click, non-open) and how to avoid duplicate sends or conflicts between sequences. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria and the assumptions made. Brand restrictions: never prices or monetary figures; never the word free or equivalents; argue the value of the offer; neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any data you assume. If any critical data ({{TEMA_WEBINAR}}, {{OFERTA}}, {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}}, {{PLATAFORMA_AUTOMATIZACION}} or {{DURACION_WEBINAR}}) is missing, ask for it before executing. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Funnel micro and macro conversion map
prompts.content: Act as a senior growth marketing analyst specialized in funnel instrumentation and measurement. The business measures {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} only by the final sale ({{ACCION_DE_CIERRE}}), so when conversion drops it does not know at which stage it broke or how far in advance. Your job is to build a micro and macro conversion map for {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} directed at {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}}, arriving via {{CANAL_PRINCIPAL}}, so that progress can be measured stage by stage, leaks detected before they impact revenue and priorities set for where to optimize. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. If {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, {{ACCION_DE_CIERRE}} or {{CANAL_PRINCIPAL}} is missing, ask before continuing; do not invent the business. Proceed as follows: (1) Reconstruct the funnel by stages choosing AARRR or TOFU-MOFU-BOFU according to which fits with {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} and {{CANAL_PRINCIPAL}}, justify in one line and describe the prospect's mental state per stage. (2) Per stage define exactly ONE macro conversion, closing event that confirms advancement, and between 2 and 4 micro conversions that predict it. (3) For each event specify technical name, trigger definition, why it is an intent signal and the capture tool within {{STACK_MEDICION}}. (4) Mark lead indicators of the macro of each stage and propose a step-through rate to monitor between each consecutive pair of events toward {{ACCION_DE_CIERRE}}. (5) Deliver a table per stage (stage, mental state, macro, micro, trigger, tool, step-through rate) plus a diagnosis of the 3 points where a declining micro conversion would reveal a leak before the sale drops, with corrective action. Rules: observable and predictive micro conversions, never vanity; distinguish lead indicators from lag indicators; do not invent figures from the account and mark external benchmarks as an explained assumption; a single coherent measurement strategy. If a tool from {{STACK_MEDICION}} does not exist for an event, mark it as a recommended assumption instead of omitting the event. {{ADJUNTOS}}

prompts.title: Funnel leak diagnosis by stage
Data-based buyer persona construction
prompts.content: Act as a senior marketing and customer research strategist with fifteen years building evidence-based buyer personas (voice of customer, jobs-to-be-done, objection analysis) that translate into campaigns and offers, not decorative profiles. I need an actionable buyer persona for {{PRODUCTO_O_SERVICIO}} directed at {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}, built from {{FUENTES_DE_DATOS}} and not from intuition, so that the team can decide with evidence what to say, in which channel and with which offer; the purpose is {{OBJETIVO_DE_NEGOCIO}} and the decision in focus is {{DECISION_DE_COMPRA}}. If {{ADJUNTOS}} brings material, use it as primary evidence. Before executing: restate the segment, the objective and the purchase decision; inventory the evidence and name the gaps; tell me which blocks are backed and which depend on assumptions, and ask me for the missing data before inventing. If product, segment, objective, sources or decision is missing, ask first. Then deliver, in order: 1) evidence inventory per source with its gaps, separating observed fact from interpretation and marking what is not backed as [ASSUMPTION]; 2) identity and demographics relevant to {{DECISION_DE_COMPRA}}, without filler; 3) context and situation: role, environment, constraints, time budget, purchase moment; 4) functional, emotional and social job-to-be-done; 5) motivations and triggers; 6) pains prioritized by intensity and frequency; 7) objections, each with its message response; 8) decision criteria, alternatives and the option of doing nothing; 9) channels, sources and trusted voices; 10) voice of customer with attributable verbatim phrases; 11) activation map with three anchor messages, two channels and one measurable metric to validate in the field, prioritizing pains and objections by impact on {{OBJETIVO_DE_NEGOCIO}}. Close with three persona risks and the minimum experiment to confirm it. Neutral and professional Spanish, no prices, no the word free, no emojis; zero invented data.

prompts.title: Target customer empathy map
Brand archetype definition
Brand tone and voice definition
prompts.content: Act as a senior Brand Voice Strategist with more than a decade designing verbal voice systems and style guides across multiple sectors. Design an operative tone and voice guide for {{NOMBRE_MARCA}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}} in {{CANALES}}, starting from the personality {{PERSONALIDAD_DESEADA}} and the references {{REFERENCIAS_TONO}}. Objective: so that any team member writes on-brand without expert review and the onboarding of writers and agencies is accelerated. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before advancing; mark every inference as [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent data. Deliver: (1) 4 to 5 voice attributes, each with a one-line definition and its explicit opposite; (2) positioning on four axes (formal to close, serious to playful, respectful to irreverent, factual to enthusiastic), point 1 to 5 per axis with justification; (3) do/don't rules per attribute (lexicon, syntax, sentence length, grammatical person, punctuation marks), each traceable to its attribute; (4) matrix of the same base message rewritten per channel from {{CANALES}} and per three situations: celebratory announcement, response to complaint, incident communication; (5) checklist of 6 to 8 points to audit before publishing. Edge cases: if {{REFERENCIAS_TONO}} contradict each other, signal the conflict and propose resolution; if {{CANALES}} is a single channel, deepen variations by situation; if the sector is regulated, constrain the voice with compliance limits. Neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis. Restate what you understood and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Unique selling proposition (USP) definition
Brand tagline and slogan generation
Brand platform with brand key model
prompts.content: Act as a senior brand strategist specialized in the Unilever Brand Key model, with a track record of aligning teams around a distilled platform that serves as the single source of truth for product, communication and commercial. I want the complete platform of {{MARCA}} with the nine components of the Brand Key, in this order and without overlapping: 1) Competitive roots: legacy and category that give authority. 2) Competitive environment: position versus {{COMPETIDORES}} and the disputed space within {{CATEGORIA}}. 3) Target: {{TARGET}} described by motivations, not just demographics. 4) Insight: the real human tension it resolves, written in the first person of the customer. 5) Benefits: functional (what it does) with its emotional pair (how it makes you feel). 6) Values and personality: 3 to 5 guiding values and a set of traits. 7) Reason to believe: proofs from {{PRUEBAS_DISPONIBLES}} that make the promise credible. 8) Discriminator: the only own, hard-to-copy reason for choice. 9) Essence: a single core phrase, permanent, that distills everything. Before drafting, restate what you understand and present your plan. If {{MARCA}}, {{CATEGORIA}}, {{TARGET}} or {{PRUEBAS_DISPONIBLES}} is missing, ask before continuing; do not invent evidence. Anchor the reason to believe only in real proofs and mark [ASSUMPTION] every inference. Verify at the end that essence, discriminator and reason to believe do not contradict each other and that the insight connects with the emotional benefit. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. Without prices, without the word that denotes absence of cost, neutral Spanish, no emojis. Deliver the nine labeled blocks plus a final coherence test paragraph ready to validate with stakeholders.

prompts.title: Brand positioning statement
prompts.content: Act as a senior brand strategist specializing in competitive positioning: distill a single defensible idea and discard generic promises. I want to fix how {{MARCA}} is positioned in the mind of {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} before writing any message, page, or campaign, to align sales, product, and communications under a single differentiating voice. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First, restate who {{MARCA}} serves, in what {{CATEGORIA_Y_BENEFICIO}} it competes, against what {{ALTERNATIVA_COMPETITIVA}} it differentiates itself, and with what {{MOTIVO_CREDIBILIDAD}} it sustains the promise; if a block is missing or ambiguous, ask about it one thing at a time. Then propose the single differentiating idea that will govern the statement and confirm it with me. Only then deliver: (1) the canonical statement in one paragraph: For {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}}, {{MARCA}} is {{CATEGORIA_Y_BENEFICIO}}, unlike {{ALTERNATIVA_COMPETITIVA}}, because {{MOTIVO_CREDIBILIDAD}}; (2) three variants that shift only the angle of the differentiator while keeping the same audience and category, each with a note on when to use it; (3) the {{ATRIBUTO_DIFERENCIADOR}} one-word attribute the brand wants to own, with a sentence justifying why it is ownable; (4) a three-line message test (headline, subheadline, anticipated objection with response) derived from the statement; (5) a completed checklist of specificity, credibility, relevance, and distinctiveness. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. Do not invent figures, awards, or clients; what is unverifiable goes [ASSUMPTION]. Each block is a single idea, free of empty adjectives, in neutral and professional Spanish, without prices or promises of free anything.

prompts.title: Brand perception and health audit
prompts.content:
Act as a senior brand strategist with experience in brand tracking, brand equity, and multi-category perception studies. I want a brand perception and health audit for {{MARCA}} in the category {{CATEGORIA}}, separating perceived image from desired positioning {{POSICIONAMIENTO_DESEADO}}, locating where the brand funnel breaks down against {{COMPETIDORES}} for the audience {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}}, and unlocking a prioritized investment plan based on evidence, not intuition. Proceed as follows: (1) Map the brand health funnel and define metrics and measurement questions for the four dimensions: awareness (aided and spontaneous), associations (attributes and imagery), consideration (purchase intent vs. {{COMPETIDORES}}), and loyalty (NPS, repurchase, advocacy). (2) Declare the model applied at each step (brand funnel, Keller CBBE, or Brand Asset Valuator) and the proposed weighting for the four dimensions, justifying each weight according to the business objective. (3) Diagnose the current state of each dimension using {{FUENTES_DE_DATOS}}; normalize each dimension to a 0–100 scale, documenting the normalization rule. If a critical data point is missing, ask for it before continuing and mark every estimate as [ASSUMPTION] with its impact on index confidence. (4) Calculate an aggregated and reproducible brand health index, contrast it against the category benchmark, and indicate the confidence level of the result (high/medium/low) based on data coverage. (5) Identify the three most critical perception gaps (perceived image vs. {{POSICIONAMIENTO_DESEADO}}) and prioritize them with an impact/effort matrix. (6) Deliver a gap-closure plan with actionable initiatives, tracking metrics, suggested owners, and a re-measurement cadence; consolidate a one-page executive dashboard (index, traffic-light by dimension, three priorities). Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Edge cases: if only qualitative data is available, declare the index as directional, not statistical; if a dimension has no data at all, mark it as non-measurable instead of inventing a value; if {{POSICIONAMIENTO_DESEADO}} is not defined, ask for it before deriving gaps. Limits: do not invent data or market figures; do not recommend investments without support. Closure: the report is considered complete only if all four dimensions are measured or marked as non-measurable, the index is reproducible, and the gap-closure plan is actionable. Neutral and professional English, without emojis. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before executing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Product or brand naming process
prompts.content: Act as a senior naming and brand strategy strategist with experience leading namings in Spanish-speaking markets. Build a naming funnel that ends in a recommended and defensible finalist trio for {{PRODUCTO_O_MARCA}}, targeting {{AUDIENCIA}}, carrying the promise {{PROMESA_CENTRAL}}, differentiating within the territory {{TERRITORIO_COMPETITIVO}}, respecting the tone {{TONO}}, and, where applicable, the architecture {{ARQUITECTURA_NOMBRE}}. Steps: 1) Restate the briefing and ask for missing data before generating; mark every inference about the business with [ASSUMPTION]. 2) Generate at least 24 candidates in 4 creative routes (semantic roots, territory metaphors, neologisms and fusions, heritage words and language twists), with each route's idea on one line; prioritize volume and variety. 3) Filter in cascade through three sieves, explicitly discarding: meaning (evocation of the promise, no negative connotations in neutral Spanish and relevant dialects, frictionless pronunciation and spelling), availability — ALWAYS as pending verification (domain, registration by Nice class, social handles, clash with competitors) — and resonance (distinctiveness, memorability, tone fit, extension to family). 4) Deliver the trio with rationale, phonetic reading, risks, availability checklist to verify, and a tagline per name. 5) Close with a prioritized recommendation and tiebreaker criterion. Consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Competitive differentiation with the 3C model
prompts.content:
Act as a senior brand and positioning strategist, expert in Kenichi Ohmae's 3C model (strategic triangle Customer-Company-Competition) and applied competitive analysis. Your objective is to find the own defensible competitive space of {{OFERTA}}: the point where a real strength coincides with an important need of {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} that the competition does not cover well, and convert it into an actionable differentiation angle and positioning statement, aligned with {{OBJETIVO_POSICIONAMIENTO}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you understand about the offering, the segment, the strengths, and the competitors; then present your analysis plan; only then execute. If {{OFERTA}}, {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}, {{FORTALEZAS}}, or at least two in {{COMPETIDORES}} are missing, ask for that data before continuing rather than inventing it.

Proceed in three phases. Phase 1: build the three vertices of the triangle independently and with evidence: (a) Customer: from {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}, list functional and emotional needs, decision criteria, and the unresolved pain, ranked by relevance; (b) Company: map {{FORTALEZAS}}, real distinctive capabilities, assets, and honest limitations of {{OFERTA}}; (c) Competition: for each entry in {{COMPETIDORES}}, their value proposition, their strengths, and the gaps they leave open. Do not assert any advantage without support; mark every inference without data as [ASSUMPTION]. Phase 2: overlay the three vertices, discard the spaces where the competition is already strong or the customer does not value, and keep only the defensible intersection where own strength + relevant need + competitive gap coincide. If no clean intersection exists, say so explicitly and propose the strength to build in order to open it. Phase 3: derive a single prioritized differentiation angle, draft a one-sentence positioning statement (for [segment] who [need], [offering] is the [category] that [unique differentiator] because [proof]), specific and verifiable; list exactly 3 risks that could erode that differentiation with an early-warning signal for each; close with 2–3 next validation steps. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if provided.

Deliverable: table of the three vertices, own space justified, prioritized differentiation angle, positioning statement, 3 risks with early-warning signal, and next steps. Neutral and professional English, without emojis. Do not mention prices.

prompts.title: Campaign creative brief
Big idea and campaign concept development
Go-to-market launch plan by phases
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Marketing Director with experience leading go-to-market launches in competitive markets. Design me a fully executable phased launch plan from start to finish for {{PRODUCTO}}, a {{CATEGORIA}} product, targeting primarily {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}, whose main differentiator against alternatives is {{DIFERENCIADOR}}, using channels {{CANALES}}, with target day zero {{FECHA_LANZAMIENTO}}.

Before drafting, restate in two lines what you understand about those five data points; if any arrives empty or ambiguous, ask me instead of inventing it. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] every data point you infer and make explicit that it must be validated with the owner.

Structure the plan in three sequential phases and, within each one, resolve in this order: measurable objective, audience and message, recommended channels, calendar in weeks relative to day zero (format W-4, W0, W+2), assets to produce, and suggested owner.

1. Pre-launch: positioning and value proposition, priority segment and core message, expectation building, interested-party list capture, and assets prior to day zero.
2. Launch: moment of release, announcement sequence by channel, coordinated activation, and entry offer (without mentioning prices).
3. Post-launch: converting interested parties into active users, early activation and retention, testimonials and social proof, and iteration based on data.

Keep the core message coherent from pre to post. Close with: (a) metrics dashboard with one main indicator per phase plus two alert signals per phase with their threshold; (b) the three most likely risks with probability, impact, and mitigation; (c) a no-launch criterion. Professional tone in neutral English, without prices or absolute promises. Deliver a document ready to review with the team and execute.

prompts.title: 360 integrated multichannel campaign plan
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Integrated Marketing Director, with experience orchestrating 360 campaigns in BFSI and technology, expert in the IMC model and the See-Think-Do-Care funnel. I need to orchestrate a 360 integrated multichannel campaign for {{PRODUCTO_O_SERVICIO}} aimed at achieving {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} with {{AUDIENCIA}}, through {{CANALES}}, during {{DURACION}}, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES_MARCA}}. The risk of any multichannel campaign is dispersion: each channel speaks on its own and the brand loses strength. I want a single governing narrative deployed coherently and sequentially, ready to execute without reinterpreting the message in each piece.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate product, objective, audience, channels, duration, and restrictions, and mark with [ASSUMPTION] everything you infer; if any critical data is missing, ask me before moving forward. First fix the governing message and verify that every channel and every phase derives from it: no asset can contradict the big idea. Present your plan before executing.

Deliver these sections in order, with a single recognizable narrative thread from end to end:
1. Core strategy: SMART objective derived from {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, primary and secondary audience with their emotional insight from {{AUDIENCIA}}, differential value proposition, and the creative big idea (governing message in one sentence) from which all assets derive.
2. Channel matrix: for each channel in {{CANALES}}, role in the See-Think-Do-Care funnel, asset format, adaptation of the governing message, call to action, and success signal per channel.
3. Phase sequence: expectation, launch, sustain, and close, with narrative, deliverable, and advancement criterion, adjusted to {{DURACION}}.
4. Editorial calendar: week-by-week table with piece, channel, owner, and dependency.
5. KPI table by funnel stage: metric, goal, measurement source, and review cadence.
6. Measurement plan and risk flags: two or three early signals that would require adjusting message, channel mix, or rhythm.

Rules: respect {{RESTRICCIONES_MARCA}}; do not invent media prices or investment amounts; express any budget allocation as relative percentages and ask for it as data if needed. Professional tone, neutral English, without emojis. Mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION].

Variables:
- {{PRODUCTO_O_SERVICIO}}: product, service, or initiative the campaign should promote
- {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}: business result sought (e.g. qualified leads, registrations, awareness, repurchase)
- {{AUDIENCIA}}: target audience (segment, role, sector, or demographic profile)
- {{CANALES}}: available channels (email, LinkedIn, paid social, search, landing, PR, events)
- {{DURACION}}: total campaign time window (e.g. 6 weeks, a quarter)
- {{RESTRICCIONES_MARCA}}: tone, brand, legal, or message restrictions (optional)

prompts.title: Seasonal and key-dates campaign plan
prompts.content: Act as a senior seasonal marketing strategist with fifteen years designing campaign calendars that connect commercial seasons and observances with real demand moments by category and region. I need an actionable seasonal campaign plan for {{MARCA_PRODUCTO}}, targeting {{AUDIENCIA}}, in {{MERCADO_REGION}}, during {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, with commercial objective {{OBJETIVO_COMERCIAL}}, activating {{CANALES_DISPONIBLES}}; mandatorily incorporate {{FECHAS_OBLIGADAS}} and consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. If brand and what it offers, audience, market, horizon with start date, objective, channels, or mandatory dates are missing, ask me for them before continuing; do not invent the offering or the regional calendar. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First, restate in one line what you understood and present your plan; then execute. Work in five phases. Inventory: list seasonal, commercial, observance, and {{FECHAS_OBLIGADAS}} candidates, each with their exact date in {{MERCADO_REGION}}. Prioritization: score each candidate from 1 to 5 on relevance to {{AUDIENCIA}}, fit with {{MARCA_PRODUCTO}}'s offering, inverse competition, and production feasibility; rank, cut the forced ones, and classify into anchor moments, support moments, and moments to ignore. Concept: for each selected date define a specific angle, value hook (without prices, without the word free), assets, channels from {{CANALES_DISPONIBLES}}, and cadence. Timeline: calculate backwards from each key date the milestones of production start, teaser, and main publication; detect collisions. Consolidation: build master calendar in table, one-page mini-brief per anchor moment, dependencies, saturation risks, and a success metric per campaign tied to {{OBJETIVO_COMERCIAL}}. Declare assumptions and mark with what must be confirmed. Neutral, professional English, without emojis. Deliver the master calendar plus mini-briefs, ready to assign to production.

prompts.title: Pre-launch sequence and hype generation
prompts.content:
Act as a senior product launch strategist, specializing in pre-launch campaigns and early demand building (waitlist, teaser cadence, and ethical scarcity). Your objective is to accumulate qualified demand and sustained attention before {{PRODUCTO}} goes public on {{FECHA_SALIDA}}, so that launch day starts with a base of already-convinced prospects instead of a cold audience. The result is delivered to {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}} through {{CANALES}}.

Deliver these components in order:
1. Sequence objective and success metrics: main metric (qualified subscribers on the waitlist and expected conversion on launch day) plus 2 or 3 guide metrics (teaser open rate/CTR, confirmation rate, cost per subscriber if applicable). Define what counts as a qualified subscriber.
2. Waitlist mechanics supported by {{BENEFICIO_DIFERENCIAL}}: value proposition for subscribing, entry hook, fields to capture (minimum viable, justify each one), confirmation sequence (double opt-in and welcome) and a membership benefit that rewards being inside before the general public.
3. List segmentation: how to distinguish the hottest from the warm ones (brief survey, micro-commitment, behavior) and how to treat each segment differently at close.
4. Teaser calendar in countdown across {{CANALES}}: number of teasers adjusted to {{DURACION_PRELANZAMIENTO}}, angle of each one (problem, partial glimpse, social proof, objection handling, date reveal), the central copy piece of each teaser, and a suggested asset.
5. Legitimate scarcity and urgency mechanisms: limited spots, early access window for the list, visible countdown and registration close, each with a real and verifiable basis. Distinguish genuine scarcity from invented urgency.
6. Day-by-day schedule from start to {{FECHA_SALIDA}}: what piece goes out each day, through what channel, with what call to action, and what metric is reviewed.
7. Contingency plan: what to do if registrations are below expectations at the midpoint of the campaign (correction levers without resorting to false urgency).
8. Pre-launch-day verification checklist.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any.

Work method: Interpret the data, plan the sequence, and only then execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before drafting the detail. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{FECHA_SALIDA}}, {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}}, {{BENEFICIO_DIFERENCIAL}}, or {{CANALES}} are missing, ask before drafting; do not invent data. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION].

Output rules: without prices and without the word free; neutral and professional English, without emojis. Every scarcity mechanism with a verifiable basis; zero invented urgency. Each teaser with a different angle, without repeating the message, with a coherent countdown. The schedule covers every day until {{FECHA_SALIDA}} with piece, channel, call to action, and metric.

Deliverable: ready-to-execute pre-launch sequence (waitlist + segmentation + teaser calendar + scarcity plan + day-by-day schedule + contingency plan + checklist).

Parameters:
- PRODUCTO: name and category of what is being launched
- FECHA_SALIDA: target public launch day
- AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO: who the launch is aimed at
- BENEFICIO_DIFERENCIAL: the core promise that distinguishes the product
- CANALES: channels available for the campaign (email, social media, community)
- DURACION_PRELANZAMIENTO: days of pre-launch before the launch day (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Account-based marketing (ABM) campaign plan
Campaign message structure using the AIDA model
Co-marketing and partner campaign plan
prompts.content: Act as a senior partner marketing strategist with experience in co-branded B2B campaigns and shared demand-gen models. Design an actionable co-marketing plan with {{PARTNER}} to jointly and fairly activate both audiences, with the objective {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}. Audiences of each party: {{AUDIENCIAS}}. Assets and channels each contributes: {{ACTIVOS_CANALES}}. Target window and desired launch: {{PERIODO}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If a key data point needed to support the alliance is missing, ask for it before continuing; if {{PARTNER}} is a direct competitor or the fit of {{AUDIENCIAS}} does not justify the alliance, say so explicitly before proceeding. Deliver the plan in numbered sections: 1) Joint value proposition (what problem they solve together that neither solves alone, shared audience, co-branded angle, and proof that supports the narrative). 2) Fit and objectives (audience overlap and complementarity, SMART objective derived from {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}, a single north metric and two or three guardrails such as unsubscribe rate or spam complaints). 3) Audience sharing (segment each party contributes according to {{AUDIENCIAS}}, legal basis for data processing and consent, who sends to whom, and how to avoid overlap or excessive cross-contact). 4) Shared assets (co-branded inventory based on {{ACTIVOS_CANALES}}: joint landing page, webinar or event, downloadable content, email sequence, social kit, press release; owner of each piece and usage rules for both logos and names). 5) Responsibility sharing (RACI matrix with no ambiguous owner, and which channels from {{ACTIVOS_CANALES}} each party contributes with their estimated reach). 6) Calendar over {{PERIODO}} (pre-launch, launch, and sustain phases with milestones and relative dates, including legal and brand approval window). 7) Measurement and results sharing (definition of shared lead, agreed attribution model, lead sharing and handoff rules with follow-up SLA, KPI dashboard, and joint review cadence). 8) Agreements and risks (minimum terms: brand use, exclusivity, data, term, and exit; risk register with probability, impact, and mitigation; success condition and abort condition). Mark all estimates as [ASSUMPTION] and separate confirmed from inferred. No prices or promises of free offerings; use relative effort and in-kind contributions if discussing investment. Neutral and professional language. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Campaign post-mortem and learnings
prompts.content: Act as a senior Head of Growth specializing in campaign closure and learning, with mastery of objective-vs-actual gap analysis, attribution by channel and by funnel stage, and blameless retrospectives. Your assignment: convert the campaign close into reusable knowledge and deliver an actionable post-mortem. Inputs: CAMPANA={{CAMPANA}} (name, period, and purpose); OBJETIVO={{OBJETIVO}} (measurable objective and targets by metric, KPI with target value); RESULTADOS={{RESULTADOS}} (actual metrics at close); PRESUPUESTO_RECURSOS={{PRESUPUESTO_RECURSOS}} (investment and resources: hours, team, spend in units; no amounts if not desired); AUDIENCIA_CANALES={{AUDIENCIA_CANALES}} (target segments and executed channels); ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}} (files, URLs, or "No attachments"). Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret those inputs; Plan by restating what you understand and presenting your plan before executing; Execute only after that framing. If any critical datum is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before proceeding and do not invent figures. Proceed as follows: (1) reconstruct the case from the inputs; (2) quantify the gap by metric, fulfillment in percentage and absolute value, classifying each as above/on/below-target with an explicit threshold (by default, on-target = 95 to 105 percent of the goal); (3) attribute causes by channel and by funnel stage (reach, consideration, conversion, retention), separating root cause from symptom and marking each unverifiable assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; (4) distill learnings with Keep / Adjust / Drop; (5) prioritize by impact and effort and deliver three to five actions, each with a suggested owner, measurable success signal, and horizon. If data do not allow clean causal attribution (no control, overlapping windows, external noise), declare the uncertainty rather than forcing the cause. Blameless professional tone: analyze decisions and mechanisms, not people. Deliver: compliance table by metric, cause map by channel and stage, Keep/Adjust/Drop block, and prioritized action list. Neutral language, no prices, no emojis.

prompts.title: Multitouch attribution model design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior marketing analytics analyst, specialist in multitouch attribution and media mix, with the judgment to distinguish correlation from causality. Design an actionable and auditable multitouch attribution model that distributes the credit of {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} across {{CANALES}} to underpin {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} within the {{VENTANA_CONVERSION}}. Before executing, restate the decision that motivates the model, the active channels, the conversion and lookback window, the metric to be attributed, and the {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}}; if anything critical is missing, ask for it and do not assume. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] every figure not provided by the user.

Deliver, in this order: (1) Typical customer journey over {{CANALES}}: frequent order of touchpoints, funnel role of each, overlaps, and fit with the {{VENTANA_CONVERSION}}. (2) Diagnosis of {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}}: cross-device, identifiers, costs by channel, and conversion volume; determine whether data-driven is viable (declare the volume threshold you assume for stable estimation) or whether rules-based is preferable, and list critical missing data. (3) Comparative table of candidate models (last-touch, first-touch, linear, time decay, positional U 40-20-40, data-driven Shapley or Markov) with bias, implicit assumption, required data, and when each is appropriate. (4) Recommended model and explicit justification against {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, sales cycle, and data maturity, never by default; state the accepted trade-off. (5) Unambiguous sharing rules: percentage by touchpoint, repeated channels, direct and branded traffic, lookback, and de-duplication. (6) Numerical example applied to a concrete journey, with a table showing the distribution of {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} by channel summing to 100% of credit. (7) Validation plan with an incremental experiment (geo-test or holdout): hypothesis, design, incrementality metric, minimum duration, and decision criterion.

Edge cases: single-touchpoint journeys, view-through without a click, non-trackable channels, and what to do if volume is insufficient for data-driven. Close with model limitations and a periodic review criterion. Do not use prices or the word free; neutral and professional language.

Variables: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} (decision that motivates the attribution), {{CANALES}} (active channels and touchpoints), {{VENTANA_CONVERSION}} (sales cycle and lookback), {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} (metric to be attributed), {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} (available tracking and data).

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Marketing KPI dashboard design
prompts.content: Act as a senior marketing analytics analyst with experience building decision dashboards in Looker Studio, Power BI, and Tableau, and in funnel modeling. Design the complete blueprint of a marketing KPI dashboard to drive {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, read by {{AUDIENCIA}}, over the funnel {{MODELO_EMBUDO}}, covering {{CANALES}} and comparing against {{COMPARACION_BASE}}, to implement in {{HERRAMIENTA_BI}}. Before executing, restate objective, audience, and funnel and explain how they condition metric selection; if a critical datum is missing, ask for it and mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver: (1) metric-objective tree that connects each metric to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and filters out what does not move it; (2) catalog of 5 to 9 primary KPIs mapped to funnel stages (acquisition, activation, conversion, retention, revenue), each with exact formula, unit, source, frequency, data owner, and justification, discarding vanity with the actionable-relevant-comparable criterion; (3) segment and dimension map over {{CANALES}} (campaign, audience, geography, device, period) plus global filters; (4) three-layer layout (executive: 3 to 5 north KPIs plus trend; tactical: breakdown by channel and campaign; diagnostic: funnel plus cohorts) ordered by {{AUDIENCIA}}, indicating for each metric the correct visualization type by analytical intent and justifying it; (5) alert matrix with targets and green/amber/red thresholds by KPI and comparison base {{COMPARACION_BASE}}; (6) governance contract with source table, single definition per metric, review cadence, and criterion for retiring or replacing a KPI. Consider edge cases (incomplete data, ambiguous multi-touch attribution, contradicting KPIs, mixed audiences) and declare assumptions, data limits, and trade-offs. Review attachments {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, and only then Execute.

prompts.title: CAC, LTV, and LTV:CAC ratio calculation
prompts.content: Act as a senior unit economics and growth marketing analyst with experience in subscription and recurring-revenue models. I need a unit economics diagnosis to decide whether to scale, sustain, or correct growth investment. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understood and present your plan; only then execute. Data: total acquisition spend for the period {{GASTO_ADQUISICION}} (includes advertising, salaries of the acquisition team, agencies, and tools), new customers in the period {{CLIENTES_NUEVOS}}, average revenue per customer {{ARPA}}, gross margin {{MARGEN_BRUTO}}, churn rate {{CHURN}} (or average customer life in months {{VIDA_PROMEDIO}} if there is no churn), reference period {{PERIODO}}, and {{ADJUNTOS}}. Proceed as follows: (1) Normalize all figures to {{PERIODO}} and a single currency; list missing data and ask if critical. (2) CAC = {{GASTO_ADQUISICION}} / {{CLIENTES_NUEVOS}}; show the formula with actual numbers. (3) LTV by margin = {{ARPA}} x {{MARGEN_BRUTO}} / {{CHURN}}; without churn use {{ARPA}} x {{MARGEN_BRUTO}} x {{VIDA_PROMEDIO}} and mark the method. (4) LTV:CAC ratio and payback = CAC / ({{ARPA}} x {{MARGEN_BRUTO}}) in months. (5) Validate that churn, revenue, and payback use the same time unit. (6) Interpret against benchmarks (ratio below 1 destroys value; 1 to 3 tight; around 3 healthy; well above 3 possible underinvestment; payback under 12 months comfortable) and issue verdict. (7) Propose three prioritized levers (lower CAC, raise {{MARGEN_BRUTO}}, reduce {{CHURN}}, raise {{ARPA}}). Mark [ASSUMPTION] on every estimated value; never invent figures. Deliver table (metric | formula | result | reading) + one-sentence verdict + three prioritized recommendations + the highest-leverage question about which datum to refine.

prompts.title: Cohort analysis and retention curves
prompts.content:
Act as a senior retention and growth analyst, expert in product analytics and reading cohort matrices for marketing and product teams. I need to understand the real health of the retention of {{PRODUCTO}} by separating the noise from growth: grouping users by entry date and comparing their curves over time makes it possible to distinguish whether the product improves cohort by cohort, where value is lost, and whether changes moved the needle. This feeds investment decisions in onboarding, channels, and retention, and produces LTV projections more honest than a global churn rate.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate the objective, confirm the definitions of active, cohort, and retention type, list missing data, and present your plan.

Parameters:
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} (product, app, or service whose users are analyzed)
- GRANULARIDAD_COHORTE: {{GRANULARIDAD_COHORTE}} (unit for grouping by entry date: weekly or monthly)
- EVENTO_ACTIVO: {{EVENTO_ACTIVO}} (event that defines a user as active in a period: login, purchase, session, key action)
- TIPO_RETENCION: {{TIPO_RETENCION}} (N-day, unbounded, or rolling)
- HORIZONTE_PERIODOS: {{HORIZONTE_PERIODOS}} (number of subsequent periods to measure per cohort)
- SEGMENTO_O_CANAL: {{SEGMENTO_O_CANAL}} (comparison dimension: channel, plan, geography, or segment; optional)

Produce a cohort and retention curve report: (1) Define cohort unit (GRANULARIDAD_COHORTE), EVENTO_ACTIVO, and TIPO_RETENCION; declare each assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. (2) Build the matrix: rows = cohort by entry date, columns = periods 0..HORIZONTE_PERIODOS, cells = percentage retention over the size of each cohort; exclude or flag immature cells (survivorship bias) and report the size (n) of each cohort. (3) Trace superimposed curves; identify floor/plateau, stabilization period, magnitude of early churn (period 0 to 1), and slope of decay. (4) Compare against SEGMENTO_O_CANAL and against time: flag improvements/deteriorations, distinguish real improvement from mix effect, and correlate breaks with launches, campaigns, or channel changes, without asserting causality. (5) Close with 3 to 5 recommendations prioritized by impact on the curve, separating early churn vs sustained decay, each with lever and metric.

Constraints: zero invented figures; every figure supported by data or marked as an assumption; do not infer causality from a temporal correlation. If any parameter is missing, ask for it before building the matrix. Deliver in neutral and professional language.

prompts.title: Measurement plan with KPI tree
prompts.content: Act as a senior Head of Marketing Analytics with experience building measurement plans and KPI trees (north-star metric, driver trees, input-output models) in digital businesses. I need a measurement plan that connects {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} to actionable metrics and traces an auditable causal chain from instrumentable activity to business value, not a board of vanity figures. Consider the candidate north metric {{METRICA_NORTE_CANDIDATA}}, the model {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}, the stages {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}}, the sources {{FUENTES_DATOS}}, and the measurement maturity {{MADUREZ_MEDICION}}. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. Deliver: (1) North-star: 1 north metric aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, its formula, why it measures value delivered to the customer and not just activity, and 1-2 health counter-metrics to prevent gaming; validate or dismiss {{METRICA_NORTE_CANDIDATA}} with an argument. (2) KPI tree: decompose the north-star into level-1 KPIs with an explicit equation (sum, product, or funnel) and each KPI into actionable level-2 drivers with an owner; use {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}} as the skeleton when the model is a funnel; present it as an indented hierarchy showing the mathematical relationship between levels. (3) Metric cards: for each north-star, KPI, and driver provide name, one-sentence definition, exact formula, unit, time granularity, cut dimensions, data source, owner, and goal/threshold with baseline. (4) Instrumentation plan: events and properties to capture according to {{FUENTES_DATOS}}, flag existing vs to-be-instrumented, event naming convention, event -> driver -> KPI -> north-star map, and a data quality validation plan. Rules: no driver is left without at least one event; every inferred figure or target is marked [ASSUMPTION] with the assumption stated; do not invent industry benchmarks, ask if needed; a driver is valid only if a team can move it directly. If {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}, {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}}, or {{FUENTES_DATOS}} are missing or ambiguous, ask before continuing. Close with a document that has a north-star section, an indented KPI tree, a metric card table, an events-to-instrument table, and an event -> north-star traceability map. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: A/B test design with statistical significance
Marketing mix modeling to measure contribution
prompts.content: Act as a senior marketing science econometrician, expert in MMM, time series, and media response curves, with the judgment to distinguish spurious correlation from causal effect. I want a documented Marketing Mix Model that estimates the incremental contribution and marginal ROI of each channel on the sales of {{MARCA_O_CATEGORIA}}, to enable {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} with evidence rather than last-click metrics. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan the approach, and only then Execute. Work as follows: (1) diagnose the data for {{CANALES}} with {{GRANULARIDAD_TEMPORAL}} granularity over {{HORIZONTE_HISTORICO}} and validate whether they are sufficient for inference, ideally two or more years of history; (2) define the exogenous control variables (seasonality, price, distribution, promotions, macro trend, events, competition) so that media contribution does not absorb them; (3) specify for each channel the adstock or carryover and saturation transformations using Hill or logarithmic form, declaring the range of decay rates to test; (4) propose the regression that decomposes sales into baseline plus contribution by channel and reports coefficients, significance, and expected sign; (5) validate with adjusted R2, MAPE, VIF, autocorrelation, and temporal stability, and discard the model if there are unjustified counterintuitive signs; (6) decompose the contribution into volume and percentage and calculate the marginal ROI, flagging saturated and underinvested channels against {{PRESUPUESTO_ACTUAL}}; (7) recommend reallocation toward the highest marginal ROI until marginal returns are equalized, with scenarios and assumptions. Rules: every figure that does not come from real data provided is marked as an assumption and do not invent numerical results; declare the model's limitations (not strict causality without experiments, sensitive to multicollinearity between channels that move together, short window degrades inference). Review {{ADJUNTOS}}; if any essential data is missing, ask me before proceeding. Deliverable: contribution and marginal ROI table by channel, decomposition of baseline versus media sales summing to the total, model validity diagnosis, and a prioritized reallocation plan with scenarios and explicit assumptions. It is a good StrategIA to start from the data and not from inertia.

prompts.title: UTM tagging plan and campaign taxonomy
prompts.content: Act as a senior marketing analytics specialist and campaign data governance expert. UTM fragmentation is the silent root cause of unreliable reports for {{MARCA}}: the same channel appears as facebook, FB, and Meta, campaigns are named manually, and attribution becomes impossible to audit in {{PLATAFORMA_MEDICION}}. I need a UTM tagging plan and a governed campaign taxonomy, ready to adopt as a standard. Before executing, reformulate what you understand and present your plan; if any essential data is missing, ask me instead of inventing it, and mark as [ASSUMPTION] any data you assume. Data: brand or business unit {{MARCA}}; active channels and platforms that will generate tagged traffic {{CANALES}}; time scheme for encoding campaigns {{PERIODO}}; platform where UTMs are consumed {{PLATAFORMA_MEDICION}}; prior conventions or nomenclatures to preserve or migrate {{CONVENCIONES_HEREDADAS}}; attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver, in this order: (1) dictionary of the five canonical parameters (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content, utm_term) with purpose, controlled vocabulary derived from {{CANALES}}, valid example per parameter, and mandatory rule; (2) non-negotiable formatting rules (lowercase, hyphen as only separator, no spaces, accents, tildes, special characters) and deterministic utm_campaign pattern as [{{PERIODO}}]-[initiative]-[channel]-[geo]; (3) medium-source mapping table that blocks invalid combinations and collapses synonyms to a canonical value; (4) governance matrix: role that creates UTMs, central registry prior to publication, validation method, and error-prevention tool that respects {{CONVENCIONES_HEREDADAS}}; (5) migration strategy for already-published URLs and redirect handling to avoid breaking history in {{PLATAFORMA_MEDICION}}; (6) pre-publication checklist and 3 to 5 anti-patterns with their corrections. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria. Deliver everything in tables. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Conversion rate analysis by funnel stage
Demand forecast and marketing pipeline model
prompts.content: Act as a senior marketing analytics analyst specialized in demand forecasting and B2B pipeline modeling, with mastery of funnel unit economics, composite conversion, and sales cycle lag. I need to anticipate how much pipeline and revenue marketing investment will generate before committing budget, to defend the allocation to finance and commercial leadership; the model must separate historical data from projections. Build the model as follows: 1) Normalize the historical inputs from {{INVERSION_Y_CANALES}} and {{TASAS_CONVERSION_HISTORICAS}}, along with {{TICKET_Y_CICLO_VENTA}}; if any critical input is missing, ask me before projecting. 2) Derive and declare the base coefficients: cost per lead by channel, leads per unit of investment, and composite end-to-end conversion rate, traceable to historical data. 3) Project the pipeline month by month for {{HORIZONTE_PROYECCION}}, applying coefficients stage by stage and lagging revenue by the sales cycle to attribute it to the closing period. 4) Generate three scenarios (conservative, base, optimistic) with justified ranges, show revenue sensitivity, and contrast the base against {{META_REVENUE}} if provided. 5) Recommend three investment reallocations between channels prioritized by marginal return. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they exist. Mark every estimated value as [ASSUMPTION] with its range, distinguish historical from projected, and declare the forecast as an estimate subject to the observed rates, without guarantee of results. Edge cases: channel with insufficient historical volume is aggregated or flagged as low-confidence; if the sales cycle exceeds the horizon, warn that part of the pipeline closes outside the window. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliverable: month-by-month table by scenario with investment, leads, MQL, SQL, opportunities, closes, and revenue; explicit coefficients; marked assumptions; and actionable reallocations.

prompts.title: Define the north star metric and its input tree
prompts.content: Act as a senior Head of Product specialized in metrics systems and growth, with experience building north star metrics (NSM) and input trees in products at stage {{ETAPA_PRODUCTO}}. For the product {{PRODUCTO}}, whose value proposition is {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} and whose monetization model is {{MODELO_MONETIZACION}}, I need an NSM that aligns product, growth, and business around the real value delivered to the customer, plus an input tree that translates that north metric into movable levers each sprint, to unlock impact-based prioritization and stop chasing vanity metrics. Analytics data available: {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, reformulate the product, value proposition, monetization model, and stage as you understand them and present your plan; if any is missing, ask before continuing. Then: 1) propose 3 to 4 NSM candidates derived from {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} and {{MODELO_MONETIZACION}}, each expressing customer value and not vanity activity; 2) score each candidate on a five-criterion matrix (reflects real value, is leading with respect to revenue, is measurable today, is influenceable by the team, resists gaming), recommend one, and justify the discards; 3) decompose the chosen NSM into 2 to 4 first-level inputs with an explicit mathematical relationship (sum, product, or weighted average) and bring each input down to 1 or 2 operable sub-inputs; 4) for each leaf define the metric, formula, current baseline (or [ASSUMPTION] if {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} does not cover it), team lever, measurement frequency, and suggested owner; 5) identify the 2 highest-leverage inputs and formulate for each one a falsifiable experiment hypothesis with success metric, threshold, and horizon; 6) define 2 to 3 guardrail metrics and one gaming anti-pattern per input, with the signal that would expose it. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every data point not provided. Deliverable: NSM in one sentence + selection matrix + indented tree + leaf table + the two quarter priorities + guardrails. Neutral and professional Spanish, no prices and no the word free.

prompts.title: Build AARRR pirate metrics tree
prompts.content:
Act as a Head of Product Analytics with experience designing lifecycle metrics frameworks for digital products (growth and retention), fluent in operational event definition and instrumentation. Build me a complete AARRR metrics tree (Dave McClure's pirate model: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue) for {{PRODUCTO}}, model {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}, usage frequency {{FRECUENCIA_USO}}, value event {{EVENTO_VALOR}}, focused on moving {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}}. I want a north metric at the top, the five stages with their primary metric, actionable drivers below, and dashboard-ready instrumentation, to move from a dashboard of scattered metrics with no causal relationship to a tree with traceable levers that show where the real lifecycle bottleneck is.

If any of those five data points is missing or arrives ambiguously, ask me before building anything and do not assume it is a B2B SaaS.

Proceed as follows: (1) Framing: validate product, model, frequency, value event, and target metric. (2) North and skeleton: derive the north metric aligned with {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} and the north skeleton plus the five stages, and justify why the north predicts value delivered and retained. (3) Metric per stage: for each stage define name, exact operational definition (numerator and denominator or counted event), time window, segment, two or three actionable drivers, and instrumentation (events plus properties). In Acquisition consider qualified new users, acquisition cost by channel, and visit-to-registration rate. In Activation anchor the aha moment in {{EVENTO_VALOR}} and define the activation event, activation rate (activated over registered), time-to-value, and onboarding drivers. In Retention fix the window according to {{FRECUENCIA_USO}} (D, W, or M), build a cohort retention curve, N-day or N-week retention, and retention plateau. In Referral define K factor, invitation rate, acceptance rate, and NPS as a proxy for willingness to recommend. In Revenue, consistent with {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}, define conversion-to-paid rate, NRR, LTV, and LTV-to-acquisition-cost ratio. (4) Close: two or three most probable bottlenecks, each with its research question. Deliver the hierarchical tree (north, stage, primary metric, drivers, instrumentation), a table of operational definitions, and a final diagnostic block.

Constraints: do not invent monetary amounts or figures; if a data point is not provided, leave the formula and mark the data as [REQUIRED]. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. No prices and no the word free.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Parameters:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: name and brief description (what it does and for whom)
- {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}: how it monetizes (subscription, transactional, freemium, marketplace, advertising, etc.)
- {{FRECUENCIA_USO}}: expected natural usage frequency (daily, weekly, or monthly)
- {{EVENTO_VALOR}}: concrete action representing the aha moment / first value experience
- {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}}: result the team wants to move (e.g., grow weekly actives, raise NRR, improve activation)

prompts.title: Apply Google's HEART framework to a feature
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Analyst specialized in experience metrics, trained in Google's HEART framework (Rodden, Hutchinson, Fu) and in the Goals-Signals-Metrics method. Operationalize HEART for {{FEATURE}} and deliver a matrix ready to instrument that takes the team from "we believe this works" to defensible metrics that inform {{DECISION_DE_PRODUCTO}}.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, and reformulate your plan in one line, then Execute. If {{FEATURE}}, {{USUARIO_Y_JOURNEY}}, or {{DECISION_DE_PRODUCTO}} is missing, ask me before proceeding; do not invent the feature.

Five phases. Phase 1 (Framing): problem solved by {{FEATURE}}, {{USUARIO_Y_JOURNEY}}, and the {{DECISION_DE_PRODUCTO}} to inform. Phase 2 (Selection): of the five HEART dimensions, mark which apply and which you discard, one line of justification per each; do not force all five. Phase 3 (Goals-Signals-Metrics matrix): one table per applied dimension, Goal in user language, observable Signals of success and failure, Metrics with formula (numerator, denominator, window, unit). Phase 4 (Instrumentation): per metric, event or survey with {{STACK_ANALITICA}}, baseline or how to obtain it, and direction of improvement in {{HORIZONTE}}. Phase 5 (Close): one primary metric, 2-3 guardrails, and concrete measurement risks (gaming, survivorship bias, unstable denominator, novelty effect).

Rules: no metric without a Goal; each metric with numerator, denominator, window, and unit; zero vanity metrics; instrumentation and direction of improvement per metric; one single primary metric; mark missing data as [ASSUMPTION]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver tables by dimension plus block of primary metric, guardrails, and risks. Neutral and professional Spanish.

Variables: {{FEATURE}}, {{USUARIO_Y_JOURNEY}}, {{DECISION_DE_PRODUCTO}}, {{STACK_ANALITICA}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Analyze cohort retention curve
Define the aha moment and the activation event
Measure stickiness with the DAU/MAU ratio
Define counter-metrics to prevent gaming
prompts.content:
You are a senior Head of Product Analytics who designs gaming-resistant metric dashboards, fluent in objective/counter-metric frameworks (counter-metrics, guardrail metrics, HEART, North Star + inputs). Your mission: build an actionable counter-metric system for {{PRODUCTO}}, so that each lever of {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}} is paired with a guardrail that detects damage before it erodes {{VALOR_A_PROTEGER}}. The guiding principle is Goodhart's Law: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure; teams and automated systems find shortcuts that raise the number without creating real value. Consider the {{ETAPA}} of the product when calibrating optimization aggressiveness and threshold severity.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate {{PRODUCTO}}, the metrics from {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}}, and {{VALOR_A_PROTEGER}}; declare explicit assumptions and flag anything ambiguous as to_confirm. Present your pairing plan before executing it.

Produce, in order: (1) Inventory of target metrics from {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}} with their declared intent. (2) Gaming model per metric: the shortcut that would raise the number without real value, who benefits (team, adversarial user, automated system), and its probability and impact. (3) Objective vs. counter-metric pairing table: the counter-metric that monitors the damage to {{VALOR_A_PROTEGER}}, the expected relationship, and why it is orthogonal to the shortcut. (4) Operational definitions: numerator, denominator, window, segment, and source for each target metric and counter-metric. (5) Guardrail thresholds: normal, alert, and blocking levels, with the action for each level. (6) Instrumentation plan: events or fields to capture (mark ASSUMPTION when inferring unconfirmed instrumentation). (7) Conflict-resolution rule for the objective vs. counter-metric conflict, and the responsible party. (8) Review protocol for the {{CADENCIA_REVISION}} cadence: what is reviewed, in what order, and the escalation criterion. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting evidence when available.

Quality rules: each metric in {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}} has exactly one paired and justified counter-metric; each pair explicitly states the concrete shortcut and why the counter-metric detects it; real orthogonality (cannot be inflated by the same move); includes the universal health counter-metric (retention or satisfaction) and a margin or cost guardrail where applicable; no vanity metrics without a guardrail; no made-up numbers; inferred instrumentation marked as ASSUMPTION; ambiguities as to_confirm. Neutral and professional English, no emojis. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{METRICAS_OBJETIVO}}, or {{VALOR_A_PROTEGER}} is missing, ask before executing. Deliver a document ready for the product committee.

prompts.title: Design a multi-level product dashboard
Measure engagement with the L7 and L28 model
Calculate the user growth Quick Ratio
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Head of Growth specializing in growth accounting and retention for digital products, with command of the Quick Ratio framework popularized by Social Capital. For {{PRODUCTO_Y_ETAPA}} I need to know whether user growth is sustainable or whether a rising active user count conceals a churn that is growing in parallel. Before calculating anything, confirm the period {{PERIODO}} and the operational definitions based on {{DEFINICION_USUARIO_ACTIVO}}; if any data is missing or ambiguous, ask me instead of assuming, and warn that the ratio is distorted when the four components are not measured with the same activity window or the same key event.

Then deliver the following. First, the Quick Ratio = ({{USUARIOS_NUEVOS}} + {{USUARIOS_RESUCITADOS}}) / {{USUARIOS_CHURNED}}, with a complete numerical breakdown: numerator, denominator, and result to two decimal places; if {{USUARIOS_CHURNED}} is zero, do not divide: report an undefined ratio and explain that the period only shows gains. Second, the decomposition of net growth = {{USUARIOS_NUEVOS}} + {{USUARIOS_RESUCITADOS}} − {{USUARIOS_CHURNED}}, with the percentage weight of new and resurrected within the numerator. Third, interpretation against thresholds (equal to or greater than 1 gains more than it loses; greater than 1.5 is healthy in an early stage; less than 1 is net contraction) and an explicit verdict of sustainable, fragile, or negative with justification. Fourth, the diagnosis of the dominant lever (acquisition, reactivation, or retention) and the main risk, distinguishing a healthy high ratio from one inflated by acquisition while churn rises. Fifth, 3 to 5 actionable recommendations prioritized by impact and effort for the next period, each linked to the component it targets and with the expected effect on the ratio. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if present.

Mark every inference as assumption, flag the risk of reading a single period as a trend, and suggest comparing two or three consecutive periods before making spending decisions. Write in neutral and professional English, no emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Validate a proxy metric against the real outcome
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Head of Product Analytics, expert in metric design, leading indicators, and lightweight causal validation of proxies. Your assignment: issue a validity ruling on the proxy metric {{METRICA_PROXY}}, which the team uses as a short-term signal for decisions assuming it predicts {{OUTCOME_REAL}}, checking whether it truly anticipates that business value or whether it is a vanity metric or gameable. The Strategy is to separate the signal that predicts from the noise that merely looks good.

I need you to produce: (1) a restatement of the proxy {{METRICA_PROXY}}, the outcome {{OUTCOME_REAL}}, and the causal hypothesis {{HIPOTESIS_CAUSAL}}, with measurable operational definitions for each one (numerator, denominator, population, window); (2) the validation window and the expected lag according to {{VENTANA_LAG}} and the history of {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, justified against the available data depth; (3) four minimum tests: (a) directional correlation proxy–outcome with the correct lag, (b) leading-lag test confirming that the proxy precedes the outcome, (c) convergent validity against an alternative metric of the same outcome, (d) gaming check that detects whether {{METRICA_PROXY}} can rise without {{OUTCOME_REAL}} improving; (4) confounders and biases (seasonality, cohort change, novelty effect, selection, regression to the mean) with a control plan for each one; (5) verdict in one of four values — valid / valid with reservations / not valid / insufficient evidence — with confidence level, the range or threshold of {{METRICA_PROXY}} associated with the {{OUTCOME_REAL}} target, and the decision: adopt, instrument more data, or discard and propose an alternative.

Method: first interpret and restate what you understand and present your plan; only then execute. If {{FUENTE_DATOS}} is insufficient for the leading-lag test, declare insufficient evidence instead of forcing conclusions. Always distinguish correlation from precedence. Mark every unverified claim with [ASSUMPTION] and ask for missing data instead of fabricating it. If {{METRICA_PROXY}}, {{OUTCOME_REAL}}, {{VENTANA_LAG}}, or {{FUENTE_DATOS}} is unclear, ask before continuing. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver a 1–2 page ruling in neutral and professional English, ready to bring to the product committee.

Parameters: {{METRICA_PROXY}}, {{OUTCOME_REAL}}, {{HIPOTESIS_CAUSAL}}, {{VENTANA_LAG}}, {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Trace the frequency power user curve
Write a one-page PRD
prompts.content: Act as a senior product lead with experience writing concise PRDs for executive committees and engineering teams. Write a one-page PRD for {{PRODUCTO_O_FUNCIONALIDAD}}. The problem driving the development is {{PROBLEMA}} and the target user is {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}}. The north-star metric is {{METRICA_NORTE}} evaluated over {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}. If any of these pieces of data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before writing; do not fabricate data. The PRD must fit on one page and have nine labeled sections: (1) Executive summary in two sentences answering what is being built and for whom; (2) Problem and evidence, articulating {{PROBLEMA}} with the signal that justifies it; (3) Target user {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}} and their primary use case; (4) Proposed solution in functional language, without designing the technical implementation; (5) Scope separated into in-scope and out-of-scope, with explicit limits; (6) Verifiable acceptance criteria that define when the solution is ready; (7) Success metrics: {{METRICA_NORTE}} as the north star plus two or three supporting ones, each with a definition and evaluated over {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}; (8) Risks and assumptions, each risk with a mitigation and each assumption marked as [ASSUMPTION] with its pending validation; (9) Dependencies and key milestones with a tentative owner. Work in three phases: confirm the framing, write with an executive tone, refine by separating facts from assumptions. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Never include prices or the word free; neutral and professional English, no emojis. Consider attachments {{ADJUNTOS}} if available. Deliver a one-page PRD ready to circulate in prioritization and kickoff.

prompts.title: Write a Working Backwards press release
Define scope and explicit out-of-scope
Write acceptance criteria in Gherkin format
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Manager with practice in Behavior-Driven Development and command of Gherkin syntax (Feature, Background, Scenario, Scenario Outline, Examples, tags). Your task is to transform the story {{HISTORIA_USUARIO}} into acceptance criteria written as Gherkin scenarios that Product, QA, and engineering adopt as a shared definition of done and executable in a BDD runner.

Context:
- User story: {{HISTORIA_USUARIO}}
- Applicable business rules: {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}
- Prior system states or data: {{ESTADOS_PREVIOS}}
- Expected behavior on errors and validations: {{CASOS_ERROR}}
- Edge cases to cover: {{CASOS_BORDE}}

Steps:
1. Restate {{HISTORIA_USUARIO}} in the As/I Want/So That template and declare the business value.
2. Derive rules, inputs, and preconditions from {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}} and {{ESTADOS_PREVIOS}}. Each scenario traces to a rule; if a rule does not generate a scenario, declare it.
3. Write the Feature block with its description (role + objective + value). Add Background only if the same precondition repeats across all scenarios.
4. Write each Scenario in declarative style: Given (state), When (a single domain action), Then (observable and verifiable result), chaining with And / But. Speak of business behavior, not clicks, selectors, or endpoints.
5. Cover the happy path, two alternative paths, the errors from {{CASOS_ERROR}}, and the {{CASOS_BORDE}} (limits, empty values, concurrency, idempotency). Where several cases share structure and only differ in data, consolidate in a Scenario Outline with an Examples table and parameters in angle brackets.
6. Keyword discipline: a single When per scenario, each Then with a single assertion, zero incidental detail, Examples without columns that no step consumes. Propose useful tags (@happy-path, @validation, @edge, @regression).
7. Close with a Definition of Done checklist traced to the scenarios, plus a business-rule-to-scenario matrix.

Avoid conjunctive steps that hide two actions, UI coupling, scenarios without a verifiable Then, and Examples with unused columns. If {{HISTORIA_USUARIO}}, {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, or {{CASOS_ERROR}} is missing or ambiguous, ask before writing. Do not fabricate rules; mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. Neutral and professional English. Return the .feature in plain text, the checklist, and the traceability matrix.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Draft user stories with INVEST criteria
Define the definition of ready for an item
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Owner with experience leading refinement in mature Scrum teams and scaling product teams. I want you to build an actionable Definition of Ready (DoR) for {{EQUIPO_Y_MARCO}}, calibrated to {{NIVEL_RIGOR}}, plus its application guide. The problem it addresses: the team drags stories into the sprint half-defined, without explicit value, with ambiguous acceptance criteria, or with unresolved dependencies, which causes rework, mid-iteration blockers, and unstable velocity. A well-built DoR turns refinement into an objective filter: only stories the team can actually finish pass to the sprint.

Before writing, confirm the context you need to calibrate the rigor: team type and framework ({{EQUIPO_Y_MARCO}}), recurring dependencies that tend to block ({{DEPENDENCIAS_TIPICAS}}), roles that validate the DoR ({{PARTICIPANTES_REFINAMIENTO}}), and how strict it should be ({{NIVEL_RIGOR}}). If something is missing, ask for it in a single batch instead of inventing it.

Then deliver: (1) 6 to 10 DoR criteria grouped by dimension (value clarity: problem, user, expected outcome; acceptance criteria in given-when-then format with edge cases; resolved dependencies: technical, data, third parties, access; estimation and size: estimated by the team, fits in a sprint, sliced if it exceeds; design and UX readiness when applicable); (2) each criterion in binary form, verifiable with yes or no, without ambiguous adjectives like clear, sufficient, or complete; (3) an application checklist for the refinement session; (4) the 2 or 3 anti-patterns the DoR prevents; (5) a progressive adoption recommendation that does not stall the flow. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] all inferences about the team and do not invent anything as data. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

MetodologIA Protocol: first reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing. Verify at the end that each criterion is verifiable with yes or no, that none duplicates the Definition of Done (the DoR looks at the sprint entry, not the exit), and that the set does not block more than necessary. The final deliverable should be ready to paste on the team's board or wiki, plus a brief application guide.

prompts.title: Agree on the team's definition of done
Translate requirements into a functional spec for engineering
prompts.content: Act as a senior technical Product Manager with experience translating user needs into specifications that engineering estimates and builds without back-and-forth, fluent in Gherkin acceptance criteria and state modeling. Convert {{NECESIDAD}} into an implementable functional specification for {{ACTOR}}, whose success is {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}, modeling the states of {{ENTIDAD}} and respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Define observable behavior, not internal implementation (no database, framework, or function names). If {{ACTOR}}, {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}, or {{ENTIDAD}} is missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent scope.
