Deliver in this order: 1) Problem summary: job-to-be-done and observable outcome, 3 to 5 lines, without a technical solution. 2) Scope: what is included and, explicitly, what is left out. 3) Actors and permissions: who interacts and what each role can do. 4) Behaviors: per interaction, rule in Given / When / Then format, with the happy path and at least one alternate path. 5) State machine of {{ENTIDAD}}: states, valid transitions with trigger, and prohibited transitions. 6) Business rules: numbered and verifiable (answerable true or false), each anchored to its originating behavior or case. 7) Edge cases and errors: empty inputs, limits, concurrency, and failure of external dependencies; behavior and message to the user. 8) Acceptance criteria: testable list that defines done, one per behavior and critical rule. 9) Open questions: ambiguities that block implementation, each with the impact of not resolving it. Mark every assumption derived from {{RESTRICCIONES}} with [ASSUMPTION] and an explicit default value. {{ADJUNTOS}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Enumerate edge cases and error states of a feature
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Product Manager specialized in specifications that survive contact with real users, with the habit of thinking first about how something fails and only then about how it succeeds. I am specifying {{FEATURE}} and my draft only covers the happy path; the real risk lives in what is unwritten: rare inputs, expired sessions, downed dependencies, corrupt data, and business rules at the limits. Each omitted edge case is a production defect or an improvised decision under pressure. I want a prioritized catalog of edge cases and error states before development.

Proceed as follows:
1. Reconstruct {{FLUJO_PRINCIPAL}} in numbered steps as a baseline; each step is a point where something can break.
2. Walk through the flow applying six failure categories against {{ENTRADAS_USUARIO}}, {{DEPENDENCIAS_EXTERNAS}}, and {{RESTRICCIONES_NEGOCIO}}: inputs (empty, min/max limits, invalid format, special characters, duplicates, injection), state (expired session, insufficient permissions, non-existent or already deleted resource, race condition, double submission), system (timeout, dependency down, partial response, high latency, no connection, retries and idempotency), data (nulls, inconsistencies, extreme volume, encoding, orphan records), business limits (quotas, dates, currencies, time zones, eligibility), and security/privacy (permission escalation, data leakage in errors, PII exposure).
3. For each case define the trigger, expected behavior, message to the user (actionable, without leaking technical details), and severity (blocker / degraded / tolerable) with justification.
4. For each blocker or degraded case add a verifiable acceptance criterion in given-when-then format.
5. Where behavior has not been decided, record it as an open question instead of inventing the answer.
6. Prioritize by probability times impact and isolate the 5 critical cases.

Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent constraints not provided. If {{FLUJO_PRINCIPAL}}, {{ENTRADAS_USUARIO}}, {{DEPENDENCIAS_EXTERNAS}}, or {{RESTRICCIONES_NEGOCIO}} is missing, ask before continuing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: edge case table by category (case, trigger, expected behavior, message to user, severity, acceptance criterion), list of open questions, and the 5 prioritized critical cases.

Variables:
- {{FEATURE}}: name and brief description of the feature.
- {{FLUJO_PRINCIPAL}}: happy path or successful flow it must cover.
- {{ENTRADAS_USUARIO}}: types of input it receives (forms, files, selections, parameters).
- {{DEPENDENCIAS_EXTERNAS}}: APIs, payment gateways, third-party services, or internal systems it depends on ("(optional)" if not applicable).
- {{RESTRICCIONES_NEGOCIO}}: rules, quotas, limits, eligibility, or policies that condition behavior.

prompts.title: Build a feature proposal one-pager
prompts.content: Act as a senior Product Manager specialized in product discovery and framing, practiced in hypothesis-driven development and presenting trade-offs to a committee. I want you to build a single-page, dense and scannable one-pager to decide whether to invest team capacity in {{FEATURE}} before committing roadmap. First briefly reframe what you understood and present your plan; if any input is missing, ask before inventing. Structure the document in eight sections in this order: 1) Title and pitch phrase: what {{FEATURE}} is, for whom, and what it unlocks. 2) Context and problem: current state based on {{PROBLEMA}}, evidence from {{EVIDENCIA}}, and why now. 3) User and job-to-be-done: {{SEGMENTO}} and the progress it seeks to make. 4) Falsifiable value hypothesis: 'We believe that [change] for {{SEGMENTO}} will produce [outcome], which we will know if we see [measurable signal]'. 5) High-level solution proposal and what is explicitly out of scope in this iteration. 6) Definition of success: 1 to 3 primary metrics from {{METRICAS_EXITO}} with baseline and target, plus guardrails that must not worsen. 7) Approximate cost in T-shirt ranges (S/M/L/XL) or team-weeks consistent with {{RESTRICCION_ESFUERZO}}, with assumptions, dependencies, and risks; never quote monetary prices or say something is free, reason only in effort, time, and capacity. 8) Alignment question: present {{DECISION_PEDIDA}} as the concrete decision and enumerate alternatives considered, including doing nothing. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Separate facts with evidence from assumptions and mark each unsupported statement as [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver a document that fits on one page, without filler, ready to circulate to the committee and resolve alignment in one session.

prompts.title: Audit a PRD with a review checklist
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Lead Product Manager expert in spec review and quality gating before development. I want you to audit the PRD for {{PRODUCTO_O_FEATURE}} before {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}} approves it and commits engineering capacity, because a PRD with gaps, non-testable requirements, or broken traceability triggers rework, disputed acceptance criteria, and features that do not move the business objective. The applicable rigor level is {{NIVEL_RIGOR}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reframe what product you are auditing, who decides, and at what rigor level; present your audit plan; only then execute. If {{PRD}} is missing or the scope is ambiguous, ask for it before auditing; never invent sections or fill in what is absent: what is missing is reported as a gap.

Audit in this order, closing each axis before the next: (1) Completeness: problem and user, measurable business objective, in/out scope, functional and non-functional requirements, dependencies, assumptions, and risks. (2) Testability: verifiable acceptance criteria (ideally Given-When-Then), metrics with baseline and target, edge cases and error cases; flag what is ambiguous or non-falsifiable. (3) Traceability: each requirement linked to an objective, no orphans or objectives without a requirement, priorities with an explicit criterion. (4) Consistency: internal contradictions, uniform terminology, resolved references, clashes with known constraints. Dig deeper into {{FOCO_CRITICO}} if indicated.

Record each finding with severity (blocker / major / minor), affected section, concrete problem, and actionable correction; zero vague findings. Build the requirement-to-objective traceability matrix that exposes orphans. Close with verdict: APPROVED, APPROVED WITH CONDITIONS, or REJECTED, justified by blockers and calibrated to {{NIVEL_RIGOR}}; if conditional, list the lifting conditions.

Deliverable: (a) findings table by axis with severity and correction, (b) traceability matrix, (c) justified verdict. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Variables:
- {{PRODUCTO_O_FEATURE}}: name and one line of what it solves
- {{PRD}}: full text of the PRD to audit
- {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}: who approves and acts on the verdict
- {{NIVEL_RIGOR}}: light / standard / strict
- {{FOCO_CRITICO}}: (optional) axis or section of greatest concern
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Document the user flow step by step
prompts.content: Act as a senior Product Manager specialized in product specification and user flow design, with UX sensibility and documentation rigor for handoff. I want to document the user flow step by step for {{RECORRIDO_OBJETIVO}} so that design and development can implement it without clarification meetings: every screen, every decision, and every transition explicit, including error paths. The actor is {{ACTOR}}, the flow is triggered when {{EVENTO_DISPARADOR}}, and is considered complete upon meeting {{CONDICION_EXITO}}, on platform {{PLATAFORMA}}, starting from the already defined screens {{PANTALLAS_CONOCIDAS}}. Work in five phases. Phase 1, framing: confirm journey, actor, trigger, and success condition; if any is missing, ask before continuing. Phase 2, happy path: trace the linear sequence from entry to success with exactly one step per screen or state, and for each step specify screen or state, what the user sees, the action they perform, data entering and exiting, the next transition, and the step criterion. Phase 3, branching: at each step identify decision points and list all branches (yes/no, valid/invalid) with the destination step for each; no branch ends in a void. Phase 4, error paths: cover at least failed validation, empty state, expired session, no connection, and missing permissions, each with its message to the user and recovery path. Phase 5, close: define preconditions, postconditions, and open questions. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent data. Deliverable: one-sentence summary, preconditions, numbered happy path sequence, decision point table, error path table with recovery, postconditions, and open questions; navigable without ambiguity. Consider attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{RECORRIDO_OBJETIVO}}, {{ACTOR}}, {{EVENTO_DISPARADOR}}, or {{CONDICION_EXITO}} is missing, ask for them before starting. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Prioritize backlog with RICE scoring
prompts.content: Act as a senior Director of Product, expert in quantitative prioritization frameworks (Intercom's RICE, portfolio scoring, cost-of-delay) with experience ordering backlogs under capacity constraints. I need to convert my backlog into a defensible roadmap: RICE-prioritized queue, cutoff line tied to real capacity, and short list of bets to validate before committing. Data: candidate initiatives = {{INICIATIVAS}}; Reach window = {{PERIODO_REACH}}; available capacity in person-months = {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}; business objective anchoring Impact = {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}; base reach or conversion metrics = {{METRICAS_BASE}}; attachments = {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before calculating, reframe what backlog you are going to prioritize, against what objective and with what capacity, then present your plan; wait for my confirmation. If a critical data point (initiatives, period, capacity, objective, or metrics) is missing, ask for it before proceeding and do not invent anything. Proceed in four phases. Framing: fix the Reach window with {{PERIODO_REACH}} and define Effort in person-months summing product, design, and engineering. Estimation: per initiative estimate Reach (reach per {{PERIODO_REACH}}), Impact on the canonical scale (3 massive, 2 high, 1 medium, 0.5 low, 0.25 minimal) anchored to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, Confidence (100, 80, or 50 percent, without exceeding 80 without solid data in {{METRICAS_BASE}}), and Effort; derive from {{METRICAS_BASE}} when available and mark [ASSUMPTION] on every inferred value. Calculation: apply RICE = (Reach x Impact x Confidence) / Effort, sort descending, and check arithmetic and scale coherence. Close: draw the cutoff line against {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}, isolate 2 to 3 highest-uncertainty initiatives with a concrete validation action, and write the sequencing with dependencies and risks of the order. Deliver a table with Initiative, Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort, RICE, and justification per factor; sorted descending; plus the justified cutoff line and the list of bets to validate. Flag RICE ties and break them by lower Effort or lower uncertainty. Neutral and professional English; no prices or monetary cost estimates.

prompts.title: Classify requirements with the MoSCoW method
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Lead Product Manager who has scoped multiple releases under MoSCoW and defends "no" as a delivery discipline, not a lack of ambition. Classify the candidate requirements for a release using MoSCoW, anchoring each decision to {{OBJETIVO_RELEASE}} (not to who requests it or how much they insist).

Before proceeding, verify that {{OBJETIVO_RELEASE}}, {{LISTA_REQUISITOS}}, and {{CAPACIDAD_O_FECHA}} exist. If any of the three is missing, ask for it and stop; do not invent scope or assume capacity. Use {{STAKEHOLDERS}} only as background information, never as a classification criterion. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide product context or constraints.

Assign each requirement from {{LISTA_REQUISITOS}} a single category, in this order of testing: Must (its absence cancels, postpones, or renders the release useless; legal, contractual, or technically blocking), Should (important and of high value, but the release survives with pain if deferred), Could (desirable, first to drop under any pressure), Won't this time (outside this cycle, explicitly deferred and not discarded forever). Apply the Must test explicitly: if you doubt whether something is a Must, it is not; if a Must depends on another requirement not included, flag that dependency.

Justify each assignment in one line anchored to {{OBJETIVO_RELEASE}}. Mark [REVIEW] when the category depends on absent information and name the missing data; mark [ASSUMPTION] any premise you took. Calculate the proportion of Must effort against {{CAPACIDAD_O_FECHA}}; reason in relative effort or size, never in monetary costs. If the Musts exceed approximately 60 percent, alert the over-commitment and propose concrete reclassifications to leave slack.

Deliverable: four tables (Must, Should, Could, Won't this time) with justification per requirement, the Must weight calculation with its balance alert, a note on dependencies or redundancies, and a release scope paragraph ready to commit. Neutral, professional English, no emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe {{OBJETIVO_RELEASE}} and the constraints you understood, present your plan, and only then execute.

prompts.title: Map initiatives on a value vs effort matrix
Classify features with the Kano model
prompts.content: Act as a senior Product Manager specialized in prioritization and quantitative discovery, with operational mastery of the Kano model (Noriaki Kano, 1984) and its functional/dysfunctional questionnaire. Your task is to classify each feature of {{LISTA_FEATURES}} for {{PRODUCTO}} by its actual effect on the satisfaction of {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} (not by effort or intuition) and return a roadmap sequence aligned to {{OBJETIVO_CICLO}}. The Kano model starts from a fact: not all features move satisfaction equally: some are expected hygiene, others compete linearly, and a few delight without being asked. Work in phases and before executing, reformulate in one line what you understood and present your plan. Phase 1, framing: confirm {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} (Kano classification changes by segment) and normalize {{LISTA_FEATURES}} to atomic, comparable, and mutually exclusive items; if an entry mixes two capabilities, split it. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}, or {{LISTA_FEATURES}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them in a single batch before proceeding. Phase 2, instrumentation: for each feature, formulate the Kano question pair — functional (how would you feel if it DID have this?) and dysfunctional (how would you feel if it DID NOT have this?) — using the canonical five-level scale: I like it / It is something basic and I expect it / It doesn't matter to me / I can tolerate it / I don't like it. Phase 3, evaluation: if {{RESPUESTAS_CUESTIONARIO}} contains data, tabulate the pairs response by response, apply the Kano evaluation table (functional x dysfunctional cross that returns one of six categories: Basic, Linear, Delighter, Indifferent, Reverse, or Questionable when the pair is contradictory), report distribution and dominant category per feature, treat Questionable as a dirty-data signal (not as a roadmap category), and, if volume allows, calculate the coefficients CS+ (satisfaction when present) and DS- (dissatisfaction when absent). If {{RESPUESTAS_CUESTIONARIO}} is No data, declare it [ASSUMPTION], classify by reasoned inference based on the nature of the feature and {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}, and mark each classification as provisional subject to validation. Never invent percentages or responses. Phase 4, synthesis: deliver a table with feature, Kano category, justification, roadmap action, and a temporal dynamics note (a today's delighter becomes basic tomorrow). Action by category: ensure and do not degrade Basics, invest proportionally to weight in Linears, dose one or two Delighters, deprioritize Indifferents, and avoid or segment Reverses. Phase 5, sequence: order the roadmap according to {{OBJETIVO_CICLO}}: unmet Basics first, then highest-weight Linears with CS+, and reserve one or two Delighters; close by naming the assumptions to validate and what evidence would confirm or refute them. Rules: each feature in exactly one category; separate data from inference; what is unsupported goes [ASSUMPTION]; no invented prices or market figures. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Order work with WSJF cost of delay
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Manager with experience in SAFe and flow economics (cost of delay, Reinertsen's queuing theory), accustomed to facilitating prioritization with teams and stakeholders. I need to decide the order in which my team builds {{LISTA_ITEMS}} to maximize the economic value delivered within {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Prioritizing by intuition leaves value on the table and delays the urgent-and-small; SAFe's WSJF converts the discussion into a traceable economic decision that sequences first the short jobs with the highest Cost of Delay.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Parameters:
- LISTA_ITEMS: {{LISTA_ITEMS}} (backlog to prioritize; each item with an ID and brief expected outcome)
- OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} (period business objective against which value is evaluated: activation, retention, revenue)
- ESCALA_ESTIMACION: {{ESCALA_ESTIMACION}} (relative scale; default Fibonacci 1,2,3,5,8,13,20)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} (hard dates, dependencies, regulatory commitments; optional)

If any data is missing, mark it [ASSUMPTION] or ask before continuing; do not invent values.

Proceed as follows: 1) Confirm that each item in {{LISTA_ITEMS}} carries an ID and expected outcome. 2) Estimate in relative terms, comparing items with each other using {{ESCALA_ESTIMACION}}, the four components: Business Value, Time Criticality, Risk Reduction or Opportunity Enablement, and Job Size. 3) Cost of Delay = Business Value + Time Criticality + Risk Reduction or Opportunity Enablement. 4) WSJF = Cost of Delay / Job Size, to one decimal. 5) Order from highest to lowest WSJF, assign sequence position, and justify the top 3 with one economic line. 6) Ties: smallest Size first; if it persists, highest Time Criticality. 7) Flag items with Size >= 13 and propose how to split them. 8) Where {{RESTRICCIONES}} forces ceding the economic order, record the explicit exception.

Deliver a table (ID, description, 4 components, Cost of Delay, WSJF, sequence) with the formula visible, plus resolved ties, splits, and dependency exceptions. Close by reminding that WSJF orders the HOW to sequence, not the WHETHER.

prompts.title: Quantify the cost of delay of an initiative
Prioritize with opportunity scoring of importance and satisfaction
prompts.content: Act as a senior Product Strategist specialized in Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) by Anthony Ulwick and in Jobs-to-be-Done, with mastery of quantitative needs research. Decide where to concentrate product investment for the cycle {{HORIZONTE_INVERSION}} for {{SEGMENTO}} on the job {{JOB_PRINCIPAL}}, avoiding improving what is already well served. First reformulate the job, the segment, and the data source and present your plan; if {{JOB_PRINCIPAL}}, {{NECESIDADES}}, or {{DATOS_IMPORTANCIA_SATISFACCION}} is missing, ask for them before calculating and do not invent figures. Then: 1) normalize each element of {{NECESIDADES}} as a measurable outcome statement (direction of improvement + metric + object + context); 2) assign importance and satisfaction on a 1 to 10 scale to each outcome using {{DATOS_IMPORTANCIA_SATISFACCION}} (explicitly convert top-2-box percentages; if the source is qualitative, derive the value and mark it ASSUMPTION); 3) calculate the opportunity score: importance + maximum(importance minus satisfaction, 0); 4) classify by zone with precise thresholds: over-served if satisfaction exceeds importance, well-served if score less than 10, solid opportunity if score between 10 and 15, extreme opportunity if score greater than 15; 5) rank from highest to lowest score, break ties by highest importance, and recommend the investment focus for the 3 to 5 most important and least served needs within {{HORIZONTE_INVERSION}}, with a justification for each and the warning about the risk of over-investing in what is satisfied. Edge cases: negative gap is truncated to zero; outcomes with missing data are listed separately as pending measurement, not ranked; separate table stakes from real differentiators. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting evidence. Deliver a ranked table (outcome, importance, satisfaction, opportunity score, zone) plus an investment focus block with justification and warnings, and close by noting that the conclusions require validation with a larger sample before committing to the roadmap. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute.

prompts.title: Facilitate a buy a feature dynamic with stakeholders
prompts.content:
Act as a senior product discovery facilitator, expert in Innovation Games (Buy a Feature by Luke Hohmann), prioritization by value and opportunity cost, and group decision dynamics. I need the complete kit to run a Buy a Feature session on {{PRODUCTO}} that unlocks {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}} with {{PARTICIPANTES}}. If {{PRESUPUESTO_TOTAL}} or {{DURACION}} are empty, calculate the former by scarcity and propose the latter; if {{FEATURES_CANDIDATAS}} is raw, refine it. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they exist. Do not invent product data: whatever is missing, mark it as an assumption.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First reformulate what you understood about {{PRODUCTO}} and {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}; then present your plan in four phases; only then execute.

Give me, in a facilitator-ready document: (1) a board of 8 to 15 features refined from {{FEATURES_CANDIDATAS}}, each with a name, a one-line description, and a cost in chips by relative effort and complexity, calibrated so that at least two features exceed the highest individual budget; (2) the allocation of {{PRESUPUESTO_TOTAL}} among {{PARTICIPANTES}} so that the group total covers only 40 to 60 percent of the aggregate cost, with the allocation rule justified; (3) a facilitation script by phases with timings that add up to {{DURACION}}: opening and rules, individual purchase, negotiation and collaborative purchase, closing; (4) the facilitator's probing questions during the purchase; (5) a capture template with feature purchased, chips invested, who endorsed it, objections; (6) the interpretation of the four signals (demanded, ignored, purchased in coalition, abandoned) translated into a roadmap recommendation aligned with {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}, with assumptions marked and next steps. Maintain facilitator neutrality. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Build a weighted multi-criteria decision matrix
Triage pending items with the urgent vs important matrix
prompts.content:
Act as a Head of Product with experience operating saturated product teams, expert in separating signal from noise under pressure. Team {{EQUIPO}} has accumulated more pending items than it can handle in {{HORIZONTE}} and the list mixes the urgent with the important, so attention disperses and the strategic yields to the noisy. Triage {{LISTA_PENDIENTES}} with the Eisenhower matrix against {{OBJETIVOS_PRODUCTO}} and deliver a focus plan.

Before classifying, sanitize: detect pending items without a date, without an owner, or without a declared impact. If a piece of data is missing that changes the quadrant, ask for it and do not invent it; if you proceed with an assumption, mark it visibly as [ASSUMPTION]. Treat urgency and importance as two independent axes: urgency = real time pressure or external dependency with a date, not a feeling of rush; importance = measurable impact on {{OBJETIVOS_PRODUCTO}}, not the preference of whoever requests it or the age of the ticket.

For each pending item, evaluate both axes separately and assign it to a single quadrant: Q1 urgent+important (do now), Q2 important+not urgent (schedule), Q3 urgent+not important (delegate), Q4 neither+neither (eliminate or defer). Justify each assignment in one line naming what makes it urgent and what makes it important, or why it is not. Select the three actions the team executes first: all from Q1 or Q2, never from Q3 or Q4. Calculate the percentage of load in Q1; if it exceeds {{UMBRAL_INCENDIO}} (use 40% if not specified), issue a firefighting-mode alert and identify what Q1 is actually Q2 poorly managed (planning debt). Close with a strategic recommendation: the ritual or process change that prevents repeating the accumulation. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they contribute impact data or dates. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: a table per quadrant Q1-Q4 with pending item, suggested owner, and a one-line justification; a First Three Actions block; a load distribution indicator by quadrant with alert if applicable; and the strategic recommendation. If {{EQUIPO}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{OBJETIVOS_PRODUCTO}}, or {{LISTA_PENDIENTES}} is missing, ask for them before triaging.

prompts.title: Force a stack ranking of competing initiatives
Prioritize by strategic themes instead of individual features
Build a roadmap in now-next-later format
Design a roadmap oriented to outcomes rather than outputs
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Head of Product expert in outcomes-oriented strategy and OKR / north-star models applied to roadmaps. I want to convert the roadmap of {{PRODUCTO}} (today a list of features that does not guarantee moving the business) into a now-next-later roadmap oriented to outcomes, defensible before leadership and with a criterion for saying no.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate what you understand about {{PRODUCTO}}, {{OBJETIVOS_NEGOCIO}}, and {{HORIZONTE}}; classify each item in {{FEATURES_ACTUALES}} as an output or outcome. Then present your plan (outcome > metric > bet chain and prioritization criterion) before executing.

When executing: define 3 to 5 outcomes with leading metric, baseline from {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}} if it exists, and goal within {{HORIZONTE}}, separating business outcomes from product outcomes; connect each outcome to one {{OBJETIVOS_NEGOCIO}}; map each feature from {{FEATURES_ACTUALES}} as a bet under its outcome and mark those that don't fit as discard candidates; prioritize by impact, confidence with evidence, and effort, naming the riskiest assumption per outcome; assemble the now-next-later with advance metric and reprioritization assumptions; close with open questions. Do not invent metrics outside {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}}; what is unavailable is marked missing and estimates are labeled as assumptions. If an essential input is missing, ask before continuing.

Variables: {{PRODUCTO}}, {{OBJETIVOS_NEGOCIO}}, {{FEATURES_ACTUALES}}, {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Fill in a product vision board
Define strategy with the Playing to Win cascade
prompts.content: Act as a senior product strategist expert in the Playing to Win cascade by A.G. Lafley and Roger Martin, with judgment to distinguish a strategic choice from an empty aspiration. Your task is to build an explicit and defensible strategy for {{PRODUCTO_O_NEGOCIO}}, operating in {{MERCADO_Y_SEGMENTOS}}, against {{COMPETIDORES}}, starting from {{PROPUESTA_DE_VALOR}}, and respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}: a strategy is an integrated set of five choices that condition each other in a cascade, not a wish list. Work in phases. Phase 1, framing: reformulate the strategic challenge and verify those inputs; if any is empty or ambiguous, ask for it in a single batch before continuing; do not invent market data or figures. Phase 2, descending cascade, resolve the five decisions in order showing how each conditions the next. Decision 1 Winning Aspiration: what winning means in measurable terms (who to serve, against whom to win, what result), not a generic mission. Decision 2 Where to Play: specific segments, geographies, channels, and categories, and where NOT to play explicitly. Decision 3 How to Win: sustainable competitive advantage, type (differentiation or cost), and why it is defensible in the chosen fields. Decision 4 Core Capabilities: three to five activities the business must master better than anyone and how they reinforce each other. Decision 5 Management Systems: systems, metrics, and routines that build and sustain those capabilities. Phase 3, ascending coherence: apply Martin's tests (the aspiration requires this where to play; where to play and how to win reinforce each other; the capabilities exist or are buildable; the systems sustain them) and correct incoherences. Phase 4, validation: per decision, the validation test (what would have to be true for it to work) and [ASSUMPTION] on every assertion without evidence. Phase 5, synthesis: cascade matrix, fragile assumptions ordered by risk (probability × impact), and the three experiments of greatest uncertainty reduction at lowest cost, with the signal that confirms or refutes each. Rules: measurable and non-generic aspiration; where to play names where NOT to play; how to win declares advantage type and defensibility; each capability tied to a system; neutral Spanish, no prices or invented figures. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Formulate product OKRs by quarter
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Director of Product who has facilitated quarterly OKR planning at digital product companies and knows the classic anti-patterns (sandbagging, output KRs, uninspiring objectives). Your assignment: convert the quarter's strategy into an operable and ready-to-share set of OKRs for {{PRODUCTO}}, avoiding the task list disguised as OKRs. Before executing, reformulate in your own words the strategy, the north star, and the quarter's focus according to {{ESTRATEGIA_O_NORTH_STAR}}, declare the information gaps, and present your plan; if any critical data is missing ({{PRODUCTO}}, {{TRIMESTRE}}, {{ESTRATEGIA_O_NORTH_STAR}}, {{METRICAS_BASE}}, or {{EQUIPO}}), ask for it in a single batch. Then deliver: (1) synthesis of strategy, north star, {{EQUIPO}} scope, and baselines from {{METRICAS_BASE}}; (2) 1 to 3 qualitative, ambitious, and memorable Objectives, without numbers in the statement; (3) per Objective, 3 to 5 outcome Key Results (adoption, retention, activation, revenue, satisfaction, or efficiency), each with metric, baseline from {{METRICAS_BASE}}, goal, and cutoff date tied to {{TRIMESTRE}}; (4) classification of each KR as roof-shot (committed) or moon-shot (aspirational, ~70% is success), with a deliberate mix; (5) dependencies, assumptions, and risks per Objective according to {{RESTRICCIONES}}, marking unconfirmed items as [ASSUMPTION]; (6) one named anti-pattern avoided per Objective. Verify before closing: 1-3 qualitative Objectives without metrics in the title, each with 3-5 outcome KRs, zero activity or deliverable KRs, all KRs attributable to {{EQUIPO}}, and roof-shot/moon-shot mix present. Close with an OKRs table (Objective | KR | metric | baseline | goal | type), a health-check section with result per criterion, and a check-in cadence paragraph (frequency, owner, and progress traffic light). Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Strategy before activity: if a KR does not withstand the question of whether it measures a change in the world or just work done, rewrite it.

Variables:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: product or line for which the OKRs are being formulated.
- {{TRIMESTRE}}: target quarter and year with cutoff date (e.g., Q3 2026, close Sep 30).
- {{ESTRATEGIA_O_NORTH_STAR}}: product strategy, north star metric, or quarter thesis from which Objectives are derived.
- {{METRICAS_BASE}}: current baselines for candidate metrics (activation, retention, NPS, revenue, etc.).
- {{EQUIPO}}: responsible team or squad and their area of control to ensure attribution.
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: dependencies, capacity, fixed dates, or prior commitments (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Align the Reforge product strategy stack
Structure a roadmap by bet confidence levels
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Director of Product with experience managing results-based roadmaps before executive committees and customers, accustomed to defending priorities with evidence and to distinguishing commitment from aspiration. A roadmap that promises everything with the same firmness loses credibility the moment an unvalidated bet falls through; structuring initiatives by confidence level turns the roadmap into an honest strategic instrument that communicates what is firm and what is in exploration without overpromising.

Restructure the roadmap of {{PRODUCTO}} into three confidence levels in service of {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} within {{HORIZONTE}}, starting from {{INICIATIVAS_Y_EVIDENCIA}}. Deliver to me: (1) the criterion for each level, (2) each initiative classified with its evidence and risk assumption, (3) the promotion path per initiative, (4) the roadmap table by levels, and (5) a communication note calibrated to {{AUDIENCIA}}.

Define the three levels as follows: Committed (high confidence: validated problem, defined solution, clear dependencies, assigned capacity), Probable (medium confidence: validated problem but solution or scope in exploration), Exploratory (low confidence: hypothesis or bet without sufficient evidence). Classify each initiative from {{INICIATIVAS_Y_EVIDENCIA}} in exactly one level, citing the concrete evidence that supports it and naming the main assumption that puts it at risk; any initiative without citable evidence defaults to exploratory. For each one define the experiment, data point, or validation that would move it up a level, and for committed ones the data point that would demote it. Do not promise dates for anything not committed within {{HORIZONTE}} and mark with [ASSUMPTION] everything you infer. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, use them as citable evidence.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, or {{INICIATIVAS_Y_EVIDENCIA}} is missing, ask before continuing. Close only when each initiative is in a single level, with cited evidence, risk assumption, and promotion path, aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and {{HORIZONTE}}, and the note to {{AUDIENCIA}} explains how to read the levels without overpromising.

prompts.title: Scan the product environment with PESTEL
prompts.content: Act as a senior product strategist specializing in macro-environment analysis, with experience translating external signals into roadmap decisions. I want an actionable PESTEL scan of {{PRODUCTO}} for {{SEGMENTO}} in {{GEOGRAFIA}} within a horizon of {{HORIZONTE}}, oriented to {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}}. Before executing, reformulate in one or two lines what you understood and present your plan; if a key piece of data is missing, ask me and do not invent. Proceed as follows: (1) Frame the scope (product and value proposition, {{SEGMENTO}}, {{GEOGRAFIA}}, {{HORIZONTE}}) and list as an explicit assumption everything not confirmed. (2) Sweep the six dimensions one by one — Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, Legal — and per dimension identify 2 to 4 concrete and specific forces for {{PRODUCTO}}, never generic ones; per force record description, direction (threat or opportunity), estimated horizon, and evidence or the marker [ASSUMPTION] when there is no verifiable backing. (3) Prioritize all forces in an impact matrix (high/medium/low) by probability (high/medium/low) and isolate the critical ones (high impact with medium or high probability). (4) Translate each critical force into an actionable implication — roadmap adjustment, hypothesis to validate, risk to mitigate, or bet to explore — connected to {{OBJETIVO_ESTRATEGICO}} when applicable, and name a tentative owner or responsible area. (5) Close with three prioritized strategic moves and a panel of early signals to monitor, each with its trigger threshold and the PESTEL dimension it watches. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, use them as primary evidence and cite them; anything not there is marked [ASSUMPTION]. Rules: do not invent figures or facts; separate facts from inferences; if two forces point in opposite directions, make the tension explicit rather than averaging them. Deliver in neutral, professional Spanish, with a table per dimension, the prioritization matrix, and the synthesis section.

prompts.title: Design a blue ocean move with eliminate-reduce-raise-create
Write product principles that guide decisions
Summarize the roadmap in a single slide for executives
prompts.content: Act as a senior Director of Product with experience presenting roadmaps to executive committees and boards of directors, fluent in Now-Next-Later and OKR. Convert the roadmap of {{PRODUCTO}} for {{PERIODO}} into the text content of a single executive slide, ready to paste into a template, plus the 20-second opening script, calibrated to {{AUDIENCIA_EJECUTIVA}}. Senior leadership does not need the backlog: they need to understand in under 90 seconds where {{PRODUCTO}} is going, what bets are being placed, and how success will be measured, so they can make the decision the slide must enable. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret (reframe {{INICIATIVAS_ROADMAP}} and the decision at stake, list critical gaps and ask about them before proceeding), Plan (present the 4-zone structure and the mapping of each input to its cell), Execute. Produce: (1) a single-line title-thesis with the Strategy of {{PERIODO}}, the why above the what; (2) the bets from {{INICIATIVAS_ROADMAP}} in Now / Next / Later horizons, 3 to 5 total with explicit priority, without falsely precise dates, each with the customer or business problem it solves; (3) 1–2 outcome goals per horizon translated from {{METAS_NEGOCIO}}, each with a metric and baseline; if the baseline is missing, flag [ASSUMPTION] and ask for it; (4) 2–3 dependencies or risks from {{DEPENDENCIAS_RIESGOS}} to unblock as a footnote; (5) 20-second opening script. One idea per cell; horizons over dates; business language with no jargon; assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. No prices; no the word free; maximum one Strategy per output. Variables: {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PERIODO}}, {{INICIATIVAS_ROADMAP}}, {{METAS_NEGOCIO}}, {{AUDIENCIA_EJECUTIVA}}, {{DEPENDENCIAS_RIESGOS}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any is missing, ask for it before drafting.

prompts.title: Audit the coherence between roadmap and strategy
Measure product-market fit with the Sean Ellis survey
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Growth Lead specializing in product-market fit, with direct experience applying the Sean Ellis method to early-stage digital products. I need an honest reading of whether {{PRODUCTO}} has product-market fit before deciding whether to scale acquisition or keep iterating on {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}. If any data is missing, ask me before proceeding; never invent figures or counts.

Deliver four blocks. Block 1, instrument: core question with exact canonical wording "How disappointed would you be if you could no longer use {{PRODUCTO}}?" and the four canonical options Very disappointed / Somewhat disappointed / Not disappointed / Not applicable because I no longer use it; three open follow-up questions (what type of person would benefit most, what is the main benefit, how to improve it) plus one closed role or segment question for cross-tabs. Block 2, sampling: apply {{FILTRO_ACTIVIDAD}} to include only those who have experienced the core value within {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}, exclude "Not applicable because I no longer use it" from the denominator, require a minimum of 40 valid responses (below that, result is directional only), specify the send channel, and warn about survivorship and non-response bias. Block 3, reading: if {{RESPUESTAS_POR_OPCION}} contains counts, calculate the Sean Ellis score = percentage of "Very disappointed" over valid responses; if not, leave the formula ready and ask for the counts; report the full distribution and, if N allows, an approximate confidence interval flagged as an estimate. Interpret against the ranges: 40 percent or more signals PMF (scale); 25 to 40 percent incipient fit (iterate on the "Very disappointed"); below 25 percent no fit (revisit segment and value proposition). Block 4, action plan: common traits of the "Very disappointed," most cited benefit by that group, and 2 to 3 prioritized levers to move "Somewhat disappointed" toward "Very disappointed." Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any.

Treat the 40 percent threshold as an empirical benchmark, not an absolute law: qualify by category and market maturity. Flag every estimate as [ASSUMPTION]. Close with the full document: instrument ready to send, sampling plan, interpreted score (or formula ready) and action plan. No prices; neutral and professional English.

Parameters:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: product or feature whose product-market fit is being measured.
- {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}: target segment to survey.
- {{FILTRO_ACTIVIDAD}}: criterion that defines a user who has already experienced the core value.
- {{RESPUESTAS_POR_OPCION}}: count per option (Very/Somewhat/Not/Not applicable) if data already exists, or "No data yet".
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Diagnose PMF with the retention engine
Isolate the segment with the highest product-market fit
prompts.content: Act as a senior Head of Product Growth specializing in quantitative product-market fit, with experience measuring fit by segment in subscription products. Your task is to isolate the subgroup of users who love {{PRODUCTO}} the most, because averaging fit across the entire base hides where the product has already won and disperses focus. Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe which product and stage you are analyzing, what data you have, and how you define an active user according to {{METRICA_USO_RECURRENTE}}; if a critical variable is missing, ask for it before proceeding and propose a proxy if the formal survey does not exist. Proceed as follows. (1) Define the segment universe from {{DIMENSIONES_SEGMENTACION}} and set the active user rule with its cadence according to {{METRICA_USO_RECURRENTE}}. (2) Apply the Sean Ellis 40% test by segment using {{SENAL_DECEPCION}}: percentage of very disappointed per cut; report aggregate and by segment, and flag as inconclusive any segment with fewer than 30–40 responses. (3) Build the retention curve by cohort and by segment from {{DATOS_USUARIOS}}; distinguish curves that flatten into a positive plateau (fit) from those that decay toward zero, and indicate the time horizon. (4) Triangulate three signals per segment: intensity of disappointment, shape of the curve, and super-user behavior (frequency, breadth of features, expansion or referrals). (5) Rank the segments and name the winner with a concrete profile: who they are, what they do, why they love the product, what job it solves. (6) Deliver 3 to 5 prioritized product and go-to-market moves to double down, plus 2 to 3 false signals to watch for. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Rules: flag [ASSUMPTION] for every inference not supported by {{DATOS_USUARIOS}}; do not recommend abandoning profitable segments even if they are not the winner; explicitly state the survivorship bias and how you compensate for it. Deliver a report with a fit table by segment (disappointment percentage, retention reading, super-user profile, sample size and confidence), justified winning segment, and prioritized moves with their expected success signal.

prompts.title: Map fit with the value proposition canvas
Define the minimum lovable product
prompts.content: Act as a senior Head of Product who has taken several products from zero to traction and masters discovery, jobs-to-be-done, and prioritization by delight, not just functionality. Define the Minimum Lovable Product (MLP) of {{PRODUCTO}} for {{SEGMENTO}}: the minimum set that people love, not just the one that proves the product works (MVP). If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{SEGMENTO}}, {{JOB_TO_BE_DONE}}, {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}}, or {{CAPACIDADES_CANDIDATAS}} are missing, ask before executing; if {{CRITERIO_DELEITE}} is missing, infer it from the job and flag it as an assumption. Deliver, in this order: (1) Framing: the central problem of {{SEGMENTO}} and the specific moment of greatest friction when solving {{JOB_TO_BE_DONE}} with {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}}. (2) Three-layer table for each capability from {{CAPACIDADES_CANDIDATAS}}, classified into exactly one: functionally indispensable (without this the job cannot be completed), reliable (without this there is no trust to repeat), lovable (converts use into preference); one-line justification; if it fits none, flag as discardable. (3) Delight moment: the exact instant in the journey where the user feels this is for me, and the lowest-cost lovable capability that activates it according to {{CRITERIO_DELEITE}}. (4) MLP definition: the union of what is functionally indispensable plus the single prioritized delight capability; explicitly state the MVP vs. MLP boundary. (5) Exclusions: what is left out, why, and the re-inclusion criterion. (6) Love signal: observable metric with baseline, success threshold, and window, distinguishing leading from lagging signal. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide evidence. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; reframe and present your plan before executing. Avoid lovable theater, never prices nor anything free, flag assumptions as such.

prompts.title: Diagnose positioning with the product-market fit pyramid
Complete a lean canvas for the product
prompts.content: Act as a senior Product Strategist practitioner of Lean Startup (Lean Canvas by Ash Maurya, pirate metrics AARRR by Dave McClure), with experience taking products from zero to traction. I need a one-page Lean Canvas for {{PRODUCTO}} that condenses its business model and, above all, exposes the riskiest hypotheses and orders what to validate first before investing more time or capital. The value is in separating assumptions from facts, not in filling boxes. Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the task, Plan your approach, and only then Execute; reframe what you understand and present your plan before proceeding. First confirm {{PRODUCTO}}, {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} with its early adopters, and {{PROBLEMA_Y_EVIDENCIA}}; if something critical is missing or ambiguous, ask me 2 to 3 questions before continuing and do not invent data. Use {{ETAPA}} to calibrate expected rigor and {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}} as a monetization hypothesis to falsify (not as a fact). Then complete the nine blocks in Lean Canvas reasoning order: 1) Customer segments and early adopters, 2) Top-3 problem plus existing alternatives showing how the customer solves it today, 3) Unique value proposition sharpened plus a high-level concept of the X for Y type, 4) Solution with 3 minimum features mapped 1:1 to the 3 problems, 5) Channels and their scalability assumption, 6) Revenue streams and cost structure describing the model and economic drivers without invented prices, 7) Key metrics for this stage chained to AARRR, 8) Unfair advantage that is hard to copy or buy. Keep problem and solution separate. For each block label certainty VALIDATED, ASSUMPTION, or UNKNOWN, name the underlying hypothesis, and if you mark VALIDATED, cite the evidence that supports it. Identify the riskiest hypothesis per block and propose a falsifiable experiment: what to measure, minimum size or duration, success and failure criterion. Close by prioritizing all hypotheses by risk × uncertainty and recommend which to validate first and why, distinguishing product risk, customer risk, and market risk. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Deliver the one-page Lean Canvas plus the table of prioritized hypotheses with their experiment. Neutral and professional English, no prices and no the word free.

prompts.title: Define the ideal customer profile for the product
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Head of Product in SaaS B2B, specialist in evidence-based go-to-market and value segmentation. Your objective is to define a sharp ICP for {{PRODUCTO}}: the account or user that gets maximum value and is, at the same time, easy and profitable to serve under {{RESTRICCION_SERVICIO}}. Remember the key distinction: the ICP answers who we should sell to (the account), not to be confused with the buyer persona (who decides or uses within that account).

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reframe in your own words {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}, and the value proposition; explicitly declare the information gaps. Then present your plan in five phases and, only then, execute.

Execute as follows: (1) Framing: synthesize the context crossing {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}, {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}, and {{DATOS_CLIENTES}}; list what is missing. (2) Value patterns: separate high-value accounts (retain, expand, refer) from low-value ones according to {{DATOS_CLIENTES}} and extract only the discriminating attributes (firmographic, technographic, behavioral), not all. (3) Cost to serve: weigh each candidate segment by effort and risk (sales cycle, acquisition cost, onboarding, support, churn risk) under {{RESTRICCION_SERVICIO}}, as a pair of the value axis. (4) ICP synthesis: definition in one sentence, inclusion criteria (must-have observables or verifiable in discovery), exclusion criteria (anti-patterns, each with the churn or overcost reason), verifiable qualification signals, and typical trigger event. (5) Operationalization: translate the ICP into a 6 to 8 criterion weighted scorecard with high/medium/low thresholds usable by sales in a call.

Flag as [ASSUMPTION] every claim without supporting data. If {{DATOS_CLIENTES}} or {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}} are insufficient to discriminate segments, ask for that data before inferring. Edge cases: pre-revenue product (hypothetical ICP, everything [ASSUMPTION] to validate); high-value segments with opposing costs to serve (declare trade-off and recommend primary focus with criterion); aspirational signals (reframe as verifiable or discard). Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide evidence.

Deliverable: ICP document (definition in one sentence, inclusion, exclusion with reason, signals, trigger event) plus a 6 to 8 criterion weighted qualification scorecard with high/medium/low thresholds, ready to prioritize pipeline.

Parameters:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: name and one-line description of the product to profile.
- {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}: main problem it solves and central value proposition.
- {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}}: universe of accounts or users to which it is sold or aspires to sell.
- {{DATOS_CLIENTES}}: current customers, retention, expansion, success cases, and churn ("no data" if none).
- {{RESTRICCION_SERVICIO}}: limits on acquisition cost, onboarding, support, or sales cycle that define "easy to serve" (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Detecting early signals of lack of product-market fit
prompts.content:
Act as a senior early-stage product leader, expert in cohort retention and product-market fit validation (Sean Ellis framework criterion and Reforge-style retention), with the discipline to separate signal from noise. I want to know, before investing more in scaling, whether {{PRODUCTO}} has real product-market fit or is simulating traction: confusing forced growth with fit leads to burning resources on an engine that stalls as soon as spending drops. I need an honest diagnosis that unlocks the correct decision between doubling down, pivoting the segment, or reformulating the problem.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate what you understand ({{PRODUCTO}}, {{SEGMENTO}}, {{MOMENTO_VALOR}}, and which metrics exist in {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}}) and flag gaps; then present the plan (which signals you will evaluate by family and what assumptions you declare when a data point is missing); only then execute. Ask me for any missing data instead of inventing it. Never fabricate figures: every absent data point is requested or marked [ASSUMPTION] with its reason.

Data:
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} (name and brief description of the product or feature to evaluate)
- SEGMENTO: {{SEGMENTO}} (current segment or target ICP being served)
- METRICAS_DISPONIBLES: {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}} (retention/cohorts, churn, NPS, referrals, CAC, paid vs. organic mix, or whatever is available)
- MODELO_CRECIMIENTO: {{MODELO_CRECIMIENTO}} (how customers are acquired today: paid, organic, sales, mixed)
- MOMENTO_VALOR: {{MOMENTO_VALOR}} (core action representing delivered value: the aha moment and its expected frequency)
- ETAPA: {{ETAPA}} (product stage and age; optional)

Evaluate the three signal families: (1) retention and churn; (2) word of mouth and organic demand; (3) forced growth. Classify each signal as red, amber, or green with framework justification and explicitly mark what is expected early-stage noise. Identify the 3 most critical flags prioritized by impact on fit. Propose the most probable root cause narrowed to one hypothesis (wrong segment, insufficiently urgent problem, or inadequate solution) with its reason and a counter-hypothesis that would falsify it. Close with the next concrete validation experiment: hypothesis, action, metric, success threshold, and time window.

Deliverable: signals matrix, fit verdict (no fit / fragile fit / emerging fit) with its confidence level, 3 critical flags prioritized, probable root cause with counter-hypothesis, and next experiment with metric and threshold. Professional English, no meta-commentary.

prompts.title: Repositioning the product with April Dunford's method
prompts.content:
Act as a senior product positioning strategist, expert in April Dunford's method (Obviously Awesome) and in B2B and B2C market research. Reposition a product the market does not understand, compares with the wrong category, or whose differential value it does not perceive — starting from the premise that value is discovered and the category is chosen to make that value obvious.

Input data:
- Product: {{PRODUCTO}}
- Current customer: {{CLIENTE_ACTUAL}}
- Symptom of bad positioning: {{SINTOMA_DE_MAL_POSICIONAMIENTO}}
- Alternatives perceived by prospects (include status quo, optional): {{ALTERNATIVAS_PERCIBIDAS}}
- Current market category (optional): {{CATEGORIA_ACTUAL}}

Before executing, reformulate what the product is, who it serves today, and why the current positioning fails; mark as assumption any unprovided data and ask for whatever critical information is missing.

Then deliver the framework as a causal chain where each link is derived from the previous one:
1. Real competitive alternatives: what the customer would do without the product, always including the status quo (doing nothing, spreadsheets, manual processes).
2. Unique attributes: what the product has that alternatives do not.
3. Value per attribute: concrete benefit, quantified where possible (time, money, risk, effort). Discard attributes with no demonstrable value.
4. Segment that values it most: profile with observable characteristics; note if it differs from the current customer.
5. Market category: the one that makes the value obvious; justify against the current one and consider at least one alternative category with its trade-off (expectations it activates, competitors it invokes, market education effort).
6. Statement in Dunford format and three tests to validate it with real customers, each with a success criterion.

Statement structure: for [segment] who [need or trigger], [product] is [category] that [differential value], unlike [alternatives], because [unique attributes].

Quality: alternatives include status quo; no attribute orphaned of value; no value without segment; no empty adjectives; category justified and not by default; three executable tests (discovery interviews, customer mirror language, A/B message test) with success criterion; assumptions marked; nothing invented.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Instrumenting a continuous PMF tracking score
Designing an A/B experiment with hypothesis and MDE
prompts.content: Act as a senior product experimentation expert (growth + applied data science), fluent in frequentist inference, power calculation, and validity bias detection. I want to design a pre-registrable A/B experiment to decide with causal evidence about {{CAMBIO_PROPUESTO}}, rather than deciding by opinion. The complete design must be frozen before the test is turned on, because changing criteria after seeing data invalidates the inference. Deliver a pre-registrable document containing: (1) falsifiable hypothesis: 'because we observe [evidence], we believe that {{CAMBIO_PROPUESTO}} will produce [directional effect] on {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}}; we will know when [threshold]', including the assumed causal mechanism; (2) primary metric with exact operational definition of {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} (trigger event, randomization unit, attribution window, inclusion criterion) plus 1-2 guardrail metrics, discarding vanity ones; (3) statistical framework with H0 and H1, appropriate test (z for proportions or t for means), one or two tails justified, and handling of the analysis unit if it differs from the randomization unit; (4) parameters from {{BASELINE_ACTUAL}} and {{MDE_OBJETIVO}}: absolute and relative MDE, alpha, power, and allocation ratio, justifying each choice against the cost of false positive versus false negative; (5) sample size per arm and duration with {{TRAFICO_SEMANAL}}, rounded to complete weeks, showing the formula and variance assumptions; (6) validity guardrails: anti-peeking or sequential correction, SRM, exclusions, novelty effect, and contamination between arms; (7) pre-registered decision criterion with threshold (ship / no ship / iterate) and expected confidence interval. Respect {{RESTRICCIONES}} if provided and consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{BASELINE_ACTUAL}}, {{MDE_OBJETIVO}}, or {{TRAFICO_SEMANAL}} are missing, stop and ask; do not invent figures and mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. If the desired power does not fit within the traffic and window, show the trade-off between more time, larger MDE, or lower power. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Calculating sample size and duration for a test
Designing an MVP to validate the idea at minimum cost
Setting up a fake door demand test
prompts.content: Act as a senior product experimentation and demand discovery expert, with mastery of smoke tests, sample sizing, and research ethics. I want to set up a fake door test to validate whether {{SEGMENTO}} truly demands {{FUNCIONALIDAD}} before investing engineering in building it: I expose an entry point in {{CANAL_EXPOSICION}} as if the feature already existed, capture the intent on click, and show an honest in-progress message. Before starting, confirm {{FUNCIONALIDAD}}, {{SEGMENTO}}, {{CANAL_EXPOSICION}}, {{TASA_OBJETIVO}}, and {{NIVEL_CONFIANZA}}; if a critical data point is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it. Then deliver: (1) falsifiable hypothesis 'if we expose {{FUNCIONALIDAD}} to {{SEGMENTO}}, we expect a click rate of at least {{TASA_OBJETIVO}}', with primary metric CTR on the door and guardrails (bounce, complaints, unsubscriptions, NPS of those exposed); (2) control version and exposure condition, plus the criterion to distinguish genuine interest from accidental click or curiosity; (3) exact exposure point in {{CANAL_EXPOSICION}}, trigger copy, and honest post-click screen copy with no inducement to deception, with an optional one-question micro-survey; (4) sample sizing and duration to conclude at {{NIVEL_CONFIANZA}} with the proportions method, visible formula, and baseline rate assumption, covering at least one usage cycle of {{SEGMENTO}}; (5) binary decision threshold around {{TASA_OBJETIVO}} (build / iterate / discard) and how to read the gray zone close to the threshold; (6) instrumentation plan with event, attributes, and per-user deduplication; (7) communication script for those who left their email, closing the loop with dignity; (8) ethical and reputational risks with mitigation, including exposure limit per user. Mark every estimate as [ASSUMPTION]. No prices or the word free; neutral, professional English. ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Designing a Wizard of Oz experiment
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Discovery Lead, expert in hypothesis validation and low-cost experiments before writing code. Design a ready-to-execute Wizard of Oz experiment, where {{SEGMENTO}} perceives an automated system while a person manually executes the backend, to validate whether {{FUNCIONALIDAD}} generates real value. First reformulate {{FUNCIONALIDAD}} and {{SEGMENTO}}, and declare the value hypothesis as a falsifiable statement (we believe {{SEGMENTO}} values [outcome] enough to take [observable action]), with the exact condition that would refute it. Then deliver: 1) the facade, precisely separating what the user sees and does versus what the wizard executes behind the scenes (intake, manual processing, output delivery with credible latency); 2) the wizard's operational script, with numbered steps, target response times, tone, output templates, and rules for unanticipated cases, executable by a third party without context; 3) the instrumentation: activation event, primary decision metric aligned with {{METRICA_EXITO}} and its quantitative threshold, secondary metrics, and qualitative signals; 4) minimum sample, duration, and stopping criteria for success, failure, and ethical or operational risk, within {{RESTRICCIONES}}; 5) method risks (wizard bias, non-scalability, user expectations, handling of real data) with mitigation; 6) the build/iterate/discard decision rule and the next experiment. Explicitly address the ethical handling of the simulation and of real data within {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. If {{FUNCIONALIDAD}}, {{SEGMENTO}}, or {{METRICA_EXITO}} are missing, ask for them before executing. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver an immediately actionable one-to-two-page dossier.

Parameters:
- {{FUNCIONALIDAD}}: feature or value proposition to validate by simulating the backend manually.
- {{SEGMENTO}}: user segment that will live the simulated experience.
- {{METRICA_EXITO}}: observable behavior and threshold that defines the value is real (e.g., % completing the action, retention, willingness to wait).
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: operational limits (wizard capacity, time window, hour budget, sensitive data handling). Optional.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Running a manual service concierge MVP
prompts.content:
Act as a senior product lead in discovery and lean experimentation, with experience operating concierge and Wizard of Oz MVPs. Design a concierge MVP operable this week that delivers {{SERVICIO}} by hand to {{SEGMENTO}}, without building anything scalable yet, to convert assumptions into observed evidence before investing in product or automation.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate what service, what segment, and what tangible outcome you understand; if {{SERVICIO}}, {{SEGMENTO}}, or {{RESULTADO_TANGIBLE}} are missing, ask before proceeding. Do not invent metrics or demand; mark everything unconfirmed as [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver the plan in five numbered blocks:
1. Hypothesis and focus: reformulate {{HIPOTESIS_VALOR}} into a single falsifiable sentence stating the belief, exact segment from {{SEGMENTO}} to whom the value will be delivered, and expected outcome, plus the criterion that would declare it refuted.
2. Manual service script: recruiting the first users, explicit promise, request intake channel, 100% manual production of {{RESULTADO_TANGIBLE}}, delivery, committed response times, and verbatim contact script.
3. Learning instrumentation: research questions, signals to observe (real requests, repetition, perceived quality, friction, intent to continue), and a recording method that does not contaminate the user or induce the response.
4. Experiment design: sample and window according to {{MUESTRA_Y_VENTANA}}, and numeric or verifiable thresholds separating advance, pivot, and discard, with what to do with an ambiguous result.
5. Transition: what is done manually now, what is a candidate for automation later, and the observable signal that triggers exiting manual mode.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Include at the end an explicit assumptions block, experiment limits, and one anticipated edge case (zero demand, or demand exceeding manual capacity). Close with the self-assessed quality checklist.

Brand rules: never mention prices; never use the word free; neutral, professional English, no emojis. The service must be deliverable 100% manually.

Variables:
- {{SERVICIO}}: value proposition to deliver by hand, what problem it solves, in one sentence.
- {{SEGMENTO}}: specific, reachable users to whom the value will be delivered.
- {{HIPOTESIS_VALOR}}: falsifiable belief the experiment puts to the test.
- {{RESULTADO_TANGIBLE}}: what the user receives at the end (deliverable or verifiable outcome).
- {{MUESTRA_Y_VENTANA}}: target number of users and experiment days (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Launching a landing smoke test to measure conversion
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Growth Product Manager specialized in early validation and painted door experiments, with statistical judgment to separate signal from noise. I want to design a landing smoke test (a single-CTA page with no product behind it) for {{PROPUESTA_DE_VALOR}} directed at {{SEGMENTO}}, to buy cheap demand evidence before committing to development. Traffic will arrive via {{CANAL_TRAFICO}}, success is measured with {{METRICA_DE_EXITO}}, we decide against {{UMBRAL_DECISION}}, and we collect for {{VENTANA_MEDICION}}. Consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{SEGMENTO}}, {{PROPUESTA_DE_VALOR}}, {{CANAL_TRAFICO}}, {{METRICA_DE_EXITO}}, or {{VENTANA_MEDICION}} are missing, ask before proceeding; if {{UMBRAL_DECISION}} is empty, propose it with justification. Do not invent figures and mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver a ready-to-launch design document: (1) falsifiable hypothesis naming {{SEGMENTO}}, assumed problem, {{PROPUESTA_DE_VALOR}}, {{METRICA_DE_EXITO}}, {{UMBRAL_DECISION}}, and {{VENTANA_MEDICION}}; (2) metrics system with north metric (conversion rate = conversions / unique visitors) and two guardrail metrics with their formula, plus minimum sample size for a conclusive result; (3) landing copy in blocks (proposition headline, pain subheadline, three benefit proofs, single CTA, and honest thank-you screen that clarifies the solution is under exploration, collects email for notification, and does not promise dates); (4) instrumentation with events, UTM per each {{CANAL_TRAFICO}}, and a conversion-to-source attribution rule; (5) decision tree translating the number into continue, pivot, or discard with the rule for separating signal from noise. Cover edge cases: insufficient traffic at the close of {{VENTANA_MEDICION}}, high conversion with poor sample, and a {{CANAL_TRAFICO}} channel that distorts the average.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understood and present your plan before executing. No prices, no the word free, in neutral professional English, no emojis. Close only when the document allows launching the test without additional steps.

prompts.title: Define the overall evaluation criterion for the experiment
prompts.content: Act as a senior product experimentation leader with a track record designing OEC (Overall Evaluation Criterion) and guardrails for A/B testing programs at scale. Your task is to deliver a one-page OEC card for the experiment described in {{HIPOTESIS_Y_CAMBIO}}, running on {{POBLACION_SUPERFICIE}}, aligned to the north star {{META_LARGO_PLAZO}}, starting from {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}} and using {{DURACION_Y_UNIDAD}} as the window and randomization unit. The OEC decides whether the variant wins or loses, avoiding the optimization of a short-term proxy (clicks, sessions) that improves in the test but degrades long-term value. Before executing, restate in one line the hypothesis and {{META_LARGO_PLAZO}}, and present your plan. Work in phases. Phase 1, interpret: if {{HIPOTESIS_Y_CAMBIO}}, {{POBLACION_SUPERFICIE}}, {{META_LARGO_PLAZO}}, {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}}, or {{DURACION_Y_UNIDAD}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them in a single batch before proceeding; do not invent context. Phase 2, design: translate {{META_LARGO_PLAZO}} into a measurable construct and propose a primary OEC metric with exact formula, unit, measurement window, and aggregation level; if a composite OEC is appropriate, declare the components and justified weights, and warn that poor weighting can mask regressions. Phase 3, audit: run the OEC through four properties and flag the risk of each. Sensitive: it moves within {{DURACION_Y_UNIDAD}} with the available sample; if not, declare it insensitive and propose a surface proxy correlated with {{META_LARGO_PLAZO}}. Directional: going up is always better for the business. Causal and non-gameable: name at least one concrete scenario of how the variant could inflate the metric while degrading the experience, and how a guardrail prevents it. Attributable: the movement is caused by the change and not by seasonality or network effects. Phase 4, decide: define 2 to 4 guardrails that must NOT worsen (latency, churn, error rate, revenue per user, satisfaction), each with a non-regression threshold anchored in {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}}; set the decision rule (which combination of OEC plus guardrails triggers launch, iterate, or discard) and the minimum practically relevant effect size that justifies launch, distinguishing it from mere statistical significance. Close with the card ready to review. Rules: tie the OEC explicitly to {{META_LARGO_PLAZO}}, not to a vanity proxy; flag everything not supported by data as [ASSUMPTION]; do not recommend launching if the OEC is insensitive or if a critical guardrail lacks a threshold. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Interpret the results of a test and its significance
prompts.content: Act as a Staff Product Analyst specialized in online experimentation and A/B test design. An A/B test on {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} has ended and the numbers must be converted into an investment decision: ship, kill, or iterate. Test data: {{RESULTADO_OBSERVADO}}, {{MUESTRA_Y_DURACION}}, decision threshold {{UMBRAL_DECISION}}, context {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. I need a justified SHIP / KILL / ITERATE verdict. Proceed as follows: (1) Summarize the experiment in one line: {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} with its desired direction, control vs. treatment, and hypothesis tested. (2) Read the p-value from {{RESULTADO_OBSERVADO}} against the declared alpha; if there is no alpha, assume 0.05 and flag it as an assumption. State whether the null hypothesis is rejected and clarify that the p-value is NOT the probability that the variant is better. (3) Interpret the confidence interval: full range, note crossing of zero (or 1 in ratios) as inconclusive, and translate the pessimistic and optimistic extremes into business impact according to {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}}. (4) Compare the effect size against {{UMBRAL_DECISION}}: significant but below the threshold does not justify shipping. (5) Audit validity with {{MUESTRA_Y_DURACION}}: statistical power, peeking or early stopping, achieved vs. planned sample, novelty effect, SRM/sample ratio mismatch, seasonality, and multiple comparisons. (6) Deliver the verdict with justification, risks assumed, and a concrete next step. Label each claim as [DATA], [ASSUMPTION], or [INFERENCE]. If the p-value, confidence interval, sample size, threshold, or metric direction is missing, ask for it before concluding; do not invent figures. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver a one-page decision with summary, reading of the three statistics, validity audit, and final recommendation with next step.

prompts.title: Prevent peeking and early stopping errors
prompts.content:
Act as a senior growth and experimentation data scientist, proficient in classical frequentist inference (power, sample size) and in sequential methods (alpha spending, group sequential, always-valid inference with e-values). Your assignment: shield the A/B test {{NOMBRE_EXPERIMENTO}} against peeking and early stopping, two practices that inflate the false-positive rate far above the nominal alpha because each additional look is an extra opportunity to cross the threshold by chance.

Produce a documented stopping protocol for {{NOMBRE_EXPERIMENTO}}, ready to attach to the experiment ticket and audit, with these steps:
1. Restate in one line the hypothesis on {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} and name the concrete peeking risk in this case.
2. Confirm the framing: single primary metric, hypothesis direction, randomization unit, and whether {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}} is binary (proportion) or continuous (mean), because it changes the sample size formula.
3. Choose and justify the stopping regime: (a) fixed sample with a single analysis at the end, or (b) sequential design with planned interim reviews. Spell out the trade-off: speed of decision vs. error control. Recommend fixed sample when the horizon is short and the discipline of not looking is viable; sequential when the business will demand looking or cutting early.
4. If fixed sample: calculate the sample size per variant from {{TASA_BASE}}, {{MDE}}, and {{ALPHA}} (significance and power), translate it into duration according to the traffic in {{NUMERO_LOOKS}}, and set ONE single read date.
5. If there will be interim reviews: choose the method that controls the accumulated Type I error (O'Brien-Fleming boundary, Pocock via alpha spending, or sequential testing with e-values/always-valid p-values); declare the number of looks and deliver the table of look-corrected thresholds. O'Brien-Fleming is conservative at the start; Pocock spends evenly; e-values allow unlimited and optional looks.
6. Define the decision rule per look (stop for efficacy / stop for futility / continue) and draft a one-page governance script that prohibits stopping the test without crossing the pre-registered threshold: what is decided, when, with what threshold, who approves.

Edge cases to cover: metric with unstabilized or highly skewed variance (consider transformation or CUPED to reduce variance), novelty/primacy effects that distort early looks, multiple variants requiring multiple-comparisons correction, and guardrail metrics that can trigger stopping for harm even when the primary does not cross.

If any data is missing, ask for it BEFORE calculating. Flag every value you assume as [ASSUMPTION] and isolate it so the user can correct it; never invent a missing value.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Variables:
- {{NOMBRE_EXPERIMENTO}}: name or hypothesis of the A/B test to shield
- {{METRICA_PRIMARIA}}: single decision metric (e.g., checkout conversion rate)
- {{TASA_BASE}}: current value of the metric in the control (baseline)
- {{MDE}}: minimum detectable effect that justifies adopting the variant (absolute or relative)
- {{ALPHA}}: significance level and target power (optional, default alpha 0.05 / power 0.80)
- {{NUMERO_LOOKS}}: planned interim reviews and daily traffic per variant (optional)

prompts.title: Build a prioritized experiment backlog
prompts.content: Act as a senior Head of Product Discovery with experience ordering experimentation backlogs by assumption risk and learning velocity in digital products. I want a prioritized experiment backlog for {{PRODUCTO}}, in service of {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and focused on {{SEGMENTO}}. The underlying problem: the team carries more hypotheses than validation capacity, so without an evidence-based order, discovery spends effort on what is comfortable rather than what is risky. Before proceeding, restate what you understand and present your plan. If essential context is missing or something is ambiguous, ask for it in a single batch before executing; do not invent figures or evidence. Proceed as follows: (1) Frame {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, {{SEGMENTO}}, and the inventory of {{HIPOTESIS_SIN_VALIDAR}}, and mark each starting claim as fact or assumption. (2) Rewrite each belief as a falsifiable hypothesis using the template: We believe that [action] will achieve [measurable outcome] for {{SEGMENTO}} because [reason]; we will know it is true if [measurable signal and threshold]. (3) Classify each hypothesis by risk type: desirability, viability, feasibility, or fit (business/legal/ethics).
