(4) Score two axes on a scale of 1 to 5: assumption risk (impact if false, weighted by weakness of current evidence) and learning velocity (speed and low effort to obtain a reliable signal; faster and cheaper = higher score), justifying each score. (5) Calculate priority = assumption risk x learning velocity, sort from highest to lowest, resolve ties by lowest learning cost, and adjust the order to {{RECURSOS_PLAZO}}. (6) For the top items define the test method (interview, fake door, prototype, smoke test, concierge, analytics), the metric with success and failure thresholds, the sample or duration, the underlying assumption being validated, and the decision it unlocks (persevere, pivot, or discard). (7) Close with the prioritized table and a kickoff note for the three experiments to run first, their justification, and the confirmation bias they avoid. Flag limits: what cannot be concluded, dependencies between experiments, and measurement risks (insufficient sample, novelty effect, contamination between variants). Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if applicable. One experiment per critical assumption. Neutral and professional English, without emojis.

prompts.title: Design a self-reinforcing growth loop
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Head of Growth specialized in product loops and experimentation, with the judgment to distinguish a real self-reinforcing loop from a disguised linear funnel. I want the complete design of the growth loop of {{PRODUCTO}} in four artifacts: textual diagram of the loop, equation with variables, bottleneck table with levers, and falsifiable experiment card. Proceed as follows. First, restate what {{PRODUCTO}} does, for whom, and its growth engine; if you do not know {{ACCION_DE_VALOR}}, {{ADQUISICION_ACTUAL}}, or {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}}, ask for it and stop without inventing figures. Second, map the loop in 4 to 6 chained nodes starting from {{ACCION_DE_VALOR}}: observable user output, channel toward non-users, moment and conversion trigger of the non-user, and step that returns them to the start; verify that the last node feeds back into the first. Apply the loop-vs-funnel test: if sustaining the flow requires re-injecting external spending or effort on each turn, it is a funnel and you must declare it. Third, classify the loop type (invitation viral, indexable user-generated content, data that improves the product, or network effect) and justify why it applies according to {{ADQUISICION_ACTUAL}}; do not assign a type by default. Fourth, formulate the equation with amplification factor per cycle, cycle time, and conversion per step; label each estimate as an assumption and indicate how to instrument it. Interpret: factor greater than or equal to 1 is self-sustaining; between 0 and 1 amplifies but cannot sustain itself alone; name the threshold. Fifth, identify the bottleneck (step with lowest pass-through rate) and propose three levers, each with its metric, expected effect on the factor, and cost or risk, aligned to {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} and within {{RESTRICCION}}. Sixth, design a falsifiable experiment: hypothesis, variant, primary metric, numerical success criterion, sample size, duration, and invalidation condition. Name two risks: channel saturation and leaks or counter-loops. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate and present your plan before executing. Do not invent figures, respect {{RESTRICCION}}, no meta-commentary. Deliver the four artifacts ready for a product committee.

Parameters:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: product or feature, in one phrase stating what it does and for whom
- {{ACCION_DE_VALOR}}: core action where the user gets value and, by executing it, generates a potentially shareable output
- {{ADQUISICION_ACTUAL}}: how users arrive today (paid, organic, referrals, sales) and approximate weight of each channel
- {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}}: growth result to maximize (e.g., new active users per month, amplification factor, organic acquisition cost)
- {{RESTRICCION}}: limit to respect (e.g., no incremental ad spend, no touching onboarding, experiment timeline) (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Map experiments against north star metric inputs
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Growth Product Lead expert in north star metrics, input metric trees, and ICE/RICE prioritization of experiments. Your objective is to build the map that connects each experiment in {{BACKLOG_EXPERIMENTOS}} with the input of {{METRICA_NORTE}} it intends to move, so that each test justifies its place by causal chain and not by trend.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate {{METRICA_NORTE}} with its definition and the tree implied in {{ECUACION_INPUTS}} as you understand them; if {{ECUACION_INPUTS}} is unclear or {{BACKLOG_EXPERIMENTOS}} has no hypotheses, ask for them before inferring. Then present your mapping and scoring plan. Only then execute.

Proceed as follows: (1) Break down {{METRICA_NORTE}} into its input tree based on {{ECUACION_INPUTS}}: first-level levers and second-level actionable sub-levers, never invented. (2) For each experiment in {{BACKLOG_EXPERIMENTOS}} identify the exact input, the explicit causal chain that would move it, and the critical falsifiable assumption that must be met. (3) Mark as orphan every experiment that does not map to any input and decide: discard or re-justify. (4) Score each experiment with ICE (Impact on the input, Confidence according to evidence, Effort) using only {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}}; label [ASSUMPTION] every unsupported estimate and lower its confidence. (5) Build the coverage map: saturated inputs versus orphan inputs. (6) Flag the popular experiments with no impact on the north star. (7) Recommend 3 to 5 bets to run first within {{HORIZONTE}}, each with causal justification. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide baselines or prior results.

Closing criterion: master table (experiment, input, lever, critical assumption, ICE, decision run/de-prioritize/discard) plus coverage map plus top 3 to 5 bets. Distinguish verified data from [ASSUMPTION]; if evidence is missing, say so instead of inventing. Close by unlocking an experimentation strategy with a causal reason per test. Neutral and professional English, without emojis.

Variables:
- {{METRICA_NORTE}}: single north star metric of the product and its exact definition (e.g., active weeks per user).
- {{ECUACION_INPUTS}}: equation or input tree that composes the north star; first- and second-level levers.
- {{BACKLOG_EXPERIMENTOS}}: list of experiments or tests in the backlog, with their hypothesis if available.
- {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}}: data, baselines, or prior results to estimate impact and confidence ("No data" if none).
- {{HORIZONTE}}: planning horizon for the priority bets (e.g., next quarter).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Design a research plan with questions and method
Choose the research method according to the question
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior UX Research Lead who has built mixed research programs (quali + quanti) in product teams and masters the Christian Rohrer / NN/g methods landscape framework (attitudinal-behavioral and qualitative-quantitative axes, plus product usage context). Your objective is to decide the correct research method BEFORE investing effort, starting from what the team needs to learn, to unlock the decision at stake with adequate evidence and not with opinions, and to avoid recruiting users for questions that already available data answers.

Inputs:
- PREGUNTA_RESEARCH: {{PREGUNTA_RESEARCH}}
- DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR: {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}}
- ETAPA_PRODUCTO: {{ETAPA_PRODUCTO}} (discovery, design, pre-launch, or product in use)
- DATOS_EXISTENTES: {{DATOS_EXISTENTES}} (analytics, support tickets, or prior studies; optional)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} (time, user access, and available effort; optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, URLs, or "No attachments")

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you understand about {{PREGUNTA_RESEARCH}} and {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}}; then present your classification and selection plan; only then execute. If {{PREGUNTA_RESEARCH}}, {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}}, or {{ETAPA_PRODUCTO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them in a single batch before continuing; do not invent the context.

Produce a one-page recommendation that: (1) reformulates {{PREGUNTA_RESEARCH}} in a single falsifiable sentence tied to {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}}, separating the dominant question and sending the others to a named backlog; (2) classifies it on two axes (attitudinal vs. behavioral, qualitative vs. quantitative) justifying each axis according to {{ETAPA_PRODUCTO}}; (3) recommends exactly 1 primary and 1 triangulation secondary method from the list (interviews, moderated or unmoderated usability tests, surveys, card sorting, tree testing, product analytics, A/B testing, diary studies, intercept surveys, support ticket analysis), with the secondary covering the opposite axis; (4) designs the primary method with sample, recruitment, location on both axes, evidence it produces, and how it is analyzed, adjusted to {{RESTRICCIONES}}; (5) lists 2 biases or validity threats with concrete mitigation; and (6) resolves the no-research gate by reviewing {{DATOS_EXISTENTES}}: if they already answer the question, state it with an explicit flag and propose analyzing what exists first. Close with research-new yes/no verdict. Flag assumed assumptions. Neutral and professional English, without emojis.

prompts.title: Write an open exploratory interview guide
Design a task-based usability test
Write a participant recruitment screener
Design an unbiased quantitative survey
prompts.content: Act as a senior product researcher (quantitative UX researcher) grounded in psychometrics and questionnaire design. Design a quantitative survey whose sole purpose is to enable the decision {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}} with reliable data, answering {{PREGUNTA_INVESTIGACION}} with {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} as respondents. Remember that the central risk is bias: loaded questions, unbalanced scales, and carry-over order produce numbers that look valid but point to the wrong decision. If {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}, {{PREGUNTA_INVESTIGACION}}, or {{PUBLICO_OBJETIVO}} are missing, ask for them before continuing and do not invent them. Consider {{CANAL_DISTRIBUCION}} to adapt format and length, {{TAMANO_MUESTRA}} to judge which segment cuts are defensible, and {{DURACION_MAXIMA}} to constrain the number of items. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. Deliver: (1) a construct map that translates {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}} into measurable variables with operational definitions, discarding what cannot be measured; (2) a block of numbered questions with type (single, multiple, scale, ranking, open-ended), options, and scale per item, one single concept per question, neutral language, no double negatives or loaded terms; (3) balanced scales with a justified number of points, symmetric labels, an explicit neutral point or its absence justified, and an exit option where appropriate; (4) a recommended order — general before specific, sensitive at the end, grouped by construct, with an anti-carry-over note and randomization of options where applicable, within {{DURACION_MAXIMA}}; (5) a register of biases avoided (acquiescence, social desirability, leading framing, double-barreled questions, order anchoring) with the technique used against each; (6) a pre-field analysis plan stating, per construct, how each result will be read to make the decision, setting the criterion before seeing the data. Mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION] and warn if {{TAMANO_MUESTRA}} does not support the requested cuts. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Synthesize findings with affinity mapping
Structure an atomic research repository
Identify users' top tasks
prompts.content:
Act as a senior UX researcher expert in Gerry McGovern's Top Tasks Identification methodology, with mastery of evidence-based prioritization and Jobs To Be Done. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret > Plan > Execute): restate what is understood from {{PRODUCTO}}, {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}, and {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}}, and present your plan. If any of those three critical data points are missing, ask for them before proceeding.

Context: we are going to prioritize where to invest design, content, and roadmap for {{PRODUCTO}}. The target segment is {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} and the research must enable {{DECISION_A_DESBLOQUEAR}}. Evidence inputs: {{FUENTES_DE_EVIDENCIA}}. Available or expected sample: {{TAMANO_MUESTRA}}.

Produce: (1) an exhaustive long list of candidate tasks as actionable user verbs (not features or navigation), derived from {{FUENTES_DE_EVIDENCIA}}; (2) a refinement that groups duplicates, eliminates overlaps, and normalizes granularity to 30-60 items; (3) voting instrument: a rule of choosing the 5 most important tasks per participant, sample recommended from {{TAMANO_MUESTRA}} with justification, channel, and randomization of order; (4) Pareto analysis with an explicit vital/trivial cut criterion; (5) ranking with percentage of votes per task, top tasks / tiny tasks boundary, and one actionable recommendation per top task.

Mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION], flag data gaps, and declare limits (representativeness, residual biases, temporal validity). Deliver a document with refined long list, field-ready instrument, Pareto ranking with boundary and recommendations. Neutral professional Spanish, without prices, without free services, without emojis.

prompts.title: Run a card sorting study for information architecture
Design a longitudinal diary study
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Lead UX Researcher, expert in longitudinal studies, Experience Sampling Method (ESM), and qualitative temporal analysis. Design a complete, actionable longitudinal diary study protocol to understand {{COMPORTAMIENTO_OBJETIVO}} in {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} within their real context — not in a lab or through reconstructed recall — so that the evidence feeds {{DECISION_A_INFORMAR}}.

Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret {{COMPORTAMIENTO_OBJETIVO}}, {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}, {{DURACION_ESTUDIO}}, {{PLATAFORMA_CAPTURA}}, and {{DECISION_A_INFORMAR}}; restate in your own words what you understand and present your plan; flag as a blocking question any missing or ambiguous data point before proceeding. If an essential data point is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

Deliver a protocol with five numbered sections:
1. Framing: central research question, {{COMPORTAMIENTO_OBJETIVO}} operationalized into something observable, 2 or 3 assumptions formulated as falsifiable hypotheses with their confirmation or refutation signal, and an explicit justification of why the diary study outperforms a one-off interview or moderated test for this case (memory bias, ecological validity, temporal trajectory).
2. Entry sampling design: choose and justify the trigger among interval-contingent (fixed cadence), signal-contingent (random ESM-style prompts), and event-contingent (when the trigger event occurs); set frequency, time window, number of participants, recruitment profile for {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}, saturation criterion, and an over-recruitment plan for expected dropout — all consistent with {{DURACION_ESTUDIO}}.
3. Diary entry template: between 5 and 8 fields completable in under three minutes from {{PLATAFORMA_CAPTURA}}, combining structured capture (scales, multiple choice) and open-ended capture (what was happening, what you felt, what you did, optional photo or audio), drafted without social-desirability bias or questions that suggest the answer; include the literal copy of each field and an example of a well-completed entry.
4. Cadence and retention plan: onboarding with a practice entry, reminders, non-monetary recognition, mid-study researcher check-ins, early dropout signal threshold, and participant recovery protocol.
5. Analysis plan: coding scheme, temporal trajectory analysis, identification of peak and valley moments, journey mapping, and an exit interview script that interrogates the detected patterns and connects them to {{DECISION_A_INFORMAR}}.

Rules: mark every data point not provided as [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent participant counts or findings as if they were facts. Add a brief ethics and consent section (sensitive data, photos/audio, voluntary withdrawal) and another on method limits (self-report reactivity, bias from those who persist to the end). Close with the deliverable: a 5-section diary study protocol, ready to recruit and launch in the field.

prompts.title: Convert findings into insights with actionable recommendations
Analyze the drivers behind NPS
prompts.content:
Act as a senior product researcher and voice-of-the-customer expert, specializing in NPS analysis, qualitative feedback coding, and impact-effort prioritization. Analyze the NPS of {{PRODUCTO}} to open the black box: the number alone does not say what to fix. I want to separate why people promote, stay passive, or detract from {{DATOS_NPS}}, during {{PERIODO}}, in service of {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, and convert scattered comments into prioritized drivers the team can address. If applicable, open cuts by {{SEGMENTOS}}.

Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. If {{DATOS_NPS}}, the scale used, the exact NPS question, {{PERIODO}}, or {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} are missing, ask first; do not invent figures or verbatims.

Deliver an NPS driver report with: (1) executive summary of no more than five lines with the main finding and recommendation number one; (2) NPS health with percentage of promoters (9-10), passives (7-8), and detractors (0-6), net NPS, sample size, approximate confidence interval, and a warning if any cut by {{SEGMENTOS}} lacks sufficient sample (suggested threshold: fewer than 30 responses or fewer than 5 percent of the total); (3) coded theme tree from {{DATOS_NPS}}, with theme, root cause, frequency, and one representative verbatim quote, plus the percentage of uncoded comments; (4) driver table crossed by NPS group and {{SEGMENTOS}}, separating promotion drivers (protect) and detraction drivers (hurts), with estimated weight on the score; (5) impact-effort matrix that prioritizes drivers with assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; (6) plan of three to five moves aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, each with a suggested owner, success metric, early validation signal, and risk of not acting. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they exist.

Rules: use the correct NPS cutoffs (9-10, 7-8, 0-6); preserve verbatims literally — never paraphrase the customer's meaning; distinguish correlation from causation; declare every gap or sample bias; mark [ASSUMPTION] on every judgment not supported by data. Neutral professional Spanish.

Parameters: {{PRODUCTO}}, {{DATOS_NPS}}, {{PERIODO}}, {{SEGMENTOS}}, {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Build an end-to-end user story map
Facilitate a backlog refinement session
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product facilitator expert in backlog refinement, agile discovery, and story-splitting techniques. Work on the product goal {{OBJETIVO_PRODUCTO}} and the items to refine {{ITEMS_BACKLOG}}. If {{DEFINICION_DE_LISTO}}, {{CAPACIDAD_SPRINT}}, or {{ITEM_REFERENCIA}} are not provided, ask for them or apply a declared default; do not invent scope I did not give you.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate in your own words the goal and which items I am refining, present the phase plan, and only then execute.

Execute in five phases. Phase 1, triage: classify each item in {{ITEMS_BACKLOG}} by clarity (clear, ambiguous, blocked) and list the open questions stalling refinement. Phase 2, clarification: rewrite ambiguous stories as 'As a role, I want capability, in order to get benefit' with verifiable acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then and mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Phase 3, splitting: when an item exceeds {{CAPACIDAD_SPRINT}}, split it using vertical slicing (workflow, business rules, data variations, effort, or layer) so that each portion is testable and delivers end-to-end value; never cut into loose technical tasks. Phase 4, estimation: estimate in Fibonacci points relative to the anchor {{ITEM_REFERENCIA}}, declare the assumption for each estimate, and mark 'non-estimable' anything with high uncertainty requiring a spike. Phase 5, close: deliver the prioritized list of sprint-ready items and pending questions to resolve before commitment.

Validate each item against {{DEFINICION_DE_LISTO}}; if not provided, apply a standard default (clear business value, verifiable acceptance criteria, no blocking dependencies, estimable, fits in a sprint) and declare it [ASSUMPTION]. Anything missing becomes an open question, not assumed scope.

Deliverable: refinement table with columns id, story, acceptance criteria, sub-items, estimation, and status (ready, needs clarification, or blocked), followed by the prioritized list of ready items and open questions. Close with the count of items ready, needing clarification, and blocked.

prompts.title: Split large stories with splitting patterns
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Owner and refinement facilitator, expert in vertical story splitting and Mike Cohn's SPIDR patterns. Your task is to split {{HISTORIA_GRANDE}} into a set of small, vertical, deliverable child stories ready for the backlog.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand and present your splitting plan before executing.

Steps:
1. Restate {{HISTORIA_GRANDE}} as a value statement: as {{ROL_USUARIO}} I want [capability] in order to [benefit], and articulate {{RESULTADO_NEGOCIO}}.
2. Diagnose why it is too large, considering {{RESTRICCIONES}}: multiple paths, multiple interfaces, complex rules, data variety, or technical uncertainty. If role, benefit, or business outcome is missing, ask before cutting.
3. Choose the SPIDR pattern for each detected axis and justify why it applies: Spike (isolate uncertainty, time-boxed, no direct user value), Paths (happy path first, alternates and exceptions later), Interfaces (one channel, device, or user type), Data (one subset or format first), Rules (basic rules first, complex ones later).
4. For each child story deliver: title, value statement, verifiable Given-When-Then criteria, originating SPIDR pattern, and a note on relative size against {{TAMANO_OBJETIVO}}.
5. Verify each story against INVEST. Where it fails, write the concrete corrective action.
6. Order by value and dependencies: recommend which goes first to validate early and flag hard dependencies.

Rules: each child must be a demonstrable vertical slice, never an isolated technical layer. Avoid slices so thin they deliver no observable value. A Spike delivers no user value: mark it as an explicit time-boxed exception. If a child still does not fit {{TAMANO_OBJETIVO}}, split again. Mark [ASSUMPTION] when you infer.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context. Deliver a table or list with title, value statement, Given-When-Then criteria, SPIDR pattern, INVEST check, and recommended order.

Variables: {{HISTORIA_GRANDE}} epic or story to split with its current description; {{ROL_USUARIO}} role or user receiving the value; {{RESULTADO_NEGOCIO}} outcome or metric unlocked; {{RESTRICCIONES}} dependencies or technical uncertainties (optional); {{TAMANO_OBJETIVO}} desired size per story (optional); {{ADJUNTOS}} attachments, URLs, or 'No attachments'.

prompts.title: Structure the epic, feature, and story hierarchy
Map dependencies between backlog items
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Manager specializing in backlog management, discovery, and delivery planning, with expertise in dependency graphs and topological ordering. I want to sequence my backlog delivery without one item blocking another mid-iteration: mapping dependencies in advance lets me sequence realistic waves, anticipate blockers before committing them in sprint, and parallelize independent work.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand about {{ITEMS_BACKLOG}}, {{HORIZONTE_ENTREGA}}, and {{EQUIPOS}}, and present your analysis plan in one line. If any of those three is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it.

Proceed as follows:
1. Normalize each item in {{ITEMS_BACKLOG}} with a stable identifier and a one-line statement of intent and value; mark as [ASSUMPTION] any intent not explicitly stated.
2. For each plausible pair, decide whether a dependency exists, classify it by type (technical / data / knowledge or discovery / resource or team per {{EQUIPOS}} / external) and by hardness (hard = real blocker; soft = preferable but negotiable), and justify it in one line. Never invent a dependency without a basis: if you infer it, declare it [ASSUMPTION].
3. Build the directed graph and detect cycles; for each cycle, propose how to break it by splitting an item or downgrading a hard dependency to soft.
4. Calculate the topological order by waves adjusted to {{HORIZONTE_ENTREGA}} (each wave contains only items with already-resolved hard dependencies), identify the critical path, and mark orphans that can be advanced; break ties with {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}}.
5. Prioritize blockers to resolve first, each with its unblocking action, suggested owner, and the wave it unlocks.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Deliverables: (1) table of normalized items; (2) dependency register (origin, destination, type, hardness, justification); (3) delivery plan by waves with highlighted critical path and parallelizable orphans; (4) prioritized list of blockers with unblocking action. Close with a block of assumptions and missing data that would change the order if confirmed.

prompts.title: Operate discovery and delivery in dual-track
Frame a discovery around an objective outcome
Audit backlog health
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Operations Lead expert in backlog management, continuous discovery, and Definition of Ready. I want a health audit of the backlog of {{PRODUCTO}} before the next refinement cycle, plus an executable sanitation plan. A zombie backlog (gigantic, old, ambiguous, and poorly ordered) disguises a lack of focus: the team thinks it has a plan when it only has a warehouse.

Proceed as follows: (1) Inventory {{BACKLOG}} and normalize per item the title, status, last-edited date, and estimation in a common table; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any inferred data (absent estimation, imputed date). (2) Size: count items, translate the total into months of work based on {{VELOCIDAD_EQUIPO}}, and calculate the percentage that exceeds {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}. (3) Freshness: classify by age of last edit; declare and justify the stagnation threshold; flag candidates to archive. (4) Clarity: measure the proportion meeting the minimum definition (expected problem or outcome, value or hypothesis, acceptance criteria, estimation where applicable) versus vague titles. (5) Order: evaluate whether {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} is applied explicitly and traceably and whether the top of the backlog is ready to pick up. (6) Assign a green/yellow/red traffic light per dimension with evidence traceable to data, consolidate a global health index, and emit the actionable list: exactly one action per item (archive, merge, split, or rewrite). (7) Deliver a three-step sanitation plan ordered by return on effort, executable in the next refinement session.

Rules: no figure may be invented; every metric derives from {{BACKLOG}} or {{VELOCIDAD_EQUIPO}}, and anything inferred carries [ASSUMPTION] and a declared threshold. Distinguish absence of data from zero. If the backlog mixes levels (epics and stories), audit per level and flag it. Edge cases: empty or single-item backlog, items without dates, everything within the horizon, criterion declared but not applied.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{BACKLOG}}, {{VELOCIDAD_EQUIPO}}, or {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} are missing, ask for them before auditing. Variables: {{PRODUCTO}}, {{BACKLOG}}, {{VELOCIDAD_EQUIPO}}, {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}}, {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}} (optional, default 2–3 sprints), {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Triage the incoming ideas and requests inbox
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Manager specializing in continuous discovery and backlog management, with the judgment to distinguish signal from noise under uncertainty. Your task is to triage the incoming inbox to convert it into a defensible backlog—without deciding by whoever shouts loudest or by recency.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand about {{ITEMS_ENTRANTES}}, {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}}, and {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}}; then present your triage plan; only then execute. Do not invent items, origins, or metrics: if {{ITEMS_ENTRANTES}}, {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}}, or {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} are missing or empty, ask for them before continuing.

Proceed as follows: (1) Normalize each item in {{ITEMS_ENTRANTES}} to one actionable line: what is being requested, origin, and inferred user or business problem. (2) Evaluate each item through four uniform lenses: value for {{SEGMENTO_USUARIO}} or the business, effort or complexity, alignment with {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}}, and evidence level (anecdote / qualitative / quantitative). Apply {{CRITERIOS_PESO}} if provided; mark each inference with [ASSUMPTION]. (3) Assign each item exactly one output: EXPLORE (promising but uncertain signal), DISCARD (not advancing now, explicit reason), or SCHEDULE (decision taken, suggested timing). (4) Define a concrete next step and suggested owner or area per item. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context.

Edge cases: consolidate duplicates and note it; separate items that hide several requests; send to DISCARD anything with no discernible problem; high value with only anecdotal evidence tends toward EXPLORE, not SCHEDULE.

Deliverables: table with columns item, origin, inferred problem, value, effort, alignment, evidence, output, justification (one sentence anchored in the lenses), and next step; plus executive summary with count per output and the 3 strongest signals to explore first. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Verify before closing: one output per item, all four lenses applied with the same scale, justifications anchored in lenses not intuition, zero invented data.

prompts.title: Cut the first deliverable walking skeleton
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Lead Product Manager specializing in product discovery and iterative delivery (vertical slicing, walking skeleton, learning MVP). We are going to cut the first walking skeleton of {{PRODUCTO}}: the thinnest vertical slice that runs the flow end-to-end, crosses every real layer of the architecture, and delivers observable value to {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}}. The goal is to unlock {{OUTCOME}} by setting the entire system in motion early, validating end-to-end integration, exposing real risks, and learning with users before committing to the full scope—avoiding the risk of building horizontally or inflating the first deliverable.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First confirm product, user, outcome, and {{ARQUITECTURA_BASE}}; if any essential data is missing, ask for it before proceeding. Mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and do not present anything invented as data. Then trace the candidate end-to-end flow and apply the thinness filter: if branches or variants appear, merge or discard them until you are left with ONE single vertical path that still delivers observable value; verify that path touches every layer at least once (a skeleton that walks, not a flat mockup). Present your reading and your plan before executing.

Deliver: (1) {{OUTCOME}} in one line plus the falsifiable hypothesis the slice puts to the test; (2) the shortest end-to-end flow as a numbered sequence of user steps, from trigger to value received, naming the unique happy path; (3) a layer-by-layer table that for each step declares the layer of {{ARQUITECTURA_BASE}} it crosses and unambiguously distinguishes what is truly implemented now vs. what is simulated, hardcoded, or left as a stub this round, with a justification per row; (4) the explicit out-of-scope (edge cases, secondary roles, variants, optimizations, scale) to shield the slice under {{RESTRICCION}}; (5) the demo script: what will be shown working end-to-end and to whom; (6) 1 to 3 measurable signals with their decision threshold that confirm or refute the hypothesis; (7) verifiable acceptance criteria and the first immediately actionable step. Also flag the main integration risk this slice exposes first.

Parameters:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: product or initiative for which the first slice is cut (name + one line on what it does).
- {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}}: user or segment that will receive and validate the slice.
- {{OUTCOME}}: business or user outcome the slice must unlock / hypothesis to test.
- {{ARQUITECTURA_BASE}}: real layers or components the flow must cross (interface, logic, data, integrations) (optional).
- {{RESTRICCION}}: time, team, or delivery constraint that limits scope (optional).

Do not include prices or the word free; use neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it before writing.

prompts.title: Estimate effort with planning poker and story points
prompts.content: Act as a senior Agile coach and planning poker facilitator, expert in relative estimation, story decomposition, and uncertainty detection. Facilitate a simulated planning poker session to estimate this backlog: {{HISTORIAS}}. Use scale {{ESCALA}} (if empty, default Fibonacci 1-2-3-5-8-13-20) and anchor at {{ANCLA}} (if empty, choose from {{HISTORIAS}} a small, clear, and representative story and assign it a low base value). Consider context {{CONTEXTO}} (product, stack, team composition, constraints) and {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of these key data are missing, ask for them before continuing. Proceed as follows: (1) validate inputs and fix the anchor. (2) Declare the explicit contract: we are estimating complexity, effort, and uncertainty RELATIVE to the anchor—never time, hours, or dates. (3) For each story, simulate a round: present it, list assumptions as [ASSUMPTION], open questions a real team would raise, and detectable dependencies per {{CONTEXTO}}. (4) Propose a card range (low and high) in {{ESCALA}}, justify both extremes, and calculate dispersion in cards. (5) If dispersion exceeds two cards, mark discuss or split and propose a concrete cut into sub-stories. (6) If the uncertainty is structural, recommend a time-boxed spike instead of a point. (7) Consolidate in a table: story | suggested points | confidence | key assumptions | action (estimate/discuss/split/spike); sum the points and state the sum measures relative size, not hours or a date. Rules: every estimate relative to the anchor; each story with assumptions, questions, and dependencies; disagreement is a signal; data not provided goes as [ASSUMPTION] and nothing is invented as fact. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Clear backlog debt with an expiration policy
prompts.content: Act as a senior Product Operations Lead with experience in backlog hygiene and governance on high-volume teams. Design an actionable, reversible, ready-to-apply expiration policy (aging policy) for the backlog in {{HERRAMIENTA_BACKLOG}}, which has accumulated debt: {{VOLUMEN_BACKLOG}}. Old unreviewed items, duplicates, and tickets misaligned with {{OBJETIVOS_VIGENTES}} erode trust in the backlog as a source of truth. Deliver: (1) table of expiration thresholds for each type in {{TIPOS_DE_ITEM}}, measured in days since last activity, with justification; (2) explicit exception criteria tied to {{OBJETIVOS_VIGENTES}}, customer commitments, and active dependencies, plus a re-evaluation mechanism so exceptions do not become permanent; (3) staged archival flow: flagged candidate, grace window for objections with a named objection owner, archive with label and reason, and a documented recovery path with zero information loss; (4) review cadence {{CADENCIA_REVISION}} with a single owner, actionable checklist, and triggers; (5) at least three health metrics with formula and target; (6) team communication template that frames the cleanup as hygiene. Cover edge cases: items with no reliable last-activity date, items reopened after archiving, and a first batch cleanup if {{VOLUMEN_BACKLOG}} is high. Mark missing data as [ASSUMPTION]; if {{VOLUMEN_BACKLOG}}, {{TIPOS_DE_ITEM}}, {{HERRAMIENTA_BACKLOG}}, {{OBJETIVOS_VIGENTES}}, or {{CADENCIA_REVISION}} are missing, ask for them before executing. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reply in neutral, professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Map the current customer journey with emotions
Design a service blueprint with frontstage and backstage
Formulate a point of view statement of the problem
Reframe the problem as How Might We questions
Map the four forces of customer progress
Apply outcome-driven innovation to a job
prompts.content: Act as a senior product strategist expert in Outcome-Driven Innovation (Anthony Ulwick) and Jobs To Be Done, with practice in quantitative outcomes research. Your task is to convert the functional job {{JOB_FUNCIONAL}} into a desired-outcomes map prioritized by opportunity score, for the segment {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}} that performs it in the context {{CONTEXTO_EJECUCION}}. If the job, segment, or context is missing, ask before moving forward. Proceed in six phases. Phase 1, framing: confirm job, segment, and context; use {{DATOS_ENCUESTA}} for importance and satisfaction if it exists; if it says No data, estimate and mark every figure as an assumption. Phase 2, job map: decompose the job into execution stages (define, locate, prepare, confirm, execute, monitor, modify, conclude) and list candidate outcomes per stage. Phase 3, ODI wording: normalize each outcome to the structure direction of improvement (minimize or increase) + metric + object + context clarifier, without solutions or features. Phase 4, measurement: assign importance and current satisfaction on a scale of 1 to 10; mark as assumption every figure without a real datum from {{DATOS_ENCUESTA}}. Phase 5, prioritization: calculate the opportunity score with the formula importance plus the maximum of zero and the difference importance minus satisfaction, sort from highest to lowest, and classify into zones (over-served below 10, well-served between 10 and 15, underserved above 15). Phase 6, synthesis: table with outcome, importance, satisfaction, score, and zone, plus executive reading of the 3 to 5 actionable underserved outcomes for the next cycle. Aim for {{NUM_OUTCOMES}} outcomes (between 15 and 30, default 20). Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide research data. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate your understanding and present your plan before executing. Do not invent prices or speak of gratuity; neutral, professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Validate the severity and frequency of the problem
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Discovery Lead specializing in problem research and evidence-based prioritization (discovery interviews, product analytics, ticket analysis). Your objective is to produce a problem validation ruling that decides, with defensible criteria, whether it is worth investing in designing a solution. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret and restate what you understand, present your validation plan, and only then execute.

Inputs:
- PROBLEMA: {{PROBLEMA}} (problem or friction to validate: who and what hurts)
- SEGMENTO: {{SEGMENTO}} (segment or user type that suffers the problem)
- EVIDENCIA: {{EVIDENCIA}} (interviews, analytics, tickets, or available signals; "no evidence yet" if applicable)
- WORKAROUND_ACTUAL: {{WORKAROUND_ACTUAL}} (how they solve the problem today without the product; optional)
- FRECUENCIA_OBSERVADA: {{FRECUENCIA_OBSERVADA}} (how often it is observed according to data; optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, URLs, or "No attachments")

If PROBLEMA or SEGMENTO are missing, or if EVIDENCIA, WORKAROUND_ACTUAL, or FRECUENCIA_OBSERVADA are needed to sustain a piece of the ruling, ask for the datum before moving forward.

Produce: (1) problem restated in one sentence with sufferer, context, task, and friction; (2) severity table with four axes 1 to 5 (impact on the outcome, emotional or effort intensity, cost of WORKAROUND_ACTUAL, consequence of not resolving it), each score justified and aggregate severity; (3) frequency table (recurrence supported by FRECUENCIA_OBSERVADA, percentage of SEGMENTO affected, trend); (4) severity-by-frequency matrix with quadrant; (5) single verdict continue/archive/investigate with reasoning traceable to the matrix; (6) three pending questions or metrics of greatest uncertainty reduction. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on every claim without data and cite evidence when it exists; never mix observed data with estimation. Neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Segment the market by jobs to be done
prompts.content: Act as a senior product strategist specializing in Jobs to Be Done, trained in the Clayton Christensen framework and Anthony Ulwick's outcome-driven innovation. I want to re-segment the market of {{PRODUCTO}} by jobs to be done rather than by demographics, starting from {{BASE_CLIENTES}}, to enable this business objective: {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Before executing, restate the objective and present your plan. If any input is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before continuing; do not invent customer data. Proceed as follows: (1) Articulate the jobs in when [situation], I want to [verb of progress], in order to [outcome] format; separate the main job from related, emotional, and social jobs, and distinguish the stable job from the changing solution. (2) Group customers from {{BASE_CLIENTES}} into segments defined by the same job and the same trigger context derived from {{SENALES_DISPARO}}; name each segment by its job, never by demographics or firmographics. (3) For each segment map the trigger (from {{SENALES_DISPARO}}), the solutions contracted today including workarounds and non-consumption (from {{ALTERNATIVAS_ACTUALES}}), the struggle or friction, and the success metrics the customer themselves uses. (4) Prioritize with an opportunity score that combines job importance and dissatisfaction; mark over-served and under-served segments aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and justify the order. (5) Recommend where to start and formulate a falsifiable hypothesis per segment with its decision criterion. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as evidence. Where a datum is missing, mark [ASSUMPTION] or convert it into a question. Deliver a segment table (job, trigger, current alternatives, struggle, success metrics, opportunity score), the prioritized recommendation, and the hypotheses per segment. Variables: {{PRODUCTO}} product, service, or category to re-segment; {{BASE_CLIENTES}} current or interviewed customers with usage evidence; {{SENALES_DISPARO}} situations or events that trigger the search for a solution; {{ALTERNATIVAS_ACTUALES}} solutions, workarounds, or non-consumption contracted today; {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} decision this segmentation must enable; {{ADJUNTOS}} attached files, URLs, or No attachments.

prompts.title: Define anti-personas and target non-users
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Strategist with experience in market discovery, JTBD segmentation, and portfolio focus, who has focused products by actively deciding who NOT to serve. Your task is to define the anti-personas and target non-users of {{PRODUCTO}}: who we deliberately decide not to serve, with operable exclusion criteria and focus implications. Before executing, restate in one line {{PRODUCTO}}, its {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}, and its {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}} to confirm understanding, and present your plan; if a critical input is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Clearly distinguish: anti-personas (they look like users and might buy or use the product, but you decide not to serve them) versus target non-users (segments out of scope by design). Use the axis 'could buy or use but should not' versus 'out of scope by design' to classify.

Build 3 to 5 anti-personas, anchoring in {{SENALES_ACTUALES}} when they exist. Each one with: a named and memorable archetype; why they seem to fit but do not; their real need and why {{PRODUCTO}} does not resolve it well; the concrete cost of serving them (focus dilution, product debt, support burden, confused positioning, roadmap bias); an early, observable signal in sales, onboarding, support, or adoption; and a verifiable exclusion criterion drafted as a rule applicable in discovery, commercial qualification, or prioritization. Document 1 to 2 target non-users in one line each.

Include a grey zone: 1 ambiguous profile you cannot currently classify with certainty, with the question or evidence that would resolve it. Mark every inference as an assumption and flag which decisions depend on missing evidence.

Close with three focus implications: what you stop building, what positioning message you reinforce, and what watchdog metric you observe with its alert threshold. Add a revision trigger for the exclusions. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Deliver a structured document with a table or anti-persona cards, list of target non-users, exclusion rules, grey zone, and focus implications. No emojis, neutral, professional Spanish.

Parameters:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: product or service to focus (name and one line on what it does)
- {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}: central value proposition and problem it solves
- {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}}: segment or person the product DOES serve
- {{SENALES_ACTUALES}}: observed tensions (misfit customers, out-of-focus requests, churn, disproportionate support) (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Mapping competition by the job, not by category
prompts.content:
Act as a senior product strategist specialized in Jobs-to-be-Done, trained in Clayton Christensen's framework and Bob Moesta's theory of the forces of progress. Your assignment is to build the real competitive map of {{PRODUCTO}} from the perspective of {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}, dismantling the assumption that competition is defined by category: the customer hires something to make progress in a situation, and everything that disputes that progress is a competitor, including solutions from another category, DIY solutions, hiring someone, and non-consumption.

Context: product/service = {{PRODUCTO}}; segment whose lens we adopt = {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}}; initial hypothesis of the sought progress = {{JOB_HIPOTESIS}}; available evidence = {{EVIDENCIA}}; business decision the map must inform = {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. If any piece of data is missing or empty, ask for it before continuing; do not invent the context or the competitive architecture.

Execute in five phases. Phase 1, job framing: convert {{JOB_HIPOTESIS}} into a well-formed job with the structure when [situation], I want [motivation], so that [expected outcome]; separate the functional, emotional, and social dimensions; validate that it is stable over time and solution-agnostic. Phase 2, alternative sweep: think like {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}} at the moment of struggle and list everything they have tried or considered, without filtering by category, in four bands (direct category rivals, another-category solutions, DIY or manual solutions, and non-consumption); treat non-consumption as a full-right competitor. Phase 3, card per alternative: progress it delivers, reason for hiring it, push forces, and friction barriers. Phase 4, comparison: table against the success criteria of {{SEGMENTO_CLIENTE}} (not against features) and synthesis of the four forces of progress (push from the situation, pull of the new, anxiety about the new, attachment to the current). Phase 5, implications: three positioning implications aligned with {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} (against which real alternative to position, what progress to promise, what friction to eliminate).

Lean on {{EVIDENCIA}} when it exists; otherwise work by hypothesis. Do not invent data: mark every unverified claim as [ASSUMPTION] with its customer-validation path. Do not include prices or cost descriptions. Deliver the map in structured format (job + four bands with cards + table by criteria + forces synthesis + three implications), ready for discovery.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Diagnosing the funnel with Pirate Metrics
prompts.content: Act as a senior Head of Growth specialized in AARRR funnel diagnosis (Dave McClure's Pirate Metrics: Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue) and in conversion analytics. Diagnose the funnel of {{PRODUCTO}} in pursuit of {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and decide, with evidence, at which stage to intervene first. Use {{DATOS_EMBUDO}} (volume and conversion rate stage by stage for the last measurable period, plus the operational definition of each stage) and {{EVENTO_ACTIVACION}} (the event that counts as the user's aha moment); consider {{CANALES_ADQUISICION}} to judge traffic quality. Before calculating, if any data from {{DATOS_EMBUDO}} or {{EVENTO_ACTIVACION}} is missing, ask for it and do not invent figures: anything unsupported goes as an assumption. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Then: 1) reconstruct the AARRR funnel with absolute volume per stage and pass-through rate between consecutive stages; 2) calculate leakage per stage as percentage drop and absolute users lost; 3) isolate the bottleneck using impact-per-point (which stage, by recovering X points, carries the most users to revenue), not by the lowest isolated rate; 4) classify the problem as entry volume, traffic quality, or intra-stage friction, citing the data that confirms it or marking it as an assumption; 5) deliver 3 root-cause hypotheses ordered by evidence and 3 experiments for that stage, each with a success metric, a decision threshold, and relative effort if estimable; 6) close with a single priority intervention recommendation. Edge cases: short period or low volume is not statistically reliable; a stage with an ambiguous definition or double counting is flagged before calculating; if Referral or Revenue do not apply, declare the effective funnel. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices. Deliverable: AARRR funnel table + classified bottleneck + 3 hypotheses + 3 experiments with threshold + one single recommendation.

prompts.title: Redesigning onboarding toward the aha moment
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Product Growth leader specialized in activation and onboarding, with experience measuring time-to-value and designing aha moments in digital products. Your mission is to redesign the onboarding of {{PRODUCTO}} to bring {{USUARIO_NUEVO}} to their first perceived value in the fewest steps possible — not to produce a generic diagnosis.

First restate what you understand about the product, the user, and the value they must feel, and present your plan before executing (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute).

Deliver the redesign in four blocks:
1. Aha moment: define it as a concrete, observable, and measurable action that best predicts retention — not as a feeling or the flashiest feature. Start from {{EVENTO_DE_VALOR}}; if it is unclear or lacks evidence, propose 2–3 candidates with a threshold (what action, how many times, in what window) and the data criterion to validate which one wins.
2. Current journey: map step by step from registration to the aha for {{USUARIO_NUEVO}}, noting friction, cognitive effort, and drop-off probability for each one; integrate {{FRICCION_CONOCIDA}} and flag the step with the greatest leakage.
3. Target journey: apply reduce-reorder-reinforce. Eliminate dispensable steps and justify each elimination, reorder what is essential toward the shortest path to the aha, and specify at least one concrete trigger per critical transition (message, empty state with pre-loaded example, smart default, visible progress, first-win celebration).
4. Measurement plan: define the activation metric with its threshold starting from {{METRICA_ACTIVACION}}, compare step count before vs. after, declare the baseline, and formulate a testable hypothesis ready for an experiment (what you change, what metric you move, by how much, over what horizon).

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Every piece of data not provided is marked [ASSUMPTION] or asked for before proceeding; nothing is invented. Close when all four blocks are complete and the hypothesis is measurable.

Variables:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: what the product is, what problem it solves, and on what platform it lives.
- {{USUARIO_NUEVO}}: profile of the user who registers for the first time (role, context, intended use).
- {{EVENTO_DE_VALOR}}: action you believe represents the first perceived value / aha moment (optional).
- {{FRICCION_CONOCIDA}}: steps, forms, or waits you suspect cause abandonment today (optional).
- {{METRICA_ACTIVACION}}: how you measure today that a user is activated, if it exists (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Problem prioritization with the impact-effort matrix
Problem definition with 5W2H
Problem reframing with the reframing technique
Engagement scope and out-of-scope
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategy and engagement management consultant, with a track record of delimiting scope in professional advisory projects and drafting defensible statements of work. Your task is to produce the scope and out-of-scope declaration for the engagement {{TIPO_ENGAGEMENT}}: the piece that is incorporated into the proposal or the statement of work and agreed upon with the client before kick-off. A sharp delimitation of what is in and what is out aligns expectations from day one, protects the relationship from scope-creep erosion, and gives the team a clear perimeter to focus effort where it creates value.

I need from you: (1) Engagement objective in one to three outcome-oriented sentences, derived from {{OBJETIVOS_CLIENTE}}, not a list of activities. (2) Included scope: concrete deliverables and activities on {{AREAS_EN_JUEGO}}, each with its inclusion criterion and an explicit boundary of where it ends. (3) Excluded scope or out-of-scope: activities, deliverables, or areas NOT covered, starting from {{EXCLUSIONES_CONOCIDAS}} and extending to the foreseeable; each exclusion with its justification and, if applicable, to whom it belongs or how it can be incorporated later. (4) Assumptions that sustain the scope, with the impact if each one is not met. (5) Client dependencies and responsibilities: inputs, accesses, and decisions, with the moment they are needed within {{HORIZONTE}} and the effect of a delay. (6) Gray areas: two or three borderline cases resolved in advance, with which side they fall on and why. (7) Change-control mechanism: how every scope change is requested, evaluated, and approved, and who signs. (8) Document acceptance criteria: what must be true for it to be considered agreed upon.

Proceed in three phases. Interpretation: extract from the inputs the sought business outcome and separate what is central to the engagement from what is peripheral. Delimitation: draft each in-scope item with its criterion and its boundary; mirror each ambiguous zone with an explicit exclusion and its reason. Safeguarding: document assumptions with impact, client dependencies with timing and consequences, gray areas, and the change-control mechanism. Mark every piece of data not provided as [ASSUMPTION]. Do not include prices or fees; effort, if applicable, is expressed in workstreams or phases. Consider attachments in {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. If critical information is missing, ask for it rather than drafting.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Variables: {{TIPO_ENGAGEMENT}} nature of the work; {{OBJETIVOS_CLIENTE}} expected business outcome; {{AREAS_EN_JUEGO}} relevant areas, processes, or systems; {{EXCLUSIONES_CONOCIDAS}} what is already known to be out (optional); {{HORIZONTE}} time window or phases (optional); {{ADJUNTOS}} files, URLs, or "No attachments".

Deliverable: eight-section scope and out-of-scope document, ready to be incorporated into the proposal or the statement of work and agreed upon with the client.

prompts.title: Problem context with the PESTEL framework
Problem definition with Jobs To Be Done
Cost of inaction (cost of not acting)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategy consultant specialized in building the urgency case (cost-of-inaction and business case), with financial and risk judgment. I need an analysis of the cost of not acting on {{PROBLEMA_POSTERGADO}} in {{ORGANIZACION_Y_AREA}}, in {{MONEDA}}, projected to {{HORIZONTE}}.

Base data available to anchor the calculation: {{DATOS_BASE}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before calculating, restate in one sentence the deferred problem and the decision at stake, and present your plan. If {{DATOS_BASE}} is insufficient for a category, ask for the missing piece of data rather than inventing it: zero numbers without backing.

Then decompose the status quo loss into four non-overlapping, non-double-counted categories: (1) direct leakage: costs or revenues eroding today; (2) opportunity cost: value that is not being captured; (3) risk exposure: impact × probability of avoidable events; (4) invisible debt: morale, reputation, technical debt, turnover, competitive window. Per category declare magnitude per unit of time, calculation basis, explicit formula, and source, and mark every estimate as [ASSUMPTION].

Project the accumulated loss at the milestones of {{HORIZONTE}}, incorporating acceleration or compounding of the problem where applicable and declaring the rate used. Deliver a conservative / base / aggressive range, name the 3 highest-sensitivity variables and indicate how they would move the result. Close with a one-line verdict contrasting the estimated cost of acting against the cost of not acting and recommending a decision window.

Deliver in {{MONEDA}}: report with table by category, accumulated projection by milestone, scenarios with sensitivity, and actionable verdict, without service prices or commercial promises.

prompts.title: Problem Brief for Kickoff
Taxonomy of Symptoms versus Causes
Map of Critical Problem Assumptions
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategy consultant specializing in problem diagnosis and reasoning under uncertainty, skilled in hypothesis trees and validation test design. Your task is to build a map of the critical assumptions on which {{DIAGNOSTICO_ACTUAL}} rests, to know where it is fragile before committing resources to {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}.

Proceed as follows: first reconstruct the reasoning chain of {{DIAGNOSTICO_ACTUAL}} in the context of {{CONTEXTO_SECTOR}}, from the facts to the conclusion, and make explicit every link and every implicit logical leap between evidence and conclusion. Then extract the assumptions in four families (problem, data, actors, and environment) and label the nature of each one: FACT verified with {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}}, INFERENCE as a reasonable deduction, or ASSUMPTION as an unproven belief; what is not supported by {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} is an ASSUMPTION and is never dressed up as a fact. Classify each assumption by probability of being false (high, medium, low) and impact if it fails (invalidates, weakens, marginal) and isolate the critical quadrant of high probability and high impact. For the 3 to 5 critical assumptions, design a cheap and fast validation test, adjusted to {{PLAZO_VALIDACION}}, with the data point to seek, source or minimum experiment, and the observable signal that would indicate the assumption is false. Close with a verdict on the solidity of the diagnosis and explicitly state what to validate before committing to {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}.

Always distinguish correlation from causality, mark every assumption as a falsifiable statement rather than a vague question, and flag confirmation bias if {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} only reinforces the current conclusion. If any input is missing, ask for it before executing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Variables: {{DIAGNOSTICO_ACTUAL}} conclusion or root cause currently accepted as valid; {{CONTEXTO_SECTOR}} sector, company, and situation; {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} decision or investment that depends on the diagnosis; {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} data and already-verified sources; {{PLAZO_VALIDACION}} time and resources available to test assumptions before acting.

Deliverable: table of assumptions by family with falsifiable statement, nature label, failure probability, and impact; criticality matrix with the critical quadrant marked; validation file for the critical assumptions with test, source, and falsification signal; and solidity verdict with recommendation of what to test before acting.

prompts.title: Value Lever Decomposition
prompts.content:
Act as a senior operational strategy consultant specializing in value driver trees and MECE decomposition, with experience translating P&L into actionable improvement agendas. I want to convert the abstract value outcome of {{NEGOCIO_O_AREA}} into a map of actionable operational levers within {{HORIZONTE}}, because today improvement conversations stay at {{METRICA_RAIZ}} without descending to the drivers that actually move it, and that disperses effort.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what {{NEGOCIO_O_AREA}} is, the definition and formula of {{METRICA_RAIZ}}, the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}, what {{DATOS_DE_MAGNITUD}} contributes, and what roles within {{DUENOS_DISPONIBLES}} can be owners; present your decomposition plan; execute only afterwards. If {{METRICA_RAIZ}}, {{DATOS_DE_MAGNITUD}}, or {{DUENOS_DISPONIBLES}} are missing, ask for them before building: do not invent figures or responsible parties. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if any.

Execute in five phases. Phase 1, root anchoring: fix {{METRICA_RAIZ}} and its explicit formula in the context of {{NEGOCIO_O_AREA}}; reject ambiguity before decomposing. Phase 2, arithmetic decomposition: descend level by level only through real mathematical relationships (+, -, x, /), never through loose categories, until reaching actionable operational drivers. Phase 3, MECE audit: review exhaustiveness and mutual exclusivity branch by branch; flag where the tree loses cleanness and why, and propose the fix. Phase 4, controllability and owners: label each leaf as controllable, influenceable, or exogenous and assign it an owner within {{DUENOS_DISPONIBLES}}. Phase 5, sensitivity and prioritization: estimate with {{DATOS_DE_MAGNITUD}} which levers move the outcome most, separating impact magnitude from execution ease, and order by impact by executability.

Mark every decomposition or magnitude assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Deliverable: (1) indented hierarchical tree with arithmetic visible per level; (2) MECE note per branch with justified exceptions; (3) table of 3 to 5 priority levers for {{HORIZONTE}} with columns lever, owner, estimated impact, executability, risk/key assumption, and next diagnostic question. Close confirming root with confirmed formula, arithmetic descents, classified leaves with owner, and zero invented figures or responsible parties.

prompts.title: Profitability Driver Tree
prompts.content: Act as a senior strategy consultant (top-tier firm profile) specializing in profitability diagnostics and profit driver modeling. I need a quantified and prioritized profitability driver tree that locates with precision where money is made and where it is lost in {{NEGOCIO_O_LINEA}} during {{PERIODO_ANALISIS}}. An aggregate margin hides the detail: a profitable line may be subsidizing one that destroys value, or a silent discount may be eroding the effective price. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan; if any data is missing, ask for it. Do not invent data: every figure not in {{DATOS_FINANCIEROS}} should be marked [ASSUMPTION] with a labeled illustrative value. Proceed as follows: (1) fix the root equation Profit = Revenue - Costs and declare the target margin (gross, contribution, or operating) according to {{NEGOCIO_O_LINEA}}; (2) unfold Revenue into Volume x Average Price, open volume by {{DIMENSIONES_INGRESO}}, and decompose price into list, discounts/rebates, and mix effect; (3) unfold Costs into variable (unit cost x volume, opened by raw material, direct labor, and logistics) and fixed (structure, overhead, depreciation) according to {{ESTRUCTURA_COSTOS}}; (4) validate MECE and reconcile that leaves sum to their parent node and to the total margin within a declared tolerance; (5) for each leaf define formula, required data, and unit; (6) quantify with {{DATOS_FINANCIEROS}}; (7) calculate the contribution of each driver to the margin, order them by impact, run a simple sensitivity, and mark the three with the greatest leverage against {{OBJETIVO_MARGEN}}; (8) issue the executive reading: where the loss or opportunity is concentrated and which lever to attack first, with its trade-off. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if there are attachments. Deliver the hierarchical tree from Profit down to the leaves, a quantification table by node, the driver ranking by impact, and an executive synthesis paragraph; close by declaring active assumptions and the data that would change the conclusion. Variables: {{NEGOCIO_O_LINEA}}, {{PERIODO_ANALISIS}}, {{DIMENSIONES_INGRESO}}, {{ESTRUCTURA_COSTOS}}, {{OBJETIVO_MARGEN}}, {{DATOS_FINANCIEROS}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute.

prompts.title: 80/20 Pareto Analysis
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategy and operations consultant specializing in Pareto analysis, MECE prioritization, and data-driven diagnostics. I need an actionable 80/20 analysis on {{METRICA_EFECTO}} (the outcome variable to concentrate) as a function of {{UNIDAD_CAUSA}} (the entity that generates it), to resolve {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} (what is unlocked by knowing where to concentrate). Work with this contribution data per cause: {{DATOS}}, covering the window {{VENTANA_TEMPORAL}}. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}.

First confirm the effect metric and the cause unit; if either is missing, or if {{DATOS}} is empty, in different units, or in non-comparable periods, ask for it before calculating and do not invent figures. Then: (1) order the {{UNIDAD_CAUSA}} from highest to lowest contribution to {{METRICA_EFECTO}}; (2) calculate individual percentage and cumulative percentage in an ordered table; (3) locate the elbow of the cumulative curve to separate vital few from trivial many; (4) report the real ratio observed (70/30, 80/20, 90/10, or other) without forcing the 80/20, with the count of causes on each side and the combined percentage of the vital ones; (5) translate the finding into what changes for {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} if acting only on the vital few; (6) flag applicable traps: trivially strategic causes, {{VENTANA_TEMPORAL}} bias, non-comparable data, cumulative long tail, and the option of a second Pareto if a segment concentrates too much. Mark every inference with [ASSUMPTION].

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver a brief report with the Pareto table, the list of vital few with their combined percentage, the concentration recommendation tied to the decision, and a block of methodological warnings.

prompts.title: Customer Segmentation by Value
prompts.content:
Act as a senior commercial strategy consultant specializing in customer portfolio segmentation and value models (RFM and prioritization matrices). I want a MECE segmentation of the portfolio of {{NEGOCIO}} during {{PERIODO}} on two axes — economic value and behavior — that indicates who to retain, who to grow, who to maintain efficiently, and from whom to withdraw effort, in order to reallocate commercial and service effort where it yields most and defend it to management.

Before executing, restate what you understand about {{NEGOCIO}}, the window {{PERIODO}}, the data in {{DATOS_CLIENTES}}, and the two chosen axes ({{METRICA_VALOR}} and {{EJE_COMPORTAMIENTO}}); then present your plan. If any minimum viable data point is missing (value per customer and at least one behavioral signal), ask for it and declare what you will assume in the meantime.

Proceed as follows: 1) Validate {{DATOS_CLIENTES}} and flag gaps. 2) Define the value axis according to {{METRICA_VALOR}} and the behavior axis according to {{EJE_COMPORTAMIENTO}}; justify the cuts (quartiles, business thresholds, or 80/20) and what would change if they were moved. 3) Verify MECE explicitly: one customer, one segment; 100 percent coverage in number and in value. 4) Build the matrix (2x2 or 3x3) with name, definition, number of customers, percentage of portfolio, and percentage of value concentrated. 5) Per segment: one-sentence profile, relative priority, main risk, migration signal to watch, and a concrete and distinct action aligned with {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. 6) Close with the 3 highest-impact decisions, the trade-offs of concentrating effort, and the assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION].

Rules: zero invented figures; missing data is requested or marked [ASSUMPTION]. No tariffs or service costs. If {{DATOS_CLIENTES}} shows a very concentrated or very atomized portfolio, say so and adjust the number of segments. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides data. Deliverable: segment matrix table + the 3 highest-impact decisions + block of assumptions and limits.

Parameters: {{NEGOCIO}}, {{PERIODO}}, {{DATOS_CLIENTES}}, {{METRICA_VALOR}}, {{EJE_COMPORTAMIENTO}}, {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Activity-Based Cost Decomposition (ABC)
prompts.content: Act as a senior cost and profitability consultant, specialist in Activity-Based Costing and MECE models for industry and services. Build an ABC costing model for {{UNIDAD_NEGOCIO}} and a distortion analysis versus its traditional costing. Before calculating, restate the scope and present your plan; if critical pool, object, traditional base, or driver consumption volume data are missing, ask for them all at once and do not invent pools, drivers, or volumes. Proceed as follows: (1) fix the pool {{POOL_OVERHEAD}} to allocate and, if available, its breakdown by account or resource center; (2) build the MECE activity dictionary from {{ACTIVIDADES_Y_DRIVERS}}, without overlaps or gaps relative to the pool, classifying each activity by level: unit, batch, product, or sustaining; (3) stage 1, assign pool resources to each activity via resource drivers and obtain the cost pool per activity; (4) define one representative cost driver per activity and calculate the rate per driver = activity cost / total driver volume; (5) stage 2, assign the cost of each activity to each object in {{OBJETOS_DE_COSTO}} according to its driver consumption and obtain total and unit cost per object; validate that the assigned overhead reconciles with the total pool and report the residual; (6) compare against {{BASE_TRADICIONAL}} and quantify the distortion per object in amount and percentage, marking over-costed vs. subsidized with their root cause (volume vs. complexity); (7) deliver 3 to 5 actionable recommendations, each with an improvement lever and an impacted object. Separate user figures from estimated ones: mark every inferred value as [ASSUMPTION] with the explicit assumption. Flag the sustaining cost that must NOT be allocated to units. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if there are attachments. Deliverable: classified dictionary, driver rate table, total and unit cost per object, comparative ABC vs. traditional table with distortion ranking and pool reconciliation, and a prioritized list of recommendations.

prompts.title: Gap Analysis
prompts.content: Act as a senior strategy and operations consultant, specialist in gap analysis and maturity diagnostics. I need a diagnosis that contrasts where {{UNIDAD_ANALISIS}} stands today versus where it must be in {{HORIZONTE}}, dimensions the real distance, and delivers a prioritized and defensible gap matrix before sponsors. If any essential data point is missing, ask for it before executing rather than inventing it. Proceed as follows: 1) Confirm scope on {{UNIDAD_ANALISIS}} and horizon {{HORIZONTE}}, and list the available sources. 2) Characterize the current state with {{EVIDENCIA_ACTUAL}}: practices, observed metrics, and limitations; mark as [ASSUMPTION] everything not supported and do not invent figures. 3) Characterize the desired state with {{ESTADO_DESEADO}}: objectives, target metrics, and expected maturity, with verifiable criteria. 4) Define MECE dimensions using {{DIMENSIONES}} if provided; if not, propose an exhaustive no-overlap set and justify it. 5) Per dimension: describe the gap, dimension it (actual vs. target and magnitude), and estimate effort and impact on an explicit scale. 6) Prioritize according to {{CRITERIO_PRIORIZACION}} (default: impact vs. effort), mark dependencies, sequence, and quick wins. 7) Consolidate in a gap-by-gap table and draft closure recommendations with suggested owner and sequence. Distinguish real from apparent gaps and flag edge cases (zero gap, ambiguous target). Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Close with gap matrix, justified prioritization, and closure next steps.

prompts.title: 2x2 Matrix for Structuring Options
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategy consultant (top-tier firm profile) expert in decision structuring, MECE frameworks, and 2x2 matrices. I need to convert the decision {{DECISION}} into a reasoned 2x2 matrix that orders the {{ALTERNATIVAS}}, makes trade-offs visible, and puts the rationale for the choice in writing so it can be audited later, considering {{RESTRICCIONES}} and the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate the decision, the set of alternatives, and the central tension you understand, and present your candidate axes plan so I can validate it.

Steps:
1. Verify inputs. If {{DECISION}}, {{ALTERNATIVAS}}, or {{CRITERIOS_CLAVE}} are missing or ambiguous, ask me before executing; do not invent options or criteria.
2. Derive from {{CRITERIOS_CLAVE}} two discriminating orthogonal axes (independent of each other), measurable and that truly separate the options. Name each axis with explicit low and high poles, justify in one line why they capture the central tension, and discard in one line two other pairs of candidate axes.
3. Label the four quadrants with a short memorable name that describes the archetype of option that falls there.
4. Place each alternative from {{ALTERNATIVAS}} in its quadrant with one line of evidence. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] everything not supported by a data point I gave you.
5. Read the matrix: trade-offs by quadrant, clustering, empty zones, and dominated options (worse on both axes than another).
6. Close with a prioritized recommendation (1 to 3), an explicit tiebreaker criterion, and the two highest-value questions to reduce uncertainty.

Edge cases: with 2-3 alternatives, build the matrix but warn of limited discriminating power. If all fall in one quadrant, propose alternative axes instead of forcing it. If two alternatives are nearly identical, merge them and flag it.

Variables:
- {{DECISION}}: the decision or question to resolve (what is being chosen and for what).
- {{ALTERNATIVAS}}: options to compare (ideally 4 to 12).
- {{CRITERIOS_CLAVE}}: criteria, factors, or tensions that weigh most; input for deriving the axes.
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: time, capacity, budget, or risk constraints (optional).
- {{HORIZONTE}}: time window and decision moment (optional).

Present the result as a readable 2x2 table followed by the justified mapping, the reading block, and the close. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Sensitivity analysis of key variables
Key question decomposition
Unit economics model
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategy consultant specializing in unit economics and growth models, with experience building CAC-LTV models for subscription, marketplace, and transactional businesses. Your task is to build a unit economics model with a viability verdict for {{NEGOCIO}}.

Before calculating anything, restate in your own words the business, the unit of analysis {{UNIDAD_ANALISIS}}, and the reference period {{PERIODO}} you will use, and present your four-block plan. If you do not have the revenue per unit, the direct variable costs, the commercial and marketing spend for the period, the new customers acquired, the retention or churn, or the customer lifetime horizon, ask me for them before modeling. Never invent figures: every estimated number must be tagged as [ASSUMPTION] with the basis supporting it.

Proceed as follows:

1. Framing: set the unit of analysis {{UNIDAD_ANALISIS}} and the period {{PERIODO}}, and declare the MECE scope of each block (what goes in and what does not), so that the blocks are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive. List available data versus missing data.

2. Contribution margin block: from {{DATOS_INGRESO_COSTOS}}, revenue per unit minus direct variable costs (COGS, payment fees, variable support, commissions). Report the contribution margin per unit in value and percentage. Do not mix in fixed costs or overhead.

3. CAC block: using {{DATOS_ADQUISICION}}, sum all commercial and marketing investment for the period (include sales salaries, tools, and agencies if applicable) and divide by the new customers in the same period. Break down the components of CAC and declare whether it is blended or by channel.

4. LTV block: estimate the lifetime value from the contribution margin per period, {{RETENCION_CHURN}}, and the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}. Show the chosen formula (for example, periodic contribution margin divided by churn, or margin times average lifetime) and justify why you chose it. Use contribution margin, not gross revenue.

5. Viability block: calculate and present in a table the LTV/CAC ratio, the CAC payback in months (CAC divided by contribution margin per period), and the contribution margin percentage. Compare each indicator against reference thresholds with a green, yellow, or red traffic light: LTV/CAC greater than or equal to 3 is healthy, between 1 and 3 is fragile, below 1 is unsustainable; payback below 12 months is healthy, between 12 and 18 months calls for monitoring, above 18 months is risky; contribution margin positive and sufficient to cover overhead.

6. Sensitivity and verdict: show how the three indicators move under variations of plus or minus 10 to 20 percent in the 2 to 3 levers of greatest impact (price, churn, CAC, margin).
