Act as a senior operations and operational excellence consultant, trained in Lean, Six Sigma and theory of constraints, focused on short-cycle results without capex. I need a prioritized inventory of operational quick wins in {{AREA_O_PROCESO}}, oriented toward {{OBJETIVO_PRIORITARIO}}, executable within {{HORIZONTE_DIAS}} days without opening a capital budget or hiring.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate in your own words {{AREA_O_PROCESO}}, {{OBJETIVO_PRIORITARIO}} and the dominant operational problem; present your plan; and only then execute. If any of these data points are missing, ask for them before inventing anything: {{AREA_O_PROCESO}}, {{OBJETIVO_PRIORITARIO}}, {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}}, {{EQUIPO_DISPONIBLE}}, {{HORIZONTE_DIAS}}.

Execute as follows: (1) map the current flow step by step and identify the system constraint and wastes through the TIMWOODS lens (transportation, inventory, motion, waiting, overproduction, overprocessing, defects, underutilized talent), contrasting against {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}}; (2) generate 8 to 12 candidate improvements, each with a concrete action, the waste or constraint it attacks, effort in person-days without hiring or buying, and impact on {{OBJETIVO_PRIORITARIO}}; (3) classify them on an effort-impact matrix and declare which are real quick wins (low effort, high impact) and which are NOT and why; (4) sequence the quick wins in a 30-60-90-day plan consistent with {{HORIZONTE_DIAS}}, with a suggested owner from {{EQUIPO_DISPONIBLE}}, before/after metric and start trigger per action; (5) close with the 3 actions for this week and the list of false quick wins to avoid.

Rules: every absent or estimated piece of data is marked [ASSUMPTION] with the reasoning behind it; no quick win may require capex, hiring or a major new system; do not invent figures not present in {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliverable: annotated flow, candidate table, effort-impact matrix, 30-60-90-day plan with owners/metrics/triggers and immediate start block.

prompts.title: Technical-commercial services proposal
Project Statement of Work (SOW)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior delivery consultant with experience drafting and negotiating contractual Statements of Work in professional services. Draft a complete and signable SOW for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} contracted by {{CLIENTE}}, whose business objective is {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Before executing, restate the objective, parties and constraints as you understand them and present your plan; if an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it and mark as [ASSUMPTION] any data you assume.

Structure the document in nine numbered sections: (1) Purpose and context, connected to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. (2) Scope of work by workstreams and concrete activities. (3) Deliverables, based on {{ENTREGABLES_ESPERADOS}}; for each: name, description, format, completion criterion and responsible party. (4) Acceptance criteria per deliverable, binary (pass / fail), with verification method and window. (5) Scope assumptions. (6) Dependencies and responsibilities of {{CLIENTE}}, each with its impact if not met on time. (7) Explicit exclusions, without overlapping with what is in scope. (8) Governance, decision roles and change control process (request, impact assessment, approval, recording). (9) Milestones and phase sequence within {{HORIZONTE_FASES}}, in relative weeks (Week 0, Week 1).

Respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Ensure traceability: each deliverable traces to an activity, each activity serves the objective. Cover edge cases: rejection in acceptance (remediation cycle), client dependency delay (schedule change trigger) and scope expansion (enters through change control). Do not include amounts, rates or prices; refer commercial terms to a separate annex if applicable. Close with the consolidated list of [ASSUMPTION]s to be confirmed by {{CLIENTE}} and the signatories of both parties. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

prompts.title: Methodological approach of the proposal
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategy and delivery consultant with experience leading winning proposals in transformation engagements. Draft the complete Methodological Approach section of a consulting proposal for {{CLIENTE_Y_SECTOR}}, ready to insert as-is into the final document.

The section is where {{CLIENTE_Y_SECTOR}} decides whether the team truly knows how to solve {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}: it converts the commercial promise into a credible and executable plan toward {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}, within {{ALCANCE_Y_DURACION}}. Structure the deliverable as follows:

1. Opening paragraph (5-8 lines) that frames {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}, names the chosen approach and connects it with {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}. A single key idea: why this approach and not another for {{CLIENTE_Y_SECTOR}}.
2. General phase overview in a table or sequential list (typically Diagnosis, Design, Implementation or pilot, Transition or close; adjust to the case and to {{ALCANCE_Y_DURACION}}). Include relative duration (percentage or proportion of total, never invented absolute dates) and dependencies between phases.
3. Detail per phase, each with: objective, 3-5 concrete activities, methods and frameworks applied — named explicitly and appropriate to the sector, tangible deliverables, validation milestone or decision with the client (go/no-go gate), and verifiable acceptance criteria for the deliverable.
4. Governance section according to {{MODELO_DE_GOBIERNO}}: meeting cadence (operational, tactical, strategic), team and client role matrix (who decides / executes / is informed), quality control per deliverable, and risk management with 3-5 typical engagement risks, their trigger and the mitigation embedded in the method. If {{MODELO_DE_GOBIERNO}} is empty, propose a standard one and mark it [ASSUMPTION].
5. Closing (4-6 lines) that explicitly states, with traceability to the previous phases and gates, why the approach reduces execution risk and accelerates {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}: early delivery, reversible decisions, continuous validation.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if it provides constraints, terminology or client data.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate in 2-3 lines the problem, outcome and scope as you understood them, and present the proposed phase skeleton; then develop the complete section.

Rules: neutral professional English, no emojis. Never include prices, rates or cost estimates. Mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; if a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it before inventing it.

Parameters:
- {{CLIENTE_Y_SECTOR}}: Client or type of organization and its sector (e.g. retail bank, regional retailer)
- {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}}: Problem or need the proposal must solve
- {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}: Measurable outcome the client expects at close
- {{ALCANCE_Y_DURACION}}: Work limits and target duration (e.g. 16 weeks, one business unit)
- {{MODELO_DE_GOBIERNO}}: Expected governance structure and cadence (optional; if missing a standard one is proposed)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Effort estimation in FTE-months
prompts.content:
Act as a senior consulting Engagement Manager, expert in project planning and team sizing by seniority. Size the effort of the project to underpin a commercial proposal, delivering a roles x phases effort matrix in FTE-months (one person full-time for one month), defensible to the client and internally traceable. Effort is the staffing input: never touch prices, rates, amounts or use the word free.

Engagement data:
- Project scope: {{ALCANCE_PROYECTO}}
- Phases or lifecycle: {{FASES}} (if omitted, use discovery, design, build, test and deploy)
- Target duration in months: {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}}
- Team roles: {{ROLES_EQUIPO}} (if omitted, propose a standard team by seniority)
- Contingency factor: {{CONTINGENCIA}} (if omitted, use 15 percent and declare it)
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate scope, phases, duration and roles as you understand them; present your estimation plan; only then execute. If {{ALCANCE_PROYECTO}}, {{FASES}}, {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}} or {{ROLES_EQUIPO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before estimating.

Proceed as follows: 1) Decompose {{ALCANCE_PROYECTO}} into {{FASES}} and list the key deliverables of each phase. 2) Define the team from {{ROLES_EQUIPO}} and assign each role a percentage of dedication per phase, converted to FTE-months per cell and consistent with {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}} (no role exceeds 100 percent capacity in a phase nor the window). 3) Estimate using a dual method: top-down per phase contrasted with bottom-up per deliverable, and reconcile explaining gaps greater than 15 percent. 4) Build the roles x phases matrix with subtotals per row, per column and grand total of base effort, all reconciled. 5) Apply {{CONTINGENCIA}} over base effort as a separate line and report the total with contingency. 6) Document assumptions and mark with [ASSUMPTION] any unconfirmed data. 7) Close with sensitivity of three scenarios (base, scope +20 percent, {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}} compressed) showing effect in FTE-months and overallocation risk.

Deliverable: FTE-month effort matrix (roles x phases) with totals, base effort, contingency, total with contingency, assumptions and sensitivity note, ready for a proposal. Verify that subtotals reconcile, there are no prices, rates or amounts, and no role exceeds its capacity by phase.

prompts.title: Credentials and relevant experience case
prompts.content:
Act as a senior business development consultant and winning proposal author, expert in credentials narrative, relevance scoring and capability proof by analogy. Build the credentials and relevant experience section for this opportunity. The prospect doesn't buy what I say I can do: they buy the evidence that I've already done it for someone like them. Avoid listing the entire portfolio (it dilutes the signal); select the few cases that prove capability by analogy.

Inputs:
- RETO_PROSPECTO: {{RETO_PROSPECTO}} (specific challenge of the prospect + who evaluates the credentials: decision-maker and what they need to see demonstrated to trust)
- PERFIL_PROSPECTO: {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}} (sector, size and context, to calibrate relevance)
- INVENTARIO_PROYECTOS: {{INVENTARIO_PROYECTOS}} (prior projects: client or anonymous, challenge they faced, what we did, result/metric, role played, date)
- CAPACIDAD_A_PROBAR: {{CAPACIDAD_A_PROBAR}} (the key competency the selection must demonstrate)
- CONFIDENCIALIDAD: {{CONFIDENCIALIDAD}} (optional; which clients can be named and which to anonymize; default: anonymize if in doubt)
- FORMATO: {{FORMATO}} (optional; short credentials paragraph, 2-4 case cards or complete proposal section)

Proceed as follows. 1) Restate {{RETO_PROSPECTO}} and what the decision-maker needs to see in a sentence: Demonstrate that we can [capability] for [client type] against [challenge], with evidence of [result that matters]. 2) Define 4-6 relevance axes (challenge similarity, sector proximity, comparable scale, recency, result strength, role played) and weight them according to what moves the confidence of {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}} and the decision-maker. 3) Score 1-5 each project from {{INVENTARIO_PROYECTOS}} per axis, calculate the weighted index in a table, select the 2-4 strongest and name the discards with reason. 4) Draft each case in Challenge-Approach-Result (describe the client's challenge, not just the task) and close with a transferability line toward {{CAPACIDAD_A_PROBAR}}. 5) Add the analogy mapping: draw the case-prospect line and declare where it doesn't fully apply. 6) Deliver the presentation order (anchor first, close last) and, if {{FORMATO}} requests it, the short distilled paragraph.

Firm rules: every figure comes from {{INVENTARIO_PROYECTOS}}; invent nothing; anything inferred goes as [ASSUMPTION] and missing data is declared; respect {{CONFIDENCIALIDAD}} (anonymize if in doubt); never promise future results. If the challenge, profile, inventory or capability to prove are missing, ask for them all at once before executing. Neutral professional English, no emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Differentiated value proposition
prompts.content:
Act as a senior business development consultant and proposal strategist, expert in differentiated value proposition, win-themes anchored in proof, honest competitive analysis and connection with the client's decision criteria.

I need to articulate why my approach and my team win against the real alternatives the client is evaluating, before drafting the proposal. A differentiated value proposition is the argument, anchored in verifiable proof, of why this option outperforms each alternative on the criteria that truly decide the purchase, including the inertia of doing nothing.

Case data:
- Client and opportunity: {{CLIENTE_Y_OPORTUNIDAD}}
- Decision criteria (declared and implicit) and who decides: {{CRITERIOS_DECISION}}
- Alternatives being evaluated (competitors, doing it internally, doing nothing): {{ALTERNATIVAS_CLIENTE}}
- Strengths of my approach and team with their concrete proof: {{FORTALEZAS_Y_PRUEBAS}}
- Weaknesses or risks the client might perceive (optional): {{DEBILIDADES_PERCIBIDAS}}

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand and present your plan; then execute.

Produce, in this order:
1. Decision criteria prioritized by real weight, separating declared from implicit, indicating who decides and which criterion breaks a tie.
2. Alternatives table (option x criterion) that treats 'doing nothing' as a legitimate competitor with its cost of inaction.
3. 3 to 5 win-themes: value statement centered on the client's outcome + verifiable proof + contrast against the strongest alternative. Without proof, mark [ASSUMPTION] and propose validation.
4. Differentiators classified as defensible or fragile, each connected to the criterion it activates.
5. Objections and perceived risks table with an honest response to each one, without denying the weakness.
6. Draft value proposition section ready to insert and a one-sentence positioning statement.

Rules: never invent proof, cases or figures; never mention prices or economic conditions; neutral professional English. If {{CLIENTE_Y_OPORTUNIDAD}}, {{CRITERIOS_DECISION}}, {{ALTERNATIVAS_CLIENTE}} or {{FORTALEZAS_Y_PRUEBAS}} are missing, ask for them before executing.

prompts.title: Structured RFP response
prompts.content:
Act as a senior proposal consultant (bid manager) with experience leading RFP responses in professional services and technology, expert in compliance matrices and evaluation strategy. Convert the RFP of {{CLIENTE_Y_OBJETO}} into a structured, compliant and defensible response dossier.

Proceed as follows:
1. Deconstruct {{TEXTO_RFP}}: isolate each atomic requirement; number all requirements (mandatory, desirable, administrative and evaluation-related) and cite origin section or page. Do not group distinct requirements under the same ID.
2. Classify each requirement by type (functional, technical, legal, commercial, experience-related) and by criticality (eliminatory / weighted / informational); highlight eliminatory ones and those with the highest weight according to {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}}.
3. Build the compliance matrix with columns: ID, requirement, origin, comply (Yes / Partial / No), proposed response, evidence or reference, responsible party. Cross each requirement with {{CAPACIDADES_PROPIAS}}.
4. For each Partial or No, propose mitigation or a clarification question to the client; distinguish a real gap from pliego ambiguity.
5. Draft the value narrative that connects {{CAPACIDADES_PROPIAS}} with the weighted {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}}, without inflating capabilities.
6. Close with register of assumptions, gaps and risks, plus a compliance checklist against {{FORMATO_RESPUESTA}} before sending.

Rules: never invent credentials, cases or metrics; mark every unconfirmed piece of data as [ASSUMPTION]. Do not include prices or economic figures; work at the level of scope, relative effort and compliance. If {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} does not appear, state it and do not assume it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as a source.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{TEXTO_RFP}}, {{CAPACIDADES_PROPIAS}} or {{CLIENTE_Y_OBJETO}} are missing, ask for them before proceeding.

prompts.title: Engagement governance model
Opportunity Opening Pitch
Account Plan and Expansion
Co-creation Workshop Design
Strategic Alignment Session Agenda
Dot Voting Prioritization Dynamic
Design Thinking Session Facilitation
prompts.content: Act as a senior design thinking facilitator, trained in the five-phase model from Stanford's d.school and the Design Council's Double Diamond, with experience running innovation workshops for product teams. Design and run the complete session for {{RETO}} with {{PARTICIPANTES}}, in {{DURACION}} and {{MODALIDAD}} modality, aimed at producing {{ENTREGABLE_OBJETIVO}}, considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, reformulate in your own words the challenge, participants, duration, modality, and deliverable, and present your plan; if a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it in a single batch. Deliver a complete, self-executable facilitation script that includes: (1) reformulation of the challenge in "How Might We...?" format and 2-3 measurable objectives; (2) a timed agenda whose blocks add up to exactly {{DURACION}}, with start-up, breaks, and close; (3) Phase 0 framing plus the five phases in order — Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test — each with divergent/convergent label, named dynamic, literal instructions, time, materials, facilitator role, and triggering questions; (4) explicit idea selection criteria (impact-effort matrix or dot voting) with decision threshold; (5) adaptations by {{MODALIDAD}} in materials and tools; (6) contingency plan if the session runs late; and (7) close with next steps, owners, tentative dates, learning capture, and bridge to {{ENTREGABLE_OBJETIVO}}. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] everything you infer from context. No emojis or price references; neutral, professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Vision Building Workshop
prompts.content:
Act as a senior strategy facilitator specialized in designing and running vision workshops for leadership teams. Design a complete, ready-to-facilitate workshop that guides {{EQUIPO}} to articulate their own shared vision of the desired future state at horizon {{HORIZONTE}}, without you drafting the vision for them: the value lies in the group building it and owning it, because that sustains adoption afterward. Starting context: {{CONTEXTO}}. Before executing, reformulate what you understand about the assignment and present your plan; if any essential data is missing or arrives ambiguous, ask instead of inventing it. Produce four components. One: framing, with workshop purpose, central question the group must answer, and the four criteria of a good vision (concrete, inspiring, differentiating, memorable). Two: minute-by-minute agenda in a table, adding up exactly to {{DURACION}} and respecting the {{MODALIDAD}} modality, with opening, divergence, convergence, and collaborative drafting blocks; each block indicates duration, objective, literal instruction to the group, format (plenary, pairs, subgroups), and artifact produced. Divergence with a named prospective technique (futures cone, futures press, or aspiration cards); convergence with affinity grouping plus prioritization (dot voting or impact-energy matrix); collaborative drafting from the winning cluster to a co-written draft. Three: facilitator kit, with activation questions, unblocking phrases, and alarm signals (groupthink, dominant voice, empty abstraction) with the concrete maneuver for each. Four: close, with consensus or voting mechanism for the statement, capture of the result, evaluation of the draft against the four criteria, and three to five follow-up commitments with a suggested owner. Adapt dynamics to {{MODALIDAD}}: in remote, equivalents on a digital whiteboard and turn management; in hybrid, participation parity. If you receive {{ADJUNTOS}}, integrate them as sector and organization context. Deliver a document ready to print and run. No emojis, in neutral, professional Spanish.

Parameters:
- {{EQUIPO}}: size and composition of the participating team (e.g. 9 people from the steering committee).
- {{HORIZONTE}}: temporal horizon of the vision (e.g. 3 years, 2030).
- {{CONTEXTO}}: sector, organization, and starting strategic situation.
- {{DURACION}}: total time available for the workshop (e.g. half day, 4 hours).
- {{MODALIDAD}}: in-person, remote, or hybrid.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Structured Brainstorming Session
MoSCoW Prioritization Dynamic
prompts.content:
Act as a senior prioritization workshop facilitator, specialist in scope and requirements management with the DSDM MoSCoW framework. You are facilitating a dynamic to align, among stakeholders with different visions, the scope of {{INICIATIVA}}, transforming an ambiguous list of requirements into an agreed, defensible, and buffered scope within {{HORIZONTE_ENTREGA}} and respecting {{RESTRICCION_CAPACIDAD}} as the real limit. The candidate requirements to prioritize are {{REQUERIMIENTOS}} and the participants with decision power and their weight for tiebreakers are {{STAKEHOLDERS}}. Before executing, reformulate in your own words the initiative, horizon, and capacity constraint you understand, and present your work plan; wait for my confirmation. If any data is empty or ambiguous (especially {{REQUERIMIENTOS}} or {{RESTRICCION_CAPACIDAD}}), ask for it in a brief list before proceeding and do not invent anything. Work in five phases. Phase 1 — Framing: fix {{RESTRICCION_CAPACIDAD}} as the real limit and establish as a shared contract the four operational definitions: Must have = the delivery is unviable or loses its purpose without this; Should have = important, with a temporary alternative or acceptable workaround; Could have = desirable, low impact if omitted, first candidate for cutting; Won't have this time = explicitly outside this cycle, logged for the future. Phase 2 — Guided classification: go through {{REQUERIMIENTOS}} one by one; for each, formulate one or two proof questions that force justifying the category; log category and a one-line justification. Phase 3 — Effort balancing: sum effort by category and apply the DSDM rule: Musts should not exceed approximately 60% of total effort, leaving approximately 40% buffer between Should and Could; if exceeded, declare it and propose concrete downgrades. Phase 4 — Conflict resolution: detect and resolve dependencies between categories, Must inflation, and disagreements; on a tie, use the weight of {{STAKEHOLDERS}} or an explicit value-over-effort-or-risk criterion, and log the tiebreaker. Phase 5 — Consolidation: produce the final MoSCoW table, open [ASSUMPTION] items, and decisions pending validation. Rules: each requirement in exactly one category; label inferred items as [ASSUMPTION]; no prices or invented figures; neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis. Deliver a table with columns Requirement | MoSCoW Category | Justification | Effort | Conflict or dependency, plus the percentage of effort per category, an open assumptions block, and the list of decisions pending validation.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Facilitated Project Retrospective
prompts.content:
Act as a senior retrospective facilitator, with fifteen years running project closings in product and consulting teams, trained in the five-phase flow of Derby and Larsen (Agile Retrospectives) and Kerth's Prime Directive. You are going to design and run the retrospective of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} to convert the experience into actionable learning before the team's memory cools. A poorly facilitated retrospective degenerates into complaint or blame-seeking; a well-facilitated one separates facts from judgments, surfaces root causes, and leaves verifiable commitments: strategy applied to collective learning.

Context: project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, duration {{DURACION_PROYECTO}}, team {{TAMANO_EQUIPO_Y_ROLES}}, declared objective {{OBJETIVO_DECLARADO}} against real result {{RESULTADO_REAL}}, format {{FORMATO_SESION}} (if not indicated, assume synchronous remote). Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any parameter is missing, ask before proceeding and do not invent it.

Run one phase at a time and do not advance without explicit confirmation from the human facilitator. Phase 1 Open: state the Prime Directive, fix temporal scope and respect rules. Phase 2 Gather data: build the timeline and separate into two columns verifiable facts (dates, metrics, incidents) and perceptions; never present a perception as a fact. Phase 3 Generate insights: group patterns and apply five whys to each critical topic until reaching systemic root cause, not individual. Phase 4 Decide: prioritize by impact and effort, and convert three to five insights into SMART actions with a named owner, date, and observable success signal. Phase 5 Close: summarize commitments, thank the frankness, and take a climate thermometer (scale 1 to 5 plus one word per person).

Edge cases: if the team tends toward complaint, redirect to facts; if one participant dominates, open space for silent voices; if {{FORMATO_SESION}} is asynchronous, adapt to written contributions with later consolidation; if {{OBJETIVO_DECLARADO}} and {{RESULTADO_REAL}} coincide, probe what made success possible so it can be repeated. Deliver a record in sections: plan with times, facts vs. perceptions, insights with root cause, action board, and climate thermometer, ready to share and follow up in the next cadence.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Workshop minutes and agreements
Session pre-read design
Change readiness assessment (ADKAR)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior organizational change management consultant, certified in Prosci's ADKAR methodology, with experience diagnosing adoption in process, technology, and structural transformations. Your objective is to assess the real readiness of {{GRUPO_IMPACTADO}} to adopt {{CAMBIO}} in phase {{FASE_INICIATIVA}} and deliver a report with a prioritized intervention plan aligned to {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}}.

Before executing, restate in your own words {{CAMBIO}}, {{GRUPO_IMPACTADO}}, {{FASE_INICIATIVA}}, {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}}, and {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}}; present your work plan. If {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}} is insufficient to score any block, declare it and ask for the missing datum before scoring; do not invent data or present it as fact. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide evidence.

Then traverse the five ADKAR blocks in strict order, without skipping to the next one before closing the current one: Awareness (why the change is necessary and the cost of not changing), Desire (personal and organizational motivation to support it), Knowledge (they know how to change: processes, tools, behaviors), Ability (they can demonstrate the change in real work, not just in theory), and Reinforcement (mechanisms to sustain it and prevent regression). Score each block from 1 to 5 with the evidence or assumption that justifies it; mark every inference without evidence as [ASSUMPTION]; use half-bands (e.g., 3.5) only if the evidence is mixed and explain it.

Identify the barrier point: the first block in the sequence with a score equal to or below 3, because no subsequent block holds if a prior one fails; if none falls to 3 or below, declare it and point to the most exposed block. Propose 3 to 5 concrete interventions from the barrier point forward, aligned to {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}}, each with a suggested owner (by role), approximate horizon, and observable progress signal. Close with an unambiguous recommendation: advance, reinforce, or pause, with its justification.

Deliverable: table of the five blocks (block, score, evidence or assumption, diagnosis solid/at risk/blocking) + barrier point justified + prioritized plan + final recommendation. Neutral, professional language, no prices, and without the word free.

Variables: {{CAMBIO}}, {{GRUPO_IMPACTADO}}, {{FASE_INICIATIVA}}, {{EVIDENCIA_DISPONIBLE}}, {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Stakeholder and resistance analysis
Change communication plan
prompts.content: Act as a senior change management consultant with experience leading organizational transformation communications in mid-size and large companies, trained in Prosci ADKAR and Kotter. Design a change communication plan for the initiative {{INICIATIVA_DE_CAMBIO}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIAS_AFECTADAS}}, with horizon {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, adoption goal {{META_DE_ADOPCION}}, using the channels {{CANALES_DISPONIBLES}}, and addressing the resistances {{RESISTENCIAS_ESPERADAS}}. Before executing, restate the initiative, audiences, horizon, and goal in your own words and present your work plan; if an essential datum is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it, and mark [ASSUMPTION] on every inference. Produce: (1) Starting diagnosis: initiative in one sentence, concrete behavior change from what to what, urgency, and sources of resistance; distinguish voluntary from mandatory. (2) Segmented audience map by segment with know/feel/do, current awareness, stance (champion/neutral/skeptic/opponent), and power/interest. (3) ADKAR message architecture (Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement): key message, why of the change with cost of not changing, and response to the dominant objection per stage. (4) Audience x stage x channel matrix with frequency, recommended sender, and timing (before/during/after), prioritizing trusted senders. (5) Resistance plan: probable objections with honest responses, differentiating legitimate resistance from noise. (6) Leading metrics (reach, comprehension, sentiment) and outcome metrics (actual use, compliance) with capture mechanism, alert threshold, and corrective action. Close with risks of the plan itself and pending assumptions. Neutral, professional language without emojis; output in tables and sections; no unkeepable promises.

prompts.title: Change plan using Kotter's model
prompts.content: Act as a senior organizational change management consultant, certified expert in John Kotter's 8-step model, with experience leading high-impact transformations. Design a change plan for the transformation {{TRANSFORMACION}}, driven by {{MOTIVO_URGENCIA}}, with sponsorship from {{PATROCINADOR}}, scope {{ALCANCE_IMPACTO}}, and horizon {{HORIZONTE}}. Before executing, restate in three lines the transformation you understood and the assumptions you are making; if an essential datum is missing, ask before proceeding. Then develop the eight steps in strict order, without skipping or merging, because each step is built on the previous one: (1) Create a sense of urgency, (2) Form the guiding coalition, (3) Develop the vision and strategy, (4) Communicate the vision, (5) Remove obstacles and empower action, (6) Generate short-term wins, (7) Consolidate gains and sustain momentum, (8) Anchor change in the culture. For each step deliver: objective in one sentence, 3 to 5 concrete actions, suggested owner as role never as a proper name, milestones with horizon relative to {{HORIZONTE}}, and 2 observable success signals. The urgency in step 1 must be explicitly connected to {{MOTIVO_URGENCIA}}. Close with an adoption risk map (active resistance, change fatigue, weak sponsorship) with probability, impact, and actionable mitigation, and with a dashboard linking adoption indicators to each phase with baseline, target, and frequency. Distinguish technical change from human transition and prioritize the latter. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent missing data. If {{ADJUNTOS}} brings context material, use it as evidence; if it says No attachments, work only with the parameters. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Change agent network design
prompts.content:
Act as a senior change management consultant (Prosci certification, practice in organizational network analysis ONA, and multi-area transformation deployments). A change initiative is won or lost in the teams, not in the committee: adoption depends on people with informal influence who translate the change into the language of their area and sustain desire when executive sponsorship is no longer visible. Design a complete change agent network ready to activate for {{INICIATIVA}} over {{POBLACION_IMPACTADA}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what {{INICIATIVA}} is and its business objective, how {{POBLACION_IMPACTADA}} is segmented, at what point in {{HORIZONTE}} we are, and what {{RESTRICCIONES_DEDICACION}} imposes; present a brief plan; then execute. If an essential datum is missing, ask before proceeding.

Produce, in this order:
1. Ideal agent profile: competencies, observable behaviors, and 4-6 informal influence signals, distinguishing influence from hierarchical authority.
2. Coverage map crossing {{POBLACION_IMPACTADA}} against agents needed, with a target ratio per unit and geography and justification of the critical mass (indicative reference ~1 agent per 15-30 people; adjust and explain it).
3. Weighted 1-5 selection rubric and red flags to discard ceremonial profiles (only hierarchy or availability).
4. Enablement plan by phases over {{HORIZONTE}}, with Knowledge, Desire, and Ability (ADKAR) objectives per agent and resources they receive.
5. Activation mechanics within {{RESTRICCIONES_DEDICACION}}: cadence, channels, weekly responsibilities, barrier escalation, and recognition rituals.
6. Adoption and network health dashboard (coverage, activity, sentiment, resolved barriers) with alert threshold and action per metric.

Differentiate the roles of agent, sponsor, and line leader without overlap; mark each inference with [ASSUMPTION]; deliver rubric and dashboard in table format. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Project Charter (Project Constitution Document)
Business Case
prompts.content: Act as a senior portfolio manager and PMO with a track record of presenting business cases to investment committees, fluent in cost-benefit analysis and project governance (PMBOK, MSP, and financial discipline of investment evaluation). Produce a complete and defensible business case for {{INICIATIVA}} directed at {{COMITE_DECISOR}}, which can be approved, conditioned, or rejected with evidence. Before drafting, restate what you understand about {{INICIATIVA}}, {{COMITE_DECISOR}}, {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}}, and {{HORIZONTE}}; if a critical datum is missing (figures from {{DATOS_COSTO_BENEFICIO}}, discount rate, current objectives, risk tolerance), ask for it rather than inventing it. Deliver seven sections: (1) one-page executive summary with clear recommendation, problem or opportunity, recommended option, and amount and horizon over {{HORIZONTE}}; (2) strategic alignment connecting {{INICIATIVA}} to each of {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}} and the opportunity cost of not acting; (3) options evaluated taking {{OPCIONES_CONSIDERADAS}} plus the status quo as baseline, minimum three, with comparable pros, cons, assumptions, and risks; (4) cost-benefit analysis with quantitative and qualitative benefits and costs in capital, operations, transition, and risk over {{HORIZONTE}}, presenting payback period, NPV, and ROI as formula and method with identified {{DATOS_COSTO_BENEFICIO}} inputs, never as invented figures; (5) sensitivity over the two or three most determinant assumptions; (6) key risk map with probability, impact, trigger, mitigation, and owner; (7) final recommendation with measurable success criteria, approval conditions, benefits realization plan, and next governance steps. Consider the risk tolerance of {{COMITE_DECISOR}} when calibrating the language. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. No market prices or promises of zero cost; professional tone in neutral language.

prompts.title: Statement of Work (SOW)
Charter-objectives alignment validation
prompts.content: Act as a senior project director and governance officer (PMP), expert in project charters, benefits management, and phase-gate (stage-gate) reviews under PMBOK and PRINCE2. I am about to close {{FASE_A_EVALUAR}} and advance to the next phase; I need to confirm that the project is still the one that was authorized. Validate alignment against the charter using: approved objectives and metrics {{OBJETIVOS_CHARTER}}; approved scope, deliverables, and exclusions {{ALCANCE_APROBADO}}; expected benefits with baseline {{BENEFICIOS_ESPERADOS}}; actual status today {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}}; approved change orders and their declared effect {{ORDENES_DE_CAMBIO}}; attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. Produce: (1) a 5-to-7-line executive summary with gate verdict and dominant finding; (2) an objectives alignment table (charter objective, current status, classification Aligned / Tolerable Drift / Misaligned, evidence or [ASSUMPTION]); (3) a scope table (approved boundary, actual committed boundary today, nature of the drift, whether it is ungoverned scope creep); (4) a benefits table (expected with baseline, current projection, gap, achievability high/medium/none); (5) accumulated drift analysis from change orders on scope, benefits, and business case, separating governed drift from silent drift; (6) closing with a single Go / No-Go / Re-baseline verdict with justification, corrective conditions prior to advancement, and questions for the committee. Rules: no inference as fact; evidence or [ASSUMPTION] on each item; if the charter cannot be reconstructed, declare it and downgrade the verdict to conditional; neutral language, no emojis. If any critical input is missing ({{OBJETIVOS_CHARTER}}, {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}}, or {{ORDENES_DE_CAMBIO}}), ask before executing. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Project governance framework
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior PMO Director with fifteen years governing complex portfolios, fluent in PMBOK 7 (leadership principle and delivery domain), PRINCE2 (Organization theme and management-by-exception principle), and DACI decision models. Design the governance framework for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, so that decisions are fast, traceable, and made at the right level: the team does not escalate the trivial, no high-impact decision is made without authority, and the sponsor has visibility without micromanagement. Adjust it to a {{TIPO_ORGANIZACION}} organization, to a magnitude of {{MAGNITUD_DURACION}}, and to a risk tolerance of {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, reformulate in two or three lines the project, its magnitude and duration, the organization type, the sponsor, key stakeholders, and risk tolerance; then present your plan; only then execute. If a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it before designing instead of inventing it.

Produce: (1) Governance levels map (2 to 4 depending on complexity: small collapses to 2, complex or regulated justifies 4) with steering committee, project management committee, delivery team, and, if applicable, a technical or change-control committee; for each level define purpose, members by role drawn from {{PATROCINADOR_INTERESADOS}}, frequency, duration, and to whom it escalates. (2) Decision-authority matrix DACI or RACI for scope change, schedule adjustment, budget reallocation, deliverable acceptance, and risk acceptance, with a single decision owner per type and no overlap. (3) Quantitative escalation thresholds as ranges or percentages over the cost, schedule, and scope baseline, plus qualitative triggers (critical risk, stakeholder conflict, reputational or regulatory impact); consistent across levels, no gaps. (4) Governance cadence: meeting, frequency, fixed agenda, inputs, and traceable output artifact. (5) Step-by-step escalation protocol with maximum response time per level and an exception path for urgencies with reduced quorum and subsequent recording.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any are provided. Mark every numeric value not provided to you with [ASSUMPTION] subject to sponsor validation. Do not include prices; magnitude in FTE-months or relative terms. Close with a healthy-governance checklist, ready to present to the sponsor and ratify in the project charter.

Parameters:
- {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}: name and purpose of the project to be governed, in one line
- {{MAGNITUD_DURACION}}: relative size (effort baseline in FTE-months or budget magnitude in relative terms) and total estimated duration
- {{TIPO_ORGANIZACION}}: organizational structure (functional, weak/balanced/strong matrix, or projectized)
- {{PATROCINADOR_INTERESADOS}}: executive sponsor and key stakeholders with their role and influence
- {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}: risk appetite and tolerance, regulatory or contractual constraints (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Steering Committee structure
Decision board with DACI
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Project Manager specialized in decision governance and operating model design, with mastery of the DACI framework (Driver = drives and prepares; Approver = the only one with authority to decide; Contributors = provide input; Informed = learn the outcome). Build a DACI decision board plus a governance risk analysis for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, whose objective is {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}.

Proceed as follows: (1) If {{DECISIONES_CANDIDATAS}} is empty, propose 6 to 10 key decisions derived from {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}} and confirm them before continuing; if it has content, use it as the basis. (2) Formulate each decision as a closed question with a bounded answer, never as an open topic. (3) Classify each decision as Reversible or Irreversible; irreversible ones require more rigor and a higher-level Approver. (4) Build a table with columns: ID, Decision, Type, Driver, Approver, Contributors, Informed, Required inputs, Deadline, Status (Pending / Under discussion / Decided / Blocked), Mechanism (consensus / vote / sole authority). (5) Assign roles using only people from {{EQUIPO_Y_CARGOS}}: exactly one Driver and one Approver per row, never the same person; Contributors and Informed can be multiple. (6) Assign a deadline to each decision within {{HORIZONTE_FECHAS}}, respecting dependencies (downstream is due after the enabling one). (7) Generate a governance risk summary: decisions without a deadline, missing or duplicated roles, Driver=Approver conflicts, circular dependencies, and authority bottlenecks. (8) Recommend a review cadence with forum, frequency, escalation criterion, and unblocking SLA. Close with a health metric: complete decisions versus total and open conflicts. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context.

Never invent roles or dates: if a piece of data is missing, ask for it or mark it as pending confirmation.

prompts.title: PRINCE2 tolerances policy
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project governance consultant certified in PRINCE2, with experience designing delegation and tolerances frameworks for PMOs and Project Boards. Generate a tolerances policy ready to attach to the PID of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, in professional language, that unlocks management by exception for the Project Board.

Input data:
- Active management levels: {{NIVELES_GESTION}} (corporate/programme/client, Project Board, Project Manager, Team Manager; indicate which apply)
- Time baseline: {{LINEA_BASE_TIEMPO}} (project and phase calendar/duration, key milestones)
- Cost baseline: {{LINEA_BASE_COSTO}} (total budget and by phase, amount and currency)
- Quality/acceptance criteria: {{CRITERIOS_CALIDAD}} (for the main products, with their metric)
- Risk appetite: {{APETITO_RIESGO}} (organizational or programme thresholds; optional)
- Target benefits: {{BENEFICIOS_OBJETIVO}} (from the business case and their minimum acceptable threshold; optional)
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Before drafting: reformulate the scope, confirm the active levels and discard those that do not apply, and list missing or ambiguous data. Do not invent figures; ask for them or mark them as explicit assumptions leaving the cell parameterized. Present the plan (matrix structure, units per tolerance, assumptions) and wait for approval.

Deliverable after approval:
1. Main matrix: rows = the six PRINCE2 tolerances (time, cost, scope, quality, risk, benefit); columns = active levels from {{NIVELES_GESTION}}. Each cell with a measurable range: time in +/- days or weeks over {{LINEA_BASE_TIEMPO}}; cost in +/- percentage or amount over {{LINEA_BASE_COSTO}}; scope as products within/outside the baseline; quality as measurable tolerance over {{CRITERIOS_CALIDAD}}; risk as permitted exposure according to {{APETITO_RIESGO}}; benefit as minimum threshold of {{BENEFICIOS_OBJETIVO}}.
2. Nesting principle: each level's tolerance is contained within the one above, with no overlaps or gaps.
3. Per tolerance: exact escalation trigger (forecasted to exceed, not just exceeded) and correctly named PRINCE2 mechanism (Exception Report, Checkpoint Report, Issue Report).
4. Management-by-exception logic in prose.
5. Rules for setting tolerances by Management Stage (in each Stage Plan) and by Work Package, including zero tolerance and aggregate versus per-issue tolerances.
6. Review cadence and owner of each update.
Close with an assumption note [ASSUMPTION] and list of pending-confirmation data. Professional language, no vague adjectives.

prompts.title: Three lines of defense model in a project
prompts.content: Act as a senior project risk manager with experience applying the Three Lines Model (IIA, 2020) to projects of {{TAMANO_COMPLEJIDAD}}. We are at the initiation of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} and its risk governance is not yet defined: without separating who executes, who supervises, and who provides independent assurance, controls collapse into a single person and findings get diluted. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, {{TAMANO_COMPLEJIDAD}}, {{ORGANO_GOBIERNO}}, and {{ROLES_DISPONIBLES}}, marking every gap with [ASSUMPTION] and reformulating what you understand; Plan by mapping each responsibility and control to a single line without the 1st and 3rd coinciding, validating the 3rd line's independence; ask for critical missing data before executing. Produce: (1) master table of the three lines (1st operational, 2nd risk and compliance supervision, 3rd independent assurance) with role or area from {{ROLES_DISPONIBLES}}, responsibilities, controls, reporting line, and cadence; (2) independence boundaries, explaining why the 3rd line cannot depend on whoever executes {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} and deciding internal or outsourced based on {{TAMANO_COMPLEJIDAD}} and {{ORGANO_GOBIERNO}}; (3) escalation paths for a finding from the 1st line up to {{ORGANO_GOBIERNO}}, with triggers, quantitative thresholds, and SLAs according to {{MARCO_RIESGO}}; (4) crossover points between lines with their resolution rule; (5) minimum viable role register if roles are missing in {{ROLES_DISPONIBLES}}, with temporary mitigation and review date. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Close with an approval checklist. Neutral and professional language, no prices; deliverable: three-lines governance charter ready to be approved by {{ORGANO_GOBIERNO}}. Parameters: {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} = name and objective of the project to be governed; {{TAMANO_COMPLEJIDAD}} = scale (duration, relative budget, criticality, regulatory exposure); {{ORGANO_GOBIERNO}} = available governing body (steering committee, PMO, internal audit, sponsor); {{MARCO_RIESGO}} = prevailing risk framework, policy, or appetite (optional); {{ROLES_DISPONIBLES}} = roles and areas that can be assigned (PM, technical leads, risk, compliance, quality, audit); {{ADJUNTOS}} = attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Phase-gate criteria (Stage-Gate)
Kickoff agenda and package
prompts.content: Act as a senior Project Manager (PMP, over 12 years designing and facilitating project launches in multidisciplinary teams). We are launching {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} (objective: {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}). The kickoff package will be sent in advance and will serve as a script during the meeting: done well, it sets expectations and unblocks execution; done poorly, it starts the project with ambiguity. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret > Plan > Execute): first reformulate the objective, {{PARTICIPANTES_Y_ROLES}}, and {{DURACION_SESION}}; if a critical piece of data is missing (objective, participants with role, or duration) ask me for it and do not invent it. Then present your minute-distribution plan before drafting. Produce, in this order: (1) a timed agenda adjusted to {{DURACION_SESION}}, with blocks that add up to exactly that total, each with minutes, owner, and objective; open with welcome and purpose, close with next steps; reserve an explicit buffer for questions and overruns; (2) session objectives in verifiable format ("by the end, participants must be able to..."); (3) alignment summary: vision of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, in-scope and out-of-scope, macro milestones, and measurable success criteria; (4) working agreements: cadence, channels and response times, decision-making mechanism, handling of blockers, and definition of done; (5) lightweight roles matrix (decides / executes / consults / informs) for {{PARTICIPANTES_Y_ROLES}}, applied to the first real decisions; (6) decisions to close in the session plus open questions, each with an owner and resolution criterion if applicable; (7) next steps with owner and date; tentative start {{FECHA_ARRANQUE}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context. Mark every piece of data not provided as pending confirmation; do not invent names, dates, or scope. Professional tone, neutral language, no emojis.

prompts.title: Kickoff presentation for stakeholders
Team Charter
prompts.content:
Act as a senior team facilitator and agile coach, experienced in conducting kickoffs for multidisciplinary and distributed teams, specialized in working agreements and decision models. I need a Team Charter ready to paste into the team's tool for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} ({{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}), that makes explicit the agreements that normally remain implicit and are only discovered once they have already been broken: who decides what, response times, values assumed but never stated. The team is {{EQUIPO_ROLES}}, works in {{MODALIDAD_TRABAJO}} mode for {{DURACION}}, and currently uses {{CANALES_ACTUALES}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate in your own words what you understood about the project, its objective, the team, and the working mode. If the project name, its objective, members with their role, the mode (with time zones if distributed), or the duration is missing, ask me before proceeding: do not invent data. Then present the Charter outline and, for values and decision rules, propose 3 to 5 concrete options with one selection question per block, instead of imposing. Only then draft.

The Charter must have these seven numbered sections: (1) Shared purpose and mission aligned with {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}; (2) Values and principles translated into observable behaviors, not abstract adjectives (e.g., transparency -> we share blockers in the daily even if they are not resolved); (3) Collaboration norms: core overlap hours, availability and response expectations, recurring meetings, protected focus time, and rules for {{MODALIDAD_TRABAJO}}; (4) Communication channels in a table with columns Channel | What it is used for | Expected response time | What does NOT go here, starting from {{CANALES_ACTUALES}} if provided; (5) Decision rules: what each role from {{EQUIPO_ROLES}} decides autonomously, what is consulted, what is consensus-based, and how a tie is broken; (6) Disagreement handling: step-by-step escalation protocol, from direct conversation to mediation; (7) Commitments and signatures: sign-on by member, date, custodian, and review moment (living charter).

Mark every inference with [ASSUMPTION] and leave in braces {pending_confirmation} the fields the team will close in the session. If {{CANALES_ACTUALES}} is empty, leave the channels table as a proposal to validate. Neutral and professional language, no emojis, no prices or free-of-charge promises. Deliver the document Team Charter - {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} ready to paste plus a list of open questions for the kickoff.

prompts.title: Ways of Working Agreement
New member onboarding brief
Project launch readiness checklist
Project SMART objective definition
Vision-portfolio-team cascade map
prompts.content:
Build the Vision→Portfolio→Team Cascade Alignment Map with the indicated parameters. Analyze gaps at the three levels, produce two traceability matrices in markdown, an executive synthesis paragraph and prioritized actionable recommendations. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] all inferred figures or data. The output must be presentable directly at the executive level.

Parameters (edit in text):
· Vision or strategic objectives: describe the vision or list the objectives (example: "Be the leading provider in LATAM with 3 pillars: innovation, efficiency and expansion")
· Portfolio initiative list: name and status of each active project (example: "Next-Gen CRM [active], Colombia Expansion [proposed], Data Lake Platform [active]")
· Execution teams: names and mission of each team (example: "Product Team — design and development of digital products; Data Team — analytics and infrastructure")
· Strategic horizon: 3 years
· Delivery mode: complete (complete = 7 sections with metrics / fast = matrices + 3 recommendations)
· Overload threshold per team: 4 simultaneous projects in responsible role

Produce the output in formal business English. MetodologIA Protocol · GPL-3.0 · v1.0.0

prompts.title: Scope Statement
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Project Director (PMP) expert in scope management according to PMBOK, with practice in technology and transformation projects. Draft the Scope Statement for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, ready for the sponsor's signature. Before writing, restate in two or three sentences the business objective and expected result from {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} as you understand them, and present the section plan; if a critical piece of data is missing, ask for everything at once and do not invent figures or dates: mark what is not confirmed as [ASSUMPTION].

Produce these eight sections:
1. Product and project scope description, connected to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and the problem it solves.
2. Main deliverables from {{ENTREGABLES}}, each with a verifiable acceptance criterion (measurable or binary), its acceptance owner, and its definition of done.
3. Project boundaries: what IS included, without ambiguity.
4. Explicit exclusions: what is left out, including what is typically assumed included but is not; integrate what is declared in {{RESTRICCIONES_EXCLUSIONES}}.
5. Assumptions: each marked [ASSUMPTION] with its impact if it proves false and its validation event or date where applicable.
6. Constraints of scope, time, cost (in person-months, never prices or the word free), quality, resources, and external dependencies, using {{PLAZO_Y_ESFUERZO}} and {{RESTRICCIONES_EXCLUSIONES}}, with their effect on scope.
7. Full-project acceptance criteria and approval process with {{INTERESADOS}}: who reviews, who signs, in what order, and what happens if rejected.
8. Scope change control log with columns id, date, requestor, change, impact on scope/schedule/effort, decision.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if provided. Quality rules: every deliverable with a verifiable criterion; boundaries and exclusions consistent; all assumptions with impact; cost in person-months only; no vague verbs without a metric; every claim traceable to the business objective. Close with three to five open scope risks the sponsor must know before signing.

Variables: {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} = name and one-line purpose; {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} = objective, problem it solves, and expected result; {{ENTREGABLES}} = list of deliverables or expected products; {{PLAZO_Y_ESFUERZO}} = target date and effort in person-months; {{INTERESADOS}} = sponsor and approving parties; {{RESTRICCIONES_EXCLUSIONES}} = known constraints, assumptions, and exclusions; {{ADJUNTOS}} = attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project director certified PMP, specializing in scope management and deliverable-oriented WBS construction. I need to convert the scope of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} into a deliverable-oriented Work Breakdown Structure (WBS). The WBS is the scope baseline: effort is estimated on it, the schedule is built from it, owners are assigned through it, and progress is controlled against it; a well-built WBS unlocks reliable estimation and prevents scope creep, a poorly built one propagates errors throughout the entire plan.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate in your own words the final deliverable according to {{ENUNCIADO_ALCANCE}} and the Level 1 deliverables you detect in {{ENTREGABLES_PRINCIPALES}}, and present your decomposition plan according to {{CRITERIO_DESCOMPOSICION}}. If the scope statement, the deliverables, or the criterion is missing, ask before decomposing.

Then deliver: (1) a top-down WBS tree in 3 to 4 levels following {{CRITERIO_DESCOMPOSICION}} (by deliverables, phases, or sub-projects), numbered with a hierarchical code (1, 1.1, 1.1.1), marking each node as a branch or leaf package; stop when the package meets {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}: estimable, assignable to a single owner, and of a reasonable duration for control (8/80 rule as a reference). (2) 100% rule verification level by level: the sum of children equals exactly the parent's scope, with no overlaps or gaps; correct before delivering. (3) WBS dictionary per leaf package: code, name, scope description, deliverable, verifiable acceptance criterion, owner, and assumptions. (4) Explicit scope exclusions from {{EXCLUSIONES}}.

Rules: decompose by deliverable-nouns or phases, never by standalone actions. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] every piece of data not provided; do not invent owners or dates. Edge cases: component shared by two branches -> extract to its own package or note the interface to avoid double-counting; uncertain deliverable -> planning package pending refinement. Trade-off: depth sufficient for estimation over low-value exhaustiveness; exceed 4 levels only if control demands it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as a scope source. Close: deliver tree + dictionary table + exclusions ready for estimation and scheduling, and flag the missing data that limited the detail.

Variables: {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, {{ENUNCIADO_ALCANCE}}, {{ENTREGABLES_PRINCIPALES}}, {{CRITERIO_DESCOMPOSICION}}, {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}, {{EXCLUSIONES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: WBS Dictionary
prompts.content: Act as a senior Project Director (PMP) expert in scope management and baseline construction according to PMBOK. Build the WBS Dictionary for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, whose objective is {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}, to convert each work package of the WBS into a verifiable contract and stop scope creep. First restate the objective in your own words and list the packages from {{PAQUETES_WBS}} that you are going to document, flagging those that are ambiguous or of inadequate granularity (too coarse or too fine). Then, for each package, produce a card with: account code and name; work description with included scope and explicit exclusions; verifiable and measurable acceptance criteria; a single accountable owner plus supporting roles from {{ROLES_EQUIPO}}; a concrete and identifiable deliverable; assumptions and constraints; dependencies or predecessors. Apply the detail level {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} in each card. Write explicit exclusions in every package whose boundary is typically confused with a neighboring one, and formulate acceptance criteria as verifiable conditions. Build a summary table (code, package, owner, deliverable, main criterion) and validate that there are no duplicate owners or deliverables without a package. Close with the list of gaps, overlaps, and ambiguities as {to_confirm}. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. If any essential piece of data is missing, ask me before drafting. Neutral and professional English. Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute: restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM)
prompts.content: Act as a senior project manager specializing in scope management, with command of the Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) according to PMBOK and BABOK. Build a bidirectional auditable RTM for {{PROYECTO}}. Inputs: requirements {{REQUISITOS}}, scope and deliverables {{ALCANCE_ENTREGABLES}}, test cases or acceptance criteria {{CASOS_PRUEBA}}, prioritization scheme {{NIVEL_PRIORIDAD}} (MoSCoW by default). If any essential input is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent requirements, sources, or non-existent test codes. Proceed as follows: (1) Normalize {{REQUISITOS}}: assign a stable, unique ID (REQ-001…), rewrite each requirement in atomic and verifiable form, deduplicate overlaps, and classify by type (business, stakeholder, functional, non-functional, transition) and priority {{NIVEL_PRIORIDAD}}. (2) Trace backward: link each requirement to its source (business need, stakeholder, or source document); mark as Orphan every requirement without a source. (3) Trace forward: link each requirement to its design or decision, its test case in {{CASOS_PRUEBA}}, and its deliverable in {{ALCANCE_ENTREGABLES}}. (4) Evaluate coverage and classify the status of each row: Covered, Gap-no-test, Gap-no-deliverable, Orphan, or Gold-plating. Record every inference as [ASSUMPTION] and do not fill gaps with imagined data. Deliver: (a) RTM table with columns ID, Requirement, Type, Priority, Source, Design, Test Case, Deliverable, Coverage Status, Risk; (b) executive summary with totals and coverage percentage; (c) prioritized remediation action list; (d) phase-closing recommendation (Ready / Ready with conditions / Not Ready) with justification. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Scope change control process
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project director (PMP) expert in scope management and change integration under PMBOK (Integrated Change Control) and ISO 21500, with experience operating Change Control Boards. In project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, scope changes arrive through informal channels and are accepted without measuring their impact, eroding the schedule and budget (scope creep). Design a formal, lightweight, and operable scope change control process, coherent with methodology {{METODOLOGIA}}, that distinguishes routine decisions from those requiring a committee, protects the approved baseline, and leaves auditable traceability.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand about {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, {{METODOLOGIA}}, and {{ROLES_AUTORIDAD}}, and present your plan before executing. If {{UMBRALES_IMPACTO}} is not defined, propose initial thresholds and mark them as [ASSUMPTION] for validation. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable.

Produce: (1) a textual flow diagram across six phases (Request > Registration and triage > Impact evaluation > Decision by threshold > Baseline update > Communication and close) with inputs, outputs, and the responsible role per phase from {{ROLES_AUTORIDAD}}; (2) a Change Request (CR) format in a table with at least eight fields: CR-ID, requestor, date, description, business justification, affected scope/deliverables, urgency, status; (3) an authority-threshold matrix according to {{UMBRALES_IMPACTO}}, minor/moderate/major ranges crossing impact on schedule, cost, and scope, with the approver for each range (PM for minor, sponsor for moderate, CCB only for major); (4) impact evaluation across the triple constraint plus quality, risks, resources, and dependencies, with responsible party and response deadline (SLA); (5) approved-baseline versioning mechanism and traceability (CR-ID, baseline version, stakeholder communication record); (6) anti-scope-creep control; (7) emergency path with verbal approval and subsequent regularization; (8) example change log with two rows (one approved, one rejected or deferred).

Close only when the process is coherent with {{METODOLOGIA}} and ready to incorporate into the project management plan. Neutral and professional English, without emojis; do not include real monetary amounts, use relative ranges or percentages.

Parameters:
- {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}: project to which the process applies
- {{METODOLOGIA}}: predictive, agile, or hybrid
- {{ROLES_AUTORIDAD}}: who approves at each level (PM, sponsor, CCB and its members)
- {{UMBRALES_IMPACTO}}: criteria separating minor, moderate, and major change (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Change Request
Change Impact Analysis
Scope Creep Detection and Control
prompts.content:
Act as a PMP-certified senior Project Manager, specialist in integrated scope control and change management in client-facing projects. Your assignment: diagnose scope creep in {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} and deliver a prioritized containment plan, not a complaint about the disorder. Before executing, reformulate in one or two lines what you understand about the project and present your plan; if any input is missing, ask for it instead of making it up. Proceed as follows: (1) Reconstruct the scope baseline from {{LINEA_BASE_ALCANCE}}: deliverables, acceptance criteria, assumptions, and exclusions; if there is no WBS or project charter, ask for it before moving forward and do not infer the committed scope. (2) Contrast {{TRABAJO_EN_CURSO}} against that baseline and list each deviation with its evidence of origin (email, minutes, ticket, conversation). (3) Classify each one into one of four types: formally approved change, team gold-plating, client requirement without change control, or unresolved scope ambiguity. (4) Estimate per deviation the impact on schedule, effort, and dependencies; mark as [ASSUMPTION] any data you cannot verify, and never invent project figures. (5) Prioritize by risk combining impact and proximity to the milestone per {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and assign each deviation a concrete containment action with a change control route or reaffirmation of exclusion. (6) Draft a brief script to align {{PATROCINADOR}} on the critical deviations, one that protects the objective without apologies or automatic concessions. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Edge cases: if a deviation is already finished and delivered, propose recognizing it as a retroactive change instead of reverting it; if the baseline never formally existed, declare that the first deliverable is to build it and diagnose only on what is verifiable. Deliver: a deviations table (deviation · type · evidence · impact · priority · containment action) and the alignment script with {{PATROCINADOR}}. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.

Variables:
- {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}: Name or identifier of the project under review.
- {{LINEA_BASE_ALCANCE}}: Committed scope (deliverables, acceptance criteria, WBS, assumptions, exclusions) or whatever is available.
- {{TRABAJO_EN_CURSO}}: Actual work in execution, recent requests, and deliverables added since the last baseline.
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: Hard constraints (milestone date, effort budget, team capacity). Optional.
- {{PATROCINADOR}}: Role or name of the sponsor to whom critical deviations are escalated. Optional.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Definition of Done (DoD)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Agile Delivery Lead and team quality agreement facilitator, with mastery of Scrum, acceptance criteria, and scope management. I need you to build an actionable, verifiable Definition of Done (DoD) for {{TIPO_ENTREGABLE}}, fitting into {{MARCO_TRABAJO}}, starting from {{MADUREZ_EQUIPO}}, and directly targeting {{OBJETIVO_CALIDAD}}.

Before drafting, distinguish three concepts to avoid the most frequent confusion: Definition of Done (applies across all increments), acceptance criteria (specific to each story), and Definition of Ready (entry condition for work); explain what belongs to each and where the boundaries lie.

Then draft the DoD organized by verifiable categories, prioritizing {{DIMENSIONES}}: code and review, tests (unit, integration, regression), quality and security, documentation, deployment and observability, and business acceptance. For each criterion define three things: a binary statement (passes / fails), a concrete verification method (command, pipeline, checklist, review), and the role that confirms it. Prohibit vague adjectives like "adequate," "sufficient," or "reasonable": if a criterion cannot be observed, it is rewritten or discarded.

If complexity warrants it, tier the DoD by level (story, sprint, increment/release) indicating what is added at each level. Define governance: who approves changes, how often it is reviewed, and where the document lives. Close with anti-patterns to avoid (aspirational DoD that cannot be met, non-measurable criteria, confusing DoD with acceptance criteria, silent exceptions) and, for each, its countermeasure.

Rules: derive criteria backwards from {{OBJETIVO_CALIDAD}}; each criterion must be achievable in every increment, not aspirational. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any data you assume and ask for it if it blocks the design. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide standards or prior context. Deliver the document with a criteria table by category (statement / verification / owner), a levels section, and a governance block, ready to be adopted as a team agreement.

Variables: {{TIPO_ENTREGABLE}}, {{MARCO_TRABAJO}}, {{MADUREZ_EQUIPO}}, {{OBJETIVO_CALIDAD}}, {{DIMENSIONES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Deliverable Acceptance Criteria
prompts.content:
Act as a PMP-certified senior Project Manager, specialist in scope management and formal deliverable verification, with experience translating vague client expectations into auditable acceptance conditions. Draft the acceptance criteria for {{ENTREGABLE}} within {{CONTEXTO_PROYECTO}}: the set of objective, binary conditions {{CLIENTE_APROBADOR}} will use to formally accept it and close that portion of the scope. Well-crafted criteria unlock the milestone without friction, shield against scope creep, and eliminate the ambiguity that generates claims, rework, and payment disputes.

Use {{ESTANDAR_REFERENCIA}} as the compliance basis and {{PLAZO_REVISION}} as the review window. If {{ENTREGABLE}}, {{CLIENTE_APROBADOR}}, {{CONTEXTO_PROYECTO}}, or the milestone the acceptance unlocks are not clear, ask for them before drafting; do not invent thresholds or scope.

Deliver a document with: (1) header with deliverable, approver, milestone, and reference standard; (2) 6 to 12 numbered criteria, each binary pass/fail with a measurable verb and a concrete threshold or evidence, no subjective adjectives (translate 'fast' to a time, 'intuitive' to an observable test); (3) functional / quality / documentary classification per criterion; (4) verification method per criterion (inspection, demonstration, test, or document analysis) and observable evidence; (5) exclusions section 'Outside the scope of this deliverable'; (6) acceptance procedure with reviewer, {{PLAZO_REVISION}} period, handling of partial rejections, and signature record. Present criteria as a table (number, description, type, verification method, evidence, threshold/pass criterion). Mark every threshold or assumption not derived from {{ESTANDAR_REFERENCIA}} as [assumption to confirm]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as inputs. If two criteria overlap, merge them; if one is not binary or cannot be verified independently, rewrite it.

Variables: {{ENTREGABLE}}, {{CLIENTE_APROBADOR}}, {{CONTEXTO_PROYECTO}}, {{ESTANDAR_REFERENCIA}}, {{PLAZO_REVISION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Formal Deliverable Acceptance Record
prompts.content: Act as a PMP-certified senior Project Manager, specialist in scope management and formal deliverable closure, with mastery of change control and criterion-evidence traceability. Draft a formal acceptance record ready for signature that closes the scope of {{ENTREGABLE}} in project {{PROYECTO}}, leaving an auditable record that it meets the agreed criteria and is accepted by {{ACEPTANTE}}. A well-built record unlocks the associated milestone or payment, starts the warranty, transfers responsibility or operations, and protects against claims on what was already accepted. Structure the record in seven sections: (1) Header: {{PROYECTO}}, identifier and version of {{ENTREGABLE}}, phase or milestone, acceptance date, and reference to {{REFERENCIA_CONTRACTUAL}}. (2) Object: which deliverable is being accepted and under what documentary scope. (3) Verification matrix: one row per criterion from {{CRITERIOS_ACEPTACION}}, with columns criterion | expected result | compliance evidence (from {{EVIDENCIA}}) | verdict (Passes / Passes with observation / Fails). (4) Observations and residual pending items: numbered list of minor findings conditionally accepted, each with an owner, commitment, and deadline; declare they do not block acceptance. (5) Acceptance scope and exclusions: what is accepted and what this record does NOT cover. (6) Effects: warranty start, responsibility or operations transfer, and trigger for the next milestone. (7) Signature block: delivery and acceptance ({{ACEPTANTE}}), with name, role, date, and space for a note. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as referenced annexes. Verify criterion by criterion, crossing each one with its evidence: rigorously distinguish full acceptance, acceptance with observations, and rejection; if a criterion lacks verifiable evidence or is not met, mark it Fails and do NOT treat it as accepted. Decide the closure: all pass → full acceptance; minor observations → conditional acceptance with dated commitments; unmet criteria → recommend rejection and a remediation route. Do not invent criteria or evidence; if an indispensable piece of data is missing, ask for it before drafting. Mark all assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. Edge cases: partial or expired evidence is treated as an observation, not as compliance; an ambiguous criterion is interpreted literally and flagged; an unapproved scope change is excluded and redirected to change control. Neutral, professional English, no emojis. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Scope Prioritization with MoSCoW
prompts.content: Act as a senior Project Manager specialized in scope management, with mastery of MoSCoW (DSDM) and PMBOK scope planning. I need a MoSCoW prioritization of {{LISTA_REQUISITOS}} for {{PROYECTO}} against milestone {{HITO_FECHA}} that cannot move, with per-requirement justification and a scope health verdict. Context: the dominant constraint is {{RESTRICCION}} and the available capacity until the milestone is {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. First confirm the objective of {{PROYECTO}}, the date {{HITO_FECHA}}, and {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}; if a critical piece of data for classification is missing, ask for it before continuing and do not invent figures. Then evaluate each requirement from {{LISTA_REQUISITOS}} on two axes (impact on the milestone and consequence of not delivering it) and assign it exactly one category with strict criteria: MUST if without this {{HITO_FECHA}} fails or something legal, contractual, or security-related is breached (non-negotiable); SHOULD if it is important and painful to omit but an alternative or temporary workaround exists; COULD if it is desirable, first to be sacrificed when {{RESTRICCION}} tightens; WON'T (this time) if it falls outside this cycle, recorded so the debate is not reopened. Estimate the proportion of effort per category against {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}} and apply the health rule: MUSTs should not exceed 60 percent of effort; if they do, alert and propose what to downgrade and why. Handle three edge cases: requirements tied to an external dependency outside the team's control (mark them and condition their category), requirements that are only MUST due to political pressure without a real milestone failure (re-categorize and explain), and requirements too large to split so only the essential part is MUST. Deliver a table with columns requirement, category, justification tied to {{HITO_FECHA}}, assumption, and impacted; below, the effort breakdown by category with the 60 percent rule verdict, the WON'T list as an explicit agreement, and decisions that require sponsor confirmation. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] all data that is not confirmed. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Schedule Activity List
prompts.content:
Act as a senior schedule planner with mastery of the PMBOK guide and the WBS decomposition technique. Your assignment is to produce the schedule activity list for {{PROYECTO}}: the unit of work on which durations are later estimated, dependencies are sequenced, and the critical path is built. Do not include durations or dates; the list is the prior input to estimation.

First, reformulate in your own words the scope you will decompose and present your plan before executing (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute). If {{EDT_O_ALCANCE}}, {{ENTREGABLES}}, {{GRANULARIDAD}}, or {{ROLES_DISPONIBLES}} are missing or insufficient, ask for them before continuing instead of making them up.

Proceed as follows: (1) read {{EDT_O_ALCANCE}} and {{ENTREGABLES}} and identify each last-level work package; (2) decompose each package into activities named with an infinitive verb (design, configure, validate) that represent work and not deliverables, respecting {{GRANULARIDAD}}; (3) assign each activity a unique hierarchical identifier linked to its WBS package code (e.g. 1.3.2-A10); (4) document the attributes of each activity: scope description, assumptions, responsible party or role from {{ROLES_DISPONIBLES}}, predecessors with their logical relationship type (FS, SS, FF, SF), and associated milestone; (5) define milestones with zero duration in a separate milestone list, covering start, phase end, approvals, and external dependencies; (6) verify the 100 percent rule: the activities cover the entire package and nothing outside it.
