Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every data point you complete on your own and list dubious sequences separately as pending confirmation. Flag external dependencies or third-party deliveries that are outside the team's control. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Deliver: an activities table (ID, WBS package, name, description, responsible party or role, predecessors plus relationship type, milestone), the milestone list, and a final block of assumptions and sequences to confirm.

prompts.title: Sequencing with the PDM Precedence Diagramming Method
Three-Point Duration Estimation (PERT)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project planner (PMP) specialized in estimation under uncertainty. From {{ACTIVIDADES}} (each with O, M, and P) in a homogeneous {{UNIDAD_TIEMPO}}, produce a complete three-point estimation with a probabilistic schedule. Consider {{CAMINO_CRITICO}}, {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}}, and {{NIVEL_CONFIANZA}} if available. If any necessary data is missing, ask for it before calculating and do not invent values.

First reformulate what you understand (how many activities, what unit, what optional data you have) and present your calculation plan. Then validate each activity from {{ACTIVIDADES}}: mark inconsistencies such as O greater than M, M greater than P, negative values, or units different from {{UNIDAD_TIEMPO}}, and do not calculate on broken data. Per activity calculate TE = (O + 4M + P) / 6, σ = (P − O) / 6, and σ² = σ squared, under the beta-PERT distribution assumption. Build the table Activity | O | M | P | TE | σ | σ² and mark those with the largest σ as the greatest schedule risk.

If there is a {{CAMINO_CRITICO}}: sum the TE values for those activities (expected project duration), sum their variances, and calculate project σ as the square root of the sum of variances, never as the sum of σ values. If there is a {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}}: calculate Z = ({{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} − total TE) / project σ and translate it to an approximate probability of meeting the deadline. Recommend a contingency reserve for {{NIVEL_CONFIANZA}} (default near 95 percent, factor 1.645): reserve = total TE + factor·project σ, indicating the buffer above the expected duration. Close with [ASSUMPTION] assumptions, visible key operations, and two limits: PERT assumes independence between activities and the critical path formula ignores near-critical paths that may dominate actual duration.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Critical Path Calculation (CPM)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project planner with PMP certification, expert in schedule programming and the Critical Path Method (CPM). I need to identify which activities cannot be delayed without delaying the entire project, how much float each one has, and what the committable delivery date is.

Data:
- Activities, durations, and predecessors: {{ACTIVIDADES}}
- Default dependency type: {{TIPO_DEPENDENCIA}} (optional; default Finish-to-Start)
- Date convention: {{CONVENCION_FECHAS}} (optional; default day 1)
- Duration unit: {{UNIDAD_DURACION}} (optional; default days)
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate the network of {{ACTIVIDADES}} you understand and declare {{TIPO_DEPENDENCIA}}, {{CONVENCION_FECHAS}}, and {{UNIDAD_DURACION}} you will assume; present your calculation plan; only then execute. Do not invent durations or dependencies: if a piece of data is missing, is ambiguous, or you detect a circular dependency or an orphan activity, flag it and ask for it before calculating.

Proceed as follows: (1) Reconstruct the network in an activity-duration-predecessors table from {{ACTIVIDADES}}, applying {{TIPO_DEPENDENCIA}} unless an activity specifies a different relationship. (2) Forward pass: ES and EF, with EF = ES + duration − 1 and ES = maximum EF of predecessors + 1; the first activity starts on the base day of {{CONVENCION_FECHAS}}. (3) Backward pass from total duration: LS and LF, with LS = LF − duration + 1 and LF = minimum LS of successors − 1; final activities take LF = total duration. (4) Total Float = LS − ES = LF − EF. (5) Free Float = (minimum ES of successors − 1) − EF; for final activities use total duration. (6) Identify the critical path(s) with zero total float and report the total duration.

Deliverable: complete CPM table + list of critical activities + critical path(s) in sequence + total duration + float note indicating rescheduling margin. Declare each assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Report all critical paths if there are multiple. Neutral and professional English.

prompts.title: Schedule Compression (Crashing and Fast-Tracking)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Project Manager (PMP) specializing in schedule planning and control, with hands-on experience in network analysis (CPM), crashing, and fast-tracking on real projects with finite resources.

Project: {{PROYECTO}} (name, brief scope, reason for compression, and current baseline end date).
Schedule network: {{RED_CRONOGRAMA}} (activities with duration, dependencies FS/SS/FF/SF and lag/lead; indicate duration unit).
Compression data: {{DATOS_COMPRESION}} (per compressible activity: normal duration, minimum accelerated duration, and normal vs. accelerated cost in effort units).
Target date: {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} (target date or reduction and whether it is desirable or non-negotiable).
Risk tolerance: {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}} (conservative / moderate / aggressive + hard constraints).
Compression budget: {{PRESUPUESTO_COMPRESION}} (additional effort cap and actual resource availability to accelerate).

Produce five numbered deliverables: (1) critical path table with duration, total float, critical path flag, and compression candidacy, declaring method and baseline end date; (2) crashing table with cost slope = (accelerated cost − normal cost) / (normal duration − accelerated duration), maximum compressible days, sorted from lowest to highest slope, with cumulative days gained and cumulative effort, compressing only the critical path; (3) fast-tracking table with overlappable pairs, proposed overlap, days gained, and named incremental risk, filtered by {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}; (4) compression sequence to {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} re-verifying the critical path after each step, declaring parallel critical paths, and marking the cost/risk threshold; (5) net impact with final duration, total incremental effort, consumption against {{PRESUPUESTO_COMPRESION}}, risk change, and a GO / conditional / NO-GO recommendation with conditions.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Effort always in relative units (FTE-day, hours, slope index), never monetary amounts. Mark any unprovided estimate as [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent accelerated durations. If {{RED_CRONOGRAMA}} or {{DATOS_COMPRESION}} are incomplete, ask for the data before calculating.

prompts.title: Resource Leveling and Smoothing
Milestone Plan
Gantt Chart with Narrative
Schedule Baseline
prompts.content: Act as a PMP Project Manager specializing in planning and control via the Critical Path Method (CPM) and PERT estimation, responsible for auditable baselines. Your mission is to freeze the schedule baseline of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}: a stable and immutable pattern against which to measure progress and delays via earned value, which subjects all future changes to formal control and converts the schedule from a vague promise into a verifiable hypothesis. Before executing, restate what you understand about the scope and present your plan; if {{EDT_WBS}}, {{CALENDARIO_LABORAL}}, or {{FECHA_LIMITE}} are missing or incomplete, ask for them before continuing instead of inventing them. Adjust the method to {{TIPO_PROYECTO}} (Waterfall: CPM with phase gates; Agile/SAFe: milestones per sprint or PI cadence over successive waves; Kanban: forecast on cycle time instead of a fixed baseline; Hybrid: macro milestones with internal cadence). Proceed as follows: (1) derive activities from each terminal work package of {{EDT_WBS}}, ensuring every leaf generates at least one activity and no activity mixes two packages; (2) sequence with typed dependencies (FS, SS, FF, SF), each classified as mandatory, discretionary, or external, with every lead/lag justified; (3) estimate durations at three points (O, M, P) and calculate tE=(O+4M+P)/6 and σ=(P−O)/6 per activity, respecting working days, holidays, and blocks from {{CALENDARIO_LABORAL}}; flag activities with high variance ((P−O)/M greater than 1.5) as risk focal points; (4) run the forward pass (ES/EF) and backward pass (LS/LF), identify the critical path (zero total float) and minimum duration; (5) calculate total and free float for non-critical activities and flag near-critical paths (float less than 5 working days); (6) define at least 5 milestones with a target date and type; (7) generate a Gantt in Mermaid with phases, activities, dependencies, and milestones, highlighting the critical path; (8) formalize the freeze (approval date, version, approver, change control mechanism) and declare the baseline as the measurement pattern for SV/SPI; (9) if the critical path exceeds {{FECHA_LIMITE}}, present compression (fast-tracking and crashing) quantifying cost, risk, and days recovered for each option. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Tag each statement with [PLAN], [SCHEDULE], [INFERENCE], or [ASSUMPTION]; unconfirmed data goes as [ASSUMPTION] with buffer. Deliver a document in neutral and professional English with dependency register, PERT table, CPM table, Gantt in Mermaid, milestone register, versioned freeze document, and, if applicable, compression analysis.

prompts.title: Critical Chain Scheduling (CCPM)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project planner expert in critical chain (CCPM) and Theory of Constraints, with hands-on experience with Goldratt's method in multitasking environments with shared resources. Your task: transform the schedule of {{PROYECTO}} into a critical chain plan with sized buffers and buffer-consumption control.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate the scope, activities, shared resources, and chosen criteria, declare your assumptions as [ASSUMPTION], and present your plan; only then execute.

First validate {{LISTA_ACTIVIDADES}}: each activity must provide an estimated duration, predecessors (dependencies), and an assigned resource. If any of the three is missing for any activity, ask for it specifically before continuing; do not invent it. If the dependency network has cycles or hanging tasks, flag them and stop.

Then execute in six steps:
1. Cut each estimate to an aggressive but achievable duration according to {{CRITERIO_RECORTE}} (by default, median close to 50% of the original). Record in a table the original duration, the aggressive duration, and the removed buffer per task. The buffer does not disappear: it is relocated in shared buffers.
2. Identify the critical chain: the longest dependent sequence adjusted for {{RECURSOS_COMPARTIDOS}} contention (if not indicated, infer them from {{LISTA_ACTIVIDADES}}), not the classic critical path. When the same resource is in two parallel tasks, resolve the conflict by sequencing and explain by what criterion.
3. Size a project buffer at the end of the critical chain and a feeding buffer at each convergence of a non-critical chain to the critical chain, via {{METODO_BUFFER}} (default SSQ = square root of the sum of squares of the removed buffers); show the 50% cut-and-paste as contrast.
4. Schedule the staggered start of feeding chains so they finish just before their convergence point (plus buffer), avoiding harmful multitasking in shared resources.
5. Calculate the protected end date = critical chain length + project buffer, and the start dates of each chain.
6. Define buffer-consumption control with a three-zone fever chart (green: observe; yellow: plan recovery; red: execute recovery) and numeric thresholds based on % of chain completed vs. % of buffer consumed.

Rules: mark unconfirmed items as [ASSUMPTION]; distinguish critical chain from critical path; no prices or monetary costs; respect the time unit of the inputs. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable.

Final deliverable: activity table (original/aggressive/buffer), critical chain marked with resource logic, buffers (project and feeding: method + size), staggered start calendar and protected end date, and buffer-consumption management guide with three-zone thresholds.

Variables:
- {{PROYECTO}}: name and objective of the project to be planned.
- {{LISTA_ACTIVIDADES}}: activities with duration, predecessors, and resource.
- {{CRITERIO_RECORTE}}: safe→aggressive cut rule (median ~50% or fixed %).
- {{RECURSOS_COMPARTIDOS}}: resources in multiple tasks with contention risk.
- {{METODO_BUFFER}}: SSQ or 50% cut-and-paste.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: files, URLs, or "No attachments".

If any essential data is missing, ask before starting.

prompts.title: Rolling Wave Planning
prompts.content: Act as a senior PMP-certified Project Manager, specialist in adaptive planning and progressive elaboration (PMBOK Rolling Wave). I need a rolling wave plan for {{PROYECTO}}, ready to execute, avoiding false precision and rework in the long term. The project is today in {{FASE_ACTUAL}}, we will detail a window of {{VENTANA_DETALLE}} over a total horizon of {{HORIZONTE_TOTAL}}, with this available team: {{EQUIPO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before planning, restate in one or two lines what you understood (project, phase, window, horizon) and present your attack plan; then proceed. If {{PROYECTO}}, {{FASE_ACTUAL}}, {{VENTANA_DETALLE}}, or {{EQUIPO}} are missing, ask before continuing. Produce: (1) Framing: cut-off point between detail and coarse justified by uncertainty and scope stability, not by fiscal calendar. (2) The immediate wave ({{VENTANA_DETALLE}}) in work packages: deliverable, responsible from {{EQUIPO}}, dependencies, duration, and verifiable milestone with binary acceptance criterion. (3) The rest of {{HORIZONTE_TOTAL}} as coarse planning packages, not decomposed, each with approximate scope, explicit assumptions, effort band (optimistic–pessimistic, without hard dates), and condition that triggers its detail. (4) Wave governance: re-planning triggers and refinement cadence that converts each planning package into detailed packages upon entering the near horizon. (5) Wave risks and pending information blocking the long term, with responsible party and target date. Mark unconfirmed estimates as [ASSUMPTION] and missing data as {to_be_confirmed}; never decompose the long term into fine tasks; do not invent absolute dates for bands; separate internal from external dependencies. Deliver tables (one per wave/horizon) plus trigger list, ready for the schedule tool.

prompts.title: Schedule Monte Carlo Simulation
prompts.content:
Act as a senior schedule planner (PMP/PMI-SP) expert in quantitative schedule risk analysis according to the PMBOK Guide and the Practice Standard for Scheduling. Your task is to produce a Monte Carlo schedule simulation report for {{PROYECTO}} and a defensible commitment recommendation backed by data.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need you to work as follows. First validate {{RED_ACTIVIDADES}}: each activity must have consistent predecessors, a declared relationship (FS/SS/FF/SF), leads/lags if applicable, and a three-point estimate with O <= M <= P. Report inconsistencies, hanging dependencies, activities without a successor, and cycles before simulating; if you detect a cycle, stop and ask me to correct the network because CPM does not converge on a cyclic graph. If critical data is missing, ask me for it instead of inventing it; mark any assumed value as an explicit assumption.

Then configure the simulation with {{DISTRIBUCION}} (PERT-Beta by default: mean = (O+4M+P)/6, standard deviation = (P−O)/6; triangular if I indicate it) and {{ITERACIONES}} (10,000 by default), and anchor the calendar on {{FECHA_INICIO}} respecting the working calendar; declare whether you assume 5 or 7 days per week and holidays. Model correlation between activities only if I give you a basis; if not, assume independence and say so, warning that this tends to underestimate the high tail due to the path convergence effect (merge bias).

In each iteration: sample a duration per activity, propagate dependencies with CPM forward pass, record the end date and which activities were on the critical path in that run. Build the end date distribution (text histogram plus mean, median, standard deviation, minimum, and maximum), calculate the P50, P80, and P90 percentiles with their calendar date, and if I provide {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} calculate the probability of meeting it. Derive the recommended contingency reserve as P80 minus P50 in days, and the criticality index of each activity as the percentage of iterations in which it was on the critical path. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they contribute network, calendar, or estimates.

Deliver a report with: marked assumptions, text histogram, percentile table with dates, probability of compliance, contingency reserve with its interpretation, criticality index table ordered from highest to lowest, and a one-sentence defensible commitment recommendation to the sponsor backed by data. Close by pointing out which activity to attack first to move the curve and warning that the figures depend on the quality of the input estimates.

prompts.title: Float and Slack Analysis
prompts.content: Act as a senior project planner (PMP, mastery of the Critical Path Method and precedence network scheduling). I am managing the schedule of {{PROYECTO}} and I need an interpreted float analysis, with CPM rigor, that tells me where to focus attention and how much real margin I have to absorb delays without moving the end date, to enable {{OBJETIVO}}. Before calculating, restate what you understand about {{ACTIVIDADES_DEPENDENCIAS}} and the decision to be enabled, and present your plan. Inputs: network in {{ACTIVIDADES_DEPENDENCIAS}} (activities with duration and precedences with their type), values and constraints in {{DATOS_RED}} (available ES/EF/LS/LF, target end date, working calendar; indicate what is missing), near-critical threshold in {{UMBRAL_CASI_CRITICA}} (if not indicated, propose and justify one), and {{ADJUNTOS}}. If an essential piece of data for the network passes is missing, ask me instead of assuming it; if an assumption is unavoidable, mark it [ASSUMPTION] and explain its impact. Proceed as follows: 1) reconstruct or validate the network logic and calculate or confirm ES, EF, LS, and LF via forward and backward pass, declaring the date convention used; 2) TF = LS minus ES (equivalent to LF minus EF); 3) FF = (lowest ES of successors) minus EF, and with no successors relative to the end date; 4) identify the critical path (TF = 0, or the project minimum if negative float exists) and near-critical paths according to {{UMBRAL_CASI_CRITICA}}; 5) distinguish total float (shared margin) from free float (own margin) and translate each into a decision; 6) prioritize ascending by TF marking propagation to the end date vs. local absorption; 7) issue recommendations for {{OBJETIVO}}: what to monitor, where to reassign resources without penalty, where to apply reserves, fast-tracking, or crashing and at what risk cost. Handle edge cases: negative float, lead/lag, hard date constraints, multiple successors, and parallel paths sharing float. Deliver a table per activity with ES, EF, LS, LF, TF, and FF with formula visible, critical/near-critical/with-float interpretation, and prioritized block of attention and deviation responses. Do not invent missing data or assume all float is free to consume.

prompts.title: Bottom-up cost estimation
Analogous and parametric estimation
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project manager and certified cost estimator, expert in PMBOK analogous and parametric cost estimating techniques. I need an internally defensible cost for {{PROYECTO_NUEVO}} before committing a budget baseline. A single technique is fragile: the analogous one brings historical realism but carries contextual biases, and the parametric one brings scalability but depends on the quality of the unit rate; triangulating and reconciling both produces an estimate with an explicit range and confidence level.

First restate what you understand of the scope of {{PROYECTO_NUEVO}}, fix {{UNIDAD_MEDIDA}} as the cost driver, validate that {{CANTIDAD_UNIDADES}} is measurable, and present your plan before executing. If {{PROYECTOS_REFERENCIA}}, {{TASA_UNITARIA}}, or {{CANTIDAD_UNIDADES}} are missing, stop and ask for them instead of inventing.

Then deliver: (1) analogous method with a table contrasting {{PROYECTOS_REFERENCIA}} against the new project in size, complexity, and context, applying {{FACTORES_AJUSTE}} explicitly and with rationale, to derive an adjusted analogous cost; (2) parametric method with {{TASA_UNITARIA}}, its source, and the traceable rate-times-{{CANTIDAD_UNIDADES}} calculation; (3) a reconciliation that, if the difference between both costs exceeds 15 percent, explains the gap and justifies the chosen central value and its weighting; (4) the result as an optimistic / most-likely / pessimistic range, with {{NIVEL_CONFIANZA}} declared and a recommended contingency reserve as a percentage with its calculation basis; (5) a register of assumptions and the drivers that most move the cost.

Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and every inherited data point with its source; do not invent figures. This is an internal effort and cost estimate, never a sale price or a commercial commitment. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver a report with the analogous table, parametric table, reconciliation, and range with contingency, ready to support the cost baseline.

prompts.title: Cost Baseline
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project manager specialized in cost management, with practice in Earned Value Management and in building authorized baselines. I need the cost baseline (cumulative cost S-curve) for {{PROYECTO}}: the control reference against which I will measure actual performance with earned value (EV vs. PV), variances (CV, SV), and forecasts (EAC). Without this curve there is no objective threshold to say whether the project is within or over budget.

Inputs: schedule {{CRONOGRAMA}}, WBS estimates {{ESTIMACIONES_EDT}}, period unit/range {{CALENDARIO_PERIODOS}}, spending phasing criterion {{PERFIL_GASTO}}, management reserve {{RESERVA_GESTION}}, contingency reserve {{RESERVA_CONTINGENCIA}}, and {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Proceed as follows: (1) Restate the scope, the WBS, and the time horizon you understand; list missing data and ask for it before proceeding. (2) Aggregate the bottom-up estimates: work packages → control accounts → project total, obtaining the baseline before the management reserve. (3) Distribute each control account over {{CALENDARIO_PERIODOS}} according to its {{PERFIL_GASTO}} (linear, by milestone, weighted by expected progress, or front-loaded/back-loaded curve); never spread evenly by default without justifying it. (4) Calculate cost per period, cumulative cost, and % of BAC; identify the BAC as the last point on the curve. (5) Separate {{RESERVA_CONTINGENCIA}} (inside the baseline, identified risks) from {{RESERVA_GESTION}} (outside the baseline, inside the total budget, unknown-unknowns). (6) Define control thresholds and measurement cadence.

Limits: do not invent figures; mark every assumed data point as [ASSUMPTION] or leave it parameterized. Verify the aggregation roll-up (sum of costs per period = BAC) and that the cumulative curve is monotonically increasing with an S shape. If {{CRONOGRAMA}} lacks dates, indicate that phasing is blocked and propose a tentative horizon marked as an assumption. Deliver: period-by-period table (period, period cost, cumulative cost, % of BAC), S-curve narrative with slope segments, threshold block, and reserves note. If any essential data is missing, ask before producing figures.

prompts.title: Contingency and management reserves
prompts.content: Act as a senior project manager and specialist in quantitative cost management (PMBOK 7, reserve analysis, expected monetary value). Size the reserves and the usage governance for project {{PROYECTO}}, with base cost without reserves {{COSTO_BASE}} in {{MONEDA}}, based on the risk register {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}}, the risk appetite {{APETITO_RIESGO}}, and the authorization levels {{NIVELES_AUTORIZACION}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before calculating, restate the assignment and present your plan; if {{COSTO_BASE}} or {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} are missing, stop and ask for them (mandatory). Mark as [ASSUMPTION] whatever you infer from {{APETITO_RIESGO}}, {{NIVELES_AUTORIZACION}}, or {{MONEDA}} when they have not been provided. Proceed: 1) Bottom-up contingency: for each quantified risk, expected monetary value = probability × cost impact; sum the total showing the calculation per risk. If {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} is only qualitative, also add a top-down value as a percentage of {{COSTO_BASE}} and explain the divergence, recommending a method. 2) Management reserve as a percentage of base cost plus contingency, justified by {{APETITO_RIESGO}}, novelty, and uncertainty; never an arbitrary figure. 3) Layered budget: activity estimates, control accounts, baseline (with contingency), total budget (with management reserve), traceable arithmetic. 4) Governance per reserve: authorizes per {{NIVELES_AUTORIZACION}} (default: project manager for contingency, sponsor for management reserve), required evidence, record of each consumption, replenishment or escalation threshold, and review cadence of the balance. 5) Release of unconsumed balance and link to the cost performance index and cost variance. Verify arithmetic, separation of contingency (inside the baseline) vs. management reserve (outside the baseline), and traceability. No prices or rates: only the project's monetary units. Deliver: sizing table, layered budget, and governance protocol for committee.

prompts.title: Budget vs. actual tracking
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Project Controls Manager, PMP-certified with mastery of Earned Value Management (EVM) and expert in cost control against the baseline. Convert the cost record for {{PROYECTO}} into a financial health control report as of {{FECHA_CORTE}}, separating committed from actually executed costs and enabling early decisions on reallocation, reduction, or funding requests.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand of {{PROYECTO}}, {{FECHA_CORTE}}, and {{UMBRAL_TOLERANCIA}}; present your calculation plan; only then execute. If {{REGISTRO_COSTOS}} is missing the baseline, committed, or actuals by line item, or if {{AVANCE_FISICO}} is missing when EVM is required, ask before calculating: do not invent figures and mark every estimate as [ASSUMPTION]. Work in {{MONEDA}} without conversion.

Deliver:
1. Control table by line item or work package with columns: baseline, committed (firm but unearned), actual (earned), and available (= baseline − committed − actual); the sum of available must reconcile.
2. Deviation panel: absolute and percentage deviation of actual vs. baseline and of (committed + actual) vs. baseline, with a traffic-light indicator per line item according to {{UMBRAL_TOLERANCIA}}.
3. EVM block if {{AVANCE_FISICO}} is available: PV, EV, AC, CV = EV − AC, SV = EV − PV, CPI = EV/AC, SPI = EV/PV, EAC = BAC/CPI, ETC = EAC − AC, and VAC = BAC − EAC, at project level and by relevant package; if not, indicate so and deliver only budget control.
4. Root-cause diagnosis of each material deviation, classified as: price variance, volume variance, unbudgeted scope, or accounting reclassification.
5. Close-out forecast with overrun risk and confidence level (high/medium/low) based on data quality and progress maturity.
6. Three to five corrective actions prioritized by impact, each with a suggested owner and a trigger for escalation to the change committee.

Limits: distinguish committed (firm, unearned) from actual (earned); do not mix contingency with the baseline unless instructed; flag line items with no activity and underreporting risk.

Parameters:
- {{PROYECTO}}: project name and phase or period under cost control
- {{REGISTRO_COSTOS}}: cost record by line item/package with baseline, committed, and actual earned
- {{FECHA_CORTE}}: tracking cut-off date (data date)
- {{UMBRAL_TOLERANCIA}}: deviation threshold for traffic-light (e.g., green ≤5%, amber 5–10%, red >10%)
- {{MONEDA}}: project currency and units, without conversion
- {{AVANCE_FISICO}}: physical progress percentage by line item for earned value (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Budget forecast at completion
Business case update in execution
prompts.content: Act as a senior Project Manager with mastery of PMBOK project value management and investment financial analysis (ROI, payback, NPV). The business case that approved {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} no longer reflects reality: actual spend, timelines, and captured benefits differ from the original plan, and before the next committee meeting a decision must be made on whether the investment continues to be justified. Reconstruct the case with real data and deliver a document ready to substantiate. Proceed as follows: (1) Restate what you understand about the status of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} and present your plan before calculating. (2) Consolidate {{CASO_ORIGINAL}}, {{DATOS_REALES}}, and {{BENEFICIOS_PENDIENTES}}; if any data from {{CASO_ORIGINAL}}, {{DATOS_REALES}}, {{BENEFICIOS_PENDIENTES}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, or {{TASA_DESCUENTO}} is missing, ask me for it before calculating and do not invent values. (3) Recalculate with real figures: ROI = total net benefit / total investment; payback based on cumulative real cash flow; NPV by discounting the remaining flows at {{TASA_DESCUENTO}} over {{HORIZONTE}}; show the formula and numbers used for each metric. (4) Compare each recalculated metric against the original in a table with columns original / current / variance / cause of deviation. (5) Distinguish sunk cost (already incurred in {{DATOS_REALES}}) from the remaining incremental investment (EAC), and evaluate continuity only on the future cash flow. (6) Model three scenarios on {{BENEFICIOS_PENDIENTES}} (conservative / base / optimistic) with their NPV and payback. (7) Mark every data point not provided as [ASSUMPTION] and list the assumptions that most move the result with their sensitivity. (8) Close with the recommendation in one line (continue / rescale / stop), its quantitative trigger, and a three-sentence script to open the presentation before the committee. Consider attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Do not use market prices or invented figures; currency in the stated unit.

prompts.title: Calculation of PV, EV, and AC
prompts.content: Act as a senior Project Controls Specialist specializing in earned value management (EVM) under PMBOK and the standard EVM practice. Calculate the three earned value baseline measurements for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} at data date {{FECHA_CORTE}}: Planned Value (PV), Earned Value (EV), and Actual Cost (AC), with full traceability and ready to feed into variances, indices, and forecasts. Inputs: BAC = {{BAC}} in {{MONEDA}}, cost baseline {{LINEA_BASE_COSTOS}}, actual physical progress {{AVANCE_REAL}}, actual costs {{COSTOS_REALES}}, measurement rule {{REGLA_MEDICION}}, and attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any essential data point is missing (BAC, temporal distribution of the baseline, progress, or actual costs), ask for it before calculating: do not invent figures and mark every estimate as [ASSUMPTION]. Proceed as follows: confirm scope, {{MONEDA}}, {{FECHA_CORTE}}, and level of calculation (full project or by control account / work package). Calculate PV by summing the budget that {{LINEA_BASE_COSTOS}} programmed to be completed through {{FECHA_CORTE}}. Calculate EV by applying {{REGLA_MEDICION}} uniformly: for each element multiply its {{AVANCE_REAL}} by its assigned budget and sum the total; always use budget, never actual cost. Calculate AC by summing {{COSTOS_REALES}} incurred and accrued through {{FECHA_CORTE}} and declare whether it includes committed costs or only accrued. Build a table by element (budget, PV, % progress, EV, AC) with a totals row that reconciles against {{BAC}}. Report inconsistencies: progress without cost, cost without progress, sum of budgets different from BAC, progress outside 0–100%, or EV greater than the element's budget. Before calculating, restate what you understand and present your plan; then execute. Deliver a final block with PV, EV, and AC consolidated in {{MONEDA}} at {{FECHA_CORTE}}, the supporting table, and the traceability notes, ready to calculate CV, SV, CPI, SPI, and EAC/ETC forecasts. Use neutral and professional English; never mention commercial prices or use the word free.

prompts.title: Performance indices CPI and SPI
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Project Controls Manager, PMP-certified, specializing in Earned Value Management (EVM) per the PMI PMBOK standard. I need a performance control dashboard for {{PROYECTO_Y_FECHA_CORTE}} that objectively diagnoses whether I am over budget and/or behind schedule, and forecasts the cost at close-out.

Before calculating, restate in your own words what you understand and present your plan; then execute.

Proceed as follows:
1. Validate that these data points all refer to the same data date and are in the same currency and unit: Planned Value PV = {{PV}}, Earned Value or progress EV_O_AVANCE = {{EV_O_AVANCE}}, Actual Cost AC = {{AC}}, Budget at Completion BAC = {{BAC}}. If only physical progress percentage is available, derive EV = % progress × BAC and declare it. If an indispensable data point is missing and cannot be derived, stop and ask me for it; do not invent figures.
2. Calculate showing the operation with my numbers: CPI = EV / AC, SPI = EV / PV, CV = EV − AC, SV = EV − PV. If AC or PV are zero, do not divide: flag the index as not calculable.
3. Interpret each index using the rule less than 1 = unfavorable, equal to 1 = on track, greater than 1 = favorable, and translate to business language. Warn that SPI tends toward 1 near close-out even if the project is behind schedule.
4. Forecast the close-out per {{SUPUESTO_EAC}}: typical deviation EAC = BAC / CPI; atypical EAC = AC + (BAC − EV); cost and schedule EAC = AC + (BAC − EV) / (CPI × SPI). Calculate ETC = EAC − AC, VAC = BAC − EAC, and TCPI = (BAC − EV) / (BAC − AC). Declare the assumption.
5. Close with 2 or 3 corrective actions prioritized by impact, with a suggested owner.

Consider the material in {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver: a table with PV, EV, AC, BAC, CPI, SPI, CV, SV, EAC, ETC, VAC, and TCPI; a one-line diagnosis per index; the forecast with its assumption; and the prioritized action list. Missing data: flag it as pending, do not invent it.

prompts.title: Cost (CV) and schedule (SV) variances
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project manager specializing in earned value management (EVM) under the PMBOK standard, with experience in project control and reporting to steering committees. I need a cost variance (CV) and schedule variance (SV) report for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} at data date {{FECHA_CORTE}}, with breakdown {{DESGLOSE}}, to serve as the basis for the control conversation with the sponsor: to decide where to intervene, justify corrective actions with evidence, and anticipate the final result before deviations become irreversible.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before calculating, restate which project and data date you will be controlling and present your calculation plan; then execute.

Input data: PV, EV, and AC aggregated and by package are in {{DATOS_EVM}}; known context on deviations in {{CONTEXTO_DESVIOS}}; attachments in {{ADJUNTOS}}. If PV, EV, AC, or the data date are missing, ask before calculating and do not proceed without them.

Proceed as follows: (1) Arrange PV/EV/AC in a table by package and validate completeness and coherence, flagging if EV exceeds the package's PV without justification. (2) Calculate by package and aggregate CV = EV − AC, SV = EV − PV, CV% = CV/EV, SV% = SV/PV; avoid division by zero when EV or PV are zero and declare it. (3) Interpret the sign of each variance (negative CV = overrun, negative SV = behind schedule, positive values = buffer) and classify each package into one of the four cost-schedule quadrants. (4) Order packages by severity combining absolute and relative deviation magnitude. (5) For the 2 or 3 most critical packages apply five whys, separating the cost causal chain from the schedule causal chain. (6) Translate each root cause into a measurable corrective action with a suggested owner and expected effect on CV and SV.

Do not invent figures: mark [ASSUMPTION] on every assumed data point, declare the source of each figure, and keep the input monetary unit without converting currencies. Deliver: variance table, quadrant matrix, root-cause analysis of critical packages, and prioritized action plan, in a structure ready for the control committee.

prompts.title: EVM Report for Executives
prompts.content:
Act as a PMO Director with PMP certification and fifteen years closing projects using earned value before steering committees, expert in translating financial strategy into actionable language. Build a one-page executive EVM dashboard for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} with status date {{FECHA_CORTE}}, which a committee can read without knowing EVM and use to decide continuity, budget, or scope.

Base data: PV = {{PV}} (cumulative Planned Value), EV = {{EV}} (cumulative Earned Value), AC = {{AC}} (cumulative Actual Cost), BAC = {{BAC}} (Budget at Completion). Audience and decision to enable: {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of the five base inputs (PV, EV, AC, BAC, FECHA_CORTE) is missing, request it before calculating; do not invent figures. If {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}} is empty, assume steering committee and continuity decision, and mark it as an assumption.

Validate coherence: EV and AC must be non-negative, PV consistent with the date, EV not greater than BAC, AC greater than zero before dividing. If a data point is zero or incoherent, stop and report it.

Calculate showing each formula: SV = EV - PV; CV = EV - AC; SPI = EV / PV; CPI = EV / AC; EAC = BAC / CPI (declare the assumption: past cost performance continues); ETC = EAC - AC; VAC = BAC - EAC; TCPI = (BAC - EV) / (BAC - AC). Round indices to two decimal places and interpret each in business terms. If TCPI > 1.10, warn that recovering the budget is unrealistic without scope change or injection.

Traffic lights for SPI, CPI, and overall health with thresholds: green 0.95–1.05; yellow 0.90–0.95; red < 0.90 or > 1.10. Overall health = worst of SPI and CPI. Executive narrative of at most five lines in business language. Three to five prioritized recommendations, each with the triggering index, suggested owner, and timeframe. Assemble in metrics table + traffic-light panel + narrative + recommendations. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any figure derived from a missing data point. No prices and no word free.

prompts.title: Earned Value S-Curve
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project control and earned value management (EVM) specialist, trained in the PMI standard (PMBOK Guide and Practice Standard for Earned Value Management), with experience reporting to steering committees. I need a complete earned value S-curve analysis for project {{PROYECTO}} at status date {{FECHA_CORTE}}.

Data: budget at completion BAC = {{BAC}}; period series {{DATOS_PERIODICOS}} with PV, EV, and AC (indicate whether cumulative or incremental); currency or unit {{MONEDA_UNIDAD}}; report audience {{AUDIENCIA}}; attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Build the deliverable in this order: (1) cumulative data table by period with PV, EV, and AC in {{MONEDA_UNIDAD}}; if {{DATOS_PERIODICOS}} comes as incremental values, convert to cumulative and state this explicitly. (2) Calculation at {{FECHA_CORTE}}: SV = EV - PV; CV = EV - AC; SPI = EV / PV; CPI = EV / AC; indices with 2 decimal places and sign interpreted as favorable, unfavorable, or on plan. (3) S-curve reading: EV vs AC separation (cost) and PV vs EV (schedule in value), and what it means when AC exceeds or falls below PV. (4) Completion forecasts with three named scenarios (optimistic EAC = AC + (BAC - EV); constant CPI EAC = BAC / CPI; realistic EAC = AC + (BAC - EV) / (CPI x SPI)), with ETC = EAC - AC and VAC = BAC - EAC for each, and a recommendation of the most prudent for {{AUDIENCIA}}. (5) TCPI = (BAC - EV) / (BAC - AC) and interpretation against the current CPI. (6) Executive diagnosis of 4 to 6 lines calibrated to {{AUDIENCIA}} with 2 or 3 corrective actions. (7) Chart specification: X-axis time by periods, Y-axis cumulative value in {{MONEDA_UNIDAD}}, series PV, EV, AC, vertical line at {{FECHA_CORTE}}, and horizontal BAC mark.

Rules: do not invent figures; if {{BAC}}, {{FECHA_CORTE}}, or any PV, EV, or AC is missing, or there are inconsistencies (EV greater than BAC, negative values, missing periods, mixed units), stop and request them. Warn that SPI loses meaning near project close. If any data is missing, request it before calculating.

prompts.title: Progress Measurement Methods (EV Rules)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project control manager (PMO), specialist in earned value (EVM) under PMBOK and the EVMS practice (ANSI/EIA-748), with experience in auditable measurement baselines.

Context: the credibility of every earned value report depends on a decision usually made without rigor: how the progress of each work package is credited. A poorly chosen rule (50/50 on a six-month package, subjective physical percent, abusive LOE) inflates EV, hides the real delay, and destroys confidence in the SV and CV indices. Defining and freezing the correct rule unlocks a defensible PMB and auditable control decisions.

Case data:
- Work packages: {{PAQUETES_TRABAJO}}
- EVM reporting frequency: {{FRECUENCIA_REPORTE}}
- Nature of work per package: {{NATURALEZA_TRABAJO}}
- Organizational tolerance for subjectivity: {{TOLERANCIA_SUBJETIVIDAD}}
- Measurement baseline status: {{ESTADO_LINEA_BASE}}

Your deliverable is a measurement rule assignment table by package plus integrity governance rules.

Proceed as follows:
1. Inventory {{PAQUETES_TRABAJO}} and classify each package by duration relative to {{FRECUENCIA_REPORTE}} (calculate the duration/period ratio) and by {{NATURALEZA_TRABAJO}}: discrete, repetitive homogeneous, or continuous support.
2. Assign each package exactly one canonical rule: 0/100, 50/50 or variants 25/75 and 75/25, weighted milestones, physical percent complete, completed units, or LOE (only for support without a discrete deliverable). Name the discarded rule and why.
3. Justify each choice with two criteria: (a) duration vs. reporting period — one or two periods lead to a fixed formula; longer, to weighted milestones or physical percent with an objective measure — and (b) objectivity of the evidence given {{TOLERANCIA_SUBJETIVIDAD}}.
4. For each package fix the credit criterion: the objective verifiable data point and its named source that triggers EV.
5. Flag each package with a gaming risk (EV inflated by subjective physical percent, delay hidden by LOE, poorly dimensioned fixed formula, milestone without acceptance criterion), with its mitigation.
6. Establish transition and freezing rules according to {{ESTADO_LINEA_BASE}} and close with three integrity governance rules, including PMB freezing, formal change control, and handling of rework/emerging scope.

Rules: do not invent data; anything not provided is marked [ASSUMPTION] or requested. Never credit EV for incurred cost. Neutral professional language, no emojis. If an essential data point is missing, request it before executing.

prompts.title: Risk Identification with RBS
prompts.content:
Act as a senior risk manager (PMI-RMP) who facilitates risk identification workshops in complex, multidisciplinary projects. Your task is to build a preliminary risk register organized by a hierarchical Risk Breakdown Structure (RBS) for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, in the early planning phase and before qualitative analysis, so that no category goes blind.

Project context:
- Objective and scope: {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}
- Critical deliverables or milestones: {{ENTREGABLES_CLAVE}}
- Current constraints and assumptions: {{RESTRICCIONES_SUPUESTOS}}
- Level 1 RBS categories (optional): {{CATEGORIAS_RBS}}
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

First restate in one or two sentences your interpretation of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, its objective, and its constraints, and present your work plan (RBS > elicitation > drafting > synthesis) before executing. If essential information is missing, request it before continuing rather than inventing it.

Then proceed as follows:
1. Build the RBS: Level 1 from {{CATEGORIAS_RBS}} (if empty, use Technical, Project Management, Organizational, External); derive Level 2 subcategories pertinent to {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}. Do not leave branches empty without justifying why.
2. By subcategory, formulate elicitation questions that surface real and specific project risks, not generic ones.
3. Draft each risk in cause-event-effect: "Due to [certain cause], [uncertain event] may occur, which would lead to [effect on objectives]". Distinguish the risk from its cause and from an already materialized problem (issue): the cause is a present fact, the risk is uncertain, the issue has already occurred and does not go in the register.
4. Assign each risk: unique ID, RBS category/subcategory, tentative owner, observable triggers, and affected objective (scope, schedule, cost, quality).
5. Include at least one opportunity (positive risk), not only threats.
6. Cover evident secondary and interdependent risks.

Do not estimate probability or impact: this is the identification phase. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any inferred risk without confirmation.

Deliverable: register table (ID, RBS L1, RBS L2, cause-event-effect statement, type threat/opportunity, tentative owner, triggers, affected objective); plus hierarchical RBS view with risk count per branch and a closing note on exposure concentrations and blind spots. Close with assumptions made and open questions for the team.

prompts.title: Risk Register
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project manager with PMP certification and command of ISO 31000. Build the complete risk register for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, whose objective is {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}, with scope and milestones {{ALCANCE_E_HITOS}} and risk tolerance {{TOLERANCIA_AL_RIESGO}}. Start from {{RIESGOS_O_FUENTES}} if it exists. First confirm objective, scope, milestones, and tolerance; explicitly declare the probability and impact criteria you will use (define what each level on the five-point scale means, against cost, time, scope, and quality). Then identify risks by working through each category (technical, external, organizational, and project management) and include threats and opportunities, without duplicating. Draft each risk using PMBOK's cause-event-effect syntax: 'Due to [certain cause], [uncertain event] may occur, which would cause [effect on objectives]'. Assign probability and impact on a five-level scale (Very Low to Very High) and calculate the exposure as probability times impact (1–25 scale), using {{TOLERANCIA_AL_RIESGO}} as the threshold. For each risk define the response strategy according to type, a concrete action, the owner, the trigger or early warning signal, the residual risk after the response, and the status (Open, Under Monitoring, Materialized, Closed). Sort the table by exposure descending and close with the critical top 5, their prioritized plan, and a qualitative contingency reserve recommendation (effort or time, never monetary figures). Mark every inference with [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent risks without basis. Deliverable: table with columns ID, category, statement, probability, impact, exposure, strategy, action, owner, trigger, residual, and status, plus the critical top 5. If {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}, {{ALCANCE_E_HITOS}}, or {{TOLERANCIA_AL_RIESGO}} is missing, request it before executing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Qualitative Probability-Impact Analysis
Quantitative Analysis with Expected Monetary Value
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project manager specialized in quantitative risk analysis (PMI-RMP training, PMBOK command, Expected Monetary Value, and Decision Tree Analysis). Your task: convert {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} into monetary exposure, resolve {{DECISIONES_A_EVALUAR}} with a decision tree, and deliver a defensible contingency reserve contrasted against {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Interpret: classify each risk from {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} as a threat or opportunity and flag missing data (probability, impact, currency, horizon, branches). If a critical input is missing, request it and do not invent figures. Mark every assumed estimate with [ASSUMPTION] and the data that would confirm it. Correct inconsistencies: probabilities outside 0-100%, impacts without a sign, mixed currencies vs. {{MONEDA_Y_HORIZONTE}}, duplicated or correlated risks.

Plan: declare the method before operating: EMV = probability x impact, sign convention (threat negative, opportunity positive), tree structure, and list of risks to calculate. If {{DECISIONES_A_EVALUAR}} is empty, omit the tree and say so.

Execute:
1. Normalize {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}}: type, probability (%), and impact in {{MONEDA_Y_HORIZONTE}}.
2. Calculate EMV per risk with the correct sign.
3. Sort in a table by exposure (absolute value of EMV) from highest to lowest; mark the subset that concentrates ~80% of the exposure.
4. If {{DECISIONES_A_EVALUAR}} has alternatives, solve the tree by rollback: per branch, chance-node EMV plus certain cost; recommend the option with the best expected value with the calculation visible and note the sensitivity to the most uncertain probability.
5. Derive the contingency reserve = EMV of threats netted against opportunities (known only); contrast it against {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}} and separate the management reserve (unknowns).

Edge cases: if the net EMV is positive, explain it and do not force a negative reserve. If {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}} is lower than the calculated reserve, flag the gap and propose responses (mitigate, transfer, avoid) on the top risks.

Deliverable: sorted EMV table, solved tree (if applicable), contingency reserve with one-line justification, separated management reserve, contrast against {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}, and top 3 by impact in priority order. Close with model limitations (EMV assumes independence and one step) and what would refine it (Monte Carlo, ranges). No market prices or quotes.

Variables:
- {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}}: risks with type, probability (%), and monetary impact per risk.
- {{MONEDA_Y_HORIZONTE}}: project currency and analysis time window.
- {{DECISIONES_A_EVALUAR}}: alternatives to compare with certain costs and chance nodes (optional).
- {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}: reserve cap or sponsor's tolerance (optional).

prompts.title: Risk Response Planning
prompts.content:
Act as a certified senior risk manager (PMP/PMI-RMP) expert in response planning per PMBOK and ISO 31000, with real-world practice in projects under constraints. Work on project {{PROYECTO}} (name, type, objective, current phase, and planning horizon). The prioritized register is {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} (risks with probability and impact or qualitative severity; indicate whether they are threats or opportunities when known). The sponsor's tolerance is {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}} (appetite and thresholds: what severity demands active response and what can be accepted). The constraints are {{RESTRICCIONES}} (time limits, team capacity, available reserves, and dependencies). Treat {{RIESGOS_FOCO}} first if specified. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Prioritization without a response does not reduce exposure: convert {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} into an actionable and defensible response plan before the committee. Before executing, restate what you understood about {{PROYECTO}}, {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}, and {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and present your plan; if the prioritized register, tolerance, or constraints context is missing, request it before proceeding and mark as [ASSUMPTION] any data not provided. Then deliver: (1) classification of each risk from {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} as a threat or opportunity with prioritized exposure (probability times impact or qualitative severity) and treatment order, respecting {{RIESGOS_FOCO}}; (2) primary strategy per risk from the correct set (threats: avoid, transfer, mitigate, accept; opportunities: exploit, share, enhance, accept), justified by {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}} and cost-benefit, with the discarded alternative; (3) actions per risk with a unique owner, target date, observable trigger, and reserve in effort or time within {{RESTRICCIONES}}; (4) contingency and fallback for the residual risk of each critical risk; (5) recalculated residual risk and secondary risks introduced by the responses; (6) response plan table and executive summary of decisions, assumptions, and gaps. Always distinguish preventive action from contingency plan; each trigger with threshold and monitoring owner. Never include monetary amounts or the word free: all costs in effort, time, or relative reserve. If a response exceeds {{RESTRICCIONES}}, declare it as a gap and propose the best feasible option. Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute.

prompts.title: Contingency Plans with Triggers
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project manager specialized in risk management, with PMP/PMI-RMP certification and command of the PMBOK framework (response planning and risk monitoring). Design contingency plans with triggers for {{RIESGOS_CRITICOS}} in project {{PROYECTO}}, so that the team moves from improvised reaction under pressure to a pre-agreed response activated by a measurable early signal, before the damage escalates.

First restate what you understand about {{PROYECTO}}, {{OBJETIVOS}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{RIESGOS_CRITICOS}}, and {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}, and present your plan; execute only afterward. If {{RIESGOS_CRITICOS}}, {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}, or {{HORIZONTE}} are missing or ambiguous, request them or propose them derived from context and mark them as [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent data.

Calibrate threshold sensitivity to {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}: low tolerance demands earlier and stricter triggers; high tolerance allows more slack before activating. For each risk in {{RIESGOS_CRITICOS}} deliver five fields: (1) the event in cause-event-effect format on {{OBJETIVOS}}; (2) the trigger as a quantitative threshold (e.g., schedule deviation greater than X percent, SPI below Y, CPI below Z) or verifiable observable condition, never subjective, with the data source and measurement frequency; (3) the pre-agreed response with strategy (mitigate, transfer, avoid, or actively accept), the first three execution steps, and the contingency reserve or plan B if the first attempt fails; (4) the trigger owner, a concrete role that monitors it, with their monitoring cadence; (5) the escalation threshold and to whom it escalates. Always distinguish trigger (signal) from response (action) and prefer leading indicators over signals that only confirm damage already done.

Close with three deliverables: contingency matrix (risk | measurable trigger + source/frequency | response + 3 steps + plan B | owner + cadence | escalation + to whom); brief narrative per risk justifying the chosen threshold; and periodic trigger review protocol aligned to {{HORIZONTE}} indicating when to recalibrate thresholds and how to retire triggers for already-closed risks. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION] and flag risks without a reliable leading indicator as a point of attention.

Variables: {{PROYECTO}}, {{OBJETIVOS}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{RIESGOS_CRITICOS}}, {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Risk Monitoring and Re-evaluation
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Project Manager (PMP) expert in monitoring and controlling risks, with command of the PMBOK Monitor Risks process, periodic re-evaluation, risk audits, and residual and secondary risk analysis. Re-evaluate the live risk register of {{PROYECTO}} in this cadence window, because the landscape is no longer what it was at kickoff: some responses left residual risk, others introduced secondary risks, and the period brought new threats and opportunities. Inputs: current register {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}}; already-applied responses with their result {{RESPUESTAS_APLICADAS}}; project status for the period {{ESTADO_PROYECTO}}; appetite and tolerances {{APETITO_RIESGO}}; cadence and next date {{CADENCIA}}; attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of these critical inputs is missing, request it before continuing; do not invent values. Deliver: (1) re-evaluated register in table form where each active risk carries probability, impact, recalculated exposure, and explicit trend (rising, falling, or stable) against the previous review; (2) residual risk of each response from {{RESPUESTAS_APLICADAS}}, quantified and judged as acceptable or not against {{APETITO_RIESGO}}; (3) secondary risks introduced by the responses, traced to the response that originated them; (4) emerging risks from the period based on {{ESTADO_PROYECTO}} - threats and opportunities - each with an observable trigger; (5) proposed closures with justification (cause extinguished or window expired); (6) for each live risk, owner, activation trigger, agreed response, and next action with date; (7) cadence note with 3 to 5 priorities and date of the next review per {{CADENCIA}}. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any probability, impact, or cause value inferred; nothing invented is presented as data. Distinguish threat from opportunity and residual risk from secondary risk. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Overall project risk assessment
prompts.content:
Act as a senior portfolio and project Risk Manager (PMI-RMP), expert in quantitative risk analysis (Monte Carlo, EMV, sensitivity) in high-uncertainty environments. Assess the OVERALL risk of {{PROYECTO}}: the combined effect of all uncertainty on the project objectives as a whole, not the sum of the individual risks already listed. The purpose is to unlock a continuity decision that is defensible before the sponsor, to size contingency and management reserves with sound judgment, and to identify where to intervene to move the needle on the entire project.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in your own words what project you are evaluating, at what phase and against which objectives, baseline, and thresholds; declare what data you are missing and present your plan; wait for validation before quantifying.

Inputs:
- PROYECTO: {{PROYECTO}} (name, current phase, and purpose)
- OBJETIVOS_Y_LINEA_BASE: {{OBJETIVOS_Y_LINEA_BASE}} (objectives and measurable baseline: scope, target date and duration, budget, quality, and expected benefits)
- REGISTRO_DE_RIESGOS: {{REGISTRO_DE_RIESGOS}} (individual risks with probability/impact, assumptions and constraints; optional)
- APETITO_DE_RIESGO: {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}} (sponsor's appetite and threshold: tolerable schedule/cost deviation and maximum acceptable level; optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Deliver a structured report with: (1) Framing that distinguishes overall risk from individual risk and sets objectives, baseline, and thresholds from {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}}. (2) Qualitative assessment at 5 levels justified by structural indicators (complexity, technological novelty, requirements ambiguity, external dependencies, team maturity, schedule/budget slack) with evidence from {{REGISTRO_DE_RIESGOS}}. (3) Quantitative assessment only when data exist: Monte Carlo for schedule and cost, aggregate EMV, P50/P80, and tornado of dominant drivers. (4) Trend and distance from appetite. (5) Project-level responses. (6) Verdict: exposure level + recommendation (proceed / proceed with conditions / reconsider) + 3 highest-leverage actions with a review trigger.

Tag every datum not provided as [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent figures. If {{OBJETIVOS_Y_LINEA_BASE}}, {{REGISTRO_DE_RIESGOS}}, or {{APETITO_DE_RIESGO}} are missing, request them before quantifying.

prompts.title: Risk appetite and tolerance framework
prompts.content: Act as a Project Risk Director (PMI-RMP) with experience in portfolio governance and risk appetite design under ISO 31000 and COSO ERM. Build a Risk Appetite and Tolerance Framework for {{PROYECTO}}, applied to the project and not in the abstract. If {{PROYECTO}}, {{OBJETIVOS}}, {{RESTRICCIONES}}, or {{HORIZONTE}} are missing, ask for them before drafting; do not invent tolerance figures. Proceed as follows: (1) Distinguish and define, as applied to the project, appetite (risk sought to achieve {{OBJETIVOS}}), tolerance (maximum acceptable deviation from baseline), and capacity (absolute limit compatible with {{RESTRICCIONES}}), without overlap. (2) Structure {{CATEGORIAS_RIESGO}} as an RBS; if a material category is missing, propose and justify it. (3) For each category set: an appetite statement (averse, cautious, open, or seeker), a quantitative tolerance threshold (schedule and cost as a percentage deviation from baseline) and a verifiable qualitative one (quality, regulatory, reputational with observable criteria), and a capacity threshold as a hard limit. (4) Translate thresholds into traffic-light zones: green (team management), yellow (active mitigation plus sponsor notification), red (committee escalation plus go/no-go); each zone with action and role-named owner. (5) Define recalibration triggers and the review cadence aligned to {{HORIZONTE}} and its next control milestone. Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Tag every assumed value with [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver: category matrix table (category | appetite | tolerance | capacity | trigger-zone | action-owner), escalation rules, recalibration triggers, and cadence, ready to attach to the risk management plan. Variables: {{PROYECTO}}, {{OBJETIVOS}}, {{CATEGORIAS_RIESGO}}, {{RESTRICCIONES}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Bow-tie analysis of a critical risk
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project risk manager, certified in ISO 31000 and practitioner of the bow-tie method and Reason's barrier model, with a track record in high-risk projects. I need a complete and actionable bow-tie analysis of a critical risk, because the flat register lists probability and impact but does not show the cause → control → event → consequence chain or where the barrier gaps are.

Project context: {{CONTEXTO_PROYECTO}}.
Central event to map: {{EVENTO_CENTRAL}}.
Known threats: {{AMENAZAS}}.
Feared consequences: {{CONSECUENCIAS}}.
Existing barriers: {{BARRERAS_EXISTENTES}}.
Risk tolerance: {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}.
Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before executing, restate in your own words the risk you understand and present your plan. If {{EVENTO_CENTRAL}}, {{CONTEXTO_PROYECTO}}, or {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask me for them with specific questions; do not invent project data.

Proceed as follows:
1. Define the central event as a specific, observable loss of control—neither cause nor consequence; rewrite {{EVENTO_CENTRAL}} if it comes mixed and explain why.
2. Left arm (prevention): list threats from {{AMENAZAS}} plus any missing ones, each with its trigger mechanism and at least one preventive barrier that reduces probability, integrating {{BARRERAS_EXISTENTES}}.
3. Right arm (recovery): list consequences from {{CONSECUENCIAS}} plus any missing ones, each with its impact on scope, schedule, cost, quality, or reputation and at least one reactive or recovery barrier.
4. Degradation: identify the escalation factors that degrade each critical barrier and the control that sustains it against that factor.
5. Governance: assign each barrier an owner, type (human, technical, or process), status (active, partial, or absent), and verification; tag as paper-barrier any barrier that exists in a document but nobody executes.
6. Close with a robustness verdict, the two most urgent gaps relative to {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}, and the actions to close them with owner and timeline.

Rules: do not mix preventive with reactive barriers; a barrier that depends on another to activate is not independent. Tag every datum not provided with [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver a textual map threats → preventive barriers → CENTRAL EVENT → reactive barriers → consequences, then the barrier table, and finally the verdict with two gaps and actions. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Assumptions and constraints register
prompts.content:
Act as a PMP-certified senior project manager, specialist in assumptions and constraints management according to PMBOK, with experience running living registers in complex projects. I will build the register with this data:

- Project: {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} (name or identifier)
- Sources: {{FUENTES}} (documents to harvest: project charter, scope/WBS, schedule, resource plan, stakeholder notes)
- Methodology: {{METODOLOGIA}} (Agile, Waterfall, Hybrid, or SAFe; sets the review cadence)
- Owners: {{RESPONSABLES}} (people or roles to validate assumptions; if missing, propose roles)
- Risk register: {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} (existing register to link to, or "no prior register")

Proceed as follows:
1. Restate the assignment: "Harvest assumptions and constraints from {{FUENTES}} of project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, prioritize by confidence × impact, and link the fragile ones to {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}}." If any essential datum above is missing, ask me for it before executing. Do not infer the project architecture: derive it from {{FUENTES}} and tag with [ASSUMPTION] what cannot be verified.
2. Harvest each assumption (unverified belief that underpins a decision) and each constraint (imposed, non-negotiable limit) from {{FUENTES}}; each entry cites its source document or conversation, with no parentless entries. If a promised source did not arrive, declare it.
3. Categorize each entry: technical, organizational, financial, resources, schedule, or external.
4. Assign each assumption a confidence level (High >80%, Medium 50–80%, Low <50%) and an impact if false (Critical, High, Medium, Low), with a one-line justification each; calculate exposure = confidence × impact and sort from highest to lowest.
5. Define per assumption a verifiable validation method (prototype, PoC, expert review, data analysis, stakeholder confirmation), an owner from {{RESPONSABLES}}, and a deadline tied to a real decision point (milestone, gate, phase start).
6. Classify constraints as hard (non-negotiable) and soft (with room); for each hard one, name its design or planning implication.
7. Tag as a risk candidate any Low × High/Critical assumption: draft the risk statement in cause-event-consequence form, define its early-warning indicator, and link it to {{REGISTRO_RIESGOS}} (or note that one must be created).
8. Assign a lifecycle status to each entry: Open, Under Validation, Validated, Invalidated, or Converted to Risk.
9. Generate the confidence × impact heat map, detect conflicting or redundant assumptions across sources, and propose a review cadence consistent with {{METODOLOGIA}}.

Tag every statement: [PLAN], [METRIC], [INFERENCE], [ASSUMPTION], [STAKEHOLDER]. Neutral and professional English, no emojis. Do not mention prices. Deliver prioritized assumptions table, hard/soft constraints table, heat map, risk candidates with indicators, and an executive summary of 4 to 6 bullets. Close by stating which source or additional confirmation would most reduce uncertainty.

prompts.title: Project pre-mortem
prompts.content: Act as a senior Project Manager (PMP) and risk management facilitator, expert in pre-mortem and prospective hindsight (Gary Klein). You are going to facilitate a pre-mortem of {{PROYECTO}} before committing resources. The technique inverts the classic analysis: instead of asking what could go wrong, the team places itself in a future where the project has ALREADY failed indisputably and explains why it happened; that inversion defeats overconfidence, groupthink, and planning optimism. Input data: project {{PROYECTO}}, measurable success objective {{OBJETIVO_MEDIBLE}}, target close date {{FECHA_CIERRE}}, committed team and resources {{EQUIPO_RECURSOS}}, key external dependencies {{DEPENDENCIAS_CLAVE}} (optional), sponsor's risk tolerance {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}} (optional). If {{PROYECTO}}, {{OBJETIVO_MEDIBLE}}, {{FECHA_CIERRE}}, or {{EQUIPO_RECURSOS}} are missing, ask for them before proceeding and do not invent metrics. Proceed as follows: (1) restate {{PROYECTO}}, {{OBJETIVO_MEDIBLE}}, and {{FECHA_CIERRE}} as you understand them and list what is missing as a question. (2) Declare the scenario in the consummated past: we are at {{FECHA_CIERRE}} and the project failed indisputably. (3) Generate 12 to 18 plausible causes of failure, distributed across at least five of these seven categories: scope, team and resources ({{EQUIPO_RECURSOS}}), external dependencies and suppliers ({{DEPENDENCIAS_CLAVE}}), technical, stakeholders and politics, business assumptions, schedule and budget; include at least one black swan of low probability and high impact. (4) Rate each cause by probability (high/medium/low) and impact (high/medium/low), prioritize it in a matrix, and tag [ASSUMPTION] on every inference due to missing data. (5) For the 5 to 7 priority risks, define a mitigation action (preventive or contingency), a named owner, and an observable, measurable early-warning signal with a trigger threshold. (6) Close with the three actions for this week that most reduce aggregate risk, consistent with {{TOLERANCIA_RIESGO}}, and a recheck of residual risk. Deliver: prioritized risks table (cause | category | prob | impact | priority | [ASSUMPTION]?) + mitigation plan (risk | preventive/contingency action | owner | early-warning signal + threshold) + the three actions for the week. Rules: consummated past, never conditional; no invented metrics; no vague signals; neutral English, no emojis, no prices. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Issue log
prompts.content:
Act as a PMP-certified senior Project Manager, expert in issue governance in multi-team projects and in preparing dashboards for steering committees. I need you to convert the raw list of active problems of {{PROYECTO}} into a single, actionable Issue Log, because today they are scattered across emails, chats, and team memory, with no clear owner or close date, and issues repeat in every meeting without progress while critical ones are discovered late.

Active problems to process:
{{INCIDENCIAS}}

Before executing, restate in your own words what you understand about the status of {{PROYECTO}} and the problems I have given you, and present your plan: the priority scale you will apply and the list of issues missing data (owner, target date, or impact) that will require an explicit assumption or a question. Wait for my confirmation of the plan before building the final table.

Then proceed as follows. First separate issues (problems that have already occurred) from risks (future events still probable); move risks to a separate list outside the log and note which ones you moved and why. Second, normalize each issue to these columns: sequential ID (INC-001, INC-002), description as an observable symptom and not a disguised solution, concrete impact (what is blocked, degraded, or delayed, with magnitude if available), priority per {{ESCALA_PRIORIDAD}}, single owner (one person only, never a team or an area), detection date, target date, status (Open / In Progress / Blocked / Pending Third Parties / Closed), and a concrete next action with responsible party and date. Third, prioritize per {{ESCALA_PRIORIDAD}}; if I do not define it, apply a four-level impact-by-urgency matrix (Critical, High, Medium, Low). Fourth, sort the table by priority descending and, within each level, by closest target date first; overdue issues are marked and moved to the top of their level. Fifth, identify which ones require a committee decision: those that exceed the owner's authority, those blocked by an external dependency, and those that have been open longer than the expected age threshold for their priority.

Tag as an explicit assumption every Critical or High issue that arrives without an owner or target date, and raise it as a governance gap rather than inventing the datum. If the owner, target date, or impact of a Critical or High issue is missing, ask for it before closing the prioritization. If an issue brings multiple causes or multiple affected parties, record it as a single row with the root cause as the description and enumerate the effects in the impact field; do not duplicate it. If two people appear as owner, choose the one with closure authority and leave the other as support in the next action. Also flag duplicates or issues that are actually the same problem with different symptoms, and consolidate them. Treat the attachments {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting context.

Do not invent priorities, dates, or metrics that do not follow from what I gave you. Work in neutral and professional English, no emojis.

Deliver three blocks: (1) the sorted and normalized Issue Log table; (2) a three-line executive summary stating how many Critical and High issues there are, how many are overdue, and which to escalate today; and (3) the list of issues for committee decision, each with the escalation reason and the decision requested. Close with a brief section on governance gaps (issues without owner or date) and the list of risks removed from the log.

Parameters:
- {{PROYECTO}}: project name, current phase, and register cut-off date.
- {{INCIDENCIAS}}: raw list of active problems; for each one, whatever is known (symptom, impact, tentative owner, target date, status).
- {{ESCALA_PRIORIDAD}}: prioritization criterion (impact × urgency matrix or Critical/High/Medium/Low levels); optional.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Issue escalation matrix
Consolidated RAID board
prompts.content: Act as a senior project manager (PMP) expert in project governance and risk management under PMBOK and ISO 31000, specialized in RAID boards. Consolidate a single RAID board for {{PROYECTO}}, turning into a living control the noise of risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies currently scattered. Start from {{RAID_ACTUAL}} and extract additional items from {{FUENTES_ENTRADA}}. Deliver: (1) executive summary of 5 to 7 lines on health in RAID terms and the dominant item demanding a decision; (2) R-Risks section: id, description as a future uncertain event, probability high/medium/low, impact high/medium/low, resulting level, response avoid/mitigate/transfer/accept, single owner, target date, escalation trigger; (3) A-Assumptions section: id, assumption, criticality, how it is validated, validation deadline, owner, and which risk or issue it converts to if false; (4) I-Issues section: id, description of the currently occurring problem, severity, age or opening date, corrective action, owner, target date, status; (5) D-Dependencies section: id, description, direction incoming/outgoing, responsible party, committed date, status on-track/at-risk/overdue, internal owner, contingency plan if it fails; (6) critical top of {{HORIZONTE}} ordered by {{CRITERIOS_PRIORIZACION}}, always including overdue or at-risk dependencies; (7) open questions and items without an owner, flagged for assignment. Apply the classification test item by item: not yet occurred and uncertain = Risk; taken as certain without confirmation = Assumption; already occurring and hurts today = Issue; depends on a third party = Dependency. Do not mix or duplicate categories; place each item in its primary and link the derived one. Derive each risk level from probability × impact with an explicit matrix and declare, consistent with {{GOBERNANZA}}, the threshold that triggers escalation and to whom it escalates. Tag each statement as verified data or [ASSUMPTION]. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan; if any datum is missing, ask for it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver in neutral and professional English, in tables by section, no emojis, ready for the governance committee.

prompts.title: Inter-team dependency map
Blockage and impediment management
prompts.content:
Act as a Scrum Master or senior PMO lead, expert in impediment management, critical dependencies, and RAID models, with practice in blockage aging and disciplined escalation. Your mission: convert the raw list of blockages from {{PROYECTO}} into an auditable impediment register and an unblocking plan that assigns a single owner and target date to each one, to recover control of the critical path before {{HITOS_PROXIMOS}}.

Inputs:
- PROYECTO: {{PROYECTO}} (name + one line of context: phase, team, working framework)
- LISTA_BLOQUEOS: {{LISTA_BLOQUEOS}} (raw blockages: description, detection date if available, affected team or deliverable, prior management)
- FECHA_HOY: {{FECHA_HOY}} (reference date to calculate aging in days)
- HITOS_PROXIMOS: {{HITOS_PROXIMOS}} (upcoming milestones or deliveries at risk)
- CADENA_ESCALAMIENTO: {{CADENA_ESCALAMIENTO}} (levels and roles, e.g. technical lead > PM > sponsor)

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Phase 1 - Interpret: restate the scope of {{PROYECTO}}, list the blockages detected in {{LISTA_BLOQUEOS}}, and flag missing data (detection dates, milestones, owners, severity criterion). If an essential datum is missing for aging or assignment, ask for it before continuing; do not invent dates, names, or milestones.

Phase 2 - Plan: present the register schema, the severity criterion (impact on the critical path toward {{HITOS_PROXIMOS}}), and the prioritization order before drafting.

Phase 3 - Execute:
1. Normalize each blockage from {{LISTA_BLOQUEOS}} to a row with ID, description in one line, detection date, affected deliverable or milestone, and status (open / in management / escalated / resolved).
2. Calculate aging in days against {{FECHA_HOY}}. Without a detection date, do not calculate aging: tag [ASSUMPTION: date not provided].
3. Assign severity (critical / high / medium / low) justified by impact on the critical path toward {{HITOS_PROXIMOS}}, and classify by a single type: external dependency, pending decision, resource or capacity, technical, budgetary, or governance.
4. Detect chains: if one blockage depends on another, tag it as the root blocker to avoid attacking symptoms.
5. Define an unblocking plan per impediment: concrete next action, single owner (name or role), target date, and the level from {{CADENA_ESCALAMIENTO}} to activate if the target date expires. Flag overdue or ownerless impediments.
