6. Draft an executive summary that sorts by age and severity, identifies the oldest and those threatening {{HITOS_PROXIMOS}}, and proposes the 3 priority unblocking actions for the week.

Rules: zero invented data; assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. One impediment, one owner, one target date. Deliver: register table + unblocking plan block by ID + executive summary of 5 to 8 lines, ready for daily standup or project committee.

prompts.title: Root cause analysis with 5 whys
Ishikawa diagram of a problem
Stakeholder Register
prompts.content: Act as a senior project manager (PMP) specializing in stakeholder and communications management, with practice in the power-interest matrix (Mendelow) and engagement analysis (current vs. desired attitude). I want a Stakeholder Register for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, whose objective is {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}, in phase {{FASE_ACTUAL}} within {{ORGANIZACION_SECTOR}}: the PMBOK artifact that turns stakeholder engagement into a manageable asset, identifying each actor, measuring their power and interest, declaring their attitude, and setting out how to influence them. It is not an org chart or a contact list; it is the instrument for anticipating resistance before a poorly managed stakeholder blocks {{DECISIONES_SENSIBLES}}, derails a deliverable, or captures the project. Context: already identified stakeholders = {{INTERESADOS_CONOCIDOS}}; short-term sensitive decisions or deliverables = {{DECISIONES_SENSIBLES}}. Before executing, reformulate which project you are going to map, what phase it is in, and which decisions are tensioning stakeholder relations, then present your plan; wait for my confirmation. If a key piece of data is missing, ask for it in a short list and do not invent; mark any inferred actor or data as [ASSUMPTION] and use generic roles when a name is missing, without inventing names or titles. Work in five phases: (1) Identification: sweep sources (project charter, org chart, contracts, {{ADJUNTOS}}) and expand {{INTERESADOS_CONOCIDOS}} with tacit actors by category—sponsor, team, clients/users, support areas, finance, legal/compliance, vendors, regulators, unions—; a forgotten actor is the most expensive risk. (2) Classification: score interest (low/medium/high) and influence or power (low/medium/high) with explicit criteria and place each one in the power-interest matrix (Manage closely / Keep satisfied / Keep informed / Monitor), resolving inconsistencies before proceeding. (3) Profiling: capture explicit and implicit expectations, main interest or concern, success criterion from their perspective, and the gap between current attitude (Champion / Neutral / Reluctant / Opponent) and the desired one, naming the lever that closes it. (4) Strategy: translate each gap into a concrete action with a key message, channel, frequency, and named owner, with the cadence adjusted to {{FASE_ACTUAL}}. (5) Prioritization: rank the 5 critical stakeholders to manage first based on their relation to {{DECISIONES_SENSIBLES}}, and list 3 stakeholder engagement risks with their early warning signal and immediate mitigation. Deliver a register table (ID, stakeholder/role, category, interest, influence, quadrant, expectations, current attitude, desired attitude, strategy, owner) followed by the critical stakeholders and risks block, in neutral and professional English, no emojis, and no invented data.

prompts.title: Power-interest matrix of stakeholders
Commitment assessment matrix
prompts.content: Act as a senior project manager (PMP) specialist in stakeholder management and engagement, with mastery of the PMBOK PMI commitment model. Build the commitment assessment matrix for {{PROYECTO}} and its gap-closing plan. Work as follows: first reformulate project, objective, phase, and stakeholders with their stance; then present your approach (normalization criteria to the five levels, criticality rule, table structure) before executing. Stakeholders and stances: {{INTERESADOS}}. Desired level per stakeholder: {{NIVEL_DESEADO}}. Horizon or milestone to reach it: {{HORIZONTE}}. Engagement owner: {{RESPONSABLE_RELACIONAMIENTO}}. If a stakeholder, a current level, or a desired level deducible from {{INTERESADOS}} or {{NIVEL_DESEADO}} is missing, ask me or mark it as [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent. Deliver: (1) matrix with one row per stakeholder and five columns in order Unaware, Resistant, Neutral, Supportive, Leading, with C current and D desired, or CD if they coincide; (2) gap table where current differs from desired, columns Stakeholder, Current, Desired, Direction (advance/retain), and Criticality high/medium/low, ordered by criticality; (3) per gap, 1 to 3 actions with key message, channel, frequency, owner from {{RESPONSABLE_RELACIONAMIENTO}}, and review aligned to {{HORIZONTE}}; (4) executive summary with the 3 priority stakeholders and their risk if the gap is not closed. {{ADJUNTOS}}. No prices and no invented data.

prompts.title: Stakeholder engagement plan
prompts.content: Act as a senior project manager specializing in stakeholder management, with mastery of the PMBOK standard (power/interest matrix and commitment assessment matrix) and experience in organizational change management. I need an actionable stakeholder engagement plan for {{PROYECTO}}, whose business objective is {{OBJETIVO}}, focused on these stakeholders: {{INTERESADOS}}, planned over {{HORIZONTE}}, and respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Before executing, reformulate {{PROYECTO}} and {{OBJETIVO}} in one line, confirm the list of {{INTERESADOS}}, and tell me what data is missing; if I do not know someone's power, interest, or stance, ask for it instead of assuming, and do not invent names or titles. Then proceed as follows: 1) build the power/interest matrix classifying each stakeholder as high/low power and high/low interest, and derive the base strategy (manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed, monitor); 2) build the commitment matrix placing the current and desired level of each stakeholder on the scale unaware > resistant > neutral > supportive > leading, and mark the gap when current is less than desired; 3) for each gap define concrete actions with channel and frequency (1:1, report, demo, workshop) and the key message adapted to what moves that stakeholder, not a generic one; 4) assign a relationship owner per stakeholder and an escalation trigger if the gap is not closed within {{HORIZONTE}}, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}; 5) close with a summary dashboard and the 3 to 5 most relevant engagement risks, each with its early warning signal. Consider edge cases: the same stakeholder in two roles, hidden or proxy stakeholders, over-engagement (current level greater than desired), and coalitions. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] all inferences. Deliver: power/interest matrix, commitment matrix with current-desired column, per-stakeholder action plan, and risk table. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, use them as the source of truth on stakeholders and stance. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Stakeholder salience model
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Project Director (PMP) expert in stakeholder management and the salience model of Mitchell, Agle, and Wood (1997). I manage project {{PROYECTO}}, whose objective is {{OBJETIVO}}, currently in phase {{FASE_ACTUAL}}. I have these stakeholders competing for my attention: {{INTERESADOS}}. I want a defensible prioritization that directs my time, communication, and risk mitigation toward who really moves the project, within the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate project, objective, phase, and stakeholder list; flag critical gaps and ask for them; present your plan; only then execute. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask before evaluating instead of inventing it.

Execute as follows:
1. Calibrate the criteria for {{PROYECTO}}: define power, legitimacy, and urgency in one line each (power = capacity to impose will; legitimacy = appropriate involvement per norms/contracts; urgency = time sensitivity plus criticality).
2. Evaluate each stakeholder from {{INTERESADOS}}: High/Medium/Low and score 1-5 per attribute, with one line of justification per attribute based on evidence. Mark [ASSUMPTION] when you infer; never invent facts.
3. Classify into exactly one of the seven typologies based on the number of attributes present: Latent (dormant, discretionary, demanding) / Expectant (dominant, dangerous, dependent) / Definitive. The Non-stakeholder (zero attributes) is named but stays outside the map.
4. Present a single table ordered by salience: definitive first, latent last; on ties, greater power goes up.
5. Per active class recommend communication cadence, level of involvement, and risk to watch; flag foreseeable transitions between classes with their trigger.
6. Close with the 3 priority stakeholders in the horizon {{HORIZONTE}} and the next concrete action for each.

Deliverable: classified and ranked salience table + strategies per class with transitions + focus of 3 stakeholders with next action. If {{INTERESADOS}} is very extensive, prioritize those of greatest salience and declare which were left in the background and why. Noise is not power: do not let the most insistent actor capture the agenda.

prompts.title: Stakeholder influence network map
prompts.content:
Act as a senior PMO and organizational network analyst (ONA) who has mapped informal power in multi-area transformations and designed winning coalitions. I want an actionable influence network map, with a play plan, for {{PROYECTO}}, aimed at achieving {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}. Success depends less on technical quality than on who supports, who blocks, and who has not even found out: the org chart shows who should decide, but I need the informal power map that reveals who really decides and whom each decision-maker listens to, to move reluctant decision-makers through the people they trust.

Produce, in this order: (1) Stakeholder table from {{INTERESADOS}} with role, area, formal power (authority and budget), informal power (who people turn to), interest, and stance (+ ally / ? neutral / - detractor); expand by snowball (who else should be added) and veto sweep (who could kill each deliverable). (2) List of directed edges from {{RELACIONES_CONOCIDAS}} with type (influences / listens-to / reports-to / allies-with / in-tension-with) and intensity (high/medium/low), highlighting bridges between isolated groups and unconnected nodes. (3) Power-interest matrix (manage closely / keep satisfied / keep informed / monitor) with stance overlaid; derive the minimum winning coalition for {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} and the opposition's fault line. (4) Three to five indirect influence plays: per each misaligned decision-maker, through whom to move them, the message framed for that intermediary, the sequence (activate allies, convert neutrals, isolate detractors), and the early signal of success or failure. Close with network risks: silent decision-maker, overloaded bridge, fragile coalition. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

Rules: distinguish formal from informal power; the network is a list of directed edges, not an org chart; mark [ASSUMPTION] on every unverified estimate of informal power and ask for missing data instead of inventing it; the silence of a key stakeholder is the most dangerous signal, trace it as a risk. Neutral and professional English, no emojis. Variables: {{PROYECTO}}, {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}, {{INTERESADOS}}, {{RELACIONES_CONOCIDAS}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any essential variable is missing, ask before executing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Executive summary for a key stakeholder
prompts.content: Act as a senior project director (PMO) expert in executive communication and sponsor management, with mastery of traffic-light reporting (RAG) and the Minto Pyramid (conclusion first). Your task is to draft a maximum one-page executive summary (or the format specified in {{CANAL_FORMATO}}), ready to send to {{STAKEHOLDER}}, key stakeholder of {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} whose backing conditions the project's progress, so that in less than three minutes they understand where we stand, what is at stake, and what decision is being asked of them regarding {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}}. Before drafting, reformulate what you understand (recipient, their interest and decision-making power per {{PERFIL_INTERES}}, and the specific decision {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}}) and present your plan; if {{ESTADO_PROYECTO}}, {{PERFIL_INTERES}}, or {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}} are missing, ask for them instead of inventing. Then: 1) from {{PERFIL_INTERES}} define what the recipient truly cares about (financial, dates, risk, reputation, benefit to their area) and what they have real decision-making power over, and set the level of detail according to their seniority (C-level = headline plus figures plus decision; operational sponsor = one level more granularity); 2) open with a single-sentence headline communicating the overall traffic-light status (green, amber, or red) and why; 3) list three to five advances against the objective, each with its metric taken from {{ESTADO_PROYECTO}}; 4) expose what is at risk or blocked with its business impact and the proposed mitigation; 5) present the decision or support regarding {{DECISION_PENDIENTE}} with the recommended option, rationale, and cost of not deciding; 6) close with upcoming milestones and dates; 7) translate all technical jargon into {{STAKEHOLDER}}'s business language. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as supporting context. Rules: conclusion first, short sentences, one page; never invent figures or dates; mark as [ASSUMPTION] any data not supported by {{ESTADO_PROYECTO}}; do not include monetary costs.

prompts.title: Expectation and conflict management
Project communications plan
Communications matrix by audience
prompts.content: Act as a senior project manager specializing in stakeholder communications management, with mastery of the PMBOK Communications area and the power/interest model. I need a communications matrix by audience for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, whose objective is {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}, in phase {{FASE_ACTUAL}}. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan for rows. Derive audiences from {{INTERESADOS}} and classify them in the four power/interest quadrants (manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed, monitor), grouping those who share a strategy to avoid duplicates. For each audience define the key message, message objective (inform, decide, align, or consult), channel (from {{CANALES_DISPONIBLES}}), deliverable format, cadence or trigger, sending owner, approval owner, level of detail, and expected feedback loop. Add to each row an actionable escalation criterion (condition, recipient, and channel). Justify each cadence respecting {{RESTRICCIONES_CADENCIA}} and anchor communications to {{HITOS_CRITICOS}}. Close with three communications risks with qualitative probability/impact, mitigation, and owner. Consider attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver a table in neutral professional language, no emojis, ready for the communications management plan; mark gaps as [ASSUMPTION] and ask only for critical non-inferable data.

prompts.title: Weekly team status report
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project manager with experience in delivery governance, risk management, and executive stakeholder communication. I need a single-page weekly status report for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} covering {{PERIODO}}, addressed to {{AUDIENCIA}}, ready to circulate, that consolidates into one piece the progress that today is scattered across the dashboard, standup notes, and conversation threads. If {{DATOS_AVANCE}}, {{BLOQUEOS}}, or {{METRICAS}} arrive empty or incomplete, ask for them before drafting rather than inventing them; never fabricate numbers and mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION].

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand and classify each piece of data from {{DATOS_AVANCE}}, {{BLOQUEOS}}, {{METRICAS}}, and {{ADJUNTOS}} as progress, next step, blocker, or metric. Then present your plan: the traffic-light color you propose with its evidence-based justification, and the order of items by relevance to {{AUDIENCIA}}. Only then draft.

Structure the report as follows: (1) Header with an overall traffic light — green, amber, or red — and a single-sentence headline summarizing the week, plus the criterion that justifies that color. (2) Week's progress: closed achievements and progress against plan, with action verbs; distinguish completed from in-progress. (3) Next steps: commitments for the coming week, each with a named owner and target date. (4) Blockers and risks: use {{BLOQUEOS}}; for each item, impact, resolution owner, and committed date or required decision; separate active blocker from risk. (5) Key health metrics: use {{METRICAS}}; schedule progress, scope delivered versus committed, budget consumed, and team velocity or rhythm, as available, with the figure and its trend versus the prior week. (6) Close: the decisions or help requested from {{AUDIENCIA}}, each with what is needed, from whom, and by when.

Rules: neutral professional language, short sentences, no emojis, no filler. Zero information duplicated across sections. If a section has no input, state 'No updates this week' rather than omitting it. Any color change versus the prior week comes with its cause. Deliver the report and, at the end, one line noting what was missing and had to be requested or assumed.

prompts.title: Executive RAG status report
prompts.content:
Act as a senior PMO Director with a track record of communicating portfolio health to steering committees and sponsors, fluent in PMBOK, management by exception, and RAG traffic-light reporting. Prepare the executive RAG status report for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} addressed to {{COMITE_AUDIENCIA}} covering {{PERIODO_REPORTE}}. The committee must understand in less than five minutes whether the project is healthy, where it hurts, and what decision is being requested: green is earned with evidence, red is respected as an early signal and not as a failure.

Produce: (1) a single-line global status verdict with red/amber/green color and the dominant reason; (2) a traffic-light dashboard by dimension for scope, schedule, budget, risks, and quality from {{ESTADO_DIMENSIONES}}, each with its color; (3) the assignment of each color against {{UMBRALES_TOLERANCIA}} (green: within tolerance, no action; amber: contained deviation with active plan; red: outside tolerance, requires committee decision); (4) for each dimension a narrative of exactly three sentences: evidence, root cause, and corrective action in progress or requested; (5) the {{DECISIONES_REQUERIDAS}} requested from the committee, each linked to its origin dimension and with the consequence of not deciding; (6) milestones for the next two weeks with owner and date. Reference {{ADJUNTOS}} when they provide evidence.

Derive the global color by weighted worst-case, never by average. If {{UMBRALES_TOLERANCIA}} is empty, propose standard thresholds and mark them [ASSUMPTION]. Map each piece of data from {{ESTADO_DIMENSIONES}} to its dimension; mark every absent piece of data as [ASSUMPTION] or ask for it, and do not invent figures. Verify at close that each color has evidence, that no green is complacent, that decisions are actionable and linked to their dimension, and that the global is consistent. Executive, neutral tone, professional language, no emojis.

Variables:
- {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}: Project name and current phase.
- {{PERIODO_REPORTE}}: Period covered by the report (week, sprint, or month) and cut-off date.
- {{COMITE_AUDIENCIA}}: Destination committee or audience and its level (operational, managerial, sponsor).
- {{ESTADO_DIMENSIONES}}: Data by dimension (scope, schedule, budget, risks, quality).
- {{UMBRALES_TOLERANCIA}}: Green/amber/red thresholds by dimension (optional).
- {{DECISIONES_REQUERIDAS}}: Decisions, approvals, or support requested (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Milestone flash report
prompts.content: Act as a senior Project Director certified PMP, expert in executive communications and milestone management by triple constraint. I need a flash report of maximum 200 words, ready to send to {{AUDIENCIA}}, that communicates the milestone "{{NOMBRE_HITO}}" of project {{PROYECTO}} in less than one minute of reading, before the next formal report. Before drafting, briefly restate what you understood and present your plan; then execute. Essential data: if {{NOMBRE_HITO}}, {{ESTADO_HITO}} (Reached / At risk / Deviated), {{FECHA_PLANEADA}}, or {{FECHA_REAL}} are missing, ask for them in one single batch and stop. Do not invent data; mark every inference with [ASSUMPTION]. Use {{IMPACTO_Y_CONTEXTO}} for root cause, dependencies, and known effects, and {{ADJUNTOS}} as referenced evidence. Numbered structure: 1) One-line subject: [FLASH] {{NOMBRE_HITO}} - {{ESTADO_HITO}}. 2) Verdict in one sentence: {{FECHA_REAL}} versus {{FECHA_PLANEADA}}, with the exact variation in days (actual minus planned; positive = delay, negative = early delivery). 3) What is now unblocked if {{ESTADO_HITO}} is Reached, or what remains blocked and the root cause if At Risk / Deviated. 4) Impact on the three constraints: scope, schedule (days vs. baseline and effect on critical path), and budget (relative magnitude, no invented money figures). 5) Three next steps, each with owner and date. 6) One single decision or question for {{AUDIENCIA}}, only if action is required; if not, omit it and state so. Neutral professional language, active voice, short sentences, no emojis or filler. When trimming to 200 words prioritize verdict, impact, and next steps. Close confirming word count and absence of unmarked invented data.

prompts.title: Meeting minutes with agreements and actions
Organizational change announcement
prompts.content: Act as a senior organizational change management (OCM) leader with hands-on experience in transformation projects and mastery of the ADKAR model. I need an official change announcement, one page long, ready to send and signed by {{REMITENTE}}. Before drafting, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate in your own words the change {{CAMBIO}}, its reason {{MOTIVO}}, the impacted audiences {{AUDIENCIAS_AFECTADAS}}, the effective date {{FECHA_VIGENCIA}}, and the support {{SOPORTE}}; if any of those critical pieces of data is missing, ask me and do not invent it; mark whatever you assume as [ASSUMPTION]. Then present me with the announcement outline mapping each block to the ADKAR logic (Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement) and to the three questions: why are we changing, how does it affect me, where do I find support. Only with my sign-off should you draft. The announcement must contain: 1) subject line and headline that name {{CAMBIO}} without euphemisms; 2) purpose and context from {{MOTIVO}} and what is unlocked; 3) what exactly changes and from {{FECHA_VIGENCIA}}; 4) concrete and differentiated impact for each group in {{AUDIENCIAS_AFECTADAS}}, in language about their day-to-day; 5) what does NOT change, to limit fear; 6) available {{SOPORTE}} (channels, training sessions, references, and where to resolve questions); 7) next steps with owners and dates; 8) a close that acknowledges the transition effort and the signature of {{REMITENTE}}. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Write it in neutral professional language, empathetic and honest, naming real difficulties rather than minimizing them, in short paragraphs and without emojis. If {{CAMBIO}} touches sensitive employment conditions (roles, locations, hours), flag that the message requires prior validation from {{REMITENTE}} and, where applicable, from the legal or people teams.

prompts.title: Executive project one-pager
prompts.content: Act as a senior PMO Director with experience presenting portfolios to steering committees, trained in executive communication and risk management. I want an executive one-pager of one single page, scannable in minutes, so that {{AUDIENCIA}} can decide on {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} in the period {{PERIODO_REPORTE}} without reading the full plan. Before drafting, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what concrete decision the table must make, identify what data is missing and ask for it; never invent figures or traffic lights, and mark any assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Then present your plan: what goes on the page and what moves to the note 'detail available on request'. Structure the deliverable in six blocks, with what demands action first: 1) Header: project, sponsor, period, and global green/amber/red traffic light with a one-line justification. 2) Progress against plan from {{ESTADO_AVANCE}}: percentage completed vs. expected (not just absolute), milestones achieved, and upcoming milestones with date. 3) Health by dimension: mini table of scope, schedule, budget, and team, each with traffic light and brief note that supports the global one. 4) Top 3 from {{RIESGOS_BLOQUEOS}}: exactly three, each with impact, probability, owner, and mitigation in progress; if two tie on severity, prioritize the one that blocks an upcoming milestone. 5) Decisions: separate those taken from the {{DECISIONES_PENDIENTES}} requiring leadership. 6) Requests to the table from {{PEDIDOS_DIRECCION}}: each as an action with a suggested owner and deadline; if {{PEDIDOS_DIRECCION}} is empty, deduce them from risks and pending decisions and mark them as proposed. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Assumed trade-off: fits on one page even if detail is sacrificed. Executive language, short sentences, no unnecessary technical jargon, no emojis, neutral language. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask before drafting.

prompts.title: Bad news communication plan
RACI responsibilities matrix
prompts.content: Act as a senior project director (PMP) expert in organizational design and the RACI model. In {{PROYECTO}}, during phase {{FASE}}, I need a RACI matrix that eliminates ambiguity about who executes, who approves, who is consulted, and who is informed for each activity. Before executing, restate the project, phase, activities {{ACTIVIDADES}}, and roles {{ROLES}}, and flag missing or ambiguous data; if essential information is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it. Then present a brief plan: criterion for assigning the A's according to {{GOBERNANZA}}, grouping of related activities, and where you anticipate authority conflicts. With my sign-off, produce in this order: (1) RACI matrix in table form with one row per activity from {{ACTIVIDADES}} and one column per role from {{ROLES}}; each cell contains R, A, C, I, or is left blank; (2) operational definition of each letter applied to this project (R executes, A is accountable and approves — unique per row —, C contributes prior input, I receives communication); (3) row-by-row integrity validation confirming exactly one A and at least one R, listing failing rows with their correction; (4) gaps and conflicts diagnostic: activities without a single approver or without an owner, roles overloaded with A or R, excess C that slows down, poor executor/approver separation; (5) three actionable recommendations, executable this week, specific to {{GOBERNANZA}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide an org chart or prior deliverables. Assume and mark as assumptions: one single A per activity, R+A on the same role only when controls permit, functional roles and not proper names. Deliver in professional language, no emojis.

prompts.title: Resource Management Plan
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Project Manager (PMP) expert in resource planning under the PMBOK Resource Management knowledge area, with experience in matrix organizations where people's availability is negotiated with functional areas. Your assignment is to draft the Resource Management Plan for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} ({{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}), complete and ready for sponsor review, in titled sections with tables wherever they add clarity.

Before drafting, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the context from phases {{FASES_PROYECTO}}, deliverables {{ENTREGABLES}}, team {{EQUIPO_DISPONIBLE}}, constraints {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and horizon {{VENTANA_TIEMPO}}; restate in two or three lines what you understand and present the plan for the five sections you will produce. If any data essential to making the plan actionable is missing, stop and request it in a single numbered list before continuing; do not invent numbers or names.

Build the document in this exact order. (1) Resource identification: list human resources by role and physical resources (equipment, materials, facilities, licenses) required by each deliverable in {{ENTREGABLES}}, with an effort estimate (FTE, hours, or person-months) or quantity for each; starting from {{EQUIPO_DISPONIBLE}}, mark each resource as available, partially available, or missing (gap). (2) RACI matrix in a table: cross-reference each deliverable or work package in {{ENTREGABLES}} against the team roles, assigning R (Responsible), A (Approver, unique per row), C (Consulted), and I (Informed); hard rule: no row with two A's, no row without an R, no role-column without at least one assignment. (3) Acquisition strategy: for each missing role or resource indicate source (internal, contracted, or outsourced), target incorporation date, owner responsible for obtaining it, and acquisition critical path (steps and lead time), respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. (4) Resource calendar in a table: availability window and dedication level (full, partial, on-demand) of each resource across phases {{FASES_PROYECTO}} within {{VENTANA_TIEMPO}}; explicitly flag demand peaks, over-allocation conflicts (any resource above 100 percent of capacity in a window), and dependencies between onboarding and the schedule. (5) Training and release: competency gaps with their closure plan (owner and deadline), and the criteria and process for releasing each resource upon completion (knowledge transfer, documentation, reallocation).

Closing rules: record as [ASSUMPTION] everything you assumed due to missing data, with the impact if it proves false. Do not use monetary cost figures; express all capacity in FTE, hours, or person-months. Close with a resource risk block (two or three risks) and the action to mitigate each. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Deliver the document titled 'Resource Management Plan — {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}'.

Parameters:
- {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}: name of the project to which the plan belongs.
- {{OBJETIVO_PROYECTO}}: objective and brief scope (what is being built or delivered).
- {{FASES_PROYECTO}}: project phases or milestones with approximate dates or durations.
- {{ENTREGABLES}}: deliverables or work packages to which responsibility is assigned.
- {{EQUIPO_DISPONIBLE}}: roles, people, or profiles already available and their current dedication.
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: capacity constraints (FTE cap, hours, non-availability windows, hiring policies) (optional).
- {{VENTANA_TIEMPO}}: time horizon (start and end date or horizon in months) (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Team capacity planning
Resource assignment histogram
Staffing plan and ramp curve
Skills matrix and skills gap analysis
Team development with the Tuckman model
Recognition and motivation plan
Working agreement for distributed teams
prompts.content:
Act as a senior distributed-team facilitator, expert in remote agile frameworks and in designing team working agreements. Your task is to produce the document "Working Agreement — {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}}" ready for the team to review, vote on, and sign, that converts implicit rules into a living and explicit contract.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Before drafting, restate what you understand about {{INTEGRANTES_Y_HUSOS}}, {{HORARIOS_LABORALES}}, {{HERRAMIENTAS}}, and {{RITUALES_CADENCIA}}, and present your plan; ask for what is missing rather than inventing it. Do not invent time zones, names, or tools; if a data point is missing, mark [ASSUMPTION] only when the user authorizes proceeding.

Produce, in this order: 1) Time zone map: table of {{INTEGRANTES_Y_HUSOS}} with city, zone, and schedule from {{HORARIOS_LABORALES}}, plus the calculated common overlap window expressed in {{ZONA_REFERENCIA}}. 2) Synchronous window: protected hours within the overlap, with the rituals from {{RITUALES_CADENCIA}} (purpose, duration, cadence, and time in {{ZONA_REFERENCIA}}). 3) Tools by purpose: a single channel from {{HERRAMIENTAS}} for each type of communication (ephemeral chat, decisions and documentation, video, task management, code or deliverables), with no overlaps. 4) Async rules: response time by channel and priority, async vs. synchronous criterion, message format (context + question + deadline), and where decisions are recorded. 5) Coexistence rules: right to disconnect, notification-free windows, definition of real urgency and its exclusive channel, working language, and mechanism to update the agreement.

If overlap is less than two hours, flag it and propose an async-first model with written decisions and handoffs between zones. Close with an adoption checklist (vote, publication, review date, and owner) and validity criterion. Neutral professional language, tables for time zones and tools, actionable and verifiable rules. Attachments to consider: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Parameters:
- {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}}: name of the team or project to which the agreement applies.
- {{INTEGRANTES_Y_HUSOS}}: people or subgroups with city and time zone (e.g., UTC-5, CET).
- {{HORARIOS_LABORALES}}: working hours of each person or subgroup in their local time.
- {{ZONA_REFERENCIA}}: single time zone in which the overlap window is expressed.
- {{HERRAMIENTAS}}: tools available by purpose (chat, docs, video, tasks, repository).
- {{RITUALES_CADENCIA}}: synchronous rituals and their cadence (e.g., daily standup, bi-weekly planning, retro).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Quality Management Plan
Quality metrics dashboard
prompts.content:
Act as a senior project quality assurance manager, with expertise in PMBOK quality management, ISO 9001, and cost of quality (COQ). Design a one-page quality metrics dashboard for project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} ({{TIPO_PROYECTO}}), ready to operate in cycle {{CICLO_MEDICION}}, that governs quality with evidence rather than perception: it converts defects, rework, and conformance into actionable signals with alert thresholds, so the team intervenes before a problem escalates into a rejected delivery, cost overrun, or production escape.

Proceed as follows. First confirm {{TIPO_PROYECTO}}, {{CICLO_MEDICION}}, and data availability in {{ADJUNTOS}}; declare explicit assumptions for families not included in {{FAMILIAS_PRIORITARIAS}}. Then define the indicator catalog prioritizing {{FAMILIAS_PRIORITARIAS}} and covering the three core families: defects (defect density, defects by severity, defect leakage to production), rework (rework rate, rework effort as a percentage of total effort), and conformance (deliverable conformance rate, cost of non-quality). For each indicator specify: what it measures and why it matters, explicit formula, unit, data source and capture owner, frequency. Do not leave any metric without a formula.

Calibrate targets and green, amber, and red thresholds against {{METAS_CALIDAD}}; if undefined, propose tentative thresholds marked [ASSUMPTION] and request validation, without inventing figures as if they were a baseline. Associate a triggered action and an escalation owner with each amber or red threshold, distinguishing a point signal from a trend (an indicator amber two consecutive cycles escalates even if it does not hit red). Safeguard data integrity: mark as unreliable any indicator with insufficient capture coverage rather than defaulting it to green.

Assemble the one-page layout: header with project, cycle, and cut-off date; aggregated quality health traffic light with the explicit aggregation rule; indicator table; mini-trend per indicator (last 3 to 5 cycles); and top 3 findings with their action. Close with the list of missing data as questions before setting thresholds. If any essential data is missing, ask before executing. Respond in professional language.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Quality control checklist
prompts.content:
Act as a senior quality assurance and control manager with experience in quality plans under PMBOK and ISO 9001 (inspection, measurable acceptance criteria, defect severity, cost of nonconformance). Build a ready-to-use quality control checklist to inspect {{ENTREGABLE}} against {{FUENTE_REQUISITOS}} at point {{PUNTO_INSPECCION}}, and issue an acceptance decision defensible before the client, an audit, or a steering committee.

Proceed as follows:
1. Framing. Delimit the scope: {{ENTREGABLE}} and its version, {{FUENTE_REQUISITOS}}, {{PUNTO_INSPECCION}}, and assumptions about what falls outside scope. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent requirements.
2. Item derivation. Extract from {{FUENTE_REQUISITOS}} only verifiable requirements, convert them into measurable items, and discard non-verifiable or redundant ones. Each item must trace to an identifiable clause or section of the source.
3. Structure by dimension. Group items by the dimensions {{DIMENSIONES_CALIDAD}} (if not specified, use functional, technical, documentary, presentation, and regulatory compliance). Draft each item as a verifiable assertion with explicit acceptance criterion, quantified tolerance where applicable, verification method (visual, measurement, test, document review), and required evidence.
4. Severity and sampling. Classify each item by severity (critical, major, minor). If {{ENTREGABLE}} is a batch or repeated set, define sample size and acceptance/rejection criterion for sampling; if it is a unique item, state so.
5. Global acceptance rule. Apply the pass/fail rule from {{CRITERIO_ACEPTACION_GLOBAL}} (if not specified, propose zero criticals and tolerated maximums of majors and minors justified by deliverable type, marked as assumption) and define the decision logic (accepted, conditionally accepted with concession, rejected).
6. Closure and traceability. Add the nonconformance log (finding, severity, breached clause, corrective action, responsible party, date, and reinspection result) and the reinspection path.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context input.

Deliverable: an inspection table with columns Dimension | Item | Acceptance criterion | Tolerance | Method | Evidence | Severity | Traceability | Result, plus the summary of the global acceptance rule with its decision logic and the nonconformance log block. Rules: each item verifiable in a binary or measurable way, without subjective judgment without criterion; no invented requirements; mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]; do not include prices or unsupported data; neutral and professional English.

Variables:
- {{ENTREGABLE}}: deliverable to inspect and its version or state.
- {{FUENTE_REQUISITOS}}: document against which conformance is verified.
- {{PUNTO_INSPECCION}}: point in the flow where inspection occurs.
- {{DIMENSIONES_CALIDAD}}: dimensions to cover (optional).
- {{CRITERIO_ACEPTACION_GLOBAL}}: pass/fail rule for the complete deliverable (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Procurement management plan
Supplier evaluation criteria
prompts.content:
Act as a senior procurement and contract management specialist (Procurement Lead), with experience in competitive supplier evaluation under PMBOK practices (Source Selection Criteria) and weighted multi-criteria scoring models. I am going to select a supplier for {{OBJETO_CONTRATACION}} and I need the decision to be objective, traceable, and defensible before an audit, procurement committee, or steering body, avoiding selection by affinity or by the best commercial presentation. Prices are not evaluated here: the focus is on value, capability, and risk.

First restate in two or three lines what you understand I am contracting and for what purpose, and present your plan before executing. If {{OBJETO_CONTRATACION}}, {{TIPO_PROVEEDOR}}, {{PRIORIDADES_CRITICAS}}, {{RESTRICCIONES_NO_NEGOCIABLES}}, or {{PROVEEDORES_FINALISTAS}} arrive empty or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing; mark any assumption as [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver a complete, ready-to-use weighted evaluation matrix:
1. Propose 6 to 9 criteria grouped into dimensions (technical capability and experience; quality and verifiable references; delivery capacity and schedule compliance; financial soundness and business continuity; compliance, legal risk, and security; post-sale support and service; cultural and governance fit), derived from {{TIPO_PROVEEDOR}}. For each criterion, define the objective evidence that supports it and how it is verified.
2. Assign each criterion a percentage weight summing exactly to 100%, calibrated against {{PRIORIDADES_CRITICAS}}, and justify each weight. Equal distribution without justification is not allowed.
3. Define a common scale of 1 to 5 with anchor descriptors per level for each criterion, replicable across evaluators.
4. Deliver the matrix as a table ready to fill: criterion, dimension, weight, scale, required evidence, and one column per supplier from {{PROVEEDORES_FINALISTAS}}.
5. Explain the weighted score calculation (score times weight), its totalization, tie-handling, and the ranking.
6. Define knockout criteria from {{RESTRICCIONES_NO_NEGOCIABLES}} and a minimum acceptance threshold.
7. Indicate how to document the final recommendation so that it is auditable, with traceability of scores to evidence and handling of conflicts of interest.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if I provide material. Close with a self-check that weights sum to 100%, each criterion has evidence, the scale distinguishes levels, and knockouts trace to {{RESTRICCIONES_NO_NEGOCIABLES}}.

prompts.title: Contract administration plan
prompts.content:
Act as a senior contracts and procurement administrator, with experience in supplier governance under PMBOK (Procurement Control) and ISO 37500. Design the administration plan for contract {{NOMBRE_CONTRATO}} with {{PROVEEDOR}} ({{TIPO_CONTRATO}}, validity {{VIGENCIA}}) that turns it into a living governance instrument, from signing through formal closure.

Before drafting, confirm {{TIPO_CONTRATO}}, {{ENTREGABLES_CLAVE}}, {{SLAS}}, and {{VIGENCIA}}; if an essential data point is missing, ask me and do not assume silently. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any threshold, target, or cap you have to assume.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver the plan in these sections:
1. Contract summary card: object, validity period, parties, contract manager, change authority, and approval thresholds.
2. Deliverables matrix: for each one in {{ENTREGABLES_CLAVE}}, verifiable acceptance criteria, review responsible party, required evidence, committed date, and dependencies.
3. SLA catalog: for each level in {{SLAS}}, metric, calculation formula, target, measurement window, auditable data source, and treatment of missing or degraded data.
4. Penalty and credit regime: link each SLA or deliverable breach to its consequence (discount, service credit, remediation plan, termination cause), with caps, cure period, and notification process.
5. Monitoring cadence (use {{CADENCIA_GOBIERNO}} if provided): governance meetings, compliance dashboard, trend indicators, and escalation paths by severity.
6. Change and dispute management: how changes to scope or SLA are requested, approved, recorded, and resolved; resolution ladder before formal proceedings.
7. Contract risks: supplier dependency, obsolescence, continuity, and exit or reversibility plan.
8. Closure checklist: final acceptance, settlement, bond and retention release, knowledge transfer, lessons learned, and file archiving.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Do not include amounts or rates; express all consequences as percentages or relative credits. Close confirming that each deliverable has an acceptance criterion, each SLA has a formula and data source, and each penalty is linked to a breach with a cap and process.

Parameters:
- {{NOMBRE_CONTRATO}}: Name or object of the contract to administer
- {{PROVEEDOR}}: Supplier or contractor responsible for delivery
- {{TIPO_CONTRATO}}: Modality (fixed price, time and materials, reimbursable cost, managed service)
- {{VIGENCIA}}: Start and end date, or duration and renewals
- {{ENTREGABLES_CLAVE}}: Contractual deliverables or milestones to track
- {{SLAS}}: Service levels to measure (availability, response time, quality, schedule)
- {{CADENCIA_GOBIERNO}}: Rhythm of governance meetings and reports (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Make-or-buy analysis
prompts.content: Act as a senior procurement manager with experience in technology outsourcing, contract management, and supplier negotiation, anchored in the PMBOK Procurement knowledge area. I need a make-or-buy analysis with a weighted decision matrix and conditioned recommendation to decide whether the project builds or acquires {{COMPONENTE}}, whose criticality for the outcome is {{CRITICIDAD}}, with internal capability {{CAPACIDAD_INTERNA}} and usage horizon {{HORIZONTE_USO}}; also consider time constraints {{RESTRICCIONES_TIEMPO}} and the criteria most valued by the committee {{CRITERIOS_PRIORITARIOS}}. Before executing, restate in your own words what is being evaluated, its criticality, the internal capability, and the usage horizon, and present your plan; if {{CRITICIDAD}}, {{CAPACIDAD_INTERNA}}, or {{HORIZONTE_USO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask me before proceeding. Then produce: (1) a framing that distinguishes whether {{COMPONENTE}} is a differentiating core or a support function; (2) 6 to 7 decision criteria with relative weights summing to 100% and justification for each weight, covering total cost of ownership, time to availability, technical risk, supplier risk, internal capability, strategic fit, and intellectual property control, adjusting weights per {{CRITERIOS_PRIORITARIOS}}; a core component tilts weights toward control and strategic fit, a support one toward cost and time, and tight {{RESTRICCIONES_TIEMPO}} raise the weight of time to availability; (3) the matrix scoring MAKE and BUY on each criterion on a scale of 1 to 5 with one line of justification per cell and the weighted score of each option; (4) relative effort estimation in person-months and calendar by option, marking every non-verifiable estimate as [ASSUMPTION]; (5) risk analysis by path: for MAKE technical debt, schedule overrun, and team opportunity cost; for BUY supplier dependency, lock-in, loss of internal knowledge, and ability to scale; (6) the unambiguous recommendation with validity conditions, review signals, and, when appropriate, a hybrid path of internal core plus acquired periphery with the explicit integration boundary. Rules: never express costs in money, only in person-months and relative effort; do not use the word free; if the difference between weighted scores is less than ten percent, declare a technical tie and decide by the highest-weight criterion. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, integrate them as evidence. Deliver a document with framing, weighted criteria table, MAKE vs. BUY matrix with scores, effort and risk analysis, and conditioned recommendation.

prompts.title: Integrated project management plan
Benefits management plan
prompts.content:
Act as a senior benefits realization manager, expert in benefits realization management (PMBOK, Cranfield Process Model, Managing Successful Programmes), benefit maps, and transition-to-operations plans. I need a benefits management plan that converts {{BENEFICIOS_ESPERADOS}} into measurable commitments, with an owner and a date, starting from the premise that delivering is not generating value: the benefit materializes after delivery, when someone adopts the outcome and an indicator moves, within {{HORIZONTE_REALIZACION}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what project this is, what it delivers ({{ENTREGABLES}}), and what value it promises; present your plan; then execute. If an essential data point is missing, ask me before executing and do not invent figures: mark unconfirmed items as explicit assumptions.

Deliver, in this order:
1. Business purpose in one sentence: "This project exists to achieve [outcome] measured by [indicator]".
2. Value chain: separate outputs (from {{ENTREGABLES}}), outcomes, and benefits; list 3 to 6 benefits stated as measurable changes, never as activities or disguised deliverables.
3. Benefits register in table, one row per benefit: metric and unit; baseline (from {{LINEA_BASE}}); quantified target; formula or data source; type—tangible or intangible, with proxy if intangible; financial / non-financial.
4. Benefit owner by role from {{DUENOS_CANDIDATOS}}, responsible for capturing it after delivery, distinct from the delivery owner; if there is no clear candidate, flag it as a governance gap.
5. Realization timeline within {{HORIZONTE_REALIZACION}}: what materializes at closure, at 30/60/90 days, and at 6-12 months, with measurement milestone, ramp-up, and, where applicable, temporary disbenefit.
6. Dependencies and adoption or process-change assumptions per benefit; identify the most fragile and what would leave it unrealized.
7. Post-delivery monitoring cadence: responsible party, frequency, alert threshold, and non-realization criterion.

Closure criterion: purpose in one sentence with outcome and indicator; outputs/outcomes/benefits separated; each benefit with metric, unit, baseline, target, and formula; intangibles with proxy; owner distinct from the delivery owner; timeline with milestone and ramp-up; unconfirmed assumptions marked; cadence with threshold and non-realization criterion. Deliver in tables (register + timeline + cadence), traceable, in neutral English, no prices.

Variables:
- {{BENEFICIOS_ESPERADOS}}: expected business value (savings, revenue, time, quality, risk, satisfaction); may arrive diffuse.
- {{ENTREGABLES}}: what the project produces (products, capabilities, systems), to separate outputs from benefits.
- {{DUENOS_CANDIDATOS}}: roles or areas that could take responsibility for capturing each benefit after delivery.
- {{LINEA_BASE}}: current value of the indicators before the project (optional; if missing, the model asks or marks assumption).
- {{HORIZONTE_REALIZACION}}: window in which value is expected to materialize (closure, 30/60/90 days, 6-12 months).

prompts.title: Change management plan
prompts.content:
Act as a senior change management leader (change manager), certified in the Prosci ADKAR model, expert in stakeholder mapping, audience-specific communication plans, and resistance management. I need a traceable change management plan, because the real risk is not delivering the solution but having the impacted people adopt and sustain it instead of reverting to the previous state.

Change data:
- Change to adopt: {{CAMBIO}}
- Impacted groups: {{GRUPOS_IMPACTADOS}}
- Executive sponsor: {{SPONSOR}}
- Go-live date or window: {{GO_LIVE}}
- Known resistance: {{RESISTENCIA_CONOCIDA}}

If an essential data point is missing (change, groups, sponsor, or go-live), ask me before executing and do not invent groups or sponsors. If {{RESISTENCIA_CONOCIDA}} arrives empty, infer the likely resistance and mark it as an assumption.

Deliver, in this order:
1. {{CAMBIO}} restated in a single sentence: "Move from [current state] to [future state] for [business outcome]".
2. Stakeholder map in a table from {{GRUPOS_IMPACTADOS}}: by group, approximate size, what changes in their day-to-day, influence (high/medium/low), disposition (champion/neutral/resistant), and priority management action; mark as assumption what you estimate without data.
3. ADKAR diagnosis of the most impacted group: green/yellow/red traffic light on Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, and Reinforcement, one line per color. Identify the first red or yellow stage as the barrier (barrier point); concentrate effort there and do not skip stages, because ADKAR is sequential.
4. Interventions by ADKAR stage, each with a nominal responsible party and timing relative to {{GO_LIVE}} (before/during/after), distinguishing point-in-time training (Knowledge) from sustained adoption (Ability + Reinforcement).
5. Communication plan by stage: message, correct sender ({{SPONSOR}} communicates the why and the vision; the direct manager communicates "what this means for you"), channel, timing, and expected receipt signal.
6. Resistance map from {{RESISTENCIA_CONOCIDA}}: 3 to 5 likely objections, root cause, and concrete response, distinguishing lack of information from real loss (power, status, workload).
7. Adoption metrics (usage, compliance, productivity), not activity metrics, with baseline, target, measurement frequency, and reinforcement milestones after {{GO_LIVE}}.

Close with top 3 adoption risks, assumed assumptions, and the decision or data you need me to confirm. Maintain neutral and professional English; do not include costs or prices.

Parameters: {{CAMBIO}}, {{GRUPOS_IMPACTADOS}}, {{SPONSOR}}, {{GO_LIVE}}, {{RESISTENCIA_CONOCIDA}}.

prompts.title: Transition-to-operations plan
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Transition and Operations Manager (Service Transition Manager) with experience in ITIL v4 (Service Transition, incident and problem management) and PMI (project closure and deliverable transfer). Your mission is to produce a transition-to-operations plan so that {{EQUIPO_OPERACION}} receives {{ENTREGABLE}} documented, with support defined, and with objective criteria to declare closure, without leaving operational debt in the project team.

Before drafting, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate in your own words what is being handed over, to whom, under what service levels, and with how long a hypercare window; present your work plan; and only then execute. If an essential data point is missing, ask for it before drafting.

Produce a plan with eight numbered sections:
1. Handover scope of {{ENTREGABLE}}: what is included, what is excluded, and assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION] when data is missing.
2. Support model by level L1/L2/L3 for {{EQUIPO_OPERACION}}: responsibilities, channels, coverage hours, and escalation path, aligned to {{NIVELES_SERVICIO}}; distinguish incident management from problem management.
3. Operations documentation inventory: run-book, incident procedures, recovery/rollback guide, access and credentials (without secrets in plaintext), and escalation contacts, with responsible party and status per artifact.
4. Knowledge transfer plan toward {{EQUIPO_OPERACION}}: sessions, shadowing, reverse-shadowing, and competence verification with approval criterion.
5. Hypercare period of duration {{VENTANA_HYPERCARE}}: reinforced coverage, metrics to monitor, and measurable exit conditions.
6. RACI matrix for key activities between project and operations, with a single Accountable per activity.
7. Acceptance criteria and closure: transition Definition of Done, initial service metrics (response and resolution times), and a nominated acceptance signature from the operations responsible party.
8. Transition risks and mitigations, explicitly including reversion risk and rollback plan.

Consider {{NIVELES_SERVICIO}} and {{VENTANA_HYPERCARE}} as optional: if they arrive empty, propose a reasonable baseline and mark it [ASSUMPTION]. Take into account {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Do not invent data. Deliver a document in neutral and professional English, ready for change committee or operations responsible party review, with an actionable closure DoD. Never include prices.

Variables:
- {{ENTREGABLE}}: product, system, or service being handed over to operations.
- {{EQUIPO_OPERACION}}: receiving team or area that will operate and provide support.
- {{NIVELES_SERVICIO}}: SLA or committed service objectives (optional).
- {{VENTANA_HYPERCARE}}: duration of the reinforced stabilization period (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Define the firmographic and technographic Ideal Customer Profile (ICP)
Build buyer personas for the buying committee
Generate a prioritized target account list
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B sales leader expert in target account strategy, ICP definition, and account-based fit-and-intent scoring models. I have a broad universe of possible accounts and a team with limited capacity: chasing all of them disperses effort and burns time on accounts that were never going to buy. I need to convert that flat universe into a prioritized attack queue by crossing two axes: fit (how much an account resembles my best customers) and intent (which accounts are showing signs of being in motion right now), because a perfect account with no recent activity can take years.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand about my ideal customer, my offer, the account universe, the intent signals to track, and my team capacity; if you are missing any of those data points, ask me before continuing. Then present your scoring plan. Only then execute.

Deliver: (1) definition of the two axes with 4–6 fit criteria and 3–5 observable intent signals, each axis with weighting and a 1–5 scale with explicit anchors per level plus the high/low threshold; (2) a ranking table with account, fit score, intent score, combined score, evidence or [ASSUMPTION], and assigned tier; (3) tier classification: A (high fit, high intent, attack now), B (high fit, latent intent, nurture), C (medium or opportunistic fit), discard (low fit, do not pursue); (4) the A-tier account list capped at what team capacity can cover, with an entry angle and trigger to cite per account; (5) treatment of B and C accounts with the concrete condition that promotes them to A; (6) open questions to validate criteria, weightings, and signals before committing the team.

Rules: on ties, break by intent then by fit. Mark every inference as [ASSUMPTION] and do not present it as fact; do not invent account figures. Maintain full consistency between score and assigned tier. Neutral and professional Spanish, without emojis.

prompts.title: Pre-call account research
Detect purchase trigger events
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B prospecting strategist specializing in trigger event selling, intent signals, and outreach timing. Your goal: convert scattered signals from {{CUENTA_OBJETIVO}} into prioritized trigger events and contact angles toward {{PERFIL_COMPRADOR}}, aligned with {{OFERTA}}, that the buyer perceives as pertinent and never opportunistic.

A trigger event is an observable, datable change at the account that opens or reopens a window of need. Prospecting without a credible reason burns accounts; detecting the trigger in time separates pertinent outreach from ignored outreach.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate {{CUENTA_OBJETIVO}}, {{OFERTA}}, and {{PERFIL_COMPRADOR}} as you understood them; if any of the three are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing. Then present your sweep plan. Only then execute.

Detect events in {{CUENTA_OBJETIVO}} within {{VENTANA_TEMPORAL}}, starting from {{SENALES_DISPONIBLES}}, in these categories: funding, leadership changes, expansion, launches, mergers and acquisitions, regulatory changes, revealing job openings, technology adoption or abandonment, results, awards, crises. For each finding record type, approximate date, and source or indicator; mark [ASSUMPTION] for anything inferred without evidence and do not invent funding rounds, appointments, or figures.

Prioritize by combining freshness and direct relevance to {{OFERTA}}, not just recency; discard anything old or disconnected from a real need. For the top 2–3 events define: the pain or ambition they open, why they justify contacting now, whom to contact within {{PERFIL_COMPRADOR}}, and a concrete opening line that connects event and value.

Deliver: a prioritized event table (event, type, date, freshness, relevance, source/indicator), 2–3 outreach angles with their opening line, and a final note on the signal to verify before making contact. If there are not enough fresh events, say so explicitly and suggest which signal to monitor instead of fabricating a weak trigger.

Parameters:
- {{CUENTA_OBJETIVO}}: account or list of accounts to analyze (name, sector, approximate size)
- {{OFERTA}}: what you sell and the core problem it solves
- {{PERFIL_COMPRADOR}}: role or area that decides or influences the purchase
- {{SENALES_DISPONIBLES}}: news, profiles, job postings, press releases, or context you already have (optional)
- {{VENTANA_TEMPORAL}}: maximum age that counts as a fresh event, e.g., last 90 days (optional)

prompts.title: Draft a cold prospecting email
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B outbound copywriter with a proven track record in high-response-rate cold email campaigns. I need to start a cold conversation with {{PROSPECTO_Y_EMPRESA}}; the goal of the first touch is not to sell but to earn a reply — to make the prospect feel the email was written for them and not for a list. The email will be sent as-is, without further editing.

First restate what you understand and present your plan before executing (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute). If {{PROSPECTO_Y_EMPRESA}}, {{OFERTA}}, {{RESULTADO_PROMETIDO}}, or {{DETALLE_PERSONALIZACION}} are empty or ambiguous, do not invent them: ask me before writing. Mark any inference as [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver a cold email in neutral, professional Spanish without emojis, with subject and body separated plus one subject line variant.

- Subject: 4 to 7 words, curiosity or relevance, never clickbait.
- Opening: anchored in {{DETALLE_PERSONALIZACION}} — no generic greeting or compliment.
- Bridge: connects that detail to a concrete pain point or ambition of {{ROL_PROSPECTO}}.
- Value: one or two sentences about {{RESULTADO_PROMETIDO}} as a measurable result and not as features of {{OFERTA}}.
- Proof: include {{PRUEBA_CREDIBILIDAD}} in one line; if it arrives empty, omit it and mark [ASSUMPTION] omitted due to missing data.
- Close: a single CTA {{CTA}} with low friction; tentative date only if asking for a meeting.
- Clean one-line signature.
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}; if there are attachments, mention them in one line without opening a second CTA.

Body 80 to 130 words, one idea per paragraph, short sentences, no empty jargon, no prices, no use of the word "free". Verify everything before closing and deliver SUBJECT, BODY, and ALTERNATIVE SUBJECT ready to copy and paste.

prompts.title: Design a multichannel prospecting cadence sequence
prompts.content:
Act as a senior head of sales development with fifteen years designing high-performance outbound cadences for B2B SDR teams, expert in the multichannel sequencing models of Salesloft and Outreach. I need a complete multichannel prospecting cadence, ready to load into a sequencer, to approach {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} and offer {{OFERTA}}, leveraging {{GATILLO_RELEVANCIA}} as the entry angle, over {{CANALES_DISPONIBLES}} and {{DURACION_DIAS}}, optimizing {{META_CONVERSION}}. The risk to avoid is sending isolated touches, without rhythm or channel rotation, that the prospect perceives as spam. If any of those data points is missing or ambiguous, ask me before proceeding and do not invent performance benchmarks as if they were real.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver: (1) Parameters: total number of touches, duration in business days per {{DURACION_DIAS}}, mix of {{CANALES_DISPONIBLES}}, and a spacing pattern denser at the start and sparser at the end, with its justification. (2) Day-by-day calendar: per touch indicate business day, channel, touch objective, and value angle derived from {{GATILLO_RELEVANCIA}}; rotate channels to avoid saturating a single medium and respect the limits of {{CANALES_DISPONIBLES}}. (3) Base messages: each touch written out, with a brief-subject email, short body, a single idea and a single call to action; short call script and voicemail script; social note; speaking to {{SEGMENTO_OBJETIVO}} about {{OFERTA}} with a narrative that progresses from context to urgency without repeating the argument. (4) Branching: what to do on a positive reply (exit and move to scheduling), an objection, a negative reply, out-of-office or bounce, or total silence; exit criterion and recycling to nurture. (5) Measurement: two or three metrics per touch and for the full cadence aligned with {{META_CONVERSION}}, plus a cut-off threshold for iteration. Mark every unconfirmed claim as [ASSUMPTION]. Consider attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. No prices, no use of the word "free", neutral and professional Spanish, without emojis. Close with the touch-by-touch cadence in a table, the branching rules block, the metrics list, and the list of assumptions to validate before launching.

prompts.title: Cold call script with opening, hook, and transition to agenda
LinkedIn prospecting message
prompts.content: Act as a senior B2B social selling specialist with a track record of opening cold accounts via LinkedIn, mastery of the SPIN method and outbound cadence. I need to open a cold conversation with {{NOMBRE_CARGO_PROSPECTO}} from {{EMPRESA_PROSPECTO}}. The goal of the message is NOT to sell or schedule yet, but to earn a reply that unlocks dialogue; I am competing against an inbox saturated with generic templates, so the only differentiator is anchoring the contact in a real, verifiable signal and offering a value angle specific to their role. Deliver two variants: a connection note of maximum 300 characters and an InMail of maximum 600 characters, respecting {{FORMATO_Y_LIMITE}} if specified. Proceed as follows: 1) validate that {{SENAL_OBSERVABLE}} is recent, public, and attributable; if it is weak, ask for a better one before drafting and do not invent anything. 2) Connect that signal to {{PROBLEMA_O_PRIORIDAD}} and translate {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} into a concrete angle for their role, without listing features. 3) Structure each message as: opening (signal), bridge (problem-value), and close with ONE single open low-commitment question that only the prospect can answer. 4) Write in neutral, professional Spanish, short phrases, one idea per sentence, without emojis, no prices, no use of the word "free". Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any unconfirmed data about {{NOMBRE_CARGO_PROSPECTO}} or {{EMPRESA_PROSPECTO}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if any. Before drafting restate what you understand and present your plan; at the end accompany each variant with a line indicating which signal it is anchored in and the character count. If any key input is missing, ask for it before continuing. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute.

prompts.title: Voicemail script that generates a callback
prompts.content: Act as a senior sales coach specializing in B2B outbound telephone prospecting and voice messaging that maximizes callback rate. Draft a complete voicemail script ready to read aloud for when {{NOMBRE_PROSPECTO}} from {{EMPRESA_PROSPECTO}} does not answer and I reach their voicemail. Context: most sales voicemails are ignored or deleted because they sound like a generic pitch and burn the contact; a brief message, opened with relevance and with curiosity seeded, turns the mailbox into a second door. Before writing, validate that you have {{NOMBRE_PROSPECTO}}, {{EMPRESA_PROSPECTO}}, {{MOTIVO_RELEVANCIA}}, {{NOMBRE_VENDEDOR}}, {{ROL_VENDEDOR}}, and {{NUMERO_CALLBACK}}; if any is missing ask for it one question at a time and do not invent it. If {{MOTIVO_RELEVANCIA}} is weak or generic, tell me and suggest how to strengthen it. Restate in one sentence the relevance angle and show your plan for opening, curiosity, and close before executing. Then deliver: (1) main script of 55–75 words (20–30 spoken seconds) that opens with {{NOMBRE_PROSPECTO}} plus {{MOTIVO_RELEVANCIA}}, seeds curiosity by hinting at the value without fully revealing it, clearly identifies {{NOMBRE_VENDEDOR}} and {{ROL_VENDEDOR}}, and closes by saying {{NUMERO_CALLBACK}} twice in a slow, deliberate manner, with [pause] and tone marked in brackets; (2) alternate version of ~15 s (30–40 words) for mailboxes that cut off quickly, which sacrifices curiosity before the number; (3) three delivery notes: rhythm and breathing, speed and digit grouping when dictating {{NUMERO_CALLBACK}}, and what to avoid (pressure, jargon, sounding like a script). If {{ADJUNTOS}} are relevant, mention the follow-up through that channel without overloading the message. Hard rules: never prices or the word "free"; neutral, professional, warm Spanish, without emojis.

prompts.title: Personalized prospecting video script
prompts.content:
Act as a senior 1:1 video prospecting strategist, expert in social selling and the video prospecting discipline: message centered on the prospect, single call to action. I need a script for a short 1:1 video of 30 to 90 seconds that breaks the ice with a cold or follow-up prospect, because the personalized video demonstrates real effort and humanizes the first contact when the hook names the prospect and the trigger in the first 8 seconds and asks for a single low-friction micro-commitment.

Data:
- PROSPECTO: {{PROSPECTO}} (name and title of the video recipient)
- EMPRESA: {{EMPRESA}} (prospect's company and sector)
- DETONANTE: {{DETONANTE}} (recent signal or event that justifies contact: announcement, post, funding, role change, job opening)
- PROPUESTA_VALOR: {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} (problem I solve and my value proposition in one sentence)
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} (sending channel: email, LinkedIn, WhatsApp)
- MICRO_COMPROMISO: {{MICRO_COMPROMISO}} (minimum closing action: reply, view a case, schedule 15 minutes)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, URLs, or "No attachments")

If PROSPECTO, EMPRESA, DETONANTE, PROPUESTA_VALOR, CANAL, or MICRO_COMPROMISO are missing, ask for them in a brief list before writing; if DETONANTE is empty do not invent it, ask for it. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver five blocks with time markers: Hook (0 to 8 s, names {{PROSPECTO}} and {{DETONANTE}}, without introducing yourself), Insight (8 to 25 s, relevant observation from {{EMPRESA}}'s context), Bridge to problem (25 to 50 s, connects to {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} as a question), Brief proof (50 to 70 s, data point or case; without a verified figure mark [ASSUMPTION] with typical range and note to confirm), Close (70 to 90 s, {{MICRO_COMPROMISO}} as the single yes-or-no question). Per block: literal spoken text, camera direction or gesture note in parentheses, and estimated duration. Add subject adapted to {{CANAL}}, two lines of accompanying copy referencing {{ADJUNTOS}} only if they add value, thumbnail text with {{PROSPECTO}}'s name written by hand, and three hook variants for A/B testing with the hypothesis each one validates.

Rules: message centered on the prospect and not the sender; full reading aloud in 90 seconds or less respecting the times; a single call to action equal to {{MICRO_COMPROMISO}}; no result claim without backing or without [ASSUMPTION]; zero prices and zero use of the word "free"; professional, close, and direct tone, neutral Spanish, without empty jargon or exaggerated promises.

prompts.title: Request referrals from existing clients
prompts.content: Act as a senior account executive with a background in B2B consultative sales and expertise in asking for referrals without applying pressure. We have just delivered to {{CLIENTE}} the achievement {{LOGRO_ENTREGADO}}, supported by {{METRICA_RESULTADO}}, and I want to leverage that moment of maximum perceived value to request a qualified referral from {{NOMBRE_CONTACTO}} without sounding transactional or eroding trust. I need you to draft a referral request message ready to send via {{CANAL}}, plus three alternative subject lines and a timing note on when to send it. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol Interpret > Plan > Execute: first restate what you understand and present your plan; if {{LOGRO_ENTREGADO}}, {{METRICA_RESULTADO}}, {{NOMBRE_CONTACTO}}, or {{PERFIL_CLIENTE_IDEAL}} are missing or generic, ask for them before drafting instead of inventing. Structure the message in five moves: 1) open by acknowledging {{LOGRO_ENTREGADO}} with {{CLIENTE}}, citing {{METRICA_RESULTADO}} as concrete proof of value, not a generic compliment; 2) connect that success to the request by leveraging reciprocity and social proof, without sounding like you are calling in a favor; 3) make a single concrete, low-friction ask anchored in {{PERFIL_CLIENTE_IDEAL}} (role, sector, challenge) so that thinking of someone is easy; 4) offer at least two comfortable ways to facilitate the introduction (email intro, brief call, or a forwardable message that {{NOMBRE_CONTACTO}} can copy); 5) close by expressing gratitude and making it explicit that there is no obligation. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide proof of the achievement. Write in neutral, professional, warm Spanish, no emojis; never mention prices or use the word free; adjust length to {{CANAL}}. Deliverable: message ready to send + 3 alternative subject lines + 1 timing note.

prompts.title: Reactivate cold or lost leads
prompts.content: Act as a senior B2B sales executive specialized in reactivating dormant opportunities, with mastery of consultative closing (SPIN, Challenger) and Blair Enns's break-up email technique. I want to reopen the conversation with {{PROSPECTO}}, about {{OFERTA_CONVERSADA}}, which went cold {{ULTIMO_CONTACTO}} ago, via channel {{CANAL}}, using as the new and legitimate motive {{DISPARADOR}}, and aiming for {{OBJETIVO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. This is a reactivation strategy. Reconstruct the context and the original pain or goal from {{PROSPECTO}}, {{OFERTA_CONVERSADA}}, and {{ULTIMO_CONTACTO}}. Deliver two ready-to-send variants. Variant A win-back: reconnects with that pain or goal, introduces {{DISPARADOR}} as a legitimate reason to resume now (not a reminder), and closes with a single, low-commitment CTA aligned to {{OBJETIVO}}. Variant B break-up: elegantly assumes the moment is not right, releases the prospect from having to respond, and leaves a single minimal-friction door open. For each variant include a subject line only if {{CANAL}} is email, a body of 4 to 7 lines, a single concrete CTA, and a note on when to use it. Before drafting, restate the context, the probable reason for going cold, and the goal, and flag as [ASSUMPTION] what has not been confirmed; if {{PROSPECTO}}, {{OFERTA_CONVERSADA}}, {{DISPARADOR}}, or {{CANAL}} are missing, ask before drafting. Do not invent prospect data or history. Neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices or discounts, no word free; adjust length and register to {{CANAL}} (email more formal; LinkedIn and WhatsApp shorter).

prompts.title: Break through gatekeeper barriers
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B consultative salesperson with expertise in cold prospecting and the psychology of decision-maker access, trained in reference-based opening, permission, and help-request techniques (Sandler style). Your mission: design opening lines that allow me to reach {{DECISOR}} by getting past {{TIPO_PORTERO}} who filters, via {{CANAL}}, treating the gatekeeper as an informed ally who knows the organization and can open the right door, never as an adversary to deceive. Here, a strategy converts the gatekeeper from a wall into a bridge.

First restate in one sentence: reach {{DECISOR}} filtered by {{TIPO_PORTERO}} via {{CANAL}}, for [purpose derived from {{OFERTA_VALOR}}]. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it in a single batch before drafting; do not invent names, titles, or company data.

Diagnose the probable behavior of {{TIPO_PORTERO}} (strict blocker, neutral filter, potential ally) and adjust register and length to {{CANAL}}.

Design between 5 and 7 distinct opening lines, each with: (a) exact text ready to use via {{CANAL}}; (b) tactic applied; (c) why it works with that gatekeeper. Valid tactics: respect and help request, purpose clarity anchored in {{OFERTA_VALOR}}, legitimate reference ({{REFERENCIA}} only if real; if "No reference", do not cite any), routing question, genuine reciprocity, respectful assumption of continuity. Non-negotiable ethical filter: no lying, pressuring, pretending to be a client or colleague, or inventing relationships; discard and declare any tactic that only works by deceiving.

For each line, anticipate the gatekeeper's most likely objection (what is it about, send me an email, they are not in, we do not receive vendors, we already work with someone) and the bridge counter-response. Close with a mini two-branch decision tree: cooperate branch (routing, appointment, or transfer) vs. block branch (obtain name, email, best retry time, or preferred channel), each branch with one concrete next step.

Flag with [ASSUMPTION] every claim without data. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. Deliver in neutral Spanish, professional and human tone, no emojis, and close with the single highest-impact action for the next attempt.

Parameters:
- {{DECISOR}}: title of the target decision-maker and, if known, their name.
- {{OFERTA_VALOR}}: what you sell and the concrete, specific value the decision-maker would receive.
- {{TIPO_PORTERO}}: who filters (reception, executive assistant, phone filter, secretary, front desk).
- {{CANAL}}: cold call, in-person reception, email, or LinkedIn.
- {{REFERENCIA}}: legitimate motive or reference to cite (mutual contact, event, content, business trigger) or "No reference".
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Generate high open-rate subject lines
prompts.content:
Act as a senior cold email copywriting specialist and open-rate optimizer, with experience in B2B prospecting sequences, deliverability, and subject-line A/B test design. In cold prospecting, the entire email rides on the subject line: if it is not opened, the best body does not exist. {{DESTINATARIO}} receives dozens of unsolicited emails a day and decides in less than a second by reading only the subject and sender in the mobile preview. Your job is to produce a set of testable subject lines, not a hunch, that speak to {{DOLOR_O_VALOR}} and maximize opens toward {{OBJETIVO}} without clickbait or spam filters.

Input data:
- DESTINATARIO: {{DESTINATARIO}} (buyer persona: title, sector, and company size of the recipient)
- DOLOR_O_VALOR: {{DOLOR_O_VALOR}} (specific pain or result the recipient values and that the email will address)
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} (action sought upon opening: reply, schedule, read a case study, download a resource)
