- TONO: {{TONO}} (approachable, executive, or measured-provocative; default executive, sober)
- PERSONALIZACION: {{PERSONALIZACION}} (real hook available for personalization: company, event, news, or recent signal from the recipient; "No hook" if none)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, URLs, or "No attachments")

If DESTINATARIO, DOLOR_O_VALOR, or OBJETIVO are missing or ambiguous, ask for them in a single batch before writing; do not invent title, pain, or hook.

Deliver in this order: (1) sentence "Get {{DESTINATARIO}} to open for {{OBJETIVO}}, appealing to {{DOLOR_O_VALOR}}"; (2) table of 10 to 12 lines with columns number, line, angle, and character count, covering at least once each angle: direct question to the pain, specific non-clickbait curiosity, reference to a peer or sector competitor, concrete data or figure, tangible benefit, and personalized mention using {{PERSONALIZACION}}; (3) 2 or 3 variants recommended for the first A/B test, from contrasting angles, each with its open hypothesis; (4) suggested preheader for the winners; (5) subject-line error to avoid with this recipient.

Hard rules per line: 4 to 9 words and approximate maximum of 50 characters; no greeting or sender name; no all-caps, no repeated marks, no spam triggers; no promise unsupported by the data. Count characters before presenting; flag [ASSUMPTION] on any line whose hook depends on absent data. Calibrate to {{TONO}}. Respond in neutral, professional Spanish.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Personalization at scale with tokens
prompts.content:
Act as a senior outbound prospecting strategist with experience running high-volume multichannel sequences and designing token systems in sales engagement platforms. I need a scale personalization system based on dynamic variables, ready to load into a sequence, that lets me send to hundreds of prospects from {{SEGMENTO}} via {{CANAL}} while maintaining individual perceived relevance without falling into the template effect that triggers discard.

Produce, in this order:
1. Dynamic variable map in three layers: identity (name, title, company), context (sector, size, observable signal or trigger), and relevance (hook that connects {{DISPARADOR}} to the proposition). For each variable indicate: token name, field from {{CAMPOS_DATOS}} that feeds it, and data source.
2. Fill rule per variable and a safe fallback value for when the data is missing, so the message never shows a gap, a broken greeting, or an unreplaced literal token.
3. Message template for {{CANAL}} with the variables in position, marking what is fixed text and what is personalized text, and closing with {{LLAMADO_ACCION}}.
4. Granularity criterion: what is personalized at the individual level, what at the segment level, and what remains constant throughout the campaign, justifying where personalization moves the needle and where it only adds cost.
5. Pre-send quality checklist: unreplaced tokens, fallbacks activated excessively (threshold that reveals a low-quality list), phrases that reveal automation, and spam signals affecting deliverability.
6. Measurement plan: what metric to observe per layer to iterate the system.

Rules: draft in {{TONO}} (default professional-approachable); the relevance layer must explicitly connect {{DISPARADOR}} to the proposition, not be decorative data. Flag any assumption as [ASSUMPTION]; if a critical field from {{CAMPOS_DATOS}} does not exist, propose how to capture it before scaling rather than inventing it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable. Neutral, professional Spanish, without sounding mass-produced, no emojis.

Variables:
- {{SEGMENTO}}: prospect profile or segment (title, industry, company size).
- {{CANAL}}: outreach channel (cold email, LinkedIn, or mixed).
- {{DISPARADOR}}: pain, event, or observable signal that justifies the contact.
- {{LLAMADO_ACCION}}: concrete action requested at the close (15-min meeting, reply, download).
- {{CAMPOS_DATOS}}: fields available per prospect in the CRM or list (name, title, company, sector, recent signal).
- {{TONO}}: desired message register (optional; default professional-approachable).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

If an essential variable is missing, ask for it before executing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Value proposition by segment
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B commercial strategist, expert in positioning, segmentation, and value proposition design using the Strategyzer canvas (Value Proposition Canvas). Your task is to build a segmented value proposition for {{SEGMENTO}} and derive 3 ready-to-use prospecting messages.

Input data:
- OFERTA: {{OFERTA}} (product or service to position, with its key capabilities)
- SEGMENTO: {{SEGMENTO}} (market segment or buyer profile: industry, role, size)
- DOLOR_DOMINANTE: {{DOLOR_DOMINANTE}} (main pain or problem observed in that segment)
- ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL: {{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}} (how the buyer solves it today: status quo, competitor, manual process)
- DIFERENCIADOR: {{DIFERENCIADOR}} (differential advantage over the current alternative; optional)

Before executing, restate in your own words the offer, {{SEGMENTO}}, and {{DOLOR_DOMINANTE}} you understood, and present your plan in one line. If any necessary data is missing, ask for it in a single batch before continuing; do not invent data.

Proceed in three phases:

Phase 1 - Problem fit. Map the customer profile for {{SEGMENTO}} separately from the value map: jobs to be done (functional, social, emotional), pains starting from {{DOLOR_DOMINANTE}}, and expected gains. Prioritize pains by intensity and frequency, do not list them flat. Flag any data not provided as [ASSUMPTION].

Phase 2 - Solution fit. Inventory the capabilities of {{OFERTA}} and build the value map (pain relievers and gain creators). Connect each relevant capability to a specific pain or gain and discard what does not fit; if a capability has no anchor, exclude it rather than inflate it.

Phase 3 - Articulation. Draft the value proposition statement: for [{{SEGMENTO}}] who [job or pain], our [{{OFERTA}}] delivers [differential benefit based on {{DIFERENCIADOR}}], unlike [{{ALTERNATIVA_ACTUAL}}]. Then derive 3 prospecting messages anchored to {{DOLOR_DOMINANTE}}, in the segment's language: (1) cold email with subject line and a single call to action; (2) LinkedIn message; (3) 2-to-3-sentence call opening hook. Each message opens with the buyer's pain, not your product, and proposes a low-friction next step.

Do not mention prices or use the word free. Deliver: (a) summarized canvas profile + map with prioritized pains, (b) one-paragraph value statement, (c) the 3 editable messages. Close with 2 key assumptions to validate with {{SEGMENTO}} before launching.

prompts.title: Qualify lead with BANT
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B sales executive expert in opportunity qualification with the BANT framework (Budget, Authority, Need, Timing). I need to decide with clear criteria whether {{OPORTUNIDAD}} deserves to advance to proposal, stay in nurturing, or be discarded, rather than investing sales time in leads that are not going to close.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the opportunity, the solution {{SOLUCION_OFRECIDA}}, and the stage {{ETAPA_PIPELINE}} as you understand them and list the missing data; if evidence for any critical BANT dimension is missing, ask for it before qualifying. Then present your plan and execute.

From {{NOTAS_DISCOVERY}} evaluate the four dimensions, each supported only by evidence from the notes: Budget (investment capacity, who controls the budget, cycle), Authority (economic buyer, influencers, blockers, internal champion), Need (business pain, urgency, impact quantification, solution fit), and Timing (event forcing the decision, cost of inaction, buying cycle). Assign each dimension a level: Strong, Partial, Weak, or No evidence, with a justification citing the specific signal. Flag every inference with [ASSUMPTION] and never invent budget figures.

Calculate a global score out of 100 by weighting (Strong=25, Partial=15, Weak=5, No evidence=0 per dimension) and make the sum transparent. Emit a single verdict: Advance to proposal (>=75 with no No-evidence dimension), Nurture and re-qualify (40-74 or recoverable gap), or Discard (<40 or Need at Weak/No evidence unrecoverable). Indicate the weakest dimension to unlock first and draft 3 to 5 open, actionable discovery questions aimed at that gap. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide signals.

Deliver a report with a table of four dimensions (level + justification cited), score out of 100 with its logic, actionable verdict, and follow-up questions. Professional, consultative tone; no prices, discounts, or word free; budget capacity only in qualitative terms.

Variables: {{OPORTUNIDAD}}, {{NOTAS_DISCOVERY}}, {{SOLUCION_OFRECIDA}}, {{ETAPA_PIPELINE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any is missing, ask for it.

prompts.title: Qualify opportunity with MEDDIC
prompts.content: Act as a senior B2B Sales Engineer with operational mastery of the MEDDIC framework in complex sales cycles. I need an actionable MEDDIC qualification sheet for {{CLIENTE}} on {{SOLUCION}} at stage {{ETAPA_PIPELINE}}, using {{NOTAS_DESCUBRIMIENTO}} as the sole source of evidence. Before executing, restate what you understand (account, solution, stage, information level) and present your plan; if an essential piece of data for qualifying is missing, ask for it rather than inventing. Then qualify the six components in order of leverage: Metrics, Economic Buyer, Decision Criteria, Decision Process, Identify Pain, and Champion. In each component, separate what is confirmed (with a quote or reference to {{NOTAS_DESCUBRIMIENTO}}) from what is assumed or unknown, flag each gap as an explicit assumption or question, and formulate the discovery question that closes the gap. The Economic Buyer is the person who signs and controls the budget, not the end user; if not identified, lower the traffic light. Assign a green, yellow, or red traffic light per component with a one-line justification. Calculate a global health score from 0 to 100 weighting Economic Buyer, Identify Pain, and Champion more, explain the logic, and emit a verdict: advance, nurture, or disqualify, contrasted with {{CRITERIO_AVANCE}} if provided. Close with three main risks (with trigger) and three actionable next steps, each with a suggested owner and time horizon. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide evidence. Do not invent client data; this qualification is your strategy for not carrying into the pipeline what is not going to close. Deliver six blocks plus an executive summary ready for CRM or pipeline review.

prompts.title: Qualify with expanded MEDDPICC
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B Sales Director, expert in enterprise qualification and pipeline coaching with MEDDPICC. I need a rigorous diagnosis of opportunity {{NOMBRE_OPORTUNIDAD}} with {{CLIENTE}}, at stage {{ETAPA_PIPELINE}} and target close {{FECHA_CIERRE_OBJETIVO}}, to expose the gaps that kill deals at late stages and decide with evidence whether to advance, nurture, or disqualify. Work from {{CONTEXTO_CONOCIDO}} and {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before diagnosing, restate the opportunity as you understand it and present your evaluation plan; if {{CONTEXTO_CONOCIDO}} is insufficient to score any element, ask for the missing data in a single batch before concluding.

Proceed as follows:
1. Map the context against the eight elements: Metrics (sought quantifiable impact and baseline), Economic Buyer (who signs and controls the budget, contacted or not), Decision Criteria (formal and informal, technical and business criteria), Decision Process (steps, committee, and dates until decision), Paper Process (procurement, legal, security, privacy, signing, and timelines), Implicate the Pain (quantified pain and cost of inaction), Champion (internal ally with power, access, and self-interest, proven or assumed), and Competition (named rivals, incumbent, and the option of not deciding).
2. For each element deliver: what we know today, the supporting evidence, a risk color (solid green / partial yellow / absent or unknown red), and the discovery question that closes the gap.
3. Calculate a health score from 0 to 100 weighting the eight elements; declare the weighting and that a single red in Economic Buyer or Champion caps the score at 'high risk'.
4. Emit a single verdict (advance / nurture / disqualify) consistent with the reds, with justification in one sentence.
5. List the three risks that most threaten the close with their early warning signal and the next steps with suggested owner and date, executable this week.

Rules: flag every inference with [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent contacts, figures, or dates; if an element cannot be scored, mark it red for unknown. Deliver a MEDDPICC table of eight rows plus a synthesis block (score, verdict, three risks, next steps) ready to paste into the CRM. Neutral, professional Spanish, no prices.

Variables:
- {{CLIENTE}}: company or account to qualify
- {{NOMBRE_OPORTUNIDAD}}: deal name or code in the pipeline
- {{ETAPA_PIPELINE}}: current stage (discovery, proposal, negotiation, etc.)
- {{FECHA_CIERRE_OBJETIVO}}: expected close date
- {{CONTEXTO_CONOCIDO}}: contacts, pains, relative budget, competitors, meeting notes
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Qualify with CHAMP
prompts.content: Act as a senior B2B consultative sales leader, expert in CHAMP, MEDDIC, and pain-based discovery. Qualify with CHAMP the opportunity {{CUENTA}} for {{SOLUCION}}, discussed with {{CONTACTO}}, from {{CONTEXTO_CONVERSACION}}, and considering {{ETAPA_PIPELINE}} and {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if account, contact, or conversation context is missing, ask for it in a single batch and do not invent client data. Deliver in this order: (1) the opportunity restated in one sentence: qualify {{CUENTA}} for {{SOLUCION}} starting from the challenge {{CONTACTO}} seeks to resolve; (2) the four dimensions starting from pain and not from budget: Challenges with prioritized challenges by impact, each linked to a concrete consequence of cost, risk, lost revenue, or time, separating real pain from symptom; Authority with decision map (decides, influences, signs, vetoes), internal champion, and gaps; Money as economic value of resolving the challenge and capacity/willingness to invest, reasoned without asking for or declaring prices or rates; Prioritization with why now, triggering event, internal competition for resources, and realistic decision date; (3) status Strong/Medium/Weak/Unknown per dimension with one line of evidence, inferred items as ASSUMPTION; (4) verdict Advance/Nurture/Discard with its logic and the signal that would reverse it; (5) pending discovery questions prioritizing Unknown, plus next steps with owner and time trigger. If {{CONTEXTO_CONVERSACION}} is contradictory, prioritize the most recent and direct source and record the tension. Never prices or rate figures. Neutral Spanish, professional, no emojis.

prompts.title: Qualify with GPCTBA/CI
prompts.content:
Act as a senior consultative sales manager with hands-on mastery of HubSpot's GPCTBA/CI framework and value-based selling. I am qualifying the opportunity with {{PROSPECTO_Y_SECTOR}}, at stage {{ETAPA_PIPELINE}}, for the offer {{OFERTA}}. I need to decide with evidence, not intuition, whether to invest more time in it.

Build a qualification scorecard from {{INSUMOS_DESCUBRIMIENTO}}: (1) Map the eight framework dimensions: Goals, Plans, Challenges, Timeline, Budget, Authority, Negative Consequences, and Positive Implications. (2) For each dimension deliver a table with available textual evidence, pending gap, level (Strong / Partial / Empty), and a ready-to-use discovery question. (3) Issue the verdict oriented toward {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} (ADVANCE / NURTURE / DISQUALIFY) with the primary reason anchored in the critical dimensions. (4) List the two major risks and the specific next step with owner and trigger.

Rules: extract only what is verifiable; anything not present in the inputs is marked Empty with its question and is never filled with assumptions. Budget is evaluated as capacity and allocation process, never as a figure. Authority and Timeline are disqualification dimensions: if both are Empty, the verdict cannot be ADVANCE. Never mention prices, cost ranges, or the word free. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they contribute evidence. If an essential input is missing, ask for it before executing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Qualify with SPICED
SPIN discovery questions
Deep pain diagnosis
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B consultative sales consultant, expert in high-value discovery and impact quantification, trained in implication and need-payoff questions (SPIN style) and in cost-of-inaction analysis. I am in the discovery phase with {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}} from the {{INDUSTRIA}} sector, who has already expressed a superficial pain: {{DOLOR_DECLARADO}}. A vague complaint does not move budgets or persuade a committee. Your job is to transform it into a quantified case for change, connected to {{METRICA_NEGOCIO}} and, if applicable, to the window {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}, that the prospect themselves can defend internally. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}}, {{INDUSTRIA}}, {{DOLOR_DECLARADO}}, and {{METRICA_NEGOCIO}}; if any is missing or ambiguous, ask before drafting. Then present your funnel plan in one line. Only then execute.

Deliver a deep pain diagnosis script with five blocks and a closing:
1. Root cause: 3–5 funnel questions from {{DOLOR_DECLARADO}} down to the structural origin (process, data, incentive, or capability), not the symptom.
2. Quantified impact: 3–5 questions asking for figures or ranges in at least four dimensions of time, money, risk, quality, and opportunity cost. If there is no figure, ask for their best estimate and how they would calculate it.
3. Cost of inaction: 3–5 questions about what happens at 6, 12, and 18 months if nothing changes, with cumulative deterioration and the decision window.
4. Organizational scope: 3–5 questions mapping who is affected, who bears the consequences, and who decides and signs.
5. Strategic connection: 3–5 questions linking the pain to {{METRICA_NEGOCIO}} and the leadership agenda.
6. Synthesis: case for change in one sentence (problem-impact-consequence) and three observable signals of urgency.

Rules: each question open, non-leading, in neutral Spanish, ready to read aloud; general to specific; never mention solution, product, or provider; each block with a brief note on what to listen for (real pain vs. cosmetic complaint). No prices or no-cost offers. Mark inferences as [ASSUMPTION].

prompts.title: Quantify the cost of inaction
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B consultative sales strategist with 15 years building quantitative business cases for buying committees. I am in discovery with {{PROSPECTO}}, who acknowledges the problem {{PROBLEMA}} but does not feel urgency; I want to quantify how much it costs them to sustain the status quo so that urgency arises from their own data, not from commercial pressure.

First, restate the problem, the sector, and the size of {{PROSPECTO}} and the {{METRICAS_BASE}} you were given, and note what data is missing. If {{METRICAS_BASE}} or {{PROBLEMA}} are insufficient to calculate, stop and ask for the specific data you need before proceeding; do not invent the prospect's figures. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any.

Then model the cost of inaction in three layers, without double-counting: (1) Direct cost, the measurable leak already occurring today; (2) Opportunity cost, the value not captured by not acting, counted separately from the direct cost; (3) Compound cost, how it accumulates month by month during {{PERIODO_ANALISIS}}, indicating whether it grows linearly or worsens. For each layer declare driver, assumption, formula, and conservative range (floor-ceiling); mark as assumption any unconfirmed data and anchor each figure to a real data point from {{METRICAS_BASE}} or an explicit benchmark.

Close with: the total consolidated over the horizon and its confidence level; a single urgency statement translated into the metric of {{DECISOR}}; and exactly three actionable validation questions. Never mention your solution's prices or the word free. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.

Variables: {{PROSPECTO}}, {{PROBLEMA}}, {{METRICAS_BASE}}, {{PERIODO_ANALISIS}}, {{DECISOR}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Commercial discovery meeting agenda
prompts.content:
Act as a senior consultative sales consultant with fifteen years closing complex B2B sales, expert in diagnostic discovery (Neil Rackham's SPIN method and the problem-impact-desired state approach of Keenan's Gap Selling). I need to run a first discovery meeting with {{PROSPECTO}} and I want to arrive with a clear agenda and clear objectives, not improvise. In discovery you learn and diagnose, you do not present a product: the risk is jumping to sell {{SOLUCION}}, not understanding the real problem or its impact, and leaving without a committed next step. I want a minute-by-minute runnable script, not a generic list of questions.

Deliverable: discovery meeting script by blocks. Design it as follows:
1. Opening and framing: brief rapport, confirm time available, declare the meeting objective, and propose a shared agenda that {{PROSPECTO}} can adjust.
2. Current state and problem diagnosis: situation questions to map context and problem questions to surface difficulties, dissatisfactions, and risks around {{PROBLEMA_HIPOTESIS}}.
3. Implication and impact: questions that quantify the cost of the problem (time, money, risk, effort) and its effect on metrics and people; here the prospect feels urgency and the cost of the status quo.
4. Desired state and need-payoff: questions that cause {{PROSPECTO}} to describe what resolving the problem looks like and the value of achieving it, in their own words.
5. Qualification: probe for decision-makers and influencers (among {{ASISTENTES}}), process and selection criteria, alternatives being evaluated, and timeline, without turning it into an interrogation.
6. Close and next step: summarize what was learned using the prospect's words, confirm problem and impact, and agree on a specific next step aligned with {{OBJETIVO_REUNION}} with owner and date; offer to draft a mutual action plan.

Design rules: distribute {{DURACION}} (assume 30–45 min if not indicated) giving weight to problem and impact (together close to half), a light opening (around 10%), and a firm, protected close (around 15%). For each block deliver the objective, time assigned, 3 to 6 drafted and runnable example questions, and the advance signal indicating the block is complete. Draft the blocks in sequence because each one feeds the next: situation before problem, problem before impact, impact before desired state, diagnosis before qualification, all before the next step. Close with a list of errors to avoid and a notes sheet with the fields to capture.

Never present {{SOLUCION}} before diagnosing; if the prospect reveals no difficulty, do not invent pain: add alternative problem questions and admit the 'no pain confirmed' signal. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any inference about {{PROSPECTO}}, their industry, or {{PROBLEMA_HIPOTESIS}}, and do not invent client data. Neutral and professional Spanish, no prices, no word free. If any needed data is missing, ask before executing.

Variables:
- {{PROSPECTO}}: prospect company or person and their context (industry, size, situation)
- {{SOLUCION}}: product or service you offer
- {{PROBLEMA_HIPOTESIS}}: problem or need you believe they face and your solution resolves
- {{ASISTENTES}}: who will attend on the prospect's side and their roles (optional)
- {{DURACION}}: planned duration (optional; assume 30–45 min if missing)
- {{OBJETIVO_REUNION}}: specific outcome you want to achieve at the close (optional)

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Map the buying decision process
Stakeholder and buying committee map
prompts.content: Act as a senior complex B2B sales strategist, expert in buying committee mapping, MEDDICC, and multi-stakeholder selling (Challenger and The JOLT Effect). I want a stakeholder map of the buying committee for the deal {{CUENTA_Y_OPORTUNIDAD}}. What I sell and the pain or business outcome it resolves: {{SOLUCION_Y_DOLOR}}. Current stage and next milestone or expected decision: {{ETAPA_Y_PROXIMO_HITO}}. Known contacts with title and the signals I have on each (stance, meetings, comments): {{CONTACTOS_Y_SENALES}}. Who controls the budget and how the decision is made: {{PRESUPUESTO_Y_DECISION}}. Active competition or status quo to displace: {{COMPETENCIA_O_STATUS_QUO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate in one or two lines what deal you understand we are mapping and present your plan; if an essential data point is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it. Work as follows: fix the context (what the client is deciding, what business outcome they are pursuing, likely buying process); classify each contact by decision role (Economic Buyer, Champion, Influencer or Technical Buyer, User Buyer, Coach, Blocker or Detractor, Legal or Procurement) and explicitly declare any critical role without an owner as a gap, especially Economic Buyer and Champion; for each actor estimate influence (High, Medium, Low), stance (Promoter, Neutral, Detractor), personal decision criterion, and risk, labeling each reading as verified data or as an assumption to validate without inventing people, titles, or intentions; place each actor on a power-vs.-stance map (allies to leverage, power to convert, noise to contain, blockers to neutralize) and define the coverage play per person; close with single-threading or fragile relationship risks and a numbered plan with next step, owner, and date per stakeholder. Do not include prices or the word free; neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. Deliver: executive summary of 5 to 7 lines; committee table; power-vs.-stance map; gaps and relationship risks; numbered action plan per stakeholder; and 3 to 5 pending discovery questions.

prompts.title: Identify and develop an internal champion
prompts.content:
Act as a senior complex B2B sales strategist with fifteen years closing long-cycle enterprise deals, expert in MEDDIC and in the Mobilizer profile of the Challenger Customer (CEB / Dixon and Adamson). My problem: in {{CUENTA}} the decision is made by a committee and I am not in the room when it is made. I need a real champion to sell {{SOLUCION}} internally, not a coach who only gives me information without risking political capital.

Give me a champion dossier with: (1) committee role map from {{COMITE_COMPRA}}, classifying each contact as champion, coach, economic buyer, blocker or detractor, and user or technical influencer; separate observed data from inferences and mark each inference as [ASSUMPTION]. (2) Qualification of {{CONTACTO_CANDIDATO}} against the four hard tests: real power and influence, own pain that {{SOLUCION}} resolves, visible personal gain, and access to the economic buyer; use {{ROL_Y_MOTIVACIONES}} as evidence and, if they do not pass, declare them a coach and say what they lack. (3) 1–5 strength scorecard in internal credibility, access to power, willingness to act, and alignment with {{SOLUCION}}, with overall reading and weakest link. (4) Empowerment plan: one-page messaging framework defensible alone before peers, business case with two or three metrics that matter in {{CUENTA}}, internal objections with response, and convincing order by role. (5) Next move and champion test: what I ask, what I deliver, and a verifiable signal that they are selling internally.

Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Do not invent names, titles, or intentions: mark [ASSUMPTION] or ask. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no prices.

Parameters:
- {{CUENTA}}: target account and deal context (industry, size, cycle stage)
- {{SOLUCION}}: solution or service you sell and the business pain it attacks
- {{CONTACTO_CANDIDATO}}: candidate for champion (title and current relationship with you)
- {{ROL_Y_MOTIVACIONES}}: what you know about their power, own pain, personal gain, and internal politics (observed data)
- {{COMITE_COMPRA}}: (optional) other known committee roles: economic buyer, users, detractors
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Access the economic buyer
Capture customer decision criteria
Establish the critical buying event
Formulate initial value hypothesis
prompts.content: Act as a senior B2B consultative sales strategist, with mastery of Jobs-to-be-Done, Customer Development value hypothesis, and MEDDIC qualification. I have an upcoming first discovery meeting with {{PROSPECTO}} (company and sector) and I want to enter with a verifiable thesis about the value I could bring, not with a generic pitch. The meeting will be with {{INTERLOCUTOR_ROL}} (person and role/function). Available research is: {{RESEARCH_SENALES}} (recent facts and signals: job openings, press, announcements, regulation, competitive moves). My offer is: {{OFERTA}} (capability or solution, without prices). Business outcome I aim to move (optional): {{RESULTADO_OBJETIVO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of these data points is missing, ask me for it before continuing instead of inventing it. Give me a preparation card with: (1) context synthesis in 3–5 facts, each tagged [DATA] (from {{RESEARCH_SENALES}} or {{ADJUNTOS}}) or [ASSUMED] (inferred, with its reason); (2) the JTBD and likely business pain of {{INTERLOCUTOR_ROL}}, tied to a metric that role cares about or to {{RESULTADO_OBJETIVO}}; (3) the central value hypothesis in a single sentence: "We believe that [segment/role] faces [costly problem] that today they solve with [current alternative]; {{OFERTA}} would allow them to achieve [measurable outcome], and we will know if [observable evidence]"; (4) 2–3 alternative hypotheses; (5) 4–6 discovery questions that confirm or refute, not that sell; (6) one confirmation signal and one invalidation signal observable in the meeting. Rules: no invented data; every claim [DATA] or [ASSUMED]; central hypothesis falsifiable; no prices or commercial terms; neutral professional Spanish. Before drafting, restate what you understood and present your plan. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute.

prompts.title: Actionable post-discovery summary
Demo preparation plan
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Enterprise Sales Director with fifteen years leading long-cycle, multi-stakeholder B2B software demonstrations. A demo without focus burns the opportunity. Your work is to convert the demo of {{SOLUCION}} for {{PROSPECTO_INDUSTRIA}} into a guided conversation toward an agreed progress commitment, so that the prospect recognizes the demo as theirs and ends with a firm next step. Accelerate the prospect's strategy, not the product catalog.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you understand about {{SOLUCION}}, {{PROSPECTO_INDUSTRIA}}, {{ASISTENTES}}, {{ETAPA_CICLO}}, {{DOLORES_DETECTADOS}}, and {{RESULTADO_OBJETIVO}}, marking with [ASSUMED] everything you infer and naming material gaps; if a datum is missing that would change the plan, ask for it before executing and do not invent prospect data. Then present your attack plan in one line. Only then produce the deliverable.

Deliver a demo preparation plan with these sections, in order: 1) Single objective as a verifiable progress commitment consistent with {{ETAPA_CICLO}}: what the prospect decides, agrees on, or authorizes when done; include observable success criterion and no-go signal. 2) Audience map from {{ASISTENTES}}: for each one, role, what matters to them, implicit question, lever, and risk if ignored; mark economic decision-maker, user, champion, and blocker. 3) Three to five key messages, each tied to a pain from {{DOLORES_DETECTADOS}} and stated as capability-plus-business-outcome with its supporting metric. 4) Scene-by-scene script: opening that restates the pain, two or three high-impact demo moments in the prospect's story order, and close that asks for the next step; with time per scene, required data or environment, and plan B if the live demo fails. 5) The five most probable objections by {{PROSPECTO_INDUSTRIA}} and role, each with bridge response and supporting proof; include how to handle price without quoting. 6) Closing advance question and next step toward {{RESULTADO_OBJETIVO}} with owner, date, and follow-up summary. Close with three buying signals to watch and how to capitalize on them. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

Use neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Avoid the all-of-it demo, internal jargon, promising what the solution does not do, and mentioning prices or discounts. Every claim about the prospect is supported by a given datum or marked [ASSUMED].

prompts.title: Value-based demo, not feature-based
prompts.content:
Act as a senior pre-sales engineer (Sales Engineer) expert in B2B consultative selling and value-selling methodology, skilled at translating technical capabilities into business impact. Design a live value-based demo script for {{PROSPECTO}}, on {{PRODUCTO}}, attacking {{DOLORES_PRIORIZADOS}} and pursuing {{OUTCOME_NEGOCIO}}, calibrated for {{PERFIL_DECISOR}} and a session of {{DURACION}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. If any of these data points is missing, ask me for it before drafting and do not invent it.

Structure the script as follows: (1) Opening reframe that states {{DOLORES_PRIORIZADOS}} and {{OUTCOME_NEGOCIO}} before showing anything from the product. (2) Pain-capability map: associate each pain with ONE single capability of {{PRODUCTO}} that resolves it, order the blocks from highest to lowest pain, and explicitly discard any capability that does not connect to a declared pain. (3) Mini-script per block with the pain in the prospect's words, the transition (let me show you how this changes), the exact clicks or steps to show, and the value phrase that closes by connecting to {{OUTCOME_NEGOCIO}}. (4) One validation question per block. (5) Close with a summary of demonstrated outcomes and one concrete, actionable next step (date, owner, progress criterion).

Adjust language to {{PERFIL_DECISOR}} (technical: architecture and mechanics; financial: avoided cost, efficiency, risk; executive: strategic outcome and time-to-value) and depth to {{DURACION}}. Anticipate a plan B per block (what to show if a feature fails) and, if a pain has no capability to resolve it, say so openly. Do not invent capabilities of {{PRODUCTO}} or metrics of {{PROSPECTO}}; mark with [ASSUMED] any unprovided datum. Before delivering, restate what you understood and present your plan; then execute.

prompts.title: Narrative demo script with tell-show-tell structure
prompts.content: Act as a senior pre-sales engineer and demo storyteller with fifteen years designing B2B demonstrations that close, expert in the tell-show-tell structure and Peter Cohan's Great Demo! method. Design the complete, executable narrative script for the demo of {{PRODUCTO}} for {{PROSPECTO}}: a story that closes, not a screen tour, that starts at the moment of greatest impact, anchors in {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} and {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}, and ends in a concrete progress commitment. Do not invent capabilities outside {{CAPACIDADES_CLAVE}} or promise results without support. If any datum is missing, ask for it before executing. Build in this order, without skipping steps. 1. Anchor the demo in one line that joins {{PROSPECTO}} + {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} + {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}; the entire script serves that outcome, never a feature tour. 2. Vision Generation opening: open with the screen or final result {{PROSPECTO}} most wants to see (the key moment), never login or setup, and connect it to {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} in one or two sentences. 3. Design 3 to 5 scenes from {{CAPACIDADES_CLAVE}}, ordered from highest to lowest impact for this prospect; each scene is illustrate-prove with the complete tell-show-tell block: opening TELL (what they will see and why it matters, in their language) then SHOW (click-by-click actions with the data or flow that proves the value) then closing TELL (business benefit tied to their metric). 4. Write the narrative transitions between scenes for a continuous story. 5. Insert at least two discovery points: open questions to confirm resonance and adapt the walkthrough; define the plan B if the answer is lukewarm or negative. 6. Anticipate {{OBJECIONES_PROBABLES}}: indicate in which scene and with which bridge phrase you neutralize them by showing live evidence, and separate what is demonstrable on screen from what is only assertable. 7. Close: recap results seen and propose a concrete progress commitment (next meeting, scoped trial, access to stakeholders), with a backup alternative. 8. Add time guards per scene according to {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}} and a 5-minute compressed version that keeps the impact opening, highest-value scene, and close; consider the format defined in {{FORMATO_REUNION}}. Write the presenter's text in quotes, mark screen actions and minutes per scene, and flag cuttable scenes. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. Mark as [ASSUMED] any datum you complete without it having been provided. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Do not include prices. Variables: {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PROSPECTO}}, {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}}, {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}, {{CAPACIDADES_CLAVE}}, {{OBJECIONES_PROBABLES}}, {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}}, {{FORMATO_REUNION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Structure a demo with the tell-show-tell pattern
prompts.content:
Act as a senior pre-sales engineer with fifteen years running B2B software demos that close, expert in value-based demos and the tell-show-tell pattern. I need {{AUDIENCIA}} to leave the demo of {{PRODUCTO}} feeling it resolves {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}}, not that they watched a screen tour. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan.

Proceed as follows:
1. Curation. From {{CASOS_USO_DEMO}}, choose only the three to five cases that directly touch {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}}; discard the rest and justify in one line why each discarded one is excluded (hard rule: if it does not touch the pain, it does not go in the demo). Mark every claim about {{PRODUCTO}} as a confirmed datum or [ASSUMED]; never invent capabilities.
2. Narrative arc. Order the blocks so the first touches the most acute pain and the last delivers the resolution that enables {{OBJETIVO_DEMO}}; each block prepares the next. Explain the ordering logic in one line.
3. Tell-show-tell blocks. For each block: Opening tell (context sentence connecting to {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} and leaving an open question), Show (live action step by step, exact click or gesture and observable result on screen), Closing tell (business benefit in the language of {{AUDIENCIA}}, closing the loop of the opening tell).
4. Transitions. Bridge phrase from each block to the next so it flows as a story, not a menu tour.
5. Anti-script per block. What NOT to say or show (out-of-focus features, jargon, dead ends, comparisons that invite objections).
6. Close. Global tell that summarizes the accumulated value and proposes a concrete next step aligned with {{OBJETIVO_DEMO}}.
7. Contingency plan. Two or three probable {{AUDIENCIA}} questions or interruptions and how to redirect without losing the arc.

Deliverable: justified selection, three to five tell-show-tell blocks, transitions, anti-script per block, close with next step, interruption handling, and list of assumptions to confirm. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. If any datum is missing, ask me before starting. Neutral professional Spanish, no prices.

Variables:
- {{PRODUCTO}}: name and brief description of the product or service to demonstrate
- {{AUDIENCIA}}: who will see the demo and who decides (role, industry, technical level)
- {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}}: concrete problem of the prospect that the demo must resolve and make felt
- {{CASOS_USO_DEMO}}: candidate features or flows to show, with what each does today
- {{OBJETIVO_DEMO}}: commercial result sought (advance to PoC, win the technical sponsor, close the next meeting)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Customize demo to the use case
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B pre-sales engineer with a track record of adapting demos to the operational reality of each prospect. Convert the out-of-the-box demo of {{PRODUCTO}} into a personalized, screen-by-screen script that makes {{AUDIENCIA}} from {{PROSPECTO}} see themselves operating {{PRODUCTO}} on their own data and priorities; the objective is to move the conversation from 'what the product does' to 'how it resolves my {{DOLOR_DECLARADO}}' and unlock the advancement of the opportunity.

Before drafting, confirm you have {{PROSPECTO}} (company, sector, size), {{PRODUCTO}}, {{DOLOR_DECLARADO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{DURACION}}; review {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. If any of these data points is missing, ask me for it before moving forward; do not invent the use case.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol in three phases. Phase 1 Interpret: restate the use case of {{PROSPECTO}} and build a map of 3 to 5 priorities against the capabilities of {{PRODUCTO}}, discarding what does not apply to {{PROSPECTO}}. Phase 2 Plan: propose the screen order (open with the heaviest pain from {{DOLOR_DECLARADO}}, close with the business outcome that unlocks the decision) and the adjustment to {{DURACION}} with a margin for questions; show me this plan before drafting. Phase 3 Execute: draft the final script.

For each screen deliver: what is shown, personalized data used (realistic equivalents of {{PROSPECTO}}'s environment, never out-of-the-box sample data), a transition phrase connecting to {{DOLOR_DECLARADO}}, a validation question to {{AUDIENCIA}}, and the estimated minute. Mark [ASSUMED] every value you invent and gather them at the end for confirmation. Add a plan B for when something does not load or {{DURACION}} is cut (essential vs. sacrificable screens), and 3 probable objections from {{AUDIENCIA}} with a one-line response. Close with a single business-outcome message and the suggested next step.

Do not use prices or cost figures; use [VALUE_TO_CONFIRM] if the close requires them. Language: neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Iterative discovery demo
prompts.content: Act as a senior B2B pre-sales engineer with mastery of consultative selling (SPIN, Sandler) and value-based demos (discovery-led / value-based demo). Design a conductible kit for an iterative discovery demo of {{PRODUCTO}} for {{PERFIL_PROSPECTO}}: a session that alternates short question blocks with short demonstration blocks, where a capability is shown only after the prospect connects it to their own pain, and each block closes with a value confirmation in their words. The pain to validate is {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} and the session objective is {{OBJETIVO_DEMO}}. Before starting, restate what you understand and present your plan; then execute. If the product and its real capabilities, the prospect's profile, the main pain, or the objective are missing, ask for them before producing the kit. Deliver in this order: (1) a 60–90-second opening script that reframes the session as a conversation, asks permission to ask questions, and invites interruptions; (2) a battery of live discovery questions in 4 layers (current situation, pain and quantifiable impact, consequence of not acting, vision of desired state), indicating for each question which capability of {{PRODUCTO}} its answer unlocks; (3) an anchor-demonstrate map for each probable pain from {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} and adjacent ones, with a 2–4-minute demo segment that resolves it, a bridge phrase connecting what the prospect said to what will be shown, and a value confirmation question at the block's close; (4) a table of real-time buying signals and friction signals, each with its micro-action (deepen, accelerate, or return to discovery); (5) close with a summary of validated pains, value confirmed by the prospect in their words, and a proposal for {{PROXIMO_PASO}}. Add a degradation plan for when the demo does not flow: pain that does not appear, capability that fails live, passive prospect, or multi-stakeholder with conflicting priorities. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Rules: never show a capability without a declared pain that justifies it; never invent features or metrics (mark unconfirmed content as [ASSUMED] and convert it into a question); no prices; neutral professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Handling objections during the demo
Demo close and next steps
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Account Executive in B2B consultative sales, expert in closing demonstrations and building mutual action plans. I have just finished a demo of {{SOLUCION}} with {{INTERLOCUTOR_Y_ROL}} and the immediate risk is closing with a "we'll review it internally" that cools the opportunity and dilutes momentum. Design the last 5 to 8 minutes of the demo so the prospect verbalizes the value they perceived and commits to next steps with owners and dates, leaving the following meeting scheduled live for {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} and not as a vague email promise.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First rephrase the situation as you understand it (confirm {{SOLUCION}}, {{INTERLOCUTOR_Y_ROL}} and {{PRIORIDAD_NEGOCIO}}) and present your plan; if {{PROCESO_DECISION}} or {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} are missing, ask for them or record them as [ASSUMPTION] before drafting. Then execute.

Deliverable: a five-block demo closing script, sequenced from lowest to highest commitment, ready to read and adapt live. 1) Open-ended value-confirmation question that forces the prospect to name the problem they saw solved and the expected impact. 2) Executive summary of 2 to 3 lines reconnecting what was demonstrated with {{PRIORIDAD_NEGOCIO}}. 3) Next-steps proposal: each action with a named owner and a date, drafted for verbal agreement. 4) Close that schedules the next meeting for {{FECHA_OBJETIVO}} before hanging up, with tentative participants according to {{PROCESO_DECISION}}. 5) Handling of the most likely postponement objection ("I need to check with the team") that converts it into a date commitment. Add a micro-variant of block 5 if {{INTERLOCUTOR_Y_ROL}} is not the final decision-maker (path to the real decision-maker) and an exit line when they ask to send everything by email (anchor to a short review call). Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Neutral, professional Spanish, no prices, no the word free, no unsustainable promises, no emojis; mark all inferences [ASSUMPTION].

prompts.title: Proof-of-concept (PoC) plan
Mutual success criteria for a PoC
prompts.content:
Act as a senior presales architect in B2B technology sales, expert in closing PoCs with verifiable acceptance criteria and buying-committee management. Your task is to produce a signable mutual success-criteria agreement for the PoC of {{SOLUCION}} with {{PROSPECTO}}: the short contract both parties agree to before starting, one that converts the trial into a purchase decision with an explicit conversion rule, not an open demo the prospect enjoys but never buys.

Before drafting, rephrase what you understand and present your plan. Work with: PROSPECTO={{PROSPECTO}}, SOLUCION={{SOLUCION}}, PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO={{PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO}}, METRICA_CLAVE={{METRICA_CLAVE}}, BASELINE={{BASELINE}} (current metric value, or "no baseline" if unknown), PLAZO_POC={{PLAZO_POC}}, DECISOR={{DECISOR}}, ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}}. If a critical data point is missing, ask for it in a single batch; do not invent client figures.

Deliver, in neutral, professional Spanish: (1) {{PROBLEMA_NEGOCIO}} rephrased in the language of {{PROSPECTO}}, not in features of {{SOLUCION}}; (2) table of 3 to 5 acceptance criteria with criterion, observable metric, baseline (use {{BASELINE}} where applicable), approved/failed target threshold, data source, measurement method, and must-have or desirable classification; at least one must-have anchored to {{METRICA_CLAVE}}; (3) scope declaring what is in and what is NOT in scope; (4) inputs that {{PROSPECTO}} must provide, each with a named owner and deadline, without which the PoC does not start; (5) {{PLAZO_POC}} with a midpoint review milestone using a traffic-light format (green continues, yellow triggers correction, red escalates to {{DECISOR}}); (6) bidirectional conversion rule: if must-haves are met, next commercial step with owner and date, and what {{DECISOR}} signs; if not met, what is offered (adjustment, bounded second iteration, or clean close); (7) assumptions and risks that could invalidate the PoC. Mark all assumed values as [ASSUMPTION]. Close with a signature line for both parties.

prompts.title: Storytelling with a success story
Structuring a commercial proposal
prompts.content: Act as a senior B2B sales consultant with fifteen years closing professional-services proposals, expert in consultative selling and in translating technical capabilities into business value. I need a commercial proposal in structured prose with block headings, ready to present, directed at {{PROSPECTO}} in the {{SECTOR}} sector, to resolve {{DOLOR_PRINCIPAL}} with {{OFERTA}}. Promised business outcome: {{RESULTADO_OBJETIVO}}. Approving decision-maker: {{DECISOR}}. Target implementation deadline: {{PLAZO_OBJETIVO}}. Reference attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before drafting: rephrase in your own words the prospect, sector, pain, and offering, and tell me what essential data is missing; if there is any, ask for it in a single batch and do not invent it. Then build five blocks chained by a single logical thread: problem → solution → value → plan → close. Problem block: name the pain in the literal language of {{PROSPECTO}}, quantify the cost of not acting, and explain why the urgency is now. Solution block: describe {{OFERTA}} and respond to each pain point by point, without empty jargon. Value block: translate into measurable outcomes tied to {{RESULTADO_OBJETIVO}}, with expected return over a time horizon; never mention prices. Plan block: phases, verifiable milestones, owners on each side, and realistic timelines up to {{PLAZO_OBJETIVO}}. Close block: defuse the two or three most likely objections, call to action directed at {{DECISOR}}, and concrete next step with a suggested date. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on every impact claim without confirmed data. Neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis, no the word free. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Drafting a proposal executive summary
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B commercial director with experience drafting executive summaries that pass buying committees and executive committees. Your task: convert {{PROPUESTA_FUENTE}} into an executive summary of at most one page, readable in under two minutes, directed at {{ROL_DECISOR}} in the {{SECTOR_CLIENTE}} sector, culminating in {{DECISION_PEDIDA}}. If you know {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}, adjust emphasis and urgency to that deadline. If {{PROPUESTA_FUENTE}}, {{ROL_DECISOR}}, {{SECTOR_CLIENTE}}, or {{DECISION_PEDIDA}} are missing, ask for them before drafting. First interpret and rephrase what you understand and present your plan; then execute. Draft five labeled blocks in this order: 1) Context and problem, one or two sentences with the pain and the cost of not acting; 2) Proposed solution, approach in business language with clear scope and no technical jargon; 3) Business result, quantified or qualified benefits connected to the priorities of {{ROL_DECISOR}}, with a time horizon; 4) Why us, one credible differentiator in one sentence; 5) Decision and next step, effort and horizon without price figures plus the concrete decision. Trace every benefit to a point in {{PROPUESTA_FUENTE}}; mark [ASSUMPTION] on any missing impact data and ask for it. Non-negotiable rules: zero price figures, never the word free, zero technical jargon, neutral professional Spanish, short sentences, no emojis. Close by confirming one page, five blocks in order, every benefit traced, and the decision explicit and actionable.

Parameters: {{PROPUESTA_FUENTE}}=complete commercial proposal to synthesize; {{ROL_DECISOR}}=title of whoever signs or approves (e.g. CFO, COO, Operations Director); {{SECTOR_CLIENTE}}=client industry and context; {{DECISION_PEDIDA}}=the concrete decision being requested (e.g. approve start of phase 1); {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}=expected decision timeline or first result date (optional).

prompts.title: Building the purchase business case
prompts.content:
Act as a senior value-selling strategist with experience building B2B business cases that pass investment committees and speak to CFOs. I am in a consultative sale to {{CLIENTE}} where the solution has already generated technical interest, but approval depends on an economic case that the internal sponsor can defend before {{DECISOR_ECONOMICO}} when I am not in the room. Build a complete, self-explanatory business case: 1) Quantify the cost of inaction for {{PROBLEMA_DE_NEGOCIO}}, translating it into money, time, risk, and sacrificed opportunity per period, drawing on {{DATOS_BASE}}. 2) Map the capabilities of {{SOLUCION_PROPUESTA}} to measurable impact (savings, additional revenue, mitigated risk, productivity) and separate hard from soft benefits. 3) Build three scenarios — conservative, expected, optimistic — with explicit assumptions, each traceable to {{DATOS_BASE}}, and declare which variable dominates the sensitivity. 4) Derive payback and relative return per scenario over {{HORIZONTE_EVALUACION}}, without prices unless provided. 5) Draft the one-page narrative for {{DECISOR_ECONOMICO}} in the language of their metric and resolve their 2–3 most likely financial objections with evidence. Never invent figures: missing items are [ASSUMPTION] to validate or a question. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if available. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan and present the plan, then Execute. Neutral professional Spanish.

Parameters:
- CLIENTE: {{CLIENTE}} (buying company, sector, and approximate size)
- PROBLEMA_DE_NEGOCIO: {{PROBLEMA_DE_NEGOCIO}} (quantifiable pain that motivates the purchase)
- SOLUCION_PROPUESTA: {{SOLUCION_PROPUESTA}} (key capabilities in outcome language)
- DECISOR_ECONOMICO: {{DECISOR_ECONOMICO}} (who approves and what metric matters to them)
- HORIZONTE_EVALUACION: {{HORIZONTE_EVALUACION}} (period to measure return)
- DATOS_BASE: {{DATOS_BASE}} (available figures; optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, URLs, or "No attachments")

prompts.title: Calculating and presenting ROI
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B business-case analyst with experience in consultative selling and value engineering. A proposal for {{CLIENTE_Y_DECISION}} is stalled because the economic buyer does not see the return clearly; build a defensible, self-explanatory, conservative ROI case that unblocks that decision and connects the investment with {{PRIORIDAD_COMPRADOR}}.

First rephrase what you understand and present your plan before calculating (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute). If {{COSTO_PROBLEMA_ACTUAL}}, {{INVERSION_TOTAL}}, or {{HORIZONTE_MESES}} are missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent figures.

Then deliver: (1) the current state quantified from {{COSTO_PROBLEMA_ACTUAL}}, separating hard from soft benefits; (2) explicit formulas (ROI = net annual benefit / {{INVERSION_TOTAL}}; payback = {{INVERSION_TOTAL}} / average monthly benefit; NPV when {{HORIZONTE_MESES}} exceeds 12, with the discount rate you assume); (3) three scenarios — conservative, base, and optimistic — moving only {{SUPUESTOS_CLAVE}}, each labeled with its source; (4) per scenario and over {{HORIZONTE_MESES}}: annual benefit, ROI at 12 and 36 months, payback in months, and NPV where applicable; (5) one-page executive summary with title anchoring the base-scenario figure, comparative table, and close connecting the figure with {{PRIORIDAD_COMPRADOR}}.

Rules: {{INVERSION_TOTAL}} includes service or license, implementation, adoption, and internal team cost; ROI uses only hard benefits; every figure not provided by the client is marked [ASSUMPTION] with a range and validation method; no third-party prices, no guaranteed-result promises; the base number is the anchor, the optimistic only the ceiling. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if available. Close with the approval question the buyer should be able to answer with a yes.

prompts.title: Total cost of ownership comparison
prompts.content:
Act as a senior value-engineering consultant specialized in total cost of ownership (TCO) models for B2B purchasing decisions, with expertise in category-based costing, break-even analysis, and uncertainty management with explicit assumptions. Your mandate is to build a TCO comparison that faces {{OPCIONES_A_COMPARAR}} (at minimum status quo + proposed solution + one competing alternative) over a horizon of {{HORIZONTE_EVALUACION}} in unit {{UNIDAD_COMPARACION}}, ready for {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}. The goal is to unblock a decision that tends to focus on upfront outlay: it makes the status-quo cost visible, neutralizes the price objection against a cheaper-upfront competitor, and reframes toward value and risk.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand about the mandate, Plan the approach and present it, and only then Execute. Work in four phases. Phase 1, Framing: fix horizon, unit, and the base assumptions that equalize the options (same functional scope, same population, same service level); list missing data as [ASSUMPTION] to validate. Phase 2, Category costing: break each option into homogeneous categories from {{CATEGORIAS_COSTO}} (acquisition or licensing, implementation and migration, integration, training, recurring operation and support, infrastructure, change or exit costs, and status-quo hidden costs: technical debt, lost hours, incident risk, uncaptured opportunity); assign costs using only {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} and mark every data point not provided as [ASSUMPTION] with a validation request before closing the model. Phase 3, Comparison: side-by-side table with subtotals per category, cumulative total per option at the close of the horizon, mark where each alternative wins or loses, and calculate the break-even point against the status quo and competitor; magnitudes as relative ranges, indexes, or multiples, never closed prices or list amounts. Phase 4, Decision narrative: one paragraph translating TCO into business consequences (risk, operational continuity, captured value) for {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}.

Edge cases: if {{OPCIONES_A_COMPARAR}} does not include a competitor, model a generic reference competitor marked [ASSUMPTION]; if the uncertainty of a data point is high, use an optimistic-pessimistic range instead of a single point; if two options tie on TCO, break the tie by risk and cost of change. Deliver: TCO comparison table by category and option + list of assumptions to validate + one-paragraph decision narrative. Inputs: OPCIONES_A_COMPARAR={{OPCIONES_A_COMPARAR}}; HORIZONTE_EVALUACION={{HORIZONTE_EVALUACION}}; UNIDAD_COMPARACION={{UNIDAD_COMPARACION}}; CATEGORIAS_COSTO={{CATEGORIAS_COSTO}}; DATOS_DISPONIBLES={{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}}; AUDIENCIA_DECISORA={{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}; ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}}. Style rules: neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis; never closed prices or the word free; zero invented figures. If an essential data point is missing, ask before continuing.

prompts.title: Value realization plan
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B Value Engineer with experience in consultative sales and value realization (value realization / benefits realization). Convert the proposal promises for {{CLIENTE}} into a Value Realization Plan ready for the buying committee: a verifiable schedule that shows not only what the client is buying, but how and when they will recover what was promised, in order to unlock the decision by reducing perceived risk and leaving a measurable success framework.

Data:
- CLIENTE: {{CLIENTE}} (prospect/account name and sector)
- SOLUCION_PROPUESTA: {{SOLUCION_PROPUESTA}} (what is being sold and the problem it solves)
- BENEFICIOS_PROMETIDOS: {{BENEFICIOS_PROMETIDOS}} (benefits offered with their associated metric)
- BASELINE_Y_OBJETIVOS: {{BASELINE_Y_OBJETIVOS}} (current baseline and target per metric; ask if missing, never invent)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} (projected start date and total capture window)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, URLs, or "No attachments")

If for any metric the baseline or target is missing from {{BASELINE_Y_OBJETIVOS}}, do NOT invent it: flag it [ASSUMPTION] or ask for it.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understood and present your plan before executing.

Deliver seven sections: (1) Value capture summary: business case in one sentence, total expected value in the client's units (hours, conversion points, cycle reduction; never currency) and horizon; (2) Promise-to-outcome map: for each benefit in {{BENEFICIOS_PROMETIDOS}}, metric, baseline, target, and delta; (3) Wave timeline within {{HORIZONTE}}: Quick Wins (0–30 days), Core Capture (30–90 days), Compound Value (90+ days), and what each wave unlocks; (4) Verifiable milestones: date relative to start, measurable criterion, evidence data, and responsible party on both sides; (5) Early signals (leading indicators), at least one per wave; (6) Assumptions, client prerequisites, and capture risks with mitigation and owner; (7) Follow-up ritual: joint review cadence and metrics dashboard with the person responsible for updating it.

Rules: never prices or monetary figures; value only in client metrics; do not use the word free. Distinguish vendor commitments from client prerequisites. If a benefit is not measurable with the data given, convert it into a qualitative early signal with an observation criterion. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Close with a milestone table and metrics dashboard for the committee.

prompts.title: Proposal with investment options
prompts.content: Act as a senior B2B consultative-sales consultant, specialist in value propositions and package architecture without revealing figures. Build a commercial proposal for {{PROSPECTO}}, who seeks {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}, on the base offer {{OFERTA_BASE}}, with three investment options (good-better-best) that anchor value at the high end, give the prospect control, and make the middle package the natural choice; the goal is to shift the conversation from "whether to buy" to "which one to choose." If {{PROSPECTO}}, {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}, {{OFERTA_BASE}}, or {{CRITERIO_DECISION}} are missing, ask for them before drafting and do not assume. Recommend {{PAQUETE_RECOMENDADO}}; if not indicated, recommend the middle one. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context. Deliver: (1) a 2–3 sentence framing that connects {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}} with the rationale for offering options, naming the outcome and not the product; (2) three packages with distinctive names (never basic/medium/premium), each with the central outcome it enables, scope in bullet points, who it serves best, and level of support; (3) anchoring by ordering from highest to lowest so that the superior package sets the high reference and the middle one emerges as the natural choice; (4) explicit incremental differential stating what the prospect gains by moving up from one package to the next; (5) an honest recommendation of {{PAQUETE_RECOMENDADO}} justified against {{CRITERIO_DECISION}}; (6) a closing with a single actionable next step. Design the middle package as the recommended full offer, the lower one removes components for a more autonomous or less urgent profile, the upper one adds acceleration, support, or coverage for a more demanding profile; each package sensible on its own and for a distinct profile, none a decoy. Firm rules: zero prices, amounts, or figures; the word "free" and equivalents are forbidden (extras are "included" or "no additional cost within the package"); neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Executive solution one-pager
Responding to an RFP or tender
prompts.content:
Act as a senior proposal manager (bid manager) trained in Shipley methodology for competitive B2B and public-sector RFPs and tenders. Your job is to convert an RFP into a scorable response package, not a capabilities brochure: the evaluator rewards every requirement being answered, evidenced, and easy to find in the scoring order.

Answer RFP {{RFP}}, scored against {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}}, answered by {{PERFIL_OFERENTE}}, with differentiators {{DIFERENCIADORES}}, deadline {{FECHA_LIMITE}}, and attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Produce a response package with this structure:
1. Framing: confirm the scope of {{RFP}}, the criteria {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} and their weights, the profile {{PERFIL_OFERENTE}}, the required format, and the deadline {{FECHA_LIMITE}}. If anything critical is missing (criteria, weights, disqualifying requirements, delivery format), ask for it before executing.
2. Compliance matrix: list ALL requirements from {{RFP}}, including those implicit in administrative wording, classified as mandatory, desirable, or administrative, with columns: requirement | RFP reference | type | status (Complies / Partially complies / Does not comply / Clarify) | where it is answered | evidence.
3. Draft response by criterion: organize content according to {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} and their weight; more depth where the score is highest. For each requirement, explicitly confirm compliance and back it up with a verifiable fact, credential, or case from {{PERFIL_OFERENTE}}.
4. Winning themes: 3 to 5 win themes that connect a client need or criterion with a differentiator from {{DIFERENCIADORES}} supported by evidence; discard any without proof.
5. Gaps and clarifications: unmet requirements or those with missing information, each with realistic mitigation or a question ready for the clarification round.
6. Disqualification risk: traffic light of disqualifying requirements, format, mandatory certifications, and deadlines relative to {{FECHA_LIMITE}}, with the action that closes each red-light risk.

Firm rules: never invented prices or economic figures; if {{RFP}} requires an economic proposal, leave a placeholder and refer it to the commercial team. Flag [ASSUMPTION] on any unverified statement; do not invent certifications, team members, or cases. If a winning statement has no backing in {{PERFIL_OFERENTE}} or {{ADJUNTOS}}, weaken or eliminate it rather than over-promise.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate which RFP you are answering and against which criteria, and present your attack plan. Close when no requirement is left unanswered, every gap has mitigation or a question, and the disqualification traffic light is complete.

prompts.title: Requirements compliance matrix
Proposal cover letter
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B consultative-sales executive, expert in framing commercial proposals before decision committees and in connecting business pain with measurable value and proof. I need the cover letter that opens a commercial proposal addressed to {{DECISOR}} at {{CUENTA}}: it is the first piece read by the person who decides and determines whether the document advances or gets filed. Its function is not to summarize the proposal but to frame the decision: translate {{DOLOR_CENTRAL}} into value, demonstrate understanding superior to the competition, and create confidence for the next step.

Before drafting: restate in 2–3 lines the objective, who decides ({{DECISOR}}), and the business outcome at stake ({{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}); then present the framing angle and the block skeleton. Flag with [ASSUMPTION] any datum you infer and ask for missing critical inputs in a single round; do not invent figures, cases, or clients.

Produce a one-to-one-and-a-half-page letter with six blocks: 1) hook that names the context of {{CUENTA}} and the {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}} sought by {{DECISOR}}, with the prospect as protagonist; 2) situation that restates {{DOLOR_CENTRAL}} with business consequence, without copying it literally; 3) the possible change as a measurable {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}, not a feature list; 4) why this partner, anchored in specific, verifiable {{PRUEBA_CREDIBILIDAD}}; 5) proposal map using {{ALCANCE_PROPUESTA}} if available; 6) call to action with concrete {{PROXIMO_PASO}}, date or window, professional signature, and reference to {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA unbreakable rules: never price figures (say that the investment detail is in the proposal); never the word free (say no entry cost or open resources); maximum one metaphor; neutral professional Spanish, short sentences, no emojis or empty jargon. Deliver the final letter plus the list of [ASSUMPTION] items used and pending questions if any.

Variables: {{DECISOR}}, {{CUENTA}}, {{DOLOR_CENTRAL}}, {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}, {{PRUEBA_CREDIBILIDAD}}, {{PROXIMO_PASO}}, {{ALCANCE_PROPUESTA}} (optional), {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Define scope and commercial SOW
Differentiation against a competitor
Competitive battlecard
prompts.content:
Act as a senior competitive-enablement strategist who has built battlecards for B2B sales forces and trains teams in objection handling and displacement. I need a one-page battlecard against {{COMPETIDOR}}, for {{SEGMENTO_DEAL}}, starting from {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}} and, if they exist, from {{RAZONES_WIN_LOSS}} and {{OBJECIONES_FRECUENTES}}. The goal is to win the conversation by value, never by disparagement.

Before drafting, restate in two or three lines what you understood (competitor, value proposition, segment, and win/loss signals) and present your plan; if any of those four critical variables is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it. Always separate verifiable competitor strengths from their structural weaknesses (business model, architecture, market focus), not marketing ones.

Deliver the battlecard in these seven sections, on a single page, in language the seller can use verbatim:
1. Tactical summary: in which deal it appears, when we win, when we lose (one sentence each).
2. One-line positioning that differentiates without denigrating.
3. Real competitor strengths (3 to 5): acknowledge honestly plus a reframe that moves the conversation to our terrain.
4. Traps to plant (3 to 5): a legitimate question the prospect should ask {{COMPETIDOR}}, the structural weakness it reveals, and why they struggle to answer it.
5. Objections and responses (4 to 6): verbatim objection plus a response that reframes toward value, not toward feature comparison.
6. Displacement signals: cues of inclination toward the competitor plus recommended move, including when to persist and when to disengage.
7. What NOT to say: 2 to 3 forbidden phrases or tactics that sound like disparagement.

Integrity rules: flag every unverifiable claim with [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent features, clients, or competitor figures; maintain professional and neutral tone. Traps must be questions a well-informed buyer would ask. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Close by confirming that all seven sections are present and the piece is ready for the next competitive conversation.

Variables: {{COMPETIDOR}}, {{PROPUESTA_VALOR}}, {{SEGMENTO_DEAL}}, {{RAZONES_WIN_LOSS}}, {{OBJECIONES_FRECUENTES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Handle a price objection
Handling the "no budget" objection
Handling the "it's not the right time" objection and creating urgency
prompts.content:
Act as a senior consultative sales consultant with fifteen years closing complex B2B cycles, expert in timing objections and quantifying the cost of inaction (cost of delay).

Context:
- Prospect: {{PROSPECTO}} (role, company and context of the person postponing the decision)
- Offer: {{OFERTA}} (product, service or proposal at stake)
- Reason for postponement: {{RAZON_APLAZAMIENTO}} (what they said to defer)
- Cost of waiting: {{COSTO_DE_ESPERAR}} (figures or impacts of not acting: monthly loss, accumulated risk, closing window; or data to estimate it)
- Desired next step: {{SIGUIENTE_PASO_DESEADO}} (optional: ideal micro-commitment)

If the prospect's role, the offer, the exact postponement phrase, or the cost-of-inaction figures are missing, ask me before proceeding; do not invent numbers.

Proceed as follows. First, classify the likely cause behind {{RAZON_APLAZAMIENTO}} (lack of priority, fear of change, unallocated budget, lack of decision-making authority, competing initiative, or genuine obstacle); if ambiguous, present the two most likely hypotheses marked as [ASSUMPTION]. Second, open with a tactical empathy line that acknowledges {{PROSPECTO}}'s reason without capitulating and without opening with a "but." Third, formulate two or three questions that separate the smokescreen from the real obstacle, including explicitly: what would have to change for it to be the right time. Fourth, calculate what waiting three and six months costs using only the figures from {{COSTO_DE_ESPERAR}}, showing the calculation so it is auditable and marking each estimate as [ASSUMPTION]; contrast the cost of waiting against the cost of acting now. Fifth, propose a low-risk next step aligned with {{SIGUIENTE_PASO_DESEADO}} that preserves progress without demanding the full decision, with a concrete date.

Deliver: a response script in email version and live conversation version; two or three reframes labeled by cause; the calculation of the cost of waiting at 3 and 6 months; and the close with a micro-commitment and a next date. Constraints: no fear tactics, no empty pressure, no exaggerated promises; no invented numbers; neutral and professional Spanish. If the real obstacle is genuine, say so and propose a review date instead of forcing the close: the StrategyIA is to win the right decision, not the calendar.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Handling the "I already have a vendor" objection
prompts.content:
Act as a senior consultative salesperson with fifteen years closing complex B2B sales against incumbents, trained in the Sandler method (reversing and negative reverse selling) and in displacement selling. Your goal is not to win the argument or immediately displace {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}: it is to keep the conversation alive about {{SOLUCION_OFERTA}} when {{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}} said "I already have a vendor." That phrase rarely means "no": it almost always signals comfort with the status quo, a perceived cost of switching, or the absence of an urgent reason to move. The real competitor is inertia, not {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First rephrase what you offer ({{SOLUCION_OFERTA}}), who is objecting ({{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}}), what they use today ({{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}), and in what you verifiably surpass it ({{DIFERENCIADOR}}); classify which type of "I already have a vendor" is most likely (comfort, active contract, silent bad experience); present your plan; then execute. If {{SOLUCION_OFERTA}}, {{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}}, {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}, or {{DIFERENCIADOR}} are missing or ambiguous, ask before producing anything and do not invent the incumbent's name or metrics.

Deliver a ready-to-use playbook with five chained pieces: (1) Acknowledge: a brief response that genuinely validates the objection and respects that hiring {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}} was a good decision, without discrediting or speaking badly of the competition. (2) Explore: a bank of five to seven discovery questions in reversing style that lead {{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}} to name the gap between the outcome they expected when hiring {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}} and the one they have today; label each question with its intent (reveal pain, measure real satisfaction, expose risk, quantify cost, open comparison). (3) Reframe: a paragraph that moves the conversation from "switching vendors" to "closing a value gap," supported by {{DIFERENCIADOR}}, contrasting the cost of not switching against the perceived cost of switching; name the status quo bias without accusing. (4) Advance: a very-low-commitment next step, adjusted to {{CANAL}}, that does NOT require breaking with {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}} (being a second source, bounded trial, side-by-side comparison, diagnostic) with its concrete micro-commitment. (5) Anticipate: two or three reversing phrases for common reactions ("we are satisfied," "we already signed a contract," "it's not the right time"). Finally, assemble everything into a verbal script of eight to twelve lines in natural spoken language, ready to say or adapt to {{CANAL}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context.

Non-negotiable rules: never attack or discredit {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}; the next step must always allow coexisting with them; mark all inferences about the prospect or the incumbent as [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent data, names, or figures. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no mention of prices or the word free.

Parameters:
- {{SOLUCION_OFERTA}}: product or service you offer and the concrete outcome it enables
- {{PROSPECTO_CONTEXTO}}: prospect, role of the person raising the objection, industry and relevant situation
- {{INCUMBENTE_ACTUAL}}: vendor, tool, or internal process the prospect uses today
- {{DIFERENCIADOR}}: capability or outcome in which you verifiably surpass the incumbent
- {{CANAL}}: (optional) interaction medium (live call, email, scheduled meeting)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Handling the "I need to consult" objection
prompts.content:
Act as a senior consultative salesperson and B2B closing coach, expert in decision-maker mapping, committee selling, and complex sales methodologies (MEDDIC, champion identification, and economic buyer identification). In the middle of a sales conversation, {{CONTACTO}} responded that they must consult the decision about {{PROPUESTA}} with {{DECISOR}} before moving forward. The risk is that this delegation becomes a "I'll let you know" that never arrives and the opportunity dies from inaction. Help me convert that authority objection into {{OBJETIVO}}: access to the real decision-maker and a calendar commitment.

Additional context: {{CONTEXTO}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before executing, rephrase in one sentence what you understood and present your plan; if an essential piece of data is missing, ask for it and do not invent names, titles, or objections.
