First, a stakeholder map: for each person in {{COMITE_INTERESADOS}}, indicate their decision role (economic, technical, user, financial, champion, or blocker), stated interest, underlying real interest, level of power and influence (high/medium/low), and current stance (in favor/neutral/against). Second, a tension map: where one stakeholder's interest clashes with another's and where common ground exists that can be used as a lever; flag at least one real conflict and one area of common ground. Third, the Mutual Gains Strategy: define your BATNA from {{POSICION_Y_LIMITES}}, estimate the counterpart's probable BATNA, rank negotiable variables by cost to you and value to them, and build a conditioned concession script where every concession is tied to an explicit counterpart (never give anything away). Fourth, an action plan: a sequence of conversations from lowest to highest risk, a message and argument per stakeholder, a tactic to neutralize the blocker, a plan to convert the champion into an internal ally, two or three drift warning signals, and how to lock in commitments in writing, taking into account {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Work only with value, scope, timeline, and terms variables; never propose prices or economic figures. If {{ADJUNTOS}} provides emails, meeting notes, or the committee org chart, use it to infer real interests and stances. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it.

prompts.title: Protecting margin under pressure
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B negotiator with fifteen years closing complex accounts, expert in value selling, margin defense, and the conditioned exchange method. I am defending the margin of {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}} against {{CLIENTE}}, who demands {{DESCUENTO_EXIGIDO}} and pushes back with a possible exit or a cheaper competitor; the apparent trigger is {{DETONANTE_PRESION}} and I need to sustain {{MARGEN_OBJETIVO}} without blindly conceding on price or breaking the relationship. If any piece of data is incomplete or ambiguous, ask before moving forward and label everything you infer with [ASSUMPTION].

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Give me a one-page negotiation plan, actionable for the next meeting, with: (1) Diagnosis that separates without mixing the four pressure causes starting from {{DETONANTE_PRESION}} (real budget, buying tactic, insufficient value perception, competitive comparison), with one diagnostic question per cause to confirm which dominates. (2) Value re-anchoring that moves the conversation from price to total cost and economic impact of {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, with at least one quantified argument (savings, revenue, risk avoided, time) and the assumptions behind the figure. (3) A table of 4 to 6 conditioned exchanges that protect {{MARGEN_OBJETIVO}}, ordered from lowest to highest margin cost, with no price concession without an explicit counterpart (volume, term, upfront payment, scope, reference, success story, multi-year renewal), marking reversible vs. irreversible. (4) Script for the four typical objections (it is too expensive / the competitor charges less / there is no budget / one more point and we close) with technique, model phrase, and next move. (5) Limits: floor relative to {{MARGEN_OBJETIVO}}, withdrawal point with BATNA, and signals to escalate or pause. Consider edge cases: sole supplier or technical lock-in, quarter-end, and procurement vs. economic buyer. Close with the recommended opening for the meeting. Neutral professional Spanish; never invented price figures or the word free: reason in margin, counterparts, and relative value.

prompts.title: Post-meeting commercial follow-up email
Nurturing sequence to mature a not-ready lead
App brief from a single sentence to an executable spec
PRD-lite for an AI-built MVP
prompts.content:
Act as a senior product manager specialized in AI-guided MVPs, with experience translating fuzzy problems into actionable contracts for code agents. Your task is to produce a PRD-lite: a one-page document that acts as a stable contract between the product vision and a code agent that will build the MVP. Without this contract the agent infers scope, over-builds, and diverts the MVP from the real problem; well delimited, the agent knows what to solve, for whom, and above all what NOT to do.

Product: {{PRODUCTO}}
Problem: {{PROBLEMA}}
Target user: {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}}
Key jobs: {{JOBS_CLAVE}}
Out of scope: {{FUERA_DE_ALCANCE}}
Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Phase 1 Interpret: restate {{PROBLEMA}} and {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}} in your own words, and list the jobs you detect in {{JOBS_CLAVE}}. If {{PROBLEMA}}, {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}}, or {{JOBS_CLAVE}} arrive empty or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing; do not invent a domain.
Phase 2 Plan: present the section order and a traceability table where each job maps to a capability in the scope and, when applicable, to a non-goal derived from {{FUERA_DE_ALCANCE}}. Wait for confirmation.
Phase 3 Execute: draft the complete PRD-lite with these numbered sections:
1. Problem: one sentence with the real pain and why it matters now, without a hidden solution.
2. Target user: who suffers it, in what context, and with what technical level; never 'everyone'.
3. Jobs-to-be-done: 3 to 5 jobs in the format 'when [situation], I want [motivation], so that [expected result]', derived from {{JOBS_CLAVE}}, ordered by priority.
4. MVP scope: minimum list of capabilities that cover the priority jobs; each one traces to a job, nothing orphaned.
5. Non-goals: what stays out starting from {{FUERA_DE_ALCANCE}}, each with its rationale, to stop the agent's scope creep.
6. Success criteria: 2 or 3 observable and measurable signals; no invented metrics, label [ASSUMPTION] on any unconfirmed threshold.
7. Assumptions and constraints: technical or business; label [ASSUMPTION] on everything not confirmed.
8. Interpretation risks for the agent: 2 or 3 points where the agent might over-build or misinterpret, with the decision that settles each ambiguity.

Edge cases: if {{JOBS_CLAVE}} exceeds 5 jobs, trim to the 5 of highest value and send the rest to non-goals with their rationale. If two jobs compete for priority, declare the tiebreaker criterion. If {{FUERA_DE_ALCANCE}} arrives empty, infer non-goals from the discarded jobs and label [ASSUMPTION]. If {{ADJUNTOS}} brings material, use it to sharpen context, not to expand scope.

Close: the PRD-lite fits on one page, without filler, ready to paste as the initial context for the code agent. Do not mention prices.

prompts.title: Feature decomposition into codeable stories
Definition of Ready and Done for an AI session
Justified technology stack selection
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software architect who has chosen and operated multiple stacks in production under team, timeline, and cost constraints, and who decides by evidence and context fit rather than trend. I want to choose the technology stack for {{PROYECTO}} and be able to defend each choice before my team and stakeholders, because a stack poorly fitted to {{RESTRICCIONES}} is paid for in time, operational cost, and rewrites. A justified selection with a tradeoffs matrix turns an opinionated decision into a traceable one and unblocks the foundational ADR and effort estimation.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, rephrase in your own words {{PROYECTO}} and {{REQUISITOS_CLAVE}}, derive the dominant quality attributes, treat {{RESTRICCIONES}} as non-negotiable limits, and present your plan. If a piece of data is missing that would change the decision, ask for it before moving forward.

Deliverable, in this order:
1. Verifiable framing: {{PROYECTO}} and {{REQUISITOS_CLAVE}} rephrased, dominant quality attributes prioritized (the 1 to 3 that govern everything) and {{RESTRICCIONES}} as non-negotiable limits. List the missing data that blocks the decision.
2. Weighted criteria: set criteria from {{CRITERIOS_DECISION}} and assign each a relative weight summing to 100 percent; if not provided, propose them and mark as assumption.
3. For each applicable layer (language, backend framework, frontend if applicable, database and data model, messaging or queues if applicable, hosting and infrastructure, authentication, observability, CI/CD) propose 2 to 3 real candidates and build the matrix: rows equal candidates, columns equal weighted criteria, cell equals score 1 to 5 with verifiable rationale, plus the weighted sum. Consider total cost of ownership: learning curve, ecosystem and hiring, maturity and support, and exit cost or lock-in.
4. Context-prioritized recommendation per layer: primary, backup, and conservative if risk is high. Explain why the primary wins given {{RESTRICCIONES}} and name the accepted tradeoff.
5. Full-stack coherence: verify interoperability and total operational complexity; flag friction between layers.
6. Validation plan: the minimum spike that confirms or refutes the riskiest choice, with success criterion; and the objective signals (metrics, thresholds) that would force a reconsideration of the stack.
7. Close: one-line summary per layer and residual risks with mitigations.

Rules: never fabricate benchmarks or figures; if you cite a data point, make it verifiable or mark it as an assumption. Do not recommend based on popularity. Distinguish hard constraint from preference. Ready to underpin a foundational ADR.

Parameters:
- {{PROYECTO}}: name and one-or-two-line description of the software to build and who it serves.
- {{REQUISITOS_CLAVE}}: main functional requirements and quality attributes that matter most (e.g., low latency, scale to X users, ship in N weeks, low operational cost).
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: hard limits (team skills, timeline, operational budget, existing ecosystem or systems, compliance, self-hosted vs. managed).
- {{CRITERIOS_DECISION}}: criteria for weighting options and their relative priority (optional; if missing, the architect proposes them and marks them as assumption).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Routes and pages map before coding
Conceptual data model from requirements
API-first contract (API-first)
Non-goals and out-of-scope for the MVP
prompts.content:
Act as a senior product engineer expert at delimiting MVP scope and writing scope guards for coding agents. I am about to start vibe coding {{PRODUCTO_MVP}} for {{USUARIO_PRIMARIO}}, whose core action is {{ACCION_CENTRAL}}. I need a scope document that shields the MVP against scope creep BEFORE generating a single line: the real risk is not what I forget to ask for, but what the agent adds on its own (complex authentication, admin panels, optimizations, integrations, edge cases) that inflates the MVP and delays the first usable version.

First rephrase in your own words the product, the primary user, and the core action; if any are missing or ambiguous, ask before continuing — don't assume. Then present your plan in one sentence and proceed.

Deliver a markdown document with these sections: (1) MVP Objectives: 3 to 5 user-observable capabilities, each traceable to {{ACCION_CENTRAL}}. (2) Non-goals: 6 to 12 exclusions grouped into five categories (deferred functionality, premature technical perfection, premature scale and performance, external integrations, edge cases and rare states); integrate {{EXCLUSIONES_CONOCIDAS}} where applicable; each non-goal carries what is excluded, why it is deferred, and the concrete signal that reopens it — using {{HORIZONTE_RECONSIDERACION}} as a reference — making it a 'not yet' and not a 'never'. (3) Agent guards: 5 to 8 imperative and verifiable rules, pasteable as-is into the system prompt (e.g.: do not add social login; do not create tables outside those listed; if a task requires touching something out of scope, stop and ask). (4) Gray areas: 3 to 5 decisions that are not clearly in or out and require my explicit confirmation before coding. (5) Scope Definition of Done: one line declaring when the document is complete and approved.

Rules: define non-goals by contrast with what IS included, never in the abstract. Do not include prices or monetary amounts. Mark any inference of yours as [ASSUMPTION]. If a guard is not checkable by the agent without interpreting, rewrite it until it is. If I provide {{ADJUNTOS}}, use them as input and indicate what you took from each one.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Parameters: {{PRODUCTO_MVP}}, {{USUARIO_PRIMARIO}}, {{ACCION_CENTRAL}}, {{EXCLUSIONES_CONOCIDAS}}, {{HORIZONTE_RECONSIDERACION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Early technical risk inventory
Greenfield project scaffold with AI
prompts.content:
Act as a senior platform engineer specializing in bootstrapping and developer experience, with idiomatic judgment per ecosystem. I need the complete and executable scaffold of a greenfield project that is clone-and-run from the first commit and passes lint, build, and test empty before the first feature.

Parameters:
- STACK: {{STACK}} (main language and framework, e.g., Node + Fastify, Python + FastAPI, standard Go, React + Vite)
- TIPO_PROYECTO: {{TIPO_PROYECTO}} (API, web app, CLI, library, monorepo)
- GESTOR_PAQUETES: {{GESTOR_PAQUETES}} (e.g., pnpm, npm, uv, poetry, go mod)
- VERSION_RUNTIME: {{VERSION_RUNTIME}} (e.g., Node 22 LTS, Python 3.12)
- CONVENCIONES: {{CONVENCIONES}} (optional; style, naming, or layout rules; if empty, use the stack's idiomatic convention)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, URLs, or "No attachments")

Before generating, rephrase what you understood and present your plan. If STACK, TIPO_PROYECTO, GESTOR_PAQUETES, or VERSION_RUNTIME are missing or ambiguous, ask me before and don't assume a default stack.

Deliver in a single block copyable to an empty folder: (1) complete tree with a one-line comment per folder; (2) each config with real and commented content: {{GESTOR_PAQUETES}} manifest with dependencies pinned to exact version and runtime separated from development, linter, formatter, type config if {{STACK}} uses it, example environment variables without real secrets, VCS ignore covering artifacts, dependencies, and environment, plus .editorconfig and runtime version pin in file if applicable; (3) install/dev/build/test/lint/format scripts with the exact {{GESTOR_PAQUETES}} command; (4) minimal README with requirements, installation, and startup; (5) ordered command sequence from an empty folder.

Pin exact versions, don't include unused dependencies, justify in one line each non-obvious dependency, respect {{CONVENCIONES}} if given, and mark with [ASSUMPTION] every decision you made on my behalf. Include a startup health note (command confirming compile + test empty) and close by reviewing against a quality checklist.

prompts.title: Monorepo vs. polyrepo decision and setup
prompts.content: Act as a senior platform architect who has set up and migrated repository structures (monorepo with pnpm/Turborepo/Nx and polyrepo with published packages) in product teams. I am starting {{PROYECTO}} and the first structural decision conditions speed, CI, ownership, and cost of change for years: monorepo (one repository with workspaces and an internal dependency graph) or polyrepo (one repository per service or package with versioning and publishing between them). Data: the apps and services are {{APPS_Y_SERVICIOS}}; the shared code is {{CODIGO_COMPARTIDO}}; the release coupling is {{ACOPLAMIENTO_RELEASE}}; the team is {{EQUIPO}}; the stack and manager are {{STACK_GESTOR}}; the constraints are {{RESTRICCIONES_CI}}; attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{APPS_Y_SERVICIOS}}, {{CODIGO_COMPARTIDO}}, {{ACOPLAMIENTO_RELEASE}}, or {{STACK_GESTOR}} are missing or ambiguous, ask before deciding; don't silently assume. Then: (1) apply a weighted criteria matrix with shared code coupling, release cadence and independence, cross-cutting change atomicity, tooling and CI overhead, governance and ownership, and scale and build times, with weight and per-option score; (2) recommend monorepo or polyrepo deriving the decision from the matrix, not from preference, with accepted tradeoffs written out and at least one trigger condition that would invalidate it; (3) mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; (4) generate scaffolding coherent with the decision: complete tree, workspace manager configuration (pnpm-workspace.yaml, turbo.json, or nx.json for monorepo; semantic versioning convention plus a published shared package and its release flow for polyrepo), an example shared types or utilities package with its manifest, root-level build/test/lint scripts, runtime and manager pin, and an aligned CI skeleton (single pipeline with affected filter and cache for monorepo; per-repo pipelines with release trigger for polyrepo); (5) deliver exact copyable commands to create everything from scratch, idempotent when possible, and a bidirectional migration note (mono to poly and poly to mono) preserving history without rewriting everything. Cover edge cases: a single service with no shared code, compliance requiring per-repo permission isolation, and polyglot stacks where the workspace manager doesn't cover all languages. Deliver document with matrix and recommendation, tree, workspace or versioning configs plus example shared package, root scripts and CI skeleton, copyable commands, and migration note. Neutral and professional English, no emojis. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Reproducible local environment setup
Agent context file (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior platform engineer specializing in coding agents and developer experience, with the ability to distill a repository into minimal operational instructions. Generate {{NOMBRE_ARCHIVO}}: the context file that a coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or other) reads at startup in the repository {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}} to operate with judgment from the very first turn, without repeating basic questions, guessing commands, or breaking conventions.

Proceed in four phases and apply the MetodologIA Protocol before drafting: Interpret what you understand, plan and present the plan, and only then execute.

Phase 1 - Inspection: read the repository's real manifests and configuration files (package.json, pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, Cargo.toml, go.mod, Makefile, Taskfile, README, Dockerfile, and the CI configuration) and cross-reference them with {{STACK}} and {{COMANDOS}}. Derive the stack, versions, and true commands. Mark each command as verified or pending.

Phase 2 - Gap resolution: anything not in the repository or in the inputs, ask for specifically. Never invent commands, versions, paths, or conventions. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] everything you assume and make explicit how to confirm it.

Phase 3 - Drafting: write {{NOMBRE_ARCHIVO}} in Markdown, in the imperative, actionable and concise, linking the README rather than duplicating it, with these sections: 1) Purpose in one line from {{PROPOSITO}}. 2) Stack and versions from {{STACK}}, verified against manifests. 3) Essential commands (install, run, test, lint, build, typecheck if applicable) from {{COMANDOS}}, each copyable, executable, and confirmed. 4) Relevant directory map with one line of purpose per folder. 5) Code and commit conventions from {{CONVENCIONES}}. 6) Branch and Pull Request flow with merge gates. 7) Explicit limits and prohibitions from {{PROHIBICIONES}} (secrets, generated files, migrations, protected branches). 8) Definition of Done as a closing checklist.

Phase 4 - Verification: confirm that every command is copyable, prohibitions are unambiguous, there are no internal contradictions, and the file stands as the single context source.

Edge cases to cover: monorepo (commands per package or workspace), no tests or lint (declare 'not configured'), multiple package managers (declare the canonical one), README vs. manifest contradiction (manifest wins, leave a note). Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it adds context. Deliver a single {{NOMBRE_ARCHIVO}} in Markdown ready to commit in the repository root. If any critical input is missing, ask before generating.

Inputs:
- {{NOMBRE_ARCHIVO}}: name of the context file (e.g., CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md)
- {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}: repository or product name
- {{PROPOSITO}}: what the project does, in one line
- {{STACK}}: languages, frameworks, package manager, and versions
- {{COMANDOS}}: known install, run, test, lint, and build commands (optional)
- {{CONVENCIONES}}: code style, formatter, commit format, and branch format (optional)
- {{PROHIBICIONES}}: what the agent must NOT touch: secrets, generated files, migrations, protected branches (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Initial code conventions and linters
Scalable feature-based folder structure
Minimal design system bootstrap
prompts.content: Act as a senior design systems engineer, specializing in design tokens and accessible UI primitive libraries. I want the scaffold of a minimal design system for {{PROJECT}} on {{STACK}}, starting from {{BRAND_BASE}} and supporting {{THEME_MODES}}, so that every screen I generate afterward inherits the same visual language without diverging hard-coded styles. Deliver it in three chained layers. Layer 1, tokens: first define a raw scale (numeric palette 50–900 derived from {{BRAND_BASE}}, modular typographic ramp, base-4 spacing units, radii, shadows, breakpoints) and on top the semantic roles (background, surface, text, muted-text, border, primary and its contrast, success, warning, danger, focus); expose everything simultaneously as CSS variables and as a typed theme object consumable by code. Layer 2, primitives: implement {{PRIMITIVES}} referencing exclusively semantic roles, zero raw values, with their variants and hover, focus, active, error, and disabled states, documenting in a comment what each one covers. Layer 3, theme and startup: resolve {{THEME_MODES}} by reassigning the role values (not by duplicating components) and deliver a ready-to-import entry file that leaves the system operational. Hard rule: no primitive touches a raw value, only roles. If {{BRAND_BASE}} says 'define from scratch' or any data is missing, propose a base and confirm it before generating. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any default you adopt and propose it as adjustable. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Close with: the three-layer code consistent with {{STACK}}, a brief note on how to add a new component or token without breaking coherence, and a verified accessibility checklist. Parameters: {{PROJECT}}, {{STACK}}, {{BRAND_BASE}}, {{PRIMITIVES}}, {{THEME_MODES}}, {{ATTACHMENTS}}.

prompts.title: Realistic test data seed
prompts.content: Act as a senior data engineer specializing in fixtures, rapid prototyping, and coherent synthetic data design. I need a realistic seed dataset in {{OUTPUT_FORMAT}}, ready to load into {{STACK}}, to iterate on the interface, validate flows, and demo the application without waiting for the real backend. Before generating, restate what you understand of {{DATA_MODEL}} and present your plan; ask for anything missing and do not invent the structure. Proceed as follows: 1) Map {{DATA_MODEL}}: entities, type of each field, optional fields, and relationships with cardinality and foreign keys. 2) Fix generation order by dependencies (parents before children) and a reproducible randomness seed. 3) Generate plausible values by type: plausible names and texts in neutral Spanish, emails and phones with valid format, dates in logical sequence (created <= updated, no incoherent futures), amounts and enumerations within their domain; vary values to avoid identical rows. 4) Produce {{RECORDS_PER_ENTITY}} per entity and connect each foreign key to an existing record so none is left orphaned and cardinality is believable (not all children hanging from one parent). 5) Inject {{EDGE_CASES}}: at least one record with empty optionals, one with long text, one with an infrequent state, values at the edges of each range, and, if applicable, special characters/unicode. Label each case. 6) Serialize in {{OUTPUT_FORMAT}} and add a brief note on how to load the seed in {{STACK}} and how to reset it. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] anything you infer. Verify before delivering: zero broken foreign keys, edge cases present, dates and enumerations coherent, volume fulfilled. No real PII. Parameters: {{DATA_MODEL}}, {{RECORDS_PER_ENTITY}}, {{EDGE_CASES}}, {{OUTPUT_FORMAT}}, {{STACK}}, {{ATTACHMENTS}}.

prompts.title: Issue and PR templates for AI workflows
Git initialization with .gitignore and hooks
prompts.content:
Act as a senior platform engineer specializing in repository hygiene and version control with git, with hands-on practice in reproducible project initialization, pre-commit hooks, and branch protection on GitHub and GitLab.

I am starting {{PROJECT}} in {{STACK}} and need to found the version control from the first commit, before the pace of work scales the disorder. The goal is that no secret, build artifact, or broken code ever enters the history, and that {{MAIN_BRANCH}} is protected so every change goes through a pull request in {{REMOTE_PLATFORM}}. If any data is missing, ask me before continuing; do not invent paths or names.

Deliver a ready-to-run initialization guide, structured as follows:
1. Framing: confirm {{STACK}}, package manager, {{REMOTE_PLATFORM}}, and name of {{MAIN_BRANCH}}; mark [ASSUMPTION] for every path or name you infer.
2. Initialization: exact commands for git init, setting {{MAIN_BRANCH}}, configuring the remote with a placeholder instead of the real URL, and creating the initial commit with a conventional message (e.g. chore: initial scaffold).
3. .gitignore: stack-specific file for {{STACK}} that excludes dependencies, build artifacts, environment files with secrets (.env and variants), caches, and editor or OS files; comment each block with its reason.
4. Pre-commit hooks: configuration of a recognized manager for {{STACK}} (pre-commit for Python, husky with lint-staged for Node, or equivalent) that runs {{VALIDATIONS}} only on staged files, with a fallback if the tool is not installed.
5. Protection of {{MAIN_BRANCH}}: rules in {{REMOTE_PLATFORM}} in UI steps and in CLI command where available (e.g. gh api or glab), requiring a pull request, at least one approved review, and green checks before merging.
6. First-clean-commit and protected-branch verification checklist.

Rules: .env and its variants are always excluded with an explicit warning not to version secrets; use placeholders instead of real credentials or tokens; each block carries a comment explaining its reason. If you detect that a secret was already committed, warn that rotating it and rewriting history are mandatory.

Parameters:
- {{PROJECT}}: name or brief description of the project to version.
- {{STACK}}: tech stack and package manager (e.g. Node with pnpm, Python with uv, Go with modules).
- {{REMOTE_PLATFORM}}: remote platform (GitHub, GitLab, or other).
- {{MAIN_BRANCH}}: name of the main branch to protect (main by default).
- {{VALIDATIONS}}: validations to enforce in pre-commit (format, lint, secret scanning; optional).
- {{ATTACHMENTS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Spec optimized for Claude Code
Cursor rules (.cursorrules) per project
prompts.content:
Act as a senior platform engineer specializing in code agent tooling and Cursor configuration (.cursor/rules/*.mdc modern and .cursorrules legacy). I need a project rules file for Cursor, ready to save without additional editing, that prevents the agent from drifting: inventing APIs, ignoring conventions, rewriting entire files, or touching forbidden zones.

Project data:
- PROJECT_AND_DOMAIN: {{PROJECT_AND_DOMAIN}} (name, what it does and who it serves, one or two lines)
- STACK_AND_VERSIONS: {{STACK_AND_VERSIONS}} (languages, framework, package manager, runtime and database with fixed versions)
- CONVENTIONS: {{CONVENTIONS}} (names, folder structure, allowed/prohibited patterns, error handling, typing)
- QUALITY_COMMANDS: {{QUALITY_COMMANDS}} (exact lint, test, and build commands that must pass before closing a change)
- LIMITS_AND_FORBIDDEN: {{LIMITS_AND_FORBIDDEN}} (secrets, environment variables, applied migrations, folders or paths the agent must never touch)
- ATTACHMENTS: {{ATTACHMENTS}} (attached files, URLs, or 'No attachments')

If STACK_AND_VERSIONS, CONVENTIONS, or QUALITY_COMMANDS are empty or ambiguous, ask me before drafting and do not invent versions, commands, or paths.

Protocol: first restate in one or two lines what you understood and present your plan; then execute.

Deliver a single file with seven numbered sections: (1) Project context from PROJECT_AND_DOMAIN; (2) Stack and versions from STACK_AND_VERSIONS, with versions explicitly fixed; (3) Code conventions from CONVENTIONS; (4) Rules for the agent: edit only what was requested, do not rewrite entire files without permission, propose a plan before large changes, cite real paths, do not invent dependencies or APIs, prefer minimal diffs; (5) Tests and quality using QUALITY_COMMANDS, with minimum coverage and the requirement that lint, test, and build pass; (6) Boundaries and security from LIMITS_AND_FORBIDDEN: never touch secrets or environment variables, do not make network calls without being asked, do not modify applied migrations, respect forbidden folders; (7) Response format: comment language, diff granularity, when to ask instead of assume.

Each rule actionable, concrete, and verifiable; no vague generalities. Deliver the content in a block ready for .cursor/rules/<name>.mdc with frontmatter (description and globs when applicable) and indicate how to also save it as a legacy .cursorrules in the repo root.

prompts.title: Prompt for generating UI in Vercel v0
prompts.content: Act as a senior frontend engineer specializing in design systems, React with TypeScript, and writing prompts for Vercel v0. Draft a single prose prompt block, ready to paste into v0, that describes {{COMPONENT}} for {{TARGET_USER}} and produces usable code with minimal iterations. Before drafting, restate what you understand and your plan; if essential data is missing, ask for it and do not invent the scope. The block must cover, in this order and without explanatory text around it: (1) intent line: what {{COMPONENT}} is and what it does; (2) anatomy: visible elements from top to bottom with hierarchy; (3) states: each of {{STATES}} described separately, including applicable edge states (long list, truncated text, single element); (4) interactions: hover, focus, click, submit, validations, and optimistic feedback as applicable; (5) example data: typed properties with realistic domain values, no generic placeholders; (6) style: aligned to {{VISUAL_REFERENCE}}, light and dark mode, shadcn/ui plus Tailwind if it fits; (7) constraints: {{TECH_CONSTRAINTS}} plus React with TypeScript, Tailwind, responsive mobile-first, and accessibility (ARIA, keyboard, visible focus, AA contrast); (8) acceptance criterion: one verifiable sentence. Do not introduce unauthorized dependencies; prefer composing small components; mark as [ASSUMPTION] every scope decision made due to missing data. If {{ATTACHMENTS}} exist, use them as brand or structure reference. Close by pointing out the 2 or 3 spots where v0 will likely improvise so the user reviews those first. Variables: {{COMPONENT}} (component or screen to generate), {{TARGET_USER}} (for whom and in what context), {{STATES}} (states to render), {{VISUAL_REFERENCE}} (visual tone or reference system), {{TECH_CONSTRAINTS}} (non-negotiable technical limits), {{ATTACHMENTS}} (files, URLs, or 'No attachments').

prompts.title: Prompt for building an app in Lovable
prompts.content:
Act as a senior full-stack product engineer specializing in Lovable, React, and Supabase, with expertise in schema design and row-level security (Row Level Security). Your output is a single structured technical brief, in numbered sections, written as direct instructions to Lovable, ready to paste and start guided construction.

App idea: {{APP_IDEA}}. Target audience: {{TARGET_AUDIENCE}}. Main data entities: {{DATA_ENTITIES}}. Access and roles: {{AUTH_AND_ROLES}}. Critical flow that cannot fail: {{CRITICAL_FLOW}}. Attachments: {{ATTACHMENTS}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in your own words the app, its user, and the outcome it seeks; present your section plan; then execute. If an indispensable piece of data is missing (the main data entity, the role that decides permissions, or the rule of the critical flow that cannot fail), ask for it before drafting; do not invent business rules.

Produce the brief with these sections:
1. Product and scope: one product sentence derived from {{APP_IDEA}}, plus the explicit first-version scope separating what is in from what is out, to prevent feature creep.
2. Pages and navigation: each page or view with its purpose, key components, and navigation links; mark each route as public or protected and describe the redirect when a user without a session hits a protected route.
3. Data model: based on {{DATA_ENTITIES}}, each table with columns, types, primary key, foreign keys, relationships, uniqueness constraints, and audit fields (created/updated, owner). For each table, at least one Row Level Security policy coherent with the roles; enable RLS by default and explicitly declare any public-read table.
4. Authentication and roles: apply the method per {{AUTH_AND_ROLES}}, define roles and a permissions matrix per role covering the four verbs (view, create, edit, delete) per entity; specify how routes are protected on the frontend and queries on the backend.
5. States and flows: detail {{CRITICAL_FLOW}} step by step, plus empty, loading, and error states for each view with data, and form validations per field (required, format, limits).
6. Edge cases and decisions: list assumed assumptions, design decisions with their justification and trade-off, and the edge cases the first version handles versus those it explicitly defers.
7. Implementation order: sequential milestones (schema and RLS first, then auth, then pages, then state polish), with a verifiable acceptance criterion per milestone.

Closing criterion: no page without backing data, no orphaned table unused in any page, RLS active on every table with user data, the permissions matrix complete, the critical flow with its three edge states, and zero time promises. Consider {{ATTACHMENTS}} if they add context. Neutral professional Spanish. Deliverable: self-contained brief in numbered sections, ready to paste into Lovable.

prompts.title: Prompt for prototyping in Bolt.new
prompts.content:
Act as a senior frontend engineer specializing in rapid prototyping with Bolt.new and in designing specs for AI code generators. I need to convert {{IDEA_PRODUCTO}} for {{USUARIO_OBJETIVO}} into a specification precise enough that Bolt.new generates a navigable, populated, and demonstrable prototype on the first attempt, without setting up infrastructure, so it can be validated with users or stakeholders.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate in your own words the idea, the target user, and the minimum navigable scope; list your assumptions tagged [ASSUMPTION] and the critical gaps; present your plan. If an essential entity, screen, or rule is missing for the prototype to hold together, ask me rather than inventing it.

Deliver the specification in six numbered sections:
1. One-line prototype summary: what it is and what it unlocks for validation.
2. Exact stack and dependencies from {{STACK}}; if omitted use React + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind; justify any extra library and prefer zero backend dependencies.
3. Data model with TypeScript types consistent with {{IDEA_PRODUCTO}}: entities, fields, types, optionality, and relationships.
4. Screens from {{PANTALLAS}}: each with its purpose, route, components, states (loading, empty, error, success), and interaction behavior.
5. Seed data from {{DATOS_EJEMPLO}} that populates the app on open covering the normal case and one edge; if none are provided, generate a realistic set tagged [ASSUMPTION].
6. Final consolidated prompt in a single block ready to paste into Bolt.new, integrating stack, persistence ({{PERSISTENCIA}}), screens, rules ({{REGLAS_CLAVE}}) with their UI trigger, empty state, and seed data.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as a reference for scope or style. Close only when the final prompt fits in a self-contained pasteable block, the stack is compatible with Bolt.new, the model covers all entities on the screens, every screen declares behavior and states, persistence works without a backend when applicable, every rule has a verifiable UI trigger, and essential gaps have been asked about.

prompts.title: Prompt for Replit Agent end-to-end
Tool comparison for choosing the right one
Code handoff between AI tools
prompts.content:
Act as a senior platform engineer specializing in porting generative AI prototypes (v0, Lovable, Bolt) to real development environments, with expertise in design systems, visual parity, and dependency management across runtimes. I have {{PROTOTIPO}}, born in {{HERRAMIENTA_ORIGEN}}, and I need to move it to {{HERRAMIENTA_DESTINO}} with target stack {{STACK_DESTINO}}, keeping maximum fidelity on {{ELEMENTOS_CRITICOS}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Produce a portable, self-contained handoff document, pasteable into {{HERRAMIENTA_DESTINO}}, so it reconstructs with verifiable parity instead of improvising. Before drafting, confirm that you have access to the exported code from {{HERRAMIENTA_ORIGEN}} or, failing that, to screenshots and the file tree; if a critical input for the inventory or fidelity is missing, ask for it before continuing.

Five sections: (1) Artifact inventory in {{HERRAMIENTA_ORIGEN}}: screens, components, routes, state, mock data, assets, styles, theme variables, and dependencies. (2) Fidelity specification: per screen and component, design tokens (color, typography, spacing, radii, shadows), breakpoints, states (hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, empty), animations, and interaction behavior, with focus on {{ELEMENTOS_CRITICOS}}. (3) Stack manifest: framework, package manager, exact versions, UI and icon library, fonts, environment variables, and differences between the {{HERRAMIENTA_ORIGEN}} runtime and {{STACK_DESTINO}} that break fidelity; every proprietary component with no equivalent at the destination is flagged with its replacement and trade-off. (4) Reconstruction instructions: numbered steps to stand up the project at the destination, file-by-file mapping, copyable installation commands, theme/fonts/assets configuration, and migration order (primitives, components, screens, routes, state/data). (5) Parity verification: checklist of identical render per screen, identical response per state, absence of console errors and broken imports, and responsive match.

Rules: tag every inference with [ASSUMPTION]; no invented versions; no prices; neutral and professional English, no emojis. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before drafting.

Parameters:
- {{PROTOTIPO}}: name and one-line description of the prototype to port and what it does
- {{HERRAMIENTA_ORIGEN}}: tool where the prototype lives today (v0, Lovable, Bolt, other)
- {{HERRAMIENTA_DESTINO}}: destination environment to move to (Cursor, Windsurf, local repo)
- {{STACK_DESTINO}}: target framework, UI library, and versions at the destination (optional; if missing, inferred from the source and tagged [ASSUMPTION])
- {{ELEMENTOS_CRITICOS}}: screens, components, or behaviors whose fidelity is non-negotiable (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: System prompt for a custom code agent
prompts.content:
Act as a senior prompt engineer specializing in code agents, with experience operating programming assistants in production repos. I need you to design the complete system prompt that will govern a custom programming agent for the project {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}. Without a behavioral contract, a code agent improvises: it invents APIs, rewrites things it should not, and delivers changes that are impossible to review; with a good system prompt it becomes a predictable and auditable collaborator. Build the system prompt with five explicit, numbered sections: 1) Role and identity (who the agent is, its seniority, and its mission in {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}); 2) Stack and conventions, fixing {{STACK_TECNICO}} and {{CONVENCIONES}} as mandatory (language, framework, package manager, runtime, linter/formatter, folder structure, patterns); 3) Hard constraints translating {{RESTRICCIONES_DURAS}} into verifiable NEVER rules, including by default: do not invent APIs or signatures, do not delete or move files without confirming, do not add dependencies without justifying, do not expose or assume secrets, do not touch CI/CD or data migrations without approval; 4) Workflow in numbered steps (read the relevant code before writing, restate the task, present a plan, execute the minimum change, self-verify) bounded by {{NIVEL_AUTONOMIA}}; 5) Output format per {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} and protocol for requesting data when something is ambiguous instead of assuming. Write in the imperative second person directed at the agent, with verifiable rules and no filler, and make the workflow always end in verification. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Before drafting, restate in one line what you understand and articulate your plan; if {{NIVEL_AUTONOMIA}}, {{STACK_TECNICO}}, or {{RESTRICCIONES_DURAS}} are empty or ambiguous, ask first. Deliver the system prompt in a single pasteable block and, below it, a brief list of assumptions tagged [ASSUMPTION] and a mini acceptance checklist.

Parameters:
- {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}: Name or codename of the project where the agent will operate.
- {{STACK_TECNICO}}: Target language, framework, package manager, and runtime.
- {{CONVENCIONES}}: Code style, linter/formatter, folder structure, and patterns to respect.
- {{RESTRICCIONES_DURAS}}: Non-negotiable hard limits for the agent (what it must NEVER do).
- {{NIVEL_AUTONOMIA}}: How far it can act without confirmation (propose only / edit with confirmation / autonomous within scope).
- {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}: What it returns in each interaction (diff, full file, explanation, test commands).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Packed repo context for the agent
prompts.content:
Act as a senior context engineer specializing in code agents, with software architecture judgment and strict token-budget discipline. A code agent is only as good as the context it receives: too much dilutes the signal and burns budget; too little makes it hallucinate the architecture. Package the repository {{REPOSITORIO}} into a context document, ready to paste as the agent's initial instruction, so it can execute {{TAREA_AGENTE}} hitting the right code on the first attempt, within {{LIMITE_TOKENS}}, without asking avoidable questions or breaking repo conventions.

Proceed as follows:
1. Mapping: reconstruct the real topology of {{REPOSITORIO}} (folders, dominant language and framework, entry point, dependency manifests, configuration, and conventions). Integrate {{ARCHIVOS_PRIORITARIOS}} as an initial curation signal. Detect conventions observed in the code, not assumed; tag [ASSUMPTION] on anything unverifiable.
2. Curation by relevance to {{TAREA_AGENTE}}: score each file and assign it a level. CRITICAL (read in full), REFERENCE (contract only: signatures, interfaces, schemas, load-bearing fragments), and CONTEXT (one line of existence and purpose). Guiding rule: maximum signal per token.
3. Critical distillation: for each CRITICAL file extract the public contract, invariants, side effects, and extension points; discard dispensable internal implementation. Preserve literal text only when load-bearing.
4. Assembly: build the document with six sections (Repo map, Rules and conventions, Distilled CRITICAL files, REFERENCE files, CONTEXT files, Omitted with reason).
5. Budget: verify it fits within {{LIMITE_TOKENS}}. If it does not fit, downgrade from higher to lower level before cutting critical content, and document each downgrade.

Non-negotiable rules: zero secrets, credentials, tokens, or PII (sanitize or use placeholders). Do not invent files or conventions. Every CRITICAL file is justified by {{TAREA_AGENTE}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

If {{REPOSITORIO}}, {{TAREA_AGENTE}}, or {{LIMITE_TOKENS}} are empty or ambiguous, ask for them before packaging. If the repo exceeds what can be inspected, propose a task-directed sampling instead of guessing.

prompts.title: Generate UI component from description
Clone UI from a screenshot
prompts.content:
Act as a senior frontend engineer specializing in translating visual designs into code, with mastery of design systems, tokens, responsive layout, and accessibility. I have the screenshot {{SCREENSHOT}} of an existing screen and I need to reproduce it as componentized code in {{STACK_OBJETIVO}} using {{SISTEMA_ESTILOS}}, with fidelity {{NIVEL_FIDELIDAD}} and responsive scope {{RESPONSIVE}}. If {{SCREENSHOT}} is missing, clipped, or {{STACK_OBJETIVO}} is undefined, ask before proceeding; a screenshot is a partial source (a single state, a single size, no interactions, no real data) and I do not want you to invent what is not visible. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver in this order: (1) Screenshot reading: describe what you see in {{SCREENSHOT}} (screen type, apparent purpose, breakpoint it represents) to confirm a shared interpretation. (2) Visual tree: hierarchy of regions and components (header, nav, hero, cards, lists, forms, footer) with nesting and layout model per region (flex, grid, stack, absolute position). (3) Inferred design tokens: color (approximate hex), typography (family, sizes, weights, line height), spacing scale, radii, shadows, borders; values not distinguishable with certainty as a range and tagged [ASSUMPTION]. (4) Code: componentized interface in {{STACK_OBJETIVO}} with {{SISTEMA_ESTILOS}}, centralized tokens (variables, theme, or constants), semantic and accessible markup (roles, labels, contrast, focus, heading hierarchy), and example data as placeholder — no scattered magic values. (5) States and responsive: declare hover, focus, active, disabled, empty, loading, and error, and the breakpoints NOT visible, respecting {{RESPONSIVE}}; propose reasonable behavior and mark it as a decision to validate. (6) Fidelity checklist: region-by-region table at the {{NIVEL_FIDELIDAD}} level comparing observed against implemented, plus the list of gaps (real text, interactions, dynamic data, brand assets, licensed fonts).

Rules: do not invent business logic, endpoints, or real data; presentation layer only. Code from the outside in. Close with minimal instructions to run or preview, and the consolidated list of assumptions and gaps.

prompts.title: Conversion-oriented landing page
prompts.content: Act as a senior product designer and conversion copywriter, specialist in single-page landing pages, AIDA model, unique value proposition, social proof, and accessible visual hierarchy. I need to convert visits into action with a landing page for {{PRODUCTO}} targeting {{AUDIENCIA}}, real, measurable, and immediately publishable — not decorative. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{ACCION_CONVERSION}}, or {{PRUEBA_SOCIAL}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before writing code. Never invent testimonials, figures, or logos: if {{PRUEBA_SOCIAL}} is missing use visible [REPLACE: ...] markers and indicate what to substitute. No prices or the word free. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret > Plan > Execute): restate the objective in one sentence ('Convince {{AUDIENCIA}} to {{ACCION_CONVERSION}} by showing the value of {{PRODUCTO}}'), list what data is missing, tag assumptions with [ASSUMPTION], and present the plan before executing. Define the architecture in hierarchy order: hero with a single benefit H1 + subtitle + CTA visible without scrolling; block of three benefits or problem-solution; social proof section from {{PRUEBA_SOCIAL}}; close with repeated CTA and micro-copy that reduces friction. Write the copy with AIDA in the tone {{TONO_ESTILO}}: headline with a concrete result, body of benefits over features, a single primary CTA with an action verb. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they contribute content or brand. Deliver a single self-contained index.html: embedded CSS without external frameworks or CDNs, responsive with a fluid grid, WCAG AA contrast, visible focus, semantic HTML with alt and aria. Close with the metrics note (CTA clicks, scroll depth, conversion rate) and the first suggested adjustment when conversion is low, prioritizing the headline. Return the index.html, copy by section, and measurement note.

prompts.title: Dashboard with metrics and charts
prompts.content:
Act as a senior frontend engineer specializing in data visualization and product dashboards, with mastery of Chart.js, grid layouts, and accessible design. I need a self-contained dashboard in a single HTML file (HTML, CSS, and JavaScript together) that opens in the browser with no backend or build step, to monitor {{DOMINIO_NEGOCIO}} and validate that the metrics, cuts, and visualizations tell the right story before investing in a production version.

Build the following:
1. A top filter bar with a date range selector with options {{RANGOS_FECHA}} and filters {{FILTROS}}; when any changes, KPIs and charts recalculate in real time.
2. A row of KPI cards for {{KPIS}}: each one with its current value, the percentage change against the equivalent prior period, and a color indicator (green if favorable, red if adverse, neutral if no change). Clarify for each KPI whether going up is good or bad.
3. A row of {{GRAFICAS}} charts responsive in a grid, using a CDN library (Chart.js or similar), with labeled legends and axes.
4. ALL data access isolated in a single getData(filters) function that today returns a realistic mock of at least 90 days embedded, and tomorrow is replaced by {{FUENTE_DATOS}} without touching the render layer or the filters.
5. Explicit handling of loading state and empty state when a filter returns no data.

Decisions and limits to respect: a single external dependency (the chart library via CDN); no frameworks or bundlers; variance calculations must guard against division by zero; dates handled in a fixed, documented timezone; the mock must be deterministic (fixed seed) for a reproducible demo. If the page opens with file:// and the CDN does not load, show a clear message instead of failing silently. Consider attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understood (domain, KPIs, charts, filters, ranges), declare your assumptions, and present your phased plan; then execute. Deliver the complete HTML file ready to save as dashboard.html and open, followed by brief instructions for connecting {{FUENTE_DATOS}}. If any essential data is missing, ask before generating the code.

prompts.title: Complex form with validation
prompts.content:
Act as a senior frontend engineer expert in complex forms, schema-driven declarative validation, and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility. Build a runnable multi-step form (wizard) in {{STACK}} with its validation, persistence, submission handling, and tests, ready to run without manual adjustments.

If any essential data is missing, ask for it before generating code instead of inventing; when a decision is not provided, mark it as [ASSUMPTION] and continue.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Inputs:
- STACK: {{STACK}} (framework + form library + validation library).
- STEPS_AND_FIELDS: {{STEPS_AND_FIELDS}} (wizard steps and, for each step, its fields with type, label, whether required, and dependencies).
- VALIDATION_RULES: {{VALIDATION_RULES}} (per-field rules and field-to-field dependencies that activate or deactivate validations).
- PERSISTENCE: {{PERSISTENCE}} (persistent state strategy, key, and rehydration policy; optional, default localStorage with versioned key).
- SUBMISSION: {{SUBMISSION}} (endpoint, payload contract, and shape of per-field server errors; optional, default mock simulating success and validation error).
- ATTACHMENTS: {{ATTACHMENTS}} (attached files, URLs, or "No attachments").

Deliver, in this order:
1. Model the steps and fields of {{STEPS_AND_FIELDS}} with type, label, required status, and dependencies; define the step machine (current step, total, conditioned advance) and document whether hidden dependent fields preserve or clear their value.
2. Declare the validation schema as the single source of truth from {{VALIDATION_RULES}}, with conditional inter-field rules; validate per field on blur and the full step before advancing, distinguishing empty required vs. invalid format.
3. Render field-specific errors (text below the input, associated with aria-describedby and aria-invalid) and a per-step error summary with focus management and a live region; block advance if the step is invalid.
4. Implement persistent state per {{PERSISTENCE}}: autosave with versioned key, rehydration on mount, step preserved on reload, policy on differing schema version, and exclusion of sensitive fields.
5. Build guarded navigation: Back without re-validating, Next that validates, accessible progress bar, and a final review step with per-section editing before submitting.
6. Handle submission to {{SUBMISSION}} with loading, success, and error states; map server errors to the field and step, move focus to the first error, prevent double submission, and handle timeout/network failure with retry.
7. Deliver decoupled components (wizard, step, field, summary), the schema, state management, error texts in English, accessibility notes, and >= 6 test cases; mark any undocumented decision as [ASSUMPTION].

Completion criterion: validation in a single schema, advance impossible with invalid fields, state surviving reload preserving the step, dependencies activating/deactivating validations, review before submission, server errors mapped to their field, keyboard and screen-reader accessibility, reusable components, assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION], and suite >= 6 cases (invalid field, conditional dependency, persistence/rehydration, advance block, mapped server error, retry after network failure).

prompts.title: Responsive and mobile-first adaptation
WCAG accessibility in generated components
prompts.content:
Act as a senior web accessibility engineer (frontend a11y) with mastery of WCAG 2.2, the ARIA Authoring Practices Guide (APG) pattern, and real tests with screen readers (NVDA, VoiceOver, TalkBack). Audit {{COMPONENT}} and return it corrected in {{FRAMEWORK}} at level {{CONFORMANCE_LEVEL}}, preserving framework, visual style, and behavior.

First restate what you understand about {{COMPONENT}}, its usage context, and the target level {{CONFORMANCE_LEVEL}}, and present your plan before executing. If something critical is missing (code or sufficient description, {{FRAMEWORK}}, whether {{DYNAMIC_CONTENT}} applies, WCAG level), ask for it instead of assuming; if an assumption is reasonable, declare it explicitly.

Phase 1 Inventory: map each interactive element of {{COMPONENT}} to its APG pattern and prioritize native semantic HTML before resorting to ARIA. Phase 2 Audit across five fronts: (1) valid, non-redundant ARIA (no role=button on a button), no aria-hidden on focusable content; (2) focus with logical DOM order, visible indicator >= 3:1, focus trap and return in modals, zero positive tabindex; (3) contrast 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text and non-text components/states, without depending on color alone; (4) full keyboard: Tab/Shift+Tab, Enter/Space, Escape, arrows in menus/tabs/radios, no traps; (5) coherent accessible names, aria-expanded/selected/checked/invalid states, live regions for {{DYNAMIC_CONTENT}}, prefers-reduced-motion respected. Phase 3 Correction: rewrite the complete and functional code with minimal style change. Phase 4 Verification: manual keyboard and screen-reader test checklist.

Deliver: (a) a prioritized findings report, each with WCAG 2.2 criterion by number, severity (blocking/serious/minor), evidence, and correction; (b) complete corrected code in {{FRAMEWORK}} at level {{CONFORMANCE_LEVEL}}; (c) manual verification checklist. Do not report false positives. Distinguish what is automatically verifiable from what requires human judgment. Close only when all five fronts are covered and the checklist is executable. This is EstrategIA applied to the interface.

Parameters:
- {{COMPONENT}}: component or UI set to audit (code or description); e.g. confirmation modal, dropdown menu, registration form.
- {{FRAMEWORK}}: target technology for returning the corrected code (HTML+CSS, React/JSX, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Web Components).
- {{CONFORMANCE_LEVEL}}: target WCAG 2.2 level (A, AA by default, AAA).
- {{DYNAMIC_CONTENT}}: (optional) live changes requiring announcement: validations, toasts, search results, counters.

prompts.title: Empty, loading, and error states per screen
prompts.content:
Act as a senior frontend engineer and interaction designer with fifteen years closing the gap between the happy path and non-happy-path states, expert in WCAG accessibility, UX writing, and UI state machines. The screen {{SCREEN}} already solves the happy path, but its non-happy-path states are undesigned: a generic spinner appears, a silent empty list, or a raw technical error that breaks trust, generates support tickets, and blocks the view from being closed. I want to convert that demo into a product.

I need three chained deliverables: (1) a state map classified by family; (2) a design card per state with real copy and a recovery action; (3) the coded and accessible state component in {{UI_STACK}}. Before executing, if {{SCREEN}}, {{STATES}}, or {{UI_STACK}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them in a single batch; do not invent the backend contract or assume the stack or design system.

Proceed as follows: First, map the non-happy-path states of {{STATES}} into three families. Empty: first time with no data, no search or filter results, deleted data, or no permission to view. Loading: initial, reload over already-visible data, pagination or infinite scroll, optimistic action. Error: network down or no connection, 500, 403, 404, 422 validation, 429 or quota exhausted, and timeout; for each error declare probable cause, whether it is retryable, and whether recovery is automatic or manual. Second, design each relevant state with its visual role (icon or illustration, title, body, primary action, optional secondary action), real copy in the {{VOICE_TONE}} tone (human, without raw technical jargon, without blaming the person, with a single dominant action), and the concrete recovery action per {{RECOVERY_ACTION}}; distinguish skeleton from spinner depending on whether the content shape is known, and define the delay threshold before showing the loading state to avoid flashes. Third, code the component in {{UI_STACK}} with an explicit state machine (idle, loading, empty, error, success) that receives the state and the retry callback via props, without mixing fetch with presentation, and include aria-busy during loading, aria-live to announce errors and results, focus managed toward the error message and its action, and appropriate touch targets. Fourth, close with a coverage checklist and the list of signals the backend must expose (stable error codes, safe message, retryable indicator, suggested retry header) that are still pending instrumentation.

Mark as [ASSUMPTION] every decision made without confirmed data. Consider {{ATTACHMENTS}} if any. Before executing, restate in one line what you understood and present your plan; then deliver.

Parameters: {{SCREEN}}, {{STATES}}, {{UI_STACK}}, {{VOICE_TONE}}, {{RECOVERY_ACTION}}, {{ATTACHMENTS}}.

prompts.title: Dark mode and theming with tokens
prompts.content:
Act as a senior front-end engineer specializing in design systems and theming with design tokens (W3C DTCG standard), with practice in CSS custom properties, WCAG 2.2 accessibility, and FOUC prevention. I need to implement light and dark mode in {{UI_STACK}} without ending up with two parallel stylesheets that must be kept in sync. The design token architecture solves this by separating the raw color value from its intended use: a semantic layer acts as indirection and the mode switch reduces to reassigning that layer, which unlocks scalable theming, verifiable accessibility, and zero rule duplication.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand about {{UI_STACK}}, {{BRAND_PALETTE}}, {{MODE_SCOPE}}, and {{CURRENT_STATE}}; if a critical input is missing to avoid inventing, ask for it before generating code. Then present your plan and only then execute.

Deliverable: complete light/dark theming for {{UI_STACK}}, governed by tokens. (1) Design the three-layer architecture: primitives (raw scale derived from {{BRAND_PALETTE}}, no semantics, identical in both modes), semantic (names by intention: surface-background, surface-elevated, text-primary, text-secondary, border, action-primary, action-primary-text, state-error, focus; the only layer that differs between modes), and optional component-level tokens referencing semantics. Name according to {{TOKEN_NOMENCLATURE}}. Prohibit layer jumps and raw colors in UI rules. (2) Materialize tokens as CSS custom properties: light mode on the root selector, dark as override via data-theme="dark", and auto mode with @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark). (3) Implement mode selection per {{MODE_SCOPE}} with three states (light, dark, system), manual override persisted in localStorage under a stable key, synchronization with prefers-color-scheme in system state, and an inline anti-FOUC script that sets data-theme before the first paint with try/catch. (4) Refactor the styles of {{CURRENT_STATE}} to consume only semantic or component-level tokens; eliminate raw values and direct primitive references in UI rules. (5) Verify accessibility: calculate the contrast ratio of each text/background pair and of significant borders and icons in BOTH modes against WCAG 2.2 (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text and non-text) and deliver a table with real ratios vs. threshold; correct each failing pair by adjusting primitives or the semantic mapping without breaking the other mode.

Edge cases: respect prefers-reduced-motion, avoid animating the theme on initial load, declare color-scheme for native controls, and handle unavailable localStorage by falling back to the system preference. Do not invent colors: mark any color or derived token without an explicit source as [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver: tokens file (three layers), stylesheet with custom properties per mode, theme-switching module (three states + persistence) + anti-FOUC snippet, refactored components, and contrast table for both modes.

Variables:
- {{UI_STACK}}: Framework, style library, and bundler (e.g. React + Tailwind + Vite, Vue + plain CSS, Next.js + CSS Modules).
- {{BRAND_PALETTE}}: Brand colors and/or existing scale (hex, names, or reference); if none, indicate so to derive a base scale.
- {{MODE_SCOPE}}: Modes to support and default behavior (only light+dark, follow system, manual override, persistence across sessions).
- {{TOKEN_NOMENCLATURE}}: Naming convention for tokens (optional, default: kebab-case by intention, e.g. surface-background, text-primary).
- {{CURRENT_STATE}}: How styles look today (hardcoded, loose variables, no system); paste a representative snippet (optional).

prompts.title: Animations and purposeful micro-interactions
prompts.content:
Act as a senior front-end engineer specializing in motion design and web performance engineering, with mastery of the browser rendering pipeline (layout > paint > composite) and motion accessibility. I want you to design a purposeful micro-interaction plan and deliver its commented implementation for {{TARGET_COMPONENTS}} in {{FRAMEWORK}} with {{STYLE_SYSTEM}}, calibrated to {{MOTION_INTENSITY}} and to {{PERFORMANCE_BUDGET}}. Before implementing, restate what you understood and present your plan. If {{FRAMEWORK}}, {{STYLE_SYSTEM}}, or {{TARGET_COMPONENTS}} are missing, ask for them before continuing. Proceed as follows: (1) Moment audit: list each candidate micro-interaction in {{TARGET_COMPONENTS}} and classify its function (confirmation, loading/progress, attention direction, layout continuity); explicitly discard purely decorative motion with no function. (2) Motion specification: for each moment define functional purpose, trigger (hover, focus, click, mount, data change, scroll), animated property, duration (120–300 ms micro, up to 500 ms for major transitions), easing curve (ease-out entrances, ease-in exits, standard easing for continuous motion) coherent with {{MOTION_INTENSITY}}, and the states (rest, hover, focus, active, loading, success, error, exit). (3) Implementation: animate exclusively transform and opacity; never width, height, top, left, margin, or properties that trigger reflow; use will-change only during the active interaction and remove it when done; prefer CSS, and if orchestrating use the Web Animations API or requestAnimationFrame instead of blocking the thread. (4) Accessibility: respect prefers-reduced-motion with a minimal or null variant that preserves feedback through non-animated means; guarantee visible focus and keyboard support where feedback depends on interaction; do not depend only on color or only on motion; respect the three-flashes-per-second threshold. (5) Deliverables in {{FRAMEWORK}}/{{STYLE_SYSTEM}}: classified inventory, motion specification table, code commented with the reason for each decision, and brief guide to verify {{PERFORMANCE_BUDGET}} (performance panel, fps capture, mid-range test) and accessibility. Mark [ASSUMPTION] for any assumption about stack, content, or behavior. Neutral and professional English, no emojis. This unlocks a more polished EstrategIA experience without rewriting the logic.

Parameters:
- {{TARGET_COMPONENTS}}: components or flows to animate (e.g. submit button, card list, modal opening, navigation).
- {{FRAMEWORK}}: UI stack (e.g. React, Vue, Svelte, HTML/CSS vanilla).
- {{STYLE_SYSTEM}}: how styles are applied (e.g. CSS modules, Tailwind, styled-components, plain CSS).
- {{MOTION_INTENSITY}}: desired motion level (e.g. subtle/minimal, balanced, expressive).
- {{PERFORMANCE_BUDGET}}: performance goal (e.g. 60 fps on mid-range, no layout animation, no blocking the main thread).

prompts.title: Componentize and extract reusable elements
prompts.content:
Act as a senior frontend engineer expert in component architecture, UI refactoring, and typed contract design, with mastery of {{FRONTEND_STACK}}. Your task: audit {{GENERATED_UI}} (AI-generated interface where UI blocks repeat with minimal variations), extract those patterns as typed reusable components, and deliver an adoption plan that does not break visual consistency.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand about {{GENERATED_UI}} and the goal, present your plan (what you will extract, in what order, what you will leave intact), and only then execute. If critical data is missing, ask for it in a single batch before touching code; do not invent {{FRONTEND_STACK}} or {{DESIGN_SYSTEM}}.

Proceed as follows: (1) audit {{GENERATED_UI}} and inventory repeated patterns, grouping variants of the same concept and estimating the frequency of each; distinguish genuine structural repetition from accidental visual coincidence. (2) Prioritize what to extract applying {{EXTRACTION_CRITERIA}}; justify what you extract and what you leave. (3) For each component define its boundary: what is a prop, what is a slot or children, what is internal state, and what set of variants it covers. (4) Design the prop contract per {{TYPED_CONTRACT}}: explicit types, required vs. optional, default values, and discriminated unions for variants, with consistent naming. (5) Implement each component with its typing in {{FRONTEND_STACK}}, aligned to {{DESIGN_SYSTEM}} and existing tokens. (6) Refactor the original usages to consume the new component and deliver the adoption diff. (7) Flag the differences that must NOT be collapsed into the same component and mark as [ASSUMPTION] any data not provided.

Quality rules: a single source of truth per element; zero visual regression; code compiles and passes the type checker; no premature abstractions. Deliver: prioritized pattern inventory, component code with their types, diff of refactored sites, and list of over-abstraction warnings and assumptions.

Variables:
- {{GENERATED_UI}}: code of the AI-generated interface to audit (files, components, or fragments where UI blocks repeat).
- {{FRONTEND_STACK}}: framework and language of the project and UI library if applicable.
- {{EXTRACTION_CRITERIA}}: rules to decide what to extract (repetition threshold, minimum complexity, maintainability vs. speed priority, what NOT to touch).
- {{TYPED_CONTRACT}}: prop contract style (interface vs. type, optional/required, discriminated unions, naming conventions).
- {{DESIGN_SYSTEM}}: design system, tokens, or conventions to respect (optional; default: infer from existing code).

prompts.title: Implement a feature end-to-end with AI
prompts.content:
Act as a senior full-stack software engineer specializing in incremental delivery through vertical slices, with strong judgment on repository conventions, tests, and reviewable diffs. Your mission is to implement feature {{FEATURE}} end-to-end (UI, state, API, business logic, and data) on branch {{BRANCH}} of project {{REPO_OR_PATH}}, directing the work step by step and not all at once: each slice is tested, reviewable, and reversible, and the branch remains functional after each step.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Before touching code, restate in your own words {{FEATURE}}, its user value, and the criteria {{ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA}}; then present your plan and wait for approval.

Phase 0 Reconnaissance: inspect {{REPO_OR_PATH}} to identify the stack {{STACK}}, folder structure, style conventions, existing libraries, data layer, and how tests and the local environment are run with {{TEST_COMMAND}}. Consider {{ATTACHMENTS}}. Restate the feature and list what remains to confirm. If a critical piece of data is missing or there is ambiguity, ask for it before assuming.

Phase 1 Plan: propose numbered vertical slices, ordered by dependency, each with the layers it touches and its objective verification criterion. Prioritize the minimal happy-path end-to-end first before edges and validations. Do not advance without my plan approval.

Phase 2 Implementation per slice: implement ONE slice at a time respecting existing conventions; write or update tests, run them with {{TEST_COMMAND}}, show the result and a diff summary (files and purpose), and pause for my sign-off before the next slice. If a test fails, diagnose and fix within the same slice before continuing.

Phase 3 Close: integrate, run the full suite with {{TEST_COMMAND}}, and deliver a final summary.

Hard rules: do not add new dependencies, destructive schema migrations, or large refactors without warning and getting approval; the feature must remain functional at the end of each slice; keep each slice's diff small and atomic; do not touch secrets without warning; mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and every known limitation explicitly.

Deliverable: {{FEATURE}} integrated in {{BRANCH}} and green in {{TEST_COMMAND}}, with a summary of files touched, steps to run it locally, the tests that cover it, and a list of debt or pending assumptions.

Parameters:
- {{FEATURE}}: feature to build and the user value it delivers.
- {{REPO_OR_PATH}}: repository or project path where it is implemented.
- {{BRANCH}}: working branch on which it is developed.
- {{ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA}}: observable conditions that define when the feature is done.
- {{TEST_COMMAND}}: command to run the test suite and/or start the local environment.
- {{STACK}}: language, framework, and data layer if known (optional).
- {{ATTACHMENTS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Business logic from natural-language rules
Explicit state machine for flows
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specializing in domain modeling and finite state machines, with mastery of discriminated unions in {{LANGUAGE}}. Convert the flow {{FLOW}}, today modeled with {{CURRENT_REPRESENTATION}}, into an explicit finite state machine where invalid states such as {{OBSERVED_IMPOSSIBLE_STATE}} are impossible to represent, not just prohibited by convention. The events that trigger transitions are {{EVENTS}}. Consider these attachments: {{ATTACHMENTS}}.

Before coding, ask me for any missing data and mark as [ASSUMPTION] every inference about the domain; confirm before advancing.

Deliver, in this order: (1) the states of {{FLOW}} as a closed, exhaustive, and mutually exclusive set, listing per state the data that exists only in it; (2) the transition table source-event-destination-guard from {{EVENTS}}, where every unlisted cell is a forbidden transition; (3) the explicit list of combinations that {{CURRENT_REPRESENTATION}} permitted and the new model makes unrepresentable, including {{OBSERVED_IMPOSSIBLE_STATE}}; (4) the model as an idiomatic discriminated union of {{LANGUAGE}}, each variant carrying only its own data; (5) a pure and total transition function that receives state and event and returns the new state or a typed error, without implicit error states; (6) a Mermaid stateDiagram-v2 diagram consistent with the table; (7) three tests: a valid transition, an invalid transition rejected with its typed error, and one that demonstrates that {{OBSERVED_IMPOSSIBLE_STATE}} does not compile or cannot be constructed.

Cover edge cases: terminal states, guards with external data, idempotent events, and re-entry. Close with the invariants now guaranteed by the type and the limits of the model. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, and then Execute.

Variables: {{FLOW}}, {{LANGUAGE}}, {{CURRENT_REPRESENTATION}}, {{EVENTS}}, {{OBSERVED_IMPOSSIBLE_STATE}}, {{ATTACHMENTS}}.

prompts.title: Search, filters, and pagination
File upload, validation, and processing with limits and feedback
Notifications and event handling
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specialized in event-driven architectures and multi-channel notification systems, with practice in pub-sub, idempotency, observability, and anti-corruption layers over external providers. I need you to design and implement a notification system decoupled by events, integrated in {{TECH_STACK}}, with code and tests. The system is triggered by business events {{BUSINESS_EVENTS}} and delivers through channels {{CHANNELS}}. The goal is to separate WHAT happens (an immutable domain fact, for example: the order was confirmed) from HOW it is notified (to whom, through which channel, with what text), so that adding channels or rules does not touch business logic, a provider outage does not bring down the purchase flow, and there is a single point for auditing what was notified. Direct coupling (calling the email client inside the order service) is the anti-pattern this design eliminates.

Target architecture: {{ARCHITECTURE}} (in-process monolith or distributed system with queue/topic; default in-process). Available providers or libraries per channel: {{PROVIDERS}}. Attachments: {{ATTACHMENTS}}. Before coding, confirm stack, actual events, channels, architecture, and providers; if a key input is missing, ask for it and do not invent providers or APIs.

Deliver by layers: (1) Domain event contract per event from {{BUSINESS_EVENTS}}, name in past tense, unique identifier, timestamp, actor, typed payload, and schema version; immutable and without presentation logic. (2) Emitter or bus that separates producer from consumers; choose in-process vs. external queue/topic according to {{ARCHITECTURE}} and justify with an explicit trade-off (latency, durability, operational complexity, ordering, exactly-once vs. at-least-once). (3) Handlers and routing: per event, a subscriber that resolves recipients, queries channel preferences, applies silence/grouping rules, and composes content from versioned templates with safe escaping; the router selects the active channels from {{CHANNELS}}. (4) Channel layer: common interface (send with typed result success/transient-error/permanent-error) and one adapter per provider from {{PROVIDERS}}; adding a channel is a new implementation, without touching business logic or handlers. (5) Reliability: idempotency by event identifier with delivery register, retries with exponential backoff and jitter only on transient errors, and dead-letter queue for those that exhaust retries. (6) In-app persistence: notification model (recipient, type, read/unread status, date, action link) with operations to list paginated, count unread, and mark as read. (7) Minimum observability: structured log and counters by event, channel, and result.

Proceed with the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the inputs and reformulate what you understand, Plan the layers and contracts before implementing, and only then Execute. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inference due to missing data and use only confirmed libraries and providers. Close by demonstrating decoupling (the producer does not import any channel client) and non-duplication on resend, with the green test suite and a brief note on how to subscribe a new handler and how to add a channel.

prompts.title: Data export feature
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specialized in report generation and data export, with mastery of CSV serialization, xlsx generation, and tabular PDF layout in {{STACK}}. I want you to build a solid, production-ready data export feature for {{DATA_ENTITY}}. A poorly made export (dates that Excel reinterprets, decimals with the wrong separator, accented characters broken by encoding, columns the user should not see) erodes trust and generates rework; your job is to prevent exactly that.

Input data:
- DATA_ENTITY: {{DATA_ENTITY}} (what is exported and how it is obtained: source endpoint or query with its filters)
- AVAILABLE_FIELDS: {{AVAILABLE_FIELDS}} (exportable fields with type and readable column name)
- OUTPUT_FORMATS: {{OUTPUT_FORMATS}} (CSV, Excel xlsx, PDF, or a combination)
- STACK: {{STACK}} (language, framework, and available or preferred libraries)
