- FORMAT_RULES: {{FORMAT_RULES}} (date format, decimal separator and precision, currency and thousands, encoding, column header language; optional, applies sensible defaults)
If any data is missing, ask for it before coding; if you decide to continue, assume a sensible default and mark it as an explicit assumption.

Deliver: (1) the service contract: input with fields validated against {{AVAILABLE_FIELDS}}, chosen format from {{OUTPUT_FORMATS}}, and filters inherited from {{DATA_ENTITY}}; output with ordered columns, readable names, and timestamp in the file name. (2) Field selection that validates against {{AVAILABLE_FIELDS}}, rejects unauthorized ones, and preserves order. (3) Centralized formatter per type according to {{FORMAT_RULES}} (dates, decimals with precision, currency with thousands, readable booleans, mapped enums, nulls as empty), reusable across formats. (4) Each exporter from {{OUTPUT_FORMATS}}: CSV with delimiter and UTF-8 with BOM when opening in Excel, escaping quotes, line breaks, and delimiter; Excel with typed columns, headers and widths, forcing text in codes to avoid auto-conversion; PDF with paginated table, repeated header, title and date. (5) Volume and edge handling: streaming or pagination for large datasets, empty dataset, nulls, and special characters; endpoint or handler with correct content-type and download header. (6) Tests covering each format and type (nulls, specials, unauthorized, empty) plus integration notes in {{STACK}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing; verify against checklist and mark assumptions at close.

prompts.title: App internationalization (i18n)
prompts.content: Act as a senior software engineer specialized in internationalization (i18n) and localization, with mastery of CLDR rules, BCP 47, and the i18n library native to {{STACK_FRAMEWORK}}. Internationalize the app end-to-end to support {{TARGET_LANGUAGES}} with a single codebase, without changing business logic or observable behavior. Follow these phases. Phase 1 Audit: traverse {{STRING_SCOPE}}, inventory every user-visible string (UI, validations, error and empty messages, notifications, emails, accessible SEO metadata) with its exact location, and separate it from text that is NOT translated (logs, internal keys, technical identifiers, domain enums); report risks such as concatenations, text embedded in images, and manual date or number formatting. Phase 2 Keys and catalogs: establish a stable, hierarchical convention by namespace or feature (for example auth.login.submit), create the {{BASE_LANGUAGE}} resource file as the source of truth, and generate the other languages from {{TARGET_LANGUAGES}} with identical mirror keys. Phase 3 Configuration: initialize the {{STACK_FRAMEWORK}} i18n provider with locale detection, fallback to {{BASE_LANGUAGE}}, user preference persistence, and namespace lazy-loading. Phase 4 Refactor: replace each string with its key via the translation API, applying {{ADVANCED_FORMATTING}}: safe variable interpolation, CLDR pluralization, gender where applicable, and dates, numbers, and currencies via the locale formatting API; never concatenate translated fragments or assume word order. Phase 5 Close: translate the {{BASE_LANGUAGE}} catalog, leave the other locales with pending values marked unambiguously, and deliver per-file diffs, per-language resource files, provider configuration, migration notes, and a localization QA checklist (hot locale switch, fallback, RTL if applicable, pseudo-localization, and long-text truncation). Define explicit assumptions (fallback policy, missing key handling, default locale in SSR) and mark any ambiguity instead of inventing it. Before executing, reformulate what you understood and present your plan. If any critical data is missing, ask for it concretely before proceeding. Variables: {{STACK_FRAMEWORK}} (language, framework, and target i18n library), {{TARGET_LANGUAGES}} (locales to support in BCP 47), {{BASE_LANGUAGE}} (source-of-truth and fallback locale), {{STRING_SCOPE}} (what is extracted and what is excluded), {{ADVANCED_FORMATTING}} (CLDR pluralization, gender, dates, numbers, and currency needs; optional).

prompts.title: Permission and role management (RBAC)
Offline-first logic and synchronization
prompts.content: Act as a senior offline-first application engineer, with proven experience in data synchronization, conflict resolution, and outbox or mutation queue design. Your goal: design the local and synchronization layer of {{APP_AND_ENTITIES}} in {{STACK}} so that it remains usable without network connectivity and never loses or duplicates the user's work on reconnection, avoiding the most expensive bug in these apps (data overwritten or duplicated on sync). Before coding, reformulate {{APP_AND_ENTITIES}}, {{STACK}}, {{CONFLICT_STRATEGY}}, and {{LOSS_TOLERANCE}}; if anything critical is missing, ask for it instead of assuming. Then deliver actionable code or pseudocode in {{STACK}} covering: 1) Local cache model with primary key, per-record version (monotonic counter or Lamport-style logical timestamp, NOT the wall clock) and status flags (dirty, synced, base_version of the last confirmed sync). 2) Mutation outbox or queue with per-operation schema (local id, type create/update/delete, entity, payload, base_version, timestamp, status pending/sending/confirmed/failed, attempt counter, idempotency_key), deterministic drain order (FIFO per entity respecting parent-child dependencies), and retries with exponential backoff, jitter, and attempt ceiling before marking failed. 3) Reconciliation engine that applies the server delta onto the cache, detects conflict (base_version differing from the server's with dirty local), and resolves according to {{CONFLICT_STRATEGY}} with trade-off justification; if omitted, recommend one coherent with {{LOSS_TOLERANCE}}. 4) Sync state machine (offline, queuing, syncing, synced, conflict) with named events and transitions (reconnect, network error, conflict detected, resolution applied, retry exhaustion). 5) Temporary IDs: local id on offline create and reconciliation with the server's definitive id (remapping of references in still-queued child mutations). 6) Idempotency: stable idempotency_key per mutation so that a resend after timeout does not duplicate on the server. Cover edge cases: update on deleted record (tombstone), delete-vs-update conflict, stale payload, resend with no confirmation, and parent-before-child create order. Declare assumptions, limits, and a verifiable acceptance criterion per point. Close with a textual flow diagram of reconnect -> queue drain -> reconciliation -> conflict resolution. Variables: {{APP_AND_ENTITIES}} = what app and which entities must work offline; {{STACK}} = target stack and local storage; {{CONFLICT_STRATEGY}} = last-write-wins, field-level merge, or manual review (optional); {{LOSS_TOLERANCE}} = how much loss is acceptable and which data is critical vs. discardable (optional). MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Error diagnosis from stacktrace
Reproduce bug with minimal case
Frontend state debugging
prompts.content: Act as a senior frontend engineer specialized in reactive UI debugging and state modeling in {{FRAMEWORK}}. In {{COMPONENT_CODE}} I observe {{SYMPTOM}} when {{INTERACTION}} occurs, using {{STATE_LIBRARY}} as the state mechanism. I want the root cause with evidence, not a blind rewrite. Before diagnosing, reformulate the observable symptom and the interaction that triggers it; if {{SYMPTOM}} is not reproducible or any data in {{COMPONENT_CODE}} is missing, ask for it in a single batch and do not assume. Proceed in four phases: (1) Reproduction: establish what was expected, what is observed, and at which step of {{INTERACTION}} it occurs. (2) State model: map each piece of state in {{STATE_LIBRARY}} (local, context, global store, server/cache), who reads it, and who writes it; mark duplications and derived state that should be calculated instead of stored. (3) Render analysis: attribute each suspect render in {{COMPONENT_CODE}} to a concrete trigger (new prop, object or function recreated on render, unstable effect or memo dependency, too-broad store subscription, unstable key in lists) and separate correct from wasted renders. (4) Verifiable fix: for each finding give the why, the exact code change, and how to verify it with before/after instrumentation. Do not memoize or optimize without a measured cause; flag premature optimizations. Cover {{FRAMEWORK}} edge cases: race conditions in concurrent fetches, double mount in strict mode, stale state in closures, SSR hydration. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] everything you assume about {{FRAMEWORK}} or {{STATE_LIBRARY}}. Consider {{ATTACHMENTS}} if applicable. Deliver a findings table (symptom, root cause, file:line), a patch per finding, the before/after verification plan, and a note on correct renders that must not be touched. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; reformulate what you understand and present the plan before executing.

prompts.title: Debug a concurrency bug or race condition
prompts.content: Act as a senior engineer in concurrent systems, expert in the memory model of {{MODELO_CONCURRENCIA}} and in race condition debugging in {{LENGUAJE}}. I have a concurrency bug that produces this symptom: {{SINTOMA}}, intermittent and difficult to reproduce, that blocks confidence in the system. I want to move from a non-deterministic failure to a verifiable fix that eliminates the class of defect, not just the symptom. Proceed as follows: (1) Over {{CODIGO}}, identify the mutable shared state between threads or tasks and list every read and write access without protection. (2) Reconstruct a concrete interleaving of operations, step by step, that reproduces {{SINTOMA}} showing the order of reads and writes that breaks the invariant; do not give vague descriptions. (3) Classify the defect (data race, check-then-act, deadlock, livelock, unsafe publication, lost update, or ABA) and name the violated invariant. (4) Propose the fix by prioritizing redesign that eliminates shared state (immutability, thread confinement, message passing, atomic operations); if not viable under {{RESTRICCION}}, apply the minimum correct synchronization taking care of a global lock acquisition order to avoid introducing deadlock, and evaluate the contention trade-off. (5) Considering {{CONTEXTO_EJECUCION}}, deliver the corrected code and a deterministic method to reproduce and verify the failure before and after the fix. Take into account {{ADJUNTOS}}. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. If {{LENGUAJE}}, {{MODELO_CONCURRENCIA}}, or {{CONTEXTO_EJECUCION}} are missing to reconstruct the interleaving, ask me before continuing. Close with a diagnostic report, corrected code block, and verification procedure, ready for a pull request. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Memory leak analysis
Assisted bisect of a regression
Add useful logging and traces
prompts.content: Act as a senior observability engineer with experience in structured logging and distributed traces in production systems. The route {{RUTA_O_FUNCION}} in {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}} is opaque today: when something fails there is no way to know why, what input caused it, or at what stage the latency went. I need to instrument it so that each incident is diagnosable from the logs, without drowning the signal in noise or leaking secrets. Diagnostic goal: {{OBJETIVO_DIAGNOSTICO}}. Logging library: {{LIBRERIA_LOGGING}} (if I say "choose an idiomatic one", select it and justify). If any critical data is missing, ask me before writing code. Work like this: first diagnose which questions today CANNOT be answered with the current logs and map each one to a concrete trace to add. Then instrument preserving the existing style, with structured logging in key-value pairs or JSON, never string concatenation. Apply levels with judgment: DEBUG (development detail), INFO (business milestones), WARN (recoverable anomalies), ERROR (failures with stack and context). Generate a correlation identifier (request_id or trace_id) at the boundary of the operation and propagate it throughout {{RUTA_O_FUNCION}} to link the lines of the same request; if it crosses a process boundary or async queue, indicate how it travels. Add an entry log and an exit log per key operation with duration in ms. Redact or explicitly exclude {{CAMPOS_SENSIBLES}}; no secret or PII should appear. For each new trace, indicate which metric or alert could be derived. Avoid logging in hot loops, do not duplicate the same event between layers, and do not raise the level of existing logs without justifying it. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver the instrumented code ready to paste (diff or complete blocks), the trace-to-metric mapping, and a brief note on how to view and verify the traces locally. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Explain someone else's code to understand it
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specializing in reading and maintaining legacy code, accustomed to providing technical onboarding to other developers. I am going to give you a code fragment that I did not write and I need to understand it thoroughly before touching it, so as not to introduce regressions or break invisible dependencies. Your deliverable is an explanatory walkthrough, NOT a proposal for changes.

Inputs:
- CODIGO: {{CODIGO}} (fragment or file to understand, pasted as-is)
- LENGUAJE: {{LENGUAJE}} (language and, if applicable, framework or version; e.g. Python 3.11, React 18)
- CONTEXTO_ARCHIVO: {{CONTEXTO_ARCHIVO}} (what the module does, where it comes from, and how it is invoked; optional)
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} (why you need to understand it: fix a bug, refactor, extend, review a PR; optional)

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what {{CODIGO}} is, in {{LENGUAJE}}, with objective {{OBJETIVO}}; present your traversal plan; then execute. If {{CODIGO}} is not there, {{LENGUAJE}} cannot be determined, or essential context is missing, ask for it before moving forward.

Proceed as follows:
1. Framing. Confirm {{LENGUAJE}}, framework/version, and {{CONTEXTO_ARCHIVO}}.
2. Walkthrough. Explain {{CODIGO}} respecting the real execution flow, line by line or block by block when they form a logical unit. In each part clarify what it does, why it is written this way, what enters and exits, and what it depends on. Mark control structures, side effects, external calls, and implicit assumptions.
3. Synthesis. Close with: (a) the responsibility of the fragment in one sentence; (b) input/output dependency map; (c) the 3 riskiest zones to modify given {{OBJETIVO}}, each with reason and minimum test that covers it.

Rules: separate the observable from the inferred (mark assumptions); do not omit relevant sections; point out dead code or bugs as observations without correcting them. The deliverable is understanding, not a solution.

prompts.title: Debug CORS and network problems
prompts.content:
Act as a senior web platform engineer, specialist in HTTP, the browser CORS model, and client-server debugging in production. A request from {{ORIGEN_FRONTEND}} to {{DESTINO_API}} is blocked by the browser and delivery stops. The console shows: {{MENSAJE_CONSOLA}}. The request code is {{CODIGO_PETICION}} and the observed response headers are {{HEADERS_RESPUESTA}}. The backend runs on {{STACK_BACKEND}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Work in three phases:
1. Triage. Separate genuine CORS from disguised network error (DNS, TLS/certificate, timeout, refused connection or server down, HTTP-over-HTTPS mixed content, extension block) using {{MENSAJE_CONSOLA}}, the pair {{ORIGEN_FRONTEND}}-{{DESTINO_API}}, and {{HEADERS_RESPUESTA}}. Cite the evidence that distinguishes each case: status 0 or ERR_* without headers indicates network; response visible in Network but hidden from JS indicates CORS.
2. Diagnosis. If it is CORS, name the subtype: simple vs preflight OPTIONS; origin absent or not matching in Access-Control-Allow-Origin; method or header not listed in Allow-Methods/Allow-Headers; credentials requiring Allow-Credentials: true with explicit origin; preflight cache by Max-Age; or missing Expose-Headers. Contrast the browser's requirement against the server's response. Mark [ASSUMPTION] for every infrastructure inference not supported by {{HEADERS_RESPUESTA}} or {{STACK_BACKEND}}.
3. Fix and verification. Root cause verdict with the responsible side (server or client). Exact headers with correct value, corrected code fragment for {{STACK_BACKEND}}, and curl that reproduces the preflight. Confirm that no request with credentials is paired with the origin wildcard.

Deliverable: verdict + header table with values + corrected code + preflight curl + security note. If {{MENSAJE_CONSOLA}}, {{CODIGO_PETICION}}, {{HEADERS_RESPUESTA}}, or the origin-destination pair are missing, ask for them and do not invent the server configuration.

prompts.title: Post-mortem of a production incident
Safe refactor with a test safety net
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specializing in legacy code refactoring, with mastery of Michael Feathers' characterization tests and seams, and Martin Fowler's small-step refactors. I need to improve the internal structure of {{MODULO_OBJETIVO}} ({{LENGUAJE_Y_FRAMEWORK}}) without altering what it does from the consumer's perspective. Touching it blindly is risky: legacy code is code without tests, so first weave a characterization test net that freezes the CURRENT behavior (quirks and bugs included), and only then refactor in small steps maintaining the green.

Proceed in strict order. First confirm the language, framework, test framework ({{FRAMEWORK_DE_PRUEBAS}}, default: the idiomatic one for the stack), and the {{COMPORTAMIENTO_A_PRESERVAR}}; if you do not see the code of {{MODULO_OBJETIVO}}, ask for it before starting and do not invent its content. Then write tests in {{FRAMEWORK_DE_PRUEBAS}} that capture the current behavior as it is today, prioritizing {{COMPORTAMIENTO_A_PRESERVAR}} and edge cases; the tests describe, they do not judge. Identify the seams needed to test without touching production. Run the net and confirm total green as the baseline; report it before moving forward. If coverage is insufficient to refactor safely, say so and expand the net before transforming.

Then refactor in small steps toward {{OLOR_O_META_REFACTOR}}: a single transformation per step (extract method, rename, eliminate duplication, invert dependency, replace conditional with polymorphism), running the net after each one. If a test goes red, stop, revert that step, and report before continuing. Each step is an atomic commit that names what was refactored and why. Do not mix refactor with bug fix or features in the same commit; a real bug is registered as a separate finding [ASSUMPTION], not fixed along the way. On closing, deliver the diff by commits, the final test net, the list of introduced seams, and the balance of eliminated vs. pending smells with their reason, all in {{LENGUAJE_Y_FRAMEWORK}} with {{FRAMEWORK_DE_PRUEBAS}}.

Data: MODULO_OBJETIVO={{MODULO_OBJETIVO}}; LENGUAJE_Y_FRAMEWORK={{LENGUAJE_Y_FRAMEWORK}}; COMPORTAMIENTO_A_PRESERVAR={{COMPORTAMIENTO_A_PRESERVAR}}; FRAMEWORK_DE_PRUEBAS={{FRAMEWORK_DE_PRUEBAS}}; OLOR_O_META_REFACTOR={{OLOR_O_META_REFACTOR}}; ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Extract functions and reduce complexity
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specializing in refactoring and code quality, with mastery of complexity metrics and the single-responsibility principle. Your goal is to transform {{FUNCION}} into a lean version that orchestrates more single-responsibility subfunctions in {{LENGUAJE}}, reducing cyclomatic complexity toward {{UMBRAL_COMPLEJIDAD}} without altering observable behavior and respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before touching the code, reformulate what you understood about {{FUNCION}} and present your plan; only after my confirmation do you apply the refactor.

Proceed by phases. Phase 1 Diagnosis: describe in clear language what {{FUNCION}} does and why it is complex; count the decision points (if, else if, for, while, case, logical operators, ternaries, early returns) and estimate the current cyclomatic complexity; map the mixed responsibilities. Phase 2 Plan: identify candidate blocks for extraction (guard clauses, validations, calculations, formatting, side effects) and propose each subfunction with name, input, output, and justification targeting {{UMBRAL_COMPLEJIDAD}}; mark for explicit approval any change to a public signature. Phase 3 Refactor: after my go-ahead, apply the extractions one by one maintaining intentional names and contracts, leaving the root function as a readable orchestrator, faithful to the original style and to {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Phase 4 Verification: compare complexity before/after per function and confirm that the same inputs produce the same outputs and effects.

Rules: preserve public signatures and contracts unless given explicit approval; do not introduce new dependencies or change observable behavior; do not invent missing data, ask for it before executing. If {{FUNCION}} is already below {{UMBRAL_COMPLEJIDAD}} or does not admit safe extractions, say so and justify it instead of fragmenting artificially.

Deliverable: refactored code block (lean function plus subfunctions) + extraction table (what was extracted and why) + cyclomatic complexity comparison before/after per function + behavioral equivalence note.

Variables:
- {{FUNCION}}: code of the function or method to refactor, with its minimum context (types, dependencies it uses).
- {{LENGUAJE}}: language and, if applicable, framework or style convention (e.g. Python PEP 8, TypeScript, Java).
- {{UMBRAL_COMPLEJIDAD}}: target cyclomatic complexity per function (e.g. 10 or fewer); if not defined, use a reasonable best practice and declare it.
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: limits to respect (immutable public signatures, no new dependencies, performance, etc.); if not applicable, indicate 'No additional restrictions'.

prompts.title: Eliminate duplicate code (DRY)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specializing in safe refactoring and abstraction design, with judgment to distinguish real duplication from accidental coincidence. I need to eliminate duplicate code in {{RUTAS_OBJETIVO}} of my project {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}}, applying DRY thoughtfully and without falling into the opposite trap: abstracting code that only looks similar by accident and ending up coupling modules that should evolve independently. If any essential data is missing, ask me before continuing; also ask me whether you have access to the code or if I paste it.

Proceed as follows. First inventory semantic duplication, not just textual: logic that does the same thing with different names, repeated validations, copied data mappings, duplicated error handling, identical query or request construction. Second, classify each finding into real duplication (same purpose and same reason to change), accidental coincidence (looks similar today but will evolve differently, do NOT touch), and tolerable duplication (unifying would cost more clarity than it saves); apply the rule of three with threshold {{UMBRAL_OCURRENCIAS}} (default 3): do not abstract with only two occurrences unless there is an explicit reason. Third, for each real duplication propose the unit of unification according to {{ESTRATEGIA_PREFERIDA}} (pure utility function, shared module, base class, hook, decorator, or parameterization) and justify why that one and not another. Fourth, apply the coupling test: if call sites would need boolean flags or if branches to differentiate themselves, declare that they were NOT the same concept and leave them separate. Fifth, refactor in small and reversible steps, migrate call sites one by one, preserve observable behavior, and respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}.

Deliverable: diffs per file, table of classified findings with occurrence count, contract of each new abstraction (signature, inputs, outputs, effects), and explicit list of migrated call sites and of code left intact with its reason. Keep tests green in the refactored area; if there are no tests in the critical area, warn before touching. Mark assumptions and pending ambiguities. Also consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Variables: {{RUTAS_OBJETIVO}}, {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}}, {{UMBRAL_OCURRENCIAS}}, {{ESTRATEGIA_PREFERIDA}}, {{RESTRICCIONES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Module renaming and reorganization
Framework or major version migration
prompts.content: Act as a senior platform engineer specializing in major-version framework migrations, with practice in strangler fig, codemods, expand-contract, and incremental refactors with the suite always green. I want to migrate {{BASE_DE_CODIGO}} to a major version per {{FRAMEWORK_Y_VERSIONES}} without freezing development or risking production, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}} and supported by {{ESTRATEGIA_DESPLIEGUE}}. Large migrations fail when done in a single jump without a safety net: they accumulate risk, block the team, and become irreversible. If any critical data needed to avoid breaking production is missing, ask before planning. Proceed as follows: (1) Framing: confirm {{FRAMEWORK_Y_VERSIONES}}, the shape of {{BASE_DE_CODIGO}}, and {{RESTRICCIONES}}. (2) Safety net: from {{COBERTURA_Y_RIESGOS}} identify the critical paths without coverage and propose characterization tests that freeze the current behavior as a reference; define the reproducible build-plus-suite command that will be the semaphore for each phase. (3) Breaking-changes inventory: based on the release notes and the official migration guide between source and target, list the incompatible changes that affect {{BASE_DE_CODIGO}} (removed or renamed APIs, changed defaults, transitive dependencies, configuration), classified by high, medium, or low impact and by whether a codemod or automated tool exists. (4) Phase plan: order the migration in small, independent phases applying expand-contract and strangler fig for large modules, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}; per phase declare the objective, affected files, green criterion, and rollback plan per {{ESTRATEGIA_DESPLIEGUE}}. (5) Execution of the first phase: apply only that phase, prefer codemods for mass mechanical changes and manual editing for semantic ones, protect the risky parts with feature flags, run build plus suite at the close, and report the semaphore. Advancement rule: never advance with the suite red. Veracity: do not invent APIs, flags, or codemods from the target version; anything not confirmable against official documentation mark [ASSUMPTION] with its verification path. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliverable: plan in verifiable phases (table phase / objective / files / green criterion / rollback) plus classified breaking-changes inventory plus safety-net status plus execution of the first phase with its semaphore plus residual risks and assumptions.

prompts.title: Incremental migration from JS to TypeScript
prompts.content:
Act as a senior TypeScript engineer specializing in progressive migrations of production JavaScript codebases. I need an executable incremental migration plan to activate TypeScript without a big-bang rewrite and without freezing development: JS/TS coexistence from the first commit, growing strictness, and a green build at every step.

Project context:
- Package manager: {{GESTOR_PAQUETES}} (npm, pnpm, yarn, bun)
- Bundler or build toolchain: {{BUNDLER}} (Vite, webpack, esbuild, tsc, Next, none)
- Framework or environment: {{FRAMEWORK}} (React, Node/Express, Vue, vanilla)
- Pilot file (leaf module without internal dependencies to migrate first): {{ARCHIVO_PILOTO}} (e.g. src/utils/format.js)
- Target strictness level: {{NIVEL_STRICT_OBJETIVO}} (noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, full strict)
- Command that defines green build: {{COMANDO_VERIFICACION}} (e.g. npx tsc --noEmit && npm test)

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand about the current state and present the plan before touching anything. If any parameter arrives empty or ambiguous, ask before advancing; do not invent the toolchain.

Execute in phases:
- Phase 0 Inventory: detect {{GESTOR_PAQUETES}}, {{BUNDLER}}, {{FRAMEWORK}}, existing tsconfig, and the green-build definition; map the dependency graph to fix the order, starting from {{ARCHIVO_PILOTO}}. Verify that the current suite passes green with {{COMANDO_VERIFICACION}} BEFORE starting (baseline); if it does not pass, stop and report it.
- Phase 1 Scaffolding: install TypeScript and the environment @types with {{GESTOR_PAQUETES}}; generate a permissive initial tsconfig.json (allowJs: true, checkJs: false); confirm green build with JS intact.
- Phase 2 Leaf migration: convert leaf modules to .ts one by one starting with {{ARCHIVO_PILOTO}}; rename .js to .ts, convert JSDoc to native types, type signatures and exports; where there is no clear type use explicit any with a // TODO: type mark; never change business logic.
- Phase 3 Strictness escalation: raise in steps up to {{NIVEL_STRICT_OBJETIVO}} (noImplicitAny, then strictNullChecks, finally strict: true); activate one flag at a time, resolve errors, and do not advance without a clean green.
- Phase 4 Closure: reach {{NIVEL_STRICT_OBJETIVO}}, eliminate the any TODO items as possible, and leave a record of remaining type debt with its location.

Hard rules: zero changes to business logic; zero new runtime dependencies (only type devDependencies); preserve the module format and bundler config; run {{COMANDO_VERIFICACION}} before each commit and keep the build green at all times.

Edge cases: libraries without @types (declare module or shim, register debt), partial or contradictory JSDoc (the signature prevails, annotate discrepancy), dependency cycles (migrate the most stable node first and document it), side-effects on import, and spreading any (bound at the module boundary).

Deliverables: commented initial tsconfig.json, justified migration order table, strictness escalation sequence with advancement criterion, per-migrated-file verification checklist, and pending type-debt record.

prompts.title: Apply a design pattern where it fits
prompts.content: Act as a senior software engineer specializing in refactor and design patterns, with mastery of the GoF catalog and Martin Fowler's smells-and-refactorings framework. Work on code in {{LENGUAJE}}. The code to evaluate is {{CODIGO}}, which feels hard to maintain; the perceived symptom is {{SINTOMA_PERCIBIDO}}. I suspect that {{PATRON_CANDIDATO}} applies (or 'no suspicion'). I want to reduce or improve {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Decide with evidence, not by trend. Steps: (1) Read {{CODIGO}} and name the concrete smells present (growing switch, branch duplication, coupling to an external dependency, low testability, polymorphic conditional, feature envy), citing the exact line or block that evidences each one; do not invent generic smells. (2) Evaluate {{PATRON_CANDIDATO}} plus at least one alternative pattern and the no-pattern option against the dominant smell, using {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} as judge; discard those that do not fit with one reason sentence each. (3) Make an unambiguous decision: which pattern to apply and where, or declare that NO pattern applies and the simple version wins. (4) If a pattern applies, justify with {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}} the before (N) vs. after (M), deliver the fully refactored code running idiomatically in {{LENGUAJE}}, the step-by-step migration guide without a big bang, and a characterization test that demonstrates identical observable behavior (same inputs, same outputs, same effects). (5) If NO pattern applies, explain the avoided abstraction cost and propose the simple improvement instead (extract function, rename, lookup table, guard clause). Hierarchy in conflict: preserved behavior over elegance; reduction of change points over number of patterns; readability over academic purism. Flag assumptions about code not shown and do not assume hidden dependencies. If {{LENGUAJE}}, {{CODIGO}}, or {{SINTOMA_PERCIBIDO}} are missing, ask before responding. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Paying down prioritized technical debt
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specializing in maintainability and systematic technical debt reduction, with the judgment to distinguish debt that slows delivery from cosmetic noise. Your mission: convert the diffuse debt of {{REPOSITORIO_O_MODULO}} into a return-prioritized payoff queue, not a reflexive one, so that every refactor executed releases measurable delivery velocity and enables {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}.

If any essential data is missing from the parameters, ask before continuing instead of assuming.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understood and present your plan; execute only when the plan is clear.

Execute in phases:
1. Inventory. Walk the {{STACK}} code and the {{SENALES_DOLOR}} evidence; list only evidenced debt: duplication, long or coupled functions, lack of tests, outdated or vulnerable dependencies, misguided abstractions, TODO/FIXME and workarounds. Group similar findings into items with a clear name and concrete location (file and line, or module). Mark as [ASSUMPTION] everything inferred; do not invent findings.
2. Scoring. Rate each item on two axes from 1 to 5: impact (how much it slows delivery, multiplies bugs, or elevates risk, considering {{SENALES_DOLOR}}) and effort (cost to pay it down). Justify each axis in one line. Calculate ROI = impact / effort.
3. Prioritization. Order the queue from highest to lowest ROI. Elevate critical security or stability debt to a separate must-fix list, even if its ROI is low.
4. Payoff plans. For the {{TOP_N}} highest-ROI items deliver a plan: proposed change, ordered steps, affected files, non-regression test, and observable success signal. Each plan must be small, reversible, and isolated.

Limits: do not refactor everything at once or rewrite the repository; one item at a time. Edge cases: if {{REPOSITORIO_O_MODULO}} has no tests, the first plan must create the minimal harness before touching logic; if two items touch the same files, declare the dependency order; if the reported pain is not evidenced in the code, say so instead of fabricating a finding.

Consider attachments if provided: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Final deliverable: (1) debt table with item, location, impact, effort, ROI, and justification; (2) security and stability must-fix list; (3) the {{TOP_N}} highest-ROI payoff plans ready to execute. Neutral and professional English, no meta-discourse.

Parameters:
- {{REPOSITORIO_O_MODULO}}: concrete repository or module on which debt is inventoried.
- {{STACK}}: language, framework, and tools (e.g. TypeScript + React + Vitest).
- {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}: goal that the debt reduction must enable (e.g. accelerate time-to-market of features).
- {{SENALES_DOLOR}}: evidence of current pain (recurring bugs, fragile modules, slow builds); optional.
- {{TOP_N}}: how many highest-ROI items to convert into an executable payoff plan (e.g. 3).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Separate layers and break dependencies
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specializing in clean architecture (ports and adapters) and test-assisted safe refactoring. I have a module in {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}} — specifically {{MODULO_OBJETIVO}} — that mixes UI, business rules, and data access or external services in the same files, which makes every change costly, renders tests fragile, and prevents reusing the domain. The observed symptoms are: {{SINTOMAS_ACOPLAMIENTO}}. The involved infrastructure is: {{DEPENDENCIAS_EXTERNAS}}. Existing test safety net: {{COBERTURA_PRUEBAS}}. I want to decouple it into three layers with explicit boundaries and dependency inversion, preserving observable behavior: zero functionality changes. If any key data from the above is missing, ask before proposing anything and do not invent the structure.

Deliverable: (1) coupling map with file and line evidence from {{SINTOMAS_ACOPLAMIENTO}}; (2) classification of each responsibility as UI, domain, or infrastructure; (3) the target dependency rule (the domain does not import UI or infrastructure; UI and infrastructure depend on the domain via ports that the domain defines); (4) the ports for {{DEPENDENCIAS_EXTERNAS}} as interfaces or contracts, their concrete adapters, and the injection mechanism; (5) a refactoring sequence in small, reversible, compilable steps verifiable against {{COBERTURA_PRUEBAS}} — extract pure domain, invert data dependencies, decouple UI — each step with a green build; (6) the final code per layer; (7) a textual before-and-after dependency diagram. If {{COBERTURA_PRUEBAS}} is empty or insufficient, add characterization tests that freeze the current behavior before moving a single line. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] everything that is not inferable from the code. Flag the risks of each step (shared mutable state, transactions crossing layers, hidden side effects, import cycles) and how to mitigate them.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Parameters: {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}}, {{MODULO_OBJETIVO}}, {{SINTOMAS_ACOPLAMIENTO}}, {{DEPENDENCIAS_EXTERNAS}}, {{COBERTURA_PRUEBAS}}.

prompts.title: Simplify an over-engineered function
prompts.content: Act as a senior software engineer specializing in legacy code refactoring, with a YAGNI mindset and behavior-preservation discipline. Simplify this over-engineered function: {{FUNCION}}. Real places where it is invoked: {{CALL_SITES}}. Constraints to respect: {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Your goal is not prettier code but less code that does exactly the same thing, verifiable against the tests. Steps: 1) Summarize in one sentence what {{FUNCION}} actually does according to observed inputs/outputs at {{CALL_SITES}}, not according to name or comments. 2) Inventory every abstraction (interfaces, factories, wrappers, optional parameters, flags, indirections, speculative generalizations) and classify each as USED or SPECULATIVE per {{CALL_SITES}}, with evidence. 3) If there are no tests covering {{FUNCION}}, write 2 or 3 characterization tests first that fix the current behavior, including at least one edge case (nulls, empties, limits, errors), before touching anything. 4) Rewrite applying in order, one change at a time: (a) eliminate parameters and branches that no call site exercises, (b) inline single-use indirections, (c) replace single-implementation design patterns with direct code, (d) preserve public signature unless justified within {{RESTRICCIONES}}. 5) Deliver before/after diff + 'what was removed and why' table traceable to {{CALL_SITES}} + test block + verification note. Rules: do not introduce new dependencies; if {{CALL_SITES}} does not allow a decision, mark [ASSUMPTION] and preserve the branch. If {{FUNCION}}, {{CALL_SITES}}, or {{RESTRICCIONES}} are missing, ask before starting. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Generate unit tests with edge cases
API integration tests
prompts.content:
Act as a senior quality engineer (QA Automation / SDET) specializing in contract and integration testing of HTTP APIs. I want an executable integration test suite that exercises real HTTP endpoints against their contract, not against mocks: the safety net that lets me refactor and iterate fast without breaking consumers. Work with these parameters:
- ENDPOINTS: {{ENDPOINTS}} (list with method and path, e.g. POST /orders, GET /orders/{id}, DELETE /orders/{id}).
- FUENTE_CONTRATO: {{FUENTE_CONTRATO}} (OpenAPI/Swagger, Postman collection, or the service code).
- STACK_PRUEBAS: {{STACK_PRUEBAS}} (language and framework, e.g. Python+pytest+httpx, Node+Jest+supertest, Go+testing+net/http).
- ESQUEMA_AUTENTICACION: {{ESQUEMA_AUTENTICACION}} (e.g. Bearer JWT, API key in header, OAuth2, session cookie).
- ESTRATEGIA_DATOS: {{ESTRATEGIA_DATOS}} (e.g. test DB with transaction per test, factories, fixed fixtures, ephemeral container).
If any of those data are missing, ask instead of assuming. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understood and show me the plan before writing tests. Proceed as follows: (1) Consolidate a table of {{ENDPOINTS}} to expected states, response schema (mandatory fields, types, formats), and headers extracted from {{FUENTE_CONTRATO}}; mark with [ASSUMPTION] everything not documented. (2) Set up the scaffolding in {{STACK_PRUEBAS}}: HTTP client, base URL parametrizable by environment variable, authentication helpers for {{ESQUEMA_AUTENTICACION}}, and the seed/cleanup cycle of {{ESTRATEGIA_DATOS}}, with a dedicated environment or schema and never production data; seed before each case and clean after for idempotency and order independence. (3) Implement per endpoint: happy case, validation error (malformed body, wrong types, missing fields), authorization per {{ESQUEMA_AUTENTICACION}} (missing token, invalid/expired, insufficient permissions), and non-existent resource where applicable; cover pagination, retry idempotency, and size-limit edge cases if the contract defines them. (4) In each test assert HTTP status code, body shape against its schema, and relevant headers. (5) Deliver test code, setup/teardown, fixtures, flakiness handling (bounded timeouts and retries, no fixed sleeps), and a single command to run the suite, ready for CI. Close only when the suite runs green on a clean run and in any order, and deliver the pending assumptions to confirm.

prompts.title: End-to-end tests with Playwright
prompts.content:
Act as a senior QA automation engineer specializing in Playwright and change-resistant UI testing. I need an executable end-to-end suite that covers the flows the business charges for over {{URL_BASE}}, so that every deployment is validated in a real browser, regressions are detected before the user, and manual QA is reduced to an automated and repeatable verification strategy.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand and present your plan; execute only after. If {{URL_BASE}}, {{FRAMEWORK}}, or {{FLUJOS_CRITICOS}} are missing, ask before generating code; do not assume business values. Mark any technical assumption as [ASSUMPTION].

Design and construction: first list each flow from {{FLUJOS_CRITICOS}} as a sequence of user steps and map for each step the accessible selector that identifies it. Then generate the Playwright configuration with baseURL={{URL_BASE}}, retries only in CI, trace on-first-retry, screenshot only-on-failure, video retain-on-failure, and one project per each browser in {{NAVEGADORES}} (default Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Create the folder structure (tests, pages, fixtures). Implement the Page Objects first, with readonly locators and chainable action methods, and then the specs that consume them, one spec per flow with test.describe and test.

Non-negotiable rules: use only web-first assertions with auto-waiting (toBeVisible, toHaveURL, toHaveText); any fixed time wait is forbidden. Apply the strict selector order: accessible role with name, then label or placeholder, then visible text, and a test identifier only as a last resort; volatile CSS classes and positional XPath are forbidden. Isolate the state of each test per {{ESTRATEGIA_DATOS}} (fixture, API seed, or dedicated account) so they are independent and executable in any order. Cover at least one happy path and one error path per flow where applicable. Consider the framework {{FRAMEWORK}} for hydration and client-side navigations.

Verify the suite against these criteria before closing: each flow from {{FLUJOS_CRITICOS}} has its spec with at least one observable-result assertion; zero fixed waits; selectors in the correct order without volatile classes or XPath; each page encapsulated in a Page Object; independent tests; config with retries in CI, trace, screenshot, and video on failure, and projects for {{NAVEGADORES}}. Deliver the complete project folder with the configuration, the Page Objects, the specs per flow, and separately the installation command, the execution command, and the command to open the trace viewer; leave everything ready to run locally and in CI. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

Parameters:
- {{URL_BASE}}: base URL of the app under test (local or staging), e.g. http://localhost:3000
- {{FRAMEWORK}}: frontend framework of the app (React, Next.js, Vue, Angular, or other)
- {{FLUJOS_CRITICOS}}: 2 to 4 user flows to automate (registration, login, checkout, search)
- {{NAVEGADORES}}: target browsers (optional; default Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit)
- {{ESTRATEGIA_DATOS}}: how test data is prepared and isolated (optional; fixtures, API seed, or dedicated account)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: AI-guided TDD
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer who practices strict Test-Driven Development in the Kent Beck style and is skilled at directing code agents so they do not skip the red phase or over-implement. I am going to build {{COMPONENTE_O_FUNCION}} by driving the Red-Green-Refactor cycle instead of requesting code and testing it afterward; the goal is for {{COMPORTAMIENTO_ESPERADO}} to become an executable specification, with code born covered and an auditable log.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before writing anything, restate in your own words {{COMPONENTE_O_FUNCION}}, {{COMPORTAMIENTO_ESPERADO}}, {{STACK_Y_FRAMEWORK_TEST}}, {{CASOS_Y_BORDES}}, and {{RESTRICCIONES}}; if you are missing any of these inputs or detect ambiguity, ask for it instead of inventing business rules or dependencies. Then present your plan: order {{CASOS_Y_BORDES}} from least to most difficult (trivial case first; errors, edge cases, and invariants afterward) and declare the order of attack.

Execute the cycle one case at a time: (1) Red: write a single test with a clear assert and a name that describes the business rule; do not write production code in this step. (2) Verify the red: declare that the test fails and why; the valid reason is absent behavior or an unmet assert, never a compilation or import error; if it would fail for the wrong reason, fix the test first. (3) Green: write the minimum production code that makes the test green and nothing more; accept the simplest possible solution (even a fixed value) as long as no test exists to rule it out; do not anticipate future cases. (4) Refactor: with the suite green, eliminate duplication, improve names, and clarify the design without changing behavior; reconfirm green. Repeat until the list is exhausted, integrating edge cases, errors, and invariants.

Close by delivering the complete suite in {{STACK_Y_FRAMEWORK_TEST}}, the production code, and a log that records for each case: red test, reason for failure, minimum code applied, and refactor performed. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every decision made without confirmed data, declare that coverage of {{CASOS_Y_BORDES}} was achieved, and respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Do not mark the work as done without the suite running green at the end.

Variables:
- {{COMPONENTE_O_FUNCION}}: name and one-line description of the unit to build (function, class, module, or endpoint).
- {{COMPORTAMIENTO_ESPERADO}}: what it must do; inputs, outputs, and observable business rules.
- {{STACK_Y_FRAMEWORK_TEST}}: language, runner, and test framework (e.g. TypeScript with Vitest, Python with pytest, Java with JUnit 5).
- {{CASOS_Y_BORDES}}: happy-path cases, edge cases, expected errors, and invariants to cover.
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: conventions, allowed dependencies, prohibitions, or assert style (optional).

prompts.title: Increase meaningful coverage, not filler coverage
prompts.content:
Act as a senior quality engineer (QE) expert in risk-based testing strategy and in distinguishing meaningful coverage from filler coverage. Your goal: raise the useful coverage of {{MODULOS_OBJETIVO}} without chasing the percentage, concentrating effort where a defect hurts in production. Stack: {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}}. Test and coverage framework: {{FRAMEWORK_TEST}}. Current coverage: {{COBERTURA_ACTUAL}}. Useful coverage goal and/or mutation score: {{META_COBERTURA}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Proceed as follows:
1. Read the coverage report from {{ADJUNTOS}} and list the lines and branches NOT covered in {{MODULOS_OBJETIVO}}, mapping each gap to its function.
2. Classify each gap as risk logic (conditionals, error handling, calculations, validations, iteration limits, concurrency, mutable state) or noise (generated code, logging, trivial accessors, configuration).
3. Prioritize the backlog by impact x failure probability: for each real gap indicate what defect it could hide and the impact if it breaks in production.
4. Design, before coding, the cases per gap: happy path, edge cases, invalid inputs, and error paths.
5. Write the tests in {{FRAMEWORK_TEST}} with the Arrange-Act-Assert pattern, descriptive names, and assertions on observable behavior (value, state, exception, effect), never asserts that only confirm the code ran.
6. Explicitly declare what is NOT worth testing and why.
7. Close with the command or method to validate real utility via mutation testing on {{MODULOS_OBJETIVO}}: a test that kills no mutation is filler.

Mark with [ASSUMPTION] everything you infer when the report or code is insufficient, and do not invent APIs or signatures not present in the code.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

If {{ADJUNTOS}}, {{LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}}, {{FRAMEWORK_TEST}}, or {{MODULOS_OBJETIVO}} is missing, ask before starting.

Deliverable: risk-prioritized backlog + test suite ready to integrate + mutation verification note.

prompts.title: UI visual regression tests
prompts.content:
Act as a senior frontend quality engineer specialized in automated visual testing, with mastery of anti-flakiness strategies and CI pipeline design. I need to shield the interface of {{COMPONENTES_O_VISTAS}} against unintentional visual changes: a CSS refactor, a dependency bump, or a theme adjustment can break the layout without any functional test noticing. A snapshot-based visual regression suite captures baselines and compares every change pixel by pixel, turning visual appearance into a versionable assertion. The known risk is fragility: if images change due to animations, fonts, or random data, the team loses confidence and silences the suite.

Deliverable: a ready-to-operate suite on {{COMPONENTES_O_VISTAS}} with complete configuration for {{STACK_Y_HERRAMIENTA}}, an example end-to-end snapshot test, and an operation runbook. If any data is missing, ask for it concretely before executing; do not invent the tool or its native snapshot capabilities.

Proceed as follows: (1) Surface inventory, prioritizing within {{COMPONENTES_O_VISTAS}} what is critical, reused, and historically fragile, and declaring what is excluded because it changes design every sprint. (2) Capture matrix, deriving from {{ESTADOS_Y_VIEWPORTS}} only the state x viewport combinations with real signal and justifying each inclusion. (3) Anti-flakiness strategy with at least five concrete measures before capturing: animations and transitions disabled, fonts preloaded, dates and randomness frozen with deterministic data or mocks, waits for stable state and not for time, and masking of dynamic regions. (4) Baseline generation and versioning in {{STACK_Y_HERRAMIENTA}}: how they are created, where they live (repository or snapshot service), and how they are regenerated in a controlled manner. (5) Comparison and tolerance according to {{TOLERANCIA_Y_CI}}, configuring the threshold in pixels and percentage, justifying the value, and describing how diffs are read. (6) CI integration: job that runs on every pull request, fails on unapproved diffs, publishes expected/actual/difference images as artifacts, and exposes an intentional-change approval flow with human review. (7) Governance: who approves new baselines, how blind-approval of diffs is prevented, and what metrics measure suite health (flake rate, execution time, critical surface coverage).

Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any data not provided. Cover edge cases: cross-browser rendering, variable-length i18n content, dark/light mode, entry animations, slow external images, and the first run without a prior baseline. Deliverable: plan + complete pasteable configuration without rewriting + an end-to-end snapshot test that runs as-is + baseline generation/update commands + runbook (run locally, update baseline, interpret a failure), all consistent with {{COMPONENTES_O_VISTAS}}, {{STACK_Y_HERRAMIENTA}}, {{ESTADOS_Y_VIEWPORTS}}, and {{TOLERANCIA_Y_CI}}. Close with a verifiable acceptance checklist.

Parameters:
- {{COMPONENTES_O_VISTAS}}: components, pages, or views that are candidates for baseline.
- {{STACK_Y_HERRAMIENTA}}: UI framework and snapshot tool.
- {{ESTADOS_Y_VIEWPORTS}}: states to capture and target viewports.
- {{TOLERANCIA_Y_CI}}: acceptable difference threshold and CI pipeline.

prompts.title: Coherent mocks, stubs, and fixtures
prompts.content: Act as a senior testing engineer specialized in test double design and fixture architecture, with strong criteria on test-implementation coupling. Design the test doubles (stub, mock, spy, fake) and a coherent fixture factory for {{MODULO_O_DEPENDENCIA}} in {{LENGUAJE_Y_FRAMEWORK_TEST}}. The goal: a suite that validates observable behavior and not implementation, anchored to the public contract, with a single source of truth for data. Proceed as follows: Phase 1, dependency map: list the collaborations of {{MODULO_O_DEPENDENCIA}} and decide double by double (stub for input data, mock to verify expected interactions, spy to observe real calls, fake for lightweight in-memory implementation) or explicitly not double; justify each choice and point out where it is NOT appropriate to double to avoid over-mocking. Phase 2, contract: extract from {{CONTRATO_PUBLICO}} the signatures, returns, and observable errors that the doubles must respect; forbidden to depend on private methods, non-contractual internal order, or unexposed data structures. Phase 3, fixture factory: define a builder/factory with a single source of truth, consistent valid defaults, and partial overrides so each test requests only what is relevant. Phase 4, doubles: implement each double according to Phase 1, connected to the factory. Phase 5, demonstration and isolation: derive the fixtures of {{CASOS_LIMITE}} from the same factory without duplicating the schema, deliver at least two executable example tests, and a setup/teardown that ensures fresh state per test, reset between cases, and zero shared mutable state or implicit order. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Mark any data not provided as [ASSUMPTION] with a reasonable default value. If the public contract or test framework is missing, ask before coding. Deliverable: code file(s) with the factory, the classified doubles, and two tests ready to run in {{LENGUAJE_Y_FRAMEWORK_TEST}}, plus a brief note on doubling decisions. Variables: {{MODULO_O_DEPENDENCIA}}, {{LENGUAJE_Y_FRAMEWORK_TEST}}, {{CONTRATO_PUBLICO}}, {{CASOS_LIMITE}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Property-based testing for invariants
prompts.content:
Act as a senior quality engineer specialized in property-based testing (PBT), with mastery of generators, shrinking, and property catalogs in the QuickCheck/Hypothesis style (John Hughes, Scott Wlaschin). Your goal: convert the contract of {{CODIGO}} into an executable PBT suite in {{FRAMEWORK}} that catches bugs at the edges where example tests never look (empty string, zero, negative, unusual unicode, duplicates, boundary date, NaN, overflow).

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate {{CODIGO}}, {{FRAMEWORK}}, and its {{CONTRATO}} (input, output, preconditions, postconditions); if {{CODIGO}}, {{FRAMEWORK}}, or {{CONTRATO}} is missing or ambiguous, ask only for those items in a single round and do not invent the signature. Then present your plan in a brief property-candidate table before writing code. Then execute.

Deliver in this order: (1) Reconstructed contract of {{CODIGO}}: what it receives, what it returns, preconditions and postconditions, with an explicit assumption for every gap. (2) Table of 4 to 8 properties classified by pattern (invariant, round-trip, oracle, idempotency, commutativity/associativity, metamorphic, conservation); one line per property with the concrete bug it would catch; integrate {{INVARIANTES}} if provided; mark [ASSUMPTION] every property that depends on an unconfirmed precondition and discard redundant ones. (3) Input generators in {{FRAMEWORK}}: valid domain per parameter and forced edge cases with explicit weight (empty, zero, negatives, unicode/emoji, NaN/Inf, duplicates, numeric and date limits, large collections); use compound, filtered, or labeled generators and declare what you exclude. (4) One executable test per property, with a descriptive name, a clear assertion, and the {{PRESUPUESTO}} configuration (number of examples + fixed seed); group common configuration. (5) Guide for reading the minimal counterexample from shrinking when a property fails, distinguishing a bug in the code from a poorly specified property. (6) Point out at least one property whose failure would be a genuine bug and, if you suspect {{CODIGO}} is already broken, declare the counterexample you anticipate.

Quality rules: no property can be a disguised example test. Avoid flakiness (no unseeded randomness, no clock or network without freezing) and indicate how to reduce examples for CI without losing detection power. Close with the suite ready to paste and run, the property table by pattern, generators with explicit edges and exclusions, and the counterexample reading guide.

Parameters: {{CODIGO}} function/module/class under test; {{FRAMEWORK}} language + PBT library; {{CONTRATO}} input/output/preconditions/postconditions; {{INVARIANTES}} suspected properties (optional); {{PRESUPUESTO}} examples + seed + time limit (optional, default 100 examples and fixed seed). If a required item is missing, ask before executing.

prompts.title: Automated accessibility tests
prompts.content:
Act as a senior web quality engineer specialized in accessibility (WCAG/ARIA) and test automation in CI/CD, with experience in axe-core and headless runners. Your mission is to deliver a ready-to-integrate automated accessibility test configuration, with severity-based gating and a versioned baseline, so that every UI change is verified against WCAG without slowing the team down.

Situation: the project deploys frequently and accessibility degrades silently: every change can introduce WCAG violations that no one detects until a user or an audit reports them. Integrating automated checks in CI turns accessibility into a verifiable pipeline property: it blocks new regressions, makes inherited debt visible without slowing the flow, and produces auditable evidence on every pull request.

Parameters:
- FRAMEWORK: {{FRAMEWORK}} (frontend stack: React/Next, Vue/Nuxt, Angular, Astro, static site, etc.)
- PLATAFORMA_CI: {{PLATAFORMA_CI}} (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines)
- RUTAS_OBJETIVO: {{RUTAS_OBJETIVO}} (critical routes or views to audit, e.g. /, /login, /checkout)
- NIVEL_WCAG: {{NIVEL_WCAG}} (target version and level; assume WCAG 2.2 AA if omitted)
- REQUIERE_AUTH: {{REQUIERE_AUTH}} (whether routes require a session and how to obtain it; optional)

If any critical data is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it; never fabricate axe-core rule identifiers or selectors you cannot justify.

Deliver these steps: (1) Define the scope: routes from RUTAS_OBJETIVO, NIVEL_WCAG, and, if REQUIERE_AUTH applies, the session flow prior to the audit. (2) Generate the CI job for PLATAFORMA_CI that installs dependencies, starts or serves the app, and runs axe-core with a headless runner (Playwright or Puppeteer) consistent with FRAMEWORK; wait for the app to be ready (health-check) before auditing. (3) Map severity (critical, serious, moderate, minor) to a gate policy: fail the build on critical and serious by default; moderate and minor as configurable warnings. (4) Create a versioned baseline of pre-existing findings (snapshot per rule + stable selector) that does not block inherited debt but breaks the build on any new or worsened finding; document how to deliberately regenerate the baseline. (5) Produce a readable report attached to the pull request: WCAG rule violated, selector of the affected node, severity, impact, and correction suggestion. (6) Document the local command equivalent to the CI one.

Assumptions and limits: declare any assumption about how the app is started, ports, and environment variables; resolve flakiness from asynchronous loading with explicit waits, not fixed sleeps; handle routes with auth via reusable session state. Visibly warn that automation covers only a fraction of WCAG criteria and that a complementary manual checklist is required (keyboard, screen reader, contextual contrast, visible focus).

Acceptance criteria: the job runs on PLATAFORMA_CI and audits all routes from RUTAS_OBJETIVO; axe-core runs with a headless runner consistent with FRAMEWORK and NIVEL_WCAG declared in config; the gate fails on critical and serious; a versioned baseline exists that distinguishes debt from regression; the REQUIERE_AUTH flow runs before auditing when applicable; the pull request report includes rule, selector, severity, and impact; the local command replicates the CI one; the partial coverage warning is present.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Basic load and performance test
prompts.content:
Act as a senior performance and SRE engineer with experience in load testing distributed systems and diagnosing resource saturation. I want to discover where {{SISTEMA_OBJETIVO}} breaks under load before users discover it in production, turning the uncertainty of whether it will handle the peak into a defensible number and a prioritized list of bottlenecks, to decide capacity, autoscaling, and release go/no-go with evidence.

I need from you, in this order: (1) SLOs and pass/fail criteria derived from {{SLO_OBJETIVO}}: p95 and p99 latency, target throughput in req/s, and maximum error rate, each as a verifiable threshold. (2) Load model from {{TRAFICO_REFERENCIA}}: target virtual users or req/s, arrival profile, weighted mix of {{ENDPOINTS_CRITICOS}} summing to 100%, and a data strategy that avoids trivial caching through parameterization and unique data per iteration. (3) Three scenarios with duration and ramp: nominal at expected load, stress with an increasing ramp until degradation, and a sudden spike. (4) Executable script with {{HERRAMIENTA}} (if empty, choose between k6, Locust, or Gatling and justify) with hardcoded thresholds that abort or mark the run as failed on SLO violation, parameterized by environment and with prior warmup. (5) List of server-side metrics to instrument in parallel: CPU, memory, connections and database connection pool, queue depth, GC or runtime pauses, and external dependency latency; with the source of each metric (APM, exporter, logs). (6) Reading method: how to locate the knee point on the latency-vs-throughput curve, how to isolate the limiting resource (CPU saturation vs concurrency/pool vs lock contention vs dependency latency), and an actionable findings checklist with severity and suggested remediation.

Rules: never test against production without an agreed window and an abort plan; declare as [ASSUMPTION] every assumed capacity or traffic data point; mark as TODO any missing real value; include a single-user baseline to separate intrinsic latency from load-induced latency; consider coordinated omission and how your generator mitigates it. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{SISTEMA_OBJETIVO}}, {{SLO_OBJETIVO}}, or {{TRAFICO_REFERENCIA}} is missing, ask for them: they are blockers. Deliver a document with a scenario table, a script commented with thresholds, a server instrumentation list, and an actionable findings checklist prioritized by severity.

prompts.title: Design a normalized database schema
prompts.content:
Act as a senior relational database engineer and data modeler, with experience in high-volume transactional schemas and query tuning. I need to design the persistence layer of an application in the domain {{DOMINIO}} on {{MOTOR_DB}}: a normalized schema, correct from day one, with key, index, and denormalization decisions justified against the real query flows {{CONSULTAS_FRECUENTES}}. A poorly modeled schema is paid for throughout the product's lifetime in update anomalies, duplicated data, costly migrations, and slow queries.

Inputs:
- MOTOR_DB: {{MOTOR_DB}} (target relational engine and version, e.g. PostgreSQL 16, MySQL 8, SQLite, SQL Server 2022)
- DOMINIO: {{DOMINIO}} (business domain and application purpose)
- ENTIDADES: {{ENTIDADES}} (main entities with their attributes, uniqueness rules, and relationships I already intuit)
- CONSULTAS_FRECUENTES: {{CONSULTAS_FRECUENTES}} (most frequent read/write flows the schema must serve quickly)
- VOLUMEN_ESTIMADO: {{VOLUMEN_ESTIMADO}} (order of magnitude of rows per table and growth rate; optional)

Before modeling, confirm {{MOTOR_DB}}, {{DOMINIO}}, {{ENTIDADES}}, {{CONSULTAS_FRECUENTES}}, and {{VOLUMEN_ESTIMADO}}; if any critical data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it. Do not assume the engine or invent entities; mark any unavoidable assumption as [ASSUMPTION] with its impact if it turns out to be false.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate domain, entities, and detected business rules and mark the gaps; then present your plan; only then execute.

Deliver in four phases. Phase 1, Understanding: entities, attributes, and detected business rules, with gaps marked. Phase 2, Logical modeling: functional dependencies, primary keys (prefer surrogate keys unless a clearly superior natural key exists, justify), relationships with FKs, many-to-many with junction tables, normalization to 3NF explaining what dependency each step resolves. Phase 3, Physical modeling: types and constraints for the {{MOTOR_DB}} dialect, NOT NULL, CHECK, and UNIQUE that encode business rules, ON DELETE / ON UPDATE policy for each FK, indexes derived from {{CONSULTAS_FRECUENTES}} (indexed FKs, composites with justified order, unique ones), and denormalizations marked with their cost. Phase 4, Delivery: complete DDL executable without editing, entity-relationship diagram in Mermaid, and a table that justifies each key, index, constraint, and normalization level.

Detect and correct anti-patterns: lists or CSVs in a column, volatile natural keys, absence of referential integrity, booleans for states that should be lookup tables, dates without time zone when it matters; for each one propose the alternative. Close with verifiable acceptance criteria: the DDL runs cleanly on {{MOTOR_DB}}, each table has a justified primary key, no FK is left unindexed, each index maps to a real flow from {{CONSULTAS_FRECUENTES}}, and every exception to 3NF is documented with reason and cost.

prompts.title: Write safe database migrations
prompts.content:
Act as a senior database engineer specialized in zero-downtime schema changes on {{MOTOR_BD}}, with experience on high-volume tables. I need to unlock the change {{CAMBIO_ESQUEMA}} on {{TABLA_Y_VOLUMEN}} without downtime or data loss, in the format of {{HERRAMIENTA_MIGRACION}} and compatible with a {{ESTRATEGIA_DESPLIEGUE}} release strategy, so that any engineer can review, execute, and revert with confidence. If any essential data is missing, ask before assuming; mark anything not provided as [ASSUMPTION] or ask.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate {{CAMBIO_ESQUEMA}}, classify it (additive, data transformation, or destructive), and present your expand-contract plan before writing code.

Proceed as follows:
1. Restate {{CAMBIO_ESQUEMA}} and classify it; list the code dependencies that touch it (reads, writes, ORM, views, triggers, FKs, jobs) and identify incompatibilities with the current code.
2. Design the expand-contract plan in backward-compatible phases (Expand, Backfill, Switch, Contract), indicating what code deployment accompanies each phase according to {{ESTRATEGIA_DESPLIEGUE}} and why each is reversible except for the final contraction.
3. For each phase write the up and down scripts, idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS / IF EXISTS or equivalent in {{MOTOR_BD}}) and transactional where the engine allows it; isolate blocking DDL from long transactions.
4. Create indexes in concurrent or non-blocking mode specific to {{MOTOR_BD}}; run the backfill on {{TABLA_Y_VOLUMEN}} in batches with a row limit and pause between batches to avoid long locks.
5. Deliver a runbook with the exact execution order, integrity verification commands (counts, nulls, validated constraints, replica lag), and rollback per phase; mark each destructive step as irreversible with its prior safety window.

Final deliverable: the up/down scripts per phase in the format of {{HERRAMIENTA_MIGRACION}} plus the deployment and rollback runbook, ready for peer review. Justify the trade-offs (window duration, double-write cost, temporary objects) and warn about edge cases: NOT NULL FK on data with orphans, type change with precision loss, constraint validation locks, and backfill retries on mid-run failure.

Parameters:
- {{CAMBIO_ESQUEMA}}: the required schema change.
- {{MOTOR_BD}}: the database engine and version.
- {{TABLA_Y_VOLUMEN}}: the affected table and approximate row count.
- {{HERRAMIENTA_MIGRACION}}: the migration tool and format.
- {{ESTRATEGIA_DESPLIEGUE}}: the release strategy.

prompts.title: Integrate a managed backend (Supabase / Firebase)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior full-stack engineer specialized in Backend as a Service integrations, with strong criteria on authentication, permission modeling, and data leak prevention. My application currently runs against mocked data or local state and needs a real backend to persist information across sessions, authenticate users, and isolate their data. Integrate a managed backend securely from the first commit.

Parameters:
- PROVEEDOR: {{PROVEEDOR}} (Supabase, Firebase, or "no preference" for you to recommend)
- STACK_FRONTEND: {{STACK_FRONTEND}} (client framework and language, e.g. React + TypeScript, Next.js, Flutter, Vue)
- ESTADO_PROYECTO: {{ESTADO_PROYECTO}} (project already created with keys on hand, or from scratch)
- ENTIDADES: {{ENTIDADES}} (data to persist and their relationships)
- REGLAS_ACCESO: {{REGLAS_ACCESO}} (who reads and writes each entity)
- METODO_AUTH: {{METODO_AUTH}} (email and password, magic link, OAuth Google/GitHub, or other)

Produce, in this order: (1) justified choice between Supabase and Firebase for {{PROVEEDOR}} and {{STACK_FRONTEND}}, without costs; if {{PROVEEDOR}} is already defined, justify how to use it better. (2) Steps to create or reuse the project according to {{ESTADO_PROYECTO}} and obtain the keys, separating public ones (client) from secret ones (service role / Admin SDK, never to the client or repo). (3) SDK configuration with environment variables, an example file without real secrets, and the .gitignore entry that protects the real file. (4) Complete authentication flow for {{METODO_AUTH}}: registration, sign-in, sign-out, session persistence and refresh, initial loading state, and route or view protection. (5) Data model for {{ENTIDADES}}: tables or collections, fields, types, relationships, and owner field. (6) Security rules (Row Level Security in Supabase or Security Rules in Firebase) that enforce {{REGLAS_ACCESO}}, denying by default and preventing cross-user access. (7) Manual test with two users that confirms the rules block reading and writing another user's data.

MetodologIA Protocol: restate {{PROVEEDOR}}, {{STACK_FRONTEND}}, {{ENTIDADES}}, {{REGLAS_ACCESO}}, and {{METODO_AUTH}}; if anything is missing or ambiguous ask in a single round. Present the plan (justified provider, entities, permission matrix per entity and operation, files to touch) before executing. Deliver applicable blocks with key placeholders marked. Close with the isolation test and a secrets checklist. Never mention prices or the word free; no real secret in code, examples, or logs; the result must run as-is when placeholders are replaced. If any parameter is missing, ask before generating code.

prompts.title: Implement secure authentication
prompts.content:
Act as a senior backend security engineer, specialist in identity management and session handling per OWASP ASVS. I need to add secure authentication to my application on {{STACK}} over {{FRAMEWORK}}: registration, login, session management, protection of {{RUTAS_PROTEGIDAS}} for {{TIPO_USUARIO}}, and logout. A correct implementation unlocks private functionality and trust; an incorrect one opens the door to credential theft, session hijacking, and data leaks.

Issue the session per {{ESTRATEGIA_SESION}}. If that value is "recommend one", choose between a server-side signed session cookie or a short-lived access JWT plus rotating refresh token and justify the choice based on my attack surface. Before generating code, confirm {{STACK}} and {{FRAMEWORK}}, where the app runs (web, pure API, mobile), whether there is multi-device session support, and what sensitive data is at stake; ask for anything missing rather than assuming.

Deliver a ready-to-integrate implementation with code commented on every security decision, by layer: 1) identity model with unique email or username and password hash, never plaintext; 2) registration and login hashing with Argon2id preferred (bcrypt or scrypt acceptable, never MD5 or SHA1), with strength validation and identifier normalization; 3) session issuance per {{ESTRATEGIA_SESION}}, with 5–15 min access tokens and a rotating revocable refresh token persisted server-side; 4) HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite cookie, never localStorage where XSS risk exists; 5) middleware that protects {{RUTAS_PROTEGIDAS}}, validates signature and expiration, and distinguishes 401 from 403; 6) logout that invalidates the session or revokes the refresh token; 7) defenses: rate limiting with progressive lockout, CSRF protection when cookies are used, anti-enumeration responses, and uniform response time. Do not hardcode secrets: deliver the list of environment variables.

Handle edge cases: password outside policy, duplicate identifier, expired or tampered token, already-rotated refresh token (reuse detection), and concurrent multi-device logout. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate what you understand and present your plan (identity schema, justified session strategy, files to touch) before executing. Close with a table of environment variables and secrets, and a testing note: registration, valid and invalid login, access to a protected route with and without a token, logout, expiration, and refresh-token reuse. Flag assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. Consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Parameters:
- {{STACK}}: backend language and runtime (e.g. Node.js, Python, Java, Go)
- {{FRAMEWORK}}: web or API framework in use (e.g. Express, FastAPI, Spring, Laravel)
- {{ESTRATEGIA_SESION}}: desired session model (server-side cookie, JWT access+refresh, or "recommend one")
- {{RUTAS_PROTEGIDAS}}: endpoints or areas requiring an authenticated user (e.g. /api/profile, admin panel)
- {{TIPO_USUARIO}}: profiles or roles to support (e.g. end user, admin)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Consume a third-party API with resilience
Inbound and outbound webhooks
prompts.content:
Act as a senior backend engineer specialized in webhook integrations and reliable event delivery on {{STACK}}. I need a production-grade implementation of a webhook receiver and emitter for {{PROVEEDOR_EXTERNO}} and own subscribers, with {{PERSISTENCIA}} migrations and an executable test suite. Before coding, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand (stack {{STACK}}, provider {{PROVEEDOR_EXTERNO}}, signature scheme, persistence {{PERSISTENCIA}}, policy {{POLITICA_REINTENTOS}}), declare as [ASSUMPTION] any missing data (signing algorithm, signature header name, timestamp format), and ask me for it if it blocks correctness; Plan by presenting the endpoint contract, the {{PERSISTENCIA}} table and key schema, and the delivery state machine (pending > delivered / retrying > dead-letter queue) before writing code; then Execute.

Inbound receiver: POST endpoint that reads the raw body before parsing, because the signature is calculated over the exact bytes; verify the HMAC-SHA256 signature from {{PROVEEDOR_EXTERNO}}'s signature header using constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks; validate the timestamp window against {{TOLERANCIA_TIMESTAMP}} and reject out-of-range requests to stop replays; apply idempotency by persisting {{CLAVE_IDEMPOTENCIA}} in {{PERSISTENCIA}} with a uniqueness constraint at the engine level, and on duplicate do not reprocess and respond 2xx; respond 2xx quickly after queuing the real processing, 4xx for non-recoverable failures like an invalid signature, 5xx for retryable transients.

Outbound emitter: assemble the payload with event id, type, ISO-8601 timestamp, and data; sign the body with HMAC-SHA256 and the subscriber's secret; attach signature and timestamp headers; deliver with retries and exponential backoff plus jitter per {{POLITICA_REINTENTOS}} on 5xx or timeouts, never retry on 4xx, and after exhausting attempts move the event to a dead-letter queue; record every attempt (status, HTTP code, latency, attempt number) in an auditable delivery log. Support secret rotation by accepting more than one valid secret during a transition window.
