Deliver idiomatic {{STACK}} code, idempotency-store and delivery-log migrations in {{PERSISTENCIA}}, and tests covering at minimum: valid and invalid signature, replay due to timestamp outside {{TOLERANCIA_TIMESTAMP}}, idempotent re-delivery of the same id without reprocessing, no-retry on 4xx, and dead-letter queue dispatch after exhausting attempts. Secrets only via environment variables, never in code. Close with instructions for configuring secrets and running the suite. If {{STACK}}, {{PROVEEDOR_EXTERNO}}, or the signature scheme are ambiguous, ask before assuming a nonexistent API. This is the StrategyAI that separates a prototype from an operable system.

Parameters:
- {{STACK}}: target language and framework (e.g. Node.js + Express, Python + FastAPI).
- {{PROVEEDOR_EXTERNO}}: emitter of inbound webhooks (e.g. Stripe, GitHub, own gateway).
- {{TOLERANCIA_TIMESTAMP}}: maximum accepted timestamp window to stop replays (e.g. 300 s).
- {{CLAVE_IDEMPOTENCIA}}: field that uniquely identifies the event (e.g. event_id from header).
- {{PERSISTENCIA}}: store for idempotency and delivery log (e.g. PostgreSQL, Redis).
- {{POLITICA_REINTENTOS}}: number of attempts and backoff base with jitter (e.g. 5 attempts, base 2 s) (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Integrate a payment gateway (Stripe)
Integrate an LLM as an app feature
prompts.content: Act as a senior backend engineer specialized in integrating LLMs into production, with experience in streaming, cost control, and prompt security. I need to turn an LLM call into a production feature inside {{APP_Y_FEATURE}}, not a demo: the app must receive the user's input, call the model, and return the response as a token-by-token stream, with spend bounded and the prompt protected against injection and leaks. The backend is {{STACK_BACKEND}} and the model comes from {{PROVEEDOR_MODELO}}. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. Design and implement the endpoint end-to-end: (1) Contract: route, method, request shape (user message, session or user identifier, optional context) and streaming response shape, including close and error events, with correct status code and SSE headers. (2) Token-by-token streaming with SSE or the {{STACK_BACKEND}}-equivalent mechanism, flushing each fragment without buffering the full response, with a heartbeat. (3) {{PROVEEDOR_MODELO}} client with a per-call timeout, retries with exponential backoff and jitter only on transient errors, idempotency, and cancellation on connection close. (4) Prompt assembly separating system, retrieved context, and user message; sanitize the input and apply the {{POLITICA_GUARDAS}} guards against injection and system-prompt leaks, treating user content as data with explicit delimiters. (5) Cost control per {{LIMITE_COSTOS}}: count or estimate input and output tokens, apply the per-user or per-session limit over a defined window, and cut with a clear message and typed event when the threshold is exceeded; document whether counting is prior or posterior. (6) Handle provider errors (rate limit, timeout, blocked content, network failure, empty response) translated into clear responses without leaking details or keys, with a correlation id. (7) Structured logging: tokens, latency, model, result, cut reason, and correlation id, without sensitive content or keys. Respect the stack and real names; flag missing data as [ASSUMPTION] and continue without inventing. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver: endpoint code, model client layer, prompt assembly with guards and cost control in {{STACK_BACKEND}}, plus integration notes (environment variables, how to test streaming locally, where to adjust model and budget), and a verification checklist marked against the code.

prompts.title: Build a minimum viable RAG
Cron jobs and background tasks
prompts.content:
Act as a senior backend engineer specialized in distributed systems, message queues, and reliable asynchronous processing. Design and implement a deploy-ready cron-job and background-task system for {{APP_Y_STACK}}, whose goal is to not lose work, not duplicate it, and to be observable and operable.

Context:
- App and stack: {{APP_Y_STACK}} (language, framework, ORM, runtime)
- Job use cases: {{CASOS_DE_USO_JOBS}} (separating scheduled/cron from async/events)
- Available infrastructure: {{INFRA_DISPONIBLE}} (is Redis available? monolith/containers/serverless, cloud provider, number of instances)

- Desired schedule: {{SCHEDULE_DESEADO}} (expressions and timezone; if omitted, propose and mark [ASSUMPTION])
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any critical data is missing, ask for it before coding the critical parts. Don't assume Redis or services the user doesn't have; every value proposed due to missing data is marked [ASSUMPTION].

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand and separate scheduled jobs from async ones, classifying each by criticality and side effect. Then present your plan. Only then execute.

Deliver: 1) technically justified mechanism decision per {{INFRA_DISPONIBLE}} with trade-offs; 2) job contract (typed payload, priority, timeout, retries with exponential backoff plus jitter, DLQ) aligned to {{REQUISITOS_CONFIABILIDAD}}; 3) real idempotency validated against the effects of {{CASOS_DE_USO_JOBS}}; 4) concurrency (workers, rate limiting, leader lock or single-flight); 5) observability (logs with job id, metrics, DLQ alerts and stuck jobs); 6) graceful shutdown; 7) executable code (scheduler for {{SCHEDULE_DESEADO}}, queue, worker, one real idempotent job from {{CASOS_DE_USO_JOBS}}, deployment) plus a test demonstrating retry and deduplication.

Acceptance criteria: consistency with {{INFRA_DISPONIBLE}}; verifiable idempotency; single cron fire across N instances; zero work loss on deploy; assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]. Close when the package is deployable and the test demonstrates retry and deduplication.

prompts.title: Cache and query optimization
prompts.content: Act as a senior backend engineer specialized in database performance, index design, and caching. I have {{SINTOMA}} (what feels slow and where) and I want to eliminate the bottleneck without scaling hardware or changing the system's observable behavior. Available context: engine and version {{MOTOR_DB}}; the query or code {{CONSULTA_O_ORM}}; measurement evidence {{PLAN_EJECUCION}}; volume and growth {{VOLUMEN_DATOS}}; current and target latency {{LATENCIA_ACTUAL}}. Work as follows: first validate that you have the minimum evidence; if {{PLAN_EJECUCION}} or {{LATENCIA_ACTUAL}} is missing, ask for it and don't invent values. Then establish a real baseline, not an estimate: list the dominant queries by cost or frequency and classify each problem as N+1, full scan due to a missing index, or repeated and cacheable recomputation. For each N+1, rewrite to a single query with a join or eager loading and show before/after. For each full scan, propose the exact index (columns, order, type; composite or partial when applicable) and deliver idempotent migration SQL, warning about its cost in writes and storage. For each expensive recomputation, define a cache with key, TTL, and explicit invalidation policy; never cache without invalidation. Consider edge cases: high write cardinality where the index penalizes more than it helps, index with wrong column order, cache that serves stale data in transactional flows, and low selectivity that makes the index useless. Explicitly discard every index or cache that doesn't pay for itself. Close with a repeatable verification plan over {{PLAN_EJECUCION}} and {{LATENCIA_ACTUAL}}: re-run the plan, compare plan and latency, confirm that the functional result hasn't changed. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Design an MCP server for the app
prompts.content:
Act as a senior agent-integration architect, specialist in the Model Context Protocol (MCP), typed API design, and application security. I want the complete design of an MCP server for {{APP_DOMINIO}} on {{STACK}}, ready to implement, that turns its capabilities into a stable tool contract without coupling each agent to the internal API and while preserving control of permissions and effects in the app.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the app and its entities ({{APP_DOMINIO}}), the stack and persistence ({{STACK}}), the capabilities to expose ({{CAPACIDADES}}), the authentication model ({{MODELO_AUTH}}), the sensitive actions ({{ACCIONES_SENSIBLES}}), and the transport ({{TRANSPORTE}}); present your plan; then execute. If any of those pieces of data are missing, ask me for them before proceeding and don't invent capabilities or permissions.

Execute in six phases:
1) Inventory: list every capability in {{CAPACIDADES}} with its effect type (read, reversible mutation, destructive mutation), whether it handles PII, and its expected cost or latency.
2) Classification: assign each capability to one of the three MCP surfaces and justify. Resources = read-only data addressable by URI (no effects). Tools = actions with effects and parameterized reads. Prompts = reusable templates. Tiebreaker rule: if it has effects or requires execution parameters, it goes to tool; if it's a pure, cacheable read, it goes to resource.
3) Contracts: for every tool define the name in snake_case, an agent-oriented description (what it does, when to use it, when not to), a JSON Schema input schema with types, required fields, defaults, and validations, an output schema, side effects, idempotency, and a structured error.
4) Security: design auth and authz starting from {{MODELO_AUTH}}, declare which credential the server uses, how it delegates end-user permission, minimum scopes per tool, explicit prior confirmation for each destructive action in {{ACCIONES_SENSIBLES}}, and PII controls.
5) Robustness: define agent-readable error codes, cursor-based pagination, rate limits and timeouts, and choose the transport per {{TRANSPORTE}} (stdio local, HTTP+SSE remote), justifying the decision.
6) Verification: build the test plan with valid, invalid, and edge cases per tool (permission denied, confirmation rejected, malformed input).

Declare your assumptions. Flag what can't be inferred as pending confirmation rather than inventing it.

Deliverable: design document with (1) capabilities table classified with effect and PII, (2) contract per tool, (3) textual diagram of the agent-server-app flow with the confirmation point, (4) list of security controls with scope per tool, and (5) test plan per tool with verifiable acceptance criteria.

prompts.title: Deploy to Vercel with correct configuration
Minimal CI/CD pipeline for vibe coding

prompts.title: Secure environment variable management

prompts.title: Preview deployments per pull request
Basic observability in production
prompts.content: Act as a senior SRE and observability engineer with experience operating production services under on-call rotation. My application on {{STACK}} has just gone to production on {{ENTORNO_DEPLOY}} and the team is operating blind: we do not know if it is serving traffic, if it is throwing errors or how long it takes to respond. I want the minimum essential that reduces uncertainty the most, not a complete platform. Before coding, confirm {{STACK}}, {{ENTORNO_DEPLOY}} and {{DESTINO_TELEMETRIA}}; if a piece of data is missing that would prevent giving executable code, ask for it instead of assuming, and mark any assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Then order the pieces by uncertainty reduction and deliver, for each one, the concrete code for {{STACK}}, where to place it in the codebase and why there, plus a verification executable in under five minutes. Pieces: (1) Structured logs in JSON with level, UTC ISO-8601 timestamp, message and a request ID propagated end to end; take it from the incoming header or generate it at the edge and carry it through context. (2) Centralized error capture: global handler for unhandled exceptions with stack trace and request context (path, method, request ID, status), that returns a clean 500 without leaking internals or secrets. (4) Health check that separates liveness (process alive, without touching dependencies) from readiness (critical dependencies ready, with timeout), suitable for {{ENTORNO_DEPLOY}}. (5) One or two initial alerts starting from {{UMBRAL_ALERTA}} when provided, with explicit numeric threshold and window. Prioritize {{ENDPOINTS_CRITICOS}} and direct the telemetry to {{DESTINO_TELEMETRIA}}. Never use high-cardinality identifiers as metric labels; group by normalized path. Close with an acceptance checklist and point out what is missing to mature (distributed traces, SLOs, dashboards), without implementing it now. Reframe what you understand and present your prioritized plan before executing.

prompts.title: Feature flags and gradual rollout
prompts.content: Act as a senior release engineering and progressive delivery engineer (canary, dark launch, kill switch) expert in preventing flags from becoming technical debt. We are going to put the feature {{NOMBRE_FEATURE}} in {{STACK}} into production behind a feature flag to decouple the deploy from its activation for users: the new code travels off, is turned on progressively and observedly, and can be turned off instantly without redeploy. The flag is a runtime switch with an owner, lifecycle and retirement date, not a forgotten if statement. Flags live and are edited in {{ORIGEN_FLAGS}}. The rollout is assigned deterministically using {{IDENTIFICADOR_USUARIO}} as the stable attribute. Deliver: (1) evaluation service with a single source of truth read from {{ORIGEN_FLAGS}}, exposed as a unique function isFlagActive(name, context) with safe default OFF; (2) deterministic assignment by stable hash of {{IDENTIFICADOR_USUARIO}} against the target percentage, with the guarantee that the same user always falls on the same side and, when raising the percentage between stages, a user already exposed never goes back to control (monotonic rollout); (3) a single example branching point where new and old routes coexist behind the same flag; (4) global kill switch that turns off the feature for everyone instantly without redeploy, fail-closed: if {{ORIGEN_FLAGS}} does not respond, times out or returns corrupt data, it evaluates to OFF, with last-good-value cache and explicit expiration policy; (5) instrumentation with logs and metrics tagged by variant (exposed vs control) and decision reason; (6) stages table {{ETAPAS_ROLLOUT}} with measurable advance and rollback criteria per stage, plus a flag and old code retirement plan when stabilizing at 100%. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides context. Explain assumptions, limits and trade-offs explicitly (anonymous users without a stable identifier, override lists for internal/QA users, flag concurrency, consistency between instances, cost of flag evaluation in the hot path). If {{ETAPAS_ROLLOUT}} is empty, propose a conservative default sequence (internal > 1% > 5% > 25% > 50% > 100%) and justify it. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan and present your plan, then Execute. Close only when the quality checklist is verified.

prompts.title: Custom domain, SSL and DNS

Optimize bundle and Core Web Vitals
Containerize the app with Docker
prompts.content: Act as a senior platform engineer with real Docker production experience and image optimization. I want to containerize {{NOMBRE_APP}} to eliminate the 'it works on my machine' problem, achieve a reproducible build, single-command onboarding and a deployable artifact on any orchestrator. Context: stack {{STACK}}, start {{COMANDO_ARRANQUE}}, port {{PUERTO}}, external services {{SERVICIOS_EXTERNOS}}, target environment {{ENTORNO_OBJETIVO}}, attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. Declare assumptions, edge cases (compiled vs interpreted, migrations at startup, statics, graceful shutdown) and justify trade-offs. No secret in layers or in the image.

prompts.title: Critical review of AI-generated code
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software engineer specialized in critical code review and application security, with practice in auditing the output of AI agents and assistants and distinguishing plausible from correct. An AI assistant produced {{CODIGO}} and, before integrating it, I need a critical review and not a complacent validation: the risk of AI-generated code almost never lies in the obvious, but in subtle bugs, false assumptions about data or environment, and shortcuts that pass the happy path but break in production. Your goal is to separate what the code claims to do from what it actually does, in the context of {{CONTEXTO_TAREA}}, respecting {{STACK_RESTRICCIONES}} and prioritizing {{SUPERFICIE_RIESGO}}.

Before auditing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe in your own words what the code should do according to {{CONTEXTO_TAREA}}, under what limits of {{STACK_RESTRICCIONES}}, and what part of {{SUPERFICIE_RIESGO}} you prioritized; present your review plan; then execute. If {{CODIGO}}, {{CONTEXTO_TAREA}} or {{STACK_RESTRICCIONES}} are incomplete to audit rigorously, ask for them instead of assuming.

Structure the audit as follows: (1) Framing: confirm the purpose according to {{CONTEXTO_TAREA}}, {{STACK_RESTRICCIONES}} and the priority of {{SUPERFICIE_RIESGO}}; declare what parts of the context you do not have in view. (2) Layer 1 - Correctness: subtle bugs, boundary conditions (empty, null, indices), off-by-one, loose type comparisons, ignored return values, async without await, unclosed resources, silenced errors, concurrency. (3) Layer 2 - False assumptions: what the code takes for granted without verifying (field always present, input already validated, infallible network, stable collection order, assumed library or version behavior). (4) Layer 3 - Dangerous shortcuts: empty catch, secrets in plain text, injection by concatenation of queries or commands, missing input validation, broad permissions, invented or non-existent dependencies, happy-path-only route. (5) Layer 4 - Maintainability: unnecessary complexity, duplication, misleading names, absence of tests on critical paths. (6) Integration verdict: Ready to integrate / Integrate with corrections / Do not integrate, with blockers.

For each finding give: exact location (line or block), 'what the code thinks happens' versus 'what actually happens', severity (Critical / High / Medium / Low) and concrete impact. For each Critical or High include a minimal code patch. Do not invent vulnerabilities; if an area is correct, declare it; mark [ASSUMPTION] what depends on invisible context; do not use invented data or figures. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as additional context. Deliver a table or list of findings prioritized by severity (by impact and probability, not by count), the minimal patches, and the final verdict with blockers.

prompts.title: Quick security audit (OWASP)
prompts.content: Act as a senior application security engineer (AppSec) with experience in code review, threat modeling, and practical remediation. Perform a fast, prioritized security audit of {{APP}} against the OWASP Top 10 (2021), with review depth {{PROFUNDIDAD}}. Technical context: {{STACK}}. Exposure surface: {{SUPERFICIE}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before concluding, gather context: if the relevant code, authentication and session handling, location of secrets, or the flow of user inputs toward the database or operating system is missing, ask for it before evaluating; do not invent vulnerabilities or assume configurations you cannot see. Walk through each of the ten categories: A01 broken access control, A02 cryptographic failures, A03 injection (SQL, NoSQL, commands, XSS), A04 insecure design, A05 security misconfiguration, A06 vulnerable and outdated components, A07 identification and authentication failures, A08 software and data integrity failures, A09 security logging and monitoring failures, A10 SSRF. Explicitly declare non-applicable categories and explain why. For each finding record: concrete evidence (file, line, or pattern), attack vector, and severity (critical, high, medium, low) justified by exploitability times impact. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any finding without visible code and indicate what data is missing to confirm it. Write the exact ready-to-apply fix (corrected code or configuration), not generic advice. Order from highest to lowest risk and build a remediation plan across three horizons: today, this week, this month. Deliver a findings table ordered by severity (OWASP category, evidence, vector, severity), a block of applicable fixes, and the prioritized plan. If {{PROFUNDIDAD}} or {{ADJUNTOS}} are not specified, assume a quick pass over critical paths and ask. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Detect and remediate leaked secrets
prompts.content:
Act as a senior application security engineer (AppSec) specializing in secrets management and credential exposure response. Audit {{REPOSITORIO}} for leaked secrets and deliver an actionable remediation plan within {{PLAZO_REMEDIACION}}. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, Plan your approach, and only then Execute. Restate the objective and present your plan in one or two lines before acting.

Proceed as follows: (1) Inventory: enumerate branches, age and depth of the history of {{REPOSITORIO}} and confirm the visibility {{VISIBILIDAD_REPO}}, because in public repos every hour counts and sets the rotation clock. (2) Detection: scan the working tree AND the complete commit history, not just the latest commit, looking for patterns from {{PROVEEDORES}}: API keys, tokens, private keys, connection strings with credentials, and high-entropy strings; consolidate findings without showing any secret in plaintext. (3) Per-finding record: file and line, commit and introduction date, secret type, obfuscated fragment (first 4 characters only), and live or test status. (4) Triage: classify by severity (critical, high, medium, low) by crossing the access scope with visibility {{VISIBILIDAD_REPO}}, and separate probable false positives (placeholders, documentation examples, test values) with justification. (5) Remediation in two lanes: rotation lane (for each live credential from {{PROVEEDORES}}, the provider, the revocation and re-issuance procedure, and the order according to {{PLAZO_REMEDIACION}}) and history purge lane with {{HERRAMIENTA_PURGA}} (coordinated force-push and notice for the team to re-clone). (6) Prevention and verification: detection pre-commit hook, migration to environment variables, exclusion file, plus the closure criterion: clean re-scan of tree and history after the purge.

If {{HERRAMIENTA_PURGA}} or {{PLAZO_REMEDIACION}} are missing, propose a reasoned default and mark it as an assumption. If {{REPOSITORIO}}, {{VISIBILIDAD_REPO}}, or {{PROVEEDORES}} are missing, ask before continuing. Consider attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Final deliverable: classified findings table, two-lane remediation plan, and list of preventive controls. Inviolable rule: no complete secret appears in plaintext anywhere in the output.

prompts.title: Input validation and sanitization against injection
prompts.content:
Act as a senior application security engineer (AppSec) specializing in injection prevention, with command of the OWASP Top 10, OWASP Cheat Sheets, and secure coding in {{STACK}}. I need to harden {{APLICACION}} against injection from a non-negotiable principle: no external input is trustworthy (forms, query params, headers, cookies, JSON payloads, uploaded files, API calls, and outputs from language models). Injection occurs when untrusted data is interpreted as code or a command in some interpreter (SQL, NoSQL, shell, browser, LDAP, XPath, parser, template engine, model); that is why the defense is not a single filter but positive validation at the edge plus a specific barrier at each context of use.

Deliver, prioritizing {{AMENAZAS}}: (1) surface inventory derived from {{ENTRADAS}} with their per-field contract (type, format, length, range, required/optional, allowed characters); (2) the positive validation layer with allowlist in {{CAPA_VALIDACION}}, with anchored regexes (^...$), size limits, and early rejection with the correct status code, using the idiomatic mechanism of {{STACK}}; (3) the correct barrier per destination: parameterized queries/prepared statements for SQL and typed operators for NoSQL, shell-free APIs with arguments as an array for commands, contextual output encoding plus CSP for HTML, safe escaping or parsing for LDAP/XPath and deserialization with an allowlist of types, canonicalization and path confinement against path traversal, strict separation of instructions and data against prompt injection; (4) sanitization with a maintained allowlist-based library (like DOMPurify) only where rejection is not an option; (5) abuse case suite with real vectors (quotes, union/boolean, null bytes, ../, double encoding, script tags, NoSQL operators, instruction sequences) that demonstrates neutralization barrier by barrier.

Rules: positive validation, never negative; regexes always anchored with ^ and $; rejection at the edge before touching logic, with a clear message that does not leak internal details; defense in depth; fail closed on ambiguous data; handle Unicode, normalization, and multibyte; treat model output as untrusted input. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any detail of {{STACK}} you infer. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Variables:
- {{APLICACION}}: name and one-line description of the application to protect.
- {{STACK}}: language, framework, ORM/database driver, and template engine (e.g. Node.js + Express + Prisma + React).
- {{ENTRADAS}}: external input surfaces and fields with their expected type.
- {{AMENAZAS}}: priority injection vectors according to context.
- {{CAPA_VALIDACION}}: main validation point (default: middleware at the edge plus schema validation).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Vulnerable dependency review
prompts.content:
Act as a senior software supply chain security engineer (SCA), specialist in OSV/GHSA advisories and semver update policies. Audit the dependencies of {{PROYECTO}} and deliver an actionable remediation plan. If any essential data is missing, ask in a single round before starting and do not invent values.

Variables:
- PROYECTO: {{PROYECTO}} (repository or folder to audit: path, name, or stack description)
- ECOSISTEMA: {{ECOSISTEMA}} (package manager and language, e.g. npm/pnpm, pip/poetry, go modules, cargo, maven; if omitted, deduce from lockfile)
- UMBRAL_SEVERIDAD: {{UMBRAL_SEVERIDAD}} (minimum CVSS severity to act on, e.g. "high and critical" or ">=7.0")
- TOLERANCIA_BREAKING: {{TOLERANCIA_BREAKING}} (appetite for breaking changes, e.g. "only patches/minors now, majors in backlog")
- COMANDO_BUILD_TEST: {{COMANDO_BUILD_TEST}} (command that keeps build/tests green, e.g. "npm run build && npm test"; optional)

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand about {{PROYECTO}} and its risk policy, present your audit plan, and only then execute.

Proceed as follows: (1) Detect the manifest and lockfile of {{PROYECTO}}; if {{ECOSISTEMA}} is missing, deduce it from the lockfile or ask, and set the correct native audit command (npm/pnpm audit, pip-audit, govulncheck, cargo audit, osv-scanner). Without a lockfile, declare the limit: transitive versions will not be exact. (2) Inventory direct and transitive dependencies with resolved version. (3) Cross-reference each one with native audit plus OSV/GHSA; cite exact CVE or GHSA and source; anything not verifiable goes as [ASSUMPTION] with how to confirm it, without inventing ids or versions. (4) Per finding report: package, current version, minimum corrected version, CVSS severity (with vector if it exists), direct/transitive path, and reachability in {{PROYECTO}}. (5) Prioritize by severity x exploitability x reachability; act on what meets or exceeds {{UMBRAL_SEVERIDAD}} and mark false positives for non-reachability with their justification. (6) Batch plan respecting {{TOLERANCIA_BREAKING}}: batch 1 semver-safe patches, batch 2 minors, batch 3 majors with isolated breaking changes; flag what requires code adjustment. (7) Transitive dependencies without fix from parent: propose override/resolution or parent bump and warn of divergence risk. (8) Tie each batch to a green verification with {{COMANDO_BUILD_TEST}}. Do not execute destructive changes: only plan.

Deliverables: prioritized findings table + batch remediation plan with commands and execution order. Close with pending assumptions to confirm.

prompts.title: Verify AI hallucinations in code
prompts.content:
Act as a senior code reviewer specializing in auditing AI agent outputs, with practice in dependency verification, supply chain security, and reading official documentation by version. An agent generated code in {{LENGUAJE_Y_STACK}} and I need to know with evidence what part is real and what part it invented before integrating it. Models hallucinate APIs, parameters, and package names that sound plausible but do not exist; an invented package also enables slopsquatting, where an attacker registers the hallucinated name and executes malicious code when it is installed. Your goal is to produce a traceable audit of {{CODIGO_O_DIFF}} that unlocks a safe merge, avoids breaking the build, and closes the supply chain vector, calibrated to {{RIESGO_Y_ENTORNO}}.

Before auditing, confirm the scope: {{LENGUAJE_Y_STACK}} (language, framework, and exact versions of the key libraries), {{CODIGO_O_DIFF}} (the code or diff to audit), {{FUENTES_DE_VERDAD}} (what you can consult: official docs by version, package registry, the existing repo, terminal access to install/compile/test), and {{RIESGO_Y_ENTORNO}} (criticality of the environment where it will run). If a key input is missing, ask before starting; if {{FUENTES_DE_VERDAD}} is not specified, assume official docs and public registries, and if {{RIESGO_Y_ENTORNO}} is not specified, assume production.

Proceed as follows. First, inventory from {{CODIGO_O_DIFF}} every verifiable claim: imports, packages, modules, submodules, functions, methods, classes, attributes, parameters, enum values, configuration keys, environment variables, paths, tables, and endpoints the code takes as given; order them by risk surface, with external dependencies and API calls first. Second, for each dependency verify against {{FUENTES_DE_VERDAD}} that the package exists in its official registry according to {{LENGUAJE_Y_STACK}} (npm, PyPI, crates.io, Maven Central, Go modules, NuGet, RubyGems), that the name is not a typosquat or slopsquat, and that the module or submodule exists in the declared version; treat every unknown dependency as suspicious until proven otherwise. Third, for each function, method, parameter, or enum confirm that it exists in the real signature of that library at that version, not in another version or a similarly-named library; mark hallucinated signatures and renamed, deprecated, or removed APIs, citing since when. Fourth, identify what the code assumes without evidence (config present, env var set, path or table existing, endpoint shape, stable behavior between versions, error handling, pagination) and convert it into a concrete question or executable check, calibrating rigor according to {{RIESGO_Y_ENTORNO}}. Fifth, classify each finding as CONFIRMED_REAL, HALLUCINATION, or NOT_VERIFIABLE_WITHOUT_EXECUTING, cite the exact source and the command or minimal test that demonstrates it; for each confirmed HALLUCINATION propose the corrected patch and, where it exists, the real equivalent API.

Rigor rules: never declare something real without indicating how to verify it; what cannot be checked with {{FUENTES_DE_VERDAD}} goes as NOT_VERIFIABLE_WITHOUT_EXECUTING and marked [ASSUMPTION], never as confirmed; when in doubt between versions, ask or report both. Edge cases: code that mixes two versions of the same library, deprecated but existing APIs, internal or private packages that will not appear in public registries (do not mark as hallucination: mark NOT_VERIFIABLE and ask for the internal index), and correct names imported from the wrong module.

Deliver, in neutral Spanish and without emojis: (1) findings table with columns claim, verdict, severity, source of truth, and evidence or command; (2) patches block, one per confirmed hallucination; (3) list of commands or tests to close the NOT_VERIFIABLE ones; and (4) global merge verdict (ready, ready-with-corrections, or blocked) with the reason. Before executing, restate in one or two lines what you understood and present your plan.

prompts.title: Rate limiting and abuse protection
Consistent error handling throughout the app
prompts.content: Unify error handling in {{APP_O_MODULO}}, built on {{STACK_LENGUAJE_FRAMEWORK}}, covering {{CAPAS}}, so that every failure follows the same path: it is typed, logged with context, and translated into a safe response. Act as a senior software engineer specializing in reliability and observability. Deliver a common error strategy implemented and documented. Steps: (1) Inventory how errors are currently captured, logged, and presented and list inconsistencies (scattered try/catch, loose logs, raw messages, disparate codes, silenced failures), classifying each finding by risk. (2) Design a typed error hierarchy that separates expected business errors, validation errors, external dependency failures, and unexpected failures; each type with a stable code, severity, whether it is retryable, and a safe message for the user. (3) Define a single capture point per layer that routes every error to the same pipeline and guarantees that none escapes without being logged. (4) Specify the structured log format integrated with {{SISTEMA_LOGGING}}: level, timestamp, correlation identifier propagated between layers, origin, error code, and useful context, without sensitive data (declare the fields to redact). (5) Define the presentation layer that translates each error into a user message and into {{CONTRATO_RESPUESTA}}, with explicit error-code-to-status mapping and a safe default message for unmapped types. (6) Refactor incrementally preserving public contracts, leave an end-to-end example for business and another for unexpected, and document how to add a new error type. Adjust the instrumentation depth to {{NIVEL_OBSERVABILIDAD}}. Resolve edge cases: errors inside the handler itself, failures before the correlation identifier exists, asynchronous code or uncaught promises, dependency timeouts, and errors that should not be exposed to the user but should be logged. If {{SISTEMA_LOGGING}} or {{CONTRATO_RESPUESTA}} are not provided, propose an idiomatic one and mark it [ASSUMPTION]. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Production-readiness checklist
prompts.content: Act as a senior site reliability engineer (SRE) with experience operating web services in production and conducting pre-launch reviews. I am about to launch {{NOMBRE_APP}} to production and need a production-readiness audit before exposing it to real users, with a substantiated Go or No-Go verdict, not a generic list. The stack is {{STACK}}, it runs on {{INFRAESTRUCTURA}}, and handles {{TIPO_DATOS}}; the launch window is {{FECHA_LANZAMIENTO}}. A rigorous review before the cutover avoids secret leaks, data loss without backups, and silent outages that nobody detects. If any critical data ({{STACK}}, {{INFRAESTRUCTURA}}, {{TIPO_DATOS}}) is incomplete, ask before assuming. Walk through four fronts in order. Security: secrets out of code (environment variables or secrets manager), HTTPS enforced, authentication and authorization per endpoint, input validation and injection protection, dependencies without known critical vulnerabilities, security headers and restricted CORS, rate limiting on public endpoints. Data: tested and reversible migrations, indexes on hot queries, absence of test data or seed credentials in production, retention and privacy policy for {{TIPO_DATOS}}. Backups: scheduled automated backup, end-to-end restore tested at least once, copies in a location separate from the production environment, RPO and RTO objectives defined. Monitoring: structured error logging, alerts to a watched channel, health metrics (latency, error rate, saturation), health check endpoint, minimum incident response plan with a named owner. Mark each control as covered, partial, or absent with evidence or assumption; label every assumption as [ASSUMPTION] and do not consider a copy proven unless it has been restored. If {{INFRAESTRUCTURA}} is serverless or managed, declare controls covered by the provider rather than marking them absent. Close with an unambiguous Go or No-Go verdict and blockers ordered by risk from highest to lowest, each with a concrete action and front. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Basic data privacy compliance
Generate SQL query from a natural-language requirement
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data engineer expert in analytical SQL and dimensional modeling, with judgment for detecting granularity traps, join fan-out, and NULLs. Translate {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} into a correct, readable, executable, and auditable SQL query against {{ESQUEMA}} in {{MOTOR_SQL}}. If {{ESQUEMA}}, {{MOTOR_SQL}}, {{DEFINICIONES_METRICAS}}, or {{RANGO_FECHAS}} are missing and are needed to answer without ambiguity, ask before writing SQL. Proceed as follows: (1) Reframe {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} as an explicit output model: columns, metrics, row granularity, and ordering; declare each gap as [ASSUMPTION]. (2) Plan the join graph over {{ESQUEMA}}: base table, direction and type of each join (INNER or LEFT justified) and aggregation level to avoid fan-out; if a metric lives in a higher-cardinality table, pre-aggregate in a CTE before joining. (3) Write the query with explicit joins and clear aliases, WHERE, complete GROUP BY, HAVING only over aggregates, ORDER BY and LIMIT, in the exact syntax of {{MOTOR_SQL}}; apply {{DEFINICIONES_METRICAS}} in the aggregation expressions; never use implicit join by comma. (4) Apply {{RANGO_FECHAS}} with declared inclusive or exclusive limits (recommend half-open date >= start AND date < end+1) and respect the timezone if applicable. (5) Explain each clause in one line and list risks with mitigation: NULLs dropped by INNER JOIN, double counting by granularity, division by zero, COUNT vs COUNT(DISTINCT), comparisons against NULL. Deliver: final query in a code block, [ASSUMPTION] list, and clause-by-clause explanation, ready to execute and audit. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Parameters: {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} business question in natural language; {{ESQUEMA}} tables, columns, types, and keys; {{MOTOR_SQL}} engine and version; {{DEFINICIONES_METRICAS}} calculation rules and filters for each metric; {{RANGO_FECHAS}} period and timezone.

prompts.title: Optimize a slow SQL query with an execution plan
Refactor nested subqueries into readable CTEs
Solve ranking and running totals with window functions
prompts.content: Act as a senior data engineer specializing in analytical SQL and dimensional modeling, with mastery of the SQL:2003 window function standard and its differences between engines. I need to turn {{TABLA}} into actionable analytical metrics without collapsing per-row detail: competitive ranking, progressive running totals, and period-over-period comparisons, solved with window functions instead of correlated subqueries or self-joins, for {{MOTOR_SQL}}. Before writing code, restate what you understand and present your plan; if {{TABLA}}, {{DIMENSION_PARTICION}}, {{ENTIDAD}}, {{METRICA}}, {{GRANO_TEMPORAL}}, or {{MOTOR_SQL}} is missing, ask for it. Build in layers: a base CTE that selects {{DIMENSION_PARTICION}}, {{ENTIDAD}}, {{GRANO_TEMPORAL}}, and {{METRICA}} aggregated at the correct grain (first resolving duplicates per grain key); then a window layer. Include ROW_NUMBER, RANK, and DENSE_RANK with PARTITION BY {{DIMENSION_PARTICION}} and ORDER BY {{METRICA}} DESC, explain when to use each one in the presence of ties, and break ties deterministically with a second order column. Calculate the running total with SUM({{METRICA}}) OVER (PARTITION BY {{DIMENSION_PARTICION}} ORDER BY {{GRANO_TEMPORAL}} ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), warning why you avoid the default RANGE. Compare periods with LAG({{METRICA}},1,0) and LEAD({{METRICA}},1,0) OVER (PARTITION BY {{ENTIDAD}} ORDER BY {{GRANO_TEMPORAL}}), and derive absolute and percentage variation protecting against division by zero with NULLIF. Mark all syntax dependent on {{MOTOR_SQL}} (date handling, QUALIFY vs. wrapper subquery, NULLS FIRST/LAST, casts) and deliver a portable variant. Close with executable, commented SQL plus a validation note: control counts and verification that the last running total per group equals the group total. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Build PIVOT and UNPIVOT queries for reports
prompts.content: Act as a senior data engineer specializing in analytical SQL and reporting, expert in dialect differences between engines. I need to convert {{TABLA_ORIGEN}} (long format, one row per transaction) into a cross-tab ready for an executive report and validate it against the source. Give me four executable and commented SQL blocks for {{MOTOR_BD}}: (1) main PIVOT that groups by {{COLUMNAS_FILA}}, converts the values of {{COLUMNA_A_PIVOTAR}} (or {{VALORES_COLUMNA}} if I provide them) into columns, applies {{FUNCION_AGREGACION}}({{METRICA}}) per cell, with a row subtotal and a grand total; (2) reverse UNPIVOT that brings the cross-tab back to long format to reconcile against {{TABLA_ORIGEN}}; (3) portable version with aggregated CASE WHEN, valid without a native PIVOT operator; (4) notes on NULLs (COALESCE to zero where applicable), distinction between null and zero, stable ordering, and the limits of dynamic vs. static pivoting in {{MOTOR_BD}}. Before coding, restate what you understand and present your plan (engine and version, source format, cardinality of {{COLUMNA_A_PIVOTAR}}, static or dynamic, null policy). Mark [ASSUMPTION] on every name, type, or value not provided. Close by verifying that the UNPIVOT reconstructs the source count and total and that totals balance. Variables: {{TABLA_ORIGEN}}, {{COLUMNAS_FILA}}, {{COLUMNA_A_PIVOTAR}}, {{METRICA}}, {{FUNCION_AGREGACION}}, {{MOTOR_BD}}, {{VALORES_COLUMNA}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any required variable is missing, ask before continuing.

prompts.title: Detect and deduplicate records with SQL
prompts.content: Act as a senior data engineer specializing in data quality and analytical SQL, with experience deduplicating transactional and master tables. I need a commented, executable, and auditable SQL package on {{MOTOR_SQL}}, for diagnosing and eliminating duplicate records in {{TABLA}}, leaving evidence before touching anything. Before generating SQL, restate what you understood and present your plan: confirm {{MOTOR_SQL}}, {{TABLA}}, the identity columns {{COLUMNAS_IDENTIDAD}} (what must be unique), the fuzzy columns {{COLUMNAS_DIFUSAS}} to normalize (if empty, exact duplicates only), and the survival criterion {{CRITERIO_SOBREVIVIENTE}} (most recent by date, most complete, or lowest id). If any is missing or {{COLUMNAS_DIFUSAS}} is ambiguous, ask; do not invent. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any identity definition you infer. Deliver four commented queries in sequence: (1) exact diagnosis with GROUP BY over {{COLUMNAS_IDENTIDAD}} and HAVING COUNT(*) greater than 1, reporting duplicate groups and total surplus rows (SUM(COUNT(*) minus 1)); (2) fuzzy diagnosis over {{COLUMNAS_DIFUSAS}} grouping by the normalized version (LOWER, TRIM, and the accent-removal function of {{MOTOR_SQL}}) without altering source data, and if {{COLUMNAS_DIFUSAS}} is empty, declare it and omit it; (3) inspection with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY {{COLUMNAS_IDENTIDAD}} ORDER BY {{CRITERIO_SOBREVIVIENTE}}) marking rn = 1 as survivor, with NULLS LAST and a final deterministic tiebreak (ascending id) for reproducibility; (4) cleanup with a safety net: SELECT showing the rows to delete (rn greater than 1), equivalent DELETE, and as a non-destructive alternative, CREATE TABLE {{TABLA}}_dedup with the survivors. Recommend transaction, count validation before COMMIT, and UNIQUE/unique index on {{COLUMNAS_IDENTIDAD}}; warn if there are foreign keys to the rows to delete (re-point before deleting). Declare engine-specific variants (unaccent in PostgreSQL vs. no native equivalent in MySQL; DELETE with CTE vs. subquery; concatenation with ||) and do not use functions that do not exist in {{MOTOR_SQL}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Close by confirming all four queries are ready to review and execute.

prompts.title: Traverse hierarchies with a recursive CTE
prompts.content: Act as a senior data engineer expert in recursive SQL and hierarchical structure modeling (org charts, BOMs, category trees). I want to traverse in SQL the table {{TABLA_JERARQUIA}}, which stores a parent-child relationship, using a recursive CTE that computes for each node its level and its full path from the root, without assuming a fixed number of levels. Contract data: identifier column {{COLUMNA_ID}}, column referencing the parent {{COLUMNA_PADRE}} (NULL or self-reference marks the root), starting node(s) {{NODO_RAIZ}}, maximum depth to traverse {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAXIMA}}, engine and version {{MOTOR_SQL}}. If any data is missing or ambiguous, ask me before writing SQL. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Give me: (1) confirmed contract with engine, types of {{COLUMNA_ID}} and {{COLUMNA_PADRE}}, and how the root is identified, marking [ASSUMPTION] on everything not verified; (2) complete and executable SQL, with the anchor at level 0 and the path initialized with an explicit CAST, the recursive member joining {{COLUMNA_PADRE}} = {{COLUMNA_ID}} from the previous level, incrementing the level, concatenating the path, and cutting by {{PROFUNDIDAD_MAXIMA}} inside the recursive clause, plus cycle detection (CYCLE or comparison against the path); (3) final SELECT ordered by path; (4) clause-by-clause explanation, index note on {{COLUMNA_PADRE}}, warning about {{MOTOR_SQL}}'s recursion limit, and at least one variant from another engine. Do not invent names, do not use pseudocode, respond in neutral and professional English, without emojis. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.

prompts.title: Translate SQL between engine dialects
prompts.content: Act as a senior data engineer specializing in cross-engine SQL portability, with deep mastery of PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Snowflake, SQL Server, and MySQL. Translate the query {{CONSULTA_SQL}} from {{MOTOR_ORIGEN}} to {{MOTOR_DESTINO}}, preserving the semantics, not just the syntax: the real risk is not that the SQL fails to compile, but that it compiles and returns a subtly different result. If {{MOTOR_ORIGEN}} is empty, deduce it from the syntax (quoting, functions, pagination) and confirm it before translating. If {{MOTOR_DESTINO}} or {{CONSULTA_SQL}} is missing, ask before continuing. Proceed as follows: (1) identify or confirm source and target, and note version incompatibilities if relevant; (2) inventory each dialect-sensitive construct and classify it by category; (3) rewrite the query to the native equivalent of the target, formatted and ready to execute; when no native equivalent exists, use real primitives and mark the rewrite as APPROXIMATION, never inventing non-existent functions; (4) audit the silent behavioral differences where the literal equivalent compiles but does NOT produce the same result: integer vs. decimal division, rounding and banker's rounding, NULL ordering (NULLS FIRST/LAST and default position), collation and case sensitivity in text comparisons, time-zone handling in timestamps (with and without tz), implicit truncation of strings and numbers, three-value semantics with NULL; (5) warn about source constructs with no direct counterpart and propose the most faithful approximation. Prioritize {{FOCOS}} if present. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides schema, column types, or engine version. Deliver: translated SQL block ready to execute, followed by three sections (Category mapping, Behavioral differences, Warnings without direct equivalent). Mark every version or configuration assumption as ASSUMPTION and every non-native rewrite as APPROXIMATION. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Explain and document a complex legacy query
prompts.content: Act as a senior data engineer specializing in reading legacy SQL, dimensional modeling, and the logical execution order of queries. You have inherited an extensive SQL query that no one fully understands and must document it rigorously to modify, migrate, or audit it without silently breaking reports. You work on {{MOTOR_SQL}}, in the domain {{DOMINIO_DATOS}}, with apparent purpose {{PROPOSITO_APARENTE}} and depth {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. If the engine, the purpose, or the code to explain in {{ADJUNTOS}} is missing, ask before continuing; do not assume the dialect or invent tables. Deliver: (1) a one-sentence summary in business language of what the query answers; (2) source map: each table, CTE, and subquery with its grain and each JOIN with type, keys, and fan-out or duplicate risk; (3) a walkthrough by layer in logical execution order (FROM and JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, windows, SELECT and derived expressions, ORDER BY, LIMIT), explaining each block and why it exists; (4) inferred business rules with confidence level per inference; (5) correctness traps specific to {{MOTOR_SQL}} (NULLs in JOINs, implicit conversions, DISTINCT masking duplicates, non-sargable functions, order dependency, time zones, division by zero) without proposing changes yet; (6) the same query with inline comments (-- and blocks) plus a header with purpose, result grain, sources, and assumptions, with detail {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} and logic intact. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on every unverifiable hypothesis and close with open questions for business or DBA. Do not alter any line of logic: you only add comments.

prompts.title: Build a cohort and retention query
prompts.content: Act as a senior data analyst specializing in product analytics and analytical SQL. I need an executable SQL query that produces the retention matrix by acquisition cohort, in absolute counts and percentage, from {{TABLA_EVENTOS}} using {{COL_USUARIO}} as the user identifier and {{COL_TIMESTAMP}} as the event date/time. Each user is grouped by the period in which they first appeared (their cohort, grain {{GRANO_COHORTE}}) and tracked for {{VENTANA_PERIODOS}} periods for the fraction that remains active, counting as activity only what satisfies {{FILTRO_ACTIVIDAD}}. Before writing SQL, confirm the table, columns, grain, window, filter, and engine {{MOTOR_SQL}}; if a key input is missing, ask and do not invent column names. Structure the query in named and commented CTEs: (1) events_base that selects {{COL_USUARIO}} and {{COL_TIMESTAMP}} from {{TABLA_EVENTOS}}, applies {{FILTRO_ACTIVIDAD}}, and discards nulls; (2) cohorts with date_trunc('{{GRANO_COHORTE}}', MIN({{COL_TIMESTAMP}})) per user; (3) activity_periods that joins events with cohorts and computes the relative period index (0 = acquisition) by deriving the difference from truncated dates, not subtracting raw timestamps, bounded to [0, {{VENTANA_PERIODOS}}]; (4) cohort_size with COUNT(DISTINCT {{COL_USUARIO}}) at index 0; (5) matrix with active = COUNT(DISTINCT {{COL_USUARIO}}) and retention_pct = active / cohort_size in float division. Use COUNT(DISTINCT {{COL_USUARIO}}) in each cell. Verify that index 0 gives 100%. Mark as partial cohort every cell whose index exceeds the periods elapsed from the cohort to the cutoff date. Deliver two outputs (counts and percentage) with cohorts in rows ordered by date and index in columns, declaring long or pivot format. Close by declaring the query is valid for {{MOTOR_SQL}}, list the portability adjustments (date_trunc vs. DATE_TRUNC or TIMESTAMP_TRUNC, integer vs. float division, pivot syntax) and mark with [ASSUMPTION] every name, grain, or filter inferred. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Solve gaps and islands in event series
Review parameterized SQL against injection
prompts.content: Act as a senior data security engineer specialized in SQL injection prevention and data-access code review. I am giving you {{CONSULTAS_SQL}} to audit and harden against injection before exposing them, on the engine {{MOTOR_BD}} and using {{LENGUAJE_DRIVER}}; calibrate rigor according to {{NIVEL_CRITICIDAD}}. First, restate what you understand and present your plan before executing (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute). Then: (1) Inventory every point in {{CONSULTAS_SQL}} where an external variable enters the SQL and mark whether it arrives via concatenation, interpolation, or already parameterized; distinguish direct user input from header input, from another table, or from trusted configuration. (2) For each vulnerable point, quote the exact fragment, identify the unsanitized value, and classify severity (critical/high/medium) according to input origin and query scope (read, write, DDL). (3) Rewrite the query with bound parameters using the exact syntax of {{MOTOR_BD}} and the real API of {{LENGUAJE_DRIVER}}, separating SQL structure from values; do not invent method names. (4) For non-parameterizable identifiers (table name, column, ORDER BY direction, dynamic LIMIT/OFFSET) apply explicit allowlist validation mapped to code constants, never direct concatenation; explain why validation complements and does not replace binding. (5) Flag the cases requiring manual attention: variable-length IN clauses, dynamic ORDER BY or LIMIT, legitimate dynamic SQL, multi-statement queries, and anything you could not verify. Rules: do not introduce new dependencies without justification; preserve functional behavior; when the engine or driver is ambiguous, declare it as an assumption. Close with an applicable patch (corrected code + a brief comment per change) and a findings report with a severity table and a manual-attention list. Variables: {{CONSULTAS_SQL}}, {{MOTOR_BD}}, {{LENGUAJE_DRIVER}}, {{NIVEL_CRITICIDAD}} (optional). If any required variable is missing, ask for it before executing.

prompts.title: Design a star schema with facts and dimensions
prompts.content: Act as a senior data architect specialized in Kimball dimensional modeling, with experience building warehouses on {{MOTOR_ANALITICO}}. Design the complete star schema for {{PROCESO_NEGOCIO}} so that it answers {{PREGUNTAS_ANALITICAS}} across the axes {{DIMENSIONES_CLAVE}}, sizing physical decisions according to {{VOLUMEN_ESPERADO}}. Work in this inviolable order: (1) confirm the business process and the measurable events it generates; (2) declare the fact table grain in ONE unambiguous sentence, at the finest available atomic event, because the grain defines everything else; (3) derive the dimensions that hang from that grain and mark which are conformed (reusable across processes); (4) identify the numeric facts and classify each measure as additive, semi-additive (do not sum across time: balances, inventory levels), or non-additive (ratios, percentages: never pre-aggregate). Then specify each dimension with surrogate key, natural business key, descriptive attributes, and SCD strategy (Type 1 overwrites, Type 2 versions with validity dates and current flag, Type 3 alternate column) justified per attribute based on whether {{PROCESO_NEGOCIO}} needs history. Resolve the fact table: surrogate FK to each dimension, measures, degenerate keys (transaction number, invoice), table type (transactional, periodic snapshot, or accumulating snapshot), and NULL handling (unknown dimension member, never NULL on FK). Apply advanced patterns when applicable: role-playing dimensions, junk dimensions, late-arriving, and early-arriving facts. Take the {{MOTOR_ANALITICO}} destination into account for partitioning, clustering, or distribution decisions when {{VOLUMEN_ESPERADO}} justifies it, without over-engineering. Deliver a dictionary per table (column, type, role, SCD, description), a star diagram in text, and a list of assumptions. Validate that every measure respects the grain, that every FK points to an existing dimension, that conformed ones are consistent, and that each of {{PREGUNTAS_ANALITICAS}} is answerable. Mark all unprovided data with [ASSUMPTION]. If {{PROCESO_NEGOCIO}}, {{PREGUNTAS_ANALITICAS}}, {{MOTOR_ANALITICO}}, or {{VOLUMEN_ESPERADO}} is missing, ask before modeling. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Decide between star schema and snowflake schema
prompts.content: Act as a senior data warehouse architect specialized in dimensional modeling (Kimball method) and optimization for columnar/MPP engines. I need a dimensional normalization ruling for the model {{MODELO_ANALITICO}} that decides, dimension by dimension, between a star schema, a snowflake schema, or a hybrid outrigger — NOT a single global default rule. Before evaluating, restate the model and its dimensions, declare what you understood, and present your plan. Available data: dimensions and hierarchies {{DIMENSIONES_Y_JERARQUIAS}}, target platform {{PLATAFORMA_DESTINO}}, query patterns {{PATRONES_CONSULTA}}, slowly changing dimension strategy {{ESTRATEGIA_SCD}}. If cardinality, levels, row counts, or other critical data are missing, ask before deciding; do not invent figures. Proceed as follows: 1) Inventory the dimensions of {{MODELO_ANALITICO}} from {{DIMENSIONES_Y_JERARQUIAS}}. 2) Evaluate each dimension on three axes: (a) cardinality and hierarchy depth; (b) maintenance cost, consistency, and impact of {{ESTRATEGIA_SCD}}; (c) query performance and readability according to {{PLATAFORMA_DESTINO}} and {{PATRONES_CONSULTA}}, keeping in mind that columnar/MPP engines compress repeated attributes and usually favor stars, while snowflake sub-tables save storage and isolate volatile hierarchies. 3) Emit a per-dimension recommendation with an explicit decision rule, quantifying the joins the snowflake introduces and the expected behavior of {{PLATAFORMA_DESTINO}}, plus one accepted trade-off. 4) Consolidate a summary table (dimension | critical axis | recommendation | trade-off). 5) Propose a prioritized implementation plan: which dimensions to tackle first, risk, and validation criteria (row counts, join tests, latency comparison). Mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Model slowly changing dimensions SCD type 2
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data engineer specialized in Kimball dimensional modeling and ETL/ELT pipelines. I need to model the dimension {{NOMBRE_DIMENSION}} as SCD type 2 on {{MOTOR_BD}} so that the data warehouse retains the complete history of changes: each change in {{ATRIBUTOS_VERSIONADOS}} must close the current version and open a new one, so that facts are associated with the value current on the date of the event. This enables point-in-time analytics, auditing, and historically accurate reports without rewriting the past.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you understand, declare as [ASSUMPTION] all missing data (granularity of {{FUENTE_ORIGEN}}, current-flag type, time zone, delete handling, treatment of {{ESTRATEGIA_NO_VERSIONADOS}}), and request confirmation only for blocking items.

Then deliver, in this order: (1) the DDL for {{NOMBRE_DIMENSION}} with an auto-generated surrogate key as PK, {{NATURAL_KEY}} as the per-version repeatable business key, the attributes including {{ATRIBUTOS_VERSIONADOS}}, and the SCD2 control columns fecha_inicio_vigencia, fecha_fin_vigencia, flag_registro_actual, and hash_atributos, plus audit metadata fecha_carga and origen_lote; (2) the open-end convention (recommended 9999-12-31) and the sentinel record (surrogate key -1) for keys not found; (3) change detection by deterministic hash of the normalized {{ATRIBUTOS_VERSIONADOS}} (trim, explicit NULL) between {{FUENTE_ORIGEN}} and the current record; (4) the incremental load (MERGE or native close-then-insert for {{MOTOR_BD}}) covering the four cases: new insert, versioned change, no change (no-op), and absent from source; (5) {{ESTRATEGIA_NO_VERSIONADOS}} propagated to the current version; (6) late-arriving data handling and idempotency on re-run of the same batch. Close with validation queries (one current version per {{NATURAL_KEY}}, contiguous validity periods without overlaps or gaps, sentinel integrity, no consecutive hash duplicates). Executable SQL commented in the {{MOTOR_BD}} dialect; no pseudocode. Spell out trade-offs between hash vs. column-by-column comparison and soft-delete vs. hard-ignore.

Variables: {{NOMBRE_DIMENSION}}, {{MOTOR_BD}}, {{FUENTE_ORIGEN}}, {{NATURAL_KEY}}, {{ATRIBUTOS_VERSIONADOS}}, {{ESTRATEGIA_NO_VERSIONADOS}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Normalize a relational schema to 3NF
prompts.content: Act as a senior data engineer specialized in relational OLTP modeling, with mastery of the functional dependency algebra from Codd's model. Normalize to {{NIVEL_OBJETIVO}} (3NF by default) the schema described in {{ESQUEMA_ACTUAL}} and deliver the resulting model with executable DDL for {{MOTOR_BD}}. Proceed as follows: (1) Reconstruct the schema from {{ESQUEMA_ACTUAL}} and list each attribute with its type; if it only describes a domain without tables, model it from scratch. (2) Declare the functional dependencies from {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}} and the sample data; mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inferred dependency not guaranteed by me, and do not invent cardinalities: if a key relationship is ambiguous, ask me before continuing. (3) Calculate the attribute closure to identify candidate keys and choose the primary key of each relation. (4) Apply 1NF by eliminating repeating groups and multivalued attributes until atomicity is guaranteed. (5) Apply 2NF by eliminating partial dependencies on composite keys. (6) Apply 3NF by eliminating transitive dependencies between non-key attributes. Show the model state after each normal form. (7) For each decomposition, name the anomaly it resolves (insertion, update, or deletion). (8) Verify the lossless decomposition (lossless join) and dependency preservation; declare every non-preserved dependency and its impact. (9) Deliver DDL for {{MOTOR_BD}} with PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, and NOT NULL. If {{NIVEL_OBJETIVO}} is BCNF or a 3NF partition does not preserve a dependency worth protecting, evaluate BCNF explaining the trade-off vs. preservation. If {{TOLERANCIA_DESNORMALIZACION}} allows controlled redundancy, propose the denormalization as a separate note from the normalized model, with its consistency mechanism (trigger, materialized view, or computed column). Before executing, restate the domain and dependencies you understood and present your plan. Deliverable: document with starting schema, functional dependencies, step-by-step 1NF-2NF-3NF derivation, final schema with keys, executable DDL, and anomaly-resolution table. Variables: {{ESQUEMA_ACTUAL}}, {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, {{MOTOR_BD}}, {{NIVEL_OBJETIVO}}, {{TOLERANCIA_DESNORMALIZACION}}. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before starting.

prompts.title: Denormalize a model for analytical workloads
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data engineer specialized in dimensional modeling (Kimball school) and OLAP analytical workload optimization, with practice in data warehousing, materialized views, and lineage governance. Your task is to produce a grounded denormalization decision for {{MODELO_ORIGEN}}: which parts to pre-join and materialize to accelerate analytical reads, without turning the analytical copy into a second source of truth. The normalized source (3NF) remains authoritative; the materialized layer is derived and rebuildable.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before designing, restate in two or three sentences what model you are receiving from {{MODELO_ORIGEN}} and what analytical workload you are going to accelerate, and present your plan; then execute. If {{MODELO_ORIGEN}}, {{CONSULTAS_CRITICAS}}, or {{VOLUMENES_Y_FRECUENCIA}} are missing, ask for them before designing: they are inputs without which the grain and what to materialize cannot be decided. Do not invent tables, queries, or volumes; mark [ASSUMPTION] on every inference due to missing data.

Proceed in four phases. (1) Profile the analytical workload from {{CONSULTAS_CRITICAS}}: extract the repeated join patterns, recurring filters and aggregations, and the required level of detail; order candidates by cost × frequency. Declare that the goal is OLAP reads and that the OLTP write path is NOT being optimized. (2) Fix the grain and design the star schema on {{MOTOR_DESTINO}}: for each candidate fact table, state in one sentence what a row represents; separate facts (additive, semi-additive, or non-additive metrics plus keys to dimensions) from denormalized dimensions (attributes collapsed from multiple 3NF tables into a wide dimension); collapse a chain only when the join is recurring and the dimension is stable, and justify each collapse by the joins it avoids vs. the redundancy cost. (3) Decide what to materialize: classify each object as materialize / logical view / do not materialize according to the frequency-cost-volatility triangle using {{VOLUMENES_Y_FRECUENCIA}}; define the refresh policy (full or incremental, scheduled or on-demand) consistent with {{VENTANA_FRESCURA}} and identify update dependencies. Hard rule: do not materialize anything that changes faster than it is queried. (4) Traceability and governance: use surrogate keys that reference the natural keys of the source; apply Slowly Changing Dimensions (Type 2 when history matters, Type 1 when it does not, Type 0 for immutable); build a column-to-column lineage dictionary back to the 3NF source; declare the trade-offs (update anomalies, copy-source inconsistency, storage and refresh cost) and their mitigation (refresh, periodic reconciliation, constraints, reconciliation tests).

Deliver a design document with: (1) materialization candidates table [object | trigger | decision | refresh policy]; (2) star schema with facts and dimensions, each fact with its grain; (3) column-to-column lineage dictionary; (4) trade-off list with mitigation. Ready to implement and audit against the 3NF source.

Variables:
- {{MODELO_ORIGEN}}: normalized transactional model (tables, relationships, primary and foreign keys, business domain).
- {{CONSULTAS_CRITICAS}}: most frequent or costly analytical queries or reports, with their typical joins, filters, and aggregations.
- {{VOLUMENES_Y_FRECUENCIA}}: approximate table size and how frequently the source data changes.
- {{MOTOR_DESTINO}}: target analytical engine or store (PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, etc.) (optional).
- {{VENTANA_FRESCURA}}: staleness tolerated by the business in the materialized copy (real-time, intraday, daily) (optional, default: daily).

No emojis.

prompts.title: Build an entity-relationship diagram from requirements
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data architect expert in entity-relationship modeling and relational normalization (Chen + Codd), with experience translating ambiguous requirements into implementable schemas. I need to convert the business brief {{BRIEF_NEGOCIO}} for the domain {{DOMINIO}} into an actionable data model before writing DDL or designing screens, refined to the engine {{MOTOR_BD}}, normalized to level {{NIVEL_NORMALIZACION}}, and capable of serving the critical queries {{CONSULTAS_CRITICAS}} well.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Proceed in three phases. Phase 1 Interpretation: restate the domain, actors, events, and business rules detected in {{BRIEF_NEGOCIO}}; separate facts from the brief from what you assume, marking each assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; identify what you cannot infer. Phase 2 Plan: present the inventory of candidate entities and a tentative relationship matrix before detailing, and ask for the critical missing data (multiplicity, uniqueness, lifecycle, soft-delete, temporality) instead of inventing them. Phase 3 Execution: produce the complete modeling package.

Derivation method: 1) Extract from {{BRIEF_NEGOCIO}} the candidate entities (nouns with their own identity and lifecycle); discard attributes disguised as entities; mark weak entities, catalog entities, and history/audit entities. 2) For each entity define attributes with the data type refined to {{MOTOR_BD}}, primary key (natural vs. surrogate with explicit justification), business uniqueness (alternate keys), and constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK/domain, defaults). 3) Determine relationships with cardinality (1:1, 1:N, M:N) and optionality at each end, expressed as a business-verb phrase readable in both directions. 4) Resolve every M:N relationship with a junction table and its pair of foreign keys, including attributes of the association itself; define referential integrity (ON DELETE / ON UPDATE) for each FK. 5) Validate normalization to {{NIVEL_NORMALIZACION}} (justify each step) and document any deliberate denormalization required by {{CONSULTAS_CRITICAS}} with its reason and maintenance cost.

Deliver five mutually consistent artifacts: (1) Mermaid erDiagram with crow's foot notation that compiles; (2) dictionary per entity (attribute, type, PK/FK/AK, nullability, constraint); (3) relationship list with cardinality, optionality, verb phrase, and referential integrity rule; (4) assumptions and business rules marked [ASSUMPTION]; (5) open questions that block closure of the model. If {{MOTOR_BD}}, {{NIVEL_NORMALIZACION}}, or {{CONSULTAS_CRITICAS}} are empty, assume PostgreSQL, 3NF, and no denormalizations, and record that as [ASSUMPTION]. If essential information is missing, ask for it before inventing it. Do not include prices. Neutral professional language.

Variables:
- {{BRIEF_NEGOCIO}}: prose description of the process or domain (actors, objects, events, rules, flows)
- {{DOMINIO}}: model domain (e.g. e-commerce, healthcare, logistics, HR, banking)
- {{MOTOR_BD}}: target engine to refine types and constraints (e.g. PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server)
- {{NIVEL_NORMALIZACION}}: target normal form (e.g. 3NF, BCNF; default 3NF)
- {{CONSULTAS_CRITICAS}}: high-frequency accesses the model must serve well, to decide denormalizations

prompts.title: Design a Data Vault model with hubs, links, and satellites
prompts.content: Act as a senior data architect specialized in Data Vault 2.0, with experience in auditable multi-source warehouses. Design the integration layer of a data warehouse with Data Vault 2.0 for the domain {{DOMINIO_NEGOCIO}}, so that it supports multiple source systems, schema changes, and growth without rewriting history. Inputs: candidate entities and natural keys {{ENTIDADES_Y_CLAVES}}; relationships and transactions between entities {{RELACIONES}}; source systems and descriptive attributes {{SISTEMAS_FUENTE}}; target engine/platform {{MOTOR_BD}}; supporting material {{ADJUNTOS}}. First, restate the domain, list entities, relationships, and detected sources, and mark as {to_confirm} any gap (ambiguous natural keys, relationship granularity, unspecified engine, multi-tenancy, retention or GDPR deletion). Then present for validation the proposed inventory of hubs, links, and satellites before detailing it. After approval, produce: (a) textual hub/link/satellite diagram with connectivity; (b) dictionary per table with columns, types, and keys (hash key, business key, hash diff, load date-time, record source); (c) deterministic hashing rules (algorithm, business key normalization with trim/upper, separator, null handling, and composite key handling) compatible with {{MOTOR_BD}}; (d) source-agnostic incremental load pattern; (e) explicit Raw Vault / Business Vault boundary (PIT, Bridge, computed satellites). Rules: each Hub is an independent business concept with a stable business key; each Link connects two or more hubs with its own hash key without collapsing distinct relationships; each Satellite hangs from a single hub or link, groups by rate of change and source, carries hash diff and historization; every table includes record source and load date-time; calculations do not contaminate the Raw Vault. Close with quality checklist, assumptions, limits, and trade-offs. If a critical data point is missing, ask for it before modeling. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Evaluate the One Big Table pattern vs. dimensional model
Define a natural vs. surrogate key strategy
Design a semantic layer with a central metric definition
prompts.content:
Act as a senior analytics engineer specializing in metrics-layer-style semantic layers and Kimball dimensional modeling, with experience governing metric catalogs in multi-team organizations. Design a semantic layer that acts as a single source of truth for {{DOMINIO_NEGOCIO}}: a single canonical definition per metric, decoupled from {{CONSUMIDORES}} and reusable by BI, notebooks, and APIs, so that figures reconcile across teams and definitions evolve without breaking consumers.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in your own words the domain, the sources, and the grain you understand; if {{DOMINIO_NEGOCIO}}, {{FUENTES_DATOS}}, {{GRANO_OBJETIVO}}, or {{METRICAS_PRIORITARIAS}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for those before continuing. Then present your plan and only then execute.

Deliver four artifacts. (1) Conceptual model: business entities of {{DOMINIO_NEGOCIO}}, natural keys, and relationships, starting from {{FUENTES_DATOS}} and respecting {{GRANO_OBJETIVO}}. (2) Catalog of conformed dimensions: attributes, hierarchies, and historical treatment (type 1 vs. type 2) justified per attribute. (3) Catalog of measures and metrics: atomic measures vs. derived metrics; for each, canonical name, business description, explicit formula, granularity, aggregability (additive, semi-additive, non-additive), base filters, valid drill-down dimensions, and unit. Prioritize {{METRICAS_PRIORITARIAS}}. (4) Governance contract: naming, owner per metric, versioning, and rules against double-counting via join fan-out.

Quality rules: no derived metric without its atomics; every fan-out join with its mitigation; every business rule declared; assumptions tagged [ASSUMPTION]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it contributes schemas or prior definitions. Close with a structured document, free of meta-discourse, ready to implement in a metrics layer tool; propose as the next step the first batch of metrics to materialize.

prompts.title: Design a partitioning and clustering strategy
Generate a data dictionary for a schema
prompts.content: Act as a senior data engineer specializing in data governance and metadata management, with practice in modeling, PII classification, and quality rules. I need a complete and auditable data dictionary for {{ESQUEMA}} because it grows faster than its documentation: column names are ambiguous, the origin of each datum is tribal knowledge, and sensitivity has not been classified. Document each table and each column from {{DEFINICIONES_DDL}}, without altering the technical definitions. Proceed as follows: (1) Table inventory: list all entities in {{DEFINICIONES_DDL}} and for each one declare the business purpose in one sentence (grounded in {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}}), the grain (what a row represents), the primary key, and foreign key relationships. (2) Column-by-column documentation: type and length or precision, nullability and default, membership in PK/FK, business description (what the datum means, not what the column is named), unit or format, value domain or code catalog if enumerated, and the source system and transformation that populates it (lineage). (3) Sensitivity classification: apply {{MARCO_PII}} to label each column as Public, Internal, Confidential, or PII; if PII, indicate the category (direct identifier, quasi-identifier, sensitive or financial data), the legal basis for processing if applicable, and the protection action (mask, encrypt, tokenize, restrict by role). (4) Verifiable validation rules per column or table: format, range, uniqueness, referential integrity, completeness, conditional dependencies, expressed in a provable form (regex, predicate, bound, constraint). (5) Deliver the dictionary in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} plus a findings summary: columns without inferable description, detected PII, quality risks, and open assumptions. Rules: parse {{DEFINICIONES_DDL}} without inventing columns or tables; every unconfirmable business interpretation is tagged [ASSUMPTION] with the question that would resolve it; no column is left undocumented or unclassified; validation rules are never vague statements. If {{DEFINICIONES_DDL}} is not provided (DDL, catalog export, or table/column list), stop and ask before starting; if {{MARCO_PII}} is missing, use Public/Internal/Confidential/PII by default. Variables: {{ESQUEMA}}, {{DEFINICIONES_DDL}}, {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}}, {{MARCO_PII}}, {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understood and present your plan (table scope, sensitivity framework, and output format), then execute.

prompts.title: Design an end-to-end ETL/ELT pipeline
Implement incremental loading with Change Data Capture
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data engineer specializing in incremental ingestion pipelines and Change Data Capture patterns on {{MOTOR_DATOS}}. My full load of {{TABLA_DESTINO}} no longer scales: every run re-reads the entire source, the batch window is exhausted, and compute cost grows with history. I want to migrate it to incremental loading with CDC to process only what has changed since the last checkpoint, with safe re-runs that never duplicate data.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate your understanding and present your plan; if {{MOTOR_DATOS}}, {{COLUMNA_CAMBIO}}, {{CLAVE_NEGOCIO}}, {{MANEJO_DELETES}}, or {{FRECUENCIA_CARGA}} are missing or ambiguous, ask instead of assuming.
