Deliver an actionable technical design plus SQL artifacts: (1) choose the change-detection mechanism comparing log-based CDC for {{MOTOR_DATOS}} (captures inserts/updates/deletes, low latency, requires enabling the feature and reading the changelog) against detection by {{COLUMNA_CAMBIO}} timestamp/version (simpler, does not capture hard deletes or changes that do not touch the column), and recommend one based on {{MOTOR_DATOS}} and {{MANEJO_DELETES}} with its explicit trade-off; (2) design the watermark governed by {{COLUMNA_CAMBIO}} with a control table that persists the last processed value, advances the watermark in the same transaction as the load, and resumes after failure without loss or duplication, considering concurrency (only one batch at a time per entity); (3) specify the idempotent MERGE on {{CLAVE_NEGOCIO}}: match with update only if the incoming version is more recent, non-match with insert, batch deduplication to keep the latest version per key, and {{MANEJO_DELETES}} handling; (4) cover late-arriving data and clock skew by reading from watermark minus an overlap window sized with {{FRECUENCIA_CARGA}}, and explain why MERGE idempotency makes reprocessing that overlap safe; (5) deliver DDL for the watermark table, the MERGE/UPSERT SQL with the real syntax of {{MOTOR_DATOS}} (not pseudocode), and a validation plan with source vs. destination counts, duplicates by {{CLAVE_NEGOCIO}}, and a double-run test (second run = zero net changes).

Closing criterion: mechanism justified with trade-off for {{MOTOR_DATOS}}, transactional watermark, idempotent and deduplicated MERGE, {{MANEJO_DELETES}} resolved, sized overlap window, engine-specific SQL, and executable validation plan. Tag everything inferred with [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent metrics or latencies.

Parameters: {{MOTOR_DATOS}}, {{TABLA_DESTINO}}, {{COLUMNA_CAMBIO}}, {{CLAVE_NEGOCIO}}, {{MANEJO_DELETES}}, {{FRECUENCIA_CARGA}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Make a pipeline idempotent and re-runnable
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data engineer specializing in idempotent and re-runnable production pipelines on {{MOTOR}}. My pipeline {{PIPELINE}} produces duplicates or corrupts data when re-run: retries after a failure, historical backfills, and manual runs leave a different state each time, forcing manual cleanups and eroding trust in dashboards. Redesign it to be idempotent: running it N times over the same window must leave exactly the same result as running it once.

Proceed as follows:
1. Diagnose where idempotency breaks (blind inserts without a key, windows based on now(), non-transactional side effects, lack of run control, late-arriving data, non-deterministic arrival order) and give the root cause and trigger of each point (retry, backfill, or manual run).
2. Define the business key from {{CLAVE_NEGOCIO}} and the exact grain of the destination, and deliver the destination DDL plus a run control table (run ledger) with watermark of the processed range, status, and timestamps.
3. Replace the load with an idempotent MERGE/upsert or delete-insert by partition for {{MOTOR}}, deduplicating by {{CLAVE_NEGOCIO}} and keeping the most recent version via an explicit tiebreaker criterion.
4. Convert data selection into a deterministic window parameterized by a cutoff date on {{COLUMNA_PARTICION}}, aligned with {{FRECUENCIA}}, never by the current time.
5. Document the backfill and window reprocessing procedure step by step, and define an idempotency test suite (double run produces the same count and the same checksum per partition).

Use native SQL for {{MOTOR}} and do not invent columns or table names not provided: tag them as [ASSUMPTION] or ask before coding. Before executing, restate what you understood about the flow (origin, destination, grain, frequency) and present your plan.

Variables:
- {{PIPELINE}}: name and purpose of the pipeline (origin, destination table, what it loads)
- {{MOTOR}}: execution platform and SQL (BigQuery, Snowflake, Postgres, Spark, or dbt)
- {{CLAVE_NEGOCIO}}: column(s) that uniquely identify each record at the destination grain (natural key)
- {{COLUMNA_PARTICION}}: date/event column that defines the deterministic load window (event_date, updated_at)
- {{FRECUENCIA}}: run cadence and window size (daily, hourly, micro-batch)

prompts.title: Model pipeline orchestration as a DAG
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data engineer specializing in production-scale pipeline orchestration on {{ORQUESTADOR}}. I need to convert {{PIPELINE}} into a reliable and operable orchestration modeled as a DAG: to move from a monolithic script or an implicit flow to an explicit graph of tasks with dependencies, retry policies, availability sensors, and measurable SLAs, to unlock reproducible runs, safe backfills, failure recovery without manual intervention, and freshness observability before it impacts the downstream consumer.

Design the orchestration as a DAG ready to code and produce: (1) decomposition into atomic and idempotent tasks, each with name, purpose, input and output contract, and the concrete mechanism that makes it re-runnable without duplicating effects (upsert key, overwritable partition, processing mark, transactional operation); (2) dependency graph in Mermaid notation (directed edges, no cycles), distinguishing data dependencies from control dependencies; (3) operational policy table per task: retries, exponential backoff with jitter, execution timeout, trigger rule (all_success, all_done, one_failed), and partial SLA, consistent with {{POLITICA_REINTENTOS}} and {{SLA_OBJETIVO}}; (4) sensor design for {{ORIGEN_DATOS}}: type (reschedule vs. poke), polling interval, timeout, and fallback to avoid worker starvation and infinite waits; (5) idempotent backfill strategy and parameterization by execution interval (execution_date or partition) aligned with {{FRECUENCIA}}; (6) observability and alerting: metrics per task, failure and SLA-breach callbacks, and to whom they escalate.

Rules: classify each failure as transient (network, rate limit, transient timeout) or deterministic (invalid schema, corrupt data, constraint violation) and do NOT retry deterministic ones; use sensors in reschedule mode by default and justify any poke; guarantee that re-running an interval produces the same result; verify that the graph is acyclic and that partial SLAs add up consistently to the end-to-end SLA {{SLA_OBJETIVO}}. Tag every unconfirmed datum as [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent real table names, bucket names, or endpoints. Deliver: task list and contracts, Mermaid DAG diagram, operational policy table per task, sensor and backfill design, and observability plan, ready to translate to {{ORQUESTADOR}} code.

Parameters: {{ORQUESTADOR}}, {{PIPELINE}}, {{ORIGEN_DATOS}}, {{FRECUENCIA}}, {{SLA_OBJETIVO}}, {{POLITICA_REINTENTOS}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Structure modular transformations in dbt style
prompts.content:
Act as a senior analytics engineer with experience leading productive dbt projects on {{MOTOR_WAREHOUSE}}. Design the complete modular transformation project in three layers (staging, intermediate, marts) for {{MOTOR_WAREHOUSE}}, with concrete SQL and YAML ready to initialize.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand, present your plan, then execute.

Inputs:
- {{MOTOR_WAREHOUSE}}: warehouse engine (defines SQL dialect and materializations).
- {{FUENTES_CRUDAS}}: source systems and tables with their main entities.
- {{DOMINIOS_NEGOCIO}}: consumption domains to organize the marts.
- {{GRANULARIDAD_MARTS}}: grain of the final facts and dimensions.
- {{ESTRATEGIA_CARGA}}: full-refresh or incremental, and expected frequency.

If any essential input is missing, ask for it before continuing; do not invent schemas or table names.

Deliver: (1) Map of {{FUENTES_CRUDAS}} and target graph source > staging > intermediate > marts, marking which {{DOMINIOS_NEGOCIO}} domain consumes what. (2) Folder and naming conventions (stg_<source>__<entity>, int_<entity>__<verb>, fct_<fact>/dim_<dimension>) and layer rules: staging 1:1 with the source without joins; intermediate isolates reusable logic; marts consume only intermediate or staging via ref(), never mart-to-mart; zero hardcoded tables. (3) One representative model per layer in SQL valid for the {{MOTOR_WAREHOUSE}} dialect, using ref()/source(). (4) schema.yml per folder with sources with freshness, descriptions, generic tests (unique, not_null, accepted_values, relationships) in the correct layer, plus at least one singular test in tests/ with its SQL. (5) Materialization table per layer (view in staging, ephemeral/view in intermediate, table or incremental in marts per {{ESTRATEGIA_CARGA}}) with justification; if incremental, define unique_key, is_incremental(), and strategy (merge/insert+delete) consistent with {{MOTOR_WAREHOUSE}}.

Edge cases: duplicate or null natural keys (deduplicate in staging with explicit criterion), one-to-many fan-out (resolve in intermediate), late-arriving data and reprocessing (idempotency), time zone and date types. Marts must respect exactly {{GRANULARIDAD_MARTS}}. Close with a verifiable acceptance checklist and tag assumptions with [ASSUMPTION].

prompts.title: Design error handling and a dead letter queue
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data engineer specializing in resilient ETL pipelines, fault-tolerance patterns (DLQ, circuit breaker, idempotency), and data observability. Your goal is to design an error handling strategy with a dead letter queue for {{MOTOR_PIPELINE}} that processes {{VOLUMEN_Y_CADENCIA}} from {{FUENTES_Y_DESTINO}}, preventing a single malformed record from aborting the entire pipeline, blocking good data, and triggering massive reprocessing. The design must isolate what has failed, keep the flow alive, alert in time, and allow controlled reprocessing, unlocking operational continuity, SLA compliance, and auditable traceability.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before designing, restate what you understand about {{MOTOR_PIPELINE}}, {{FUENTES_Y_DESTINO}}, {{VOLUMEN_Y_CADENCIA}}, {{SLA_Y_TOLERANCIA}}, and {{DESTINO_CUARENTENA}}; present your plan and wait for confirmation. If {{ERRORES_FRECUENTES}}, {{SLA_Y_TOLERANCIA}}, or {{DESTINO_CUARENTENA}} are missing, ask for them before assuming and tag any assumption as [ASSUMPTION].

Produce a design document ready to implement with these sections:
1. Error taxonomy: classify transient (timeouts, locks, rate limits, network failures, temporary unavailability) vs. permanent (invalid schema, type violation, broken business rule, missing PII, source duplicate). Define action by class: retry vs. quarantine directly. Incorporate {{ERRORES_FRECUENTES}} if provided and include a gray zone (ambiguous errors) with a default decision rule.
2. Capture pattern: try/catch boundary at record and batch level, skip-and-route isolation policy (no fail-fast), and quantified batch abort threshold, tied to {{SLA_Y_TOLERANCIA}}. Include behavior on poison pill (record that breaks the deserializer before validation).
3. DLQ/quarantine structure: schema of the failed record (original raw payload, error_type, error_class, error_message, stage, pipeline_run_id, timestamp, source_offset/source_id, attempts, correlation_id, schema_version), persistence in {{DESTINO_CUARENTENA}}, retention, and partitioning.
4. Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts per error class, circuit breaker on source outage, and idempotency of reprocessing with an explicit deduplication key to avoid duplicates.
5. Alerts and observability: at least 3 metrics (error rate by stage, DLQ depth, age of oldest message, reprocessing success rate), trigger thresholds, named notification channel, and end-to-end traceability by correlation_id. Distinguish actionable alert from noise.
6. Reprocessing flow: inspection, correction, and re-injection (manual or automatic) preserving order and consistency, with a permanent discard criterion (terminal DLQ) and prevention of infinite reprocessing loops.

Close with: textual diagram happy path vs. error path, assumptions tagged [ASSUMPTION], edge cases (poison pill, DLQ full, prolonged source outage, reprocessing that fails again), and prioritized implementation checklist P0/P1/P2. Neutral professional English, no emojis. Never invent environment details.

Parameters:
- {{MOTOR_PIPELINE}}: Orchestration/processing engine (e.g., Airflow + Spark, dbt, Kafka Streams, batch SQL)
- {{FUENTES_Y_DESTINO}}: Data origins and final destination (lake, warehouse, topic)
- {{VOLUMEN_Y_CADENCIA}}: Volume per run and frequency (e.g., 50M rows/day, every hour)
- {{ERRORES_FRECUENTES}}: Most common failure types today (optional)
- {{SLA_Y_TOLERANCIA}}: Freshness SLA and tolerance for record loss (optional)
- {{DESTINO_CUARENTENA}}: Where to persist failed records (table, DLQ topic, bucket) (optional)

prompts.title: Plan a controlled historical backfill
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data engineer specializing in large-scale reprocessing pipelines, with mastery of idempotency, partitioning, and cost control on modern data platforms. I need an executable and resumable historical backfill plan to reprocess {{TABLA_OBJETIVO}} over the window {{VENTANA_HISTORICA}}, without degrading the production service or breaking downstream consumers.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate what you understand about {{TABLA_OBJETIVO}}, {{VENTANA_HISTORICA}}, {{GRANO_LOTE}}, {{FUENTE_ORIGEN}}, {{RESTRICCIONES_COSTO}}, and {{REGLA_VALIDACION}}, declare your assumptions, and present your plan. If a critical datum is missing (volume per partition, natural key, schema, downstream dependencies), ask for it; do not invent volumes or schemas.

Deliver numbered:
1. Framing: scope, natural deduplication key, downstream dependencies of {{TABLA_OBJETIVO}}, assumptions tagged as ASSUMPTION, and reason for the backfill (historical correction, new column fill, or data recovery), because the reason changes the strategy.
2. Batching strategy by {{GRANO_LOTE}} and order: batch size, sequence (oldest to most recent unless a dependency requires another order), and a pilot batch to size before the full sweep.
3. Idempotency: safe write technique (merge/upsert by natural key, delete-insert by partition, or versioned snapshot) that avoids duplicates and orphan rows on retries; justify based on the {{TABLA_OBJETIVO}} engine.
4. Cost and concurrency control within {{RESTRICCIONES_COSTO}}: batch size, maximum parallelism, low-traffic time window, throttling, and spending cap in consumed capacity, plus the effect on live incremental loads.
5. Batch-by-batch validation against {{REGLA_VALIDACION}}: expected vs. actual counts, control sums, parity with {{FUENTE_ORIGEN}}, gap and duplicate detection, and late-arriving data handling during the backfill.
6. Stop gates and rollback: explicit tolerance threshold per metric, action on deviation, and isolation of already-validated batches.
7. Resumable runbook: numbered steps with persistent checkpoint, idempotent resumption without reprocessing validated batches, log, and consumer communication.
8. Final reconciliation: zero gaps and zero duplicates over {{VENTANA_HISTORICA}}, aggregate parity against {{FUENTE_ORIGEN}}, and formal closure criterion.

Consider attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.
Return a table per batch (range, order, dependency, validation, gate) plus the numbered runbook and final reconciliation. Tag uncertainty with ASSUMPTION; do not invent volumes or schemas.

prompts.title: Deciding between batch and streaming processing
Managing schema evolution in ingestion
prompts.content: Act as a senior data engineer specializing in ingestion platforms and data contracts, with expertise in Avro/Protobuf schema evolution rules, schema registry, and bronze/silver/gold modeling. Source {{FUENTE}} feeding {{MOTOR_INGESTION}} ({{FORMATO_DATOS}} toward {{DESTINO}}) is going to change its schema and the team needs to absorb {{CAMBIOS_PROPUESTOS}} without breaking downstream consumers or blindly reprocessing history, under policy {{POLITICA_COMPATIBILIDAD}}. The goal is to unblock continuous changes with a data-contract discipline that makes evolution predictable, versioned, and auditable, avoiding silently corrupt loads and schema debt. Deliver an actionable and versioned strategy. To achieve this: (1) Classify each change in {{CAMBIOS_PROPUESTOS}} as backward-compatible, forward-compatible, or breaking applying Avro/Protobuf rules, declaring what breaks and for whom; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any inference about consumers, volumes, or undeclared environments. (2) Define handling rules by type: new columns with explicit default and tolerance for absence; renames via alias/mapping, never DROP+ADD that loses data; type changes distinguishing safe promotions (int to long, int to string, adding a union member) from unsafe conversions (string to int, narrowing, precision change) that require a shadow column and controlled backfill. (3) Draft the versioned data contract with a concrete schema, owner, semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (MAJOR=breaking, MINOR=additive compatible, PATCH=metadata), compatibility policy, and a dated deprecation window. (4) Design enforcement: validation against the schema registry in CI and at runtime, dead-letter quarantine with reprocessing criterion, and drift detection between the actual schema of {{FUENTE}} and the contract. (5) Deliver the version promotion runbook and the reversible rollback plan, with intermediate dual-write/dual-read states and the cutover criterion when applicable. Cover edge cases: nullable to required, positional reordering, unrecognized new enum value, and change of timezone or unit without renaming the field (semantically invisible change to the schema). State the trade-offs between adoption speed and safety. If {{CAMBIOS_PROPUESTOS}} is empty or the schema diff is missing, ask for it before classifying; do not invent the content of the change. If you receive {{ADJUNTOS}}, use them as the source of truth for the current schema. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Flattening and normalizing nested JSON to tables
prompts.content: Act as a senior data engineer specializing in relational modeling and semi-structured data transformation, with expertise in JSON flattening, Codd's normal forms, and each engine's native flattening functions (JSON_TABLE, lateral flatten, UNNEST, OPENJSON). I have data in {{JSON_FUENTE}} with nested objects and arrays that a relational engine cannot query with plain SQL, and I need to convert it into a normalized, traceable, and idempotently loadable tabular model for {{MOTOR_DESTINO}}. Proceed as follows: (1) Profile the structure by traversing {{JSON_FUENTE}} and building a path tree; for each node declare type (object, array of objects, array of scalars, array of arrays, scalar), cardinality, nullability, and depth; report inconsistencies across records: optional fields, mixed types at the same path, JSON null vs. absent key, numbers encoded as strings, and dates with heterogeneous formats or timezones. (2) Partition into tables: flatten each 1:1 object into columns of the same table using path notation and {{CONVENCION_NOMBRES}}; convert each array of objects into a 1:N child table; resolve arrays of scalars per {{ESTRATEGIA_ARRAYS}}; decompose arrays of arrays into successive levels of child tables. (3) Define keys: use {{CLAVE_PRIMARIA}} as the root entity key only if it is stable, non-null, and unique, or generate a deterministic surrogate (hash of the business identity) if it is not; propagate the parent FK to each child; retain the array position index as part of the child key when order matters. (4) Normalize to 3NF: eliminate repeating groups, partial dependencies, and transitive dependencies; justify each deliberate denormalization by query. (5) Map types to the {{MOTOR_DESTINO}} dialect (integer, decimal with scale, text, boolean, date/time with or without timezone in ISO 8601, native JSON for residuals) and define the NULL policy; flag ambiguous types. (6) Deliver CREATE TABLE DDL per table with PK, FK, and constraints; transformation logic (native SQL for {{MOTOR_DESTINO}} or pseudocode if portable); a textual entity-relationship diagram; a path-to-column lineage map; and an idempotent load plan (UPSERT by merge key) with source-to-destination reconciliation queries. Mark as assumption any inference not confirmed by {{JSON_FUENTE}}. If {{JSON_FUENTE}} is not provided or is not representative, ask for it. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Work in neutral professional English.

prompts.title: Structuring a lakehouse with bronze, silver, and gold layers
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data engineer specializing in lakehouse architectures and the medallion pattern, with experience in data quality contracts and data governance. I want an actionable medallion architecture contract that the team can implement directly on {{MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE}} for domains {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}}: each layer (bronze, silver, gold) with unambiguous responsibilities and predictable, auditable, and reproducible data promotion. The purpose is to unlock reliable analytical consumption and avoid three anti-patterns: business logic leaking into bronze, silver accumulating duplicates, and gold serving data without quality guarantees.

Deliver:
1. A table per layer: purpose, owner, physical format, granularity, retention, and schema policy (schema-on-read vs. enforced), with no overlap of responsibilities.
2. Promotion rules bronze->silver and silver->gold: transformations, deduplication, conforming of dimensions and facts, null handling, and business rules per hop. Explicitly declare what does NOT happen in each layer.
3. A quality gate matrix per layer: schema validations, referential integrity, freshness (per {{SLA_FRESCURA}}), completeness, and uniqueness; with an action on failure per {{POLITICA_CALIDAD}} (quarantine, hard reject, alert and continue) and the threshold that triggers it. If {{HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION}} is provided, express each gate as an assertion implementable in that tool.
4. Engineering guarantees per layer: load idempotency, reprocessing and backfill, schema evolution (new columns, type change, rename), partitioning and ordering, anchored to real mechanisms of {{MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE}} (MERGE, time travel, OPTIMIZE), not generic.
5. Lineage model and minimum metadata per table: source, ingestion timestamp, schema version, run id, and control hash, to trace a gold record back to its origin in bronze.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Confirm {{MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE}}, {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}}, {{SLA_FRESCURA}}, {{HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION}}, and {{POLITICA_CALIDAD}}. If a key piece of data is missing, ask for it; anything unconfirmed is marked [ASSUMPTION]. Do not invent engine capabilities: if MERGE, time travel, or schema enforcement support is not established, declare it as an assumption to validate. Close with a contract ready to implement on {{MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE}}, without prices or invented data.

Parameters: {{MOTOR_LAKEHOUSE}}, {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}}, {{SLA_FRESCURA}}, {{HERRAMIENTA_ORQUESTACION}}, {{POLITICA_CALIDAD}}.

prompts.title: Optimizing the cost of a cloud data pipeline
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data engineer with practice in FinOps and optimization of analytical cloud platforms (columnar warehouses and data lakes on object storage). Your assignment: deliver an actionable and validatable plan to cut the compute and storage cost of {{PIPELINE}} on {{PLATAFORMA_MOTOR}} without degrading freshness or correctness, targeting the few high-leverage vectors: bytes scanned per query, recomputation of data that has not changed, and poorly structured storage.

Before proposing, separate compute from storage and declare the billing model you assume from {{PLATAFORMA_MOTOR}}. If an input is missing that would change the recommendation, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent billing figures or assume an engine.

Proceed in four phases. (1) Diagnosis per stage (ingestion, transformation, materialization, consumption): identify the dominant driver from {{COSTO_ACTUAL}} and apply 80/20 to isolate the vectors that concentrate spend, separating compute from storage. (2) Design of levers in order: partition pruning and predicate pushdown against {{PATRONES_CONSULTA}} (critical tables partitioned by the dominant filter column with appropriate granularity, without over-partitioning or small files; filters on the partition column, not on an expression that disables it); compressed columnar format and compaction over {{VOLUMEN_DATOS}} (Parquet/ORC, target file size of hundreds of MB, clustering/sort by frequent filter columns); selective materialization table by table (view / incremental by delta / full-refresh) justified against {{FRESCURA_REQUERIDA}} and recomputation cost, eliminating intermediates with no consumer; storage and retention by moving cold data to lower-cost tiers in {{PLATAFORMA_MOTOR}} and defining expiration of staging and temporary tables. (3) Prioritization in a table by estimated savings (relative or per bytes/time, never in currency unless {{COSTO_ACTUAL}} allows it) vs. effort vs. impact on freshness/risk. (4) Plan and validation: concrete changes (partitioning DDL, query rewrites, materialization configuration, tiering policies) and a result parity protocol (counts, control sums, before/after comparison) plus measured cost regression. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on all unconfirmed data.

Variables:
- {{PIPELINE}}: name and one-line description (purpose, layers, consumption outputs).
- {{PLATAFORMA_MOTOR}}: cloud and query/transformation engine (columnar warehouse, engine on data lake, orchestrator) and billing model if known.
- {{VOLUMEN_DATOS}}: total volume and per critical table, growth, current partition/storage format.
- {{PATRONES_CONSULTA}}: most frequent or costly queries and jobs, dominant filter columns, and consumption SLAs.
- {{COSTO_ACTUAL}}: known cost breakdown by stage or service (compute vs. storage) or top queries/jobs by spend (optional).
- {{FRESCURA_REQUERIDA}}: latency tolerated per table or layer (real-time, hourly, daily) (optional).

prompts.title: Designing a decision-oriented executive dashboard
Choosing the right chart type for each dataset
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data visualization specialist, trained in Andrew Abela's chart selection framework (Chart Suggestions, 2006), the Cleveland-McGill perceptual hierarchy (1984), and Edward Tufte's graphic integrity principles (lie-factor). Your task is to recommend the correct chart type to communicate {{MENSAJE}} about {{DATOS}}, to {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}}, so that the reader understands the insight at a glance and without being led to a false conclusion: the visual form serves the message, it does not distort it.

Parameters:
- MENSAJE: {{MENSAJE}} (main message in one sentence, the insight the audience must understand; e.g., "northern region sales are triple the rest", "churn rises every quarter")
- DATOS: {{DATOS}} (structure: variables, number of categories or data points, whether there is a temporal dimension, whether the parts sum to a total)
- AUDIENCIA_MEDIO: {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}} (who reads it and where it will be seen: executive report, live dashboard, slide, mobile, printed)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} (tool limits, space, accessibility such as color blindness or black-and-white, or others; optional)

If {{MENSAJE}}, the structure of {{DATOS}}, or the medium in {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}} are missing, ask for them before continuing and do not invent numbers or figures not provided.

Return, in neutral professional English without emojis: (1) Framing that restates the message and confirms structure, audience, medium, and constraints, marking [ASSUMPTION] on what is inferred; (2) Intent in one of five families — compare across categories, compare over time or trend, distribution, relationship or correlation, part-to-whole composition — with the others dismissed in one line; (3) Primary chart and alternative justified with Cleveland-McGill (position on common axis, length, angle or area, color or volume), prioritizing the encoding with the lowest error and dismissing the tempting but inferior option; (4) Encoding: axes, category order, what to highlight, linear or logarithmic scale, and the zero rule; (5) Anti-patterns to avoid in this case with the specific distortion of each; (6) Accessibility adjusted to {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}} and {{RESTRICCIONES}}; (7) Close in one actionable sentence ready to build. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.

prompts.title: Structuring a KPI hierarchy with drill-down
Critique and redesign of an overloaded dashboard
Adapting a dashboard to a responsive and mobile layout
prompts.content:
Act as a senior dashboard designer and responsive data visualization specialist, with expertise in mobile-first, progressive disclosure, inverted data pyramid, and KPI visual hierarchy. Reorganize {{DASHBOARD}} into a mobile-first responsive layout where {{MENSAJE_PRINCIPAL}} is read in the first seconds without scrolling, and detail is revealed progressively, so that {{AUDIENCIA}} can decide from the phone with the same confidence as on desktop. The framework contributes information hierarchy applied to the small screen.

Inputs:
- DASHBOARD: {{DASHBOARD}} (what it measures and how it is used)
- VISUALES: {{VISUALES}} (inventory of current cards, charts, tables, and filters)
- MENSAJE_PRINCIPAL: {{MENSAJE_PRINCIPAL}} (conclusion or decision that must be read first)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} (who consults it on mobile and in what context)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} (BI tool, breakpoints, supported interactions; optional)

If {{VISUALES}}, {{MENSAJE_PRINCIPAL}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before continuing; do not invent metrics or visuals. Deliver in this order: (1) sentence '[role] reviews [decision] in [context]'; (2) main message readable in about three seconds without scrolling; (3) classification of each visual from {{VISUALES}} into Level 1/2/3 with a one-line justification; (4) vertical order in one column by inverted pyramid adjusted to {{AUDIENCIA}}; (5) reassignment of each chart to a narrow-screen-readable format respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}, with before, after, and reason; (6) responsive rules: collapse breakpoint, what is hidden or moved to a menu, filter mutation, and minimum tap area; (7) what is NOT shown on mobile and why; (8) resolved mobile validation checklist. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on every decision without confirmed data. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Define filters, parameters and interactivity
Apply accessibility and color palette to visualizations
prompts.content: Act as a senior accessible data visualization specialist, experienced in applying WCAG 2.1 and color-blind-safe palettes (Okabe-Ito, ColorBrewer) in production dashboards. Audit the color accessibility of a {{TIPO_GRAFICO}} visualization that must distinguish these series or categories: {{SERIES_CATEGORIAS}}. The current palette is {{PALETA_ACTUAL}}, the target WCAG level is {{NIVEL_WCAG}}, and the usage context is {{CONTEXTO_USO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any input is missing or ambiguous, ask for all of it in one single round before continuing. Then diagnose the palette on three axes: color-blindness safety by simulating deuteranopia, protanopia, and tritanopia and marking pairs that collapse; contrast by calculating the ratio of each color against the background and between adjacent series against the applicable thresholds (3:1 non-text graphic and borders, 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text); and exclusive dependence on color. Then redesign: assign each series a hex from a validated and named system, ordered by maximum perceptual distance; use a single-hue sequential scale for magnitude and a diverging scale with a neutral center for deviation. Add at least one redundant encoding layer appropriate to the type (shape, pattern, direct label, line weight or style, position). If {{CONTEXTO_USO}} includes print or projection, address its contrast degradation separately. Do not invent brand colors or assume the BI tool; mark any unconfirmed data as an assumption. Deliver: palette table (series, hex, contrast against background, redundant layer), report of non-compliant pairs with numerical ratio, verification checklist with validation instructions, and final compliance verdict with prioritized pending adjustments. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Design threshold alerts and traffic lights in reports
Add narrative and annotations to a dashboard
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Business Intelligence analyst expert in data storytelling, with mastery of visual hierarchy and executive dashboard design. Your task is to convert {{DASHBOARD}} for the period {{PERIODO}} into a decision-making tool for {{AUDIENCIA}}, readable in seconds with the suggested action made explicit.

MetodologIA Protocol: first Interpret (restate what you understand about {{DASHBOARD}}, {{METRICAS_CLAVE}}, {{PERIODO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{EVENTOS_CONTEXTO}}; name the 2–3 dominant findings), then Plan (present the reading order and the finding-chart-title-annotation mapping), and only then Execute. If an essential piece of information is missing, ask before continuing; never invent figures or causes.

Deliver four components ready to apply: 1) Actionable titles: rewrite each chart title from {{DASHBOARD}} in the format subject + figure + direction + cause (when the cause is in the data), in a table of current title vs. actionable title. 2) Contextual annotations: for each relevant series define one annotation anchored to a specific point using {{EVENTOS_CONTEXTO}}, classified as event, anomaly, or critical threshold (target, SLA, break-even), with a brief label explaining the why; table: chart, point/date, type, label. 3) Executive summary: 3 to 5 sentences from {{METRICAS_CLAVE}} data answering what happened, why it matters, and what decision is suggested, plus a template version with placeholders for regenerating when data changes. 4) Reading order: order the recommendations in an F or Z pattern, with the critical content at the top left and justification.

Mark [ASSUMPTION] on any unconfirmed cause or figure in the inputs. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Close by verifying: every title with figure and direction, every annotation anchored and classified, summary <= 5 sentences in both versions, zero invented metrics. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Design a self-service analytics experience
prompts.content: Act as a senior self-service analytics and BI architect, with experience in semantic layer modeling, data governance, and adoption programs. Design a self-service analytics experience for business users in {{SECTOR}} on {{HERRAMIENTA_BI}}, enabling them to autonomously explore the domains {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}} starting from an analytical maturity of {{MADUREZ_ANALITICA}}, without parallel reports with contradictory figures or decisions on uncertified data, oriented toward {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}}. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. If {{SECTOR}}, {{HERRAMIENTA_BI}}, {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}}, {{MADUREZ_ANALITICA}}, or {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}} are missing, ask first; mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver a document with five blocks. 1) Semantic layer: 2 to 4 domain datasets, each with grain, dimensions, certified metrics with their business formula in plain language, source of each field, and certified/experimental separation; include one anti-pattern to avoid. 2) Visualization template library (KPI tracking, time comparison, ranking, distribution, funnel), each with the business question it answers, when to use it, and when NOT to. 3) Guardrail matrix: row-level and domain permissions, PII and sensitive data, freshness and quality, certified vs. uncertified label, and performance limits. 4) Enablement model: consumer, explorer, and author levels with learning path, promotion criteria, and a process for certifying ad hoc content. 5) Metrics dashboard aligned with {{OBJETIVO_ADOPCION}}: adoption, autonomy, reduction of requests, and confidence in figures, each with definition, measurement method, and baseline, plus a common adoption risk and its mitigation. Close with acceptance criteria. No prices. Neutral and professional English, no invented figures or tools.

prompts.title: Define the product North Star metric
Build a metrics and drivers tree
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data and business analytics analyst specialized in driver trees and metrics decomposition, with experience connecting result KPIs with operable inputs in {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}} businesses. Your deliverable is a driver tree with explicit causal relationships, a table of actionable leaves, a leverage ranking, and the selection of focus drivers. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Proceed as follows:

1. Framing. Confirm the definition of {{METRICA_RESULTADO}} (formula, unit, period, population) and its current value from {{DEFINICION_METRICA}}. If the definition is ambiguous, propose two possible readings and declare which one you assume. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any data not in {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} and do not invent baselines or elasticities. If critical context is missing, ask for it before decomposing.

2. Decomposition. Decompose {{METRICA_RESULTADO}} into first-level drivers with an EXPLICIT mathematical relationship per node (product, sum, or weighted average) and take each branch down to leaves that are actionable inputs, not aggregates. A leaf is actionable if a specific team can move it with a decision; if it is still an aggregate, keep decomposing. Avoid double-counting: the same quantity cannot appear in two branches that are then summed.

3. Nature of each edge. On each edge distinguish accounting identity (certain by definition) from causal hypothesis (assumed correlation); mark hypotheses as [ASSUMPTION] if {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}} does not support them and indicate their expected direction and strength.

4. Leaf profile. For each leaf define: name of the input, formula or event that measures it, current baseline (or [ASSUMPTION] if data is missing), unit, concrete lever that moves it, and the area or responsible owner.

5. Leverage. Estimate how much a 10 percent change in each leaf moves {{METRICA_RESULTADO}} according to the tree relationships, make the elasticity assumption explicit, and rank from highest to lowest. If data is insufficient, prioritize by judgment marking it [ASSUMPTION]. Distinguish theoretical leverage from real actionability within {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}: a high-impact but uncontrollable leaf is not a focus.

6. Focus and protection. Recommend the 2–3 drivers with the highest leverage and real control within {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}, one lever per driver with its tracking metric, and 1–2 guardrails against side effects.

Expected deliverable: indented tree with relationship per node and identity/hypothesis label per edge, leaf table (input, formula/event, baseline, unit, lever, owner, leverage) ordered by leverage, and the 2–3 focus drivers one sentence each with lever, tracking metric, and guardrail.

Variables:
- {{METRICA_RESULTADO}}: result KPI the business wants to move (e.g. monthly revenue, churn, margin, NPS).
- {{DEFINICION_METRICA}}: formula, unit, period, population, and current value of the metric (if missing, ask).
- {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}: how the business operates and makes money (transactional, subscription, marketplace, usage).
- {{DATOS_DISPONIBLES}}: tables, events, metrics, and existing analytics sources for estimating baselines.
- {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}: window in which levers will be acted upon (e.g. quarter, semester).

Neutral and professional English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Specify the formula and calculation logic of a metric
prompts.content: Act as a senior analytics engineer with more than a decade designing semantic layers and metric dictionaries (dbt Semantic Layer, LookML, Cube), responsible for unique and auditable definitions. I need a versioned specification sheet (metric spec) for {{NOMBRE_METRICA}}, ready to implement without reinterpretation. Before drafting, restate in your own words the metric, its source, and its grain, and present your plan; flag as a question any missing data instead of inventing it. Then deliver: (1) {{NOMBRE_METRICA}} in one business sentence and the question it answers; (2) the formula as numerator / denominator, or base aggregation if it is a count or sum, naming each field and table within {{FUENTE_DATOS}}; (3) the granularity {{GRANULARIDAD}} (what one row represents) and the unit of measure; (4) valid dimensions {{DIMENSIONES}} and the filters that ALWAYS apply according to {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}; (5) time window, dating criterion, and canonical time zone; (6) explicit resolution of {{CASOS_BORDE}}: division by zero, nulls, duplicates, refunds or reversals, late-arriving data, currency and conversion, definition changes over time; (7) the final formula in readable pseudo-SQL; (8) two worked numerical examples step by step, one normal and one edge case; (9) actionable validation tests: expected ranges, reconciliation against source of truth, behavior on empty partition, and one non-regression test. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if provided. Label each rule as CONFIRMED or ASSUMPTION; do not invent numbers or fields. Close with assumptions to confirm and the proposed version of the spec. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Distinguish vanity metrics from actionable metrics
prompts.content:
Act as a senior product and data analyst, specialist in actionable metric design (AARRR/pirate frameworks, North Star Metric, and the vanity vs. actionable distinction from Lean Analytics). You are going to audit the dashboard of {{EQUIPO_O_PRODUCTO}} and convert it into a system of signals that change decisions, not a wall of counts that only go up.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate which metrics are in {{LISTA_METRICAS}}, which decision they should inform ({{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}), and what the moment of value is ({{MOMENTO_DE_VALOR}}); flag what is ambiguous (funnel, who decides, time window), and if something blocks the analysis, ask for it before continuing. Then present your plan. Only then execute.

Execution:
1. Inventory each metric in {{LISTA_METRICAS}} and apply the actionability test: which decision in {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} would change if that number went up or down 20 percent. If the answer is none, it is a vanity candidate.
2. Classify each one as Actionable, Vanity, Questionable, or Guardrail (health that does not decide but protects). Justify in one line.
3. For each Vanity, design an actionable replacement, preferably a ratio or normalized rate (over cohort, session, or stage) rather than an absolute count, anchored to {{MOMENTO_DE_VALOR}}.
4. Define each new metric: name, explicit formula, owner, threshold or range that triggers action (linked to {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}} when applicable), and the decision it enables.
5. Flag gaps: metrics missing to cover the full funnel or {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}.

Edge cases: if a metric is leading for an Actionable one, mark it Questionable and explain the link; do not eliminate guardrails even if they do not decide; if two metrics measure the same thing, recommend consolidating. Do not invent figures or business data; anything not verifiable goes marked [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver: audit table (metric | classification | why | replacement) and definitions block (name | formula | owner | threshold | decision) ready for the dashboard. Close with the 3 highest-leverage metrics. Variables: {{LISTA_METRICAS}}, {{EQUIPO_O_PRODUCTO}}, {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}}, {{MOMENTO_DE_VALOR}}, {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}. If any is missing, ask for it before auditing.

prompts.title: Define funnel metrics with the AARRR framework
prompts.content: Act as a senior Analytics Lead with fifteen years of experience instrumenting product funnels and defining actionable metrics using Dave McClure's AARRR (Pirate Metrics) framework and retention cohort analysis. I need a metrics framework that makes the entire user lifecycle measurable before optimizing anything: it exposes where value is gained and where it leaks, connects the stages with comparable conversion rates, and enables a defensible effort-investment decision. Context: business {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}, already-instrumented events {{EVENTOS_DISPONIBLES}}, reference period {{PERIODO_ANALISIS}}, decision to enable {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}. If any of those four pieces of data is missing or arrives ambiguously, ask for all of them in one single round before continuing. Proceed as follows. First, frame: confirm inputs, fix the business model and the A-A-R-R-R order; do not assume benchmarks or market figures, and if you infer something, mark it as an assumption. Second, define each AARRR stage (Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue) with: operational definition (entry event and advance event), main metric with explicit numerator/denominator formula and window, instrumentation events marked [DATA] if they exist in {{EVENTOS_DISPONIBLES}} or [ASSUMPTION] if missing, and conversion rate to the next stage (advanced / entered) with a coherent denominator and window to chain the funnel. Apply the focus specific to each stage: Acquisition by channel and effort cost without monetary figures; Activation at the aha moment; Retention by cohorts distinguished from aggregate; Referral with an invitation coefficient; Revenue with conversion to payment and expansion. Third, consolidate the funnel table (stage, main metric, formula, conversion to next stage, data source), declare one North Star aligned to {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}} and explain its relationship to the five stages, and identify the highest-leakage stage with the quantitative signal that would confirm or discard it. Defer all optimization tactics: the deliverable is metric definition. Close by declaring current assumptions and instrumentation gaps that would block the calculation. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Translate OKRs into measurable indicators with source, baseline, and target
Balance leading and lagging indicators
Define guardrail metrics for experiments
Create a governed catalog of certified metrics
prompts.content:
Act as a senior analytics engineer specializing in metrics governance and semantic layer design, with experience migrating organizations from scattered definitions to a single certified catalog. Your job: convert the conflicting metrics of {{DOMINIO_NEGOCIO}} into a governed catalog with a single source of truth, where every metric has a reproducible definition, traceable lineage, and responsible owners.

Inputs: catalog {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}} (definitions or calculations as they stand, even if conflicting); rely on {{STACK_DATOS}} (warehouse, BI, and semantic or catalog layer) for source and lineage; assign business owner and technical owner from {{OWNERS}}; and use {{NIVEL_CERTIFICACION}} as the standard for deciding when a metric is certified. If {{DOMINIO_NEGOCIO}}, {{METRICAS_ACTUALES}}, {{STACK_DATOS}}, or {{OWNERS}} are missing, ask before executing; do not invent definitions, owners, or lineage.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the problem as you understand it and present your plan; only then produce the deliverables.

Deliver three pieces. (1) Catalog in table format, one row per certified metric, with: unique canonical name, aliases or synonyms, one-sentence business description, formula with numerator, denominator, and explicit granularity, business owner and technical owner from {{OWNERS}}, source and origin table according to {{STACK_DATOS}}, permitted cut dimensions, update period, and certification status using exactly four values: certified, under review, deprecated, candidate. (2) Governance policy: objective criteria for moving from candidate to certified aligned with {{NIVEL_CERTIFICACION}}, roles for who proposes, reviews, and approves, versioning of definition changes, and deprecation protocol. (3) 30-60-90 day adoption plan naming dashboards and consumers of {{DOMINIO_NEGOCIO}} to migrate in priority order.

Method: inventory and disambiguate (group synonyms, flag duplicates and conflicts, resolve or flag as pending with a responsible party); complete the canonical card; define governance; close with the adoption plan. Tag [ASSUMPTION] on any inferred criterion, distinguish vanity metrics from actionable metrics, and for each deprecated metric indicate its replacement metric. Closing: catalog ready to paste into the catalog tool or semantic layer, with no invented definitions or owners.

prompts.title: Perform initial exploratory profiling of a dataset
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data analyst specializing in exploratory analysis and quality profiling. Deliver an initial exploratory profiling report for {{DATASET}}, without transforming, imputing, or deleting data: only diagnose the real shape of what is there. The intended downstream use is {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}} and the grain of each row is {{GRANO_FILA}}.

Protocol: first confirm that you received data, a row sample, or a schema with types; if missing, ask before continuing. If you are working on a partial sample, declare it as an assumption and warn that distributions may not be representative of the full population.

Structure the report in six sections. (1) General summary: rows, columns, one sentence on {{GRANO_FILA}}, and an aptitude verdict in three levels (apt, apt with reservations, not apt) for {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}}. (2) Column inventory: for each column, name, detected data type (continuous numeric, discrete numeric, categorical, boolean, date/time, free text, identifier), semantic role (measure, dimension, identifier, timestamp), and a real example. (3) Nulls: count and percentage per column from highest to lowest, tagging [ALERT] when exceeding {{UMBRAL_NULOS}}; distinguish true absence from sentinel values (0, -1, 'N/A', empty string) that simulate valid data. (4) Cardinality: unique values per column; identify identifiers, constants, and high-cardinality categoricals. (5) Distributions and ranges: numeric with min, max, mean, median, standard deviation, and IQR outliers; categoricals with the {{TOP_CATEGORIAS}} most frequent categories and their frequency plus residual count; dates with temporal range and evident gaps. (6) Findings and quality flags: anomalies prioritized by impact on {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}} (inconsistent types, impossible negatives, out-of-range dates, key duplicates, mixed encodings or units) and 3 to 5 actionable questions before modeling.

Firm rules: diagnose, do not transform; do not invent statistics; every figure derives from what was received and, if it cannot be calculated, say why. Tag inferences against what was verified. Close with the aptitude verdict and the next step.

Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Detect and treat outlier values
prompts.content: Act as a senior data scientist specializing in exploratory analysis (EDA) and data quality, with the judgment to separate noise from signal. I need an outlier diagnosis and a traceable, auditable treatment plan for {{DATASET}}, evaluating the columns {{COLUMNAS_NUMERICAS}} with objective {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}}. Before executing, restate in one line what you are analyzing and present your plan; if you are missing the dataset, the columns, the domain limits in {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, or the final use, ask me instead of assuming. Proceed as follows: (1) Profile each numeric column in {{COLUMNAS_NUMERICAS}} (count, nulls, minimum, maximum, mean, median, skew, tails) and choose the dominant method based on the shape of the distribution. (2) Apply IQR: outlier outside [Q1 - 1.5*IQR, Q3 + 1.5*IQR], extreme outside [Q1 - 3*IQR, Q3 + 3*IQR]. (3) Apply z-score with threshold {{UMBRAL_ZSCORE}}; if the distribution is skewed, warn that the normality assumption breaks and use the modified z-score (median + MAD). (4) Apply the business rules from {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}} to detect logically impossible values that statistics cannot see. (5) Triangulate the three methods and classify each outlier by confirmation level (1, 2, or 3 methods), prioritizing confirmed outliers and logically impossible ones. (6) For each group, recommend winsorize, exclude, investigate, or keep, with justification and concrete action; never delete silently. (7) Simulate the impact by recalculating mean, median, and standard deviation before and after, and report the delta. Align each decision with {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}}. Tag [ASSUMPTION] on what you infer. Deliverable: (a) table per column of outliers by method, (b) prioritized list of cases to investigate, (c) recommended treatment table with reason, and (d) impact table on statistics before vs. after. Variables: {{DATASET}}, {{COLUMNAS_NUMERICAS}}, {{UMBRAL_ZSCORE}}, {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Explore correlations and relationships between variables
prompts.content: Act as a senior data analyst specializing in exploratory analysis and applied statistics, with the judgment to choose the correct coefficient and the discipline not to confuse association with causality. Work on {{DATASET}} looking for relationships with {{VARIABLE_OBJETIVO}}, for an audience {{AUDIENCIA}} and to inform the decision {{DECISION_DE_NEGOCIO}}. If {{DATASET}} is not available or columns, format, the target variable, or the decision are missing, ask before continuing and do not invent values. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Produce a structured report that: (1) classifies each variable by type (continuous, discrete, ordinal, categorical) and reports rows, missing values per column, and null treatment; (2) for each pair chooses and justifies the coefficient: Pearson (two continuous, linear, no extreme outliers), Spearman (non-linear monotonicity, ordinals, or outliers), point-biserial (continuous vs. binary), Cramer's V or corrected V (two categoricals); (3) builds the matrix with the chosen coefficients, reports effective n per pair, and where applicable, p-value or confidence interval, warning about multiple comparisons; (4) delivers a ranking of pairs by absolute magnitude with strength (weak <0.3, moderate 0.3-0.7, strong >0.7) and direction, highlighting pairs with {{VARIABLE_OBJETIVO}}; (5) for each strong correlation lists rival explanations (confounder, reverse causality, selection bias, mediator, coincidence, spurious due to trend or seasonality) before implying cause; (6) closes with actionable findings aligned with {{DECISION_DE_NEGOCIO}} and the required confirmatory design for what is to be treated as causal. Maintain association language, never assert cause without confirmatory design, tag what is unprovided as [ASSUMPTION], and do not invent figures. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.

prompts.title: Compare distributions across segments
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data analyst specializing in exploratory analysis (EDA), with mastery of descriptive statistics, detection of sampling biases, and communication of findings for decision-making. Your task is to contrast how {{METRICA}} behaves across the segments of {{VARIABLE_SEGMENTO}} within {{DATASET}}, to distinguish real and actionable differences from variations due to noise or sparse samples, in service of {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}. If these inputs are not clear, ask me in a single batch before proceeding; do not invent columns, values, or segments.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understood and present your plan; then execute.

Proceed as follows: (1) Confirm that {{METRICA}} is numeric and {{VARIABLE_SEGMENTO}} is categorical with comparable segments; if they cannot be identified with certainty in {{DATASET}}, ask for them. Declare assumptions about types, unit of analysis, and period. (2) Report coverage per segment: n, nulls, and proportion of missing values; apply {{TRATAMIENTO_OUTLIERS}} explicitly and consistently to missing values and outliers, and fix the comparable base. (3) For each segment calculate the summary: n, mean, median, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, minimum, P25/P50/P75, P90, maximum, and interquartile range. (4) Describe the shape of each distribution (skewness, tails, multimodality) with histograms per segment and a comparative boxplot; if you cannot plot, deliver a table ready to plot and describe the shape with percentiles. (5) Quantify differences with an interpretable effect size (difference in medians and its relative magnitude; optionally interquartile range overlap) and flag every comparison with insufficient sample or strong imbalance. (6) Synthesize 2 or 3 prioritized findings with numerical evidence, affected segment, magnitude, and suggested action oriented toward {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}.

Edge cases: segment with very low n is reported as inconclusive; long tail of segments is grouped into Others with justification; zeros or negatives that are relevant are flagged. Avoid deciding based on averages when the median and the shape tell a different story. Tag every inference not supported by the data as an assumption. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Close when there is a comparative table per segment, shape descriptions, and prioritized findings with action.

prompts.title: Decompose a time series into trend and seasonality
prompts.content: Act as a senior data analyst specializing in time series, with mastery of classical decomposition, STL, and exploratory diagnosis. I need to decompose {{SERIE}} into trend, seasonality, and residual to inform {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Before executing, restate what you understand about the series and the objective, and present your plan. If {{FRECUENCIA}}, {{PERIODO_ESTACIONAL}}, {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, or {{UMBRAL_ANOMALIA}} are missing or clash with the data, ask before continuing; do not invent data or impute values silently. Proceed in four phases. Phase 1, diagnosis: confirm that {{FRECUENCIA}} matches the timestamps and verify chronological order, gaps, duplicate dates, and missing values; report each incident and propose treatment (interpolation, imputation, or exclusion). Phase 2, model: choose additive vs. multiplicative based on whether the seasonal amplitude is constant or grows with the level, justify with the variance-magnitude relationship, and confirm or adjust {{PERIODO_ESTACIONAL}} evaluating multiple seasonality. Phase 3, decomposition: isolate the three components and describe the direction and breaks of the trend, the seasonal pattern profile (peaks and troughs), and the strength of each component (explained variance), in business language. Phase 4, anomalies and close: flag extreme residuals according to {{UMBRAL_ANOMALIA}} and for each report the date, magnitude, and a verifiable causal hypothesis. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Tag each assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver a report with a component summary table (strength and reading), a prioritized anomaly list, and a monitoring strategy, with everything tied to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}.

prompts.title: Convert a business question into an analysis plan
prompts.content: Act as a senior data scientist with experience in product analytics, experimental design, and translation of business questions into exploratory analysis plans. Convert {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} (even if it arrives vague) into an executable analysis plan that unlocks {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}}, before querying a single table, using {{FUENTES_DISPONIBLES}} within {{VENTANA_Y_POBLACION}}. If any of those data points are missing, ask before continuing; do not invent business data. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand and present your plan; then execute it. Produce in this order: (1) Question rewritten precisely: what is measured, the unit of analysis, and the decision it unlocks. (2) Three to five falsifiable, non-overlapping, and jointly exhaustive hypotheses; each as a testable statement with a directional prediction and the exact condition that would refute it. (3) Data required per hypothesis: sources or tables from {{FUENTES_DISPONIBLES}}, fields, granularity, window, and population according to {{VENTANA_Y_POBLACION}}; flag missing data instead of inventing it. (4) Verification method per hypothesis: technique (cohorts, metric decomposition, correlation, mean difference test, time series), decision metric, and signal/noise threshold. (5) Confounders and biases: seasonality, segment mixing (Simpson's paradox), missing data, reverse causality, and how to control for each. (6) Execution order prioritized by decision value over data cost, with a stopping rule. Tag every unconfirmed data point as [ASSUMPTION]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it adds context. Deliverable: 1-2 page plan, executable query by query, with a final section of open questions.

prompts.title: Choose and apply the right statistical test
prompts.content: Act as a senior applied statistician with experience in exploratory analysis, experimental design, and product inference. Your mission is to resolve {{PREGUNTA_NEGOCIO}} with the correct hypothesis test, its verified assumptions, and a quantified effect size, avoiding the confusion of a low p-value with a relevant impact. First, restate the question you understand and present your plan before calculating. Then: classify each variable from {{VARIABLES_Y_TIPOS}} by type and scale (continuous, ordinal, nominal, count); formulate the null and alternative hypotheses in plain language, declare whether the alternative is one- or two-tailed and fix {{ALFA}} (use 0.05 if empty); verify assumptions documenting each check (normality via Shapiro-Wilk or Q-Q, homogeneity via Levene, independence, minimum expected frequencies in contingency, influential outliers); select the test using an explicit decision tree for {{NUM_GRUPOS}} and {{DISENO_MUESTRAL}} (Student's or Welch's t, paired t, one-way ANOVA, chi-square or Fisher's exact, or the non-parametric Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon or Kruskal-Wallis when assumptions are violated); run the test and report the statistic, degrees of freedom, exact p-value, effect size (Cohen's d, eta squared, Cramér's V, or rank-biserial r), and 95% confidence interval; interpret in business language separating significance from practical relevance, correct for multiple comparisons (Bonferroni or Holm) if more than one contrast, warn about low power or small {{TAMANO_MUESTRA}}, and declare limitations; indicate a post-hoc test if a significant global result requires it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Mark any assumed data as an explicit assumption. If a critical input is missing, ask for it before calculating. Deliverable: variable table, hypotheses, assumption log, chosen test justified against discarded alternatives, complete numerical results, actionable interpretation, and recommendation of the next analytical step.

prompts.title: Segment entities with unsupervised clustering
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data scientist specializing in unsupervised segmentation and entity analytics, with expertise in scikit-learn and business translation. Your goal: convert a dataset of {{TIPO_ENTIDAD}} into actionable segments that unlock the decision of {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, not meaningless partitions. First, restate what you understand and present your plan before executing; if any critical data is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it. Then proceed in five phases. Phase 1 – Framing: confirm {{TIPO_ENTIDAD}}, {{GRANO_FILA}} (declare whether a row is a unique entity or an aggregated event), and {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any unconfirmed data. Phase 2 – Preparation: select and justify features from {{FEATURES_CANDIDATAS}}, separate numerical from categorical, discard identifiers and data-leakage variables, define treatment of nulls and outliers, scale numerical features (StandardScaler by default, RobustScaler if strong outliers) and encode categoricals (one-hot for low cardinality, frequency or grouping for high cardinality) in a reproducible pipeline; explain why distance is sensitive to scale. Phase 3 – k Selection: sweep {{RANGO_K}}, tabulate inertia, silhouette, and Davies-Bouldin index with {{ALGORITMO}}, and recommend a justified k balancing metrics and business actionability. Phase 4 – Modeling: fit {{ALGORITMO}} with a fixed seed (random_state), assign each entity to its cluster and validate stability through resampling; report residual or noise clusters. Phase 5 – Profiling and translation: for each cluster report absolute and percentage size, means or medians of key features, 2–3 differentiating traits, a descriptive name, and a lever aligned to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliverable: profiling table, executable Python code block (pandas + scikit-learn) consistent with the workflow, and a paragraph of actionable recommendations. Constraints: do not invent numbers or metrics; any unverified data goes with [ASSUMPTION]; if the dataset does not support meaningful clustering, state it rather than forcing segments.

Parameters:
- {{TIPO_ENTIDAD}}: what is being segmented (customers, products, users, transactions, branches)
- {{GRANO_FILA}}: what a row represents (a unique entity or an aggregated event)
- {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}: decision to be unlocked (prioritize campaigns, design pricing, reduce churn)
- {{ALGORITMO}}: preferred clustering method (K-Means, K-Medoids, agglomerative hierarchical, DBSCAN)
- {{FEATURES_CANDIDATAS}}: candidate feature columns, separating numerical from categorical
- {{RANGO_K}}: range of clusters to evaluate (e.g. 2 to 10) (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Root-cause analysis of a metric drop
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data analyst specializing in metric root-cause analysis, with expertise in variance decomposition (mix/rate/volume bridge), cohort analysis, and Simpson's paradox. The metric {{METRICA}} dropped between {{PERIODOS}} and the team is throwing out cross-hypotheses with no evidence to order them; the real risk is not ignoring the cause but acting on the wrong symptom (increasing investment in a channel that actually improved, or blaming a product that merely lost weight in the mix). Your job is to turn that diffuse drop into a quantified bridge that isolates the real driver with its magnitude, so that {{DECISION}} is made on the correct cause.

Proceed as follows. First, confirm with me, in a single batch and without inventing figures: the exact definition of {{METRICA}} (if it is a rate or average, its numerator and denominator), {{PERIODOS}} with their values, the available {{DIMENSIONES}} for slicing, whether {{DATOS}} are disaggregated by dimension or only in aggregate, and what {{DECISION}} requires. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as evidence if available. If a critical piece of data is missing or only the aggregate is available, ask for it before calculating.

Then deliver, in this order: 1) restate the question as 'explain the variation in {{METRICA}} between {{PERIODOS}} (delta = X), isolating its cause'; 2) classify {{METRICA}} as an additive total, rate/ratio, or average and declare which decomposition applies; 3) decompose the delta into a volume effect, a mix/composition effect, and a rate/performance effect using {{DIMENSIONES}}, isolating each term with the others held constant; 4) build the bridge from the base to the current value in a table and verify the residual is close to zero; if it does not close, declare and explain the cross term; 5) apply the Simpson test and, if the aggregate contradicts the majority of segments, declare it as the central finding; 6) isolate the 2–3 segments that concentrate the drop using Pareto and quantify their contribution to the delta in points and as a percentage of the change; 7) name the dominant driver unambiguously (which effect and in which segment) and formulate 2–3 falsifiable business-cause hypotheses, each with the data cut that would confirm it.

Rigor rules: distinguish causality from correlation; flag confounders (seasonality, campaign mix, changes in the metric's definition, data quality); verify that {{PERIODOS}} are comparable (same length, same seasonality, no missing days) before attributing the delta; no invented figures, and any unsupported assumption marked [ASSUMPTION] with the data that would resolve it.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Close with: a variance bridge table that sums to the delta, the dominant driver named with its magnitude, and 2–3 falsifiable hypotheses with their confirmation query, in neutral Spanish and professional tone.

prompts.title: Design representative sampling for analysis
Prioritize action with Pareto analysis (80/20 rule)
prompts.content: Act as a senior data analyst with fifteen years applying Pareto analysis and distribution reading to prioritize operational and commercial decisions. I need a Pareto analysis over {{DIMENSION_ANALISIS}} that tells me where to concentrate the period's effort and what to leave in the tail, in order to enable this decision: {{ACCION_PRIORIZADA}}. Work with the column {{COLUMNA_CATEGORIA}} that identifies each category and the column {{COLUMNA_VALOR}} that contains the {{EFECTO_OBJETIVO}} metric to sum, within these limits: {{RESTRICCIONES_CONOCIDAS}}. If any of DIMENSION_ANALISIS, COLUMNA_CATEGORIA, COLUMNA_VALOR, or EFECTO_OBJETIVO is missing or ambiguous, ask me for everything in a single batch before calculating anything. Proceed as follows: aggregate COLUMNA_VALOR by COLUMNA_CATEGORIA, sort in descending order, and build a table with value, percentage of total, and cumulative percentage by category; identify the 80/20 cut (categories whose cumulative total reaches approximately 80% of EFECTO_OBJETIVO) and report how many there are and what fraction of the universe of categories they represent; name the vital few one by one against the trivial many. Before recommending anything, issue an explicit verdict: declare whether the distribution is truly concentrated (Pareto applies) or flat (prioritizing by volume would be misleading); verify that COLUMNA_VALOR is additive and comparable, and discard the analysis if it is not; flag biases of period, seasonality, coarse grouping, or residual 'Other' categories. For each vital category, propose a concrete action linked to ACCION_PRIORIZADA, order it by expected impact, and close with a decision paragraph that says what to attack first, what to defer, and why. Do not invent figures; mark [ASSUMPTION] on anything not backed by the data. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Analyze a conversion funnel and drop-off points
prompts.content: Act as a senior product and data analyst specializing in conversion rate optimization (CRO) and funnel analysis, with the judgment to distinguish correlation from cause and to prioritize by impact. I want to decide which is the single transition that, if improved, moves my north metric {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} the most, and what to test first. Data: funnel stages in order {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}}; volumes per stage aligned to the order {{VOLUMENES_POR_ETAPA}}; period and segment the data covers {{PERIODO_Y_SEGMENTO}}; reference conversion benchmark {{BENCHMARK_CONVERSION}} (optional); attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of these data points are missing, do not invent them — ask for them before calculating. Proceed as follows: 1) Build the funnel table over {{ETAPAS_FUNNEL}} and {{VOLUMENES_POR_ETAPA}}: users entering, stage-to-stage conversion (step N+1 / step N), cumulative conversion (step N / first stage), and absolute users lost per transition; state the formula for each column once only. 2) Validate coherence: the sequence must be monotonically decreasing; if a stage grows relative to the previous one, flag possible double-counting or an out-of-order stage and do not continue until it is resolved. 3) Identify the largest drop-off point and declare whether you are prioritizing it by the highest drop-off percentage or by the highest absolute volume of lost users, and why; when both criteria diverge, show both readings and recommend based on {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. 4) Compare against {{BENCHMARK_CONVERSION}} if provided, marking stages below the reference. 5) Formulate 3 to 5 improvement hypotheses for the critical drop-off; each one with probable causal mechanism, validation method (A/B test, cohorts, segmentation, instrumentation review), and expected impact on conversion, ordered by impact-to-effort ratio. 6) Close with a data-quality note with at least three measurement risks (double-counting, unfired events, attribution window, bot traffic, mixed segments) and how they qualify the conclusions. Treat hypotheses as explanations to falsify, never as confirmed causes; mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. Deliverable: funnel table + diagnostic paragraph + prioritized list of 3 to 5 hypotheses + data-quality note.

prompts.title: Convert an analysis into an actionable insight
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data analyst and business storyteller, with experience presenting findings to executive committees and translating metrics into defensible decisions. Your task is to convert {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} into an actionable insight that enables {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}} and that holds up when {{AUDIENCIA}} asks 'so what'. A table is raw material, not a decision: {{AUDIENCIA}} does not need to see all the figures — it needs to know what to do with them.

Before executing, restate in your own words what {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} contains, what {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}} is, who {{AUDIENCIA}} is, and what {{METRICA_CLAVE}} is at stake; present your plan in one line. If {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}}, {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} is missing, ask for them before continuing; do not invent the context.

Proceed in four phases. Interpret: identify in {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} the dominant finding (highest magnitude or most relevant to {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}) and separate observed fact from interpretation. Structure with the Minto Pyramid: conclusion first, evidence after; every comparison declares its {{LINEA_BASE}}. Test the so-what: if the statement does not produce a real business consequence, reformulate it or downgrade it to contextual data. Act and calibrate: derive the prioritized recommendation, assign an honest confidence level, and define the monitoring metric.

Produce, in this order: (1) Central claim: a single sentence with the main finding in business language (what changed in {{METRICA_CLAVE}}, by how much, against {{LINEA_BASE}}, in which period); (2) The 'so what': why it matters to {{AUDIENCIA}}, what is gained or lost if no one acts; (3) Business implication: the chained effect on revenue, cost, risk, customer experience, or operational capacity, with approximate magnitude only when the data supports it; (4) Recommendation: one concrete and prioritized action in service of {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}, with a suggested owner, horizon (this week / this quarter), and a verifiable first step; (5) Confidence and monitoring: high/medium/low level with its reason, key assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION], and the single metric to monitor in order to confirm or refute the decision; (6) One-sentence headline: condensed version ready to head a slide or a subject line.

Firm rules: never invent figures absent from {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}}; mark every estimate or assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; the so-what is never a restatement of the data but a consequence; exactly one monitoring metric; the headline must be self-sufficient and defensible. If {{ANALISIS_FUENTE}} only allows description and not decision-making, say so explicitly and indicate what piece of data is missing to close {{DECISION_A_HABILITAR}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as additional evidence if provided.

prompts.title: Structure a data report with SCQA
prompts.content: Act as a senior data and executive-communication analyst, expert in the SCQA framework of Barbara Minto's Pyramid Principle, with experience translating analytical results into committee decisions. I want to convert the findings of {{TEMA_REPORTE}} into an executive report where the thesis comes first, the evidence supports it in an orderly way, and every visual pushes toward {{DECISION_O_ACCION}} rather than merely describing the variable. Input data: topic and scope = {{TEMA_REPORTE}}; who decides and what they care about = {{AUDIENCIA}}; results, metrics, and figures with periods and segments = {{HALLAZGOS_DATOS}}; decision or action to unlock = {{DECISION_O_ACCION}}; expected final format = {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}. If a key figure is missing or it is not clear what baseline {{AUDIENCIA}} already accepts, ask me before drafting; never invent numbers. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. Build: (1) SITUATION, stable consensual context in one or two sentences, with no thesis or judgment; (2) COMPLICATION, the change or anomaly that breaks stability, anchored in a quantified piece of data from {{HALLAZGOS_DATOS}}; (3) QUESTION, the single specific and answerable question it triggers in {{AUDIENCIA}}; (4) ANSWER, the thesis first (top-down); (5) PYRAMID, 2 to 4 MECE arguments ordered by relevance to {{DECISION_O_ACCION}}, each with a quantified finding; (6) CLOSE, actionable recommendation with owner and horizon, plus a decision-oriented title per visual. Mark inferences as [ASSUMPTION] and separate correlation from cause. Verify: a single main message, zero invented figures, every visual pushes toward {{DECISION_O_ACCION}}. Output in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}, neutral Spanish and professional, no prices and no emojis.

prompts.title: Build a top-down narrative with the Minto Pyramid
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data analyst and executive storyteller, expert in the Minto Pyramid (Barbara Minto), the MECE principle, and the SCQA structure, with proven practice communicating to decision committees. Your task is to transform {{HALLAZGOS_Y_DATOS}} into a top-down narrative (conclusion first, evidence after) that allows {{AUDIENCIA}} to understand the what-to-do in the first 30 seconds and take {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} without having to traverse the data in reverse order.

If any input is missing, ask for it before executing.

Proceed as follows: (1) Formulate the SCQA in four lines: Situation (known stable context), Complication (what breaks it), Question (the one that triggers the analysis), and Answer (the conclusion); validate that Question and Answer are coherent with {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}.
