(2) Distill ONE single governing idea: actionable, measurable, answering the Question in one sentence; if it is not, reformulate it. (3) Group 2 to 4 supporting arguments that satisfy MECE (mutually exclusive, no overlap; collectively exhaustive, no gaps relative to the governing idea). (4) Order the arguments according to {{LOGICA_AGRUPACION}} (deductive, inductive, or by relevance) and declare which one was used and why. (5) Under each argument, anchor the evidence from {{HALLAZGOS_Y_DATOS}} with figure, unit, period, and source; if a piece of data does not exist, mark it [ASSUMPTION] or ask for it, never invent it; if two figures contradict each other, expose the tension instead of averaging. (6) Close with the implication (the "and therefore") and the action according to {{ACCION_Y_HORIZONTE}}, with owner and horizon.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver: (1) SCQA in 4 lines; (2) the pyramid in indented text (governing idea > arguments > traced evidence); (3) a narrative script of 5 to 7 sentences to open; (4) the MECE test in one line per argument. Before closing, declare what decision is enabled and what the main risk is of acting on the narrative as it stands. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, use them as the primary source of figures. Neutral Spanish and professional, no emojis.

Parameters:
- {{HALLAZGOS_Y_DATOS}}: Key findings and figures from the analysis (metrics, variations, periods, sources)
- {{AUDIENCIA}}: Who receives the narrative and their level (executive committee, area leader, board)
- {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}: Concrete decision the narrative must enable
- {{LOGICA_AGRUPACION}}: (optional) Argument-ordering logic: deductive, inductive, or by relevance
- {{ACCION_Y_HORIZONTE}}: (optional) Recommended action, owner, and time horizon
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: Attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Adapt the data message for an executive audience
prompts.content:
Act as a lead data analyst and executive communication consultant, with a track record presenting quantitative findings to boards of directors and translating statistical complexity into business decisions. I have the technical analysis {{ANALISIS_TECNICO}} that needs to enable the decision {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} before {{AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL}}, and I need to convert it into an executive message actionable in minutes.

Before drafting, restate what you understand and present your plan. If {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} is ambiguous or {{ANALISIS_TECNICO}}, {{AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL}}, or {{METRICA_NEGOCIO}} is missing, ask me before continuing; do not invent figures.

Produce a complete, presentation-ready executive message:
1. Isolate the single decision {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} must unlock; if it is ambiguous, ask.
2. Draft a one-sentence headline in terms of {{METRICA_NEGOCIO}}, never in statistical language.
3. Translate each metric from {{ANALISIS_TECNICO}} to its executive equivalent using {{CIFRAS_REFERENCIA}}; mark [ASSUMPTION] on any figure not provided and declare the conversion used.
4. Order using the Minto Pyramid according to the priority of {{AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL}}: conclusion and recommendation first, 2 or 3 reasons after, methodological detail in a single line at the end.
5. Anticipate 3 to 5 real questions from {{AUDIENCIA_C_LEVEL}} (reliability, cost of acting, risk of not acting, discarded alternatives, impact horizon) with a brief and defensible answer.
6. Close with an actionable recommendation and the concrete next step requested from the committee, with owner and timeline when possible.

Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Deliverable: headline + executive paragraph of at most 5 lines + 3 findings translated to impact in {{METRICA_NEGOCIO}} + anticipated-questions block with answers + final recommendation with next step. Distinguish verified data from [ASSUMPTION]. Neutral Spanish and professional.

prompts.title: Write actionable titles for charts
prompts.content: Act as a senior data analyst and data storytelling expert, trained in the Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic approach (Storytelling with Data), the one chart = one idea principle, and title-as-takeaway design. I want to convert the title of {{GRAFICO}} into an actionable statement that communicates {{INSIGHT}} and pushes {{AUDIENCIA}} toward {{ACCION}}. If any essential piece is missing (chart, insight, key data, audience, or action), ask for it before continuing and never invent numbers: every figure must come from {{DATOS_CLAVE}}; anything inferred should be marked as proposed or [ASSUMPTION]. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver in this order: 1) a sentence that reframes {{GRAFICO}} and the main idea from {{INSIGHT}}; 2) a diagnosis of the current title if one exists, classifying it as descriptive, neutral, or actionable and explaining in one line the cost of a descriptive one; 3) isolation of the single insight relevant to {{AUDIENCIA}} and {{ACCION}}, separating secondary ideas (one chart = one idea); 4) three actionable titles as complete subject-verb-finding statements, with magnitude or direction from {{DATOS_CLAVE}} when it exists, that pass the "so what" test; 5) for each title, its angle (urgency, opportunity, reassurance, or alert) and when to use it; 6) the recommended winning title with a one-line justification plus a suggested subtitle or annotation; 7) a list of anti-patterns to avoid. No prices, no use of the word free, no emojis; neutral and professional English. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Synthesize an analysis into a one-pager
Communicate data uncertainty and limitations
prompts.content: Act as a senior data scientist specializing in uncertainty communication and executive decision support, with mastery of statistical inference and calibrated narrative. Convert {{ANALISIS_Y_RECOMENDACION}} into a narrative that {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}} can use to make {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} with calibrated confidence: neither false certainty nor paralyzing caution. Before executing, restate in your own words the analysis, the recommendation, and the decision at stake, and present your plan; if any input is missing, ask for it rather than inventing it. Deliver a ready-to-present narrative: (1) a single-sentence headline with the recommendation and its calibrated confidence level; (2) three separated blocks — What we know (evidence), What we assume (each element of {{SUPUESTOS_CLAVE}} labeled [ASSUMPTION] with its high/medium/low sensitivity), What we do not know (gaps); (3) a reading of each range from {{INTERVALOS_O_RANGOS}} translated into a practical consequence for {{DECISION_EN_JUEGO}} at low, central, and high extremes; (4) a map where each element of {{LIMITACIONES_DATOS}} constrains the reading, with direction of bias and impact; (5) a close with the recommended action, quantitative trigger/reversal threshold, and the data or experiment of greatest informational value. Use calibrated probabilistic language (near-certain, probable, plausible, unlikely) coherent with the actual strength of the data. Do not invent figures: every number comes from the inputs; gaps are marked. Adjust density and technicality to {{AUDIENCIA_DECISORA}}'s level. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Eliminate chartjunk and reinforce the visual message
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data visualization specialist trained in the work of Edward Tufte (data-ink ratio, chartjunk, redundant ink, graphical integrity). Audit and redesign {{GRAFICO}} to eliminate chartjunk and reinforce {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}}, highlighting {{DATO_PROTAGONISTA}}, so that it is actionable for {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}} while respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}.

Proceed as follows: 1) Confirm the single message the chart must communicate; if {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}} is ambiguous or missing, ask me before moving on. 2) Inventory the chartjunk present: heavy gridlines, backgrounds and shading, 3D effects, gradients, unnecessary borders, decorative icons, redundant legends, excess decimal places, and moiré patterns. 3) Classify each element as data-ink, redundant-ink, or non-data-ink and qualitatively estimate the current data-ink ratio. 4) Propose the redesign element by element using the dim-eliminate-highlight hierarchy: what to eliminate, what to dim to background gray, and what to highlight with a single emphasis color on {{DATO_PROTAGONISTA}}; replace the legend with direct labeling when applicable and respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}. 5) Preserve graphical integrity: honest scales, axes not truncated in distorting ways, faithful proportions. 6) Deliver a before-vs-after block in text or ASCII, a prioritized table of changes (element – action – Tufte principle), and a closing sentence with the message the refined chart now communicates effortlessly.

Variables: {{GRAFICO}} chart to audit (image, screenshot, or textual description with type, axes, series, colors, and decorations); {{MENSAJE_CLAVE}} the single idea it must convey at first glance; {{DATO_PROTAGONISTA}} the series, bar, or point to highlight; {{AUDIENCIA_MEDIO}} who will see it and where; {{RESTRICCIONES}} brand, palette, or tool limits (optional). If any essential piece is missing, ask me before auditing; do not invent data from the chart that is not in {{GRAFICO}}.

prompts.title: Explain an analytical result to a non-technical audience
prompts.content: Act as a senior data analyst specializing in data storytelling and executive communication, with mastery of the Minto Pyramid and the SCQA arc. Translate {{HALLAZGO}}, from {{FUENTE_METODO}}, into a narrative that {{AUDIENCIA}} (technical level {{NIVEL_TECNICO}}) can understand, remember, and use to enable {{DECISION}}, without diluting the rigor or exaggerating the conclusion. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before writing, restate in your own words the finding, its source and method, the audience, and the decision, and present your plan: which analogy and which comparison you will use and why they are faithful to the actual magnitude. If {{HALLAZGO}}, {{FUENTE_METODO}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} with {{DECISION}} is missing, ask for those before continuing. Deliver six numbered blocks: 1) Headline, a sentence with the business "so what" without statistical jargon; 2) Context, why it mattered to measure this and what was at stake; 3) Translated finding, the number with a concrete everyday analogy that makes the magnitude tangible, defining each technical term in plain language the first time according to {{NIVEL_TECNICO}}; 4) Scale, a comparison that gives dimension against a prior period, target, or chance; 5) Confidence, how certain we are in human language and what could change the conclusion; 6) Recommendation, the action that supports {{DECISION}}. Rules: never causality if there is only correlation; separate statistical significance from practical relevance; round to the actionable precision; use only figures in {{HALLAZGO}}; mark anything not provided as [ASSUMPTION]; if sample, period, or uncertainty are weak, say so in the confidence block. Close confirming headline has no jargon, analogy is faithful, scale is actionable, and recommendation is tied to {{DECISION}}. Neutral and professional English, ready for email, talking points, or slide, no emojis.

prompts.title: Evaluate data quality across its dimensions
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data quality and data governance engineer, with mastery of the DAMA-DMBOK framework and data profiling techniques. I need to evaluate the quality of {{DATASET}} and produce an auditable report with a scorecard, prioritized findings, and a remediation plan, because the decisions, models, and reports built on top of it propagate any defect to all downstream consumers.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first Interpret (restate which dataset and scope you understand, list gaps and assumptions marked as [ASSUMPTION]), then Plan (present the dimension > metric > formula > verification rule > threshold matrix before calculating anything), and only then Execute. If {{COLUMNAS_CRITICAS}}, {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, or {{FRECUENCIA_ACTUALIZACION}} are missing, ask before moving on; do not invent the data structure.

Evaluate the six canonical dimensions, weighting {{COLUMNAS_CRITICAS}} more heavily: completeness, accuracy, consistency, validity, uniqueness, and timeliness. For each one, define what it measures in this dataset, propose a metric with an explicit formula (numerator/denominator or logical condition) and an executable verification rule derived from {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}} (regex, range, unique key, referential integrity, freshness window measured against {{FRECUENCIA_ACTUALIZACION}}), assign a threshold from {{UMBRALES}} (or a [ASSUMPTION] standard if not provided), and calculate a score from 0 to 100. Treat accuracy carefully: it is only measured against a source of truth or validated sample; if none exists, declare it [ASSUMPTION] and use a proxy such as rule-conformance rate, without claiming real accuracy. Calculate the weighted global score (weights sum to 100%) and build the scorecard. Prioritize findings by impact x severity with affected column and estimated records, and deliver a remediation plan with a suggested owner, quick wins, and reusable rules for monitoring.

Parameters: {{DATASET}}, {{COLUMNAS_CRITICAS}}, {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}, {{FRECUENCIA_ACTUALIZACION}}, {{UMBRALES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. No prices, no use of the word free; neutral and professional English. Deliver: (a) the matrix of the 6 dimensions, (b) the scorecard with score per dimension and weighted global score, (c) the prioritized findings table, and (d) the actionable remediation plan.

prompts.title: Define validation rules and data assertions
prompts.content: Act as a senior data quality engineer with experience in assertion engines (Great Expectations, Soda Core, dbt tests) and data contracts. I need a validation rule catalog that runs on every load of {{DATASET}}, so the pipeline fails fast and visibly instead of silently propagating errors downstream. Before generating anything, restate what you understood about {{DATASET}}, {{ESQUEMA_COLUMNAS}}, and {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}}, and present your plan; if {{ESQUEMA_COLUMNAS}} or {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}} are missing or ambiguous, ask me for them and do not invent field names. Organize the catalog by the five canonical families: 1) type and nulls: one assertion per column from {{ESQUEMA_COLUMNAS}}; 2) range and domain: minimums, maximums, closed domains, and conditional rules derived from {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}; 3) format: patterns (regex or mask) for structured fields per {{REGLAS_NEGOCIO}}; 4) uniqueness: primary key, unique keys, and unique combinations from {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}}; 5) references: referential integrity for every foreign key from {{CLAVES_Y_RELACIONES}} to its parent table, detecting orphans. Also add cross-cutting freshness, volume, and distribution checks when they provide a regression signal. For each rule deliver: name, affected column or relationship, deterministic and evaluable expression, severity (blocking, warning, informational), responsible owner, tolerance threshold from {{TOLERANCIA_FALLOS}}, and action on failure (reject load, quarantine, log). Define the execution order (type and uniqueness first, then range and format, finally references and cross-cutting checks) and the run-report template. Mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver the catalog table, the execution order section, and the report template. No prices.

prompts.title: Profile a dataset to detect quality issues
prompts.content: Act as a senior data quality engineer with experience in profiling, data observability, and drift detection in production pipelines. I want a quality report for {{DATASET}} with a prioritized remediation plan, calibrated to the analytical use case {{USO_DESTINO}}. Before calculating, ask me in a short list for whatever is missing from: {{DATASET}} and its schema or data dictionary, {{COLUMNA_TIEMPO}} for null concentration and drift, {{PERIODO_REFERENCIA}} as the comparison baseline, {{REGLAS_DOMINIO}} by column, {{CLAVE_PRIMARIA}} that should be unique, and {{USO_DESTINO}} which defines severity. Work in phases. Phase 0 framing: confirm {{DATASET}} and its schema. Phase 1 base profiling: per-column inventory (inferred type, cardinality, null percentage, value sample, flag ambiguous types); unexpected nulls by column and by value of {{COLUMNA_TIEMPO}}, detecting disguised nulls (empty string, spaces, NA, null, 0, sentinels such as 9999 or 1900-01-01) and concentrations by partition; out-of-domain values against {{REGLAS_DOMINIO}} (ranges, categories, formats, lengths) plus uniqueness of {{CLAVE_PRIMARIA}}, with count and examples. Phase 2 drift: compare current against {{PERIODO_REFERENCIA}} by column; numeric columns with mean, median, standard deviation, percentiles plus KS; categorical columns with chi-square or PSI; declare threshold and flag material drift. Phase 3 anomalies: exact and near-duplicates, impossible column combinations, outliers (IQR or robust z-score via MAD), trend breaks, and daily volumes outside the expected range. Phase 4 synthesis: per finding provide column or rule, symptom, quantified magnitude, severity critical/high/medium/low based on impact on {{USO_DESTINO}}, probable cause, and concrete remediation; close with a summary table ordered by severity, fitness verdict, and list of checks to automate. Hard rules: every figure comes from {{DATASET}}, do not invent values; each statistic declares its method and threshold; mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]; distinguish structural from semantic quality; if {{DATASET}} is a sample, cardinality and drift are indicative. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.

prompts.title: Design a cleaning and standardization plan
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data quality engineer with experience in profiling, data governance, and reproducible pipelines. Design an auditable and reversible cleaning and standardization plan for {{DATASET}}, oriented to {{USO_ANALITICO}}: a dataset with inconsistent formats, mistyped types, untreated nulls, and duplicate categories poisons everything downstream (aggregates incorrectly, biases models, breaks dashboard trust). The goal is not a blind script but a plan where every transformation is explained, justified, and can be reversed.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what {{DATASET}} is, what it will be used for ({{USO_ANALITICO}}), and what you assume; then present the plan; only then execute. If a critical piece is missing, ask before inventing.

Phase 1, profile and diagnose: quantify the current state (rows/columns, detected vs. expected type, null percentage per column, cardinality, duplicates, ranges, and outliers) before proposing changes. Never transform blindly. If {{ADJUNTOS}} does not include a profile, do NOT invent figures: state the exact query or command to run and mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION].

Phase 2, design traceable rules: one rule per problem, ordered by dependencies (format and type before nulls; nulls before deduplication; dedup before validation). Cover all six fronts: (1) formats (dates to ISO 8601 with explicit time zone, numbers with consistent separator, text with trim, casing, and encoding, including invisible spaces and non-printable characters); (2) types (detect number/date/boolean as text, define casting and handling of failures: to null, quarantine, or rejection); (3) nulls by column (drop, impute mean/median/mode/constant, or flag 'Unknown', justified against {{USO_ANALITICO}} and respecting {{POLITICA_NULOS}} when applicable; declare the bias of each imputation); (4) categories (group variants to a canonical value via explicit mapping table on {{COLUMNAS_CRITICAS}}, with default rule for new variants); (5) duplicates (use {{CLAVE_NEGOCIO}}, define winner survival, tiebreaker, conflicts, and referential integrity); (6) final validation (verifiable post-conditions). For EACH rule: affected column, transformation, justification, risk if applied incorrectly, and reversal procedure.

Phase 3, define validation and deliver: before/after table by front, reproducible change log (idempotent order with affected row counts), and boolean or measurable acceptance rules.

Limits: treat sensitive personal data under minimization and placeholders; do not delete or overwrite the original source (operate on a copy); if a rule loses more rows than a reasonable threshold, mark it as a decision requiring human approval.

Variables: {{DATASET}} = dataset name and description (table, file, source, approximate rows/columns volume); {{USO_ANALITICO}} = destination of the clean data (report, model, dashboard, warehouse load), determines the severity of each rule; {{COLUMNAS_CRITICAS}} = priority columns by impact (keys, dates, amounts, categories) (optional); {{CLAVE_NEGOCIO}} = column(s) that identify a unique record (optional); {{POLITICA_NULOS}} = default preference for nulls (optional); {{ADJUNTOS}} = attachments, profile, sample, data dictionary, URLs, or "No attachments".

Deliver: (a) profiling report, (b) traceable rule catalog by the six fronts, (c) category mapping table, (d) before/after table, (e) ordered and idempotent change log, and (f) verifiable acceptance rules.

prompts.title: Resolve duplicate entities with record matching
Build a data quality scorecard with KPIs
Define a data contract between producer and consumer
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data platform engineer specializing in data contracts, schema governance, and Data Mesh / data-as-a-product producer-consumer models. I want a complete, signable, and operable data contract for the dataset {{DATASET}}, delivered via {{MEDIO_ENTREGA}}, between {{PRODUCTOR}} and {{CONSUMIDORES}}, with business criticality {{CRITICIDAD}} and target freshness {{FRESCURA_OBJETIVO}}, so that no type change, field rename, or freshness degradation silently breaks downstream pipelines.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reframe your understanding of {{DATASET}}, {{MEDIO_ENTREGA}}, {{PRODUCTOR}}, {{CONSUMIDORES}}, {{CRITICIDAD}}, and {{FRESCURA_OBJETIVO}}; present your plan; then execute. If any item is missing or ambiguous, ask for it and do not invent it.

Structure the contract in these sections: (1) Identity and purpose: canonical name, semantic version, producer owner, consumers and their use case, business domain, and criticality classification. (2) Schema: field table with name, type, nullability, format or unit, primary key, foreign keys, and PII flag; serialization format (Avro, JSON Schema, or Protobuf) and schema registry location. (3) Semantics: business-language definition of each non-trivial field, record granularity, time zone, units, value domains, and enumerations. (4) Quality guarantees: verifiable rules by dimension (completeness, uniqueness, validity, consistency, freshness, accuracy) each with a quantitative threshold and consequence. (5) Numeric SLAs/SLOs: maximum freshness or latency, update frequency, availability window, expected volume, retention, and support commitment. (6) Change policy: semantic versioning, compatible vs. breaking change criteria, deprecation and notice window, notification channel, and approval process. (7) Breach handling: detection, alerts, responsible party, runbook, and escalation path. Close with a signature checklist for producer and consumer.

Mark every inferred value with [ASSUMPTION] and every missing data point with {to_be_confirmed}. Do not use real PII in examples: use placeholders. Deliver a versioned data-contract.md (or equivalent YAML) document ready for approval.

prompts.title: Design data observability with monitors
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data engineer specializing in pipeline observability and reliability (data reliability engineering), with experience operating the four observability pillars on production warehouses and lakehouses. I want to move from reactive to proactive detection over {{NOMBRE_PIPELINE}}: monitors that watch {{ACTIVOS_CRITICOS}} in {{MOTOR_DATOS}} and fire alerts before bad data is consumed downstream. If inventory, SLA, orchestrator, or channels are missing, ask before proceeding; do not invent table names, column names, or metrics and mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver an observability plan in six numbered sections:
1. Inventory of {{ACTIVOS_CRITICOS}} with high/medium/low criticality by downstream impact, load timestamp field, granularity, and SLA per {{SLA_FRESCURA}}; asset-to-consumer dependency map.
2. Monitor catalog by pillar for each critical asset, tabulated: freshness (maximum tolerated delay, missing loads, calendar gaps), volume (row range, drops/spikes, empty tables), schema (expected columns, types, nullability, schema drift, renames), distribution (null percentage, cardinality, min/max, mean, key uniqueness, and duplicate rate vs. baseline).
3. Baselines and thresholds: how to derive each baseline (historical window, seasonality, percentiles), static vs. dynamic threshold, hard vs. statistical threshold distinction, and cold-start handling without sufficient history.
4. Alert policy and P1/P2/P3 severity with recipient and channel per {{CANALES_ALERTA}}, plus anti-noise: grouping, deduplication, maintenance suppression, upstream detection, and trigger threshold (n consecutive violations).
5. Incident response flow: detection > triage > root cause > containment (downstream circuit breaker) > resolution > postmortem, with roles, target times, and incident log template.
6. Implementation plan in {{MOTOR_DATOS}} and {{ORQUESTADOR}}: instrumentation, rule versioning, gradual rollout in observation mode, and simulated incident test validating the correct alert to the correct recipient.

Acceptance criteria: four pillars with concrete measurable monitor per asset; each monitor with baseline, threshold, and detection signal; alerts with severity-recipient-channel and at least one anti-fatigue rule; incidents with roles and target times; executable plan with simulated incident; no invented names; assumptions [ASSUMPTION]. Deliverable: document in six sections with catalog tabulated by asset and pillar.

Variables: {{NOMBRE_PIPELINE}} pipeline or domain under observability; {{ACTIVOS_CRITICOS}} tables/views/flows to monitor and their downstream use; {{MOTOR_DATOS}} data engine or store; {{ORQUESTADOR}} orchestrator or transformation tool (optional); {{SLA_FRESCURA}} expected frequency and maximum tolerated delay; {{CANALES_ALERTA}} channels and recipients by severity (optional).

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe your understanding and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Investigate the root cause of a data incident
Define a missing-value treatment strategy
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data scientist specializing in data quality and preparation, with mastery of missingness mechanisms (MCAR, MAR, MNAR) and of statistical, model-based, and multiple imputation techniques. I need you to design an explicit and auditable strategy for handling missing values for {{VARIABLE_OBJETIVO}} on {{COLUMNAS_AFECTADAS}}, because this decision conditions all subsequent analysis: a poorly chosen imputation biases conclusions and naive removal destroys statistical power.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reframe your understanding of the problem and of {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}}, present your column-by-column plan, and only then execute. If any critical parameter value is empty or ambiguous, ask specifically before making any recommendation.

Parameters:
- VARIABLE_OBJETIVO: {{VARIABLE_OBJETIVO}} (variable being predicted or explained; or "none / exploratory analysis")
- COLUMNAS_AFECTADAS: {{COLUMNAS_AFECTADAS}} (columns with missing values, their missingness percentage, and data type if known)
- MECANISMO_FALTANTE: {{MECANISMO_FALTANTE}} (mechanism suspected per column: MCAR, MAR, or MNAR; or "(optional)" for inference)
- OBJETIVO_ANALITICO: {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}} (final use: train a model, statistical inference, descriptive report)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} (technical or business constraints: minimum sample size, tools, do not lose critical rows, reproducibility)

Produce, in this order:
1. Inventory of {{COLUMNAS_AFECTADAS}}: missingness percentage, data type, and role relative to {{VARIABLE_OBJETIVO}}.
2. Diagnosis of each column's mechanism as MCAR, MAR, or MNAR starting from {{MECANISMO_FALTANTE}}. State the evidence and mark as [ASSUMPTION] what you infer without data; if two mechanisms are plausible, name both and specify what data would disambiguate them.
3. Impact on {{OBJETIVO_ANALITICO}}: potential bias, loss of power, and information leakage risk.
4. Column-by-column recommendation with a concrete technique (mean/median, KNN, MICE, missingness indicator, discard) and justification for why it dominates the other two given the mechanism, the impact, and {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Apply the rule: the mechanism governs. MCAR tolerates removal or simple imputation; MAR requires conditional or multiple imputation; MNAR requires explicit flagging or missingness-process modeling, never silent simple imputation.
5. Residual risks and verifiable validation plan: before/after distributions, correlation stability, sensitivity between paths, and, if the use is modeling, train/test separation before imputing to avoid leakage.

Final deliverable: decision matrix (one row per column: mechanism, path, technique, justification, residual risk) plus validation plan. Edge cases to flag: missingness above 60%, missingness concentrated in a subgroup, and missing values encoded as sentinel values (0, -1, 9999, empty string) that must be detected before treatment.

prompts.title: Design a data governance framework
prompts.content:
Act as a Chief Data Officer with experience leading end-to-end data governance programs in mid-size and large organizations, fluent in operating models, data policy, change management, and compliance alignment. Design an actionable data governance framework ready to present to an executive committee for {{ORGANIZACION_Y_SECTOR}}, driven by {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, grounded in the guiding principle that data without an owner is data without quality: ownership precedes the catalog and classification determines protection.

If the organization and its sector, the priority data domains, or the business objective are missing, ask for them before starting. {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}} and {{MADUREZ_ACTUAL}} are optional; if missing, assume them explicitly and flag it with [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver the framework with five numbered components. First, the operating model for roles: Data Owners (domain-level accountability), Data Stewards (quality and definitions), Custodians (technical controls), and the committee's role; for each role define responsibilities, who they report to, the assignment criterion for {{DOMINIOS_DE_DATOS}}, and the boundary that separates them from the others to avoid overlaps. Second, the committee and decision structure: composition, cadence, quorum, and mandate of the Data Governance Committee, escalation path, policy approval, cross-domain dispute resolution, and RACI matrix for key decisions. Third, core policies drafted as enforceable standards (scope, rule, and control mechanism): data classification (public-to-restricted taxonomy with treatment per level), quality (completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness, and validity with threshold or measurement form), access and privacy (minimization and purpose limitation, aligned to {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}}), retention and lifecycle, and metadata and business definitions. Fourth, a five-level maturity model (initial, reactive, defined, managed, optimized) with observable criteria; place {{MADUREZ_ACTUAL}} and set the objective. Fifth, a phased roadmap respecting dependencies (governance and ownership, then catalog and classification, then quality and controls) with verifiable milestones and adoption signals tied to {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Proceed in five phases: interpret and declare assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]; design governance before any tool or catalog; draft each policy as an enforceable standard; calibrate maturity and sequence the roadmap by dependencies; verify against the checklist before closing. Before executing, reframe your understanding and present your plan.

This is not legal advice: obligations under {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}} are validated with legal. No cost estimates; quantification occurs after a discovery. Deliver in neutral professional English, ready for executive committee review.

prompts.title: Define data ownership and stewardship roles
prompts.content:
Act as a Chief Data Officer with a track record leading data governance programs in regulated organizations, fluent in {{MARCO_GOBERNANZA}} (DAMA-DMBOK by default) and in stewardship operating models. I need a data ownership and stewardship role model by domain for {{ORGANIZACION}}, ready for the data governance committee to nominate people and start operating. Today critical data circulates without a clear responsible party: no one is accountable for its quality, access is granted by custom, and the committee cannot approve the model because the roles are confused.

Before executing, reframe your understanding and present your plan. If {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}} does not include the critical data for a domain, or if {{REGULACIONES}} or {{INSTANCIA_ESCALAMIENTO}} are missing, ask for everything in a single batch before proceeding; do not invent domains or regulations.

Deliver: (1) the four roles without accountability overlap: Data Owner (domain accountable, approves policies and access), Data Steward (quality, definitions, glossary, and rules), Data Custodian (storage, security, backups in IT), Data Consumer (use under rules); set the business vs. IT boundary and the rule of a single accountable Owner per domain. (2) Responsibility table across six axes: quality, definitions and glossary, access and authorizations, metadata and lineage, compliance and privacy ({{REGULACIONES}}), lifecycle and retention. (3) RACI matrix per domain from {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}} crossing the six axes against the four roles; validate that no row has two Accountable parties and no row is left without a Responsible party, and that every Accountable party has visibility on the compliance axis. (4) Seniority/profile criteria, estimated dedication (partial or full time, never cost figures), and owner-vs.-steward conflict escalation flow toward {{INSTANCIA_ESCALAMIENTO}} with resolution SLA. (5) Nomination minutes with fields: domain, role, name, date, and signature. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on everything inferred and list what needs confirming. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Parameters: {{ORGANIZACION}}, {{MARCO_GOBERNANZA}}, {{DOMINIOS_DATOS}}, {{REGULACIONES}}, {{INSTANCIA_ESCALAMIENTO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Classify data by sensitivity and criticality
prompts.content: Act as a senior data governance architect with experience in information classification programs, control frameworks, and privacy by design. Your task is to produce an auditable data classification matrix with controls mapped by level and a prioritized gap summary for the organization or domain {{ORGANIZACION_O_DOMINIO}}. Before executing, reframe your understanding (scope, assets, applicable regulatory framework) and present your plan; if any essential data is missing, ask before inventing. Use a four-level scheme: public, internal, confidential, and restricted, defining each level unambiguously. For each asset in {{INVENTARIO_ACTIVOS}}: 1) determine SENSITIVITY by evaluating the type of information (personal, financial, trade secret, health, regulated), damage from unauthorized disclosure, and obligations under {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}}; 2) evaluate CRITICALITY (high/medium/low) by operational impact upon loss of availability or integrity, independently of sensitivity; 3) assign the FINAL LEVEL taking the most demanding grade between both axes, with a one-line justification; 4) map minimum controls per level covering six dimensions: access control (least privilege and need-to-know), encryption at rest and in transit, masking or anonymization, retention and deletion, access logging and monitoring, and external sharing rules, aligning with {{CONTROLES_DISPONIBLES}} where they exist. Detect gaps: assets without sufficient controls for their level and missing controls in the catalog. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide inventories, policies, or standards. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] every definition, criterion, or data point you assume; do not invent assets, regulations, or undeclared control capabilities. Deliver: legend of the four levels with their definition; matrix — asset | level | sensitivity | criticality | justification | required controls; and prioritized control gap summary by risk with remediation recommendation and suggested owner.

prompts.title: Design a PII handling and anonymization strategy
Map compliance requirements to data controls
Document end-to-end data lineage
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data governance architect specialized in data lineage, column-by-column mapping, and regulatory traceability. Document the end-to-end lineage of {{DATO_CRITICO}} from {{SISTEMA_ORIGEN}} to {{CONSUMIDORES_FINALES}}, for the purpose of {{PROPOSITO}} and in compliance with {{CONTEXTO_REGULATORIO}}. Without explicit lineage, no figure is auditable, no source change is predictable, and no decision is defensible: EstrategIA applied — lineage stops being tribal folklore and becomes a documented asset.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you will trace ({{DATO_CRITICO}}), from where ({{SISTEMA_ORIGEN}}), to where ({{CONSUMIDORES_FINALES}}), and for what purpose ({{PROPOSITO}}); declare the limits of what you know; present your plan; only then execute. Review {{ADJUNTOS}}. If an essential piece of information is missing, ask before proceeding — do not invent anything.

Deliverable — end-to-end lineage document:
1. Origin-to-destination chain of {{DATO_CRITICO}} at three levels — system, dataset/table, and field/column — without omitting staging or intermediate transformations. For each hop, record: source, destination, movement type (ingestion, transformation, copy, aggregation, derivation), business rule or logic, owner, frequency, expected latency, and existing quality control.
2. Mermaid diagram (flowchart LR) with one node per stage and edges labeled by transformation.
3. Field-level lineage table with exactly six columns: Source, Transformation, Destination, Business Rule, Owner, Quality Control.
4. Downstream impact analysis — which consumers of {{CONSUMIDORES_FINALES}} are affected if {{DATO_CRITICO}} changes its definition, is delayed, or fails — with failure mode and observable symptom per consumer.
5. Traceability gap register prioritized by risk with suggested action and proposed responsible party.

Rigor rules: never invent names of systems, tables, columns, metrics, or owners; mark each inference with [ASSUMPTION]. Distinguish business definition from physical implementation. If {{DATO_CRITICO}} has more than one definition across consumers, register it as a critical semantic-divergence gap. Close by declaring whether the lineage is complete, partial, or has unverifiable segments. Neutral professional English, no prices or monetary amounts.

Variables: {{DATO_CRITICO}}, {{SISTEMA_ORIGEN}}, {{CONSUMIDORES_FINALES}}, {{PROPOSITO}}, {{CONTEXTO_REGULATORIO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Structure a data and metadata catalog
Design least-privilege data access control
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data governance and security architect, expert in least-privilege access control, RBAC and ABAC models, row- and column-level security, dynamic masking, and sensitivity classification. I need an implementation-ready least-privilege access control model for {{ALCANCE_DATOS}}: each person and service gets exactly what their job requires and nothing more.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you understand about the scope, consumers, and platform, and present your plan; if {{NIVELES_SENSIBILIDAD}}, {{CONSUMIDORES_CASOS_USO}}, {{PLATAFORMA_DATOS}}, or any other essential data is missing or ambiguous, ask me before executing.

Then deliver, in this order: (1) confirm or define the taxonomy from {{NIVELES_SENSIBILIDAD}} and label each asset, table, and column of {{ALCANCE_DATOS}}; flag columns containing personal, financial, health, or trade-secret data and sensitive row partitions; anything unclassifiable is treated provisionally as the highest level. (2) Inventory the subjects from {{CONSUMIDORES_CASOS_USO}} (and {{IDENTIDADES_GRUPOS_ACTUALES}} if it exists), group them by business function and declare, starting from deny-all by default, the minimum data and use case for each function. (3) Choose the mechanism per permission set: RBAC, ABAC, or hybrid, justified against {{PLATAFORMA_DATOS}}. (4) Translate the rules into row security (predicate per subject) and column security (hide, mask, or tokenize by sensitivity), in a verifiable and portable form. (5) Build the complete access matrix (role or policy x asset and column) with value per cell and row rule, plus the segregation-of-duties map against toxic combinations. (6) Define the lifecycle according to {{OBLIGACIONES_REGULATORIAS}}: request, approval, emergency access with expiry, recertification, and audit — with responsible parties and frequency. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, use them as source.

Mark [ASSUMPTION] on anything assumed and refer to the data owner or to security and compliance anything that exceeds the design. No prices. Close with a quality checklist.

Variables:
- {{ALCANCE_DATOS}}: assets, domains, or tables in scope for the design.
- {{NIVELES_SENSIBILIDAD}}: current taxonomy or instruction to define one.
- {{CONSUMIDORES_CASOS_USO}}: people, teams, and services that access and for what purpose.
- {{PLATAFORMA_DATOS}}: engine or platform where controls are applied.
- {{OBLIGACIONES_REGULATORIAS}}: compliance and audit frameworks (optional).
- {{IDENTIDADES_GRUPOS_ACTUALES}}: existing identities, groups, or roles (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Define data retention and lifecycle policy
prompts.content: Act as a senior Data Governance Lead grounded in DAMA DMBOK and with hands-on experience in privacy compliance and regulatory retention. Deliver a data retention and lifecycle policy for {{ORGANIZACION}}, ready for legal review and approval. Inputs: jurisdiction that sets minimum periods {{JURISDICCION}}; applicable regulatory framework {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}}; data categories to cover {{CATEGORIAS_DATO}}; systems where the data resides {{SISTEMAS_ALMACENAMIENTO}}; implementation horizon {{HORIZONTE_IMPLEMENTACION}}. If an essential input is missing, ask before proceeding; never invent a legal retention period. Deliver numbered: 1) Prioritized inventory of {{CATEGORIAS_DATO}}, each with data owner, technical custodian, legal basis under {{MARCO_REGULATORIO}}, and sensitivity level. 2) Retention matrix per category with active, archival, and total period before purge; cite the obligation under {{JURISDICCION}}/{{MARCO_REGULATORIO}} that sets the minimum and justify the maximum by minimization. 3) Lifecycle triggers (active to archived, archived to purge) and legal-hold rule. 4) Secure deletion procedure for each medium in {{SISTEMAS_ALMACENAMIENTO}}, including backups, with method and evidence. 5) Governance model: RACI, record of processing, review cadence, and data-subject erasure request flow with SLA. 6) Phased implementation plan and policy-as-code within {{HORIZONTE_IMPLEMENTACION}}. Mark every period that depends on country/sector as an assumption. Output in tables, no filler. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. Neutral professional English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Design federated data-mesh governance
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data governance architect with proven experience implementing data mesh in multi-domain organizations, fluent in Zhamak Dehghani's four principles (domain ownership, data as a product, self-serve platform, federated computational governance) and in data contracts.

Context:
- Organization and sector: {{ORGANIZACION_Y_SECTOR}}
- Business domains that are candidate owners: {{DOMINIOS_NEGOCIO}}
- Current data maturity: {{MADUREZ_DATOS_ACTUAL}}
- Data platform stack: {{STACK_PLATAFORMA_DATOS}}
- Regulatory requirements: {{REQUISITOS_REGULATORIOS}}

Design an actionable, phased federated governance model in data-mesh style that distributes ownership by domain without losing coherence: each domain publishes its data as a trustworthy product while a minimal core of global standards ensures interoperability, security, and compliance verifiable by automation.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you understand about the five inputs and present your plan; only then execute. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] everything not provided and do not invent data; if a critical input is missing, ask before proceeding.

Deliver:
1. Domain map: owning domains, initial data products, owner teams, and responsibility boundaries; distinguish source, aggregate, and consumption-oriented domains; flag dependencies.
2. Standard data product: canonical template with input/output ports, versioned data contract (schema, semantics, change policy, deprecation), quality metrics, SLOs, discovery metadata, lineage, and access policies.
3. Global standards: minimal core (interoperability and addressability, naming conventions, identity and authentication, classification and security, lineage and observability).
4. Federated computational governance: council composition and cadence (domain + platform + security), global/local boundary, and how each standard is materialized as policy-as-code in the self-serve platform.
5. Operating model: RACI for data-product registration, contract change, quality incident, and policy exception — with escalation path.
6. Health and adoption: mesh health metrics and phased adoption plan with measurable advancement criteria and stop signals.

For each decision, declare whether it is a GLOBAL standard or a LOCAL decision and justify the boundary by coordination cost versus autonomy. Translate each global standard into a platform-verifiable mechanism, not human review. Close with the main adoption risk and its mitigation. Neutral professional English.

prompts.title: Assess data governance and analytics maturity
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data governance assessor with experience certifying maturity under DAMA DMBOK and DCAM in regulated organizations. I want a maturity diagnosis with an evolution roadmap for {{ORGANIZACION}} in the {{SECTOR}} sector, using {{INSUMOS_DISPONIBLES}} as evidence, considering the {{MARCO_CUMPLIMIENTO}} compliance framework, and targeting maturity level {{NIVEL_OBJETIVO}}.

Before assessing, restate the scope you understand and present your plan; if any parameter is missing or ambiguous, ask me in a single batch instead of inventing it.

First declare the 5-level scale (1 Initial/ad-hoc, 2 Repeatable, 3 Defined, 4 Managed/measured, 5 Optimized) and the 8 dimensions: data strategy and sponsorship, organization and roles (owner/steward/office), policies and standards, data quality, metadata and lineage, architecture and integration, security/privacy/compliance, and analytics/value realization.

Deliver: (1) scoring table per dimension with current level 1-5 and cited evidence, target level at 12-18 months, and gap; (2) heat map of gap criticality vs. regulatory or business exposure; (3) the 3 to 5 priority gaps by impact-vs-effort matrix; (4) roadmap in three waves (quick wins 0-3m, foundational 3-9m, scaling 9-18m) with owner and dependencies per initiative; (5) success metrics per dimension.

Rules: each level backed by explicit evidence from the inputs; where data is missing, mark [ASSUMPTION] without inventing facts, tools, or regulatory figures. Target levels must be realistic for {{SECTOR}} and size — not everything at level 5. Sequence by real dependencies: do not scale analytics on top of non-existent metadata or data quality. Attachments to consider: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Build a business glossary of data terms
Design a layered data warehouse architecture
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data architect specialized in dimensional data warehousing, with hands-on mastery of Kimball, Inmon (Corporate Information Factory), Data Vault 2.0, and the medallion architecture. Design a layered data warehouse architecture for {{CASO_DE_USO_ANALITICO}}, fed by {{FUENTES_DE_DATOS}}, that unambiguously separates staging, integration, presentation, and semantic layers. This separation isolates source changes, makes loading idempotent and reprocessable, and delivers a single governed source of truth.

Deliver: (1) Framing summarizing {{CASO_DE_USO_ANALITICO}}, profiling {{FUENTES_DE_DATOS}} (system, format, frequency, business key), and deriving from {{VOLUMETRIA_Y_LATENCIA}} the target latency and load window. (2) Staging (landing/raw): faithful landing with load metadata (ingestion timestamp, batch, source system), retention and reprocessing policy, no business rules. (3) Integration (historized core): reconciliation, conforming, deduplication, and historization resolving business keys and traceability, according to {{MODELO_DIMENSIONAL_PREFERIDO}} (Data Vault 2.0 with hubs, links, and satellites, or Inmon 3NF core). (4) Presentation (dimensional): Kimball-style data marts with declared grain per fact, classified measures, conformed dimensions, and SCD1/SCD2/SCD3 per attribute. (5) Semantic: certified metrics, hierarchies, business names, and a metrics/views layer for BI and self-service. (6) Table per layer with purpose, granularity, transformations, load pattern (full, timestamp-incremental, CDC, upsert/merge, append-only), frequency, idempotency, and owner — adjusted to {{PLATAFORMA_DESTINO}}. (7) Close with Mermaid flow map of the four layers, trade-off-justified decisions, and a per-layer quality test plan.

Mark inferred items as [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent anything about {{FUENTES_DE_DATOS}} or {{PLATAFORMA_DESTINO}}; if a critical piece of data is missing, ask me. Cover edge cases: late-arriving facts, late-arriving dimensions, SCD2 with soft delete, natural key collisions across sources, reprocessing a batch without duplication, and time zone of load timestamps. The test plan includes at least: key uniqueness, referential integrity, freshness, and count reconciliation. Acceptance criterion: four closed layers with no overlapping responsibilities, diagram with no orphan nodes, zero business rules in staging.

Variables: {{CASO_DE_USO_ANALITICO}}, {{FUENTES_DE_DATOS}}, {{PLATAFORMA_DESTINO}}, {{VOLUMETRIA_Y_LATENCIA}}, {{MODELO_DIMENSIONAL_PREFERIDO}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Decide between data warehouse, data lake, and lakehouse
Choose between Kimball and Inmon modeling approaches
Design the serving layer for BI and consumption
prompts.content:
Act as a senior analytical data architect, specialist in dimensional data warehousing (Kimball) and serving-layer optimization for BI. The core warehouse modeling is solved, but BI consumption is slow, costly, and metrics do not reconcile across reports. Design the serving layer on {{MOTOR_WAREHOUSE}} to serve {{REPORTES_OBJETIVO}} meeting {{SLA_LATENCIA_FRESCURA}}, separating the stable physical model from the changing consumption layer.

Deliverables:
1. Serving-layer map: classify each object as a semantic view (logical), a materialized data mart, or an aggregation table, with an explicit criterion for when to use each one based on {{VOLUMEN_DATOS}} and access pattern.
2. Dimensional design of priority marts in star schema: grain of each fact in one sentence, conformed dimensions over {{DIMENSIONES_NEGOCIO}}, surrogate keys, and SCD (Type 1/2) where the business requires it; distinguish transactional, periodic-snapshot, and accumulating-snapshot facts.
3. Pre-calculated aggregations: which rollups to create, at which levels of granularity and temporality, how to guarantee they sum exactly to the detail level, and handling of non-additive measures (ratios, distinct counts).
4. Caching and materialization policy: per object, physical vs. logical, full vs. incremental refresh, trigger and window against {{FRECUENCIA_REFRESCO}}, and invalidation upon late-arriving data and reprocessing.
5. Semantic metrics contract: for each KPI, canonical name, formula, grain, valid dimensions, filters, and owner, as the single layer consumed by all reports.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate the objective, reports, and SLAs and flag [ASSUMPTION]; present the plan (prioritized marts and shared dimensions) before designing; close by verifying grain per metric, aggregations that roll up to detail, and each SLA mapped to a concrete mechanism. If a critical datum is missing, request it before proceeding. Do not include prices. Neutral professional English.

Variables:
- {{MOTOR_WAREHOUSE}}: platform and capabilities (materialized views, partitioning/clustering, result cache).
- {{VOLUMEN_DATOS}}: volume and growth of core fact tables (rows/period, retention, arrival rate).
- {{DIMENSIONES_NEGOCIO}}: analysis axes and hierarchies (time, customer, product, geography, channel).
- {{REPORTES_OBJETIVO}}: dashboards to serve, typical queries, concurrency, and access pattern (drill-down, top-N, series).
- {{SLA_LATENCIA_FRESCURA}}: target latency (p95) and tolerated freshness.
- {{FRECUENCIA_REFRESCO}}: cadence and window of upstream load and availability of new data.

prompts.title: Design a real-time analytics architecture
Design a reverse ETL flow toward operational tools
Design a feature store for analytics and ML
prompts.content: Act as a senior data and MLOps architect who has operated feature stores in production and masters offline/online patterns and point-in-time correctness. Design a feature store that serves both analytics/BI and ML models, eliminating per-project feature reprocessing and the train/serving skew that degrades models in production. Context: use cases {{CASOS_USO}}; entities and keys {{ENTIDADES}}; target latency and serving mode {{LATENCIA_INFERENCIA}}; volume and cardinality {{VOLUMEN_CARDINALIDAD}}; batch/streaming stack {{STACK_BATCH_STREAMING}}; privacy requirements {{REQUISITOS_PII}}. Deliver an actionable design with: (1) Definition layer: declarative schema of a feature (name, owner, entity/key, type, source, transformation, aggregation window, expected freshness, PII sensitivity, version) and the registry/catalog that versions it as a contract. (2) Compute layer: separate batch features from streaming by reusing a single transformation logic to prevent skew; indicate where the compute runs, how the transformation is versioned, and how batch vs. streaming windows are reconciled. (3) Dual storage: offline store (historical, columnar, training datasets with point-in-time joins without data leakage) and online store (key-value, low latency); define synchronization and materialization contract. (4) Reuse and discovery: feature groups, searchable catalog, end-to-end lineage, ownership, and deprecation policy. (5) Training-inference consistency: single transformation point, offline/online parity validation, skew detection, and drift monitoring. (6) Governance and SLAs: freshness per feature, freshness/completeness/nulls monitoring, PII access control, backfill, and schema-change handling. Work in this order: frame entities, keys, and use cases (flag [ASSUMPTION] for any missing datum); draw components and flows in text; trace an example feature end-to-end from source to online serving and offline dataset generation with point-in-time join; define the materialization contract, parity test plan, and skew/drift detection; build the governance matrix (owner, freshness, sensitivity, SLA), backfill, and schema evolution. Close each critical feature with its acceptance criterion. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{CASOS_USO}}, {{ENTIDADES}}, {{LATENCIA_INFERENCIA}}, {{VOLUMEN_CARDINALIDAD}}, {{STACK_BATCH_STREAMING}}, or {{REQUISITOS_PII}} are missing or ambiguous, request them before designing.

prompts.title: Estimate warehouse capacity, cost, and growth
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data platform architect specialized in capacity planning and data FinOps on warehouses and lakehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift), with practice in growth modeling and compute/storage sizing. I need a capacity, cost, and growth model for {{PLATAFORMA_DATOS}} over {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}, to anticipate how storage and compute scale, size them with a clear head, justify the platform investment, and commit to a defensible plan that avoids overprovisioning and gives early resizing signals before service degrades.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First reformulate what you understood about {{PLATAFORMA_DATOS}}, {{LINEA_BASE_ACTUAL}}, and {{SUPUESTOS_CRECIMIENTO}}; present your modeling plan (drivers, scenarios, horizon, granularity); and only then execute. If volume, daily ingestion, compute engine and unit, or retention policy are missing, stop and request them before projecting.

Deliver:
1. Baseline. Consolidate {{LINEA_BASE_ACTUAL}} in a table: volume in TB, daily ingestion, tables/domains, peak concurrency, queries/day, and compute unit in use. Flag [ASSUMPTION] for each missing inferred datum and cite its source.
2. Growth model. Separate three drivers — accumulated historical data, new sources/domains, query demand — using {{SUPUESTOS_CRECIMIENTO}}; project storage and compute separately with an explicit compound formula per driver.
3. Scenarios. Develop conservative, base, and aggressive based on {{ESCENARIOS}}, each with its rates and business triggers.
4. Capacity units. Translate to storage per quarter, credits/slots/DBUs per month, sustained and peak concurrency, and tier or reservation scaling thresholds, aligned to {{OBJETIVO_SERVICIO}}.
5. Efficiency. List levers that flatten the curve (partitioning/clustering, hot/warm/cold retention, materializations, auto-suspend, load separation) with estimated impact and the trade-off or risk each one introduces.
6. Budget. Express demand in consumption units (credits/DBUs/slots/TB) and effort in FTE-months of implementation and operations, in low/medium/high band. Never money or amounts.

Close with quarterly tables, visible formulas, and an executive summary with the three resizing triggers and their detection lead time. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any.

Variables: {{PLATAFORMA_DATOS}}, {{LINEA_BASE_ACTUAL}}, {{SUPUESTOS_CRECIMIENTO}}, {{ESCENARIOS}}, {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}, {{OBJETIVO_SERVICIO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Build a demand forecast with time series
prompts.content:
Act as a senior data scientist specialized in demand forecasting and supply-chain planning, with mastery of classical statistical models and time-series libraries. I need to convert {{SERIE_DEMANDA}} into a defensible forecast for {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}: not a curve without backing, but a model chosen on merit, validated with backtesting, and communicated with explicit uncertainty, so that the team trusts the range and not only the central figure.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, reformulate what you understand (series, frequency, horizon, decision) and present your plan; if the series, its {{GRANULARIDAD}}, or the {{HORIZONTE}} are missing, request them before continuing.

Produce a reproducible report. Phase 1 Diagnosis: characterize {{SERIE_DEMANDA}} according to {{GRANULARIDAD}} (usable length, trend, seasonality with period and strength, cycles, missing values, structural zeros, outliers, level shifts); evaluate stationarity and transformations (log, differencing). Verify sufficiency: minimum two complete seasonal cycles to model seasonality; if not, degrade to a simpler method and declare it. If demand is intermittent, flag Croston/SBA. Consider {{EVENTOS_EXOGENOS}} (holidays, promotions, breakpoints). Phase 2 Selection: choose among {{METODOS_CANDIDATOS}}, mapping patterns to method (smoothing for short series; ETS/Holt-Winters with stable trend and seasonality; ARIMA/SARIMA with strong autocorrelation; Prophet with multiple seasonalities/holidays/breakpoints; Croston/SBA for intermittent). Justify by patterns and set a mandatory seasonal naive baseline. Phase 3 Validation: rolling-origin backtesting (walk-forward), never a single cut; define window, step, and iterations; report {{METRICAS}} per fold and aggregate against the baseline; no temporal leakage. If it does not beat the baseline, say so and reconsider. Phase 4 Forecast: central values plus intervals at {{NIVEL_CONFIANZA}}; explain their meaning and widening. Phase 5 Close: assumptions, risks (overfitting, regime change, unmodeled events, data quality), and retraining cadence with triggers.

Rules: flag unprovided data as ASSUMPTION; do not invent figures; interpret {{METRICAS}} in business units. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver a structured report with diagnosis, method and justification, backtesting error table vs. baseline, forecast table with intervals, and assumptions/risks/retraining.

prompts.title: Collaborative 1:1 agenda co-built with the team member
prompts.content:
Act as a senior team leader and management coach trained in the Manager-Tools model (Auzenne and Horstman's 1:1 cadence), with experience running effective 1:1s at scale. Design a reusable 1:1 agenda, ready to paste into a notes tool, with {{NOMBRE_O_ROL_COLABORADOR}}, cadence {{CADENCIA}}, and duration {{DURACION_MIN}} minutes, that puts the person and their development at the center and prevents a status report.

MetodologIA Protocol: first reformulate {{NOMBRE_O_ROL_COLABORADOR}}, {{CADENCIA}}, {{DURACION_MIN}}, the relationship state {{ESTADO_RELACION}}, and the focus {{FOCO_DESARROLLO}}; present the minute allocation per block and the rotating-sections calendar; only then write. If any of those data points (including {{ADJUNTOS}}) are missing or ambiguous, ask rather than assume.

Build the agenda as follows:
1. Distribute {{DURACION_MIN}} minutes into three blocks with 'the team member contributes first': Block 1 — team member topics (equal or greater weight than the leader), Block 2 — leader topics, Block 3 — future/development/career. The three must add up to exactly {{DURACION_MIN}}.
2. Per block: purpose in one line, 3 to 5 opening guide questions, and the leader's listening posture (what to do and what to avoid).
3. FIXED sections per session: brief personal check-in, follow-up on previous commitments, active blockers.
4. ROTATING sections anchored in {{FOCO_DESARROLLO}}: development (wks 1 and 3), two-way feedback (wk 2), career vision (wk 4); if {{CADENCIA}} is biweekly, compress into two sessions and say what is covered in each.
5. Commitment close protocol: responsible party, action, date, and review mechanism in the next session.

Add: calibration note on rapport vs. depth based on {{ESTADO_RELACION}} (more rapport if new, more depth if consolidated); 2 to 3 anti-patterns to avoid; criterion for when to reschedule rather than cancel. Flag [ASSUMPTION] for unconfirmed items. Professional tone in neutral English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Script for the first 1:1 with a new direct report
prompts.content:
Act as a senior manager with a track record of building high-performance teams, trained in leadership practices (Michael Lopp, The Manager's Path) and psychological safety (Amy Edmondson). I need a complete script for my first 1:1 with {{NOMBRE_REPORTE}}, my new direct report in the role of {{ROL_REPORTE}}, in {{MODALIDAD}} mode and lasting {{DURACION}}. I want to project a {{ESTILO_LIDERAZGO}} leadership style. This first meeting sets the tone for the entire relationship: the goal is NOT to review pending items but to build trust, learn their story, align mutual expectations, and agree on how we will work together.

Before writing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: reformulate in one or two sentences what you understood and present your plan (allocation of {{DURACION}} across the five blocks). If {{ESTILO_LIDERAZGO}} is empty, assume warm and direct and declare it. If another critical datum is missing, request it before writing.

Deliver the script in five blocks, each with a suggested time that adds up to {{DURACION}}:
1. Opening and framing: purpose of the 1:1, that it is the person's space, why I invest in them.
2. Story and motivations: 4–5 open questions about trajectory, what energizes them, what drains them, how they define success.
3. Work and communication style: how they prefer feedback, how they like to be recognized, their communication rhythm, warning signals.
4. Mutual expectations: what I expect from {{NOMBRE_REPORTE}} and what they expect from me, explicitly in both directions.
5. Cadence agreements and close: frequency, duration, who sets the agenda, notes tool, first concrete commitment.

For each block: first-person script, exact questions (open, not yes/no), and a brief note on why it matters. Close with three errors to avoid and a bridge phrase to the next session. Adapt the tone to {{MODALIDAD}} and {{ESTILO_LIDERAZGO}}. Neutral and warm English, no jargon, no emojis. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides context about the report or the team. Deliverable: script readable in one continuous flow on one page, ready for the meeting.

prompts.title: Question bank for skip-level meetings
prompts.content:
Act as a senior executive coach specialized in manager-of-managers leadership, with applied mastery of psychological safety (Edmondson), the five team dysfunctions (Lencioni), and intrinsic motivation of autonomy, mastery, and purpose (Pink). I am going to conduct a skip-level meeting with {{ROL_PERSONA}}, who reports to {{MANAGER_INTERMEDIO}} in a team of {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}}, within this context: {{CONTEXTO_RELACION}}. Primary session objective: {{OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. The well-done skip-level unlocks information that does not travel up the normal chain (early risks, burnout, clarity gaps) and strengthens culture; done poorly it undermines the intermediate manager, generates triangulation, and burns trust.

Before generating anything, reformulate what you understand and present your calibration plan. If {{CONTEXTO_RELACION}} or {{OBJETIVO_PRINCIPAL}} are missing or ambiguous and would change the bank, request them before continuing.

Deliver a ready-to-use facilitation package, in this order: (1) Opening script of 3 to 5 sentences with the real purpose, explicit confidentiality framing (aggregated synthesis, no attribution, not an evaluation of {{MANAGER_INTERMEDIO}}), and anxiety reduction for {{ROL_PERSONA}}. (2) Bank of 18 to 24 open questions across six dimensions: clarity and purpose; psychological safety; workload and sustainability; growth and development; quality of collaboration with the manager; process and tool friction. Every question invites a concrete story, none is yes/no, and none asks the participant to evaluate or criticize {{MANAGER_INTERMEDIO}}: use system-level, personal-experience, and desired-future angles. (3) Per dimension, one follow-up question and one observable alarm signal. (4) Closing script with follow-up commitments and how you will return value without exposing the person. (5) Post-meeting protocol: how to synthesize patterns, what to bring to the manager as support (not reproach), and what to keep for your own action.

Quality rules: zero yes/no questions; zero questions asking to rate {{MANAGER_INTERMEDIO}}; opening frames aggregated, non-attributed confidentiality; each dimension has a follow-up and an alarm signal; the protocol separates manager support from direct action without exposing sources. Before closing, verify that no question induces evaluating the manager, all are open, and the protocol protects confidentiality. Professional and warm tone, neutral English, no emojis. Close with the single recommended opening question to set the tone.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Mood and workload check-in (RAG status)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior leadership coach specialized in team health and 1:1 conversations, with practice in RAG-status check-in frameworks (red-amber-green) and early overload detection. I am going to open my next 1:1 meeting with {{NOMBRE_PERSONA}} ({{ROL_PERSONA}}). I want to open with a traffic-light check-in on three dimensions (energy, workload, and blockers) BEFORE jumping to tasks and deliverables, because when you go straight to tactical matters, exhaustion and overload are detected late. Recent context: {{CONTEXTO_RECIENTE}}. 1:1 frequency: {{FRECUENCIA_1A1}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Deliver a ready-to-use opening script, in spoken language, brief and human, without technical jargon and without emojis, with these components in order: (1) a table with the three dimensions and the definition in one line of red, amber, and green for each, with observable and unambiguous criteria; (2) a warm opening question that invites {{NOMBRE_PERSONA}} to self-classify across the three dimensions without feeling evaluated on their performance; (3) per dimension, one follow-up question per color: for red and amber focused on root cause and concrete support, for green focused on reinforcing and capturing what is working; (4) a transition step that connects the declared state to the tactical agenda, with a simple rule for deciding whether a topic is addressed, reordered, or postponed; (5) three psychological safety phrases to open with and one closing line that summarizes agreements and names the follow-up. Frame that the traffic light serves to open conversation and not to score {{NOMBRE_PERSONA}}, and adjust the tone to the reporting relationship of {{ROL_PERSONA}} and to {{FRECUENCIA_1A1}}. Treat what they share as confidential except in the case of risk to themselves or others. Keep a single color per dimension and do not interpret silence as green. If {{CONTEXTO_RECIENTE}} is empty, do not invent signals: write a neutral version and flag the assumption. If any datum is missing, request it before writing.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: 1:1 long-term career conversation
prompts.content:
Act as a senior people manager and career coach, trained in the practice of development 1:1s and in the career-cone metaphor (growth in breadth vs. growth in height). I am going to conduct a 1:1 dedicated entirely to the long-term career of {{PERSONA}}, on the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}. This is not a status meeting or a project meeting: it is an aspirations conversation that rarely happens in the day-to-day. The purpose is to give the person a safe space to articulate how they see themselves growing, help them think with clarity, and unlock intentional development actions rather than leaving their trajectory to chance. What gets unlocked: retention through purpose, trust in the manager–person relationship, and a growth plan the person feels ownership over.

Data:
- PERSONA: {{PERSONA}} (name or alias and seniority level)
- ROL_ACTUAL: {{ROL_ACTUAL}} (role, responsibilities, and time in the role)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} (conversation horizon; default 1–3 years)
- CONTEXTO_PERSONA: {{CONTEXTO_PERSONA}} (known interests, strengths, frustrations, or aspirations; optional)
- SENAL_DETONANTE: {{SENAL_DETONANTE}} (recent comment, request, or evaluation that motivates the 1:1; optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If any essential data is missing to personalize, ask me before producing. Do not invent data about the person; flag any assumption as [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver, in this order:
1. Opening frame (2–4 sentences) that I can say literally to establish that the space is safe, confidential, and non-evaluative, and that today the protagonist is {{PERSONA}}'s career; include a bridge sentence that separates this conversation from the performance review.
2. A bank of open questions in three blocks calibrated to {{ROL_ACTUAL}} and seniority: (a) Vision of success in {{HORIZONTE}} in their own words; (b) Career-cone map, separating breadth (deepening/expanding impact in {{ROL_ACTUAL}}) from height (next level or role); (c) Real motivators and constraints (energy, personal life, desired learning). Each block with 1–2 probing follow-up questions and at least one question to surface the unspoken desire.
3. A method to help the person name 2–3 growth directions, without forcing promotion if their legitimate desire is to deepen breadth; include how to reflect the tension between aspiration and reality without closing the door.
4. A close that translates what was discussed into 2–3 development experiments, each with an owner, a horizon, and an observable signal of progress, plus my explicit commitment as manager and the date of the next review.

Conduct guide: tell me where to listen more than I talk, paraphrase to validate, and resist solving for the person; the plan belongs to the person, not to me. Neutral professional language. Flag risks (saying what they think I want to hear, confusing this with a promotion or salary negotiation) and how to mitigate them. Do not promise promotions, promotion timelines, or compensation: frame everything as exploration and development. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: 1:1 notes and commitments synthesis
prompts.content: Act as a senior manager with proven discipline in 1:1 cadences and commitment follow-up; you think in terms of clarity, accountability, and people development. From {{NOTAS_CRUDAS}} of the 1:1 meeting with {{NOMBRE_COLABORADOR}} on {{FECHA_REUNION}}, produce a structured synthesis in four blocks. First restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Block 1: executive summary of 3 to 5 lines covering mood, central topics, and perceived emotional state (as perception, not fact). Block 2: group all points from {{NOTAS_CRUDAS}} by topic (development and career, workload, blockers and dependencies, feedback, team relationships, personal life only if {{NOMBRE_COLABORADOR}} brought it up) without losing anything relevant. Block 3: agreements table Commitment | Owner (manager or {{NOMBRE_COLABORADOR}}) | Due Date | Action Verb; each row starts with an action verb and a concrete date; if a date is missing, propose one consistent with {{CADENCIA}} and mark it [proposed]. Block 4: points to revisit and 2 to 3 opening questions for the next 1:1. Distinguish what was said from what was inferred and mark ambiguities [to be confirmed]; do not invent commitments; treat sensitive feedback and {{ADJUNTOS}} with discretion. If {{NOTAS_CRUDAS}}, {{NOMBRE_COLABORADOR}}, or {{FECHA_REUNION}} are missing, ask for them before continuing. Neutral, professional language, no emojis, ready to archive.

prompts.title: Reactivate stalled or cancelled 1:1s
Asynchronous 1:1 for distributed teams
prompts.content: Act as a remote leadership coach specializing in multi-timezone distributed teams, trained in situation-behavior-impact (SBI) feedback and asynchronous listening. Design a written asynchronous 1:1 between a leader and {{NOMBRE_ROL_PERSONA}}, who work with {{DIFERENCIA_HORARIA}}, where a synchronous 1:1 is not viable or falls in inconvenient hours. The risk to avoid: degrading the 1:1 into a cold status report that loses human connection, space for real blockers, and coaching depth. Deliver a leader opening message ready to paste plus the back-and-forth thread script in four blocks: (1) Human connection — a warm, context-specific opening to {{NOMBRE_ROL_PERSONA}} according to {{TONO_RELACION}}, no generic template, that creates space without pressuring an immediate reply; (2) Their agenda first — 3 to 4 open questions so the person brings their topics, blockers, and energy level before the leader's agenda; (3) My part — feedback in situation-behavior-impact format on {{TEMAS_PENDIENTES}} plus a specific recognition and one topic from the leader's side, human and non-evaluative tone; (4) Agreements and next step — how to capture decisions, responsibility per action, and how to close the thread within {{VENTANA_CIERRE}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context. For each block deliver the actual text to paste and a brief note on why it works asynchronously. Before drafting, confirm the input data; if any is missing, ask before drafting and do not invent sensitive relationship data. Hard rules: person's agenda before leader's; explicit SBI feedback; no question pressures an immediate reply or forces overexposure; recognition specific, not generic. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Questions to build early trust
Inviting upward feedback in the 1:1
Intrinsic motivation diagnosis in a 1:1
prompts.content: Act as a senior leadership coach specializing in intrinsic motivation of technical teams, trained in Daniel Pink's Drive model. I am going to conduct a 1:1 with {{COLABORADOR}} ({{ROL_RESPONSABILIDADES}}) whose motivation seems to have changed according to these signals: {{SENALES_OBSERVADAS}}. I want to go beyond task status and understand what drives them internally before applying the wrong lever (more money or more control where what is missing is purpose or mastery). Prior 1:1 history: {{HISTORIAL_1A1}}. Specific objective of this session: {{OBJETIVO_SESION}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any key datum is missing, ask before moving forward; do not invent data about the person. Deliver, in this order: (1) Prior hypothesis per dimension — for autonomy, mastery, and purpose — with current status (satisfied, at risk, or blocked), evidence supporting it, and probable dominant lever, marking [ASSUMPTION] for anything not backed by {{SENALES_OBSERVADAS}} or {{HISTORIAL_1A1}}. (2) Conversation script: 9 to 12 open questions (3 to 4 per dimension), ordered from a warm opening to a close with commitments, non-leading, in the second person, distinguishing intrinsic from extrinsic motivation; add 2 follow-up questions when tension arises and 1 elegant exit question if the person closes off. (3) Reading and close plan: criteria for interpreting responses (signals of a satisfied vs. at-risk dimension, plus social-desirability signals that would invalidate a response), 3 sample agreements per possible lever, and a closing question that returns agency to {{COLABORADOR}}. Exclude performance, evaluation, or corrective feedback questions. Note limits (hypothesis to validate, not verdict) and flag ambiguities as {to_be_confirmed}. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. No prices; neutral professional language.

prompts.title: 1:1 containment agenda after a critical week
prompts.content: Act as a senior executive coach specializing in leadership of technical teams under pressure and in psychological safety, with mastery of Amy Edmondson's model and the blameless post-mortem logic.
