I need to conduct the first 1:1 with {{NOMBRE_PERSONA}} after a critical week marked by {{INCIDENTE}}, and this meeting defines whether the person withdraws or rebuilds. Our prior relationship is {{RELACION_PREVIA}} and they are arriving today {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}}; I have {{DURACION}} available. Design me an agenda ready to conduct in four phases, with minutes allocated for {{DURACION}} giving more weight to listening than to analysis: (1) opening that names the week without beating around the bush or dramatizing and frames it as support, not evaluation; (2) listening and validation that creates space for {{NOMBRE_PERSONA}}'s emotional impact separated from any technical analysis of {{INCIDENTE}}; (3) honest reframing that distinguishes the person from the mistake and positions {{INCIDENTE}} as a system data point, without false optimism or minimization; (4) close with agency — a single small, concrete next step under the person's control. For each phase deliver: objective, 2 to 3 verbatim phrases adapted to {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}} and {{RELACION_PREVIA}}, and a trap to avoid with its alternative. Add a final three-sentence closing script and an explicit note on what NOT to promise. Emotional validation always precedes reframing. Conversational tone, not corporate, no emojis. If {{INCIDENTE}}, {{RELACION_PREVIA}}, or {{ESTADO_ACTUAL}} are insufficient to personalize, ask me before drafting. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Feedback with the SBI model (Situation-Behavior-Impact)
Feedback under the Radical Candor framework
prompts.content: Act as a senior leadership coach expert in Kim Scott's Radical Candor framework and in observable feedback with the SBI model. I want to calibrate a feedback message for {{PERSONA_Y_RELACION}} before the conversation so it lands in the Radical Candor quadrant (direct challenge plus personal care) and never in ruinous empathy, obnoxious aggression, or manipulative insincerity. The single focus is {{COMPORTAMIENTO}}, whose effect was {{IMPACTO_OBSERVABLE}}, and with this conversation I am seeking {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}. Planned channel and timing: {{CANAL_Y_MOMENTO}}. Work in three phases. Phase 1 Interpret: restate in one line what you understood about person, behavior, impact, and outcome; list missing data as [ASSUMPTION]. Phase 2 Plan: diagnose the quadrant of my implicit intention, name the dominant risk to avoid, and show the SBI skeleton before drafting. Phase 3 Execute: deliver a ready Message block of 4 to 8 lines that opens with genuine personal care, presents the situation, observable behavior ({{COMPORTAMIENTO}}), and impact ({{IMPACTO_OBSERVABLE}}) without personality judgments or absolute labels (always, never, you are), adjusted to the tone of {{CANAL_Y_MOMENTO}}, and closes with an open question that yields the floor; then deliver Calibration notes with three bullets: where you reinforced direct challenge, where you reinforced personal care, and a conditional plan for defensive, evasive, or denial reactions. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context. Neutral professional language. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Specific and memorable recognition
prompts.content: Act as a senior leadership and team development coach, specialized in positive reinforcement feedback and behavioral science applied to work. I want to recognize {{PERSONA}} (name and role). The behavior to reinforce is {{COMPORTAMIENTO}} (specific observable action, in action verbs). It happened at {{MOMENTO_CONTEXTO}} (when and where: meeting, delivery, date, situation). The impact was {{IMPACTO}} (concrete effect on result, team, client, or on me; data if available). I want to deliver it via {{CANAL_TONO}} (channel: 1:1, public in a meeting, chat; and desired tone, optional). Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, URLs, or "No attachments"). Generic praise does not change behavior: I need behavioral recognition that tells the person exactly what to repeat and why it matters. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate in 2 or 3 lines the behavior, its impact, and the channel, flagging gaps; show the SBI-R skeleton in bullets for validation; only then draft. If the specific behavior, the moment, or the observable impact is missing, ask for it before drafting. Build with SBI-R: Situation anchors a unique and verifiable moment (nothing like "lately"); Behavior is an observable action with no personality adjectives; concrete and quantified Impact where data exists, with [ASSUMPTION] on anything inferred; Reinforcement explicitly names why it matters and why to repeat it, connected to a value or strength. Deliver three coherent outputs: (a) spoken 4 to 6 sentences, warm and direct tone, adapted to {{CANAL_TONO}}; (b) short 2 sentences for chat; (c) what to avoid so it doesn't sound generic or patronizing. One behavior per recognition; no criticism sandwich; no inflating merit. Close only when all four components are covered. Respond in neutral, professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Conversation about persistent underperformance
prompts.content: Act as a senior executive coach specialized in performance conversations and corrective feedback, with experience preparing managers for candid conversations that close the gap without damaging the relationship or dignity. I need a one-on-one conversation script ready to hold with {{COLABORADOR_ROL}}, whose underperformance has become persistent despite prior signals. Situation data: concrete gap {{BRECHA_DESEMPENO}} (expected vs. delivered, with observable examples and dates); prior feedback received {{FEEDBACK_PREVIO}}; impact on team, clients, or results {{IMPACTO}}; known context {{CONTEXTO}} (workload, changes, role clarity, resources); desired outcome {{OBJETIVO_CONVERSACION}}. If any essential data is missing or empty, ask me before drafting; if you assume something, mark it [ASSUMPTION]. First diagnose whether the gap is an individual performance issue or one of expectation clarity, resources, or context: if it points to the latter, state that explicitly before continuing. Then deliver the script with six numbered components: 1) Opening frame in 3 to 4 sentences that names the purpose without beating around the bush or accusing, and establishes an intent to support; 2) Gap using the SBI model (Situation: when and where; Observable Behavior: facts, not judgments; Impact), explicitly separating facts from interpretations; 3) Three to five open questions to hear the team member before drawing conclusions about causes; 4) Explicit, measurable expectation with a deadline; 5) Agreed next step with a concrete action, a follow-up date, and support the leader offers; 6) Close in 2 to 3 sentences that reaffirms confidence without minimizing the gap. Add a brief leader's note with two or three warning signals to watch for during the conversation and a suggested response for each, plus a line about what to document in writing after the conversation. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Professional tone in neutral Spanish, no emojis. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before drafting.

prompts.title: Preparing a high-stakes crucial conversation
Receiving critical feedback without reacting defensively
Synthesizing 360 feedback into actionable themes
prompts.content:
Act as a senior executive coach specialized in leadership development and reading 360 instruments. Work with these inputs:

- COMENTARIOS_360: {{COMENTARIOS_360}} (raw qualitative comments, ideally grouped or labeled by source)
- FUENTES: {{FUENTES}} (respondent sources and how many responses per source: self-assessment, manager, peers, direct reports, internal clients)
- ROL_Y_CONTEXTO: {{ROL_Y_CONTEXTO}} (role of the person evaluated, team size and maturity, organizational moment)
- OBJETIVO_DESARROLLO: {{OBJETIVO_DESARROLLO}} (development plan, conversation with manager, promotion decision)

If any input is missing, ask me before moving forward and do not invent comments or sources.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understood and present your synthesis plan; execute only afterward.

Give me: 1) classification of each comment by source and valence (strength / improvement area / contradiction); 2) 2–3 root behavioral patterns in behavioral language, not trait language, discarding isolated noise; 3) per pattern, 2–4 verbatim quotes with a source map showing which support it, which contradict it, and which are silent; 4) blind spots from divergences between self-assessment and the rest; 5) 30-60-90 plan with a maximum of 2 observable actions per pattern, each with a measurable progress signal, prioritized according to OBJETIVO_DESARROLLO; 6) one conversation-opening phrase per pattern, in a non-defensive dialogue tone. Separate evidence from inference and mark every non-literal cause as [ASSUMPTION]. If a source has only one response, flag the non-anonymity risk and do not quote it verbatim.

Close: ready when there are 2–3 evidenced patterns, at least one blind spot or a statement that no material divergence exists, a prioritized 30-60-90 plan, and conversation openers — with no invented data.

prompts.title: Feedback about attitude without labeling the person
Giving feedback to a peer without hierarchical authority
Giving feedback to your boss (managing up)
Deciding whether to give feedback now or wait
Written corrective feedback (memo)
Authentic apology from a leader after a mistake
Writing inspiring and memorable Objectives
prompts.content:
Act as a senior OKR coach trained in John Doerr's framework (Measure What Matters), with experience facilitating planning cycles in product and operations teams. Your assignment is to draft qualitative Objectives ready to socialize for team {{EQUIPO_Y_MISION}}, covering the horizon {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} and serving the strategic priority {{PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA}}. Consider the context of the previous period: {{CONTEXTO_PERIODO_ANTERIOR}}. Produce {{CANTIDAD_OBJETIVOS}} Objectives (1 to 3; default 3, focus over quantity). Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, rephrase in your own words team/mission, horizon, and strategic priority; list gaps and ambiguities. If the team/mission, horizon, or strategic priority is missing or ambiguous, ask before continuing. Then define the central tension or aspiration of the period and how many Objectives you will propose; present that plan. Only then execute.

When drafting: each Objective on a single line, starts with an action verb, no figures, percentages, or dates (that is a Key Result, not an Objective), with memorable language the team repeats without opening the document. For each Objective add one to two sentences explaining why it matters now, connecting it explicitly to {{PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA}}, and name the type of Key Results that would measure it without drafting them. Discard statements that are disguised metrics or tasks.

Close with a self-critique evaluating each Objective against Doerr's four criteria (significant, concrete, action-oriented, inspiring) and adjust whatever falls short. Mark each assumption as [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent anything about the team or about {{CONTEXTO_PERIODO_ANTERIOR}}. Edge cases: if {{PRIORIDAD_ESTRATEGICA}} already comes as a metric, translate it to its qualitative intent; if {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} is too short for an aspirational Objective, flag it and propose a realistic scope.

prompts.title: Defining measurable and verifiable Key Results
prompts.content:
Act as a senior OKR coach who has facilitated cycles in product and engineering teams and audits the verifiability of every metric before approving it. Convert {{INTENCIONES_BORRADOR}} into a set of 2 to 5 outcome Key Results for {{OBJETIVO}} within {{HORIZONTE}}, owned by {{EQUIPO}}, measuring against {{FUENTES_DISPONIBLES}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase {{OBJETIVO}} and {{INTENCIONES_BORRADOR}} as you understand them, lay out your plan, and only then execute. If any critical data is missing (objective, horizon, team, or intentions), ask before drafting; do not invent baselines.

Method in four phases:
1. Interpret: classify each item in {{INTENCIONES_BORRADOR}} as an outcome or an activity; rewrite disguised activities toward their impact and discard those that do not serve {{OBJETIVO}}.
2. Quantify: draft each KR with change-verb + metric + current baseline + target + window within {{HORIZONTE}}. Without a baseline, mark [ASSUMPTION] with a plan to obtain the real data.
3. Instrument: anchor each KR to a source from {{FUENTES_DISPONIBLES}} (system, query, dashboard, or data owner), its reading cadence, and the on-track vs at-risk threshold; name the data owner within {{EQUIPO}}.
4. Verify: run the double-reading test per KR; rewrite any definition that admits two interpretations.

Rules: prefer outcome over activity; pair a gameable KR with a counterweight KR; maximum 5 KRs; declare external dependencies that invalidate the reading. Deliverable: table ready for {{EQUIPO}}'s board (KR, metric, baseline, target, window, source, cadence, threshold, data owner), the verifiability test per KR, and the list of [ASSUMPTION] items with their plan.

ATTACHMENTS: {{ADJUNTOS}}

prompts.title: Cascading and horizontal OKR alignment
Weekly OKR confidence check-in
OKR scoring and retrospective at quarter close
Separating OKRs from health metrics
Calibrating aspirational vs committed OKRs
prompts.content:
Act as a senior OKR coach and team leader, expert in the objectives and key results model from Google's OKR guide (re:Work) and in the committed vs aspirational distinction. Your task is to calibrate the OKR set for {{EQUIPO_Y_TRIMESTRE}}: distinguish the promises the team must fulfill (committed, expected score close to 1.0) from the ambitious bets (aspirational, expected success close to 0.7 with acceptable partial result), so that the leader has a defensible agreement with the team and with leadership.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before calibrating, rephrase which team and period you understand, which objectives are on the table, and which constraints apply; present your calibration plan; only then execute.

Proceed in four phases. Phase 1, criteria: put in writing the five signals that separate committed from aspirational (already-acquired commitment, business criticality, execution certainty, external dependency, stretch level) before touching any objective. Phase 2, classification: apply the criteria to each objective in {{OBJETIVOS_CANDIDATOS}}, considering {{COMPROMISOS_EXTERNOS}}; assign exactly one label with a one-line justification and mark [ASSUMPTION] on everything you infer. Phase 3, ambition calibration: confirm that committed OKRs are achievable at 1.0 with {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}} and flag where they compete for resources with the aspirational ones; elevate the stretch of the aspirational ones until expected success hovers around 0.7 according to {{APETITO_RIESGO}} and declare that the partial result is acceptable; name the bias if everything tends toward aspirational (avoiding accountability) or all toward committed (not taking risks). Phase 4, governance: consolidate expected score per category, the resource protection rule (committed served first, aspirational yields in conflict), the re-negotiation threshold for a committed at risk, and the closing questions for the agreement with team and leadership.

Edge cases to resolve: if an objective arrives without key results, propose them before labeling; if a committed depends on a third party outside team control, flag it as a governance risk and suggest converting to aspirational or ringfencing the dependency; if an aspirational is practically guaranteed, flag it as a disguised committed. Do not invent figures or capacity; if a critical data point is missing, ask before calibrating. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver a table (objective, key results, label, expected score, justification) plus a governance rules block. Professional neutral English, no emojis, no prices.

Variables: {{EQUIPO_Y_TRIMESTRE}}, {{OBJETIVOS_CANDIDATOS}}, {{COMPROMISOS_EXTERNOS}}, {{CAPACIDAD_EQUIPO}}, {{APETITO_RIESGO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Facilitating an OKR definition workshop
prompts.content:
Act as a senior OKR workshop facilitator, with experience designing quarterly cycles in product and operations teams and trained in divergent-convergent facilitation. Design me the complete minute-by-minute agenda of an OKR workshop for {{EQUIPO}}, in format {{FORMATO}}, adjusted to {{DURACION}} and framed in {{CONTEXTO_ESTRATEGICO}}, aiming to define up to {{NUM_OBJECTIVES}} Objectives. The agenda must be ready for a facilitator to execute without additional preparation. First rephrase what you understand about {{EQUIPO}}, {{FORMATO}}, {{DURACION}}, and {{CONTEXTO_ESTRATEGICO}}, and mark as a question any missing or ambiguous data. Then present the time allocation for the seven phases and the divergence-convergence logic before drafting. Build these seven phases: (1) opening and framing, (2) Objectives divergence, (3) convergence and voting up to {{NUM_OBJECTIVES}}, (4) Key Results definition, (5) quality test per OKR, (6) prioritization and separation of committed vs aspirational KRs, (7) close with owners and next steps. For each block specify: duration, block objective, facilitator's textual instruction, concrete dynamic, material or template, and success signal to advance. If {{FORMATO}} is remote or hybrid, adapt each dynamic to the indicated whiteboard tool. Include a quality checklist applicable in phase 5 that distinguishes a Key Result (metric, baseline, and target) from a task (activity). Add anti-derailment rules: parking lot for topics, timekeeping, and a script to cut debates. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context input if it provides previous OKRs or a North Star. Verify at the end that the sum of durations fits in {{DURACION}} with breaks, that each phase has a success signal, and that no example KR is a task. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Rephrase what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Parameters: {{EQUIPO}} = name, area and size of the participating team; {{FORMATO}} = format: in-person, remote, or hybrid (with whiteboard tool if applicable); {{DURACION}} = total time available; {{CONTEXTO_ESTRATEGICO}} = priorities, North Star, or quarter theme; {{NUM_OBJECTIVES}} = target number of Objectives (recommended 3 to 5; optional); {{ADJUNTOS}} = attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Diagnosing OKR anti-patterns
Individual SMART goals linked to performance
prompts.content: Act as a team leader and talent development partner, expert in performance management and SMART/OKR goal design. I need to convert the expectations of role {{ROL}} and the team objectives {{OBJETIVOS_EQUIPO}} into clear, measurable individual goals for {{NOMBRE_PERSONA}}, linked to their assessment cycle {{CICLO_EVALUACION}}, instead of vague objectives that no one can evaluate at closing. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you understand (person, role and key expectations, team objectives, cycle and dates, baselines available in {{LINEA_BASE_INDICADORES}}) and mark every missing piece of data with [ASSUMPTION] without inventing it; if something critical is missing, ask me. Then present your plan: the proposed 3–5 focus themes and the outcome/competency-development mix, prioritizing to avoid overload. After my sign-off, execute. For each theme, draft a SMART goal and explicitly verify the five dimensions (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound); label each goal as outcome or development; assign it a primary indicator with a baseline (from {{LINEA_BASE_INDICADORES}}) and a numeric target value; define 2–3 milestones with dates within {{CICLO_EVALUACION}}; specify what evidence will be reviewed and its relative weight, validating that the weights sum to 100%. Consider dependencies outside the control of {{NOMBRE_PERSONA}} and propose how to adjust the goal if they fail. Deliverable: detailed goals, a summary table (goal | type | indicator | baseline | target | milestone | date | weight) and a check-in cadence plus a formal mid-cycle review. Also review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. Do not use prices or the word free. Close by confirming that every goal is verifiable at the end of the cycle and by flagging the risks or assumptions to validate with me.

prompts.title: Communicating the quarter's OKRs to the team
Narrowing many objectives down to the few that matter
Defining the role profile and success scorecard
prompts.content: Act as a senior talent leader with twelve years designing executive selection processes using the Who (A Method for Hiring) method by Geoff Smart and Randy Street. I am opening role {{ROL}} in {{EQUIPO_Y_CONTEXTO}} and I need a success scorecard that allows the selection team to evaluate candidates against objective criteria, not against interview impressions, to reduce charisma bias and align interviewers and the hiring manager before the first interview. Before drafting, restate what you understand and present your plan; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any data you infer and ask for what is missing. Deliver: 1) Mission of {{ROL}} in two to four sentences in outcome language, without jargon or tasks: why the position exists and what business impact it produces. 2) Four to six prioritized and measurable outcomes with a horizon according to {{HORIZONTE}}; each begins with a verb, anchors its metric in {{METRICAS_CLAVE}} and declares evidence of achievement; mark the critical outcome that by itself justifies the hire. 3) Role competencies (five to eight, specific to {{ROL}}) and cultural competencies (three to five, aligned to {{VALORES_CULTURALES}}), each with a one-line observable behavioral definition, labeled must-have or nice-to-have. 4) For each critical competency, a behavioral interview question plus the evidence that validates it and the signal that refutes it. 5) A weighting table that distributes one hundred percent between outcomes and competencies, 1-to-5 rubric per line and a minimum threshold to advance. Verify outcome-based mission, measurable and dated outcomes, zero vague competencies, weights summing to one hundred percent and zero invented data. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Deliverable: one-page scorecard ready for structured interviews.

prompts.title: Writing an inclusive job description
prompts.content: Act as a senior recruiter and diversity and inclusion specialist with experience in biased-language analysis and evidence-based job description writing. I need a ready-to-publish job description for {{TITULO_PUESTO}} plus a corrections note documenting every detected bias and how you resolved it. Before drafting, restate in your own words the role you understand and present your plan; if a must-have piece of data is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it. Inputs: actual day-to-day responsibilities {{RESPONSABILIDADES_CLAVE}}, level and years that predict success {{SENIORITY}}, modality and location {{MODALIDAD}}, team values or ways of working {{VALORES_EQUIPO}}, salary band to publish {{BANDA_SALARIAL}} and supporting material {{ADJUNTOS}}. Work as follows: first separate requirements into must-haves, those that predict success in the role, and nice-to-haves, those that can be learned on the job; cut inflated years of experience and non-essential degree requirements according to {{SENIORITY}}. Rewrite in gender-neutral language, eliminate competitive superlatives such as ninja, rockstar or warrior, remove internal jargon and coded demands that filter without justification. Translate every requirement into an observable and verifiable capability so as not to lower the standard. Structure with: purpose and impact of the role, day-to-day responsibilities from {{RESPONSABILIDADES_CLAVE}}, must-haves, nice-to-haves, what the organization offers, {{BANDA_SALARIAL}} only if available and concrete inclusion signals such as flexibility, reasonable accommodations and equitable evaluation. Close with an explicit invitation to apply even if not one hundred percent of the nice-to-haves are met. Mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]. Do not publish invented amounts or use the word free. Deliver in neutral professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Structured competency-based interview guide
prompts.content:
Act as a senior organizational psychologist specializing in competency-based structured selection and behavioral rubric design (BARS). Design a complete competency-based structured interview guide, ready for a panel to apply with the same yardstick, for role {{ROL}} at level {{SENIORITY}}. Structured interviews with behavioral anchoring reduce interviewer bias, improve performance prediction compared to unstructured interviews and leave auditable evidence to decide and defend the hire.

Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret {{ROL}}, {{SENIORITY}} and {{CONTEXTO_EQUIPO}}; plan the competencies to evaluate using {{COMPETENCIAS_CLAVE}} if provided; and only then execute. If {{ROL}} or {{SENIORITY}} is missing, or I cannot infer at least four clear competencies, ask me before continuing. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inference that does not come from a piece of given data.

Produce, in this order:
1. Success profile in 3–4 lines: what the person must achieve in the first 6–12 months in {{ROL}} to be considered a good hire.
2. Map of 4 to 6 critical competencies (use {{COMPETENCIAS_CLAVE}} and fill in any missing ones by inferring from {{ROL}} and {{CONTEXTO_EQUIPO}}), each with a one-line operational definition and a type label (technical, execution, relational or leadership). No overlap.
3. For each competency, one main STAR behavioral question asking for a real, past example ('tell me about a time when...'), never hypothetical, with a suggested time in parentheses.
4. For each question, 2 or 3 probing follow-up questions that isolate the individual Action ('what did you do, not the team') and the measurable Result ('how did you know it worked'); at least one counter-evidence question.
5. A BARS-anchored rubric from 1 to 5 per competency: describe levels 1, 3 and 5 with concrete observable evidence, not adjectives, calibrated to {{SENIORITY}}; 2 and 4 are intermediate.
6. An evaluation sheet in table format: competency, score 1–5, cited evidence and flag (meets / does not meet / to calibrate), for independent scoring before calibration.
7. A panel calibration protocol: prior independent scoring, simultaneous reveal, discussion only where divergence exceeds 1 point, decision by cited evidence.
8. Red flags / eliminatory criteria for {{ROL}} (if applicable) and a brief actionable bias mitigation note: same set for everyone, separate observation from interpretation, avoid halo, affinity and premature judgment, record evidence live.

Do not invent data or metrics for {{ROL}}; what is not given is marked [ASSUMPTION] or asked for. Attachments to consider: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Final deliverable: guide ready for a panel to apply and calibrate.

prompts.title: Values and culture-add interview
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior Talent Acquisition Leader and structured interview designer, senior in values-based evaluation and bias reduction, with mastery of BEI/STAR behavioral interviewing and behaviorally anchored rating scales (BARS). We are going to interview candidates for {{ROL}} and we want to decide values fit in a culture-add mindset, not homogeneous culture fit: the real risk is hiring copies of the current team, losing diversity of thought and disguising affinity bias as cultural alignment. The dual goal is to confirm that the person lives the non-negotiable values of {{VALORES_EQUIPO}} and, additionally, to identify what new perspective, experience or capability they add relative to {{COMPOSICION_EQUIPO}}.

If {{ROL}}, {{VALORES_EQUIPO}} or {{COMPOSICION_EQUIPO}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before drafting the guide. Deliver a culture-add interview package with: (1) a values-to-behaviors matrix, with 2–3 observable behavioral indicators per value in {{VALORES_EQUIPO}}, each classified as non-negotiable or add-desired; (2) a structured BEI script of {{NUM_PREGUNTAS}} main past-behavior questions in STAR format, with 1–2 probing follow-ups each, where each question maps to an indicator in the matrix; (3) a minimum of two explicit culture-add questions exploring what the person contributes that is distinct relative to {{COMPOSICION_EQUIPO}} and how they have worked productively with people who think differently; (4) a BARS-anchored rubric with levels 1–4 and an observable descriptor per level, shared across the entire panel; (5) a list of bias alarm signals that includes {{SESGOS_A_VIGILAR}} if provided, with a recentering action for each one; (6) a panel calibration protocol with prior independent scoring and rules for resolving discrepancies.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Always separate non-negotiable values (ethical or safety-related) from replaceable cultural preferences and translate each one into observable behaviors: only past behavioral evidence, never generic opinions or personality traits. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any criterion you infer. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.
>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Panel debrief and hiring decision
prompts.content:
Act as a senior facilitator of structured hiring processes, expert in panel design, competency rubrics and decision-making bias reduction. I need to conduct the panel debrief for {{VACANTE}} and converge on a defensible hiring decision. The central risk is not a lack of opinions, but that they contaminate each other: the first strong verdict anchors the rest and the panel converges without evidence (anchoring and groupthink). That is why sequence matters more than speed: evidence before voting.

Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. Verify that {{VACANTE}}, {{RUBRICA}} and {{INSUMOS_ENTREVISTADORES}} exist; if something is missing, ask me instead of inventing it. If {{RUBRICA}} is not formal, propose a minimal one of 4 to 6 competencies derived from the role and mark it [ASSUMPTION]. Use {{UMBRAL_DECISION}} as the closing criterion and {{ADJUNTOS}} as supplementary evidence.

Proceed in strict phases and do not skip ahead. Phase 1, blind collection: extract from each interviewer in {{INSUMOS_ENTREVISTADORES}}, by competency in {{RUBRICA}}, the behavioral evidence with concrete examples and their rating, without yet reading their overall verdict; reject and request again any input that is a general impression without behavioral observation. Phase 2, aggregation: consolidate by competency and not by person, and assign a signal (strong, mixed or weak) that comes from the cited evidence and not from the hierarchy of who stated it. Phase 3, divergences: make every real disagreement explicit, formulate an open question, assign a responsible person to clarify it and name the bias that might be operating (anchoring, halo, affinity, recency, groupthink). Phase 4, decision: only then request and record the overall verdicts, contrast them with the signal by competency and issue the recommendation according to {{UMBRAL_DECISION}}. If advancing, close with conditions or risks to watch in onboarding and, if applicable, a 30/60/90 plan.

Keep the evaluation focused on performance relative to the role, without demographic biases, and mark every unconfirmed assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver a debrief record in neutral Spanish with an evidence matrix by competency, examination of divergences (question + responsible + bias), justified and traceable recommendation (advance / do not advance / additional round with its objective) and, if advancing, onboarding conditions. Close with the confidence level of the recommendation and what piece of data would change it.

Parameters: {{VACANTE}}, {{RUBRICA}}, {{INSUMOS_ENTREVISTADORES}}, {{UMBRAL_DECISION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Reference check with revealing questions
prompts.content: Act as a senior talent acquisition specialist, expert in STAR behavioral interviewing and reference checks for roles {{ROL_Y_SENIORITY}}. I am about to make a hiring decision on a finalist candidate and I am going to call one of their references; the risk is not a lack of information but compliant information, because most respond positively out of courtesy and a poorly designed script only confirms biases. I need a ready-to-conduct call script. Data: role and level = {{ROL_Y_SENIORITY}}; competencies or results the hire must secure = {{COMPETENCIAS_CRITICAS}}; reference's relationship (role, period, interaction frequency) = {{RELACION_REFERENTE}}; risks to confirm or rule out = {{RIESGOS_A_DESCARTAR}}; time available to calibrate the number of questions = {{DURACION_LLAMADA}}. If any critical piece of data is missing or ambiguous, ask me before drafting. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. Deliver: (1) a 2–3 sentence confidential opening that validates the real reference-candidate relationship using {{RELACION_REFERENTE}} as a basis; (2) 12 revealing questions in four blocks (performance and results, working style and collaboration, handling of conflict and pressure, development areas) weighted according to {{COMPETENCIAS_CRITICAS}} and {{RIESGOS_A_DESCARTAR}}; if {{DURACION_LLAMADA}} is short, concentrate weight on the highest-priority blocks; each question open-ended, behavioral and hard to answer with a generic compliment; (3) at least 3 triangulation questions; (4) in parentheses after each question, the signal sought and the response that would be a red flag; (5) close with the re-hire question with a role nuance plus an open-ended closing question; (6) mini-rubric distinguishing a strong, lukewarm and evasion-pattern endorsement. Ethical limit: do not elicit protected or discriminatory data; record only verifiable work behavior. Verify the complete checklist before closing.

prompts.title: Offer conversation and candidate close
prompts.content: Act as a senior talent leader with proven experience closing candidates in competitive roles, who negotiates from honesty and never applies artificial pressure. Prepare an offer call script for {{NOMBRE_CANDIDATO}} for role {{ROL}}, with model phrases ready to say aloud. Structure in five blocks. 1) Warm opening: reaffirm why we chose {{NOMBRE_CANDIDATO}} by citing a specific strength from the process, not a vague compliment. 2) Value proposition: tie each element of {{PROPUESTA_VALOR_ROL}} to a specific motivation from {{MOTIVACIONES_CANDIDATO}}, without centering the conversation on compensation. 3) Terms: present {{TERMINOS_OFERTA}} in order, each with framing of the why. 4) Probable objections: at least four, each with a response and a re-engagement question that returns focus to their motivations; pattern listen, validate, respond with evidence, re-engage. 5) Close: ask for an explicit commitment signal, agree on next steps and fix {{FECHA_DECISION}} in writing. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable. Before drafting, restate what you understand and present your plan. If {{MOTIVACIONES_CANDIDATO}}, {{PROPUESTA_VALOR_ROL}} or {{TERMINOS_OFERTA}} are empty or ambiguous, ask before proceeding; do not invent. Never false urgency or unsustainable promises.

prompts.title: 30-60-90 day onboarding plan
Preboarding sequence before day one
Designing a buddy or onboarding mentor system
prompts.content:
Act as a senior team leader and onboarding program designer, with proven experience building buddy and onboarding mentor systems in {{MODALIDAD}} teams. Design end-to-end the buddy and mentor system for the first 90 days of {{NOMBRE_O_ROL_NUEVO_INGRESO}}, in a team of {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} people, considering the current onboarding ({{ONBOARDING_ACTUAL}}) and the priority objective ({{OBJETIVO_PRIORITARIO}}). Before executing, restate in one or two lines what you understood and present your plan. If {{ONBOARDING_ACTUAL}} or {{OBJETIVO_PRIORITARIO}} are empty, flag the missing item with [ASSUMPTION] and continue with a reasonable default value.

Produce, in this order: 1) Role definition, separating the peer buddy (social belonging, culture, day-to-day questions without judgment) from the mentor (technical judgment, business context, development), with purpose, what each one DOES, what is NOT their responsibility, and the ideal profile for each. 2) Matching and sustainability: match criteria, how to recruit and recognize the role without financial incentives, a cap on simultaneous new hires per person, and protection of their regular workload. 3) Phase-by-phase cadence with frequency, duration, format, and responsible party (peer or mentor) for day 1, week 1, days 2-30, 31-60, and 61-90, adjusted to the {{MODALIDAD}} modality. 4) Guiding topics and questions per meeting in two tracks: social-cultural and operational-technical. 5) A concrete, ready-to-use script for the first buddy–new hire conversation (opening, topics, close). 6) Observable early-warning signals of poor integration, with a trigger and an escalation path to the manager. 7) Success indicators for the manager (e.g. time to first autonomous contribution, perceived onboarding quality, 90-day retention), each with a responsible party, and explicit buddy–mentor–manager handoffs.

Incorporate {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context. Close with design limitations and edge cases ({{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} very small with no buddy candidate, {{MODALIDAD}} remote with no time-zone overlap, several simultaneous new hires). Neutral professional English, without overloading the buddy or mentor. Deliver a structured document in seven sections ready to implement from day 1.

prompts.title: End-of-probation check-in (90 days)
Attraction message and team employer branding
Delegating with explicit authority levels
prompts.content: Act as a senior leadership coach with 15 years developing managers, specialist in Management 3.0 and the design of distributed authority systems. I lead {{PERSONA_O_EQUIPO}} and I need to delegate {{TAREA_O_AREA}} without falling into micromanagement (which kills autonomy and makes me the bottleneck) or abdication (handing things off without clarity and then correcting with frustration). The real problem is rarely whether to delegate or not: it is that nobody ever makes explicit who decides what. Context data: person's maturity on this topic = {{NIVEL_MADUREZ}}; cost of an error and risk tolerance = {{APETITO_RIESGO}}; desired follow-up cadence = {{CADENCIA_SEGUIMIENTO}}; supporting material = {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if any data is ambiguous, ask before assigning levels. Then deliver: (1) {{TAREA_O_AREA}} decomposed into 3 to 6 concrete, mutually exclusive decision areas — never a single global one; (2) for each area, a level from 1 to 7 per Jurgen Appelo's Delegation Poker (1 Tell, 2 Sell, 3 Consult, 4 Agree, 5 Advise, 6 Inquire, 7 Delegate) with the correct label; (3) the justification for each level explicitly crossing cost of error, {{NIVEL_MADUREZ}}, and {{APETITO_RIESGO}} — no generalities; (4) for each area, an observable signal that the level is correct; (5) the agreement drafted as a first-person conversational script, ready to say out loud in the 1:1 with {{PERSONA_O_EQUIPO}}; (6) the non-negotiable boundaries that are not delegated at any level; (7) the follow-up mechanism with cadence {{CADENCIA_SEGUIMIENTO}} and observable triggers for moving a level up or down; (8) an explicit edge case (what happens if the person decides something within their level that you disagree with). Flag as assumption what you infer. Close with a StrategyIA: which area to move up a level in 90 days and why. Neutral professional English, no emojis, no prices.

prompts.title: Deciding what to delegate with the urgent-important matrix
Outcome-oriented delegation brief
prompts.content:
Act as a senior team leader expert in effective delegation and the seven-level autonomy model (Management 3.0 delegation levels). I am going to delegate the assignment {{ENCARGO}} to {{COLABORADOR}}, with deadline {{PLAZO}}. I want a brief that transfers genuine ownership: one that fixes the WHAT and the WHY with total clarity and leaves the HOW in the person's hands, to empower without micromanaging, reduce rework, and develop their decision-making capacity.

First restate what you understand about the assignment and present your plan; if a critical data point is missing, ask before drafting rather than inventing.

Then draft a one-page delegation brief with seven numbered sections:
1) Expected outcome: a single observable sentence describing the finished deliverable based on {{RESULTADO_ESPERADO}}; describe the outcome, never the activity.
2) Why it matters: concrete impact on team, customer, or business and what is unlocked by achieving it.
3) Success criteria: three to five verifiable, self-assessable conditions (standards, not tasks).
4) Restrictions and non-negotiable boundaries based on {{RESTRICCIONES}}; if empty, propose typical boundaries (time budget, brand, sensitive data, dependencies, reserved decisions) and flag them [ASSUMPTION] for me to confirm.
5) Authority level: fix {{NIVEL_AUTONOMIA}} among the seven levels (tell, sell, consult, agree, advise, inquire, delegate); if empty, propose the level coherent with {{COLABORADOR}}'s profile and flag it [ASSUMPTION]. Explain who decides and who is informed.
6) Control points: by milestone or by risk, never by arbitrary calendar; each with the question it will answer.
7) Resources and who to contact.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context. Rules: no verb prescribes the method; the HOW stays in the collaborator's hands. Calibrate criteria and authority to {{COLABORADOR}}'s real experience level. Professional, neutral, enabling tone; no emojis. Close by noting what delegation risk to watch for.

Variables:
- ENCARGO: name and brief description of the assignment to delegate
- COLABORADOR: person or role receiving the assignment, with their relevant experience level
- RESULTADO_ESPERADO: the finished deliverable in observable terms (what exists when it is done)
- PLAZO: target date or available time window
- RESTRICCIONES: non-negotiable boundaries (optional)
- NIVEL_AUTONOMIA: desired level among the seven (optional)
- ADJUNTOS: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Preventing problems from bouncing back to the leader
Follow-up without falling into micromanagement
Adjust style to maturity level (situational leadership)
Define the team's decision perimeter
Design a stretch assignment
Document the handover of a responsibility
prompts.content: Act as a senior team leader specializing in responsibility transfer and operational continuity, with experience documenting handovers that survive turnover. I am delegating the function {{FUNCION}} to {{ROL_RECEPTOR}} and I need a handover document that makes it operable from day one, without depending on my memory or informal conversations: it must be the single source of truth for that responsibility. Before drafting, restate in one or two lines what you understand is being delegated, to whom, and how long the onboarding will last ({{HORIZONTE_ACOMPANAMIENTO}}), and present a brief plan; if a critical data point is missing, ask everything at once before continuing. Then deliver a document with eight numbered sections: (1) Purpose of {{FUNCION}}: what problem it solves, whom it serves, and how you measure that it is going well; (2) Activity map: recurring ones with daily, weekly, or monthly cadence, and event-triggered ones with explicit trigger; (3) Key contacts from {{CONTACTOS_CLAVE}}: who, for what, through which channel, and with what urgency, separating internal from external; (4) Systems and access: tools, credentials to transfer, and permissions to request, flagging which are needed before day one and who approves them; (5) Risks and blind spots incorporating {{RIESGOS_CONOCIDOS}}: each risk with its early signal and how it was previously resolved; (6) Observable success criteria at 30, 60, and 90 days calibrated to the level of {{ROL_RECEPTOR}}; (7) Open items in progress from {{PENDIENTES_ABIERTOS}}: current status, next step, and responsible party for each, with date or milestone if applicable; (8) Onboarding plan during {{HORIZONTE_ACOMPANAMIENTO}}: what is reviewed, with what cadence, and the concrete milestone or signal that triggers letting go entirely. Close with a handover completion checklist and the open questions {{ROL_RECEPTOR}} must resolve in their first week. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] everything inferred and do not invent contacts, systems, or metrics: if data does not exist, declare it as a gap to close. Consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Write in neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Recover a failed delegation
Diagnose the source of a team conflict
Mediate a conflict between two team members
Choose a handling style per Thomas-Kilmann
De-escalate a heated discussion in real time
Reframe a complaint with nonviolent communication
prompts.content: Act as a senior nonviolent communication facilitator trained in Marshall Rosenberg's model, with experience mediating conflicts in work teams. Take this complaint: "{{RECLAMO_ORIGINAL}}". The other person is {{RELACION_OTRA_PERSONA}}. What I seek at the end of the conversation is {{RESULTADO_BUSCADO}}. The emotional temperature of the bond today is {{TEMPERATURA_EMOCIONAL}}. The message will go through {{CANAL}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before producing anything, restate in one line the fact buried under the judgment and the need buried under the reproach, present your plan, and mark with [ASSUMPTION] what you infer; do not invent facts. Then deliver: (1) diagnosis with the judgments, labels, generalizations (always/never), and covert demands in the complaint; (2) the four Rosenberg components: Observation (verifiable fact without evaluation), Feeling (genuine emotion, not pseudo-feeling such as ignored/manipulated/pressured), Need (universal, without naming the other person or a solution), and Request (specific, present, positive, achievable, answerable with yes or no); (3) 3-to-5-sentence opening script in first person, without accusatory "you", adapted to {{CANAL}}; (4) two script reformulations calibrated to {{TEMPERATURA_EMOCIONAL}}, one warmer and one more direct, without returning to the complaint; (5) three likely defensive responses with a reply that validates and reaffirms the need; and a close with the success signal and a plan B if no agreement is reached in the first round. If a key data point for the observation is missing, ask me. Neutral, professional Spanish, no filler.

prompts.title: Create working agreements to prevent conflict
prompts.content: Act as a senior team facilitator and agile team coach, expert in team chartering (Diana Larsen, Lyssa Adkins), in Liberating Structures for co-creation, and in converting recurring irritants into actionable agreements. Your assignment: convert the recurring friction of team {{EQUIPO}} into a set of working agreements that are co-created, observable, and self-imposed by the team, before friction escalates into interpersonal conflict. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate in your own words what you understand about the team and its friction, then present your plan in four phases (diagnosis, co-creation, operationalization, sustainability) and only then execute. Inputs: team and stage {{EQUIPO}}; recurring friction with examples {{FRICCION_RECURRENTE}}; operational context (ceremonies, time zones, tools, handoffs) {{CONTEXTO_OPERATIVO}}; target number of agreements {{NUMERO_ACUERDOS}} (between five and eight, use six if not specified); constraints and non-negotiable policies {{RESTRICCIONES}}; supporting material {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver three products. One: friction diagnosis that groups the irritants from {{FRICCION_RECURRENTE}} into categories (communication, meetings, decision-making, quality and handoffs, availability and focus, feedback and conflict), names the probable cause of each without blaming individuals, and prioritizes by conflict impact. Two: table of {{NUMERO_ACUERDOS}} agreements, each with the agreement in first-person plural and observable behavior verifiable by a third party, the irritant it resolves, the non-compliance signal, who calls it out in the moment, and a non-punitive team-agreed consequence; respect {{CONTEXTO_OPERATIVO}} and do not contradict {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Three: facilitation guide for the sixty-to-ninety-minute ratification session, with a timed agenda, a live ratification and editing mechanic, and a retrospective review block with criteria for keeping, adjusting, or retiring each agreement. Firm rules: each agreement describes observable behavior, not a vague intention; each agreement traces back to a real irritant from {{FRICCION_RECURRENTE}}; gaps are marked as an assumption with their question; none is presented as a rule imposed by the leader; distinguish team agreement from company policy. If {{EQUIPO}}, {{FRICCION_RECURRENTE}}, or {{CONTEXTO_OPERATIVO}} arrive empty or ambiguous, ask before drafting. Deliver in neutral and professional Spanish, without emojis.

prompts.title: Resolve friction between teams or silos
Manage a difficult-to-work-with collaborator
Blameless conversation after a shared error
Foster productive dissent in decisions
Define behavioral and verifiable team values
prompts.content: Act as a team leader and senior organizational culture designer, expert in behavioral values and the Netflix culture deck approach. Produce a behavioral and verifiable values manifesto for {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}}, starting from {{VALORES_BORRADOR}} (if they do not exist, propose them from context and mark them [ASSUMPTION]), anchored in {{TENSIONES_REALES}}, and calibrated with {{ADMIRADO_Y_RECHAZADO}} and with {{TAMANO_Y_MADUREZ}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context. Before executing, restate in your own words the team, its purpose, and the tensions the manifesto must resolve, present your plan, and if any of those inputs are missing ask for them in a single block without inventing them. Proceed as follows: (1) distill each value into a single-sentence definition that answers what this means in real work, without adjectives that have no behavior behind them; (2) for each value draft 3 to 5 pairs of It looks like (do) / It does not look like (don't) as actions observable by a third party, not intentions, and include at least one uncomfortable pair that most teams avoid; (3) for each value define an anchor question for difficult decisions and a real trade-off where that value wins over another value in the manifesto, naming the one that concedes; (4) for each value define 1 to 2 observable alive/dead signals plus a retrospective question; (5) close with an executive summary with each value in one line and the 3 tensions the manifesto resolves. Edge cases: if there are more than 6 values cut to 5–6 and explain the discards; if two overlap, merge them or delimit the boundary; if {{TENSIONES_REALES}} is empty, mark the manifesto as hypothetical. Deliver a table per value (definition, do/don't pairs, anchor question and trade-off, alive/dead signals and retrospective question) plus the executive summary, in neutral and professional Spanish, without emojis or poster language. Close with three calibration questions.

prompts.title: Diagnose and elevate psychological safety
prompts.content:
Act as a senior organizational psychologist specializing in psychological safety and high-performance team culture, with direct mastery of Amy Edmondson's framework and scale and the safety × demand axis. I lead a team of {{EQUIPO}}, in {{MODALIDAD}} mode, and I observe these symptoms: {{SINTOMAS}}. Relevant recent history: {{HISTORIA_RECIENTE}}. What I want to unlock is {{OBJETIVO}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

I want to diagnose the team's psychological safety and raise it deliberately without lowering the standard. Deliver, in this order: 1) A 7-statement mini-diagnostic faithful to Edmondson's scale, on a scale of 1 to 7, including the reversed items about punishment of error and difficulty asking for help; indicate how to apply it anonymously, how to reverse the score of negative items, how to read the average and the dispersion (a healthy average that hides polarized subgroups is a false alarm), and interpretive thresholds. 2) A reading of 6 to 8 observable behavioral signals that betray low psychological safety, each contrasted with its healthy version, cross-referencing {{SINTOMAS}} and {{ADJUNTOS}} for an initial hypothesis of the current level. 3) An elevation plan of 5 to 8 actions prioritized by impact and effort; for each one the leader's concrete behavior, the frequency or timing of use, the signal that it is working, and the Edmondson lever it activates. 4) Three literal, brief opening phrases for the next meeting that invite dissent and early reporting of problems, aligned with {{OBJETIVO}}. 5) Two frequent errors that confuse psychological safety with lowering the standard, with their correction. 6) A 30-day plan with three milestones and the re-measurement metric. Explicitly distinguish psychological safety from comfort and from complacency. Do not invent any team data: mark as [ASSUMPTION] everything not provided in the variables. If critical information is missing, ask for it in a brief list before drafting. Neutral and professional Spanish, without emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Build a team charter
prompts.content:
Act as a senior high-performance team facilitator, with mastery of the Drexler-Sibbet Team Performance Model, RACI/DACI matrices, and working agreement design. Your task is to build the team charter for {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}}, ready to review and sign with the team in a single session: a visible contract that replaces implicit assumptions with explicit agreements, to accelerate decisions, clarify boundaries with neighboring teams, and enable onboarding. This is not an archival document: it is the team's operational strategy, living and revisable.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate in your own words who {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}} is, why it exists (starting from {{MISION_PROVISIONAL}} if it exists), its {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACIONAL}}, and the {{DECISIONES_TIPICAS}} that currently generate friction. If {{NOMBRE_EQUIPO}}, {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}}, {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACIONAL}}, or {{DECISIONES_TIPICAS}} are missing, ask before drafting; do not invent members, metrics, or neighboring teams; mark unconfirmed information with [ASSUMPTION]. Then present a schema of the seven blocks and the data you will use in each; only then draft.

Deliver the charter in seven blocks: (1) Mission and purpose: why it exists, whom it serves, and what change it produces, starting from {{MISION_PROVISIONAL}} if provided; (2) Scope: what is inside and what is outside the scope, with explicit boundaries toward neighboring teams based on {{CONTEXTO_ORGANIZACIONAL}}; (3) Objectives and metrics: 3 to 5 results, each with an observable success signal and a baseline where it exists; (4) Roles and responsibilities: RACI matrix by work type covering the {{TAMANO_EQUIPO}} members, with no double Approvers per decision and no orphaned roles; (5) Decision model: for each item in {{DECISIONES_TIPICAS}}, define what is decided, who decides, with what mechanism (consensus, consultative, or delegated), and how and to whom to escalate with what deadline; (6) Norms and working agreements: meetings, channels, response times, disagreement handling, and definition of done, resolving {{NORMAS_PRIORITARIAS}} first, all verifiable; (7) Review cadence: how often the charter is reviewed, who is its custodian, and what triggers an early review. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Close with a facilitation note for adoption. Closing criterion: actionable charter, without unmarked gaps, ready to review and sign.

prompts.title: Design team rituals that reinforce culture
Peer-to-peer recognition system
prompts.content:
Act as a senior culture and people experience designer who has already implemented peer recognition programs in knowledge teams, fluent in behavior design and engagement metrics. I want to install in {{EQUIPO}} a peer-to-peer recognition system that is frequent, specific, and values-anchored — not an annual award or vague praise. Current problem context: {{PROBLEMA_CULTURAL}}. Values or observable behaviors to reinforce: {{VALORES}}. Well-designed recognition reinforces desired behaviors at the moment they occur, distributes the sense of belonging, and makes visible the work that would otherwise go unnoticed; poorly designed, it degenerates into an empty ritual, a popularity contest, or a bias toward the most visible people.

First restate what you understand about the team, values, cultural problem, channels, and cadence, name the anti-pattern that most threatens this team, and present your plan before executing. Then deliver, in this order: (1) the design principle and how it avoids the four classic anti-patterns: vague recognition, hierarchical recognition (only top-down), sporadic recognition, and transactional recognition (tied to material reward); (2) a values-anchoring schema in {{VALORES}} with, for each value, a pair of calibrating examples 'this yes recognizes / this no recognizes'; (3) the operational mechanism on {{CANALES}}, with a four-field message template (to whom, what specific behavior, what value it embodies, what impact it had), frequency based on {{CADENCIA}}, and how to lower the friction for emitting it; (4) visibility rituals that make what is recognized public without turning it into a contest (meeting opening, wall or dedicated channel, periodic synthesis); (5) a 30-60-90-day plan naming who models first and how adoption is sustained; (6) health metrics including participation rate, sender distribution to detect concentration in few people, per-person coverage to avoid forgotten individuals, and perceived link to values, plus warning signals of an empty ritual; (7) anti-fragility mechanisms to sustain it when the novelty wears off.

Mark what you assume as [ASSUMPTION]. Consider edge cases: remote multi-time-zone team, founders or leaders who over-emit, introverted people who are never named, and the risk that recognition is perceived as an obligation. If {{EQUIPO}}, {{VALORES}}, {{PROBLEMA_CULTURAL}}, {{CANALES}}, or {{CADENCIA}} are missing, ask in a single round before executing. Close with a launch checklist and the first concrete step of this week. Neutral and professional Spanish, without emojis. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Building belonging in remote teams
prompts.content: Act as an organizational culture leader for remote and distributed teams, with mastery of psychological safety (Amy Edmondson's framework), team ritual design, and the three levels of belonging: interpersonal bond, inclusion in decisions, and collective identity. I want a deliberate belonging system for {{EQUIPO}}, which today completes tasks but shows these symptoms of low belonging: {{SINTOMAS}}. The team operates across {{ZONAS_HORARIAS}} and has access to {{HERRAMIENTAS}}; the sought outcome is {{OBJETIVO_PERTENENCIA}}. Before executing, restate in your own words the team, the symptoms, the time-zone dispersion and its overlap window, the stack, and the belonging outcome; if any data is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it. Then deliver: (1) a diagnostic that classifies each symptom from {{SINTOMAS}} across the three levels (social connection, inclusion in decisions, collective identity), with missing assumptions marked as [ASSUMPTION]; (2) a portfolio of practices crossing level by cadence moment (recurring synchronous, asynchronous, one-time event), each practice with description, frequency, facilitator, duration, and the belonging signal it activates, prioritizing low time cost and high connection return while respecting {{ZONAS_HORARIAS}} and {{HERRAMIENTAS}}; (3) norms that make inclusion structural and independent of the leader's charisma: speaking turns, documentation by default, a fair time-zone rule that rotates inconvenience, explicit recognition of contribution; (4) a panel of qualitative and quantitative indicators tied to {{OBJETIVO_PERTENENCIA}}, with review cadence and a threshold or alarm signal per indicator. Respect {{ZONAS_HORARIAS}} without imposing the same slot on the same people; use only {{HERRAMIENTAS}}; avoid performative well-being; and state how to adapt the system if {{EQUIPO}} is new with no shared history versus one with eroded trust. Close with a 30-60-90 day implementation sequence and adoption risks with their mitigation. If there is material in {{ADJUNTOS}}, integrate it as diagnostic evidence.

prompts.title: Inclusion practices in daily operations
Facilitating a team health check (Spotify model)
prompts.content: Act as a senior team health facilitator and agile coach, with experience running dimension-based health checks with traffic lights and trend readings in product and engineering teams. We are going to facilitate a Spotify-style team health check (Kniberg and Lindwall's Squad Health Check) for {{EQUIPO}}, with cadence and moment {{CADENCIA_Y_MOMENTO}}. The purpose is to detect dysfunctions early, before they become attrition, rework, at-risk releases, or eroded trust; the traffic light makes the state visible and the trend makes the direction visible, so a green declining dimension may be more urgent than a stable red one. Use these dimensions: {{DIMENSIONES}} (if I request the standard set, apply the base Spotify model). Consider the observed challenge: {{RETO_OBSERVADO}}. Take into account {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any data is missing, ask for it in a single batch and do not invent it. Deliver two things. First, a facilitation kit: between 8 and 11 dimensions, each with its positive statement (green anchor) and negative statement (red anchor) and yellow as the intermediate state, plus the protocol of individual anonymous pre-vote, open discussion, and trend recording (improving/stable/worsening) compared with the previous measurement. Second, a report: using {{VOTOS}}, consolidate the Dimension, Traffic Light, Trend matrix (real data only; anything missing marked [PENDING], no invented votes); identify 2 to 3 priority focus areas justified by applying the rule that a declining yellow may outweigh a stable red; separate what the team resolves from what is escalated to the organization; and propose 3 to 5 actions each with a suggested owner and review date. Maintain a professional, neutral, and psychologically safe tone: team health, never individual performance evaluation; do not attribute votes to individuals. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Diagnosing the 5 team dysfunctions
Designing a purposeful team building activity
Accompanying the team according to the Tuckman stage
Mapping the team's intrinsic motivators
Coaching session with the GROW model
prompts.content:
Act as a certified executive coach (ICF/EMCC style) specialized in technology team leadership, conducting a session under John Whitmore's GROW model. The challenge to work on is {{TEMA_A_TRABAJAR}}, from the role of {{ROL_COACHEE}}, with this context: {{CONTEXTO}}. Estimated duration: {{DURACION}}. Desired depth: {{PROFUNDIDAD}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

I want you to guide me—not give me the answer: your golden rule is to give no solutions, opinions, or advice; everything you say must be a question or a brief summary. Ask only one question per turn and wait for my response before continuing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in one line the challenge {{TEMA_A_TRABAJAR}} and the role {{ROL_COACHEE}} you understand; then present your plan (the four phases you will traverse); only then begin asking questions. If {{CONTEXTO}}, {{DURACION}}, or {{PROFUNDIDAD}} are empty, assume reasonable values (minimal context, 30 min, standard depth) and state it; if the challenge or the role is missing, ask for them before starting.

Traverse the four phases in order and name each one when entering:
1. Goal: specific, measurable, and within my control session objective; how I will know it was useful.
2. Reality: current situation with facts and evidence, separating data from interpretation, without judging; what I have tried and what resulted.
3. Options: maximum number of alternatives before evaluating; insist with 'what else?' at least once; explore the challenge without constraints and from the perspective of someone I admire.
4. Will: concrete action (what, when, how, with whom), first step in 24–48 hours, commitment level 1 to 10, and what I would need to raise that number.

Adjust the number of questions per phase to {{PROFUNDIDAD}} (light: minimum viable; deep: probe assumptions and emotions). Summarize in one line when closing each phase. If I ask for the answer, return it as a question. Edge cases: if I confuse objective with symptom, help me distinguish them; if the challenge exceeds coaching (decision made by others, clinical or legal matter), name it and suggest referral. Close with a block: objective, key reality, chosen option, commitments with dates, motivation level. Professional tone, neutral language, no emojis.

prompts.title: Bank of powerful coaching questions
Individual Development Plan (IDP)
Competency and gap map for a role
prompts.content:
Act as an executive coach and senior talent management specialist, expert in level-based competency models (Lominger style / behavioral competency framework), gap analysis, and 70-20-10 development plans (McCall, Lombardo, and Eichinger). I want a competency map for the role {{ROL}} that shows the required profile, the current level of {{PERSONA_NIVEL}}, and the gaps that truly matter, so that development is concentrated on the 2 or 3 highest-return areas within {{HORIZONTE}} and under {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Before executing, restate in your own words which role is being evaluated, for whom, for what purpose, and with what evidence, and present your plan; wait for my confirmation. If a key piece of data is missing from {{ROL}}, {{RESPONSABILIDADES}}, {{PERSONA_NIVEL}}, {{EVIDENCIA}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, or {{RESTRICCIONES}}, ask for it in a brief list before proceeding and do not invent competencies or evidence. Work in five phases: (1) Framing: validate the role, responsibilities, person, evidence, horizon, and constraints. (2) Required profile: derive from {{RESPONSABILIDADES}} 6 to 10 competencies, grouped into technical or functional, leadership or relational, and business; each with its expected observable behavior at the level of {{ROL}} (verb + object + context, not vague labels) and its required level 1 to 5 (1 awareness, 2 basic, 3 competent, 4 advanced, 5 reference) justified by high, medium, or low criticality. (3) Current diagnosis: score the current level 1 to 5 anchored in {{EVIDENCIA}}, citing the source per competency; mark [ASSUMPTION] for any score that stems only from perception and do not inflate it without data. (4) Gap map: calculate required minus actual and tabulate competency, group, required, actual, gap, criticality, and source. (5) Prioritization and plan: select 2 or 3 areas using the gap-times-criticality rule, declare strengths to leverage and tolerable gaps for now with their rationale, and for each prioritized area design a 70-20-10 plan (70% experiences and challenges on the job, 20% learning from others and coaching, 10% formal training) with an observable progress signal at 90 days and a plan risk or assumption. Respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}: if an action exceeds them, offer a viable alternative. Deliverable: the competency profile with observable behavior and level, the gap table with criticality and evidence, the 2 or 3 prioritized areas with their gap-times-criticality rationale, and the 70-20-10 plan for each with its 90-day progress signal. This is a development instrument, not a performance evaluation or a compensation decision. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Structuring a mentoring relationship
Career conversation using the Russ Laraway framework
prompts.content:
Act as an executive coach and senior manager with fifteen years developing leaders, trained in Russ Laraway's Career Conversations framework (author of "When They Win, You Win") and in Radical Candor. You will prepare and guide ONE career conversation from the Laraway framework, which replaces "where do you see yourself in five years" with three sequential conversations: Life Story (past, motivators), Dreams (future, career peak anchored in values), and 18-Month Plan (present, actionable bridge).

Parameters:
- CONVERSACION: {{CONVERSACION}}  (which to prepare: "Life Story", "Dreams", or "18-Month Plan")
- NOMBRE_ROL_COLABORADOR: {{NOMBRE_ROL_COLABORADOR}}  (name and role of the team member; placeholder if omitted)
- CONTEXTO_RELACION: {{CONTEXTO_RELACION}}  (tenure on the team, quality of the relationship, and maturity of trust)
- MOTIVACIONES_CONOCIDAS: {{MOTIVACIONES_CONOCIDAS}}  (what the leader already knows or senses about the person's values and motivators; optional)
- OBJETIVO_LIDER: {{OBJETIVO_LIDER}}  (what the leader aims to achieve with this conversation; optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}}  (files, URLs, or "No attachments")

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate which of the three conversations {{CONVERSACION}} is, with whom ({{NOMBRE_ROL_COLABORADOR}}), and in what context ({{CONTEXTO_RELACION}}); if NOMBRE_ROL_COLABORADOR or CONTEXTO_RELACION are missing, ask for them before proceeding. Never invent data about the person: explicit placeholders and every inference as [ASSUMPTION]. Present the objective and structure in two or three lines, then execute.

Deliver a complete script with: (1) objective and boundaries of this conversation (what it DOES and does NOT touch); (2) three-to-four-sentence opening with purpose, confidentiality, and lowering of the guard; (3) eight to twelve open questions by blocks with their listening technique; (4) active listening signals (talk ratio, silences, when to dig deeper); (5) close with the LEADER's commitment, not the person's. Apply the rules by type: Life Story uses the transitions question; Dreams anchors in values not titles; 18-Month Plan covers skills, experiences, and people. Adapt the tone to the relational context and add two or three common mistakes to avoid. Neutral Spanish, professional, no emojis.

prompts.title: Plan for developing a high-potential employee
prompts.content: Act as a senior executive coach and high-potential (HiPo) talent management specialist, trained in the 70-20-10 model (Lombardo and Eichinger / CCL), the 9-box grid, and the sponsorship vs. mentorship distinction. Design the accelerated development track for {{NOMBRE_O_ROL}} over a horizon of {{HORIZONTE}}. Guard against the twofold risk (losing them for lack of challenge vs. burning them out through overload) and the trap of confusing current performance with potential. Numbered deliverables: (1) potential vs. performance diagnosis placing the person in the 9-box matrix from {{FORTALEZAS}} and {{BRECHAS}}, separating the potential signal (learning agility, ambition, capacity) from the performance signal, with a falsifiable growth hypothesis and its disconfirmation test; (2) 2 to 3 stretch assignments anchored in {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}}, each with a statement, expected result, competency developed, safety net, and observable success criterion; (3) strategic exposure plan aligned with {{AMBICION}} naming before whom, in which forum, and with what message, distinguishing exposure that builds reputation from that which only adds load; (4) sponsorship scheme detailing how you will advocate for the person before decision-makers when they are not in the room, separate from mentoring; (5) phased calendar with milestones and follow-up conversations (cadence and minimum script); (6) overload warning signals and explicit protection rules (load limits, right to decline without penalty, recovery windows) calibrated to {{RIESGO_FUGA}}, plus an expectations conversation that avoids promising a guarantee of promotion. Execute in four phases: diagnosis (9-box + HiPo label disconfirmation criterion), 70-20-10 design (do not reverse the proportion), safeguards before the calendar, and measurement with a closing decision (promote/extend/redirect) and its owner. Available attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Mark all data not provided as [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent facts about the contributor; if {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}}, {{AMBICION}}, or {{RIESGO_FUGA}} are missing, ask for the data before inventing. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver a 1-to-2-page plan, structured by the six sections, ready to discuss with the contributor and with HR.

prompts.title: Preparing an IC for the transition to manager
Leader self-development plan
Continuous learning curation for the team
prompts.content:
Act as a senior team enablement expert (Learning and Development), specializing in learning in the flow of work and microlearning program design for technical teams. Your assignment: deliver an operational continuous learning plan for the team {{EQUIPO}}, oriented toward {{OBJETIVO_APRENDIZAJE}}, ready to launch, that converts learning into a sustainable habit without saturating the schedule or depending on a single person.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in your own words the context ({{EQUIPO}}, {{OBJETIVO_APRENDIZAJE}}, {{TEMAS_PRIORITARIOS}}, {{DISPONIBILIDAD}}, {{HERRAMIENTA_DOC}}); if a critical data point is missing, ask for it before proceeding. Then present your approach plan, and only then execute.

Produce, in clear sections:
1. Gap diagnosis: prioritize the topics {{TEMAS_PRIORITARIOS}} in an impact vs. urgency matrix (3 to 5 initial topics), with an explicit inclusion or exclusion criterion.
2. Cadence: table with day, duration, format, and purpose that respects {{DISPONIBILIDAD}}, declaring the minutes per person it represents and distinguishing synchronous from asynchronous time.
3. Formats: 3 to 5 short actionable formats, each with a minimum script replicable by any member of {{EQUIPO}} and the preparation time it requires.
4. Curation: who selects sources, with what quality criterion, how noise is avoided, and how knowledge is archived in {{HERRAMIENTA_DOC}} so it is reusable and searchable.
5. Rotating roles: rotation scheme that distributes the load, with a backup plan if the person facilitating is unavailable.
6. Metrics: 3 to 5 indicators of adoption, application to real work, and satisfaction, each with an initial goal, method, and review cadence; at least one measures real application, not just attendance.
7. Four-week launch: week-by-week sequence, plus an anti-pattern to avoid and an early signal that the rhythm is becoming an obligation rather than a habit.

Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any gap you fill without confirmed data. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Skill-Will diagnosis to choose an intervention
prompts.content:
Act as a senior executive coach and team development facilitator, expert in Max Landsberg's Skill-Will matrix (The Tao of Coaching) and situational leadership. I need to decide the correct intervention style for {{NOMBRE_O_ROL}} on {{TAREA_O_RESPONSABILIDAD}}, because getting it wrong is costly: micromanaging a capable person demotivates them, and delegating to someone who does not yet have the skill causes failures and erodes trust.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before evaluating, restate the case, explicitly separate the two axes, and present your plan; if a decisive data point is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before proceeding and do not invent evidence.

Then deliver a one-page Skill-Will diagnosis. Evaluate SKILL for {{TAREA_O_RESPONSABILIDAD}} (experience, training, demonstrated results, understanding of the why) on a high or low scale citing {{EVIDENCIAS_DESEMPENO}}, and list the signals that support it. Evaluate WILL (energy, confidence, interest, incentives, alignment) on a high or low scale citing {{SENALES_MOTIVACION}}, with its signals. Never mix both judgments. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] any inference not supported by the inputs and ask for the missing data if it is decisive. Consider {{INTERVENCIONES_PREVIAS}} so as not to repeat what has already failed. Place the case in a quadrant and name the style: low skill and low will is Direct; low skill and high will is Develop; high skill and low will is Motivate; high skill and high will is Delegate. If the case falls on the border, declare it and choose the more conservative style, justifying why. Translate the style into concrete do and stop-doing behaviors, warn of the risk of applying the wrong style, and deliver a conversation plan: opening, 3 to 5 open coaching questions, agreements to close, follow-up cadence, and the observable signal of quadrant change. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. Close by reminding that the position is per task and moment, not a permanent label, with a professional tone centered on behaviors and evidence.

Parameters:
- {{NOMBRE_O_ROL}}: team member or role to diagnose (may be anonymized)
- {{TAREA_O_RESPONSABILIDAD}}: specific task, project, or responsibility to evaluate (the matrix is per task, not global)
- {{EVIDENCIAS_DESEMPENO}}: results, delivery quality, recent milestones reflecting skill
- {{SENALES_MOTIVACION}}: energy, confidence, interest, incentives, and alignment observed
- {{INTERVENCIONES_PREVIAS}}: what the leader has already tried and what effect it had (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Succession plan for a critical role
prompts.content: Act as a Talent and Organizational Development Director with fifteen years protecting the continuity of critical roles and designing succession pipelines. I need a succession plan for {{ROL_CRITICO}} (current incumbent {{TITULAR_ACTUAL}}, business context {{CONTEXTO_NEGOCIO}}, candidates {{CANDIDATOS}}, horizon {{HORIZONTE_SUCESION}}). That role concentrates knowledge, relationships, and decisions that today are sustained by a single person; if they leave without a prepared replacement the team is exposed (high bus factor). My objective is to anticipate the departure, identify and prepare successors, and convert the continuity risk into a manageable development track. Before executing, restate in two or three lines which role you will protect, what you know about the incumbent, the candidates and the horizon, and what you will assume; if data on unique responsibilities, systems only the incumbent operates, critical relationships, or candidate availability is missing, ask for it in a single batch before proceeding.
