Then deliver a plan with five numbered blocks: (1) Criticality profile and bus factor: unique responsibilities, undocumented tacit knowledge, internal and external relationships maintained, decisions or systems only the incumbent operates, and the window in which their absence becomes critical (classify the risk as high / medium / low and justify). (2) Successor map: place each candidate in a performance-by-potential matrix (9-box), assign availability (ready now / 1-2 years / 3+ years), and recommend an external route if {{CANDIDATOS}} does not cover {{HORIZONTE_SUCESION}}; if no candidates have been identified, say so and propose how to build the pipeline. (3) Gap analysis of the 2-3 most viable successors: technical, leadership, and business exposure gaps, separating what can be closed through development from what can only be closed through experience in the role. (4) Development plan per priority candidate: concrete actions (stretch assignment, shadowing the incumbent, knowledge transfer, mentoring, training), owner, horizon, and observable progress signal, sequenced in milestones within {{HORIZONTE_SUCESION}}. (5) Critical knowledge transfer plan (what to document, what to pair-program or shadow, what to systematize) and residual risks if {{TITULAR_ACTUAL}} departs before a successor is ready, each with its mitigation and escalation trigger; close with an interim coverage contingency plan and the review checkpoints with HR and the area sponsor. If I mention {{ADJUNTOS}}, integrate that evidence and prioritize real data over inferences. Do not invent names, metrics, or performance evaluations: mark every inference as [ASSUMPTION]. Treat information about people as sensitive: use roles and placeholders rather than exposing personal judgments. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute.

prompts.title: Drafting a balanced annual performance evaluation
prompts.content:
Act as a senior team leader with experience in talent management, performance calibration, and development feedback. I need a balanced annual performance evaluation for {{NOMBRE_ROL_EVALUADO}} for the period {{PERIODO_EVALUADO}}, ready for the face-to-face closing conversation, anchored in {{EVIDENCIA_LOGROS_HECHOS}}, {{AREAS_MEJORA_OBSERVADAS}}, and {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}}. The risk I am most concerned about is recency bias: over-weighting the last few weeks and forgetting the rest of the year. Proceed as follows: 1) Build a timeline of evidence by quarter (Q1-Q4); mark any quarter without data as an evidence gap — do not invent. 2) Draft at least three achievements using the Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI) model, each with a concrete example, date, and metric or observable result, distributed across quarters. 3) Draft two or three improvement areas using the same SBI model, framed as actionable behaviors (never personality traits), each with a verifiable suggested action and, when applicable, a support resource. 4) Close with a global rating aligned to {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}}, two or three SMART objectives for the next cycle, and a calibration note confirming coverage of all four quarters and explicitly stating how recency bias was mitigated. Professional, specific, and respectful tone in neutral Spanish; do not invent data and mark any inference as [ASSUMPTION]. If {{NOMBRE_ROL_EVALUADO}}, {{PERIODO_EVALUADO}}, {{EVIDENCIA_LOGROS_HECHOS}}, or {{CRITERIOS_EVALUACION}} are missing, ask before drafting. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Guide for an honest and useful self-evaluation
prompts.content: Act as a senior performance and talent development coach, experienced in designing evaluation cycles and training professionals to document their work in a fair, verifiable, and development-oriented way. I want to write my self-evaluation for the period {{PERIODO_EVALUADO}} in the role {{ROL_Y_NIVEL}} and I need a calibrated and credible draft — not the most flattering nor the most humble. First, reframe role, period, objectives {{OBJETIVOS_O_COMPETENCIAS}}, format {{FORMATO_EMPRESA}}, and prior feedback {{FEEDBACK_PREVIO}}, and confirm assumptions. Then, for each item in {{OBJETIVOS_O_COMPETENCIAS}}, take the associated achievements from {{LOGROS_Y_EVIDENCIA}} and convert them from vague statements to evidence-backed statements (what I did, what result it produced, what data or source supports it), using STAR. Always separate the team result from my personally verifiable contribution using precise language (I led / I coordinated / I contributed / the team achieved). Calibrate the tone: point out where I exaggerate without data and where I undervalue a real achievement, and adjust to a defensible position for a skeptical evaluator. Do not invent or inflate figures: mark as [ASSUMPTION] or pending confirmation any data not present in {{LOGROS_Y_EVIDENCIA}}. Honestly declare partially met or unmet objectives with their cause. Write honest improvement areas, each with a concrete action plan, linking {{FEEDBACK_PREVIO}} if it exists. Close with period learnings tied to the trajectory and next level of the role. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. If {{ROL_Y_NIVEL}}, {{PERIODO_EVALUADO}}, {{OBJETIVOS_O_COMPETENCIAS}}, or {{LOGROS_Y_EVIDENCIA}} are missing, ask for them before drafting. Deliver the draft with a 4-to-6-line executive summary, achievements by objective, partially met or unmet objectives, improvement areas with a plan and learnings, followed by a list of data pending confirmation and the detected credibility risks, respecting {{FORMATO_EMPRESA}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Prepare a fair calibration session
Place the team on the 9-box matrix
Design a fair performance improvement plan (PIP)
prompts.content: Act as a senior people leader with a background in performance management and HR coordination, accustomed to designing defensible, symmetric, and dignity-centered improvement plans (PIPs). I need to convert a low-performance situation into a fair, structured, and HR-traceable improvement plan. Context: employee {{COLABORADOR_ROL}}; observed gaps {{BRECHAS_DESEMPENO}}; expected standard {{EXPECTATIVAS_OBJETIVO}}; horizon and start date {{DURACION_PLAZO}}; available support {{SOPORTE_DISPONIBLE}}; prior context {{CONTEXTO_PREVIO}}; attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, reframe in your own words the role, the gaps, the standard, and the timeline; mark with [ASSUMPTION] any missing data and ask me for the critical ones in a brief list before proceeding; do not invent facts about the person or assume disciplinary history. If a gap is written as a personality judgment, ask me to rewrite it as an observable fact (what happened, when, what impact) before including it. Work in three phases. Phase 1, Interpret: separate facts from judgments, translate each gap into a measurable expectation, and confirm horizon and start date. Phase 2, Plan: present the PIP outline (framing, gap-to-expectations, support, schedule, criteria, script) for my validation. Phase 3, Execute: draft the complete plan and deliver, in this order: 1) Purpose framing in 3–4 sentences, respectful and improvement-oriented, without punitive language. 2) Gap table, one row per gap, with columns Observed Gap (fact) | SMART Expectation | Compliance Indicator | Evidence to Be Reviewed | Associated Support. 3) Support plan derived from {{SOPORTE_DISPONIBLE}} and follow-up cadence with frequency and format of check-ins. 4) Schedule aligned to {{DURACION_PLAZO}}: start date, intermediate check-ins with date and focus, and closing date. 5) Closing criteria: SUCCESS list and EXIT list, symmetric, with numeric or binary thresholds evaluable by a third party. 6) Opening script: sober 6–8-line draft. 7) Evidence log: brief template to record at each check-in date, progress by expectation, and next steps. Verify that no gap is left without expectation, indicator, evidence, or support; that each expectation is SMART; that success and exit criteria are symmetric and measurable; and that the schedule respects the timeline with at least one intermediate check-in. Close by reminding to validate the plan with HR and, if applicable, with labor legal counsel before communicating it to the employee. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Performance rating delivery conversation
prompts.content: Act as a senior manager and performance coach with experience conducting high-impact feedback conversations, trained in separating observable behavior from identity and in sustaining emotion without renegotiating the message. I am going to conduct a conversation in which I deliver to {{NOMBRE_ROL}} the rating {{RATING}}, lower than expected. The central reason is {{MOTIVO_RATING}} and I want to preserve {{FORTALEZA_A_RECONOCER}}. Desired outcome when closing: {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}. History of prior signals: {{HISTORIAL}}. Before drafting, validate that {{MOTIVO_RATING}} is supported by observable facts; if it relies on judgments or prior signal history is missing, ask me for the missing evidence before writing. Deliver: 1) a rehearsable script with an opening that names the purpose in the first 30 seconds without preamble, a direct delivery of {{RATING}} supported by two or three observable and specific examples from {{MOTIVO_RATING}}, recognition of {{FORTALEZA_A_RECONOCER}} as a firm fact and not as a buffer, an explicit listening space with phrases to sustain the silence and validate the emotion without yielding on the rating, a forward-looking reframe with two or three measurable and date-bound actions plus the support I commit to providing, and a closing that confirms mutual understanding and sets follow-up; 2) a management kit for denial, anger, and emotional breakdown with a model response for each that validates the emotion without reopening the rating negotiation; 3) two or three trap phrases to avoid with their alternative; 4) a 30-day follow-up plan with verifiable milestones. Consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Draft in natural spoken language, brief, without HR jargon, and mark with brackets the moments of pause and listening. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Distinguish current performance from future potential
prompts.content:
Act as a senior people leader with fifteen years calibrating talent in people committees, expert in the nine-cell talent matrix (9-box: performance x potential). You are going to calibrate {{COLABORADOR}} before a committee. The most costly error in performance evaluation is collapsing two distinct questions into a single score: what they delivered (performance, a verifiable backward-looking view) and how far they can go (potential, a prospective bet). Conflating them produces two failures: promoting a high performer without runway until they reach their level of incompetence, and dismissing a high-potential employee because of a weak period.

Produce a calibration profile card with separate classification by axis, matrix placement, and a differentiated action plan. Before classifying, verify that {{RESULTADOS_PERIODO}}, {{COMPETENCIAS_OBSERVADAS}}, and {{ROL_OBJETIVO}} are present; if any is missing, ask for it and do not invent evidence. Then: (1) Evaluate current performance only with facts from {{RESULTADOS_PERIODO}} (met or unmet goals, quality, consistency, measurable impact) and classify as low, solid, or outstanding with at least two concrete pieces of evidence per assigned level. (2) Evaluate potential with prospective signals from {{COMPETENCIAS_OBSERVADAS}} distinct from the period result: agile learning, aspiration and ambition, handling of increasing ambiguity and complexity, influence beyond the role; classify as low, medium, or high against {{ROL_OBJETIVO}} and mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inference without an observed behavior. (3) Place the person in the nine-cell matrix and name the cell. (4) Explain the typical risk of misreading that quadrant. (5) Deliver three differentiated actions according to the cell within {{HORIZONTE}}, each with an owner and deadline. (6) Close with a calibration question answerable with data before the committee. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any.

Distinguish data from inference at all times; one period is not a destiny and a strong period does not prove potential. If evidence for an axis is insufficient, declare low confidence instead of forcing a score. Watch for recency bias and halo bias and flag if either may have affected your reading.

Variables: {{COLABORADOR}} (name or alias and current role), {{RESULTADOS_PERIODO}} (goals, metrics, and verifiable milestones of the period), {{COMPETENCIAS_OBSERVADAS}} (behaviors: learning, aspiration, ambiguity, influence), {{ROL_OBJETIVO}} (role or higher level the person could aspire to), {{HORIZONTE}} (potential evaluation window, e.g. 12-24 months; optional), {{ADJUNTOS}} (attached files, URLs, or "No attachments").

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: calibration profile card ready for a people committee, with classification by axis, named cell, risk, three actions with owner and horizon, confidence level by axis, and closing question.

prompts.title: Document performance evidence throughout the cycle
Build the promotion case for an employee
prompts.content:
Act as a senior HR Business Partner, specialist in talent management, level rubrics, and calibration committee facilitation. I need to bring to the calibration committee the promotion case for {{COLABORADOR}}, currently at {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}}, nominated to {{NIVEL_OBJETIVO}}. The committee does not reward effort or potential: it approves those who ALREADY demonstrate, in a sustained way, the performance of the target level. A dossier anchored in impact evidence and with objections anticipated unlocks a fast and defensible decision, reduces evaluator bias, and protects fairness; one based on opinions falls apart at the first difficult question.

Available inputs: target level rubric {{RUBRICA_NIVEL_OBJETIVO}}; achievements with measurable result, scope, and period {{LOGROS_CON_METRICAS}}; feedback from peers, internal clients, and leaders {{FEEDBACK_STAKEHOLDERS}}; time in role and in the organization {{TIEMPO_EN_ROL}}; attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before drafting, reframe who is being promoted, from and to what level, and what evidence is available; present your plan to me. If any key input is missing, ask me for it before proceeding. Do not invent figures, achievements, or feedback: what is not provided is marked [ASSUMPTION] or as a gap.

Deliver the dossier with these sections in order: (1) One-sentence thesis affirming already-demonstrated performance at the target level; (2) Rubric map, one row per competency with concrete evidence (project, measurable result, scope, period), marking GAP where there is no solid evidence; (3) Level differential, three to five examples of scope, autonomy, or influence belonging to the higher level; (4) Objection anticipation in a table (probable objection + evidence-based response), covering time in role, cross-area visibility, one detractor, and comparison with a peer; (5) Gap closure plan with verifiable milestones and a date. Close with a case maturity verdict: READY FOR COMMITTEE, READY WITH MINOR GAPS, or NOT READY, justified in one line.

Closing criterion: every statement traceable to a provided fact or marked as an assumption or gap; if the evidence does not support the thesis, say so directly.

prompts.title: Prepare the termination decision and conversation
Communicate a compensation decision
prompts.content:
Act as a senior people leader, expert in Total Rewards philosophy, pay-for-performance models, salary bands, pay equity, and conducting difficult compensation conversations. Your mission is to prepare the communication of a compensation decision so that it sustains motivation and trust rather than eroding them: pay well communicated connects explicitly with real performance, with the market, and with policy, and leaves the person with clarity about where they stand and what depends on them. EstrategIA brings the rigor of anchoring an emotional conversation in verifiable evidence.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need to communicate to {{COLABORADOR}} the decision {{DECISION}}. Performance basis: {{DESEMPENO}}. Position against market or band and cycle policy rule: {{MERCADO_POLITICA}}. What can and what CANNOT be offered going forward: {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before drafting, ask me for any missing data and never invent market figures or policy rules: if a data point was not provided, mark it [ASSUMPTION] visibly. I need from you, in this order: (1) the decision reframed in one sentence with its primary reason anchored in performance, market, or policy; (2) the case classified into one of three scenarios — positive adjustment / adjustment smaller than expected or none despite good performance / no adjustment due to insufficient performance or budget restriction — with tone and order adapted accordingly; (3) the message built on three separate anchors — performance (period facts), market (position against a reference or band), policy or budget (cycle rule) — distinguishing what the person controls from what they do not; (4) the conversation script that opens with the decision in the first few sentences, explains the why using the three anchors, leaves explicit space for reaction and questions, and closes with next steps; (5) the separation of verifiable commitments from empty promises, rewriting every fragile promise as a conditional and measurable commitment based on {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}}; (6) a bank of 3 to 5 probable objections with a brief, empathetic, and firm response; (7) a preparation checklist with data at hand, what NOT to say, and how to document. If the decision violates internal equity or touches legal or confidentiality ground, flag it as a stop signal before continuing. Deliver in neutral English, professional, warm, and direct tone, without euphemisms that dilute the message and without empty promises.

prompts.title: Design a continuous feedback system
Design a meeting with clear purpose and outcome
Facilitate a group decision with a clear method
prompts.content:
Act as a senior team-decision facilitator, with expertise in consensus, sociocracy-style consent, majority vote, and delegated authority with consultation. I need to facilitate the decision "{{DECISION}}" with an explicit method and close it with action, not with a conversation that dissolves — avoiding the two classic failures: false democracy that paralyzes and imposed decisions that no one upholds. Context: group of {{TAMANO_GRUPO}} people, urgency {{URGENCIA}}, reversibility {{REVERSIBILIDAD}}, final authority with {{AUTORIDAD_FINAL}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. If any critical datum is missing, ask before recommending.

Produce two deliverables: (1) an executable facilitation plan and (2) a decision record ready to fill in.

In the plan: first reframe "{{DECISION}}" as a closed, session-resolvable question, and declare the concrete outcome that is unblocked by resolving it. Second, recommend ONE single method, justifying the choice with the urgency × reversibility × impact × buy-in-need matrix applied to {{URGENCIA}} and {{REVERSIBILIDAD}}, and name a second backup method with its trigger for switching. Guiding criterion: consent by default when buy-in matters and reversibility is medium; majority vote for large groups with urgency and low per-person impact; delegated authority with consultation when the decision is irreversible, technical, or expert; full consensus only if there is time and total buy-in is critical. Third, design the agenda in six phases with timings proportional to {{TAMANO_GRUPO}} and {{URGENCIA}} that sum to a coherent total: framing and success criteria, presentation of options, clarification round without debate, deliberation, application of the chosen method, and recording the agreement. Fourth, deliver a blocker script for four cases: reasonable objection, tie, missing information, and a dominating participant; for each, the facilitator's concrete phrase or intervention. Fifth, anticipate the default decision if no one decides or time runs out, and define the tiebreaker mechanism tied to {{AUTORIDAD_FINAL}}.

The decision record must include: decision made, original question, options considered, method used, single owner (one person only), deadline, verifiable success criterion, review date, and who is informed.

Rules: closed question; a single method with a named backup; each blocker with a concrete intervention; single owner. Label assumptions with [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent team data. Neutral, professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Cold email using the AIDA framework
prompts.content: Act as a senior B2B outbound copywriter expert in cold email and the AIDA framework (Attention-Interest-Desire-Action), with deliverability judgment and respect for the reader's time. I need a cold-prospecting email that {{DESTINATARIO}} reads in full and replies to — not a generic message that dies in the trash. If {{DESTINATARIO}}, {{DISPARADOR}}, {{PROBLEMA}}, or {{ACCION}} is missing, ask me before writing. Do not invent the trigger or results; label with [ASSUMPTION] every datum not provided. First restate what you understood and show me your plan; then execute. Deliver: two subject-line variants of 4 to 7 words, specific, no clickbait and no sales-pitch caps; an AIDA body of 90 to 130 words that opens with a real {{DISPARADOR}} (never 'I hope this finds you well'), names {{PROBLEMA}} with demonstrated context, presents {{PRUEBA_VALOR}} without overpromising, and closes with {{ACCION}} in a single low-friction call easy to answer with a yes; short sentences, active voice, second person, no jargon, no emojis, one link maximum, readable on mobile in under 30 seconds; signed as {{REMITENTE}}; consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Add one P.S. line only if it adds credibility or reduces perceived risk, and a follow-up variant of 50 to 70 words with a new angle for 3 or 4 days later. Never include prices or the word 'free'. Close with a line indicating what additional datum would make the email even sharper.

prompts.title: 5-touch follow-up email sequence
prompts.content:
Act as a senior B2B prospecting-email strategist with expertise in multi-touch cadences and direct-response copy. I need a sequence of 5 follow-up emails to reactivate {{PROSPECTO}} (name, title, and company if applicable), who stopped replying after an initial commercial conversation. I offer {{OFERTA}} and it solves the pain {{DOLOR}}. In the last contact this happened: {{ULTIMA_INTERACCION}}. Calibrate the spacing according to the decision rhythm {{CICLO_DECISION}}. Available attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before drafting, restate {{PROSPECTO}}, {{OFERTA}}, {{DOLOR}}, and {{ULTIMA_INTERACCION}}, and present the cadence plan (days and angle for each touch). If any of those four is missing, ask before writing; label assumptions with [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver 5 emails with distinct, non-repeated angles: (1) friendly reminder with added value; (2) resource or useful insight for {{PROSPECTO}}'s context; (3) verifiable social proof or analogous case; (4) reframing of {{DOLOR}} from a new angle; (5) dignified open-door close that releases without pressure or guilt. For each email: suggested day, subject line of maximum 50 characters, body of 60 to 110 words, a single concrete and low-friction CTA, and a one-line note on why that angle works at that moment. Default spacing: days 1, 4, 8, 14, 21; recalibrate per {{CICLO_DECISION}} (fast compresses, slow expands) and explain.

Rules: neutral, professional, warm, and consultive Spanish; no emojis; no prices; no the word free; do not invent data or numbers; social proof must be attributable or requested from the user; do not repeat openings or CTAs. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} only if they support the CTA, without saturating. Close by reporting the quality checklist and deliver the 5 emails as a block ready to personalize and load into the sending tool.

prompts.title: Corporate apology email for an incident
Email to say no gracefully
prompts.content:
Act as a senior executive writer specialized in relationship communication and difficult conversations. I need a complete email (subject plus body) that declines {{SOLICITUD}} without breaking the relationship, plus two alternative subject lines. A clumsy refusal burns relationships; a well-built one protects reputation, keeps the door open, and leaves the other person with a useful way out. The email will be sent as is, so it must be ready to paste and send.

Data:
- SOLICITUD: {{SOLICITUD}} (who is asking and what they request or propose exactly)
- RAZON: {{RAZON}} (honest, brief reason for declining)
- RELACION: {{RELACION}} (relationship to preserve and why it matters: client, boss, ally, colleague)
- ALTERNATIVA: {{ALTERNATIVA}} (what I can offer instead: reschedule, refer, reduced version, future opening; or "no alternative")
- TONO: {{TONO}} (register and language, e.g., warm-professional Spanish; optional)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, URLs, or "No attachments")

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the data; if SOLICITUD, RAZON, RELACION, or ALTERNATIVA is missing, ask me before drafting and do not invent anything. Plan in one line the angle of each block and the subject. Execute the email in this order:
1. Empathy: sincerely acknowledge who is asking and the value of {{SOLICITUD}}, specific, without flattery.
2. Reason and no: communicate the unambiguous no grounded in {{RAZON}} in one or two sentences; without disguising it as a conditional yes.
3. Alternative: offer {{ALTERNATIVA}} concretely and actionably (date, name, next step); if it is "no alternative", leave the door open honestly without inventing anything.
4. Close: reinforce {{RELACION}} in one line, without overpromising.
5. Clear, non-evasive subject line, plus two variants.

Rules: draft in {{TONO}} (default warm-professional, neutral Spanish), no emojis, no the word free, no prices; body of 8 to 14 lines; a single no per email. Deliver the Subject block, then the body, and at the end Alternative subject lines with two options.

prompts.title: Payment reminder email in firm-cordial tone
prompts.content:
Act as a senior collections and accounts-receivable specialist, expert in payment-reminder escalation that recovers cash without burning the commercial relationship. Your goal is to draft a firm-cordial email that unblocks collection of invoice {{NUMERO_FACTURA}} from {{CLIENTE}}, leaves a written follow-up record, and preserves the commercial relationship.

Proceed as follows:
1. Restate the brief in one sentence: "Payment reminder for {{NUMERO_FACTURA}} of {{MONTO_ADEUDADO}}, past due {{DIAS_MORA}}, to {{CLIENTE}}, in tone [level]". If {{NUMERO_FACTURA}}, {{MONTO_ADEUDADO}}, {{CLIENTE}}, or {{DIAS_MORA}} is missing, ask before writing. Never invent amounts, dates, or numbers; mark anything missing with [ASSUMPTION].
2. Calibrate the tone by {{DIAS_MORA}} and declare the level and why: 1 to 7 days = friendly; 8 to 30 = firm-cordial with a concrete payment date; 31 to 60 = firm with a declared consequence (service pause, late-payment interest if the contract provides, escalation) without threatening; more than 60 = formal, last instance before external collection. If {{HISTORIAL_PREVIO}} is empty, assume first reminder and label it [ASSUMPTION].
3. Write 2 subject-line variants: clear, specific, actionable, without alarm or sustained caps; include {{NUMERO_FACTURA}}.
4. Draft the body in this order: greeting to {{CLIENTE}}; good-faith line; hard data ({{NUMERO_FACTURA}}, {{MONTO_ADEUDADO}}, due date, {{DIAS_MORA}}); request with deadline; {{MEDIO_PAGO}} and instructions, plus what to do if already paid (confirm remittance); close that preserves the relationship. Readable in under 30 seconds. Attach or reference {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable.
5. Define a single CTA with an explicit deadline.
6. Deliver a backup follow-up line to resend after the deadline, adjusted to {{HISTORIAL_PREVIO}}.

Safeguards: no humiliating language, threats, or irony; no discounts, write-offs, or unauthorized payment plans; do not assert consequences you cannot substantiate.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Double-introduction email between contacts
prompts.content: Act as a senior professional connector, expert in high-value networking and the double-introduction email etiquette (double opt-in). I want to connect {{PERSONA_A}} and {{PERSONA_B}} from my network because {{MOTIVO_CONEXION}}. The benefit for each is {{VALOR_MUTUO}}, the expected next step is {{SIGUIENTE_PASO}}, and the attachments are {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of these data points is missing or ambiguous — especially {{PERSONA_A}}, {{PERSONA_B}}, {{MOTIVO_CONEXION}}, or {{VALOR_MUTUO}} — ask me before drafting. Deliver, in this order: (1) a brief diagnosis that separates what was confirmed from what was inferred, labels as [ASSUMPTION] any datum about the people that I did not provide, and verifies that the benefit is mutual from {{VALOR_MUTUO}}; if only one party gains, tell me and propose how to balance it or whether the introduction should not be made; (2) two short permission messages, one for {{PERSONA_A}} and one for {{PERSONA_B}}, that in one line explain who the other person is and why I am proposing them, and ask for a low-commitment yes/no; (3) the introduction email with both in copy, to send only when both confirm: subject that names {{PERSONA_A}} and {{PERSONA_B}} or the topic; greeting to both; one or two context lines per person relevant to the other, without inflating titles or accomplishments; the {{MOTIVO_CONEXION}}; the explicit value for {{PERSONA_A}} and for {{PERSONA_B}}; and a close that executes {{SIGUIENTE_PASO}} handing the ball to whoever owns it with a concrete action; (4) a note with the formula for moving the introducer to blind copy (move to bcc) once both have replied, and an alternative subject-line variant. Rules: never invent titles, accomplishments, or numbers; neutral, professional Spanish; no emojis; no prices and no the word free; keep the email brief so each person can reply without having to reread it.

prompts.title: Email to request a referral or recommendation
Inactive client reactivation email
prompts.content: Act as a senior retention and relationship marketing specialist (lifecycle/CRM), expert in B2B and B2C win-back campaigns that balance reactivation rate with relationship care. Produce a reactivation email package ready to send to {{NOMBRE_CLIENTE}}, client of {{MARCA}} who has gone {{TIEMPO_INACTIVO}} without buying or engaging after having used {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, offering {{INCENTIVO_RETORNO}} as a return bridge and aiming to get them to perform {{ACCION_DESEADA}}. Before drafting, restate in one line who you are writing to, how long they have been inactive and what incentive you are offering; if any of those data points or {{ADJUNTOS}} are missing, ask for them all in a single round. Work in three phases. Diagnosis: infer the probable reason for the pause and the strongest value memory from {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, marking each inference with [ASSUMPTION]. Win-back structure: acknowledge the absence without blame, recall the value, offer {{INCENTIVO_RETORNO}}, request one single action toward {{ACCION_DESEADA}}. Drafting: neutral and professional tone, no emojis, no false urgency, no prices or the word free; at most one StrategyIA wordplay if it adds value. Deliverable: three subject lines of up to 50 characters (one emotional, one curiosity-driven, one direct), a complementary preheader that does not repeat the subject, body A with opening, bridge to value, presentation of {{INCENTIVO_RETORNO}}, a single call to action toward {{ACCION_DESEADA}} and a warm close signed by {{MARCA}}, plus a shorter B variant for A/B testing. Close with a two-line note: which segment suits each subject line and which signal to measure as success (reply or reactivation, never open rate alone). Integrate {{ADJUNTOS}} only if they support the return; if "No attachments", omit them. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Counter-proposal negotiation email
prompts.content:
Act as a professional negotiator and senior commercial communication writer, trained in interest-based negotiation (Fisher and Ury, Getting to Yes), value anchoring, and the design of exchange options. Your goal is to draft a ready-to-send counter-proposal email that reopens the conversation with {{CONTRAPARTE}} after a received offer without closing it or damaging the relationship, moving {{OFERTA_Y_PUNTO}} by relying on {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}} rather than bargaining.

Before writing, restate the assignment in one sentence: "Reply to {{CONTRAPARTE}} to move {{OFERTA_Y_PUNTO}} anchoring {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}}, protecting the relationship and leaving a path forward." If {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}} or {{INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA}} are empty or vague, ask for them before drafting rather than inventing.

Proceed in five steps. First, framing: separate the stance from the underlying interests (from {{INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA}}) and identify which interest of {{CONTRAPARTE}} each element of value satisfies, so the anchor is relevant rather than self-promotional. Second, value architecture: order the results and differentiators from {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}} from most to least relevant for the counterpart and place them before the counter-proposal, so the adjustment reads as a consequence of value. Third, counter-proposal design: reframe {{OFERTA_Y_PUNTO}} as a shared problem and build one or two exchange options (varying scope, timelines, conditions, guarantees, or sequence) that expand value for both parties; use the alternative from {{INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA}} to set the boundary without threatening. Fourth, drafting: a continuity subject line never a rejection one, an opening that thanks and acknowledges mutual interest without submission or defensiveness, a value block anchored to interests, counter-proposal with alternatives, and close with concrete next step, with tone {{TONO}}. Fifth, quality control: value precedes every condition, no figures, and close leaves a path forward.

Non-negotiable rules: never mention prices or economic figures; express the adjustment in value, scope, conditions, or exchange. Never use "free" or offer work without consideration. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on all unverifiable data; do not invent results or metrics. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as backing and reference them only if they strengthen the value anchor. Neutral, professional language, no emojis.

Deliverable: the complete email (subject, opening, value block anchored to interests, counter-proposal with one or two exchange alternatives, close with next step), plus a brief three-line note: which interest you anchor, which point you move, and what the implicit boundary is.

Variables:
- {{CONTRAPARTE}}: who is sending the offer and what relationship exists (e.g. recurring client, new prospect, employer in hiring process).
- {{OFERTA_Y_PUNTO}}: what the offer proposes and which specific point I want to move.
- {{VALOR_RESULTADOS}}: value, verifiable results, scope, and differentiators to anchor.
- {{INTERESES_ALTERNATIVA}}: my own underlying interests (not just my stance) and my best alternative if no agreement is reached (BATNA).
- {{TONO}}: closing tone (firm, collaborative, or relationship-continuity).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Post-meeting thank-you email with next steps
prompts.content:
A professional meeting just ended and I need to put the agreements in writing before the context cools off. Act as a senior consultant in professional communication and relationship management, specialized in closing emails that sustain the traceability of agreements. Draft a ready-to-send post-meeting thank-you email about {{TEMA_REUNION}}, addressed to {{DESTINATARIOS}}, with this structure: (1) a specific subject line that names {{TEMA_REUNION}} and signals a summary with next steps; (2) a greeting to {{DESTINATARIOS}} and a brief, genuine thank-you for the time; (3) the purpose and central {{ACUERDOS}} in no more than three sentences, without reopening debates; (4) {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}} in a scannable table or list with action + owner + delivery date per line; (5) a proposed next contact on {{FECHA_SEGUIMIENTO}} if applicable, availability for questions, and a reference to {{ADJUNTOS}} if any; (6) a professional close and signature. Before drafting, restate what you understand and show me your plan. If {{TEMA_REUNION}}, {{DESTINATARIOS}}, {{ACUERDOS}}, or {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}} are missing, or if any action lacks an owner or date, ask me instead of inventing; never fabricate names, dates, or commitments. Write in neutral language, professional and cordial tone, short sentences, no emojis or filler. Deliver the complete email: subject, body, and signature, ready to copy and send.

Variables:
- {{TEMA_REUNION}}: central topic discussed (e.g.: project kickoff, proposal review, scope alignment)
- {{DESTINATARIOS}}: people or team receiving the email, with their role if relevant
- {{ACUERDOS}}: decisions and conclusions closed during the meeting
- {{PROXIMOS_PASOS}}: pending actions with owner and delivery date
- {{FECHA_SEGUIMIENTO}}: date or milestone for the next contact (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Client onboarding welcome email
prompts.content:
Act as a senior customer onboarding and relationship communication specialist, focused on early activation (time-to-first-value). Draft the welcome email that {{NOMBRE_CLIENTE}} receives right after closing with {{EMPRESA_SERVICIO}}: the first message defines the relationship, so it must reaffirm their decision without flattery, set expectations for the first milestone, deliver actionable first steps, and leave the support channel open, so they can move forward without writing to ask 'what's next'.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understood and, if {{PRIMER_HITO}}, {{PRIMEROS_PASOS}}, or {{CANAL_SOPORTE}} are missing, ask for them in a short list and wait for a response, because without them the email loses its activation value. Then define a single central message ('welcome, here is what comes next and this is your first step') and order the blocks from highest to lowest priority for mobile reading. Then draft.

Deliverable: (1) three subject lines of 6 to 9 words, without clickbait or all-caps; (2) personalized greeting to {{NOMBRE_CLIENTE}}; (3) welcome paragraph that reaffirms the decision in no more than two sentences; (4) 'What's next' block with action, deadline, and explicit {{PRIMER_HITO}}; (5) 'Your first steps' block with {{PRIMEROS_PASOS}} numbered, each with an estimated time; (6) support line naming {{CANAL_SOPORTE}} and its response time; (7) close with {{REMITENTE}} signature. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable. Body of 120 to 180 words, neutral language, professional, warm, and direct tone, mobile-scannable. No emojis, no prices, no the word free, no unkept promises. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any data you infer and list them at the end.

Variables:
- {{NOMBRE_CLIENTE}}: name of the person or account receiving the welcome
- {{EMPRESA_SERVICIO}}: your company, product, or service the client contracted
- {{PRIMER_HITO}}: first onboarding deliverable or milestone and its deadline (e.g. kickoff in 3 days)
- {{PRIMEROS_PASOS}}: 2 or 3 actions the client must take now, with estimated time
- {{CANAL_SOPORTE}}: support channel and committed response time (e.g. support@ within 24h)
- {{REMITENTE}}: person or team signing the email
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or 'No attachments'

prompts.title: Internal problem escalation email
prompts.content: Act as a senior operations leader with experience escalating critical issues to senior management in a calm, actionable, and noise-free manner. I need you to draft a ready-to-send internal escalation email plus an alternative subject line, addressed to {{DESTINATARIO_Y_NIVEL}}. Before drafting, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand (the problem {{PROBLEMA}}, the recipient and their level, what was already tried at my level according to {{ACCIONES_YA_INTENTADAS}}, the impact {{IMPACTO_CUANTIFICADO}}, the decision {{DECISION_SOLICITADA}}, and the deadline {{FECHA_LIMITE}}), present your plan, and only then execute. If {{PROBLEMA}}, {{IMPACTO_CUANTIFICADO}}, or {{DECISION_SOLICITADA}} are missing or ambiguous, ask me for them before writing; do not invent figures or facts. The email must allow {{DESTINATARIO_Y_NIVEL}} to understand the issue in less than thirty seconds and know exactly what decision is being requested. Structure: (1) a subject line naming {{PROBLEMA}} and explicitly signaling that a DECISION is requested, not just information; (2) a first sentence summarizing problem and impact; (3) brief context: what happened, since when, and what {{ACCIONES_YA_INTENTADAS}} shows about what was already tried at my level; (4) the impact based on {{IMPACTO_CUANTIFICADO}} in concrete terms of time, scope, clients, or deliverables, marking as [ASSUMPTION] any unconfirmed data; (5) between two and three decision options, each with its implication and, if applicable, a trade-off; (6) the specific decision {{DECISION_SOLICITADA}} with the deadline {{FECHA_LIMITE}} and the concrete consequence of not deciding in time; (7) a close offering availability to elaborate and integrating {{ADJUNTOS}} when supporting material exists. Maintain a calm, professional, and solution-oriented tone: no alarmism, no blaming individuals, no complaints, no vague jargon, no emojis, in neutral language. Flag my recommendation if I have one, separating it from the facts. Do not include prices or economic figures you were not given. Deliver the complete email (subject, body, close) plus an alternative subject line, and list at the end any data that remains as an assumption or pending confirmation.

prompts.title: Event invitation email with RSVP
Contract or subscription renewal email
Pitch deck with the 10-20-30 rule
prompts.content:
Act as a senior pitch deck strategist for investment and sales, expert in applying Guy Kawasaki's 10-20-30 method (10 slides, 20 minutes, body minimum 30 points) and in business storytelling. I want the complete script for a pitch deck of exactly 10 slides to present {{PRODUCTO}} to {{AUDIENCIA}}, with the goal of {{OBJETIVO}}. The central problem it solves is {{PROBLEMA}} and my unique advantage versus alternatives is {{DIFERENCIADOR}}. Available traction and figures: {{METRICAS}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before drafting, restate in one line the central promise of the deck and confirm the emphasis according to {{AUDIENCIA}}: with investors prioritize market size, business model, and projections; with a buying committee or corporate client prioritize problem, ROI, and differentiator. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{PROBLEMA}}, {{DIFERENCIADOR}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, or {{OBJETIVO}} are missing, ask for them in concrete questions and do not invent data.

Structure the narrative in the canonical Kawasaki sequence: 1 Title and promise, 2 Problem, 3 Value proposition, 4 Magic or how it works, 5 Business model, 6 Go to market, 7 Competition, 8 Team, 9 Projections, 10 Status and call to action. For each slide deliver: impact headline of up to 7 words, 3 to 5 bullets (one short sentence per bullet, no paragraphs, low density 30+ size), speaking notes of 2 to 3 sentences, a probable objection from the decision-maker with a brief response, and the target time in minutes. Distribute the 20 minutes with more weight on slides 2, 3, 5, and 9, less on 1, 8, and 10, leaving 2 to 3 minutes of buffer for questions within the total. Integrate {{METRICAS}} on slide 9 and mark with [ASSUMPTION] all figures or market data not provided. Close slide 10 with current status, calendar, and the call to action aligned with {{OBJETIVO}}.

At the end verify and report: exactly 10 canonical slides, no headline over 7 words, each bullet one single sentence, sum of minutes = 20, and every figure not provided marked as assumption. Neutral, professional language, no emojis, no dense tables. Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Presentation opening with an impact hook
prompts.content: Act as a senior speaker coach specialized in designing the first 60 seconds of high-impact keynotes and conferences. Your assignment: produce the complete opening of the presentation on {{TEMA_CHARLA}}, because those first 60 seconds decide whether the room follows you or disconnects. Before drafting, confirm the minimum context: {{TEMA_CHARLA}}, {{PERFIL_AUDIENCIA}} (role, knowledge level, expectation, emotional state on arrival), {{OBJETIVO_PRESENTACION}} (what the audience must think, feel, or do at the end), {{DURACION_TOTAL}}, and {{TONO}}. If any is missing or ambiguous, ask for it before proceeding; do not invent the talk content or figures. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Then proceed in four steps. First, anchor the opening in a real tension of {{PERFIL_AUDIENCIA}} coherent with {{TONO}}. Second, propose three hooks, one per lever: (a) a rhetorical question that confronts a belief of {{PERFIL_AUDIENCIA}}; (b) a counterintuitive data point that breaks expectations, with a declared source or marked [ASSUMPTION] if not provided, never with invented figures; (c) a brief first-person anecdote that creates narrative tension. Each hook deliverable in under 60 seconds and connected explicitly with {{TEMA_CHARLA}} and {{OBJETIVO_PRESENTACION}}. Third, for the recommended hook write the word-for-word script of the 60 seconds, with [pause] marks, *emphasis* marks, and the bridge sentence to the next section; indicate the approximate time per block. Fourth, close with a one-line justification of why that hook wins over the other two for this audience, plus a risk note: when it might fail and which backup variant to use. Constraints: zero clichés (no lengthy greetings, protocol thanks, or opening apologies), nothing that promises what the talk does not deliver, opening pronounceable naturally; if {{DURACION_TOTAL}} is very short, adjust the hook to 20-30 seconds and state that explicitly. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Final deliverable: three compared hooks + timed script of the recommended hook + justification + risk note, ready to rehearse.

prompts.title: Problem-agitation-solution narrative for a deck
prompts.content: Act as a senior narrative strategist for executive presentations, with experience structuring sales decks and decision committees under the Problem-Agitation-Solution arc (PAS). I want a slide-by-slide storyline for this audience and decision: {{AUDIENCIA_Y_DECISION}}. Before drafting, restate what you understood and show me your plan: confirm audience, decision to make when the deck closes, and the single idea they must remember; if a key data point is missing, ask me for it instead of inventing it. Structure in four blocks. Context: audience, decision, and central idea. Problem: name {{PROBLEMA_CENTRAL}} in the exact language of the audience, without revealing the solution. Agitation: amplify {{COSTO_INACCION}} with consequences, opportunity cost, and growing risk, with verifiable figures or facts and without gratuitous fear. Solution: present {{PROPUESTA}} as the resolution of the tension, backed by {{PRUEBA}}, and close with a call to action aligned with the requested decision. Before detailing, distribute the slides among the blocks; adjust the total to {{NUM_SLIDES}} if indicated, otherwise propose the minimum quantity that sustains the arc. For each slide deliver: number and title, unique idea in one sentence, two to four bullets, suggested visual or data piece, and the spoken transition to the next slide. Reread the arc and verify that tension rises in Agitation and drops when resolved in Solution, that no slide carries two ideas, and that it flows when read aloud. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any inferred data pending confirmation. Deliver in neutral and professional language, no emojis, and close by noting which slides rest on assumptions and what you need to confirm them.

prompts.title: Presentation close with call to action
prompts.content:
Act as a senior executive communication strategist specializing in high-impact presentation closes and call-to-action design. Build the final slide and the spoken close of a presentation on {{TEMA_PRESENTACION}} for {{AUDIENCIA}}, whose goal is for them to execute {{ACCION_DESEADA}} within {{PLAZO}}, motivated by {{BENEFICIO_O_COSTO}}. Consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate what you understood and show me your plan.

1) Distill the central message into a memorable phrase of at most 12 words, one {{AUDIENCIA}} can repeat from memory as they leave the room. 2) Formulate ONE single primary call to action based on {{ACCION_DESEADA}}: imperative verb, concrete and observable; discard verbs of intention such as consider or think. 3) Make the action unambiguous by defining exactly what, who executes it, by when according to {{PLAZO}}, and what the actionable first step is; if {{PLAZO}} is empty, propose one and flag it [ASSUMPTION]. 4) Add the why that connects the action to {{BENEFICIO_O_COSTO}}; if empty, derive a plausible benefit from the topic and flag it [ASSUMPTION]. 5) Propose the visual structure of the slide (headline, subtitle, highlighted action element, optional closing anchor such as a data point, date or question) and a verbal transition line to say aloud when showing it.

If {{AUDIENCIA}} lacks the authority to execute {{ACCION_DESEADA}}, add a backup action within their reach (decide, schedule, authorize, escalate). Deliver the block ready for the slide (headline + subtitle + highlighted CTA + optional anchor) and a two-line speaking note. Neutral and professional English, no emojis, no prices, no use of the word free.

prompts.title: Speaker script per slide (speaker notes)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior executive speaking coach and presentation designer, with expertise in structured storytelling, on-stage time management, and speaker note design. I am going to present "{{TITULO_PRESENTACION}}" before {{AUDIENCIA}} with the objective of {{OBJETIVO}} in {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}}. The deck already exists ({{CONTENIDO_SLIDES}}); without a script the risk is reading the slides, losing the thread at transitions, running over time, and diluting the message. I want a complete speaker script, one entry per slide, plus a time summary table squared against {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}}.

If {{CONTENIDO_SLIDES}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{OBJETIVO}}, or {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}} are missing, ask me before drafting; do not invent the deck content. If {{TONO}} is not provided, assume neutral professional register and declare it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides supporting material.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate in two or three lines what you understood; plan the narrative arc (opening with a hook, development with an argument, close with a call to action) and the time budget allocation; only then execute.

Steps: (1) Map the narrative arc of {{CONTENIDO_SLIDES}} and verify that the order supports it; if a slide breaks the flow, flag it and propose relocating it. (2) For each slide produce five elements: key message in a single sentence; speaker notes in natural, speakable spoken language — not literal text to read nor copied bullets; transition phrase toward the next slide; time in seconds; pacing or emphasis cue when it adds value (pause, question to the audience, data point to highlight, tone change, eye contact). (3) One message per slide; overloaded ones are flagged with a split suggestion. (4) Reserve 10 to 15 percent of the time as a buffer for questions and transitions and deduct it from the usable budget. (5) Close with a summary table (slide, key message, seconds), total sum, and compare against {{DURACION_OBJETIVO}}; if the gap exceeds 10 percent, deliver a trimming or expansion plan indicating which slides to adjust and by how many seconds.

Acceptance criteria: each slide with its five elements; speakable notes; explicit transitions; squared table with actionable recommendation. Edge case: if the deck has no close with a call to action, propose one aligned to {{OBJETIVO}} and label it as a suggestion. Neutral and professional language, no emojis, in the tone {{TONO}}, ready to paste into the deck notes.

prompts.title: One-idea-per-slide rewrite
prompts.content: Act as a senior executive presentation designer, expert in the one-idea-per-slide principle, Michael Alley's assertion-evidence model, the action titles used by consulting firms, Minto's pyramid-type storyline, and Nancy Duarte's glance test. Refactor the saturated deck {{DECK_ACTUAL}} into a presentation where each slide conveys a single idea with an affirmative headline, for {{OBJETIVO_PRESENTACION}} before {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}}, anchored in {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}} (if missing, derive it from the content and flag it as an assumption). Attached material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Proceed as follows: 1) Diagnose {{DECK_ACTUAL}} slide by slide: count distinct messages, flag with [MULTI-MESSAGE] those that carry more than one idea, record the current title, and flag as weak titles thematic labels. 2) Atomize: assign each new slide a single verifiable assertion aligned with {{MENSAJE_CENTRAL}}; split each slide with N ideas into N slides. 3) Rewrite each title as an action title (affirmative sentence with subject and verb stating the conclusion); if the concrete data is not in {{DECK_ACTUAL}}, leave the pattern and flag it [DATA TO CONFIRM], never invent the figure. 4) Apply assertion-evidence: per slide name the single visual evidence that supports the title and list what is removed for noise or because it belongs to another slide; the body never repeats the title text. 5) Order the slides in a coherent storyline for {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}} and run the headline-only read test and the glance test; if the sequence does not tell the story or a slide is not understood in three seconds, return to step 2. Deliver: (a) diagnostic table, (b) refactor map table slide by slide (new number, single idea, action title, preserved evidence, what was removed, source slide of origin), and (c) the sequence of headlines that passes the headline-only read test. If {{DECK_ACTUAL}}, {{OBJETIVO_PRESENTACION}}, or {{AUDIENCIA_DECISION}} are missing, ask before executing. Neutral and professional language, no emojis, no prices, no use of the word free; diagnostic and map in tables.

prompts.title: Benefit-oriented product demo script
prompts.content: Act as a senior presales engineer and demo scriptwriter with fifteen years converting demonstrations into decisions, trained in Peter Cohan's Great Demo! method, the Feature-Advantage-Benefit (FAB) translation, and the Tell-Show-Tell technique. I need the complete script for a demo of {{PRODUCTO}} for {{COMPRADOR_Y_ROL}}: not a menu tour or a feature list, but a demonstration where each capability translates into a benefit that {{COMPRADOR_Y_ROL}} recognizes as their own. The risk to avoid is the feature dump. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{COMPRADOR_Y_ROL}}, {{DOLORES_PRIORITARIOS}}, or {{RESULTADO_VALORADO}} are missing, ask before starting and do not invent. Proceed in five phases. Phase 1, diagnosis: based on {{COMPRADOR_Y_ROL}} and {{DOLORES_PRIORITARIOS}}, fix two or three pains that will guide the demo, determine whether {{COMPRADOR_Y_ROL}} decides as an economic buyer (business results and risk) or technical buyer (viability, integration, and control), and name {{RESULTADO_VALORADO}}; flag as [ASSUMPTION] what is inferred. Phase 2, translation: per item in {{FUNCIONALIDADES_CLAVE}}, one row with feature, advantage, and benefit in the language of {{RESULTADO_VALORADO}}; discard what does not tie to a pain and record what you left out and why. Phase 3, reverse Do It architecture: order from the end, define the highest-impact moment, show it first, confirm, and then the few clicks to get there; avoid the exhaustive tour. Phase 4, script: section-by-section with SAYS, DOES, and BENEFIT (Tell-Show-Tell bridge) plus the bridge phrase "so that this matters to you"; opening under ninety seconds that names the pain and promises the result; close that summarizes benefits, ties them to a metric of {{RESULTADO_VALORADO}}, and proposes a next step. Fit everything within {{DURACION}} if indicated. Phase 5, anticipation: three probable objections with benefit-oriented answers and a contingency plan if something fails live. Do not invent capabilities or figures: flag every estimate as [ASSUMPTION]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. No prices, no word free, neutral and professional language, no emojis.

prompts.title: Quarterly results presentation to the board
Presentation storyline with Minto's pyramid
Anticipated objection-handling slides
Action titles for every slide
prompts.content:
Act as a senior executive communication consultant specializing in action titles and the so-what principle, McKinsey/Minto school. My presentation is about {{TEMA_PRESENTACION}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, and I want them to make this decision: {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}. Today my headings are descriptive titles ({{TITULOS_ACTUALES}}) that name the topic but do not communicate the conclusion, so the audience has to read the entire slide and the story is lost. Convert each title into an action title that asserts a conclusion, in tone {{TONO}}, and verify that the sequence tells a coherent story that leads to {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

First, restate what you understand about TEMA_PRESENTACION, AUDIENCIA, OBJETIVO_DECISION, and the list TITULOS_ACTUALES; if any is missing, ask me and do not invent content or figures. Present your plan before executing.

Execute as follows: (1) Diagnosis: classify each title in TITULOS_ACTUALES as a label (only names a topic) or an assertion (already says something). (2) Rewrite: apply the so-what by asking "and what does this mean for {{AUDIENCIA}}?" until reaching an actionable assertion; one single idea per title, neutral language, maximum 12–14 words, no generic labels, no emojis; figures only if they come from TITULOS_ACTUALES, otherwise flag them [ASSUMPTION]. (3) Add the one-line so-what per title. (4) Storyline: chain the numbered titles and check the situation, complication, resolution flow toward OBJETIVO_DECISION. (5) Control: adjust length, grammatical parallelism, and tone per {{TONO}}.

Deliver: table per slide (original title, action title, so-what); then the complete numbered storyline; at the end the coherence notes flagging logical jumps, redundant titles, or still-descriptive ones, each with a proposed adjustment.

prompts.title: Demand-generation webinar structure
Advertising headlines with the 4U formula
Landing page copy with the PAS framework
Value proposition in one sentence
Benefit bullets with feature-advantage translation
prompts.content:
Act as a senior direct-response copywriter with twelve years of writing converting bullets for landing pages, proposals, and product sheets, expert in the Features-Advantages-Benefits (FAB) model and in the laddering technique "and what does that mean for the customer?". Convert the flat list of features of {{PRODUCTO}} into bullets that answer the only question the reader cares about: what's in it for me, to achieve {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}.

Data:
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} (name and brief description of the product or service)
- LISTA_CARACTERISTICAS: {{LISTA_CARACTERISTICAS}} (technical or functional features as they currently exist)
- CLIENTE_OBJETIVO: {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}} (role, context, what matters to them, what problem they face)
- RESULTADO_DESEADO: {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}} (what the reader must feel or do after reading the bullets)
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} (optional: landing, proposal, product sheet, email, slide)
- TONO: {{TONO}} (optional: approachable, technical, executive, within neutral professional English)

If {{PRODUCTO}}, {{LISTA_CARACTERISTICAS}}, {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}}, or {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}} is missing, or a feature is ambiguous, ask before proceeding. Do not invent features not present in the input.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what product it is, who the bullets are speaking to, and what result they must produce, flagging ambiguous features or missing data; present the plan (how many bullets, hierarchy order, laddering depth per feature); then execute.

When executing: translate each feature with the FAB chain (feature → technical advantage → benefit for {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}}), applying "and what does that mean for you?" two or three times until reaching a concrete and verifiable benefit aligned with {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}. Write each bullet opening with the benefit and closing with the proof, with result verbs; use only figures and timelines from the input (if a data point is missing, placeholder in curly braces). Rank by impact for {{CLIENTE_OBJETIVO}}, not by original order. Polish to one or two lines, parallel structure, no jargon or empty adjectives without proof, adjusted to {{CANAL}} and {{TONO}}.

Deliver (a) the auditable feature → advantage → benefit table for each element and (b) the final ranked bullet set, ready to paste. Neutral and professional English, no emojis, no prices, and no word "free".

prompts.title: Call-to-action variants for A/B testing
prompts.content: Act as a senior conversion copywriter (CRO) specializing in microcopy experimentation and CTA design. I need a set of 6 to 8 call-to-action variants ready to run an A/B test on {{ACCION_DESEADA}}, located at {{UBICACION}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, competing against the control {{CTA_CONTROL}}, optimizing {{METRICA_EXITO}} and attacking the friction {{FRICCION_PRINCIPAL}}. If {{ADJUNTOS}} contributes brand voice, prior data, or screenshots, use it as context. Before writing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if any key data is missing, ask for it in a single batch before proceeding. Classify the variants into four hypothesis families: (a) direct action verb, (b) concrete benefit or result, (c) reduction of {{FRICCION_PRINCIPAL}}, (d) social proof or legitimate urgency. Write each variant starting with an action verb, with no filler, respecting the approximate length of {{CTA_CONTROL}}. For each variant document: exact text, family, psychological lever, falsifiable hypothesis ("if... then... because..." format), primary metric ({{METRICA_EXITO}}), and a guard metric. Mark one variant as the control. One distinct lever per variant to avoid cannibalization. Close with an effort-vs-expected-impact prioritization table, recommended testing order, and a note on minimum sample size or duration to conclude. Brand rules: never prices or discounts; never the word "free" or its implicit promise; neutral and professional English, no emojis; no unsustainable promises. Deliver the documented block of variants plus the prioritization table, ready to load into the experiment.

prompts.title: Launch email marketing sequence
prompts.content:
Act as a senior direct-response email marketing strategist, specialist in launch sequences and ethical scarcity. I want a complete launch email sequence for {{OFERTA}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, promising the transformation {{TRANSFORMACION}} and closing with the scarcity reason {{MOTIVO_ESCASEZ}} within the window {{VENTANA_OFERTA}}. Use {{PRUEBA}} as evidence and consider {{ADJUNTOS}}.

The sequence must take the reader from indifference to decision: warm them up before asking, install desire with a unique mechanism and proof, and close with a real window that gives an honest reason to act now.

Before writing, restate in your own words {{OFERTA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{TRANSFORMACION}}, {{MOTIVO_ESCASEZ}}, and {{VENTANA_OFERTA}}; if any of those five is missing, ask me for it concretely and do not invent it. Then present your plan: how many emails per phase (anticipation, desire, close with scarcity), the purpose of each one, and send interval anchored to {{VENTANA_OFERTA}}. Wait for my go-ahead.

Once the plan is approved, write each email with: phase and purpose, two subject-line options (one direct and one curiosity-based, both under 50 characters), preheader that does not repeat the subject, body of 120 to 220 words, a single explicit CTA, and a note of when to send it. Chain the emails. The desire phase includes one email with the unique mechanism and {{PRUEBA}} (if no proof, mark [ASSUMPTION] and ask for it) and one email that deactivates objections. The close phase activates {{MOTIVO_ESCASEZ}} in a verifiable way within {{VENTANA_OFERTA}}; if the reason cannot sustain a real limit, mark it [ASSUMPTION] and offer an honest alternative.

Close with summarized send calendar (email, relative day/time, chosen subject) and three metrics with reference value: open rate, click rate, window conversion. No prices and no word "free". Neutral and professional English, no emojis. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Conversion-oriented product description
prompts.content:
Act as a senior conversion copywriter with fifteen years writing product sheets for e-commerce, B2B catalogs, and landing pages, expert in FAB (feature, advantage, benefit) and PAS (problem, agitation, solution). Before writing, restate in one sentence what you are going to describe, for whom, and in which channel, and present your plan; if any essential data is missing, ask for it in a single batch. Write a publication-ready product sheet using:
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} (name, category, and what it does in one sentence)
- COMPRADOR_OBJETIVO: {{COMPRADOR_OBJETIVO}} (who they are, what they seek, in what context they buy, and their awareness stage)
- ESPECIFICACIONES: {{ESPECIFICACIONES}} (real and verifiable technical data: materials, dimensions, compatibility, performance, warranty)
- BENEFICIO_PRINCIPAL: {{BENEFICIO_PRINCIPAL}} (central differentiator that most drives the purchase)
- OBJECION_DOMINANTE: {{OBJECION_DOMINANTE}} (main barrier; if empty, infer it and mark it as [ASSUMPTION])
- CANAL: {{CANAL}} (e-commerce, B2B catalog, or landing page; adjust length and CTA)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}}
Deliver in this order: (1) benefit headline + subheadline; (2) PAS opening according to awareness stage; (3) benefits block with FAB translation per feature, discarding features that do not contribute a clear benefit; (4) table of verifiable specifications separated from the emotional body; (5) deactivation of the dominant objection with proof or assurance; (6) CTA adjusted to the channel, without artificial pressure. Mark every figure as confirmed data or [ASSUMPTION]; clean up empty adjectives; neutral and professional English, no emojis, no prices, and no word "free". Close listing the data that still needs confirmation before publishing.

prompts.title: Interface microcopy and empty states oriented to action
prompts.content:
Act as a senior UX writer with more than ten years writing interface microcopy for digital products, expert in UX writing heuristics (clarity over cleverness, consistent voice and tone, action-first in buttons), in the Nielsen Norman Group error message formula, and in accessible and internationalizable writing. You are going to write the microcopy of {{PRODUCTO}} for its critical states and deliver a string table ready for design and engineering to implement without reinterpreting.

Data:
- PRODUCTO: {{PRODUCTO}} (product or screen and what the user does there)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} (target user and their familiarity with the product)
- ESTADOS_A_CUBRIR: {{ESTADOS_A_CUBRIR}} (buttons, errors, empty states, loading, and confirmations to write)
- VOZ_DE_MARCA: {{VOZ_DE_MARCA}} (optional: already-defined voice or tone traits)
- RESTRICCIONES_UI: {{RESTRICCIONES_UI}} (optional: language, platform, and character limits per component)
- ACCIONES_CRITICAS: {{ACCIONES_CRITICAS}} (optional: destructive, irreversible, or payment actions requiring explicit confirmation)
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, URLs, or screenshots; or "No attachments")

If an essential data point is missing, ask for it in a single batch before writing. Do not invent function names, brand names, error codes, or data: mark [ASSUMPTION] for every inference about {{PRODUCTO}} or {{AUDIENCIA}}.

Proceed in three phases. Phase 1 Framing: from {{PRODUCTO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, and {{VOZ_DE_MARCA}} declare three to five voice traits and map the tone per state according to its emotional moment (error, wait, success, empty); set the character budget per component type from {{RESTRICCIONES_UI}} and, where not given, use standard values marked [ASSUMPTION]. Phase 2 Writing (states in risk order: errors and empty states first): buttons with action-first verb oriented toward the user's result, without ambiguous labels, with the secondary button defined; for each item in {{ACCIONES_CRITICAS}} a confirmation with explicit consequence, specific label on confirm, and undo option when possible; errors with the four-part formula distinguishing inline validation, system, and permission; empty states distinguishing first use, search without results, and empty due to error or permission; loading choosing the correct pattern (skeleton, spinner, or progress bar); confirmations that close the loop without overacting; second person, active voice, positive language. Phase 3 Verification: each string against its budget, anti-patterns, voice consistency, and accessibility (accessible label for icons and states, not relying solely on color); for i18n leave variables as {variable} with their plural rule, avoid concatenating fragments, allow 30 to 40 percent expansion when translating, and define truncation when text exceeds its limit.

Deliver: voice and tone guide with tone by state; string table with technical key, context, copy, short and long version where applicable, character limit, variable or plural rule, accessible label, and tone note; destructive actions block with its pattern; and list of anti-patterns with corrected example. Never mention prices or use the word "free"; neutral and professional English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Search ads with character limits
prompts.content: Act as a senior performance marketing copywriter specializing in Google Ads and responsive search ads (RSA), with an obsessive focus on keyword-message-destination relevance and exact character-limit compliance. I need a complete RSA set ready to paste to promote {{PRODUCTO_SERVICIO}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, triggered by {{PALABRAS_CLAVE}}, that drives {{ACCION_DESEADA}}, aligned with the promise of {{PAGINA_DESTINO}} and leveraged on {{DIFERENCIADOR}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any critical data is missing (product, audience, keywords, action, destination), ask me before writing; do not invent. Deliver: (1) 15 headlines of maximum 30 characters, numbered, with exact count in parentheses; (2) 4 descriptions of maximum 90 characters, numbered with count; (3) 2 display paths of maximum 15 characters with count. Treat each headline and description as an autonomous message, because Google combines them dynamically: no narrative dependencies between lines, no repeated ideas, no phrases that only work in a fixed order. Incorporate the main keyword from {{PALABRAS_CLAVE}} naturally in at least 3 headlines and, if it fits, in 1 description and 1 path, without keyword stuffing. Diversify angles: benefit, proof or authority, legitimate urgency, call to {{ACCION_DESEADA}}, and {{DIFERENCIADOR}}; reserve at least 2 headlines of 15 characters or fewer as flexible assembly pieces. Count every character including spaces and punctuation; trim character by character without forced abbreviations or sustained caps. Close with a quality-control block that lists every line at or near the limit (within 1-2 characters), confirms angle coverage, flags redundancies, and verifies brand rules. Neutral and professional English, no emojis, no prices, no word "free" or equivalents, no promising what {{PAGINA_DESTINO}} cannot sustain. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Paid social media ad copy
prompts.content:
Act as a senior direct-response copywriter specializing in paid social, with high-performing ads on Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, and Instagram. You apply Eugene Schwartz's five awareness levels and the problem-agitate-solve structure. I want the text of a paid social ad for {{OFERTA}} on {{PLATAFORMA}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, to achieve {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}. In paid social the feed moves at high speed: if the first line does not stop the scroll, the rest of the budget is wasted.

Before writing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret > Plan > Execute): restate {{OFERTA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{PLATAFORMA}}, and {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}} as you understand them, and present your plan in one line. If any of those four is missing, ask for it before continuing; do not invent market data.

Deliver in this order: (1) Awareness diagnosis: classify {{AUDIENCIA}} in relation to {{OFERTA}} at one of the five levels (unaware, problem-aware, solution-aware, product-aware, most aware), justify in one sentence, and derive how much context the hook carries and which angle dominates. (2) Main hook: the first line that stops the scroll, concrete and specific to the pain or desire, fully readable before the "see more" cut of {{PLATAFORMA}}, without empty clickbait. (3) Problem-agitate-solve body: name the problem in {{AUDIENCIA}}'s words, agitate the cost of not solving it, present {{OFERTA}} as the bridge, and back it with {{PRUEBA}} if it exists. (4) Call to action: a single low-friction CTA, clear verb, aligned with {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}. (5) Three alternative hooks labeled by angle (pain, desire, counterintuitive, or proof) for A/B test, plus the headline or descriptive text appropriate to {{PLATAFORMA}}. (6) Platform adaptation: length and tone adjusted to {{PLATAFORMA}}'s format, within its practical character limit.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they add context. Firm rules: never prices or cost figures; never the word "free"; do not invent data, figures, or testimonials, mark [ASSUMPTION] for what you infer and leave in brackets the gaps the advertiser must fill; sustainable promise; neutral and professional English, no emojis. Close with a marked compliance checklist.

Variables:
- {{OFERTA}}: product, service, or promotion to advertise, in one or two sentences.
- {{AUDIENCIA}}: who you are speaking to (role, context, pain or desire) and their awareness level if known.
- {{PLATAFORMA}}: network and ad format (Meta feed, LinkedIn, TikTok, Instagram Stories).
- {{OBJETIVO_CAMPANA}}: action the ad must trigger (signup, download, message, schedule demo, visit page).
- {{PRUEBA}}: (optional) data point, testimonial, result, or evidence that backs the promise.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or 'No attachments'.

prompts.title: Long-form sales page with complete structure
prompts.content:
Act as a senior direct-response copywriter specializing in info-product and high-value service launches, with a sober editorial lens (Schwartz/Halbert school adapted to a neutral professional voice). You are going to write a direct-response long-form sales page ready to publish for {{PRODUCTO}}, directed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, that moves the reader from {{DOLOR_DESEO}} to {{CTA}} through a complete persuasive sequence.

Before writing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if {{PRODUCTO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{TRANSFORMACION}}, {{PRUEBA}}, {{OFERTA}}, or {{CTA}} are incomplete, ask for them in a single batch before executing.

Phases: (1) Diagnosis: determine the awareness level of {{AUDIENCIA}} and the dominant pain/desire {{DOLOR_DESEO}}; define and name the unique mechanism of {{PRODUCTO}}. (2) Architecture: map the sequence and the promise of each section. (3) Writing: concrete headlines, short sentences, transitions; insert {{CTA}} in the lead, after the offer, and in the close. (4) Brand sanitization: eliminate prices and monetary figures, eliminate "free" and equivalents, verify attribution of every result, clean up hyperbole.

Deliver in Markdown with a heading per section, in this order: (1) Lead that opens with {{DOLOR_DESEO}} and promises {{TRANSFORMACION}} in headline plus subheadline; (2) Problem and honest agitation with the real cost of not solving it; (3) Solution: present {{PRODUCTO}} and articulate the unique mechanism; (4) Proof: organize {{PRUEBA}} in testimonials, cases, data, and credentials, every figure attributed or marked [ASSUMPTION]; (5) Offer: break down {{OFERTA}} in deliverables and bonuses, with "who it is for" and "who it is not for"; (6) Guarantee: present {{GARANTIA}} as risk reversal (if missing, propose an honest one marked [ASSUMPTION]); (7) Objections: 4 to 6 most probable doubts of {{AUDIENCIA}} answered; (8) FAQ: 6 to 10 real questions with concrete answers; (9) Close: value summary, legitimate urgency (slots, date, cohort), and {{CTA}} repeated at least twice. If there are {{ADJUNTOS}}, use them as a source of proof and context. Close with assumptions and pending log.

Rules: neutral and professional English, no emojis; never prices or monetary figures or "free"; zero invented data; {{CTA}} coherent in every appearance; every result traceable or marked [ASSUMPTION].

prompts.title: Social proof and testimonials block
prompts.content:
Act as a senior conversion copywriting strategist specializing in social proof and objection psychology, with hands-on experience in landing pages and B2B proposals. Your task: build a paste-ready social proof block for {{CANAL_DESTINO}} where every testimonial, metric, or recognition dissolves a precise objection from {{PERFIL_COMPRADOR}} regarding {{OFERTA}} — not a generic compliment. Before executing, restate your understanding and present your plan (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute). If {{PERFIL_COMPRADOR}}, {{OFERTA}}, or {{TESTIMONIOS_Y_METRICAS}} arrive incomplete, ask for what is missing before proceeding.

Proceed as follows: (1) Inventory 3 to 5 objections that hold {{PERFIL_COMPRADOR}} back, starting from {{OBJECIONES_CLAVE}} and from the typical doubts of their role and sector, in the buyer's language; rank them by impact on the decision. (2) Map each objection to the best available proof in {{TESTIMONIOS_Y_METRICAS}}, choosing by credibility: quantified result > named case > attributable opinion.
