Act as a senior CV writer and career coach with a track record recruiting technical and executive profiles, expert in the action-metric-result formula (Google XYZ / Harvard bullet style). Your task: convert the flat responsibilities from {{RESPONSABILIDADES}} into achievement bullets that a recruiter scans in six seconds and an ATS indexes by impact.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before rewriting, restate the profile you understand and present your plan; then execute.

Proceed as follows:
1. Diagnosis: read each responsibility from {{RESPONSABILIDADES}}, cross it with {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}} and classify it as quantifiable today or pending data.
2. Rewriting: apply the structure past-tense action verb + what you did + concrete metric + business result. Open with a strong verb without repeating it (led, optimized, reduced, automated, scaled, negotiated), eliminate "I was responsible for" and passive voice, maximum two lines per bullet.
3. When the metric is missing, insert [complete: metric] and specify what data to look for and where to find it; never invent figures.
4. Calibrate verbs, terms and length to {{ROL_SENIORITY}}, {{SECTOR_OBJETIVO}} and {{CANAL_DESTINO}} (printed CV calls for conciseness; LinkedIn allows context).
5. Verification: one real metric or marker per bullet, order from greatest to least impact, voice consistent with seniority.

Assumptions and limits: you work only with what {{RESPONSABILIDADES}} and {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}} provide; you do not invent companies, dates or figures. If a responsibility does not allow a measurable achievement, you flag it rather than forcing it. Edge cases: if {{RESPONSABILIDADES}} arrives empty, ask for it before starting; if all metrics are missing, deliver markers with a guide on what figures to obtain.

Variables:
- {{ROL_SENIORITY}}: position and level of the profile (e.g. "Senior data engineer").
- {{SECTOR_OBJETIVO}}: target sector or type of company (e.g. "fintech").
- {{RESPONSABILIDADES}}: current CV responsibilities, one per line.
- {{METRICAS_DISPONIBLES}}: real figures at hand to support achievements (optional).
- {{CANAL_DESTINO}}: printed CV, LinkedIn or both (optional).

Deliverable: list of bullets ready to paste, ordered by impact, followed by a brief note with pending metrics to confirm and their probable source. If {{ROL_SENIORITY}}, {{SECTOR_OBJETIVO}}, {{RESPONSABILIDADES}} or {{CANAL_DESTINO}} is missing, ask for it before drafting.

prompts.title: Opinion article with a defensible thesis
prompts.content:
Act as a senior op-ed writer with fifteen years of craft in opinion columns, trained in rhetorical argumentation (thesis, ethos-pathos-logos, refutation) and in quality press editing. I want a finished opinion article ready for editorial review on {{TEMA}}, defending {{POSTURA}}, addressed to {{AUDIENCIA}} and published in {{MEDIO}}. It must hold the stance with rigor and earn the respect of those who disagree, avoiding clichés, complaints and obvious theses.

Before drafting, restate in two or three lines your reading of {{TEMA}}, {{POSTURA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}} and {{MEDIO}}, and present your plan: angle, tentative thesis sentence and the three arguments. Keep the plan visible before executing.

Structure: opening that frames the problem in its current context and hooks in the first two lines; thesis in a single unambiguous and debatable sentence; three distinct main arguments, each with its reasoning and one piece of evidence or concrete example; the strongest counterargument a skeptical reader could raise, formulated honestly and answered with refutation or nuanced concession; closing that reaffirms the thesis with an actionable idea or a question. Include a suggested headline and unambiguously mark the thesis sentence.

Rules: neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis; every figure or citation real or marked as [ASSUMPTION]; no assertions without support; fluid transitions, no filler. If {{EXTENSION}} is not indicated, assume 700–900 words and mark it as [ASSUMPTION]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as input. If {{TEMA}}, {{POSTURA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}} or {{MEDIO}} is missing, ask me before writing.

Parameters: {{TEMA}}, {{POSTURA}}, {{AUDIENCIA}}, {{MEDIO}}, {{EXTENSION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Clarity and conciseness audit of a text
prompts.content:
Audit the following text applying the indicated parameters. Run the complete diagnosis, generate the revised version and deliver comparative metrics. If your confidence in the parameters is ≥ 0.85, start directly.

Parameters (edit in text):
· Target audience: corporate professionals with university education
· Desired tone: formal-neutral
· Intervention level: C — rewrite completely
· Reduction target: 25% fewer words without losing meaning
· Output language: same as the input text
· Special emphasis: eliminate redundancies and filler phrases

Expected output: diagnosis in table, numbered problem map, revised version with changes in bold, change log in table, comparative metrics and 3-5 editorial recommendations.

[TEXT TO AUDIT]
(Paste text here)

— MetodologIA Protocol: each output is traceable, evidenced and oriented so the user learns while receiving the deliverable.

prompts.title: Tone adjustment for the target audience
prompts.content:
Act as a senior communication editor specialized in register adaptation by audience, with the editorial judgment to shift the tone without betraying the intent or inventing data. Your goal is to recalibrate an already-written text so that a specific audience reads it in full and reacts as intended — not to dilute it into a neutral message that connects with no one.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

Proceed as follows:
1. Restate the assignment in one sentence: "Recalibrate {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}} for {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}} so that {{EFECTO_BUSCADO}}, preserving message, data and {{ELEMENTOS_INTOCABLES}}". If {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}} or {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}} is missing, ask for it before proceeding.
2. Diagnose the current tone of {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}} with evidence from the text itself: register, lexical density, average sentence length, level of technical language and distance with the reader.
3. Profile {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}}: what they know, what matters to them, what jargon they recognize, what puts them off. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every unconfirmed inference.
4. Name the gaps between the current tone and what {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}} expects given {{NIVEL_FORMALIDAD}}.
5. Rewrite the full text adjusting only register, vocabulary, sentence length, examples and technical language to provoke {{EFECTO_BUSCADO}}. Do not change the message or the data; respect {{ELEMENTOS_INTOCABLES}} without altering them.
6. Deliver a table of key changes: element, before, after, reason.

Do not invent facts or figures. If a register change would require distorting a piece of data, flag it rather than applying it. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as reference context. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. Variables: {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}}, {{AUDIENCIA_OBJETIVO}}, {{EFECTO_BUSCADO}}, {{NIVEL_FORMALIDAD}}, {{ELEMENTOS_INTOCABLES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Restructuring with the pyramid principle
prompts.content: Act as a senior executive editor trained in Minto's pyramid principle, specialized in reordering business communication for senior-level readers. You are working on {{DOCUMENTO}}, read by {{AUDIENCIA}}, with the focus of enabling the reader to {{DECISION_O_ACCION}} after reading. This is structural editing, not rewriting: you preserve the content and change the order and hierarchy. If {{DOCUMENTO}}, {{AUDIENCIA}} or {{DECISION_O_ACCION}} is missing, ask for it before starting. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. Then deliver: 1) Diagnosis of the current structure: real main idea, supporting arguments, where the conclusion was buried, logical gaps and non-MECE groups. 2) New pyramid: one governing idea in a single sentence, plus two to four MECE supporting groups, each answering the question (why or how) at the level above; indicate whether the logic is deductive or inductive. 3) SCQA opening (Situation, Complication, Question, Answer) calibrated to {{AUDIENCIA}} with the Answer first. 4) Reordered document preserving the original text, with [MISSING SUPPORT] where an assertion has no evidence. 5) Record of structural changes, one move per line with justification. Do not invent content or evidence. If {{DOCUMENTO}} is already well structured, say so and propose only minor adjustments. If two governing ideas compete, declare it and recommend which one to prioritize based on {{DECISION_O_ACCION}}. Deliver in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} when specified; if not, use indented outline plus text. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any.

prompts.title: Cutting a text in half without losing the essence
prompts.content: Act as a senior editor specialized in condensation and economy of language, with the judgment to distinguish core from ornament. Your task: cut {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}} to {{PORCENTAJE_REDUCCION}} (default 50 percent) without losing what is essential or altering meaning, voice or register, calibrating for {{PUBLICO}} and preserving no matter what {{NO_NEGOCIABLES}}. If the text, the percentage, the audience or the non-negotiables are missing, ask for them before starting. Proceed in four phases. Diagnosis: count the starting words, set the target with a tolerance of plus or minus 5 percent and detect the thesis, logical structure and conclusion or call to action. Idea-by-idea triage: separate the untouchable core (thesis, indispensable arguments, closing and the {{NO_NEGOCIABLES}}) from the dispensable (redundant examples, ornamental adjectives, filler, repetitions, detours, empty connectors). Condensation: rewrite by merging sentences, eliminating redundancy and using strong verbs instead of periphrases; never invent content, never change data or register; calibrate tone and technical terms for {{PUBLICO}}. Verification: confirm the actual percentage is within tolerance, that no content was invented and that every non-negotiable was preserved. If a non-negotiable and the length target conflict, prioritize the non-negotiable and report the deviation. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. Deliverable: condensed text, a count table (before / after / actual percentage) and a list of preserved versus sacrificed. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan and present your plan before Executing. Neutral and professional Spanish.

prompts.title: Inclusive and respectful language review
prompts.content:
Act as a senior editor specialized in inclusive communication and non-sexist language, with a proven track record in neutral professional Spanish and mastery of resources that maintain fluency. You are going to audit {{TEXTO}}, which will circulate before {{PUBLICO}} through {{CANAL_Y_REGISTRO}}, where a term or construction may exclude, stereotype or render invisible part of the audience. Your objective is to enable an informed decision: correct real exclusions, preserve the original voice and leave traceability for every change.

Before auditing, confirm {{PUBLICO}}, {{CANAL_Y_REGISTRO}} and {{RESTRICCIONES_ESTILO}} (mandatory guide, permitted resources, untouchable terms). If any data is missing or ambiguous, ask; do not assume.

Sweep the text along seven axes of bias: gender (generic masculine, role stereotypes), disability/ability, age, origin and ethnicity, sexual orientation and identity, socioeconomic level and health condition; prioritize {{EJES_PRIORITARIOS}} if indicated. Also flag what infantilizes, victimizes or exoticizes. For each finding: original fragment, type of bias, why it excludes or stereotypes, and rewriting. Prioritize collective nouns, epicene forms, paraphrases, direct address and reformulation; avoid serial splitting, the @ symbol, x or e unless {{PUBLICO}} or {{RESTRICCIONES_ESTILO}} require it, marking it as a justified exception. Label each finding as a mandatory change (real exclusion) or style suggestion. Flag borderline cases rather than imposing them.

Deliver: (a) traceable findings table, (b) full rewritten text already integrated preserving meaning, register, technical terminology and approximate length, and (c) 2–3 line rationale note. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Do not invent data; mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Brand voice consistency verification
Professional style and grammar correction
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Spanish style editor, with command of the Pan-Hispanic RAE standard (Ortografía de la lengua española, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, Nueva gramática) and a track record of correcting corporate documents without distorting the intent of the person who signs them. Your objective is to deliver an impeccable version, ready to send or publish, that preserves the author's voice intact and teaches them what to correct to write better next time.

Work on this document: {{DOCUMENTO}}. Consider that it is a {{TIPO_DOCUMENTO}} addressed to {{AUDIENCIA}}, with a {{NIVEL_FORMALIDAD}} register and reinforced attention on {{FOCO_PRIORITARIO}}. Also review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. If any necessary data is missing or there is ambiguity that would change correction decisions, ask before touching the text.

First detect the document's actual register based on its audience and formality. Then review on three planes: spelling (accentuation, punctuation, capitalization, diacritical accent marks, quotation marks and em dashes), grammar (agreement, prepositional government, verb tenses and moods, connectors, queísmo and dequeísmo) and style (clarity, conciseness, filler phrases, redundancies, avoidable anglicisms, overloaded paragraphs), with emphasis on {{FOCO_PRIORITARIO}}. Classify the issues by plane before modifying anything.

Correct surgically: minimum necessary adjustments, distinguishing normative error from legitimate stylistic variation (which is not touched). Do not rewrite from scratch or change the meaning. Flag as a suggestion, not an imposition, any debatable correction or one that depends on a brand convention you are unaware of.

Deliver in this order: (1) corrected document, clean and ready to use; (2) change table with columns original, corrected and reason (rule applied), grouping minor recurring errors in one row; (3) three substantive observations about recurring style patterns. Each correction is justified by a specific rule, not by subjective preference.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Readability and scannability improvement
prompts.content:
Act as a senior digital content editor and information architect, expert in readability, scannability, and on-screen reading design. Your mission is to redesign the reading surface of a dense text so the message is grasped in seconds, without rewriting the content or inventing data: same substance, instant access.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before reformatting, reformulate in your own words what text you received, where it will be read, and who reads it, and present your restructuring plan (summary, blocks, where lists will go versus paragraphs).

Input data:
- TEXTO_ORIGINAL: {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}} (dense text to reformat; if empty, request it before executing)
- CANAL_DESTINO: {{CANAL_DESTINO}} (email, intranet, mobile web, PDF, Notion)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} (who reads it and how much urgency they have)
- MAX_LINEAS_PARRAFO: {{MAX_LINEAS_PARRAFO}} (maximum lines per paragraph; use 3-4 if not specified)
- ELEMENTOS_INTOCABLES: {{ELEMENTOS_INTOCABLES}} (quotes, figures, names, or clauses that must remain literal)

Proceed as follows: extract the central idea and write it as a one- or two-sentence summary at the beginning (inverted pyramid). Segment the body of {{TEXTO_ORIGINAL}} into thematic blocks and give each one a descriptive subheading that previews its content, never generic. Break up the prose into paragraphs of maximum {{MAX_LINEAS_PARRAFO}} lines, one single idea per paragraph. Convert enumerations, steps, and criteria into bullet points or numbered lists. Apply selective bold, maximum one or two emphases per block. Adapt the density to {{CANAL_DESTINO}} and the urgency level of {{AUDIENCIA}}: mobile web calls for very short paragraphs and frequent subheadings; PDF tolerates slightly larger blocks. Keep meaning, tone, and voice intact, and reproduce {{ELEMENTOS_INTOCABLES}} literally.

Verify by rereading against the original to confirm no nuance was lost or added. Mark with [SUPUESTO] any inference about segmentation or hierarchy, and ask if an ambiguity prevents proceeding faithfully. Deliver the reformatted text ready to paste in {{CANAL_DESTINO}}, followed by a brief note with the structural changes applied and the assumptions made.

prompts.title: Headline optimization by variants
prompts.content:
Act as a senior headline editor and direct-response copywriter, with practice in message optimization and A/B testing of headings for different channels. I want to choose the strongest headline for {{MEDIO}} starting from the draft {{TITULAR_BASE}}, aimed at {{AUDIENCIA}}, comparing it against alternatives with explicit criteria rather than intuition, because the headline decides whether the piece is read or ignored. If {{TITULAR_BASE}}, {{MEDIO}}, or {{AUDIENCIA}} are missing, ask me for them before starting; if {{RESTRICCIONES}} or {{NUMERO_VARIANTES}} are not provided, assume reasonable values (5-7 variants by default) and declare them. Proceed as follows. First, framing: confirm base headline, medium, audience, desired action, and constraints {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and define in one line each axis: Clarity (understood on first reading, without ambiguity), Hook (curiosity or tension that invites continuing) and Promise (what the reader explicitly gains). Second, generate {{NUMERO_VARIANTES}} variants covering genuinely different angles: direct benefit, curiosity, legitimate urgency, proof or specificity, and contrast or question; no cosmetic rewrites. Third, table with each variant scored 1 to 5 on Clarity, Hook, and Promise, total out of 15, and a sentence that justifies the scores and names the main risk. Fourth, rank from highest to lowest score, resolve ties in favor of the best Clarity, declare the winner and explain why it fits {{MEDIO}} and {{AUDIENCIA}}. Fifth, deliver two concrete micro-adjustments on the winner. Penalize sensationalism that the piece cannot deliver and any violation of constraints; mark with [SUPUESTO] any unverifiable performance claim and do not invent open-rate or conversion metrics. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides context. Deliver in neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Cultural localization of a message
Results-oriented meeting agenda
Effective Slack or chat message
prompts.content: Act as a senior facilitator of internal asynchronous communication, expert in drafting Slack and team chat messages with a high first-reply rate, with a strict criterion of reader time economy. I am going to ask you to write a chat message to get {{PEDIDO}} from {{DESTINATARIO}} via an asynchronous channel, where I cannot clarify doubts in real time, so the message must give them everything needed to reply in a single pass. If {{DESTINATARIO}}, {{PEDIDO}}, {{CONTEXTO}}, or {{PLAZO}} are missing, ask me for them before drafting; do not invent names, dates, or figures. Proceed as follows: (1) reformulate the objective in one sentence "Get {{PEDIDO}} from {{DESTINATARIO}} before {{PLAZO}}"; (2) classify the message as decision, review, data, or task-unblocking, because that defines the expected reply; (3) design the message backward from the exact reply that counts as resolved, eliminating everything that does not enable it; (4) draft it scannably in this order: first line that summarizes the request and urgency and can stand alone as a notification, minimum context derived from {{CONTEXTO}} and covering only what the recipient does not know, the request as a closed question or concrete action and numbered if there are several, explicit deadline from {{PLAZO}} with date, time, and what it unblocks, and if applicable a default option of the type "if you do not reply before [time] I will assume X and move forward". Adjust the tone according to {{CANAL_TONO}}: direct and cordial, neutral Spanish, no emojis, no apologies or corporate filler, no aggressive pressure. Incorporate {{ADJUNTOS}} with a brief reference to what to look at in each one. Before the final version, reread it as if you were {{DESTINATARIO}} and confirm they could reply without asking anything again; trim every dispensable word. Deliver the message ready to paste and, below it, in a single line, any assumed data marked as [SUPUESTO]. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Team announcement of an initiative
Structured feedback with the SBI model (Situation-Behavior-Impact)
prompts.content: Act as a senior facilitator of internal communication and leadership coach trained in the SBI (Situation-Behavior-Impact) model from the Center for Creative Leadership, with experience conducting high-tension feedback conversations. I need a {{TIPO_FEEDBACK}} feedback message addressed to {{NOMBRE_O_ROL_RECEPTOR}}, ready to deliver in conversation, built with SBI. First reformulate who it is addressed to, the type of feedback, the episode {{SITUACION_OBSERVADA}}, and {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}}; mark with [SUPUESTO] any data I have not confirmed and ask me for what is missing before drafting. Then isolate the observable fact from your interpretation and sketch the three components separately. Situation: anchor a single concrete moment (when and where) from {{SITUACION_OBSERVADA}}, without generalizing with always or never. Behavior: describe only what {{NOMBRE_O_ROL_RECEPTOR}} said or did in neutral language, without judgment adjectives or attribution of intentions; if the data came from a third party, say so explicitly. Impact: name the concrete effect on the team, the client, or the result, and distinguish the factual impact from your personal interpretation using a formula such as what I saw was X, what I interpreted was Y. If {{TIPO_FEEDBACK}} is reinforcing, make explicit the behavior to repeat; if it is redirecting, orient toward {{RESULTADO_DESEADO}} without solving it for the person, preserving their autonomy. Close with an open question. Do not use the sandwich format. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Deliver three pieces: SBI message in brief prose, labeled S/B/I breakdown with [SUPUESTO] visible, and closing question. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: One-on-one conversation script
prompts.content:
Act as a senior leadership coach and one-on-one conversation facilitator, expert in the model of effective 1:1s (Manager Tools style), bidirectional feedback (Radical Candor with the situation-behavior-impact pattern) and professional development with the GROW framework. I need to prepare a one-on-one meeting with {{PERSONA}}, where my relationship and authority are {{ROL_RELACION}}, that is the person's time and not a disguised status report. Before drafting, reformulate in one sentence the relationship, frequency, duration, and objective of the meeting from {{ROL_RELACION}} and {{FRECUENCIA_CONTEXTO}}; if an essential piece of data is missing, ask me and do not invent facts about {{PERSONA}} or cite achievements or frictions not provided in {{SENALES_RECIENTES}}. Then design the agenda in five blocks with suggested time allocation over the duration of {{FRECUENCIA_CONTEXTO}}: (a) Human check-in, (b) Progress and achievements, (c) Blockers and impediments, (d) Bidirectional feedback, (e) Professional development; reprioritize according to {{TEMAS_PRIORITARIOS}}. For each block deliver: purpose in one line, 2 to 4 open questions ready to read aloud, and an alert signal. Anchor Progress and Blockers in {{SENALES_RECIENTES}}; in Blockers distinguish what the person resolves, what they need from me, and what escalates, and assign an owner and next step for each. In Feedback, draft a concrete observation with situation-behavior-impact and a question to request feedback about myself; mark [SUPUESTO] any inferred observation. In Development, apply GROW on a career aspiration of {{PERSONA}}, not quarterly tasks. Close with an agreements block: commitments with owner and date, plus a single closing sentence in a caring tone. Adapt to the real authority of {{ROL_RELACION}}: if peer or mentor without reporting line, reformulate feedback as peer-to-peer observation and agreements as voluntary commitments. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Deliver in neutral Spanish, professional and warm tone, no emojis. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Parameters:
- {{ROL_RELACION}}: relationship with the person and authority I have (direct leader, peer, or mentor)
- {{PERSONA}}: who they are (role, tenure, and what is relevant to discuss)
- {{FRECUENCIA_CONTEXTO}}: how often we meet and how long this meeting lasts
- {{TEMAS_PRIORITARIOS}}: topics I definitely want to cover today (optional)
- {{SENALES_RECIENTES}}: achievements, frictions, changes, or open items since the last meeting (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Building a zero-based annual budget
prompts.content: Act as a senior Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A) Director, expert in Zero-Based Budgeting and management control, capable of translating operational activity into a defensible cost structure. Build the annual budget of {{UNIDAD_O_AREA}} for {{PERIODO_FISCAL}} using zero-based methodology: no line item starts from the prior period's spend or is adjusted by default for inflation; every dollar is re-justified from zero against an activity driver and an objective. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol (Interpret > Plan > Execute): first reformulate what you understand about {{UNIDAD_O_AREA}}, {{PERIODO_FISCAL}}, {{DRIVERS_DE_NEGOCIO}}, {{TECHO_PRESUPUESTAL}}, and {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}}; present your plan; then execute. Proceed as follows: (1) break down {{UNIDAD_O_AREA}} into budgetable decision units; (2) for each unit identify the driver from {{DRIVERS_DE_NEGOCIO}} that explains its resource consumption and establish the cost-driver relationship; (3) build for each unit at least three incremental packages (minimum viable, current operations, enhanced) with driver volume, justified cost, and benefit or risk of each level; (4) rank all packages in a single prioritized list by value-cost and mark the cut-off point according to {{TECHO_PRESUPUESTAL}}, indicating what is inside and outside; (5) consolidate by unit and by month aligned with {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}}, narrate the budget strategy, and close with 3 to 5 estimation risks with their monitoring metric. Rules: do not invent figures; if key data is missing, ask before calculating; label every own estimation as [SUPUESTO]; verify the consolidated total matches the sum of approved packages. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliverable: decision units table, prioritized packages table with cut-off, monthly consolidated by unit, brief strategy narrative, and risks table with monitoring metrics.

prompts.title: Build an incremental budget based on historical data
prompts.content: Act as a senior Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) manager with experience in incremental budgeting and scenario building for committee review. I need to build the budget for {{PERIODO_OBJETIVO}} in {{MONEDA}}, starting from the prior actual close and adjusting each line for inflation, growth, and known events, in order to take it to committee with a line-by-line defense. Before calculating, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand (objective, period, currency, scope of line items) and list the gaps; Plan by showing how you classify each line (fixed, variable, semi-variable), its adjustment driver, and the inflation and growth ranges per scenario; Execute only after. Inputs: actual historical figures by line {{HISTORICO_LINEAS}} (ideally 2–3 periods), expected inflation {{INFLACION_ESPERADA}}, growth or cut targets {{METAS_CRECIMIENTO}}, known events {{EVENTOS_CONOCIDOS}}. Ask for anything missing; do not invent figures: any data not provided is marked [ASSUMPTION] with its assumed value and source. Project each line with adjusted base = prior actual × (1 + inflation) × (1 + growth) ± one-time events, showing formula, projected amount, absolute delta, and percentage delta versus the prior period. Build base, conservative, and aggressive scenarios by varying inflation and growth; summarize the impact on total revenue, total expenses, and margin. Prioritize assumptions by sensitivity and close with a risk note and recommendations. Edge cases: negative or zero base, adjust on the amount; non-recurring event, exclude it from the next base and state it explicitly; no line history, build it bottom-up and mark it [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver: line-by-line table + three-scenario comparison + numbered list of assumptions prioritized by sensitivity + risk note, in {{MONEDA}} with consistent formatting, ready for committee.

prompts.title: Model a driver-based budget
prompts.content: Act as a senior FP&A Director expert in driver-based budgeting, flexible financial modeling, and cost-behavior analysis (fixed, variable, and semi-variable or step-fixed). Convert the budget of {{UNIDAD_DE_NEGOCIO}} into a recalculable driver-based model, where the budget reforecasts automatically when a driver changes and it becomes explicit which portion of spending is structurally fixed. Inputs: income-statement lines with base amounts {{LINEAS_PRESUPUESTO}}, measurable operational drivers and their projected values {{DRIVERS_DISPONIBLES}}, known historical rates or ratios {{TASAS_HISTORICAS}}, horizon and granularity {{HORIZONTE}}, currency {{MONEDA}}, sensitivity ranges {{RANGOS_SENSIBILIDAD}}, and supporting materials {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before modeling, restate what you understand and identify gaps; if line detail, drivers, rates, horizon, or currency is missing, ask in a single round before proceeding. Do not invent figures and mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver: (1) mapping of each line in {{LINEAS_PRESUPUESTO}} to its primary driver from {{DRIVERS_DISPONIBLES}} with fixed/variable/semi-variable classification; (2) formula for each variable and semi-variable line (driver × unit rate + fixed component when applicable) using {{TASAS_HISTORICAS}}, deriving missing rates as base amount divided by historical driver; (3) driver cascade separating root from derived, without circular dependencies; (4) recalculable base budget in {{HORIZONTE}} and {{MONEDA}} with driver, unit rate, fixed component, formula, and amount per line, reconciled against current totals with the difference explained; (5) sensitivity table moving revenue, costs, contribution margin, and EBITDA against variations in {{RANGOS_SENSIBILIDAD}} for key drivers, with consistent signs; (6) [ASSUMPTION] items, model risks (rate linearity, relevant range, correlated drivers) and control points for reviewing rates. Close by explaining how to reforecast by changing a single driver. Do not include market prices or external quotes. Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, and Execute, restating what you understand and presenting your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Design a flexible budget by activity levels
prompts.content:
Act as a senior FP&A financial controller expert in management accounting, flexible budgeting, and variance analysis, with mastery of cost behavior and the cost-volume-profit model. Your task is to build a flexible budget for {{UNIDAD_NEGOCIO}} that recalibrates expected spending to the volume actually achieved, so that management control stops blending the volume effect with the efficiency effect.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate what you understand about {{UNIDAD_NEGOCIO}}, the driver {{INDUCTOR_ACTIVIDAD}}, and {{PARTIDAS_COSTO}}; then present your plan; then execute. If any essential data is missing, ask for it before calculating.

Proceed as follows: 1) Confirm the driver {{INDUCTOR_ACTIVIDAD}} and the {{RANGO_RELEVANTE}} where cost relationships are stable. 2) Classify each line item in {{PARTIDAS_COSTO}} as fixed, variable, or semi-variable with an explicit criterion. 3) For each semi-variable line separate the fixed and variable component using the high-low method or regression if there is sufficient history; if not, mark the assumption and report limitations. 4) Derive the variable rate per driver unit for each variable line and the fixed amount per period for each fixed line. 5) Apply the master formula: Total budgeted cost = Total fixed costs + (variable rate per unit × actual volume). 6) Generate the flexible budget table for the {{NIVELES_ACTIVIDAD}}, with {{VOLUMEN_ESPERADO}} as the base case, and report the total unit cost per tier. 7) If actuals are available, build the three-way analysis (static vs. flexible = volume; flexible vs. actual = spending/efficiency), label favorable/unfavorable and verify the sum equals the total variance. 8) Calculate the breakeven point in driver units and the safety margin relative to {{VOLUMEN_ESPERADO}}. 9) Close with an executive reading of 4 to 6 bullet points that separates variances due to volume from variances due to spending management and proposes the associated decision. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

Rules: do not invent data; every estimate is marked as [ASSUMPTION]; do not project outside {{RANGO_RELEVANTE}} without warning that relationships may break down. Deliver the table by activity tier, formulas by line item, the three-way variance analysis when applicable, and the executive reading.

Parameters:
- {{UNIDAD_NEGOCIO}}: area, product line, or cost center to budget
- {{INDUCTOR_ACTIVIDAD}}: volume driver on which the budget flexes
- {{PARTIDAS_COSTO}}: line items with historical amounts and, if known, their behavior
- {{VOLUMEN_ESPERADO}}: expected base level in driver units
- {{NIVELES_ACTIVIDAD}}: volume tiers to budget
- {{RANGO_RELEVANTE}}: (optional) range where cost relationships are stable
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Separate and plan a CapEx vs. OpEx budget
prompts.content: Act as a senior financial controller with experience in budget planning, capitalization policies, and accounting close under {{MARCO_CONTABLE}}. I have {{LISTA_DESEMBOLSOS}} planned for {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}} and they are mixed without distinguishing investment from expense. I need to separate CapEx from OpEx with an auditable criterion, because misclassifying a line item distorts operating profit, EBITDA, the asset base, and the cash projection, and may violate {{MARCO_CONTABLE}}. Before executing, confirm {{MARCO_CONTABLE}}, {{UMBRAL_CAPITALIZACION}}, {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}, and {{POLITICAS_DEPRECIACION}}; if a critical piece of data is missing, ask me for it rather than assuming it. Then apply this decision tree to each line item in {{LISTA_DESEMBOLSOS}}: it is CapEx only if it creates or improves a long-lived asset, its economic benefit exceeds one fiscal year, and it exceeds {{UMBRAL_CAPITALIZACION}}; otherwise it is OpEx. Flag and justify edge cases (major maintenance vs. repair, licensed software vs. capitalizable development, finance lease vs. operating lease, leasehold improvements, R&D, cloud implementation costs, pre-operating expenses) according to {{MARCO_CONTABLE}}. For each CapEx item define the useful life, depreciation/amortization method from {{POLITICAS_DEPRECIACION}}, residual value if applicable, and month of commissioning, distinguishing disbursement date from depreciation start date. Build the monthly disbursement calendar for {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}, separating CapEx and OpEx. Project the impact on the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement, reconcile that disbursements tie to the projected cash flow, and flag the accrual-to-cash gap. Deliver a classification table with criterion per line item, the disbursement calendar, the depreciation schedule, the impact projection in the three statements, and an executive summary with three readings (operating profit, cash, assets). Do not invent figures, useful lives, or rates: any data not provided should be marked [ASSUMPTION]. Close with two sensitivities: treating an ambiguous line as OpEx instead of CapEx, and advancing or delaying a commissioning date. Parameters: {{LISTA_DESEMBOLSOS}}, {{UMBRAL_CAPITALIZACION}}, {{POLITICAS_DEPRECIACION}}, {{MARCO_CONTABLE}}, {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Set up a departmental budget with owners
prompts.content:
Act as a senior financial controller specialized in FP&A and cost-center budgeting, with experience in spending governance and zero-based budgeting. Convert the global budget of {{ORGANIZACION}} for the period {{PERIODO}} into governed departmental pools: every monetary unit with a named owner, caps that warn before overspending, and reallocation rules that are agile but traceable. The deliverable goes to the financial committee and supports month-by-month tracking.

Proceed as follows: (1) Master table by cost center from {{DEPARTAMENTOS}}: name, amount, percentage of total, a single owner, and the criterion for the amount; report the reconciliation against {{PRESUPUESTO_GLOBAL}}. (2) Break each cost center into relevant expense lines. (3) For each line define a hard cap and a soft cap (e.g., 80 percent) with the action each one triggers. (4) Three-level reallocation rules (owner alone / superior / committee), each level with a limit in amount and percentage of the pool, per {{POLITICA_REASIGNACION}}. (5) Central contingency with release criterion and approver. (6) Review cycle and approval workflow. Close with three over-execution risks and their mitigation.

Apply {{CRITERIOS_ASIGNACION}} to distribute; if not provided, propose a base method (historical adjusted for priorities) and mark it [ASSUMPTION]. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Golden rule: allocations plus contingency must equal {{PRESUPUESTO_GLOBAL}} exactly; never invent figures and ask for any critical missing data before calculating.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Parameters: {{ORGANIZACION}}, {{PERIODO}}, {{PRESUPUESTO_GLOBAL}}, {{DEPARTAMENTOS}}, {{CRITERIOS_ASIGNACION}}, {{POLITICA_REASIGNACION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Budget a project by WBS
prompts.content: Act as a senior project manager and certified cost estimator (PMP/PMI-SP) with experience building bottom-up WBS budgets. I need a defensible budget before a sponsor or committee for {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, auditable package by package, separating work from reserve and known risks from unknown. Build the complete budget as follows: (1) decompose {{ALCANCE_ENTREGABLES}} into a 3-level hierarchical WBS (major deliverable > component > work package) coded 1, 1.1, 1.1.1, each package a unit that can be estimated and assigned, applying the 100% rule (covers all scope and nothing outside, with no duplicates); (2) estimate each package bottom-up using {{ROLES_TARIFAS}}, indicating role, hours per role, and cost per hour, summing to the direct cost of the package, and mark every productivity or rate assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; (3) roll up from package to component to base cost, consistent with {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}; (4) add {{COSTOS_INDIRECTOS}} (tools, licenses, infrastructure, travel) as explicit lines separate from the work; (5) calculate the contingency reserve (known risks) using {{PORCENTAJE_CONTINGENCIA}} or deriving it from estimation maturity, and the management reserve (unknown risks) as a separate percentage, each with a rationale, never mixing them; (6) present the cost baseline (base cost + contingency) and the total budget (baseline + management reserve) with the distinction made explicit. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan. If {{COSTOS_INDIRECTOS}} or {{PORCENTAJE_CONTINGENCIA}} arrive empty, work with what is given and mark the assumption; do not invent rates or hours as factual. Deliver: a coded WBS table, an estimation table by package (role, hours, cost), a roll-up summary by level, and a reserves block with rationale, in hours and parameterized amounts without assuming a currency unless stated. Variables: {{NOMBRE_PROYECTO}}, {{ALCANCE_ENTREGABLES}}, {{ROLES_TARIFAS}}, {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}, {{COSTOS_INDIRECTOS}}, {{PORCENTAJE_CONTINGENCIA}}.

prompts.title: Allocate the marketing budget by expected ROI
prompts.content: Act as a Marketing Finance Director (growth finance lead) with expertise in unit economics, marginal-return budget allocation, and channel saturation models. I need a plan to allocate my marketing budget {{PRESUPUESTO_PERIODO}} across the channels {{CANALES_HISTORICO}} to maximize the projected return per unit invested at the margin — not to distribute by inertia or by last period's spending. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understand and restate it, Plan and present your plan before executing, then Execute. Always work in my currency. Before calculating, ask me for any missing data: do not invent conversion rates, LTV, CAC, or channel figures; if they are missing, request them. Deliver the plan in this order. 1) Framing: confirm the budget, period, channels, the thresholds {{UMBRALES}}, and the constraints {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and declare every assumption you use marked as [ASSUMPTION]. 2) Diagnosis by channel: for each channel in {{CANALES_HISTORICO}} calculate using the formula and the visible data: CAC = investment divided by acquired customers; ROAS = attributed revenue divided by investment; LTV/CAC using {{LTV_MARGEN}}; and payback period = CAC divided by monthly contribution margin per customer. 3) Marginal return: estimate the effect of the next euro invested in each channel, acknowledging diminishing returns and saturation; do not assume the historical average holds at scale and make explicit the point where marginal efficiency falls below the threshold. 4) Allocation: rank channels by marginal efficiency and allocate from highest to lowest return, stopping at each channel when its marginal return falls below the threshold or its capacity cap is reached; respect the contractual minimums from {{RESTRICCIONES}} and explicitly reserve a fraction for experimentation in channels without sufficient history. 5) Resulting portfolio: present a table with amount, percentage of total, expected CAC, and expected payback by channel, plus the portfolio-weighted LTV/CAC and ROAS, and the difference versus last period's allocation. 6) Dynamic reallocation rules: three to five actionable triggers indicating when to move money between channels based on observed CAC, payback, or saturation, with the metric, threshold, and action. Close with a risk and verification block: confirm the allocated sum equals the total budget, list the assumptions that most move the result and their sensitivity, and flag overlapping attribution or seasonality if applicable. Do not include service proposal prices. If {{ADJUNTOS}} contains data, use it as the primary source. Parameters: {{PRESUPUESTO_PERIODO}}, {{CANALES_HISTORICO}}, {{LTV_MARGEN}}, {{UMBRALES}}, {{RESTRICCIONES}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Design the budgeting calendar and process
prompts.content:
Act as an FP&A Director with experience leading the end-to-end annual budget cycle at medium and large companies, fluent in financial governance and board reporting. Design the master calendar and budgeting process for {{ORGANIZACION}}, a fiscal year starting in {{INICIO_ANO_FISCAL}}, with {{NUMERO_AREAS}} areas loading bottom-up and approval via {{INSTANCIAS_APROBACION}}, with granularity {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} and budget approach {{ENFOQUE_PRESUPUESTAL}}. If any critical data is missing, ask for it before executing.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Produce: (1) a phase calendar with dates in week -N relative to the fiscal-year start, counting backward from board approval: executive guidance, assumptions book, templates and kickoff, bottom-up load by area, consolidation, first management review, adjustment iterations, committee review, and board approval; (2) a RACI matrix by milestone across CFO, FP&A, area leaders, controller, CEO, and board, with a single R and a single A per milestone; (3) concrete deliverables by phase (guidance memo, assumptions book, load templates, consolidated P&L, board deck, approved budget, frozen baseline); (4) quality gates with verifiable exit criteria between phases; (5) risk plan (load delays, misaligned assumptions, sandbagging, lack of quorum, post-freeze re-opening) with actionable mitigations and an owner.

Calibrate the number of iterations according to {{ORGANIZACION}}. Mark inferred items with [ASSUMPTION]; no invented figures. The sequence closes before day 1 of the fiscal year with slack for one contingency iteration. Deliver everything in tables ready to present to finance and the board. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

prompts.title: Prepare a budget defense for management
prompts.content:
Act as a Finance Director (fractional CFO) with a track record leading budget defenses and investment reviews before management committees and boards. You are going to defend the request {{SOLICITUD_PRESUPUESTAL}} before {{AUDIENCIA_DIRECCION}}, in a setting where the decision is won or lost on the strength of the case, not the figure. The investment enables or protects {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}, operates under the constraint {{RESTRICCION_CLAVE}}, and is evaluated against {{DATOS_LINEA_BASE}} with a return horizon of {{HORIZONTE_RETORNO}}. If any essential data is missing or ambiguous, ask me for it before proceeding rather than inventing it.

MetodologIA Protocol: first interpret and restate what you understand about the assignment, then present your plan, and only then execute.

Deliver a document with seven numbered components: 1) One-page executive summary with the ask, the business result it enables, and your recommendation. 2) Current baseline and gap justifying the request, using figures from {{DATOS_LINEA_BASE}} and declared assumptions. 3) Three quantified scenarios (conservative, base, ambitious) with drivers, expected return, and horizon {{HORIZONTE_RETORNO}} — distinguishable from one another. 4) Trade-off table covering approve in full, approve partially, and reject: what is gained, what is deferred, and what is put at risk in each case under {{RESTRICCION_CLAVE}}. 5) Map of likely objections by each member of {{AUDIENCIA_DIRECCION}} according to their dominant priority, with a prepared response, supporting data, and the cost of not deciding. 6) Measurable success indicators with control points and re-evaluation thresholds. 7) Final ask with actionable next steps, owner, and date.

Rules: never use prices or absolute amounts beyond those provided in {{DATOS_LINEA_BASE}}; express magnitudes in person-months, capacity, risk, and relative return. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] every figure not provided and, if it is critical, ask for it before modeling. Do not present savings as revenue. Consider attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. Neutral professional English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Build a 13-week rolling cash forecast
Maintain a 12-month rolling forecast
prompts.content: Act as a Senior FP&A Analyst expert in P&L rolling forecasts, driver-based modeling, and variance analysis with bridges/walks. I maintain a continuous 12-month forecast and {{MES_CIERRE}} has just closed, moving from projection to actual and defining the new window. Proceed as follows. First, roll the window: mark {{MES_CIERRE}} as actual, reorder the horizon to 12 contiguous periods, and declare the new month 12 entering. Second, calculate the closed-month variance line by line comparing {{REALES_MES_CIERRE}} against what was projected in {{FORECAST_VIGENTE_12M}}: actual minus projected, decompose each deviation into price, volume, mix, timing, and one-off, and classify it as permanent (moves the run-rate) or transitory. Third, re-project the remaining 11 months and the new month from {{DRIVERS_POR_LINEA}}, propagating the corrected run-rate and {{SUPUESTOS_EVENTOS}}; no line without an explicit driver or assumption. Fourth, build the NTM walk from {{FORECAST_VIGENTE_12M}} to the new forecast, quantifying each movement by cause (carryover from the close, driver changes, new month, management decisions) so that the sum explains exactly the delta. Fifth, close with the executive read of the new number, the bias per {{HISTORIAL_PRECISION}}, live risks and opportunities, and assumptions to validate. Do not invent figures: if a data point is missing ask for it before calculating and label every estimate as an explicit assumption. Verify in each month that revenue minus COGS equals gross margin and gross margin minus OPEX equals EBITDA. Deliver the 12-month rolling P&L table (actual vs. projected), the close variance table with decomposition and permanent/transitory label, the NTM walk table, the list of drivers and assumptions by line, and a 6-to-8-line executive close. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

prompts.title: Project revenue bottom-up by pipeline
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior FP&A Analyst specializing in pipeline revenue forecasting: probability-weighted bottom-up models, revenue recognition, and scenario analysis. I need a reliable, auditable revenue forecast that supports cash, hiring, and commercial target defense decisions, built bottom-up opportunity by opportunity.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand from the inputs, present your calculation plan, then execute. If essential data is missing, ask before calculating: do not invent figures or dates.

Inputs:
- PIPELINE: {{PIPELINE}} (list of opportunities; each with identifier, contract amount, close probability 0–100%, funnel stage, and expected close date)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} (periods to project, e.g. next 4 quarters or next 12 months)
- GRANULARIDAD: {{GRANULARIDAD}} (aggregation unit: monthly or quarterly)
- TERMINOS_PAGO: {{TERMINOS_PAGO}} (how revenue is recognized per opportunity: single payment, monthly recurring, or by milestone; default single payment on the close date)
- UMBRAL_ESCENARIOS: {{UMBRAL_ESCENARIOS}} (criteria for conservative/base/optimistic; e.g. conservative = probability >= 70% or final stage)
- META_PERIODO: {{META_PERIODO}} (revenue target per period against which to measure pipeline gaps; optional)

Proceed as follows:
1. Normalize the pipeline: validate identifier, amount, probability, stage, and close date per opportunity; label [ASSUMPTION] for inferred data and [VERIFY] for what the business must confirm; detect duplicates, out-of-range probabilities, past-due dates, and stages inconsistent with the stated probability.
2. Calculate weighted value (amount × probability) and prorate recognition according to TERMINOS_PAGO (single/recurring/milestones), stating the rule when the source is ambiguous.
3. Aggregate by period according to GRANULARIDAD covering the full HORIZONTE.
4. Derive conservative, base, and optimistic from the same pipeline by changing only UMBRAL_ESCENARIOS thresholds, with each criterion explicit.
5. Report period table (3 lines), top drivers, assumptions and limits, concentration risks, and gaps vs. META_PERIODO.

Close: forecast table, top drivers, assumptions/limits, concentration risks, and follow-up strategy with refresh cadence and re-forecast triggers. Verify that the sum of weighted amounts by period equals the horizon total.

prompts.title: Project revenue top-down by market
prompts.content: Act as a CFO/FP&A Director with experience in B2B go-to-market models and in validating forecasts before investment committees. Build a top-down revenue projection by scenarios for {{MERCADO_OBJETIVO}} over a horizon of {{HORIZONTE}}, defensible before a committee. Before calculating, restate the assignment and present your plan; if an essential input is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it. Proceed as follows: (1) Size the funnel TAM ({{TAM}}) > SAM (reachable by geography/segment/fit) > SOM (capturable within the horizon), justifying and citing the origin of each cut; label as [ASSUMPTION] any figure without a source. (2) Set the target share ({{SHARE_OBJETIVO}}) over the SAM and trace a non-linear adoption curve with a slow start, never a simple proportional ramp. (3) Apply the capture rate ({{TASA_CAPTURA}}) discounting real funnel losses (unqualified leads, unclosed opportunities, sales-cycle effect), not the direct share. (4) Convert the captured quota to revenue via {{TICKET_PROMEDIO}}, incorporating recurrence and churn if the model is subscription-based; separate new revenue from recurring. (5) Cross the revenue against {{CAPACIDAD_ENTREGA}}: if the forecast exceeds it, mark the break-even point, cap it at the deliverable level, and report the capacity gap. (6) Deliver three scenarios (conservative, base, optimistic) with differential assumptions, isolate 3–5 highest-sensitivity levers, and declare risks and the condition that invalidates the forecast. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Return the step-by-step traceable calculation, the forecast capped to the deliverable level, and a log of assumptions and risks.

prompts.title: Forecast demand with time series
prompts.content: Act as a Senior Demand Planning Analyst (S&OP) with expertise in time-series forecasting and classical decomposition. I need to project the future demand of {{PRODUCTO_O_SKU}} from its historical series to support {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} with a basis — not by intuition: the value is not the number, it is the decision it enables. Proceed as follows. First, review the series {{SERIE_HISTORICA}} at frequency {{FRECUENCIA}} and the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}; if anything critical for modeling is missing, ask before continuing. Second, diagnose the series: length, gaps, zeros, outliers, level shifts, and questionable data, which you will flag explicitly and treat before modeling (do not model on dirty data). Third, decompose into trend, seasonality, and residual; fix the seasonal period and decide whether seasonality is additive (constant amplitude) or multiplicative (amplitude grows with the level), and justify. Fourth, select the smoothing method consistent with the pattern: moving average or simple exponential smoothing with no trend or seasonality, Holt with trend, Holt-Winters with trend and seasonality; explain why that method. Fifth, project the {{HORIZONTE}} periods with low, mid, and high bands derived from the residual dispersion, and translate the interval into the recommended coverage. Sixth, validate with backtesting on a holdout of the last periods and report MAPE, MAE, and over/under-forecast bias; if the error is high, say so and propose an alternative. Seventh, deliver a forecast table, numbered assumptions, limits vs. {{EVENTOS_CONOCIDOS}}, and a re-forecast plan with cadence and triggers. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide context. Truthfulness rule: every number comes from the provided series or is labeled [ASSUMPTION] with its rationale; never invent figures. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Measure and improve forecast accuracy
Project expenses by run-rate and commitments
prompts.content: Act as a Senior FP&A Analyst expert in OpEx forecasting by run-rate, contractual commitments, and headcount planning with fully-loaded cost. I need to project the expenses of {{UNIDAD}} for {{PERIODO_PROYECTADO}}, starting from {{PERIODO_BASE}}, in {{MONEDA_PERIODICIDAD}}, with a figure defensible before management or a committee — not a back-of-the-envelope estimate. Before calculating, restate the task in one sentence naming the unit, the projected period, the base period, and the periodicity; if {{GASTO_BASE}}, {{COMPROMISOS}}, or {{NUEVAS_CONTRATACIONES}} is missing, ask and do not invent figures or contracts. Then: (1) calculate the base run-rate using only the recurring costs of {{GASTO_BASE}}, exclude one-offs declaring them so, and normalize to the target periodicity; (2) incorporate {{COMPROMISOS}} adding only the portion within {{PERIODO_PROYECTADO}}, prorating starts and ends at mid-period and applying contractual escalations; (3) model {{NUEVAS_CONTRATACIONES}} with fully-loaded cost and a ramp per start date, so that a role starting mid-period only contributes the remaining months; (4) apply {{AJUSTES}} (salary increases, renewals with price changes, confirmed departures, inflation escalation) and label [ASSUMPTION] where no data was given; (5) add contingency as its own line (3–8% of variable OpEx) justifying the percentage; (6) present the forecast in a table by category and sub-period separating base run-rate, commitment delta, hiring delta, adjustments, and contingency, with row and column totals that tie; (7) reconcile the bottom-up against the simple annualized run-rate, decompose the delta, and declare the three most sensitive assumptions with their approximate impact. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Work in neutral professional Spanish with no selling prices or commercial rates: this is an internal expense projection. Close with the main risk of coming in short or over and what data would resolve it.

prompts.title: Model headcount and labor cost forecast
Adjust forecast for seasonality
prompts.content:
Act as a Senior FP&A Analyst specializing in financial planning and seasonality modeling. Your deliverable is a seasonalized monthly forecast table reconciled exactly to the annual total. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

Input data:
- Annual total to distribute: {{TOTAL_ANUAL}} (revenue and costs, with currency and forecast year)
- Monthly historical series: {{HISTORICO_MENSUAL}} (at least one complete cycle, ideally 2–3 years of the same months)
- Years of history available: {{ANIOS_HISTORICO}} (optional; inferred from the series if missing)
- Cost seasonality: {{COSTOS_SIGUEN_INGRESOS}} (whether it mirrors revenue seasonality or uses its own pattern; optional)
- Fixed costs: {{COSTOS_FIJOS}} (to distribute as linear and exclude from seasonalization; optional)

Do not calculate with missing data: ask for what is needed. First validate the quality of the historical data (coverage, gaps, zeros, negatives, atypical years from non-recurring events); label with [ASSUMPTION] anything inferred and propose excluding or adjusting the atypical year explaining its impact before continuing.

Calculate the seasonal index for each month using the ratio-to-moving-average method: each month over the average monthly value of its cycle, averaged across years. Normalize to average 1 (sum 12) and correct the rounding deviation in the highest-weight month. Apply the indices to {{TOTAL_ANUAL}} for revenue and cost in each month; leave {{COSTOS_FIJOS}} as linear and seasonalize only the variable portion. If {{COSTOS_SIGUEN_INGRESOS}} indicates its own pattern, derive a second set of indices. Reconcile the twelve-month sum against the annual total (difference 0 after tie-out) and show the adjustment. Calculate the monthly margin and flag peak and trough months.

Deliver a 12-row-plus-totals table (month, normalized index, revenue, cost, margin) and a note with method, assumptions, excluded years, peak/trough months, and a warning if the historical data is insufficient.

prompts.title: Define re-forecast triggers
prompts.content:
You are a Senior FP&A Director with experience in rolling forecasts, monthly closes, and variance governance in {{TIPO_NEGOCIO}}, accustomed to defending thresholds before a committee and a board. Design a re-forecast trigger policy that distinguishes normal noise from structural signal, for a forecast with a horizon of {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}} and the monitoring metrics {{METRICAS_VIGIA}}.

Before proposing figures, confirm {{TIPO_NEGOCIO}}, {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}, and {{METRICAS_VIGIA}}; if currency, critical line items, {{TOLERANCIA_DESVIACION}}, or {{GOBIERNO}} is missing, ask for it. Do not invent historical data or volatility figures; label everything you assume as an explicit assumption.

Deliver: (1) Monitoring metrics map {{METRICAS_VIGIA}}, each with reading frequency and comparison base (vs. plan, vs. current forecast, vs. same period prior year). (2) Quantitative triggers: thresholds in percentage and absolute, separating point deviation from year-to-date accumulated, each threshold with its rationale (historical volatility, materiality, decision irreversibility) and a persistence rule to avoid firing on a single isolated outlier. (3) Qualitative or event-based triggers: loss of anchor client, regulatory change, FX shock, merger or acquisition, pricing change, rupture of a base assumption. (4) Three-level severity matrix — watch / partial re-forecast / full re-forecast — each level with detector, validator, approver, and deadline, using {{GOBIERNO}} if defined. (5) Step-by-step activation protocol, from detection to publication and communication, with an auditable log (date, metric, deviation, decision, responsible party). Close with 2 to 3 test scenarios showing each trigger firing or not, no trivial false positives or blindness to real breaks.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

Rules: no prices or free-of-charge promises; neutral professional Spanish; every figure not provided labeled as an assumption. Deliverable: policy document ready for committee review.

Parameters:
- {{TIPO_NEGOCIO}}: business model and revenue type that defines the expected volatility by line item
- {{HORIZONTE_PLANEACION}}: horizon and cadence of the current forecast
- {{METRICAS_VIGIA}}: metrics to monitor as a re-forecast signal
- {{TOLERANCIA_DESVIACION}}: existing tolerance or noise band already accepted, if any (optional)
- {{GOBIERNO}}: roles available to detect, validate, and approve (optional)

prompts.title: Calculate SaaS unit economics
prompts.content: Act as a Senior SaaS Finance Analyst specializing in unit economics, with experience in revenue quality due diligence and cohort-level CAC/LTV models. I need to know whether the unit economics of my SaaS are sustainable: whether each customer returns more value than it costs to acquire and serve, and how long it takes to recover the investment. Build a unit economics model with a health verdict using these inputs: sales and marketing spend for the period {{GASTO_VENTAS_MARKETING}}, new customers in the same period {{CLIENTES_NUEVOS}}, average monthly recurring revenue per account {{ARPA_MENSUAL}}, gross margin {{MARGEN_BRUTO_PCT}}, monthly churn {{CHURN_MENSUAL_PCT}}, segment or cohort to analyze {{SEGMENTO}}, and attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. First normalize: make the currency and period explicit, and express {{MARGEN_BRUTO_PCT}} and {{CHURN_MENSUAL_PCT}} as decimal fractions consistent with a monthly horizon; if any data point is missing, ambiguous, or inconsistent (e.g. {{GASTO_VENTAS_MARKETING}} without a period or {{CHURN_MENSUAL_PCT}} annual mixed with {{ARPA_MENSUAL}} monthly), ask for it and do not invent figures. Second, CAC = {{GASTO_VENTAS_MARKETING}} / {{CLIENTES_NUEVOS}}; clarify whether blended or fully-loaded. Third, monthly contribution margin per customer = {{ARPA_MENSUAL}} × {{MARGEN_BRUTO_PCT}}. Fourth, LTV = ({{ARPA_MENSUAL}} × {{MARGEN_BRUTO_PCT}}) / {{CHURN_MENSUAL_PCT}}, with implied lifetime 1 / {{CHURN_MENSUAL_PCT}} in months and discounted LTV variant if the horizon is long. Fifth, CAC payback = CAC / monthly contribution margin, in months. Sixth, derive LTV:CAC and, if data exist, NDR, GRR, logo churn, Magic Number, and Rule of 40; segment by {{SEGMENTO}}. Seventh, benchmark and issue verdict. Show each formula with its substituted figures before each result. Label every own estimate as [ASSUMPTION]; never invent market figures. Edge cases: if {{CHURN_MENSUAL_PCT}} is zero or near zero, declare LTV unbounded and use an explicit cut-off horizon; if the contribution margin is negative, declare infinite payback and suspend LTV. Warn when a blended average may hide a value-destroying cohort. Deliver a table with CAC, contribution margin, LTV, payback, and LTV:CAC; the segmented calculation by {{SEGMENTO}}; the benchmark comparison; and a verdict with two or three prioritized levers. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Calculate and interpret the LTV/CAC ratio
Calculate the CAC payback period
Calculate contribution margin by product
prompts.content:
Act as a senior financial controller specialized in unit economics and product costing, with the ability to distinguish variable from fixed costs and to translate numbers into mix decisions.

My goal is to read the true profitability of my portfolio and decide the mix: what to push, what to reformulate, and what to discontinue.

Input data:
- Products to analyze: {{PRODUCTOS}} (name or code per SKU)
- Net unit selling price: {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}} (excluding pass-through taxes)
- Unit variable costs: {{COSTOS_VARIABLES_UNITARIOS}} (raw materials, commissions, freight, packaging, transactional)
- Volume for the period: {{VOLUMEN_VENTAS}} (units sold or projected per product)
- Analysis period: {{PERIODO}}
- Minimum acceptable ratio threshold: {{UMBRAL_RATIO}} (optional, as a percentage)
- Constrained resource: {{RECURSO_RESTRINGIDO}} (optional: machine-hours, m², person-hours)

Proceed as follows:
1. Confirm that you have {{PRODUCTOS}}, {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}}, {{COSTOS_VARIABLES_UNITARIOS}}, {{VOLUMEN_VENTAS}}, and {{PERIODO}}; if something essential is missing, ask for it in a brief list before calculating. Do not invent figures.
2. Classify each cost as variable or fixed with one line of justification; leave fixed costs out of the unit calculation and noted separately. If there are semi-variable costs, separate the fixed from the variable portion and declare the assumption.
3. Calculate unit margin = {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}} minus unit variable cost.
4. Calculate ratio = unit margin / {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}}, as a percentage.
5. Calculate total contribution = unit margin x {{VOLUMEN_VENTAS}}.
6. Sort by total contribution and flag products with a negative ratio or below {{UMBRAL_RATIO}}.
7. If there is a {{RECURSO_RESTRINGIDO}}, re-prioritize by contribution per unit of that resource, not just by ratio.
8. Issue three to five mix decisions (push, reformulate, discontinue) with estimated impact on aggregate contribution and the assumption supporting it.

Mark [ASSUMPTION] on every figure not supported by my data. Verify that unit margin × volume reconciles with total contribution. Neutral language, professional tone. Warn that contribution margin is not net profit.

prompts.title: Calculate the operating break-even point
prompts.content: Act as a senior financial controller specialized in unit economics and cost-volume-profit analysis (CVP model). I need to know the exact operating threshold of my business: the minimum volume and revenue where I stop losing and start gaining, plus the distance separating me from risk. Data: net selling price per unit = {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}}; direct variable cost per unit = {{COSTO_VARIABLE_UNITARIO}}; operating fixed costs for the period = {{COSTOS_FIJOS_PERIODO}}; horizon = {{PERIODO}}; current or projected sales for safety margin (optional) = {{VENTAS_REFERENCIA}}; attachments = {{ADJUNTOS}}. Follow this order. First validate: if {{COSTO_VARIABLE_UNITARIO}} is greater than or equal to {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}}, stop and warn that no break-even is possible (negative or zero contribution margin); if an essential data point is missing, ask for it. Second, calculate unit contribution margin ({{PRECIO_UNITARIO}} minus {{COSTO_VARIABLE_UNITARIO}}) and margin ratio (unit margin over {{PRECIO_UNITARIO}}). Third, calculate break-even in units ({{COSTOS_FIJOS_PERIODO}} divided by unit margin, rounded up to the next whole number) and in revenue ({{COSTOS_FIJOS_PERIODO}} divided by margin ratio). Fourth, if {{VENTAS_REFERENCIA}} is provided, calculate safety margin in units, currency, and percentage. Fifth, build three scenarios (pessimistic, base, optimistic) adjusting the three levers, recalculate the break-even in each, and identify the dominant one. Show every formula with numeric substitution step by step. Label assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent figures. Neutral currency, no market prices. If any data is empty, ask for it before calculating. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Close with a three-line executive reading: required volume, distance from risk, and dominant lever.

prompts.title: Model unit economics of a marketplace
Build unit economics for an ecommerce order
Analyze profitability by customer
Compare profitability by sales channel
prompts.content: Act as a senior Finance and Operations Director specialized in multichannel unit economics and go-to-market design. I need to compare the true profitability of my sales channels for {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}} in the period {{PERIODO}}. Today I decide the mix by intuition or gross revenue, without seeing the net contribution margin each channel leaves after cost-to-serve and acquisition costs. Before calculating, restate what you understand and ask for any missing data. Inputs: per channel, {{CANALES_Y_DATOS}} (revenue for the period, number of customers or transactions, and known costs); cost structure {{ESTRUCTURA_COSTOS}} (variable, cost-to-serve, and acquisition costs, indicating which are shared); period {{PERIODO}}; decision {{OBJETIVO_DECISION}}; and, if available, {{VALOR_VIDA_RETENCION}} (lifetime value or retention by channel for LTV/CAC and payback). Proceed as follows: 1) attribute revenue by channel and allocate costs in three layers (direct variable, per-channel service/fulfillment cost, per-channel acquisition/commissions); for any shared cost declare the proration basis and mark it [ASSUMPTION]. 2) Calculate per channel: revenue, total variable cost, absolute and percentage contribution margin, cost of acquisition per customer, and if {{VALOR_VIDA_RETENCION}} is available, LTV/CAC and payback. 3) Build a comparative table sorted by percentage margin and describe a waterfall of each channel's contribution to total margin. 4) Identify the most profitable channel by margin, the highest-volume channel, and the most acquisition-efficient channel, and make the tensions explicit. 5) Recommend the go-to-market mix reallocation with quantitative rationale, sensitivity to changes in proration assumptions, and two risks. Rules: only provided figures, never invent numbers, mark every estimate [ASSUMPTION] with its basis, reconcile channel margins against the total, and flag where a channel stops being worthwhile. Close with one actionable sentence ready for committee.

prompts.title: Analyze retention and revenue cohorts
prompts.content: Act as a senior SaaS finance and RevOps analyst specialized in unit economics and revenue cohort models. I need to analyze my customer base by sign-up cohorts grouped by {{UNIDAD_COHORTE}}, using {{FUENTE_DATOS}} as the source and within the window {{VENTANA_OBSERVACION}}, to separate new from retained revenue and support the decision of {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}}. Proceed as follows. First, validate integrity: confirm that a sign-up date per customer exists, recurring revenue by period, observation period, and the definition of active customer per {{DEFINICION_ACTIVO}}; if any is missing, ask for it before calculating and never invent figures. Second, declare conventions: currency and periodicity of {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, revenue normalization (MRR or ARR), treatment of reactivations, upgrades, downgrades, prorations, and customers with zero revenue but an active contract. Third, build the matrix by {{UNIDAD_COHORTE}} (rows = sign-up cohort, columns = tenure 0, 1, 2, …) and calculate per cell logo retention and revenue retention; mark as immature the cells with few observed periods and do not project them. Fourth, separate GRR (only churn and contraction, capped at 100%) from NRR (includes expansion) with explicit formula and basis. Fifth, decompose each period into opening base plus expansion minus contraction minus churn and verify the bridge reconciles against observed revenue. Sixth, identify the logo curve stabilization and estimate average lifetime with its logic; if {{SEGMENTO}} applies, compare segments. Seventh, compare the NRR of recent mature cohorts against older ones, evaluate against {{NRR_OBJETIVO}}, and triangulate with GRR to see whether health comes from low leakage or from expansion that masks contraction. Close with three actionable findings aligned with {{OBJETIVO_NEGOCIO}} and a warning if NRR falls below 100% or {{NRR_OBJETIVO}}. Respect the currency, mark every estimate as an assumption, do not invent results or discuss prices. Deliver readable tables and a brief narrative of the underlying strategy.

prompts.title: Build a financial KPI tree
prompts.content:
Act as a senior FP&A Director who builds driver trees for executive committees in {{SECTOR_NEGOCIO}}. I need a KPI tree that decomposes {{METRICA_NORTE}} from its accounting formula all the way down to the operational KPIs that an area can actually move in {{HORIZONTE_ACCION}}, plus a prioritized lever table.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate {{METRICA_NORTE}} and its formula, confirm which data is available in {{CIFRAS_BASE}} and which is missing, and present the tree plan; only then execute.

Proceed as follows:
1. Confirm {{METRICA_NORTE}} and write its exact accounting formula.
2. Level 1: arithmetic components directly derived from {{METRICA_NORTE}} (additions/subtractions).
3. Level 2: decompose each component into its drivers (e.g., revenue = volume × price; cost = units × unit cost).
4. Levels 3–4: drill down to controllable operational metrics specific to {{SECTOR_NEGOCIO}} (conversion, shrinkage, days outstanding, occupancy, churn, average ticket).
5. For each node declare the formula, mathematical relationship with the parent node (addend, multiplicative factor, or divisor), and the owning area.
6. For each leaf driver mark the direct or inverse relationship with {{METRICA_NORTE}} and its relative elasticity (high/medium/low) with the rationale.
7. Deliver a table of 3 to 5 highest-leverage levers: KPI, owner, formula, base value per {{CIFRAS_BASE}}, concrete action for {{HORIZONTE_ACCION}}, and warning signal with threshold.

Rigor rules:
- Arithmetically consistent tree: every node reconstructs exactly from its children up to the root; a residual that does not reconcile goes as an 'other/reconciliation' node, not forced.
- Do not mix volume, price, and mix in the same node: separate them so the lever is unambiguous.
- Do not invent figures; every estimate is marked [ASSUMPTION] with its calculation basis.
- If a node has more than one owner, name the primary and note shared responsibility.

If {{METRICA_NORTE}}, {{SECTOR_NEGOCIO}}, {{CIFRAS_BASE}}, or {{PERIODO}} are missing, ask before proceeding. Deliver the hierarchical tree (root {{METRICA_NORTE}} to operational leaves) for {{PERIODO}} plus the prioritized lever table.

Variables:
- {{METRICA_NORTE}}: the apex metric to decompose and its accounting formula if known
- {{SECTOR_NEGOCIO}}: sector and business model to anchor the operational drivers
- {{CIFRAS_BASE}}: current values of the metric and its components; optional if only the structure is needed
- {{PERIODO}}: period of the figures' analysis
- {{HORIZONTE_ACCION}}: window in which the owner of each lever can move the driver

prompts.title: Define the North Star metric and support system
prompts.content: Act as a senior management-control analyst specialized in designing metrics systems for growing companies, with mastery of the North Star Metric framework and input/output metrics trees. I need to define a single North Star metric for {{NEGOCIO}}, which generates revenue via {{MODELO_INGRESOS}} and is in stage {{ETAPA_EMPRESA}}, where the value delivered to the customer or aha moment is {{VALOR_CLIENTE}} and the data available for measurement are {{FUENTE_DATOS}}. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, and Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Interpret: confirm business, revenue model, stage, value definition, and data sources; if a datum is missing, ask me for it and mark as [ASSUMPTION] any assumption. Plan: propose 2 to 3 North Star candidates and evaluate each against five criteria (reflects customer value, predicts future revenue, is actionable, is measurable with {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, resists cosmetic manipulation); present the matrix before recommending. Execute: deliver (1) a single North Star with operational profile (phrase, numerator, denominator, time window, segment, frequency, initial threshold if there is a baseline); (2) tree of 3 to 5 input metrics movable by a team, each with causal relationship to the North Star, owner, and lever; (3) 2 to 3 health counter-metrics; (4) at least 3 discarded vanity metrics with their reason. Close with how to instrument it in the dashboard. {{ADJUNTOS}} provides additional context when present. Do not mix brands, do not give prices or use the word free, write in neutral and professional Spanish without emojis.

prompts.title: Design a Balanced Scorecard
prompts.content:
Act as a senior management-control and strategy consultant, trained in the Balanced Scorecard by Robert Kaplan and David Norton (HBR, 1992; The Balanced Scorecard, 1996) and experienced in designing strategy maps and KPI systems. I need to translate the strategy of {{ORGANIZACION_UNIDAD}} into a measurement system that connects day-to-day work with the underlying objectives, avoiding a dashboard of loose, unbalanced KPIs.

Context:
- Strategy or priorities for the period: {{ESTRATEGIA}}
- Horizon and cadence: {{HORIZONTE}}
- Existing KPIs, baselines, targets, or reports: {{EVIDENCIA}}

Proceed as follows.
1. Framing: restate {{ESTRATEGIA}} as a verifiable intent sentence, confirm the unit {{ORGANIZACION_UNIDAD}}, the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}, and inventory {{EVIDENCIA}} to avoid duplicating KPIs. Mark every piece of undelivered data as [ASSUMPTION].
2. Build the four perspectives bottom-up in this order: Learning and growth, Internal processes, Customer, and Financial, with 2 to 4 objectives each phrased as verb plus focus, ensuring each objective in one layer enables one in the layer above.
