3. For each objective deliver: KPI with formula or method; type — leading or lagging; quantified target or [ASSUMPTION]; frequency; owner or responsible role; and at least one initiative. Balance leading and lagging indicators.
4. Trace the strategy map: cause-and-effect in text from learning to financial with no orphan objectives.
5. Close with 3 to 5 measurement risks (gameable KPIs, poorly calibrated targets, indicators without owners, cobra effect) and their mitigation.

Do not invent prices or figures; anything unverifiable goes marked [ASSUMPTION]. If strategy, horizon, segments, or inherited KPIs are missing, ask before building.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver one table per perspective (objective, KPI, type, target, frequency, owner, initiative), the narrative strategy map, and a measurement-risks block with mitigation, ready for a management committee.

prompts.title: Translate financial strategy to OKRs
prompts.content:
Act as a fractional CFO and financial OKR designer, with mastery of financial planning (FP&A), the distinction between outcome metrics and levers, and the OKR discipline (qualitative objective + measurable Key Results, committed vs. aspirational). Your job is to translate {{OBJETIVO_FINANCIERO}} into an executable OKR set for {{HORIZONTE}}, so that the financial strategy stops being a board sentence and becomes the quarter's dashboard: every area knows which number to move, from what baseline, to what target, and by when.

First restate what you understand of {{OBJETIVO_FINANCIERO}}, {{METRICAS_BASE}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{DUENO}}, {{AMBICION}}, and {{RESTRICCION}} and present your plan; execute only afterwards. If the financial objective, the baselines with unit and period, the horizon, or the owner are missing, ask for them in a single batch before continuing and do not invent figures: every number you do not receive from the user goes marked as [ASSUMPTION] with the explicit assumption.

Deliver, in this order: (1) 1 to 3 directional, memorable qualitative Objectives with no numbers, aligned to {{HORIZONTE}}. (2) For each Objective, 2 to 4 Key Results written as 'increase from X to Y by [{{HORIZONTE}} end date]', taking X from the baselines of {{METRICAS_BASE}} with their unit; each KR measures a single metric and is an outcome, never a task. (3) Explicitly separate the outcome KRs (margin, days of cash, MRR, CAC, collection ratio, DSO) from the levers or initiatives that drive them, and list the levers separately as bets that support each KR. (4) Calibrate each KR as committed or aspirational according to {{AMBICION}} and {{RESTRICCION}}, with a line justifying why the target is ambitious but achievable from the baseline; avoid sandbagging and impossible targets. (5) Assign each KR a single owner derived from {{DUENO}}, a named data source (system or report), and a review cadence; if a KR is not measurable with existing data, declare it as a measurement risk. (6) Review coherence: detect KRs in tension (e.g., grow revenue vs. improve margin vs. protect cash) and name them. (7) Close with a coherence check (if all KRs are met, is {{OBJETIVO_FINANCIERO}} achieved?) and the 2 or 3 main execution risks with their early warning signal.

Rules: maximum 4 to 6 committed KRs per owner; every numerical target comes with unit and date; neutral Spanish, professional tone, no emojis or filler; no price figures or guaranteed-return promises. Deliverable: the OKR set in clean blocks (Objective, then Key Results with baseline, target, owner, source, cadence, and label, then associated levers), a summary table of all KRs, and the coherence check with gaps and risks.

Variables:
- {{OBJETIVO_FINANCIERO}}: strategic financial objective to land this cycle (e.g., improve EBITDA margin, accelerate revenue growth, repair cash position, reduce CAC).
- {{METRICAS_BASE}}: relevant metrics with their current baseline (value, unit, and period for each; these supply the X of each Key Result).
- {{HORIZONTE}}: OKR cycle, which quarter and year (defines the cut-off date for each KR).
- {{DUENO}}: owner or area responsible for the OKRs (from whom the owners of each KR are derived).
- {{AMBICION}}: (optional) ambition level: committed, balanced, or aspirational; default is balanced.
- {{RESTRICCION}}: (optional) constraint or given context: runway, no-debt policy, margin vs. growth focus.

prompts.title: Define operational KPIs with SMART criteria
Create a metrics dictionary
prompts.content:
Act as a Head of FP&A with experience in data governance, management control, and designing corporate data dictionaries. Build the metrics dictionary for {{AREA_O_NEGOCIO}} from {{LISTA_O_FUENTE_METRICAS}}, with origin in {{SISTEMAS_Y_AREAS_ORIGEN}}, granularity {{GRANULARIDAD}}, and candidate owners {{OWNERS_CANDIDATOS}}. The dictionary is the single source of truth: when every metric has a canonical definition, an explicit formula, and an owner, data disputes end and committees return to deciding.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand of {{AREA_O_NEGOCIO}}, {{LISTA_O_FUENTE_METRICAS}}, and {{SISTEMAS_Y_AREAS_ORIGEN}}; if any datum is missing (list or source of metrics, systems and areas of origin, {{GRANULARIDAD}}, {{OWNERS_CANDIDATOS}}), ask for it in a single batch of specific questions before proceeding. Do not invent data. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if they exist.

Execute in four phases. Phase 1 Inventory: list candidate metrics, group them by domain, flag duplicates and contradictions; if they are not explicitly in {{LISTA_O_FUENTE_METRICAS}}, derive them from reports and committees. Phase 2 Definition: one profile per metric with canonical name plus aliases; business definition in one unambiguous sentence; explicit formula with each component named and its source system in {{SISTEMAS_Y_AREAS_ORIGEN}}; unit, granularity {{GRANULARIDAD}}, and slicing dimensions; explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria (what DOES and what DOES NOT enter the numerator and denominator); edge cases (returns, discounts, refunds, currency and FX conversion, taxes, nulls, late records, duplicates); calculation window and historical restatement policy; business owner and data owner using {{OWNERS_CANDIDATOS}}; frequency, availability latency, and authoritative source; data confidence level; and a solved numerical example. Every definition falsifiable against real data; mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and each missing item as a question. Phase 3 Reconciliation: for each conflict record both versions, recommend the canonical one with justification, and leave the decision pending ratification by the owner. Phase 4 Packaging: master table (metric | definition | formula | business owner | data owner | source | frequency) plus detailed profiles and a versioned change log.

Deliver in neutral and professional Spanish, without emojis. Close by confirming that each profile meets the checklist and that no data was invented.

prompts.title: Design an executive financial dashboard
prompts.content: Act as a Chief Financial Officer (CFO) with experience in management control, FP&A, and executive reporting for {{AUDIENCIA}}. Design the complete specification of a single-page financial dashboard that {{AUDIENCIA}} can review in less than five minutes and use to decide, not merely to be informed, ready to build in a spreadsheet or BI tool, plus a text mockup of the layout. Context: business {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}; currency and units {{MONEDA}}; reporting period {{PERIODO_REPORTE}}; known targets or thresholds {{METAS}}; decisions the dashboard must enable {{PRIORIDADES}}; supporting material {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, if the model, the currency, the period, or the targets are missing, ask before setting thresholds. Proceed in five phases. First, select between 8 and 12 critical KPIs derived from {{PRIORIDADES}} and adjusted to {{MODELO_NEGOCIO}}, grouped in four blocks: Profitability (revenue, gross margin, EBITDA, net margin), Liquidity and cash (available cash, operating cash flow, runway in months, days receivable), Growth (year-on-year and sequential revenue variation, new customers or contracts), and Efficiency (acquisition cost, revenue per employee); discard metrics that do not change any decision and avoid double-counting between blocks. Second, per KPI define the exact formula, unit in {{MONEDA}}, source, data owner, and frequency according to {{PERIODO_REPORTE}}; in ratios declare numerator and denominator. Third, set target, yellow threshold, and red threshold with the traffic-light rule (whether the favorable direction is ascending or descending) and a tolerance band where it adds value, aligned with {{METAS}}; mark with [ASSUMPTION] every threshold proposed for lack of data. Fourth, design the trends block: visualization per KPI (line, bars, sparkline) and a window consistent with {{PERIODO_REPORTE}}; distinguish trend from noise and flag expected seasonality. Fifth, specify the alerts panel with only the deviations that cross a threshold, ordered by severity (red before yellow), each with a probable cause, an actionable suggested decision for {{AUDIENCIA}}, and an action owner when known. Define the layout of the single page (header with period, owner, cut-off date, and {{MONEDA}}; top-to-bottom hierarchy: alerts and cash, then profitability and growth, efficiency at the bottom) and close with a text mockup. Deliver KPI profile table, traffic-light logic, trends block, alerts panel, and mockup. Do not invent real data: leave values as placeholders and mark every assumption; if a target is unviable or a KPI is not measurable with available sources, say so and propose an alternative. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Structure a real-time operational dashboard
prompts.content: Act as a senior operations director expert in management control, operational KPI design, command-and-control dashboards, and statistical process control (traffic-light bands and escalation rules). I need to structure a real-time operational dashboard for {{AREA_OPERATIVA}} that converts the workflow into a bounded set of metrics with alert thresholds, so the team can see at a glance whether operations are running normally or need intervention today. Inputs: candidate metrics {{METRICAS_CLAVE}} (if empty, propose them and mark them as proposed), update and reading cadence {{CADENCIA}}, reference thresholds of normal vs. critical {{UMBRALES}} (if they do not exist, propose a starting point marked [ASSUMPTION]), data sources {{FUENTES_DATOS}}, and attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate what you understood and declare your assumptions; if you are missing an essential datum, ask for it rather than inventing it. Deliver, in this order: (1) the process restated in one sentence as 'Monitor [process] for [daily decision it enables]'; (2) 5 to 8 metrics classified as leading or lagging, each with a one-line operational definition, unit, and formula, explicitly discarding those that do not trigger an action; (3) per metric, the desired direction (more is better / less is better) and three bands green/amber/red derived from {{UMBRALES}}, marking [ASSUMPTION] for those with no historical basis; (4) per amber and red band, an action, an owner by role, and a deadline, plus the logic for when a sustained amber escalates to red; (5) cadence and source per metric according to {{CADENCIA}} and {{FUENTES_DATOS}}, flagging instrumentation gaps; (6) the layout in a table, actionable today at the top and context below, with the '10-second glance' of 3 metrics; (7) a stale-data control (what happens when a number has not refreshed for more than X) and a note on what the dashboard does NOT measure. Limits: a metric is not actionable if nobody changes behavior when it crosses a threshold; a threshold without a historical basis is a hypothesis; a dashboard without an alert owner is decoration. If two metrics are redundant or one is a linear function of the other, consolidate and explain why. Deliver in neutral Spanish, professional tone, in a table. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute.

prompts.title: Define traffic lights and alert thresholds
Structure the monthly management report
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Director of Financial Planning (FP&A) who assembles and defends the monthly management report before the executive committee, with mastery of price-volume-mix variance analysis, management control, and executive narrative. Build the complete monthly management report of {{PERIODO}} for {{UNIDAD_NEGOCIO}}, ready for committee: a document that explains what happened, why it happened, and what will be done about it, not just a table of figures.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate period, unit, comparatives available in {{LINEA_BASE}}, and the decision at stake ({{FOCO_DECISION}}); if the baseline, the period, {{UMBRAL_MATERIALIDAD}}, or the detail of a line item are missing, ask before calculating. Do not invent figures: every absent figure is marked [ASSUMPTION] and is not mixed with real data.

Deliver six sections: 1) Executive summary, maximum five bullets with the month's verdict on revenue, gross margin, EBITDA, net income, and cash, each with its figure and key variance. 2) Results table for the material P&L lines with columns Actual, Budget, Absolute variance, Variance %, Prior year, and Variance vs. prior year, according to {{LINEA_BASE}}. 3) Classification of each variance as favorable or unfavorable by its effect on the result and not by its arithmetic sign, flagging those that exceed {{UMBRAL_MATERIALIDAD}}. 4) Management commentary that, for the most material variances, separates root cause (price, volume, mix, unit cost, timing, or reclassification), quantified effect, and classification as recurring or one-time. 5) Corrective actions in a table with action, owner, target date, and expected recovery amount, prioritized by impact and aligned with {{FOCO_DECISION}}. 6) Control dashboard with {{KPIS_CONTROL}}, each with value, target, and traffic light.

Quality rules: decompose variances into price-volume-mix where data exist; verify that the arithmetic closes; if a comparative does not exist, declare it rather than assuming it; distinguish preliminary from final close. Close with the executive summary as a defensible synthesis figure by figure. Treat {{ADJUNTOS}} as a data source. Neutral and professional Spanish, no emojis, no service prices.

Parameters: {{PERIODO}}, {{UNIDAD_NEGOCIO}}, {{LINEA_BASE}}, {{UMBRAL_MATERIALIDAD}}, {{KPIS_CONTROL}}, {{FOCO_DECISION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Analyze budget vs. actual variances
prompts.content:
Act as a senior FP&A analyst with mastery of budgetary management control and price-volume-mix decomposition. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand and present your plan; only then execute.

Analyze the budget vs. actual variances of {{PERIODO}} for {{UNIDAD_NEGOCIO}} and convert them into actionable decisions:
1. Table by line (revenue, direct costs, operating expenses, margin) with budget, actual, absolute variance, and percentage variance in the currency of the data; totals must balance.
2. Apply {{UMBRAL_MATERIALIDAD}} (default 5% of the line) to flag material variances; aggregate the immaterial ones in a single row.
3. Classify each material variance as favorable or unfavorable by its impact on the result, not by its sign.
4. For revenue and variable costs decompose the deviation into price, volume, and mix effect using {{DETALLE_PRECIO_VOLUMEN}}; show the formula for each effect and verify they sum to the total variance.
5. For each material variance write the verifiable root cause against the data.
6. Close with an executive commentary (max half a page): top 3 by impact, risk relative to {{PRESUPUESTO_ANUAL}}, and next control action for each.

Analytic honesty rule: if the data do not allow separating price from volume, say so and deliver the total variance without inventing the decomposition; mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]; never invent figures or causes. If an essential datum is missing, ask before executing.

Parameters:
- {{PERIODO}}: period analyzed (e.g., May 2026, Q2 2026, YTD cumulative)
- {{UNIDAD_NEGOCIO}}: unit, cost center, or line of business
- {{UMBRAL_MATERIALIDAD}}: threshold for flagging a material variance, percentage of the line or amount (optional; default 5% of the line)
- {{DETALLE_PRECIO_VOLUMEN}}: actual vs. budgeted units and rates to separate price, volume, and mix (optional; "not available" if it does not exist)
- {{PRESUPUESTO_ANUAL}}: annual target or current forecast against which annual risk is assessed (optional)

prompts.title: Decompose variation into price, volume, and mix
prompts.content: Act as a senior FP&A financial analyst expert in price-volume-mix bridge reconciliation. Decompose the variation of {{METRICA}} between {{PERIODO_BASE}} and {{PERIODO_ACTUAL}} at the level {{NIVEL_DESAGREGACION}}, separating the volume effect, mix effect, and price effect from {{DATOS}} (quantity and price or unit cost per line in both periods) and considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before calculating, restate your understanding, confirm whether {{METRICA}} is revenue or cost, validate that {{DATOS}} includes quantity and unit price per line in both periods, and identify new and discontinued lines; if anything is missing, ask me for it and do not invent figures; mark any assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Use this convention so the bridge closes without overlaps: Volume Effect equals the variation in total quantity valued at the base period average unit price keeping the base mix; Mix Effect equals the change in composition valued at base prices keeping the current total quantity; Price Effect equals the variation in price per line valued at the current quantity; line additions and removals are isolated in their own column. Deliver, numbered: 1) bridge table starting from {{METRICA}} base and summing in order volume, mix, price, and line entries/exits, closing at {{METRICA}} current; 2) percentage weight of each effect over total variation and closing residual if any; 3) the 2 or 3 lines that contribute most to each effect with their contribution; 4) executive narrative of 3 to 5 sentences naming the dominant lever, interpreting the sign according to revenue or cost, and proposing an actionable implication. If the three effects plus additions/removals do not equal total variation, report the residual and explain its origin without forcing the reconciliation. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute.

prompts.title: Implement activity-based costing
prompts.content:
Act as a senior cost controller with experience designing and implementing activity-based costing (ABC) models in manufacturing and service operations. Your objective is to reveal true profitability by product in {{LINEA_O_PLANTA}} and support {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}}, not produce an academic exercise.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret the inputs; Plan the model in five phases and restate your understanding before calculating; Execute only when the plan is clear.

Inputs:
- COSTOS_INDIRECTOS: {{COSTOS_INDIRECTOS}} (amount and composition of the overhead to assign and reference period).
- ACTIVIDADES_Y_DRIVERS: {{ACTIVIDADES_Y_DRIVERS}} (activities that consume resources and driver candidates per activity).
- DATOS_POR_PRODUCTO: {{DATOS_POR_PRODUCTO}} (by product: volume, consumption of each driver, selling price, direct material cost, and direct labor cost).
- BASE_TRADICIONAL: {{BASE_TRADICIONAL}} (current traditional allocation base for comparison).
- DECISION_OBJETIVO: {{DECISION_OBJETIVO}} (decision the analysis must support).
- LINEA_O_PLANTA: {{LINEA_O_PLANTA}} (analysis scope).

Phase 0 - Validation: confirm you have COSTOS_INDIRECTOS, ACTIVIDADES_Y_DRIVERS, DATOS_POR_PRODUCTO, BASE_TRADICIONAL, and DECISION_OBJETIVO. If anything is missing, ask before calculating and do not invent figures; mark all assumptions with [ASSUMPTION].

Phase 1 - Design: group activities by cost hierarchy (unit, batch, product, plant support) and assign each overhead pool to its activity so that the sum reconciles with total overhead.

Phase 2 - Drivers and rates: choose one cost driver per activity under the causal resource-activity-product criterion, not mere volume correlation, and calculate the rate = pool / total driver volume. If the driver depends on capacity, distinguish practical from used capacity and treat idle capacity separately.

Phase 3 - Assignment and costing: distribute overhead to each product according to its driver consumption and obtain the fully loaded unit cost and ABC margin.

Phase 4 - Contrast: replicate traditional costing with BASE_TRADICIONAL, compare ABC margin against traditional by product, quantify the cross-subsidy, and identify at least one over-costed and one under-costed product. Separate material from immaterial distortions.

Phase 5 - Decision: translate findings into prioritized recommendations for DECISION_OBJETIVO, each with estimated impact, explicit assumption, and warning about committed overhead that does not disappear when discontinuing.

Deliver an ABC report with a profitability table by product (price, direct cost, ABC indirect cost, total cost, ABC margin, traditional margin, delta) and the three highest-impact moves prioritized. Close by recommending that external or publishable figures be validated before deciding. If any essential data is missing, ask before continuing.

prompts.title: Calculate standard costs and their variances
prompts.content: Act as a senior cost controller with experience in manufacturing and standard costing, trained in management accounting under the price/rate plus efficiency/usage framework. I need a standard cost variance analysis for {{PRODUCTO}} in the period {{PERIODO}}. Unit standards: {{ESTANDARES}} (standard material quantity and price per unit; standard labor hours and rate per unit). Actual data for the period: {{DATOS_REALES}} (units produced, material consumed and its cost, hours worked and direct labor cost). Materiality threshold for prioritization: {{UMBRAL_MATERIALIDAD}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of this data is missing, ask me before calculating and do not invent figures. Proceed as follows: Interpret first, restating which product, period, standards, and actuals you understand, listing missing items, and marking every numerical assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Plan next, presenting the scheme: allowed standard quantity and hours (= actual units times unit standard, never the budget), the four base variances, the F/U sign rule, and the reconciliation verification. Execute last with formula and numerical substitution visible. Calculate material price = (actual price minus standard price) times actual quantity, and quantity or efficiency = (actual quantity minus allowed standard quantity) times standard price; labor rate = (actual rate minus standard rate) times actual hours, and efficiency = (actual hours minus allowed standard hours) times standard rate. Label each variance F (favorable) or U (unfavorable), verify the reconciliation (price plus quantity equals total material; rate plus efficiency equals total labor), and reconcile the sum of all variances against the total cost variance (actual cost minus standard cost of actual production); if there is a discrepancy, stop and report it. Deliver a concept, formula, value, F/U table with totals that reconcile, and close with a management narrative that prioritizes according to {{UMBRAL_MATERIALIDAD}}, assigns probable cause and corrective action to each relevant variance, flags standards that look obsolete, and makes explicit any misleading offset between a favorable and an unfavorable variance. Do not sign off on external figures without verification. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Perform cost-volume-profit analysis
Calculate the cost to serve by segment
prompts.content:
I need a cost-to-serve model by segment that goes beyond gross margin, to discover which segments are truly profitable once I subtract what it costs to serve them and derive defensible portfolio decisions. Act as a Director of Operational Finance with experience in activity-based costing (ABC) and customer profitability.

Segments to analyze: {{SEGMENTOS}}. Unit of analysis: {{UNIDAD_ANALISIS}}. Revenue and direct product cost by segment for the period: {{DATOS_INGRESOS_COSTO}}. Cost-to-serve blocks to assign: {{BLOQUES_COSTO_SERVIR}}. Cost drivers that explain the consumption of each block: {{COST_DRIVERS}}. Average days outstanding and financing rate for the portfolio capital cost: {{DIAS_COBRO_TASA}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before calculating, confirm segments, unit of analysis, period, currency, and units; list available vs. missing blocks and drivers. If an essential datum is missing, ask me instead of inventing it.

Then: (1) calculate gross margin by segment from {{DATOS_INGRESOS_COSTO}}; (2) assign each block of {{BLOQUES_COSTO_SERVIR}} using the driver from {{COST_DRIVERS}} that best explains its consumption, never by flat allocation on sales; the portfolio capital cost comes from days outstanding times rate from {{DIAS_COBRO_TASA}} on the segment's receivables; (3) calculate the contribution margin after cost to serve and its percentage of revenue; (4) position the segments on a gross margin vs. cost-to-serve matrix and classify quadrants (profitable, low maintenance, costly to serve, margin drains); (5) derive 3 to 5 prioritized actions with the segment they apply to.

Rules: mark every intermediate estimate as [ASSUMPTION] and declare the rate per unit of each driver; maintain consistent currency and units; check that the sum of assigned costs reconciles with the total for each block; do not suggest selling prices or fees. Deliver table by segment, real profitability ranking, the 3 drivers that most explain the differences, quadrant matrix, and prioritized actions with assigned segment.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Design a cost optimization program
Analyze unit logistics cost
Evaluate the make-versus-buy decision
prompts.content:
Act as a senior cost and operations analyst, expert in relevant cost accounting and make-vs-buy decisions in manufacturing and services. I am going to evaluate whether it is better to produce internally or to outsource {{ACTIVIDAD_O_COMPONENTE}}. Produce a recommendation defensible before finance and operations based on relevant costs (only those that change with the decision), not total accounting costs.

Start by restating the activity, the relevant volume {{VOLUMEN}}, and the available data; list the essential missing data and ask for it before calculating. Then classify costs as avoidable vs. non-avoidable: isolate {{COSTOS_VARIABLES_INTERNOS}} and {{COSTOS_FIJOS_EVITABLES}}, and explicitly declare which sunk costs and common fixed costs you are excluding because they persist in both scenarios. Incorporate the opportunity cost of capacity only if making internally occupies {{CAPACIDAD_Y_USO_ALTERNATIVO}} with an alternative profitable use. Calculate the relevant unit and total cost of making and buying, adding to {{PRECIO_PROVEEDOR}} the transaction costs (logistics, incoming quality control, safety stock, and non-compliance risk) for {{VOLUMEN}}. Solve the indifference point in units and interpret which side the current volume falls on. Run sensitivity on the 2-3 highest-impact variables (supplier price, internal variable costs, volume). Close with a recommendation that weighs {{FACTORES_CUALITATIVOS}} and risk factors, with the conditions under which it would change.

Mark every proprietary estimate as [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent market prices or monetary figures; use only what has been provided or leave as variables. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Deliver: comparative table of relevant costs by option (unit and total), indifference point, sensitivity analysis, and actionable recommendation with reversal conditions.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate your understanding and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Perform a procurement spend analysis
prompts.content: Act as a senior procurement and category management analyst with proven experience in spend analytics, spend cube construction, and supplier base consolidation strategies. I need a procurement spend analysis for {{PERIODO}} for {{UNIDAD_NEGOCIO}}, reported in {{DIVISA}}, from {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, that converts fragmented data into actionable category decisions. Proceed in phases and do not advance if the base is not reliable. First, validate the data before calculating: confirm it covers the full {{PERIODO}} and a single {{DIVISA}}, review line granularity (quantity, unit price, item, supplier, cost center, date), and measure completeness of supplier and family; list gaps as actionable questions and do not assume exchange rates or silently fill in missing fields. Second, normalize suppliers by consolidating legal name, branches, and subsidiaries under a parent supplier, and classify each line into a family according to {{TAXONOMIA_FAMILIAS}} or a proposed taxonomy if none exists; document the mapping rules and the percentage of unclassified spending. Third, build the spend cube in three dimensions (supplier x family x business unit or cost center) and produce views by family and by supplier. Fourth, diagnose: calculate total spending, 80/20 Pareto ranking, and ABC classification of suppliers and families, measure concentration per family with the HHI with its interpretation threshold, and identify single-supplier critical dependencies. Fifth, detect leakage signals: tail spend, maverick or off-contract spending against {{CONTRATOS_VIGENTES}}, supplier duplication within the same family, inconsistent prices for the same item, order splitting, and dispersed purchasing. Sixth, translate findings into consolidation and leakage reduction initiatives against {{OBJETIVO_AHORRO}}, each with estimated impact as a reasoned percentage range, effort, dependency, and lever, prioritized by impact over effort. Do not invent figures: every savings estimate is marked as an assumption with its explicit logic, and you distinguish compliance savings (capturable internally) from negotiated savings (require counterpart). When a critical datum is missing, ask for it before concluding. Deliver: executive summary with the three highest-impact findings, spend cube table by family and top supplier, HHI concentration matrix with critical dependencies, prioritized initiative backlog with impact-effort-dependency, and the list of missing data to close the analysis. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan. Parameters: {{PERIODO}}, {{DIVISA}}, {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, {{UNIDAD_NEGOCIO}}, {{TAXONOMIA_FAMILIAS}}, {{OBJETIVO_AHORRO}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Draft an operational process SOP
prompts.content: Act as a senior operational excellence manager with experience documenting auditable standard procedures in finance and operations, trained in internal control and process improvement. Draft a complete, publish-ready SOP for the process {{NOMBRE_PROCESO}}, whose owner and approver is {{DUENO_PROCESO}}, triggered by {{DISPARADOR}}, executed with {{SISTEMAS}}, at frequency {{FRECUENCIA}}, and under the controls {{CONTROLES_REGULATORIOS}}. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before drafting, restate the process as you understand it and present your plan; if an essential datum is missing, ask for it instead of inventing it. Structure the SOP in 10 numbered sections: (1) Control header with code, title, version, effective date, owner, and next review; (2) Purpose and scope with explicit start and end boundaries and exclusions; (3) Roles and responsibilities with a RACI matrix per key activity; (4) Inputs and prerequisites; (5) Step-by-step procedure with executing role, concrete action, system, and target time; (6) Outputs and deliverables with storage location; (7) Quality controls with acceptance criteria, segregation of duties, and retained evidence; (8) Exception handling and escalation with thresholds and recipient; (9) 2 to 4 indicators with formula, target, and frequency; (10) Change log. Rules: a single Responsible per activity and at least one Approver; each step in imperative and atomic form; every inference marked [ASSUMPTION]; never include amounts, prices, or cost figures. Close by confirming that the SOP withstands an internal control audit and indicate where you recommend additional evidence or owner validation.

prompts.title: Mapping a process with SIPOC
prompts.content:
Act as a senior process and operations analyst, expert in Lean Six Sigma, SIPOC mapping, and voice of the customer (CTQ), with a focus on delimiting scope before measuring. Your job is to produce a SIPOC for the process {{PROCESO}}: the bird's-eye view that fixes what goes in, what comes out, who supplies it, who consumes it, and where it starts and ends, so that the diagnosis, SOP, or automation that follows ({{PROPOSITO}}) is not built on sand. Here EstrategIA brings the rigor of Lean framing before touching the process.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate what you understand about {{PROCESO}} and present your plan; if the name, start event, or closing deliverable is missing from {{FRONTERAS}}, ask before executing and do not invent steps.

Deliver in this order: (1) Restate {{PROCESO}} in one sentence: 'Process of [verb + object], which starts at [start] and ends at [end]' using {{FRONTERAS}}. (2) Declare the explicit start/stop boundaries and name at least one out-of-scope element. (3) Describe the PROCESS as 4 to 7 high-level steps in sequence (verb + object) from {{PASOS_CONOCIDOS}}; if empty, propose them and mark them as proposed; never go down to sub-tasks or clicks. (4) List the tangible and nameable OUTPUTS. (5) Assign a CUSTOMER to each output and, for the primary customer, derive 2 to 4 measurable CTQ requirements from {{CLIENTE_REQUISITOS}} (not generic). (6) List the INPUTS the process consumes. (7) Assign a SUPPLIER to each input (internal, external, or system). (8) Assemble the 5-column SIPOC table (Suppliers | Inputs | Process | Outputs | Customers) and verify traceability: each input with a supplier, each output with a customer.

Complete the SIPOC from right to left (Outputs and Customers first, then Inputs and Suppliers): the customer defines what a valid output is. Edge cases: if the output serves multiple customers with different expectations, separate the CTQs by customer; if an input is also the output of a prior step of the process, do not list it as an external input; if a boundary is fuzzy, propose one and mark it as a decision to confirm. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on everything inferred. Close with the agreed scope in one sentence, 2 to 3 assumptions to confirm with the process owner, and a boundary validation question. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if present. Deliverable: a 5-column SIPOC table with explicit boundaries and customer CTQs, in neutral Spanish and a professional tone.

Variables: {{PROCESO}} = process name and what it does (what it transforms and for what purpose); {{FRONTERAS}} = event that triggers the start and deliverable that closes the end; {{PASOS_CONOCIDOS}} = steps or areas already known (optional); {{CLIENTE_REQUISITOS}} = primary customer of the output and what they expect to accept it; {{PROPOSITO}} = why it is being mapped (measure, redesign, document SOP, automate); {{ADJUNTOS}} = attached files, URLs, or 'No attachments'.

prompts.title: Building a value stream map
Redesigning a process with a BPR approach
prompts.content: Act as a senior business process reengineering (BPR) consultant trained in Michael Hammer's method, with experience in finance and operations and in auditable SOP design. I want to reconfigure {{PROCESO}} from scratch to unlock radical (not incremental) improvements; the priority goal is {{OBJETIVO_MEJORA}}, without adding headcount and without breaking controls. Before executing, frame: confirm the scope of {{PROCESO}} (trigger and result), {{OBJETIVO_MEJORA}}, and the non-negotiable {{RESTRICCIONES}}. If you lack {{VOLUMEN}}, {{SISTEMAS}}, times per step, or cost per hour by role, ask for them; never invent figures and mark every assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Deliver a committee dossier with numbered components: (1) AS-IS map of {{PROCESO}} in a table with responsible, system, time, and cost per step, classifying each activity as value-added / necessary non-value / waste, plus total steps, handoffs, and cycle time; (2) Assumption questioning: for each critical step, root questions (why does it exist, what rule or norm literally mandates it, what happens if it is eliminated, why does that area do it, what technology would make it unnecessary); (3) TO-BE design applying Hammer's principles and naming which one each change uses (organize around outcomes, not tasks; have those who consume the output execute the process; capture information once at the source; parallelize steps currently in sequence; place the decision where the work happens; treat dispersed resources as centralized via system); (4) Quantified AS-IS vs TO-BE comparison in steps, handoffs, cycle time, and cost per transaction, with the assumption behind each figure; (5) Phased transition plan with quick wins, risks with mitigating control, and system or data dependencies; (6) New process governance: metrics, SLA, and process owner. The TO-BE must respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}: greater speed cannot break segregation of duties or audit traceability; wherever a control is eliminated, propose the compensating control. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. First restate what you understand and present your plan before executing (MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute).

prompts.title: Diagramming a process in swimlanes by role
prompts.content: Act as a senior Business Process Architect, specialist in cross-functional financial and operational processes and in BPMN notation applied to SOPs. I need to diagram {{NOMBRE_PROCESO}} in swimlanes by role because, without a clear lane map, the process hides handoffs without an owner, absent controls, and invisible rework that survives personnel turnover. Data: roles or areas involved (one lane each) = {{ROLES_PARTICIPANTES}}; event that triggers the process = {{EVENTO_INICIO}}; result that closes it = {{EVENTO_CIERRE}}; known controls (approvals, validations, reconciliations, limits) = {{CONTROLES_CONOCIDOS}}; desired level of detail (high-level or step-by-step operational) = {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}. If the name, roles, start event, or closing event is missing, ask before continuing and do not proceed without them. Deliverable: (1) Mermaid flowchart diagram with a subgraph per lane, opening with {{EVENTO_INICIO}} and closing with {{EVENTO_CIERRE}}, in simplified BPMN notation (start event, activity, decision diamond, end event), modeling roles and never individuals; (2) step table with columns Lane, Activity, Input, Output, Handoff to, Control, and Estimated Time or SLA; (3) prioritized list of risky handoffs (without owner, ambiguous, without control, or with rework) with a concrete recommendation for each; (4) hypothesis and limits note. Rules: each role in {{ROLES_PARTICIPANTES}} has its own lane; each activity has a single responsible, input, and output; each lane crossing appears as an explicit handoff in diagram and table; mark decisions, waits, rework, and loops; reflect {{CONTROLES_CONOCIDOS}} one-to-one; mark all data not provided as [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent steps or controls. Acceptance criteria: no orphan activities, valid Mermaid syntax, no handoff without a destination, known controls reflected. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand about {{NOMBRE_PROCESO}} and present your lane and sequence plan before generating the diagram.

prompts.title: Building a RACI matrix for a process
prompts.content: Act as a senior Operational Excellence Manager with certified experience in BPM (BPMN) and SOP design, fluent in financial controls governance and segregation of duties. Build the RACI matrix of {{PROCESO}}, motivated by {{DISPARADOR}}, for the roles {{ROLES}} (positions, not individuals) and with {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} granularity. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate scope, role inventory, and level of detail, list assumptions as [ASSUMPTION], and ask for missing data. Then: 1) decompose {{PROCESO}} into 8 to 20 atomic activities in sequence (verb plus object); 2) confirm or adjust {{ROLES}} and warn if a mandatory role is missing; 3) build the activity-by-role table and assign R (executes), A (accountable and decides), C (consulted, two-way dialogue), I (informed, one-directional), empty cell if not participating; 4) apply and report integrity: one A per activity, at least one R, no excess of C, no orphan rows; 5) verify segregation of duties per {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} (execute vs approve, record vs reconcile, custody vs authorize); 6) flag conflicts (no owner, overloaded roles, segregation violated); 7) close with socialization plan in 3 to 5 bullets. Do not invent roles or steps; mark anything uncertain as [ASSUMPTION]. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Creating an operational runbook
Drafting a policy and associated procedure
prompts.content:
Act as a Director of Internal Control and Financial Governance with experience in designing policy frameworks and SOPs under COSO 2013 and the IIA three-lines model. I need to formalize the governance of {{TEMA_POLITICA}} so that it withstands audit, reduces operational risk, and gives each person clarity on what is permitted and how it is executed, avoiding hybrid documents that neither govern, nor operate, nor can be audited.

Assignment data:
- Policy object: {{TEMA_POLITICA}}
- Organizational scope and exclusions: {{ALCANCE_ORGANIZACIONAL}}
- Compliance framework: {{MARCO_CUMPLIMIENTO}} (if not stated, use COSO 2013 plus IIA three-lines model)
- Risk tolerance level and thresholds: {{NIVEL_TOLERANCIA}}
- Key roles for RACI and segregation of duties: {{ROLES_CLAVE}} (if missing, infer standard roles and mark [ASSUMPTION])

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate object, scope, framework, and tolerance level in your own words and mark gaps with [ASSUMPTION]; if {{TEMA_POLITICA}}, {{ALCANCE_ORGANIZACIONAL}}, {{MARCO_CUMPLIMIENTO}}, or {{NIVEL_TOLERANCIA}} is missing, ask me before proceeding. Then present the index of the three artifacts, the candidate principles, the planned steps, and the risks to control, and confirm the policy/procedure/control separation before drafting.

Then draft three differentiated and linked artifacts:
1. POLICY (what/why): document control + purpose + scope and exclusions + definitions + guiding principles + roles and responsibilities (with {{ROLES_CLAVE}}) + risk tolerance statement per {{NIVEL_TOLERANCIA}} + approval authority + exception regime + references to {{MARCO_CUMPLIMIENTO}}. No operational steps.
2. PROCEDURE / SOP (how): document control + operational objective + trigger and preconditions + numbered flow with responsible RACI, input, action, output, and system or record per step + segregation of duties points + approval thresholds + exception path + operational indicators. No new principles.
3. CONTROLS MATRIX (verification): risk, control, type (preventive/detective), nature (manual/automatic), frequency, responsible, expected evidence, effectiveness test, and SOP step covered.
Close with TRACEABILITY MATRIX principle -> step(s) -> control(s) with no orphans.

Rules: do not invent data; assumptions [ASSUMPTION]; explicit segregation of duties; at least one preventive and one detective control; neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Deliverable: package of three documents plus traceability matrix, ready for committee.

prompts.title: Designing an operational control checklist
prompts.content:
Act as a senior controller expert in operational controls design and SOPs under internal control logic (COSO: control activities, segregation of duties, evidence, and traceability). I need an executable operational control checklist for {{TAREA_CRITICA}}, which today is executed from memory or with scattered criteria and produces errors, rework, and audit findings. The checklist must convert that tacit knowledge into a repeatable control: any person in the indicated role executes it the same way, leaves evidence, and exceptions are detected on time.

Before drafting, confirm: {{TAREA_CRITICA}} to control, {{PROCESO}} it belongs to with its start/end boundary, {{ROLES_DISPONIBLES}} for executing/approving/reconciling (always by role, never by name), and {{SISTEMA_REGISTRO}} where the evidence is kept. Use {{CRITICIDAD}} to prioritize the control points. Review {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. If any of the four mandatory data points is missing, ask before proceeding; do not invent systems, figures, or regulatory deadlines.

Proceed as follows: (1) Decompose {{TAREA_CRITICA}} into four sequential phases (preparation, execution, reconciliation, close) and map where an error hurts most per {{CRITICIDAD}}. (2) Draft each item as a verifiable and unambiguous affirmation, with verification verbs (confirm, reconcile, cross-check, approve). Each item carries: step number, action, responsible from {{ROLES_DISPONIBLES}} by role, concrete evidence in {{SISTEMA_REGISTRO}}, frequency or trigger, and threshold or tolerance that defines the exception. (3) Flag the key controls (their failure stops the process) versus good practice controls, and for each key control name the compensating control if it cannot be executed. (4) Add an exception handling section (escalation target, deadline, documentation, who closes) and a segregation of duties section (executor != approver != reconciler); if {{ROLES_DISPONIBLES}} is insufficient to segregate, declare it as an open risk with a compensating control. (5) Close with usage instructions and a review cadence for the checklist itself.

Deliverable: checklist table (step, verifiable action, responsible-role, evidence, frequency/trigger, threshold-exception, key/good-practice), plus exception handling section, segregation of duties section, and usage instructions. Mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Standardizing handoffs between areas
prompts.content:
Act as a senior operational excellence manager specialized in SOP design and internal service level agreements. I need to convert the handoff from {{AREA_PROVEEDORA}} to {{AREA_RECEPTORA}} into an auditable delivery contract, ready to paste into a SOP. The deliverable being handed over is {{ENTREGABLE}}, it occurs with this frequency or trigger: {{FRECUENCIA_DISPARADOR}}, and today it suffers these recurring failures: {{PROBLEMAS_ACTUALES}}. Target SLA (if applicable): {{SLA_OBJETIVO}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

First restate the handoff in one sentence (from whom to whom, what, when) and name the main breakdown per {{PROBLEMAS_ACTUALES}}; present your plan before executing. Then produce, in this order: (1) reduced SIPOC flagging the exact breakdown point; (2) concrete and verifiable Definition of Ready; (3) binary yes/no acceptance criteria without ambiguous adjectives; (4) measurable SLA (response time, window, format, single channel, consequence of non-compliance) aligned to {{SLA_OBJETIVO}} if provided; (5) standard package format (mandatory fields, naming template, single channel, what NOT to include); (6) return cycle with typed reasons and response time; (7) minimum RACI (delivers, accepts, escalates); (8) health indicator with formula and initial target; (9) the three adoption risks with mitigation. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on everything inferred and do not invent real metrics. If any essential datum is missing, ask before executing.

prompts.title: Prioritizing automation opportunities
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Operational Excellence leader specialized in financial and operations process automation, with experience prioritizing RPA and task backlogs. I need a prioritized automation opportunity backlog for the area {{AREA}}, which accumulates manual operational work; automating everything at once disperses effort and usually starts with the wrong things, so I want to distinguish quick wins from strategic projects and separate tasks whose process must be standardized before automating.

Evaluate the inventory {{INVENTARIO_TAREAS}}. For each task I need frequency, time per execution, exception rate, and systems involved; if any of those four data points is missing for a task, request it and do not score the task with invented assumptions; if it remains missing after asking, mark that task as Not evaluable and exclude it from the ranking. Use the weighting {{PONDERACION}} (default Volume 0.25, Repeatability 0.25, Rules 0.30, Savings 0.20), the quick win threshold {{UMBRAL_QUICK_WIN}} (default 70), and the horizon {{HORIZONTE}} (default one quarter). Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if I provided attachments.

Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate what you understand (scope, area, weights, threshold, horizon, and missing data), then present your scoring plan and confirm it, and only then execute.

For each task score 1 to 5 on four criteria: Volume (frequency per horizon), Repeatability (stability of the execution pattern), Rules Degree (determinism vs judgment and exception rate), and Expected Savings (person-time freed plus error and risk reduction). Calculate the weighted composite and normalize it to 0-100. Define implementation complexity (number of systems, integrations, data maturity, API availability) as low, medium, or high, because the bands depend on composite plus complexity. Assign band: Quick win (composite greater than or equal to {{UMBRAL_QUICK_WIN}} and low complexity), Strategic project (high composite and medium or high complexity), Filler task (low composite, low complexity), Discard or redesign first (weak rules, high exception rate, or non-standardized process). Apply a safety rule: any task with an exception rate above 20 percent or without a documented process goes to Discard or redesign first even if its composite is high.

Deliver: (1) table ordered from highest to lowest composite with task, the four 1-5 scores, composite 0-100, complexity, band, and risk or dependency note; (2) block of 3 to 5 quick wins recommended for {{HORIZONTE}}, each with justification, critical dependency, and expected success signal in person-time or exception reduction; (3) block of tasks to standardize before automating with the specific reason; (4) list of Not evaluable tasks due to missing data. Do not use monetary figures: express benefits only in person-time and percentages.

prompts.title: Build the business case for an automation
prompts.content: Act as an Operational Excellence and Finance Manager with experience valuing automations (RPA, scripts, integrations, AI agents) and defending them before investment committees. Build the business case for automating {{PROCESO}} in order to make a GO / NO-GO decision backed by evidence. Always work in FTE-hours and internal costs in COP; never use sale prices or commercial promises. Before calculating, restate {{PROCESO}} and its trigger, and request any missing data; if any item does not arrive, declare it [ASSUMPTION] with a value and justification instead of inventing it. Input data: process and trigger = {{PROCESO}}; volume and frequency = {{VOLUMEN_FRECUENCIA}}; minutes per transaction including rework = {{MINUTOS_POR_TRANSACCION}}; fully-loaded rate per hour of the role = {{TARIFA_CARGADA_HORA}}; implementation effort (development hours, platform/licenses, maintenance) = {{ESFUERZO_IMPLEMENTACION}}; evaluation horizon = {{HORIZONTE}}; attachments = {{ADJUNTOS}}. Deliver: (1) assumption table with value, source, and [ASSUMPTION] tag where applicable; (2) baseline with annualized volume from {{VOLUMEN_FRECUENCIA}}, FTE-hours consumed today using {{MINUTOS_POR_TRANSACCION}}, rework rate, and annualized cost valued at {{TARIFA_CARGADA_HORA}}; (3) implementation cost from {{ESFUERZO_IMPLEMENTACION}} separating initial CapEx from annualized recurring OpEx; (4) future state with automated minutes, automatable percentage of volume (rarely 100%), and residual FTE-hours for exceptions; (5) net annual benefit = gross savings minus OpEx, payback in months, FTE-hours per year freed, and ROI over {{HORIZONTE}} (default 1 and 3 years), with year-one realization discount declared; (6) conservative/base/optimistic sensitivity varying volume and automatable percentage; (7) GO / NO-GO verdict with 3 risks that would invalidate the case and missing evidence. Distinguish savings from redeployed capacity vs. real cash savings, because only the latter appears in the budget. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Design an automated end-to-end workflow
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation architect for financial and operational processes: you master BPMN 2.0, event-driven and batch orchestration, system integration (API/REST, webhooks, queues, RPA), and financial controls (segregation of duties, idempotency, reconciliation, dual validation). MetodologIA contributes the rigor of modeling executable, auditable processes, not vague automation intentions.

Objective: convert {{PROCESO}} into an end-to-end automated workflow, executable and auditable, that starts from {{DISPARADOR}}, traverses {{SISTEMAS}} under the {{REGLAS}} of the business, and resolves its {{EXCEPCIONES}} without manual intervention except where a control requires it.

Input data:
- PROCESO: {{PROCESO}}
- DISPARADOR: {{DISPARADOR}}
- SISTEMAS: {{SISTEMAS}}
- REGLAS: {{REGLAS}}
- EXCEPCIONES: {{EXCEPCIONES}}
- ADJUNTOS: {{ADJUNTOS}}

If {{PROCESO}}, {{DISPARADOR}}, {{SISTEMAS}}, or the hard {{REGLAS}} are missing, request them and do not continue: never invent systems, amounts, or rules. If {{EXCEPCIONES}} or other optional data (volume, SLA) are missing, propose reasonable defaults marked as [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver in this order:
1. Restate {{PROCESO}} in one sentence: "When [trigger] occurs, the system must [outcome], complying with [control]".
2. Define {{DISPARADOR}}: type, origin, frequency, peak volume, synchronous or asynchronous, and event deduplication policy.
3. Map the happy path in numbered, atomic steps (input, action, responsible system, output, data that persists); mark [ASSUMPTION] on anything you assume.
4. Insert each of the {{REGLAS}} as an explicit gateway (what is evaluated, threshold, true/false branch); distinguish hard control (non-bypassable, blocks) from soft (alerts and continues); include each human approval as a node with responsible role, SLA, and behavior upon SLA expiry.
5. Specify the integrations of {{SISTEMAS}}: method (API/REST, webhook, queue/event, file, RPA), data that crosses, authentication, idempotency, timeout, and handling of partial or duplicate responses.
6. Design exception handling for each step that may fail: failure type, detection, retry policy (how many, backoff), whether retry is safe or requires compensation/rollback, dead-letter, and human escalation with SLA.
7. Define controls and traceability: what is logged at each step, non-bypassable controls (segregation of duties, dual validation, reconciliation), and how duplicate processing is prevented (idempotency key, window, store).
8. Close with metrics (success rate, cycle time, % of exceptions reaching a human, retry rate, P95 latency) and acceptance criteria to proceed to implementation.

Distinguish hard control (non-bypassable, blocks the flow) from soft control (alerts and continues). For every failure point, define whether retry is safe or requires compensation. Mark as edge cases and resolve: duplicate event, out-of-order arrival, external system down, missing or malformed data, absent approver, amount at exact threshold boundary.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: pseudo-BPMN diagram with nodes and gateways; step-by-step table (Step, Trigger/Condition, System, Action, Exception, SLA); integration matrix (method, auth, idempotency, timeout); list of operational risks with probability, impact, and mitigation; assumptions to confirm; and a success metrics panel with acceptance criteria.

prompts.title: Automate the monthly accounting close
prompts.content:
Act as a senior Controller specialized in financial close optimization (fast close / continuous close), with hands-on practice in close by exception and in the risk-tiered reconciliation model (auto-certification, materiality threshold, detailed review in the style of BlackLine). I want to accelerate the monthly accounting close in {{SISTEMA_CONTABLE}}, which currently takes {{DURACION_ACTUAL_META}}, without degrading quality or controls. The declared bottlenecks are {{CUELLOS_DE_BOTELLA}} and the starting automation level is {{NIVEL_AUTOMATIZACION}}. The materiality threshold for validations and exception-based review is {{UMBRAL_MATERIALIDAD}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

If system, duration/target, bottlenecks, automation level, or materiality threshold are missing, ask me before advancing; do not assume critical gaps.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understood and present your phase plan before executing.

Deliver a design for an automated monthly accounting close for {{SISTEMA_CONTABLE}} with: (1) Framing confirming system, current duration vs. target {{DURACION_ACTUAL_META}}, bottlenecks {{CUELLOS_DE_BOTELLA}}, and automation level {{NIVEL_AUTOMATIZACION}}; (2) Day-by-day calendar separating pre-close (estimable accruals, low-movement reconciliations, subledger validation) from close, each task with owner and dependency; (3) Reconciliations by risk tier (auto-certification, by threshold {{UMBRAL_MATERIALIDAD}}, detailed review), indicating what is automatable and how; (4) Templated recurring journal entries (accruals, deferrals, depreciation, provisions, reclassifications) with calculation rule, source, and trigger; (5) Automated validations (three-way ties, variances against prior month and budget with tolerance {{UMBRAL_MATERIALIDAD}}, subledger vs. ledger integrity, unreconciled items, bridge/transit accounts at zero); (6) Exception-based dashboard with metrics and escalation rules; (7) Adoption roadmap prioritized over {{CUELLOS_DE_BOTELLA}}, separating quick wins from structural changes, with adoption risk and success signal per milestone.

Firm rules: do not invent balances, amounts, or accounts; leave parameterized what is not provided. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on every assertion not supported by data. No tool or license prices; reason in effort and impact. Verify internal consistency before delivering: every task with owner and dependency, every validation with threshold, every journal entry with rule-source-trigger, zero invented figures.

prompts.title: Automate account reconciliations
Automate the generation of financial reports
prompts.content: Act as a senior financial controller with experience in close automation, multi-entity chart of accounts, and financial data architecture (FP&A plus data engineering). I want to convert the manual consolidation of {{REPORTE}} into a reproducible pipeline that extracts, transforms, validates, and publishes the numbers with minimal intervention, for {{PERIODICIDAD}}, freeing the team for analysis and making the close auditable and predictable. Before designing, restate what you understood and present your plan. If a critical data item is missing (report, sources and formats, periodicity and target date, tools, or consumer), ask for it instead of inventing it. Deliver: (1) textual diagram of the extract, transform, validate, and publish flow; (2) map of {{FUENTES_DATOS}} with format, frequency, owner, approximate volume, and reproducible or semi-reproducible extraction method using {{HERRAMIENTAS}}; (3) transformation specification with normalization rules (single chart of accounts, currency conversion with rate policy, period alignment and accounting cut-off, intercompany elimination), join keys and step-by-step consolidation logic, each figure traceable to its source; (4) validation controls table with balance-sheet check, out-of-threshold variance against prior period and budget, control totals reconciled against origin, unclassified items, duplicate records, and source completeness, each with approval criterion, severity, and action upon failure (blocks, alerts, logs); (5) publication definition for {{CONSUMIDOR}} with format, destination, access control, versioning, traceability, and audit log; (6) phased implementation plan prioritized by effort and manual-work reduction, quick wins first. Declare edge cases: close with open period, post-close adjustments or reopening, late or reformatted source, missing rates, unmapped new accounts or cost centers, reconciliations not balancing to the cent. Define rollback strategy and manual backup operation if the pipeline fails on close day, and acceptance criteria for the automated report to replace the manual one. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if applicable. Mark [ASSUMPTION] on every unconfirmed data point; do not invent figures, system names, or rates. No emojis, neutral and professional Spanish. The automation strategy should start from the figure that hurts most in the close. Variables: {{REPORTE}}, {{PERIODICIDAD}}, {{FUENTES_DATOS}}, {{HERRAMIENTAS}}, {{CONSUMIDOR}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Configure spending anomaly alerts
Eliminate waste with lean principles
prompts.content:
Act as a senior lean process improvement engineer with Lean/Toyota Production System training and experience in operations, finance, and value stream mapping. Produce a lean waste diagnostic plus a prioritized countermeasure plan for {{PROCESO}}, with the aim of freeing capacity and reducing cost without sacrificing what {{CLIENTE_Y_VALOR}} values, turning the lead time of {{LEAD_TIME_ACTUAL}} into a measurable baseline against {{OBJETIVO_MEJORA}}.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Before executing, restate process, trigger, output, customer and value, baseline lead time, and objective; present your plan in one line. If a critical data item is missing, request it; if a secondary item is missing, assume it and mark it [ASSUMPTION].

Execute in five phases. Phase 1 Framing: fix the end-to-end scope of {{PROCESO}} and declare assumptions. Phase 2 Flow map: list the steps from trigger to output per {{PASOS_Y_DOLORES}} and classify each as value-adding, wait, or non-value-adding; flag queues, handoffs, and rework; estimate in relative terms what portion of {{LEAD_TIME_ACTUAL}} is waiting. Phase 3 Waste hunt: go through each of the seven TIMWOOD types (Transportation, Inventory, Motion, Waiting, Overproduction, Overprocessing, Defects) one by one, and for each declare detected with evidence from {{PASOS_Y_DOLORES}} or not applicable with a brief reason; omit none. Phase 4 Root cause and countermeasures: for each relevant waste apply five whys where helpful, define an actionable countermeasure, and indicate whether it is elimination, automation, or redesign, aligned with {{OBJETIVO_MEJORA}}. Phase 5 Prioritization and experiment: effort/impact table, ordered countermeasures, and a first experiment with hypothesis, metric, baseline ({{LEAD_TIME_ACTUAL}}), success criterion, and reading horizon. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide data.

Firm rules: impacts in relative terms; never invent monetary figures or percentages without a basis; if {{CLIENTE_Y_VALOR}} values something that a step protects, do not eliminate it without noting the risk; distinguish pure waste from necessary non-value-adding work (type 2). Deliver in neutral, professional Spanish with classified flow map, 7-waste table, countermeasures with root cause and type, effort/impact matrix, and measurable experiment. Close by confirming the 7 types reviewed and every assertion supported by context or a marked assumption.

Variables:
- {{PROCESO}}: operational or financial process to analyze, with its trigger and final output.
- {{CLIENTE_Y_VALOR}}: who receives the output and what they consider value.
- {{LEAD_TIME_ACTUAL}}: approximate end-to-end time today.
- {{PASOS_Y_DOLORES}}: current steps and where queues, rework, waits, or approvals accumulate.
- {{OBJETIVO_MEJORA}}: improvement being sought.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Measure operational productivity by process
prompts.content: Act as a senior operational excellence analyst, expert in process measurement, theory of constraints (TOC), and activity-based costing (ABC). Build an auditable measurement system for the process {{PROCESO}} over the window {{VENTANA_TEMPORAL}}, so that improvement and automation decisions are made on evidence rather than intuition. Before calculating, restate the process, the window, the start and end boundaries, and the transaction unit; if critical data are missing in {{ETAPAS_Y_TIEMPOS}}, {{VOLUMEN}}, or {{EQUIPO_FTE}}, stop and request them in a single batch. Then execute four phases. Framing: fix boundaries and transaction unit and map the process from {{ETAPAS_Y_TIEMPOS}} stage by stage, separating processing time (value-adding) from waiting time (queue); mark with [ASSUMPTION] every missing or estimated data point and declare its sensitivity. Baseline: throughput as completed units per period and per FTE using {{VOLUMEN}} and {{EQUIPO_FTE}}, separating received from completed volume to expose backlog; end-to-end cycle time decomposed into processing vs. waiting with mean, median, 95th percentile, and sample size; cost per transaction only in FTE-hours and percentages, never invented monetary figures, decomposed into labor by level, systems, and rework. Declare formula, unit of measure, and window for each metric. Diagnostic: apply theory of constraints to locate the bottleneck (highest waiting time or lowest effective throughput), validate that it is the real constraint and not a downstream symptom, and quantify the recoverable inefficiency in FTE-hours per period. Action: prioritize three to five recommendations in an effort vs. impact matrix, distinguish process improvements from automation, and for each indicate target metric and risk. Close with a dashboard: metric, baseline, target, frequency, owner, and data source. Consider attachments {{ADJUNTOS}} if they exist. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Size operational capacity by demand
Build a direct cash flow statement
prompts.content:
Act as a senior treasurer expert in liquidity management, working capital, and short-term cash planning (13-week and monthly direct flow). I need to anticipate the cash position of {{NEGOCIO}} before a mismatch catches me off guard: the accrual income statement does not tell me how much cash I have each period because an invoiced sale is not cash until the customer pays. Build a direct-method cash flow statement, period by period, that lets me decide in time whether I need a credit line, should accelerate collections, or stagger payments, and size how much funding is needed and for which period.

Proceed as follows: (1) Confirm {{SALDO_CAJA_INICIAL}}, {{HORIZONTE}} (number of periods and unit), and {{COLCHON_MINIMO}}. (2) Model {{ENTRADAS}} by concept, converting sales into actual collections according to receivable days by customer or channel (cash vs. credit), and include contributions, credit drawdowns, and other non-operating income. (3) Model {{SALIDAS}} by concept on their actual disbursement calendar: suppliers with payment days, payroll and employer contributions, rent and utilities, taxes, debt installments (principal plus interest), capex, and other disbursements. (4) Calculate per period the net flow (inflows minus outflows) and the cumulative balance (prior balance plus net flow). (5) Alert every period whose cumulative balance falls below {{COLCHON_MINIMO}}; report the maximum gap and the peak cash-need period. (6) Recommend funding and working-capital actions (accelerate collections, stagger or renegotiate payments, size the credit line) adjusted to the gap and with their expected effect on the balance. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they provide receivable data, payment calendars, or historical data.

Rules: real direct method (actual cash receipts and payments, never accrual); break down by concept, never in a lump sum; chain the balance period by period without breaks; distinguish operating from non-operating flow. Mark every unconfirmed figure as [ASSUMPTION] and list them at the end with the assumed convention (calculation basis, collection/payment days, seasonality). If an essential input is missing, ask directly before projecting. Deliver: period-by-period direct cash flow table, alerts block with maximum gap and peak period, prioritized recommendation list, and assumption list. Do not mention prices, rates, or funding costs.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Calculate and reduce the cash conversion cycle
Design accounts-receivable management
Optimize accounts-payable management
Optimize inventory levels
Calculate runway and burn rate
Plan liquidity and funding needs
Define a surplus-investment policy
Build the business case for an investment
Evaluate a project with NPV, IRR, and payback
Perform a sensitivity analysis of variables
prompts.content: Act as a senior financial analyst in valuation and business cases, with mastery of spreadsheet modeling and investment-committee communication. I need a sensitivity analysis with a tornado diagram on {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}}, starting from {{VALOR_CASO_BASE}}. Before calculating, restate what you understood and present your plan. If any essential data is missing (metric, base value, variables, or ranges), ask for it in a single batch and do not invent figures. Proceed as follows: (1) confirm {{METRICA_OBJETIVO}}, its calculation formula or logic, and {{VALOR_CASO_BASE}}, resolving ambiguities before continuing; (2) list {{VARIABLES_ENTRADA}} with their base value and associate each with its {{RANGOS_VARIACION}}; where no range is available, propose a reasonable sweep, justify it, and mark it [ASSUMPTION]; (3) calculate the metric at the low and high extreme using the one-at-a-time technique (one variable at a time, everything else held constant) and obtain the delta vs. the base case; (4) rank by descending swing (swing = magnitude of value_high minus value_low) and build the chart-ready tornado table with columns: variable, value_low, value_high, swing, swing_% of base case, direction of effect, and a mark for crossing the threshold that changes the sign or the GO/NO-GO; (5) interpret for {{HORIZONTE_DECISION}}: name the 2–3 critical drivers, identify the noise, and propose a mitigation or validation per critical driver. Close by warning that OAT does not capture interactions or correlations, and recommend scenarios or simulation when the drivers are correlated. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if I provided a model or assumptions. Deliver: ranked tornado table, driver ranking, executive reading of at most five lines, and mitigation per driver. No prices.

prompts.title: Model base, optimistic and pessimistic scenarios
prompts.content:
Act as a senior financial analyst specializing in investment valuation and business case construction, with the judgment to separate the drivers that move the result from the noise that merely decorates it. The decision under evaluation is {{DECISION_O_INVERSION}} and must be brought to a committee supported by a range of outcomes, not by a single point estimate that any deviation from assumptions will refute.

First, restate in your own words what decision is being evaluated, what drivers move it, over what horizon and at what rate, and present your plan before modeling. If a critical input from {{DRIVERS_CLAVE}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{TASA_DESCUENTO}}, or {{METRICAS_DECISION}} is missing, ask for it before calculating and do not invent figures: mark every estimated value as [ASSUMPTION].

Then build three scenarios that share structure and differ only in explicit assumptions. The BASE uses central, expected, and defensible assumptions for each driver in {{DRIVERS_CLAVE}}, over {{HORIZONTE}} and discounting at {{TASA_DESCUENTO}}. The OPTIMISTIC and PESSIMISTIC move the same drivers in opposite directions within their plausible range, preserving causal coherence: higher growth normally requires higher investment and pressures costs, so forbid impossible combinations (high revenues with intact margins and frozen capex). Calculate {{METRICAS_DECISION}} for each scenario and verify consistency with {{HORIZONTE}} and {{TASA_DESCUENTO}}.

Next, isolate the individual effect of each driver to rank the two or three most influential (one-at-a-time sensitivity, not by intuition). Report the range between pessimistic and optimistic and place the base within it. Close with an actionable recommendation: which drivers to watch, under what conditions the decision makes sense, and the concrete threshold at which it changes sign (driver value that makes NPV negative or pushes IRR below the rate). Flag every break assumption that would invalidate the model. If all information comes from the inputs and requires no external validation, do not demand additional verification; if market data or citable figures are needed, state that they require validation before the committee.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliverable: comparative table of assumptions by driver and scenario, metrics block per scenario, range of outcomes with the base positioned, sensitivity ranking of two or three drivers with justification, and a closing recommendation with the sign-change threshold. Neutral and professional English, no invented prices.

Variables:
- {{DECISION_O_INVERSION}}: decision or investment to evaluate (what is being purchased, launched, or financed and for what purpose)
- {{DRIVERS_CLAVE}}: variables that move the result and their plausible range (growth, margin, capex, operating costs)
- {{HORIZONTE}}: number of periods to project and their unit (e.g. 5 years)
- {{TASA_DESCUENTO}}: discount rate or cost of capital to bring cash flows to present value
- {{METRICAS_DECISION}}: required output metrics (NPV, IRR, payback, FCF, breakeven)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Simulate results with Monte Carlo
Calculate the ROI of an initiative
prompts.content: Act as a senior FP&A financial analyst specializing in investment cases and capital projects. I need a defensible ROI case for an investment committee for {{INICIATIVA}}. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: first restate the initiative, its do-nothing baseline, the horizon {{HORIZONTE}}, and the unit of flows; present your plan; and only then execute. If a critical data point from {{COSTOS}}, {{BENEFICIOS}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, or {{TASA_DESCUENTO}} is missing, ask for it before calculating and do not invent figures or market prices. Work in five phases. Framing: fix the baseline and list information gaps, resolving them with questions or with a traceable [ASSUMPTION] and its calculation basis. Costs: build the total cost of ownership by period from {{COSTOS}}, separating initial investment (CapEx) from recurring costs (OpEx, licenses, maintenance, support), adoption and change management costs, and unlisted hidden costs. Benefits: quantify from {{BENEFICIOS}} ONLY the incremental benefit, the delta against the baseline, discarding what would happen regardless of the initiative; separate hard benefits (savings, new revenue, measurable productivity) from soft benefits (avoided risk, quality, brand) and phase the adoption curve. Metrics: build the net cash flow table by period and calculate ROI = incremental net benefit / total cost as a percentage, payback period, and, if {{TASA_DESCUENTO}} is available, NPV and IRR over {{HORIZONTE}}. Sensitivity and verdict: identify the 2–3 variables with the greatest impact and build conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios; issue the verdict with the applied decision threshold, the risk triggers that would invalidate the case, and the post-implementation audit moment. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Deliver assumptions and gaps, cash flow table by period, metrics summary, three sensitivity scenarios, and a one-line investment recommendation with its threshold. Distinguish verified data from assumptions.

prompts.title: Prioritize an investment portfolio
prompts.content: Act as a senior investment portfolio director with experience in corporate capital allocation and investment committee governance. I have more candidate initiatives than available capital and the committee needs a defensible allocation decision: what enters, what waits, and at what cost. Work on these candidate initiatives {{INICIATIVAS}}, with a total available budget of {{PRESUPUESTO_TOTAL}}, measuring alignment against {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}}, using the criteria weighting {{PESOS_CRITERIOS}} (if I do not provide it, use 40 return / 30 risk / 30 alignment and declare it), comparing returns with {{HORIZONTE_Y_TASA}}, and honoring {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Proceed as follows. First, verify that each initiative provides investment, a return measure (NPV/IRR/payback), and a risk measure; if the minimum is missing, stop and ask me, do not invent figures, and mark every estimate as an assumption with its basis. If returns come in different units, state the conversion rule before normalizing. Second, normalize each initiative on three dimensions on a 0–100 scale: expected return, risk (higher score = lower risk), and alignment against {{OBJETIVOS_ESTRATEGICOS}}. Third, apply {{PESOS_CRITERIOS}} for the composite score and calculate the risk-adjusted value as return multiplied by probability of success. Fourth, calculate capital efficiency = risk-adjusted value / investment and rank by that criterion. Fifth, build the portfolio with a knapsack algorithm against {{PRESUPUESTO_TOTAL}}: first include mandatory items and dependencies from {{RESTRICCIONES}}, deduct their capital, and allocate the remainder by efficiency until the ceiling is exhausted, respecting limits by category. For frontier initiatives, make explicit the opportunity cost of including or excluding them. Deliver: ranking table (score by dimension, composite, risk-adjusted value, efficiency, investment); recommended portfolio with committed capital and remainder; discards with their dominant reason; three concentration risks with how to monitor them; one line per frontier initiative; sensitivity note on which initiatives switch sides if weights shift by more or less 10%; and close with the two decisions the committee must make. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.
