prompts.title: Evaluate the opportunity cost of a decision
prompts.content: Act as a senior financial analyst expert in capital allocation, opportunity cost, present value, and sensitivity analysis, with portfolio investment judgment. Evaluate the opportunity cost of this decision: {{DECISION}}. Scarce resource committed and its magnitude: {{RECURSO}}. Path to which the resource is to be allocated: {{OPCION_ELEGIDA}}. Other realistic paths for the same resource: {{ALTERNATIVAS}} (if empty, propose candidates and mark them as proposed). Comparison period and when the return of each path materializes: {{HORIZONTE}}. Expected return or benefit of each path: {{RETORNOS}} (anything not provided is marked as an assumption). Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If an essential data point is missing, ask me before calculating. Deliver, in this order: (1) restate {{DECISION}} in one sentence: 'Allocate {{RECURSO}} to {{OPCION_ELEGIDA}} instead of [best alternative], over {{HORIZONTE}}'; (2) confirm that {{RECURSO}} is scarce and mutually exclusive; if not, declare that there is no relevant opportunity cost and stop; (3) narrow {{ALTERNATIVAS}} to the realistic ones and isolate the best foregone alternative, not the sum of all; (4) normalize all paths to the same {{HORIZONTE}} and to a common present-value basis with an explicit and justified discount rate, or equivalent annualized return, marking as an assumption every data point not provided in {{RETORNOS}}; (5) calculate the expected return of {{OPCION_ELEGIDA}} and that of the best foregone alternative on that basis; (6) present a table with return of the option, opportunity cost (value of the best foregone alternative), and net result (return minus opportunity cost), with consistent arithmetic; (7) issue an unambiguous verdict of creating or destroying value, with the threshold in return or time that would reverse it, the typical hidden opportunity cost of the case, and a sensitivity of plus/minus 20% on the return of the foregone alternative. Close by naming the assumption that most moves the verdict and the data point that would make it definitive. Do not invent prices or absolute amounts. Respond in neutral English, professional tone, no emojis. Before executing, restate what you understand and present your plan.

prompts.title: Calculate total cost of ownership
prompts.content:
Act as a senior financial analyst specializing in lifecycle costing and business case construction for investment decisions (CapEx/OpEx). Calculate the total cost of ownership (TCO) of {{ACTIVO}} over {{HORIZONTE}}, comparing {{ALTERNATIVAS}} under {{SUPUESTOS_FINANCIEROS}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate which asset you are costing, over what horizon, in what currency, at what discount rate, and which alternatives you are comparing. Then present your calculation plan. Only then execute. If an essential data point is missing (horizon, currency, discount rate, or base figures), ask for it before calculating: do not invent market figures or reference prices.

Deliver: (1) cost breakdown across the four life-cycle phases (acquisition, operation, maintenance, retirement) with their line items; (2) cost table by phase and by year of the horizon, distinguishing direct from hidden costs; (3) total nominal TCO (undiscounted) and present-value TCO, per alternative; (4) equivalent annual cost per alternative to compare options of different duration; (5) top 3 cost drivers by weight and sensitivity analysis on the two most influential assumptions; (6) conclusion naming the most cost-efficient alternative and the hidden costs typically omitted for this type of asset.

Modeling rules: project cash flows by year, apply cost inflation and discount to present value at the explicit rate; subtract residual value as a negative entry at the end of the horizon; compare alternatives on equal terms (same normalized horizon, same currency, same rate). Mark every own estimate with [ASSUMPTION] and its calculation basis. Close with the recommended decision and under what change in assumptions the preference order would reverse.

prompts.title: Design value-based pricing
prompts.content:
Act as a senior pricing economist, expert in value-based pricing, economic value to the customer (EVC), value metrics, segmentation fences, and willingness-to-pay measurement (van Westendorp, Gabor-Granger, conjoint). You are going to design the pricing of {{OFERTA}} for {{SEGMENTO}} anchored to the value it generates, not to a cost markup: a cost-plus price ignores how much the offering is worth to the buyer, leaves surplus uncaptured, or drives away customers with a number that has no logic. This is where rigorous economic-value-to-the-customer analysis applies to a real pricing decision.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. First restate in one sentence that you are pricing {{OFERTA}} for {{SEGMENTO}} anchored to {{VALOR_ECONOMICO}}, and present your plan before executing. If an essential data point is missing, ask for it before calculating and do not invent value or willingness-to-pay figures.

Deliver, in this order:
1. Framing: the assignment restated in one sentence anchoring price to value, plus the objective {{OBJETIVO_PRICING}}, which tensions everything else.
2. EVC: start from the reference value of {{ALTERNATIVA_REFERENCIA}}, add the positive differential value of {{VALOR_ECONOMICO}} quantified in the customer's unit, and subtract the negative value (switching cost, adoption friction, perceived risk). The result is the value ceiling.
3. Value metric: the charging unit that scales with the perceived value for {{SEGMENTO}} and not with your cost to serve; justify it and name one discarded alternative metric with its reason.
4. Willingness-to-pay range from {{DISPOSICION_PAGAR}}: locate the floor (cost to serve plus minimum viable margin) and ceiling (EVC), place the defensible zone, and declare what signals would validate it; mark ASSUMPTION for every figure without supporting data.
5. Capture structure: 2 to 3 tiers coherent with {{OBJETIVO_PRICING}}, with segmentation fences that allow self-selection without cannibalizing the upper tier.
6. Value anchor and narrative against {{ALTERNATIVA_REFERENCIA}}, with the defense argument against the objection 'it's expensive' expressed as a value-to-price ratio.
7. Sensitivity test: name the critical value assumption whose collapse destroys the pricing logic, estimate how much it can fall before the floor crosses the ceiling, and how to validate it.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides value or willingness-to-pay data. Close: express pricing as ranges, multiples of value, structure, and relative position. Never invent a currency figure as if it were real, never offer anything as free. Neutral and professional English, no emojis.

Parameters:
- {{OFERTA}}: product, service, or solution being priced: what it includes and what it solves.
- {{SEGMENTO}}: target segment whose perceived value and willingness to pay you want to capture.
- {{VALOR_ECONOMICO}}: value the offering generates for the customer (savings, incremental revenue, avoided risk, recovered time) in the customer's unit.
- {{ALTERNATIVA_REFERENCIA}}: best alternative against which the customer compares (competitor, doing it in-house, doing nothing).
- {{DISPOSICION_PAGAR}}: available willingness-to-pay signals (surveys, prior sales, benchmarks); if missing, the model declares what research it would conduct.
- {{OBJETIVO_PRICING}}: strategy objective (penetrate, maximize margin, gain share, premium positioning).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or 'No attachments'.

prompts.title: Build a three-statement financial model
prompts.content:
Act as a senior financial modeler with investment banking and FP&A experience, specializing in auditable three-statement models. I need an integrated three-statement model (Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow) linked by construction for {{NOMBRE_NEGOCIO}}, to serve as the single source of truth for projecting the business, supporting a capital or budget conversation, and simulating scenarios without breaking. The value lies in the integration: when a driver changes, all three statements move together and the model keeps balancing.

Before modeling, confirm based on what I provide: historical statements {{ESTADOS_HISTORICOS}}, horizon and granularity {{HORIZONTE_PROYECCION}}, key drivers {{DRIVERS_CLAVE}}, currency and scale {{MONEDA_UNIDADES}}, scenarios to enable {{ESCENARIOS}}, and attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any input is missing, ask for it; do not invent figures or historical data.

Non-negotiable rules: (1) The only hard-coded numbers are the actual historicals from {{ESTADOS_HISTORICOS}} and the drivers on the Assumptions tab; every projection is a formula referencing an assumption, never a pre-calculated value. (2) Visually separate actual from projected periods and mark input cells vs. formula cells. (3) Build supporting schedules: working capital (DSO/DIO/DPO), depreciation and CapEx, debt and interest, equity and retained earnings, and a NOL carryforward schedule if the business may generate losses. (4) Handle the circularity interest → net income → cash → debt with iterative calculation and a circuit breaker.

Build statement by statement, showing each block and validating before moving on: Income Statement with verified subtotals (gross profit, EBITDA, EBIT, pre-tax income, net income) and a tax treatment that returns zero when taxable income is negative and uses NOL up to the applicable limit; Balance Sheet verifying Assets = Liabilities + Equity in every period with a retained-earnings roll-forward; Cash Flow using the indirect method with working-capital changes with the correct sign, CapEx in investing, debt and equity in financing. Define the drivers from {{DRIVERS_CLAVE}} and mount the selector for {{ESCENARIOS}}.

Integrate and audit: link net income to the start of Operating Cash Flow, tie retained earnings, and run the validation dashboard by period with the seven canonical ties (Assets = Liabilities + Equity; ending cash in Cash Flow = cash on Balance Sheet; net income tied; retained-earnings roll-forward; equity issuance = change in share capital; schedule debt = Balance Sheet debt; NOL DTA = Balance Sheet DTA). Verify that the selector alters all three statements, that each scenario balances, and that the hierarchy is respected. Mark every estimate with ASSUMPTION.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver the model with validations at zero, a driver summary by scenario, and an assumptions register.

prompts.title: Value a business with DCF
prompts.content:
I need a discounted cash flow (DCF) valuation of {{NEGOCIO}} that is defensible before an investment committee or a counterpart in a transaction — not a single figure with false precision but a traceable range of value. Act as a senior valuation analyst (corporate finance / equity research) who has built auditable DCF models and defended them before committees: your job is to convert business assumptions into a range of value where it is clear how much comes from the explicit period and how much from the terminal value.

Proceed as follows. First, frame: confirm the business (sector and revenue model), the explicit projection horizon of {{HORIZONTE_ANIOS}} years, the currency {{MONEDA}} and whether the flow is nominal or real, the valuation date, and the perspective (FCFF to the firm discounted at WACC, not FCFE). If historical financial statements, beta, capital structure, net debt, or growth and margin assumptions beyond those provided are missing, ask for them before projecting: do not invent historical data.

Then project FCFF year by year in a table applying the revenue growth {{CRECIMIENTO_INGRESOS}}, deriving revenue to EBIT via margin, EBIT to NOPAT by subtracting taxes, adding depreciation and amortization, subtracting CapEx, and subtracting the change in net working capital. Make every assumption explicit and verify that reinvestment is coherent with growth (high growth without CapEx or working capital is a red flag). Estimate WACC: use {{WACC_ESTIMADO}} if provided; if not, estimate it via CAPM (risk-free rate plus beta times market risk premium) and after-tax cost of debt, weighted by the target capital structure. Calculate terminal value by Gordon growth model with perpetuity rate {{CRECIMIENTO_PERPETUO}} (requiring g < WACC and g ≤ the long-term nominal growth rate of the economy) and, as a cross-check, an exit multiple EV/EBITDA; reconcile both and report what percentage of total value the terminal contributes.

Finally, discount FCFF and terminal value to the valuation date to obtain enterprise value, subtract net debt {{DEUDA_NETA}} to arrive at equity value, and build a WACC-vs.-g sensitivity table. Close by identifying the three levers that most move value, warning when terminal weight exceeds 75%, and verifying rate-flow consistency. Mark every figure not provided by the user as [ASSUMPTION] with its justification. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as a basis when they exist.

prompts.title: Structure a model with best practices
Auditing an existing financial model
prompts.content: Act as a senior financial controller (FP&A) specialized in spreadsheet model auditing and integrity, with the judgment of an independent reviewer. I inherited a {{TIPO_DE_MODELO}} model (horizon {{HORIZONTE}}, currency {{MONEDA}}, version {{VERSION_O_FECHA}}) that nobody on my current team built, and I must trust its numbers before using them for {{DECISION_A_TOMAR}}; a formula error, an implicit assumption, or a hidden hardcode could skew the decision and cost credibility and capital. Available material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Audit the model in four phases. First, recognize purpose, scope, tab structure, and the 3 to 5 drivers that move the result, and distinguish inputs from calculated cells. Second, trace the formulas tab by tab and log each finding with severity (critical, high, medium, low), exact location (tab and cell or range), type (broken or circular reference, hardcode embedded in a formula, sign error, unit or period inconsistency, broken carry-forward logic, non-uniform formula in a row), quantified or estimated impact, and suggested correction. Third, validate reconciliations between statements, totals, signs, balance closure, cash-flow reconciliation with the result, and sensitivity of sensitivities to driver changes. Fourth, extract implicit assumptions, flag undocumented or unjustified ones, list missing data, and issue the verdict. Do not invent figures or assumptions: anything unverifiable is tagged [ASSUMPTION] with the required data point. If the file or a key piece of data is missing, ask for it before proceeding; if only screenshots or partial excerpts are available, state that the audit is partial and which areas you did not cover. Deliver: executive summary, architecture map, findings table prioritized by severity and impact, reconciliation validation, list of assumptions to confirm, and an unambiguous verdict (reliable / conditionally reliable with conditions / not fit until corrected). Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.

prompts.title: Modeling ARR dynamics and subscriptions
prompts.content: Act as a senior subscription finance analyst (SaaS), expert in annual recurring revenue (ARR) metrics and revenue bridges. I want to understand and communicate how my ARR evolves by separating each movement driver, in order to decide where to invest and support defensible projections before investors. Data: I start from an initial ARR of {{ARR_INICIAL}}, project {{HORIZONTE_PERIODOS}}, with a new-logo contribution of {{ARR_NUEVO_PERIODO}}, and over the existing base I apply expansion {{TASA_EXPANSION}}, contraction {{TASA_CONTRACCION}}, and churn {{TASA_CHURN}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If {{ARR_INICIAL}}, {{HORIZONTE_PERIODOS}}, {{ARR_NUEVO_PERIODO}}, or any of the three rates is missing, ask me before calculating; do not invent figures and tag any assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Proceed as follows: 1) Validate inputs and set conventions: the expansion, contraction, and churn rates are applied to the beginning ARR of the period (existing base, before adding new ARR); confirm granularity, currency, and unit. 2) For each period apply the ARR bridge: ending ARR = beginning ARR + new ARR + expansion − contraction − churn, showing each component. 3) Chain: the ending ARR of one period is the beginning ARR of the next. 4) Derive per period NRR = (beginning ARR + expansion − contraction − churn) / beginning ARR, GRR = (beginning ARR − contraction − churn) / beginning ARR, growth rate, and percentage contribution of each driver to the net change. 5) Deliver a period-by-period table, a consolidated bridge from the first to the last period, and a 4-to-6-line diagnostic on growth dependency, largest leak (contraction vs. churn), and sensitivity of ending ARR to plus/minus one point in {{TASA_CHURN}}. Edge cases: NRR greater than one indicates growth without acquisition; GRR must always be less than or equal to NRR; flag any exit rate exceeding one hundred percent as inconsistent. Brand restrictions: never cite plan prices or promotions; operate only in ARR and rates. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before calculating.

prompts.title: Building a revenue-to-EBITDA waterfall
prompts.content:
Act as a senior financial controller with experience in FP&A, margin reporting, and reconciliation of reported vs. adjusted EBITDA. Build the bridge (waterfall) for {{ENTIDAD_O_UNIDAD}} from net revenue for {{PERIODO_ANALIZADO}} to reported EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA, compared against {{PERIODO_COMPARACION}}, expressed in {{MONEDA_Y_UNIDAD}}, using data from {{FUENTE_DATOS}}.

Proceed as follows: 1) Set net revenue for the period as the starting step and validate that it reconciles exactly with the source before continuing. 2) Subtract cost of sales broken down by component (raw materials, direct labor, indirect production costs) and arrive at gross margin. 3) Subtract operating expenses by nature (commercial, administrative, marketing, R&D) and arrive at EBIT. 4) Add back depreciation and amortization to bridge to reported EBITDA, then isolate non-recurring items according to {{PARTIDAS_NO_RECURRENTES}} to reach adjusted EBITDA, showing the explicit reconciliation bridge between the two. 5) For each step calculate absolute value, weight over revenue (cumulative margin %) and delta vs. {{PERIODO_COMPARACION}}, with impact sign (+ adds margin, − removes margin). 6) Express the EBITDA margin variation in basis points. 7) Write the narrative for the three highest-impact levers on the margin, explaining cause and effect without filler.

Rigor rules: do not invent figures; if {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, {{PERIODO_COMPARACION}}, {{PARTIDAS_NO_RECURRENTES}}, or {{MONEDA_Y_UNIDAD}} is missing, ask before calculating. Tag every estimate [ASSUMPTION] and declare its limits. Verify that each subtotal closes arithmetically and that the bridge EBITDA equals the source EBITDA; if it does not reconcile, report the difference instead of forcing it. Always distinguish reported EBITDA from adjusted EBITDA. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: step-by-step bridge table (absolute, % of revenue, signed delta), reported vs. adjusted EBITDA reconciliation block, EBITDA margin % indicator with its basis-points variation, and narrative of the three dominant levers.

Parameters: {{ENTIDAD_O_UNIDAD}}, {{PERIODO_ANALIZADO}}, {{PERIODO_COMPARACION}}, {{MONEDA_Y_UNIDAD}}, {{PARTIDAS_NO_RECURRENTES}}, {{FUENTE_DATOS}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Modeling resource capacity and cost
Consolidating multi-entity results
prompts.content: Act as a senior consolidation controller with mastery of IFRS 10 / IFRS standards, IAS 21 (foreign currency translation), intercompany eliminations, and minority interest. I need the consolidated income statement and balance sheet of {{NOMBRE_GRUPO}} for {{PERIODO}}, expressed in {{MONEDA_PRESENTACION}}, with an eliminations sheet, conversion adjustments, minority interest, and an auditable reconciliation table. Before calculating, restate what you understand and present your plan; if any data from {{ENTIDADES_Y_PARTICIPACION}}, {{TIPOS_DE_CAMBIO}}, or {{OPERACIONES_INTERCOMPANY}} is missing, ask and do not invent figures: tag each gap as [ASSUMPTION]. Proceed in phases: (1) confirm the scope from {{ENTIDADES_Y_PARTICIPACION}} and assign each entity its consolidation method based on effective control (full consolidation if control exists, equity method for associates with significant influence, proportionate consolidation only for joint ventures when applicable); (2) normalize each entity's chart of accounts and accounting policies to a common structure before aggregating, aligning recognition criteria and the same closing date; (3) sum individual results and balance sheets of the scope line by line; (4) eliminate every intercompany transaction from {{OPERACIONES_INTERCOMPANY}} with its exact counterpart (internal sales/purchases, loans and interest, internal dividends, and unrealized margin in inventory and in fixed assets transferred within the group), verifying that internal revenues and expenses cancel out; (5) convert each entity from its functional currency to {{MONEDA_PRESENTACION}} using {{TIPOS_DE_CAMBIO}}, applying the average rate to results and the closing rate to the balance sheet, recording the cumulative translation difference in equity (other comprehensive income), never in profit or loss; (6) calculate minority interest on equity and on profit where ownership is below 100%, separating controlling from non-controlling interest; (7) build the reconciliation: sum of individuals minus eliminations plus/minus conversion adjustments equals consolidated. Flag any imbalance with its amount and probable cause instead of forcing the close. Treat as edge cases: cross or layered holdings, entities acquired or sold mid-{{PERIODO}} (partial consolidation by months), hyperinflationary economies (IAS 29), elimination of already-accrued dividends, and goodwill or acquisition difference if reported. Deliver the two consolidated statements, the documented debit/credit eliminations sheet, the detail of conversion adjustments, minority interest, and the reconciliation table, plus an assumptions block and an auditability caveats block. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

prompts.title: Universal GTD capture of all pending items
prompts.content:
Act as a senior personal productivity coach certified in Getting Things Done (David Allen), specialized in the Capture step and in facilitating trigger-guided mind-sweeps. My mind is saturated with open commitments, loose ideas, and pending items that keep circling without being recorded anywhere trustworthy, which generates stress and attention leakage. I want to execute the GTD Capture step over the domains {{DOMINIOS}} in {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}: empty my mind completely and consolidate everything into a single inbox that will live in {{DESTINO_INBOX}}, without processing or organizing yet. The goal is the mind-like-water feeling, where everything that had my attention lives outside my head in a reliable system.

Guide me through a four-phase session. Phase 1, Framing: confirm the domains {{DOMINIOS}}, the {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, the {{DESTINO_INBOX}}, and the level of detail {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}; remind me that this session only captures, it does not process, prioritize, or organize, and set the golden rule: a captured concern no longer occupies the mind, so everything is released, even the trivial. Phase 2, Guided sweep: go through {{DOMINIOS}} one at a time with triggers adapted to the level of detail (what worries or circles you here, what you promised and did not deliver, what you left half-done, what decision you are postponing, what is waiting for someone else's response). Work in short rounds and wait for my responses before continuing; before moving to a new area, ask whether there is anything more. Phase 3, Faithful capture: record each thing as a loose item, exactly as I say it, without reformulating, grouping, or converting it into a next action; mark vague items with [clarify]. Phase 4, Consolidation: deliver the single inbox as a flat numbered list, grouped only by source domain, with ambiguous items tagged [clarify].

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if I provided material. Do not invent pending items I have not mentioned. If any data is missing, ask before beginning. Close by reminding me that the next GTD step is Clarify, in a separate session.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Clarifying the GTD inbox
Defining the concrete physical next action
prompts.content:
Act as a senior personal productivity coach trained in Getting Things Done (David Allen), specialist in the next-action discipline and in distinguishing projects from actions. Your goal is to transform a vague or stuck task into the concrete physical next action: the single visible and specific step that is executed without thinking again.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First, restate in your own words the received task and classify why it is stuck; present your reading and your plan before drafting the final action.

Vague task to land: {{TAREA_VAGA}}
Execution context (desk, phone, street, home, errands): {{CONTEXTO_GTD}}
Tools or people at hand: {{HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES}}
Real time window to start: {{RESTRICCIONES_TIEMPO}}

Steps:
1. Diagnose the cause of the stuck state in {{TAREA_VAGA}}: a multi-step project disguised as a task, absence of a physical verb, dependency on a third party, diffuse ending, or lack of prior information.
2. If completing it requires several steps, name it as a project (statement of the desired outcome) and isolate ONLY its next action; do not deliver the full list.
3. Draft ONE single next action that starts with a physical observable verb (call, write, open, search, draft, send, print, schedule); never decide, organize, plan, or think.
4. Ensure it is the real first move and that it can start ideally in under two minutes; associate it with {{CONTEXTO_GTD}}, {{HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES}}, and {{RESTRICCIONES_TIEMPO}} when they exist.
5. Connect the action with the outcome it unblocks in one sentence.

Edge cases: if the action depends on a third party, the next action is yours (draft and send the message, not wait for a reply). If {{TAREA_VAGA}} is already a clear physical action, confirm it and refine it instead of inventing a project. If a data point essential to concretizing the verb is missing, ask in a single question before delivering.

Limits: one single action, not a list or an objective; do not invent tools or deadlines not declared; neutral, professional English, no emojis.

Deliverable: block with the next action ready to paste, its context, and if applicable the name of the associated project, plus the sentence connecting the action with the outcome.

prompts.title: Organizing tasks by GTD context lists
Defining GTD projects by desired outcome
prompts.content: Act as a senior coach certified in GTD (Getting Things Done by David Allen), expert in refining personal productivity systems with the desired-outcome-plus-single-next-action discipline. My current focus area is {{AREA_FOCO}} and I want to prioritize by {{CRITERIO_PRIORIDAD}}. I hand you this raw list of mixed commitments, pending items, and ideas: {{LISTA_PENDIENTES}}. Connect the projects, when applicable, to these higher horizons: {{HORIZONTE_SUPERIOR}} (if I leave it empty, infer the horizon from the list itself and mark it as inferred). Also consider these support materials: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any essential data is missing (focus area, criterion, or list content), ask me before continuing; do not invent items or assume outcomes I have not stated. Proceed as follows. First, capture: normalize the list, separate each element, and remove duplicates. Second, clarify: classify each element as a single action (one step) or a project (more than one step); if a next action is still multi-step it is a sub-project and you break it down. Third, organize: per project draft one desired outcome as an already-fulfilled, verifiable success statement, and a single physical, visible next action starting with a verb and with an explicit context; assign a horizon and note dependencies, waits, or dates. Fourth, prioritize: order by {{CRITERIO_PRIORIDAD}} and flag blocks. Deliver a table with columns Project, Desired outcome, Next action, Context, Horizon/Notes, plus a separate list of single actions. Tag ambiguous items {to confirm}. Before executing, restate in one line what you understood and present your plan. Respond in neutral, professional English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Apply the two-minute rule
Daily review of actionable lists
prompts.content:
Act as a senior productivity coach specialized in GTD (Getting Things Done by David Allen), with mastery of contexts, next actions, the two-minute rule, and the distinction between task and project. I want to decide my focus for the day before the day decides it for me: convert a packed calendar and a vague list of pending items into 1 to 3 realistic priorities for {{FECHA}}, protect discretionary time, and enter execution with clear criteria.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understand and present your plan; execute only after.

Deliver a day plan on a single screen following these steps. 1) Restate my calendar {{CALENDARIO_HOY}} and my energy {{ENERGIA_DISPONIBLE}}; subtract the fixed blocks and calculate the discretionary time available for {{FECHA}}. 2) Take {{SIGUIENTES_ACCIONES}} and group them by context (computer, calls, errands, waiting-for, home) when the data exists. 3) Recommend 1 to 3 priorities that fit within the discretionary time, justifying each one by impact and deadline; the sum of estimated durations must not exceed the discretionary time. 4) Explicitly declare what will NOT be done today and why it is deferred. 5) Flag overdue actions or those at risk and every item that is a project disguised as a task (requires more than one action) and reformulate it as its concrete next physical and visible action.

Rules: each priority must be expressed as a concrete next action starting with a verb. If an item fits in less than two minutes, suggest doing it immediately instead of scheduling it. Do not invent commitments or data; mark any inference as [ASSUMPTION]. If {{CALENDARIO_HOY}}, {{SIGUIENTES_ACCIONES}}, or {{ENERGIA_DISPONIBLE}} are missing or ambiguous, ask for them before planning. Also consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if it provides context. Do not use prices.

Close with the plan on a single screen: suggested time blocks, the 1 to 3 priorities with their first next action, list of deferrals, and alerts for overdue items or disguised projects.

Parameters:
- {{FECHA}}: day of the review (defaults to today)
- {{CALENDARIO_HOY}}: meetings and fixed blocks with their schedule
- {{SIGUIENTES_ACCIONES}}: list of pending items with context, duration, and deadline if available
- {{ENERGIA_DISPONIBLE}}: level and hours of real expected focus today
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Curate the Someday/Maybe list
Manage the Waiting For delegation list
Map the six GTD horizons of focus
Mind-like-water diagnosis
prompts.content:
Act as a senior coach certified in David Allen's Getting Things Done (GTD), specialized in the mind-like-water principle and in facilitating mind sweeps. My goal: empty my head and recover focus by externalizing the open loops the mind cycles through in a loop because it does not trust they are captured outside of it.

My context: {{CONTEXTO_ACTUAL}}.
Stress level and perceived source: {{NIVEL_ESTRES}}.
Domains to sweep: {{DOMINIOS_FOCO}}.
Time available for the session: {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}.
Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before executing, follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret {{CONTEXTO_ACTUAL}}, {{NIVEL_ESTRES}}, and {{DOMINIOS_FOCO}}; Plan and present the sweep plan (domain order and depth calibrated to {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}); and only then Execute. If {{CONTEXTO_ACTUAL}}, {{DOMINIOS_FOCO}}, or {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}} are missing or ambiguous, ask before inventing.

Then: (1) restate my context and stress level, confirm the domains. (2) Conduct the mind sweep domain by domain, one area at a time, with trigger questions that surface pending items, postponed decisions, unclosed promises, and diffuse worries; do not advance until the area is exhausted; log every loop in raw form. (3) Classify each loop: concrete action / project (more than one step) / waiting for someone else / reference / someday-maybe. (4) For each action define the next physical and visible step in a phrase starting with a verb; flag projects to decompose. (5) Identify the 3 loops with the highest emotional load as priority closes with their justification.

Deliverable: (1) complete inventory of loops classified by category, (2) list of actionable next steps, (3) top 3 to close first with justification, and (4) a brief reflection on the pattern the inventory reveals. An accompanying tone, zero judgments about the person.

prompts.title: Reach inbox zero with GTD
prompts.content:
Act as a senior personal-productivity coach certified in David Allen's Getting Things Done (GTD), specialized in high-volume email management. My goal is to get my inbox to inbox zero today: not to read everything, but to decide about everything, so every action lives in a reliable system and the inbox stops being my to-do list.

Proceed as follows. First validate that {{CORREOS}} contains processable material (sender, subject, and body or summary); if it is missing or incomplete, ask for it before proceeding and do not invent content. Confirm how many emails there are and group them into manageable batches, addressing first what appears in {{PRIORIDADES}}.

Then process each email one by one using the GTD decision tree and record a single decision per email with a one-line justification:
1) Not actionable: delete or archive as reference.
2) Actionable under 2 minutes: do it now by drafting the reply immediately.
3) Actionable over 2 minutes: delegate to someone in {{DELEGADOS}} and draft the delegation message with the expected result and date, or defer as a task with an action verb, context, and suggested date.
4) If it depends on a third party, log it as waiting-for with the responsible party and a follow-up date; if it is not actionable now but perhaps later, incubate it as someday-maybe.

Calibrate how much you resolve now versus what you defer based on {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}; if time runs out, prioritize deciding and deferring over executing. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} when evaluating each email. When information needed to resolve is missing, do not invent it: flag it as a blocker and propose the next step.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

At close deliver: table with the decision and justification per email; ready-to-copy-and-send reply and delegation drafts; clean next-actions list; and summary with count per category confirming inbox at zero.

Variables:
- {{CORREOS}}: list or dump of the emails to process (sender, subject, and body or summary).
- {{PRIORIDADES}}: senders, projects, or topics requiring priority attention (optional).
- {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}: real minutes available today to resolve emails inline (optional).
- {{DELEGADOS}}: people or roles to whom tasks can be delegated, with their area (optional).
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

prompts.title: Classify tasks with the Eisenhower matrix
prompts.content: Act as a senior personal-productivity and time-management coach, expert in the Eisenhower matrix and in deep-focus habits. I have this accumulated task list: {{LISTA_TAREAS}}. My known deadlines per task are {{PLAZOS}} and my medium and long-term objectives that define what is important are {{OBJETIVOS}}. For delegating or automating I have {{RECURSOS_DELEGACION}}. The planning horizon for the final plan is {{HORIZONTE}}. I want a complete classification plus a prioritized action plan. First operationally define important (moves {{OBJETIVOS}}, high consequence, or non-transferable) and urgent (real near-term deadline in {{PLAZOS}} or immediate consequence); do not confuse feeling urgent with being important. Then assign each task from {{LISTA_TAREAS}} to exactly one quadrant: Q1 important and urgent, Q2 important and not urgent, Q3 not important and urgent, Q4 not important and not urgent. Map each quadrant to its decision: Q1 do now; Q2 schedule with a date and block (strategy lives here); Q3 delegate or automate with {{RECURSOS_DELEGACION}}; Q4 eliminate or postpone. For each task deliver the quadrant, a one-line justification anchored to importance and urgency, the decision, and the date or responsible party when applicable. Close with a plan for {{HORIZONTE}} that separates what to do today, what to schedule, what to delegate, and what to release, with an alert if Q1 is overloaded and how to offload it via Q2. If a task generates recurring value, propose converting it into a habit or system. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Mark as an assumption any importance or urgency criterion you infer due to missing data, and if a critical piece of data is missing, ask for it before classifying.

prompts.title: Prioritize with the MoSCoW method
Plan the day with the 1-3-5 rule
prompts.content:
Act as a senior personal-productivity coach, expert in prioritization methods (1-3-5, Eisenhower, time-blocking) and in designing sustainable workdays. Your goal is to convert my vague list of pending items into a calibrated 1-3-5 daily plan: 1 big task, 3 medium tasks, and 5 small tasks, adjusted to my real hours, my fixed commitments, and my peak-energy slot.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understood and present your plan before executing.

Data:
- List of candidate pending items: {{LISTA_PENDIENTES}}
- Effective working hours available today: {{HORAS_DISPONIBLES}}
- Fixed commitments with their schedule: {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}}
- Peak focus and energy slot: {{NIVEL_ENERGIA}}

Proceed as follows:
1. Confirm that you have {{LISTA_PENDIENTES}} and {{HORAS_DISPONIBLES}}. If either is missing, ask for it before continuing; if {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}} or {{NIVEL_ENERGIA}} are missing, assume a reasonable scenario and mark it as an assumption.
2. Classify each pending item by size: big (more than 90 min or high complexity), medium (30-90 min), small (less than 30 min or administrative). Mark impact as high, medium, or low.
3. Choose the single big task by impact, not by urgency or comfort, and explain why in one line.
4. Select 3 medium and 5 small tasks. Discard extras explicitly with justification; if fewer real candidates exist, deliver fewer and say so.
5. Add up durations, subtract them from {{HORAS_DISPONIBLES}}, and verify at least a 15% buffer. If it does not fit, indicate what to leave out.
6. Assign time blocks: the big task in the {{NIVEL_ENERGIA}} slot, medium tasks around it, the 5 small tasks in a single short block, respecting {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}}.
7. Define the first concrete startup micro-action (under 5 min) for the big task and each medium task.

Mark [ASSUMPTION] on every estimated duration, impact, or energy level inferred.

Deliverable: table with columns task, size, impact, time block, and first micro-action; below it, total planned versus {{HORAS_DISPONIBLES}} with the resulting buffer; close with a single focus sentence for the day.

prompts.title: Define the six priorities using the Ivy Lee method
Apply the Pareto principle to tasks
Choose the frog of the day (eat the frog)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior personal productivity coach, expert in Brian Tracy's Eat That Frog method and in ABCDE prioritization. My objective: have you choose ONE single frog of the day (the highest-impact task I am avoiding the most) and deliver a plan to execute it in my first focus window.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what you understood and present your plan before executing.

Data:
- PENDIENTES: {{PENDIENTES}} (list of today's pending tasks, one per line, with whatever detail I have: deadline, context, who is involved)
- HORA_INICIO: {{HORA_INICIO}} (real time I start my workday today)
- RESULTADO_SEMANA: {{RESULTADO_SEMANA}} (the most important result I need to move this week, against which impact is measured)
- VENTANA_FOCO: {{VENTANA_FOCO}} (uninterrupted focus minutes I can protect in the morning; optional)

If PENDIENTES, HORA_INICIO, or RESULTADO_SEMANA are missing, ask me before continuing; do not invent tasks or deadlines, and mark [ASSUMPTION] where there is no data.

Then: 1) Score each pending item on impact (1 to 5 against RESULTADO_SEMANA or the consequence of not doing it) and resistance (1 to 5, how much I avoid it), with a one-line justification. 2) Choose the frog: highest impact among those with high resistance (4 to 5); ties are broken by the worst consequence of not doing it today. Declare it: 'Today I eat: [task] because [impact]'. 3) If the frog turns out to be comfortable, flag it as a selection error and correct it. 4) If it is a project, isolate only the first chunk that fits VENTANA_FOCO. 5) Classify the rest with ABCDE (A grave / B should / C nice / D delegate / E eliminate), with at least one to delegate or eliminate. 6) Design the plan: a window as early as possible after HORA_INICIO, estimated duration, a 2-minute startup micro-step, 2 to 3 distractions to turn off. 7) Define a verifiable done signal and a 1-line plan B.

Deliver: the frog in one sentence, the impact/resistance table, the ABCDE classification of the rest, and the morning attack plan. Neutral professional English, no filler.

prompts.title: Sort tasks with an effort vs. impact matrix
prompts.content: Act as a senior personal productivity strategist with mastery of the effort-impact matrix (2x2) and capacity management. Work on these initiatives: {{LISTA_INICIATIVAS}} (one per line, with estimated duration if I know it). My period objective is {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}}, my real capacity is {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}}, the planning horizon is {{HORIZONTE}}, and the dominant impact dimension is {{CRITERIO_IMPACTO}}. If an essential piece of data is missing to classify or I cannot distinguish impact between initiatives, ask me before continuing. Anchor the high-impact threshold to {{OBJETIVO_PERIODO}} and {{CRITERIO_IMPACTO}}, not to urgency. For each initiative estimate Effort (High/Low: hours, dependencies, complexity, energy) and Impact (High/Low: proximity to the objective and cost of not doing it); mark [ASSUMPTION] for any estimate without data; when tied, prioritize lower effort at equal impact and greater reversibility. Assign each initiative to a single quadrant (Quick Wins, Big Bets, Fillers, Drains) and show the matrix as a table (Initiative | Effort | Impact | Quadrant | Action). Build the plan: execute Quick Wins now; sequence Big Bets within {{CAPACIDAD_DISPONIBLE}} with order, first step, and hours, summing hours and warning if they exceed the limit; schedule Fillers only if capacity remains; discard or delegate Drains with justification. Close with three concrete moves for the next segment of {{HORIZONTE}}. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Neutral professional English, no prices.

prompts.title: Prioritize personal projects with RICE scoring
prompts.content: Act as a senior personal productivity coach expert in product prioritization frameworks adapted to individual life (RICE, ICE, WSJF). I have more personal projects than time and I have been deciding among them by intuition or apparent urgency, not by real value. I want to rank {{PROYECTOS}} with RICE to invest my energy where it yields the most and make explicit the assumptions behind each decision. Before calculating anything, confirm {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}} as the evaluation window, {{CRITERIO_IMPACTO}} as the definition of moving the needle, and {{UNIDAD_ESFUERZO}} as the single unit of work (the same for all, without mixing). If any is missing or the project list is empty, ask for it instead of inventing figures. Then: 1) Define the four factors in my context: Reach (areas or people touched by frequency within {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}), Impact (scale 3 massive, 2 high, 1 medium, 0.5 low, 0.25 minimal per {{CRITERIO_IMPACTO}}), Confidence (100% high with evidence, 80% medium, 50% low, below 50% gut feeling), and Effort (total in {{UNIDAD_ESFUERZO}}). 2) Score each project in {{PROYECTOS}} on the four factors with a one-line justification per factor; mark [ASSUMPTION] for any estimated value without data I have provided. 3) Calculate the score with (Reach x Impact x Confidence as a decimal) divided by Effort, verifying unit consistency. 4) Sort from highest to lowest in a table with the formula visible per row. Close with: top 3, alert on projects with confidence below 50% to validate before investing, the highest-leverage factor per project, note on ties or scores with less than 10% difference that call for a tiebreaker, and flag for any project whose effort does not fit within {{HORIZONTE_TEMPORAL}}. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context if provided. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliverable: sorted RICE table plus actionable read of 3 to 5 lines stating what to start, what to postpone, and what to validate first.

prompts.title: Make better decisions with the WRAP process
Compare options with a weighted decision matrix
prompts.content: Act as a senior decision analyst and weighted decision matrix designer (weighted scoring model), with the judgment to detect poorly framed criteria, correlated criteria, and weighting biases. I want to resolve {{DECISION}} objectively and traceably comparing these options: {{OPCIONES}}, according to these criteria: {{CRITERIOS}}. Use these weights: {{PESOS}} (if they do not sum to 100% normalize them and show the distribution; if missing, distribute equally and warn me) and this scale: {{ESCALA}} (default 1 to 5 oriented toward benefit). Keep this context and non-negotiables in mind: {{CONTEXTO_DECISION}}. Supporting material: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Work as follows. Confirm the decision, options, and criteria; if anything is missing or ambiguous, ask before advancing and do not invent data. Validate that the criteria are independent: if two measure nearly the same thing, warn and propose merging or reweighting. Orient everything toward benefit; invert cost or risk criteria and say so. Anchor each scale level with a brief rubric. Score each option on each criterion with a one-line justification and mark [ASSUMPTION] when you fill in data. Calculate the weighted value per cell and the total per option; present the matrix as a table with totals and an ordered ranking, and flag dominated options. Close with the first-to-second margin, the break-even weight or score that reverses the result, a 2 to 3-sentence recommendation, and conditions for reconsidering. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Run a pre-mortem on an important decision
prompts.content: Act as a senior strategic decision facilitator, expert in Gary Klein's pre-mortem technique (HBR 2007) and in cognitive biases (optimism, prior commitment, planning fallacy, survivorship). I am about to make this decision: {{DECISION}}. Context and motivation: {{CONTEXTO}}. Horizon for judging whether it worked: {{HORIZONTE}}. Success signals (3 to 5): {{CRITERIOS_EXITO}}. Time, money, energy, or people constraints: {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Reversibility of the decision: {{REVERSIBILIDAD}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any critical data is missing or ambiguous, ask for it one at a time before advancing. Then: 1) reframe the decision in one clear sentence and normalize the success criteria into measurable signals; 2) travel to the end of the horizon and declare that the decision failed outright; 3) perform the autopsy: 8 to 12 plausible causes grouped by origin (false assumptions, execution, external factors, human or emotional dynamics, lack of resources), each with a brief narrative; 4) score each cause with probability (high/medium/low) and impact (high/medium/low) in a table, and name 2 or 3 blind spots each linked to a concrete bias; 5) for each critical cause deliver a preventive countermeasure now, an observable early warning signal, and a plan B; 6) define a kill-switch: the concrete threshold that, if crossed, forces reversal or abort; 7) close with an unambiguous verdict (reinforce / postpone / rethink) with justification. The autopsy starts from the failure already accomplished, not from conditional hypotheses. Anything not stated, mark as [ASSUMPTION]. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.

prompts.title: Evaluate the opportunity cost of a commitment
prompts.content: Act as a senior personal productivity and decision-making coach, expert in behavioral economics (opportunity cost, sunk costs, commitment bias) and attention management. I am evaluating {{COMPROMISO}} and I want to decide with awareness of the trade-off, not out of inertia, guilt, or in-the-moment enthusiasm. Before calculating, reframe the commitment in one sentence in the format "Accepting [what] would cost me [main resource] for [period]" and confirm that you have {{RECURSOS}}, {{ALTERNATIVAS}}, and {{HORIZONTE}}; if anything essential is missing, ask me for it; do not invent obligations or alternatives. Then deliver: (1) the real cost with {{RECURSOS}}, separating visible cost (hours per week or month) from hidden cost (context switches, preparation, recovery, implicit availability) and energy or mental load with reason; (2) opportunity cost over {{ALTERNATIVAS}}: 2 to 4 displaced things, each with importance and whether it is replaceable or loses its window (if {{ALTERNATIVAS}} is empty, propose candidates marked as proposals); (3) sunk-cost filter: what has already been invested does not weigh in, only the net future value; (4) comparison of the expected value of the commitment against the best displaced alternative within {{HORIZONTE}}, with the margin and its magnitude (clear, adjusted, or tied); (5) single verdict among accept, accept with conditions (renegotiate scope, timeline, or frequency), or decline, with a ready-to-use sentence that protects the relationship if you decline or renegotiate; (6) consistency check against {{CRITERIO_DECISION}}, naming contradictions without hedging. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any estimate without my data. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Neutral professional English, no emojis, no "it depends". Variables: {{COMPROMISO}}, {{RECURSOS}}, {{ALTERNATIVAS}}, {{HORIZONTE}}, {{CRITERIO_DECISION}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Apply the 10-10-10 rule to a decision
prompts.content: Act as a senior expert in decision-making and personal criterion architecture, trained in Suzy Welch's 10-10-10 framework and in trade-off analysis under uncertainty. Work on this decision: {{DECISION}}. Real options on the table: {{OPCIONES}}. What I most want to protect: {{LO_QUE_IMPORTA}}. Emotion or pressure dominating me right now: {{EMOCION_ACTUAL}}. Horizon that weighs most on me (or 'all three equally'): {{HORIZONTE_RELEVANTE}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before analyzing, reframe {{DECISION}} and {{OPCIONES}} in your own words and name how {{EMOCION_ACTUAL}} could bias my choice; if {{DECISION}}, {{OPCIONES}}, or {{LO_QUE_IMPORTA}} are missing or ambiguous, ask me before continuing. Then, for each option, analyze the three horizons separately without mixing them: 10 minutes (immediate relief or tension), 10 months (effect on routine, relationships, finances, projects), and 10 years (alignment with my values and who I want to be), evaluating each horizon against {{LO_QUE_IMPORTA}} and not in the abstract. Contrast the horizons giving weight to {{HORIZONTE_RELEVANTE}}: mark where the impulse of the moment contradicts long-term interest and separate the reversible from the irreversible. Close with a recommendation backed by a single main reason, the trade-offs I accept declared without varnish, and a concrete and observable signal of when to reopen the decision. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent data. Respond in neutral professional English.

prompts.title: Design the day's agenda with time blocking
Apply timeboxing to a task with no clear end
Structure a work session with Pomodoro
Conduct a time-use audit
prompts.content: Act as a senior personal productivity coach specializing in time-use audits, with expertise in time-tracking, the Eisenhower matrix, energy-time mapping, Parkinson's Law, and context-switching costs (attention residue). I want an honest audit of the period {{PERIODO_REGISTRO}} to stop operating on autopilot and reallocate hours toward what matters. Before classifying, restate my log, objective, and constraints; mark ambiguous windows or periods without data and ask for what is missing. Work with: REGISTRO_TIEMPO={{REGISTRO_TIEMPO}}, COMPROMISOS_FIJOS={{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}}, OBJETIVO_REASIGNACION={{OBJETIVO_REASIGNACION}}, ADJUNTOS={{ADJUNTOS}}. Normalize the log to {{GRANULARIDAD}} and classify each window on three axes: category (deep work / reactive / meetings / administration / rest / leisure / commute / personal), value (high / medium / low / leak), and energy (high / medium / low). Quantify hours and percentage by category and by value, with an explicit and traceable calculation of leak hours (multitasking, context switches, decision-free meetings, waiting, scrolling) and the counting method. Detect patterns: energy-time peak misalignment, fragmentation, low-return commitments, and Parkinson's Law. Deliver the plan: top 3 leaks with a cut or redesign action, protected blocks in energy peaks that respect {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}}, and a one-week experiment toward {{OBJETIVO_REASIGNACION}} with a target of hours to recover and a success metric, plus one adherence risk and its mitigation. Mark every inference [ASSUMPTION]; do not fill windows without data and declare those reconstructed from memory; do not include prices or monetary costs unless figures are given. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Assign themes to the days of the week
Group similar tasks into batches (batching)
prompts.content: Act as a senior personal productivity coach, expert in task batching, attention management, and time-blocking design to reduce mental switching costs (context switching). I want a batching plan that groups my tasks by mental mode, tool, and energy, places them in protected blocks, and gives me real focus back. Context: tasks I repeat and how often = {{TAREAS_RECURRENTES}}; mental modes or categories I recognize = {{TIPOS_DE_TAREA}}; actually free time windows with their time = {{BLOQUES_DISPONIBLES}}; tool or environment each task type requires = {{HERRAMIENTAS_CONTEXTO}}; schedule, energy, or fixed-agenda limits I cannot move = {{RESTRICCIONES}}; what typically pulls me out of focus = {{INTERRUPCIONES_TIPICAS}}. The principle: every jump between work types leaves an attention residue and forces a re-start; by grouping into batches I pay the start-up cost once per batch. Before executing, restate what you understand about my work and my week and present your plan; wait for my confirmation. If a key data point is missing, ask for it in a brief list before continuing and do not invent; mark as [ASSUMPTION] any frequency, duration, or energy level you infer. Work in four phases: (1) Classify each task by dominant mental mode, tool, and energy (high/medium/low), grouping by mode and not just by topic. (2) Form named batches that share mode, tool, and energy, with a realistic duration (aim for 25–90 min; break if they exceed ~90); neither micro-batches that do not justify the start-up cost nor batches that cause fatigue. (3) Assign each batch to {{BLOQUES_DISPONIBLES}} respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}} and the energy curve: deep work in the peak, administrative in the valley, external contact concentrated, with slack between batches. (4) Protect and route against {{INTERRUPCIONES_TIPICAS}}: notification status and do-not-disturb signal, the only criterion that DOES justify interrupting a batch (irreversible urgency with a deadline inside the block), and a capture protocol to a single inbox that parks what arrives out of batch without breaking the current one. Deliver classification table, named batches with duration, weekly plan by block, protection rules, capture protocol, and two or three measurable metrics with baseline and target. If any task type cannot fit without violating a constraint, say so and propose the minimum adjustment. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis, no invented figures.

prompts.title: Insert buffer time into the agenda
Plan the week with thematic blocks
Combat Parkinson's Law with short deadlines
prompts.content: Act as a senior personal productivity coach specializing in evidence-based time management (Parkinson's Law, timeboxing, the 80/20 rule, and fixed-time work). I have the task {{TAREA}}, which tends to expand, and I want a short, defensible, actionable-today deadline plan that frees up hours for other priorities and turns closing into a decision by design, not by exhaustion. Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before developing it. Data: time baseline {{TIEMPO_ACTUAL}}; time actually available before the next commitment {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}; verifiable outcome that declares it done {{DEFINICION_HECHO}}; quality level sufficient for this case {{NIVEL_CALIDAD}} (optional); supporting material {{ADJUNTOS}}. If TAREA, TIEMPO_ACTUAL, TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE, or DEFINICION_HECHO is missing, ask before continuing and do not invent assumptions; mark ambiguities as pending confirmation. Deliver, on a single page ready to execute: (1) {{TAREA}} reformulated in a verifiable-outcome sentence anchored to {{DEFINICION_HECHO}}, separating core from accessory with 80/20 and naming what falls out; (2) an aggressive but defensible deadline, typically 50 to 70 percent of {{TIEMPO_ACTUAL}} and never greater than {{TIEMPO_DISPONIBLE}}, with one justification line; (3) if the deadline exceeds 90 minutes, timeboxing blocks of 25 to 50 minutes with a micro-deliverable and start/end time, plus micro-breaks; (4) exactly three anti-expansion constraints (written scope limit, version zero before polishing, explicit signal to stop perfectionism) calibrated to {{NIVEL_CALIDAD}}; (5) a close protocol with the good-enough criterion, action if the clock runs out (scope cut or useful partial delivery), and action if time remains (close and reallocate, do not expand). If {{TIEMPO_ACTUAL}} is already less than or equal to the minimum reasonable deadline, say so and propose optimizing the method instead of compressing. Neutral professional Spanish, zero theoretical filler.

prompts.title: Plan the day according to the energy curve
Design an ideal reference week
Protect maker time blocks vs manager time
prompts.content:
Act as a senior personal productivity strategist, expert in Paul Graham's Maker's Schedule, Manager's Schedule framework and in Cal Newport's Deep Work-style time-blocking. My goal is to reclaim uninterrupted creation time that today is fragmented by meetings, because a single mid-morning meeting can render two half-blocks of deep work useless and triggers context-switching costs.

Proceed as follows: 1) Diagnose {{SEMANA_TIPO}}: quantify the real maker time available today in useful block-hours (only continuous stretches of 90 minutes or more), identify where meetings fragment creation, and name the context-switching cost. 2) Classify each commitment in {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}} and {{SEMANA_TIPO}} as maker, manager, or hybrid; flag which are unmovable, negotiable, or movable. 3) Design a typical week that consolidates manager time into defensive windows or designated days and reserves {{BLOQUES_MAKER_OBJETIVO}} in the {{CRONOTIPO}} window, in minimum 90-minute stretches with no meetings interspersed and a transition buffer before and after, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. 4) Define shielding rules actionable today: block naming conventions on the calendar, policy for responding to invitations that land in maker time, office hours for asynchronous or synchronous queries, and a brief script to renegotiate meetings that invade creation time. 5) Deliver a two-week transition plan and three measurable verification metrics.

Rules: do not invent availability; respect {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}} and {{RESTRICCIONES}} as stated; mark every assumption. If {{SEMANA_TIPO}}, {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}}, {{BLOQUES_MAKER_OBJETIVO}}, {{CRONOTIPO}}, or {{RESTRICCIONES}} are missing or incomplete, ask before executing.

Variables:
- {{SEMANA_TIPO}}: description of the current typical week (recurring meetings, schedules, creation tasks and how they are distributed today)
- {{COMPROMISOS_FIJOS}}: fixed, unmovable meetings and commitments with day and time (standups, committees, 1:1s, classes)
- {{BLOQUES_MAKER_OBJETIVO}}: how many deep-creation blocks I want to protect per week and their desired length
- {{CRONOTIPO}}: highest-energy and focus window (morning/afternoon/evening) and low-performance hours
- {{RESTRICCIONES}}: team time zone, non-negotiable meetings, personal-life limits, and other boundaries (optional)

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: typical-week table (day × window with maker/manager/hybrid labels), shielding rules list, renegotiation script, 2-week transition plan, and 3 tracking metrics.

prompts.title: Draft responses to say no to commitments
prompts.content: Act as a senior productivity and assertive communication coach, specialized in boundary management and priority strategy. I need to decline {{PETICION}} from {{SOLICITANTE}} because it conflicts with {{PRIORIDAD_CHOCA}}, without opening a negotiation or accumulating guilt, while preserving the relationship ({{RELACION}}). The reply will go through {{CANAL}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. My willingness to offer something in return: {{ALTERNATIVA}} (can be "none"). First restate in one sentence what you understand: what is being asked, who is asking, which of my priorities is displaced, the type of relationship, and the channel. If {{PETICION}}, {{SOLICITANTE}}, {{PRIORIDAD_CHOCA}}, {{RELACION}}, or {{CANAL}} is missing, ask before drafting instead of inventing them; mark any assumption as [ASSUMPTION]. Then present your plan: the angle of each variant (one warm, one direct) and whether each will include an alternative or not according to {{ALTERNATIVA}}. Then deliver two ready-to-send responses for {{CANAL}} plus an anti-spiral closing line. Each variant follows the positive-no framework in order: sincere and brief acknowledgment; honest reason anchored in {{PRIORIDAD_CHOCA}}, with no invented excuses or repeated apologies; unequivocal decline with no maybe, I'll try, or it depends; and a single, bounded alternative only if {{ALTERNATIVA}} exists. The closing line stops the spiral of justifications and does not reopen the door. Calibrate length, formality, and closeness according to {{RELACION}} and {{CANAL}}. If {{ALTERNATIVA}} is "none", do not invent one. Respond in neutral, professional Spanish, no emojis. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute.

prompts.title: Design a habit using the four atomic laws
Create a chain with habit stacking
prompts.content:
Act as a senior behavior design coach, trained in BJ Fogg's B=MAP model and James Clear's Atomic Habits framework. Turn {{HABITO_NUEVO}} into an automatic link in a routine I already do without thinking, using habit stacking, so that the chain sustains itself and reinforces the identity of {{MOTIVACION}} without depending on motivation or memory.

Data I provide:
- HABITO_NUEVO: {{HABITO_NUEVO}} (observable action, e.g. 'do 10 squats')
- MOTIVACION: {{MOTIVACION}} (why I want it and what identity it reinforces)
- RUTINAS_ACTUALES: {{RUTINAS_ACTUALES}} (3 to 5 automatic daily routines, with approximate time and physical context)
- NIVEL_DIFICULTAD: {{NIVEL_DIFICULTAD}} (how hard it currently is for me to start this habit and why; optional)
- HORIZONTE: {{HORIZONTE}} (period for the gradual progression, e.g. '4 weeks')

If HABITO_NUEVO, MOTIVACION, or RUTINAS_ACTUALES are missing, ask me before continuing and do not invent routines.

Deliver in this order: (1) sentence restating {{HABITO_NUEVO}} + {{MOTIVACION}} to confirm understanding; (2) anchor routine chosen from {{RUTINAS_ACTUALES}}, justified with four filters (same frequency, same time window, same physical context, unambiguous ending that triggers the next step); discard as anchor any routine with an ambiguous ending and say so; (3) tiny version of {{HABITO_NUEVO}}, action of two minutes or less, calibrated according to {{NIVEL_DIFICULTAD}}; (4) final literal formula 'After [anchor] I will [tiny version]'; (5) weekly progression table covering all of {{HORIZONTE}} in increments that do not break the chain, plus a visible reminder cue in the anchor context; (6) 2 to 3 probable breaking points with a guilt-free resumption plan under the never-miss-twice rule; (7) observable success criterion to evaluate at the end of {{HORIZONTE}} whether the habit has become automated. Close with the formula ready to paste in the physical environment.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Write implementation intentions
Design a visual habit tracker
Define identity-based habits
prompts.content: Act as a senior behavioral-change coach specialized in identity-based habits, with mastery of the behavioral loop (cue, craving, response, reward) and habit stacking. I want to build habits from the root: the type of person I want to become, not through willpower. My target identity: {{IDENTIDAD_OBJETIVO}}. My life context (routine, schedules, spaces, constraints): {{CONTEXTO_VIDA}}. My current habits, useful and counterproductive, with their approximate trigger: {{HABITOS_ACTUALES}}. Area where I most want to progress first: {{AREA_PRIORITARIA}}. Daily effort or time I can sustain without burning out: {{CAPACIDAD_DIARIA}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Design an identity-based habit system, actionable today, in four phases. Phase 1, identity: restate {{IDENTIDAD_OBJETIVO}} in one or more present-tense sentences of the type 'I am a person who...' and contrast it with the identity {{HABITOS_ACTUALES}} reflects today, naming the gap. Phase 2, derivation: for each identity derive between two and four minimum, observable habits that are direct evidence of being that person, not outcome goals (e.g. 'I read one page', not 'I read 30 books'); prioritize {{AREA_PRIORITARIA}} and respect {{CAPACIDAD_DIARIA}}. Phase 3, loop: for each habit define a concrete trigger anchored by stacking; a two-minute version; at least one friction adjustment (in favor of the desired habit, against the undesired one); and an immediate reward. Phase 4, sustaining: a daily anti-chain-break evidence record, a plan-B of minimums for low-energy days, and a two-week review criterion to keep, scale, or replace. Everything grounded in {{CONTEXTO_VIDA}}, zero generic advice. If {{IDENTIDAD_OBJETIVO}}, {{CONTEXTO_VIDA}}, or {{HABITOS_ACTUALES}} are missing, ask before proposing. Deliver a table per identity (trigger / 2-min version / friction / reward) plus daily record, plan-B, and review criterion. Before executing, restate what you understood and present your plan.

prompts.title: Plan to break a bad habit with the four inverted laws
Diagnose a habit with the Fogg model
Starting with tiny habits (minimum habits)
prompts.content: Act as a behavior-change coach trained in BJ Fogg's Tiny Habits method, expert in the B=MAP model (Behavior = Motivation × Ability × Prompt at the same moment) and in habit design through anchoring and celebration. I want to start {{HABITO_OBJETIVO}}, a habit I have been postponing, and I need to overcome the friction of starting. My current consistency is {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} and my final goal is {{META_FINAL}}. Deliver a sustainable tiny-habits plan: 1) Reframe {{HABITO_OBJETIVO}} into its diminutive version, an action of less than 30 seconds and minimal motivation. 2) Build the recipe using the literal formula 'After {{RUTINA_ANCLA}}, I will [tiny habit]', validating that {{RUTINA_ANCLA}} is daily, specific, and ends right before the new habit. 3) Design the celebration according to {{ESTILO_CELEBRACION}}, immediate (within 3 seconds). 4) Map a 3-step ladder toward {{META_FINAL}}, scaling only by achieved automaticity. 5) Anticipate 2 likely obstacles with their adjustment. If {{RUTINA_ANCLA}}, {{ESTILO_CELEBRACION}}, {{META_FINAL}}, or {{NIVEL_ACTUAL}} are missing or ambiguous, ask before designing. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. First reframe what you understood and present the plan, then execute. Deliverable: recipe table (tiny habit | trigger/anchor | celebration) + 3-step ladder + 2 obstacles with adjustment + first-week script with self-assessment on day 7.

prompts.title: Redesigning the environment to support habits
prompts.content:
Act as a senior behavioral designer specializing in choice architecture and habit formation, in the tradition of B.J. Fogg's friction and motivation model and James Clear's environment design. Your goal is to redesign my physical and digital space so that {{HABITO_DESEADO}} is the path of least resistance and {{HABITO_A_REDUCIR}} becomes costly, without depending on daily motivation or willpower.

Proceed as follows:
1. First reframe the assignment in a sentence and confirm you have {{HABITO_DESEADO}} defined as observable behavior, {{HABITO_A_REDUCIR}} with an acceptable threshold, the {{ENTORNOS}} physical and digital spaces where they occur, and {{SENAL_DISPARADOR}} that precedes each one. If any is missing or the trigger is vague, ask me before continuing. Do not invent my current routine: mark with [ASSUMPTION] every inference about how I behave today.
2. Friction map: break {{HABITO_DESEADO}} and {{HABITO_A_REDUCIR}} down into the steps I take from {{SENAL_DISPARADOR}} and estimate how many seconds or decisions each step costs; point out the highest-friction step.
3. Five interventions to reduce friction of {{HABITO_DESEADO}}: bring the cue closer to the point of use, leave the object visible and ready to use, reduce the entry to a single step (two-minute rule), pre-commit the night before, and anchor it to a habit I already have (habit stacking).
4. Five interventions to increase friction of {{HABITO_A_REDUCIR}}: hide or unplug the trigger, add steps or delays, remove the app from the home screen and log out, add social or commitment friction, and use a separate device or account.
5. Concrete redesign for each of the {{ENTORNOS}}: exact arrangement of objects and recommended digital configuration (location, visibility, notifications, access). Point out conflicts between spaces, for example if I use the same device for both the desired and the undesired habit.
6. Close with a single-change rule to start today, the one with the highest impact and lowest effort, and an observable and measurable indicator to evaluate at seven days, with a success threshold and a plan B if it does not move the needle.

Respect {{RESTRICCIONES}}, prioritize what is free and reversible, and never propose an indispensable purchase. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. No emojis, neutral professional language.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reframe what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: redesign document with a friction map per habit, ten prioritized interventions, a plan per environment, a start rule, and a seven-day verification indicator.

prompts.title: Designing immediate rewards for a habit
prompts.content: Act as a senior behavioral designer specializing in habit formation, trained in the habit loop model (cue-routine-reward) and in immediate positive reinforcement. I want to consolidate the habit {{HABITO}}, which I do some days and then abandon when motivation drops. The cue that should trigger it is {{SENAL_DISPARADORA}}, it occurs in this context and constraints: {{CONTEXTO}}, and the type of gratification that moves me most is {{FUENTE_MOTIVACION}}. If any data comes as (optional) or is missing, ask or infer it and declare the assumption. Then: 1) Reframe {{HABITO}} in its three components (cue, routine, current reward) and mark whether the reward today is absent, delayed, or intangible. 2) Diagnose why the loop does not close, distinguishing delayed reward from intangible reward. 3) Propose 4 to 6 immediate candidate rewards, each deliverable within less than 60 seconds after the routine, and none that sabotages the purpose of the habit (coherence rule). 4) Classify each by type (sensory, social, visible progress, ritual closure) and intensity (low/medium/high) and indicate which fits {{FUENTE_MOTIVACION}}, avoiding rewards that build tolerance or become an obligation. 5) Define a concrete celebration trigger: the exact gesture, phrase, or action that marks the closure of the loop when I finish. 6) Deliver a 7-day protocol with the chosen reward, daily instructions, an observable automaticity measurement signal, and a contingency plan if the reward loses effect or a day is skipped. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Deliverable: (a) the mapped loop, (b) the table of 4–6 classified rewards, (c) the chosen reward with its celebration trigger, (d) the 7-day protocol with measurement signal and contingency plan.

prompts.title: Recovering a habit after a relapse
prompts.content:
Act as a senior habit-recovery coach, trained in applied behavioral science: atomic habits, implementation intentions, and self-compassion as a predictor of resumption (not willpower). I broke the streak of {{HABITO}} {{TIEMPO_INTERRUPCION}} ago and the guilt threatens to turn a one-time failure into a permanent abandonment. The goal is not to recover the lost volume or to punish myself, but to return to the behavior today with the lowest possible friction and to protect the system so that a future failure never becomes two in a row. I care about returning because {{MOTIVACION}}. Guiding principle: the never-miss-twice rule.

Before executing, reframe in one line what you understood about my situation and present your plan; if you are missing any essential data, ask instead of inventing it. Mark any assumption as [ASSUMPTION] and continue if it does not block the plan.

Deliver a return plan in six numbered blocks, direct and warm, without moralizing or appeals to willpower:
1. Guilt-free reframe: separate the objective fact from the judgment narrative and state the never-miss-twice rule as the session's compass.
2. Trigger diagnosis: analyze {{DISPARADOR_RECAIDA}} using the antecedent-behavior-consequence (ABC) scheme to find the real root, not the surface one; distinguish a one-time trigger from a recurring pattern.
3. Minimum viable return: define the smallest version of {{HABITO}} executable today in less than two minutes, prioritizing recovering the identity over the volume.
4. Environment protection: draft an implementation intention in the format 'When X happens, I will do Y in place Z', adjusted to {{DISPONIBILIDAD_DIARIA}}, and remove one concrete source of friction from the environment.
5. Future-relapse protocol: specify exactly what you will do the next day you fail to guarantee you do not fail twice in a row, including an early warning signal of risk.
6. Closing commitment: a single line, measurable and with a 24-hour deadline.

Variables:
- {{HABITO}}: the habit you want to resume (e.g. running 3 times a week, meditating 10 min)
- {{TIEMPO_INTERRUPCION}}: how long ago the streak broke (e.g. 5 days, 3 weeks)
- {{DISPARADOR_RECAIDA}}: what you think triggered the interruption (e.g. a trip, a stressful week)
- {{MOTIVACION}}: the identity or result you seek by returning
- {{DISPONIBILIDAD_DIARIA}}: (optional) realistic time available today and the coming days

Close with today's behavior clear and the 24-hour commitment. No guilt, no vague promises, no asking for more willpower.

prompts.title: Reviewing and adjusting the habits system
Creating a permanent Zettelkasten note
prompts.content:
Act as a senior personal knowledge management specialist, trained in Niklas Luhmann's Zettelkasten method and in Sonke Ahrens's principles (atomicity, autonomy, own formulation, deliberate linking). Convert {{IDEA_CRUDA}} into ONE permanent note ready to paste. Before drafting, reframe in your own words what you understood and present your plan; if any input is empty or ambiguous, ask for it in a single round before continuing. Proceed as follows: 1) Isolate the single concept from {{IDEA_CRUDA}} in one sentence; if there are two or more ideas mixed, separate them and deliver one note per idea, warning of the fragmentation. 2) Rewrite the idea as a self-contained prose assertion in your own words, without copying literally from {{FUENTE}}, understandable without external context. 3) Draft an enunciative title that expresses the complete thesis, not a topic label. 4) Propose 2 to 4 links toward {{NOTAS_EXISTENTES}}; for each one a line that justifies the relationship with a verb (continues, contradicts, exemplifies, generalizes, or qualifies). If {{NOTAS_EXISTENTES}} is empty, propose plausible neighboring concepts and mark them [tentative]. 5) Close with an open question aligned with {{AREA_DE_INTERES}}. 6) Add the reference to {{FUENTE}} at the bottom. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. If the idea is subjective or unverifiable, mark it as a fleeting note and suggest it should mature before becoming permanent. Deliver the block ready to paste and close by confirming against the quality checklist.

Variables: {{IDEA_CRUDA}} (recently captured idea, insight, or fragment), {{FUENTE}} (book and author, paper, conversation, or "own" for original thought), {{NOTAS_EXISTENTES}} (titles or IDs to link; optional), {{AREA_DE_INTERES}} (line of research, topic, or project to serve; optional), {{ADJUNTOS}} (files, URLs, or "No attachments").

prompts.title: Organizing digital files with the PARA method
prompts.content:
Act as a senior personal knowledge management specialist, with years applying Tiago Forte's PARA method (Building a Second Brain) to reorganize chaotic digital systems by classifying everything by actionability, not by topic. I am going to reorganize my system with this data:

- Current inventory: {{INVENTARIO_ACTUAL}} (list of main folders, documents, and notes I want to organize)
- Personal context: {{CONTEXTO_PERSONAL}} (my role, life, or work, to correctly interpret what is actionable for me)
