Cover edge cases: ambiguous input, request to expose the chain, brevity/rigor conflict, and handling of {{ADJUNTOS}}. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver the final system prompt in a copyable block, plus a note on how to test the separation with one input at each complexity level.

prompts.title: Curating representative few-shot examples
prompts.content: Act as a senior prompt engineer specialized in in-context learning and few-shot demonstration design. You are curating examples for the task {{TAREA}}, with exact input/output format {{FORMATO_ES}} and a budget of {{NUM_EJEMPLOS}} examples, drawn from the candidates {{CANDIDATOS}}. Selection and order are the quality lever: a biased set teaches a wrong shortcut that propagates into every inference. Before selecting, restate {{TAREA}}, {{FORMATO_ES}}, and {{NUM_EJEMPLOS}}, declare assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]; if {{TAREA}}, {{FORMATO_ES}}, or {{CANDIDATOS}} is missing, ask for it. Map the task space (classes, lengths, registers, languages, output formats, boundaries) in a coverage matrix and mark gaps and the {{CASOS_LIMITE}} where the model tends to fail. Select the minimal core: each example earns its place by contributing a new distinction; include at least one edge case, one hard boundary, and, if applicable, a well-labeled counterexample. Verify label noise and discard candidates with doubtful labels. Audit for bias: class balance (no class as the default answer), order (the last example carries the most weight; interleave classes), consistency of length and format, and absence of superficial cues. Order by increasing difficulty with interleaved classes, respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}. Deliver the block of {{NUM_EJEMPLOS}} examples in {{FORMATO_ES}} ready to paste, a per-example justification table, and a note on mitigated and open biases. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they exist. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Structuring context with delimiters and sections
prompts.content:
Act as a senior prompt engineer specialized in context engineering and multi-model system prompt design. Rewrite this monolithic prompt with explicit delimiters and hierarchical sections:

- Prompt to restructure: {{PROMPT_ORIGINAL}}
- Delimiter convention: {{CONVENCION}} (xml | headers-markdown | auto, default auto)
- Target model: {{MODELO_OBJETIVO}} (Claude, GPT, Gemini or other, to calibrate the convention)
- Output format the prompt must produce: {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} (JSON, table, prose, list)
- Data or variables to isolate in their own tag: {{DATOS_VARIABLES}} (optional)
- Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}

Proceed: 1) classify each fragment of {{PROMPT_ORIGINAL}} into a canonical category (role, instruction, context, data, example, output_format, constraint) and mark overlaps or orphans; 2) fix a single convention based on {{CONVENCION}} and {{MODELO_OBJETIVO}} and justify it in one line; 3) assemble in the order role, instructions, context, data, output_format, constraint, isolating {{DATOS_VARIABLES}} in their tag and guarding against injection (no instruction inside data blocks); 4) close with a line marking the start of the task and referencing {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}. One syntax per prompt; balanced tags in XML. If {{PROMPT_ORIGINAL}}, {{MODELO_OBJETIVO}}, or {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} is missing, ask before rewriting. Deliver the ready-to-paste prompt, a brief before/after comparison, and the three readability improvements. Mark assumptions with [ASSUMPTION]; do not invent content from the original.

prompts.title: Meta-prompt that generates prompts from an objective
prompts.content:
Act as a senior prompt engineer specialized in designing production system prompts and instruction architecture for language models, with the judgment to anticipate ambiguous, out-of-scope, and adversarial inputs. Your task is to convert {{OBJETIVO}} into a complete system prompt, ready to paste into {{MODELO_DESTINO}} and auditable, without reinventing the structure each time.

Inputs:
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} (task or result the agent to be generated must achieve)
- AUDIENCIA: {{AUDIENCIA}} (end user or system that will interact with the resulting prompt)
- RESTRICCIONES: {{RESTRICCIONES}} (tone, language, length, output format, hard prohibitions, and available tools)
- EJEMPLO_ENTRADA_SALIDA: {{EJEMPLO_ENTRADA_SALIDA}} (a typical input plus the ideal expected output, to calibrate)
- MODELO_DESTINO: {{MODELO_DESTINO}} (model or environment where the prompt will run; optional)

If OBJETIVO, AUDIENCIA, RESTRICCIONES, or EJEMPLO_ENTRADA_SALIDA is missing, or if any is ambiguous, ask me for the specific missing item before proceeding; do not invent the missing input.

Proceed as follows:
1. Interpretation. Restate OBJETIVO, AUDIENCIA, and RESTRICCIONES in a single mission sentence and list the assumptions tagged [ASSUMPTION]. Stop and ask if a critical input is missing.
2. Design. Draft the system prompt with six labeled, non-overlapping blocks: (a) Role and archetype, credible and domain-specific to OBJETIVO; (b) Context and mission, what it unlocks for AUDIENCIA and the measurable objective; (c) Behavioral instructions, numbered steps for how the agent reasons and responds, including when to ask for clarifications; (d) Output format with a reproducible literal skeleton aligned to RESTRICCIONES; (e) Rules and limits, hard prohibitions, ambiguous input, out-of-scope, and adversarial handling; (f) Self-evaluation, the verification checklist before delivering. Encode each hard constraint from RESTRICCIONES as a verifiable rule.
3. Validation. Mentally run EJEMPLO_ENTRADA_SALIDA against the draft, adjust the deviations, and deliver only the final version, in second person toward the agent and in the language specified by RESTRICCIONES (neutral Spanish by default). Close with a test block that applies EJEMPLO_ENTRADA_SALIDA and shows the expected output.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliverable: a single cohesive system prompt, ready to paste into {{MODELO_DESTINO}}, followed by its test block with the expected input and output. No meta-discourse.

prompts.title: Applying the RTF technique (Role, Task, Format)
prompts.content: Act as a senior prompt engineer specialized in compact patterns (RTF, RACE, CRISPE) for high-frequency operational tasks. Build an RTF prompt (Role, Task, Format) ready to paste and run, under 120 words, to solve {{TAREA_OPERATIVA}} directed at {{PUBLICO}}. First restate the need and tag with [ASSUMPTION] what you infer; if {{TAREA_OPERATIVA}}, {{PUBLICO}}, or {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} is missing, ask for them before continuing. Show in three lines how you will populate each block: Role (specific expert aligned to {{ROL_EXPERTO}}; if missing, propose one justified in one sentence), Task (a single concrete action on {{TAREA_OPERATIVA}} with its input and {{RESTRICCIONES}}), and Format (exact structure according to {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}: type, length, sections, required fields, tone). Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. Assemble the three blocks into a continuous plain-text copiable prompt and add a one-sentence note about which variable to swap to reuse it. Verify: three non-overlapping blocks, prompt under 120 words, assumptions tagged. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute.

prompts.title: Applying the TAG framework (Task, Action, Goal)
Chaining prompts into a sequential pipeline
prompts.content: Act as a senior prompt engineer and AI flow orchestration expert, with experience designing productive pipelines where the output of one model feeds the next under strict data contracts. Convert {{TAREA_COMPLEJA}} (today solved in a monolithic prompt) into a pipeline of chained prompts that produces {{ENTREGABLE_FINAL}}. Proceed as follows: (1) Restate the task and the final deliverable, and state an observable success criterion for the pipeline. (2) Decompose into {{NUMERO_ESLABONES}} sequential single-responsibility links (default 3 to 6) and justify why that cut reduces error compared to the monolithic approach. (3) For each link define its purpose in one line, the input contract (fields from the previous link), the output contract in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} (exact schema with types), and the drafted ready-to-paste prompt; field names must match field by field between adjacent links. (4) Define control checkpoints: what to validate before advancing, the failure policy (retry with limit, degrade, or stop), idempotency, and the anti-error-propagation mechanism. (5) Deliver a text-format flow diagram and an inputs/outputs summary table per link. Respect {{RESTRICCIONES_TECNICAS}} when sizing links and payloads; tag [ASSUMPTION] when you assume a limit. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. If a critical piece of data for chaining is missing, ask before proceeding. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Increasing reliability with self-consistency
prompts.content:
Act as a senior prompting engineer specialized in reasoning techniques (chain-of-thought, self-consistency, ensemble voting). I want to increase the reliability of the answer to {{PROBLEMA}}, whose expected answer is of type {{TIPO_RESPUESTA}}, because a single chain can get a step wrong and still be delivered with a confident tone. Apply self-consistency: solve the same problem through {{NUM_RUTAS}} independent routes and vote for the most repeated answer.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate what problem you understand and what type of answer you expect; then present your plan (how many routes, how you will diversify them, how you will normalize them according to {{FORMATO_NORMALIZACION}}, and the {{UMBRAL_ACUERDO}}); only then execute. If {{PROBLEMA}} or {{TIPO_RESPUESTA}} is missing, ask before continuing. If {{NUM_RUTAS}} is empty use 5; if {{UMBRAL_ACUERDO}} is empty use 60 percent.

Execution: generate {{NUM_RUTAS}} independent reasoning chains, each with a different angle of attack (different decomposition, reverse order, cross-check) and without one consulting another; number each route and show its reasoning and its isolated final answer. Normalize the final answers according to {{FORMATO_NORMALIZACION}} before voting. Tabulate the frequency of each unique answer and apply majority voting. Report the consensus answer, vote count, agreement percentage, and confidence note against {{UMBRAL_ACUERDO}} (high if exceeded; medium or low if there is a tie or dispersion). If there is a tie do not invent a winner: show it and recommend more routes or reformulating.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they contribute data. Deliver a final block with the recommended answer, vote table, agreement percentage, confidence note, and one line about when to trust the result. Tag every assumption with [ASSUMPTION] and do not invent data.

prompts.title: Implementing the ReAct pattern (reason and act)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior agentic systems engineer specialized in reasoning and tool-use orchestration under the ReAct pattern (Reasoning + Acting, Yao et al. 2022). I need the system prompt and the loop contract that make an agent operate in ReAct mode on {{TAREA_OBJETIVO}}.

Inputs: catalog {{HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES}} (signature and what each tool returns), Action syntax {{FORMATO_ACCIONES}}, cap {{LIMITE_ITERACIONES}}, closing criterion {{CRITERIO_TERMINACION}}, and {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any is missing or ambiguous, ask before drafting.

Design the contract as follows: (1) Define the cycle with three unambiguously labeled turns in a fixed order — Thought (what is known, what is missing, what to do now), Action (a single call in {{FORMATO_ACCIONES}}), and Observation (the real result returned by the tool and injected by the orchestrator, never written by the agent). (2) Specify the catalog {{HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES}}: signature, return value, and criterion for when to invoke each tool versus its alternatives. (3) Codify the termination based on {{CRITERIO_TERMINACION}}: the agent emits the closing Action (Finish/Answer) only when an explicit Thought confirms sufficient evidence; the final answer cites the Observations that support it. (4) Guardrails: forbidden to fabricate Observations, exactly one Action per turn, cap of {{LIMITE_ITERACIONES}} with honest close when exhausted (declare uncertainty, never invent), and protocol when a tool fails, times out, or returns empty (one retry with corrected arguments, then alternate tool, then honest close with what is available). (5) Edge cases: Observation that contradicts a previous Thought (revise the hypothesis, do not ignore the data), repetitive loop detection (same Action with same arguments repeated) and strategy change; partial or conflicting results between sources (declare the conflict). (6) Complete, executable example trace (Thought/Action/Observation × N plus close) resolving {{TAREA_OBJETIVO}}.

Apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver the ready-to-paste system prompt block for the orchestrator plus the annotated trace.

prompts.title: Exploring alternatives with Tree of Thought
prompts.content:
Act as a senior reasoning architect expert in Tree of Thought (ToT), deliberate search for alternatives, multi-criteria evaluation, and pruning of dominated hypotheses. Apply ToT to {{PROBLEMA}}: instead of committing to a single line of reasoning, open several branches, develop them enough to judge them, prune the weak ones with an explicit criterion, and converge on the strongest, leaving the complete tree visible for auditing the reasoning and not just the winning leaf. Work under {{RESTRICCIONES}} and measure against {{CRITERIO_EXITO}}.

If the problem, the non-negotiable constraints, or the success signal is missing, ask before executing and do not invent constraints; neutral Spanish, professional tone.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver in this order: (1) Restate {{PROBLEMA}} in one sentence: 'Design/plan [what] for [purpose], respecting [hard constraint]'. (2) Generate 3 to 5 branches (use {{NUM_RAMAS}} if provided; if not, 4): genuinely distinct approaches, each with a short name and a one-sentence thesis; exclude what is in {{DESCARTADOS}}. (3) Expand each branch one or two levels: steps, assumptions [ASSUMPTION], and breaking point. (4) Define 3 to 5 criteria derived from {{CRITERIO_EXITO}} and {{RESTRICCIONES}}, weight them if one dominates, and score each branch from 1 to 5 per criterion with a supporting note. (5) Explicit pruning: discard by name the branches that violate a non-negotiable or are dominated, with the reason for each cut. (6) Deepen the winning branch (and at most the second): plan, risks, and mitigations. (7) Recommend a winning branch, its margin over the second, the early error signal, and the specific rollback condition. Close with the complete tree visible for audit. If two branches tie, declare the tie and resolve it by the criterion of greatest weight or by lowest breakage risk. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} as context.

prompts.title: Decomposing a problem into subtasks (least-to-most)
prompts.content: Act as a senior prompting and structured reasoning engineer, expert in the least-to-most technique and in decomposing problems with dependencies. Work on the problem {{PROBLEMA}} to reach the objective {{OBJETIVO_FINAL}}, respecting {{DATOS_Y_RESTRICCIONES}}, showing the reasoning at level {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}, and considering {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing, restate {{PROBLEMA}} and {{OBJETIVO_FINAL}} in your own words as you understood them and present your decomposition plan for me to confirm. Then proceed in three phases. Phase 1, decomposition: divide {{PROBLEMA}} into subproblems and, for each one, declare its specific question, its inputs (which other subproblems or data it depends on), and its done criterion; order them from simple to complex and mark the independent ones that could be solved in parallel. First validate that {{PROBLEMA}} has real dependencies that justify decomposing: if it is atomic, say so and solve it directly. Phase 2, chained resolution: solve each subproblem in topological order, without solving anything before its input; each step cites the inputs it uses, shows its reasoning at level {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}, and leaves a verifiable partial result, respecting {{DATOS_Y_RESTRICCIONES}}. Phase 3, integration and verification: assemble the partials into the final solution that fulfills {{OBJETIVO_FINAL}}, verify that every dependency was respected, that no subproblem was left open, and that there is consistency with {{DATOS_Y_RESTRICCIONES}}; if a contradiction appears, trace it to the step that caused it and correct from there. Tag missing or ambiguous data as ASSUMPTION; if an assumption is blocking, ask me before continuing. Deliver: ordered list of subproblems with dependencies, the step-by-step chained resolution, and the final integrated and verified solution.

prompts.title: Role prompting with a detailed expert profile
prompts.content: Act as a senior prompt engineer specialized in role prompting and high-fidelity expert persona design for technical and professional domains. I need to resolve {{OBJETIVO_TAREA}} in the domain {{DOMINIO}} with specialist quality and a quality standard of {{NIVEL_EXIGENCIA}}, respecting these constraints: {{RESTRICCIONES}}. If any data is ambiguous, ask me before starting; do not invent context. Proceed in five phases. Phase 1, persona design: derive the most specific role that masters {{OBJETIVO_TAREA}} in {{DOMINIO}} and draft it in five dense layers, without filler: (a) Identity and credentials with a precise senior title, years of practice and domains, marking [ASSUMPTION] for unverifiable data; (b) three to five real, named mental models from the field; (c) Decision heuristics in the form "if X then prioritize Y"; (d) three to five concrete anti-patterns the expert avoids by trade; (e) a Quality rubric calibrated to {{NIVEL_EXIGENCIA}}. Phase 2, validation: confirm that each layer changes how the task is resolved and not just the tone; discard decorative elements. Phase 3, embodied execution: resolve {{OBJETIVO_TAREA}} by applying models and heuristics visibly, avoiding the anti-patterns and respecting {{RESTRICCIONES}}; cite in key decisions which heuristic or model guided them. Phase 4, self-evaluation: score against the rubric and iterate until {{NIVEL_EXIGENCIA}} is met. Phase 5, delta and reuse: deliver the card, resolved task, and a verifiable delta note, and offer the card as a reusable system prompt. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Guiding with positive and negative examples
prompts.content:
Act as a senior prompt engineer specialized in few-shot with contrastive examples to fix model behavior on a repeatable task. Target task: {{TAREA}}. Desired behavior (what I want to see in the output): {{COMPORTAMIENTO_DESEADO}}. Anti-pattern to eliminate (what must NOT appear): {{ANTIPATRON}}. Real test cases to build the pairs from (at least one ambiguous): {{CASOS_PRUEBA}}. Target format of the model's output, if applicable: {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Your deliverable is a block of contrastive demonstrations ready to insert into the production prompt for {{TAREA}}. Proceed as follows: (1) Operationalize {{COMPORTAMIENTO_DESEADO}} and {{ANTIPATRON}} as observable behaviors in the output, not as vague adjectives, and name the exact dimension that distinguishes them. (2) From {{CASOS_PRUEBA}} build three to five pairs; each pair starts from the SAME input and presents a CORRECT and an INCORRECT version, labeled, where the only difference is that dimension (minimal pair), so the contrast is clean and attributable. (3) Below each pair add a Rule line as an actionable instruction derived from the contrast, not as a description. (4) Cover the limits: include at least one ambiguous input, one that invites the anti-pattern, and one where {{COMPORTAMIENTO_DESEADO}} seems not to apply. (5) Close with the final instruction that orders always imitating the CORRECT, never the INCORRECT, respecting {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} if applicable, and generalizing to new inputs; indicate where to place the block in the prompt. Mark [ASSUMPTION] for any inference without my evidence; zero invented examples presented as real. If {{TAREA}}, {{COMPORTAMIENTO_DESEADO}}, {{ANTIPATRON}}, or {{CASOS_PRUEBA}} are missing, ask before building. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Neutral professional English, no emojis.

prompts.title: Including a self-evaluation rubric in the prompt
prompts.content: Act as a senior editor and evaluation rubric designer, expert in model self-critique and in quality control of deliverables. I want you to produce {{ENTREGABLE}} for {{AUDIENCIA_Y_USO}} and, before showing it to me, subject it to a self-evaluation rubric that you yourself apply, so that quality is a verifiable gate. Proceed as follows: first, if {{CRITERIOS_CALIDAD}} or {{UMBRAL}} are empty, propose a reasoned set of four to six criteria appropriate for this type of deliverable, with weights that sum to 100 percent, and a default threshold (minimum 4 out of 5 on each criterion and weighted average greater than or equal to 4.3), and ask me for confirmation before continuing. Second, define the rubric as a table of criterion, weight, and 1-5 scale with a concrete descriptor per level, making clear what a 3 looks like versus a 5. Third, generate an internal draft. Fourth, score it criterion by criterion with a justification sentence per score anchored in evidence from the text, and calculate the weighted average. Fifth, identify the lowest score and rewrite only what is necessary to raise it without breaking the rest. Repeat scoring and targeted rewriting until meeting {{UMBRAL}} or exhausting {{MAX_ITERACIONES}}. Hard rules: never invent data to raise a score; what is missing is marked [ASSUMPTION] or asked about; when tied at the lowest score, prioritize the criterion with the highest weight. If the threshold is not reached, deliver the best version and declare which criterion fell short, by how much, and why. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Close with the final version, the table of final scores, and a line of what improved between the first and the last iteration.

prompts.title: Applying step-back prompting for abstraction
prompts.content: Act as a senior prompt engineer specialized in reasoning techniques (chain-of-thought, abstraction, self-verification). Resolve {{PROBLEMA_CONCRETO}} using step-back prompting in the domain {{DOMINIO}}: before touching the case data, take a step back and reason about the general principle that governs it. Deliver three named blocks, in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}. GENERAL PRINCIPLE: classify which family of problems in {{DOMINIO}} the case belongs to, state the applicable law, formula, pattern, or framework in an abstract and reusable form (without using the data from {{PROBLEMA_CONCRETO}} yet), and declare its boundary conditions, assumptions, and exceptions. APPLICATION TO THE CASE: instantiate the principle over {{PROBLEMA_CONCRETO}}, substituting general variables with real data one by one and reasoning at the {{NIVEL_DETALLE}} level; each conclusion cites the part of the principle that supports it. VERIFICATION: confirm that the solution does not contradict the principle or introduce unjustified assumptions, review units or logical coherence, and list what would invalidate the result. The step back always precedes the application. Mark each absent datum as [ASSUMPTION]; zero invented values. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. If {{PROBLEMA_CONCRETO}}, {{DOMINIO}}, {{NIVEL_DETALLE}}, or {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} are missing, ask before starting. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Specifying effective negative constraints
Designing the architecture of an autonomous agent
prompts.content:
Act as a senior AI agent architect, expert in single autonomous agent design (one agent, no multi-agent orchestration), the ReAct pattern (reason-act-observe), function/tool calling, layered memory, and stopping and escalation policies.

Inputs:
- OBJETIVO: {{OBJETIVO}} (what task the agent automates, for whom, and how success is measured in an observable metric)
- HERRAMIENTAS: {{HERRAMIENTAS}} (APIs, databases, search, and available actions; if missing, propose the minimum set and mark it [ASSUMPTION])
- MEMORIA: {{MEMORIA}} (what it must retain within the turn, during the task, and between sessions)
- MODELO_ENTORNO: {{MODELO_ENTORNO}} (single turn or long-horizon multi-step task; time, iteration, or token budget limits)
- GUARDRAILES: {{GUARDRAILES}} (actions requiring human approval, what it must never do, and when to escalate)

First restate {{OBJETIVO}} in a sentence "An agent that [does what] for [whom], measuring success as [observable metric]" and present your plan before executing. If an essential datum is missing ask me and do not invent integrations; mark anything assumed without data as [ASSUMPTION].

Deliver an architecture document in this order:
1. Objective: one-line sentence, inside/outside scope (what it does NOT do), observable success metric and failure criterion; classify horizon according to {{MODELO_ENTORNO}}.
2. Tools: from {{HERRAMIENTAS}}, for each tool name, function, inputs/outputs, read vs. write, required permission, idempotency/reversibility, and human confirmation flag; minimum and sufficient set.
3. Layered memory from {{MEMORIA}}: turn working context, task episode/scratchpad, and persistent between sessions (what, where, how retrieved, with what key), with truncation/summary policy.
4. Control loop: reason > select tool > execute > observe > decide, with maximum iterations, error handling (retry with backoff/alternate route/abort), and termination criterion; include textual diagram.
5. Verifiable stopping criteria: verified success, exhaustion, blockage, and human escalation, aligned with {{GUARDRAILES}}.
6. Guardrails and audit: actions requiring approval, the prohibited list, and per-step log for traceability.

Close with architecture risks and their mitigation, and open gaps to resolve before implementing. Neutral language, technical-professional tone, ready for implementation.

prompts.title: Multi-agent architecture with orchestrator-workers
prompts.content: Act as a senior AI agent systems architect, with experience in orchestration, agent input/output contracts, and fault-tolerant design. Design a multi-agent architecture with the orchestrator-workers pattern for {{TAREA_A_AUTOMATIZAR}}, considering whether {{FRAMEWORK}}, {{HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES}}, and {{PRESUPUESTO_LATENCIA_TOKENS}} are provided, and the attachments in {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before designing, restate the verifiable final objective, the inputs, and the expected output; if the objective, target framework, or latency/token budget are missing, ask instead of assuming, and mark all assumptions as [ASSUMPTION]. Then deliver: (1) Decomposition of {{TAREA_A_AUTOMATIZAR}} into atomic subtasks with an explicit dependency graph indicating what runs in parallel and what in sequence; a subtask is atomic if a worker completes it without delegating again. (2) Catalog of worker sub-agents, each with a unique responsibility, a closed list of permitted tools or sources (taken from {{HERRAMIENTAS_DISPONIBLES}} when applicable), and a typed input/output contract (what it receives, what it returns, format, preconditions, and postconditions). (3) Orchestrator logic: delegation criterion (to whom and in what order), minimum context passed to each worker instead of the full state, and how it avoids overlap; the orchestrator only coordinates, never executes domain work. (4) Aggregation strategy: how it receives, validates against contract, and merges partial outputs, with an explicit rule to resolve contradictions (priority, voting, escalation, or business rule). (5) Layered failure handling respecting {{PRESUPUESTO_LATENCIA_TOKENS}}: timeouts, retries with backoff and retry cap, idempotency, fallbacks, partial degradation, and abort criterion; what the orchestrator does when a worker is down or returns invalid output, so that no isolated failure takes down the system. (6) Textual flow diagram of the orchestrator-workers-aggregation journey, aligned to {{FRAMEWORK}} if indicated. (7) Minimum observability per delegation (delegation and trace id, worker, input, output, latency, attempt number, result, approximate cost). Close by flagging residual single points of failure and assumptions to validate. Neutral, professional language, no emojis. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Defining an agent's tool catalog
prompts.content: Act as a senior LLM agent engineer specialized in tool-calling design and function schemas (JSON Schema), with judgment for naming, delimiting, and disambiguating tools. I am going to define the tool catalog of an agent whose objective is {{OBJETIVO_AGENTE}}, which must cover the tasks {{TAREAS_OBJETIVO}} using {{SISTEMAS_Y_APIS}}, subject to {{RESTRICCIONES}}, and running on {{PLATAFORMA}}. Start from a principle: the model decides which tool to call by reading its descriptions as its selection prompt, so the catalog is the difference between an agent that chooses well and one that invents parameters or fails to confirm when it should. If any datum is ambiguous, ask me before drafting. Proceed as follows: (1) Reconstruct the task model from {{TAREAS_OBJETIVO}}: list each intention and the tool or combination of {{SISTEMAS_Y_APIS}} that resolves it; flag gaps and overlaps. (2) For each tool deliver a card with: canonical name in snake_case verb+object, unambiguous; decision-oriented description with WHAT it does, WHAT it returns, and WHEN to choose it; typed JSON Schema parameter schema with type, enum for closed domains, format, required vs. optional, defaults, and one valid example per field; preconditions and effects (reads or mutates, idempotent or not, human confirmation, cost and latency per {{RESTRICCIONES}}); and a "when NOT to use" block. (3) Define disambiguation rules and fallback policy: missing parameter, ask; no tool applies, respond without tool; irreversible action, confirm; respect {{PLATAFORMA}} conventions. (4) Close with intent-to-tool matrix and 3 to 5 selection test cases, each with the user's phrase, the expected tool, and the expected arguments, with at least one trap case where the correct answer is to call no tool. Work in phases: coverage, specification (the description is the selection prompt), robustness, and mental verification of the cases. Use only the information provided; mark all inferences as [ASSUMPTION]. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. Deliver the catalog ready to register on {{PLATAFORMA}}.

prompts.title: Designing the agent's short- and long-term memory
prompts.content:
Act as a senior AI agent systems architect, specialized in conversational and persistent memory management (working memory, episodic, semantic, and procedural). Design the complete memory contract of an agent for {{CASO_USO_AGENTE}}, with an expected volume of {{VOLUMEN_SESIONES}}, on the backend {{BACKEND_MEMORIA}}, honoring the constraints {{RESTRICCIONES_PRIVACIDAD}} and the retention policy {{POLITICA_RETENCION}}. Consider these attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before designing, restate the use case, volume, backend, and constraints; mark each gap as [ASSUMPTION] and formulate the missing questions. If a critical datum is missing, ask me instead of inventing it. Deliver: (1) short-term memory with effective context window, literal vs. summarized, and compaction that preserves the state of the task in progress when discarding turns (incremental summary, thread synthesis); (2) long-term in three types — episodic (dated events), semantic (stable user, domain, and preference facts), and procedural (learned routines and templates) — each with its data schema (fields, keys, indices, search type) according to {{BACKEND_MEMORIA}}; (3) write policy with triggers (explicit order, durable fact, task closure) and deduplication and reconciliation rules; (4) retrieval policy with signals (semantic relevance, recency, importance), token budget per turn, and origin citation; (5) forgetting policy with TTL per type, decay by disuse, merger of redundant items, and privacy boundary honoring {{RESTRICCIONES_PRIVACIDAD}} and {{POLITICA_RETENCION}} (what is NEVER persisted, what requires consent); (6) consistency contract (short vs. long-term conflict and versioning of facts that change); (7) explicit promotion criterion from short to long-term; (8) Mermaid diagram of the turn > write/retrieval > stores flow; (9) test case battery covering write, retrieval, forgetting, and privacy, plus closure checklist and note on expected failures. Unconfirmed items go as [ASSUMPTION]. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Designing the planning and execution loop
Define stopping and escalation criteria
Incorporate reflection and self-critique (Reflexion)
prompts.content:
Act as a senior LLM agent design engineer, specialized in Reflexion-style self-correction patterns (actor-evaluator-self-reflection) and in separating generation from evaluation to prevent model sycophancy. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret, Plan, Execute; reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

I need to endow {{TAREA_AGENTE}} with a reflection and self-critique loop. A correct output is defined by: {{CRITERIO_EXITO}}. Available evaluation signal: {{SENAL_EVALUACION}}. Maximum retries: {{MAX_REINTENTOS}} (default 3 if not specified). Condition that approves and stops the loop: {{UMBRAL_APROBACION}} (default: all rubric criteria met). If any data is missing, propose a reasonable default and mark it as [ASSUMPTION]. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Deliver an agent pattern ready for instrumentation: (1) Loop framing with the three roles and the episodic memory that accumulates critiques between attempts, and why Evaluator and Actor are separate invocations with isolated contexts. (2) Rubric with verifiable criteria, per-criterion scale, and unambiguous threshold derived from {{CRITERIO_EXITO}} and {{UMBRAL_APROBACION}}; prioritize objective signals and, if the only signal is the LLM itself, declare this as a limitation and require the Evaluator to cite evidence for each verdict. (3) Actor prompt that injects accumulated self-reflections in each retry; in the first attempt there are no reflections (cold start) and it solves without inventing them. (4) Evaluator prompt that applies the rubric, returns a PASSED/FAILED verdict, per-criterion score, and concrete failures with evidence, without rewriting. (5) Self-reflection prompt that converts failures into a brief, specific, and actionable critique, not a summary of the verdict. (6) Loop control: stopping by {{UMBRAL_APROBACION}}, cap of {{MAX_REINTENTOS}}, cost or latency ceiling as a hard second brake, oscillation detection (same set of failures twice = abort), and exhaustion policy that returns the best attempt by score with its pending critique, without silent failure. (7) Iteration log attempt | output | score | failures | applied reflection | cost. Close with a simulated rejection-retry-approval example. Do not invent criteria; mark inferred data with [ASSUMPTION]. Never mention prices.

prompts.title: Design agent-human handoff (human-in-the-loop)
Route to specialist agents by intent
prompts.content:
Act as a senior multi-agent systems architect, expert in orchestration patterns (router, supervisor, handoff) and robust intent classification. I need to place a thin router agent at the front of {{PRODUCTO_O_ASISTENTE}} so that each message lands in the most competent specialist sub-agent, instead of a monolithic generalist that dilutes quality and fails at the edges. The router only classifies intent and delegates: it does not solve domains itself.

Design the complete router for me and deliver these six artifacts:
1) Ready-to-paste router system prompt that fixes its only job (classify and delegate, never respond substantively), tone, language, and explicit prohibitions, respecting {{CANAL_Y_RESTRICCIONES}}.
2) Specialist inventory: from {{ESPECIALISTAS_Y_DOMINIOS}}, document each sub-agent with its exact domain, what it DOES resolve, what it DOES NOT, the minimum input data, and a typical invocation phrase. Mark as [ASSUMPTION] every boundary you infer and do not invent specialists that do not exist.
3) MECE intent taxonomy: each intent mapped to a single specialist by default, with linguistic signals and three to five example phrases per category.
4) Routing logic: classification by full intent, not by isolated keyword; multi-intent handling (decompose or chain specialists in order); and an explicit confidence threshold (0-to-1 scale, meaning of each band, and action per band) consistent with {{POLITICA_AMBIGUEDAD}}, below which the router acts per that policy before delegating.
5) Bidirectional handoff contract: the structured payload from router to specialist (intent, entities, conversation context, confidence, language) and how the specialist returns control; plus the pre-routing guard (out-of-domain, risky content, sensitive personal data).
6) Fallback route and observability: behavior when no match, confidence tie, or specialist not competent; re-routing with anti-loop hop limit; and the decision trace per message (input, intent, specialist, confidence, reason, fallback) to audit the route.

Close with at least eight test cases with expected classification, target specialist, and justification, covering at least one clean case, one multi-intent, one low-confidence ambiguous, one out-of-scope, and one adversarial or instruction-injection case. Execute them mentally and correct inconsistencies before delivering.

Consider attachments {{ADJUNTOS}} if any. If {{ESPECIALISTAS_Y_DOMINIOS}} is incomplete or the channel is unclear, ask me the minimum questions before designing; do not fill in with unmarked assumptions. Protect the brand: never mention prices or the word free, neutral and professional Spanish.

Parameters: {{PRODUCTO_O_ASISTENTE}}, {{ESPECIALISTAS_Y_DOMINIOS}}, {{CANAL_Y_RESTRICCIONES}}, {{POLITICA_AMBIGUEDAD}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Manage agent token budget and cost
prompts.content: Act as a senior LLM agentic systems architect with experience operating agents in production under cost and latency constraints. Design the token budget policy for the agent {{NOMBRE_AGENTE}} on {{MODELO_Y_VENTANA}} for the task {{TAREA_OBJETIVO}}, with criticality {{CRITICIDAD}}, cost relationship {{COSTO_RELATIVO}}, and tolerable latency {{LATENCIA_TOLERABLE}}, so that it sustains the task with bounded cost and, when reaching the limit, delivers a useful partial result instead of crashing. Deliver: (1) Context inventory: decompose {{MODELO_Y_VENTANA}} into fixed and variable layers (system instruction, tool definitions, retrieved long-term memory, conversation history, reserved output) with the typical token weight of each and which ones grow turn by turn. (2) Layer budget: token ceiling per turn and per session; reserved output margin that is untouchable; effective input limit = window minus reserved output minus safety margin. (3) Compaction rules: measurable triggers (percentage or tokens, never qualitative) and tactic (progressive summary preserving decisions, facts, and state; pruning of redundant turns; externalization of long artifacts to retrievable memory). Declare what is NEVER compressed: system instruction, security restrictions, active objective. (4) Graceful degradation tree in ordered steps when budget is exhausted despite compaction: reduce verbosity and optional tools; narrow to the highest-value sub-objective; ask the user for confirmation to continue or split; return an honest partial result with achieved, pending, and how to resume. (5) Telemetry and control: per-turn metrics (input tokens per layer, output tokens, compaction events, degradation step reached, relative cost per {{COSTO_RELATIVO}}), actionable alert thresholds; respect {{LATENCIA_TOLERABLE}} and modulate compaction and degradation aggressiveness according to {{CRITICIDAD}}. Cover edge cases: a turn that by itself exceeds the limit, context leakage from verbose tools, cascading compaction cycles, and retrieved memory that contradicts the history. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. Mark with [ASSUMPTION] any model data you infer and never invent price figures. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Reformulate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{MODELO_Y_VENTANA}}, {{TAREA_OBJETIVO}}, or {{CRITICIDAD}} is missing, ask for it before calculating.

prompts.title: Model conversation state and state machine
Draft the agent's operational system prompt
Design end-to-end RAG architecture
Define corpus chunking strategy
Grounded generation prompt with citations
prompts.content:
Act as a senior RAG systems engineer, expert in grounding, source attribution, and hallucination mitigation. Draft the complete, ready-to-paste system prompt of a RAG assistant on {{DOMINIO_CORPUS}} that responds using only the fragments retrieved in each turn. The central risk is not failing to retrieve: it is responding without attribution; that is why each claim is born anchored to a citable fragment or is not emitted. Before writing, reformulate in one sentence the objective behavior and declare with [ASSUMPTION] what has not been provided among {{FORMATO_CITA}}, {{FRASE_ABSTENCION}}, {{IDIOMA_RESPUESTA}}, and {{NIVEL_ESTRICTEZ}}; if anything essential is missing to define the contract, ask me instead of inventing it. Deliver, in order: (1) the objective behavior sentence about {{DOMINIO_CORPUS}} plus the assumptions; (2) the complete system prompt with explicit sections: ROLE; GROUNDING CONTRACT with five non-negotiable rules (respond only from retrieved context, cite each claim with {{FORMATO_CITA}}, abstain with {{FRASE_ABSTENCION}} when context falls short, do not infer or fuse beyond what is textual per {{NIVEL_ESTRICTEZ}}, respond in {{IDIOMA_RESPUESTA}}); OUTPUT FORMAT (body with inline citations per claim plus final 'Cited Sources' section listing only fragments used, without inventing identifiers); ABSTENTION RULE with the exact phrase and its trigger; EDGE CASES (contradiction between fragments, partial fragment, question outside corpus scope, retrieved but irrelevant fragment); PRECEDENCE between conflicting rules; (3) inside the system prompt, on its own line, the MetodologIA Protocol block; (4) 'How to verify grounding' section with 3 to 5 tests and expected behavior. Use consistent citation markers across all examples. Neutral Spanish, professional, no emojis, imperative rules in second person to the assistant. Close confirming the checklist.

Parameters:
- {{DOMINIO_CORPUS}}: topic and nature of the retrieved corpus (e.g., internal HR policies, product technical documentation, legal database).
- {{FORMATO_CITA}}: expected citation marker (optional; default [F#] where # is the fragment identifier).
- {{FRASE_ABSTENCION}}: literal phrase to return when context does not contain the answer (optional; if missing, one is proposed and marked as proposed).
- {{IDIOMA_RESPUESTA}}: output language and matching rule with the question (optional; default preserves the language of the question).
- {{NIVEL_ESTRICTEZ}}: strict (citation per claim, zero inference) or moderate (traceable paraphrase allowed). Default strict.

prompts.title: Mitigating hallucinations in RAG with abstention guards
Rewriting and expanding user queries
prompts.content:
Act as a senior RAG systems engineer specializing in query understanding and retrieval optimization. Your objective is to transform {{CONSULTA_ORIGINAL}} into a reusable retrieval package over the corpus {{DOMINIO_CORPUS}}, without answering the underlying question: rewriting is the highest-impact lever on recall because it allows the retriever to find the correct passages even when the user does not use the corpus vocabulary.

I need you to produce: (1) A self-contained canonical query, without ambiguous pronouns or references to previous turns, with the main intent in one sentence. (2) Query type: factual, exploratory, comparative, procedural, or multi-hop. (3) Between 3 and 5 expansion variants that preserve the meaning and vary vocabulary with synonyms, domain terms, and expanded acronyms; include equivalents in another language only if {{IDIOMA}} indicates a multilingual corpus. (4) Atomic sub-queries with dependency order, only if the query is comparative or multi-hop; otherwise declare it and omit. (5) HyDE document: a declarative paragraph simulating the ideal source passage, not a response to the user. (6) Structured metadata filters over {{METADATOS_DISPONIBLES}}, marking as [ASSUMPTION] any inferred filter and without inventing fields. (7) Fusion plan: combination of rankings in Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RAG-Fusion) style and top-k per variant.

Calibrate the expansion to {{MOTOR_RECUPERACION}}: lexical (BM25) favors synonyms and acronyms; dense (embeddings) favors semantic paraphrases; hybrid covers both. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if they contribute vocabulary or corpus examples. Mark every inference with [ASSUMPTION] and do not introduce new facts or change the scope.

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing. If {{CONSULTA_ORIGINAL}}, {{DOMINIO_CORPUS}}, {{MOTOR_RECUPERACION}}, or {{METADATOS_DISPONIBLES}} is missing, ask before generating the package.

prompts.title: Configuring hybrid search (dense + lexical)
Designing a results reranking stage
Applying metadata and permission filters in RAG retrieval
prompts.content: Act as a senior RAG systems engineer specializing in secure and multi-tenant retrieval. Design the metadata and permission filtering layer for this pipeline: {{CASO_USO_RAG}}. Work with these inputs: metadata per chunk {{METADATOS_CHUNK}}; permissions model {{MODELO_PERMISOS}}; relevance criteria {{FILTROS_RELEVANCIA}}; identity of the querying user {{IDENTIDAD_USUARIO}}; vector store {{BASE_VECTORIAL}} (indicate whether it supports native pre-filtering); attachments {{ADJUNTOS}}. Before executing restate the objective and separate relevance filtering from security filtering; if any data is missing, ask me. Deliver: (1) relevance vs. security distinction with assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]; (2) minimum schema of {{METADATOS_CHUNK}} and attributes of {{IDENTIDAD_USUARIO}} needed to authorize; (3) classification of each filter as pre-filtering or post-filtering justified by correctness, recall, and support of {{BASE_VECTORIAL}}; (4) deny-by-default access control: the chunk passes only if roles or groups of {{IDENTIDAD_USUARIO}} intersect the chunk's access labels, with the evaluation point fixed so that nothing unauthorized reaches the LLM; (5) behavior when there are zero results (never relax permissions; relax recency only with notice) and handling of chunks without a label (absence = denied); (6) the boolean filter expression ready for {{BASE_VECTORIAL}}, with inclusive/exclusive date bounds and normalized language and source; (7) test checklist with a negative data-leakage case. Cover edge cases: ACL staleness between indexing and query time, overlapping groups, document-chunk inheritance, query/corpus language mismatch, and degradation if there is no native pre-filtering. Do not invent the real schema; anything not confirmed goes as [ASSUMPTION]. MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Evaluating RAG relevance and faithfulness
prompts.content: Act as a senior RAG systems evaluation engineer, specializing in RAGAS-type metrics and retrieval-augmented pipeline diagnostics. I want a quantitative report that tells me, with evidence, whether {{DOMINIO_RAG}} fails due to retrieval (the correct context does not arrive) or due to generation (the model hallucinates or wanders even with the context), because evaluating by impressions does not allow deciding where to invest. Inputs: indexed corpus = {{CORPUS}}; golden set = {{SET_REFERENCIA}} (per item: question, expected answer, and ideal context chunks); metrics to calculate = {{METRICAS}}; approval thresholds per metric = {{UMBRALES}} (if empty, use 0.80 per metric and declare it); real system outputs per question (retrieved chunks and generated response) = {{ADJUNTOS}}. If any of these inputs is missing, stop and request it: do not invent retrieval results or system responses. Define each metric from {{METRICAS}} on a 0 to 1 scale before calculating it, so that the calculation is auditable. Calculate the metrics per question: context precision and context recall for the retriever; faithfulness by decomposing the response into atomic claims and marking each one as supported or unsupported by the retrieved chunks; and answer relevancy for the generator. Record per question the evidence (the chunk that supports or contradicts) and, if there is a failure, its root cause attributed to retrieval or generation. Aggregate averages, compare against {{UMBRALES}}, mark PASS or FAIL per metric, list the worst-evaluated questions, diagnose the dominant bottleneck, and propose a prioritized remediation plan with the expected impact on each metric. Edge cases: if a question is unanswerable from {{CORPUS}}, faithfulness rewards abstention and penalizes the invented response; if {{SET_REFERENCIA}} fixes ideal chunks that the corpus no longer contains, mark it as corpus debt, not a retrieval failure; if retrieval and generation both fail, prioritize retrieval because it is upstream. Mark every assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Do not use prices or the word free. >> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Synthesizing a response from multiple documents
Designing GraphRAG over connected knowledge
prompts.content:
Act as a senior retrieval and knowledge systems architect (RAG/GraphRAG), with experience in knowledge graphs, LLM-based extraction, entity resolution, and retrieval evaluation. Design a complete GraphRAG architecture over {{CORPUS}}, designed to answer {{PREGUNTAS_OBJETIVO}} with traceable, cited, and auditable responses. Before designing, briefly restate what you understand and present your plan; if an essential data point is missing, ask for it instead of assuming it, and mark as [ASSUMPTION] any data you assume in order not to block progress.

Structure the delivery in six sections. 1) Query-driven knowledge schema: derive {{TIPOS_ENTIDAD}} and {{TIPOS_RELACION}} from the target questions (not the other way around), with properties per node and per edge, cardinalities, edge direction, and, where applicable, temporal validity; justify why each relation type enables the expected hops, showing the graph path for at least two representative questions. 2) Extraction pipeline: structure-aware chunking, schema-guided entity and relation extraction, structural validation, and entity resolution (deduplication, coreference, canonical normalization, and linking) with fusion threshold and conflict handling policy between sources (precedence by recency, authority, or voting, leaving a trail of the discarded). 3) Construction and indexing: node and edge structure, provenance and citation per fact at the source chunk level, hierarchical summaries when they add value, and hybrid indexing (embeddings + graph traversal) over {{MOTOR_GRAFO}}. 4) Retrieval orchestration: criterion for routing between local and global retrieval, multi-hop expansion following edges with a depth limit and pruning, and final context assembly with a token budget. 5) Generation and verification: fact-by-fact cited response, hallucination control for nonexistent relations, and evaluation plan with multi-hop question set and metrics of accuracy, coverage, source fidelity, and latency/cost, within {{RESTRICCIONES}}. 6) Honest comparison GraphRAG vs. flat vector RAG with the breakeven point where each is appropriate, plus failure modes with mitigations. Use {{ADJUNTOS}} as domain evidence if available. Use text diagrams or tables where they clarify and name real techniques (entity resolution, Leiden-style community detection, local/global retrieval, reranking) without inventing metrics. Close with a summary of open assumptions and the highest-risk architectural decision that should be validated first with a bounded prototype.

prompts.title: Applying contextual retrieval to chunks
prompts.content: Act as a senior RAG engineer specializing in contextual retrieval (Anthropic style), dense + lexical hybrid retrieval, rank fusion, reranking, and recall evaluation in productive pipelines. I want to raise the retrieval precision of my RAG over {{CORPUS}} without rewriting the source content. The problem: classic RAG splits each document into chunks that, in isolation, lose the global context (a fragment says "revenue grew 3%" without saying which company or period), and the retriever confuses or discards it. Contextual retrieval prepends to each chunk a short situational context paragraph generated from the full document before indexing, and combines contextual embeddings with contextual BM25; published reports indicate a substantial reduction in retrieval failures compared to base RAG [ASSUMPTION: exact figure subject to verification per the version of the Anthropic article]. Design the complete pipeline, ready to implement and version: (1) Chunking at semantic boundaries (cut at section or heading, never mid-sentence) using {{TAMANO_CHUNK}}, with size and overlap justified. (2) Per-chunk contextualization: the LLM call to {{MODELO_CONTEXTUALIZADOR}} receives the full document (or a structured summary if it exceeds the window) plus the chunk, and produces 1-3 sentences that situate it (entity, period, section, relation to the whole) without rewriting or summarizing the chunk; leverage prompt caching of the document to avoid resending the full text for each chunk and reduce the sweep cost according to {{VOLUMEN_DOCS}}. (3) Dual indexing: for each chunk concatenate context + original text (contextualized_text) and generate (a) its embedding with {{MODELO_EMBEDDINGS}} and (b) its entry in a BM25 index over the same contextualized text, in {{ALMACEN_VECTORIAL}}, to capture semantic similarity and exact matches of terms, codes, and identifiers. (4) Hybrid retrieval: at query time, retrieve top-k dense and top-k BM25, fuse with rank fusion (e.g. Reciprocal Rank Fusion), and apply a reranker to keep the N most relevant; declare initial values of k and N and how to tune them. (5) Delivery to the generator: pass to the model the ORIGINAL chunk (not the prepended context); the context serves only to improve matching, preserving citation fidelity. (6) Storage schema: specify the persisted fields (id, doc_id, position, original_text, contextualized_text, embedding, hash, source metadata, and version) and how to map from retrieved chunk to source document. (7) Evaluation: define recall@k (and optionally nDCG and MRR) over a set of questions with known answers, and an A/B protocol against base RAG without context to quantify the improvement. Cover edge cases: documents that exceed the window, tables and numerical data, multilingual, deduplication of nearly identical chunks, incremental reindexing when a document changes, and fallback if the generated context introduces noise or contradicts the chunk. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}. If a key input is missing ask before designing; do not invent APIs or benchmark figures, mark anything not confirmed as [ASSUMPTION]. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret what you understood, Plan and present the plan, then Execute. Deliver a design document with stages, exact contextualization prompt, storage schema, hybrid retrieval strategy, edge cases, and recall@k evaluation plan with baseline.

prompts.title: Designing a base workflow in n8n
prompts.content: Act as a senior n8n automation engineer, specializing in event-driven workflows with explicit data contracts, idempotency, and resilience to failures. I need the complete design of a base workflow in n8n whose objective is {{OBJETIVO_FLUJO}}, triggered by {{EVENTO_DISPARADOR}} and closing with {{ACCION_FINAL}}, not a sketch: each node with its exact type, clear data contract, and recovery path, so that anyone on the team can import, read, and operate it. Before designing, restate what you understand and present your plan; if {{OBJETIVO_FLUJO}}, {{EVENTO_DISPARADOR}}, {{LOGICA_NEGOCIO}}, {{ACCION_FINAL}}, or {{POLITICA_ERROR}} are incomplete, ask for them instead of inventing them. Proceed as follows: (1) Map the flow into four blocks: Trigger, Logic, Action, and Error Handling. (2) Define each node with its exact n8n type (Webhook, Schedule Trigger, IF, Switch, Set, Code, HTTP Request, Merge, NoOp, Error Trigger, etc.), its expected input, and its output; the Trigger must actually correspond to {{EVENTO_DISPARADOR}}. (3) Specify the data contract: input payload with required and optional fields and their types, normalized JSON output, and behavior when a field is missing, empty, or malformed according to {{LOGICA_NEGOCIO}} (reject, sanitize, or route to error). (4) Resolve idempotency: key that prevents reprocessing or duplicating if {{EVENTO_DISPARADOR}} fires twice. (5) Design the error path using the node's error output or Error Trigger applying {{POLITICA_ERROR}}: retries, wait, backoff, and notification when exhausted, distinguishing transient errors (timeout, 429, 5xx) from permanent ones (4xx, invalid data). (6) Add observability: what is logged at each step to audit a failed execution. (7) Deliver a text diagram of the happy path and one of the error path. (8) Close with a pre-production checklist covering credentials and secrets, idempotency, rate limits, empty payload, and a test with {{ADJUNTOS}} or invalid data. Mark as an explicit assumption every decision without confirmed data. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Configure an AI agent node in n8n with tools, memory, and model
Expose a workflow via webhook with response
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation engineer specialized in n8n, with experience in idempotent HTTP API design. I need to turn an n8n workflow into a reliable and synchronous HTTP endpoint for the use case {{CASO_USO}}: an external system will send requests to {{METODO_RUTA}} and expects a structured, predictable, and deterministic response. The risks to avoid are a webhook that responds 200 to garbage data, leaks internal stack traces in errors, or emits two responses in the same execution.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the use case, the method and route, the payload fields, the authentication, and the expected response format; then present your plan; only then execute. If an essential piece of data is missing, ask me before inventing it; never invent the business domain.

Data:
- Use case / domain: {{CASO_USO}}
- Webhook method and route: {{METODO_RUTA}} (if missing, assume POST)
- Payload fields (name:type, required/optional, format): {{CAMPOS_PAYLOAD}}
- Expected success response: {{RESPUESTA_EXITO}} (if missing, propose standard contract with status, data, and requestId, marked [ASSUMPTION])
- Authentication: {{AUTENTICACION}} (header token, basic, or none)

Produce in this order: (1) Schema of {{CAMPOS_PAYLOAD}} as a table with name, type, required/optional, format or rule, default value, and example. (2) Response contract: success JSON (based on {{RESPUESTA_EXITO}} or the standard) and error JSON with code, message, and fields[] (field + reason), without internal stack traces. (3) Node-by-node design: Webhook with Respond = 'Using Respond to Webhook Node' and method/route from {{METODO_RUTA}}; Code validation node; IF/Switch valid vs invalid; domain processing nodes for {{CASO_USO}}; success Respond (200/201); error Respond (400, 401, 413, 429, 500). (4) Pasteable snippet in a Code node that checks existence, type, and format of each required field from {{CAMPOS_PAYLOAD}} and returns fields[]. (5) Hardening: application of {{AUTENTICACION}}, idempotency by key with deduplication window, payload size limit, and rate limiting.

Rules: exactly one Respond to Webhook per branch; never two responses in the same execution; internal errors in a generic message; all data not provided marked [ASSUMPTION]. Close with verifiable quality checklist.

prompts.title: Design error handling and retries in n8n
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation engineer expert in n8n, integrations, and resilient production workflows. I need to harden {{WORKFLOW_OBJETIVO}}, which currently fails silently: a node goes down, a credential expires, or an API rate-limits, and the execution stops without anyone noticing until the business spots the missing data. Design the complete resilience strategy. Before executing, restate the objective and present your plan; if any key data is missing (purpose, critical nodes, retry policy, channel, environment), ask in a single batch rather than assuming.

Deliver: (1) Centralized Error Workflow with an Error Trigger that consumes n8n's error object (execution.id, execution.url, workflow.name, node.name, error.message, error.stack), with the exact instruction to link it in Settings > Error Workflow of {{WORKFLOW_OBJETIVO}}, and the warning that the Error Trigger does not capture nodes with Continue On Fail active. (2) Retry matrix for the nodes in {{NODOS_CRITICOS}} according to {{POLITICA_REINTENTOS}}: Retry On Fail, Max Tries (3-5 suggested), Wait Between Tries in ms, transient classification (timeout, 429, 5xx, ECONNRESET -> retry) vs permanent (400, 401, 403, 404, 422, validation -> fail fast). (3) Stepped backoff or manual IF + Wait + counter pattern in $getWorkflowStaticData, respecting the Retry-After header where present. (4) Degradation: Continue On Fail / error output on non-critical nodes, with a route to a degradation branch or persistent dead-letter queue. (5) Notification: Set/Code node that normalizes {severity, workflow, node, message, ISO timestamp America/Bogota, link} and sends it to {{CANAL_NOTIFICACION}}, with anti-storm deduplication. (6) Idempotency in {{ENTORNO}} for writes, payments, and sends. (7) Test runbook that forces each failure mode and validates retries, single alert, and no duplication. Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided.

Assumptions: without explicit policy, use Max Tries 3 and stepped Wait 2000-5000 ms; 5xx and 429 = transient unless otherwise stated. Limits: do not invent version-dependent n8n features; mark {to_confirm} for unverified items. Close: ready when Error Workflow, matrix, payload, idempotency, and runbook allow implementation with no pending decisions. Neutral professional English.

Parameters:
- {{WORKFLOW_OBJETIVO}}: name and purpose of the workflow to harden
- {{NODOS_CRITICOS}}: nodes whose failure is likely or costly
- {{POLITICA_REINTENTOS}}: max tries, spacing, and desired classification (optional)
- {{CANAL_NOTIFICACION}}: alert destination (Slack, email, Telegram, webhook)
- {{ENTORNO}}: n8n Cloud or self-hosted, version, and base URL (optional)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: JSON export, screenshots, logs, or 'No attachments'

prompts.title: Process data in bulk with Split In Batches
Build a RAG pipeline in n8n
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation engineer specialized in n8n and production RAG architectures. I need a knowledge base queryable in natural language built inside n8n, without depending on custom code that only I can maintain: the visual flow makes it auditable and reusable, and allows answering questions grounded in my own documents with the sources cited. Deliver the design of TWO decoupled n8n workflows, ready to build node by node.

INGESTION Workflow: ordered list of nodes with their exact type: Trigger over {{FUENTE_INGESTA}}, Default Data Loader, Recursive Character Text Splitter, Embeddings ({{MODELO_EMBEDDING}}), Vector Store ({{VECTOR_STORE}}) in insert or upsert mode. Define the metadata schema per chunk (source, document path or id, indexing date, chunk number, total chunks, and document hash) and the anti-duplicate strategy on re-ingestion (upsert by hash, or prior deletion of chunks from the same document before reinserting). Include a branch for unchanged documents (same hash, skip) to avoid reprocessing or inflating costs.

QUERY Workflow: {{DISPARADOR}}, retrieval node (Vector Store in retrieve mode or Retriever), Chat Model ({{MODELO_LLM}}), Question and Answer Chain or Agent with a system prompt that mandates citing sources and abstaining without context, and Respond to Webhook. Key configuration per node: vector dimension matching {{MODELO_EMBEDDING}}, similarity metric, chunk size and overlap, k value (top-k), minimum similarity threshold, and generation prompt template.

Close with error handling (retries with backoff, failure branch via Error Trigger or continue-on-fail, no-context response, and vector-store-down response), justified criteria for adjusting chunk, overlap, and k based on density, and the versioning and reuse procedure (export JSON, parameterize credentials and vector store via environment variables, what to change for a new use case).

Rules: each node must exist in n8n with its exact type and order; the vector store dimension must match {{MODELO_EMBEDDING}}; ingestion and query must be separate. Justify chunk, overlap, and k; do not use arbitrary numbers. If {{FUENTE_INGESTA}}, {{VECTOR_STORE}}, {{MODELO_EMBEDDING}}, {{MODELO_LLM}}, or {{DISPARADOR}} are missing or inconsistent (e.g., embedding dimension that does not match the index), stop and ask. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

prompts.title: Transform data with expressions and Code node
Modularize with reusable subworkflows
prompts.content:
Act as a senior n8n automation architect specialized in modular design and reuse patterns (Execute Workflow, data contracts, idempotency, subworkflow versioning). Several workflows repeat {{LOGICA_REPETIDA}} copied and pasted; each change forces touching N places and that multiplies divergence and silent errors. I want to move from copy-paste to a strategy of reusable components without stopping production. Design the complete modularization of {{LOGICA_REPETIDA}} present in {{FLUJOS_CONSUMIDORES}}. Deliver: (1) inventory of {{LOGICA_REPETIDA}} grouped by single responsibility, with subworkflow candidates named with the convention sub-<domain>-<action>; (2) data contract per subworkflow according to {{CONTRATO_DATOS}}: input fields for the Execute Workflow trigger, output fields, types, required/optional, and default values; (3) internal design of each subworkflow: key nodes, input validation at the start, error branches, and output node with stable versioned shape; (4) resulting parent workflow: replacement of the embedded block with Execute Workflow, execution mode, and exact parameter mapping; (5) error strategy aligned with {{POLITICA_ERRORES}}: continueOnFail vs Error Trigger node, propagation to parent, idempotency with natural keys, and retries with backoff; (6) incremental migration plan flow by flow on n8n {{VERSION_N8N}}, without breaking production, with per-stage parity verification and rollback. Consider nesting depth, sensitive data crossing the contract, and node compatibility by version. Take {{ADJUNTOS}} into account. Mark each assumption with [ASSUMPTION]. Before designing, restate what you understood and present your plan; if critical data is missing, ask instead of inventing.

Variables: {{LOGICA_REPETIDA}}, {{FLUJOS_CONSUMIDORES}}, {{CONTRATO_DATOS}}, {{POLITICA_ERRORES}}, {{VERSION_N8N}}, {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Design a base scenario in Make
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation architect in Make (formerly Integromat), with experience in production scenarios with routers, filters, iterators, aggregators, and data mapping between apps. Design an executable base scenario for {{ESCENARIO_OBJETIVO}} connecting {{APPS_CONECTADAS}}, taking it from a mental design to a module-by-module replicable blueprint in the visual editor, without rework.

Before executing, apply the MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret {{ESCENARIO_OBJETIVO}} in a sentence from end to end (origin, transformation, destination), restate what you understand, present your plan, and then execute. If key information is missing, ask for it before inventing; never assume credentials, IDs, endpoints, or real field names.

Deliver the design in this order: (1) Framing that confirms objective, apps and role according to {{APPS_CONECTADAS}}, trigger and {{LOGICA_RAMIFICACION}}, and lists assumptions marked [ASSUMPTION]. (2) Trigger derived from {{EVENTO_DISPARADOR}} with declared type (instant by webhook / scheduled / polling), app, operation, and data it delivers to the flow. (3) Numbered module sequence in execution order over {{APPS_CONECTADAS}}, each one with app, operation, type (action, search, iterator, aggregator), and purpose. (4) Routers where {{LOGICA_RAMIFICACION}} requires branching, with each route named, its distinctive criterion, and the fallback route. (5) Filters with exact condition (field, operator, value) indicating which bundles pass and which are discarded. (6) Data mapping per action: table target field <- source field with originating module, applied transformation (formatDate, trim, ifempty, parseNumber, etc.), and handling of missing fields. (7) Robustness: error handling routes (break / resume / rollback / ignore) per critical module, retries, and operations estimate per execution. (8) Test before activating: sample data, what to verify in each module with "Run once", and activation criterion.

Parameters:
- {{ESCENARIO_OBJETIVO}}: process to automate and expected result.
- {{APPS_CONECTADAS}}: apps to connect and their role (origin, destination, enrichment).
- {{EVENTO_DISPARADOR}}: what starts the scenario (instant by webhook, scheduled, polling for new records).
- {{LOGICA_RAMIFICACION}}: branching and filtering rules.
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments".

Closing criterion: the scenario is ready when trigger, modules, routers, filters, and mapping are unambiguous, everything unconfirmed is marked [ASSUMPTION], and it includes error plan, operations estimate, and test script. No emojis, neutral professional English.

prompts.title: Branch logic with routers and filters in Make
prompts.content: Act as a senior automation architect in Make (Integromat), specialized in high-volume scenarios and conditional routing. Design the branching logic of a scenario that processes records from {{ORIGEN_DATOS}} for {{CASO_USO}}, where today all follow the same path or consume operations on irrelevant records. Deliver: (1) decision fields table from {{CAMPOS_DECISION}} with name, type (text/number/date/boolean/list), and role in routing; (2) discard filters that eliminate {{CRITERIOS_DESCARTE}}, placed on the link BEFORE the router to avoid spending operations; (3) router design according to {{RUTAS_CONDICIONES}}, each output with a readable name, its filter (field + correct operator by type + value), and the subsequent modules; (4) top-down evaluation order, resolution of records matching more than one condition, and a fallback or catch-all route without filter and marked as such so nothing is silently discarded; (5) recommended operators by type (text: equal/contains; number: greater/less; date: later/earlier; existence: exists/does not exist), handling of empty or null fields, and AND (same row) / OR (separate rows) logic. Follow the MetodologIA Protocol: restate use case, source, and routes, mark assumptions and ask for missing data; present route map for validation; then develop detailed design and verify against checklist. If {{CASO_USO}}, {{ORIGEN_DATOS}}, {{CAMPOS_DECISION}}, {{RUTAS_CONDICIONES}}, or {{CRITERIOS_DESCARTE}} are empty or ambiguous, ask for them before designing. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

prompts.title: Configure error handling in Make
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation architect specialized in Make (Integromat), with experience in transactional production scenarios and fault tolerance design. Design a complete error handling plan ready to configure in Make for the scenario {{ESCENARIO}}, currently fragile on failures.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate {{ESCENARIO}}, its resilience objective, and {{POLITICA_FALLO}}; then present the plan skeleton and detected assumptions and wait for confirmation; only then develop the detail.

Deliver these blocks: (1) Failure map: for each module of {{MODULOS_CRITICOS}} identify the expected error (timeout, 429 rate limit, 4xx vs 5xx, missing or malformed data, dropped connection, duplicate payload), classify severity (critical, high, medium), and whether it is transient or permanent. (2) Error handlers per module: assign the correct Make directive and justify it according to {{POLITICA_FALLO}}, distinguishing Resume, Rollback, Commit, Ignore, and Break and their correct use case; if {{SISTEMA_TRANSACCIONAL}} requires it, indicate when to activate sequential processing and transaction handling for Rollback to be effective. (3) Recovery and retry routes: define the policy according to {{TOLERANCIA_REINTENTOS}} (number, wait, backoff), separate retryable from non-retryable errors going to review, the use of Break toward incomplete executions with reprocessing criterion and idempotency to avoid duplicating, and alternative routes that recover the flow without losing the data. (4) Observability and alert: define what to notify {{CANAL_ALERTA}} with minimum actionable context (execution id, module, payload reference, received error, timestamp, action taken) and a threshold to avoid flooding. Verify against checklist and note residual risks.

Consider {{ADJUNTOS}} if provided. Mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION] and ask for missing data instead of inventing it; never mention prices.

Parameters:
- {{ESCENARIO}}: name and purpose of the Make scenario (what triggers it, what it does, what systems it touches)
- {{MODULOS_CRITICOS}}: modules that may fail (HTTP/API, database, data store, third parties with rate limit)
- {{POLITICA_FALLO}}: what to do on failure (revert everything, continue with the rest, retry, stop clean)
- {{SISTEMA_TRANSACCIONAL}}: whether there are operations requiring atomicity/rollback (yes/no and which ones)
- {{TOLERANCIA_REINTENTOS}}: number of retries and wait between attempts (optional)
- {{CANAL_ALERTA}}: where to notify failures (email, Slack, webhook, other)
- {{ADJUNTOS}}: attached files, URLs, or "No attachments"

prompts.title: Processing arrays with Iterator and Aggregator in Make
prompts.content:
Act as a senior automation architect in Make (Integromat), expert in high-volume scenarios and operation consumption control. In Make I have a scenario where a module delivers {{ARRAY_ORIGEN}} and I need to process each element separately to return a single reaggregated result in {{FORMATO_SALIDA}}. Each item has the shape {{ESTRUCTURA_ITEM}} and per element I must {{TRANSFORMACION_POR_ITEM}}; if I need several groups instead of one, I will group by {{GROUP_BY}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

If {{ARRAY_ORIGEN}}, {{ESTRUCTURA_ITEM}}, or {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} is missing, ask for them before proceeding; do not invent data and mark assumptions as [ASSUMPTION].

>> MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. Restate what you understand and present your plan before executing.

Deliver: 1) Diagnosis of which array to iterate in {{ARRAY_ORIGEN}}, where it originates, and why Iterator is preferable over direct mapping (or why it is NOT needed if the module already emits bundles). 2) Iterator configuration: the array field you map. 3) Per-item transformation ({{TRANSFORMACION_POR_ITEM}}): modules between Iterator and Aggregator and how to reference the current item. 4) Aggregator choice based on {{FORMATO_SALIDA}} (Array/Text/Numeric/JSON) with a one-line justification. 5) Aggregator configuration: Source Module pointing to Iterator, aggregated fields, separator or Group by ({{GROUP_BY}}) and bundle order. 6) Operation control: estimate the pattern's consumption and how to limit it. 7) Three common errors and prevention. Close with the guide ready to reproduce module by module.

prompts.title: Building a multi-step Zap with logic
Normalizing data with Zapier Formatter
prompts.content:
Act as a senior no-code automation engineer, specialist in Zapier and in the Formatter by Zapier step (Date/Time, Numbers, and Text transformations). I need the complete design of a Formatter step chain that intercepts between the trigger of {{APP_ORIGEN}} and the final action of {{APP_DESTINO}}, so that raw data arrives typed, predictable, and clean, without silent errors or stopped Zaps.

Fields to normalize with their raw example value: {{CAMPOS_CRUDOS}}. Expected output format per field: {{FORMATO_DESTINO}}. Time zone and locale (decimal/thousands separator): {{TZ_LOCALE}}. Attachments: {{ADJUNTOS}}.

Before designing, ask for what is missing and do not invent it: if I do not have a real raw example, the destination format, the time zone, or the locale, ask for them; do not assume date format or time zone.

MetodologIA Protocol: Interpret > Plan > Execute. First restate the normalization in a sentence of the type 'Clean [fields] from {{APP_ORIGEN}} before sending them to {{APP_DESTINO}} so that [result]' and present your plan; then execute.

Deliver: (1) field table with field, raw example value, target type (date / number / text / boolean), and expected value; (2) for each field, the exact Formatter step: category, Transform, mapped input and precise parameters (date tokens, to/from timezone, decimals, currency), indicating whether grouping is preferable; (3) resolved edge cases: empty or null (Default Value before transforming), ambiguous date (explicit input format), thousands separator and currency, spaces and line breaks (Trim), out-of-range values, encoding; (4) step order and mapping of each Formatter output to the destination field (step N to step N+1); (5) test plan with 3 to 5 inputs (include one empty and one with a different format) and expected output for Test step; (6) robustness note: Filter or Paths, idempotency, and Zap History review.

Mark every decision made without my data with [ASSUMPTION]. Neutral professional Spanish, no emojis. Do not include prices.

prompts.title: Inserting an AI step into a Zap
Choosing the right automation platform
Automating ticket triage and classification
prompts.content:
